title: Request an export of your account data
summary: Request a verified account-data copy, download its report and ZIP parts within seven days, and follow exact code, archive, retention and retry limits.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/components/account/privacy-section.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/data-rights.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/data/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/data/verify.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/account/export/constants.ts on 2026-10-14. Production UI was not exercised.
body: Open **Profile → Privacy → Get a copy of your data** from a signed-in browser session. An API key cannot read or start this account-level request. ## Steps 1. Select **Request it**. Dosya records an access request with a 30-day response deadline and emails a six-digit confirmation code. 2. Enter the code under **We emailed you a code**, then select **Confirm**. A code lasts 15 minutes, resending is limited to once every 60 seconds, and five wrong attempts burn that code. 3. Leave the page open while **Your code was accepted and we are putting your copy together** appears. A build stuck for 15 minutes is marked failed so **Try again** becomes available. 4. Download the readable report, manifest, and every numbered ZIP archive shown. These downloads expire seven days after creation. 5. If you ask again within one hour, Dosya returns the same current copy instead of walking the account again. The report contains account and workspace records plus structured JSON/CSV. Archives contain files you uploaded when download permissions allow. Archive planning stops at 50,000 files, splits parts at 5,000 entries or 4 GiB, and keeps at most 10,000 recent activity records. A truncated delivery stays open and explains what remains owed. ## Expected result The Privacy panel records the request and deadline. A completed answer exposes the report and all available archive parts until their expiry; no files, settings, or sessions are changed by requesting the copy. If the page says **That code is not correct**, retry the current code before its fifth failed attempt. For **That code has expired. Request a new one.**, use **Send me a code** after the countdown. Preserve the displayed request record when an export has expired; the legal record remains even though its download links disappear. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Delete an account](/account/delete-account)

title: Delete your Dosya account
summary: Review what account deletion removes, resolve workspace blockers, schedule deletion with an email code, or cancel during the waiting period.
verification: Reviewed the account deletion preview, confirmation, waiting-period and cancellation flows against the local current web app and API on 2026-10-12. The screenshot uses isolated representative account data.
body: Deleting your account permanently removes the account and its data after a waiting period. Dosya shows a review before it sends the confirmation code, so you can copy data and resolve workspace ownership first. ## Before you start - Download any files, billing records or account information you need to keep. - Check every workspace you own. A workspace with other members blocks deletion until you transfer ownership or remove those members. - If you only want to stop a paid plan or leave one workspace, use that workspace's billing or membership controls instead. - Keep access to your account email. Dosya sends a six-digit confirmation code there. - Do not begin while important uploads, transfers or downloads are still running. ## Steps: review and schedule account deletion 1. Sign in to Dosya and open **Profile**. 2. Select **Delete account**. 3. Review the deletion summary. Check the number of owned workspaces, files, the waiting period and any blockers. 4. If Dosya lists a workspace blocker, open that workspace and transfer ownership or remove its remaining members. Return to the deletion page and refresh the review. 5. Select the option to request the confirmation code. 6. Open the message sent to your account email and enter its six-digit code. A code expires, so request a new one if it is no longer accepted. 7. Confirm the deletion request. Dosya schedules deletion and signs you out. ## Expected result Dosya confirms that deletion is scheduled, shows the final deletion date and signs you out. The current waiting period is shown in your own deletion review; do not calculate it from this guide. You may sign in again before that deadline and cancel the scheduled deletion. After a successful cancellation, your account remains active and you can use it normally. ## Limits and consequences - The action applies to the whole account. It is broader than cancelling a subscription or leaving a workspace. - Deletion cannot be scheduled while an owned workspace still has other members. - Everything covered by the deletion review is destroyed when the countdown ends. Treat the deadline as final. - A confirmation code only proves access to the email; it does not bypass workspace blockers. - If you use Vault, make any needed local copies while you can still unlock the encrypted files. ## Troubleshooting **The page says a workspace blocks deletion.** Open the named workspace. Transfer ownership to another suitable member if the workspace must continue, or remove the other members if it should be deleted with your account. Then reload the review. **The code did not arrive.** Confirm the email shown on the page, check spam or filtering folders, wait a few minutes, then request another code. Use only the newest valid code. **The code is rejected.** Enter all six digits without surrounding spaces. Request a replacement if the code expired or if you requested another one afterward. **You changed your mind.** Sign in before the displayed deletion deadline and use the cancellation action. If the deadline has already passed, the deletion cannot be reversed through the cancellation flow. **You only need to end billing.** Return to the affected workspace's billing settings. Do not schedule account deletion solely to stop a plan. ## Related guides - [Update your profile settings](/account/profile-settings) - [Reset your password](/account/reset-password) - [Recover access when two-factor authentication is unavailable](/account/two-factor-recovery)

title: Document suspicious account activity for support
summary: Capture the session time, device, browser, available IP and location evidence support needs while keeping passwords, codes, cookies and keys private.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/profile/sessions.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/profile/shared.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts on 2026-10-14. Production support intake was not exercised.
body: Use **Profile → Sessions** to identify an unfamiliar login before contacting support. The list is account-wide and requires an authenticated browser session. ## Steps 1. Find the questionable row under **Active sessions**. Record its displayed device, browser, available IP/location, and relative activity time; note whether another row carries the **Current** badge. 2. Capture the time zone shown by your device and the exact Dosya URL or workspace/file identifier involved. Describe the action you observed and its first and most recent occurrence. 3. Save relevant notification or error text verbatim. Include a redacted screenshot when it clarifies which row or resource is affected. 4. Select **Revoke all other sessions** when you do not recognize one or more noncurrent sessions. Success reports **Sessions revoked** and signs those sessions out; the current session remains. 5. Send support the evidence through the private support route. Exclude passwords, email verification codes, two-factor codes, recovery keys, API keys, session cookies, share passwords, and full payment-card details. A successful bulk action deletes other browser sessions, marks other mobile tokens revoked, and schedules their cache invalidation; it cannot restore work an affected device had not saved. If the suspicious row is the current session, secure the account from another trusted device and change the password, because the bulk control intentionally preserves the session making the request. ## Expected result Support receives a reproducible timeline tied to a specific session and resource, while reusable credentials remain undisclosed. After revocation, the current browser session remains, as do caller-linked Files or File Provider credentials for that same device and any sessions authenticated afterward. If Sessions shows **No sessions** or does not load, reload while still signed in and record the failure time. A failed bulk action reports **Revoke failed** with the server message; do not assume the other devices were signed out until **Sessions revoked** appears. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Respond to suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Review all workspaces on your account
summary: Read the My workspaces list, identify each membership and role, and use the workspace switcher when you need to inspect its files or settings.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/profile/workspaces.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/workspace-dashboard.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/workspace/member-workspaces.ts. The review remained local and made no production, database, or provider request.
body: The **My workspaces** profile page is an account-wide membership list. It shows every non-deleting workspace the signed-in user can reach, including workspaces owned by somebody else. It does not change the active workspace or open a workspace row. Each entry contains the workspace name, icon, the relative date you joined, and a role badge. Built-in badges are **Owner**, **Admin**, **Member**, and **Viewer**. A workspace-defined role appears here as **Custom role** because this list does not receive the custom role's name. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile** and select **My workspaces**. On a phone-width web view, open **Profile** first and choose the **My workspaces** row. 2. Match the workspace name and icon with the membership you expect. The list is ordered by workspace creation time, so it is not a recent-workspaces list. 3. Read the role badge. **Owner** controls ownership; **Admin**, **Member**, and **Viewer** have different permissions; **Custom role** means the precise name must be checked inside that workspace's team settings. 4. Note the **Joined** time if you are investigating a membership you do not recognize. 5. To inspect content, use the main workspace switcher and select the same workspace. Confirm the workspace name again before changing files, members, storage rules, or sharing settings. 6. To leave or delete a workspace, use its supported membership or workspace action. The profile list itself is read-only. ## What the list includes The server excludes a workspace whose content state is already **deleting**. Ordinary browser and mobile sessions receive every membership for the current user. A workspace-pinned API key receives only its pinned workspace, but API-key access is not the normal profile workflow. Membership in other people's workspaces does not count against the Free plan's creation limit. The Free plan limit applies to workspaces the account owns: it can own at most **3**. This page can therefore show more than three memberships. ## Troubleshooting If the page says **No workspaces**, refresh after confirming the email shown in the profile header. If a workspace is missing, it may have been removed from your memberships or entered deletion. If a badge says **Custom role**, open that workspace's team page to see the role name and its permissions. For an unfamiliar membership, avoid changing content until the owner and invitation are identified. Use the join date and workspace name when reporting the issue. ## Expected result You can account for every listed workspace, understand the displayed role, and switch into the intended workspace only when further inspection is needed. ## Related guides - [Switch workspaces](/account/switch-workspaces) - [Leave or delete a workspace](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Filter activity by action
summary: Pick exact workspace event types, combine them with other activity filters, and verify that only matching actions remain while paging restarts.
verification: Reviewed on 2026-10-14 using local browser filter components, the generated action vocabulary, API query construction, paging policy, and permission/response tests in apps/web/src/pages/activity.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/activity-catalog.generated.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/activity.test.tsx. No production verification was performed.
body: Use **Action** to isolate exact operations such as a download, permanent deletion, revoked invitation, or changed workspace setting. The choice is read-only and cannot reverse the operation recorded by a row. ## Available action labels With **Category** left at **All categories**, the browser offers these filterable actions: - Files: **File uploaded**, **Version uploaded**, **File downloaded**, **File deleted**, **Permanently deleted**, **File restored**, **File renamed**, **File moved**, **File copied**, **File locked**, and **File hidden**. - Folders: **Folder created**, **Folder renamed**, **Folder moved**, and **Folder deleted**. - Sharing: **File shared (link)**, **File shared (email)**, **Folder shared**, **Link revoked**, **File request created**, **Request upload**, and **Request revoked**. - Members: **Member invited**, **Member joined**, **Member removed**, **Member left**, **Invite revoked**, **Ownership transferred**, **Member role changed**, and **Folder access changed**. - Workspace: **Workspace created**, **Workspace updated**, **Settings changed**, **Role updated**, and **Role deleted**. - Comments: **Comment added** and **Comment deleted**. The activity feed can display additional event codes that are readable in a row but are not in this filter list. For example, the shared label catalog includes sync, group, profile, plan, coupon, and favourite events. Those rows remain visible under **All actions** but cannot be targeted by this menu until their codes become filter options. The web route requires **View activity log** and refuses members confined to a single folder. Action filtering has no separate paid-plan requirement. Desktop currently presents its activity feed in 50-row pages without Category, Member, or Action menus, so perform this procedure in the browser app. ## Steps 1. Set the intended workspace, then open the top search field and enter `Activity`. 2. Choose the **Activity** page result and verify that **Activity log** appears. 3. If the action menu is unexpectedly short, inspect **Category** first. Selected categories deliberately restrict which action names are offered. 4. Open **Action**. Its initial label is **All actions**. 5. In **Action**, check each operation you want to include. The menu stays open so several actions can be selected in one pass. 6. Close the menu and review the total marked **(filtered)**. A change to Action immediately reloads the feed and places you on **Page 1**. 7. Optionally choose **Category** or **Member** as additional boundaries. Selected actions are alternatives to one another; those other menus are simultaneous requirements. If you alter **Category** after step 5, Dosya removes the Action checks. This prevents an action hidden by the new category set from continuing as an invisible constraint. ## Expected result Every displayed row has one of the checked action types and also satisfies any active Category or Member condition. One choice replaces **All actions** with that label; multiple choices display the number selected. More than 30 matches create numbered pages, and the result count covers all pages rather than only the visible rows. ## Troubleshooting the selection **Only some action labels appear.** Remove the checks under **Category**, then reopen Action. With no category selected, the menu restores every currently catalogued action type. **A known event does not appear.** Choose **Clear filters**, confirm the event exists in the full newest-first feed, and then select its exact action label. Similar operations have separate values, such as **File deleted** and **Permanently deleted**. **The page reports No activity found.** At least one cross-menu condition has no common event. Relax Member or Category before concluding that the audit record is missing. **The screen displays Could not load the activity log.** Use **Try again**. If the detail says **You don't have permission to view the activity log**, an owner or admin must change the role; retrying does not grant access. ## Related guides - [Interpret workspace audit entries](/workspaces/activity) - [Review custom and built-in roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Group events by product category](/workspaces/activity-filter-category) - [Open and page through activity](/workspaces/activity-open-log)

title: Filter activity by category
summary: Choose one or more activity categories, learn which events each group contains, and confirm the matching total returns to page one after changes.
verification: Reviewed on 2026-10-14 against local browser activity UI, shared activity catalog, API filter and paging implementation, permission gates, and activity tests in apps/web/src/pages/activity.tsx, packages/shared/src/activity/catalog.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.*.unit.test.ts. No production verification was performed.
body: Use **Category** when you know the part of the workspace involved but not the exact event name. The browser app can show several categories at once and combine that choice with **Member** or **Action**. ## What the category choices include The current **Category** menu contains six groups: - **Files** covers uploads, downloads, versions, file deletion and recovery, rename, move, copy, lock, and visibility changes. - **Folders** groups folder creation, rename, move, and deletion. - **Sharing** includes file or folder shares, revoked links, and file-request creation, upload, or revocation. - **Members** contains invitations, joins, removals, departures, revoked invitations, ownership transfers, role changes, and folder-access changes. - **Workspace** matches workspace creation or updates, setting changes, and role updates or deletions. - **Comments** limits the feed to added and deleted comments. These groups cover the action IDs listed in Dosya's activity catalog. An event whose newer action ID has not been assigned to one of those groups may still appear in the unfiltered feed but will not be returned by a category selection. You need **View activity log** for the page. A member restricted to one folder cannot open this workspace-wide log, even if their role otherwise grants that permission. The route does not inspect the subscription tier; access depends on membership scope and role permissions. Category filtering only reads audit records and cannot change, undo, or delete any workspace item. ## Steps 1. In the browser app, select the active workspace you want to investigate. 2. From **Dashboard**, find the **Activity** card and choose **All**. You can instead use the top search field, type `Activity`, and open the **Activity** result. 3. Confirm the heading says **Activity log** and note the total shown beneath it. 4. Open **Category**, whose unfiltered value is **All categories**. 5. Check one or more category names. Each check immediately requests a new result set; there is no separate Apply button. 6. Read the count again. Dosya adds **(filtered)** and resets the pagination control to **Page 1** whenever the category selection changes. 7. If needed, add **Member** or **Action** constraints. Multiple categories match any selected category, while a different filter menu must also match. For example, **Files** plus member Ada means file-category events attributed to Ada. Changing the category selection clears every current **Action** choice because the available action list is rebuilt from the chosen groups. Select the categories first when you intend to use both menus. ## Expected result The header reports the number of events matching the complete filter combination, followed by **(filtered)**. Rows remain ordered from newest to oldest. A result set longer than 30 rows displays **Page 1 of N** with next and previous controls. ## If the result looks wrong **A category produces no rows.** The page shows **No activity found** and **Try adjusting your filters**. Remove a Member or Action condition, or choose **Clear filters** to return all three menus to their `All` state. **The action you need is absent after choosing a category.** Open Category and add the group that owns that action, or remove all category checks so **Action** offers every catalogued type. **Activity is not available.** A resolved permission check shows **You do not have access to this page.** Ask an owner or admin to grant **View activity log**. Folder-confined access cannot be expanded from this screen. **The request fails instead of returning zero events.** The error card says **Could not load the activity log** and includes **Try again**. Retry after checking the connection; a successful empty query uses the distinct **No activity found** state. ## Related guides - [Read event fields and privacy boundaries](/workspaces/activity) - [Understand role permissions](/workspaces/roles) - [Narrow the log to exact actions](/workspaces/activity-filter-action) - [Review events from selected members](/workspaces/activity-filter-member)

title: Filter activity by workspace member
summary: Choose current workspace members, combine the selection with other filters, and verify the log shows only events attributed to those people.
verification: Reviewed on 2026-10-14 from local browser activity controls, API member-filter and roster gates, response privacy shaping, paging code, and focused tests in apps/web/src/pages/activity.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.roster-gate.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.gate.unit.test.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.confined.unit.test.ts. No production verification was performed.
body: The **Member** filter narrows the audit feed by recorded actor. Use it to review one person's workspace operations or compare a controlled set of current members without changing their roles, files, or sessions. ## Permissions and member availability Opening the dedicated audit page requires **View activity log**. Populating its Member menu additionally requires **View team members**, because that menu contains the workspace roster, including names and email addresses. A role with the first permission but not the second can still read permitted activity rows, while the Member menu opens with **No options**. Neither the roster selector nor the log applies a subscription-tier test. The two permission keys and the absence of a folder restriction determine whether this workflow is available. The choices are current members sorted by name. Dosya displays a member's name, falling back to their email when the name is empty. Someone who left or was removed may still have historical events, but they are no longer in the selectable roster; investigate those rows through time, category, and action instead. A request accepts at most 50 selected member IDs. If a large workspace needs more than 50 actors checked, divide the review into smaller groups so every intended person reaches the server. ## Steps 1. Choose the relevant workspace in the browser app. 2. Open **Activity log** by selecting **All** on Dashboard's Activity card, or search the top bar for `Activity` and open that page result. 3. Select **Member**. With no constraint, the trigger reads **All members**. 4. Check the person or people whose actions you are tracing. The dropdown remains available for multiple selections and shows one name or `N selected` in its trigger. 5. Let the page refresh; selecting or removing any member returns the feed to **Page 1** without an Apply step. 6. Under **Activity log**, verify each visible row names one of the chosen actors. If Category or Action is also active, confirm the row satisfies those conditions too. 7. Read the updated total beneath **Activity log**. The **(filtered)** marker means at least one of the three menus is constraining the results. Within Member, the checked people are alternatives: an event by any one of them qualifies. Across menus the logic is cumulative, so two members plus **Sharing** shows sharing-category events by either selected actor. Each browser page contains up to 30 matching rows. ## Expected result The count covers every audit event attributed to one of the selected current members that also meets the active Category and Action constraints. The visible slice begins on page 1, and the rows keep descending timestamp order. Filtering by a person does not expand what you may learn about that person. Owners and admins can see available forensic fields. Other roles with log access receive another member's event with source IP, device, location, session, and request identifier removed; inaccessible file or folder names are withheld as well. ## Resolve missing members or events **Member opens with No options.** Confirm the role has **View team members** as well as **View activity log**. This state can be correct even while activity rows load normally. **A former member is absent.** The selector is built from present workspace memberships. Clear Member, then narrow with Action or Category and identify the historical actor in the returned rows. **The list shows No activity found.** Choose **Clear filters**, reselect a smaller actor set, and add other conditions one at a time. The empty message is a successful query, unlike a failed request. **Could not load the activity log appears.** Select **Try again** after checking connectivity. A folder-confined account receives **Not a member** for this workspace-wide endpoint and needs an unrestricted membership to use the page. ## Related guides - [Understand visible audit metadata](/workspaces/activity) - [Configure workspace role access](/workspaces/roles) - [Reach the complete workspace log](/workspaces/activity-open-log) - [Limit results to exact operations](/workspaces/activity-filter-action)

title: Inspect activity event details
summary: Expand one workspace activity row to read its timestamp, source, outcome, resource, device, and available identifiers without exposing hidden names.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/activity.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/activity.int.test.ts. Production behavior was not changed.
body: An expanded activity row provides investigation context while the API withholds fields and resource names the viewer is not allowed to receive. ## Before you start - Select the correct workspace and open **Activity log**. - Your role needs **View activity log**; a folder-confined membership cannot open the workspace-wide page. - Keep the approximate time, actor, action, or resource name available. The page loads 30 rows per page. ## Steps 1. Use **Category**, **Member**, and **Action** to narrow the event list; changing a filter returns the view to page 1. 2. Select the row that matches the actor, relative time, action phrase, and visible resource name. 3. Expand the row and read **When**, which shows the local absolute timestamp and its relative age. 4. Record **Where**, **Device**, **Source**, and **Outcome** only when those fields appear; missing context is not reconstructed by the client. 5. Copy the **Resource** or **Session** value that is actually displayed, keeping IP and session values private. 6. Open the linked resource when available and compare its present state with the recorded outcome before drawing a conclusion. ## What the expanded row can show **Where** combines the recorded source IP with approximate city and country data when available. **Device** is parsed from the user-agent string. **Outcome** may include a reason, while failure and denial also receive a visible badge. Not every event carries every field. For another member’s event, the server removes sensitive forensic fields unless the viewer has the required activity access. Hidden or locked resources can lose their names while the event itself remains. An audit row records a request outcome; it is not a file snapshot, packet trace, or recovery tool. ## Expected result The selected event is identified by its actor, action, absolute time, and any permitted context. Restricted names or forensic values remain absent, and the current resource is checked independently. ## Troubleshooting **Could not load the activity log.** Confirm **View activity log**, remove any folder confinement through an authorized administrator, and use **Try again**. **No activity found.** Select **Clear filters**, then page backward through older results. **A resource name is blank.** A live or trashed target may be hidden or behind a locked folder. Purged file and folder events retain their recorded names; unresolved link or group targets are stripped defensively. ## Related guides - [Read workspace activity](/workspaces/activity) - [Understand workspace roles](/workspaces/roles)

title: Open the workspace activity log
summary: Open the browser activity log, confirm access and event ordering, then read the count, paging controls, row details, and privacy limits safely.
verification: Reviewed on 2026-10-14 against local browser navigation, activity rendering, API response shaping, paging, permission gates, and visibility tests in apps/web/src/pages/dashboard.tsx, apps/web/src/components/layout/global-search.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/activity.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.*.unit.test.ts. No production verification was performed.
body: The browser **Activity log** is the workspace-wide audit feed. It answers who performed a supported operation, what action was recorded, which accessible resource it concerned, and when it happened. Opening or filtering this page does not alter the underlying event or resource. ## Access and platform rules - The selected workspace role must grant **View activity log**. Built-in owners and admins have this permission; a custom role depends on its configured keys. - A folder-restricted membership cannot use the full log because the endpoint has no safe way to reduce a workspace-wide audit trail to one subtree. - Activity is not checked against a subscription plan. Membership, folder scope, and role permissions decide availability. - The browser page uses 30 events per page. The desktop Activity screen uses 50 per page and has a different, unfiltered interface; mobile has its own Activity screen and filter sheet. - A separate **View team members** permission controls whether the browser receives the current roster for the Member filter. It does not control the event feed itself. ## Steps 1. Sign in to the browser app and select the workspace whose history you need. 2. On **Dashboard**, locate the **Activity** card and select **All**. If that card is outside the current view, focus **Search files, settings, integrations, help**, type `Activity`, and choose the matching **Activity** result. 3. Confirm the page heading is **Activity log**. Beneath it, Dosya shows `N activity` for one event or `N activities` for any other total. 4. Wait until **Loading...** changes to an activity total. The first row is the newest timestamp because the service orders events by descending recorded time. 5. Use the arrow controls when the header count exceeds 30. The centre label reads **Page X of Y**; the previous arrow is disabled on page 1 and the next arrow is disabled on the final page. 6. Select an activity row to expand **When** and the other available details. Pressing Enter or Space while that row has keyboard focus performs the same toggle. ## What a row can show The collapsed line contains the actor name, a human-readable action phrase, an accessible resource name, and relative time. Depending on the event, badges can add **failure** or **denied**, an on-behalf-of identity, a non-web source, old and new names, an email, a multi-file count, or a `via` value. Expanded details can display: - **When**, with local date/time and the relative age; - **Where**, with source IP and approximate city or country when recorded; - **Device**, reduced from the user agent to browser and operating system; - **Source**, **Outcome** and an available reason; - **Resource**, optionally linked to a page the viewer may open; and - **Session**, when the event includes a session identifier. Privacy shaping happens before the response reaches the page. Owners and admins can receive forensic fields for every visible row. A non-privileged custom or built-in role can receive those fields for its own actions, but another member's IP, device, location, session, and request identifier are removed. Names for files or folders the viewer cannot open are also stripped while the event itself remains. The current browser panel does not render a **Request ID** field, even when that identifier is available to an authorized client. Preserve the fields you can see if you need to report an event. New events do not stream into a list that is already open. Reload the browser page, change a filter, or move between pages to request the feed again before deciding that a recent operation was not recorded. ## Expected result The current workspace's permitted audit events appear newest first, the total corresponds to all matching rows, and the page position describes the 30-row slice being displayed. Expanding an event adds only the details allowed for the signed-in member and resource. ## Recover from an unavailable log **The route shows You do not have access to this page.** The client already resolved the permission map and found no **View activity log** grant. Ask a workspace owner or admin to update the role. **The error card says Could not load the activity log.** Read the detail below it, correct the connection or access issue, and choose **Try again**. An API refusal can include **You don't have permission to view the activity log** or **Not a member**. **The successful page says No activity found.** The workspace has no matching events. If any filters are active, it also says **Try adjusting your filters**; select **Clear filters** before treating the log as empty. **A resource name or forensic field is absent.** That can be the intended access boundary rather than missing audit data. Use the action and timestamp you can see, and ask an authorized owner or admin to investigate restricted context. ## Related guides - [Read expanded activity evidence](/workspaces/activity) - [Check the View activity log permission](/workspaces/roles) - [Select activity categories](/workspaces/activity-filter-category) - [Trace actions to workspace members](/workspaces/activity-filter-member)

title: Connect an AI app to Dosya
summary: Connect an AI client to one readable workspace, inspect its verified destination and scopes, then confirm the saved grant before using private files.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/connect/ai.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/profile/ai-apps.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/authorize.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/oauth/consent.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/oauth/consent.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/consent.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/consent.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/server.ts; apps/api/src/mcp-principal.ts; apps/api/src/mcp-gateway.ts; apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts; and apps/api/src/lib/oauth/connections.ts. Repository UI, OAuth and permission contracts were checked without sending production authorization requests or using live credentials.
body: An AI client connects to Dosya through OAuth at `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp`. The approval grants read access to one workspace; it does not give the app your password or an API key. ## Before you connect - Start from the client you intend to use and enter the Dosya MCP server URL there. A bare browser visit is not a connection request. - Sign in to the Dosya account that belongs to the target workspace. The consent transaction lasts **10 minutes**; an expired request must be started again from the AI client. - Issued access tokens last **1 hour**. Refresh use keeps a connection alive only while it is used at least once every **30 days**, and every grant reaches an absolute **180-day** reconnect ceiling. - Use a harmless file for the first read. Once an external app reads content, disconnecting cannot delete copies already held by that app. - A regular workspace can be offered when you are a member. End-to-end encrypted Spaces are excluded because the server cannot read their files. Approval has no paid-plan gate and cannot bypass workspace membership. - The source catalog gives each Free-plan connection **100 text file reads** and **25 image conversions** per UTC day. The current paid-plan defaults are unlimited for those two counters; a plan change is read on the next call. ## Steps 1. In Claude, ChatGPT or another MCP client, add `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp` as the server and begin its connect flow. 2. Complete Dosya sign-in if prompted. If the page says **That link is not valid**, return to the client and start again; do not reuse or edit the URL. 3. Read the identity badge. Claude and ChatGPT are shown as verified only when the authorization code will return to a recognized Claude or ChatGPT hostname. A different remote client shows **Not verified · sends to _host_**. A loopback callback warns, **This sends access to an app on your computer**. 4. Under **Workspace it can read**, select the intended workspace. With one eligible workspace, Dosya selects it automatically; with several, **Allow** stays disabled until you choose one. If none qualify, the page says **You have no workspace this app can read. End-to-end encrypted Spaces cannot be connected.** 5. Review the scope list. **Find and read files in _workspace_** is required and cannot be unchecked. If the client asked for `account.read`, **See your plan and storage** appears as an optional checked permission that you may clear. 6. Confirm the exclusions shown on the page: the grant cannot change, share or delete anything, and cannot open other workspaces or your Vault. 7. Select **Allow _app name_**. To abandon the request without creating a grant, select **Deny** instead. Dosya then returns the authorization result to the callback host displayed on the page. ## Expected result The client resumes after authorization and can find and read files only in the selected workspace. Open the account menu, choose **Profile**, then **Connected AI apps**. Its row shows the client name, workspace, connection time and permission chips such as **Read files** and, when granted, **Plan and storage**. Try one read of a non-confidential item. A file from another workspace, an E2EE Space or the Vault must remain unavailable, and the connector has no write, share or delete permission. ## If the connection fails - **This request expired. Go back to your AI app and connect again.** means the ten-minute consent handle is no longer usable. - **Could not connect the app. Please try again.** covers an unexpected client or network failure. Restart at the client if a retry does not resume the same request. - **The server returned an unexpected destination** means the returned host differed from the one shown before approval. Stop and initiate a new connection; do not follow a replacement address manually. - A `401` during the flow sends you through Dosya sign-in. The approval still has to belong to the same signed-in user who opened the consent request. - If the row cannot be inspected, **Connected apps could not be loaded. Try again in a moment.** reports a listing failure; it does not prove that no grant exists. ## Related guides - [Review AI app permissions](/integrations/ai-app-permissions) - [Disconnect an AI app](/integrations/disconnect-ai-app) - [Respond to suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Disconnect an AI app
summary: Revoke one saved AI grant, verify refusal after the one-minute token-cache window, and separately secure keys, sessions, or retained copies.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/shared.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/profile/index.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/profile/ai-apps.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/profile/ai-apps.test.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/ai-connections/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/ai-connections/[id].ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/connections.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/connections.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/token-cache.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/token-cache.unit.test.ts; and apps/api/src/lib/oauth/server.ts. Listing, revocation, and the one-minute validated-token cache were checked in repository code and tests; no production grant was revoked.
body: Disconnecting deletes one OAuth grant. A token already validated by a warm server isolate can continue working for up to 60 seconds; after that cache window, a new validation fails. Disconnect does not sign out browser sessions, revoke API keys, affect other AI rows or erase material already copied outside Dosya. ## Before revoking access - Ask the client to stop active work if an incomplete read would be confusing. A token that this server isolate already validated may remain accepted for no more than 60 seconds after revocation. - Record which row you intend to remove. The list shows application name, workspace name, relative connection time and scopes, newest connection first. - Save anything you need from the client itself. Dosya controls the authorization grant, not the app's chat history, local cache, exports or retained copies. - This setting requires an interactive signed-in session. An API key or connected-app token cannot list or administer sibling grants. ## Steps 1. Open the account menu and select **Profile**. 2. In the profile navigation, choose **Connected AI apps**. The direct route is `/profile/ai-apps`. 3. Find the row whose app name and workspace match the connection you want to revoke. Check the **Read files** and optional **Plan and storage** chips when similarly named rows exist. 4. Select **Disconnect** on that row. There is no second confirmation dialog in this screen, so the click is the revocation action. 5. Wait for **App disconnected**. Its message names the client and confirms that it can no longer read the workspace; the page then reloads the connection list. 6. Wait at least 60 seconds, then return to the AI client and retry a harmless read. It should require a new authorization or report that access is unavailable. 7. If the client also uses a Dosya API key, open **Profile → API keys** and handle that credential separately. Review **Sessions** as a separate account control when unauthorized sign-in is also a concern. ## Expected result The selected row disappears after the list refreshes, while unrelated clients and workspaces remain. The server has removed the grant; once the accepted validation cache expires within 60 seconds, previously issued tokens fail validation. Dosya also records a successful `mcp_grant_revoked` audit event against that workspace. Revocation cannot be undone for the same grant. To restore access, start a fresh connect request in the AI client and review a new consent screen. The new approval may select different optional access, but it cannot recover or constrain data the old connection already received. ## When disconnect does not complete - **Disconnect failed · Not found** means the grant was absent from your current user's listing, which can occur if it was already removed or the page was stale. Reload before acting on a different row. - **Could not disconnect right now. Try again in a moment.** is returned when grant listing or provider revocation fails. The row should be treated as active until a retry succeeds and the row disappears. - **Connected apps could not be loaded. Try again in a moment.** means Dosya could not obtain the list. It intentionally does not show the empty-state sentence in that case. - **No AI apps are connected** appears only after a successful load returns zero grants; it also displays the MCP address for a future connection. - If the former client can still read immediately after the success toast, wait until more than 60 seconds have passed and test a fresh read. Continued access after that points to a different connection row, a separate API key, previously cached file content or another Dosya account. ## Related guides - [Connect an AI app](/integrations/ai-app-connect) - [Review sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Review AI app permissions
summary: Interpret each AI consent label, limit the grant to one readable workspace, remove optional account access, and deny suspicious callback destinations.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/connect/ai.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/ai-brands.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/consent.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/consent.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/server.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/server.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/oauth/consent.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/oauth/consent.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/mcp-principal.ts; apps/api/src/mcp-gateway.ts; apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts; and apps/web/src/pages/profile/ai-apps.tsx. Local source and unit-test contracts were examined; no production OAuth decision was submitted.
body: The consent screen is the enforceable boundary for an AI connection. Dosya recognizes only `files.read` and `account.read`, binds the grant to one workspace, and discards unknown requested scopes. ## What each control means | Consent control | Access granted | | --- | --- | | **Workspace it can read** | Restricts the connector principal to that single workspace ID. Other workspaces and the Vault remain outside the grant. | | **Find and read files in _workspace_** | The required `files.read` scope. It permits discovery and reading, so Dosya does not offer a connection without it. | | **See your plan and storage** | Optional `account.read`. It lets the client read plan and storage information; clear it when the task only needs files. | | **Allow _name_** | Approves the displayed destination and selected scope set. | | **Deny** | Completes the request as denied and creates no usable grant. | The page also states two permanent exclusions for this connector: it cannot change, share or delete content, and it cannot open any unselected workspace or Vault data. A workspace role may already expose fewer files; OAuth permission never increases that membership access. ## Steps 1. Compare the app identity with the action you just took. A badge beginning **Verified:** is based on the exact callback hostname, not the self-declared app name. Dosya currently recognizes `claude.ai`, `claude.com`, `chatgpt.com` and `chat.openai.com` for branded verification. 2. Treat **Not verified · sends to _host_** as a destination disclosure. Approve only when that host belongs to the client you deliberately configured. For a localhost callback, proceed only while the expected local application is waiting for access. 3. Inspect **Workspace it can read**. The menu contains your eligible non-E2EE workspace memberships; selecting a workspace does not add you as a member or change your role. 4. Leave **Find and read files in _workspace_** selected. It is required by the resource server and is always inserted even if the client omitted it from its request. 5. Decide whether the client needs account facts. Uncheck **See your plan and storage** when it does not. Dosya grants optional scopes only when the client requested them, the page offered them, and you left them selected. 6. Read **Access goes to _host_** and the signed-in email at the bottom. If either is unexpected, choose **Deny**, close the client request, and investigate before trying again. 7. After approval, open **Profile → Connected AI apps** and compare the row's workspace and chips with your decision. The chips use **Read files** and **Plan and storage**. ## Expected result The saved connection names exactly one workspace and always displays **Read files**. **Plan and storage** appears only when you approved `account.read`. A read in the chosen workspace succeeds; attempts to write, share, delete, inspect another workspace or reach an E2EE Space are outside the connector's permission model. Approval is reversible by disconnecting the grant. That action stops later token use but cannot recall file contents or account information the client already received. Free-plan limits are counted separately for each grant: **100 text reads** and **25 image conversions**, resetting at UTC midnight; current paid-plan defaults leave both counters unlimited. ## Refuse or recover safely - Choose **Deny** when the callback host, client identity, signed-in email or workspace differs from your expectation. - **You have no workspace this app can read. End-to-end encrypted Spaces cannot be connected.** means the account has no eligible selection; moving data out of an E2EE Space solely to satisfy a connector changes its security boundary. - If **Allow** is unavailable, choose a workspace. The button remains disabled while the workspace value is empty. - An expired consent request returns `410` and the page instructs you to begin again. The ten-minute handle cannot be extended or replayed. - Unknown scopes are not displayed or granted. If a client claims it received a permission absent from the screen, disconnect the row and treat that behavior as an external-client issue. ## Related guides - [Connect an AI app](/integrations/ai-app-connect) - [Choose API-key permission](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Complete and verify an API upload
summary: Upload every multipart segment, complete the session once, recover a lost response through status, and confirm the returned file record safely.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/part/[partNumber].ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/stale-multiparts.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/cron.ts. Production status: the revised completion workflow has not yet been rechecked live.
body: Multipart completion turns uploaded parts into a file record. It applies only when session creation returned a non-null `resumable` object; a small single-PUT upload finishes on its upload URL instead. ## Before completion Upload parts to `PUT /api/upload/:sessionId/part/:partNumber`. Part numbers start at 1 and cannot exceed `total_parts`. Build every nonfinal body at exactly the returned `part_size`; the final body must be nonempty and may be shorter. The current part size is 10 MiB, and no body may exceed that ceiling. Repeating a part number already accepted returns `already_uploaded:true` with the stored ETag instead of sending the bytes again. `GET /api/upload/:sessionId/status` reports `status`, `size_bytes`, `part_size`, `total_parts`, `bytes_uploaded`, the numeric `uploaded_parts` array, and `has_multipart`. Its `file_id` stays null until completion succeeds. ## Steps 1. Fetch the session status and compare `uploaded_parts` with every number from 1 through `total_parts`. 2. Resend only missing parts, preserving the exact nonfinal `part_size` and accepting `already_uploaded:true` as success for a prior retry. 3. Call `POST /api/upload/:sessionId/complete` without a JSON body after every required part is present. 4. Save the HTTP 201 response's `file.id`, actual `size_bytes`, `version`, `etag`, name, extension, MIME type, region, and creation time. 5. If the completion response is lost, request the status endpoint before retrying; `status:"complete"` and its non-null `file_id` recover the outcome. 6. Fetch `GET /api/files/:fileId` with a read-capable credential or confirm the result in Dosya, then compare the destination, filename, and actual byte count. ## Completion responses A successful multipart completion returns `content_hash:null` and `hash_verified:false`. That Boolean means the assembled parts were not checked against a client digest; it does not mean a checksum mismatch occurred. Dosya refuses an unknown session with `Upload session not found`. It returns `No multipart upload in progress - upload at least one part first` when no storage multipart exists, and `Only X of Y parts uploaded. Upload remaining parts before completing.` for an incomplete set. A repeated completion returns 409 `Upload session is already complete`. A stale claim can answer `Upload session is no longer active - start the upload again`. A pending, uploading, or failed multipart session becomes eligible for stale cleanup after 24 hours without activity; that is not a guaranteed sweep time. Later upload initialization can schedule cleanup, and the hourly billing job runs a bounded D1-home pass. Durable Object-home sessions depend on later member activity, while the storage lifecycle aborts unfinished multipart state seven days after initiation as a backstop. For D1-home workspaces, the billing job removes completed and failed session rows after seven days, so status-based recovery of a lost completion response is bounded by that retention window. The cited cleanup path does not establish the same row-retention period for Durable Object-home sessions; recover a lost receipt promptly while the status route still resolves. Pending rows have a separate 600-second stale cutoff in cleanup paths, and an unrenewed credential transfer slot self-heals after 15 minutes. Completion releases that slot. The final storage and database write cannot be rolled back through the upload session; subsequent removal uses the normal file trash and purge workflow. A live same-name file can be adopted as a new version. Use a unique destination name when the requirement is a separate file. ## Expected result One HTTP 201 response identifies the completed file and reports the bytes counted from uploaded parts. A later status request returns `status:"complete"` and the same file identifier. ## Related guides - [Upload through the API](/developers/api-upload-file) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Create an API folder and verify its parent
summary: Create one folder through the REST API, interpret reused path segments correctly, and verify the returned child beneath the intended parent folder.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/children.ts, apps/api/src/lib/listing/folder-children-core.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.create-gated.unit.test.ts. Production status: the rewritten parent-verification flow has not yet been checked live.
body: Folder creation accepts either one name or a nested path. The response distinguishes the leaf that now exists from the path segments that this request actually inserted. ## Access requirements Use a **Full access** key with the **REST API** surface so the same credential may create and then read. **Upload only** can call the create route but cannot perform the verification GET. A key may be pinned to the target workspace; adding a folder anchor disables REST use. The member role needs `create_folders` for the mutation and `access_files` for the child-folder listing. ## Steps 1. Choose a visible parent folder and copy its `fld_…` identifier, or plan to omit `parent_id` when creating at workspace root. 2. Pick a unique one-segment test name, no longer than 100 characters, so the expected `created_count` is unambiguous. 3. Send `POST /api/folders` with `{ "workspace_id":"wks_…", "parent_id":"fld_…", "name":"API verification" }`. 4. Require HTTP 201 and record `folder.id`, `folder.parent_id`, `created_count`, and the `created_folders` array from the response. 5. Call `GET /api/folders/children?workspace_id=wks_…&parent_id=fld_…`; omit `parent_id` only when the chosen parent is workspace root. 6. Find exactly one returned folder whose id equals `folder.id`, then compare its name and parent before retaining or trashing the test folder. ## Path behavior The create route splits both `/` and `\`, so `Reports/2026/October` can create several levels in one request. The complete path is capped at 500 characters and each segment at 100. Existing segments are reused: a successful retry can return `created_count:0`, and a mixed path can report fewer created folders than segments. The 201 body contains the leaf as `folder:{id,name,parent_id,workspace_id}`. `created_folders` contains only rows inserted by that request. Creation changes the workspace tree immediately; removing the test later is a separate mutation. ## Expected result The leaf identifier from the create response appears as a direct child of the requested parent. A unique single-segment test returns `created_count:1` and one entry in `created_folders`. ## Troubleshooting `workspace_id is required` or `Folder name is required` means the body is incomplete. Membership and role failures read `Not a member of this workspace` or `You don't have permission to create folders`. Missing and locked destinations return `Parent folder not found` or a structured `folder_locked` response. A race can produce 409 `A folder named "" already exists here`; list the parent before deciding whether to retry. ## Related guides - [Use folder operations](/developers/api-folder-operations) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Create a REST API upload session
summary: Start a REST API upload with the correct destination, size, scope, and multipart settings, then inspect the returned session before sending bytes.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/body-pipeline.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/upload-page-gate.unit.test.ts, and src/pages/developer/api.astro. Production status: the new session instructions remain pending live verification.
body: Create an upload session only after the destination and credential boundaries are known. The REST base is `https://api.dosya.dev/api`, and requests authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer dos_…`. ## Requirements Use an **Upload only** or **Full access** key that permits the **REST API** surface. A workspace pin is compatible with REST; a folder anchor is not. Folder-anchored keys are rejected before the upload route runs. An ordinary REST upload requires both `upload_files` and `access_upload` in the current workspace role. Only the SFTP gateway bypasses the upload-page gate because its separate `access_sftp` permission governs that surface. Dosya can answer `You don't have upload permission in this workspace` or `You don't have access to the upload page` when either REST role gate fails. ## Steps 1. Choose the destination workspace and, when the file belongs below a folder, record that folder's `fld_…` identifier. 2. Send `POST /api/upload/init` with JSON containing `workspace_id`, `file_name`, and the byte value `file_size`; add `folder_id` only for a non-root destination. 3. Add `mime_type` when known. It defaults to `application/octet-stream`; `file_id` and `expected_version` are for deliberate version replacement, while `force_multipart` must be a Boolean. 4. Check the 201 response for the same workspace, sanitized filename, declared size, MIME type, extension, region, and a new `session_id`. 5. Read `resumable`: `null` means send one PUT to `upload_url`; an object means use its `part_upload_url`, `complete_url`, and `status_url` values. 6. Store the session details beside the local transfer state, then begin sending bytes only after the returned destination and transfer mode match the intended upload. ## Request rules and limits A filename is sanitized before validation and may contain at most 255 characters. Supply an accurate numeric `file_size`; omission is treated as zero, and a negative value is refused. `expected_version`, when present, must be a non-negative integer. `force_multipart:true` requires a file larger than zero bytes. Files above 50 MiB use multipart automatically. A smaller file can opt in with `force_multipart:true`. Multipart sessions use 10 MiB parts and report `total_parts`; smaller ordinary sessions return `resumable:null`. Initialization also checks storage quota, the credential's maximum file size, workspace extension and size policies, per-member storage, the destination folder, locks, and concurrency. There is no separate `Idempotency-Key` header for this endpoint. ## Expected result The API returns HTTP 201 with `ok:true`, a unique `session_id`, `upload_url`, normalized file details, and either a multipart instruction object or `resumable:null`. No file is complete merely because the session exists. ## Troubleshooting `workspace_id is required`, `file_name is required`, and `file_size must not be negative` identify malformed input. `force_multipart must be a boolean` and `force_multipart requires a file_size greater than 0` explain multipart setup errors. A 403 mentioning a folder anchor means the key must be recreated without that REST-incompatible restriction. ## Related guides - [Upload through the API](/developers/api-upload-file) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Download a file with the REST API
summary: Obtain a signed REST download URL, choose its lifetime or file version, fetch and verify bytes, and resolve locks, permissions and usage failures.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Evidence: apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download-url.ts; apps/api/src/lib/download-ttl.ts; apps/api/src/lib/download-ttl.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/files/download-grant-core.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download-url.access.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/files/version-one.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/unlock.ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts; apps/api/src/middleware.ts; apps/api/src/lib/r2-presign.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/enforce.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/plan-limits.ts; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx. Repository contracts and tests verified locally; no production requests or credentials used.
body: Download a stored file with the REST API in two requests: obtain an authorized temporary URL from `GET /api/files/{file_id}/download-url`, then fetch that URL from storage. The grant response is JSON, not file bytes and not a redirect. Keep the URL private because anyone holding it can fetch the authorized object until it expires. ## Select a file you are allowed to download Use a **Read only** or **Full access** API key with **REST API** enabled. Create it at **Profile → API keys → New API key** if needed, then save the complete token before closing its one-time reveal. A workspace pin may restrict the key; an ordinary folder-anchored key is refused on this protocol. Use `GET /api/files?workspace_id=WORKSPACE_ID` to find a file ID. Add `folder_id` when looking inside a particular folder. The selected file must belong to a workspace you are a member of, lie inside any member confinement, be visible to you and permit downloads. Your role needs access to the files page and **download_files**; being able to preview a file is insufficient. ## Steps: request and consume the grant Set `DOSYA_API_KEY` privately and replace the file placeholder below. This Bash example uses curl and Python 3, stores the grant with private file permissions and does not print its signed URL: ```bash set -e umask 077 DOSYA_FILE_ID='REPLACE_WITH_FILE_ID' DOSYA_GRANT_FILE=$(mktemp) curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ "https://api.dosya.dev/api/files/$DOSYA_FILE_ID/download-url" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ -o "$DOSYA_GRANT_FILE" python3 - "$DOSYA_GRANT_FILE" <<'PYTHON' import json, sys from urllib.request import urlopen grant = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])) with urlopen(grant["url"]) as response, open("dosya-download.bin", "wb") as output: while chunk := response.read(1024 * 1024): output.write(chunk) from pathlib import Path actual = Path("dosya-download.bin").stat().st_size if actual != grant["size"]: raise SystemExit(f"Size mismatch: received {actual}, expected {grant['size']}") print("Downloaded", grant["name"], "bytes:", actual, "region:", grant["region"]) PYTHON rm -f "$DOSYA_GRANT_FILE" ``` Stop after an unsuccessful grant instead of reading an older JSON file. The Python example requires Python **3.8 or later**. It writes to `dosya-download.bin`; choose a new local output name before rerunning if you need to preserve an earlier download. A successful **200** grant contains exactly the needed fields: `url`, `size` in bytes, `name` and `region`. This route does not include `ok: true`. Fetch the `url` as returned, including all signing parameters, without attaching your Dosya API key to that storage request. The grant checks your rights; storage uses the URL's signature. Check the downloaded size against `size`. For stronger integrity verification, compare a local SHA-256 with a trusted source digest: a matching filename or length alone cannot prove identical contents. Preserve the chosen file/version identity with the verification result. ## URL lifetime, versions and accounting | Query parameter | Supported behavior | | --- | --- | | `ttl` | Integer seconds; defaults to **300 seconds (5 minutes)**. Positive values are capped at **3,600 seconds (1 hour)**. Missing, invalid or nonpositive values use 300. | | `version` | A positive version number selects that stored revision; omit it for the current file. A nonexistent valid version yields **404** `Version not found`. | | `region` | Optional expected region. A mismatch returns **404** `File not found`; it does not redirect the file to a new location. | | `ut` | A valid unlock token for this user's fully locked file, when required. It does not bypass role or visibility checks. | For example, `/api/files/FILE_ID/download-url?version=1&ttl=3600` requests the first version with a one-hour URL. The initial version of a never-edited file is supported even though no earlier-version entry exists. Use explicit positive integers: malformed `version` input is not a reliable way to select a revision. Expiration matters for later Range requests as well as the first GET. For a long-running downloader or media player, request an adequate TTL up to the one-hour ceiling. If storage refuses an expired URL, obtain a fresh grant using a still-authorized credential; editing the old URL's expiry parameters invalidates its signature. The applicable credential/plan download-byte allowance is charged using the selected version's full size **when the grant is issued**, even if you never fetch it or only read a range. Repeated grants can therefore consume the allowance multiple times. Cache a private unexpired grant within the intended job rather than requesting a new URL for every chunk. A download audit event records issuance; it is not proof that a recipient received every byte. ## Diagnose an unavailable download | Status and error | Meaning and recovery | | --- | --- | | **401**, `Invalid or expired API key` | Replace the missing, revoked or expired token before requesting another grant. | | **403**, `Access denied` | You are not a member of the file's workspace. | | **403**, `This file is outside the folder you're confined to` | The membership's folder boundary excludes this file. | | **403**, `You don't have download permission` | Ask an administrator for the download action; preview permission cannot substitute. | | **403**, `This file is view-only and cannot be downloaded` | Respect its view-only lock; this endpoint will not provide downloadable bytes. | | **403**, `This file is locked. Enter the lock password to access it.` | Obtain a valid file unlock token through the authorized unlock flow, then send `ut`. | | **403**, `Invalid or expired unlock token. Please re-enter the password.` | Repeat authorized unlocking; the old token is no longer valid. | | **404**, `File not found` | Check ID and optional region. Hidden content and locked ancestors deliberately use the same response as missing content. | | **429** with `Retry-After` | Wait in seconds; a key's request or download-byte limit can refuse a grant before a URL exists. | | **500**, `Download failed: …` | URL signing failed. Preserve the sanitized error and retry later; do not publish storage details or credentials in logs. | A full-lock file can be unlocked with `POST /api/files/{file_id}/unlock` and JSON `{"password":"REPLACE_WITH_LOCK_PASSWORD"}`. The returned `unlock_token` is valid for **one hour**, belongs to the caller and does not remove the lock. That POST is a full-scope operation: a read-only REST key cannot call it. Use a separately authorized full-access credential for that password step or the signed-in app, then keep the token private. Avoid repeated password guessing; unlocking is throttled. Access checks run before URL signing: workspace membership, files-page access, confinement, download permission, hidden/ancestor locks, the file's own lock, selected version and byte allowance. An expired grant does not erase the stored file, and downloading does not create a share link or notify a chosen recipient. ## Protect the downloaded copy and URL Revoking the API key prevents new authenticated grants, but does not revoke an already issued storage URL; allow its short TTL to expire. Avoid putting signed URLs in screenshots, issue reports, query logs or analytics. Do not run commands with shell tracing while secrets are present. The local file is now a separate copy under your control. Deleting or changing the cloud file does not remove that downloaded copy. Remove the temporary grant file after use and store downloaded data with the permissions its contents require. ## Expected result Your local output has the selected file version and the grant’s reported size. The stored file remains in its workspace; the temporary URL grants access only for its lifetime, and a downloaded copy remains available independently of that lifetime. ## Related guides - [REST API authentication and workspace listing](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [Manage the credential used for download grants](/developers/api-key)

title: Handle REST API errors and pagination
summary: Process page-number results without skipping files, classify Dosya API failures by status and body, and retry only operations that are safe to repeat.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/middleware.ts, apps/api/src/lib/rate-limit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts, and src/pages/developer/api.astro. Production status: the rewritten error and paging flow has not yet been compared with live responses.
body: A reliable client treats paging state, authentication failures, authorization refusals, conflicts, and transient limits as different outcomes. Dosya does not use a continuation token for file lists. ## Response model Successful JSON normally includes `ok:true`. Failures normally use `{ "ok":false, "error":"…" }`; structured errors such as `folder_locked` can add fields. Preserve the HTTP status and the complete error body in redacted logs. `GET /api/files` uses `page` and `per_page`. The response's `pagination` object supplies `page`, `per_page`, `total_files`, and `total_pages`. ## Steps 1. Request page 1 with a stable workspace, folder, filter, sort, and `per_page`, then keep those query values unchanged for the run. 2. Process each file by `id`, store the current numeric page, and read `pagination.total_pages` from the same response. 3. Increment `page` until the processed page equals `total_pages`; do not look for a cursor, continuation, or `next_page` field. 4. On a non-success response, record status, `error`, `Retry-After`, and rate-limit headers without storing the bearer key. 5. Retry 429 and retryable 503 responses after `Retry-After`; repeat GET, HEAD, or a documented multipart-part retry, but inspect state before replaying a mutation. 6. Reconcile processed file ids at the end, leaving unresolved failures visible rather than marking the whole page complete. ## Status and timing rules 401 `Invalid or expired API key` calls for credential or expiry investigation. A transient authentication lookup instead returns 503 `Service temporarily unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5`. A 403 can come from scope, surface, workspace pin, role, lock, or another access rule. A 404 may intentionally conceal a hidden or confined resource. A 409 reports a state conflict. A 429 body says `Too many requests`. Most API responses expose `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Authenticated file-list polling receives a 600-per-minute user tier and still passes the 600-per-60-second IP guard. General REST traffic and upload initialization use 300 per minute per user; a lower plan or per-key ceiling can bind first. Because file paging is offset-based, inserts and deletes during traversal can shift later pages. Pause concurrent mutations for a stable export and deduplicate by file id when that is impossible. ## Expected result Every numeric page is handled at most once for the run, every file id is reconciled, and retryable responses wait for the server's stated delay while permanent refusals remain actionable. ## Related guides - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [API-key scopes](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Distinguish unavailable and unauthorized API files
summary: Interpret file 404 and 403 responses without probing unrelated identifiers, leaking a hidden resource, or mistaking a permissions failure for deletion.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/files-page.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/member-anchor.homes.unit.test.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.folder-lock.unit.test.ts. Production status: live 403 and 404 response sampling has not yet followed this rewrite.
keywords: api file not found vs forbidden
body: A file request can return 404 to avoid disclosing a resource, so status alone cannot prove whether a record was deleted. Diagnose only identifiers your integration already received legitimately. ## What each response can mean For `GET /api/files/:id`, 404 `File not found` covers an unknown or unresolvable id, a file hidden from this requester, and a WordPress-site key aimed outside its site folder. That shared answer prevents existence disclosure. A resolved file can return 403 `Access denied` when its workspace membership is missing. Other 403 bodies identify a narrower cause: `You don't have access to the files page`, `This file is outside the folder you're confined to`, a structured `folder_locked` result, workspace-pin mismatch, or API-key scope and surface rejection. ## Steps 1. Start with a file id previously returned to the same integration and note the expected workspace, folder, and key identity. 2. Confirm that the credential is complete, unexpired, allowed on the REST API surface, and not anchored to a folder. 3. Compare its workspace pin with the known file workspace and check that the current member still belongs there. 4. Request `GET /api/files/:id`, retaining the exact status and redacted error body rather than collapsing both into “missing.” 5. For 403, resolve the named scope, surface, pin, role, confinement, or lock rule; for 404, check trusted application state and the Dosya UI instead of probing adjacent ids. 6. Retry the known id only after correcting the relevant condition, then treat a continuing privacy-preserving 404 as unavailable to that caller. ## Safe client behavior Do not enumerate guessed `file_…` values to distinguish the cases. A hidden file deliberately behaves as absent. A folder-anchored ordinary API key is refused on all REST file requests before this handler, even when its anchor contains the file; use WebDAV or S3 for that credential design. The structured locked response is HTTP 403 with `error:"folder_locked"`, its `folder_id`, and `lock_mode:"full_lock"`. It gives a caller with legitimate access enough information to follow the unlock flow while a hidden file remains a 404. ## Expected result The client preserves privacy by treating 404 as unavailable, surfaces precise 403 causes to an authorized operator, and never uses unrelated identifiers to infer whether private data exists. ## Related guides - [List files with the API](/developers/api-list-files) - [Handle API errors](/developers/api-errors-pagination)

title: Create and move folders with the REST API
summary: Create, rename, and move folders through their exact REST endpoints, then verify the final parent while preserving names and avoiding tree conflicts.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/rename.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/move.ts, apps/api/src/lib/entity-name.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/move.conflict.unit.test.ts. Production status: the revised create, rename, and move sequence awaits live verification.
body: Dosya exposes separate folder routes for creation, renaming, and moving. A move can also apply the final name atomically, avoiding an intermediate destination collision. ## Permissions and naming Use a **Full access** credential with REST enabled. Creating requires the role permission `create_folders`; renaming and moving require `rename_folders`; verification through a listing requires `access_files`. A workspace pin works, while an API-key folder anchor does not work on REST. A create path may be 500 characters across multiple segments. Rename and move names are single segments with a 100-character maximum. ## Steps 1. Create a disposable source with `POST /api/folders` and retain the returned leaf id plus its original `parent_id`. 2. Rename it through `PUT /api/folders/:id/rename` using `{ "name":"Quarterly archive" }`, then require `{ "ok":true,"name":"Quarterly archive" }`. 3. Select a visible destination folder that is outside the source subtree and does not already contain the final name. 4. Move with `PUT /api/folders/:id/move` and `{ "parent_id":"fld_destination","name":"Published archive" }`; use null to move to workspace root. 5. Confirm the move response reports the final `name`, including the optional atomic rename rather than the old source label. 6. List the destination's direct children and verify the folder id occurs there once, while the old parent's listing no longer contains it. ## Refusals to handle A self-target answers `Cannot move a folder into itself`; a descendant target answers `Cannot move a folder into its own subfolder`. Dosya reports `Destination folder not found` when the target is absent or hidden, and `You don't have permission to move folders` when the current role lacks the operation. A no-op move produces `Folder is already here`. A destination name collision is HTTP 409 with `A folder with this name already exists in the target folder`. Locked backup trees reject rename or relocation. Do not turn those responses into automatic alternate names unless the caller explicitly accepts that behavior. The move and rename commit changes the shared tree and invalidates affected listings.
