It is reversible with another authorized operation, but clients can observe the new path immediately. ## Expected result The same folder id keeps its identity, the move response names its final label, and a destination listing shows the new parent relationship without a duplicate in the source. ## Related guides - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [API-key scopes](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Fetch file metadata by API identifier
summary: Fetch one file record by identifier, interpret every returned metadata field and null value, and separate missing, hidden, locked, and denied responses.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/types.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.content-hash.unit.test.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.folder-lock.unit.test.ts. Production status: the updated field list has not yet been revalidated against a live response.
body: The single-file endpoint returns identity, storage, location, version, visibility, and collaboration counts in one record. Null fields are valid data, not necessarily a failed lookup. ## Access requirements Call `GET https://api.dosya.dev/api/files/:id` with a **Read only** or **Full access** key permitted on **REST API**. The key may be workspace-pinned, but a folder anchor makes REST unavailable. The current member role must include `access_files`. ## Steps 1. Obtain a known `file_…` id from a trusted list, upload response, or webhook and keep its expected workspace alongside it. 2. Send `GET /api/files/:id` with the bearer header and require JSON rather than following a UI-formatted value. 3. Match `file.id`, `workspace_id`, `folder_id`, and `name` to the record the integration selected. 4. Compare `size_bytes`, `mime_type`, `extension`, `region`, `current_version`, `etag`, and `content_hash` with the operation being verified. 5. Interpret `created_at` and `updated_at` as Unix seconds, and allow nullable values such as `uploader_name` or `content_hash`. 6. Record the metadata needed by the application, omit visibility or identity details from public logs, and handle 403/404 by their exact body. ## Returned file fields A successful body is `{ok:true,file:{…}}`. The file object includes `id`, `name`, `size_bytes`, `mime_type`, `extension`, `region`, `uploaded_by`, `uploader_name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`, `lock_mode`, `is_hidden`, `hidden_mode`, `current_version`, `workspace_id`, `folder_id`, `content_hash`, `etag`, `share_count`, and `comment_count`. `content_hash:null` is expected for work that has not yet received a verified or lazy-computed hash. A missing uploader row can make `uploader_name` null while `uploaded_by` remains present. ## Expected result HTTP 200 returns the same file id and workspace expected by the caller, with byte size and version metadata suitable for an integrity or synchronization decision. ## Troubleshooting `Missing file ID` is a 400 route-input error. `File not found` may indicate absence or a privacy-preserving hidden/confinement decision. A 403 can name membership, files-page permission, member-folder confinement, full-folder lock, key scope, surface, or workspace pin. Do not convert these distinct conditions into a generic retry loop. ## Related guides - [List files with the API](/developers/api-list-files) - [Handle API errors](/developers/api-errors-pagination)

title: Rotate an expiring API key
summary: Duplicate an expiring key’s available settings, restore omitted limits and expiry, validate the replacement, then revoke the old secret without downtime.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/api-key-auth.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-defer.ts, apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.unit.test.ts. Production status: this replacement and revocation sequence has not yet been rerun live.
body: Rotation requires an overlap: create and validate the replacement while the existing key still works, then revoke the old credential after every client has moved. ## Before you rotate Open **Profile → API keys** at `/profile/api` and expand the expiring key. The UI marks future dates as **Expires _date_** and highlights keys expiring within 30 days. Expired keys still count toward the free-plan cap of 3 and the absolute cap of 20. Keys cannot be edited. **Duplicate settings** opens a replacement draft, but the expiry starts at **Never expires** and stored usage limits start blank because the list endpoint does not return them. S3 secret material is not copied. ## Steps 1. Inventory every client using the old key, including its protocol, workspace, folder reach, IP or active-hours guard, and any usage ceiling recorded outside Dosya. 2. Select **Duplicate settings**, change the name to identify the rotation, then review **Restrictions and expiry** instead of assuming every field was cloned. 3. Re-enter requests per minute, download per day, maximum file size, and concurrent-transfer limits; choose **Expires in 30 days**, **Expires in 90 days**, or **Never expires** deliberately. 4. Press **Generate key**, copy the `dos_…` secret from the one-time **is ready** dialog, and create new S3 credentials separately when the client uses that gateway. 5. Deploy the replacement to one client at a time and prove an actual allowed request plus its expected reach before removing the former secret. 6. Expand the old row, choose **Revoke**, read the irreversible warning, confirm, and verify the retired credential is refused while the replacement continues. ## Timing and recovery Authentication checks expiry when loading a key, while the auth cache lives for 300 seconds. Treat the displayed deadline as the stop time and rotate early; do not depend on a warm cache extending access. Revocation irreversibly deletes the row and schedules deletion of REST and S3 cache entries. Stop the old client, allow up to five minutes for cached authentication, and verify refusal before treating the retired secret as unusable everywhere. If a Free account has 3 keys, deleting an unused key or upgrading can create room. The absolute limit is 20 keys on every plan, so reaching 20 requires deleting a confirmed-unused credential; an upgrade cannot raise that ceiling. Do not revoke the active key merely to make room until a safe replacement path exists. ## Expected result The integration operates with the newly generated secret and restored restrictions. The old key is absent from active use and returns an authentication failure after irrevocable revocation. ## Related guides - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [Inspect webhook deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Restrict an API key to a workspace folder
summary: Anchor a credential to one folder for WebDAV or S3, verify the mounted subtree, and understand what trashing or permanently deleting the anchor does.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].anchor-homes.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/s3-credentials.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/gate.ts, apps/api/src/middleware.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/folder-scoped-keys.ts, apps/ftp-server/src/sftp.ts, and apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx. Production status: live anchor behavior remains to be rechecked after publication.
body: A folder anchor makes the selected subtree the credential's visible root. This restriction is implemented at the WebDAV and S3 gateways, not at REST or SFTP. ## Supported combination Open **Profile → API keys**, choose **New API key**, then expand **Restrictions and expiry**. Under **Where can it reach?**, select one workspace and use **Choose folder…**. The picker title is **Limit key to a folder** and its confirmation is **Select folder**. Select **WebDAV** or **S3 gateway** under Protocols. The workspace role must include `access_webdav` for WebDAV or `access_s3` for S3. Ordinary REST answers JSON with `This API key is anchored at a folder and can only be used over WebDAV or the S3 gateway`; an SFTP client instead reports its gateway authentication or request failure. ## Steps 1. Create a disposable workspace tree containing one file inside the intended anchor and another file in a sibling folder. 2. In the key dialog, choose the needed operation permission, pin the workspace, select the anchor through **Choose folder…**, and allow WebDAV or S3. 3. Generate the `dos_…` secret for WebDAV. For S3, expand the saved key, choose **Enable** under **S3 credentials**, and copy the one-time **Access key ID**, **Secret access key**, **Endpoint**, and **Region**. 4. Confirm the member role has the matching protocol permission, then mount WebDAV or address the S3 workspace and require its root to begin at the selected folder. 5. Read or write the permitted test item inside that subtree according to the chosen key permission. 6. Request the sibling path and require denial, then revoke the disposable key after recording the verified boundary. ## Anchor lifecycle Scope, protocol, the current member role, locks, and other key conditions continue to apply. WebDAV returns text such as `This API key is not permitted to use WebDAV` or `This role is not permitted to use WebDAV`. S3 returns an XML `AccessDenied` response with the equivalent gateway or role message. A human member's own folder confinement can narrow the credential further; an incompatible pair returns `This API key is anchored outside your permitted folder`. Trashing the anchor makes WebDAV and S3 answer `This API key's anchor folder is no longer available`. Restoring that live folder can make its id usable again. Permanently purging the anchor or a containing subtree deletes every key anchored there and clears its REST/S3 authentication caches; that key removal is irreversible. Moving or renaming a live anchor keeps the stored folder id, so clients see the same subtree at its new place or label rather than receiving a newly scoped credential. ## Expected result The protocol root exposes the selected folder and descendants, sibling data is unreachable, and a trashed or permanently purged anchor fails closed instead of widening access. ## Related guides - [Create and manage an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Choose key permission](/developers/api-key-scopes) - [Restrict a member to a folder](/workspaces/folder-access)

title: Create a full-access API key safely
summary: Create a Full access key with explicit reach, protocol, origin, usage, and expiry guards, then prove its required mutation and configured boundary.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/s3-credentials.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-defer.ts, and apps/api/src/middleware.ts. Production status: the revised Full access workflow is awaiting a live verification run.
body: **Full access** permits every operation class the credential can otherwise reach. It still inherits the account member's role and every configured guard. ## Decide whether Full access is required The UI describes this permission as **Everything your account can do: read, upload, move, delete.** Choose it for a client that must perform management mutations such as rename, move, share creation, or deletion. A read/reporting client or ingest-only job should use a narrower permission. ## Steps 1. Go to **Profile → API keys**, press **New API key**, and enter a purpose-specific name in **What is it for?**. 2. Under **What can it do?**, select **Full access** and read the **most permissive** badge before continuing. 3. Open **Restrictions and expiry**, choose only the protocol doors the client uses, and pin one workspace when whole-account reach is unnecessary. 4. Configure allowed IP ranges, active hours, usage ceilings, and a 30- or 90-day expiry when those controls fit the client; do not add an IP range to a key that must use SFTP. 5. Press **Generate key** and store the one-time `dos_…` value. For S3, expand the row, choose **Enable** under **S3 credentials**, and save the separate Access key ID, one-time secret, endpoint, and region before testing. 6. Cross one harmless configured boundary, such as an excluded protocol or different workspace, and require refusal before allowing production data. ## Effective permission Full access does not override the current member role, workspace policy, a workspace or folder pin, hidden and locked data, protocol selection, IP or time conditions, usage limits, plan ceilings, or backup locks. Each applicable rule narrows the request. Folder anchoring is valid only for WebDAV and S3. For REST management, use a workspace pin without a folder anchor. An IP-restricted key cannot use SFTP because the proxy cannot verify the person's source address. Keys cannot be edited after creation; **Duplicate settings** creates a new secret when restrictions need to change. The `dos_…` value appears only in the **is ready** dialog, and an S3 secret appears only when its credentials are enabled. Revocation irreversibly deletes the key row and schedules invalidation of REST and S3 cache entries. A cached authentication result can survive for up to five minutes, so stop the client and verify that every retired credential is rejected before treating the cutoff as complete. ## Expected result The credential completes the specific management mutation and read its client requires, while the deliberately excluded workspace, protocol, origin, or time window remains inaccessible. ## Related guides - [Create an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Choose key scopes](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Review when a Dosya API key was last used
summary: Use the API-key table’s Last used signal as a coarse activity clue, correlate it with the owning client, and revoke only after confirming it is unused.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts, apps/api/src/middleware.ts, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/lib/usage-throttle.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/usage-throttle.unit.test.ts. Production status: live Last used display timing has not yet been sampled for this revision.
body: The **Last used** column is designed for credential hygiene. It is a delayed activity clue, not a request-by-request audit record and not proof that a client has been retired. ## What the table shows Open **Profile → API keys**. Each row displays Name, Permission, Protocols, Reach, and Last used. Expanding a row also shows Created, Expires, IP allowlist, active hours, and a masked key fingerprint. `Never` means the server has no `last_used_at` value. The summary marks a key **unused for 90+ days** when its last recorded use is older than 90 days; a never-used credential is compared with `created_at` instead. ## Steps 1. Search by the key's name or masked prefix and expand the matching row rather than judging a similarly named credential. 2. Compare Permission, Protocols, Reach, Created, Expires, and guard details with the client inventory maintained by its owner. 3. Read **Last used** as an approximate timestamp and note whether the 90-day stale indicator is present. 4. Check the integration's own logs and Dosya API-key Analytics for expected recent calls without copying the secret into diagnostics. 5. Disable or replace the credential in its client first, then observe an appropriate quiet period for scheduled or infrequent jobs. 6. Select **Revoke** only after ownership is resolved, accept the irreversible warning, and monitor the client for an unexpected refusal. ## Why the value can lag REST, SFTP, WebDAV, and S3 update `last_used_at` as best-effort background telemetry. SFTP reaches the REST middleware through its classified gateway request, so its accepted traffic touches the same key field. Writes are throttled to at most once per key per 15 minutes in each running isolate. A request can therefore succeed without moving the displayed value immediately, and separate isolates can write on their own windows. Use Analytics or application evidence when an exact request history matters. The Last used field is appropriate for finding candidates, not for proving absence. ## Expected result Each stale or unexpected key has an identified owner and client evidence. Revoked rows correspond only to integrations confirmed inactive or already migrated to a replacement credential. ## Related guides - [Create an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Choose key scopes](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Name an API key for its owner and purpose
summary: Apply a searchable 64-character key name that identifies its client and purpose, then replace the credential safely when that label must change.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.ts. Production status: the rewritten naming and replacement flow has not yet been checked live.
body: An API-key name is a searchable label stored beside the credential. Dosya does not parse it into owner, environment, or purpose fields, and duplicate labels are allowed. ## Choose a useful convention In **Profile → API keys**, the **New API key** dialog asks **What is it for?** and suggests `e.g. rclone backup`. A practical convention is `client-environment-owner` or `client-purpose`, such as `rclone-prod-ops`. This is an organizational choice rather than a server-enforced format. ## Steps 1. Identify the single application, environment, and responsible team or person that will own the credential. 2. Form a compact label with the distinguishing facts, avoiding the secret, customer data, or temporary ticket numbers. 3. Enter it under **What is it for?** and keep the result within the 64-character limit. 4. Finish permission and restriction choices, press **Generate key**, and store the one-time `dos_…` value separately from its label. 5. Return to the API-key table and use **Search name or prefix** to confirm that the new row can be found unambiguously. 6. If the label later becomes wrong, duplicate the settings into a correctly named replacement, migrate the client, and revoke the old key. ## Validation and identity The exact API errors are `Name is required` and `Name must be 64 characters or less`. The web helper says **Just a label, so you can recognise it later.** A name is not an authentication value and need not be unique. The list shows a masked fingerprint and lets operators search by name or stored prefix. Existing names cannot be edited in place. Replacement creates a different secret, so revocation must wait until the client has been updated. The account may hold at most 20 API keys, while the free plan permits 3. Expired rows still count until they are deleted. ## Expected result The row is recognizable from its label and masked fingerprint without revealing the credential, and an operator can trace it to one client before rotation or revocation. ## Related guides - [Create an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Choose key scopes](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Limit an API key to selected protocol surfaces
summary: Limit one API key to selected REST, WebDAV, SFTP, or S3 surfaces, test an allowed and refused door, and avoid combinations the server cannot enforce.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/s3-credentials.ts, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/gate.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/credential.ts, apps/api/src/middleware.ts, apps/ftp-server/src/access.ts, and apps/ftp-server/src/sftp.ts. Production status: the protocol compatibility matrix awaits confirmation on the live service.
body: Protocol controls decide which network doors accept a secret. They operate alongside permission, workspace reach, role checks, origin conditions, and usage limits. ## Available surfaces Inside **Restrictions and expiry** → **Where can it reach?**, choose **All protocols** or **Only the ones I pick**. The selectable surfaces are **WebDAV**, **SFTP**, **S3 gateway**, and **REST API**. When selecting individual protocols, tick at least one. The create model sends no restriction for an empty selected set, which the server stores as unrestricted access to all surfaces. ## Steps 1. Determine the actual door used by the client rather than inferring it from the tool's product name. 2. Open **New API key**, choose the smallest operation permission, and expand **Restrictions and expiry**. 3. Select **Only the ones I pick** and tick each required surface, leaving unrelated doors unchecked. 4. Review workspace reach and do not mix a folder anchor with REST or SFTP; an anchored credential is usable only through WebDAV and S3 even if other boxes were selected. 5. Generate and store the key. For S3, separately choose **Enable** under **S3 credentials** and copy its one-time Access key ID and secret with the endpoint and region. 6. Complete a harmless request through one checked door, then test an unchecked door and require that protocol's refusal rather than a successful operation. ## Compatibility rules Selecting a surface does not grant read or write capability. A **Read only** key cannot mutate through an enabled protocol, and **Upload only** does not gain listing rights. The current role also needs `access_webdav`, `access_sftp`, or `access_s3` for those gateways; REST routes apply their own role permissions. Folder anchors are enforced only at WebDAV and S3; adding REST or SFTP does not make that combination usable. S3 never authenticates with the displayed `dos_…` value: it needs the separately enabled Access key ID and Secret access key. A key with **Allowed IP ranges** cannot use SFTP because the SFTP server connects on the user's behalf. Its refusal explains that the source address cannot be verified and directs the operator to another protocol or removal of the IP restriction. Refusal bodies follow each door. REST returns JSON such as `This API key is not permitted to use the api surface`; WebDAV returns a DAV XML error carrying its text message; S3 returns XML `AccessDenied`; and SFTP exposes an authentication or operation failure through the client rather than REST JSON. Changing protocol access requires a replacement key because saved credentials are immutable. Validate the new door before irrevocably revoking the old row. ## Expected result Authentication succeeds through every selected surface needed by the client, an excluded door returns its protocol-specific 403 response or client failure, and no selection widens the credential's operation permission. ## Related guides - [Create and manage an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Use rclone](/integrations/rclone)

title: Create a read-only Dosya API key
summary: Create a Read only key for listing and downloads, apply compatible reach controls, and prove that an attempted folder creation is refused by scope.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/middleware.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/kv-defer.ts. Production status: live Read only scope checks have not yet been repeated for this text.
body: A **Read only** credential can list and download but cannot open upload transactions or change stored data. Use it for reporting, backup reads, or inventory jobs. ## Configure compatible reach The permission card says **List and download. Cannot upload, move or delete anything.** For a REST client, select **REST API** and optionally pin one workspace. Do not choose a folder anchor for REST because anchored credentials work only through WebDAV or S3. The current role still needs `access_files`, and hidden or locked resources remain subject to their normal gates. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → API keys**, select **New API key**, and give the reporting or download client a distinct name. 2. Choose **Read only** under **What can it do?**, then open **Restrictions and expiry**. 3. Permit **REST API**, pin the intended workspace when possible, and set origin, usage, or expiry controls appropriate to the job. 4. Press **Generate key**, copy the secret once, and store it in the client's credential mechanism. 5. Prove the allowed side with `GET /api/files?workspace_id=wks_…` and confirm the response contains the expected listing. 6. Prove the denied side with a disposable `POST /api/folders`; require a scope 403 and confirm no folder was created. ## Scope boundary REST treats GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS as read capability. Documented bulk-download POST routes are classified as reads because they return existing bytes. Upload endpoints and `POST /api/folders` require write capability; rename, move, share, and delete operations generally require Full access. The denied folder request reads `This credential's scope is 'read' and cannot perform POST /api/folders`. A different 403 can still come from surface, pin, role, or lock rules and should be diagnosed separately. Revocation irreversibly deletes the key row and schedules REST/S3 cache invalidation. Cached authentication can remain valid for up to five minutes, so stop the client and verify that the retired secret is refused before considering access closed. Keep a production read credential only after the intended list/download action and its mutation refusal both pass. ## Expected result The credential returns permitted metadata or downloads, while the harmless create test is rejected before data changes and the workspace boundary remains intact. ## Related guides - [Create an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Choose key scopes](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Choose read, upload or full API-key permission
summary: Choose Read only, Upload only, or Full access from the operation the client needs, then prove both an allowed request and a denied boundary.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.unit.test.ts, and apps/api/src/middleware.ts. Production status: the revised permission examples remain unverified on the live service.
body: Dosya permissions are separate operation classes rather than a ladder. **Upload only** does not include reads, and enabled protocols never add missing capabilities. ## Permission model **Read only** lists and downloads. **Upload only** owns upload transactions and can create destination folders, but cannot list or delete existing data. **Full access** covers read, upload, move, delete, and other management mutations, still bounded by the member role and restrictions. For REST, GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS normally require read. Every `/api/upload/*` route and `POST /api/folders` require write. Unclassified mutations fail closed as Full access operations. ## Steps 1. Write down the exact endpoints and methods the client will call, including verification or cleanup requests. 2. Choose **Read only** when all required work is listing or downloading, or **Upload only** when the job only ingests and can verify elsewhere. 3. Select **Full access** only when the workflow must rename, move, share, delete, or combine reads with restricted writes. 4. Add protocol, workspace, origin, usage, and expiry guards without assuming they replace the operation permission. 5. Generate the key and run one intended request whose status and output prove the chosen capability works. 6. Run one harmless request outside that class and require `This credential's scope is '' and cannot perform METHOD /path`. ## Important upload detail The Upload only card says **Add new files. Cannot read or delete what is already there.** At the upload endpoint, a live same-name target can be adopted as a new version. Use a unique filename when the integration must never alter an existing file's version history. A key's effective access is the intersection of permission, selected surface, workspace or folder reach, current role, IP and time conditions, usage limits, plan rules, and content locks. Full access does not bypass any of those controls. Keys cannot be edited after creation. To narrow or widen a production credential, duplicate its available settings, generate a new secret, migrate the client, and revoke the former key after validation. ## Expected result The selected key performs the one required operation class, the deliberate boundary request receives the exact scope refusal, and no restriction is mistaken for an additional grant. ## Related guides - [Create and manage an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Restrict a key to a folder](/developers/api-key-folder-access) - [Limit protocol surfaces](/developers/api-key-protocols)

title: Create an upload-only Dosya API key
summary: Create an Upload only REST key, start and finish a file transfer without list access, and verify the result through the response or another trusted view.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/upload-page-gate.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.ts, and apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts. Production status: the Upload only transaction and denial checks have not yet been rerun live.
body: An **Upload only** REST credential can create folders and run an upload transaction, including its status request. It cannot list the file afterward with that same key. ## Compatible configuration The permission card reads **Add new files. Cannot read or delete what is already there.** Select the **REST API** surface and use a workspace pin when possible. A folder anchor blocks REST entirely, so choose the destination with `folder_id` in each upload-init body instead. An ordinary REST upload requires both `upload_files` and `access_upload` in the workspace role. Only SFTP bypasses `access_upload` because `access_sftp` controls that gateway. Creating a destination folder additionally needs `create_folders`. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → API keys**, press **New API key**, name the ingest job, and choose **Upload only**. 2. Under **Restrictions and expiry**, enable **REST API**, pin the destination workspace, and leave the folder anchor unset. 3. Generate the one-time secret, then start a small unique-named test with `POST /api/upload/init` and the intended `folder_id`. 4. Send the bytes through the returned single-PUT or multipart URLs and preserve the completion response's `file.id` and actual `size_bytes`. 5. Attempt `GET /api/files?workspace_id=wks_…` with the upload credential and require the scope refusal rather than a listing. 6. Verify the new file through its completion receipt, the Dosya UI, or a separate trusted read credential, then revoke the test key if it is disposable. ## Allowed and denied operations The complete `/api/upload` prefix is write capability, even its GET status route, so the key that created a session can resume it. `POST /api/folders` is also write capability. Ordinary reads, moves, deletions, and management mutations are outside Upload only. The denied listing reads `This credential's scope is 'upload' and cannot perform GET /api/files`. Surface, pin, role, size, quota, extension, lock, and concurrency rules can refuse an upload earlier with their own messages. A same-name live file can become a new version during completion. Use a unique destination name for create-only ingest. Completion commits storage and file metadata; removing the result later requires the normal trash workflow. ## Expected result The upload receipt identifies the stored file, the destination is verified through an independent view, and the same key receives a 403 when it attempts to enumerate workspace files. ## Related guides - [Create an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Choose key scopes](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Creating and managing an API key
summary: Generate a key in Profile, choose its permissions and restrictions, save it while it is displayed, and replace or revoke it later.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Repository contracts and tests verified locally; no production requests or credentials used.
body: Open **Profile → API keys**, select **New API key**, name it, and choose what it can do. Review **Restrictions and expiry** before selecting **Generate key**, then copy the key while the result dialog is open. The full key is shown only once. ## Before you start - Sign in to the account the integration should use. API keys are managed in your account profile; they can also be restricted to one workspace. - Check which protocol and permissions your tool needs. Create a separate key for each tool so you can identify and revoke it independently. - Prepare private credential storage for the key. Do not put it in a public repository, a shared screenshot or a support message. - If you want a workspace or folder restriction, make sure you belong to that workspace and know which folder the integration should reach. ## Steps: generate and save a key 1. **Find API keys.** Open the avatar's **Account menu**, select **Profile**, then select **API keys** in the profile navigation. You can also open [API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api) directly. 2. **Open the form.** Select **New API key** in the strip above the key list. 3. **Name its purpose.** In **What is it for?**, enter a label you will recognize later, such as a tool name and its purpose. The label identifies the key; it is not the credential. Names may contain at most **64 characters**. 4. **Choose its permission.** Under **What can it do?**, select **Read only**, **Upload only** or **Full access**. **Read only** supports listing and downloading. **Upload only** permits upload transactions and folder creation, but does not grant access to list, download or delete existing files. It is not a create-only guarantee: a same-name REST upload may add a version to an existing file when your access permits it. **Full access** is the most permissive option. The form initially selects **Full access**, so make an explicit choice. 5. **Review restrictions.** Open **Restrictions and expiry**. Follow the options below to limit the key to the intended protocols, workspace, addresses, schedule and usage. A new unrestricted form also starts with **Whole account**, **All protocols** and **Never expires**. 6. **Read the summary.** Check the description at the bottom of the form against the tool's purpose. Confirm that the reach, permission and expiry are intentional. 7. **Generate the credential.** Select **Generate key**. If creation succeeds, a dialog headed with the key's name and **is ready** displays the full key. 8. **Save it before closing.** Use **Copy** beside the displayed key and store it privately, then enter it into your tool's credential settings. Select **Done** only after saving it. Closing the dialog removes this opportunity to see the full key. ## Choose restrictions that fit your tool The expanded form groups options by question: - **Where can it reach?** Under **Protocols**, choose **All protocols** or **Only the ones I pick**. If you choose the latter, check at least one of **REST API**, **WebDAV**, **SFTP** or **S3 gateway**. If no protocol is checked, the form omits the restriction and the key remains allowed on all protocols. Select the actual required protocol before generating it. Choose a **Workspace** to replace **Whole account** with one workspace. After selecting a workspace, **Choose folder…** can restrict reach to a folder and its descendants; the picker uses **Select folder** to confirm. - **Where can it be used from?** Add comma-separated addresses or CIDR ranges under **Allowed IP ranges**, or turn on **Only during a weekly window** and choose the timezone, days, **From** and **To** times. - **How much can it use?** Optionally enter **Requests / minute**, **Download / day (GB)**, **Max file size (MB)** or **Concurrent transfers**. Blank fields add no key-specific usage limit; they do not override your plan or other applicable service limits. - **When should it stop working?** Choose **Never expires**, **Expires in 30 days** or **Expires in 90 days**. Two protocol constraints matter before you save: a folder-restricted key can be used only over WebDAV or the S3 gateway, and adding an IP allowlist stops SFTP working with that key. Review the form's explanations when combining these options. ## Expected result The new key appears in the **API keys** list. Its row shows **Permission**, **Protocols**, **Reach** and **Last used**, with expiry information when applicable. The list displays a partial identifier instead of the full credential. Configure the tool to use the selected protocol and try its intended operation. A key with the wrong permission, reach or access conditions can exist successfully yet be refused for that operation. ## Review, replace or revoke a key Use **Search name or prefix** and the permission filter to find a key. Open the expand control at the end of its row to see **Configuration**, **Guards** and **Actions**. Keys cannot be edited after creation. **Duplicate settings** opens a new-key form with several existing settings filled in. Review the replacement's settings carefully: its expiry starts at **Never expires**, and usage limits start blank. Set the intended expiry and limits again before generating it. Generate and save the replacement, update the tool, and then revoke the old credential when appropriate. To revoke a key, expand its row, select **Revoke**, check the confirmation dialog, and select **Revoke** again. This cannot be undone. Tools still using that key will be refused. Multiple row checkboxes also make a **Revoke** action available for the selected keys. ## S3 credentials An API token and an S3 credential pair are different settings. If the key allows **S3 gateway**, expand its row and select **Enable** beside **S3 credentials**. The resulting dialog provides **Access key ID**, **Secret access key**, **Endpoint** and **Region** for an S3-compatible client. Save the secret before selecting **Done**. **Active · show** can reopen the other S3 details later, but it cannot retrieve the secret. An expired key cannot be used to enable S3 access, and a key excluding S3 shows **Not allowed**. ## Account caps and the exact failure messages The free plan allows **3 API keys per user** across the account; other plans are still capped at **20 total**. These counts include expired keys until you revoke them. A workspace restriction changes reach, not how keys are counted. You can generate keys on the free plan, and naming a workspace requires membership there. | Creation response | Recovery | | --- | --- | | `Name is required` | Fill **What is it for?** with a nonblank label. | | `Name must be 64 characters or less` | Shorten the label; changing it does not change the token's security. | | `Maximum of 20 API keys reached` | Revoke an unused credential before generating another. | | `The free plan allows 3 API keys. Delete one or upgrade for more.` | Review the entire key list, including expired entries. | | `Not a member of that workspace` | Select a workspace you belong to; key creation does not add membership. | | `Folder not found in that workspace` | Reopen the folder picker in the selected workspace and choose a live folder. | | `Invalid IP/CIDR entry: "…"` | Correct the named address or subnet instead of deleting the intended access boundary. | The 20-key cap is checked before the free-plan cap. A successfully generated key can still be denied at use time: the protocol, address/time conditions, folder anchor, operation scope and workspace pin are checked before request usage is charged. A role remains an additional boundary, even with **Full access**. ## Units and expiry that affect a working integration **Download / day (GB)** and **Max file size (MB)** use 1024-based units: 1 GB is **1,073,741,824 bytes** and 1 MB is **1,048,576 bytes**. Requests and concurrent transfers are counts. Positive integer values are required for stored usage limits; zero is not the way to request unlimited use. Leave an optional field blank for no key-specific limit, while applicable plan and workspace constraints still apply. **Expires in 30 days** and **Expires in 90 days** are measured from creation, not first use. **Never expires** sets no scheduled expiry. The credential becomes usable once creation succeeds, so store and configure it before enabling a job. Treat the displayed expiry as the stop time; do not depend on a warm authentication cache extending access. For REST, the stricter of explicit key limits and applicable plan ceilings controls request counts, transfer concurrency and download bytes. WebDAV, S3 and SFTP do not apply plan ceilings to request counts or transfer concurrency, but explicit credential limits still apply, and download byte ceilings remain relevant on every protocol. Requesting a signed download URL counts its file size when the URL is granted, even if the URL is never fetched. Daily download counters reset at **UTC midnight**; the weekly active-hours window uses the timezone you selected instead. ## Use and verify the token For a REST client, send `Authorization: Bearer` followed by the complete `dos_` token. A **Read only** credential can make this harmless request; an **Upload only** credential cannot list workspaces: ```bash # DOSYA_API_KEY must already be supplied privately by your secret store. curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/workspaces' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" ``` Check HTTP 200 and the `workspaces` array against the intended account. A pin narrows this array to the selected workspace. For an upload credential, verify with a small upload and its returned file ID instead; its session status is allowed, but ordinary file listing is not. A **401** carrying `Invalid or expired API key` means the token is invalid, expired or revoked. A **403** naming the `api surface` means REST API is excluded. A message naming the credential's scope, request method and path means the operation needs a different permission; widening workspace access will not fix that. A **429** supplies `Retry-After` in seconds. A temporary **503** during authentication asks for a five-second retry and does not mean the key was lost. API-key administration itself requires your signed-in account session: a bearer token cannot create, list or revoke other keys through the profile endpoints. This protects sibling credentials even when the presented key has **Full access**. ## Limitations and troubleshooting The full API key and the S3 secret are not retrievable later. If either is lost, create replacement credentials and revoke the old key as needed. Copying a partial identifier from the list will not authenticate a tool. If **Generate key** fails, check the name and the error message. If you have reached your account's key limit, remove an unneeded key or review your plan before creating another. Expired keys still appear in the list, so review them when checking your total. If a tool is refused, check **Permission**, **Protocols**, **Reach**, expiry, IP allowlist and active hours. A folder-restricted key will not work over REST API or SFTP. An SFTP client will not work with an IP-restricted key. Do not resolve these errors by granting broader access before checking the actual requirement. Use [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) for a persistent credential problem. Share the key's label, selected protocol and error message; omit the full key, authorization headers, S3 secret and generated credential commands. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I display the full key again after selecting Done? No. The full token is shown only at creation. Create a replacement if you did not save it, update the integration, and revoke the unused old key. ### Does Duplicate settings preserve every restriction? No. Review the replacement form: usage limits start blank, and expiry starts at **Never expires**. Set those options explicitly before generating the replacement. ### Does revoking sessions also revoke API keys? API keys are managed separately. Revoke the key on this page when an integration should stop authenticating. Use **Profile → Sessions** to review signed-in browsers and apps. ## Related guides - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Watch the existing API-key tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/create-an-api-key/) - [Watch the existing WebDAV tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/mount-your-storage-with-webdav/)

title: Paginate through REST API file results
summary: Walk numeric REST file pages from page 1 through total_pages, respect the 10–500 page-size bounds, and prevent duplicate processing during changes.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts, apps/api/src/lib/listing/folder-listing-core.ts, and src/pages/developer/api.astro. Production status: live numeric pagination has not yet been sampled after this rewrite.
body: File listings use numeric offset pages. There is no continuation token, cursor, or next-page value to save from `GET /api/files`. ## Request and response Call `GET /api/files?workspace_id=wks_…&folder_id=fld_…&page=1&per_page=100`. Omit `folder_id` for workspace root. `page` defaults to 1; `per_page` defaults to 100 and is clamped from 10 through 500. Page numbers are capped at 10,000,000, fractions are floored, and malformed values fall back safely. The response contains `folders`, paged `files`, `breadcrumbs`, resolved `workspace_id` and `folder_id`, `can_lock`, `can_hide`, `folder_view_only`, and `pagination`. ## Steps 1. Freeze the workspace, folder, filter, search, and sort inputs for the traversal, and choose a `per_page` value between 10 and 500. 2. Request `page=1`, require `ok:true`, and record `pagination.page`, `per_page`, `total_files`, and `total_pages`. 3. Process each element of `files` by its stable `id`; treat the `folders` array as directory context rather than part of the file-page count. 4. Increment the numeric page and repeat the identical query until the returned page equals `pagination.total_pages`. 5. Deduplicate file ids and avoid concurrent uploads, moves, or deletes when the run must represent one stable export. 6. Reconcile the number of unique processed ids with the visible result set, retaining any 403, 404, 429, or 503 page failure for recovery. ## Paging details `pagination.total_files` counts files, not folders. `total_pages` is at least 1 even when no files match. Because this is limit/offset paging, mutations during the run can shift rows between pages; id-based deduplication prevents double processing but cannot recreate a historical snapshot. The endpoint supports response ETags. A conditional request can return HTTP 304 when the serialized listing is unchanged. Use a **Read only** or **Full access** key with REST enabled and a role holding `access_files`. Upload only is refused with `This credential's scope is 'upload' and cannot perform GET /api/files`. Folder-anchored keys cannot use this REST route. ## Expected result The client visits pages 1 through `total_pages`, processes every visible file id once for the chosen query, and never waits for a continuation field the API does not return. ## Related guides - [List files with the API](/developers/api-list-files) - [Handle API errors](/developers/api-errors-pagination)

title: List folders and files with the REST API
summary: Call GET /api/files with a read-capable key, page through one workspace or folder, and interpret access, lock, hidden-content and scope failures.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified query parameters, paging bounds, response fields, sorting, workspace and folder gates, hidden and locked-folder behavior, role permission and REST scope enforcement in apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts; apps/api/src/lib/listing/folder-listing-core.ts; apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts; apps/api/src/lib/list-sort.ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.homes.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.hidden-parent.unit.test.ts; and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.folder-lock-ancestor.unit.test.ts. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Use `GET https://api.dosya.dev/api/files` to list the folders and files visible in one workspace location. The request returns metadata, breadcrumbs, permissions, and file-page pagination; it does not return file bytes or create a share link. ## Credential and access requirements Create a **Read only** or **Full access** API key with **REST API** allowed under **Protocols**. Pin it to the intended workspace when the integration should not enumerate other workspaces. Ordinary folder-anchored API keys are refused over REST, so use a workspace pin without a folder anchor for this endpoint. The key narrows the account that created it. The account must still be a workspace member, and its role needs `access_files`. Folder confinement, hidden-folder rules, full locks, and workspace membership are enforced before the listing is returned. An **Upload only** key cannot call this GET endpoint. Its refusal names the exact operation: `This credential's scope is 'upload' and cannot perform GET /api/files`. ## Steps Set the secret privately and use a workspace ID returned by `GET /api/workspaces`: ```bash read -r -s -p 'API key: ' DOSYA_API_KEY printf '\n' export DOSYA_API_KEY DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID='ws_REPLACE_ME' curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --get \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/files' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ --data-urlencode "workspace_id=$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" \ --data-urlencode 'page=1' \ --data-urlencode 'per_page=100' \ --data-urlencode 'sort=name' \ --data-urlencode 'dir=asc' \ -o files-page-1.json python3 -m json.tool files-page-1.json ``` `workspace_id` is required; omitting it returns `workspace_id is required`. With no `folder_id`, the route lists the workspace root, or the member's confined root when that human account is folder-confined. The successful JSON contains: - `folders`: child folder metadata for the current location. - `files`: the current page of file metadata, including IDs used by later file routes. - `breadcrumbs`: root-to-current folder labels when listing a subfolder. - `workspace_id` and the resolved `folder_id`. - `can_lock`, `can_hide`, and `folder_view_only` for the caller's current role and folder state. - `pagination.page`, `per_page`, `total_files`, and `total_pages`. Folders and files are separate arrays. `total_files` and `total_pages` describe the file page, not the number of child folders. ## List a subfolder or filter by name Pass a known folder ID to list that folder's direct children: ```bash DOSYA_FOLDER_ID='fld_REPLACE_ME' curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --get \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/files' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ --data-urlencode "workspace_id=$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" \ --data-urlencode "folder_id=$DOSYA_FOLDER_ID" \ --data-urlencode 'q=invoice' \ --data-urlencode 'page=1' \ --data-urlencode 'per_page=100' ``` `q` is trimmed and matched case-insensitively against names. Special wildcard characters are treated as search text rather than raw SQL patterns. A confined member who explicitly names a folder outside the permitted subtree receives `This folder is outside the folder you're confined to` with HTTP 403. Supported sort keys include `name`, `size`, `created`, `modified`, `taken`, `type`, `extension`, `version`, `uploader`, `region`, `origin`, `shares`, and `comments`. Use `dir=asc` or `dir=desc` with a bare key. Legacy values such as `newest`, `oldest`, `largest`, and `smallest` are also accepted. Unknown sort input safely falls back to newest-first. ## Fetch every file page The default page size is 100. `per_page` is clamped to **10–500**, and `page` starts at 1. Continue until the returned page reaches `pagination.total_pages`: ```python import json, os, urllib.parse, urllib.request base = 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/files' workspace = os.environ['DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID'] key = os.environ['DOSYA_API_KEY'] page = 1 while True: query = urllib.parse.urlencode({ 'workspace_id': workspace, 'page': page, 'per_page': 500, 'sort': 'name', 'dir': 'asc', }) req = urllib.request.Request(base + '?' + query, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response: body = json.load(response) for item in body['files']: print(item['id'], item['name'], item['size_bytes']) if page >= body['pagination']['total_pages']: break page += 1 ``` Files can change between offset-based pages. For a stable export, avoid concurrent renames, uploads, and deletes during the run, and deduplicate collected rows by file ID. ## Interpret access and lock responses | Response | Meaning and next action | | --- | --- | | **401**, `Not authenticated` or invalid-key text | Restore the complete bearer token and check expiry or revocation. | | **403**, `This API key is not permitted to use the api surface` | Create a key whose protocol selection includes REST API. | | **403**, `Not a member of this workspace` | Confirm the workspace ID and restore membership; a key cannot grant membership. | | **403**, `You don't have access to the files page` | The current role lacks `access_files`; ask a workspace administrator to adjust it. | | **403** with `error: "folder_locked"` and `lock_mode: "full_lock"` | Unlock the folder through an authorized flow and supply its current `ut` token if the integration supports locked folders. | | **404**, `Folder not found` | The folder does not exist for this requester, including a hidden folder or one under a hidden ancestor. Do not use the response to infer hidden content. | Hidden files and folders are removed from ordinary results unless the caller has permission to manage hidden content. A `view_only` folder can still be listed, and the response sets `folder_view_only: true` so clients can suppress download actions. ## Expected result Each request returns HTTP 200 with only the folders and files the credential owner may see in the requested location. Following `pagination.total_pages` yields the accessible file set without downloading bytes or modifying the workspace. ## Related guides - [Start with the REST API](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [Choose a read-capable API key](/developers/api-key-scopes) - [Handle API errors and pagination](/developers/api-errors-pagination)

title: List direct child folders with the REST API
summary: List only the direct child folders beneath one parent, interpret each folder row, and use the separate file-list endpoint when files are also required.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/children.ts, apps/api/src/lib/listing/folder-children-core.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/types.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/hidden-gate.routes.unit.test.ts. Production status: live direct-child output remains to be rechecked after this change.
body: The folder-children endpoint returns directories only. Use it to lazy-load one tree level; use the file-list endpoint when the caller also needs files. ## Endpoint contract Call `GET /api/folders/children?workspace_id=wks_…&parent_id=fld_…`. Omitting `parent_id` requests root folders. The response is `{ok:true,folders:[…]}` with direct children only and no pagination. Each row provides `id`, `name`, `parent_id`, `file_count`, and `has_children`. Internal hidden-state columns are removed before serialization. ## Steps 1. Use a **Read only** or **Full access** key that permits REST, is not folder-anchored, and belongs to a role with `access_files`. 2. Choose a known parent id from a trusted folder response, or deliberately omit the parameter for workspace root. 3. Send the children request with `workspace_id` and the optional `parent_id`, then require HTTP 200 and `ok:true`. 4. Confirm every returned row has the requested `parent_id`, and use `has_children` to decide whether the interface should offer expansion. 5. Treat `file_count` as folder-row metadata; do not expect file objects or a continuation field in this response. 6. When files are required, call `GET /api/files?workspace_id=wks_…&folder_id=fld_…` and reconcile its separate `folders`, `files`, and pagination data. ## Access and privacy behavior A missing `workspace_id` returns `workspace_id is required`. Lack of membership answers `Not a member`. A parent hidden from this requester returns 404 `Folder not found`, while a parent outside a human member's confined subtree returns `This folder is outside the folder you're confined to`. For a folder-confined human member, omitting `parent_id` resolves the listing root to that member's anchor. This is different from an API-key folder anchor: an ordinary anchored credential is refused on REST and must use WebDAV or S3. The endpoint does not return descendants recursively. Call it again for a returned id whose `has_children` value is truthy. ## Expected result The body contains only the visible folders immediately below the chosen parent. File retrieval, file pagination, and deeper expansion occur through their own explicit requests. ## Related guides - [List files with the API](/developers/api-list-files) - [Handle API errors](/developers/api-errors-pagination)

title: Move a file through the REST API safely
summary: Move a file atomically with the REST API, handle scope, lock, and name conflicts, then verify its stable ID and parent with route-specific reads.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/resolve.ts, apps/api/src/lib/db.ts, and apps/api/src/middleware.ts. Production was not changed or exercised.
body: `PUT /api/files/:id/move` changes a file’s parent without changing its ID or versions. Send `folder_id` as a destination folder ID, or `null` for the workspace root. Add `name` only when the same atomic request should also rename the file. ## Before you start - Use a full-access REST API key; read-only and upload-only keys cannot move files. - Your workspace role must include `upload_files`. A request that also supplies `name` requires `rename_files`. - Record the file ID, its current folder, and the destination folder. Pick a disposable file when testing automation. - The destination must belong to the same workspace and must be visible to the caller. ## Steps 1. Read the file and destination first. Record the file ID, current parent, and exact destination ID before sending the mutation. 2. Prepare JSON with the destination: `{"folder_id":"folder_destination"}`. Use `{"folder_id":null}` for root, or add `"name":"renamed.pdf"` for a combined move and rename. 3. Send `PUT /api/files/file_id/move` with `Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY` and `Content-Type: application/json`. Do not retry blindly after a lost response. 4. Require HTTP 200 and read `{ "ok": true, "name": "…" }`. A 400 can mean the file is already in that folder, 403 covers permission or lock refusal, 404 hides an unavailable resource, and 409 reports a same-folder name conflict. 5. Send `GET /api/files/file_id` and confirm the same ID reports the intended `folder_id` and optional new name. Carry `X-D1-Bookmark` when the mutation returned one, but treat it only as ordering for D1-backed reads; file content metadata can come from the workspace repository. 6. List both the former and destination parents if downstream work depends on membership. Continue only when the old parent omits the ID and the destination contains it. ## Expected result The API returns 200 with `ok: true`; a route-specific metadata read shows the original file ID under the chosen parent. A combined rename exposes the supplied name in that verified result. ## Troubleshooting **The request returns 409.** Choose a different `name`, or resolve the existing item in the destination before retrying. **The request returns 403.** Check `upload_files`, add `rename_files` for a combined rename, and inspect lock state. Changing API-key scope does not bypass a workspace role or lock. **The response was lost.** Read the file before sending another mutation. The move route has no idempotency key; a verified destination means the first request already committed. ## Related guides - [Use folder operations](/developers/api-folder-operations) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Handle Dosya API rate limits
summary: Read Dosya rate-limit headers, honor Retry-After, add bounded jitter, and retry safely without turning a temporary 429 into a tight request loop.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/middleware.ts, apps/api/src/lib/rate-limit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/usage/enforce.ts, and apps/cli/src/client.ts. Production was not load-tested.
body: Dosya enforces more than one limit. General authenticated and upload traffic is limited to 300 requests per minute per user, listing traffic to 600 per minute, and authenticated IP traffic to 600 per minute outside the desktop-sync exception. An API key may also have its own requests-per-minute allowance. ## Before you start - Make the caller preserve response status and headers; a JSON parser alone loses the retry signal. - Decide whether the request is safe to replay. Reads are usually safe; mutations need a route-specific receipt or idempotency contract. - Keep concurrency below the documented limit instead of relying on retries as flow control. ## Steps 1. Inspect every response for `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. The general limiter also includes those headers on successful requests. 2. When status is 429, read `Retry-After` before parsing the body. A per-key refusal can say `This API key has exceeded its requests-per-minute limit` and is only guaranteed to include `Retry-After`. 3. Pause for the server delay, then add a small random jitter so parallel workers do not wake together. Cap a malformed or excessive delay according to your job deadline. 4. Retry a read or an idempotent upload after waiting. For an uncertain move, rename, trash, or other mutation, verify the remote state instead of replaying it automatically. 5. Limit the retry count. Dosya CLI uses at most three retries, a fallback sequence of 1, 3, and 8 seconds, and caps a valid `Retry-After` value at 60 seconds. 6. Record the route, status, attempt number, and wait duration without logging credentials. Reduce concurrency when 429s recur after a complete reset window. ## Expected result The client waits instead of spinning, succeeds after capacity returns, and stops after its bounded retry budget. Automation distinguishes a key-level allowance from the broader user or IP limiter without assuming identical headers. ## Troubleshooting **`Retry-After` is absent.** Use a conservative exponential delay with jitter; the CLI’s fallback is 1, 3, then 8 seconds. **A mutation timed out before its status arrived.** Read the resource or receipt endpoint. Only replay when that operation documents idempotency. **429 continues after the reset.** Lower concurrency and inspect the API key’s configured requests-per-minute allowance. A new key does not remove user- or IP-level protection. ## Related guides - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [Inspect webhook deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Rename a file through the REST API
summary: Rename a file by ID with exact filename validation, preserve its parent and identity, and resolve lock, permission, or same-folder conflicts safely.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/rename.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/resolve.ts, apps/api/src/lib/db.ts, apps/api/src/middleware.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/validation-policy.generated.ts. Production was not changed.
body: `PUT /api/files/:id/rename` changes the stored name while keeping the file ID, parent, and version history. The extension is part of `name`; changing it can change how clients classify or preview the file. ## Before you start - Use a full-access API key and a workspace role with `rename_files`. - Read the current file so you know its ID, parent, lock state, and existing name. - Choose a name of 1–255 characters after trimming. It cannot contain `/`, `\`, C0 control characters, or consist entirely of `.` or `..`. ## Steps 1. Fetch `GET /api/files/file_id` and preserve its parent ID. If an extension matters, include the desired extension explicitly in the new name. 2. Build the exact JSON body, for example `{"name":"Q4 forecast.pdf"}`. Quotes and angle brackets are accepted; clients must still escape JSON correctly. 3. Send `PUT /api/files/file_id/rename` with bearer authorization and `Content-Type: application/json`. Keep this call separate from unrelated batch work. 4. Require HTTP 200 and `{ "ok": true, "name": "Q4 forecast.pdf" }`. Treat 400 as invalid input, 403 as scope, role, or lock refusal, 404 as unavailable, and 409 as a sibling name collision. 5. Read the same file ID again and confirm `name` changed while the parent ID did not. Carry a returned `X-D1-Bookmark` for D1-backed checks, without treating it as an ordering guarantee for workspace-object content. 6. Open or download the renamed file when the extension changed. That check catches automation that accidentally changed the suffix even though the bytes remained intact. ## Expected result The success receipt echoes the normalized name. A fresh metadata read shows the same file ID and parent with the new name; its versions remain attached to that ID. ## Troubleshooting **The server returns 400.** Trim the value and check length, slash, backslash, control-character, `.` and `..` rules. **The server returns 409.** A sibling already uses the requested name. Choose another name or resolve that sibling before a new request. **The server returns 403.** Confirm full key scope, `rename_files`, and that the file is not locked against the caller. ## Related guides - [Use folder operations](/developers/api-folder-operations) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Resume an interrupted API upload
summary: Resume multipart API uploads from recorded part numbers, retry missing chunks safely, and complete only after every expected 10 MiB part has landed.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/part/[partNumber].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/session-id.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/stale-multiparts.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/cron.ts, and apps/api/src/middleware.ts. Production was not exercised.
body: Dosya selects multipart upload above 50 MiB. A client can request it for a smaller nonempty file with `force_multipart: true`. Multipart sessions use 10 MiB parts and resume by uploaded part number, not by a raw byte offset. ## Before you start - Retain the `session_id`, source file, declared `file_size`, and any content hash until completion succeeds. - Resume as the same Dosya user in the same workspace with the original session and unchanged file. The credential may be an authorized replacement API key; it does not have to be the key that initialized the session. - An unstarted pending session becomes eligible for cleanup after 10 minutes, and multipart work can be retired after 24 hours without a landed part. The bucket’s seven-day multipart lifecycle is only a backstop, while complete or failed session rows can be pruned after seven days; status is the authority, not any promised expiry time. ## Steps 1. Call `GET /api/upload/session_id/status`. Read `status`, `size_bytes`, `part_size`, `total_parts`, `bytes_uploaded`, `uploaded_parts`, `has_multipart`, and `file_id` when completion has already produced one. 2. If status already represents completion and `file_id` is present, verify that file instead of uploading more. For an active session, compute the missing integers from 1 through `total_parts`. 3. Seek the local source to `(partNumber - 1) × part_size` and upload only each missing part to `PUT /api/upload/session_id/part/partNumber`. The final part may be shorter than 10 MiB. 4. Treat a successful repeated part response with `already_uploaded: true` as confirmation, not duplication. Re-read status after transport failures because the server may have stored the part before the connection broke. 5. Send `POST /api/upload/session_id/complete` only when status lists every expected part. If it says `Only N of M parts uploaded. Upload remaining parts before completing.`, return to the missing-part calculation. 6. Require the completion receipt’s file ID, then fetch its metadata and compare the final measured size or configured hash. Delete the local resume record only after that verification. ## Expected result Every expected part number appears in status, completion returns the stored file receipt, and a metadata read shows the finished object. Re-sending a recorded part does not add a second part. ## Troubleshooting **Status is missing or expired.** Start a new session only after confirming the old session can no longer be resumed. **The source file changed locally.** Abort the resume. Part numbers from one byte sequence cannot safely finish another. **Completion reports missing parts.** Trust `uploaded_parts`, upload only absent numbers, and call complete again. Do not translate `bytes_uploaded` into a byte-offset resume. ## Related guides - [Upload through the API](/developers/api-upload-file) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Stream an API download to disk
summary: Follow Dosya’s guarded download redirect without forwarding the API key, stream storage bytes to disk, and validate the saved file against metadata.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download-url.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/raw.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/download-ttl.ts. Production was not downloaded from.
body: The standard download route authorizes the request, then returns HTTP 302 to a five-minute presigned storage URL. The raw route stays on Dosya and supports byte ranges. These are distinct contracts; a 302 response is not itself a file stream. ## Before you start - A read-scoped API key is sufficient, but the workspace role must expose the Files page and include `download_files`. - Know the file ID. Add `version=N` for a previous version or `ut=token` only when your flow received an unlock token. - Write to a temporary local path so an interrupted response never replaces a known-good file. ## Steps 1. Fetch metadata first and record the expected name and size. Refuse the job if the selected version or unlock context is not the one the caller intended. 2. Request `GET /api/files/file_id/download` without automatic redirect handling. Require 302 and read `Location`; the signed URL normally expires after 300 seconds. 3. Open `Location` as a separate request without `Authorization` or the Dosya API key. Stream response chunks into the temporary file instead of buffering the full object. 4. Alternatively, call `GET /api/files/file_id/download-url`; its JSON contains `url`, `size`, `name`, and `region`. A requested TTL defaults to 300 seconds and is capped at 3600. 5. For resumable byte transfer, use `GET /api/files/file_id/raw` with `Range: bytes=start-`. Expect 206 and `Accept-Ranges`; a range outside the object returns 416. 6. After the stream closes, compare bytes written with metadata or the download-url `size`. Rename the temporary file into place only after validation. ## Expected result The client stores the complete object without exposing its API credential to the storage host. A full download matches the expected byte count; a resumed raw request returns the correct remaining range. ## Troubleshooting **The first response is 302.** That is the standard route’s success contract. Follow `Location` in a credential-free request. **The signed URL expired.** Request a new URL after reauthorizing; do not edit its query string. **The raw request returns 416.** Compare the local partial size with the current remote size. Restart when the partial file exceeds or belongs to another version. ## Related guides - [List files with the API](/developers/api-list-files) - [Handle API errors](/developers/api-errors-pagination)

title: Move a file to Deleted items through the API
summary: Trash a file idempotently with trash_only, verify it in the deleted listing, and avoid a second bare DELETE that permanently erases every version.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/files/delete-mode.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts. Production data was not deleted.
body: Use `DELETE /api/files/:id?trash_only=1` when automation intends a recoverable delete. The safeguard makes repeated delivery harmless. A bare DELETE is state-dependent: it trashes a live file, but permanently purges an already trashed file. ## Before you start - Use a full-access API key. The workspace role needs `delete_own_files` for the caller’s files or `delete_any_file` for other owners’ files. - Record the file ID, name, version count, and current parent before deletion. - Deleted items continue to consume storage until permanent purge. Purge is irreversible. ## Steps 1. Read the target metadata and confirm the ID belongs to the intended workspace. Stop if it is already deleted unless the job explicitly handles that state. 2. Send `DELETE /api/files/file_id?trash_only=1` with the bearer key. Keep `permanent=1` out of the request; the two flags must not be combined. 3. Accept `{ "ok": true, "permanent": false }` for the first trash action. A repeated safe request may return `{ "ok": true, "already_trashed": true }`. 4. Query `GET /api/files?deleted=1` and locate the same ID. Its absence from the normal listing alone is insufficient evidence because filters and pagination can also hide an item. 5. Store the trash receipt with the job record. Do not issue an unqualified second DELETE as a generic retry because the server would interpret the trashed state as permission to purge. 6. If permanent removal is explicitly approved, send `DELETE /api/files/file_id?permanent=1` and verify disappearance from the deleted listing. Treat that action and all versions as unrecoverable. ## Expected result The safe request moves a live file to Deleted items, and repeating it reports `already_trashed` instead of purging. Storage usage falls only after a separately requested permanent deletion. ## Troubleshooting **The file is not in the deleted listing.** Check pagination, workspace, and the response status before retrying. **The request returns 403.** Confirm full key scope, ownership permission, and lock rules. **A bare DELETE response was lost.** Inspect both normal and deleted listings before any new call. Never use an unqualified retry against an item that might already be trashed. ## Related guides - [Use folder operations](/developers/api-folder-operations) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Upload a file with the REST API
summary: Initialize a REST upload, send single or resumable multipart bytes, verify the stored file, and recover safely from limits, conflicts and lost responses.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Repository contracts and tests verified locally; no production requests or credentials used.
body: Upload a file with the REST API by opening an upload session, sending its bytes and reading the final file response. An initialization response reserves a transfer; it does **not** mean a stored file is ready. Small files finish with one PUT; multipart uploads need a separate completion call. ## Credential and destination Open [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api), select **New API key**, choose **Upload only**, then open **Restrictions and expiry → Protocols**, choose **Only the ones I pick** and check **REST API**. Save the one-time token from **Generate key** privately. A workspace pin is supported; a folder anchor on an ordinary key is not supported over REST. You need the destination's `workspace_id` and, for a subfolder, `folder_id`. An upload-only key can open and poll upload sessions but cannot list ordinary files or workspaces. Obtain IDs with a separately authorized read credential or from the signed-in app's requests. Do not temporarily broaden a production upload key just to discover its destination. To discover IDs with an authorized read key, supply it privately as `DOSYA_READ_API_KEY` and request the workspace list: ```bash curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/workspaces' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_READ_API_KEY" ``` Copy the intended workspace's `id` from `workspaces`. Then request `GET /api/files?workspace_id=THAT_ID` with the same read authorization to inspect its root listing; copy a destination folder's ID from the returned folders. To inspect a nested folder, also supply `folder_id`. Use those IDs with the upload credential; human-readable names are not API IDs. Your workspace membership must permit **upload_files** and access to the upload page. The destination must lie inside any member confinement, be visible to that member and permit new content. A folder lock, file lock, extension rule, owner storage quota, member storage cap or workspace concurrency setting can stop the transfer. ## Steps: upload a small test file with curl Supply `DOSYA_API_KEY` privately, and replace the workspace placeholder with a real authorized ID. This example needs curl and Python 3.
