It creates a **12-byte** file and uploads it to the workspace root: ```bash set -e printf 'Hello dosya\n' > dosya-api-test.txt DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID='REPLACE_WITH_WORKSPACE_ID' python3 - "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" <<'PYTHON' > upload-request.json import json, sys print(json.dumps({"workspace_id": sys.argv[1], "file_name": "dosya-api-test.txt", "file_size": 12, "mime_type": "text/plain"})) PYTHON curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/upload/init' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary @upload-request.json -o upload-init.json DOSYA_UPLOAD_PATH=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("upload-init.json"))["upload_url"])') curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --request PUT \ "https://api.dosya.dev$DOSYA_UPLOAD_PATH" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \ --data-binary @dosya-api-test.txt -o upload-result.json python3 -m json.tool upload-result.json ``` Stop if initialization fails; do not run the PUT with a stale path from a previous attempt. Add `"folder_id": "REPLACE_WITH_FOLDER_ID"` to the initialization JSON for a known destination folder. Names are sanitized to remove path separators, traversal and control characters, then checked against the **255-character** filename limit. Send actual integer bytes in `file_size`, not MB or a formatted string. Initialization returns **201** with `session_id`, `upload_url`, `workspace_id`, `file_name`, `file_size`, `mime_type`, `extension`, `region` and `resumable`. For a file of at most **52,428,800 bytes (50 MiB)**, `resumable` is null unless `force_multipart: true` was requested. Region comes from the workspace; a client-supplied region does not move the file. The PUT's **201** response contains `ok: true` and `file`, including `id`, `name`, `size_bytes`, `version`, `region`, `content_hash`, `hash_verified` and `etag`. Check `size_bytes` against the local file and retain the ID. An upload-only key can verify completion through session status; use the signed-in file list or a read key to inspect the resulting file independently. Uploading alone does not create a public link or email a recipient. ## Multipart transfer and resume Above 50 MiB, use the returned `resumable` values. Parts are **10,485,760 bytes (10 MiB)**, except the shorter final part. `total_parts` is the declared size divided by the part size, rounded up. A positive-size file may also request `force_multipart: true`; zero-byte forced multipart is rejected. For a larger local file, build a fresh initialization body from its actual size instead of keeping the 12-byte test values. This Python command replaces `upload-request.json` using the already selected workspace; change `path` and add a known `folder_id` if needed: ```bash python3 - "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" <<'PYTHON' > upload-request.json import json, sys from pathlib import Path path = Path("REPLACE_WITH_LOCAL_FILE_PATH") print(json.dumps({"workspace_id": sys.argv[1], "file_name": path.name, "file_size": path.stat().st_size, "mime_type": "application/octet-stream"})) PYTHON ``` Run the earlier `POST /api/upload/init` with that body, save its response to `upload-init.json`, and use the same unchanged local file in the resumable program below. Keep the successful initialization JSON so an interrupted run can resume the same session. The following Python 3 program sends missing parts sequentially and completes them. Save it as `resume-upload.py`, set the private `DOSYA_API_KEY` environment variable, and run `python3 resume-upload.py PATH_TO_UNCHANGED_FILE upload-init.json`. It requires an initialization whose `resumable` is non-null: ```python import json, os, sys from pathlib import Path from urllib.request import Request, urlopen base = "https://api.dosya.dev" init = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text()) r = init["resumable"] if r is None: raise SystemExit("Use the single PUT flow for this session") file = Path(sys.argv[1]) if file.stat().st_size != init["file_size"]: raise SystemExit("Local size changed; open a new upload session") headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["DOSYA_API_KEY"]} def call(path, method="GET", body=None): req = Request(base + path, data=body, method=method, headers={**headers, "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream"}) with urlopen(req) as response: return json.load(response) state = call(r["status_url"]) if state["status"] == "complete": print("Already complete; file:", state["file_id"]) raise SystemExit(0) if state["status"] == "failed": raise SystemExit("Session failed; open a fresh session and resend the file") done = set(state["uploaded_parts"]) with file.open("rb") as stream: for number in range(1, r["total_parts"] + 1): chunk = stream.read(r["part_size"]) if number not in done: call(r["part_upload_url"] + "/" + str(number), "PUT", chunk) result = call(r["complete_url"], "POST", b"") print("Stored file:", result["file"]["id"], "bytes:", result["file"]["size_bytes"]) ``` Keep the local file unchanged; equal size does not guarantee equal content. A part number is one-based and must not exceed `total_parts`. Retrying an already-recorded part returns its saved ETag with `already_uploaded: true`; it does not replace that part's bytes. HTTP **413** with `Part exceeds the 10 MB part size` means the chunk is too large. Empty parts are refused as `Empty part data`. A completion request is `POST` to `complete_url`; parts are already tracked by the server, so no client ETag array is required. A missing-part response says `Only N of M parts uploaded. Upload remaining parts before completing.` Poll status, send the missing numbers and complete again. Do not replay initialization as an idempotent operation: it opens another session, and no `Idempotency-Key` header protects this endpoint. ## Timeouts, conflicts and safe recovery `GET /api/upload/{session_id}/status` returns `status`, `bytes_uploaded`, `uploaded_parts`, `part_size`, `total_parts`, `has_multipart` and `file_id`. `file_id` is null until completion. After losing a final response, check this endpoint first: a `complete` session and its ID let you recover without uploading another version. A never-started pending session can be retired after **10 minutes** without activity. Started multipart sessions are eligible for retirement after **24 hours** without a landed write; cleanup timing is not an exact expiry promise. Restart a retired session using new initialization and resend all parts. An abandoned credential concurrency slot expires after **15 minutes** without renewal; part requests renew an active upload's slot. | Error | Recovery | | --- | --- | | **403**, `You don't have upload permission in this workspace` | Ask the workspace administrator to grant the required action, or select an allowed destination. | | **403**, `You don't have access to the upload page` | The role needs page access as well as upload permission for REST uploads. | | **404**, `Destination folder not found` | Confirm the ID belongs to this workspace and is visible; do not substitute a folder name. | | **403**, `folder_locked` | Resolve the destination lock with an authorized administrator before retrying. | | **400**, `File exceeds the … GB size limit for this workspace` | Use a smaller file or have the administrator change that workspace rule. | | **413** for a credential file-size limit | Replace the key only if a larger cap is authorized; the server also checks actual received bytes. | | **400** with `error_code: concurrent_upload_limit` | Finish or cancel other transfers; inspect `max_concurrent_uploads` in the response. | | **409**, `Upload session is already complete` | Poll status and recover the stored file ID. | | **429** or retryable **503** | Honor `Retry-After`; retain multipart state and retry missing parts rather than opening parallel replacement sessions. | Storage, size/extension, per-member and concurrent-upload checks precede destination/version validation. Completion rechecks applicable limits against received bytes, so passing initialization is not a promise that finalization will succeed. A same-name upload may become a new version of an existing file when your access permits it; uploading is not always create-only. For a deliberate replacement, send `file_id` and the last-seen `expected_version` at initialization. A stale version produces **409** `version_conflict`; refresh and decide whether to replace the newer data. Use a unique test filename to avoid accidental version changes. The workspace’s max_versions retention rule can permanently prune old version objects after a successful replacement; the default is **10 retained version entries** when that setting is absent. Save any older revision you need before replacing a file, rather than assuming every upload preserves unlimited history. To abandon an unfinished session, send `DELETE /api/upload/{session_id}` with the same authorization. It aborts partial storage and retires the session; absent or failed sessions return `ok: true` with `already_gone: true`. Completed sessions return **409** and are not deleted by this cancellation endpoint. Cancellation discards unsaved transfer progress; it does not undo a completed file or version. For the single PUT path, optionally send `X-Dosya-Sha256` containing exactly 64 hex characters of the expected SHA-256. A matching digest sets `hash_verified: true`; mismatch is **400** `hash_mismatch`, with expected and received hashes. Without that header, false means no client digest was supplied, not failed verification. Multipart completion does not provide this same one-shot hash guarantee; verify downloaded bytes separately when integrity is essential. Keep tokens out of debug traces and store session metadata privately. A lost token cannot be recovered from its masked list row. Revoke compromised credentials; do not send upload authorization headers to support. ## Expected result A completed session names a durable file in the selected workspace and folder. Its returned byte count reflects the received body; an existing same-name target can instead have a new version. Confirm the ID, size and version before marking the transfer successful. ## Related guides - [Create a scoped API credential](/developers/api-key) - [Verify file bytes by downloading them](/developers/api-download-file)

title: Use idempotency keys for API uploads
summary: Protect one-shot uploads with a UUID-v4 idempotency key, distinguish replay from in-flight work, and reject accidental reuse for different bytes.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/file.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/idempotency.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/upload/idempotency.unit.test.ts. Production uploads were not created.
body: Dosya idempotency applies to the one-shot `PUT /api/upload/file` route. Send a UUID-v4 value in `X-Dosya-Idempotency-Key`; multipart session routes have their own part-number resume contract. ## Before you start - Generate one fresh UUID v4 for one logical upload and persist it with that job until the result is verified. - Keep workspace, folder, raw filename, and `Content-Length` unchanged across retries; these values form the request fingerprint. - The request body must be replayable before automatic retry is enabled. ## Steps 1. Create a UUID v4 such as `3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6` and associate it with the local source path and intended destination. 2. Send `PUT /api/upload/file?file_name=report.pdf&folder_id=folder_id` with the exact `Content-Length`, bearer key, body, and `X-Dosya-Idempotency-Key`. 3. On HTTP 201, store the returned file receipt. The server retains a completed idempotency record for 86,400 seconds, so a matching retry can recover the response. 4. After an ambiguous transport failure, repeat the identical request with the identical key. HTTP 200 plus `X-Dosya-Idempotent-Replay: true` means Dosya returned the earlier result without a second file. 5. For HTTP 409 with `Retry-After: 5`, another matching request is still in progress. Wait and retry; abandoned in-progress ownership can be taken over after 600 seconds. 6. For 409 with code `idempotency_key_reused`, stop. The key was paired with a different workspace, folder, raw filename, or declared length; generate a new key only for a genuinely new upload. ## Expected result The first accepted upload returns 201. An identical replay returns the same logical result with status 200 and the replay header, while a mismatched fingerprint is refused rather than creating uncertain data. ## Troubleshooting **The body cannot be replayed.** Spool it to a temporary file before the first request or disable automatic retries. **The response is 409 without the reuse code.** Honor `Retry-After: 5`; do not create a new key while the original operation may still finish. **The file bytes changed but length did not.** Use `X-Dosya-Sha256` as an integrity check and a new idempotency key for the new logical upload. ## Related guides - [Upload through the API](/developers/api-upload-file) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Validate file size during an API upload
summary: Apply declared and measured upload-size gates, add SHA-256 integrity, and read the final measured byte size from Dosya’s stored-file receipt.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/file.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/body-pipeline.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/measured-body.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/extension-policy.ts, apps/api/src/lib/usage/enforce.ts, and apps/api/src/middleware.ts. Production uploads were not created.
body: Dosya checks the declared size before accepting bytes and measures the body while reading it. One-shot uploads require a decimal `Content-Length`; files above 50 MiB must use the upload-session flow. ## Before you start - Check the API key’s `max_file_size_bytes`, the workspace storage quota, and the workspace `max_file_size_gb` setting. REST uploads do not apply a role-level file-size cap. - The key must reach the selected workspace, and the member role must allow `upload_files` plus `access_upload` for this REST upload surface. - Compute a lowercase 64-character SHA-256 digest when end-to-end byte identity matters. - Treat `Content-Length` as a gate, not proof of the stored size; the final receipt reflects bytes actually received. ## Steps 1. Measure the source before transfer. Use one-shot upload at or below 50 MiB; initialize a resumable upload above that boundary. 2. For one-shot transfer, send a digits-only `Content-Length`. Missing or malformed length returns 411; an amount over 50 MiB returns 413 with `Files over 50 MB use /api/upload/init and the resumable upload`. 3. Add `X-Dosya-Sha256: digest` when available. A mismatch returns 400 with `hash_mismatch` and expected and received values. 4. Send the body while retaining the status and JSON error. A measured body that crosses the allowed buffer can return 413 with `upload_declared_size_mismatch`. 5. Handle policy refusals literally: `This API key does not permit files larger than N bytes (max_file_size_bytes)`, `File exceeds the X GB size limit for this workspace`, or the storage-quota response. 6. On success, read the receipt’s actual stored size and file ID, then fetch metadata. Do not reject a successful upload merely because fewer bytes arrived than declared; decide against the measured result and digest. ## Expected result An allowed body produces a file receipt whose measured size matches metadata, and an optional SHA-256 confirms the bytes. Oversized, disallowed, or corrupt input fails before it becomes a trusted result. ## Troubleshooting **The server returns 411.** Supply the actual decimal byte length; chunked one-shot transfer does not replace that requirement. **The file is over 50 MiB.** Use `/api/upload/init`, 10 MiB parts, and the completion route. **Declared and stored sizes differ.** Treat the receipt as authoritative, compare the digest, and investigate the producer before continuing. ## Related guides - [Upload through the API](/developers/api-upload-file) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Review Dosya API usage analytics
summary: Filter account-level API analytics by key and time range, inspect request and error totals, and page through 50-row REST and S3 activity logs.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/pages/api-analytics.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-analytics/series.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-analytics/logs.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/api-analytics.ts. Production analytics were not opened.
body: API analytics are account-level, not limited to the currently active workspace. Open the Analytics action from an API key card in Profile, then choose all owned keys or one owned key. ## Before you start - Sign in through the browser; this page uses the web session rather than an API key in the request. - Allow one to two minutes for recent activity to appear. - Pick the investigation window: 24 hours uses one-hour buckets, 7 days uses six-hour buckets, and 30 days uses one-day buckets. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile**, find the relevant API key card, and select **Analytics**. The page route includes `?key=` when opened for one key. 2. Choose **All keys** for an account-wide view or select one owned key. Changing workspaces does not change this account-level ownership filter. 3. Set **24h**, **7d**, or **30d** and read **Requests** and **Errors**. Errors count responses whose status is 400 or higher. 4. Inspect **Requests over time** using the bucket size for that range. Compare a spike with deployment time before attributing it to one route. 5. Review **Recent requests**. Rows show Time, optional Key, Action, Source, Status, IP, Country, and Client; avoid copying IP details into public tickets. 6. Use **Load more** to fetch another 50 log rows. Save the chosen key, range, timestamps, statuses, and actions as the investigation receipt. ## Expected result The totals, time series, and paginated request rows reflect the selected account key filter and range. A recent call may appear after the normal one-to-two-minute ingestion delay. ## Troubleshooting **The page says `Analytics temporarily unavailable`.** The backing request returned 502; retry later without rotating a working key. **A request is missing.** Wait two minutes, confirm the account owns the selected key, expand the range, and load more rows. **Counts look different from one workspace.** The dashboard follows account-owned keys across workspaces; filter to the specific key used by that workspace. ## Related guides - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [Inspect webhook deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Verify an API mutation before the next step
summary: Verify each API write with its route receipt and postcondition read, while using D1 bookmarks only to order the D1-backed parts of a request.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/api/src/lib/db.ts, apps/api/src/middleware.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/rename.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/file.ts, and apps/cli/src/client.ts. Production mutations were not run.
body: A 2xx response proves that the route accepted its own contract; a route-specific read proves the next step can observe the intended state. Dosya’s `X-D1-Bookmark` orders D1 session reads, while file content may live in a workspace object outside that ordering. ## Before you start - Define the postcondition before sending the mutation: exact ID, parent, name, deleted state, version, or byte size. - Know the route’s replay behavior. One-shot upload has an idempotency key; a bare file DELETE can become a permanent purge on its second call. - Keep status and response body as the operation receipt. Retain `X-D1-Bookmark` when present for later D1-backed reads. ## Steps 1. Read the resource and record its current ID and state. Reject a stale local assumption before it becomes a write request. 2. Send one narrowly scoped mutation. Require its documented status and fields, such as move or rename `{ "ok": true, "name": "…" }` or an upload file receipt. 3. Capture `X-D1-Bookmark` when the response supplies it. Send it on the next request to order that request’s D1 session; it does not create cross-storage ordering for a workspace object. 4. Perform the mutation’s own verification read: fetch the same ID after move or rename, query the deleted listing after trash, or fetch the file ID returned by upload. 5. Compare the read to the predeclared postcondition. Do not substitute an empty old listing for proof that the item exists in its intended new state. 6. Persist the mutation receipt and verified state before the next dependent action. If verification is inconclusive, pause and inspect rather than replaying an unsafe write. ## Expected result The receipt and route-specific read agree on the same resource and committed state. Downstream automation starts only after the operation-specific postcondition is visible; a bookmark helps only where the read uses D1. ## Troubleshooting **The mutation succeeded but the read looks stale.** Confirm the follow-up targets the same ID and workspace. Carry the response bookmark for D1 state, but judge workspace-object content from the route response itself. **The response was lost.** Read first. Replay only when the route documents idempotency or the observed precondition proves the original request did not commit. **The old location is empty.** Check the destination or deleted listing by ID; absence is not a complete postcondition. ## Related guides - [Use folder operations](/developers/api-folder-operations) - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart)

title: Choose light or dark appearance
summary: Switch Light, Dark, or System mode, choose among eight color themes, verify account sync, and recover from an appearance save failure on this device.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/appearance.tsx, apps/web/src/components/layout/profile-menu.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/theme.ts, apps/web/src/lib/themes.ts, apps/web/src/lib/boot.ts, apps/api/src/lib/appearance.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/appearance.ts. No production profile was updated; the inspection applied no persistent user theme.
body: Appearance is an account preference with two parts: a color **Theme** and a **Mode**. Mode can be **Light**, **Dark**, or **System**; System follows the device’s light/dark setting. The selection changes Dosya’s interface, never file contents, shared-link styling, or a recipient’s own view. ## Available choices The full **Appearance** page offers eight themes: **Default**, **Mono**, **Claude**, **Amber**, **Ocean**, **Bubblegum**, **Vercel**, and **Neo-Brutalism**. Each theme works with all three modes. A new or invalid preference falls back to the **Default** theme and **System** mode. The avatar menu contains a compact **Appearance** row with **Light mode** and **Dark mode** radio controls only. Those controls keep the menu open and preserve the selected color theme. Open the linked Appearance page when you need **System** or a different palette. ## Steps 1. Open the account menu and choose **Appearance**, or go directly to `/profile/appearance`. 2. Under **Mode**, select **Light**, **Dark**, or **System**. 3. Under **Theme**, choose one of the eight labelled swatches. 4. Inspect navigation, Files, a settings form, focus indicators, status colors, and any code or document preview you rely on. 5. Reload the page. The applied mode and theme should return from the account profile. 6. Sign in on another supported browser or device and confirm the account preference is reconciled there. The page previews each change immediately, writes it to local storage, and sends the complete theme-and-mode pair to the account API. No plan or workspace permission is required. Every choice is reversible and does not modify stored files. ## Saving, motion, and recovery On the full Appearance page, a rejected save restores the prior mode and palette and shows **Couldn’t save**, followed by the server error or “Your theme could not be saved.” Reconnect, make one selection, and reload before testing another device. The avatar-menu light/dark control applies locally at once and starts its account save in the background. Because that shortcut does not display a save result, a reload is the decisive persistence check. Supported browsers animate a user-initiated theme change with a short visual wipe. Dosya skips that transition when the device reports **prefers-reduced-motion: reduce** or when the browser lacks the View Transitions API. System mode listens for operating-system scheme changes while the app is open. If a palette makes a control difficult to read, switch to **Default** and the clearest mode for the environment. Appearance changes do not alter permissions, storage, uploads, links, or notification delivery. ## Expected result The chosen palette and mode apply immediately, survive a reload after a successful save, and reconcile when the same account starts another supported session. System mode changes with the device scheme, while explicit Light or Dark stays fixed. ## Related guides - [Update profile settings](/account/profile-settings) - [Navigate the web app](/account/navigate-web-app)

title: Browse folders inside an archive
summary: Browse folders and filter entries inside ZIP, ISO, and IMG files without extraction; understand listing caps and truncated archive results in Dosya.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/ArchiveViewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-tree.ts, apps/api/src/lib/zip/central-directory.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/container/iso/directory.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The archive tree lets you inspect nested paths without creating Dosya folders or copying entry bytes. Browser and desktop use a collapsible tree; mobile uses one directory level at a time. ## How the tree works The service reads ZIP central-directory records or ISO 9660 directory records and returns display-safe entries. It addresses a member by its directory index, not by a caller-supplied extraction path. The interface then builds folders from those cleaned names. Browsing changes only local interface state; it does not expand the container in storage. Each directory begins closed and shows its descendant file count. Files show their uncompressed size when they are openable. Password-protected members carry a lock, while unsupported compression displays a separate unavailable marker. These disabled rows remain focusable so keyboard and screen-reader users can hear the refusal reason. ## Steps 1. Open the archive and wait for **Archive contents** to replace the loading rows. 2. Select a folder row, or press Enter or Space while it has keyboard focus, to expand it. Repeat for deeper directories. 3. Select the same row again to collapse that branch. Closing a folder does not lose or modify any archive data. 4. To find a name, enter a case-insensitive fragment in **Filter entries**. Matching files remain visible and their ancestor folders open automatically for the search. 5. Clear the field to return to your explicit open-folder state. The filter does not search file contents. 6. If the bottom of the tree says **Showing the first X of Y entries**, treat the result as incomplete. Use the returned portion to inspect known names, or download the entire archive for a complete local listing. ## Limits and unusual archives A response contains no more than 20,000 entries. ZIP and ISO directory processing is capped at 16 MiB, all decoded names together at 2 MiB, and ISO traversal at 400 directory reads. A name-budget or entry-count overflow can return a truncated listing. A larger directory structure can instead return 413 and instruct you to download the archive. An empty result displays **There is nothing inside this archive.** This can describe a genuinely empty container or one whose unusable display names were removed while the safe tree was built. It does not create an empty Dosya folder. If a familiar path is absent, first clear **Filter entries**, reopen its parents, and check the truncation notice. Next verify that you opened the intended file version. Download the original for local inspection when the server's directory limits intentionally prevent a complete list. ## Expected result The viewer reveals the returned hierarchy and makes the desired safe entry reachable. No entry bytes move until you preview, download, or save a file, and browsing itself leaves cloud storage unchanged. ## Related guides - [Inspect archives](/files/archive-preview) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Download one archive entry
summary: Download one eligible file from a ZIP, ISO, or IMG archive while keeping the stored archive unchanged and respecting view-only access controls.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/ArchiveViewer.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/entry.ts, apps/api/src/lib/files/download-gate.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/container/refusals.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: Download a single item when you do not need the complete ZIP or disk image. The operation streams the chosen central-directory entry and leaves the archive stored in Dosya unchanged. ## Requirements - The entry must be a file compressed with STORE or DEFLATE. Folders, encrypted items, and unsupported compression methods cannot be streamed. - The archive must remain viewable, and its byte-copy gate must pass. The entry route does not separately test the role's `download_files` permission; it refuses an archive marked view-only and any blocked view-only, locked, or hidden ancestor. - Browser downloads use the browser's configured download location. The desktop app opens its native save dialog and requests the selected entry index, not the whole archive. ## Steps 1. Open the archive from **Files**, then expand the directory that contains the item. 2. Select the row and compare the displayed file name and uncompressed size with what you intend to receive. 3. Choose **Download** in the selected-entry header. If the format has no inline renderer, use **Download this file** on its fallback card. 4. In the desktop app, choose a local destination in the system save dialog. In a browser, wait for the browser download to finish. 5. Open the saved item with an appropriate local application. Verify its name, size, and content before deleting or changing the source archive. ## Refusals and recovery The download request includes `dl=1`, which runs the byte-copy gate after the archive has passed the preview path. An archive whose own lock mode is view-only returns **This file is view-only and cannot be downloaded** with 403. A blocked ancestor is concealed as **File not found** with 404. Unlock the relevant full lock or have an administrator change the lock, hidden state, or folder access; reopening the same URL does not bypass the chain. Other server responses distinguish the failure: - **That entry is a folder, not a file.** means the selected index names a directory. - **This entry is password-protected.** means Dosya cannot decrypt it. - **This entry uses … compression, which is not supported.** names the unsupported method. - **No such entry in this archive.** can occur when the chosen version and entry index no longer correspond. - **Archive not found in storage.** means the metadata exists but the archive bytes cannot be read. Download usage and transfer limits are charged against the entry's uncompressed size before streaming begins. If a usage, egress, or concurrency limit refuses the operation, wait for an active transfer to finish or resolve the account limit, then retry. A partially written local file is not a verified result; remove it and start the download again. ## Expected result Exactly one local file is produced from the selected archive index. Its content matches the listing and preview, while the cloud archive, its version history, and every other entry remain untouched. ## Related guides - [Inspect archives](/files/archive-preview) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Verify an entry downloaded from an archive
summary: Download one eligible archive member by its indexed row, check access and compression refusals, and verify a local copy without changing the archive.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/entry.ts, apps/api/src/lib/container/refusals.ts, and apps/web/src/lib/archive-tree.ts. Production download behavior was not re-tested.
body: Downloading one member creates a local copy of that member; it does not extract every item or alter the ZIP, ISO, or IMG stored in Dosya. ### Before you start - You must be able to view the archive through its folder path. A `view_only` file or locked or hidden ancestor can block the entry request. - ZIP members using Store (method 0) or Deflate (method 8) are eligible. Password-protected members and unsupported compression methods cannot be downloaded through this viewer. - Use the entry path and uncompressed size to distinguish duplicate base names in different folders. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, open the archive and wait for **Archive contents** to appear. 2. Expand the relevant folders or enter part of the name in **Filter entries**. Select the exact file row, not a folder row. 3. Check the displayed path, cleaned display name, and size. A blocked row explains **This entry is password-protected** or **Compressed with a method this viewer cannot open (method N)**. 4. In the entry stage, choose **Download**. For a format without an inline renderer, use **Download this file** on the fallback card. 5. Allow the browser to save the response. The download header uses the raw final path segment as its UTF-8 filename, so the browser or operating system may sanitize it differently from Dosya’s cleaned display name. Compare its byte size and contents with the selected member. ### If the download is refused **That entry is a folder, not a file.** means the numeric row now addresses a directory. Reopen the archive and choose a file. A 409 response identifies an encrypted entry, while a 415 response names unsupported compression. A 413 listing refusal means the archive directory exceeded its processing budget; download the whole archive and inspect it locally instead. Archive requests identify members by their numeric directory index rather than accepting a pathname from the URL. Display names also lose control characters, bidi controls, and `.` or `..` segments. The numeric index prevents a crafted path from selecting a different server-side member. Browser and operating-system filename rules control the local destination, so choose an isolated folder and continue to treat the bytes as untrusted. ## Expected result The browser saves the chosen member using the response filename derived from the archive’s raw final path segment; local filename sanitization can change what appears on disk. No folder or file is added to Dosya, and the stored archive and its version remain unchanged; delete the local copy through your operating system if it is no longer needed. ## Related guides - [Inspect an archive before extracting files](/files/archive-preview) - [Save one archive entry to Dosya](/files/archive-save-entry)

title: Preview one file inside an archive
summary: Preview a supported file inside a ZIP, ISO, or IMG archive, including text limits, blocked compression methods, and view-only behavior in Dosya.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/ArchiveViewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/text-detect.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/entry.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/container/refusals.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The archive viewer can render one supported member without first saving it as a separate Dosya file. This is useful for confirming content, but it does not grant download permission or alter the container. ## What can preview Browser and desktop archive views render images, PDF documents, video, audio, and readable text. For an archive member, text detection uses only its filename: common source, configuration, markup, subtitle, and plain-text extensions plus recognized extensionless names such as `README` and `Dockerfile`. The archive viewer supplies no MIME type to this check. Text entries larger than 2 MiB are not fetched for inline display. The card reports **Too large to preview inline (size)** and offers **Download this file**. For an eligible text member, Dosya fetches the complete entry but renders at most 200,000 characters; when shortened, it says **Showing the first 200,000 characters. Download the file to see the rest.** ## Steps 1. Open the ZIP, ISO, or IMG in the browser or desktop client. 2. Navigate the **Archive contents** list, or type into **Filter entries** to narrow it by name. 3. Select a file row that shows a size. Directory rows expand or collapse and do not become preview selections. 4. Confirm the selected-entry bar names the intended member. The caption on image, media, and text stages includes the cleaned file name and uncompressed size. 5. Use the native controls inside PDF, video, or audio previews as needed. Unsupported file types show a download card rather than misleading rendered content. 6. Close the viewer when inspection is complete. No extraction is required for this workflow. ## Access and failure behavior Preview requests use the viewable-file permission path. A view-only archive or ancestor may still allow this display, even though **Download** and **Save to dosya** are later rejected by their stricter gates. Full locks, hidden content, or a folder outside a member's allowed anchor remain unavailable. Only STORE and DEFLATE members open. Password protection produces **This entry is password-protected**. Other algorithms return an error such as **This entry uses Deflate64 compression, which is not supported.** If the data length differs from the declared size, Dosya treats the container as malformed rather than streaming unchecked bytes. **This entry could not be opened.** indicates a fetch or decoding failure in the text view. Reselect the row once, confirm that the correct archive version is open, and try downloading the whole archive with a trusted local utility if the same preview continues to fail. Entry responses can remain in a private cache for 3,600 seconds, and version-specific URLs prevent one version's member from being confused with another. ## Expected result The preview displays the exact selected member, or gives a download-only or refusal state that explains why inline rendering is unavailable. The stored archive receives no new version and no extracted cloud item is created. ## Related guides - [Inspect archives](/files/archive-preview) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Inspect an archive folder tree
summary: Expand an archive hierarchy safely, interpret implied folders and cleaned paths, and use filtering and listing limits before opening any nested member.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-tree.ts, apps/api/src/lib/zip/central-directory.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/container/iso/directory.ts. Production archive indexing was not re-tested.
body: The archive viewer builds a safe hierarchy from directory records and initially leaves folders collapsed. It can show explicit folders and inferred parents created from nested member paths. ### Before you start - The browser viewer recognizes ZIP plus ISO 9660 content stored as `.iso` or `.img`; EPUB and CBZ use separate readers. - Listing reads archive-directory ranges rather than extracting member bodies. Inspection itself is read-only. - Confirm the selected file version. Index responses are privately cacheable for 3,600 seconds, and the version number is part of the request. ## Steps 1. Open the container from **Files** and wait until its entry count, archive size, and container kind appear above **Archive contents**. 2. Expand the first directory. Continue one level at a time, using Enter or Space when keyboard focus is on a folder row. 3. Compare every parent segment before selecting a leaf. The tree sorts directories before files and compares names naturally without case sensitivity, so a numeric sequence such as `2` and `10` stays readable. 4. Use **Filter entries** for a long hierarchy. Filtering opens parents needed to reveal matches, but it searches only the entries returned by the server. 5. Select the intended leaf and confirm its full position, size, and availability marker before previewing, downloading, or saving it. ### How paths are presented Backslashes are normalized to `/`. Blank, `.` and `..` segments are discarded, and control and bidirectional formatting characters are removed from displayed names. An inferred folder may therefore appear even when the archive did not contain a separate directory record. Entry operations use the server-provided numeric index, so a displayed path is descriptive rather than a local extraction destination. ZIP and ISO directory processing each stop at 20,000 entries and a 16 MiB directory-data budget. Decoded names share a 2 MiB budget, and ISO traversal permits at most 400 directory reads. **Showing the first X of Y entries** means the returned tree is incomplete. **This archive is too large to list** means you must download the original and use a trusted local archive tool. ## Expected result The expanded rows identify the intended member through its complete cleaned hierarchy. Merely expanding, filtering, and selecting nodes creates no extracted files and makes no change to the source object. ## Related guides - [Inspect an archive before extracting files](/files/archive-preview) - [Review nested archive paths](/files/archive-review-nested-paths)

title: Preview a supported archive entry
summary: Preview an eligible archive member by checking its path, compression, size, and renderer limits while leaving the original cloud archive untouched.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-tree.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/entry.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/container/refusals.ts. Production preview behavior was not re-tested.
body: Dosya previews selected members directly from a ZIP or supported disk image. Previewing reads one member and does not extract the archive into cloud storage. ### Before you start - Choose an unencrypted file. ZIP entries must use Store (0) or Deflate (8); other compression methods remain visible but unavailable. - The entry request inherits the archive's view gate, including ancestor locks and hidden paths. - Supported stages include image, PDF, video, audio, and recognized text. Availability also depends on browser decoding for media. ## Steps 1. Open the archive in **Files**, then expand **Archive contents** to the correct folder. 2. Select the leaf row whose path and uncompressed size match the item you intend to inspect. 3. Check that the row does not show a lock or unsupported-compression marker. If it does, use a trusted local tool after downloading the whole container. 4. Wait for the right-hand stage. An image, PDF, audio, or video response opens its corresponding viewer; a recognized text filename opens the text stage. 5. Compare the preview with the selected row before taking any **Download** or **Save to dosya** action. ### Preview limits and recovery Text is fetched inline only up to 2 MiB. Even within that limit, the renderer shows at most 200,000 characters and says **Showing the first 200,000 characters. Download the file to see the rest.** Text recognition uses the filename or extension because the archive preview supplies no MIME value. A larger eligible entry displays **Too large to preview inline (size)** with **Download this file**. An unsupported content type also gets the download card. **This entry could not be opened.** indicates that the selected member fetch failed; reopen the container to refresh its index and confirm that you did not switch file versions. Password protection produces a 409 refusal. Unsupported compression produces a 415 response that names the method. A malformed or changed container can produce 422 even when its outer file still exists. ## Expected result The stage renders the member selected by numeric index and identifies it with its cleaned name and size. The archive remains byte-for-byte unchanged, and no standalone Dosya file exists unless you later choose **Save to dosya**. ## Related guides - [Inspect an archive before extracting files](/files/archive-preview) - [Save an entry from an archive](/files/archive-save-entry)

title: Troubleshoot an archive that will not preview
summary: Diagnose invalid, oversized, unsupported, or changed archives by matching Dosya’s exact error state to format, listing, and entry-level limits.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/container/refusals.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/index.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/entry.ts. Production errors were not reproduced.
body: An archive can fail while Dosya reads its directory, while it retrieves one indexed member, or while the browser decodes that member. The visible message tells you which layer to test. ### Before you start - Keep the original archive available. Repacking or uploading a replacement creates different bytes and may create a new Dosya version. - Test in the same account, workspace, and folder path so ancestor lock and visibility rules remain comparable. - Use a small known-good ZIP containing one Deflate image as the control file. ## Steps 1. Reopen the stored container and record the exact heading. **This file isn't a valid zip** or **This file isn't a valid disk image** means parsing returned 422. 2. If the heading is **This archive is too large to list**, download the whole file. A 413 response means its directory exceeded a 16 MiB budget or another listing ceiling; retrying the same bytes will not reduce it. 3. If you see **This archive could not be opened**, verify access to the archive and its ancestors, refresh the network session, and retry once. The fallback detail can say **Network error. Please try again.** 4. If the tree loads but one row does not, inspect its marker. Encrypted entries are refused with **This entry is password-protected**; methods other than Store and Deflate are unsupported in ZIP preview. 5. Open the same known-good image archive. If it renders, the original container or member is the cause. If it also fails, retry in another supported browser and check workspace access. ### Choose the recovery that matches the failure For a valid but oversized directory, use **Download the file** and inspect it locally. For encryption or unsupported compression, extract with a trusted local application and upload only the reviewed result if a cloud copy is needed. For an entry too large for its inline renderer, use **Download this file** instead of modifying the archive. Archive indexes may be privately cached for up to 3,600 seconds, but requests include the selected version. Close the viewer and reopen the intended version after replacing the file; do not assume a tree from one version describes another. ## Expected result The failing archive is classified as access/network, malformed format, directory limit, entry encryption/compression, or renderer limitation. Diagnosis alone does not rewrite, delete, or extract the stored object. ## Related guides - [Inspect an archive before extracting files](/files/archive-preview) - [Preview files in Dosya](/files/preview-files)

title: Inspect an archive before extracting files
summary: Inspect ZIP, ISO, and IMG contents without extracting the whole file; understand listing limits, preview rules, and safe save options in Dosya.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/ArchiveViewer.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/zip/central-directory.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/container/iso/directory.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: Dosya can inspect `.zip`, `.iso`, and `.img` files in the browser and desktop app without extracting the whole container first. EPUB and CBZ files use their readers instead. An `.img` file must contain an ISO 9660 image; raw FAT or ext4 images are not supported by this viewer. ## Before you start - You need access to view the stored archive and every containing folder. A full lock or hidden ancestor can prevent the archive from opening. - Listing is read-only. Downloads and **Save to dosya** have separate permission checks. - Treat unfamiliar entry names as untrusted. Dosya neutralizes unsafe display names and identifies entries by their directory index, but it does not evaluate an extracted file for you. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, open the ZIP, ISO, or IMG file. Wait while the viewer shows **Opening…** and loads only the archive directory. 2. Read the summary above the tree. It reports the total entry count, stored archive size, and whether Dosya opened it as an archive or disk image. 3. Expand folders in **Archive contents**. Directories start closed so a large container does not render every nested row at once. 4. Enter part of a name in **Filter entries** when the tree is long. Matching descendants remain reachable because filtering opens their parent folders in the result view. 5. Select an eligible file. Stored and Deflate entries, compression methods 0 and 8, can open. A lock marks an encrypted entry; the tooltip says **This entry is password-protected**. Other compression methods are marked unavailable and name their numeric method. 6. Review the right-hand stage. Images, PDFs, video, audio, and readable text can preview there. Other formats present **Download this file** instead of inventing a preview. 7. Choose **Download** for a local copy or **Save to dosya** for a new cloud file only after the path, displayed name, and uncompressed size are the ones you expect. ## Listing limits and errors Dosya lists at most 20,000 entries. ZIP central-directory data and ISO directory data each have a 16 MiB processing ceiling, and decoded entry names have a combined 2 MiB budget. ISO traversal also stops after 400 directory reads. If a valid container exceeds a directory budget, the service responds with a 413 refusal and the viewer tells you to download the file instead. A truncated result says **Showing the first X of Y entries**; filtering searches only the entries that were returned. **This file isn't a valid zip** or the disk-image equivalent means the parser rejected the container. **This archive could not be opened** can also mean access, storage, or network failure. Retry once after confirming the file version and connection. If the 413 message remains, download the original archive and inspect it with a trusted local tool. Archive index and entry responses are private-cacheable for up to 3,600 seconds. Dosya includes the selected version in its requests; if another upload creates a newer version, close the viewer and open the intended version rather than assuming the old tree describes the new bytes. ## Expected result The left pane shows the allowed portion of the archive hierarchy, and selecting an openable file displays that same indexed entry on the right. Inspection alone creates no folder, extracted file, or modification to the source archive. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Organize files](/files/organize-files)

title: Review unsafe or nested archive paths
summary: Review cleaned archive paths, inferred folders, duplicate names, and unsafe nested members before previewing or copying any entry out of the container.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/lib/archive-tree.ts, apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/entry.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/save.ts, and apps/web/src/lib/archive-save.ts. Production extraction was not tested.
body: Archive names can contain deep hierarchies, duplicate base names, backslashes, control codes, or traversal-looking segments. Dosya cleans the displayed tree and addresses actions by directory index. ### Before you start - Obtain the expected package layout from the sender when possible. - Use an isolated local folder for downloads of untrusted content. Do not open unknown executables merely because the archive viewer listed them. - Remember that **Save to dosya** creates a new cloud object; **Download** creates a local copy. ## Steps 1. Open the archive and expand folders slowly. Compare the full hierarchy, not only the final filename. 2. Look for unexpected siblings, repeated names, embedded archives, executable extensions, or a large difference between compressed and uncompressed sizes. 3. Understand the normalized view: `\` becomes `/`; blank, `.` and `..` segments disappear; control and bidirectional formatting characters are stripped. Missing parent records can become inferred folders. 4. Select only the row whose cleaned path and size match the expected member. Dosya sends its numeric directory index to the entry endpoint instead of sending a client-controlled extraction path. 5. Preview supported content first. If a fallback offers **Download this file**, save it into the isolated folder and scan or inspect it with a suitable local tool before moving it elsewhere. ### What Dosya's path handling does and does not do The numeric index prevents a crafted name such as `../../report.pdf` from choosing a server-side member or destination by pathname. When saving to Dosya, the chosen destination folder is supplied separately and the server validates the resulting filename. These controls stop path traversal through the viewer; they do not establish that the bytes are harmless. Folder extraction preserves the reviewed hierarchy for eligible files, skips encrypted and unsupported ZIP methods, and never silently rolls back files already saved before cancellation or a later failure. A whole-folder save is capped at 500 eligible files. For unknown packages, prefer one reviewed entry at a time. ## Expected result You can state which cleaned tree row corresponds to the intended member and why it is acceptable to preview, download, or save. Inspection leaves both the source archive and trusted local files unchanged. ## Related guides - [Inspect an archive folder tree](/files/archive-inspect-folder-tree) - [Save an archive entry to Dosya](/files/archive-save-entry)

title: Save an archive entry to Dosya
summary: Save one eligible archive entry as a new Dosya file, choose an allowed destination, and understand size, permission, quota, and failure rules.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-save.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/save.ts, apps/api/src/lib/files/download-gate.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/ingest/register.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: **Save to dosya** extracts one eligible archive member into the same workspace as a normal cloud file. It does not remove the member from the source container, and an existing same-name file causes the new item to receive a collision-safe suffix. ## Requirements The source archive must be viewable and pass the same byte-copy gate used for entry downloads: its own view-only lock or a blocked ancestor refuses extraction. This route does not separately require the role's `download_files` permission. Saving does require **upload files** access in the workspace. Folder-confined members can choose only a destination inside their assigned anchor, never workspace root. The destination must exist, remain visible, and accept content; full locks and locked WordPress backup folders refuse writes. The selected member must use STORE or DEFLATE, must not be password-protected, and cannot exceed 4 GiB. Your plan, credential file-size policy, remaining storage quota, egress allowance, and concurrent-transfer ceiling can impose lower effective limits. ## Steps 1. Open the archive, locate the desired row, and compare its displayed name and uncompressed size with the content you expect. 2. Select the file and choose **Save to dosya** in the action bar. 3. In **Save to folder**, navigate to an allowed destination and select **Save here**. A root choice is valid only when your membership is not folder-confined. 4. Wait for **Saved to dosya**. Its detail text is the actual name registered in the destination, including any suffix added to resolve a collision. 5. Open the destination folder and preview the new item. Compare its returned size and content with the archive member before relying on it. ## Failure and recovery **You don't have upload permission in this workspace** requires a role change. **Destination folder not found** means the chosen folder was removed, hidden, or unavailable; reopen the picker and select a live location. A locked destination returns a `folder_locked` refusal. **This entry is larger than 4 GiB. Download the archive to extract it.** cannot be resolved by choosing another cloud folder. The server validates the declared entry length as it streams. **This entry's data does not match its declared size; the archive is malformed.** requires a corrected source container. **Could not write the extracted file to storage** means registration did not complete; the service attempts to remove the partial object, so verify the destination before retrying. Saving a single entry is atomic from the interface's perspective: a successful response creates the new file and records a `file_uploaded` activity with archive extraction metadata. The source archive stays intact. If you later remove the saved copy, normal trash and retention behavior applies to that separate file. For a folder or **Save all to dosya**, your role also needs **create folders** permission. The client processes at most 500 eligible files, creates a wrapper folder and nested directories, then saves members sequentially. Cancellation stops before the next file; folders and files already created remain. Password-protected or unsupported members are skipped, and earlier successes are not rolled back when a later member fails. ## Expected result The selected member appears as an independent Dosya file in the chosen permitted folder, with a safe name and the declared byte count. The archive and its versions are unchanged. ## Related guides - [Inspect archives](/files/archive-preview) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Save one archive entry to Dosya
summary: Save one eligible archive member as an independent Dosya file, with destination, quota, 4 GiB, permission, and partial-effect checks explained.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/archive-viewer/archive-viewer.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/save.ts, apps/api/src/lib/container/refusals.ts, and apps/web/src/components/folder-picker-dialog.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/ingest/register.ts. Production saving was not re-tested.
body: **Save to dosya** copies one archive member into a new standalone cloud file. It leaves the source container intact and consumes storage quota for the new object. ### Before you start - You need view access to the source archive and upload permission in the destination folder. - The entry must be a file, not a directory; encrypted ZIP members and compression methods other than Store or Deflate are refused. - One saved member cannot exceed 4 GiB. The workspace also needs enough remaining quota and must accept the filename and file-size policy. ## Steps 1. Open the archive in **Files** and select the exact eligible row under **Archive contents**. 2. Review its cleaned name, full folder position, and uncompressed size. Preview it first when a renderer is available. 3. Choose **Save to dosya**. In **Save to folder**, navigate to the intended accessible destination. 4. Select the folder and press **Save here**. The selection alone does not start the copy. 5. Wait for the creation response, then open the destination in **Files** and compare the returned filename, byte size, and preview with the source member. A collision becomes `name (2).ext`, then `name (3).ext`, rather than a new version of the existing file. ### Refusals and recovery **This entry is password-protected.** is a 409 refusal. Unsupported compression returns 415, and a malformed archive can return 422. A member larger than 4 GiB returns 413. Destination failures can also come from upload permission, a locked or hidden path, filename rules, file-size limits, or insufficient workspace quota. If the request fails before registration, no new file should appear. Registration preserves the selected destination folder but resolves an active-name collision with a numeric suffix before the extension; after 50 collisions it uses a short file-ID marker. If the response is uncertain after an interrupted connection, refresh the chosen destination and search for the intended name before retrying; repeating a completed request can create another independent file. Deleting a successfully saved copy later is a separate trash action. Unlike **Save all to dosya**, a one-entry operation has no 500-file folder cap because it processes one numeric index. The saved copy no longer depends on the archive for ordinary access. ## Expected result The selected destination contains one independent file whose content and size match the member; its name may carry a collision suffix. The original ZIP, ISO, or IMG stays in place and is not shortened, renamed, or marked as extracted. ## Related guides - [Save files from an archive](/files/archive-save-entry) - [Inspect an archive before extracting files](/files/archive-preview)

title: Review audio artwork and metadata
summary: Inspect browser audio title, artist, album, artwork, bitrate, and sample rate while understanding 256 KiB tag reads and format-specific fallbacks.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-tags.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, packages/audio-player/src/tags/parse.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/id3.ts, and packages/audio-player/src/tags/mp4.ts. Production media was not tested.
body: The web player reads a 256 KiB byte range from the start of an audio file and parses recognized embedded tags locally in the browser. It does not write those tags back to Dosya. ### Supported tag sources MP3 parsing recognizes ID3v2.2, v2.3, and v2.4 title, artist, album, embedded artwork, lyrics, bitrate, and sample rate. MP4/M4A parsing can provide title, artist, album, duration, and artwork, but not lyrics, bitrate, or sample rate in this player. In the web viewer, the entire tag and artwork payload must be reachable within the first 256 KiB fetched from the file. The shared parser also rejects an individual JPEG or PNG artwork payload over 2 MiB when a caller supplies more data. ## Steps 1. Open an audio file in the browser file viewer and wait for its metadata range request to finish. 2. Compare the large player title with the Dosya filename. When no embedded title is found, the player removes the extension and uses the remaining filename. 3. Check the artist and album lines. Missing values are simply omitted; Dosya does not manufacture **Unknown artist** or **Unknown album** labels. 4. Inspect the artwork area. Valid embedded cover art appears there; otherwise the fallback tile shows an audio glyph and the extension. 5. Read the chips below the identity. Extension and file size are always available, while bitrate and sample rate appear only when the parser extracted them. ### Why correct metadata can look missing Only bytes `0–262143` are requested by the web viewer. Large leading artwork can consume that range, and an ID3 frame or MP4 `moov` atom placed after it is unavailable. The parser’s separate 2 MiB artwork cap does not expand this 256 KiB web read. Unsupported containers also fall back silently. The player does not present a metadata parse error because playback may still work. To fix source tags, edit a local copy with a trusted tag editor and upload the corrected media as the intended file or version. That upload changes cloud content and may affect anyone using the current version; recheck title and artwork after processing the new bytes. ## Expected result The player shows every supported field found within the inspected head range and uses filename artwork fallbacks for the rest. Reading metadata creates no new cloud object and never modifies the audio file. ## Related guides - [Preview media files](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Troubleshoot missing audio metadata](/files/audio-troubleshoot-missing-metadata)

title: Use keyboard controls for audio playback
summary: Control browser audio with Space, K, J, L, M, and arrow shortcuts, including exact seek distances, queue movement, and focused-input exceptions.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-keys.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, and apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.test.tsx. Production keyboard behavior was not re-tested.
body: Dosya's browser audio viewer installs shortcuts while the player is open. It ignores keystrokes originating in text fields, selects, and content-editable controls so typing does not change playback. ### Shortcut reference - Space or K toggles play and pause. - J seeks back 15 seconds; L seeks forward 15 seconds. - Left Arrow and Right Arrow seek by 5 seconds. - Shift+Left Arrow selects the previous queue track; Shift+Right Arrow selects the next one. - M toggles mute. ## Steps 1. Open a playable audio file in the web viewer and select **Play** once so the browser has authorized media playback. 2. Move focus away from any text input, select box, or editable comment field. 3. Press Space or K and confirm the play/pause icon and elapsed time respond together. 4. Press J and L to test 15-second movement. Near either end, the target clamps between 0 and the known duration. 5. Test the bare arrow keys for 5-second adjustment. Dosya prevents those handled arrows from navigating the outer file viewer. 6. If **Up next** contains siblings, use Shift+Left and Shift+Right. The keyboard's Shift+Left action always requests the previous row; unlike the visible **Previous track** button, it does not first restart a track that is more than 3 seconds in. 7. Press M and verify the volume icon reflects muted or restored state. ### When a shortcut does nothing Meta, Control, or Alt modified keys are ignored. A command is also ignored while focus is inside an input, textarea, select, or editable element. Click the player background and retry. Previous and next queue actions stop at their list boundaries. If the player reports **This browser can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.**, shortcuts cannot make that browser decode the source. Downloading produces a local copy; it does not repair the cloud file. ## Expected result Elapsed time, playback state, mute state, or active queue row changes exactly once for each supported shortcut. The underlying file and queue order remain unchanged. ## Related guides - [Manage the audio play queue](/files/audio-queue) - [Seek through audio with the waveform](/files/audio-waveform-seek)

title: Troubleshoot missing audio lyrics
summary: Restore the Lyrics tab by checking MP3 ID3 frames, 256 KiB placement, encoding, and unsupported MP4/M4A behavior without editing files in Dosya.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-tags.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/use-lyrics.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/id3.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/mp4.ts, and packages/audio-player/src/lyrics/lrc.ts. Production tags were not tested.
body: The web player shows **Lyrics** only when its metadata parser finds nonempty lyric text. There is no manual Lyrics tab when no supported frame was read. ### Before you start - Use the browser player for this check. Client feature sets can differ. - Dosya reads only the first 256 KiB of the audio file for tags. - Lyrics are parsed from MP3 ID3 frames. The current MP4/M4A parser does not return lyrics, and the player does not look for a neighboring `.lrc` file. ## Steps 1. Open the affected MP3 in Dosya and check whether **Lyrics** appears beside **Up next** and other player sections. 2. Inspect a local copy with a trusted tag editor. Look for ID3 `USLT`/`ULT`, or a `TXXX`/`TXX` field whose description is `USLT`, `LYRICS`, or `UNSYNCEDLYRICS`. 3. Confirm that the frame and its text fit within the tag data reachable in the first 262,144 bytes. Large leading artwork can push later frames beyond Dosya's range. 4. Save a small test copy with UTF text and one supported lyrics frame. Upload it under a clearly different name before replacing any existing version. 5. Reopen that test file. If **Lyrics** appears, retag the source locally and upload the corrected bytes only after preserving any original you need. ### How timing text is interpreted Lines beginning with `[mm:ss]`, `[mm:ss.xx]`, or `[mm:ss:xx]` can become timed cues; one to three minute digits and exactly two second digits are accepted. If at least one timed cue parses, Dosya returns only parsed timed cues: untimed text, malformed timestamp lines, and metadata headers are omitted. When no timed cue parses anywhere, every nonempty raw line is shown as plain untimed text, including header-looking lines. Dosya has no in-app audio tag editor. Re-uploading a corrected file or version changes the cloud content and can affect shared recipients; deleting the original afterward is a separate action. ## Expected result A supported, reachable ID3 lyric frame makes the browser **Lyrics** section available. Unsupported or absent tag text continues to hide it while playback and filename fallback can still work. ## Related guides - [Show synchronized audio lyrics](/files/audio-lyrics) - [Review audio artwork and metadata](/files/audio-artwork-metadata)

title: Show synchronized or embedded lyrics
summary: Display embedded MP3 lyrics in Dosya, distinguish timed LRC cues from plain lines, and diagnose a missing Lyrics tab without altering the audio file.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-tags.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/use-lyrics.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/lyrics-panel.tsx and packages/audio-player/src/tags/id3.ts. Production audio tags were not changed and no production action was performed.
body: The web player reads the first 262,144 bytes of the stored audio through one range request. For MP3 files it can extract an ID3 USLT frame or a lyrics-labeled TXXX frame; Dosya does not search the folder for a separate LRC file. ## Before you start - Use an MP3 with embedded lyric metadata. The shared parser recognizes ID3 at the start of the file or by the MP3 extension; MP4 and M4A metadata parsing currently returns title, artist, album, duration, and artwork but no lyrics. - A lyric block must be inside the file's own tag header. A sibling file such as song.lrc is not loaded by the web viewer. - Opening lyrics is read-only. No lyric text is uploaded, edited, or sent to an external lookup service. ## Steps 1. Open the MP3 in **Files** and wait for the tag request to complete. The player still uses the filename when title metadata is absent. 2. Look beside **Up next** for **Lyrics**. The tab is rendered only when the parsed tag contains at least one non-empty lyric line. 3. Select **Lyrics**, then start playback. Timed content accepts leading cues in **[mm:ss]**, **[mm:ss.xx]**, or **[mm:ss:xxx]** form, including multiple leading timestamps for one line. 4. Confirm the current line becomes bold as playback crosses its cue. The panel centers that line smoothly, or jumps without animation when reduced motion is enabled. 5. For untimed text, verify that each non-empty source line appears in order. Untimed lines remain static because they all have no usable playback cue. 6. Switch tracks and recheck the tab. A Lyrics tab from the prior file is closed automatically when the new track carries none. ## When lyrics do not appear No tab means the first 256 KiB contained no supported non-empty lyrics, the tag request failed, or the container parser does not expose lyrics. Metadata headers such as **[ar:...]** and blank timestamped lines are discarded; timestamps embedded after ordinary lyric text are treated as text rather than cues. The panel has a **No lyrics in this file** state, but the player normally hides the Lyrics tab when parsing returns no lines. Playback and the queue continue without lyrics. Download the original and inspect its tags in a dedicated editor if you need to confirm or add metadata; any edit made outside Dosya must be uploaded as a new version to appear here. ## Expected result A supported embedded tag produces a Lyrics tab for that track. Timed lines follow playback, plain lines remain readable, and missing metadata does not interrupt audio or change the stored file. ## Related guides - [Media preview controls](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Read audio title and artist metadata
summary: Learn which audio tags Dosya reads on web, desktop and mobile, why filenames appear as fallbacks, and how to troubleshoot missing metadata safely.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-tags.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/parse.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/id3.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/mp4.ts, apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/extract.ts, and apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/metadataStore.ts on 2026-10-14; production playback was not exercised for this revision.
body: Dosya reads embedded audio tags in the client that opens the file. Reading metadata does not change the file, write corrected tags, or send tag values back to the file record. ## What Dosya can read On the web and desktop app, Dosya requests only the first 262,144 bytes (256 KiB) of the file. It recognizes MP3 ID3v2.2, ID3v2.3, and ID3v2.4 tags and MP4-family metadata in `.m4a`, `.mp4`, or `.m4b` files. MP3 parsing can supply title, artist, album, cover art, lyrics, duration, bitrate, and sample rate. MP4 parsing can supply title, artist, album, duration, and cover art. Embedded artwork above 2 MiB is ignored for both ID3-tagged MP3 and MP4-family files. The mobile app reads the locally cached copy instead of making a tag request. It accepts the MP4 family plus `.aac` and `.alac`, but skips tag parsing when the cached file is larger than 50 MiB. Mobile caches extracted data by file ID, size, and modification time, so a changed or reuploaded version is read again. Every client falls back to the filename without its extension when no embedded title is available. Web and desktop omit missing artist or album rows. Mobile can use the containing folder or source name as the fallback artist in the player queue. The mobile file preview shows cached artwork and tags only after the player has extracted them. ## Steps 1. Open **Files**, choose an audio file that your role can read, and unlock it first if it uses full-file locking. 2. Open the audio preview or player. Compare the displayed title, artist, and album with the tags in the source file rather than with its filename alone. 3. On web or desktop, inspect the chips below the title. Dosya can show the uppercase extension, file size, and any bitrate or sample rate found in the MP3 tag. 4. On mobile, play the cached file once if its preview still shows only the filename or generic audio artwork. Return to the preview after extraction completes. 5. If a field is absent, check the platform limit above. A large ID3 block, MP4 metadata stored after the first 256 KiB, artwork over 2 MiB, or a mobile file over 50 MiB can produce a valid filename fallback. ## Expected result The player shows supported embedded values when they are present and readable. Missing or unreadable tags fall back without changing the stored audio file. A decode failure is separate from missing metadata: web says `This browser can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.` and desktop says `This app can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.` ## Troubleshooting - **The filename appears instead of the title.** Confirm that the source really contains a supported title tag and that it sits within the platform's read limit. - **Artwork is absent but text tags appear.** Check the embedded image and keep it at or below 2 MiB for an ID3-tagged MP3 or an MP4-family file. - **Mobile still shows old metadata.** Confirm that the uploaded file's size or modification time changed; those values invalidate the mobile metadata cache. - **The file will not play.** Download it and use another app when the exact decode message above appears. Changing tags does not add codec support. ## Related guides - [Media preview controls](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Recover an audio queue on the wrong track
summary: Correct a mismatched web audio queue by checking loaded siblings, active-row bars, direct selection, and the distinct Previous button and shortcut rules.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, apps/web/src/components/audio/queue-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-keys.ts, and their focused tests. Production queue playback was not re-tested.
body: The web viewer builds **Up next** from audio siblings already loaded into its file-viewer list. It does not fetch unseen pages or search other folders to complete the queue. ### Before you start - Return to the folder and note its active listing, then reopen the intended file. - Expect the web queue to contain only audio items supplied to the viewer. A file elsewhere in the workspace will not be added automatically. - Queue operations control playback only; they do not move or duplicate cloud files. ## Steps 1. Open **Up next**. The current row replaces its index number with three bars; they animate while playing and remain static while paused. 2. Compare that row's filename stem and size with the large title. Embedded tags can make the displayed track title differ from its cloud filename. 3. Select the exact desired row. Direct row selection navigates the viewer to that file and resets the prior track's A-B loop. 4. Test **Next track**. Natural playback completion also advances sequentially, and the final row has no next target. 5. Test the visible **Previous track** button: after more than 3 seconds it restarts the current track at zero; at 3 seconds or less it goes to the preceding row. 6.
