If you use Shift+Left instead, remember that the keyboard shortcut always requests the previous row and does not apply the button's 3-second restart rule. ### If the expected row is missing Close the viewer, load the correct folder/listing page, and reopen the track so the viewer receives the intended siblings. The browser queue cannot add or remove individual rows and cannot reorder them by dragging. Its visible **Shuffle queue** and **Repeat queue** buttons currently have no click handlers, so they cannot repair order. For a decoding refusal, Dosya says **This browser can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.** That track can remain selected while producing no browser audio; use its filename and error state rather than sound alone to identify it. ## Expected result The bar-marked row, main player identity, and audible content refer to the same file. Subsequent skips follow the visible sibling order and no cloud object is edited. ## Related guides - [Manage the audio play queue](/files/audio-queue) - [Use audio keyboard controls](/files/audio-keyboard-controls)

title: Manage the audio play queue
summary: Use Dosya's web and mobile audio queues, understand their ordering and 500-track mobile cap, and recover when a track cannot be decoded or loaded.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, apps/web/src/components/audio/queue-panel.tsx, apps/mobile/src/player/queue.ts and apps/mobile/src/player/controller.ts. Production playback was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: The web viewer builds **Up next** from audio files already present in its loaded file list. Mobile can fetch the remaining pages in the same folder, filter, and sort order, but stops at 500 playable tracks. ## Before you start - Open an unrestricted audio file from the intended folder. Mobile excludes files whose lock mode is not **none** from its queue; locked audio can have a separate inline playback path after unlock. - Check the current Files sort and filter on mobile because the queue preserves that listing order while fetching later pages. - Web does not fetch unseen listing pages for **Up next**. A track absent from the current viewer file set will not appear merely because it exists elsewhere in the folder. ## Steps 1. Start an audio preview and locate **Up next**. The count is the number of audio siblings available to the current viewer. 2. Find the active row. Its numbered position changes to three bars; the bars pulse while playing and remain still while paused. 3. Select another row to navigate directly to that track. The player source, tags, waveform, loop state, and active index update for the selected file. 4. Use **Next track** to move one row forward. At natural track end, web also advances to the next row; the control is disabled on the last entry. 5. Use **Previous track**. When playback is more than 3 seconds into the current track, it restarts at 0; at 3 seconds or less, it selects the preceding row and is disabled at the queue start. 6. On mobile, **Shuffle** randomizes only the tracks after the one currently playing and can restore the original order. **Repeat** cycles off, queue, then track. A folder over 500 eligible tracks reports **Queue capped at 500 tracks.** ## Current web limits and recovery The web **Up next** list is read-only: selecting a row changes playback, but there is no drag-to-reorder or remove command. The visible **Shuffle queue** and **Repeat queue** buttons currently have no mutation handlers in the web player, so verify order through the rows and skip controls rather than assuming those two buttons changed it. If web reports **This browser can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.**, the queue stays intact but that track cannot play in the browser. Downloading creates a separate local copy. Queue operations themselves do not move, copy, rename, or delete cloud files, and the web queue is reconstructed rather than persisted as a playlist. ## Expected result The highlighted row matches the audible track, direct selection and skip controls follow the visible order, and mobile queues stop cleanly at 500 items. Cloud files remain in their original folders. ## Related guides - [Media preview controls](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Choose repeat and shuffle modes
summary: Understand that web Shuffle queue and Repeat queue are currently inactive, then use working sequential queue and A-B loop controls without assumptions.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-modes.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/queue-panel.tsx, and corresponding unit tests. Production playback controls were not re-tested.
body: The browser player renders **Shuffle queue** and **Repeat queue**, but the current controls have no click handlers and do not change playback. Web queue order remains sequential. ### What works today **Up next** selects a row directly, **Previous track** and **Next track** move through the list, and a track that reaches its end advances to the next sibling. The last track does not wrap to the first. A-B looping within one file is implemented separately from queue repeat. ## Steps 1. Open an audio file with at least two loaded audio siblings and expand **Up next**. 2. Record the row order. Select a middle row and confirm its three-bar active indicator. 3. Press **Shuffle queue**. Observe that no row order, active state, or mode status changes; do not treat the icon as confirmation of random playback. 4. Press **Repeat queue**. It likewise does not enable track or queue repetition in the web player. 5. To repeat a segment, use **A-B**: press once at the start point, again at the end, and a third time to clear. Dosya enforces a minimum 2-second region and moves the end to at least two seconds after A when necessary. 6. For ordinary listening, use direct row selection or the skip controls and expect sequential progression. ### Mode details Opening a different track clears the prior A-B boundaries because positions do not carry safely between files. A sleep timer, when set, is separate and can survive a track change. Playback speed cycles through 0.5×, 0.75×, 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 1.75×, and 2×; it does not alter queue sequence. Queue controls do not mutate uploaded objects. There is therefore no cloud-data recovery step after testing them. If your browser session appears to shuffle or repeat, compare the active row with the visible list and reload before reporting it, because the current source contains no web state transition for those icons. ## Expected result Web playback follows the listed sibling order, the inactive shuffle and repeat icons leave that order unchanged, and A-B repeats only the chosen section of the current track. ## Related guides - [Manage the audio play queue](/files/audio-queue) - [Fix a queue playing the wrong track](/files/audio-queue-wrong-track)

title: Correct lyrics that do not match playback
summary: Fix lyric highlighting by validating accepted timestamp syntax, sorted cues, current playback time, and untimed fallback behavior in the browser player.
verification: Verified locally against packages/audio-player/src/lyrics/lrc.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/use-lyrics.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/lyrics-panel.tsx, and their unit tests. Production lyric timing was not re-tested.
body: The web player highlights the last parsed lyric cue whose time is at or before the current playback position. It scrolls that cue toward the center, or jumps without smooth motion when reduced motion is enabled. ### Accepted timing syntax A timed line must begin with `[mm:ss]`, `[mm:ss.xx]`, or `[mm:ss:xx]`. Minutes use one to three digits and seconds use exactly two. Several timestamps may precede one lyric line; Dosya creates a cue for each and sorts all cues by time. Once any timed cue parses, lines without a valid leading timestamp and metadata headers are omitted from the displayed result. ## Steps 1. Open the MP3 in the browser and choose **Lyrics**. Start playback at a clearly identifiable line. 2. Compare the displayed elapsed time with the active lyric. Seeking to just before and just after the cue helps distinguish a bad timestamp from delayed audio encoding. 3. Inspect a local copy's embedded lyric frame. Check for missing brackets, one-digit seconds, unsupported hour fields, decimal commas, or timestamps placed after the text. 4. Verify that lyrics are in a supported ID3 `USLT`/`ULT` frame or approved `TXXX`/`TXX` description and reachable within the first 256 KiB. 5. Correct the timestamps locally and upload a separate test file. Reopen it and seek across several cue boundaries before replacing the original version. ### Untimed and offset results Plain fallback is all-or-nothing. If zero timed cues parse, every nonempty raw line displays at time zero without highlighting, including malformed or header-looking lines. If even one timed cue parses, only valid timed cues display; untimed lines do not remain beside them. The parser sorts out-of-order timed cues; it does not infer a global offset or compensate for silence encoded before the music. If all cues are consistently early or late, adjust their timestamps in the source lyrics. Dosya provides no in-app lyric editor. Uploading corrected media changes cloud bytes and may affect shares using the current file, so retain the original until the test is verified. ## Expected result With timed input, each valid cue becomes active as playback crosses its parsed time and non-cue lines are absent. With zero parsed cues, all nonempty lines remain readable without synchronization. Testing and seeking do not alter the stored audio. ## Related guides - [Show synchronized audio lyrics](/files/audio-lyrics) - [Troubleshoot missing lyrics](/files/audio-lyrics-troubleshoot)

title: Fix missing audio metadata
summary: Explain missing audio tags by checking supported MP3 and M4A fields, the 256 KiB head range, 2 MiB artwork cap, and safe local retagging steps.
verification: Verified locally against packages/audio-player/src/tags/parse.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/id3.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/mp4.ts, and apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-tags.ts. Production metadata parsing was not re-tested.
body: Missing title, artist, album, or cover art does not necessarily prevent playback. The browser parser fails softly and uses the cloud filename as the title fallback. ### Fields Dosya reads MP3 ID3v2.2–v2.4 can supply title, artist, album, artwork, lyrics, bitrate, and sample rate. MP4/M4A parsing supplies title, artist, album, duration, and artwork. The current M4A path does not expose lyrics, bitrate, or sample rate. Other containers may play through the browser while providing no supported tags. ## Steps 1. Open the file in the web viewer and compare the large title with its cloud filename. A filename without its extension indicates the fallback is active. 2. Note which optional artist, album, bitrate, sample-rate, or artwork elements are absent rather than assuming all metadata failed. 3. Inspect the downloaded original with a trusted tag utility. Confirm the expected values exist in a supported ID3 or MP4 metadata atom. 4. Check placement and size. The web viewer requests bytes `0–262143`, so an artwork frame must fit inside that head read along with its tag headers; later MP4 atoms or ID3 frames are unseen. The shared parser additionally rejects artwork payloads over 2 MiB when another caller provides more bytes. 5. Retag a copy with modest artwork and early metadata, then upload it under a temporary name and reopen it in Dosya. ### Safe recovery There is no metadata editing action in the Dosya web player. Replacing or versioning the cloud audio with locally changed bytes is the only repair path, and that can alter what collaborators or share recipients receive. Keep the original until the corrected test displays and plays as expected. Range-request or parse failure produces no dedicated tag error in the player. If a known-good tagged MP3 also falls back to its filename, refresh access and network state before changing source files. ## Expected result Supported tags within the inspected head appear, while missing or unsupported fields use a filename or artwork fallback without blocking audio. Diagnosis alone is read-only. ## Related guides - [Review audio artwork and metadata](/files/audio-artwork-metadata) - [Preview media files](/files/media-preview-controls)

title: Troubleshoot audio that will not start
summary: Diagnose browser audio that will not start by separating autoplay, access, transfer, decode, queue, and source-file problems with exact recovery checks.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, apps/web/src/components/audio/use-audio-keys.ts, apps/mobile/src/player/controller.ts, and focused player tests. Production playback and network delivery were not re-tested.
body: A browser can refuse audio before playback permission, while fetching bytes, or while decoding the media. Dosya exposes a specific decode message but does not classify every rejected browser `play()` promise. ### Before you start - Lower device volume and use a non-sensitive test track. - Confirm you can open the file and every ancestor folder in the intended workspace. - Keep a small known-good MP3 available in the same location for comparison. ## Steps 1. Open the affected audio in the web viewer and press the visible **Play** control once. Browsers can require a direct user gesture before sound starts. 2. Verify that elapsed time changes and that **Mute** is off with volume above zero. Press M once only if the icon indicates muted state. 3. Read the stage for **This browser can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.** That message means the browser rejected the supplied media format or bytes. 4. Open the known-good MP3 through the same account and folder. If it plays, download the affected source and inspect it locally; if both fail, retry the browser session and network path. 5. If **Up next** highlights a different row, select the intended track directly. Filename, embedded title, and audible content can disagree when tags were copied from another file. 6. Compare in a supported mobile client when useful, remembering that platform decoders and queue construction differ. ### Recovery and file effects For a decode refusal, use **Download** and play the local copy in a compatible application or transcode a separate copy to a browser-supported format. Uploading a replacement changes cloud content; preserve the original until verification is complete. Testing player controls never repairs or rewrites media. If a download also fails, investigate file access or delivery rather than codec metadata. The web error surface has no dedicated timeout string for every network failure, so a known-good file and refreshed session provide the clean comparison. ## Expected result The failure is narrowed to user playback authorization, mute/volume, wrong queue row, access or transfer, browser decoding, or source bytes. Any successful repair is verified against a separate test copy first. ## Related guides - [Preview media files](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Fix an audio queue playing the wrong track](/files/audio-queue-wrong-track)

title: Handle unavailable audio seeking
summary: Recover audio seeking when waveform analysis is unavailable by using the plain seek range and checking the 80 MiB analysis and duration requirements.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/use-peaks.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/waveform.tsx, apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, and packages/audio-player/src/peaks/extract.ts. Production seeking was not re-tested.
body: Waveform generation and media seeking are separate. When peak analysis is unavailable, Dosya renders a plain **Seek** slider as long as the audio player can establish useful duration. ### Why the waveform can disappear The browser downloads the complete raw file for peak analysis only when its stored size is at most 80 MiB. It decodes at 8 kHz, reduces the result to 900 peaks, and caches peaks by file ID and version. An oversized file, raw fetch failure, or decode failure selects the fallback range instead. ## Steps 1. Open the file and wait for media metadata. Check whether you see the canvas waveform or a plain slider labelled **Seek**. 2. If the plain range appears, drag its thumb after duration is displayed. Bare Left Arrow or Right Arrow also moves playback by 5 seconds when the player handles the key. 3. Confirm elapsed time changes. Seeking clamps to zero and the known duration, so a stream reporting duration `0` cannot move to a later position. 4. Test a small known-good audio file. A waveform there confirms that analysis is available and the original likely exceeded 80 MiB or failed decoding. 5. If the player shows **This browser can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.**, use a compatible local player or upload a separately transcoded test copy. ### What retrying changes Peak extraction runs in the browser and has no server processing queue to wait for. Reopening the same version can recover a transient fetch failure, while a cached successful peak set should return for that file/version. Uploading different bytes creates a distinct analysis target. The fallback slider can exist even without waveform peaks. If it remains at zero, check browser support and source duration rather than repeatedly waiting for a nonexistent background job. Playback controls and analysis do not edit cloud bytes. ## Expected result Either the waveform rendered from a 900-value peak array or the plain **Seek** control moves playback to a valid time. A documented size or decode constraint explains cases where visualization or seeking remains unavailable. ## Related guides - [Seek through audio with the waveform](/files/audio-waveform-seek) - [Troubleshoot audio playback](/files/audio-troubleshoot-no-playback)

title: Seek through audio with the waveform
summary: Seek precisely on the browser waveform by clicking, dragging, using five-second keys, reading hover time, and understanding 80 MiB analysis fallback.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/audio/waveform.tsx, apps/web/src/components/audio/use-peaks.ts, apps/web/src/components/audio/audio-player.tsx, and packages/audio-player/src/peaks/extract.ts. Production waveform interaction was not re-tested.
body: The web waveform maps horizontal position to the current track duration. Analysis produces 900 peak values, then the canvas resamples them to the number of bars that fit its current width. Timed comment buttons sit in a separate row above the canvas. ### Before you start - Wait until the browser knows the media duration. - Waveform analysis fetches the full raw file only when stored size is 80 MiB or less. - Lower volume before jumping into an unknown section. ## Steps 1. Open a supported audio file and find the waveform beneath the player identity. 2. Move the pointer across it. The floating time label previews the position represented by that horizontal point. 3. Click once at a controlled location and compare the new playhead with the elapsed `mm:ss` value. 4. Press and drag across the waveform for continuous positioning, then release at the desired moment. 5. Focus the waveform and use Left Arrow or Right Arrow to change the target by 5 seconds. Values are clamped between zero and the track duration. 6. If a timed comment button is present above the waveform, select it to seek to its saved millisecond and open that comment. ### Rendering and fallback Peak extraction decodes at 8 kHz and reduces the result to 900 values. At render time, the canvas takes the maximum within each resampled bucket to fit its viewport-dependent bar count. Successful data is cached under file ID and version. The waveform grows in over 620 ms; with reduced motion, it appears immediately. For files above 80 MiB or when fetch/decode fails, Dosya shows the ordinary **Seek** range. That fallback can still move playback once duration is known. It does not mean the audio is waiting on a server waveform job because analysis is entirely local to the browser. Changing the playhead, selecting comments, and caching peaks do not create a new version or alter bytes. A later uploaded version gets its own cache key. ## Expected result The playhead and elapsed time jump to the clicked, dragged, keyed, or comment-marked position. If peaks are unavailable, the fallback range provides the supported seek path. ## Related guides - [Preview media files](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Handle unavailable audio seeking](/files/audio-troubleshoot-seek-unavailable)

title: Rotate an automation API key
summary: Replace an automation credential without downtime, test the new secret, and revoke the old key so every later request uses the intended access.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.ts. Production behavior for “Rotate an automation API key” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Rotate an API key by overlapping the old and new credentials only long enough to test the replacement. Dosya keys cannot be edited, and the full `dos_…` secret is shown only once, so save it directly into the automation’s encrypted credential field. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings → API keys**, expand the key used by the automation, and record its **Permission**, **Protocols**, **Reach**, expiry, IP allowlist, and active hours. 2. Choose **Duplicate settings**; keep the prefilled restrictions unless the automation now needs less access, give the replacement a distinct name, and create it. 3. Copy the newly issued key from the **is ready** dialog before closing it; Dosya cannot reveal that secret again. 4. Replace the credential in Zapier, n8n, or the calling system, then run one read or upload that matches the key scope and confirm the run succeeds. 5. Return to the key list and compare **Last used**; confirm the replacement handled the test rather than a cached result. 6. Expand the old row, choose **Revoke**, approve the irreversible deletion, and run the same automation once more to prove only the new key works. A revoked key is refused immediately after its cache entry is cleared; the interface confirms **Key revoked** and says anything still using it will be refused. A free account may hold 3 keys and every account has a hard maximum of 20, so revoke an unused key first if creation reports a cap. Revoking a `wp_site` key also disconnects that WordPress site; rotate those credentials through the site connection flow instead. ## Expected result The replacement row has the intended restrictions, the production automation succeeds with its newly stored secret, and requests that still present the retired key receive an authentication refusal. Keep the new secret in the automation’s credential store, not in a task note or run log. ## Related guides - [Connect Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Connect n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect)

title: Add several files to a group
summary: Add several files to one Dosya group through repeated single-item actions, with exact duplicate, access, confinement, and no-batch limits explained.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/mobile/src/groups/AddToGroupSheet.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/groups/[id].ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/groups/index.ts. Production group updates were not re-tested.
body: Dosya currently has no bulk **Add to group** command. The web and mobile flows submit one `file_id` or one `folder_id` per request, so several files must be assigned individually. ### Before you start - Create the destination group in the same workspace. Group names can contain at most 100 characters. - You must belong to the workspace, see the target, and own the user-scoped group. Folder-confined membership limits targets to the assigned subtree. - Adding an item is organizational metadata; it does not move, copy, rename, share, or delete that cloud object. ## Steps 1. In web **Files**, open the first item's context menu and choose **Add to group**. Do not select several rows expecting a batch group action. 2. In the **Add to group** dialog, check the line **Select a group for name**, then choose the intended group. 3. Wait for **Added to group** and the detail **The file was added to group-name.** 4. Repeat those actions for every additional reviewed file. Keep a checklist because each request succeeds or fails independently. 5. Open the group from the sidebar and compare its members with the checklist. Refresh before retrying an uncertain result. 6. On mobile, open the one item's sheet, use **Add name to group**, and choose an existing group or **New group…**; the target is still singular. ### Errors and partial results If no group exists, web says **No groups** and **No groups yet. Create one in the sidebar.** A list failure uses **Something went wrong** and **Could not load your groups.** Assignment failure says **The file could not be added to the group.** The API returns `File already in this group` with 409 for a duplicate, although web can surface a generic toast. Because every file is a separate request, an interruption can leave a partially completed set. Existing successes remain; verify the group and resume only with missing items. Removing a membership later changes the group list, not the stored file. ## Expected result The chosen group contains each file added through its own successful request, without duplicate memberships. All source items remain in their original folders with unchanged bytes and permissions. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Select multiple files](/files/select-multiple-files)

title: Delete multiple items together
summary: Delete many Dosya files and folders safely, understand chunk limits, locked-item refusals and partial results, then verify each item in Deleted.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/bulk-run.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/batch-delete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/backup-lock.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: A normal batch delete is recoverable: it moves selected files and complete folder subtrees into **Deleted**. The bytes continue counting against workspace storage until a later permanent deletion. ## Before you start - `delete_any_file` permits deletion regardless of creator. `delete_own_files` applies only to items owned by the signed-in user and to subtrees whose contents pass the same ownership check. - A locked selected file, or a live file below a locked ancestor, refuses the whole API chunk. Hidden rows are omitted from processing. - A live WordPress backup lock is a separate preflight guard. If any selected file or folder touches the protected tree, the API returns HTTP 423 with `error: backup_locked` and refuses the entire mixed request before writing either half. After that guard passes, a folder that fails ownership, its own or an ancestor lock, or subtree authorization is skipped while eligible folders continue. - A folder selection includes every live child folder and file in its authorized snapshot. The confirmation names the selected roots rather than every descendant. - The API accepts at most 500 file IDs per request. Web divides the overall selection into sequential chunks of 20 combined file and folder IDs so progress can advance. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, select the rows to remove. Selecting a Live Photo still automatically includes its paired video in the delete request; the confirmation states how many extra videos are included. 2. Choose **Delete** in the selection bar. 3. Read **Delete selected items?** and verify its separate file and folder counts. If folders are included, read the notice that everything inside them is deleted too. 4. Press **Delete**. Soft-delete progress cannot be cancelled after it begins; wait for all chunks to settle. 5. Read **Deleted** for complete success or **Some items could not be deleted** with the chunk-level deleted and failed counts. 6. Open **Deleted** and confirm each intended file or folder root. A folder’s descendants stay attached to that trash root and are restored with it rather than shown as independent roots. ## Expected result Successful rows leave the live listing and remain recoverable. File and folder share links are revoked during trashing. Storage usage does not fall, and deleted data has no automatic expiry job. A later **Delete permanently** action removes bytes and cannot be undone. ## Troubleshooting - **“This file is locked and cannot be deleted.”** One visible file in that chunk has `view_only` or `full_lock`. Remove it from the selection or have the owner change the lock. - **“This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to delete it.”** Unlock the ancestor, then select the remaining rows again. - **The response is HTTP 423 with `error: backup_locked`.** At least one requested file or folder touches a live protected WordPress backup. Nothing in that mixed request was deleted; wait until its returned `locked_until` time before selecting the batch again. - **A folder stayed live although the request completed.** Batch folder deletion is best effort. It skips a root when the role lacks rights to any required descendant, the tree is locked, or the folder is hidden. Delete that folder separately to receive its specific refusal. - **The success count looks larger than Deleted.** Web counts a successful 20-item request as the chunk size, while the endpoint can omit hidden, missing, already-deleted, or unauthorized rows. Verify actual trash roots and retry only visible survivors. - **You need storage immediately.** Open **Deleted**, select the confirmed trash items, and choose **Delete permanently**. That separate action is irreversible and large folders can require several bounded purge passes. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Move several files together
summary: Move a mixed file and folder selection in Dosya, understand partial results and Live Photo pairs, and recover from permission or destination conflicts.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/bulk-run.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/move.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Moving a selection changes each item’s parent inside one workspace. Dosya does not copy file bytes during a move, but a mixed selection is processed item by item, so one refusal does not roll back items that already moved. ## Before you start - Open **Files** in the intended workspace. The destination picker stays within that workspace; this workflow cannot move items between workspaces. - File moves require the role permission `upload_files`. Folder moves require `rename_folders`. The **Move** button appears when either permission exists, so a mixed selection can include rows your role cannot move. - Unlock the selected file, its ancestor folders, and the destination when required. A locked WordPress backup cannot be moved into, out of, or within. - Check the destination for same-name files and folders. Dosya does not merge or overwrite on a move. ## Steps 1. Select the checkboxes beside the files and folders. Use **Select all** only after checking the current folder, filters, and page. 2. Read the selection count in the bulk bar, then choose **Move**. 3. In **Move to folder**, open the intended destination or leave the picker at the workspace root. The picker omits a single folder being moved, but a descendant can still be browsed; the server rejects that cycle. 4. Choose **Move**. The web client keeps up to six item requests in flight. A selected Live Photo still also moves its paired video, although the twin is not added to the displayed selection count. 5. Read the completion toast. Web reports **Moved** when every selected row succeeds, or **Move finished** with “N moved, M skipped” after partial completion. Those counts omit the extra Live Photo video request, so **Moved** can still appear when that paired-video move failed. 6. Open both source and destination. Confirm each expected item appears once, verify that every selected Live Photo still and its paired video arrived together, and check that any skipped row remains at the source. ## Expected result Each successful file keeps its ID, bytes, versions, and storage usage while its folder reference changes. A successful folder carries its complete subtree to the new parent. Existing links address the same IDs, and sync or WebDAV listings refresh for the old and new locations. ## Troubleshooting - **“File is already in this folder” or “Folder is already here.”** Pick a different destination. That item stays where it was. - **A same-name item blocks the move.** Files return **A file with this name already exists in the target folder**; folders return **A folder with this name already exists in the target folder**. Rename one item before retrying. - **A folder is skipped.** Do not choose the folder itself or any folder below it. The exact cycle errors are **Cannot move a folder into itself** and **Cannot move a folder into its own subfolder**. - **Only part of the selection moved.** Permissions, confinement, hidden state, locks, or destination conflicts are evaluated for each item. Correct the skipped rows, select those remaining at the source, and run a second move. - **A Live Photo split across two folders despite “Moved.”** The web result ignores the added paired-video request. Locate the still and video, move the remaining half to the intended destination, and verify the pair there. - **Desktop says items moved after individual error toasts.** Desktop currently catches per-item failures while continuing the batch. Treat the refreshed source and destination as authoritative. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Apply a promotion or coupon
summary: Validate a Promo code against the selected billing interval and available seats, then verify its duration, Discount row and final total before purchase.
verification: Reviewed from apps/web/src/components/billing/plan-chooser.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/coupon/validate.ts, apps/api/src/lib/billing/promo-interval.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/billing/promo-seats.ts. No real code was redeemed and no production or Stripe lookup occurred.
body: A promotion code is validated against the active **Monthly** or **Annual** cart before payment or subscription update. A valid result shows **Code [CODE] applied**, adds a **Discount** row, and recalculates **Total**. Validation alone does not charge the account or consume the code. Codes can be limited by billing interval, expiration, activation status, total redemption seats, discount duration, currency, or eligible products. The server validates again when checkout or an existing subscription update is submitted; do not rely on a manually calculated discount. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing**, then choose **Choose a plan** or **Change plan**. 2. Select **Monthly** or **Annual** first. Interval-restricted codes are evaluated against this choice. 3. Choose the plan and add-ons so the cart represents the purchase you intend to make. 4. Enter the code in **Promo code** and select **Apply**. 5. Read the success copy. A one-use discount says **discounts your first payment only**; a repeating promotion states how many months it applies. 6. Confirm a green **Discount** line appears and that **Total** shows the expected `/mo` or `/yr` period. 7. For an existing subscription, also review **Estimated next invoice (incl. proration)**. Promotion savings and proration are separate parts of the calculation. 8. Continue only after the checkout or update summary still displays the intended plan, interval, storage, and discounted amount. ## Errors and limits - **Enter a promo code** means the submitted field was empty after trimming. - **That promo code is invalid or expired** covers an unknown or unavailable code. - **This code is for yearly billing only.** or its monthly equivalent means the cart uses the wrong period. - **This code cannot be used with this billing period.** means its configured interval list does not allow the selection. - **This code has no seats left.** means the campaign's Stripe and recorded manual redemptions reached its cap. - **Too many promo code attempts. Try again in [n] minutes.** is an account lockout after repeated unknown-code guesses. An IP limiter also allows at most 30 lookup attempts per minute. Switching from Annual to Monthly, or the reverse, automatically removes a code restricted to the other period and explains why. Apply a different eligible code or restore the supported interval. ## Expected result The code remains attached to the chosen interval, its duration is clear, and the Discount and Total rows agree before any payment or subscription update. ## Related guides - [Review invoices and payments](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Choose or change a plan](/account/choose-plan)

title: Distinguish a receipt from an invoice
summary: Use Dosya’s checkout receipt for payment confirmation and the Stripe invoice PDF for tax-ready billing details, dates, status and totals before filing.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/checkout-success.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts on 2026-10-14. Production Stripe records were not opened.
body: Dosya presents two related records after Stripe checkout. The **Order receipt · Stripe** panel confirms the completed transaction; the linked Stripe invoice is the durable billing document. ## Steps 1. On the purchase-success page, inspect **Order receipt · Stripe**. It may show Invoice, Date, Plan, Amount, Card, Email, and Storage. 2. Confirm the status says **Payment received**. **Payment processing** means Stripe has not yet marked the checkout paid; capacity appears after settlement. 3. Select **View invoice** when an invoice URL is available. Use that hosted/PDF document when accounting needs the invoice number, supplier/customer identity, tax details, currency, line items, and formal payment status. 4. For an older transaction, open **Billing → Invoices**, match the period and amount, then use the icon titled **Download PDF**. The success-page receipt is a convenient on-screen summary and can omit a row Stripe did not return. The Billing list excludes draft and void invoices, includes up to 12 Stripe invoices, and may prepend an **upcoming** estimate without a PDF. ## Expected result You retain the invoice PDF for bookkeeping and use the receipt panel to verify the checkout that led to it. Downloading either document does not change the subscription or storage entitlement. If receipt details say they could not be loaded, open Billing and use the invoice list or **Open Stripe portal**. An upcoming estimate is not proof of payment; wait for a paid invoice covering the completed period. ## Related guides - [Find invoices and payment details](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Locate an invoice period](/account/billing-locate-invoice-period)

title: Download a payment receipt
summary: Download the Stripe invoice PDF for a completed payment, then match its billing period, amount and status to the corresponding Dosya row before filing it.
verification: Reviewed and reconciled locally with apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/checkout-success.tsx. No invoice was fetched from Stripe or a production account.
body: The **Invoices** card fetches the latest **12** Stripe invoices for the signed-in account, then omits draft and void records. Each remaining row shows its billing-period start and end dates, amount, status, and a PDF download icon when Stripe supplied an invoice PDF URL. An **upcoming** row is a forecast and has no PDF link. Use a completed row, normally one marked **paid**, when you need a payment document. The downloaded file is the provider's invoice PDF; Dosya does not generate or rewrite its contents. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing** for the account that made the payment. 2. Scroll to **Invoices** and find the row whose period and amount match the charge. 3. Check the status. Do not use the **upcoming** row as proof of payment. 4. On a row with a PDF URL, select the download icon whose tooltip is **Download PDF**. The document opens in a new browser tab or follows the browser's PDF-download preference. 5. Save the PDF in an approved location if it contains billing details. 6. Compare the PDF with the Dosya row: billing-period dates, charged amount, currency shown in the document, invoice status, and billed customer details should correspond to the intended payment. ## If the PDF icon is missing Dosya shows an empty icon space when Stripe supplies no `invoice_pdf` URL. This is expected for the synthetic **upcoming** estimate. A draft or void invoice is omitted from the list entirely. Select **Open Stripe portal** in the **Invoices** header to review the provider's invoice history. The portal is also the supported fallback when the completed payment exists but its PDF link is absent from the Dosya row. The checkout success page can show the amount paid, currency, invoice number, payment time, billing email, and card brand with last four digits when Stripe returns them. Those values are confirmation details; the durable downloadable document remains the invoice PDF or hosted invoice available through Stripe. ## Troubleshooting If Billing says **Failed to load billing information.**, reload after confirming the signed-in email. Invoice retrieval is bounded by a 10-second provider request; a temporary provider failure can leave the list empty without altering the subscription. If the wrong customer or amount appears, stop and return to Dosya instead of editing provider data. Recheck which Dosya account is signed in, because Billing does not switch with the active workspace. ## Expected result You have the PDF for the intended completed payment and its period, amount, status, currency, and customer details agree with the billing record. ## Related guides - [Review invoices and payments](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Choose or change a plan](/account/choose-plan)

title: Compare monthly and annual billing
summary: Compare Monthly and Annual carts by exact total, plan availability, add-ons, promotion rules and the existing subscription's proration preview.
verification: Reviewed apps/web/src/components/billing/plan-chooser.tsx, apps/web/src/components/billing/plan-selector.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/billing/cart-math.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/billing/cart.ts. The comparison used repository data only and sent nothing to production or Stripe.
body: The **Monthly** and **Annual** buttons control the entire plan-change cart: the base plan, storage add-ons, promotion eligibility, and total. Annual plans display a general **save ~17%** hint when annual prices exist, but the exact cart total is the figure to compare. A plan or add-on may be sold on only one interval. Switching periods can remove unavailable add-ons, invalidate an interval-restricted promo code, or make the selected plan unavailable. Review every message before submitting. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing** and select **Choose a plan** or **Change plan**. 2. Select **Monthly** and choose the plan you are considering. 3. Record the line-item prices, **Discount** if present, **Total …/mo**, **New storage**, and for an existing subscription **Estimated next invoice (incl. proration)**. 4. Select **Annual** without changing the plan. Record **Total …/yr** and the same supporting rows. 5. Check every add-on row. If an add-on is unavailable, the chooser says it **isn't sold on annual billing** or **isn't sold on monthly billing** and excludes it. 6. Reapply or re-evaluate a promo code if the chooser removes it when the interval changes. 7. For an existing subscriber, compare the proration estimate with the recurring interval total. The estimate describes the next invoice adjustment; it is not the recurring annual or monthly price. 8. Submit only after the chosen interval, storage total, and final cart match your decision. ## How to compare fairly Annual prices are charged per year and monthly prices per month. To compare like with like, divide the annual total by 12 for an average monthly cost, or multiply the monthly total by 12 for a one-year projection. Taxes and provider-calculated adjustments can change the amount ultimately charged, so treat the cart and checkout summary as authoritative. Choosing a smaller base plan replaces the current plan even if add-ons keep total storage high. Dosya requires the checkbox **Yes, move me to [plan]** for a base-plan downgrade. Add-ons and redeemed packages stay unless the chooser explicitly reports that an add-on is unavailable at the new interval. ## Troubleshooting If a plan says it **isn't available on annual billing** or monthly billing, switch back or choose a different plan. If changing the interval removes a code, the message identifies the code and restricted period. A server response of **Invalid billing interval** means the submitted period was neither month nor year. ## Expected result You can explain the exact recurring total, storage entitlement, included add-ons, promotion status, and immediate proration for the interval you selected. ## Related guides - [Review invoices and payments](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Choose or change a plan](/account/choose-plan)

title: Locate an invoice for a billing period
summary: Match a Dosya charge to its Stripe billing period, amount and status, then securely download the correct PDF from the 12-entry invoice history.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts on 2026-10-14, including the 12-invoice, status-filter, PDF, upcoming-invoice, and 10-second timeout paths. Production Stripe records were not opened.
body: The **Invoices** card on Billing lists Stripe periods as start date **to** end date, followed by amount, status, and a PDF action when Stripe supplies one. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing** for the account that owns the subscription. Workspace roles do not grant access to another person’s billing account. 2. Write down the charge date, amount, currency, and card statement reference you are reconciling. 3. In **Invoices**, compare the displayed period and amount. The API fetches at most 12 invoices and removes draft and void records. 4. Do not select the row marked **upcoming** for a past charge. It is an estimate, has no PDF, and can change before Stripe finalizes it. 5. Open **Download PDF** on the matching finalized row and verify the invoice number and paid/open status inside Stripe’s document. The list amount is Stripe’s `amount_paid`, falling back to `amount_due`; it is not reconstructed from today’s catalog price. That matters for discounts, legacy prices, taxes, credits, and prorations. ## Expected result The saved PDF covers the intended start/end period and agrees with the relevant account charge. Opening or downloading it is read-only. If the period is older than the visible 12 records, select **Open Stripe portal** and use Stripe’s longer customer history. **No invoices yet** means the API returned no eligible entries; verify the signed-in account before contacting billing support. ## Related guides - [Review invoice identity](/account/billing-review-invoice-identity) - [Reconcile an invoice with a plan](/account/billing-reconcile-invoice-plan)

title: Understand a pending downgrade
summary: Interpret the Cancelling billing state, confirm the paid-period end date and 14-day storage grace period, and know when Free limits apply on the account.
verification: Reviewed with apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/components/billing/cancel-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/cancel.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts. No Stripe session, production subscription, or external request was created.
body: On the Dosya Billing page, the pending downgrade state is a subscription scheduled to end at its current paid-period boundary. The page labels the subscription **Cancelling** and shows **Ends [date]**. Your plan and all subscription add-ons remain active through that date; this is not an immediate plan reduction. After the paid period ends, Dosya keeps the old storage limit for a **14-day grace period**. When that grace ends, the Free plan's **5 GB** limit applies. Files are not automatically deleted. If total use is above the available limit, new uploads are blocked until storage is reduced or paid capacity is restored. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing** while signed into the account that owns the subscription. Billing is account-level; changing the active workspace does not select another billing customer. 2. Find the amber state panel. Confirm it says **Ends [date]** and that the subscription badge says **Cancelling**. 3. Read the current storage figure under the end date and compare it with **Storage ledger → Total limit** and the amount in use. 4. Note the paid-period end date. Until then, the current plan, add-ons, and storage entitlement remain active. 5. Add 14 days to that boundary for the storage grace window. Use the displayed date as the authoritative start because billing intervals and renewal dates differ by account. 6. If you want to keep the subscription, select **Resume subscription** before the end date. The Billing page should return to **Active** and show a renewal date. 7. If you intend to continue to Free, reduce usage toward 5 GB and empty Trash where necessary before the grace period expires. ## What remains and what changes Scheduling cancellation covers the plan, subscription add-ons, and any custom package carried on the same subscription. It does not delete stored files. Redeemed external packages and other entitlement sources are reported separately in the storage ledger and may continue according to their own status. The page can show **Next invoice** only when an upcoming invoice exists and cancellation is not scheduled. Its absence during **Cancelling** is expected. ## Troubleshooting If **Resume subscription** fails, the page shows the returned billing error. Refresh Billing before retrying so the local state agrees with the provider record. If the account says **No subscription**, there is no period-end cancellation to resume. If usage exceeds the later limit, downloading files alone does not free cloud storage. Delete unneeded cloud items and empty Trash, or restore paid storage before attempting new uploads. ## Expected result You can identify the last paid-plan date, the following 14-day storage grace period, the future 5 GB allowance, and whether resuming is still available. ## Related guides - [Review invoices and payments](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Choose or change a plan](/account/choose-plan)

title: Open the billing management portal
summary: Open the Stripe customer portal from Dosya to manage the saved payment method or provider invoice history, then return to Billing without changing plans.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/api/billing.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/portal.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/stripe.ts. No portal session or production Stripe customer was opened during verification.
body: Dosya opens Stripe's customer portal for the billing customer attached to the signed-in account. Use it for the saved payment method and provider invoice history. Plan switching and subscription cancellation are handled on Dosya's own **Billing** page so its storage, add-on, and downgrade checks can run. Two Dosya controls create the same type of portal session: **Manage payment method** in the Subscription card and **Open Stripe portal** in the Invoices header. A portal session is temporary and returns to `/billing` when you leave it. ## Steps 1. Sign into the Dosya account whose subscription you intend to manage and open **Billing**. Workspace switching does not change the billing customer. 2. Review the Subscription card's plan, status, renewal or end date, and card brand with last four digits when available. 3. For a payment-method task, select **Manage payment method**. For provider invoice history, select **Open Stripe portal** above **Invoices**. 4. Wait while the button reads **Opening…**. Dosya requests a customer-portal URL and redirects the browser to it. 5. In Stripe, confirm the customer or billing email and subscription context before changing payment details or downloading a document. 6. Complete the provider action, then use its return control to go back to Dosya Billing. 7. Reload Billing and verify the saved card summary or invoice list. Provider changes can take a short time to appear in Dosya's mirrored status. ## Access and scope Portal access requires an authenticated account session and an existing Stripe customer ID. API keys are file-access credentials and cannot create billing portal sessions. Workspace roles do not grant access to another user's billing customer. If the account has never subscribed, the server returns **No billing account found. Subscribe to a plan first.** Use **Choose a plan** to start a subscription instead. The portal URL is a bearer credential. Do not paste it into support messages, screenshots, or shared documents. Open a new portal session from Billing if an old link has expired. ## Troubleshooting If the Dosya page reports a portal error, stay on Billing and retry after a refresh. **Failed to create portal session** means no usable provider URL was returned. If Stripe shows the wrong customer, close the portal without making changes, sign out of the unintended Dosya account, and start again from the correct one. For plan changes, add-ons, or cancellation, return to Dosya. Those actions need **Change plan**, **Add storage**, or **Cancel subscription** rather than the payment-method workflow. ## Expected result The portal opens for the correct Dosya billing customer, the intended payment or invoice action completes, and the browser returns to the Billing page. ## Related guides - [Review invoices and payments](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Choose or change a plan](/account/choose-plan)

title: Reconcile an invoice with the active plan
summary: Compare the charged subscription item, billing interval, storage ledger and prorations with the invoice that covers the same billing period.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/checkout-success.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts on 2026-10-14. Production Stripe records were not opened.
body: Reconcile an invoice against the subscription state that generated it, because the current public catalog may differ from a legacy, promotional, or prorated charge. ## Steps 1. Open Billing and record the **Subscription** price, `/mo` or `/yr` interval, plan name, renewal date, and masked card. 2. Under **Storage ledger**, record the base-plan row and every add-on, active redeemed package, and **Referral bonus**. The bold **Total limit** is the effective account ceiling. 3. Choose the invoice whose displayed period contains the charge. Download its PDF and compare line descriptions, quantity, discounts, tax, credits, and final total. 4. For a plan change, check the checkout receipt’s **Next invoice** and **Invoice date** rows. Existing-subscription changes use Stripe prorations and may land on the next invoice instead of producing an immediate checkout charge. 5. Treat the plan item’s mirrored Stripe unit amount as authoritative when it differs from the catalog’s current list price. Owned-workspace usage is summed across the account. Add-ons, active license grants, and referral credit stack on the base plan, so an invoice line alone does not describe every byte in **Total limit**. ## Expected result Each billed line has a matching subscription item, proration, tax, or discount explanation, and the Billing ledger accounts for the resulting storage allowance. If the ledger and total briefly disagree, reload after a few seconds; the interface explicitly treats **Total limit** as authoritative. Preserve the invoice number and checkout reference before reporting an unexplained difference. ## Related guides - [Locate an invoice period](/account/billing-locate-invoice-period) - [Verify a plan change](/account/verify-plan-change)

title: Review billing identity on an invoice
summary: Check the Stripe invoice customer, billing address, tax fields, currency and invoice number before saving it for accounting or reimbursement.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/checkout-success.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/portal.ts on 2026-10-14. Production invoices were not opened.
body: Review billing identity in Stripe’s invoice, because Dosya’s Billing list shows the period, amount and status but does not render customer-address or tax fields. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing → Invoices** and download the PDF for the correct period, or follow **View invoice** from a completed checkout. 2. Check the invoice number, issue/payment date, currency, customer name, email, billing address, and any tax identifier shown by Stripe. 3. Match the plan or add-on description and quantity to the Dosya **Storage ledger**. Confirm the invoice amount against the row in Billing. 4. Verify the masked card only as a supporting clue; Dosya displays brand and last four digits when Stripe returns a default card. 5. If identity fields are wrong, record the invoice number and contact billing support before the next invoice. Dosya exposes payment-method and invoice access, but no billing-identity editor in this flow. Changing portal details does not rewrite an already finalized invoice automatically. Keep the original and corrected record required by your accounting process, and ask billing support about a historical correction. ## Expected result The invoice identifies the intended customer and transaction and can be filed with a clear match to the Dosya subscription period. Reviewing it makes no account changes. If no PDF icon appears, the row may be **upcoming** or Stripe supplied no `invoice_pdf`. Open the portal for the hosted invoice, or wait until the estimate finalizes. ## Related guides - [Distinguish receipts and invoices](/account/billing-distinguish-receipt-invoice) - [Update a payment method](/account/billing-update-payment-method)

title: Troubleshoot a failed payment or unexpected bill
summary: Reconcile the subscription, storage ledger, next invoice and payment state before retrying checkout or reporting an unexpected private charge.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/api/billing.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/portal.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/checkout.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/sync.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts, apps/api/src/lib/billing/cart.ts, apps/api/src/lib/billing/sync-items.ts. Production behavior for “Troubleshoot a failed payment or unexpected bill” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Billing separates the subscription state, storage entitlement, upcoming invoice, and completed invoices. Reconcile those receipts before retrying a checkout or reporting a charge. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing**. If the page shows **Failed to load billing information.**, reload once and record the time rather than inferring that the subscription disappeared. 2. Read **Subscription**, its status, interval, cancellation date, and **Total limit**. **Over the limit** means uploads are paused across every workspace; it does not mean files were deleted. 3. Reconcile **Storage ledger** lines for the base plan, subscription add-ons or custom storage, active external-license packages, and **Referral bonus**. A line can lag the latest change by a few seconds. 4. Compare **Next invoice** with the **Invoices** list. Invoice history includes at most 12 non-draft, non-void invoices; missing upcoming data alone does not prove there is no charge. 5. For card attention, select **Manage payment method** and wait through **Opening…**. A past-due subscription must be repaired there; starting another checkout is refused to avoid a second subscription attempt. 6. If records still disagree, contact private support with invoice ID, amount, date, displayed status, expected change, and card brand/last four only. Do not provide a full card number or private portal URL. ## Expected result The problem is narrowed to a page-load failure, entitlement lag, upcoming invoice, completed invoice, unpaid subscription, or provider-portal error, with a safe receipt for resolution. A current subscription checkout returns **You already have an active subscription. Use 'Update subscription' to change it.** A past-due one returns **Your subscription has an unpaid invoice. Fix the payment via 'Manage billing' instead of starting a new subscription.** The older `?success` checkout return performs a sync and another check after about 2.5 seconds. That timing is not a guarantee that every provider update settles within 2.5 seconds. ## Related guides - [Find invoices and payment details](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Upgrade or add storage](/account/upgrade-storage) - [Cancel or downgrade](/account/cancel-or-downgrade) - [Contact private support](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Update a payment method in the billing portal
summary: Open the protected Stripe portal from Dosya Billing, replace the subscription payment method, and verify the masked card safely after returning.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/api/billing.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/portal.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts on 2026-10-14. Production Stripe portal behavior was not exercised.
body: Payment details are managed in Stripe’s customer portal. Dosya creates the portal session only for a signed-in account that already has a Stripe customer record. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing** and verify the subscription plan, renewal date, and displayed card brand/last four digits. 2. Select **Manage payment method**. The button changes to **Opening…** while Dosya requests a short-lived portal URL. 3. In Stripe, add or replace the payment method and make it the subscription default when prompted. Follow Stripe’s authentication step if the bank requires it. 4. Return to Dosya Billing using the portal’s return action, then reload and check the masked card line. The same portal opens from **Open Stripe portal** above Invoices. Dosya configures self-service plan switching and cancellation through its own guarded flows; use **Change plan** or **Cancel subscription** in Billing for those actions. ## Expected result Stripe stores the replacement method and Dosya subsequently shows its brand and final four digits. Card numbers are not exposed in the Dosya UI. **No billing account found. Subscribe to a plan first.** means the account has no Stripe customer to manage. **Failed to create portal session** means no usable portal URL was returned; reload Billing before retrying. A missing card line can also mean Stripe did not return a default card even though the subscription exists. ## Related guides - [Find invoices and payment details](/account/invoices-and-payment) - [Review invoice identity](/account/billing-review-invoice-identity)

title: Browse a deep folder tree
summary: Navigate deep Files breadcrumbs and destination-picker trees, including lazy expansion, 250 ms search, 50-result cap, role scope, and confirmation.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/folder-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/folder-tree.tsx, and apps/web/src/lib/folders.ts. Production navigation was not re-tested.
body: Dosya exposes folders in two related interfaces: the main **Files** view opens one location at a time with breadcrumbs, while move and save dialogs show a lazily loaded destination tree. ### Before you start - Confirm the active workspace. **Root** means the highest location your current role can access; folder-confined members do not escape their assigned anchor. - Locked, hidden, or otherwise inaccessible branches may be absent or refused. - Opening and selecting folders is read-only until an action such as **Move here** or **Save here** is confirmed. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, open a folder row. The content pane changes to that folder, and the breadcrumb adds its name. 2. Continue through each segment. Use the breadcrumb to move back to a known ancestor and verify the visible pane belongs to the expected path. 3. When a move or save operation opens a picker, expand **Root** or a visible folder. Children load one level on demand rather than downloading the entire workspace tree. 4. For a long hierarchy, type into **Search folders...**. Search waits 250 ms after input and returns at most 50 server matches with ancestor context. 5. Select the exact destination row. If creation is allowed, use **New folder in “name”** or **New folder at root**; success reports **Folder created** and **“name” is ready to use.** 6. Press the operation's confirmation button only after checking the highlighted folder and breadcrumb. Closing the dialog before confirmation leaves files unchanged. ### Empty and error states An unloaded empty branch says **No folders yet**. Search can say **No folders match “query”**. A failed creation reports **Folder creation failed**. If a role or lock changed while the picker was open, refresh the workspace and rebuild the path instead of assuming the stale row is writable. Picker selection does not change the main Files location. Likewise, browsing the main pane does not commit a pending move or archive save. ## Expected result The Files breadcrumb identifies the open content location, while any picker highlights the intended accessible destination. No object changes location until its separate confirmation succeeds. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files or folders](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Cancel a scheduled account deletion
summary: Cancel during the 30-day recovery window, preserve the account and stored files, and understand why a previously canceled subscription stays canceled.
verification: Verified in apps/web/src/pages/profile/delete.tsx, apps/web/src/components/deletion-banner.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/delete-cancel.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/account/preview.ts. No production account, email, or billing-provider action was performed.
body: Confirming account deletion schedules it **30 days** later; it does not erase files immediately. After signing in again, Dosya shows a persistent banner with the exact deletion date and days remaining. Cancellation must be explicit: signing in to download a last file does not silently call off the deletion. Use **Cancel deletion** before the scheduled date. The cancel action clears the deletion timestamps and attempt counter, invalidates any unconsumed deletion code, and keeps the account, eligible workspaces, and files in place. ## Steps 1. Sign in to the scheduled account. Scheduling revoked every previous browser session, mobile token, and linked extension credential, so a fresh login is expected. 2. Read the banner: **Your account is scheduled for deletion on [date] — [n] days left.** Select its **Cancel deletion** link. 3. On **Profile → Delete account**, confirm the page says **Deletion scheduled** and shows the same date. It also states **Nothing has been deleted yet.** 4. Select **Cancel deletion**. No email code or password confirmation is required to stop destruction. 5. Wait for **Deletion cancelled — Your account will not be deleted.** 6. Confirm the scheduled section clears. The global banner should disappear after the account state refreshes; reload once if it remains temporarily. 7. Open an expected workspace and a known file to verify continued access. ## What cancellation preserves The deletion preview counts files, including trashed files, in workspaces that would be destroyed with the account. Files the user uploaded into somebody else's workspace are not part of that destructive count and survive under a tombstone identity. Canceling before the sweep leaves the account and its still-existing data as they are. Scheduling account deletion also attempts to cancel the Stripe subscription immediately so the user is not charged during the recovery window. **Cancel deletion does not resume that subscription.** After recovering the account, open Billing and check whether a new subscription or other paid capacity is needed. At the due date, an hourly sweeper can begin permanent purge. After the account and sole-owned workspace data have been removed, support cannot use this cancel action to reconstruct them. Treat the displayed scheduled date as the deadline rather than waiting for the final hour. ## Troubleshooting **No deletion is scheduled for this account.** means the server no longer has a pending timestamp. Refresh the profile and confirm the signed-in email; the deletion may already have been canceled or completed. If the button reports another error while the banner remains, retry from a normal signed-in browser session. API keys cannot cancel account deletion. Record the exact scheduled date and error text when contacting support, without including passwords, deletion codes, or session cookies. ## Expected result The deletion banner and scheduled date disappear, the account and remaining cloud files stay accessible, and Billing accurately shows whether paid service must be started again. ## Related guides - [Update profile settings](/account/profile-settings) - [Review sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Cancel or downgrade without losing track of files
summary: Schedule cancellation or confirm a smaller plan, understand proration and storage effects, and recover safely before uploads become paused again.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/components/billing/cancel-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/billing/plan-chooser.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/cancel.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/subscription.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/cron.ts on 2026-10-14. Production billing was not changed.
body: Cancellation and a lower plan are different operations. **Cancel subscription** schedules every subscription item to end; **Change plan** immediately submits a new item set with Stripe prorations. ## Steps 1. In Billing, compare owned-workspace usage with **Total limit** and the destination plan’s capacity. 2. To stop renewal, select **Cancel subscription**, read **Cancel subscription?**, then confirm. **Keep subscription** closes the dialog without changing billing. 3. The plan and every add-on remain active through the displayed end date. After that, the old limit continues for a 14-day grace period before Free’s 5 GB applies. 4. To choose a smaller paid tier instead, select **Change plan**. Dosya requires a second confirmation stating exactly which current plan/capacity is replaced by which new plan/capacity. 5. After either action, reload Billing. Cancellation shows **Cancelling**, **Ends [date]**, and **Resume subscription**; a plan change opens the success page and receipt. Files are never automatically deleted because of cancellation or over-quota status. Once usage exceeds the effective limit, uploads pause across every owned workspace until space is freed or capacity is restored. ## Expected result The subscription either carries a reversible period-end cancellation or reflects the confirmed smaller plan. Existing files remain readable subject to their normal permissions. Use **Resume subscription** before the end date to undo cancellation. If a lower plan was chosen accidentally, open **Change plan** again and select the intended tier; the correction can create another Stripe proration. ## Related guides - [Prepare an over-quota account](/account/plan-prepare-over-quota) - [Review a pending downgrade](/account/plan-review-pending-downgrade)

title: Canceling an upload safely
summary: Stop the intended queued or active upload, check the other transfers, and confirm whether a complete file already exists in Files.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/uploads/upload-dock.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/web/src/stores/uploads.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-persistence.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId].ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/stale-multiparts.ts, and focused cancel, persistence, and stale-multipart tests. Screenshots use fictional transfers. Production cleanup timing was not measured.
body: Cancel an individual **Queued** or **Uploading** row from the upload list at the bottom right. The X has the tooltip **Cancel**; right-clicking the row offers **Cancel upload**. Both apply immediately without a confirmation dialog, so verify the filename first. Canceling one attempt does not remove a file that already reached **Done**, and it does not cancel the other rows. Check **Files** after cancellation to determine what is actually stored. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace and intended destination. - Read the exact filename, size and state. Similar names can represent an older completed copy and a new attempt. - Keep the source file if you might upload it later. Cancel discards the browser's handle to that source, and the row cannot use **Resume** afterward. - Let any file that you still need continue. Cancel is scoped to the selected row, so choose carefully. ## Steps: cancel the intended upload 1. Expand the upload list at the bottom right of the web app. 2. Find the exact row. An active item shows progress and has an X control; a queued item can also be canceled before it starts. 3. Select the row's X labeled **Cancel**, or right-click that row and choose **Cancel upload**. 4. Expect the action to apply immediately. The current web UI does not ask for confirmation. 5. Confirm that the selected row changes to **Canceled**. Check that unrelated active, queued and Done rows keep their own states. ## Steps: check the result 1. Confirm **Canceled** on the intended row. If it still shows Uploading, make sure you used the control for that row. 2. Review the other transfers. A completed row should remain **Done**, and another active or queued file should continue under its own state. 3. Open **Files** and inspect the intended destination. Cancellation stops browser requests, but a file that finished just before the action can already be recorded as complete. 4. If a file with the same name already exists, compare its size, modified time, version information or contents. It can be an older completed copy rather than the attempt you just canceled. 5. If you still need the canceled file and no verified completed copy exists, start a new upload from the unchanged original. ## Steps: clear the queue only after checking Files 1. Record any error or state information you still need. 2. Verify completed files through **View file**, **Go to location** or Files. 3. Use **Clear done** on the Upload page, or **Clear** in the dock, only to tidy terminal rows. These controls remove complete, error and canceled entries while leaving queued, uploading and interrupted work visible. 4. Delete an unwanted completed file from **Files** through the normal file action. Clearing its upload row does not delete the stored object. ## Expected result The chosen active or queued attempt changes to **Canceled**, while unrelated transfers retain their states. Files contains only the copies that completed independently. If the canceled file is still required, a new attempt starts from the original after you have checked for an existing completed copy. ## Limits and cleanup behavior - **Cancel** aborts every active byte-transfer request for the selected file, including concurrent multipart parts. Other queue rows have separate request sets and keep running. - A file that already shows **Done** is complete and cannot be undone through the transfer's Cancel action. Delete it from Files if removal is intended. - Do not use the presence or absence of a queue row as a storage inventory. Verify Files, versions and trash where relevant. - Incomplete multipart parts are not a completed cloud file and are cleaned separately. A session whose first part never arrived becomes stale after **10 minutes**. Once a multipart upload has begun, it becomes eligible for the application sweep after no part has landed for **24 hours**; the bucket's **7-day** lifecycle remains the cleanup backstop. These timings do not promise an immediate dashboard decrease. - Clearing queue history only changes the local display. It does not cancel an active transfer, delete a completed file or prove partial data has been reclaimed. - Cancel is irreversible for that queue attempt. If you still need the content, create a new upload after confirming that no complete copy or unintended new version already exists. ## Troubleshooting **I canceled the wrong file.** Preserve the original and check Files immediately. If the selected attempt did not complete, add that original again. Do not restart unrelated Done rows. **The file still appears in Files.** It may have completed before cancellation, or it may be an older copy with the same name. Compare size, time, version information and contents. If you intend to remove a verified completed file, use its Files action. **Available storage did not change immediately.** Completed parts and usage counters can settle through separate cleanup paths. Check Files and Deleted first, refresh after current transfers stop, and contact support with the cancellation time and approximate size if the displayed quota remains unexplained after the stated idle window. **Canceled disappeared after I selected Clear.** Clear removes transfer history from the display. Check Files for the actual result. If no completed copy exists and the file is needed, begin a new upload. **There is no Cancel action.** A **Done** item is complete. An **Error**, **Interrupted**, or **Canceled** row is not transferring; use its available **Retry**, **Resume**, or **Remove** control instead. **Another upload stopped too.** Inspect its own state and message. A connection loss or page close can interrupt multiple rows even though Cancel itself targets one transfer. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I cancel one upload without stopping the others? Yes.
