title: Clear filters that hide files
summary: Clear search text, sidebar filters, group views, and map date or folder filters so the intended Dosya file list becomes visible again on web.
verification: Verified from local sources apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/files-params.ts, apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, and apps/web/src/components/map-filter-panel.tsx on 2026-10-14; production filter state was not changed.
body: The web Files page has independent query, folder, sidebar-filter, and group state. It does not have one clear-all button, so remove the state that is hiding the item while preserving any scope you still need. ## Steps 1. Check the breadcrumb first. If the wrong folder is open, choose the required breadcrumb or **Home**. Folder navigation preserves the current search text and type filter, so continue through the remaining checks. 2. Clear the **Search files...** field. The page waits 300 milliseconds before applying the empty query and automatically returns pagination to page 1. 3. In the sidebar, select **All** to leave **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared**, **Deleted**, or **Hidden**, and to close an active group view. **All** keeps your current folder and any text query. Entering or leaving **Deleted** instead returns to that view's root because trashed folder IDs have a separate meaning. 4. Confirm the URL no longer contains an unwanted q, filter, or group value. A folder is represented separately, so keep or clear it according to the intended scope. 5. Do not reset layout, tile size, columns, or sort unless you want to change presentation; those are view preferences rather than filters. 6. If the hidden item was on **Map**, use its **Clear** button. Map **Clear** removes the selected folder, **From**, and **To**, but leaves **Show approximate locations** unchanged. ## Expected result The Files list returns to the chosen folder without an active query, group, or sidebar filter. Query, filter, and folder transitions reset pagination, so the first result page is shown. Clearing controls is read-only and does not restore deleted files, unlock protected files, or reveal items outside the member's assigned folder tree. ## Troubleshooting - **Files remain missing after selecting All.** Empty **Search files...**, verify the breadcrumb, and check whether the item is deleted, hidden, or fully locked. - **Folders remain while a search is active.** This is expected. The filename query filters direct file rows; folder rows are loaded independently. - **The result says No files match your search.** Clear or change the filename query. If loading failed instead, use **Try again** under **Could not load this folder**. - **A map pin remains hidden after Clear.** Turn on **Show approximate locations** if the item has only an upload-origin coordinate. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Organize files](/files/organize-files)

title: Clear a multi-file selection
summary: Clear every selected file and folder from the Files bulk bar, understand automatic selection resets, and avoid carrying stale items into an action.
verification: Source reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/hooks/use-files-listing.ts, apps/web/src/lib/files-request.ts, and apps/web/src/lib/library-request.ts. The selection workflow was not exercised on the production Files page.
body: The browser Files page keeps selected file IDs and folder IDs in client memory. **Clear** drops both sets without calling the API, so no stored object or server job changes. ## Before you start - Use the browser Files page; the described bulk bar is a web control. - Check the badge, such as **3 selected**, before clearing so you can verify the complete reset. - If a confirmation dialog for Delete or another operation is already open, cancel that dialog first. Clearing selection does not reverse a request that has already started. ## Steps 1. Find the highlighted rows or cards. Folders and files contribute to the same selected count. 2. In the bulk action bar, select **Clear** beside **Select all**. 3. Wait for the bar's 140 ms collapse animation, or its immediate reduced-motion equivalent. 4. Confirm the selected badge disappears and every checkbox, ring, or highlighted row returns to its ordinary state. 5. Start the next selection from zero. Changing the workspace, folder, filter, group, search text, sort, regular-list page, library kind, or library sort also clears selection automatically. A background data refresh does not wipe an in-progress set merely because rows changed. ## Expected result The current selection count becomes zero, the bulk bar is inert and collapsed, and no batch endpoint receives a request. Files, folders, favourites, groups, versions, and storage totals remain untouched. There is no undo record because clearing is only a local UI reset. Re-select the required items if you cleared by mistake. ## Troubleshooting **Clear is not visible.** The bulk bar appears only after at least one checkbox or modifier-click selection. If no item is highlighted, there is nothing left to clear. **The old count flashes while the bar closes.** The component intentionally retains its final count during the 140 ms collapse so the label does not briefly read zero. It cannot be clicked once selection is empty. **A batch action continued.** Clear does not cancel a move, delete, restore, or archive job already submitted. Read that operation's result toast and refresh the affected folder. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Authenticate the Dosya CLI safely
summary: Sign in interactively, through stdin, or with DOSYA_API_KEY; verify the account, understand credential precedence, and revoke stored access safely.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified login forms, key validation, credential precedence, config storage, file permissions, account output, logout and server-side revocation in apps/cli/src/commands/auth.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/whoami.ts; apps/cli/src/config.ts; apps/cli/src/output.ts; apps/cli/tests/integration/auth.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/integration/whoami.test.ts; and apps/cli/README.md. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: The Dosya CLI authenticates with a `dos_` API key. Use the hidden interactive prompt on a personal terminal, pipe the key through standard input for a setup script, or provide `DOSYA_API_KEY` to an automation environment. Avoid putting a reusable secret directly after `--key`, where shell history and the process list can expose it. ## Create a key for this CLI installation Open [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api), select **New API key**, and label it for this machine or automation job. Choose the smallest permission that supports the intended commands: - **Read only** can list and download but cannot upload, move, or delete. - **Upload only** can add files but cannot list or download stored files. - **Full access** supports commands that read and modify content, subject to workspace role permissions. Under **Protocols**, include **REST API** because the CLI calls REST endpoints. Add a workspace pin, IP ranges, active hours, usage limits, or expiry when those restrictions fit the job. Save the one-time full token; the key table shows only a prefix afterward. ## Steps Run the interactive command and paste the key when the hidden prompt appears: ```bash dosya auth login dosya whoami ``` Successful login prints `Authenticated as NAME (EMAIL)`. `dosya whoami` then prints the account name, email, user ID, and workspace count; `dosya whoami --json` emits the account object for a script. The CLI stores the token and API base in `~/.dosya/config.json`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dosya/config.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. The directory is created with mode `0700` and the file with `0600` on Unix-like systems. The key is plain text inside that protected file. If restored permissions allow group or other users to read it, the CLI warns with a corrective `chmod 600` command. ## Authenticate a setup script without argv exposure Pipe the key through stdin: ```bash printf '%s\n' "$MY_KEY" | dosya auth login --key - dosya whoami --json ``` An empty pipe fails with `No API key on stdin.` A non-interactive run without `--key -` or `DOSYA_API_KEY` fails with `Cannot prompt for API key in non-interactive mode.` A value that does not begin with `dos_` is rejected before the network request. For CI or a short-lived container, inject the key as an environment secret and skip writing it to disk: ```bash export DOSYA_API_KEY="$MY_KEY" dosya whoami --json ``` Credential precedence is `--key`, then `DOSYA_API_KEY`, then the stored config. API endpoint precedence is `DOSYA_API_BASE`, then the config file, then `https://api.dosya.dev`. Know which source wins before diagnosing a surprising account or environment. ## Fix common authentication failures | CLI output | What to do | | --- | --- | | `Authentication failed: invalid API key.` | Copy the complete one-time token or create a replacement if the original value is no longer available. | | `Not authenticated. Run: dosya auth login` | Supply `DOSYA_API_KEY` or complete a stored login. | | `Authentication failed. Run 'dosya auth login' to re-authenticate.` | The server returned 401; check expiry or revocation and replace the credential. | | `Permission denied. You don't have access to this resource (403).` | The key remains live, but its scope, protocol, source conditions, workspace pin, or current role refused the operation. | | A key works locally but fails in CI | Compare the injected key, `DOSYA_API_BASE`, source IP allowlist, active-hours timezone, and selected workspace membership. | Exit code **3** means authentication failure, **5** means a live credential was forbidden, **4** means a network failure, and **2** means invalid CLI usage. Automation should not respond to exit 5 by repeatedly logging in again. ## Log out or revoke the key `dosya auth logout` removes the local config file only. The API key continues working elsewhere until it expires or is revoked: ```bash dosya auth logout ``` To destroy the stored key on the server and then clear the local file, run: ```bash dosya auth logout --revoke ``` Server-side revocation is irreversible and immediately breaks every process using that key. If revocation fails, the CLI keeps the local credential so the command can be retried. A 401 means the stored key is already invalid, so the CLI safely clears it. An environment-only `DOSYA_API_KEY` is not managed by logout; revoke that credential from **Profile → API keys**. ## Expected result `dosya whoami` identifies the intended account without printing the key. The credential source and endpoint are known, the stored file is owner-readable only when used, and the key can be independently revoked when this CLI installation is retired. ## Related guides - [Install the Dosya CLI](/developers/cli-install) - [Select the default CLI workspace](/developers/cli-workspace) - [Choose API-key permission](/developers/api-key-scopes)

title: Download a folder with the Dosya CLI
summary: Resolve a remote folder, download its tree into an empty local directory, review partial failures, and compare the resulting names and sizes safely.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified recursive command syntax, folder resolution, snapshots, relative-path containment, 500-file manifest chunks, temporary files, output and failure behavior in apps/cli/src/commands/download.ts; apps/cli/src/resolver.ts; apps/cli/src/sync/remote.ts; apps/cli/src/sync/safe-path.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/sync/download-manifest.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/sync-safe-path.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/sync-safe-path-symlink.test.ts; and apps/cli/README.md. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Use `dosya download --recursive` to copy every visible file under one Dosya folder into a local directory while preserving its relative tree. Start with an empty destination: recursive mode writes each returned path without asking for per-file overwrite confirmation. ## Prepare the source and destination The credential needs read access to the workspace, and the workspace role must permit file access and downloads. Folder confinement, hidden content, and locks can narrow what the snapshot returns. List the parent first and copy the folder ID or confirm its exact path: ```bash DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID='ws_REPLACE_ME' dosya ls --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" ``` Create a new local destination and ensure it is empty: ```bash DEST='./dosya-folder-check' mkdir -p "$DEST" find "$DEST" -mindepth 1 -print -quit ``` If the last command prints anything, choose another directory. The recursive downloader does not apply the single-file command's interactive overwrite prompt, `--force` check, segmented resume sidecar, or ETag integrity verifier. ## Steps Use a workspace-relative path: ```bash dosya download --recursive reports/2026 \ --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" \ --output "$DEST" ``` You can instead use a folder ID or embed the workspace in the reference: ```bash dosya download -r fld_REPLACE_ME -w "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" -o "$DEST" dosya download -r "${DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID}:reports/2026" -o "$DEST" ``` The `ws_ID:path` form overrides `--workspace`; `--workspace` overrides the saved default. A path that cannot be resolved reports `No such folder: …` or `No such file or folder: …`. Supplying a file to recursive mode fails because the resolver explicitly expects a folder. The command takes one remote snapshot, builds paths below the chosen folder, and requests temporary download URLs in groups of at most **500 file IDs**. Each object is first written to a `.dosya-partial` path and renamed only after that response completes. Server-provided paths that escape the destination, including traversal or unsafe symlink paths, are refused. An empty remote folder prints `No files to download.` and exits successfully. Folders themselves are represented by downloaded file paths, so an empty nested subfolder may not produce a local directory. ## Read the completion result Interactive output ends with `Downloaded N file(s) to DEST/`. If one file fails, the command prints a line such as `Failed: relative/path: HTTP STATUS`, continues with remaining files, summarizes completed downloads, and exits nonzero. For automation, request structured output: ```bash dosya download --recursive reports/2026 \ --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" \ --output "$DEST" \ --json > recursive-download-result.json python3 -m json.tool recursive-download-result.json ``` The JSON has `ok`, `downloaded`, and `failures`. Treat `ok: false` or any failure item as an incomplete local copy. Because completed files remain in the destination, decide whether to retry into a new empty directory or deliberately reconcile the partial tree. Do not assume a second run is an atomic replacement. ## Compare remote and local content Record the local tree and sizes without modifying it: ```bash find "$DEST" -type f -print0 \ | sort -z \ | xargs -0 -n1 sh -c 'wc -c < "$1" | tr -d "\n"; printf " %s\n" "$1"' sh ``` Compare the count, relative names, and byte sizes with the Dosya folder. For high-assurance backup verification, download critical files individually with `dosya download FILE -o NEW_PATH`, which performs the CLI's supported ETag content check, or compute and compare an application-level checksum you already trust. Recursive mode confirms HTTP completion and the reported failures; it does not hash every saved file. ## Recover from common failures **`Folder required.`** Place the remote folder after `--recursive`, for example `dosya download -r reports -o ./backup`. **`No workspace for "…".`** Add `ws_ID:` to the path, pass `--workspace`, or set a default workspace. **Some paths are missing but no HTTP error appears.** Check whether the key or member is folder-confined, whether content is hidden, and whether the current role has download access. **A local file already existed.** Recursive mode is designed for a prepared destination and does not ask before each path. Restore the prior local copy from its backup if it was replaced, then repeat into an empty directory. **A run stopped midway.** Review the failure array or stderr, preserve it for diagnosis, and use a new destination for a clean verification run. The single-file `.dosya-download` resume behavior does not apply to folder recursion. ## Expected result The command exits successfully with zero failures, and the destination contains the same visible file paths and byte sizes as the selected remote subtree. The pre-existing local directory remained empty until this controlled download began. ## Related guides - [Upload and download individual files](/developers/cli-transfer) - [Verify the CLI workspace](/developers/cli-workspace) - [Download a folder from the web app](/uploading/download-folder-archive)

title: Handle Dosya CLI exit codes
summary: Branch scripts on Dosya CLI exit codes, preserve stderr, and distinguish usage, authentication, network, permission, and maintenance failures.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/cli/src/index.ts, apps/cli/src/output.ts, apps/cli/src/errors.ts, apps/cli/src/client.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/rm.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/mv.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/download.ts, and apps/cli/src/commands/sync.ts. Production commands were not executed.
body: Dosya CLI uses stable process statuses for automation: 0 success, 1 generic failure, 2 usage, 3 authentication, 4 network, 5 forbidden, and 75 maintenance. Signal exits remain 130 for SIGINT and 143 for SIGTERM. ## Before you start - Capture stdout, stderr, and `$?` separately. Routine text and JSON use stdout; diagnostics, warnings, debug output, and progress use stderr. - Decide which classes the job may retry. Authentication and permission failures need correction, not a tight retry. - A 503 response with code `surface_disabled` maps directly to maintenance exit 75. ## Steps 1. Run the command without piping stdout directly into another process; first preserve both streams and the original exit status. 2. Treat 0 as command success. When a batch command was invoked with `--json`, one or more failed members normally produce command-specific JSON and exit 1; parse that receipt to retain successful counts and failure details. 3. Map 2 to invalid command syntax or arguments, 3 to a missing or rejected credential, and 5 to an authenticated caller lacking permission. 4. Map 4 to transport or connectivity failure. Apply bounded retry only when the command itself is safe to repeat. 5. Map 75 to temporary maintenance, including `surface_disabled`. Reschedule after an operator-approved delay rather than treating it as a permanent configuration error. 6. Record stderr and the numeric status. Preserve 130 and 143 as cancellations so a scheduler does not mislabel an interrupted job as application failure. ## Expected result Automation branches on the original numeric status, retains human-readable diagnostics from stderr, and never parses an error message to guess whether failure was usage, auth, network, forbidden, or maintenance. ## Troubleshooting **A pipeline reports the parser’s status.** Save the Dosya process status before invoking `jq`, or enable shell pipeline-status handling deliberately. **Exit 1 has little detail.** Inspect stderr; it is the generic class for failures that do not map to a narrower status. **A retry could mutate data twice.** Verify remote state first. An exit code identifies the failure class, not whether the server committed before the connection ended. ## Related guides - [Authenticate the Dosya CLI](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Use CLI JSON output](/developers/cli-json-output)

title: Install the Dosya CLI
summary: Install Dosya CLI on macOS, Linux or Windows, verify the executable, authenticate securely, and understand upgrades and removal.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14: src/pages/developer/cli.astro; apps/cli/package.json; .github/workflows/cli-release.yml; apps/api/src/pages/api/cli/install.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/cli/latest.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/cli/latest.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/middleware.ts; apps/cli/src/index.ts; apps/cli/src/config.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/auth.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/workspace.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/upgrade.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/upgrade-policy.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/uninstall.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/upgrade-host-guard.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/upgrade-manifest-guard.test.ts; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx. Removed unrelated Zapier image. Regenerated existing CLI-install light/dark illustration because its former first step named a nonexistent Integrations CLI control; no production installation or authentication performed. Local repository review; commands checked without production credentials.
body: Install the Dosya CLI from the official download service, then run `dosya --version` and `dosya --help` before connecting your account. The release is a standalone executable; an installed binary does not require Node.js, npm or Bun. ## Supported platforms and prerequisites | Computer | Release selector | Installation | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux x86-64 | `linux` | Shell installer or downloaded binary | | macOS Apple Silicon | `mac-arm64` | Shell installer or downloaded binary | | macOS Intel | `mac-x64` | Shell installer or downloaded binary | | Windows x64 | `windows` | Download `dosya.exe` with PowerShell | The installer and updater reject other OS/architecture combinations; Linux ARM64 and Windows ARM64 builds are not provided by this release configuration. You need an HTTPS connection and permission to write the installation directory. Installing or reading help does not require a Dosya account; file operations require an API key and the relevant workspace permissions. This illustration summarizes the install sequence. The commands below come from the current installer and CLI reference; it is not a terminal recording of a completed installation. ## Steps: install on macOS or Linux Run this in your ordinary terminal: ```sh curl -fsSL https://api.dosya.dev/api/cli/install | sh ``` The script detects the platform, downloads the matching binary into `/tmp/dosya`, makes it executable and moves it to `/usr/local/bin/dosya`. If `/usr/local/bin` is not writable, it asks `sudo` to perform that move. On macOS it also attempts to remove the downloaded binary's quarantine attribute. The final installer output includes **dosya CLI installed successfully!** and runs the version command. If you prefer to inspect the script before executing it, download it to a file first: ```sh curl -fsSL https://api.dosya.dev/api/cli/install -o dosya-install.sh less dosya-install.sh sh dosya-install.sh ``` Review it before the last command. Installation replaces any executable already stored at `/usr/local/bin/dosya`; retain a trusted older binary separately if you need a local rollback. The installer does not keep a backup or provide a version-selection flag. For a manual download, use `https://api.dosya.dev/api/cli/latest?platform=linux`, replacing `linux` with the selector in the table. Rename the downloaded file to `dosya`, make it executable on Unix, and place it in a directory already on your PATH. The public [CLI page](https://dosya.dev/developer/cli) is the installation reference, rather than an in-app **Integrations → CLI** control. ## Install on Windows In PowerShell, download the x64 executable and move it into the documented user PATH folder: ```powershell curl.exe -fsSL -o dosya.exe "https://api.dosya.dev/api/cli/latest?platform=windows" Move-Item dosya.exe "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\WindowsApps\" dosya --version dosya --help ``` Use `curl.exe`, which calls the executable instead of PowerShell's `curl` alias. This user directory avoids an administrator installation. Check that it is on your PATH if `dosya` is not found. If `Move-Item` reports an existing destination, identify the current binary and retain a copy before deliberately replacing it; do not silently overwrite an unknown executable. ## Confirm which executable runs ```sh dosya --version dosya --help dosya upload --help ``` The version output begins with `dosya` followed by the installed release number. Help lists commands and flags without logging in. On macOS/Linux, `command -v dosya` shows the executable selected by your shell; on PowerShell, use `Get-Command dosya`. An older binary earlier on PATH can take precedence even after a successful install. For **command not found**, open a new terminal after a PATH change and check the installation directory. `/usr/local/bin/dosya --version` on Unix or `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\WindowsApps\dosya.exe" --version` on Windows tests the documented location directly. If it works there, fix PATH rather than reinstalling repeatedly. ## Connect your account and workspace 1. Open [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api), select **New API key**, give it a CLI-specific name, and choose permissions for your intended tasks. For browsing and uploading, use **Full access**; that scope also permits destructive operations wherever your role allows them. 2. Under **Restrictions and expiry**, allow **REST API** if you select individual protocols. Leave **Folder** unset: an ordinary folder-anchored key cannot use the CLI’s REST requests and is refused with **This API key is anchored at a folder and can only be used over WebDAV or the S3 gateway**. Review workspace, expiry and usage restrictions, then select **Generate key**. Store the full `dos_` key while it is displayed; a row prefix cannot authenticate. 3. Run `dosya auth login` and paste the key at **Enter API key:**. The interactive prompt hides the key. Successful authentication prints **Authenticated as** with your account name and email. 4. Run `dosya workspace list`, then `dosya workspace use ws_example` using an actual returned workspace ID. This sets the default for later commands; explicit `--workspace` overrides it. The CLI stores one local configuration, not named login profiles. By default it is `~/.dosya/config.json`; setting `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` places it in that directory's `dosya` subdirectory. Login preserves an existing default workspace. The file contains your key and is written with owner-only permissions on Unix. For automation, use a privately supplied `DOSYA_API_KEY` environment variable, or pipe a secret into `dosya auth login --key -`; avoid a literal key in command arguments or shell history. `DOSYA_API_BASE` overrides the saved API address, whose normal value is `https://api.dosya.dev`. ## Upgrade, rollback and uninstall Run `dosya upgrade` from an installed binary. It checks the latest manifest, verifies the published SHA-256, then replaces the executable at its current location. **Already on latest version** means no replacement was needed. An upgrade refuses a missing or malformed checksum and reports **Checksum mismatch - refusing to install** if the bytes differ. It can require write permission for that location. A manifest request times out after **30 seconds**; the binary download has a **5 minute** timeout. A configured untrusted API host is refused unless you explicitly allow it; restore the official API setting before a normal update. `--force` permits reinstallation or a downgrade reported by the configured server, but it does not select a historical version. Keep a separately saved trusted binary for rollback; replacing the executable does not migrate or remove the local configuration. Latest downloads can remain cached for up to **1 hour** after release, so confirm the actual version after an update. `dosya uninstall` asks for confirmation and removes the installed executable plus the entire CLI configuration directory, including the saved login and default workspace. There is no undo command. It does not delete your cloud files or revoke the API key server-side; revoke the key in Profile if the computer should lose access. Running uninstall from a source checkout removes configuration only, and `dosya upgrade` refuses source execution. **Unsupported platform** means the detected system has no matching release. **No CLI build found for** a selector means that release file is unavailable; retry the official download later. **Authentication failed: invalid API key.** requires checking the full key, expiry and revocation, rather than downloading the CLI again. ## Expected result The official executable is selected by your shell, reports its version and help, and authenticates as the intended account. Installing alone creates no workspace files; the saved default workspace applies only after you select it. ## Related guides - [Upload a directory with the CLI](/developers/cli-upload-directory) - [API key management](/developers/api-key)

title: Use JSON output from the Dosya CLI
summary: Use --json for command-specific Dosya CLI receipts, keep warnings off stdout, and inspect each command’s documented object instead of one schema.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/cli/src/parse-args.ts, apps/cli/src/output.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/whoami.ts, and apps/cli/src/commands/config-cmd.ts. Production commands were not run.
body: Pass `--json` or `-j` to request pretty-printed JSON on stdout. Dosya does not wrap every command in a universal `{ok,data}` schema: `whoami` emits the user object, listing commands retain their API shape, and usage builds its own report. ## Before you start - Confirm the chosen command supports the fields your script needs by running it once against disposable or read-only data. - Capture stderr separately; warnings and debug information remain there even in JSON mode. - `config get` redacts the stored API key, so its JSON is safe for diagnosis but cannot reproduce the credential. ## Steps 1. Run a read-only probe such as `dosya whoami --json`, redirecting stdout and stderr to separate files. 2. Save the exit code before parsing. A nonzero command can leave empty or incomplete stdout even when stderr clearly explains the failure. 3. Parse the actual top-level shape. For `whoami`, read user fields directly; for `ls`, inspect its listing wrapper rather than expecting the same keys. 4. Select only required values with `jq -e` so a missing field makes the script fail. Avoid storing the entire account or file response when one ID is enough. 5. Keep stderr with the job log and JSON stdout with the machine receipt. Never merge them with `2>&1` before a JSON parser. 6. Validate the command result semantically, such as the intended workspace ID or returned file ID, before starting a dependent command. ## Expected result A successful command writes one valid, command-specific JSON document to stdout while progress and warnings remain on stderr. The script checks both exit status and required fields. ## Troubleshooting **`jq` reports invalid JSON.** Confirm stdout and stderr were not merged, then inspect the original exit code. **A field from another command is absent.** Read this command’s output shape; there is no universal result envelope. **The key value is masked.** That is expected for `config get`. Obtain secrets from the secret store that provisioned them, not from CLI diagnostic output. ## Related guides - [Install the CLI](/developers/cli-install) - [Transfer with the CLI](/developers/cli-transfer)

title: Parse Dosya CLI JSON in a script
summary: Preserve the Dosya CLI exit status, parse valid command-specific JSON even for partial failures, and gate dependent work on a verified success.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/cli/src/output.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/whoami.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/ls.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/rm.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/mv.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/download.ts, and apps/cli/src/commands/sync.ts. Production commands were not run.
body: A robust shell wrapper preserves the Dosya process status before running `jq`. JSON output is command-specific, and batch commands normally emit usable success and failure receipts before exiting 1 when any member failed. ## Before you start - Use temporary files with restrictive permissions for outputs that may contain names or IDs. - Keep `set -o pipefail` when using a pipeline, or avoid a pipeline so the parser cannot hide the CLI status. - Choose a precise `jq -e` assertion for the command’s documented response. ## Steps 1. Create separate stdout and stderr files, then run the command with `--json`; for example, `dosya whoami --json >result.json 2>result.err`. 2. Capture `status=$?` immediately and classify it without replacing it with `jq`’s status. Keep stderr beside that original numeric result. 3. When stdout is nonempty, run `jq -e . result.json` even after a nonzero exit. Preserve valid command output; if parsing fails, report that separately without losing the Dosya status. 4. Apply a command-specific selector, such as the required user identifier from `whoami` or the expected item collection from `ls`. There is no universal response envelope. 5. For `mv`, `rm`, recursive download, trash, star, or sync batches, inspect the command’s `failures` entries and successful counts. Partial work normally produces valid JSON and exits 1. 6. Start dependent work only when the Dosya status is 0 and the command-specific postcondition passes. Retain a sanitized partial receipt for recovery, then remove sensitive temporary files. ## Expected result The wrapper preserves the CLI failure class, extracts useful receipts from valid nonzero output, and starts dependent work only after exit 0 and the command-specific postcondition both pass. ## Troubleshooting **The JSON file is empty.** Read stderr and the saved process status; do not let `jq` become the reported failure. **A batch exits 1 with valid JSON.** Preserve successful counts and failure entries, repair or report each failed member, and keep the overall task unsuccessful. **Warnings break parsing.** They should be on stderr. Remove stream merging and confirm the wrapper invokes the current CLI binary. ## Related guides - [Authenticate the Dosya CLI](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Use CLI JSON output](/developers/cli-json-output)

title: Review Dosya CLI configuration
summary: Locate the active config, inspect the API endpoint and workspace without exposing the stored key, and identify environment or flag overrides before a command.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified supported config keys, redaction, file location, API-base precedence, workspace precedence, sync settings and permission warnings in apps/cli/src/commands/config-cmd.ts; apps/cli/src/config.ts; apps/cli/src/resolver.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/auth.ts; apps/cli/tests/integration/config.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/resolver.test.ts; and apps/cli/README.md. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Review the CLI configuration before diagnosing an unexpected account, workspace, or server. The safe commands redact the stored API key while showing the API base, default workspace, and sync options that influence later operations. ## Steps ```bash dosya config path dosya config get dosya config get --json ``` `config path` prints `~/.dosya/config.json` unless `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` redirects it to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dosya/config.json`. `config get` displays these supported values: - `api_base`: server used for REST requests. - `default_workspace`: workspace inherited by commands without an explicit context. - `sync_delta`: `true` enables opt-in block-level delta uploads for eligible sync changes. - `sync_parallel`: concurrent sync transfers, with a default of 8 and a maximum of 16. The no-argument and JSON forms never print the token; they return `api_key: ""` when a stored key exists. An unknown name fails with `Unknown config key: NAME. Available keys: api_base, default_workspace, sync_delta, sync_parallel`. ## Determine the effective endpoint and credential The default API base is `https://api.dosya.dev`. Effective endpoint precedence is: 1. `DOSYA_API_BASE` in the process environment. 2. The stored `api_base` value. 3. The built-in production default. Credential precedence is different: 1. `--key` or `-k` on the command. 2. `DOSYA_API_KEY` in the environment. 3. `api_key` in the config file. Check whether the shell is overriding stored values without printing their contents: ```bash if test -n "${DOSYA_API_KEY+x}"; then echo 'DOSYA_API_KEY is set'; else echo 'DOSYA_API_KEY is not set'; fi if test -n "${DOSYA_API_BASE+x}"; then printf 'DOSYA_API_BASE=%s\n' "$DOSYA_API_BASE"; else echo 'DOSYA_API_BASE is not set'; fi dosya whoami ``` `dosya whoami` is the effective credential test. It prints the account identity reached by the winning key and endpoint. A successful stored login does not prove a later shell without the same home directory or `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` will read that file. ## Review workspace resolution ```bash dosya config get default_workspace dosya ls ``` For normal path references, `ws_ID:path` overrides `--workspace`, which overrides `default_workspace`. The default affects future CLI commands only; it does not change the active workspace in the browser. If the listing is unfamiliar, compare its `workspace_id` in `dosya ls --json` with the ID returned by `dosya workspace list`. ## Change only supported values ```bash dosya config set default_workspace ws_REPLACE_ME dosya config set api_base https://api.dosya.dev dosya config set sync_delta true dosya config set sync_parallel 12 ``` `config set` requires an existing config; otherwise it returns `Not authenticated. Run: dosya auth login`. Values are written as strings. Re-run `config get KEY` and one harmless command after changing context. Use an explicit `--workspace` in deployment scripts when the destination should remain fixed even if a machine default changes. Do not hand-edit `api_key` through `config set`; it is intentionally excluded from allowed keys. Use `dosya auth login` for stored authentication or `DOSYA_API_KEY` for an injected secret. ## Protect the config file The file contains the stored API key in plain text. On Unix-like systems, login creates it with mode `0600` inside a `0700` directory. If a backup, copy, or archive loosens the file mode, the CLI emits a warning naming the path and recommended `chmod 600` correction. Windows does not use that mode check. Do not attach the raw file to a support request. Prefer `dosya config get --json`, `dosya whoami --json`, the command line with its key removed, the exit code, and sanitized error output. Debug logs must never include `DOSYA_API_KEY` or a literal `--key` value. ## Resolve mismatches **`config get` says no configuration exists.** Confirm the current home directory and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, then run `dosya auth login` for this environment. **The displayed `api_base` is production but requests reach another server.** Check `DOSYA_API_BASE`, which takes precedence over the file. **`whoami` shows a different account.** Remove a command-line key override or check which `DOSYA_API_KEY` the process inherited. **The correct account lists the wrong workspace.** Inspect a `ws_ID:` path prefix and `--workspace` before changing the saved default. **Changing `api_base` breaks authentication.** API keys belong to the service that issued them. Restore `https://api.dosya.dev` unless a trusted Dosya environment explicitly gave you another endpoint. ## Expected result The config path is known, the key remains redacted, and `dosya whoami` plus a read-only listing confirm the effective endpoint, account, and workspace. Environment and command-line overrides are either deliberate or removed before production commands run. ## Related guides - [Authenticate without exposing a token](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Choose and verify a workspace](/developers/cli-workspace) - [Upload and download with the CLI](/developers/cli-transfer)

title: Separate Dosya CLI profiles
summary: Isolate Dosya CLI credentials with separate XDG config roots or environment keys, then verify each account and target workspace before every job.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/cli/src/config.ts, apps/cli/src/parse-args.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/config-cmd.ts, and apps/cli/src/commands/whoami.ts. Production profiles were not changed.
body: The CLI has no named-profile store and no `--profile` flag. Isolate identities with different `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` directories, or inject different `DOSYA_API_KEY` values for each process. ## Before you start - The normal XDG file is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dosya/config.json`; without XDG configuration, the fallback is `~/.dosya/config.json`. - Key precedence is command-line `--key`, then `DOSYA_API_KEY`, then config. Base URL environment configuration precedes the saved value and built-in default. - The CLI creates its config directory with mode 0700 and file with 0600; loose existing modes produce a warning. ## Steps 1. Create one private config root per identity, for example `~/.config/dosya-work` and `~/.config/dosya-personal`, and restrict each parent to the account owner. 2. Set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for the desired identity, then save its key through stdin rather than a literal argument. Never invent `--profile`; argument parsing does not support it. 3. Run `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=… dosya whoami --json` and assert the expected account identifier before any mutation. 4. Pass the intended workspace explicitly to commands that accept it, or verify the current workspace returned by the relevant read command. Config isolation does not choose a workspace for you. 5. For ephemeral jobs, prefer `DOSYA_API_KEY` from the scheduler’s secret store and an isolated empty XDG root. Remember that `--key` overrides both. 6. Log the nonsecret profile label, config root, verified account ID, and workspace ID. Refuse to run if any value differs from the job definition. ## Expected result Each process resolves one intended key from a private config root or environment, verifies its account, and acts only in the explicitly checked workspace. No unsupported profile flag is required. ## Troubleshooting **The wrong account appears.** Check for a higher-precedence `--key` or `DOSYA_API_KEY` before editing the config file. **The CLI warns about permissions.** Restore 0700 on the directory and 0600 on `config.json`, then verify ownership. **Two jobs still interfere.** Give them different `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` values and avoid exporting one shared key in the parent shell. ## Related guides - [Authenticate the Dosya CLI](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Use CLI JSON output](/developers/cli-json-output)

title: Upload and download files with the Dosya CLI
summary: Transfer a test file with explicit workspace and paths, understand resume, concurrency and overwrite behavior, then verify the downloaded bytes safely.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified command flags, path resolution, upload screening, retry and multipart thresholds, sidecar resume, download segmentation, URL refresh, overwrite prompts, ETag verification, JSON output and exit behavior in apps/cli/src/commands/upload.ts; apps/cli/src/batch-upload.ts; apps/cli/src/multipart.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/download.ts; apps/cli/src/resolver.ts; apps/cli/tests/integration/upload.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/integration/download.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/multipart.test.ts; and apps/cli/README.md. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Start with one non-confidential file, an explicit workspace, and separate local source and download paths. A successful upload creates stored content in Dosya; a download with `--force` can replace a local file. Verify the round trip before putting either command into automation. ## Steps Choose a workspace and, optionally, a destination folder ID: ```bash DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID='ws_REPLACE_ME' DOSYA_FOLDER_ID='fld_REPLACE_ME' printf 'Dosya CLI transfer check\n' > cli-transfer-check.txt dosya upload ./cli-transfer-check.txt \ --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" \ --folder "$DOSYA_FOLDER_ID" ``` Omit `--folder` to upload to the workspace root. If neither `--workspace` nor a saved default is available, the command stops with `Workspace ID required. Use -w or set default: dosya workspace use `. A missing local path produces `File not found: …`; a directory without `--recursive` is refused instead of being flattened unexpectedly. The CLI reads current workspace upload rules before transferring when that endpoint is available. Blocked extensions and files over the configured maximum are rejected locally with the server's rule. A total larger than remaining storage produces a warning, while the server remains the final quota authority. The role and key must both permit uploads. Files above **50 MB** use multipart upload. Individual parts are retried, and a `.dosya-upload` sidecar records the resumable session. Re-run the same command after interruption; the sidecar is used only when the file size and modification time still match, and it is removed after success. Smaller files use one streamed request with retry delays of 1, 3, and 8 seconds for retryable failures. ## Capture the uploaded file ID For scripts, use JSON rather than parsing progress text: ```bash dosya upload ./cli-transfer-check.txt \ --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" \ --folder "$DOSYA_FOLDER_ID" \ --json > upload-result.json DOSYA_FILE_ID=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("upload-result.json"))["file"]["id"])') printf '%s\n' "$DOSYA_FILE_ID" ``` The single-file response contains `file.id` and `file.name`. Preserve `upload-result.json` only if its metadata is needed; it does not contain the API key. To upload a deliberate replacement as a new version, use `--version-of` with an existing file ID or path: ```bash dosya upload ./report-v2.pdf --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" --version-of reports/report.pdf ``` Version upload changes the stored file's current version; keep the local source until the new version appears in Dosya. Do not use `--version-of` when creating a separate file. ## Download to a new local path Address the file by returned ID or by a workspace-relative path: ```bash mkdir -p ./dosya-transfer-check dosya download "$DOSYA_FILE_ID" --output ./dosya-transfer-check/received.txt cmp ./cli-transfer-check.txt ./dosya-transfer-check/received.txt ``` When `--output` names a directory, the server's filename is used inside it. With no output flag, the current directory is used. An existing destination prompts before overwrite on an interactive terminal; JSON or non-interactive execution stops with `already exists. Use --force to overwrite.` `--force` replaces that local path without another confirmation. Downloads use one connection for small files and up to **8 parallel connections by default** for larger objects; `--connections` accepts 1–16. Interrupted segmented downloads persist `.dosya-download`; rerun the same command with the same file and path to continue completed ranges. Expired temporary URLs are refreshed up to three times. After transfer, the CLI checks the saved content against a recognized origin ETag: a normal MD5 or Dosya's multipart composite form. Unknown ETag formats are skipped rather than guessed. `--no-verify` disables this integrity check and should be reserved for a diagnosed compatibility problem. Size alone does not detect every corruption. ## Transfer folders and multiple files Upload a directory with `--recursive`; by default Dosya creates a top-level folder named after the local directory. Add `--contents` to place only its contents into the selected destination: ```bash dosya upload ./project --recursive --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" --parallel 3 dosya upload ./project --recursive --contents --workspace "$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" ``` Upload concurrency defaults to 3 and is capped at 16, then reduced further when the workspace has a smaller concurrent-upload limit. For a remote folder download, use the dedicated recursive workflow. For several specific files in one archive, use `dosya download --zip FILE... -o bundle.zip`. ## Expected result The upload reports a concrete file ID in the intended workspace and folder. Downloading that ID to a new local path completes without overwrite ambiguity, and `cmp` or the CLI integrity check confirms the received bytes match the source. ## Related guides - [Select the correct CLI workspace](/developers/cli-workspace) - [Download an entire folder tree](/developers/cli-download-folder) - [Upload files in the web app](/uploading/files-and-folders)

title: Troubleshoot Dosya CLI authentication and transfers
summary: Use CLI exit codes and debug output to isolate installation, API base, credentials, workspace, permission, timeout, quota, and upload errors.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/cli/src/index.ts; apps/cli/src/config.ts; apps/cli/src/client.ts; apps/cli/src/errors.ts; apps/cli/src/output.ts; apps/cli/src/runtime.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/auth.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/whoami.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/workspace.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/ls.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/upload.ts; apps/cli/src/multipart.ts. Commands were not run with production credentials.
body: Run a read-only command before retrying a transfer. The Dosya CLI separates usage, authentication, network, permission and maintenance failures with exit codes, so preserve the message and `$?`/`%ERRORLEVEL%` rather than responding to every refusal by creating a new key. ## Steps Run these in order: ```sh dosya --version dosya --help dosya whoami dosya workspace list dosya ls --workspace REPLACE_WITH_WORKSPACE_ID ``` `--version` failing means the executable is missing, blocked, or not on `PATH`. `--help` succeeding while `whoami` fails means the binary starts and the problem is configuration, network or authorization. `whoami` prints the authenticated name, email, account ID and workspace count; verify that identity before any write. Use `--debug` to print request method, URL, attempt and HTTP status to stderr. It does not intentionally print the API key, but review output before sharing it because commands, paths and server messages can still reveal private names. `--json` keeps machine-readable results on stdout while diagnostics remain on stderr. ## Fix credential and API-origin problems Credential precedence is `--key`, then `DOSYA_API_KEY`, then the saved config. A stale environment variable can therefore override a newly stored login. Inspect the environment and rerun `dosya whoami` without unintended overrides. The normal API base is `https://api.dosya.dev`. `DOSYA_API_BASE` overrides both saved configuration and the default. If it points to the marketing site or another HTML endpoint, a 4xx message includes **the API returned a non-JSON response - check DOSYA_API_BASE** and the configured origin. Use `dosya auth login` for the hidden interactive prompt, or pipe a key with `dosya auth login --key -`. Passing the literal through `--key ` exposes it to shell history and the process list. Keys must begin `dos_`; create them at `https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api`. | Message / exit | Meaning | Correct action | | --- | --- | --- | | **Not authenticated. Run: dosya auth login** / exit 3 | No flag, environment or saved key was available | Authenticate or set `DOSYA_API_KEY` for that process. | | **Authentication failed. Run 'dosya auth login' to re-authenticate.** / exit 3 | Server returned 401; key is invalid, expired or revoked | Replace the credential and retest `whoami`. | | Server permission message / exit 5 | Server returned 403; credential is live but scope, protocol, IP/time rule, membership or role refused it | Fix that named restriction. Re-authenticating with the same authority will loop. | | **Cannot reach … Check your internet connection.** / exit 4 | DNS, connectivity or transport failed | Check network and the API base, then retry a read-only request. | | **Request timed out after …s.** / exit 4 | Request exceeded its timeout | Confirm service/network state; increase `--timeout ` only when the operation is expected to need longer. | | **The dosya CLI is paused for maintenance.** / exit 75 | Administrative platform switch disabled CLI requests | Nothing was uploaded or changed; monitor `https://status.dosya.dev` and rerun later. | The saved config path is shown by `dosya config path`. On macOS/Linux it normally lives under `~/.dosya/config.json` or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dosya/config.json` with mode 0600. If the CLI warns that the file is readable by other users, apply the displayed `chmod 600` command and rotate a key that may have been exposed. ## Correct workspace context Run `dosya workspace list` and copy the intended workspace ID. `dosya workspace use ` stores a default but does not contact the server to validate the ID, so confirm it with: ```sh dosya ls --workspace ws_example ``` An explicit `--workspace` is safer during diagnosis than relying on a stale default. **Workspace ID required** exits with code 2 and performs no request. A 403 after selecting a real workspace indicates membership/role or key reach; a 404 can mean the resource/path no longer exists or is not visible. ## Diagnose upload failures Before retrying, compare the local file name/size and destination with workspace upload rules and available storage. The CLI prechecks allowed/blocked extensions, maximum file size and remaining storage when that endpoint is available; the server remains authoritative. `dosya upload` defaults to three concurrent files, accepts `--parallel` up to 16, and clamps to the workspace's active concurrent-upload limit. When no slot is available it waits 0.5, 1.5, 3, 5 and 8 seconds before returning the server refusal. Other devices and pending sessions share that capacity. Small streamed uploads retry transport/5xx failures three times after 1, 3 and 8 seconds, rebuilding the stream each time. Files above the multipart threshold retain a `.dosya-upload` sidecar so rerunning the same source can resume uploaded parts. Keep that sidecar beside the unchanged file until completion; changing source size or API origin makes the saved session unsuitable. Metadata requests use a 30-second default timeout. Upload/download paths use longer operation-specific defaults, including 10 minutes for a whole-file upload, unless an explicit global `--timeout` replaces them. A 4xx is a policy/input refusal and is not repaired by replaying identical bytes. The HTTP client automatically retries GET, HEAD and PUT after eligible 5xx/transport failures using 1, 3 and 8-second delays. It does not blindly replay POST, because doing so could create duplicates, or DELETE, because a repeated delete can become permanent deletion. After an ambiguous write error, inspect Dosya before running the command again. ## Expected result 1. Confirm `dosya whoami` reports the intended account. 2. List the target with an explicit workspace ID. 3. Retry one uniquely named harmless file with the smallest practical concurrency. 4. Open Dosya **Files**, check its name, size and folder, then download/compare the sample where integrity matters. If the same minimal command fails, send private support the CLI version, operating system, exact command with secrets removed, exit code, approximate time/timezone, workspace ID, file size, and sanitized debug/error output. Never include a complete key, environment dump, config file or confidential file bytes. ## Related guides - [Install the CLI](/developers/cli-install) - [Authenticate the CLI](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Select a workspace](/developers/cli-workspace)

title: Update the Dosya CLI
summary: Check the installed Dosya CLI version, verify the trusted release checksum, and replace only a supported compiled binary with an approved build.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/cli/src/commands/upgrade.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/upgrade-policy.ts, apps/cli/src/runtime.ts, and apps/cli/package.json. Production binaries were not replaced.
body: `dosya upgrade` is for an installed compiled binary, not a source checkout. Supported release targets are Linux x64, macOS arm64 or x64, and Windows x64. ## Before you start - Run `dosya --version` and record the current binary path before changing it. - Use the official trusted API origin. A custom release host requires the explicit custom-host allowance and should be approved by your organization. - The release manifest request times out after 30 seconds; the binary download allows 300 seconds. ## Steps 1. Run `dosya --version` and confirm the active executable with the operating system’s path lookup. Stop if the job is invoking a development checkout. 2. Invoke `dosya upgrade` from an interactive maintenance window. Use `--force` only to reinstall the same version or make an intentionally approved downgrade. 3. Let the updater select the platform artifact. Reject an unsupported architecture instead of substituting a similarly named binary. 4. Require the downloaded SHA-256 to match the release manifest. A checksum failure must leave the installed binary untrusted and unchanged. 5. Allow the updater to stage an executable temporary file with mode 0755 and replace the target through rename or its copy fallback. 6. Run `dosya --version` again from a fresh shell, then perform a read-only `whoami --json` check before re-enabling scheduled jobs. ## Expected result The supported compiled binary is replaced only after manifest and SHA-256 verification. A fresh invocation reports the approved version and can authenticate for a read-only check. ## Troubleshooting **Upgrade says the runtime is unsupported.** Install a published compiled binary for the supported operating system and architecture. **The checksum differs.** Delete the staged artifact and retry from the trusted origin; never bypass verification. **The old version still runs.** Inspect command lookup order and long-lived processes. A successful file replacement does not change an already running process. ## Related guides - [Install the CLI](/developers/cli-install) - [Transfer with the CLI](/developers/cli-transfer)

title: Upload a directory with the Dosya CLI
summary: Upload a folder from the command line with workspace and folder flags, recursive paths, progress, partial-failure reporting and resumable transfers.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14: apps/cli/src/index.ts; apps/cli/src/config.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/auth.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/workspace.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/ls.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/upload.ts; apps/cli/src/batch-upload.ts; apps/cli/src/multipart.ts; apps/cli/src/output.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/upload-folder-paths.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/upload-parallel.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/batch-upload.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/multipart.test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/body-pipeline.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/finalize-session.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/batch.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts; apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts. Examples parser/help checked locally without network; retained workflow illustration, removed marketing overview figure as it does not show the transfer. Local repository review; commands checked without production credentials.
body: Use `dosya upload ./sample-source --recursive --workspace ws_example` to upload a folder from the command line. Replace the workspace placeholder with your actual ID. By default Dosya creates or reuses a destination folder named `sample-source` and preserves the file paths beneath it; `--contents` instead places those contents directly into the chosen target. The workflow image is an illustration. The flags and limits below were checked against the current command parser and transfer implementation. ## Authenticate and choose the destination Have the CLI installed and confirm `dosya upload --help`. In [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api), select **New API key**, choose **Full access** for the browse-and-upload workflow, allow **REST API** under protocol restrictions, and pin the intended workspace if needed. Save the full key after **Generate key**. ```sh dosya auth login dosya workspace list dosya workspace use ws_example ``` Enter the credential at the hidden **Enter API key:** prompt. Use the ID returned by the workspace list in place of `ws_example`; the last command saves that default. You can omit it and supply `--workspace` on every upload instead. An environment-supplied `DOSYA_API_KEY` takes precedence over the saved key. The CLI has one saved configuration, rather than named account profiles, so check the authenticated account and workspace before transferring private files. Your membership must permit uploading and creating any required folders. An upload-only key cannot perform the browsing/verification sequence; a read-only key cannot upload. Workspace rules, key limits, storage allowance and any folder restriction still apply to a full-access key. To select an existing folder, get its ID from `dosya ls --workspace ws_example`, then pass `--folder fld_example`. The folder must belong to the selected workspace and be within your allowed reach. ## Review the local tree before uploading - Nested directories are traversed recursively. Hidden regular files, including `.env` and dotfiles, are included; there is no ignore-file or exclusion flag on this command. Make a curated source directory if it contains secrets or files you do not intend to upload. - Nested symlinks, sockets and device entries are skipped, with a **Skipping … non-regular file(s)** message in normal output. The supplied top-level path is resolved with a normal filesystem stat, so do not use a symlink as the source path if you intend to avoid its target. - Only directories needed by accepted files are created. Empty subdirectories are not copied, and a tree with no regular files fails with **Directory is empty.** - Matching live filenames in the same destination folder are adopted as new versions, rather than a second unrelated file. This is an upload operation, not an incremental synchronization comparison: rerunning can create versions even for unchanged files. Remote-only files are not removed. Keep the source files unchanged until transfer and verification finish. Choose a new test folder first if the destination already contains working copies. ## Steps: run the directory upload ```sh dosya upload ./sample-source --recursive --workspace ws_example --parallel 3 ``` To nest it beneath an existing remote folder: ```sh dosya upload ./sample-source --recursive --workspace ws_example --folder fld_example ``` To skip the extra `sample-source` level: ```sh dosya upload ./sample-source --recursive --contents --workspace ws_example --folder fld_example ``` Quote local paths with spaces. `--recursive` has short form `-r`; `--workspace` is `-w`. File concurrency defaults to **3** and is capped at **16**; `--parallel` or `-c` sets it, and the CLI reduces directory-upload concurrency to a lower workspace session limit. For a single multipart file, this flag controls parallel parts instead. Small regular files of at most **5 MiB** are packed into requests with at most **200 files** and **48 MiB** of file data. Up to **4** such batches run concurrently, bounded further by your selected concurrency. If a batch cannot be used, the client falls back to individual uploads. Files larger than **50 MiB** use resumable uploads with **10 MiB** parts; the last part can be smaller. These are transfer thresholds, not an entitlement to upload a file of any size: extension rules, maximum file size, member allowance and available storage can still refuse it. The CLI reads workspace rules before creating folders. Normal output lists up to **10** rejected paths and continues with accepted files; skipped rule violations are therefore not proof that the complete directory uploaded. With `--json`, any rejected files produce `files_rejected` and exit **2** before folder creation. If the quota estimate does not fit, the client warns and lets the server decide each file; some may fail. ## Read the result and verify the remote tree Normal output first reports the file count and total size. Interactive progress goes to stderr, followed by **Done. N uploaded, M failed.** Use JSON when a script needs file IDs and per-file outcomes: ```sh dosya upload ./sample-source --recursive --workspace ws_example --json > upload-result.json ``` The directory result contains `uploaded`, `failed`, `failures` and `files`; successful entries include the file ID, name, size and version. Check the process exit status as well as the JSON. A transfer or folder-creation failure exits **1**, even if other files completed. Global error categories also include **2** usage, **3** authentication, **4** network, **5** forbidden and **75** maintenance; success is **0**. Open **Files** in the same workspace and inspect the created root and nested folders. Compare filenames, sizes and expected counts with the local tree, then download and open a representative file. Review all skipped paths and warnings. A folder-creation warning can cause descendant files to fall back into a surviving parent, so a success count alone does not prove the directory structure is correct. ## Interruptions, resuming and safe retries Ctrl+C prints **Interrupted.** and exits **130**. Completed files and created folders remain in cloud storage; interruption is not a transaction rollback and does not remove them. For multipart files the client writes `.dosya-upload` before sending bytes and removes it after completion. A later upload of that exact file can reuse stored parts if its byte size and modification time still match and the resume URLs belong to the configured API host. Keep the sidecar for a resumable retry and do not edit it. Single-stream uploads retry transient failures up to **3** times after waits of **1, 3 and 8 seconds**; a 4xx refusal is not replayed as a transient error. For an interrupted directory, use the summary and destination listing to identify incomplete files, then retry those individually into their existing folder IDs. Blindly rerunning the entire tree also uploads successful files again and can create extra versions. Its scanner includes regular `.dosya-upload` sidecar files, so do not treat a recursive rerun as a filtered resume job. If an old session is no longer usable, remove only that file's sidecar when deliberately restarting it; already stored cloud files are unaffected by local sidecar removal. ## Resolve the exact refusal | Output | Next action | | --- | --- | | `Use --recursive to upload a directory.` | Add `--recursive` after checking the source tree. | | `Workspace ID required.` | Supply `--workspace` or set a default with `dosya workspace use`. | | `Every file was refused by this workspace's upload rules.` | Review extension and size restrictions; do not retry unchanged input. | | `--version-of can only be used with a single file.` | Use an ordinary recursive upload, or upload one replacement file with an explicit version target. | | `Warning: failed to create folder` | Stop relying on counts, inspect where its files landed, and correct the folder permission or destination before retrying. | The `--version-of` flag is available for one file, not a directory. It lets you target an existing file explicitly. Version recovery is limited by workspace history retention, so keep your original local folder until verification is complete. ## Expected result Accepted files appear beneath the chosen target with their expected relative paths, or directly in the target when you used --contents. The complete result includes skipped/rejected paths and partial failures as well as uploaded files; inspect those before declaring the folder complete. ## Related guides - [Install the Dosya CLI](/developers/cli-install) - [File version history](/files/version-history)

title: Pass a CLI credential without printing it
summary: Supply a Dosya API key through stdin or a secret environment variable, retain private file modes, and revoke stored credentials without logging them.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/cli/src/commands/auth.ts, apps/cli/src/config.ts, apps/cli/src/commands/config-cmd.ts, and apps/cli/tests. Production credentials were not created or revoked.
body: Dosya API keys begin with `dos_`. Avoid literal secret arguments because process listings and shell history can expose them; the CLI warns when a key is passed directly on the command line. ## Before you start - Retrieve the key from an approved secret manager at runtime. - Use a private `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when saving it; config directories and files should remain 0700 and 0600. - `config get` redacts the key. Do not build workflows that try to read it back. ## Steps 1. Load the secret into a transient environment variable without echoing it. Disable command tracing around the retrieval and CLI invocation. 2. For one command, export `DOSYA_API_KEY` only to that process. For saved authentication, pipe the secret to the supported key-from-stdin form using `--key -`. 3. Run `dosya whoami --json` and validate the expected identity. Capture stdout and stderr without printing the environment. 4. Unset the shell variable immediately after the process. Ensure job logs, crash reports, and debug wrappers do not dump the environment. 5. Use local logout when only the machine’s saved credential should be removed. Use `logout --revoke` when the server key must also be invalidated. 6. Check the revoke result: a failed server revoke retains the local key so it can be retried, while a 401 clears an already unusable local credential. Verify config output remains redacted. ## Expected result The CLI authenticates without placing the key in argv or logs, its stored file remains private, and logout behavior matches the chosen local-only or server-revoke intent. ## Troubleshooting **The CLI warns about a literal key.** Rotate the exposed credential and switch to stdin or a secret environment injection. **Revoke fails with a network error.** The local key remains so the server action can be retried; protect the config file until then. **A CI log contains environment output.** Remove environment-dump steps and rotate the key. Redaction in `config get` cannot sanitize unrelated logging tools. ## Related guides - [Authenticate the Dosya CLI](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Use CLI JSON output](/developers/cli-json-output)

title: Verify a scheduled CLI job
summary: Run a Dosya CLI job with explicit paths, secret, and workspace, preserve JSON and exit evidence, then verify its remote result before success.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/cli/src/index.ts, apps/cli/src/runtime.ts, apps/cli/src/config.ts, apps/cli/src/output.ts, and packages/prod-smoke. Production schedules were not run.
body: Schedulers provide a sparse environment and may run from an unexpected directory. A reliable Dosya job uses absolute paths, explicit credential isolation, structured output, and a separate verification read. ## Before you start - Use the absolute CLI binary and local input path. The default request timeout is 30 seconds; set a positive `--timeout` only when the operation needs a different bound. - Inject `DOSYA_API_KEY` from the scheduler or assign a private `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; there is no `--profile` option. - Pin and verify the intended workspace before changing data. ## Steps 1. At job start, record the UTC time, CLI version, absolute executable, nonsecret job name, and expected workspace. Do not log the secret or full environment. 2. Run `whoami --json` with the scheduled credential and reject an unexpected account. Confirm the target workspace through an explicit read. 3. Invoke the business command with absolute paths, `--json`, and the approved timeout. Redirect stdout and stderr to separate protected files. 4. Save the original process status. Classify 3 as auth, 4 as network, 5 as forbidden, 75 as maintenance, and 130 or 143 as cancellation; retry only operations safe to repeat. 5. Parse the command-specific receipt and extract its resource ID. Check partial batch failures rather than trusting a generic success assumption. 6. Perform a read-only remote verification for the expected ID, parent, name, size, or deleted state. Mark the schedule successful only after that postcondition matches. ## Expected result The scheduler records identity, command receipt, exit status, and a read-only remote postcondition. A local zero exit without the expected remote state cannot become a successful run. ## Troubleshooting **It works interactively but not on schedule.** Compare executable path, working directory, XDG root, secret injection, and network access. **The job times out.** Increase a positive `--timeout` only after confirming the operation and scheduler deadline permit it. **A mutation has network exit 4.** Read remote state before retrying. A transport failure does not prove the server rejected the write. ## Related guides - [Authenticate the Dosya CLI](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Use CLI JSON output](/developers/cli-json-output)

title: Select and verify a Dosya CLI workspace
summary: List workspace IDs, set or override the CLI default, understand path precedence, and verify the destination before upload, move, or delete commands.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified workspace list/use commands, stored configuration, resolver precedence, path syntax, listing behavior and exact missing-context errors in apps/cli/src/commands/workspace.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/config-cmd.ts; apps/cli/src/commands/ls.ts; apps/cli/src/resolver.ts; apps/cli/src/config.ts; apps/cli/tests/integration/workspace.test.ts; apps/cli/tests/unit/resolver.test.ts; and apps/cli/README.md. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Most CLI paths are relative to a workspace. Set a default for routine commands, pass `--workspace` for a one-off override, or prefix a path with `ws_ID:` when the reference must identify its own workspace. Verify the resulting context before any upload, move, copy, or delete. ## Steps Authenticate first, then list every workspace visible to the credential: ```bash dosya workspace list ``` The table shows **ID**, **NAME**, and **STORAGE**. Use the value beginning with `ws_`; display names are not accepted as workspace identifiers. For scripts, `dosya workspace list --json` returns the server response with a `workspaces` array. A workspace-pinned API key can expose only its pinned workspace. An account-wide key still sees only workspaces where its owner remains a member. If the expected row is absent, check the API key's **Reach**, current membership, and endpoint before setting any default. ## Set and inspect the default Store the chosen ID: ```bash dosya workspace use ws_REPLACE_ME dosya config get default_workspace dosya ls ``` `workspace use` writes `default_workspace` to the CLI config and prints `Default workspace set to …`. It does not contact the API or validate that the ID exists. The following `dosya ls` is the decisive check: compare a known root folder or file with the same workspace in the web app. Use `dosya config path` to locate the active config file. It is normally `~/.dosya/config.json` or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dosya/config.json`. Logging in again merges authentication values into this file and preserves the default workspace. ## Override the default deliberately For path-aware commands, workspace precedence is: 1. An explicit `ws_ID:path/to/item` prefix on the reference. 2. `--workspace ws_ID` or `-w ws_ID` on the command. 3. The saved `default_workspace`. Examples: ```bash # Uses the saved default. dosya info reports/q3.pdf # Overrides the default for this command. dosya info reports/q3.pdf --workspace ws_OTHER # The prefix belongs to the reference and wins over --workspace. dosya info ws_EXPLICIT:reports/q3.pdf --workspace ws_OTHER ``` Raw file IDs such as `file_…` are globally addressable and do not require a workspace for lookup. Raw folder IDs and names used by commands that need a workspace can still require context. When a path has none, the resolver reports `No workspace for "PATH". Use ws_id:path, --workspace , or set a default workspace.` `dosya ls` has its own positional form: `dosya ls ws_ID` chooses its first argument before `--workspace` and the saved default. Prefer one context mechanism per command so a reviewer does not need to reason about competing values. ## Check before a write or delete Run a harmless read with the same context you plan to use: ```bash TARGET_WORKSPACE='ws_REPLACE_ME' dosya ls --workspace "$TARGET_WORKSPACE" --json > workspace-check.json ``` Inspect `workspace_id`, known folder names, and the returned file IDs. Then pass the same `--workspace` value to the write: ```bash dosya upload ./sample.txt --workspace "$TARGET_WORKSPACE" --folder fld_REPLACE_ME ``` For automation, an explicit `--workspace` or `ws_ID:` prefix is easier to audit than inheriting a mutable machine default. A changed default affects future path-based commands but does not move existing files or alter the web app's active workspace. ## Troubleshoot unexpected context **`Workspace ID required.`** Supply `dosya ls ws_ID`, add `--workspace ws_ID`, or set `default_workspace`. **A path resolves in the wrong workspace.** Check for a `ws_ID:` prefix first, then command flags, then `dosya config get default_workspace`. **The default was accepted but listing fails.** `workspace use` stores text locally without validating it. Copy the current ID from `dosya workspace list` and set it again. **The workspace is listed but an operation returns 403.** Selection succeeded; compare the key permission, protocol access, workspace role, folder confinement, locks, and source conditions for the attempted operation. **Two workspaces contain the same file path.** Use `ws_ID:path` or a raw file ID in repeatable scripts. Folder and file names alone are not account-wide identifiers. ## Expected result The harmless listing and the web app identify the same workspace and known content. Subsequent commands either carry the intended workspace explicitly or inherit a verified default, with no ambiguous display-name lookup. ## Related guides - [Authenticate the CLI](/developers/cli-authenticate) - [Review CLI endpoint and config](/developers/cli-review-config) - [Switch workspaces in the web app](/account/switch-workspaces)

title: Browse a connected cloud account before importing
summary: Navigate a connected provider safely, interpret picker labels and paging, and keep an exact selection while moving between remote folders before import.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/use-cloud-browser.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/browse.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/types.ts.
