body: The provider picker is a read-only browser for Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox. Opening a folder changes what you can inspect; checking a folder selects its entire subtree for import without requiring you to open every child. ## Steps 1. Open the provider integration page, choose **Import files**, and verify the dialog title says **Import from Google Drive**, **OneDrive**, or **Dropbox** as intended. 2. If an account selector appears, match its email before browsing; changing accounts resets the breadcrumb to **Home** and clears the old selection. 3. Choose a folder name to enter it, then use the breadcrumb back to **Home** without losing selections in that account. 4. Check only wanted rows; leave **Cannot be imported** entries disabled and note the exact extension on any provider document marked **will import as …**. 5. Choose **Load more** whenever it appears because the current list is only one provider page; an empty completed page instead says **This folder is empty.** 6. Compare the footer’s selected count with your checklist, confirm it says **importing into workspace root**, and leave the dialog open until the review is complete. A provider 429 keeps the current view and displays that it is “retrying automatically in Ns”; wait for that timer rather than reconnecting. **Could not list that folder** has a manual **Retry** control. **This account needs to be reconnected before you can import** means the saved provider token was rejected and requires the separate **Reconnect** flow. ## Expected result The breadcrumb identifies the inspected remote path, every checked row belongs to the chosen provider email, all result pages have been loaded, and the footer count equals the roots you intend to import. Selecting one folder counts as one root even though discovery later expands its descendants. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Monitor an import](/integrations/import-progress)

title: Cancel a cloud import before it transfers
summary: Exit the provider picker before a job exists, understand what Cancel clears, and verify that no cloud discovery or file transfer has started.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/use-cloud-browser.ts, apps/web/src/stores/cloud-imports.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/index.ts. body: Use this procedure while you are still inside the **Import from …** picker. At this stage the checked rows live only in browser state; Dosya does not create a cloud-import job until you choose **Import** and receive **Import started**. ## Steps 1. Before acting, check the footer; when **Import** is enabled and no start toast exists, the create request has not been submitted. 2. In the cloud-import picker, record any remote names you may want later because closing it discards the breadcrumb and checked rows. 3. Choose the footer’s **Cancel** button or close the dialog, and do not press **Import** while it is closing. 4. Reopen **Import files** from the same provider page and confirm the breadcrumb begins at **Home** with `0 selected`. 5. Check the provider page and the Integrations sidebar; neither should show a discovering or running cloud-import indicator from this abandoned selection. 6. If an **Import started** toast appeared before cancellation, treat it as a created job and follow the active-job cancellation guide instead. Closing the picker makes no API call to `/api/cloud/imports`, so it creates no folders, files, job receipt, or storage charge. The reset is irreversible only for the unsent selection state: you must browse and check the remote items again. The footer **Cancel** is distinct from the progress card’s **Cancel**, which stops a server-side job. ## Expected result Reopening the picker shows **Home**, no checked boxes, and `0 selected`; no new progress card or cloud-import completion toast appears. Provider account access remains connected because cancelling the draft does not disconnect OAuth. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Browse provider files](/integrations/cloud-import-browse-provider)

title: Cancel a cloud import
summary: Stop an active cloud import, distinguish cancellation from completion races, and understand which copied files and skipped work remain afterward.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/import-progress-card.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/[id]/cancel.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/durable-object.ts. Production behavior for “Cancel a cloud import” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: An import can be cancelled only while its progress card is **Preparing import** or **Importing**. Cancellation stops later discovery or transfer work, but it does not roll back files and folders that already reached the destination. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** or the matching provider page and locate the active card by provider and source account email. 2. Read its state and counts first; note that **Preparing import** has an unknown total, while **Importing X of Y files** has finished discovery. 3. Choose **Cancel** on that active card once and wait for the request to finish instead of repeatedly pressing it. 4. Watch for the **Import cancelled** toast with **From account@example.com**; a job that finished during the request may instead report its real terminal result. 5. After **Import cancelled**, open the destination workspace root; completed cloud-import files are deliberately retained. 6. Compare the retained result with the provider tree before starting another import, avoiding a second selection of files that already landed. The server marks leftover pending and processing items as skipped and aborts unfinished multipart uploads. It leaves completed file rows and storage usage intact. A second cancel against a complete, failed, or already-cancelled job is refused as **Job is already …**; terminal status is never rewritten merely to satisfy a late click. ## Expected result The active progress card disappears and a cancellation toast identifies the provider account. No new items continue transferring, while fully imported files remain available in Dosya and require an ordinary delete if you do not want them. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Monitor an import](/integrations/import-progress)

title: Choose the correct cloud-provider account
summary: Identify the exact connected provider account by email, switch without carrying stale state, and confirm the intended source before starting import.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/connected-accounts-card.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/api/cloud-import.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/accounts/index.ts. body: Dosya stores each linked Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox identity as a separate account row. The picker exposes an email selector only when more than one account for that provider is connected. ## Steps 1. Open the provider setup page and inspect **Connected accounts**, where each row shows its provider email and relative connection time. 2. Use the **Import** button on the intended row when available; that row’s account ID is preselected in the picker. 3. If you opened the general **Import files** button, choose the matching email from the picker’s account selector. 4. After switching, verify the breadcrumb returned to **Home**, the list reloaded, and the selected count reset instead of carrying another account’s folder IDs. 5. Within the chosen cloud-provider email, browse one identifying folder or filename, then select only the required import roots. 6. Choose **Import** and confirm the **Import started** toast says **From** followed by the same email you reviewed. The account name supplied by a provider is stored but the current selection surface uses `account_email`; use that email as the decisive identifier. Accounts are user-scoped rather than workspace-scoped, while the import is written to the workspace active in Dosya. Switching accounts intentionally drops the previous breadcrumb and checks. ## Expected result The source email in the start toast and progress card matches the account selected on the integration page. Remote names come from that identity, and no selection from another linked account survives the switch. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Browse provider files](/integrations/cloud-import-browse-provider)

title: Compare cloud-import item counts
summary: Reconcile a cloud import using its discovered total, completed, failed, and skipped counts, then verify delivered files in the workspace root.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/import-progress-card.tsx, apps/web/src/stores/cloud-imports.ts, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover.ts. Production imports were not run.
body: The number beside **selected** is the count of checked roots in the provider picker, not the number of files that will arrive. A checked folder can contain many descendants. Dosya discovers that subtree first, then establishes the file total used by the transfer. ## Know what each number means - **N selected** counts the checked files and folders submitted from Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox. A single selected folder is one root even when it contains thousands of files. The request accepts at most **500** selected roots. - **Preparing import - N files found so far** is a growing discovery count. The progress bar is intentionally indeterminate at this stage because the final denominator is unknown. - **Importing C of T files** means discovery has finished. `T` contains supported direct selections plus supported files discovered inside selected folders. - **Completed** records files that were delivered. **Failed** records supported files that were not delivered. Ordinary transfer failures retire on the third strike; a policy refusal or locked-backup destination can fail immediately. - **Skipped** is reported separately for unsupported provider entries found during traversal. Those entries are not included in `T`. Therefore the supported-file equation is **completed + failed = total**. Do not add skipped items to `total`, and do not expect the provider picker's selected-root count to equal any of those values. ## Steps 1. Before selecting **Import**, record the footer's **N selected - importing into workspace root** value and note which checked entries are folders. 2. After **Import started**, watch the active card. During **Preparing import**, wait for discovery rather than comparing the changing value with the provider's folder count. 3. When the card changes to **Importing C of T files**, record `T`. The page refreshes active job data every **5 seconds**. 4. Keep the app open long enough to receive the terminal toast. **Import complete** reports the completed count and appends skipped and failed counts when either is nonzero. 5. Verify the arithmetic with the recorded `T`: `completed + failed` must equal `T`; log `skipped` on its own line. 6. Open **Files** at the active workspace root. Count representative delivered files inside each imported root folder, and compare names plus paths against the provider account. ## If the numbers appear inconsistent Terminal jobs disappear from the active progress card. The current browser UI has no persistent result drawer for reopening prior counts, so capture the running total and completion toast during the operation. If the toast was missed, inspect the destination rather than inventing a total from **N selected**. Native provider documents may display **will import as .pdf**, `.xlsx`, `.docx`, or `.pptx`; count the exported Dosya file, not both the source document and its converted output. A same-name destination collision is not overwritten silently: that item eventually contributes to **failed**. Unsupported entries marked **Cannot be imported** cannot be checked directly, while unsupported descendants discovered below a selected folder contribute to **skipped**. Cancelling stops remaining work but does not roll back files already completed. Likewise, a failed job can leave successful earlier items in the destination. Check the cloud tree before retrying, because a new import is a new job rather than an atomic retry of the old result. ## Expected result The recorded supported total equals completed plus failed, skipped entries are documented separately, and the delivered tree contains the files counted as complete. Any difference is traced to a named failed, skipped, exported, or already-delivered item instead of the original selected-root number. ## Related guides - [Monitor import progress](/integrations/import-progress) - [Verify folder structure](/integrations/cloud-import-verify-folders)

title: Choose a cloud-import destination deliberately
summary: Confirm the active workspace and the picker’s workspace-root destination before importing, then verify every selected root in Dosya Files safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/google.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/onedrive.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/dropbox.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/index.ts. Production destinations were not modified.
body: The released Google Drive, OneDrive, and Dropbox integration pages import into the **root of the active Dosya workspace**. Their provider picker does not currently offer a Dosya destination-folder control. Its breadcrumbs navigate the provider account; they do not choose a Dosya folder. ## Before you start You must be a member of the destination and your role must allow file uploads. The start request returns **Not a member of this workspace** when membership is missing and **No upload permission** when the role cannot add files. Clean up or rename any live destination folders that would unintentionally merge with selected provider roots. The importer reuses a same-name folder under the same parent. It does not create an isolated migration snapshot around every job. ## Steps 1. Use the Dosya workspace switcher to select the destination workspace before opening the integration. 2. Open **Integrations**, choose Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox, and select **Import** for the intended connected account. 3. Browse the cloud-import provider hierarchy. If multiple accounts are connected, verify the email in the account selector before checking anything. 4. Select the required files and folder roots. A checked folder brings its whole subtree, even when it is not expanded in the dialog. 5. Read the footer before submission. It must say **N selected - importing into workspace root**. The `N` is the number of checked roots, not the eventual file count. 6. Select **Import**. The button changes to **Starting...** while the request is submitted, then Dosya shows **Import started** with **From account@example.com** when the account is known. 7. After **Import complete**, return to **Files** and inspect the workspace root. Direct selected files belong there; each checked folder maps to a named root, although an existing live folder with that same name can be reused. ## If you need a subfolder destination Do not infer a Dosya path from the provider breadcrumb. The integration page supplies `workspace root` as the destination, and there is no released subfolder selector in this flow. Import a controlled set into the correct workspace, verify completion, then move the delivered files and root folders in **Files** using your normal move permissions. Starting the job records its workspace and destination. Switching the visible workspace afterward does not retarget the running import. Return to the originally selected workspace to monitor and verify it. ## Troubleshooting - **Import failed to start** followed by **No upload permission** requires a role change; reconnecting the provider does not change Dosya permissions. - **Destination folder not found** applies to callers that submit a folder ID through the import API. The current provider integration pages submit no folder ID and use root. - **This account needs to be reconnected before you can import** means provider authorization is stale. Select **Reconnect**, complete the provider flow, and reopen the picker. - A rate-limit banner says the provider is **retrying automatically in Ns**. Wait for that countdown rather than creating duplicate jobs. Moving imported content afterward is a separate cloud mutation. Confirm the moved tree before deleting any duplicate source or destination material; an import itself reads the provider and does not remove provider data. ## Expected result The chosen provider account imports into the root of the workspace that was active at submission. Dosya Files shows direct selections at root and each selected provider folder under its named local root, including deliberate reuse of an existing same-name root when applicable. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Browse provider files](/integrations/cloud-import-browse-provider)

title: Connect a cloud account for imports
summary: Connect Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox through the released OAuth flow, verify the returned identity, and recover from exact callback errors.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/integrations.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/cloud-connect-notice.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/connect/[provider].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/callback/[provider].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/providers.ts. body: Connect from Dosya’s integration page so the server can create a signed, session-bound OAuth request. The provider grants read access for import; Dosya never asks you to paste a provider password or access token. ## Steps 1. Sign in to Dosya in the browser, open **Integrations**, and choose a configured provider’s **Connect account** control. 2. On the Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox consent screen, verify the signed-in email and requested read access before approving Dosya. 3. Return to the provider setup page and find that email under **Connected accounts**; the account row is the success receipt. 4. If the page says **Connection cancelled**, **sign-in attempt expired**, **provider did not accept the sign-in**, or **failed while saving**, start a fresh connection from Dosya. 5. Choose **Import** beside the new account, browse a harmless file or folder, and verify the picker can list it. 6. Close the picker without importing if this was only a connection test, or select reviewed content and continue with the import guide. Only providers configured in the deployed API are listed; the registered set is Google Drive, OneDrive, and Dropbox. The OAuth state is single-use and tied to the signed-in session. A connection belongs to the Dosya user, so it can later be used to import into a workspace where that user has `upload_files` permission. ## Expected result The provider page contains a **Connected accounts** row with the approved email and connection age, and its **Import** action opens the remote root. Query parameters from the callback are removed after the page consumes them, so refreshing does not replay a stale notice. ## Related guides - [Import from Google Drive](/integrations/google-drive) - [Import from OneDrive](/integrations/onedrive) - [Import from Dropbox](/integrations/dropbox) - [Disconnect a cloud import account](/integrations/disconnect-cloud-account)

title: Choose a cloud-import destination
summary: Confirm where provider imports land in the current release, select the active workspace first, and verify the root destination before transfer.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/google.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/onedrive.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/dropbox.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/index.ts. body: The released Google Drive, OneDrive, and Dropbox setup pages currently pass `destFolderId=null`; their picker therefore imports into the active workspace root. The footer is the authoritative destination label and says **importing into workspace root**. ## Steps 1. Switch Dosya to the workspace that should receive the files before opening the provider integration page. 2. Confirm your role can upload there; the API refuses a non-member with **Not a member of this workspace** and a restricted role with **No upload permission**. 3. Choose the account’s **Import** action, select one reviewed file or folder, and read the footer before submission. 4. Require the footer to show the intended count followed by **importing into workspace root**; stop if you expected a nested folder picker. 5. Choose **Import** and wait for **Import started**, which fixes the workspace and null root destination on the job. 6. After completion, open the active workspace root and locate the imported top-level file or selected folder. The dialog component can accept a folder ID, and the API validates that such a destination is live, but no released provider page currently supplies one. Do not promise a nested target based on test-only component support. Selecting a remote folder creates or reuses that folder at the workspace root and maps its descendants below it. ## Expected result The import appears in the active workspace root. A selected remote file lands directly there; a selected remote folder appears as a top-level folder whose subtree is discovered in the background. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Monitor cloud-import progress](/integrations/import-progress) - [Import from Google Drive](/integrations/google-drive) - [Organize files after import](/files/organize-files)

title: Disconnect a cloud account after verification
summary: Verify the imported result before removing provider access, then disconnect safely while preserving complete Dosya copies and their storage use.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/integrations.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/connected-accounts-card.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/accounts/[id].ts, apps/api/migrations/0148_control_plane_fks_to_object_tables.sql. Production behavior for “Disconnect a cloud account after verification” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Disconnect only after the job has reached a terminal toast and you have opened representative results. Deleting a connected account also cascades its cloud-import job records, so you lose the server-side receipt and any unfinished work. ## Steps 1. Wait for **Import complete**, **Import failed**, or **Import cancelled**; do not disconnect while a progress card still says **Preparing import** or **Importing**. 2. Open the cloud-import workspace root; compare expected top-level folders, filenames, and one file’s contents with the provider source. 3. Resolve cloud-import omissions, duplicate-name failures, and policy refusals before removing the provider account needed to browse them again. 4. Open **Settings → Integrations**, locate the provider group, and match the exact account email used by the import. 5. Choose **Disconnect** on that row and wait for **Account disconnected — The account has been removed.** 6. Return to Files and open the verified sample again, confirming the Dosya copy remains independent of the provider connection. A user-initiated disconnect deletes Dosya’s stored account and tokens without sending an involuntary-disconnect notification. It does not delete completed files, refund their storage, or remove the provider application grant from the provider’s own security dashboard. Reconnect later if another import is needed. ## Expected result The chosen email disappears from **Connected accounts**, future browsing from that row is unavailable, and previously completed Dosya files still open. The old import job history is no longer available after the account row is deleted. ## Related guides - [Monitor import progress](/integrations/import-progress) - [Verify folder structure](/integrations/cloud-import-verify-folders)

title: Disconnect a cloud import account
summary: Remove a linked cloud account without mistaking token removal for rollback, and protect active transfer jobs by completing or cancelling them first.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/integrations.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/connected-accounts-card.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/accounts/[id].ts, apps/api/migrations/0148_control_plane_fks_to_object_tables.sql. body: The **Disconnect** action removes one linked provider identity immediately and has no confirmation dialog. Because import jobs reference that account with cascade deletion, finish or cancel active work before using it. ## Steps 1. Check **Files** and the provider page for an active import card associated with the account email you plan to remove. 2. Let the job finish, or choose its progress-card **Cancel** and wait for the **Import cancelled** toast. 3. Open **Settings → Integrations**, find the Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox group, and verify the complete email. 4. Choose the row’s **Disconnect** once; while the request runs the control shows a spinner and is disabled. 5. Require the success toast **Account disconnected** with **The account has been removed.** and confirm the row disappears. 6. Open an already imported file, then visit the provider’s security settings separately if you also want to revoke Dosya’s app grant there. If deletion fails, Dosya shows **Disconnect failed** and either the API message or **The account could not be disconnected.** The server returns **Account not found** for a stale or non-owned ID. Completed files are normal Dosya objects and remain; the linked account, its import job rows, and unfinished item records do not. ## Expected result The selected provider email is absent from Settings and its provider page. Existing copies remain readable, and the next import attempt requires reconnecting an account. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Monitor an import](/integrations/import-progress) - [Import from Google Drive](/integrations/google-drive) - [Review active Dosya sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Handle duplicate names during a cloud import
summary: Predict folder merges and file-name conflicts during cloud import, run a controlled sample, and avoid deleting either source before careful review.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover-d1.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.ts, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.repo.unit.test.ts. Production behavior for “Handle duplicate names during a cloud import” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Cloud imports do not apply a universal “keep both” rename rule. A live destination folder with the same name is reused, while a file name already occupied in that destination causes the incoming item to fail instead of replacing or renaming the existing file. ## Steps 1. In the provider, choose a small folder containing a filename that also exists in the Dosya workspace root or matching destination folder. 2. Record both versions’ size or content before import, since matching names alone cannot tell you which file is already in Dosya. 3. Select the duplicate file-name test folder, confirm the import root label, and start the job. 4. Watch the import completion toast; a duplicate file name increases its failed count even when other items complete. 5. Open the reused Dosya folder and compare the existing same-named file to your pre-import record; it must remain unchanged. 6. Rename one side deliberately before a second missing-only import if both files need to coexist in the same Dosya folder. Folder discovery searches for a live same-named folder under the same parent and maps the remote subtree into it. File insertion uses the destination’s unique name rule; a conflicting row produces an item failure after storage reservation is released. No automatic `(2)` suffix is created by the cloud-import engine. ## Expected result Existing content remains intact, non-conflicting children import into the created or reused folder, and the duplicate file is counted as failed. After a deliberate rename, a new import can create a separate row without overwriting either version. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Monitor an import](/integrations/import-progress)

title: Monitor and verify a cloud import
summary: Read discovery, byte progress, speed, ETA, and terminal toasts accurately, then verify the destination because active cards do not become history.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/import-progress-card.tsx, apps/web/src/stores/cloud-imports.ts, apps/web/src/components/layout/cloud-import-indicator.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts, apps/web/src/lib/import-rate.ts. Production behavior for “Monitor and verify a cloud import” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya polls cloud-import jobs every 5 seconds while at least one job is active. The main Files page shows all active providers; each provider setup page filters its card to that provider, and the sidebar ring follows imports across pages. ## Steps 1. Locate the card by its provider label and **from account@example.com** source line before interpreting its counts. 2. During discovery, read **Preparing import — N files found so far** and the indeterminate bar; totals and percentages are not final yet. 3. During transfer, use **Importing X of Y files** plus bytes; speed and a remaining-time estimate need two valid samples and disappear on a stall. 4. Keep Dosya open for 5-second import progress polls; the Integrations sidebar combines percentages for sized active jobs. 5. Read the terminal toast: **Import complete** includes completed, skipped, and failed counts; **Import failed** carries the job error; cancellation names its account. 6. Open the workspace root immediately after the toast and verify representative folders and files because the active card disappears at terminal status. The released web UI does not provide a persistent import-history screen or expose the API’s per-item problem list. Discovery bytes mean “found so far,” not a final denominator. Completion invalidates Files and Photos caches, but a source-versus-destination check is still required before deleting provider data. ## Expected result You can distinguish discovery from transfer, avoid treating an early count as final, and retain the terminal toast counts long enough to record them. Destination samples open successfully and agree with the source tree. ## Related guides - [Choose an import destination](/integrations/import-destination) - [Troubleshoot cloud imports](/troubleshooting/cloud-imports) - [Review exact duplicates](/files/review-duplicates) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Reconnect an expired cloud import account
summary: Recover a provider connection rejected by the remote service, complete a fresh OAuth round trip, and verify the same identity can browse again.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/use-cloud-browser.ts, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/browse.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/tokens.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/callback/[provider].ts. Production behavior for “Reconnect an expired cloud import account” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya shows the reconnect state only when browsing receives a 401 with `RECONNECT_REQUIRED`. Ordinary provider throttling instead shows a timed automatic retry, and a transient listing error offers **Retry**; neither should trigger OAuth. ## Steps 1. Open **Import files** and confirm the exact message **This account needs to be reconnected before you can import.** 2. Choose **Reconnect**, which starts the same signed OAuth flow used for a new connection. 3. At the cloud provider, select the stale Dosya row’s email, and approve read access. 4. Return to the provider page and verify **Connected accounts** shows that email once rather than assuming the callback alone succeeded. 5. Choose **Import** for that row and wait for the **Home** listing to load without the reconnect warning. 6. Browse one known remote item, then cancel the picker or run a small import to confirm the refreshed token works end to end. Account storage upserts on the provider’s stable identity, including refreshed access and refresh tokens, so reconnecting the same provider account updates its row rather than intentionally creating a duplicate. A different provider identity creates a separate connected-account row. ## Expected result The picker lists the reauthorized account’s root and no longer displays **Reconnect**. The connected account email remains the intended identity, and a browse or test import succeeds. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Monitor an import](/integrations/import-progress)

title: Retry only failed cloud-import items
summary: Recover failed cloud-import files with a missing-only second import, since the released web app has no per-item retry button or problem list.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/[id]/index.ts, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx. Production behavior for “Retry only failed cloud-import items” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: There is no released **Retry failed items** action. The server retries ordinary item errors internally up to three attempts, retires deterministic policy refusals immediately, and reports terminal counts through the completion toast. ## Steps 1. Record the **Import complete** toast’s failed and skipped counts before it fades; a job-level failure instead shows **Import failed** and its error text. 2. Correct the likely cause first: free storage, allow the final extension, raise the workspace file-size limit, resolve a same-name conflict, or reconnect provider access. 3. Compare the provider selection with the Dosya workspace root and make a list containing only files that are absent or known to have failed. 4. Open the same cloud-provider account and select each failed or missing source directly instead of reselecting the original folder. 5. Start this new import and monitor its own card; it is a separate job, not a continuation of the previous receipt. 6. After the retry import’s toast, open every recovered file and confirm completed originals were not reselected into name collisions. The API can return up to 50 failed or skipped problem rows for a job, but the current web client does not render that endpoint. Provider 429 responses and workspace migrations use job-level backoff without consuming an item attempt. Other transient failures consume one attempt and become permanent on the third strike. ## Expected result A new, narrowly selected job imports the formerly missing files after their cause is fixed. Previously completed items remain single copies because the retry selection excluded them. ## Related guides - [Monitor import progress](/integrations/import-progress) - [Verify folder structure](/integrations/cloud-import-verify-folders)

title: Review duplicate names after a cloud import
summary: Audit same-name outcomes after import, distinguish merged folders from failed files, and retain both sources until content identity is proven.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover-d1.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/types.ts, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts. Production behavior for “Review duplicate names after a cloud import” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Review duplicates with the engine’s actual two rules in mind: same-named live folders under one parent are merged, while a same-named file in one destination folder blocks the imported file. The completion toast exposes counts, not the conflicting filenames. ## Steps 1. Save the terminal toast counts, especially any failed value, before navigating away from the import result. 2. Open the imported top-level folder and identify places where a remote folder name matched a folder that already existed in Dosya. 3. Compare the provider child list with the merged Dosya folder, checking names and opening content rather than relying only on item totals. 4. For every expected file that is absent, look for a same-named Dosya row in that exact folder and inspect its size, date, and contents. 5. Keep both the provider source and existing Dosya file until you decide whether to rename the source, rename the destination, or retain only one. 6. After making a unique name, import only the missing source and verify the second row opens before deleting anything elsewhere. A file collision is an item failure, not an overwrite receipt, and no conflict copy is synthesized. Reused folders keep their existing identity and dates; only newly created imported folders receive provider source dates when the provider supplies them. Dropbox exposes no folder timestamps. ## Expected result Each expected source file is either present as a verified Dosya copy or accounted for by a same-name failure. No existing file was replaced, and any merged folder’s combined children have been consciously reviewed. ## Related guides - [Monitor import progress](/integrations/import-progress) - [Verify folder structure](/integrations/cloud-import-verify-folders)

title: Review a cloud-import picker selection
summary: Audit every selected import root before submission, account for paging and exports, and avoid assuming a checked folder shows all descendants.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/use-cloud-browser.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover.ts. Production behavior for “Review a cloud-import picker selection” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The picker retains checked roots while you navigate within one account, but it does not expand a checked folder into a visible preflight list. Recursive discovery happens only after import starts, so review folder contents manually when scope matters. ## Steps 1. Confirm the provider email above the browser and start from the **Home** breadcrumb for a predictable review. 2. Visit each folder you may select, use **Load more** through every page, and note unsupported rows or provider-native export extensions. 3. Return through the cloud-import breadcrumb and check the intended folder root; that single check includes its descendant tree. 4. Uncheck each mistaken cloud-import file or folder, and watch the picker footer count change immediately. 5. Compare the count with your root-level checklist and require the footer to say **importing into workspace root**. 6. Choose **Import** only after the source email, selected roots, and destination label all agree; otherwise use **Cancel** and restart cleanly. The service accepts at most 500 selected roots in one request and refuses zero roots with **Select at least one file or folder**. That limit is not a cap on descendants inside checked folders. Reopening the dialog or changing provider accounts clears both navigation and selection. ## Expected result The submitted roots are exactly those on the checklist, provider-native conversions are anticipated, and recursive folders contain no surprise area you skipped during review. The start toast identifies the account used. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Browse provider files](/integrations/cloud-import-browse-provider)

title: Import one provider folder as a test
summary: Run a low-risk provider-folder import that exercises recursive discovery, conversion, permissions, and destination rules before a larger move.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover-d1.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.ts. Production behavior for “Import one provider folder as a test” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A useful test folder contains a few small ordinary files, one nested folder, and—if relevant—one provider-native document. Because released provider imports target the active workspace root, give the test root a unique name. ## Steps 1. Create or choose a non-confidential provider folder with a unique name and known child count; keep its total small enough to inspect manually. 2. Switch Dosya to the intended workspace and verify your role has the `upload_files` permission required by cloud-import jobs. 3. Open the matching provider account, inspect the test folder, and note every conversion label or **Cannot be imported** row. 4. Return to its parent, select the test folder itself, confirm `1 selected — importing into workspace root`, and choose **Import**. 5. Observe discovery until it changes from **Preparing import** to transfer, then retain the terminal toast’s completed, skipped, and failed totals. 6. Open the new root folder in Dosya, traverse the nested branch, and download or preview each representative file before scaling up. Recursive discovery preserves the remote hierarchy by creating or reusing same-named folders. Unsupported provider objects are skipped; exported native documents gain the displayed Office or PDF extension. Workspace extension, per-file size, and available-storage policies still apply to every discovered file. ## Expected result The uniquely named test root appears in the active workspace root, its nested hierarchy is intact, and every supported sample opens. Any skip or failure is explained before a larger import begins. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Browse provider files](/integrations/cloud-import-browse-provider)

title: Troubleshoot a cloud import
summary: Isolate a cloud import failure with one supported item, the exact destination and job receipt, then handle reconnect, quota or partial completion safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/use-cloud-browser.ts, apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/import-progress-card.tsx, apps/web/src/stores/cloud-imports.ts, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/[id]/cancel.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/sweep.ts. Production behavior for “Troubleshoot a cloud import” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Cloud imports expose provider browsing, destination authorization, discovery, and transfer as separate stages. Test one supported item to identify which stage failed. ## Steps 1. Open Google Drive, OneDrive, or Dropbox import and confirm the connected email. Use **Connect an account** for **No account connected yet.** or **Reconnect** only when the picker says the account needs reconnection. 2. At **Home**, select one ordinary supported file. Rows marked **Cannot be imported** are disabled; a provider-native document may instead say **will import as `.ext`**. If provider browsing is rate-limited, the picker displays its retry countdown and retries automatically. 3. Before **Import**, read the footer ` selected - importing into `. The destination is chosen outside the provider browser and requires workspace membership plus `upload_files`. 4. Start the test. Respect **Select at least one file or folder** and the maximum of 500 selected roots; preserve **Import failed to start** and its exact API message if no job is created. 5. Follow the active card, polled every five seconds, through **Preparing import** and **Importing X of Y files**. At a terminal state the card disappears: **Import complete** reports completed, skipped, and failed counts; **Import failed** shows the job error; **Import cancelled** identifies the provider or account source. A picker rate-limit countdown defaults to 30 seconds when the provider supplies no valid delay. 6. Verify completed Dosya files before removing provider originals. If the completion toast reports failed or skipped items, make a new narrow source selection from your own source inventory; the web UI does not expose their names from the job-detail response. ## Expected result The controlled file reaches the named destination, or the job exposes a specific reconnect, unsupported-type, membership, **No upload permission**, **Destination folder not found**, quota, or transfer result. Imports stream in 10 MiB chunks, cap one buffered stream at 32 MiB, and allow three item attempts; a provider rate limit does not consume an attempt. Completed jobs can still report failed or skipped items. Cancelling skips pending or processing work and aborts active multipart state, but already completed files remain. A terminal job refuses cancellation with **Job is already ``**; cancellation does not roll back imported files. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Choose an import destination](/integrations/import-destination) - [Monitor and verify an import](/integrations/import-progress) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Verify imported folder structure
summary: Validate imported hierarchy with source-to-Dosya checkpoints, including merged names, skipped objects, conversions, and terminal job counts.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover-d1.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.ts, apps/web/src/lib/cloud-import-toasts.ts. Production behavior for “Verify imported folder structure” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Verify folder structure after the terminal toast, not during discovery, because totals grow while the provider tree is walked. Use several checkpoints across depth rather than trusting a single top-level count. ## Steps 1. Record the source’s selected roots and a child-count checkpoint at the root, a middle folder, and the deepest meaningful branch. 2. Wait for **Import complete** or another terminal toast, and save its completed, skipped, and failed numbers. 3. Open the active Dosya workspace root and match each selected remote folder to its created or reused top-level folder. 4. Follow the three imported folder checkpoints; compare names, unsupported skips, and native-document export extensions. 5. Open at least one file from each checkpoint and verify its contents; a visible filename alone does not prove transfer integrity. 6. Investigate absent imported files for same-name collisions and workspace policies before disconnecting the cloud provider or deleting its source. A selected folder is mapped before its descendants are discovered, and live same-name folders under the same parent are reused. Provider source timestamps are stored when available, but Dropbox folders do not supply them and directly selected roots lack transmitted dates. Terminal cards are not retained as history in the web UI. ## Expected result Every reviewed source path resolves to the intended Dosya folder, supported files open, and differences are accounted for by conversion, skip, collision, cancellation, or policy. The provider stays connected until that reconciliation is complete. ## Related guides - [Connect a cloud account](/integrations/connect-cloud-account) - [Monitor an import](/integrations/import-progress)

title: Verify imported folder hierarchy
summary: Confirm that imported roots and nested folders retain their provider hierarchy, while accounting for renamed, merged, exported, skipped, or failed items.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/cloud-import/provider-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/cloud/imports/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/discover-d1.ts, apps/api/src/lib/cloud-import/transfer.ts, and apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx. No production provider account was used.
body: Selecting a provider folder imports that folder as a real root under the Dosya destination and walks its descendants. You do not need to expand every provider level before checking the folder. A separately selected file lands directly in the destination instead. ## Before you start Record a small source manifest with each selected root name, one representative nested path, and one leaf filename. Include two roots that contain the same child-folder name when possible; this proves those branches remain separated by their parents. Wait for **Import complete** or note any **failed** and **skipped** totals. Cancelling or closing after partial progress does not remove already delivered files, so a partially completed job cannot prove the full hierarchy. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the workspace that was active when the import began. Current provider integration dialogs submit to that workspace's root. 2. Find every checked provider folder at the top level in Dosya. A live same-name folder can be reused, so confirm the imported branch by its descendants. A direct checked file should be beside those roots at workspace root. 3. Open each imported root and follow the representative path from your manifest, level by level. Compare the parent at every step rather than searching only for the leaf filename. 4. For two roots containing a child such as `2026`, confirm each child remains under its own imported parent. The importer maps folders by provider identity and local parent, so sibling trees should not collapse into one cross-root folder. 5. Open a delivered file's detail panel when attribution is uncertain. **Source** and **Account** identify the provider and connected account used for the import. 6. Compare cloud-import missing items with the completion toast's **failed** and **skipped** counts before starting another job. ## Expected differences Dosya sanitizes imported folder names before creating them. Forward and back slashes become hyphens; leading dots, hyphens, and whitespace are trimmed; an empty result becomes `Untitled`; and folder names are limited to **255 characters**. Compare the resulting name using those rules rather than treating every normalized name as data loss. If a live folder with the same name already exists under the same parent, the importer reuses it. The new content can therefore merge into a pre-existing destination folder. This is not a fresh snapshot directory, so inspect existing content before importing into a populated workspace. Provider-native documents are exported to the format shown beside the picker entry, such as PDF or Microsoft Office formats. Unsupported descendants are skipped. When a file with the same name already occupies the destination folder, the importer does not overwrite it; after its attempts fail, it appears in the failed count. ## Troubleshooting - A root is absent but some children are at the workspace root: confirm whether you checked individual files instead of the folder itself. - A branch stops early: review the terminal skipped/failed figures, then check whether the provider item was unsupported or a destination filename already existed. - Content appears inside an older same-name folder: the find-or-create behavior intentionally reuses a live matching folder at that parent. - A source folder changed after selection: the job walks provider state while running; use the recorded manifest and run a new controlled import for later provider changes. ## Expected result Each selected folder maps to its named Dosya root, which may be a reused live folder; supported descendants retain their parent-child relationships, and every exception is explained by sanitation, reuse, conversion, skipping, or failure. ## Related guides - [Monitor import progress](/integrations/import-progress) - [Verify folder structure](/integrations/cloud-import-verify-folders)

title: Add a comment to a Dosya file
summary: Add a file comment with a page or playback anchor, mentions, and clear review context; then confirm its author, timestamp, and recipient delivery state.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/components/comments/mention-composer.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/index.ts on 2026-10-14. These source-backed instructions are not a production smoke test.
body: Comments keep review decisions beside the file they concern. In the web viewer, a comment can also capture the PDF page or media playback position that was active when you focused the composer. **Before you start.** Sign in to the workspace that owns the file. You need workspace membership, file access, and the `access_files` permission. A full-lock folder must be unlocked first; the file’s own download lock does not block its discussion. ## Steps 1. Open **Files**, select the item, and open its preview. Choose **Comments** in the inspector. The count beside the tab is the number of messages already attached to this file. 2. For a PDF, display the page you mean before focusing the composer. For audio or video, seek to the relevant moment first. Dosya records a PDF page from 1 upward or a whole-millisecond media position from 0 upward. 3. In **Write a comment… Use @ to mention**, enter the decision, requested change, and enough location detail to recognize it later. The body is trimmed and must contain text. The maximum is 5,000 characters; a counter appears after 4,500. 4. Type `@` to choose a colleague who can see this file. The picker waits 150 ms after typing, searches at most 50 eligible members, and shows up to 10 choices. One comment may mention at most 20 people. 5. Choose **Send**, or press Enter. Use Shift+Enter for a new line. Enter during an input-method composition does not submit. 6. Confirm the new entry shows your name and timestamp. If you attached a page or playback point, use its anchor to return to the same context. **What other people receive.** Each eligible mentioned member gets one comment notice. If you are not the file owner, the owner is notified too; other thread participants can receive a notice unless they were already covered as owner or mention. Folder-comment notifications are different and are not used by this file workflow. **If posting fails.** `Comment body is required` means trimming left no text. Shorten a body that triggers `Comment too long (max 5000 characters)`. `Too many mentions (max 20)` requires removing recipients. The viewer otherwise reports **Could not post comment**; the standalone page reports **Comment failed — Your comment could not be posted.** Refresh before retrying so a delayed success is not duplicated. ## Expected result The comment appears once in oldest-to-newest order with your identity and time. Its optional page, playback point, and version association stay attached to that message; inaccessible mention candidates are omitted without exposing them. ## Related guides - [Review the complete file-comment workflow](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Open a file in the preview viewer](/files/preview-files)

title: Commenting on a file and managing replies
summary: Open a file conversation, post and reply to feedback, and understand who can read, edit or delete each comment.
verification: Verified the current English file conversation page, web/API source and focused comment tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use an isolated local owner workspace with controlled current-API fixtures and fictional people and comments. The review confirmed chronological threads, replies, 5,000-character validation, author-only editing, author/admin/owner deletion, edited labels, target visibility and folder-lock gates, and plain-text rendering. Production notifications and multi-user timing were not exercised.
body: Open a file's **Comments** action to start a workspace conversation about that file. Comments appear in chronological order, replies quote the comment they answer, and your own messages provide edit and delete controls. File comments are visible to workspace members who can access the underlying item. They are separate from questions and replies on public Help Center articles. ## Before you start - Select the workspace that contains the file and confirm your role can access **Files**. - The file must be visible within your permitted folder tree. Hidden-item and locked-folder rules also protect its conversation. - Use comments for feedback about the file. Do not paste passwords, private sharing URLs, API keys or other secrets. - A comment can contain up to 5,000 characters. The composer shows a counter when you approach that limit. ## Steps: open the file conversation 1. Open **Files** and find the intended file. 2. Open its menu and choose **Comments**. A comment-count badge can also open the conversation when the file already has messages. 3. Check the file name at the top of the page. On larger screens, the right panel also shows file details and preview or download actions. 4. Read the thread before adding feedback. Messages are grouped by date and author, with the oldest first. ## Post a comment or reply 1. Enter a short, actionable note in **Write a message…**. 2. Select the send button, or press **Ctrl+Enter** on Windows and Linux or **Command+Enter** on macOS. 3. To answer a particular comment, point to its message and choose **Reply**. 4. Check the **Replying to** bar above the composer. It shows the author and a preview of the comment you selected. 5. Write and send the response. Use the close control in the reply bar if you want to return to an ordinary top-level comment. ## Edit or delete a comment 1. Point to one of your own message bubbles. 2. Choose **Edit**, update the text, then choose **Save**. The thread marks the message **edited**. 3. Choose **Delete** when your own comment should be removed. 4. Workspace owners and admins can also delete another person's comment when moderation is needed. Other members cannot edit someone else's text and cannot delete it unless their workspace role has that administrative authority. 5. Review replies before deleting a parent. Deleting a comment also removes replies attached to it. ## Visibility and permission limits Comments follow the underlying file or folder's workspace access. A member must still belong to the workspace, have access to Files, remain within any folder confinement and pass the item's hidden and parent-folder lock checks. A file's own password lock does not turn comments into a public discussion. Comments remain an authenticated workspace feature. Public share recipients do not receive this workspace conversation through the sharing link. Comment text is displayed as plain text with line breaks. A URL typed into a comment is not a privileged sharing mechanism and does not change access to its destination. ## Expected result The new message appears in the selected file's conversation. Replies identify their parent, edits carry an **edited** label, and only supported author or moderator controls are available. Other permitted members see the same thread after it refreshes. ## Troubleshooting **Comments is missing.** Confirm you are in the live Files view and your role can access Files. Open the file menu or its comment-count badge. **The thread says the file cannot be found.** The file may have moved outside your permitted folder tree, become hidden from you or been removed. Ask the file owner to confirm its current location and visibility. **The thread reports a locked folder.** Unlock the protected parent folder, then reopen the conversation. A thread can contain details about the file, so the parent-folder gate applies to comments too. **Edit or Delete is absent.** You can edit only your own comment. You can delete your own comment; deleting another person's message requires owner or admin authority. **A long comment will not send.** Reduce it to 5,000 characters or fewer. Attach detailed work in the file itself and use the comment to explain the requested action. **A message did not appear.** Check the connection, reload the thread and avoid submitting the same text repeatedly until you know whether the first request succeeded. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I edit or delete my own comment? Yes. Point to your message to reveal **Edit** and **Delete**. An edited message is labelled, and deleting a parent removes its replies. ### Who can see a file comment? Workspace members who can access the underlying item can read its thread. Hidden items, folder confinement and locked parent folders can remove access. ### Are Help Center questions part of this thread? No. File comments are workspace collaboration content. Help Center questions are a separate, moderated support surface. ## Related guides - [Locking or hiding a file and understanding access](/files/lock-and-hide) - [Using version history and restoring an earlier version](/files/version-history) - [Organizing files with folders, favourites and groups](/files/organize-files) - [Contacting support with useful information](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Correct your own file comment
summary: Edit a comment you authored, preserve its original file anchor, update mentions safely, and verify the corrected text without duplicating the thread.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/[id].ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/comments.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: Edit an existing message when its meaning needs a small correction. Editing keeps the comment in place and preserves the page, playback position, and file-version anchor captured when it was first posted. **Who can edit.** The current web interface shows **Edit** only on comments you authored. You must still be a member who can access the target file; the API rejects another author’s message with `You can only edit your own comments`. ## Steps 1. Open the affected file, select **Comments**, and locate your message by its text, author, and time. On the standalone Comments page, edited entries are marked `edited`. 2. Open the comment menu and choose **Edit**. The composer changes to **Save** and offers **Cancel**. 3. Correct the smallest necessary portion. A saved body must contain text after trimming and must be no longer than 5,000 characters. 4. Review any `@mentions`. Up to 20 eligible members can remain. A person must still be able to see the file to be accepted as a mention. 5. Choose **Save**. Confirm the message itself changes and no second top-level comment appears. 6. Reopen the page or media anchor. Editing cannot move the original anchor to a different PDF page, playback time, or version; post a new comment when the review context changed. **Notification behavior.** A text-only correction does not repeat the normal owner and thread-participant notices. Newly added eligible mentions are notified, which is useful when the correction assigns a new reviewer. **If saving fails.** `Comment body is required` indicates an empty edit. `Comment too long (max 5000 characters)` requires shortening it. `Too many mentions (max 20)` means the recipient list must be reduced. If access or membership changed, reopen the correct workspace and verify the file is visible before retrying. Choose **Cancel** if you cannot confirm the intended change; the stored comment remains as it was. ## Expected result Your existing message displays the corrected body and retains its original thread position and context anchor. Only newly introduced valid mentions can create fresh mention notifications. ## Related guides - [Understand file-comment authorship and replies](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Find the exact discussion before editing](/files/comments-open-file-thread)

title: Delete an accidental comment
summary: Remove an accidental comment after verifying its file, author, and replies; understand the immediate cascade and the lack of comment recovery.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx and apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/[id].ts on 2026-10-14. The deletion flow has not been retested on production.
body: Delete an accidental post only after matching the file and message. The current web control deletes immediately: there is no confirmation dialog or comment trash. **Understand the effect first.** Deleting a top-level comment also deletes every reply beneath it. This is irreversible through Dosya’s interface and API. The file, its versions, and unrelated comments remain. ## Steps 1. Open the file named in the accidental message and select **Comments**. Match the text, your author identity, timestamp, and any page or playback anchor. 2. Check whether replies sit beneath the message. Copy any context the team still needs into a new comment before removal, because deleting the root removes the reply chain too. 3. Open your comment’s menu and choose **Delete** once. Do not expect an extra confirmation step. 4. Wait for the entry to leave the thread. Refresh and confirm the same message remains absent while the surrounding discussion and file are still present. 5. If the click appears to fail, refresh before trying again. A delayed deletion followed by a second click can make it harder to tell which message you targeted. **Permissions.** The web app exposes deletion on your own messages. The API also permits a workspace owner or administrator to remove another author’s comment, but the current comment menu does not expose that administrative action. An author who is no longer a current member cannot delete the old message through this flow. **If removal fails.** The standalone page reports **Delete failed — Your comment could not be deleted.** The viewer can show **Could not delete**. Recheck the active workspace, file visibility, and authorship. There is no restore button after a successful deletion; reconstructing the message requires posting it again, and it receives a new time and identity record. ## Expected result Only the selected comment disappears, unless it was a thread root with replies, in which case that entire reply branch disappears. File bytes, versions, and other discussion branches do not change. ## Related guides - [Check reply structure before removing a comment](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Locate the file-bound thread for cleanup](/files/comments-open-file-thread)

title: Delete your own file comment
summary: Delete a comment you wrote, confirm the author-only control and reply impact, and verify that the file and unrelated discussion remain intact.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/comments.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/[id].ts on 2026-10-14. No production delete was run.
body: You can remove a comment you authored while it is still accessible in the workspace. The action affects the discussion record, not the underlying file. **Before deleting.** Make sure you are signed into the account that wrote the message. The interface hides **Delete** on other authors’ comments. Current membership, `access_files`, the confinement boundary, and an unlocked enclosing full-lock folder still govern access to the thread. ## Steps 1. Preview the file and choose **Comments**, or open its standalone Comments page from the Files context action **Comments**. 2. Find your message by author and timestamp. If it has replies, read them before continuing: deleting a root comment cascades to those replies. 3. Open the message menu and choose **Delete**. The released web app does not ask you to confirm. 4. Confirm the entry vanishes. Reopen the file preview and verify the file still loads and unrelated messages remain. 5. Refresh once. If the deleted text returns, the request did not complete; do not repeatedly delete neighboring entries. **Failure and recovery.** The viewer uses **Could not delete** for an unsuccessful request; the standalone page uses **Delete failed — Your comment could not be deleted.** Loss of membership or file visibility can cause the operation to fail even though you originally wrote the text. A successful deletion cannot be undone. Posting the wording again creates a different comment with a new timestamp and does not restore deleted replies. **Administrative scope.** Owners and administrators are accepted by the delete API for other people’s comments, but that capability is not surfaced on those messages in the current web UI. This guide covers the author control that users can see. ## Expected result Your chosen comment is absent after reload. Its reply descendants are also absent when it was a thread root, while the file, versions, shares, and separate comment branches remain available. ## Related guides - [Learn which file comments can be removed](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Verify the file itself in Preview](/files/preview-files)

title: Edit your own file comment
summary: Edit a comment you authored, keep or change its mentions, and understand save limits, access checks, failure behavior, and the lack of undo.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, mention-composer.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/comments.tsx, apps/mobile/app/comments.tsx, apps/mobile/src/comments/thread.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/comments/gate.ts, and route unit tests. No production comment was edited.
body: Editing replaces the stored body of a comment you authored. It does not create a visible revision history, change the comment's parent, or move its time or PDF-page anchor. The available editor depends on where you opened the conversation. ## Before you start - Open the correct file conversation and find a comment posted by the signed-in account. - Only the author sees **Edit**. Workspace owners and admins may delete another person's comment, but they cannot edit it; an author must also remain a member of that workspace. - Copy important original wording elsewhere first. The product stores the replacement text and offers no comment revision viewer. ## Steps 1. Choose the editing surface that is already showing the conversation: - On the dedicated browser **Comments** page, hover your bubble and select **Edit**. Its plain textarea changes the body only; use **Save** or **Cancel**. - In the browser file-preview comments panel, select **Edit** beneath your comment. This opens the mention-aware composer with the existing body and current mention identities. - On mobile, select the inline **Edit** action below your own bubble. The replacement field, **Cancel**, and **Save** stay inside that bubble. 2. Correct the prefilled text. The trimmed saved body must contain 1 to 5,000 characters on every surface. 3. In the file-preview panel only, review @mentions. Its counter appears above 4,500 characters, Escape cancels when the mention picker is closed, and Save sends the active mention list. At most 20 distinct recipients are accepted, and newly mentioned people must be able to see the target. 4. On the dedicated Comments page or mobile, save the body-only edit. Because those clients omit `mention_user_ids`, the API preserves the comment's stored mentions instead of clearing or revalidating them. 5. Wait for the thread to reload and compare the displayed body with the intended correction. The dedicated browser Comments page and mobile show an **edited** marker; the file-preview panel refreshes the text without rendering that marker. The API returns “You can only edit your own comments” for a non-author, “Comment not found” for a missing ID, “Comment body is required” for empty text, and “Comment too long (max 5000 characters)” above the limit. Every edit requires the author and current workspace membership. Only the file-preview panel's mention-aware request also rechecks Files access, confinement, hidden state, and enclosing folder locks. ## Expected result The same comment ID and thread position now show the trimmed replacement body. Its creation time, parent relationship, and anchor remain intact; the update time and edited state change. There is no one-click undo. To recover an earlier version, edit again and paste wording you saved separately. ## Troubleshooting **Edit is absent.** Verify that the comment's author is your current account. Administrators do not receive an override for rewriting somebody else's words. **Save failed after access changed.** First confirm you are still a workspace member. A file-preview edit that includes mentions must also pass the file visibility gates; restore legitimate access or remove the mention change before retrying from a body-only surface. **Your correction remains in the field.** That means the request did not succeed. The browser keeps edit mode and mobile retains its edit text on failure, so resolve the shown error before trying again. ## Related guides - [Comment on a file](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Open the comment thread for a file
summary: Open the discussion for the intended file from Preview or Files, verify workspace and filename context, and resolve loading or access failures.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/comments.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/index.ts on 2026-10-14. Production routing was not invoked.
body: Dosya exposes the same file discussion in the preview inspector and on a standalone Comments page. Use the file name and workspace context to avoid responding in a similarly named item’s thread. **Access rules.** You must be a workspace member with `access_files`. Folder confinement and hidden-item visibility apply, and a still-locked enclosing full-lock folder blocks access. A lock placed directly on the file does not by itself hide its comments. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, identify the item by name and parent folder. Open its preview, then choose the inspector tab **Comments**; the tab also displays the current message count. 2. Alternatively, open the file’s context menu and choose **Comments**. Dosya routes to `/comments` with the file ID, workspace ID, and display name in the query. 3. On the standalone page, confirm the title and the right-side **FILE DETAILS** values before reading or replying. Messages are displayed chronologically and grouped under **Today**, **Yesterday**, or a calendar date. 4. If someone sent a direct comment URL, switch to the workspace named in the link before assuming the thread is empty. 5. Refresh and verify that the same discussion returns for the same file ID. A filename alone is not a unique identifier because different folders can contain files with the same name. **If the thread does not load.** Return to Files and confirm the item is visible. A membership, `access_files`, confinement, hidden-file, or parent full-lock restriction can make the target unavailable. Unlock the enclosing protected folder through its normal flow when authorized. If the file moved, opening it from its new folder produces the same thread because comments follow the file ID. **Composer differences.** The viewer says **Write a comment… Use @ to mention** and the standalone page says **Write a message...**. Both attach the resulting text to the selected file. Do not use an empty thread as proof that the similarly named file is correct; check its details first. ## Expected result The page or inspector shows the messages attached to the intended file, oldest first, with the correct workspace and file metadata. Refreshing preserves that association. ## Related guides - [Use the controls inside a file discussion](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Inspect the selected file before commenting](/files/preview-files)

title: Preserve review context before replacing a file
summary: Record review context before uploading a new file version, preserve page or playback anchors, and distinguish earlier-version comments afterward.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/comments/anchor.ts on 2026-10-14. Production version uploads were not tested.
body: Comments survive a new version upload, but an anchored comment continues to describe the version that was current when the anchor was created. Record the decision before replacing content so later readers can separate old feedback from the new file. **What an anchor stores.** A top-level PDF comment can keep a page number of 1 or greater. Audio and video comments can keep a whole-millisecond position starting at 0. Dosya also records the current version number with that anchor. Replies do not carry their own anchors. ## Steps 1. Open the current file version and choose **Comments**. Navigate to the relevant page or playback position before focusing the new-comment field; focusing media commentary pauses playback while capturing the position. 2. Summarize what was approved, what remains open, and what the replacement is expected to change. Mention an eligible reviewer if the handoff needs attention. 3. Send the comment and use its page or time control to verify the location. Keep the comment under 5,000 characters and limit mentions to 20. 4. Upload the replacement through the file’s version workflow only after the context is visible in the thread. 5. Reopen **Comments** on the new version. When an anchored comment belongs to an earlier revision, Dosya labels it `vN`; selecting it reports **Comment was left on vN** rather than pretending the old position belongs to the current bytes. 6. Add a fresh current-version comment if the new document or media needs a new anchor. Editing the old message cannot move its original version anchor. **What remains and what changes.** Uploading a version does not delete the existing discussion. The old comment text, author, time, and version anchor remain. Page numbers and media positions may no longer describe the same visual content in the replacement, so readers should follow the `vN` marker rather than infer equivalence. **If context is missing.** Check that you posted to the correct file ID before uploading.
