If the old version comment was deleted, it cannot be restored through comment history; write a new message that explicitly identifies the earlier version and source of the recovered information. ## Expected result The replacement becomes the current file version while the prior review remains readable and visibly associated with its original `vN` context. New feedback can use a new current-version anchor. ## Related guides - [Understand anchors in file discussions](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Reopen the same thread after versioning](/files/comments-open-file-thread)

title: Reply to the correct file comment
summary: Reply beneath the right parent comment, confirm the file and discussion context, and understand reply anchors, permissions, and notifications.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/comments.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/comments.ts on 2026-10-14. Production notifications were not sent.
body: A reply should stay beneath the message it answers. Verify the parent and file before typing, especially when several files have similar review discussions. **Before replying.** You need current workspace membership, `access_files`, visibility of the target, and access through its folder boundary. The parent must belong to the same file; the API rejects a mismatched or missing parent with `Parent comment not found`. ## Steps 1. Open the file and select **Comments**. Match the parent by author, timestamp, text, and any `vN`, PDF-page, or media-time context. 2. Choose **Reply** on that specific message. In Preview, confirm **Replying to {name}** appears above the bottom composer. On the standalone Comments page, verify the separate **Replying to** bar above its single bottom composer names and quotes the intended parent. 3. Write a focused answer. The trimmed body must be nonempty and no longer than 5,000 characters. You may mention up to 20 eligible people. 4. Choose **Send** or press Enter; use Shift+Enter for a line break. 5. Confirm Preview nests the message below the intended parent, or that the standalone page shows the correct parent quote on the new message. Refresh and check the relationship again. **Reply anchors.** Replies inherit their conversational context from the parent and cannot carry a separate page, playback, or version anchor. The API returns `Replies cannot carry an anchor` if a client tries to attach one. To discuss a different page, time, or version, create a new top-level comment from that location. **Who is notified.** Eligible mentions receive one notice each. The file owner can receive a notice when someone else replies, and existing thread participants can be notified unless already included as owner or mention. A participant who can no longer see the file is not exposed through the mention picker. **If the answer lands incorrectly.** Delete your own reply and post it under the right parent. Deletion is immediate and has no undo; if the reply itself acquired descendants, deleting it also removes that branch. `Comment body is required`, `Comment too long (max 5000 characters)`, and `Too many mentions (max 20)` describe the corrective action directly. ## Expected result The new message appears once with the chosen parent relationship: nested in Preview or carrying that parent’s quote on the standalone page. It has no independent content anchor, and only eligible recipients can receive its comment notifications. ## Related guides - [Compare top-level comments with replies](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Confirm the file thread before answering](/files/comments-open-file-thread)

title: Reply to a file comment
summary: Reply beneath a top-level file comment, use mentions within current limits, and recover safely when access changes or the post request fails.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 with apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, mention-composer.tsx, api.ts, apps/mobile/app/comments.tsx, apps/mobile/src/comments/api.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/comments/gate.ts, and comment route tests. Production comments were not posted.
body: A reply belongs to the same file thread as its parent. The browser nests replies under a top-level comment; mobile keeps a flat chat layout and shows a quote from the parent. You need current workspace membership, Files page access, and visibility of the target file. Folder confinement, hidden rules, and an unopened full-lock ancestor can refuse the thread. ## Before you start - Open the file preview and select **Comments**, or open **Comments** from the file's action menu on mobile. - Confirm the filename and parent author's name before composing. - A comment body is limited to 5,000 characters. The counter appears after 4,500 characters; the send control is disabled for blank or over-limit text. ## Steps 1. In the browser, choose **Reply** below the top-level comment. Replies themselves do not expose another Reply button there. 2. On mobile, press the reply action on the desired bubble; mobile permits selecting any visible comment as the parent. 3. Confirm the composer says **Replying to NAME**. Use **cancel** in the browser or **Cancel reply** on mobile if it names the wrong person. 4. Enter the response. In the browser, typing @ searches eligible people after a 150 ms debounce; at most 20 distinct other users can be submitted. 5. Browser users select **Send** or press Enter; Shift+Enter inserts a line break. Mobile users tap **Send comment**. 6. Wait for success before leaving the file. Browser adds the returned comment to the current thread; mobile clears the composer and reloads only after the server accepts it. Replies cannot carry a time or PDF-page anchor. The server trims surrounding whitespace, checks that the parent still exists on the same file, and answers “Parent comment not found” with 404 if it was deleted or belongs elsewhere. Mention recipients who cannot see the file are silently omitted to avoid exposing restricted membership. ## Expected result The accepted response appears once with the signed-in author and its parent relationship. A browser reply sits under the root comment; the mobile row quotes the parent author and excerpt. Posting is reversible by deleting your reply. Be careful when deleting a top-level parent: the confirmation warns that its replies are deleted too, and the server removes that subtree. ## Troubleshooting **The conversation will not load.** Browser shows “Couldn't load comments”; mobile shows “Could not load this conversation.” Retry after confirming workspace, Files access, target visibility, and folder unlock state. **Send stayed disabled.** Remove whitespace-only content or reduce the trimmed response to 5,000 characters. **The post failed.** Both clients preserve the typed body, and the reply target remains selected. Read the error toast, correct access or connectivity, and submit once rather than duplicating the draft. ## Related guides - [Comment on a file](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Start a clear file review thread
summary: Start a useful file review with a precise request, page or time context, eligible mentions, and a clear check that responses stay on one thread.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/comments/mention-composer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/comments/mentionable.ts on 2026-10-14. Production delivery was not exercised.
body: Start a review with one actionable top-level comment. A precise request gives replies a stable parent and keeps the decision attached to the file rather than scattered across separate messages. **Prepare the context.** Open the exact file and current version. For a PDF, display the target page. For audio or video, seek to the relevant moment. Do not include passwords, recovery codes, payment details, or other secrets in a comment or screenshot. ## Steps 1. In Preview, choose **Comments** and verify the file name and workspace. Use the general composer, not **Reply**, to start a new top-level thread. 2. State the location, observed issue, requested change, and acceptance check. Example: “Page 4, pricing table: align the annual total with the monthly column; reply after the PDF export is replaced.” 3. Add `@mentions` only for people who need to act. The search begins after a 150 ms pause, evaluates up to 50 eligible workspace candidates, and displays no more than 10 matches. The query is capped at 64 characters. 4. Keep the complete body within 5,000 characters and no more than 20 mentions. Choose **Send** once. 5. Confirm your identity, timestamp, and optional page or playback anchor. Ask reviewers to use **Reply** beneath this message so the discussion remains grouped. **Visibility and delivery.** Only members who can see the target can be accepted as mentions; inaccessible candidates are silently omitted. Mentioned people, the file owner when different from the author, and eligible thread participants can receive notices without duplicate delivery for overlapping roles. **If the thread cannot start.** A blank body produces `Comment body is required`; an oversized body produces `Comment too long (max 5000 characters)`; too many recipients produce `Too many mentions (max 20)`. A hidden or confined target, missing `access_files`, or locked parent folder can prevent access before composition. Resolve that access condition instead of moving the discussion to an unrelated file. ## Expected result One top-level comment identifies the file, review location, requested outcome, and responsible people. Replies can stay beneath it, and later versions retain the original message’s version context. ## Related guides - [Structure a complete file review discussion](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Open the intended thread before inviting reviewers](/files/comments-open-file-thread)

title: What to include in a Dosya support request
summary: Prepare a Dosya support request with the exact time, steps and redacted evidence while keeping passwords, recovery codes and API keys private.
verification: Reviewed locally against the Get help and New support ticket interface in apps/web/src/pages/support.tsx, attachment validation in apps/web/src/components/support/attach-images.tsx, and ticket length validation in apps/api/src/lib/validation-policy.generated.ts on 2026-10-14.
keywords: what to include in a Dosya support request
never share API keys with support
body: Before you send a ticket from **Profile > Get help**, record the action, exact time and timezone, expected result, actual result, client version and any visible error. Remove passwords, sign-in codes, recovery codes, API keys, cookies and private link tokens from the message and attachments. Use the signed-in **Get help** page for account-specific assistance. If you need the complete ticket workflow, follow [how to contact Dosya support](/troubleshooting/contact-support). ## Steps: prepare useful support details 1. From **Profile**, open **Get help** and select **New ticket**. 2. In **Subject**, name the failed task and result in one line. 3. In **Description**, list the exact actions that produced the issue, in order. 4. Add **Expected** and **Actual** lines so the difference is clear. 5. In **Description**, add the date, local time and timezone, plus when the action last worked if the issue is intermittent. 6. Add the Dosya app or browser version and the operating system. 7. In **Description**, paste the exact error text after removing tokens, private URLs and personal data. Use a harmless sample when you can reproduce the problem safely. For upload or download issues, include the file type, approximate size, destination and visible progress state. For protocol or API issues, include the request method, HTTP status, timestamp and a redacted request identifier. ## Information you must remove Do not send a password, verification code, two-factor code, recovery code, session cookie, API key, S3 secret, WebDAV credential, private share URL or complete payment-card number. Dosya support does not need an authentication secret to investigate a ticket. If a secret is already visible in a draft or screenshot, remove the attachment and redact the text. If you already sent or exposed the secret, revoke or rotate it first, then tell support that it was replaced. Use [the suspicious activity response steps](/account/suspicious-activity) if you do not recognize access to the account. ## Prepare a redacted screenshot - Capture only the control, status or error needed to explain the issue. - Cover private filenames, email addresses, local user paths, payment details and link tokens. - Check the redacted image at full size before attaching it. - Keep the label and error readable so support can identify the failing step. The ticket form accepts up to three PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF images per message. Each image must be under 5 MB. For more detail about safe diagnostic evidence, read [how to share diagnostic information safely](/troubleshooting/support-privacy). ## Expected result The ticket describes one reproducible problem and includes enough nonsecret context to investigate it. After **Create ticket** succeeds, the conversation opens under **Open** and you can keep later evidence in the same thread. ## Related guides - [Contacting support with useful information](/troubleshooting/contact-support) - [Share diagnostic information with support safely](/troubleshooting/support-privacy) - [Respond to suspicious account activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Contacting support with useful information
summary: Open a private support ticket with reproducible steps, safe diagnostics and redacted screenshots so the team can investigate without receiving account secrets.
verification: Verified the current English Get help page locally on 2026-10-12 with an isolated sample account and workspace. The capture confirmed the New ticket action, technical category, subject and description fields, image attachment control and Open and Closed ticket tabs. Current web and API source confirmed subject and message length validation, up to three PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF images per message under 5 MB each, and separate Report a bug diagnostics. A ticket was deliberately not submitted and no production support record was created. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Use Dosya's signed-in **Get help** page for a private account, billing or technical question. A useful ticket explains the task, the expected result, what happened instead and when it happened. Include enough context to reproduce the problem while keeping passwords, verification codes, keys and private links out of the message. Check [status.dosya.dev](https://status.dosya.dev/) first when several pages fail at once. A known incident may already explain the behavior and can save you from repeating a risky action. ## Before you start - Sign in to the affected Dosya account. The ticket is attached to that account and can include the active workspace context. - Try the action once more only when repeating it is safe. Record the exact error instead of repeatedly submitting a payment, invitation, deletion or large transfer. - Note the approximate date, time and timezone. For an intermittent issue, note when it last worked. - Redact screenshots before attaching them. Hide private filenames, email addresses, share tokens, recovery codes, payment details and content unrelated to the problem. - Never send a password, six-digit verification or two-factor code, recovery code, session cookie, API key, WebDAV/S3 secret, private share URL or complete payment-card number. ## Steps: open a private support ticket 1. In the web app, open the profile menu in the upper-right and choose **Get help**. 2. Select **New ticket**. 3. Write a short subject that names the action and result, such as “Upload stops after reconnecting.” Avoid a subject such as “Help” that does not identify the problem. 4. Choose the category that best matches the issue. Use **Technical issue** for broken behavior; select the account, billing, feature-request or other category when that is a closer match. 5. In the description, give the task, exact steps, expected result, actual result, time and timezone, app or browser and operating-system version, and the visible error text. 6. Attach only redacted images that help locate the control or error. 7. Review the message for secrets, then select **Create ticket** once. ## Use this description template Copy the headings that apply and replace the examples: ```text Task: Upload a 2 GB sample file to Onboarding samples. Steps: Open Uploads, choose the file, disconnect Wi-Fi, then reconnect. Expected: The upload resumes. Actual: The item remains paused. Time: 12 Oct 2026, 14:20 AEST. Environment: Chrome 140 on macOS 15. Error: Upload paused. Frequency: Reproduced twice with this sample file. Already tried: Reloaded once and confirmed enough workspace storage. ``` Use a harmless sample filename where possible. If only one confidential file triggers the issue, describe its type and approximate size first. Support can tell you whether a private transfer is needed; do not attach the source file to an ordinary screenshot control. ## Useful details by problem type | Problem | Include | Keep out | | --- | --- | --- | | Upload or download | File type, approximate size, destination, connection change, progress state, exact error | Confidential file contents, signed download URLs, session cookies | | Share link | Whether the problem affects creation, opening or downloading; browser; expiry setting; time | The private link token or link password in the first message | | Desktop sync | Desktop app version, operating system, sync mode, affected relative path, last successful sync | Full home-directory paths when they reveal names, passwords or key files | | API, WebDAV or S3 | Protocol, request method or client, HTTP status, timestamp, redacted request identifier | Authorization headers, API keys, access-key secrets or complete request bodies with private data | | Account access | Account email, sign-in method, approximate time and displayed error | Passwords, verification codes, recovery codes or identity-provider tokens | | Billing | Plan, invoice date or last four digits only when needed, displayed error | Complete card number, security code or bank credentials | ## Ticket and attachment limits The subject accepts up to 200 characters and the description up to 10,000 characters. Each message can include up to three images. Supported image types are PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF, and each image must be under 5 MB. Crop or compress an image if it is too large, but keep the control label and error readable. A short screen recording or document is not accepted by the image attachment control; describe the sequence in text and wait for support to request another transfer method if needed. For a product defect, **Report a bug** on the Get help page opens a separate reporting flow that can collect structured diagnostics. Review those details before sending them. Use **New ticket** when you need a support conversation or the issue involves account-specific help. ## Expected result The new ticket appears under **Open** with the selected category and your first message. Return to Get help to read replies and add requested information in the same ticket. After the issue is resolved, the conversation can move to **Closed**. ## Security and privacy limits Support staff do not need authentication secrets to investigate. A legitimate response should not ask for your password, two-factor code, recovery code or complete API secret. If a diagnostic log contains authorization headers, cookies, private URLs, local usernames or file paths, remove those values before pasting it. A screenshot attachment belongs to the support conversation but can still expose information to staff handling the ticket. Include the smallest relevant area and use fictional or redacted data when reproducing a visual problem. ## Troubleshooting **Get help does not open.** Confirm that you are signed in and reload the web app once. Check the public status page. If account access itself is broken, use the support path offered by the sign-in or verification screen. **Create ticket stays disabled.** Enter both a non-empty subject and description. Keep the subject within 200 characters and the description within 10,000. **An image is rejected.** Attach PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF only. Keep each image under 5 MB and the message at no more than three images. **The issue involves a private share link or API key.** Do not paste the secret. Describe the action, time and redacted identifier. Revoke a value immediately if it was already exposed, then tell support that it was rotated. **The same issue has an existing ticket.** Reply in that ticket so the history stays together. Include new timestamps or reproduction results instead of opening duplicates. **A browser or app error has no visible details.** Record the page or feature, time, version and last successful action. Use Report a bug if its diagnostics cover the failure, or ask support which additional log is safe to provide. ## Frequently asked questions ### Should I email my password so support can reproduce the problem? No. Support does not need your password or any temporary authentication code. ### Can I attach the file that fails to upload? The ticket form accepts images, not arbitrary source files. Describe the type and size and attach a redacted screenshot. Wait for support to provide an approved private transfer method if the original file is necessary. ### Should I open another ticket for an update? No. Add the update to the existing Open ticket so the investigation and timestamps remain together. ### What time information is useful? Give the date, local time and timezone. This lets support align your action with service and audit records. ## Related guides - [Recovering a failed or interrupted upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Web app navigation](/account/navigate-web-app) - [Turning on two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor)

title: Back up contacts from your phone
summary: Export all readable phone contacts to a dated vCard, track the queued upload, and verify the cloud file instead of relying on the initial count.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/backupContacts.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/contactsSource.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcard.ts, and apps/mobile/src/backup/folders.ts on 2026-10-14; production uploads were not started.
body: Mobile contact backup creates one cloud vCard from the full readable address book. It is a manual snapshot, not continuous synchronisation. ## Before backing up Select the workspace first. The role must create missing folders and upload files. Destination is **Mobile Backup** > device name > **Contacts**. Dosya reuses exact-name folders. It reads 100 contacts per page and retains names, nonempty phones, and nonempty emails. Output is vCard 3.0 with MIME type text/vcard; photos and other fields are omitted. ## Steps 1. Review the address book because there is no per-contact selection. 2. Open **Settings** > **Contacts** and grant access. 3. Select **Back up contacts now** once. The label becomes **Backing up…**. 4. Note **Backing up N contacts**. Filename is contacts-YYYY-MM-DD.vcf using local date. 5. Watch the upload queue. **Last backup** is recorded immediately after enqueueing, before server success. 6. Verify the file in the device Contacts folder. A second backup that day uses the same name and can create another version of an existing visible, unlocked file. ## Expected result One vCard enters the active workspace queue and appears in its device-specific folder after completion. The source address book stays unchanged. The export contains readable personal data. Trash retains stored bytes until permanent deletion under workspace rules. ## Troubleshooting - **Actions are disabled.** Grant OS Contacts permission. - **Folder creation fails.** Check the role and visibility of Mobile Backup. - **Upload errors.** Resolve the reported policy, quota, lock, collision, or network issue. - **Last backup changed without a file.** That timestamp proves enqueueing only; inspect queue status and file history. ## Related guides - [Mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Mobile backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Troubleshoot mobile contacts permission
summary: Restore Contacts access for Dosya, understand when the prompt appears, and re-enable backup or restore without exposing the address book unexpectedly.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/contactsSource.ts, restoreContacts.ts, and their tests on 2026-10-14; production device permission prompts were not exercised.
body: Dosya can ask for address-book access from the mobile **Contacts** screen or when you restore an opened vCard to the phone. Phone permission and workspace cloud rules are separate checks. ## Permission behavior Before access is granted, the **Contacts** screen explains that the address book becomes one .vcf in the workspace and says **Access only happens when you tap Allow**. Opening that screen checks status without prompting. **Back up contacts now** and **Restore from latest backup** remain disabled until Contacts access is granted and an active workspace exists. On the **Contacts** screen, **Allow contacts access** is the only control that can open the permission prompt before either action is enabled. Its label becomes **Requesting…**, and a concurrent second tap is ignored. After denial, that button disappears and Dosya says **Contacts access was declined. You can turn it on from your device Settings, then come back here.** There is a second request path outside that screen: open a `.vcf` file in **Files**, open its actions, and choose **Restore to phone**. Restore requests Contacts permission before it adds anything. If access is refused, the toast reads **Contacts permission was denied** and no contact is added. ## Steps 1. Open mobile **Settings** > **Contacts**. 2. Select **Allow contacts access** once and accept the OS request. 3. After a prior refusal, enable Contacts for Dosya in device Settings. 4. Return to Dosya. The screen rechecks permission whenever focus returns. 5. Confirm a workspace is active, then start backup or restore. Both **Contacts**-screen actions require that workspace and granted Contacts permission; a lower-level refusal reads **Contacts permission was denied**. ## Expected result The primer disappears when the OS reports access as granted. With an active workspace, both **Contacts**-screen actions enable. Role, lock, folder, quota, and network checks can still refuse the cloud operation. Revoking permission later blocks new scans and restores. It does not delete existing cloud vCards, contacts already added to the phone, or copies shared from Files. ## Troubleshooting - **The prompt does not return.** Enable access in device Settings, then reopen Contacts. - **Buttons stay disabled.** Select an active workspace, then leave and re-enter the screen so its permission focus check finishes. - **Backup still fails.** Confirm folder creation, upload access, and storage. - **Latest restore fails.** Verify reachability and download access. ## Related guides - [Mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Mobile backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Restore contacts to a phone
summary: Restore a chosen or latest vCard additively, understand duplicate and partial-failure behavior, and safely verify exact added counts on the phone.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/restoreContacts.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcard.ts, and apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx on 2026-10-14; production address books were not modified.
body: Contact restore adds records from a Dosya vCard. It never merges with existing people, so restoring the same backup twice can create duplicates. ## Choose a source **Restore from latest backup** searches the active workspace's **Mobile Backup** > current device name > **Contacts** path. It requests up to 500 items, keeps .vcf files, and picks greatest created_at. Missing content reports **No contacts backup found**. This path requires a downloadable URL. For a specific vCard, open it in mobile Files and select **Restore to phone**. The action appears for a .vcf extension or text/vcard MIME type. View-only preview bytes can restore even when saving a copy is disabled; unlock a full lock first. ## Steps 1. Check the file's date, sample names, and count. 2. Grant Contacts permission for record insertion. 3. Choose latest restore or the selected file's **Restore to phone** action. 4. Keep Dosya active while additions run sequentially. 5. Read **Added N contacts** or partial result **Added N contacts, M failed**. 6. Verify names, phones, and emails in the phone Contacts app. ## Expected result Each supported card becomes a new person containing parsed name, phone, and email values. Unknown properties are ignored, and one failed insertion does not stop later cards. There is no atomic rollback or Dosya undo. Earlier additions remain on the phone; the cloud source stays unchanged. Removing additions in Contacts may sync to its provider. ## Troubleshooting - **Permission was denied.** Enable access in device Settings. - **No backup found.** Check active workspace and device-specific folder, or open a file directly. - **Added 0 contacts.** Confirm complete BEGIN:VCARD and END:VCARD blocks. - **Some failed.** There is no per-contact failure list; compare manually. - **Restore failed.** Check reachability, lock, network, and download access before retrying, which can duplicate successes. ## Related guides - [Mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Mobile backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Control which phone contacts Dosya backs up
summary: Understand the contact scope used by Dosya mobile backup, review the phone address book before export, and create a verified vCard copy in your active cloud workspace.
verification: Verified against current local product source for the Contacts screen, device permission flow, paged address-book reader, vCard export, workspace folder path, and restore behavior on 2026-10-14.
body: Dosya backs up the contacts that the phone exposes through its system address book permission. The current Dosya mobile app does not include an account picker for Google, iCloud, Exchange, SIM, or local-only contact sources. When you tap **Back up contacts now**, Dosya reads all contacts available to the app and writes them into one `.vcf` file. ## Before you start ### Review the source before backing up 1. Open the phone's Contacts app and review the contacts currently available on the device. 2. If your Contacts app can filter by account or list, use that view to understand which accounts contribute records. A filtered view in the Contacts app does not necessarily change what other apps can read. 3. Merge or remove unwanted duplicates in the phone's address book before the backup if you do not want them included. 4. In Dosya, confirm the active workspace. Contact backups are written to that workspace under **Mobile Backup / [device name] / Contacts**. 5. Open **Settings → Contacts** in Dosya. ## Steps: allow access and create the vCard backup 1. Read the permission explanation on the **Contacts** screen. 2. Tap **Allow contacts access**, then approve the operating-system prompt. Dosya asks from this screen so you can see why access is needed before the OS dialog appears. 3. Tap **Back up contacts now**. 4. Wait for the confirmation showing how many contacts were queued and the generated filename, such as `contacts-2026-10-14.vcf`. 5. Check **Last backup** on the Contacts screen, then browse the active workspace to confirm the new file exists in the Contacts folder. The vCard contains contact names plus available phone numbers and email addresses. Photos and account-provider metadata are not part of this export. Dosya reads the address book in pages, so a large contact list is still exported into a single file. ## Back up only one account Because Dosya has no source selector, do not assume choosing a filtered list in the phone's Contacts app limits the export. If you require a backup from only one provider, export that account from the provider or the phone's contact-management tools as a separate `.vcf`, then upload that file to Dosya. This preserves the intended scope without temporarily deleting contacts from the device. ## Troubleshooting ### If contacts access is missing If access was declined, the Dosya screen tells you to enable it in device settings. Open the operating-system app settings for Dosya, allow Contacts access, return to Dosya, and reopen **Contacts**. The screen checks permission again whenever it receives focus. Before using **Restore from latest backup**, remember that restore adds records to the phone and does not merge them with existing contacts. Review the latest `.vcf` first because restoring the same backup twice can create duplicates. ## Expected result The Contacts screen shows a recent **Last backup** time and the active workspace contains one dated vCard in **Mobile Backup / [device name] / Contacts**. ## Limits and important details Dosya exports all contacts exposed by the operating system and has no per-account selector. Restore adds records without merging, so duplicate contacts are possible. ## Related guides - [Manage mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Choose mobile backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Export contacts as a vCard
summary: Create Dosya’s mobile vCard export, understand its supported fields and cloud destination, then download or share the verified file with care.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/src/contacts/backupContacts.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcard.ts, apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, and apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx on 2026-10-14; production exports and shares were not created.
body: Dosya's contact export is **Back up contacts now**. It creates one cloud vCard; the Contacts screen has no separate export picker, local-save command, or share sheet. ## Format and privacy Output is contacts-YYYY-MM-DD.vcf in local time, uploaded as text/vcard. vCard 3.0 records use N, FN, TEL, and EMAIL. Names, nonempty numbers, and nonempty emails are included; photos, accounts, notes, organisations, addresses, birthdays, and identifiers are not. ## Steps 1. Select the workspace and review the whole address book; no subset selector exists. 2. Open **Settings** > **Contacts**, grant access, and choose **Back up contacts now**. 3. Wait beyond **Backing up N contacts** until upload completes. 4. Open **Files** > **Mobile Backup** > device name > **Contacts**. 5. Compare count and sample names. Structured mobile preview applies through 5 MiB. 6. Use normal download or **Share via…** only when role and lock rules allow it. ## Expected result A compatible vCard containing supported fields appears in the device Contacts folder. Export does not modify source records. Download or sharing makes a plaintext copy outside workspace controls. Revoking a Dosya link cannot erase a recipient's saved copy. ## Troubleshooting - **No Export button exists.** The backup action produces the export. - **A property is missing.** Confirm it is a supported name, phone, or email. - **Today's name exists.** Inspect version history because another same-name upload can update it. - **Share via… is absent.** The file must be downloadable for this role and lock mode. - **Import fails elsewhere.** Verify upload integrity and use a vCard 3.0-compatible app. ## Related guides - [Mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Mobile backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Copy a file to another folder
summary: Copy a Dosya file into another folder, account for full duplicate storage, and resolve name, permission, lock, quota, or Live Photo failures.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/mobile/app/pick-destination.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/mutations.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/copy.ts, and its conflict, quota, target, and metadata tests. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Copy creates a new file ID and a second stored object in the same workspace. The source remains unchanged, while workspace usage grows by the source file’s full byte size. ## Before you start - Copy requires `upload_files`, membership in the source workspace, and access to both source and destination within any folder confinement. - A file with its own lock cannot be copied, and an ancestor full lock can refuse the source. Copying out of a locked WordPress backup is allowed, but copying into a protected backup is not. - Check quota and any credential-specific maximum file size. Copy is treated like creating a new file and can be refused before bytes move. - Choose a destination without the resolved copy name. Dosya never overwrites an existing file. ## Steps 1. Choose the platform path: - On mobile, open the file actions, select **Make a copy**, browse **Copy to…**, and tap **Copy here**. - On desktop, select **Copy to...**, choose a folder in **Copy “filename”**, then press **Copy here**. - On web, **Copy** immediately adds a copy to the folder currently open. To place it elsewhere, copy first and use **Move to...** on the new row. 2. For a different destination, confirm the chosen folder is live and belongs to the same workspace. 3. Submit the copy once and wait for **Copied**, **Copied successfully**, or **A copy has been added to this folder**. 4. Open the destination and compare filename, size, and content with the source. 5. Confirm the source still exists. The two rows can now be renamed, moved, shared, versioned, or deleted independently. ## Expected result Another file row and object exist in the destination. A copy to another folder keeps the source name; an in-place copy without an explicit name becomes **Copy of filename**. Content hash and source timestamps are preserved, but shares and later changes do not link the two files. ## Troubleshooting - **“You don’t have permission to copy files.”** The role lacks `upload_files`. - **“A file with this name already exists in the target folder.”** Rename or move the existing item, or select another destination. Repeating an in-place copy can collide with the existing **Copy of …** row. - **“Target folder not found.”** Refresh the picker; the folder may be trashed, hidden, stale, or outside this workspace. - **Storage or maximum-file-size refusal.** Free storage, raise the workspace allocation if permitted, or use a credential whose single-file cap accepts the source size. - **A Live Photo warning says only the photo copied.** Web and desktop issue a second request for the paired video. The still is already copied when that request fails; delete the incomplete copy or copy the video separately before retrying. - **“Source file not found in storage.”** The metadata exists but its stored object could not be read. Retrying will not repair missing source bytes; restore a healthy version or contact support. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Organize files](/files/organize-files)

title: Resolve a copied-file name conflict
summary: Resolve a copied-file name conflict without overwriting the destination, understand Copy of naming, and retry safely with a unique name or folder.
verification: Reviewed against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/copy.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/file-copy.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx on 2026-10-14. No production copy was attempted.
body: Dosya never silently replaces an existing file during copy. The web Files page copies into the current folder immediately; it does not show a conflict-resolution dialog or ask for a destination. **How the automatic name works.** A copy made into the source folder defaults to `Copy of {filename}`. A copy requested through another client or API into a different folder defaults to the original name. If that target name already exists, the API returns `A file with this name already exists in the target folder` with status 409. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, open the folder that contains the source. Check whether `Copy of {filename}` already exists before choosing **Copy** from the source’s context menu. 2. If no collision exists, choose **Copy**. A successful web operation reports **Copied — A copy has been added to this folder.** 3. If the web page reports **Copy failed — The file could not be copied**, refresh the folder and check for the automatic name. The web toast does not expose the API’s detailed conflict text. 4. To keep both files, rename or move the existing `Copy of …` item, then retry. A client that supports an explicit copy name or target folder can instead provide a unique destination name. 5. Verify the pre-existing destination item’s file ID and content remain unchanged. Open the new copy separately and confirm its new identity. **Permissions and storage.** Copy requires `upload_files`, visibility of the source and destination, and enough workspace quota for the full file size. A file or enclosing folder lock can block the source, and a protected WordPress backup destination refuses new content. Folder confinement permits a copy only when both source and target are within the allowed boundary. **Other copy failures.** The API can report `This file is locked and cannot be copied`, `This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to copy it.`, `You don't have permission to copy files`, `Target folder not found`, quota or credential-size errors, `Source file not found in storage`, or `Could not copy file in storage`. Correct the named condition rather than deleting the existing destination. ## Expected result The original destination file is preserved byte-for-byte. A successful retry creates a separately identified copy under a unique name and consumes storage equal to the copied object. ## Related guides - [Preview both files before resolving the collision](/files/preview-files) - [Rename or move the existing destination item](/files/organize-files)

title: Creating an account and verifying your email
summary: Create a Dosya account with an identity provider or email and password, enter the six-digit verification code and recover when the message does not arrive.
verification: Verified the current English signup and email-verification screens on 2026-10-12 with an isolated sample account. The capture confirmed Google, GitHub and Apple choices; name, email, password and terms controls; a six-digit code field; resend, support, different-email and login paths. Current-source API integration tests cover signup validation, duplicate accounts, consent persistence, verification success, invalid or expired codes, attempt limits and resend cooldowns. Production email delivery and third-party OAuth consent screens were not exercised.
body: Create a Dosya account at [app.dosya.dev/sign-up](https://app.dosya.dev/sign-up). You can continue with Google, GitHub or Apple, or register with an email address and password. Email-and-password registration requires a six-digit code before you can use the account. You do not enter payment-card details on the signup form. Your first personal workspace is created automatically after registration, so a successful verification takes you into the welcome flow rather than asking you to build a workspace first. ## Before you start - Use an email address that you can open now. Check the spelling before creating the account; the verification screen shows the address receiving the code. - If you choose email and password, use at least 8 characters. A longer unique passphrase is easier to remember and safer than reusing a password from another service. - Keep the signup tab open while checking your inbox. You can return to the verification screen without starting another account. - If you were invited to a workspace, open the original invitation after signing in if the app does not return you to it automatically. ## Steps: create the account 1. Open [Dosya signup](https://app.dosya.dev/sign-up). 2. Choose one registration method: - Select **Continue with Google**, **Continue with GitHub** or **Continue with Apple**, then complete that provider's own consent flow. - To use email and password, enter your **Name**, **Email** and **Password**. 3. Review the linked Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. For email-and-password registration, select the agreement checkbox. 4. Select **Create Account**. If the form reports a weak password, invalid address or existing account, correct that item before trying again. The provider buttons can create an account without using the email form. Follow the provider's prompts and check that it returns you to `app.dosya.dev` before entering any Dosya information. If you intended to use an existing account, use **Log in** at the bottom instead of creating another one. ## Verify an email-and-password account 1. Open the newest Dosya verification message in the inbox for the address shown on screen. Check Spam, Junk, Promotions and mail rules if it is not in the main inbox. 2. Enter the complete six-digit code. The field accepts digits and stops at six characters. 3. Select **Verify email**. A valid current code signs you in and opens the welcome flow. 4. Complete or skip the welcome tour. Your automatically created personal workspace is ready for your first upload. Use the newest code after requesting a resend. Verification codes expire and have an attempt limit, so do not keep guessing after a code is rejected. Wait for the latest message and copy its six digits carefully. ## Expected result The account email is verified, the browser is signed in and the welcome flow opens the automatically created personal workspace. Finishing or skipping the welcome flow takes you to the workspace's first-run dashboard. ## If the verification email does not arrive Work through these checks in order: 1. Confirm the address shown on the verification screen. A typo means the message went to the wrong address; choose **Use a different email** and register with the correct one. 2. Search the mailbox for `dosya` and inspect Spam, Junk, Promotions, quarantine and blocked-sender rules. 3. Allow a few minutes for the mail provider to process the first message. Repeated clicks do not make the provider deliver faster. 4. Select **Resend code** once. The app can temporarily refuse another resend when one was requested recently; wait for the displayed cooldown rather than repeatedly clicking. 5. If neither message arrives, select **Contact support** from the verification screen. Include the address, approximate request time and the error text. Do not send your password or a verification code. ## Limits and security checks Verification codes expire, accept only a limited number of attempts and can be resent only after a short cooldown. These checks mean an older email may contain a code that no longer works. Use the newest message and follow any retry time shown by the app. Account creation can also be rate-limited when many requests come from one address. Wait for the stated period instead of changing details or repeatedly submitting the form. ## Troubleshooting **The form says an account already exists.** Open [Log in](https://app.dosya.dev/login) with that address. Use the password-reset route if you no longer know its password. Creating another account with spelling or alias changes can separate files and workspace memberships. **The code is invalid.** Make sure all six digits came from the newest Dosya message. Request a new code when the old one expired. A code is tied to the account address and cannot verify another signup. **Too many attempts.** Stop trying codes and wait for the stated retry period. Request a new code when the screen permits it. This limit protects the account from repeated guesses. **The verification screen shows the wrong address.** Choose **Use a different email**. Do not verify an address you do not control. **The page cannot reach the server.** Check [Dosya status](https://status.dosya.dev/), confirm your connection, then retry. A privacy extension, corporate filter or blocked browser challenge can also prevent an authentication request from completing. **An identity-provider button returns an error.** Confirm you selected the intended Google, GitHub or Apple account and that the provider returned to `app.dosya.dev`. If you previously used email and password with the same address, try logging in with that original method. ## Frequently asked questions ### Do I need a payment card to create an account? No card field appears in the signup flow. Plan choices and billing changes are handled separately after account creation. ### Can I change the email before verification? Use **Use a different email** on the verification screen and complete signup with the correct address. ### Why did verification open a welcome screen instead of workspace creation? New accounts receive a personal workspace automatically. The welcome screen introduces the first upload and other common tasks. ### Should I share my verification code with support? No. Support does not need your password or six-digit verification code. Share only the address, time and visible error through a private support route. ## Related guides - [Turning on two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders)

title: Create a folder in the right workspace
summary: Create one folder or a nested path in the correct Dosya workspace, using exact name limits while avoiding locked, hidden, or confined locations.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/mutations.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.ts, and packages/shared/src/validation/policy.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: **Create new folder** can create one folder or several nested levels in one request. The active workspace and current folder determine where the first missing segment is inserted. ## Before you start - Select the intended workspace and open the parent folder. A folder-confined member who creates at root is redirected to the membership anchor. - Your role needs `create_folders`; otherwise **New folder** is hidden on web and mobile or the API returns **You don’t have permission to create folders**. - The full typed path is limited to 500 characters. Each retained segment is limited to 100 characters and cannot be `.`, `..`, or contain control characters; empty pieces between separators are ignored. - Both `/` and `\` separate levels. For example, `Projects/Q2/Designs` creates up to three nested folders. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, verify the workspace switcher and breadcrumb, then choose **New folder**. 2. In **Create new folder**, type a single name or a nested path. Web shows the placeholder **e.g. Brand Assets or Projects/Q2/Designs**. 3. Press **Create** or Enter. Dosya walks from the current parent, reuses live segments already present, and creates each missing segment. 4. Wait for **Folder created**. In a group view, the new root-level folder is also enrolled in that group when the follow-up succeeds. 5. Open the returned leaf and check its breadcrumb. For a nested path, verify each intermediate level once. ## Expected result The final folder opens under the requested parent. Existing segments and their contents remain unchanged; new segments start empty. A repeated request for the same complete path can succeed with `created_count: 0` and returns the existing leaf rather than producing a duplicate. ## Troubleshooting - **“Path too long (max 500 chars).”** Shorten the full nested path, including separators. - **“Folder name ‘…’ is too long (max 100 chars)” or “Folder name ‘…’ contains invalid characters.”** Fix the named segment and submit again. - **“Parent folder not found.”** The displayed parent was deleted or became unavailable. Return to a live breadcrumb and reopen the dialog. - **A lock prompt or `folder_locked` refusal appears.** Unlock the parent chain. New content cannot be created inside a full-lock folder without a valid unlock state. - **The folder exists but is missing from a group.** Creation succeeded even if the separate group-enrolment request failed. Find the folder at the workspace root, then add it to the group again. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Create a secure file sharing link
summary: Create and test a cloud file sharing URL with the right recipient access, password, expiry, download controls and workspace policy.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/shared.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/share.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/share-bundle.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/expiry.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/recipients.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/downloads.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/download-session.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/egress.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/lock-gate.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/view-only-image.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/view-only-image.unit.test.ts, public share routes and focused tests. Verified current labels, role and workspace gates, public versus restricted recipients, password/expiry/download limits and preview byte-session counting, format-specific View-only image delivery, Free-plan ceilings, configured locks versus personal unlocks, notification outcomes, separate link-result and email-send completion paths, immediate revocation and the current unsaved By-link title field. Existing creation and result captures were inspected and remain accurate.
body: In **Files**, choose **Share** on a completed file, select **By link** for a public URL or **By email** for named recipients, configure its access controls, then test the result privately before sending it. ## Before you start - Verify the active workspace, filename and completed upload. A sharing URL points to the selected workspace item; it does not upload a replacement. - Your role needs **create share links** permission. A folder-confined member may share only targets inside the assigned subtree. - A hidden target appears unavailable to a member it is hidden from. A target or ancestor with configured **Full lock** cannot receive a public link, even if your current member session has a personal unlock grant. - Decide whether the URL can be forwarded. **By link** is public to anyone holding it, subject to password, expiry and other controls. **By email** can restrict access to verified addresses. - Keep sensitive URLs and passwords out of public tickets and screenshots. ## Steps ### Choose who can open the share 1. Open **Files**, locate the completed file, and select **Share** from its row/card menu or right-click menu. 2. Verify the target name under the **Share** heading. 3. Select the recipient path that matches this delivery: - **By link** displays **Anyone with the link can access this file.** It creates a bearer URL and sends no invitation. - **By email** accepts up to 50 distinct valid addresses. Leave **Only these people can open it.** selected for a private link. Each visitor must enter an invited address and a one-time code emailed to it. 4. For restricted email access, know the timing: the code lasts 15 minutes, permits five incorrect attempts, and a successful recipient grant lasts up to 30 minutes. Forwarding the URL alone does not add another address. ### Configure expiry and download behavior 1. Review **Expires in**. The web choices are **1 hour**, **24 hours**, **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, **Custom date…** and **Never**. 2. A custom timestamp must be at least one minute ahead and no more than 3,650 days away. Workspace policy can silently shorten a longer selection and can supply the initial default, so check the stored expiry after creation. 3. Expand **Advanced options** and apply only the controls the delivery needs: - **Password (optional)** requires eight or more trimmed characters. It is independent of recipient email verification. - **View only.** blocks the normal attachment download and serves eligible inline previews. JPEG, PNG and HEIC are re-encoded as WebP with the longest edge capped at 1,600 px. WebP, AVIF, GIF, SVG, BMP and ICO lack that server decoder and can be shown inline as their original bytes, so View only does not promise that every image preview withholds the source bytes. Any visible material can still be captured. - **Remove photo metadata.** strips location, camera and capture-time metadata from delivered photos while leaving the workspace original unchanged. - **Download limit (optional)** accepts a whole number from 1 through 10,000. The first eligible preview or download byte session claims one slot, including a View-only preview. Later Range requests for that same file within its one-hour signed session reuse the claim; a new browser or later session can consume another. 4. The current dialog also displays **Title (optional)**. The current **By link** request does not persist that field, so do not rely on it to identify or secure the public delivery. Use the target name and the row in **Shared**. ### Create and verify the delivery 1. On **By link**, generate and copy the URL; on **By email**, send the invitations: - For **By link**, select **Generate link**, wait for **Share link created**, use the copy icon, and select **Done**. Automatic clipboard success is confirmed by **Link copied — Share link copied to clipboard.** - For **By email**, select **Send**. The success notice reports how many addresses received the invitation and lists any failures. The modal then resets and closes; it does not show **Share link created** or a copy result. 2. Open **Shared → By me** and inspect the saved row. Its detail states who can open it, the stored expiry, password state and **Downloads: Allowed** or **View only**. This is also where you retrieve the saved URL after the email modal closes. 3. For a public bearer link, open the copied address in a private window. For a restricted email delivery, retrieve the address from **Shared → By me** and test with an invited inbox that can receive its one-time code. 4. Confirm the target, password prompt, recipient challenge, expiry and download behavior that you intended. Do not open file bytes while testing a one-slot delivery: even an eligible inline preview consumes its only slot. Use a limit of at least two when the private-window byte test and one recipient session must both succeed. 5. Distribute a **By link** address only after that check, sending its password separately when practical. **By email** has already sent invitations; correct and retry any addresses named as failures instead of waiting for a generated-link result. ## Expected result The new row appears under **Shared → By me** with the selected target, final expiry, password state, recipient scope and download mode. The private-window visitor reaches the intended file and encounters every configured challenge before any protected bytes are served. ## Plan and workspace limits - A Free-plan creator can hold five active sharing links across workspaces. The exact refusal is **The free plan allows 5 active share links at a time. Revoke one, let one expire, or upgrade for unlimited links.** - Free links are clamped to seven days even if **Never** or a longer duration was chosen. A tighter workspace maximum wins. - Revoked and expired URLs no longer occupy an active-link slot. - Public share traffic owned by a Free account has a 10 GiB allowance per UTC day. When exhausted, recipients see **This link's owner has reached their free plan's daily share-transfer allowance. Try again later - or the owner can upgrade for unmetered sharing.** - A workspace can disable share links, require every link to have a password, impose a default expiry or cap the maximum expiry. - A multi-file link supports 1 through 100 files. A selection of 101 is refused with **Maximum 100 files per share link**. These limits apply to what is ultimately saved, not merely what the form showed. Verify the final row in **Shared** before distribution. ## Locks, hiding and later changes Public link creation deliberately ignores a member’s temporary unlock. If the selected file or an ancestor is configured **Full lock**, remove or change that configured lock with the appropriate authority, or share a separate delivery copy. A hidden file is reported as not found to a role that cannot see it. If a target receives **Full lock** or becomes hidden from the link creator after the URL was created, public access is blocked at open time. Removing that configured state can make an unrevised, unrevoked link reachable again. Revocation is different: it permanently ends the token. A target-level **View only** setting also makes the link effectively view-only even when the link itself was created with downloads allowed. Personal unlock grants never bypass any of these public-link decisions. ## Revocation and irreversible outcomes Open **Shared → By me**, locate the precise row, select **Revoke share link**, and confirm **Revoke**. Subsequent requests immediately return **This share link has been revoked**. The URL cannot be reactivated; create another one when access should resume. Revocation does not erase the source file, recall a downloaded copy, retract an email already delivered or change other active URLs for the same target. Review all rows when the item must no longer be shared anywhere. ## Troubleshooting **Generate link says sharing is disabled or a password is required.** Follow the workspace policy shown by the exact message. Only an authorized workspace administrator should change those controls. **The selected expiry is shorter in Shared.** Free-plan and workspace ceilings clamp longer choices. The saved timestamp is authoritative. **The form reports a locked or missing file.** Confirm the item is visible to your role and not beneath a configured Full lock. Re-entering a personal unlock password cannot authorize a persistent public token. **A private recipient cannot continue.** They must use the exact invited address. One-time codes expire after 15 minutes and are replaced when a new code is sent. After five wrong attempts, request another code. **The download limit ended too early.** Your private-window preview or download can consume a slot. Range requests for one file within the same one-hour signed session are counted together, but another browser, another file or a later session can claim another place. **The recipient gets a Free-plan transfer message.** Wait for the UTC-day allowance to reset or have the owning account change plan. Regenerating another link under the same Free owner does not create a separate allowance. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does a public recipient need a Dosya account? No. A **By link** visitor opens the public page subject to the URL’s controls. Restricted **By email** access proves control of an invited inbox instead of requiring workspace membership. ### Can I edit the URL after sending it? The authenticated API supports in-place updates to several settings, while the current web flow creates and revokes links. Use the controls actually present in your interface and retest after any change. ### Is a sharing password the same as Full lock? No. A share password protects that URL. **Full lock** is configured on the workspace target or folder tree and blocks creation or public access regardless of a member’s temporary unlock. ## Related guides - [Password-protect a sharing link](/sharing/password-link) - [Restrict a link to named recipients](/sharing/named-recipients) - [Disable downloads with View only](/sharing/share-disable-downloads) - [Set and verify link expiry](/sharing/link-expiry) - [Revoke a sharing URL](/sharing/revoke-link) - [Share a cloud folder](/sharing/folder-link)

title: Creating a workspace and choosing its storage location
summary: Understand the automatically created personal workspace, create another workspace and choose the permanent storage location before adding files.
verification: Verified the current English workspace creation flow on 2026-10-12 with an isolated owner account. The live capture searched the location catalog, selected Sydney Australia, submitted the form, confirmed the new workspace through the API with default_region ap-southeast-2 and reopened it from the two-workspace switcher. Current-source API tests cover suggested locations, valid and unknown region codes, fallback selection, owner membership, storage allocation checks, workspace caps and refusal of post-creation location edits. Cross-region file migration and production object placement were not exercised for this article. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Every new account receives a personal workspace automatically. Dosya chooses that first workspace's location from the signup request's geographic suggestion, with a platform fallback when no location signal is available. When you create an additional workspace, you choose its storage location in the creation form. The choice is fixed for that workspace, and new files in it use the workspace location. Check the location before creating the workspace and before uploading data that has geographic or contractual requirements. ## Before you start - Sign in to the web app and decide whether you need a separate workspace. A folder in an existing workspace may be enough when the files, team and policies can remain together. - Estimate the storage you intend to allocate. The optional workspace storage limit cannot exceed the unallocated amount shown by the form. - Choose a location based on your own operational, contractual and legal requirements. A city label by itself does not certify compliance with a particular law or standard. - Do not upload files until you have confirmed the new workspace name and location. The location field cannot be edited after creation. ## Understand your first personal workspace Password signup and supported identity-provider signup create a workspace named **Personal** as part of account creation. After verification or provider login, the welcome flow opens that workspace. You do not choose this first location in the signup form. Dosya uses the nearest catalog suggestion available from the signup request. If you need a specific location, create another workspace with that location before uploading the affected files. ## Steps: create another workspace 1. Select the current workspace name at the top of the left sidebar. 2. Choose **Create new workspace**. You can also open **Workspace dashboard** and start creation from there. 3. Enter a clear **Workspace name**, up to 80 characters. The preview tile shows the initials that will appear in the switcher. 4. Choose a colour to distinguish the workspace from others in your account. 5. Under **Location**, review the preselected suggestion. Search by city, country or region code when you need a specific entry, then select that row. 6. Optionally enter a **Storage limit** in GB. Leave **No limit** when you do not want a workspace-specific cap within the account's available storage. 7. Review the name, selected location and allocation, then select **Create workspace**. After creation, Dosya makes the new workspace active and opens its dashboard. An empty workspace shows the first-run upload screen. Confirm the workspace name at the top of the sidebar before adding a file. ## Confirm the result 1. Select the workspace name to reopen the switcher. 2. Confirm that the new name appears under **Your workspaces** and carries the active check. 3. Open **Settings** and review the workspace overview. The location is displayed as workspace information rather than an editable field. 4. Upload a harmless sample file only after the name and location are correct. 5. Return to the switcher and select another workspace to confirm that each keeps its own files, storage usage, members and settings. ## Expected result The new workspace appears in the switcher, becomes active and displays the location chosen during creation in its workspace information. It starts with its own empty file tree, membership and settings, ready for a verified sample upload. ## Choosing a location The location is a workspace-level choice. Every ordinary file uploaded to that workspace is labelled with the workspace's location. The picker groups entries by continent and lets you search a city, country or region code. Use a nearby location when latency is your main concern, but consider where collaborators work and what your organization requires. The transfer route a request takes and the location chosen for durable workspace storage are different concepts; a nearby network edge does not change the workspace's selected location. The web form prevents an unknown region code from being selected, and the API rejects unknown codes. If the location list cannot load, the form can let the server choose its current suggestion rather than permanently blocking workspace creation. Wait for the catalog and make an explicit choice when location matters to you. ## Storage limits and ownership The optional limit caps how much storage that workspace can use. It does not add storage to the account. The creation screen shows the plan total and how much remains unallocated; a value above the remainder is refused. The person creating the workspace becomes its owner. After creation, use **Team** to invite members and assign suitable roles. Workspace roles do not merge accounts or copy files from another workspace. Accounts and plans can limit how many workspaces one person owns. If creation is refused because of a workspace cap, review unused workspaces or the current plan instead of repeatedly submitting the same form. ## Troubleshooting **The Create workspace button is unavailable.** Enter a non-empty name and select a location from the loaded list. If the location catalog failed, use **Try again** and wait for it to load. **The location I need does not appear.** Search the city, country and known region code. Do not substitute a similarly named city without confirming it meets your requirement. Contact private support if the current catalog does not offer the required location. **The storage limit is rejected.** Enter a positive number no greater than the unallocated amount shown. A workspace limit cannot create capacity beyond the account plan. **I created the workspace in the wrong location.** Stop before uploading additional files. The location is fixed and cannot be edited in workspace settings. Contact private support with the workspace name and requirement before reorganizing data; do not assume changing a label moves existing bytes. **My old files are missing.** The new workspace starts with its own file tree. Open the switcher and return to the previous workspace. Creating or switching workspaces does not move files. **I cannot see Create new workspace.** Your account or plan may have reached an ownership limit, or the current surface may be restricted. Open **Workspace dashboard** and review the available action; contact support if the reason is unclear. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I change the workspace location later? No. The current web app treats the location as fixed after workspace creation and refuses location edits. ### Does switching workspace change where existing files are stored? No. It changes the active view. Existing files remain with their original workspace. ### Does the optional storage limit buy more storage? No. It assigns a ceiling within the account's available allocation. Plan and billing controls determine the total entitlement. ### Why was my first workspace created without this picker? Signup creates a personal workspace automatically and uses the request's suggested location. Create another workspace before uploading when you require a specific location. ## Related guides - [Web app navigation](/account/navigate-web-app) - [Inviting people to a workspace](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Connecting to Dosya with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav)

title: Browse an archive in the desktop app
summary: Browse ZIP, ISO, and IMG contents without extracting the complete archive, preview supported entries, and save folders of up to 500 files into Dosya.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/ArchiveViewer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/archive-tree.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/archive-save.ts, apps/api/src/lib/archive-entries.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/ArchiveViewer.test.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/archive-tree.test.ts and apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/archive-save.test.ts. Verified supported containers and compression methods, the 2 MiB text ceiling, 200,000-character display cap, 500-file folder-save limit and error copy. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The desktop archive viewer lists ZIP files and ISO/IMG disk images without first extracting the whole container to a local folder. Browsing is read-only; **Download this file**, **Save to dosya** and **Save all to dosya** have separate effects. ## Before you start Open a `.zip`, `.iso` or `.img` file you can view. EPUB and CBZ files use the reader instead. ZIP entry preview supports stored method 0 and deflate method 8; encrypted entries remain listed but cannot be opened. ## Steps 1. Open the archive and review its entry count and archive size. Folders begin collapsed so very large trees do not expand at once. 2. Expand the required directory and select an entry. Images, video, audio, PDF and supported text can preview when the entry is readable. 3. For text, keep the uncompressed entry at or below **2 MiB**. The display truncates after **200,000 characters**, although the entry request processes the full selected entry. 4. Choose **Download this file** to write that entry through the operating system's save flow. 5. Choose **Save to dosya** for one entry, or **Save all to dosya** for a folder. Pick a destination in the active workspace. A folder save accepts at most **500 files**; created cloud copies consume storage and can later be deleted like normal files. The completion notice reports saved, skipped and failed counts, plus cancellation when applicable. Listing or previewing alone creates no extracted cloud files. ## Expected result The tree exposes safe indexed entries without unpacking the container as a whole. An explicit save creates new Dosya items at the chosen destination; a download creates local output only. ## Troubleshooting For status 422, the viewer says **“This file isn't a valid zip”** or the corresponding disk-image message. Status 413 appears as **“This archive is too large to list”**; other index failures show **“This archive could not be opened”**. Use **Download the file** when the container is unsupported or damaged. An oversized folder displays **“This folder has … files. Save smaller folders (up to 500), or download the archive.”** Encrypted entries and unsupported ZIP compression must be extracted with another archive tool. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Show lyrics in the desktop audio player
summary: Read embedded lyrics in a desktop audio preview, follow timestamped lines during playback, and diagnose why the Lyrics tab may be unavailable.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/AudioPlayer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/LyricsPanel.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/useLyrics.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/useAudioTags.ts, packages/audio-player/src/lyrics/lrc.ts, packages/audio-player/src/tags/parse.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/audio-viewer.spec.ts. Verified the 256 KiB head read, ID3-only lyric extraction, timed and untimed rendering, active-line scrolling and missing-tab behavior. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: Dosya shows lyrics found in an ID3 lyric frame near the start of an audio file. It does not search for a sibling `.lrc` file, fetch lyrics from an outside service or extract lyrics from MP4/M4A metadata. ## Before you start Choose an ID3-tagged track whose lyric data fits within the first **256 KiB**. The desktop player makes one ranged read of those leading bytes through the authorized raw URL; a larger tag cut off by that range can yield partial or empty metadata. The MP4/M4A parser can return title, artist, album and artwork, but it does not return lyrics. No parsed tag is written back to cloud storage. ## Steps 1. Open the track in **Files** and wait for its metadata to load. 2. Select the **Lyrics** tab beside **Up next**. The tab is offered only when non-empty embedded lyric text was found. 3. Start playback. Timestamped, LRC-style lines inside the lyric tag highlight as their cue time is reached and scroll toward the middle of the panel. 4. For lyrics without timestamps, read the plain lines in order. Untimed text has no active-line tracking. The highlighted lyric follows the audio element's current time, so seeking backward or forward recalculates the active line. Reduced-motion settings change the automatic scroll from smooth to immediate. ## Expected result Embedded words appear without changing the source file. Synchronized lines follow the current playback position; untagged timing produces a static lyric sheet. ## Troubleshooting If **Lyrics** is missing, the 256 KiB head read did not expose usable ID3 lyric text. Add lyrics to an ID3-compatible file with a separate tag editor, upload the revised file as appropriate, and reopen it. An MP4/M4A lyric field or adjacent `.lrc` file will not populate this panel. A player decode failure is separate from lyric parsing. When Dosya displays **“This app can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.”**, download the track for playback in software that supports its codec. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Manage the audio queue](/files/audio-queue)

title: Use the audio queue in the desktop app
summary: Play audio siblings in existing folder order, choose another track, and learn how previous, next, and automatic advancement behave at queue boundaries.
