verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/AudioPlayer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/QueuePanel.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/useAudioKeys.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/file-type.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/audio-viewer.spec.ts. Verified sibling filtering, fixed queue order, navigation boundaries, the three-second restart rule and automatic next-track behavior. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The desktop queue is built automatically from audio siblings already loaded in the current file viewer. It follows their existing order; the queue panel has no reorder or add control. ## Before you start Open an audio file from a folder containing at least one other recognized audio file. The **Up next** tab appears only when the queue contains more than one track. Access is the same as file access; there is no separate queue plan or role setting. ## Steps 1. Open the first track, then select **Up next**. Its badge reports the number of audio files in the viewer's sibling list. 2. Check the highlighted row. Each row shows a sequence number, track name and file size; the active row uses a playing indicator. 3. Select a different row to open that file. This navigates the viewer to the selected cloud file without copying or moving it. 4. Use **Next** to advance unless the current track is last. Select the **Previous** button within the first three seconds to open the prior item; after three seconds that button restarts the current track at 00:00. 5. Let a track finish to test automatic advancement. Ended playback opens the following queue item when one exists and stops at the final item. The keyboard actions differ slightly: **Shift+Right Arrow** opens the next track, while **Shift+Left Arrow** always opens the previous track regardless of elapsed playback time. The player ignores these keys while typing into an input, select or editable control. ## Expected result Selecting a queue row opens that exact audio file, and completion advances once through the existing order. Queue use does not rename, reorder or otherwise change any stored item. ## Troubleshooting If **Up next** is absent, return to the folder and open a track while multiple supported audio siblings are present. A filtered or incomplete file list can produce a one-item queue. If next or previous does nothing, check whether you are already at the corresponding end. When playback itself fails, the player displays **“This app can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.”** ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Manage the audio queue](/files/audio-queue)

title: Seek with the desktop audio waveform
summary: Seek precisely in a desktop audio preview, use keyboard jumps, and understand when large or unsupported tracks fall back to a plain seek control.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/AudioPlayer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/Waveform.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/usePeaks.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/useAudioKeys.ts, packages/audio-player/src/peaks/extract.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/audio-viewer.spec.ts. Verified the 80 MiB analysis ceiling, five- and fifteen-second keyboard jumps, cached peaks, fallback seek control and decode error. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The desktop audio preview draws a seekable waveform for tracks it can analyse. It is a playback aid: seeking changes only the current player position and never edits the audio file or its cloud metadata. ## Before you start Open an audio file that you can view in the active workspace. Dosya routes MP3, WAV, OGG/OGA, Opus, FLAC, AAC, M4A, MKA and WMA extensions to this player, but playback still depends on Chromium having the required codec. The waveform analysis limit is **80 MiB**. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, open an audio file and wait for its duration to appear. 2. Move the pointer across the waveform to read the hover time, then click or drag to the required point. The solid section shows played audio and the vertical playhead marks the current position. 3. Focus the waveform and press **Left Arrow** or **Right Arrow** to move by five seconds. During normal playback, **J** and **L** jump 15 seconds and **Space** or **K** toggles play/pause. Shortcuts are ignored while focus is in a form field. 4. Compare the elapsed time at the left of the waveform with the total duration at the right. The player caches calculated peaks by file ID and version. A track over 80 MiB, an analysis download failure or an undecodable analysis stream falls back to a standard range control labeled **Seek**; that fallback does not by itself stop audio playback. ## Expected result The playhead moves to the chosen time and playback resumes from there. No new file, version or activity event is created because seeking is local player state. ## Troubleshooting If the player says **“This app can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.”**, use the file download and open it in a compatible player. WMA files and files whose extension hides an unsupported codec are common examples. If a flat seek slider remains, confirm the file is at most 80 MiB and retry on a stable connection. The slider still permits seeking even when peak generation is unavailable. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Manage the audio queue](/files/audio-queue)

title: Check for desktop app updates
summary: Check a direct-download desktop build for updates, follow each download state, and install safely across Windows, macOS, and Linux without losing work.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/UpdatesSection.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/updater.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/update-install.ts and apps/desktop/src/main/update-install.test.ts. Production update feeds and installers were not invoked; no production action was performed.
body: A direct-download Dosya build checks the Dosya update feed itself. Store installations use their store instead and do not display the self-update controls or downloadable installer list described here. ## Before you start - Open **Settings > Updates** and confirm the card says **dosya Desktop** with **You’re on v…**. - Save editor work and let uploads, downloads, and sync changes settle before restarting. Updating is available to all signed-in plans and does not require a workspace role. - This procedure applies to direct downloads on Windows, macOS, and Linux. If the page says updates are managed by Microsoft Store, Mac App Store, or Snap Store, use the store guide instead. - Keep network access to **api.dosya.dev**. The packaged app schedules a feed check 5 seconds after every startup. Outside crash-loop protection, it also checks every 4 hours while running. ## Steps 1. Select **Check for updates**. The button becomes busy and the status reads **Checking for updates…**. 2. If a release exists, watch **Downloading _percent_%**. The control remains disabled during the check and background download. 3. When Windows or macOS reports **Update ready: v_version_**, choose **Restart & install**. The app announces **Installing… dosya will reopen in a moment**, closes its windows, installs, and relaunches. 4. On Linux AppImage, the **Update Downloaded** notification says that the file was downloaded and must replace the current AppImage. Triggering install reveals that downloaded file rather than relying on automatic replacement. 5. After reopening, return to **Settings > Updates** and confirm **You’re on v_version_** matches the intended release. Also check that sync pairs returned to their expected state. 6. When no newer release exists, record **Up to date** and the displayed current version; no restart is needed. ## Statuses, timing, and safeguards The updater broadcasts **Downloading 0%** immediately when it finds a release, then the page can progress through **Downloading 0%–100%**, **Update ready: v…**, and **Installing… dosya will reopen in a moment**. Other visible states are **Checking for updates…**, **Update check failed**, and **Up to date**. The release list separately labels builds **Latest**, **Installed**, **Pre-release**, or **Not available** for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Once installation starts on Windows or macOS, a 15-second watchdog force-closes any app window still blocking the updater. Save work before pressing the button because unsaved local interface state can be lost. Linux does not use this restart installer path. Crash-loop protection examines recent launches. If three prior launch records are still within a 30-second window, the next startup disables automatic download and install and suppresses only the recurring four-hour check; the one check scheduled five seconds after startup still runs. Running stably for 60 seconds clears the record. Manual diagnosis is safer than repeatedly relaunching a failing version. ## Troubleshooting - **Update check failed** exposes only the state, while the updater retains the underlying message in its status. Confirm internet access and retry once. - **Couldn’t load builds.** affects the release history list. Use **Try again**; the live updater may still work independently. - **No builds published yet.** means the release endpoint returned no entries for the list. - If a platform row says **Not available**, that release has no installer for the selected OS. Select the correct Windows, macOS, or Linux tab. - When **Restart & install** does not appear, wait for **Update ready**. A store-managed build intentionally hides this button. - On Linux, replace the active AppImage with the revealed download, preserve executable permission, and start that new file before deleting the previous one. ## Expected result The direct build either reports **Up to date** or downloads the matching platform release. Windows and macOS restart into the new version; Linux exposes the AppImage for manual replacement. The version line provides the final verification. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Diagnose desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues)

title: Choose the correct desktop update path
summary: Match the installed Dosya desktop channel to its direct, Microsoft Store, Mac App Store, Snap, or Linux AppImage update procedure without mixing sources.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/main/distribution.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/updater.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/UpdatesSection.tsx, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/about-info.ts. Store pages, the live update feed, and production installers were not opened.
body: Dosya chooses its update controls from the installed distribution. Check that channel first: a direct build can use Dosya’s updater, while Microsoft Store, Mac App Store, and Snap installations stay with their owning store. **Before you start** - Open **About dosya** and read **Channel**. Its value is **Direct download**, **Microsoft Store**, **Mac App Store**, or **Snap Store**. - Save unsaved work before any direct Windows or macOS installation restart. No workspace role or paid plan is required to inspect or update the desktop client. ## Steps 1. Open **About dosya** from the application menu and record both `Version` and **Channel**. The channel comes from the packaged distribution, not the workspace or signed-in account. 2. For **Direct download**, open **Settings > Updates** and choose **Check for updates**. A check can move through **Checking for updates…**, **Downloading _percent_%**, and **Update ready: v_version_**. 3. On direct Windows or macOS builds, wait for **Update ready**, then select **Restart & install**. **Installing… dosya will reopen in a moment** means the native updater owns the restart. 4. On a direct Linux AppImage, reveal the downloaded AppImage when the update is ready, replace the old AppImage manually, retain executable permission, and launch the replacement. 5. For **Microsoft Store** or **Mac App Store**, use **Open Microsoft Store** or **Open Mac App Store**. These builds do not fetch or install Dosya’s direct packages. 6. For **Snap Store**, run `snap refresh dosya` through the Snap installation environment. The Updates card deliberately has no store-opening button for this channel. ## Expected result The Updates card confirms which service controls the installed build. A direct Windows or macOS installation reopens on the new version, Linux runs the replacement AppImage, and each store reports its own update result. If the expected control is absent, return to **About dosya**. A store-managed build intentionally hides **Restart & install**, and Snap intentionally omits an in-app update action. ## Related guides - [Install and sign in to the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Check for desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Collect desktop version and system context
summary: Collect Dosya version, channel, system, workspace, sync summary, error reference, and event time without attaching unnecessary private data.
verification: Reviewed locally using apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/AboutPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/about-info.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/ipc.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/bug-report.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/bug-report.ts. No report was transmitted to the production support service.
body: A useful desktop incident record identifies the build and machine without copying file contents. **About dosya** provides a reusable client summary; the Report Problem diagnostics add the exact system release, workspace ID, page, and captured error. **Before you start** - Leave the affected account signed in and keep the relevant workspace selected. - Reproduce the problem once if doing so cannot overwrite data, then note the local clock time immediately. ## Steps 1. Open **About dosya** and record `Version`, **Channel**, **System**, and **Engine**. **System** is the Electron platform name plus architecture; it is not the full OS release. 2. Choose **Copy Details** and wait for the button to read **Copied**. The confirmation lasts 1.5 seconds, and the copied block also includes account and sync context when available. 3. Open **Help > Report a Problem…** or press `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B`. Do not send yet; inspect the Diagnostics card first. 4. Record **App**, **System**, **Workspace**, **Page**, **Error reference**, **Error**, and **Sync** rows that appear. This **System** value includes the recognizable OS name and kernel release. 5. Add the occurrence time and the exact action that preceded the fault. Diagnostics store `captured_at` in Unix seconds, but the card does not replace the user’s incident timeline. 6. Copy only the needed context into the support conversation. Common home-directory paths are replaced with `` and each diagnostic string is limited to 300 characters, but arbitrary secrets are not guaranteed to be removed. ## Expected result The record now separates build facts from incident facts: About supplies the installed client/channel, while Diagnostics supplies the system release, active workspace ID, route, sync summary, and captured error. If a row is missing, do not invent it. **Workspace** requires an active workspace, and error fields appear only when the dialog was opened with matching error context. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Create a desktop problem report](/desktop/desktop-problem-report)

title: Troubleshoot a desktop deep link
summary: Diagnose Dosya authentication and sync-folder links across macOS, Windows, and Linux while rejecting unsupported, expired, or unsafe destinations.
verification: Locally reviewed against apps/desktop/src/main/deep-link.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/deep-link-path.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts, apps/desktop/build/installer.nsh, and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/deep-link-protocol.spec.ts. Production OAuth callbacks and OS protocol registration were not exercised.
body: The desktop client accepts two `dosya://` destinations: an authentication callback and a local sync-folder request. Other paths do not have a browser fallback, so first identify which supported link failed. **Before you start** - Keep the full link private because an authentication callback can contain a token. - Confirm Dosya is installed. Sign-in is required for sync activity, while the authentication callback is itself part of signing in. ## Steps 1. Classify the link as `dosya://auth/callback?token=…&state=…` or `dosya://sync?path=…`. Any other host or route is unsupported and may be ignored without opening a page. 2. If nothing launches, start Dosya once and retry. Packaged builds register the scheme; Windows additionally repairs its protocol-client registration at startup, while macOS uses `open-url` and Windows/Linux receive URL arguments. 3. For an authentication callback, restart the sign-in flow instead of replaying an old URL. The callback needs the pending single-use `state`; a missing or mismatched state is refused. 4. After a valid callback, confirm the client reaches the authenticated dashboard. The resulting session cookie is set for 30 days; do not paste the callback token into a report. 5. For a sync link, verify `path` names an existing absolute directory. The decoded value must stay within 1,000 characters and contain no control characters, NUL, or `..` path segments. 6. Retry the validated sync link and confirm Dosya opens `/sync?localPath=…`. Cold-start links wait for the renderer; malformed and unsupported links remain rejected rather than redirecting to a browser. ## Expected result A valid callback completes the pending sign-in, while a valid sync link opens the Sync page with the checked local directory. Repeated encoding is decoded at most five times before refusal. If the OS opens another program or does nothing after Dosya has launched once, repair or reinstall the packaged client for that operating system; there is no in-app “open in browser” recovery path. ## Related guides - [Use the desktop system tray](/desktop/desktop-system-tray) - [Check desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Protect against unexpected mass deletion
summary: Review a paused mass deletion, choose whether cloud copies stay or move to trash, and recover safely from permission or network failures in desktop sync.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/deletion-guard.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx and apps/desktop/src/main/sync/sync-engine-refusals.test.ts. Production behavior was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: Dosya pauses a sync pair when a local disappearance looks more like an unreadable or unplugged folder than an intentional deletion. The guard activates only when the pair tracks more than 10 files and one watcher batch would remove both more than 5 files and more than half of all tracked files. ## Before you start - Reconnect an external drive, remount a network volume, or restore the moved local folder before making a decision. - Open **Sync** and identify the pair by both its cloud folder name and local path. The warning includes up to five missing sample paths and the remaining count. - Stop other tools from changing the same local tree until the pair is healthy. - Deleting an item you uploaded requires **delete_own_files**; deleting another member’s item requires **delete_any_file**. A mixed batch can therefore complete only partly. The guard is part of desktop sync on supported Windows, macOS, and Linux builds and has no separate plan entitlement. ## Steps 1. Find the warning beginning **dosya paused this folder: _N_ files disappeared locally.** 2. Compare the displayed cloud folder, local path, sample names, and total count with the device. If a drive was unplugged or a folder moved accidentally, restore that path first. 3. Choose **Keep the cloud copies** when the local disappearance was accidental or uncertain. Dosya clears the held batch without changing the server, restarts the watcher, and performs a full rescan. 4. Choose **Delete from the cloud too** only when every listed disappearance was intentional. The button changes to **Deleting...** while Dosya submits the held IDs as one cloud batch. 5. Review the result toast and Sync activity. A complete deletion says **Deleted _N_ files from the cloud**. Keeping them says **Cloud copies kept**. 6. If a partial server result deleted fewer objects than requested, use the activity record to identify the shortfall; Dosya keeps those remaining rows tracked rather than falsely reporting success. ## What each choice changes **Keep the cloud copies** does not delete server data. A subsequent rescan reconciles the still-present cloud copies according to the pair’s sync mode, so they may return locally where downloads are enabled. **Delete from the cloud too** moves the accepted cloud files to cloud trash. That action changes shared storage and may affect every device syncing the folder. Recovery is possible only while the trash retention policy still keeps the files; permanent purge or an expired trash item cannot be reversed from the desktop guard. While the question is open, the watcher is stopped and the pair reports **needs-confirmation**. There is only one held deletion batch per pair, and unrelated changes wait for the full rescan after the decision. ## Troubleshooting - **No delete permission** or another 403 restores the same hold. Ask a workspace owner or administrator for the correct delete permission, then retry. - **session expired** means sign in again before confirming. The pending files remain held. - A rate-limit refusal tells you to try again in a minute; the app does not drop the question or claim that deletion happened. - **Could not apply that - try again** leaves the pair paused. Fix connectivity and use the existing prompt instead of recreating the sync pair. - A scan that cannot read a folder may report that files **were not deleted this time** and that Dosya will retry after the next healthy scan. Repair access to the path first. ## Expected result The chosen pair resumes only after the held batch is kept or successfully processed. Keeping preserves server files; confirming trashes only the IDs the server accepts. Refusals retain the hold and tracked records so the user can recover without silent data loss. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes)

title: Clean up duplicates from the desktop app
summary: Select reviewed duplicate copies, understand permission and lock failures, move them to cloud trash in 500-file batches, and verify the keeper.
verification: Verified cleanup controls against `apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/DuplicatesPage.tsx`, `renderer/lib/duplicates.ts`, and API `files/batch-delete.ts` on 2026-10-14. Production deletion was not performed.
body: Use the desktop **Duplicates** page only after reviewing paths and choosing a keeper. Its delete action soft-deletes selected cloud files to trash. Trashed data continues to consume storage until it is permanently purged, and active share links on moved files are revoked. ## Before you start - Finish the review while **Still scanning N files** is absent, or accept that more groups can appear later. - Open each keeper from its folder path and confirm it is accessible where collaborators expect it. - The **Delete** button appears only when the member has `delete_any_file` or `delete_own_files`. The server restricts own-file permission to copies uploaded by that member. - Locked files, files inside locked folders and locked WordPress backup content can refuse an entire batch. Unlock or remove those selections before retrying. ## Steps 1. Open **Duplicates** in the intended workspace. Select individual copies or choose **Select all but newest**, then audit the checkboxes. 2. Read the summary's selected bytes. This value adds the full size of each selected copy. It is an estimate of content moved out of the live set; quota is not released while the files remain in trash. 3. Select **Delete N**. The dialog title is **Move N files to trash?** and its explanation says **They go to trash, not straight out.** 4. If the warning says one or more groups have every copy selected, choose **Cancel** and leave a keeper unless removing the content entirely is intentional. The desktop allows an all-copy selection but never hides that consequence. 5. Select **Move to trash**. The desktop sends at most **500 file IDs per request**, splitting a larger selection into sequential chunks. 6. Wait for **Moved to trash** and the description **N files moved to trash.** The page clears the selection and refreshes Duplicates and Files. 7. Open the keeper in its expected folder. Then check Deleted items if you need to confirm or restore a moved copy. Restoration is possible only while the trash entry still exists. ## Expected result Successfully authorized copies leave the live duplicate groups and appear in cloud trash. Their active share links are revoked. The retained copy stays in its reviewed folder. Storage accounting remains unchanged until a later permanent purge, so the confirmation's reclaimable figure does not mean quota is immediately freed. Cleanup is not all-or-nothing across more than 500 selected files. Each chunk is a separate request. If a later chunk fails, earlier chunks can already be in trash; the refresh shows what actually moved. Within one request, a visible locked file or out-of-scope ID refuses the whole batch before deletion. ## Troubleshooting **Delete is missing.** Your role has neither delete permission. Ask a workspace administrator to remove the copies or grant the appropriate role capability. **Delete failed says No delete permission.** Your current role has neither delete capability. Ask a workspace administrator to perform the cleanup or change the role. **The error says This file is locked and cannot be deleted.** Unlock that file and submit again. For **This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to delete it.**, resolve the ancestor lock first. **The toast count does not match what moved.** With only `delete_own_files`, the server filters the request to your uploads, while the desktop success description uses the selected count. Treat the refreshed Duplicates and Files views as authoritative. **Some files moved before the error.** This can occur between 500-file chunks. Refresh, compare the current duplicate groups with Deleted items, and retry only the remaining reviewed copies. **I selected every copy by mistake.** If the items remain in cloud trash, restore the required copy before it is purged. A permanent purge is irreversible and cannot be recovered through this cleanup page. ## Related guides - [Review exact duplicates](/files/review-duplicates) - [Restore deleted files](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Review duplicate files in the desktop app
summary: Review exact-content duplicate groups by path, age, copy count, and reclaimable bytes before choosing which cloud files should remain in each workspace.
verification: Reviewed duplicate grouping and visibility in `apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/DuplicatesPage.tsx`, `renderer/lib/duplicates.ts`, and API `duplicates.ts`/`lib/duplicates/group.ts` on 2026-10-14. Production scan state was not sampled.
body: Open **Duplicates** to review live files that share the same content hash. Grouping compares content, not filename. A group can therefore contain differently named files, while same-named files with different bytes remain separate. ## Before you start - Select the correct workspace. Results never combine files from different workspaces. - You need file-page access. Folder-confined members see only duplicates within their authorized subtree, and hidden items they cannot view are removed before groups are formed. - Wait for the scan signal to settle before concluding that the workspace is clean. Hashing reads file contents and finishes asynchronously. - Keep business, legal or workflow context in mind. Identical bytes do not mean two paths serve the same purpose. ## Steps 1. Choose **Duplicates** in the desktop navigation. The subtitle states **Identical files, by content - not by name**. 2. If the banner says **Still scanning N files. This list will fill in as it goes.**, leave the page open. The desktop refreshes every **15 seconds** while pending candidates remain. 3. Read the summary: **N duplicate groups · X reclaimable**. The total reclaimable value represents keeping one copy from every exact-content group. Groups are ordered by the largest reclaimable amount, and the page displays at most **100 groups** even though the summary totals cover the full result set. 4. In each card, compare the copy count and reclaimable bytes. Copies are sorted newest first; the first carries the **newest** badge. Newest describes creation time, not correctness or preferred folder. 5. Select a displayed folder path such as **Workspace root** to open that file in the Files detail panel. Confirm the name, uploader, path and intended use before selecting its checkbox. 6. If appropriate, choose **Select all but newest**. This selects every copy after the newest entry in every displayed group. Review every selected row; use **Clear** to discard the selection without changing files. Files larger than **256 MiB** are marked too large by the current hash scanner and are not hashed in this version. Hash candidates stop retrying after **3 attempts**. These limits can explain why files you believe are identical do not appear together. ## Expected result Each visible card contains two or more live files with the same content hash, their folder locations, ages and a calculated reclaimable amount. Your selection contains only copies you have personally reviewed. No file changes until you use **Delete** and confirm the trash dialog. A **No duplicates** state means no exact-content group is currently returned for this member's visible scope. Duplicate scanning is opt-in per workspace, but the current desktop page does not render the API's `scan_enabled` flag; disabled scanning can therefore look like an empty result. If scanning is pending, disabled, exhausted its retries, or skipped a file over the hash limit, do not treat the empty state as proof that every stored object was compared. ## Troubleshooting **The page says Couldn't check for duplicates.** Select **Retry**. Confirm the workspace still exists, your session is active and your role has file access. **A hidden copy is absent.** The API applies the same hidden-item visibility rules as Files before grouping. Ask an authorized workspace administrator to review it; the duplicates page will not disclose hidden paths. **Select all but newest chose the wrong keeper.** Choose **Clear**, then select individual rows. The newest marker is based on `created_at`, with ID used only as a stable tie-breaker. **The summary exceeds what is on screen.** Only the top 100 groups are returned, sorted by reclaimable bytes. Clean reviewed groups and refresh to expose later results. ## Related guides - [Review exact duplicates](/files/review-duplicates) - [Restore deleted files](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Open file details in the desktop app
summary: Open desktop file metadata, distinguish the compact info dialog from the action panel, and understand locks, versions, shares, and identifiers.
verification: Verified labels and gated actions in `apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/FileInfoDialog.tsx`, `FileDetailPanel.tsx`, `FileBrowserPage.tsx`, and `main/menu-template.ts` on 2026-10-14. Production was not opened.
body: Dosya has two information surfaces. **View → Show File Details** opens the right-side **File details** panel for exactly one selected file; it rejects folders. A file or folder's context-menu **Get info** command opens the compact, read-only metadata dialog. ## Before you start - Open **Files** in the correct workspace and locate the intended file. - Select exactly one file before using the application menu. **Show File Details** is enabled on the Files route when the combined selection count is one, but its handler opens the panel only when that selection is a file and no folder is selected. - Opening **Get info** does not change, download or delete the item. Actions inside the side panel can change cloud state, so verify the filename first. - Members need access to the file listing. Delete, share, restore and comment actions remain subject to role, ownership, folder scope and lock rules. ## Steps 1. Select exactly one file in **Files**, then choose **View → Show File Details** or press **Command-I** on macOS / **Ctrl-I** on Windows or Linux. This opens the right-side **File details** panel; selecting a folder does not open it. 2. Use the panel's **Details** tab to inspect its preview, version history, **Properties**, active **Share links**, and the available **View file**, **Download**, **Share**, **Copy file**, and **Delete file** actions. The **Comments** tab shows the file discussion. 3. For compact metadata, right-click a file or folder and choose **Get info**. Match the name and header type before reading the rows. 4. A file dialog can show **Kind**, **Size**, **Where** when supplied, **Created**, **Modified**, **Versions**, **Uploaded by**, **Region**, **Sharing**, **Status**, and **ID**. A folder dialog instead reports its item count, aggregate size and folder metadata. Size includes a readable value and the exact byte count. 5. Read **Status** carefully. An unrestricted visible item shows **Normal**. Other badges can show **Locked**, **Lock**, or **Hidden**. Select the ID row, whose tooltip is **Copy ID**, when support or an API workflow needs the stable identifier. Choose **Close** when finished; **Get info** has no save operation. 6. For a `full_lock` file, enter its password in **Enter password** and select **Unlock**. Until the server returns an unlock token, the panel hides versions and share links and displays **This file is locked**. An invalid attempt can show the server error or **Incorrect password**; a connectivity failure says **Can't reach the server. Check your connection and try again.** ## Expected result The selected filename and identifier agree across the Files row and the surface you opened. **Get info** reports stored metadata for a file or folder without modifying it. **Show File Details** exposes only the information and operations available for its one selected file; a fully locked file remains gated until the correct password is accepted. Version restore, share revocation and deletion are separate mutations. A successful restore shows **Restored** and **Restored to vN.** Revoking can fail with **Revoke failed** / **The share link could not be revoked.** Deleting enters the normal trash workflow rather than occurring merely because the details panel was opened. ## Troubleshooting **Show File Details is disabled.** Return to Files and select exactly one item. The command is disabled elsewhere and with zero or multiple selections. **A folder is selected but no side panel opens.** The menu command's selection-count gate includes folders, but the handler rejects every folder selection. Right-click the folder and choose **Get info** for its compact metadata dialog. **Where is absent.** The row is conditional; use the Files breadcrumb or folder path to establish location. Its absence does not mean the file is at the workspace root. **Versions or share links do not appear.** A single-version file does not show version history. Revoked links are filtered out. A fully locked file loads neither list until it is unlocked. **Metadata looks stale.** Close the panel or dialog, refresh the file listing, and reopen the same ID. Use the ID rather than a repeated filename to distinguish same-named copies. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Find text in a desktop file preview
summary: Search a desktop plain-text preview case-insensitively, move through wrapping matches, and understand its 2 MiB and 300 KiB rendering limits.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/FileViewer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/TextFindBar.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/use-in-file-find.ts and apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/find-matches.ts. Verified case-insensitive non-overlapping matches, wrap navigation, exact labels, the 2 MiB preview limit, 300 KiB syntax threshold and 8,192-character binary sample. No dedicated desktop text-find test was found; production behavior was not re-tested.
body: Find searches only the rendered contents of the desktop plain-text viewer. It compares text without case sensitivity, highlights non-overlapping matches and never changes the cloud file. ## Before you start Open a plain-text or code file at most **2 MiB**, such as TXT, JSON, XML, logs, YAML, TOML, INI, common source-code extensions, HTML or CSS. Syntax coloring is limited to files at most **300 KiB**; larger previewable files remain plain text and searchable. Markdown opens in its own rendered/source viewer, while CSV opens through Office Preview, so neither surface provides this in-file Find bar. ## Steps 1. With the preview open, choose **Edit > Find…**, or press **Ctrl+F** on Windows/Linux or **Command+F** on macOS. 2. Type into the field labeled **Find in file**. The counter changes to `current/total`; a query without a match reports **No results**. 3. Press **Enter** or select **Next** to advance. Use **Shift+Enter** or **Previous** to move backward. Navigation wraps after the final or first occurrence. 4. Press **Esc** to close Find and clear its highlights. The match operation runs in the displayed document and does not send the query as a file edit. Leaving the viewer also removes the temporary ranges. ## Expected result Every visible occurrence matching the entered letters is highlighted, and the active result advances in document order with wraparound. ## Troubleshooting If **Find…** is unavailable, the current file may be in Markdown, Office Preview or another specialized viewer rather than the plain-text viewer. A text file above 2 MiB receives a download fallback instead of searchable content. **“This file is not text-previewable.”** means binary data was detected in the first 8,192 characters. **“Failed to load file content.”** indicates the raw text request failed; confirm access and connectivity, then reopen the file. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Find the installed Dosya desktop version
summary: Find the exact Dosya desktop version, distribution channel, system architecture, engine versions, signed-in account, and current sync summary.
verification: Verified in local source at apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/AboutPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/about-info.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/about-window.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/menu-template.ts. The published desktop packages were not launched in production.
body: **About dosya** is the authoritative in-app view for the running client. It distinguishes the application version from its distribution channel and provides a copyable block for support. **Before you start** - Open the running desktop client whose version you need; do not rely on an installer filename or an old download. - This lookup is local and does not require a workspace role, update check, or production change. ## Steps 1. Open the application menu and select **About dosya**. The dedicated panel is 400 by 540 pixels and opens over the main window when that window exists. 2. Read the first line, `Version _version_`. This value identifies the executable currently running, including after a completed update. 3. Read **Channel**: **Direct download**, **Mac App Store**, **Microsoft Store**, or **Snap Store**. The row is part of the loaded About data rather than an optional release label. 4. Record **System**, which reports platform and CPU architecture, and **Engine**, which reports Electron and Chromium versions. Use Report Problem diagnostics when support needs the OS kernel release. 5. Check **Signed in as** and **Sync** to tie the version to the observed session. Sync can report **No folders**, **Paused**, errors, active syncing, files not synced, or **All synced**. 6. Select **Copy Details**. Confirm **Copied** appears for 1.5 seconds, then paste the block into a private note or support report and remove any account detail that is unnecessary. ## Expected result The copied record identifies the running Dosya version, channel, system architecture, engines, account, and sync summary. An optional **Finder location** row can also identify the macOS app location. If About does not load, record what remains visible and use **Help > Report a Problem…** for diagnostics; do not substitute the version of a downloaded installer for the active executable. ## Related guides - [Install and sign in to the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Check for desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Review a first-sync plan
summary: Choose folders, direction, conflict and exclusion rules before the first desktop sync, then verify the immediate comparison without silent overwrites.
verification: Reviewed the wizard and first comparison in `apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx`, `main/sync/index.ts`, `first-sync.test.ts`, `planner.ts`, and `deletion-guard.ts` on 2026-10-14. Production was not exercised.
body: The desktop wizard lets you review folders, direction, conflict handling and exclusions before a first run. It does **not** show a file-by-file operation preview. Selecting **Start syncing** creates an enabled pairing and begins the comparison immediately. ## Before you start - Keep an independent copy of important files and test with small folders first. - Compare the existing local and cloud contents. Same names with different bytes can become conflicts; a matching name and size can be adopted as the same item during initial state building. - Ensure the signed-in workspace member can access the cloud destination and perform the uploads, downloads or deletions required by the selected mode. - Decide how deletions should behave. **Full Sync** applies them both ways; **Push to Cloud** applies local deletion remotely; **Pull from Cloud** applies cloud deletion locally. **Protect & Upload** keeps cloud copies, and **Save to Device** keeps local copies. ## Steps 1. Open **Sync → Add sync folder**. In **Folders**, choose a **Cloud folder** or **Root (entire workspace)**, then set **Local folder** with **Browse**. Desktop, Documents, Pictures and Downloads can appear as quick choices when the operating system provides them. 2. Select **Continue** and choose one of five modes. The initial selection is **Protect & Upload**, which uploads local changes and never deletes a cloud copy because its local source disappeared. 3. If you select **Full Sync**, choose **Keep both copies** or **Last write wins** under **Conflict resolution**. Keep both is the default and preserves competing content as separate copies; last-write selection can replace the other side's version. 4. Continue to **Advanced** and review the exclusion patterns. Virtual filesystems `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, and `/run` are always skipped even if you change the visible list. 5. Read the size estimate. At **50,000 files** or when counting is truncated, the wizard warns **This folder contains about … files.** or **This folder contains more than … files.** It also says large folders can take many hours and use substantial memory and bandwidth. Select **Sync it anyway** before the final button becomes available. 6. Recheck both destinations and the mode, then select **Start syncing** once. Success shows **Sync folder added**. A creation error reports its message or the fallback **Failed to add sync pair**. 7. Watch Overview and Activity. The first Full Sync can pass through **Connecting to server...**, **Comparing with server...**, **Scanning local files...**, and **Checking for changes...** before visible transfer progress. Do not interpret comparison time as a stall unless Activity reports no progress. During an empty-state first comparison, cloud-only content downloads in download-capable modes and local-only content uploads in upload-capable modes. Tests pin that pre-existing content on only one side is not silently deleted, and that different content colliding at the same path becomes a conflict instead of an automatic overwrite. ## Expected result The new row shows the chosen cloud folder, local path and **Mode**. Eligible files reach the destinations permitted by that mode, while exclusions and conflicts remain visible for review. The initial poll interval is 30 seconds, but the first comparison starts on creation rather than waiting for that interval. For deletion-capable upload modes, a safety valve pauses a suspicious local disappearance when more than 5 files and more than half of a pairing with over 10 tracked files would be removed. Choose **Keep the cloud copies** to leave the server unchanged or authorize the displayed cloud deletion, which moves those items to cloud trash. Cloud-driven local deletion tries the operating-system trash first and can permanently unlink when trash is unavailable. ## Troubleshooting **Start syncing is disabled.** Choose both folders and a mode, complete the prior wizard steps, and acknowledge **Sync it anyway** when the large-folder warning is present. **The row remains on comparison.** Check Activity for the current count. Inactivity must exceed 30 seconds, and the engine evaluates that condition on its next 30-second recovery tick, so the first **Still working:** entry normally appears about 30–60 seconds after the last progress. Keep the app awake and connected; large trees can legitimately take hours. **A collision appears.** Compare both copies before resolving it. Keep both preserves content for manual review; last-write behavior may not select the version you intended. **The destination is wrong.** Pause the row immediately. **Remove** stops the relationship without deleting existing local or cloud files, but recreating it starts a fresh comparison and does not undo transfers already completed. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes)

title: Inspect a desktop sync issue safely
summary: Read desktop sync pair errors, macOS permission loss, conflict notices, and per-file failure records without exposing contents or credentials.
verification: Locally reviewed against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/status-assembly.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/status-assembly.test.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/report-problem-store.ts. No production sync pair was retried or cleared.
body: Desktop sync has two evidence locations. **Issues** shows pair-level errors, permission loss, notices, and unresolved conflicts; **Overview** expands the per-file error ledger from the `N files not synced` badge. **Before you start** - Select the workspace that owns the sync pair, then open **Sync**. - Avoid copying file contents or credentials. Paths and filenames can themselves be private, so share only what support needs. ## Steps 1. Open **Issues** and locate the affected remote folder. A pair error card shows the folder name, exact error message, local path, **Retry**, and **Report**; there is no separate details drawer. 2. For `macOS needs permission to this folder again.`, choose **Reselect folder**. This Mac App Store state needs a renewed sandbox grant and deliberately does not offer **Retry**. 3. Read nonfatal notices before acting. A conflict-copy notice offers **Show both versions**; degraded watching, skipped files, or held deletions describe conditions that an ordinary retry cannot repair. 4. Return to **Overview** when the row shows `N files not synced`, then expand that badge. The true count remains visible even when the client lists only the 200 most recent attempts. 5. For each listed file, record its path, message, timestamp tooltip, and **will retry** or **won’t retry** label. These labels distinguish transient attempts from entries the engine stopped retrying automatically. 6. After fixing the named cause, use **Retry** to reset every failed file in the pair, including permanent and undisplayed entries. **Clear** only dismisses the ledger; later scans can try those files again. ## Expected result The evidence identifies whether the fault belongs to the whole pair, a lost macOS grant, a conflict/notice, or individual files. **Report** opens the problem form with the pair’s error message prefilled. A successful retry leaves rows listed until their files sync. If the pair remains in **Error**, preserve the exact message and submit a report rather than guessing from generic permission or storage causes. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Create a desktop problem report](/desktop/desktop-problem-report)

title: Installing and signing in to the desktop app
summary: Download the desktop app for your operating system, sign in to your existing account, and check the workspace before setting up folder sync.
verification: Verified sign-in and workspace selection in the current locally built macOS desktop app 3.1.1 against an isolated real API on 2026-10-10. Actual sign-in and workspace screenshots reviewed. Official download instructions checked; Windows, Linux, store installation and production sign-in were not run. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Download Dosya from the [official desktop download page](https://dosya.dev/desktop/#downloads), install the package for your operating system, and sign in with your Dosya account. After signing in, check the workspace selector at the top of the sidebar before uploading files or adding a sync folder. ## Before you start - Have a Dosya account and the sign-in method you normally use. If two-factor authentication is enabled, keep your authenticator or other required factor available. - Check the current requirements on the download page. Installer versions, supported systems and store availability can change; use the options shown there. - Choose a small sample folder for your first sync. Installing and signing in do not automatically pair every folder on your computer. - If your organization controls software installation, use its approved installation process. ## Steps: download and install 1. **Open the official download section.** Go to [Get the app](https://dosya.dev/desktop/#downloads). The page selects an operating system based on your browser; use **Windows**, **macOS** or **Linux** if it selected the wrong one. 2. **Choose the package for this computer.** Use the download or store option shown for your system. Check the architecture and system requirements rather than choosing a package from its filename alone. 3. **Install the app.** On Windows, run the downloaded installer and follow its prompts. On macOS, open the disk image and copy the app to Applications, then open it there. On Linux, follow the package instructions on the download page: an AppImage needs executable permission, while a Debian package uses the system package installer. A store installation follows that store's prompts. 4. **Check an unexpected installer warning.** Confirm the source and compare the SHA-512 checksum using the page's **Checksum and requirements** instructions. If verification fails, download a fresh copy from the official page and stop using the mismatched package. 5. **Open Dosya.** Follow the introductory screens or select **Skip onboarding** to reach sign-in. ## Steps: sign in and check the workspace 1. **Use your existing account.** On **Welcome back**, enter **Email** and **Password**, then select **Sign in**. If you use a provider, select the corresponding **Continue with Google**, **Continue with GitHub** or **Continue with Apple** button and complete its browser flow. 2. **Complete any additional verification.** Follow the account's two-factor prompt if shown. Do not create another account to work around a missing factor; use your configured recovery method or contact support. 3. **Check the account.** Your name and email appear at the bottom of the sidebar after sign-in. Make sure they belong to the account whose files you want to use. 4. **Check the destination workspace.** Open the workspace name at the top of the sidebar to select the intended workspace. A team workspace may have different permissions and storage limits from your personal workspace. 5. **Choose the next task.** Use **Files** to browse, **Upload** for a manual transfer or **Sync** to pair a local folder. Follow the sync setup guide before adding an important working folder. ## Expected result The dashboard opens, the sidebar shows the correct account, and the workspace selector shows your intended destination. Open **Files** and confirm that you recognize that workspace's folders. If this is a new account, an empty file list is expected. A successful sign-in is the starting point for sync. Add and verify a folder pairing separately; no local folder is selected by these sign-in steps. ## Limitations The screenshots show the current macOS app with a disposable sample account. System installer dialogs and permission prompts differ across platforms and installation sources. Provider sign-in and every operating system's installer were not exercised for this guide. The app needs network access for account sign-in and cloud operations. Sync transfers also depend on the selected workspace's access and available storage. Ordinary desktop folder sync and **Vault** are separate workflows; choosing a sync folder does not make it a Vault folder. ## Troubleshooting **The download is for the wrong system.** Select the correct platform in Get the app and check its architecture requirements before downloading again. **Sign-in is refused.** Confirm the email and normal sign-in method. Use **Forgot password?** for a password account. If the account uses a provider, try that provider's button. Follow the displayed two-factor instructions when applicable. **Sign-in reports a connection error.** Confirm that the computer is online and that a VPN, proxy or firewall permits Dosya connections. Check [service status](https://status.dosya.dev/) and retry after connectivity returns. **The dashboard has the wrong files.** Check both the account email and workspace selector. If a team workspace is missing, ask its owner to confirm your membership and permissions. **The provider browser flow completes but the app remains signed out.** Return to Dosya, check whether the browser offered to reopen the app, and retry from the app's sign-in button. Share the displayed error and operating system with [support](https://dosya.dev/contact/), without passwords, verification codes or session tokens. ## Frequently asked questions ### Do I need a new account for desktop? No. Use the account you already use in the web app. ### Will signing in upload my computer's folders? No. Choose files for manual upload or create a sync pairing for a specific local folder. ### Can I switch between personal and team files? Use the workspace selector. Check it again before setting up each sync pairing. ## Related guides - [Desktop sync setup](/desktop/sync-folder) - [Choosing a desktop sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Start Dosya automatically after sign-in
summary: Enable Dosya at operating-system sign-in, verify its hidden macOS or Windows start, and keep sync pairs ready without reopening the app manually.
verification: Reviewed the setting label and login-item registration to `apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx`, `main/ipc.ts`, and `main/window-show.ts` on 2026-10-14. Production startup remains untested.
body: Enable **Launch at login** when this computer should start Dosya automatically after the operating-system user signs in. On macOS and Windows, the automatic start is deliberately hidden so sync can initialize without placing the main window in front of other apps. ## Before you start - Sign in to the Dosya desktop app and make sure its current sync pairings are the ones this computer should run. - Use the operating-system account that needs the startup entry. The setting is per computer user, not per Dosya workspace. - On the Mac App Store build, macOS 13 or later is required. Direct-download macOS builds and non-Apple-store builds use the regular login helper. - Save open work before the verification sign-out. Pausing sync first is sensible when files are actively changing. ## Steps 1. Open **Sync** in the desktop sidebar, select **Settings**, and scroll to **Desktop app**. 2. Turn on **Launch at login**. The description below it reads **Start dosya automatically when you sign in**. This toggle applies immediately; the separate **Save settings** button controls sync values such as concurrency and does not need to be pressed for startup registration. 3. Leave Settings and reopen it. Confirm the toggle remains on. The app reads the state back from the operating system, so an off state means registration was not applied. 4. Sign out of the current operating-system session and sign in again. On macOS and Windows, do not expect the main window to open: the login entry uses hidden startup. 5. Open the tray or menu-bar icon and bring up Dosya. Navigate to **Sync → Overview** and confirm each pairing shows its expected state. **Synced**, **Syncing**, **Paused**, **Offline**, **Waiting**, **Needs attention**, and **Needs permission** are distinct outcomes; automatic launch does not override a pause or error. ## Expected result Dosya starts once after the operating-system sign-in. On macOS or Windows, it remains in the tray or menu bar until opened. Existing enabled pairings become available to the sync engine, subject to their mode, permissions, battery preference, network and any saved pause. Enabling startup creates no new pairing and moves no file by itself. Turning **Launch at login** off later only changes future computer sign-ins. It does not quit the current process, disable a saved pairing, revoke the Dosya session or remove local and cloud content. ## Troubleshooting **Launch at login is missing.** The Mac App Store build cannot register its required service on macOS 12, so the app hides the toggle. Upgrade that computer to macOS 13 or newer or open Dosya manually after sign-in. **The toggle will not stay enabled.** The operating system did not report the login item as active. Check its login-item or startup-app settings and device policy, then repeat the in-app action. **Sync stayed Paused after startup.** A manual global pause persists. Use **Resume all**. A timed snooze of 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours or 8 hours resumes at its saved deadline; startup does not cancel it. **The app opens in front after login.** On supported macOS and Windows paths, login startup carries a hidden signal. Confirm Dosya was started by its registered login item rather than another shortcut or launcher. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Diagnose desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues)

title: Expand a photo cluster on desktop
summary: Open dense desktop map clusters, understand the zoom-16 clustering ceiling and count badges, and handle files sharing identical coordinates.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/MapPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/map/map-cluster.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/map/map-pins.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/map.spec.ts. Verified the 60-pixel radius, maximum cluster zoom 16, expansion behavior, coincident-point fallback, six representative samples, compact count labels and viewport-only markers. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The desktop map groups nearby pins into clusters so dense areas remain usable. Clustering uses a **60-pixel radius** through zoom level **16** and recalculates for the visible viewport as you pan or zoom. ## Before you start Open **Map** with at least two nearby located items visible. Cluster contents can include exact EXIF positions and approximate upload-IP positions when **Show approximate locations** is enabled. ## Steps 1. Find a numbered cluster. Counts through 999 display in full; larger badges are shortened by thousands, so 1,000 displays as **1k**. 2. Select the cluster. The map eases to Supercluster's expansion zoom when its members can separate. 3. Repeat until individual markers appear, then select a file pin to open its viewer or a folder pin to navigate to that folder. 4. Pan the map and observe that only markers for the current bounds are rendered. A cluster can therefore change as the viewport or zoom changes. A cluster may use up to six representative items internally and prefers a raster-photo cover where one is available. Those samples do not limit the number reported by its badge. ## Expected result A normal cluster expands toward separate markers without changing coordinates or file metadata. Map navigation remains read-only. ## Troubleshooting Items with identical coordinates cannot be separated spatially, even at the clustering ceiling. When such a cluster contains a file, selecting it at maximum expansion opens the first file sample as a practical fallback. If a cluster disappears after zooming or panning, return to its previous bounds or clear active folder/date filters. Turning off approximate locations can also remove every member of an upload-IP cluster. ## Related guides - [Explore the map](/files/file-map) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Filter the desktop photo map
summary: Filter the desktop map by a folder subtree or inclusive local-date range, see immediate marker updates, and reset all query criteria with Clear.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/map/MapFilterPanel.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/MapPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/map/map-pins.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/map.spec.ts. Verified Everywhere/folder controls, recursive folder scope, local inclusive day boundaries, captured-date fallback, immediate queries, Clear behavior and approximate-location independence. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: Desktop map filtering supports a folder and a **From**/**To** date range. There is no file-type filter and no Apply button; changing a control immediately requests and frames the matching pins. ## Before you start Open **Map** in the intended workspace. The folder selector lists folders returned for your accessible area. **Everywhere** removes the optional narrower folder choice; for a member confined to one folder, the API still anchors this request to that assigned folder and its descendants. Filters change only the current map query. ## Steps 1. Open the folder selector and choose a folder. Its descendants are included recursively, so nested located items remain eligible. 2. Set **From** to include records from 00:00:00 on that local calendar day. 3. Set **To** to include records through 23:59:59 on the chosen local day. A photo's captured/taken time is used when available; otherwise filtering falls back to upload time. 4. Watch the markers update after each control change. Use **Show approximate locations** separately if upload-IP pins should be included. 5. Select **Clear** to remove the chosen folder and both dates. The button appears only while at least one of those three controls is active. A folder-confined member returns to the assigned subtree rather than gaining a workspace-wide view. No stored metadata is rewritten by filtering. Local-day boundaries mean the same date selection can represent different Unix timestamps in different system time zones. ## Expected result Only pins inside the selected folder subtree and inclusive date interval remain. Clearing restores the broadest query your role permits while keeping the approximate-location toggle at its current setting; folder-confined access remains anchored. ## Troubleshooting If a photo appears outside the date you expected, check whether it has a captured timestamp; items without one use upload time. Also confirm the computer's current time zone before comparing day boundaries. If choosing a parent omits a nested item, clear the date fields and verify that the item has a usable GPS or approximate location. **No pins to show** can also mean all remaining pins are approximate while their toggle is off. ## Related guides - [Explore the map](/files/file-map) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Review desktop notifications
summary: Use the desktop notification bell and full inbox, mark or dismiss items, load older pages, and understand which actions have desktop routes.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/NotificationsPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/notifications-api.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/index.ts. Production behavior was not tested and no notification state was changed.
body: Desktop notifications belong to the signed-in Dosya account. The title-bar bell gives a ten-item preview, while **View all** opens the paginated inbox for older personal and broadcast messages. ## Before you start - Sign in to the account that should own the notification. Inbox access is account-scoped and is not limited by plan or workspace role. - Confirm the desktop app is online. The unread summary refreshes every 60 seconds; opening the bell fetches a fresh preview. - Treat a notification action as a real product action. Read the title, body, actor, age, and destination before choosing an action label. ## Steps 1. Select the title-bar **Notifications** bell. Its accessible label includes the exact unread count; the visible badge shows **99+** once the count exceeds 99. 2. In **Notifications**, inspect the newest ten items grouped by day. An unread item has a dot and a heavier title. The line below may show relative time and the actor’s name. 3. Click a row to mark it read. If its stored web path has a desktop equivalent, Dosya also opens that destination; otherwise the item remains readable without navigating to a broken route. 4. Use **Mark all read** to clear the unread state for every active personal and broadcast notification on the account. 5. Select the **Dismiss _title_** control to hide one item. Action labels supplied inside a notification may also dismiss it or navigate to a supported desktop route. 6. Choose **View all** for the full **Notifications** page. It requests 30 items per page and shows **Load older** while a cursor remains; the server accepts at most 50 per request. 7. Choose **Settings** from the preview to open the desktop profile settings when you need to change notification preferences. ## Read, dismiss, and navigation behavior Read and dismiss operations update the server and invalidate the unread summary. The full inbox applies the change immediately in the interface; if the request fails, it discards the optimistic state and refetches the authoritative list. Dismissing is different from reading. A read item stays in history, while a dismissed item is excluded from subsequent inbox queries. The desktop interface has no undo button for dismissal, so verify the title before selecting the X control. Notification paths are authored as web routes and mapped to known desktop destinations. Unsupported navigation actions are intentionally hidden. A message can therefore be valid even when clicking its row does not leave the inbox. ## Troubleshooting - **Loading…** that never resolves usually indicates an expired session or network failure. Reconnect, sign in again if required, and reopen the bell. - **You’re all caught up.** means the current query has no visible items; it can also appear after dismissing the last item. - When a badge remains stale after marking read, wait for the mutation and summary refresh, or close and reopen the bell. - If **Load older** fails, keep the current page and retry later. Loaded notifications are deduplicated by ID, so retrying does not create duplicate rows. - A notification that belongs to another account will not appear after an account switch; return to the account that received it. ## Expected result The bell and full inbox show only the authenticated account’s visible notifications. Read state persists, dismissal removes an item from future lists, older pages load in chronological groups, and only actions with valid desktop destinations navigate. ## Related guides - [Use the desktop system tray](/desktop/desktop-system-tray) - [Check desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Preview an Office document in the desktop app
summary: Preview Office files as server-converted PDF in the desktop app, understand the 50 MiB source limit, and recover from conversion or network errors.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/OfficePreview.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/file-type.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/preview-pdf.ts, apps/api/src/lib/onlyoffice/convert.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/office-preview.spec.ts. Verified formats, 50 MiB limits, the 3-second retry interval, 20-attempt timeout, version handling and exact failure messages. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The desktop app requests a server-side PDF conversion and displays the returned PDF in a read-only embedded viewer. The document is not converted solely on your device, and previewing does not edit the source. ## Before you start Use a DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, DOC, XLS, PPT, ODT, ODS, ODP, RTF or CSV file no larger than **50 MiB**. You must be signed in and allowed to view the selected file; no separate desktop-preview role control is present. ## Steps 1. Open the Office file from **Files**. 2. While the server converts it, leave the viewer open at **Preparing preview…**. A busy conversion is retried every **3 seconds**, up to **20 attempts**. 3. Read the PDF result with the embedded PDF controls. This surface is for viewing; use the product's separate editor workflow when you need to change document content. 4. If you selected an older file version before opening the viewer, verify that version's pages; the current version is cached separately from version-specific requests. The temporary PDF blob URL is revoked when the component closes. That cleanup affects only the local preview resource, not the stored Office document. ## Expected result The converted pages become readable inside the desktop window while the original cloud object and version history remain unchanged. ## Troubleshooting After the retry window, the app says **“This preview is taking too long. Download the file instead.”** A source over the limit produces **“This file is too large to preview. Download it instead.”** **“This file type cannot be previewed. Download it instead.”** identifies an unsupported conversion type. **“Could not reach the server.”** indicates connectivity trouble, while **“Could not prepare a preview for this file.”** covers another conversion failure. Download the original when retrying cannot produce a preview. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Uploading from desktop without creating a sync pair
summary: Choose a workspace folder on the desktop Upload page, drop or browse for files, and verify completion without creating an ongoing local-folder relationship.
verification: Verified the current native macOS desktop Upload page against an isolated local API/D1/R2 environment on 2026-10-12. A 31-byte text sample uploaded to the selected workspace root and reached the Complete queue state. Folder selection, retry, pause, cancel, multipart threshold and workspace-switch cancellation were source reviewed; Windows/Linux and production were not exercised. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Open **Upload** in the desktop sidebar when you want to send selected files once without pairing a local folder. Choose the destination before adding files, then wait for every queue row to reach **Complete** and verify the cloud copy in Files. ## One-off upload compared with sync A one-off upload sends the selected file to the chosen workspace folder. Later edits to the local original are not watched or uploaded automatically. A sync pair creates an ongoing relationship between a local folder and a cloud folder. Its mode can carry later edits and, in some modes, deletions. Use one-off upload for an occasional handoff; use Sync when you deliberately want continuing behavior. ## Before you start - Select the correct workspace in the sidebar. - Decide which cloud folder should receive the file. The default is **Root (top level)**. - Keep the app open and the computer awake for the transfer. - Check workspace storage and your upload permission. - Use a harmless small sample first if the destination or account is new. ## Steps: choose the destination 1. Select **Upload** in the sidebar, or use **Upload files** from Dashboard. 2. In **Upload options**, select **Folder**. 3. Choose **Root (top level)** or a listed folder, then select **Select folder**. You can also create a folder from the Upload page. 4. Check the destination name shown near the Upload heading before adding files. ## Upload the files 1. Drag files from your file manager onto **Drop files here to upload**, or select the drop zone and browse your computer. 2. Watch each item in the queue. Up to three items can transfer concurrently. 3. Use the queue's pause control to stop starting pending work temporarily. Cancel returns active items to the pending state and pauses the queue. 4. If an item shows an error, correct the cause and use its **Retry** control or **Retry all failed**. 5. Wait until the header says **Complete** and each intended row has a check mark. 6. Open **Files**, browse to the chosen destination and open or download your sample to verify it. ## What happens during transfer Files larger than 50 MB use the desktop app's resumable multipart path; smaller files use a single upload request. The service still enforces its current upload and workspace limits. The destination is captured when a file enters the queue. Changing the folder selector afterward does not retarget items already queued. Choose the new destination before adding the next files. Switching to another workspace while a queue contains items cancels the queue rather than silently sending them to the old workspace. Select the new workspace and add the files again after checking its destination. ## Expected result Every intended row reaches **Complete**, and the file appears in the chosen workspace folder. No sync pair is created, and later changes to the local original do not update the uploaded cloud copy automatically. ## Limits and safety notes - The page uploads files, rather than creating an ongoing relationship or mirroring a folder tree. - Leaving the page aborts active requests. Wait for completion before navigating away. - Pause affects this upload queue. It is separate from the desktop Sync pause controls. - Removing a pending or failed row removes it from the current queue; it does not delete a cloud file that already completed. - **Clear done** only clears completed rows from the screen. - Uploads use the workspace's configured storage location; the Upload page chooses the folder, not a region. ## Troubleshooting **The file went to the wrong folder.** Check the destination that was selected when the file entered the queue. Move the completed cloud file in Files, then choose the intended destination before adding another file. **The queue paused.** Select Resume on the queue. If the app or computer was offline, reconnect first. **An item failed.** Read its error, check the connection, storage and permission, then use Retry. For repeated failure, test a small harmless file in the workspace root. **The queue cleared after switching workspace.** This is deliberate. It prevents pending files from uploading to a workspace that is no longer active. Add them again in the new workspace. **Complete is shown but I cannot find the file.** Recheck the workspace and folder selected at enqueue time, refresh Files and search for the exact filename. Do not create a sync pair to compensate for an unknown destination. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does a one-off upload sync later edits? No. Upload the changed file again to create a new cloud version or use a deliberately configured sync pair. ### Can I upload without opening the Sync page? Yes. Use **Upload** in the sidebar or **Upload files** from Dashboard. ### Can I change the destination after files are queued? The new selection applies to files added afterward. Each queued item keeps the workspace and folder captured when it was added. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Desktop sync setup](/desktop/sync-folder) - [Pausing, resuming or stopping desktop sync](/desktop/pause-resume-sync) - [Fixing a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload)

title: Open Dosya from the system tray or menu bar
summary: Open or recreate Dosya from its Windows or Linux system tray or macOS menu bar while sync remains active in the resident background process.
verification: Reviewed locally in apps/desktop/src/main/tray.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/window-show.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/window-reclaim.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/window-reclaim.test.ts. Native production tray environments were not controlled.
body: Closing the Dosya window normally hides it instead of ending the app. The tray or menu-bar icon can reveal the window again and continues to reflect sync state while the renderer is hidden. **Before you start** - Look for the **dosya** icon in the Windows/Linux system tray or macOS menu bar. - If a Linux desktop does not expose its tray icon, relaunching Dosya asks the resident single instance to show or recreate the hidden window. ## Steps 1. Check the icon tooltip. It reads **dosya** before status is available or `dosya - _sync summary_` when the sync engine has reported its current state. 2. Single-click the tray icon, or open its menu and select **Open dosya**. Windows also accepts a double-click on the icon. 3. Wait for the main window to appear and receive focus. If its hidden renderer was reclaimed after the default five-minute delay, Dosya creates a replacement window instead of restoring the old renderer. 4. Confirm the expected account and workspace after recreation. Window geometry is persisted, while authentication and the main-process sync engine survive ordinary hide/reclaim behavior. 5. Inspect the tray’s sync controls when needed: **Resume Sync** or **Pause Sync**, **Sync All Now**, and **Open Sync Folder** appear when pairs exist; **Upload File...** opens the upload route. 6. Use **Quit dosya** only when the process must stop.
