Closing the visible window returns supported tray builds to the background and does not perform the quit workflow. ## Expected result Dosya becomes visible and refreshes its sync store after the show event. Background sync may have continued even when a five-minute hidden-window reclaim destroyed the renderer. If the icon is missing after closing the window, launch Dosya again. The single-instance handler asks the resident process to show or recreate its window on Windows and Linux; macOS uses its normal activation path. ## Related guides - [Use the desktop system tray](/desktop/desktop-system-tray) - [Check desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Open the photo map in the desktop app
summary: Open the active workspace map, distinguish GPS and approximate locations, handle scanning or basemap failures, and open mapped files or folders.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/MapPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/map/map-pins.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/map/map-cluster.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/map/pins.ts, apps/api/src/lib/location/origin.ts and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/map.spec.ts. Verified EXIF/IP sources, the upload-origin setting gate, count labels, empty and basemap states, initial fit, click destinations and read-only behavior. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The desktop **Map** visualizes locations available to the active workspace. Photo GPS metadata creates exact pins; when upload-origin recording is enabled for the workspace, upload-IP data can create approximate file or folder locations that the map shows by default. ## Before you start Sign in, select the intended workspace and choose **Map** in desktop navigation. The map reads accessible location records; opening it does not add GPS metadata, move files or alter upload history. ## Steps 1. Read the status chip: it reports values such as **2 located**, **3 approximate** and **1 scanning…**. 2. Leave **Show approximate locations** enabled to include recorded upload-IP positions, or turn it off when you only want GPS-derived items. The toggle cannot restore approximate data that the workspace's upload-origin setting did not record. 3. Allow the first result set to frame automatically. The initial fit is capped at zoom level 12 so nearby pins retain context. 4. Select a file marker to open that file's viewer. Selecting a folder marker navigates to that folder in **Files**. Exact coordinates come from EXIF data, while approximate coordinates can reflect an upload network rather than the place where the content was created. Consider that distinction before treating a pin as evidence of a person's location. ## Expected result Accessible located items appear for the selected workspace, and choosing a pin opens its associated file or folder without modifying it. ## Troubleshooting **“Map background unavailable right now. Your pins still work.”** means the basemap failed while interactive markers remain usable. **“No geotagged photos yet”** appears when nothing is located. If processing continues, the page instead shows **“No files or folders with a location yet”** and **“Scanning your files for location…”**. With approximate locations hidden, **“No pins to show”** may be followed by **“All located items are approximate - enable the toggle above to see them.”** If no approximate markers or folders appear, check whether upload-origin recording is enabled for that workspace. Disabling it excludes IP-derived records from the map; the approximate-location toggle only filters records the API returns. ## Related guides - [Explore the map](/files/file-map) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Prepare a safe desktop problem report
summary: Prepare a useful Dosya desktop bug ticket while controlling screenshot, diagnostics, recent-log filenames, body length, and sensitive data exposure.
verification: Locally reviewed using apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/ReportProblemDialog.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/ReportProblemDialog.test.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/bug-report.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/bug-report.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/bug-report.test.ts. The production support endpoint received no ticket.
body: The desktop problem form sends an authenticated support ticket. Its screenshot and diagnostics start enabled, while the recent log is opt-in because it can disclose filenames from synced folders. **Before you start** - Sign in first; otherwise the dialog instructs you to sign in and reopen **Help > Report a Problem…**. - Arrange the window so its visible content is safe before sending because the screenshot is captured at send time and has no preview. ## Steps 1. Open **Help > Report a Problem…** or press `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B`. The dialog title is **Report a bug** and it creates a support ticket tied to the account. 2. In **What went wrong? What did you expect instead?**, provide the smallest repeatable sequence, expected behavior, actual behavior, and approximate time. Blank text keeps **Send** disabled. 3. Review **Attach a screenshot of this window**, enabled by default. Hide unrelated names or content before sending; the image is captured only after **Send** is pressed. 4. Inspect the enabled **Diagnostics** rows: **App**, **System**, **Workspace**, **Page**, **Error reference**, **Error**, and **Sync** appear when values exist. Untick **Include** when that context is unnecessary. 5. Leave **Include the recent log (last 200 lines)** off unless support needs it. The reader takes at most 64 KiB from the end of the log, and those lines can contain synced filenames. 6. Select **Send**. The user text plus optional log is limited to 9,500 characters; a screenshot over 4,500,000 bytes or a failed capture is skipped while the ticket still submits. ## Expected result Success shows **Report sent**, says replies go to the account email, and includes the first eight ticket-ID characters when available. **Screenshot skipped** explains whether capture failed or the image was too large. On **Could not send report**, keep the dialog open, review the returned description, and retry later. Common home paths are redacted in diagnostics, but that filter does not promise removal of every secret from text, screenshots, or logs. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Create a desktop problem report](/desktop/desktop-problem-report)

title: Send a desktop problem report
summary: Send a signed-in desktop bug report with optional diagnostics, screenshot, and log tail while controlling exactly which private data is included.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/ReportProblemDialog.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/bug-report.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/bug-report.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/support/tickets/index.ts. Production submission was not tested and no support ticket was created.
body: The desktop reporter creates a private support ticket on the signed-in account. You control three distinct payloads: your description, an optional screenshot of the current window, and optional diagnostics or recent application log. ## Before you start - Reproduce the problem once and record the expected behavior, actual behavior, and the shortest sequence that triggers it. - Sign in first. When signed out, the dialog says **Sign in first, then open Help > Report a problem again. Your report is sent as a support ticket on your account.** - Remove passwords, recovery keys, API tokens, and personal file contents from the visible window and your written description. - Any signed-in plan can create a report. The API allows 5 new tickets per account per hour and at most 10 tickets that are not closed. ## Steps 1. Open **Help > Report a problem**. The dialog title is **Report a bug** and explains that it creates a support ticket you can follow on the web. 2. In **What went wrong? What did you expect instead?**, provide exact steps and the time the failure occurred. The desktop app caps the submitted body at 9,500 characters, leaving room below the server’s 10,000-character limit. 3. Review **Attach a screenshot of this window**. It is on by default and captures the window only when you press **Send report**. Untick it if any visible content is private. 4. Leave **Include the recent log (last 200 lines)** off unless support needs it. The reader takes at most 64 KiB from the end of the desktop log, then keeps the newest 200 lines; logs can contain names from synced folders. 5. Inspect **Diagnostics** and untick **Include** if needed. The card may include app version, distribution and CPU architecture, operating-system release, locale, workspace ID, page path, error reference, error message, and a count-only sync summary. 6. Select **Send report**. Keep the dialog open while it reads optional data and uploads the ticket. ## Privacy and size behavior Diagnostics redact file URLs and common macOS, Linux, and Windows user paths to ****, strip query strings from the page, and clamp every diagnostics string to 300 characters. The diagnostics panel states **Nothing from your files is included.** That promise covers the structured diagnostics; a screenshot can display visible file content, and the optional log can name files. The screenshot is sent as one JPEG named **window.jpg**. If capture fails or exceeds 4,500,000 bytes, the report still sends and Dosya shows **Screenshot skipped** with the reason. The support endpoint accepts up to three images under 5 MB each, but this desktop form supplies only the single window capture. ## Submission and recovery Success closes the dialog and shows **Report sent**. The message includes the first eight characters of the ticket ID when available and says that support replies at the account email. The report is stored as an open support ticket; use the web support area to follow or close it. On failure, the dialog remains open and shows **Could not send report** with the returned reason. Copy your description before restarting if you need to preserve it. A report cannot be recalled from this dialog after submission; close the ticket or add a correction through the web ticket instead. ## Expected result One bug ticket is created with the description and only the optional data left enabled. The active workspace ID is attached only when the signed-in user still belongs to it. You receive a confirmation reference, and subsequent support replies go to the account email. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Diagnose desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues)

title: Read a desktop sync activity row
summary: Interpret desktop Sync Activity timestamps, pair names, raw messages, live elapsed state, and the separate structured transfer progress view.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/sync/types.ts. Production sync logs and customer workspace data were not read.
body: A row in **Sync > Activity** is a timestamped engine message, not a structured transfer receipt. File direction, byte progress, percentage, and ETA appear separately on **Overview** while a transfer is active. **Before you start** - Open **Sync** and identify the pair or remote folder involved. - Remember that Activity receives the global recent log list; changing workspaces does not prove every visible line belongs to the selected workspace. ## Steps 1. Select **Activity**. When no entries exist, the page says **No sync activity yet** and **Activity will appear here when syncing starts**. 2. Read the first column as local time with hours, minutes, and seconds. It marks when the engine appended the message, not a server-side completion receipt. 3. Read the second column as the remote folder name. If the current pair list cannot resolve the log’s pair ID, Dosya shows the first eight ID characters instead. 4. Read the remaining text as the raw engine message. Interpret exactly what it says; the row has no separate direction, progress, or final-state fields. 5. Use the live header above the log for currently syncing pairs. It shows the remote folder, `statusText` or **Syncing…**, and an elapsed clock that updates every second. 6. Switch to **Overview** for active upload/download icons, filenames, bytes transferred, file counts, percentage, speed context, and ETA. At most five active transfer rows appear before a `+N more transferring...` line. ## Expected result The correct interpretation ties a time and raw message to a pair without inventing structured fields. The engine retains up to 200 log entries, while each status response exposes the latest 50. If progress appears stalled, compare the live header and Overview status before reporting it. Activity can stay quiet during a long phase even while the one-second elapsed clock confirms the pair remains active. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Create a desktop problem report](/desktop/desktop-problem-report)

title: Restart the desktop app safely
summary: Quit and reopen Dosya through its cleanup path so sync state is retained, interrupted operations requeue, and partial receive files are removed.
verification: Locally reviewed against apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/quit-state.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/lan-receive.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/vault-save.ts. No production client process was restarted.
body: A window close usually hides Dosya to the tray, so a real restart must use **Quit dosya** or the application’s Quit command. That path gives the sync engine and receive sinks a bounded cleanup window. **Before you start** - Save work in other editors; Dosya cannot preserve unsaved changes owned by another application. - Note the affected pair’s status and any `N files not synced` count so the reopened state can be compared. ## Steps 1. Inspect **Sync > Overview** and note active transfers, pair states, and file-error counts. You may pause deliberately, but pausing is not required for the engine’s write-through persistence. 2. Open the tray or menu-bar menu and choose **Quit dosya**, or use the operating system’s application Quit command. Do not use the window close button as proof the process ended. 3. Allow up to five seconds for shutdown. Dosya stops watchers and pollers, releases folder access, aborts LAN receives, and aborts Vault plaintext sinks before the bounded quit completes. 4. Launch Dosya again and sign in if the session is no longer valid. The sync engine does not start without a session, and an account change removes stale pairs to prevent cross-account data exposure. 5. Return to **Sync > Overview**. Database operations left as `running` by the stopped process are reset to pending at startup, and enabled pairs resume unless sync is globally paused. 6. Verify the earlier pair state and error ledger. Interrupted LAN or Vault destination files should not remain as apparently complete partial files; retry any source operation that still needs delivery. ## Expected result Completed sync mutations remain recorded because the engine writes changes through as they happen. Interrupted queued operations resume from pending rather than depending on an end-of-process save. If Dosya merely disappears into the tray, choose **Quit dosya** again. A forced operating-system termination can bypass the normal five-second cleanup, although the next start still requeues database operations left running. ## Related guides - [Install and sign in to the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Check for desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Review launch-at-login behavior
summary: Audit Dosya's saved launch-at-login state across supported desktop builds, test one sign-in, and diagnose a missing or refused startup setting.
verification: Reviewed startup support and applied-state handling in `apps/desktop/src/main/login-item.ts`, `ipc.ts`, `window-show.ts`, and their tests on 2026-10-14. No production sign-in cycle was run.
body: Review **Launch at login** when Dosya starts unexpectedly, fails to start, or appears to ignore its saved switch. The preference belongs to the operating-system user account. It does not depend on the active Dosya workspace, subscription or workspace role. ## Before you start - Open **Sync → Settings** and locate the **Desktop app** section. - Record the installed distribution and operating-system version. The Mac App Store build supports this switch on macOS 13 or later; it is hidden on macOS 12 and when that build cannot read a supported system version. - Finish or pause important transfers before signing out of the computer. Signing out interrupts in-flight work. - Close duplicate Dosya windows and check whether another manually created operating-system startup entry also launches the app. ## Steps 1. Read **Launch at login** and its description, **Start dosya automatically when you sign in**. The displayed switch comes from the operating system's applied login-item state, not only a local preference file. 2. Toggle the setting once, wait for the control to settle, then leave and reopen Settings. The app asks the operating system to update the login item and reads the applied state back. If the system refuses registration, the switch can remain off. 3. Test with one real operating-system sign-out and sign-in. Do not treat quitting and reopening Dosya as a login-item test. 4. On macOS or Windows, allow several seconds for the background app to initialize, then open Dosya from its tray or menu-bar icon. Login launches are intentionally hidden: macOS reports `wasOpenedAsHidden`, while Windows registers the `--hidden` argument. The main window should not steal focus. 5. On Linux and non-Apple-store distributions, registration uses Electron's regular helper mechanism. The explicit hidden-launch detection in the desktop code is implemented for macOS and Windows, so judge Linux by whether Dosya starts rather than assuming identical tray behavior. 6. Return to **Sync → Settings**. Confirm the switch still matches the result you wanted and check **Overview** for the expected pairings. ## Expected result When enabled on a supported build, Dosya registers once for the current operating-system account and launches at the next sign-in. A macOS or Windows login launch stays hidden until you open it from the tray or menu bar. Disabling the switch removes that requested login behavior; it does not sign out of Dosya, remove sync pairs or delete files. ## Troubleshooting **The switch is absent.** A sandboxed Mac App Store build hides it on macOS 12 or when the OS version is unreadable. Update macOS to 13 or later, or start Dosya manually. Workspace permissions will not make this control appear. **The switch returns to off.** The app reports the state accepted by the operating system. Check the system's login-item controls and security policy, then try once more. Reinstalling is unnecessary until you have ruled out an OS refusal. **Two copies appear to start.** Remove any separate shortcut, scheduled task or manually added login item, then keep the in-app switch as the single registration. The Windows getter also recognizes an older executable login entry, which can explain a legacy setup. **Dosya started but no window appeared on macOS or Windows.** That is the intended hidden state for an automatic login launch. Use the tray or menu-bar icon; then inspect Sync Overview for errors. ## Related guides - [Install and sign in to the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Check for desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Use desktop search from the keyboard
summary: Open workspace search with Command-K or Control-K, use its 250 ms live query, filter result types, and navigate safely to the matching item.
verification: Reviewed locally in apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/layout/AppShell.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SearchPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/menu-template.ts, and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/search-shortcut.spec.ts. Production search data was not queried.
body: The authenticated desktop shell reserves `⌘K` on macOS and `Ctrl+K` elsewhere for Dosya search. Results come from the active workspace and are separated into files, folders, shares, and file requests. **Before you start** - Focus the Dosya main window and confirm the intended workspace in the sidebar. - The global shortcut is available inside the authenticated shell; it does not operate from the signed-out screen. ## Steps 1. Press `⌘K` on macOS or `Ctrl+K` on Windows and Linux. The same action is available as **Search dosya…** in the application menu. 2. Confirm `/search` opens and the field **Search files, folders, shares...** receives focus. The sidebar also displays the platform-specific shortcut beside **Search...**. 3. Type a distinctive complete or partial name. The input updates the URL and runs the workspace query after a 250 ms pause; pressing Enter also submits immediately. 4. Check the result count, then narrow with **All**, **Files**, **Folders**, **Shared**, or **Requests**. Each badge reflects the matching count in that group. 5. Select the matching row only after confirming its type and identifying metadata. A file result navigates to its containing folder rather than promising to open the viewer directly. 6. If the result is absent, clear the field with the `X`, verify the active workspace, and try a less restrictive term. An empty query sends no search request. ## Expected result Search returns workspace-scoped matches across files, folders, shared links, and file requests. The selected result routes to the relevant desktop location for further inspection. If `Cmd/Ctrl+K` does nothing, refocus the authenticated Dosya window and use **Search dosya…**. Operating-system shortcuts or another foreground application can receive keystrokes before Dosya. ## Related guides - [Use the desktop system tray](/desktop/desktop-system-tray) - [Check desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Install an update from an app store
summary: Update Microsoft Store, Mac App Store, or Snap installations through their owning store, then verify the installed Dosya version and sync state.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/UpdatesSection.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/distribution.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/updater.ts and apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/store-surfaces.test.ts. Production stores were not opened and no production action was performed.
body: Microsoft Store, Mac App Store, and Snap installations are store-managed. Dosya disables its direct-download updater in these builds so two update systems cannot race to replace the same installation. ## Before you start - Open **Settings > Updates** and read the distribution named after **Updates are managed by the…**. The app detects Microsoft Store from its Windows package container, Mac App Store from the macOS store build, and Snap only when the running package identifies itself as the **dosya** snap. - Save open work and allow active transfers to finish before applying a store update. - Store delivery has no Dosya plan or workspace-role requirement. Your operating-system store account, administrator policy, and package-manager permissions decide whether installation is allowed. - Do not download a direct installer over the store copy. Store builds intentionally hide Dosya’s installer history and **Check for updates** control. ## Steps 1. In **Settings > Updates**, note **You’re on v_version_** so you have a before value. 2. For Microsoft Store, choose **Open Microsoft Store**. Dosya opens the store’s **Downloads and updates** destination; request updates there and install the Dosya entry. 3. For Mac App Store, choose **Open Mac App Store**. The deep link opens the Updates page; install the available Dosya version with the Apple ID that owns the app. 4. For Snap Store, there is no open-store button. Snapd refreshes installed snaps on its own schedule. To request it immediately, run **snap refresh dosya** in a terminal with the permissions required by that machine. 5. Wait for the store or snap command to complete, then fully quit and reopen Dosya if the platform did not restart it. 6. Return to **Settings > Updates** and compare **You’re on v_version_** with the version recorded before the update. ## What the store owns A store build reports **store-managed** internally. Its self-update check, install, and reveal-file handlers are no-ops, and the updater does not contact Dosya’s executable feed. Microsoft Store and Mac App Store builds can open their native update pages; Snap relies on snapd and exposes no clickable page. The store controls download size, rollout timing, approval prompts, rollback availability, and whether an organization blocks the release. Dosya can display the installed version but cannot force a delayed store rollout to arrive. ## Troubleshooting - **Version unknown** means the renderer did not receive the installed app version. Restart Dosya after the store operation before assuming installation failed. - If Microsoft Store or Mac App Store opens without a Dosya update, refresh its update list and confirm the same store account installed the app. A staged release may not yet be offered to that device. - If **snap refresh dosya** reports insufficient permission, run it through the machine’s approved administrator workflow. Do not replace the snap with an AppImage unless you intend to change distribution channels. - If the page displays direct-download controls, this installation was detected as **direct**. Use the direct update guide instead of a store workflow. - When the version changes but sync remains stopped, reopen the relevant workspace and diagnose sync separately; store installation does not alter cloud files. ## Expected result The owning store replaces the application package and Dosya reopens with a newer **You’re on v…** value. Existing cloud data remains in the account. Update rollback follows the store’s rules. Preserve unsynced local work before any package replacement. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Diagnose desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues)

title: Switch workspaces in the desktop app
summary: Switch the Dosya desktop workspace, verify its saved selection and scoped queries, and interpret each workspace storage and sync status indicator.
verification: Locally verified with apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/workspace-context.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SearchPage.tsx. No production workspace was selected.
body: The workspace switcher changes the active ID used by desktop file, folder, search, and dashboard queries. Its rows can also expose available storage and a compact sync-state indicator. **Before you start** - Sign in to an account that belongs to at least two workspaces. - Finish any form whose unsaved values should stay associated with the current workspace before changing context. ## Steps 1. Select the current workspace control at the top of the sidebar. The menu lists only workspaces returned for the signed-in account. 2. Review each row’s name and icon. When storage data is available, the row shows `_free_ free of _total_`; a dot or spinner can indicate error, syncing, paused, or synced pairs. 3. Choose a different workspace. A check marks the active row, and Dosya displays **Switching workspace…** with the selected icon and name. 4. Wait for the overlay to close after its two-second display window. The selection is stored as `dosya_active_workspace`, allowing a later launch to request the same workspace when membership still exists. 5. Open **Files**, **Dashboard**, or Search and confirm its content belongs to the selected workspace. File and search query keys include the active workspace ID, causing separate data retrieval. 6. If the saved workspace is unavailable, let Dosya fall back to the first authorized workspace. Reopen the menu and verify the check before uploading, deleting, or sharing anything. ## Expected result The sidebar identifies the new active workspace and workspace-scoped pages use its ID. The workspace list has a 10-second stale time, refetches on window focus, and retries an initial post-login failure three times at 500 ms. A sync indicator describes pairs assigned to that workspace; it does not mean every global Activity log line is workspace-filtered. Use the pair name before acting on Activity evidence. ## Related guides - [Use the desktop system tray](/desktop/desktop-system-tray) - [Check desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Check storage before starting desktop sync
summary: Check cloud capacity, large-folder count warnings, and the desktop download guard before starting a storage-intensive sync pair with fewer surprises.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/DashboardPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/folder-estimate.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, and apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts. Production quota and disk limits were not tested.
body: Dosya exposes cloud usage and a large-folder entry count, but it does not calculate one combined local-size, disk-free, and workspace-headroom forecast. Check each available signal before starting a large pair. **Before you start** - Select the destination workspace and decide whether the pair uploads, downloads, or works in both directions. - Use the operating system’s storage view when you need the volume’s current free bytes; the Add sync flow does not display that number. ## Steps 1. Open **Dashboard** and read **Storage used**, its percentage, and `_used_ of _total_`. Include the displayed trash bytes because trashed workspace items still consume cloud capacity. 2. Open the workspace switcher as a second capacity check. A workspace row with storage data reports `_free_ free of _total_`; absence of that subline is not evidence of unlimited space. 3. In **Sync**, choose **Add sync folder**, select the cloud and local folders, and continue to **Advanced**. Dosya estimates file and folder counts without calculating their byte size. 4. Interpret the estimate bounds: the breadth-first read stops after five seconds or 200,000 entries, skips unreadable directories and symlinks, and marks the result truncated when its budget ends. 5. When the folder has at least 50,000 files or the estimate is truncated, read the many-hours/memory/bandwidth warning and enable **Sync it anyway** only after checking the source independently. 6. For a planned download batch, Dosya sums every new or updated remote file before writing bytes; a pull preflight likewise sums every new or changed file in the remote snapshot. Keep that combined total plus 256 MiB free or the pair records `Low disk space: _free_ MB free, need ~_required_ MB. Free up space to continue syncing.` ## Expected result The pair starts only after any large-folder acknowledgement, and the destination workspace has enough visible cloud headroom for expected uploads. Upload-only work intentionally has no local free-space guard. The guard runs once for the whole planned download set or pull snapshot, before those bytes are written. When `statfs` is unavailable, such as on some network drives, Dosya permits the attempt, so external disk monitoring remains necessary. ## Related guides - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Set up a sync folder](/desktop/sync-folder)

title: Stop a repeated desktop sync conflict loop
summary: Stop recurring desktop sync conflicts by pausing edits, comparing conflict copies, choosing an authoritative result, and verifying stable convergence.
verification: Locally reviewed against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/deletion-guard.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/conflict-name.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/conflict-name.test.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/sync/upload-metadata.ts. Production files were not resolved or deleted.
body: A conflict can recur when another editor or device keeps changing the same path. First stop new writes, then decide between the original remote version and the timestamped local conflict copy. **Before you start** - Identify every device or editor changing the path and save any unsaved work. - A resolution can upload over the remote version, remove a local file, or create another copy. **Keep remote** tries operating-system trash first, then permanently unlinks the local file if trash refuses. ## Steps 1. Open **Sync > Overview**, find the affected pair, and choose its **Pause** action. Stop editing the same path on other devices before resolving anything. 2. Open **Issues**. Under the default **Keep both copies** strategy, Dosya often resolves automatically and shows a conflict-copy notice with **Show both versions**. 3. Select **Show both versions** and compare the original path with `name (conflict copy YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS from Device).ext`. Numbered suffixes prevent same-second copies from overwriting each other. 4. For an unresolved card, use **Keep local** only when local bytes should replace the remote version. This explicit choice uploads without the stale version guard that originally caused the conflict. 5. Choose **Keep remote** only when the cloud copy is authoritative. Dosya tries to move the tracked local file to OS trash, permanently unlinks it if trash refuses, drops its local index row, and triggers an immediate poll. Choose **Keep both** to rename and upload the local variant. 6. Delete an unwanted duplicate only after the desired content exists safely, then resume the pair with one writer. Confirm no new conflict-copy notice or unresolved card returns on the next cycle. ## Expected result The path converges to the chosen content, or both named versions remain intentionally side by side. A successful **Keep remote** can leave the discarded local version in OS trash or remove it permanently when trash is unavailable; a failed resolution re-adds its conflict card. If copies keep appearing, pause again and find the remaining writer. Repeated conflict copies are evidence of continuing divergence, not a signal to keep deleting whichever file appears newest. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync issues](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Resolve conflicts](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Resolving desktop sync conflicts and keeping both copies
summary: Recognize an automatic conflict copy, use Keep both for an unresolved conflict, and verify both versions before choosing what to retain.
verification: Reviewed the current SQLite reconciliation, adopted-history safety, conflict naming and resolution source on 2026-10-11. Actual native macOS runs against isolated API/D1/R2 verified a genuine permission-denied resolution error, successful manual Keep both, and automatic Keep both after a fresh launch. Manual 36/46-byte and automatic 41/56-byte sample versions matched both local and downloaded cloud copies, with exactly one preserved copy per original and three clean requested cycles after each recovery. Destructive choices, simultaneous active-transfer retries, other modes, Windows, Linux and production behavior were not manually exercised. The matching desktop fixes must ship before these instructions are deployed.
body: With **Keep both copies**, the desktop app normally preserves a conflict automatically and reports it in **Sync → Issues**. The local version is renamed as a dated **conflict copy**; the cloud version returns under the original filename on a following cycle. If an unresolved conflict card remains, select **Keep both**, let sync finish and verify both files before removing either. ## Before you start - Select the workspace and pairing containing the affected file. Check the cloud folder, local path and **Mode** in **Sync → Overview**. - These steps use **Full Sync**, where changes can travel in both directions. [One-way modes](/desktop/sync-modes) have different transfer rules; do not change a pairing's mode as a first response to a conflict. - Close the file in applications that might keep saving it while you resolve the conflict. Ask other collaborators to finish their edits before you choose a final version. - Keep separate copies of important versions before selecting an action that can replace or remove one. If you are unsure which version to keep, retain both. - Leave the desktop app open, with the relevant drive connected and a working network, so the renamed copy can upload and the original can download. ## Why a conflict happens A conflict can occur when the same file changes on this computer and in the cloud before either side has received the other change. It can also occur when the same path already exists on both sides without a shared sync history. For a new Full Sync pairing, the wizard defaults to **Keep both copies** under **Conflict resolution**. Existing pairings retain their saved rule. **Last write wins** can choose one update based on modification times; it does not always create a second copy. A later time does not establish which version contains the work you want. ## Steps: find an automatically kept conflict copy 1. **Open Sync → Issues.** Find the notice for the affected folder. A notice that both versions were kept means the app handled the conflict rather than waiting for a manual choice. You may see this notice without a card containing resolution buttons. 2. **Select Show both versions.** This opens the local sync folder. The same folder is available through **Overview → the row's three-dot menu → Open folder**. Look beside the original filename for a name containing **conflict copy**, a date and time, and the device name. 3. **Allow the following cycle to finish.** The local version was renamed, so the original filename may be temporarily absent. In Full Sync, the cloud version is downloaded to that original path on a following cycle. Check **Activity** or use the row's **Sync now** control if a fresh cycle is needed. Check Overview for failed files if either transfer has not completed. 4. **Verify both versions.** Open your own files and confirm which changes each contains. The dated conflict copy represents the local version at the time it was renamed; the original filename receives the cloud version. Confirm both files also appear in the intended cloud folder before you rely on that destination as a copy. ## Steps: use Keep both on an unresolved conflict 1. **Find the conflict card in Issues.** Match its filename and local path to the affected pairing. The card has **Local** and **Remote** details and three buttons: **Keep local**, **Keep remote** and **Keep both**. Local means this computer; Remote means the cloud counterpart. 2. **Check the local folder is available.** Reconnect its drive and resolve any access error. If the automatic copy could not be created, correct that cause before trying again. The sizes and displayed times help identify the versions; they do not prove which version should win. 3. **Select Keep both.** This preserves the local version under a separate conflict-copy filename and uploads that copy. For Full Sync, let a following cycle bring the cloud version back under the original filename. Do not choose Keep local or Keep remote merely to clear the card. 4. **Confirm the outcome.** Return to Overview and Activity, let the transfers finish, then check the local and cloud folders. The conflict card should disappear after successful resolution. Confirm both versions are present and contain the changes you expected. A **Conflict resolved** toast alone is not sufficient proof. ## Expected result After Full Sync settles, the folder contains the cloud version under its original filename and the local version under a name such as `notes (conflict copy 2026-10-11 09-30-00 from My Computer).txt`. The actual date, time and device name vary. The filename extension is retained; an additional numbered suffix can distinguish copies created at the same time. Both versions should be available at the intended destinations, with no unresolved conflict or failed-file entry for their transfers. An informational conflict-copy notice can remain after the conflict card is gone. Open and check your own copies before treating the recovery as complete. ## Choose a final version after preserving both If you want to compare or combine the versions, pause the pairing in Overview while you work on your own copies. Keep a separate backup of both originals, then use the appropriate application to create the version you want. Resume the pairing when you are ready for the resulting changes to transfer and verify the cloud copy again. Deleting a conflict copy is optional. In Full Sync, deleting a local file can delete its cloud counterpart, and deleting it in the cloud can remove the local counterpart. Keep both until you have verified the final version and no longer need the other copy. ## What the other buttons do **Keep local** sends the current local version to replace the cloud version. Use it only after confirming that this computer holds the version you want. It does not retain a separate conflict copy automatically. **Keep remote** chooses the cloud version. It can remove the tracked local file before downloading the cloud version. The app attempts the operating system's trash first, but can permanently remove the local file if trash is unavailable. Preserve a separate local copy before selecting it when that version matters. These choices do not merge edits. If a version was replaced already, check [Version history](/files/version-history) for an available earlier version. Its availability and retention limits apply; do not assume every replaced version is recoverable. ## Limitations Keep both is a preservation step, not a decision about which version is correct. Copies need sufficient cloud storage, local disk space and the relevant permissions to finish transferring. If the copy or upload fails, a conflict can remain or return. The card's sizes and relative time labels are identification hints. Times can be affected by clocks, timestamp handling and the last known sync record. Do not use them as the sole reason to discard a version. The original-name download described here is the Full Sync workflow. Upload-only and download-only modes have different behavior, so do not assume that Keep both turns a one-way pairing into a two-way mirror. This guide covers regular folder sync, not Vault. ## Troubleshooting **I see Show both versions but no Keep both button.** The default rule can resolve the conflict automatically. Use the notice to open the folder and verify the resulting copies. **The original filename is missing after Keep both.** The local version was renamed. Leave the app open for the following Full Sync cycle, check Activity and look for failed files in Overview. Do not delete the renamed copy while waiting. **The conflict returns after a success message.** Check the actual files and the failed-file list. If a dated conflict copy already exists, preserve it and check its transfer before choosing Keep both again. A copy can be created before its upload fails, so repeating the choice can affect a different file now at the original path. Restore folder access, connectivity or available storage and use the failed-file recovery controls to finish transferring the preserved copy. If no copy was created and the original local version is still present, retry the unresolved conflict after correcting the cause. Further edits from either side can also produce another conflict. **I cannot find the conflict copy.** Open the exact local path shown for the pairing, rather than another folder with the same name. Look for **conflict copy** in the filename and check the intended cloud folder. Use [Issues and Activity](/desktop/sync-issues) to diagnose an incomplete transfer. **I keep getting more conflict copies.** Stop editing on both sides at once while you resolve the versions. Coordinate with collaborators, pause the pairing while combining your own copies, and resume when the intended final version is ready. If new copies appear without further edits, pause the pairing and use **Help → Report a Problem…** to report the filename, mode and relevant Issues/Activity messages before deleting copies. **An update was replaced without creating a copy.** The pairing may use Last write wins. Check available Version history and preserve the current version before restoring an older one. Do not recreate the pairing as an undo operation. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does the local version keep the original filename? With Keep both, the current desktop engine renames the local version as the conflict copy. In Full Sync, the cloud version returns under the original filename on a following cycle. ### Does Keep both combine the changes? No. It keeps separate files so you can compare or combine your own versions in the appropriate application. ### Must I delete the extra copy? No. You can retain both. If you remove one later, review your mode's deletion behavior and keep a separate backup if you still need that version. ### Will every conflict have a card with three buttons? No. Keep both copies normally handles a conflict automatically and leaves a notice. An unresolved card offers the manual choices when a conflict remains. ## Related guides - [Diagnosing desktop sync with Issues and Activity](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Choosing a desktop sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Using version history and restoring an earlier version](/files/version-history)

title: Pausing, resuming or stopping desktop sync
summary: Pause one folder or all transfers, resume or run a fresh cycle, and remove a pairing without deleting its existing local or cloud files.
verification: Verified the current native macOS app with an isolated saved sync pair on 2026-10-12: pausing changed the pair to Paused and exposed Resume; the row menu displayed Open folder and Remove. Global, workspace and tray/menu controls plus removal retention were source and test reviewed. Remove was not executed against production data. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Use the controls in **Sync → Overview** to pause one pair, pause the workspace's pairs, resume them or request **Sync now**. To stop managing a folder as a pair, open its three-dot menu and choose **Remove**. Removing the pair leaves existing local and cloud files in place. ## Before you start - Identify the pair by its cloud folder, local path and mode. - Check **Activity** for work already in progress and allow important transfers to finish when possible. - Preserve separate copies of important files before allowing the two sides to diverge during a pause. - Record the mode and exclusion list before removing a pair because a recreated pair performs a fresh comparison. ## Choose the action you need | Goal | Action | | --- | --- | | Temporarily stop one folder | Select its **Pause** control | | Temporarily stop every pair shown for the workspace | Select **Pause all** at the top of Sync | | Stop every pair across the app for a while | Use the tray or app menu **Pause Sync**, or the timed pause in the app's Sync settings/menu where offered | | Restart a paused pair | Select **Resume** on its row | | Ask for a fresh comparison | Select **Sync now** after fixing any cause | | End the relationship between two folders | Open the row menu and select **Remove** | ## Steps: pause and resume one folder 1. Open **Sync** and stay on **Overview**. 2. Match the pair by its cloud folder, local path and mode. 3. Select the pause icon in that row. Wait for **Status** to show **Paused**. 4. Make any safe local or cloud changes only when you understand what the selected mode will do after resuming. 5. Select the row's **Resume** control. Check **Activity**, then verify the intended destination when the cycle settles. ## Pause or resume several folders The top **Pause all** or **Resume all** control applies to the pairs shown for the active workspace. The tray and application Sync menu also offer a global pause and resume across the app. A timed **Pause for 1 Hour** or duration control resumes automatically. Check the banner and each row after using a broad control. A folder can also need permission, be offline or have its own error; global resume does not repair those conditions. ## Use Sync now **Sync now** requests a fresh cycle for one row. Use it after restoring a drive, connection or permission, or when you want the app to compare changes without waiting for the normal poll. It does not override a pause, exclusion, conflict decision, workspace permission or storage limit. Avoid pressing Sync now repeatedly during an active cycle. Follow progress in **Activity** and check **Issues** or the failed-file badge if completion is not clean. ## Remove a pairing 1. Wait for active transfers to finish, or pause the pair and inspect Activity. 2. Record the cloud folder, local path, mode and exclusions in case you need to recreate it. 3. Keep a separate copy of important work and check both sides. 4. Open the row's three-dot menu and select **Remove**. 5. Confirm that the row disappears, then check that the existing local folder and cloud files remain. Remove clears the saved sync relationship and its local sync state. It does not send a delete operation for all files on either side. Adding the folders again later creates a fresh pair and a fresh comparison, so review the mode before doing that. ## Closing the window and quitting Closing the main window is not the same as pausing sync. The desktop app can continue running from the menu bar or system tray. Use **Quit** when you intend to stop the application process. After reopening, inspect Sync rather than assuming a prior temporary state. Computer sleep, shutdown and a quit app cannot perform transfers. Resume with the app open, the local path available and the network connected. ## Expected result A paused pair shows **Paused** and stops starting new sync work until resumed. A resumed pair returns to its normal cycle. A removed pair disappears from Overview while the existing local and cloud files remain available in their respective locations. ## Limits and important boundaries - Pausing does not roll back a transfer that already completed. - Files changed while paused are compared when the pair resumes, according to its mode and conflict strategy. - Removing a pair is different from deleting files. Deleting through Files or the operating system can propagate in modes that carry deletions. - A global resume does not grant a missing macOS folder permission or reconnect an unavailable drive. - **Sync now** is a request to run; it is not proof that every file synced. Check Issues and the destination. ## Troubleshooting **The row still says Paused after Resume.** Check for a global pause banner, then use the global **Resume all**. If it remains paused, restart the app and inspect Issues. **Closing the window did not stop transfers.** The app is designed to continue from the tray or menu bar. Pause sync or quit the app explicitly. **A removed pair returned.** Confirm the removal completed and that another device or separate pair is not targeting the same cloud folder. Restart the app and inspect Overview. **Changes made while paused produced a conflict.** Preserve both versions and follow the conflict guide. The pause allowed the two sides to diverge; resuming did not choose which edit to discard. **Resume starts but a file remains missing.** Check the mode, exclusions, Issues, failed-file list and available storage. Resume only releases the paused state. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does Remove delete my files? No. It removes the pair and its saved sync state. Existing local and cloud files remain. ### Is closing the desktop window enough to pause sync? No. The app can keep running in the tray or menu bar. Use a pause control or Quit. ### Can I pause only one workspace? Use **Pause all** in the active workspace's Sync view for the pairs shown there. Use the row control for the narrowest pause. ## Related guides - [Desktop sync setup](/desktop/sync-folder) - [Diagnosing sync with Issues and Activity](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Choosing a desktop sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Resolving desktop sync conflicts](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Exclude temporary files from desktop sync
summary: Exclude cache, build, log, and temporary paths while creating a desktop sync pair, including immutable skips and existing-pair recreation limits.
verification: Verified locally using apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/ignore-rules.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/ignore-rules.test.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/ipc-handlers.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts. No production pair configuration changed.
body: The released desktop UI configures exclusions only while creating a sync pair. Existing pairs have no exclusion editor, so changing their patterns requires removing and recreating the pair. **Before you start** - Name the exact cache, build, log, or temporary entry to exclude and confirm it does not contain source material that belongs in the cloud. - Removing an existing pair deletes its local sync index and conflict state, although it does not delete the local folder or cloud files. ## Steps 1. Choose **Sync > Add sync folder**, select the cloud and local locations, choose a sync mode, and continue to **Advanced**. 2. Review **Excluded files & folders** before adding anything. The visible defaults already cover entries such as `node_modules`, `.git`, `.env`, `*.log`, `*.part`, and anchored system paths. 3. Enter the narrowest supported pattern and choose **Add**. Use an exact name, a suffix such as `*.log`, a prefix ending in `*`, or an absolute anchored path such as `/bin`; do not assume arbitrary glob behavior. 4. Remove any default that should sync, or choose **Reset to defaults** to restore the shipped list. `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, and `/run` remain skipped regardless of the visible choices. 5. Choose **Start syncing**. Internal `.dosya-sync-` files, Office/LibreOffice lock files, editor backups ending in `~`, and AppleDouble metadata remain technical skips outside the editable list. 6. For an existing pair, use its menu **Remove**, then recreate it with the corrected Advanced list. The removal immediately deletes pair configuration/index state, so expect a fresh scan after recreation. ## Expected result The new pair stores the selected exclusion patterns and omits matching entries during scanning and watching. The interface shows **Sync folder added** after successful creation. There is no Save action or released pattern editor for an existing pair. Removing a pair leaves local and cloud files intact, but its prior local index, queued state, and conflicts cannot be recovered from that pair record. ## Related guides - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Set up a sync folder](/desktop/sync-folder)

title: Excluding files and folders from desktop sync
summary: Review the visible default exclusions, add exact names or supported wildcard patterns before pairing, and verify a matching sample is skipped.
verification: Reviewed the current desktop wizard, shared scanner and watcher ignore logic, IPC validation and default pattern list on 2026-10-12. The current Advanced-step screenshot was captured from the local macOS app. Exact names, suffix wildcards, prefix wildcards and root-anchored absolute paths are source and unit-test reviewed; a new end-to-end exclusion transfer was not run in production. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Configure exclusions in the **Advanced** step while adding a sync folder. The list is saved with that folder pair and applies to its initial scan and later file watching. A matching item is skipped; it is not uploaded, downloaded or deleted by that pair. ## Before you start - Decide whether the item is safe to omit on both sides of the pairing. Exclusions apply to the pair, regardless of which direction a supported mode would otherwise transfer it. - Use a disposable test folder first. Put one matching file and one near-match inside it so you can verify the boundary. - Review the visible defaults. The wizard currently starts with common development, system and temporary names, but every visible default can be removed. - If a copy already exists in Dosya, preserve or manage it separately. Adding an exclusion does not remove an existing cloud file. ## Steps: add exclusions when creating a pair 1. Open **Sync** and select **Add sync folder**. 2. Choose the cloud folder and local folder, then select **Continue**. 3. Choose the sync mode and conflict behavior, then continue to **Advanced**. 4. Review every entry under **Excluded files & folders**. 5. Enter one supported pattern in the input and select **Add**. Repeat for additional patterns. 6. Use the remove control beside any default you deliberately want included. **Reset to defaults** restores the starting list. 7. Select **Start syncing**, then inspect **Activity** and both folders using your matching and near-match samples. ## Supported pattern forms | Pattern | What it matches | | --- | --- | | `node_modules` | A file or folder with that exact name at any depth; a skipped folder includes its subtree | | `.env` | An exact dotfile or folder name at any depth | | `*.log` | Names ending in `.log` | | `test_*` | Names beginning with `test_` | | `/bin` | Only that exact absolute filesystem path, not a project folder named `bin` | Patterns are simple name rules. They are not a full regular-expression language. A middle wildcard such as `foo*bar` is passed to the file watcher, but the initial scanner's supported matcher is limited to exact names, `*.suffix`, `prefix*` and exact absolute paths. Use the documented forms so the initial scan and later watching behave consistently. ## Verify that a pattern is correct For `*.log`, create `excluded.log` and `included.log.txt` in the local test folder. After the first cycle, the `.log` file should be absent from the cloud destination while the near-match appears. Check **Activity** for a skip reason if the app records one. For a folder-name rule such as `cache`, place a harmless file inside `cache/` and another inside `cache-copy/`. The exact `cache` directory is skipped as a subtree; `cache-copy` should remain eligible. ## Limits and existing files An exclusion controls what this pair considers for transfer. It does not delete a copy that already exists in the cloud, and it does not retroactively hide that copy from Files. Manage the existing cloud item separately after confirming that you no longer need it. The current Overview does not edit the saved exclusion list. To change it, pause the pair, record its mode and destinations, remove the pair, then create it again with the intended list. Existing local and cloud files remain when the pair is removed, but the new pair performs a fresh comparison. ## Always-skipped technical items The engine always skips its own temporary sync markers, transient Office or editor lock files, editor backup files ending in `~`, macOS AppleDouble sidecars and the real virtual filesystem roots `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev` and `/run`. These technical safeguards do not appear as removable preferences. ## Expected result The matching test item stays outside the pair's transfer set while a near-match transfers normally. The pair completes without treating the exclusion as a failed file. ## Troubleshooting **A pattern skipped too much.** Compare it with the supported forms and test an exact near-match. Remove the pair and recreate it with a narrower pattern after preserving important copies. **A matching file already exists in the cloud.** The exclusion did not delete it. It was uploaded before the rule, arrived through another upload path or belongs to another pair. Check Activity and manage that copy separately. **A file was not skipped.** Confirm that the pattern was present before selecting **Start syncing** and that the file is inside this pair's local folder. Check capitalization and use a documented pattern form. **I removed a default but the item is still skipped.** Some transient and virtual-system items are always skipped for safe operation. For other names, make sure another pattern in the list does not also match. **I need to change a saved list.** Record the pair's cloud folder, local path and mode. Pause and remove the pair, then recreate it with the corrected exclusions. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does an exclusion delete files already in Dosya? No. It keeps matching items out of this pair's future transfer set. Existing cloud files remain until someone manages them separately. ### Can I exclude one absolute system path without excluding project folders with the same name? Yes. A leading slash anchors the match to the exact absolute path. `/bin` does not match a project's own `bin` folder. ### Are exclusions a backup policy? No. They define this sync pair's transfer set. Keep a separate backup for important files, including items you deliberately exclude. ## Related guides - [Desktop sync setup](/desktop/sync-folder) - [Choosing a desktop sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Diagnosing sync with Issues and Activity](/desktop/sync-issues)

title: Sync an existing local folder safely
summary: Pair an existing folder without losing either side: choose the mode and conflict rule, start with a backup, then verify each first-sync outcome.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/planner.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/first-sync.test.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/system-paths.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx; this first-sync workflow was not exercised in production.
body: Pairing two folders that already contain files is a merge operation. Dosya does not show a dry-run before **Start syncing**, so back up irreplaceable local data and choose the deletion and conflict rules before creating the pair. ## Before you start Open **Sync** in the current desktop client and sign in to the intended workspace. A local folder cannot overlap another configured sync root; Dosya rejects that selection and tells you to remove the existing pair or choose another folder. The safest starting point for a local folder whose contents must reach the cloud is **Protect & Upload**. It uploads local changes and never deletes cloud files. Use **Full Sync** only when local and cloud changes, including deletions, should travel both ways. ## Steps 1. Copy the important local folder to a separate backup location that is outside every Dosya sync root. 2. In **Sync**, select **Add sync folder**, choose the destination under **Cloud folder**, and choose the existing path under **Local folder**. 3. Select **Protect & Upload** when the local folder is authoritative; choose **Full Sync** only if cloud-only items should download and deletions should mirror. 4. For **Full Sync**, leave **Keep both copies** selected when independent files may share a path, or select **Last write wins** only after checking timestamps. 5. Review exclusions and folder size, then select **Start syncing**; this creates the pair and begins work immediately. 6. Inspect **Activity**, **Issues**, the local folder, and the cloud destination until a small known file has the expected path and bytes. On the first Full Sync, a local-only file uploads and a cloud-only file downloads. When both sides independently contain the same path, **Keep both copies** automatically renames the local version to a dated, device-named conflict copy and uploads it; the following cycle restores the cloud version at the original path. Dosya records a notice explaining that both versions were kept. **Last write wins** instead compares the cloud update time with the local modification time and transfers the newer side. ## Expected result The pair appears in Sync and the sample item reaches its expected destination. Cloud-only content is not mistaken for a deletion during initial reconciliation, and **Keep both copies** leaves two named files rather than discarding either version. If Dosya reports that the folder is inside, contains, or duplicates another sync folder, remove the conflicting pair or choose a non-overlapping local path. Removing a pair stops synchronization; it does not delete files on either side. ## Related guides - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Set up a sync folder](/desktop/sync-folder)

title: Setting up a desktop sync folder
summary: Pair a local folder with a cloud folder, review the mode and exclusions, then confirm a sample file reached the intended destination.
verification: Verified the current local macOS desktop wizard, folder pairing and Protect & Upload transfer against isolated real D1/R2 on 2026-10-10. Downloaded sample bytes matched the local original. Signed upload transport was adapted to local R2; native folder selection was automated. Other modes, deletion behavior and exclusions were source reviewed, not exercised end to end in production.
body: Open **Sync → Add sync folder**, choose a cloud destination and a local folder, then review **Sync mode** and **Advanced** before selecting **Start syncing**. Start with a small sample and confirm its destination copy before adding your main working folder. ## Before you start - [Install the desktop app and sign in](/desktop/install-and-sign-in). Select the workspace you want in the sidebar. - Confirm that you can upload to the cloud destination and have enough available storage. - Create a small local sample folder with a harmless text file. Keep a separate copy of important files while checking the pairing and mode. - Close applications actively rewriting your sample file during the first transfer. - Review [sync modes](/desktop/sync-modes). The current wizard defaults to **Protect & Upload**, which uploads local changes without deleting cloud files. ## Steps: select the folders 1. **Open Sync.** Select **Sync** in the sidebar, then **Add sync folder** near the top right. An empty Sync view also offers this action in the main area. 2. **Choose the cloud folder.** In **Folders**, select your destination under **Cloud folder**. **Root (entire workspace)** pairs the local folder with the workspace root; select a specific folder to keep the test contained. Create that cloud folder in Files first if needed. 3. **Choose the local folder.** Select **Browse**, choose the folder on your computer and confirm the operating system's picker. The field beside Browse should show its path. **Quick backup** offers Desktop, Documents, Pictures and Downloads shortcuts; those choices can include far more files than a small test folder. 4. **Check both choices.** Confirm the selected cloud folder and local path before selecting **Continue**. On systems that request folder access, grant access only to the folder you intend to sync. ## Steps: review the mode and exclusions 1. **Choose Sync mode.** Read its direction and deletion behavior. For this upload test, use **Protect & Upload**. Choose another mode only when its behavior matches your purpose, then select **Continue**. 2. **Review Excluded files & folders.** The **Advanced** step shows the patterns that will be skipped. Defaults include development and temporary items such as node_modules, .git, .env, .DS_Store and *.tmp. A file matching an exclusion will not appear in the destination through this pairing. 3. **Adjust only what you need.** Enter an additional folder name or wildcard pattern and select **Add** to exclude it. The remove control beside a pattern removes that exclusion; **Reset to defaults** restores the default list. Removing a default may include files you did not intend to transfer. 4. **Review a large-folder notice if shown.** A very large folder requires **Sync it anyway** before continuing. Check that the folder choice is deliberate and allow time, bandwidth and disk space for the operation. 5. **Start the pairing.** Select **Start syncing**. Return to **Overview** to follow the folder's status. ## Expected result The pairing appears in **Overview** with the cloud folder, local path, **Mode**, **Status** and **Last synced**. For the sample upload, wait until activity settles, then open the same cloud folder in Files or the web app. Confirm the sample filename, download it and compare it with your original. Also check **Issues** and any per-file notice. A row can say **Synced** while reporting a file that did not sync; the status label alone is not proof that every file reached the destination. ## Pause, resume or stop a pairing Use the folder row's pause or resume control for one pairing. **Pause all** stops transfers across pairings; resume them when you are ready. **Sync now** requests a fresh sync cycle for a row. Open the row's three-dot menu for **Open folder** and **Remove**. Remove stops the pairing and clears its sync configuration; it does not delete the existing local or cloud files. Check that transfers have stopped before changing the relationship between the two folders. ## Limitations The chosen mode governs direction, updates and deletions. Protect & Upload preserves cloud files when local files are removed, but changed local files can still update cloud versions. It is not an immutable archive or a substitute for a separate backup. Transfers run while the desktop app and computer can run them. Sleep, network loss, inaccessible external drives, paused sync, storage limits and permission changes can delay completion. Excluded items and unsupported virtual system folders are skipped. Vault uses a separate workflow. ## Troubleshooting **Continue is disabled.** Select a local folder through Browse and confirm the picker. Check that its path appears beside Browse. **A file is missing from the cloud folder.** Verify the workspace, destination, mode, exclusion patterns and Issues. Check that the local file is inside the chosen folder, rather than beside it. **The new pairing is missing or does not start.** Refresh the Sync view, check the workspace and any paused state, then restart the app if needed. In this local verification, the first pairing required an app restart before the engine began transferring. Do not add the same pairing repeatedly while checking its saved state. **Transfers remain stalled.** Check connectivity, storage and access to the local drive. Use Sync now after correcting the cause. Share the mode, error text and sample filename with [support](https://dosya.dev/contact/); omit credentials and private file contents. **I need a different mode or exclusion list.** The current Overview has no editor for those saved settings. Pause and remove the pairing, then recreate it with the intended choices. Review the files already on both sides first; a recreated pairing makes a new comparison. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does Remove delete my files? It removes the sync pairing. Existing local and cloud files remain. ### Why is an excluded file missing? Exclusions deliberately skip matching paths. Review them in Advanced when creating the pairing. ### Can I use a whole workspace as the destination? Yes, by selecting Root (entire workspace). A dedicated folder is easier to verify for a first test. ## Related guides - [Installing and signing in to desktop](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Choosing a desktop sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders)

title: Fix a desktop sync invalid-name error
summary: Use the exact desktop sync error to decide whether a name needs changing, retry that item, and confirm the corrected path reaches the cloud.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/sync/commit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/entity-name.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/validation-policy.generated.ts; production invalid-name handling was not rerun.
body: An unusual name is not automatically invalid. Use the exact message in **Issues** before renaming anything, because the upload service sanitizes some characters and different operating systems impose different local rules. ## Before you start Open **Sync** and expand the **N files not synced** pill. The expanded list is titled **N files could not be synced** and shows the path, the server or operating-system error, and either **will retry** or **won’t retry**. Keep a copy before renaming a path used by another application. Dosya’s direct upload endpoint trims whitespace, replaces `/` and `\` with `_`, strips control characters, and changes a whole `.` or `..` name to `_`. It rejects a blank result and a name over 255 characters with **Name too long (max 255)**. Characters such as `<`, `>`, double quotes, and apostrophes are not universally rejected by that server policy. ## Steps 1. Expand the pair's failed-file list and locate the item that did not sync; **Retry** acts on every listed error for that pair. 2. Copy the complete path and exact error text before choosing whether a rename is needed. 3. If the message is **Name too long (max 255)**, shorten the final name to 255 characters or fewer while retaining any useful extension. 4. For a local filesystem refusal, remove only the character or path form named by that operating-system error and keep the corrected name unique in its folder. 5. Return to the pair and select its single **Retry** control only after every listed error is ready to run again; avoid **Clear** because it only dismisses the recorded issues. 6. Confirm the row disappears after transfer and check the corrected cloud path, file size, and readable contents. A failed item is normally retried up to five times before the ledger marks it **won’t retry**. Renaming many files based on a generic portability list can create needless changes or collisions, so fix one representative path first. ## Expected result The corrected item uploads under the intended unique name and no longer appears in the failed-file list. The local original remains available under its new name, and unrelated files are unchanged. If a renamed item still fails, record the new exact error. A separator may have been sanitized already, while a permission, collision, path-length, or locked-file failure needs a different remedy. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync issues](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Resolve conflicts](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Diagnosing desktop sync with Issues and Activity
summary: Find folder errors, notices and failed files, use Activity to understand progress, then retry after correcting the cause and verify the destination.
verification: Reviewed current Sync UI, IPC handlers, error ledger, real-poller Retry and queued reconciliation source on 2026-10-11. Actual native macOS captures against isolated API/D1/R2 show Issues, Activity and Overview failed-file controls. A genuine EACCES on an unreadable 41-byte sample produced its failed-file entry; restoring permission and selecting Retry uploaded the sample, cleared its error and matched the downloaded destination bytes. Manual and automatic Keep both also settled cleanly. Busy-transfer Retry has automated SQLite/poller coverage. Network recovery, folder-error Retry, Clear, Windows/Linux, sandboxed Mac App Store permission recovery and production behavior remain source reviewed or unverified. The matching desktop fixes must ship before these instructions are deployed. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Open **Sync**, check the affected folder in **Overview**, then use **Issues** for folder errors and notices and **Activity** for recent operations. For individual failed files, select the **N files not synced** badge in Overview. Correct the cause before selecting **Retry**, and confirm the intended files reached their destination afterward. ## Before you start - Select the workspace containing the affected pairing. Note its cloud folder, local path and **Mode** in Overview. - Keep the desktop app open and the computer awake while checking a transfer. Reconnect any external drive used by the pairing. - Keep a separate copy of important work before making a recovery decision that could replace or remove a file. - Check the [sync mode's direction](/desktop/sync-modes). A local change will not upload through Pull from Cloud or Save to Device; a cloud change will not download through Push to Cloud or Protect & Upload. - Record the error text before clearing a list or restarting. Filenames and paths may be personal; omit credentials and private material from any report. ## Steps: identify what needs attention 1. **Find the pairing in Overview.** Select **Sync** in the sidebar. Match the cloud folder and local path, then check **Mode** and **Status**. **Paused** needs a resume action, **Offline** indicates a connection problem, and **Waiting** can indicate a temporary rate limit. **Synced** describes the folder's current cycle; also check for a failed-file badge. 2. **Open Issues.** Select the **Issues** tab. A folder error shows its message, path, **Retry** and **Report**. A macOS permission prompt offers **Reselect folder**: select the intended local folder again in the operating system's picker. Notices explain conditions such as delayed watching, skipped files or a conflict copy. Read the notice before deciding what to do; a notice does not necessarily mean the entire folder stopped syncing. 3. **Check individual failed files in Overview.** Return to **Overview** and select **N files not synced** beneath the folder's status, if shown. The expanded list gives each path, reason and either **will retry** or **won't retry**. **Won't retry** means automatic attempts have stopped; it does not prevent a manual retry after you fix the cause. 4. **Check Activity for progress and context.** Select **Activity**. Read the operation messages for the affected folder. During a cycle, a live header shows the current phase and elapsed time. Preparation can take time before a transfer percentage appears. Activity can include pairings from other workspaces, so use the folder name to identify the relevant entries. ## Steps: correct the cause and retry 1. **Fix the reason shown.** Restore the connection or drive, close an application holding a file busy, or correct local access permissions. For a cloud storage or workspace permission error, resolve the applicable limit or ask the workspace administrator for the required access. For a download, also check available space on this computer. 2. **Resume a deliberately paused pairing.** In Overview, use the row's **Resume** control. A workspace's **Resume all** button resumes its paused pairings. If the overview banner says **Sync is paused for all folders**, its **Resume all** action releases the global pause. A folder awaiting macOS permission still needs **Reselect folder**. 3. **Use the appropriate Retry.** For a folder error, select **Retry** on its Issues card.
