For failed files, expand **N files not synced** in Overview and select that list's **Retry**. This retries all failed files for the pairing, including entries marked **won't retry**. They stay listed until successful transfers clear their errors. 4. **Allow the cycle to finish.** Use the row's **Sync now** control if a fresh cycle is needed after correcting a cause. It requests work; it does not grant permissions or resolve a conflict. Avoid repeatedly pressing it while a cycle is already running. Check Activity for the result. 5. **Verify the destination.** Follow the pairing's direction to the correct cloud or local folder. Confirm the intended filenames and open your own destination copies to check that they are the versions you expected. For important files, compare with the separate copies you retained. ## Expected result The affected files arrive at their intended destination and their failed-file entries disappear. The folder returns to its normal state after the cycle, with no relevant unresolved error or conflict. A remaining informational notice may still explain a limitation of the pairing. Check the destination as well as the interface. **Sync complete**, **Synced**, a recent **Last synced** label or a successful toast does not by itself establish that every file transferred. An excluded file is outside the pairing's transfer set. ## Actions to use carefully **Clear** in the failed-file list dismisses the recorded errors. It does not repair the cause or prove a successful transfer. The files can be attempted again on a later cycle. Prefer Retry after fixing the cause when you want to confirm recovery. The row's three-dot menu contains **Open folder** and **Remove**. Remove stops the pairing and clears its saved relationship and sync state; existing local and cloud files remain. Removing and adding a pairing again starts a fresh comparison. Use it only when you deliberately need to rebuild the relationship, after recording the destination, mode and exclusions and preserving important copies. If Overview asks about files that disappeared locally, reconnect or locate the intended drive or folder first. **Keep the cloud copies** declines the held cloud deletion. **Delete from the cloud too** authorizes that deletion and moves the affected files to cloud trash. Do not use the delete action to dismiss an unexplained prompt. ## Limitations Issues is not a complete list of individual failed files. Its badge also does not count every notice or permission prompt. Check Overview's failed-file badge even if Issues says **No issues**. Activity shows recent sync messages, rather than a complete permanent history. The current status snapshot carries the latest 50 entries across pairings. A failed-file list shows up to 200 recent errors for a pairing; its total can be larger. Retry covers the pairing's failed files, including those outside the displayed list. The chosen mode, exclusions and permissions still govern transfers after retrying. This guide covers regular folder sync; Vault uses a separate workflow. A Mac App Store folder-access prompt is specific to the sandboxed macOS build. ## Troubleshooting **The folder is Offline.** Restore connectivity and leave the app open. Sync checks for recovery and resumes when the connection is available. If Activity identifies maintenance, wait for the service to become available. Recreating the pairing does not restore a connection. **The row says Waiting.** A rate limit can temporarily pause requests. Let the waiting period expire; the engine schedules its own resume. Repeated retries do not remove the limit. **Issues says No issues, but a file is missing.** Check Overview's failed-file badge, the active workspace, mode and local path. Check whether an exclusion applies. Then inspect the expected destination. **Retry succeeds as an action, but the error returns.** Re-read the reason: the underlying cause may still apply. A manual retry resets automatic retry eligibility; it does not change storage limits or permissions. **Activity seems busy for a different folder.** It can show multiple workspaces. Match the folder name to the pairing you are diagnosing and confirm the selected workspace in Overview. **The app cannot display sync status.** Overview offers **Try again** when it cannot reach the sync engine. Use that action, then restart the desktop app if the status remains unavailable. Record any visible error first. **I still cannot identify the cause.** Select **Report** on the folder error or open **Help → Report a Problem…**. Describe the expected direction, affected folder, error and what you already tried. Review the screenshot and diagnostics options before **Send report**. The optional recent log includes filenames; it is off by default. A screenshot is taken when you send, so show only what you intend to share. ## Frequently asked questions ### Why can a Synced folder still show files not synced? The row's status and the per-file error list describe different things. A cycle can finish while some files remain failed. Expand the badge and verify those files individually. ### Does Retry include files marked won't retry? Yes. The failed-file list's Retry resets the pairing's failed files for another attempt, including those marked won't retry. Fix the cause first. ### Does Clear delete the failed files? No. It clears the error list. The files remain where they are, and a later cycle can try them again. ### Should I change sync mode to make a missing file appear? First check whether the current mode matches your intended direction. Changing the relationship can introduce different update and deletion behavior. Diagnose errors and exclusions before deciding to create a different pairing. ## Related guides - [Desktop sync setup](/desktop/sync-folder) - [Choosing a desktop sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Resolving desktop sync conflicts and keeping both copies](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Recover desktop sync when local disk space is low
summary: Recover a download blocked by low disk space: reserve its bytes plus Dosya’s 256 MiB margin, retry the transfer, and verify the final local file.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/remote-client.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx; low-space recovery was not repeated against production.
body: Dosya checks free space before downloading. The destination volume must hold the download plus a 256 MiB safety margin, and a batch needs room for the combined download actions before it starts. ## Before you start Find the affected pair or file in **Sync**. The exact preflight message is **Low disk space: {freeMB} MB free, need ~{needMB} MB. Free up space to continue syncing.** This guard applies to downloads; an upload-only action does not need a local destination copy. A download writes resumable data under `.dosya-sync-tmp` and renames the completed file into place. Dosya cleans abandoned temporary entries when the pair starts, but the final file and temporary work still need space on the same destination volume. ## Steps 1. Record the sync path, download size, reported free megabytes, and approximate required megabytes from the desktop error. 2. Pause the affected pair so additional cloud changes do not add more download work while capacity is being cleared. 3. Delete disposable data from the destination volume or move it to another volume, leaving at least the reported requirement, which includes Dosya’s 256 MiB margin. 4. If that volume cannot be expanded, choose **Remove** for the pair and add a smaller cloud folder or stronger exclusions; Remove does not delete local or cloud files. 5. Resume the pair and select its single **Retry** control to retry every listed error, or use **Sync now** when the pair has no retained failed-file list. 6. Verify the final local path opens, matches the cloud file size, and is no longer represented only by temporary data. On some network filesystems the operating system cannot report free bytes. Dosya then skips the early space guard, and the write can still fail later with the underlying filesystem message. ## Expected result The download completes after the destination has enough working capacity. The visible file replaces its temporary download state, opens normally, and the low-space issue clears. If space falls again during a batch, pause the pair and free more than the minimum. Repeatedly clearing the error without reserving capacity can leave the remaining downloads blocked. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync issues](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Resolve conflicts](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Fix a desktop sync local-permission error
summary: Distinguish a lost macOS folder grant from an unreadable file, restore the required access, and verify that the corrected desktop path can sync again.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/bookmarks.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx; macOS permission recovery was not retested in production.
body: A macOS folder authorization problem has a different recovery path from a locked or unreadable file. Read the pair status and failed-item message before changing operating-system permissions. ## Before you start A sandboxed macOS installation can show **Needs permission** with **macOS needs permission to this folder again.** The action is **Reselect folder**. Ordinary access failures appear in **N files not synced**, where the row includes its local path, error, and retry state. Close editors, media applications, backup tools, or security scanners that may be holding the item. Do not grant broad disk access until the specific path and operating-system refusal have been identified. ## Steps 1. Open **Sync** and determine whether the pair says **Needs permission** or a single file appears in the failed-file list. 2. For **Needs permission**, select **Reselect folder** and authorize the original folder, or its new location if it was moved or renamed. 3. For an unreadable sync item, close the process holding it and restore desktop read or write access for the signed-in operating-system user. 4. Reopen the pair and confirm the displayed local root is the intended path before allowing transfers to continue. 5. Read each row's **will retry** or **won't retry** state, repair every listed cause, then select the pair's single **Retry** control to reset and retry all listed errors. 6. Check that the pair leaves **Needs permission** or the failed row clears, then verify the file on the destination side. Outside the macOS bookmark flow, a root that cannot be accessed can surface as **Sync folder not found: **. Confirm that the drive is mounted and the folder exists before recreating a pair. ## Expected result The desktop process can read or write the selected path again. The pair resumes with its original mapping, and the previously blocked item reaches the intended destination. Transfer paths do not classify every access failure alike: large-file and live-watcher branches can mark messages containing `permission` or `EPERM` as permanent, while other paths use a narrower upload-error classifier. The row's **will retry** or **won't retry** label is authoritative; after repair, pair-level **Retry** resets even the listed permanent rows. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync issues](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Resolve conflicts](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Choosing a desktop sync mode
summary: Compare all five sync modes, understand which deletions propagate, and choose a conflict rule before starting a folder pairing.
verification: Reviewed all five mode definitions, direction and deletion rules against current desktop source on 2026-10-10. Captured real local wizard states including Full Sync conflict choices. Protect & Upload completed a byte-verified sample transfer in isolated D1/R2; the other four modes, conflicts and deletions were not manually exercised end to end or in production. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body:
Choose the mode in **Sync → Add sync folder → Sync mode**. Use **Full Sync** for changes in both directions, **Protect & Upload** for local-to-cloud transfers that keep cloud files after local deletion, or **Save to Device** for cloud-to-local transfers that keep local files after cloud deletion. The two other one-way modes also propagate deletions from their source side. ## Before you start - Decide which side is the source of your changes: this computer, the cloud folder or both. - Keep a separate copy of important files while testing a new pairing. Use a small disposable folder when testing deletion or conflict behavior. - Check the workspace and cloud destination. A mistaken destination can affect files already stored there. - Read the deletion column below. A mode that keeps destination files after deletion can still update them when its source changes. ## Compare the five modes
Mode in the appDirection of changesDeletionsUse when
Full SyncLocal ↔ cloudApplied in both directionsYou edit on both sides and want them to mirror each other.
Push to CloudLocal → cloudLocal deletion can remove the cloud counterpartThis computer is the source and the cloud should follow it.
Protect & UploadLocal → cloudLocal deletion does not delete the cloud counterpartYou want local changes uploaded while retaining cloud copies of removed local files.
Pull from CloudCloud → localCloud deletion can remove the local counterpartThe cloud is the source and this computer should follow it.
Save to DeviceCloud → localCloud deletion does not delete the local counterpartYou want cloud changes downloaded while retaining local copies of removed cloud files.
For one-way modes, changes made only on the destination are not sent back to the source. They can still be affected by later source updates. For example, editing a downloaded file in Save to Device does not upload that edit. ## Steps: choose the mode 1. **Open the pairing wizard.** Select **Sync → Add sync folder**, choose both folders in **Folders**, then select **Continue**. 2. **Choose the direction.** Select the mode that matches your intended source. The current wizard initially selects **Protect & Upload**; it does not initially select Full Sync. 3. **Check deletion behavior.** Read the selected description. If you expect a destination copy to remain after removing the source, use the corresponding protective mode and test that expectation with disposable files. 4. **Choose a conflict rule for Full Sync.** Selecting Full Sync reveals **Conflict resolution**. Choose **Keep both copies** if you want both versions retained when a conflict occurs, or **Last write wins** if the later change should replace the other version. The default is Keep both copies. 5. **Review Advanced.** Select **Continue**, check exclusions and any folder-size notice, then select **Start syncing**. 6. **Verify the direction with a sample.** Add a harmless sample on the source side and confirm it arrives at the destination. For Full Sync, repeat with a different sample created on the other side. Check Issues as well as the row status. ## Expected result The pairing's **Mode** column matches your selection. Samples created on a source side reach the intended destination, and the destination-only sample in a one-way mode is not uploaded or downloaded back to the source. If you need to confirm a deletion rule, use a disposable test file with copies already present on both sides. Remove it from the source, let sync settle and check both folders. Avoid testing a destructive rule with a file you need to keep. ## Changing a saved pairing's mode The current app displays the saved mode but has no mode-edit control in Overview. Record the local path and cloud destination, pause the pairing, use its three-dot menu's **Remove**, and create a new pairing with the intended mode. Remove stops the relationship without deleting existing files. Review the files already present before restarting. Recreating a pairing is a fresh comparison; it is not an undo operation for earlier deletions or replacements. Use [Deleted files](/files/restore-deleted) or [Version history](/files/version-history) when those recovery options apply. ## Limitations The protective modes preserve destination copies when their source is deleted. They still transfer changes, so they do not freeze every historical version indefinitely. Available recovery and retained versions depend on the file and account's applicable limits. Conflict rules apply when Full Sync detects competing changes. Keep both copies avoids choosing one winner automatically; it can leave extra copies for you to reconcile. Last write wins does not mean that the chosen version is the one you intended to keep. Check **Issues** for unresolved conflicts and skipped files. ## Troubleshooting **A local edit did not reach the cloud.** Check whether the pairing is Pull from Cloud or Save to Device. Those modes take changes from the cloud, so local edits do not upload through that pairing. **A cloud change did not reach this computer.** Check whether the mode is Push to Cloud or Protect & Upload. Those modes upload local changes and do not pull cloud edits. **A destination copy disappeared after source deletion.** Check for Full Sync, Push to Cloud or Pull from Cloud, which propagate the relevant deletions. Pause the pairing before recovering a file, then review its mode so the same relationship does not repeat the removal. **There are duplicate conflict copies.** Check Issues and the conflict rule. With Keep both copies, compare your own copies, keep the intended version and resolve the conflict before continuing important work. **The mode looks right but a sample is missing.** Check paused state, workspace, exclusions, storage and per-file errors. Follow the folder setup troubleshooting before recreating a pairing. ## Frequently asked questions ### Which mode is selected by default? The current wizard defaults to Protect & Upload. ### Does one-way sync stop people editing the destination? No. It describes the transfer direction, not permissions. Destination edits do not propagate back and can be affected by later source updates. ### Can I make a deletion-proof backup by choosing a protective mode? It prevents deletion propagation in the stated direction. Source updates still transfer, so keep an independent backup if you need a separately recoverable copy. ## Related guides - [Desktop sync setup](/desktop/sync-folder) - [Restoring an earlier version](/files/version-history) - [Restoring deleted files](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Understand Offline desktop sync status
summary: Understand the Offline state, its 30-second recovery probe, and the activity receipt that proves an existing sync pair resumed after reconnection.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/network-errors.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/tray.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/sync-status-summary.ts; no production outage was induced.
body: **Offline** means the desktop sync engine cannot currently reach Dosya. The pair is retained, local files remain in place, and the client checks for a usable session again instead of requiring a new configuration. ## Before you start Open **Sync** and identify the affected pair by its workspace, cloud folder, and local root. Its message can read **Cannot connect to dosya.dev right now. Sync resumes automatically when the connection is back.** The tray summary shows **Offline** when all pairs are disconnected or **N offline** when only some are affected. ## Steps 1. Record the pair name, current **Offline** status, and its latest entry under **Activity**. 2. Confirm that the device has internet access and that a firewall, VPN, captive portal, or proxy is not blocking Dosya. 3. Restore desktop connectivity without removing the sync pair, changing its folders, or duplicating the same local work. 4. Bring Dosya online or wake the device to request an immediate sync check; otherwise allow up to 30 seconds for the periodic recovery probe. 5. Wait while the successful workspace-region probe returns desktop sync to its normal scan and polling cycle. 6. Verify a known pending sync change reaches the other side and the pair's current status has recovered; the earlier connection-loss entry remains in **Activity** as history. The activity receipt for this transition is **Lost the connection to dosya.dev - sync will resume by itself when it is back**. Recovery can pass through an idle or syncing state before **Synced**, so the label need not change directly from Offline to Synced. ## Expected result The existing pair reconnects and resumes its queued or newly detected work. No folder mapping is recreated, and a known pending change provides the final receipt. A user-paused, rate-limited, permission-blocked, or confirmation-required pair keeps that condition instead of being replaced by Offline. Resolve the displayed state if connectivity is already healthy. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes)

title: Choose a desktop sync mode for a folder
summary: Choose among Dosya’s five desktop sync modes by deciding which side may change, which deletions propagate, and how Full Sync resolves conflicts.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/types.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/sync/planner.ts; destructive mode effects were not exercised in production.
body: A sync mode decides which changes cross the boundary and whether a deletion on one side may remove a file on the other. Choose it from the intended source of truth before selecting **Start syncing**. ## Before you start In **Sync**, select **Add sync folder**, then choose the cloud and local folders. Dosya currently exposes all five modes in the desktop wizard; no separate subscription-plan switch controls this list. - **Full Sync** mirrors changes and deletions in both directions. - **Push to Cloud** sends local changes and local deletions; cloud changes are ignored locally. - **Protect & Upload** uploads local files but never deletes cloud content. - **Pull from Cloud** downloads cloud changes and applies cloud deletions locally; local changes are ignored. - **Save to Device** downloads cloud files but never deletes local content. ## Steps 1. Decide whether the local folder, the cloud folder, or both locations are allowed to originate changes. 2. Decide separately whether a local deletion may remove cloud data and whether a cloud deletion may remove local data. 3. Choose **Protect & Upload** for a local source that must not delete cloud files, or **Push to Cloud** when local deletions should propagate. 4. Choose **Save to Device** for a protected local copy, or **Pull from Cloud** when cloud deletions should also clear the device. 5. Choose **Full Sync** for two-way ownership, then select **Keep both copies** or **Last write wins** for same-path conflicts. 6. Start desktop sync with a disposable file and deletion test, then verify the mode’s transfer direction and allowed deletion behavior. One-way modes filter transfer and deletion operations, but a same-path conflict can still require attention. **Protect & Upload** is the wizard default and provides the least destructive cloud behavior for a new pair. ## Expected result The sample change travels only in the direction allowed by the selected mode. A deletion affects the opposite side only when that mode explicitly includes deletion propagation. If the test behaves differently, pause or remove the pair before adding more data. Removing the mapping stops future sync and leaves existing local and cloud files in place. ## Related guides - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Set up a sync folder](/desktop/sync-folder)

title: Reconnect sync after sleep or network change
summary: Recover desktop sync after Wi-Fi, sleep, proxy, or session interruptions; understand automatic retry timing and verify resumed files at both ends.
verification: Reviewed reconnect state through `apps/desktop/src/main/sync/network-errors.ts`, `remote-client.ts`, `index.ts`, `remote-poller.ts`, and Sync Overview controls on 2026-10-14. Production recovery was not run.
body: Dosya parks an affected pairing as **Offline** when it cannot reach the service and resumes after connectivity returns. The exact message is **Cannot connect to dosya.dev right now. Sync resumes automatically when the connection is back.** Keep the app running while you restore the network. ## Before you start - Confirm that the affected local folder or external drive is still mounted. A network recovery cannot repair a missing local path. - Note the row's status and full error tooltip before restarting anything. **Offline**, **Waiting**, **Needs permission**, **Needs attention**, and **Error** require different responses. - Keep partial local files and Dosya temporary data in place during recovery. Removing them can discard resumable download state. - Workspace and file permissions still apply after reconnecting; an authenticated member with insufficient access will not be fixed by Wi-Fi recovery. ## Steps 1. Open **Sync → Overview** and identify the pairing by cloud folder and local path. If status loading itself fails, the page says **Couldn't read sync status** and **The app couldn't reach its sync engine - try restarting dosya.** Select **Try again** before restarting. 2. Restore Wi-Fi, Ethernet, VPN or proxy access. Open a normal Dosya workspace view to confirm the service is reachable, but do not create a replacement pairing. 3. Leave the desktop process open. Network requests use retry delays of roughly **1, 3 and 8 seconds** for retryable failures. A parked Offline pair is probed on the engine's **30-second** recovery cycle. 4. A browser `online` event or computer wake requests a recovery pass immediately and clears the cached proxy decision. Otherwise, a changed proxy route can remain cached for up to **60 seconds** before being recalculated. 5. Watch Activity for **Connection restored - resuming sync**. Depending on mode, recovery restarts its watcher and poller and can run a new scan. A stalled active cycle becomes eligible for a **Still working:** entry only after inactivity exceeds 30 seconds; because the check runs on the next 30-second recovery tick, the entry normally appears about 30–60 seconds after the last progress. 6. Select the row's **Sync now** only after the connection is healthy when you want a fresh pass. If a configured pairing lost its runtime, that control also attempts to start it again. 7. Verify one affected file at the destination. Resumable downloads use a `.dosya-sync-tmp` file and validators; multipart uploads can continue missing parts. The final filename should appear only after a completed download is promoted. ## Expected result The Offline warning clears after a successful server probe, the pairing returns to work, and pending eligible changes continue according to its mode. Files that completed before the interruption remain complete; resumed work should not require rebuilding the pairing. Sleep and wake use a transient pause, so a matching wake resumes without persisting a manual global pause. A deliberate **Pause sync** or **Pause all** is different and must be resumed by the user. Timed snoozes retain their 30-minute, 1-hour, 4-hour or 8-hour deadline across an app restart. ## Troubleshooting **The message is Session expired. Please log in again.** Sign in again. A refreshed session triggers an immediate recovery check; the background loop also probes session-expired pairs every 30 seconds. Reconnecting the network alone does not renew authentication. **The row says Waiting.** Respect the displayed rate-limit wait. The engine schedules recovery using the server retry interval plus a one-second buffer; repeatedly selecting Sync now does not shorten it. **macOS says it needs permission again.** Select **Reselect folder** and choose the same local folder. This is a sandbox bookmark problem, not a network failure. **Connectivity changed without going offline.** A VPN or corporate proxy switch may not emit the app's online event. Wait out the 60-second proxy cache or restart Dosya if the route remains stale. **Errors remain after recovery.** Expand **N files not synced**, fix each cause, then select that list's **Retry**. Connectivity can resume transport while a lock, storage limit or filesystem permission continues to block a file. ## Related guides - [Diagnose desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes)

title: Review a desktop first-sync plan
summary: Review folders, mode, conflicts, exclusions, and the large-folder estimate before starting; Dosya has no dry-run list of planned operations.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/folder-estimate.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/sync/planner.ts; the released production wizard was not rerun.
body: Dosya has no dry-run screen listing every planned upload, download, conflict, or deletion. The safe review happens in the **Add sync folder** wizard, followed by a small controlled first transfer. ## Before you start Back up valuable local data and use a cloud destination whose contents you understand. Prepare a small test folder when a full pair could cause costly transfers or deletions. The size estimate is advisory. Dosya warns when it sees at least 50,000 files or the scan is truncated, then requires **Sync it anyway**. Estimation stops after 200,000 entries or five seconds, ignores symlinks, and does not count unreadable directories, so the displayed total may be incomplete. ## Steps 1. In **Add sync folder**, confirm the exact **Cloud folder** and **Local folder**, including whether the cloud choice is **Root (entire workspace)**. 2. Select a named mode and restate its deletion behavior before proceeding: Full Sync, Push to Cloud, Protect & Upload, Pull from Cloud, or Save to Device. 3. If using **Full Sync**, choose **Keep both copies** for independent same-path files or **Last write wins** only when timestamps are trusted. 4. Review **Excluded files & folders** and add patterns for generated data, secrets, caches, or other paths that must stay out. 5. Read the file-and-byte estimate; for a large or truncated scan, validate the local tree before enabling **Sync it anyway**. 6. Select **Start syncing** only for the controlled scope, then use **Activity** and **Issues** to inspect the actual first operations. The button creates the pair and starts work immediately. There is no intervening list to approve, so a disposable sample is the only reliable way to observe the chosen mode before applying it to valuable content. ## Expected result The initial sample follows the chosen direction, deletion rule, conflict policy, and exclusions. Activity provides the post-start receipt, while Issues identifies work that needs intervention. If the estimate seems implausibly small, check inaccessible directories and symlinks instead of treating it as an inventory. Cancel the wizard and narrow the selected root before any transfer begins. ## Related guides - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes) - [Set up a sync folder](/desktop/sync-folder)

title: Recover desktop sync when workspace storage is full
summary: Identify the exact account, workspace, or member storage limit, free or raise capacity, then verify that the blocked desktop upload succeeds.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/remote-client.ts, apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/measured-quota.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/DashboardPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/WorkspaceDashboardPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SettingsPage.tsx, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx; production storage limits were not altered.
body: A desktop upload can be blocked by the account owner’s plan, a workspace storage cap, or a per-member limit. The exact server message identifies which capacity must change. ## Before you start Open the failed item under **Sync** and retain its full message. Common receipts include: - **You've used {used} of {limit} across all your workspaces. Empty the trash to free up space, or upgrade...** - **This workspace has a {capGb} GB storage limit and this doesn't fit. Empty the trash here or raise the limit in workspace settings.** - **You've reached your {N} GB per-member storage limit** - **Another upload just filled the remaining space - try again.** Workspace and account storage views show used, free, and limit values. Items in Trash still consume capacity until they are deleted permanently. ## Steps 1. Copy the failed file path, its byte size, and the complete quota message from the desktop issue row. 2. Open storage usage for the named account or workspace and determine whether the owner plan, workspace cap, or member allowance is full. 3. Permanently delete only confirmed disposable Trash items, understanding that **Delete permanently** cannot be undone. 4. If more capacity is required, ask a workspace owner or admin to raise the applicable workspace or member setting, or have the account owner upgrade its plan. 5. Return to Sync and use the pair's single **Retry** control after every listed error is ready to run again; use **Sync now** only when no failed-file list remains. 6. Confirm the upload appears at the cloud path with the expected size and the quota error clears from Issues. A capacity race can occur when another upload consumes the last available bytes between measurement and commit. Recheck current usage before repeating that file. ## Expected result Once sufficient capacity exists under the applicable limit, the queued upload completes and the desktop issue disappears. The cloud object supplies the final path-and-size receipt. If only an owner or admin can change the setting, a member should send them the exact message and requested file size. Repeated Retry attempts do not increase storage. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync issues](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Resolve conflicts](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Use the Dosya system tray
summary: Read every sync pair from the Dosya tray, use its pause, resume, sync, folder, upload, and window actions, then confirm the result in the app.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/tray.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync-status-summary.ts, and their tests; tray actions were not rechecked on production builds.
body: The Dosya tray or menu-bar icon summarizes every configured sync pair. It provides quick controls for the whole engine and individual folders; it does not select an active workspace or desktop session. ## Before you start Find the Dosya icon in the Windows notification area, macOS menu bar, or the tray implementation provided by the Linux desktop environment. A click opens the main window; Windows also supports double-click. ## Steps 1. Open the tray menu and read the disabled **Sync: {summary}** line before taking action. 2. Review each **workspaceName/remoteFolderName - {status}** entry to identify the pair that needs attention. 3. Choose **Pause Sync** or **Resume Sync** for the engine, or select **Sync All Now** to request an immediate pass. 4. Use **Open Sync Folder** for a mapped local path, or choose **Upload File...** to open the app's **Upload** route and select a file there. 5. Select **Open dosya** or click the tray icon to bring the main window forward. 6. Open **Sync** in the app and confirm the same pair status, failed-file count, or resumed activity. Pair labels include **Synced**, **Syncing…**, **Paused**, **Error**, **Waiting**, **Offline**, **Needs attention**, and **Needs permission**. Global summaries can report maintenance pause, errors, offline pairs, folders needing attention, files syncing, files not synced, paused pairs, or **All synced**. The tooltip follows `dosya - {summary}`. The menu rebuild is throttled to at most once per second, so a rapidly changing count can trail the Sync page briefly. **Quit dosya** stops the client; closing or hiding its window is a different action. ## Expected result The requested tray action affects the intended pair or global engine, and the main Sync page confirms the same underlying state after refresh. If the tray count briefly differs from Sync, wait at least one second and reopen the menu. Status changes are throttled to one rebuild per second, and the scheduled rebuild uses the newest state. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Diagnose desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues)

title: Adjust desktop transfer concurrency
summary: Set desktop sync concurrency and bandwidth limits, understand the real worker counts, and verify throughput without overloading your computer.
verification: Reviewed against `apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/main/sync/types.ts`, `transfer-concurrency.ts`, and live semaphore updates in `index.ts` on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not exercised for this rewrite.
body: Use **Sync → Settings** to balance transfer speed against CPU, memory, disk and network use. **Max concurrent transfers** advertises a range of 1–10 and defaults to 3. Treat that range as the recommended operating range: the current save path accepts any positive number, including values above 10 and fractions. The setting changes the engine immediately after you save it; active work does not require a restart. ## Before you start - Leave an important folder unchanged while testing. Use a pairing with several disposable files so more than one transfer can run. - Note the current **Max concurrent transfers**, **Upload limit (KB/s)** and **Download limit (KB/s)** values before editing them. - Confirm the pairing is not **Paused**, **Offline**, **Waiting**, **Needs attention** or **Needs permission**. Concurrency cannot bypass those states. - This is a device-wide sync setting, not a workspace role or plan control. The signed-in member still needs permission to read and write the relevant cloud files. ## Steps 1. Open **Sync**, select **Settings**, and find **Max concurrent transfers**. 2. Enter a whole number from **1** through **10**, the range advertised by the numeric control. Start with the default **3**. Choose 1–2 on a constrained computer or connection; raise the value one step at a time when both device and network remain responsive. Although the current save and engine paths accept positive fractions and values above 10, those inputs are not validated as supported settings and can create surprising worker counts. 3. If bandwidth is the actual constraint, set **Upload limit (KB/s)** or **Download limit (KB/s)**. A value of **0** means unlimited, and each limit is shared across all transfers rather than granted to every file. 4. Select **Save settings**. The confirmation is **Sync settings saved**. The app stores the rate fields as bytes per second and updates the running transfer gate. 5. Return to **Overview**, choose **Sync now** for the test pairing, and watch its progress. The live row can show percentage, file or byte counts, speed and estimated time. Open **Activity** to distinguish scanning and comparison from byte transfer. The number is a base budget, not a promise that exactly that many network requests appear at every moment. General sync work uses the saved positive value for its transfer semaphore across pairings. Direct presigned batches first floor the value, then derive wider worker pools: standard or mixed files use `min(12, max(2, floor(setting) × 2))`, while files of **256 KiB or smaller** can use up to twice that standard count, capped at 16. At the default 3, those batch ceilings are 6 standard and 12 tiny-file workers. A single file, scanning, API throttling and bandwidth limits can all leave capacity unused. ## Expected result After **Save settings**, a busy test cycle continues under the new device-level budget. Files reach the destination required by the pairing's mode, and the app remains usable. The app does not display a separate counter for the derived direct-upload workers, so verify completed files, speed and errors instead of trying to infer concurrency from one progress bar. ## Troubleshooting **The value behaves unexpectedly.** Return to a whole number from 1 to 10. The control advertises that range, but the current save path does not enforce its maximum or require an integer. Do not use zero to mean unlimited here; zero has that meaning only for the two bandwidth fields. **A higher value is slower.** Return to the previous value. Many small files, disk contention, server rate limits or a shared bandwidth cap can make extra workers unhelpful. A **Waiting** row resumes according to the server's retry timing. **Transfers still look sequential.** Make sure several eligible files are ready at once. One large file, a scan phase, a conflict or a one-file queue cannot demonstrate parallel work. **The settings page saved, but files failed.** Expand **N files not synced** in Overview and read the per-file reason. Concurrency does not repair permissions, storage limits, locks or an unavailable local path. ## Related guides - [Diagnose sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Choose a sync mode](/desktop/sync-modes)

title: Uninstall the desktop app while preserving cloud files
summary: Verify cloud and local-only files, remove each sync pair, then uninstall with the correct Windows, macOS, or Linux data-retention expectation.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx; no production installation was uninstalled.
body: Uninstalling Dosya does not issue cloud deletion requests or erase synchronized folders. Protect any local-only work first, remove active sync pairs, and then apply the operating system’s uninstall behavior. ## Before you start For each pair, inspect **Issues** and wait for important uploads to finish. Verify irreplaceable cloud copies through the web app, including path, size, and readable content. Copy every failed or local-only item to a location outside the sync root. The Sync page states: **Removing a sync pair stops syncing but does not delete any files on either side.** This is the preferred way to prevent a retained configuration from resuming after reinstall. ## Steps 1. List each sync pair, its local root, cloud destination, mode, and any file shown under **N files not synced**. 2. Open the web app and verify the important cloud objects independently of the desktop client. 3. Back up local-only or failed items to a folder that is not managed by Dosya. 4. From each pair’s menu choose **Remove**, then confirm that local and cloud files still exist in their respective locations. 5. Uninstall Dosya using the operating system’s standard application removal flow. 6. Sign in through the web app again and verify the same cloud paths, then decide whether retained local folders should be reused after reinstall. On Windows, the NSIS uninstaller deletes `%APPDATA%/dosya`, including session, pair configuration, and local sync index, while leaving sync folders untouched. The macOS and Linux packages do not request equivalent automatic user-data deletion, so configuration may remain on disk. ## Expected result Cloud files remain available because pair removal and uninstall do not delete them. Local sync folders also remain, while Windows clears Dosya application data and macOS or Linux may retain it. If a cloud file is absent before uninstall, stop and recover it from the local copy or failed-item evidence. Removing the client cannot complete an upload that never reached the service. ## Related guides - [Install and sign in to the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Check for desktop updates](/desktop/desktop-check-updates)

title: Handle unsupported media in the desktop app
summary: When desktop preview cannot render a media file, use Download, open the saved copy in a compatible app, and confirm the cloud object stays unchanged.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/FileViewer.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/OfficePreview.tsx, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/audio/AudioPlayer.tsx; production media downloads were not repeated.
body: An inline preview can fail even when the stored file is intact. Download the object through Dosya, then open that saved copy in an application that supports its codec or format. ## Before you start Confirm the selected file’s name, extension, size, and workspace. Your role must include `download_files`; without that permission, the recovery action is unavailable even though you can see file metadata. The viewer can show **This file type cannot be previewed. Download it instead.** Office conversion, video decoding, and audio decoding also have their own fallback messages. Text files larger than 2 MiB are not previewed inline, and syntax highlighting is limited to 300 KiB. ## Steps 1. Open the media file in the desktop viewer and record the exact preview or decode message instead of assuming the stored bytes are corrupt. 2. Compare the unsupported media extension and size with the source or expected Dosya upload receipt. 3. Select **Download** in the desktop viewer and choose a trusted local destination in the save dialog. 4. Wait for the **Downloaded** toast, note the displayed path, and use **Show in Folder** if needed. 5. Open the saved copy with a compatible local application and test the media, document, or text content. 6. Return to Dosya and confirm the original cloud path and metadata remain unchanged after the download. A successful download is non-destructive: it creates a local copy and does not change the cloud object. The desktop app does not expose an **Open with** action for this fallback; opening externally happens after saving. ## Expected result The saved local copy opens in a compatible application and matches the expected file. The cloud item remains at its original path because downloading does not move, rename, or delete it. If the toast says **Download failed**, verify `download_files`, available disk space, and connectivity. A file that also fails in an independent application may need a fresh upload from a known-good source. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Manage the audio queue](/files/audio-queue)

title: Review Vault members in the desktop app
summary: Review Vault membership, invite an existing Dosya user, revoke access with key rotation, and understand the permissions and limits involved.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/vault/VaultMembers.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/vault/engine.ts, packages/e2ee-client/src/workspace.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/role-gates.unit.test.ts. Production behavior was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: The **Members** dialog lists the accounts whose encryption keys can open the selected Space. Sharing seals the Space key to an existing Dosya user’s public encryption key; Dosya stores that sealed grant without learning the Space key. ## Before you start - Unlock Vault and open the intended Space; the dialog title reads **Members: _Space name_**. - The target must already have a Dosya account and an E2EE identity. If the key directory has no identity for that email, the app reports **That user hasn't set up encryption yet**. - For a Space attached to a storage workspace, viewing requires **view_team_members**, inviting requires **invite_members**, and revoking another person requires **manage_roles**. Unscoped legacy Spaces use encrypted-Space membership because no workspace role exists to consult. - Vault is not separately plan-gated. Workspace roles and current Space membership control these actions. ## Steps 1. Click **Members** in the open Space. Find your email; the roster marks it with **you** and does not show a revoke button for that row. 2. To invite someone, type their exact account email in the **teammate@example.com** field and choose **Invite**. Pressing Enter performs the same action. 3. Verify the person through another channel before sharing. The dialog warns: **Access is granted by trust-on-first-use. Verify a contact out of band; automatic key-transparency protection is coming.** 4. Confirm the new email appears in the roster. The recipient discovers the Space under **Shared with me** after their desktop app refreshes its membership list; no plaintext file is emailed. 5. To remove another member, select **Revoke access**, read **Revoke access?**, and choose **Revoke** only after confirming both email and Space name. ## What revocation changes Revocation rotates the Space key and re-seals file and folder records for every remaining member. A large Space can therefore remain busy for a noticeable period; keep Dosya open until the roster refreshes. Future content is unreadable to the removed person, but anything they downloaded earlier remains in their possession and cannot be recalled. The signed-in member cannot revoke their own access: the desktop UI omits **Revoke access** on that member’s row, and the encryption client rejects self-revocation before posting a rotation. Another current member can target the Space creator from the roster; the rotation endpoint rejects that request with **The creator of this workspace cannot be revoked**. Revocation is security-sensitive and is not undone automatically—access must be granted again with a new sealed key if removal was a mistake. ## Troubleshooting - **You don’t have permission to view members of this workspace**: request **view_team_members** from a workspace administrator. - **You don’t have permission to add members to this workspace**: an owner or role manager must grant **invite_members** or perform the invite. - **You don’t have permission to remove members from this workspace**: the current role lacks **manage_roles**. - **Revoke failed** leaves the existing membership in place. Retry after connectivity or permission is restored; do not assume key rotation completed. - **No members yet** can mean the roster request returned no visible rows. Reopen the Space after confirming you still have membership before attempting a grant. ## Expected result The roster reflects a completed grant or revocation. An invited user receives encrypted access through their own keys. A revoked account loses future Space access after successful key rotation, while previously exported copies remain outside Dosya’s control. ## Related guides - [Understand Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Recover Vault](/files/vault-recovery)

title: Save a Vault file locally from desktop
summary: Unlock Vault, download and decrypt one file to a trusted local destination, then protect the plaintext copy that remains outside Vault on disk.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/vault/VaultBrowser.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/vault/UnlockGate.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/vault/store.ts, and apps/desktop/src/main/vault-save.ts; no production Vault file was decrypted.
body: Saving from Vault decrypts the selected object on the device and writes a plaintext local copy. That result is no longer protected by Vault encryption, so choose its destination and retention deliberately. ## Before you start Open **Vault** and use **Unlock Vault** with the passphrase or **Unlock with recovery key**. Verify the target item’s name and size before starting. The desktop saver allows up to four simultaneous or pending destinations; another attempt can return **Too many downloads in progress**. ## Steps 1. Unlock Vault and select the known encrypted item in the active Vault workspace. 2. Use the item’s **Download** control; this opens the operating-system dialog titled **Save decrypted file**. 3. Choose a trusted destination, review the sanitized output name, and confirm the save; cancelling here prevents decryption from starting. 4. Wait while the Vault content is decrypted in 4 MiB plaintext chunks and streamed to the desktop destination. 5. Confirm the **Saved** toast and its **Saved to {path}** receipt, then open the file and compare its expected contents. 6. Move, encrypt, or delete the plaintext copy according to local policy when it is no longer needed. A newly created output receives owner-only mode `0600` where the platform supports it. Overwriting an existing file retains that file’s prior permissions. Write or decryption failure shows **Download failed**, aborts the sink, and removes the partial plaintext output. The save operation does not delete or alter the encrypted Vault item. There is no overall file-size ceiling in this flow, although each IPC chunk is guarded at 64 MiB. ## Expected result The selected item remains encrypted in Vault and a readable plaintext copy exists at the approved local path. The Saved receipt identifies exactly where that copy was written. Treat the local result as ordinary sensitive data. Vault recovery keys and encryption no longer protect it after successful decryption. ## Related guides - [Understand Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Recover Vault](/files/vault-recovery)

title: Browse Vault Spaces on desktop
summary: Find the Vault Spaces attached to the active workspace, distinguish your Spaces from shared ones, and safely open encrypted folder trees on desktop.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/vault/VaultBrowser.tsx, VaultSpaces.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/vault/store.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/my-workspaces.ts. Production behavior was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: Vault Spaces are end-to-end encrypted containers inside the desktop app. The Space list is scoped to your signed-in account: **My Spaces** shows Spaces you created for the active storage workspace, while **Shared with me** shows encrypted Spaces another Dosya user granted to you. ## Before you start - Sign in to the Dosya desktop app and select the storage workspace whose own Spaces you need. Vault is available to signed-in accounts without a separate plan switch. - Unlock **Vault** with your encryption passphrase or recovery key. The Space browser is hidden while Vault is locked. - Allow the first refresh to finish. A newly shared item may initially read **Shared Space** while the client decrypts its real name in the background. ## Steps 1. Select **Vault** in the desktop sidebar. The unlocked header must show **End-to-end encrypted** and a **Lock** button. 2. In **My Spaces**, choose the Space tied to the active storage workspace. Legacy Spaces without a stored workspace association also appear here. 3. Use **Shared with me** for a Space granted by another member. Those Spaces remain visible when you switch the active storage workspace because the grant belongs to your account. 4. Open a folder card labelled **Encrypted folder**. Use the breadcrumb at the top of the browser to return to the Space root or an earlier folder. 5. Confirm the file and folder names match the intended Space before uploading, downloading, or opening **Members**. ## How Space selection behaves Opening a Space verifies its signed membership history, decrypts its index locally, and then loads the root folder. The server returns only Space IDs that the signed-in account currently belongs to. A Space created on this device is kept as a locally trusted founder record; a discovered or shared Space is opened with trust-on-first-use checks. The Space menu collapses automatically when the viewport is 1,000 pixels wide or narrower. At wider sizes, use the **Collapse** or **Expand** control; that preference is stored only on this computer. ## If a Space is missing or will not open - **Could not check for shared Spaces.** Confirm the desktop session is online, then lock and unlock Vault to request the account’s membership list again. - **Could not open Space.** Do not recreate the Space. Retry after checking connectivity and membership; creating another Space produces a different encrypted container. - A former member no longer receives a Space in discovery after revocation. Ask a member with the required workspace permission to grant access again. - When switching accounts, the client clears the previous account’s Space names, active Space, members, and one-time recovery key from memory before loading the next account. ## Expected result The chosen Space opens at its encrypted root, its real name replaces any temporary placeholder, and the browser lists only entries decrypted for that Space. Merely browsing does not upload, delete, rename, or change membership. ## Related guides - [Understand Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Recover Vault](/files/vault-recovery)

title: Unlock Vault in the desktop app
summary: Unlock Vault with a passphrase or 32-byte recovery key, understand local key handling, and avoid the irreversible destroy-and-reset path on desktop.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/vault/UnlockGate.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/vault/store.ts, packages/e2ee-client/src/session.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/oprf-evaluate.ts. Production behavior was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: Unlocking reconstructs the encryption session on this computer. Dosya never receives the raw passphrase: the client blinds it for a verified OPRF exchange, applies Argon2id locally, and unwraps the private identity keys only in memory. ## Before you start - Sign in to the correct Dosya account and keep an internet connection for the identity record and passphrase-hardening exchange. - Use the Vault encryption passphrase, not necessarily the account password. The account password is requested only for **Destroy vault and start over**. - If the passphrase is unavailable, locate the 32-byte recovery key shown once at setup as 64 hexadecimal characters. Spaces, dashes, and line breaks added when storing it are ignored. ## Steps 1. Open **Vault** in the desktop sidebar. Wait while the client checks whether this account already has an encrypted identity. 2. In **Unlock Vault**, enter **Your encryption passphrase**, then click **Unlock**. The control reads **Unlocking…** while local key derivation runs. 3. For recovery, select **Use recovery key**, paste the value into **Recovery key**, and click **Unlock**. Select **Use passphrase** to switch back. 4. When the Vault browser appears, confirm the header shows **End-to-end encrypted** and your Spaces begin loading. 5. Select **Lock** when leaving the computer. Locking removes the active session, open Space, folder entries, and member list from application memory. ## Errors and retry timing - **Couldn’t check encryption status** leaves the identity state unknown and offers **Retry**. Never choose setup as a workaround; replacing real identity keys would orphan existing encrypted data. - A wrong passphrase produces **Incorrect passphrase or no identity found.** A wrong recovery value produces **That recovery key did not unlock your Vault.** These messages deliberately reveal no internal cryptographic detail. - **Recovery key unlock is not available in this version yet. Please try again after the next update.** Update the desktop app before attempting recovery again. - The authenticated OPRF endpoint applies an in-isolate sliding-window limit of 10 evaluations per account over 3,600 seconds; it is not a globally distributed counter. If a request returns **Too many requests**, stop guessing and follow its **Retry-After** or **X-RateLimit-Reset** timing, or use the saved recovery key. ## Last-resort reset Use **Destroy vault and start over** only when both unlock methods are permanently lost. The dialog requires the Dosya **Account password** and the acknowledgement **I understand my encrypted files cannot be recovered after this**. An authenticator-app 2FA account also needs a **Two-factor code**; the field accepts up to 10 non-space characters even though its placeholder says **6-digit code**. Email-code 2FA cannot complete this one-request reauthentication and returns **Destroying a vault is not available on accounts using email codes for two-factor authentication. Switch to an authenticator app in your security settings, then try again.** Clicking **Destroy my vault** deletes this account’s Vault identity, sealed grants, and membership rows. It deliberately leaves workspace heads, folder indexes, manifests, encrypted chunks, and the membership log intact so remaining members of a shared Space keep their data. The old ciphertext becomes permanently unreadable to this account; a fresh setup creates unrelated keys and cannot restore its former access. ## Expected result A valid passphrase or recovery key changes the session to unlocked and exposes only Spaces whose keys the account can open. Failed attempts keep Vault locked. Destroying the identity is the sole irreversible path described here and must never be used as routine troubleshooting. ## Related guides - [Understand Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Recover Vault](/files/vault-recovery)

title: Upload an encrypted Vault file on desktop
summary: Upload files to an unlocked Vault Space, understand local encryption and storage limits, and recover cleanly from folder or quota failures on desktop.
verification: Verified locally against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/vault/VaultBrowser.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/vault/store.ts, packages/e2ee-core/src/chunker.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/chunk-upload-url.ts. Production behavior was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: Vault encrypts each selected file on the computer before ciphertext is uploaded. The current desktop uploader reads one whole file into memory, then divides it into content-defined chunks with a 256 KiB target minimum, about 1 MiB average, and 4 MiB plaintext hard maximum; the final chunk can be smaller than 256 KiB. ## Before you start - Unlock **Vault**, open a Space, and navigate to the destination folder shown in the breadcrumb. - Check free storage for the storage workspace attached to that Space. Vault bytes count against the owner’s active plan and any whole-GB workspace storage cap; the quota refusal directs you to empty trash or increase available capacity. - Choose files that fit available device memory. Because the desktop renderer buffers each file before encryption, very large files can fail locally even when the cloud quota has room. - You must still be a member of the encrypted Space. Upload is not restricted by a separate Vault plan, but the destination workspace must exist and have quota available. ## Steps 1. In **Vault**, select the correct Space and open the destination folder. 2. Click **Upload**, select one or more files, and confirm the operating-system picker. The grid shows a busy state while files are handled sequentially. 3. Alternatively, drag loose files onto the dashed Vault area. When a dropped selection contains a directory, the app shows **Folders are not supported in the Vault yet**. Only loose top-level files are uploaded; nested folder contents are not imported. 4. Keep the app open until the toast says **Uploaded** and names the file or number of files. 5. Verify each new encrypted file card appears in the same folder. The card’s extension label is derived from its name; it is not a decrypted preview. ## Storage, encryption, and recovery Each encrypted chunk may contain at most 4,194,304 plaintext bytes; authenticated encryption adds 16 bytes to that chunk on the wire. An encrypted file manifest records the chunk sequence and integrity root, while a separately signed root manifest binds the folder-index Merkle root. The chunk ceiling is not a 4 MiB file-size limit. If an older Space has no live storage-workspace association, the first upload may receive HTTP 412. The desktop app then attaches the Space to the active storage workspace and retries once. This association determines which workspace pays for the bytes, so confirm the active workspace before the upload. ## Troubleshooting - **Upload failed** followed by a quota message: empty that workspace’s trash, raise its admin storage cap, or move to a plan with enough account-wide storage. - **This Space is not attached to a storage workspace yet - attach it to one of your workspaces before adding files** means no valid workspace can be charged. Select a valid active workspace and retry. - **Could not upload file.** Retry one small file to separate a memory or connectivity problem from a specific file. Successful earlier files in a multi-file selection remain uploaded; the operation is not an all-or-nothing batch. - Do not assume dropping a folder preserved its tree. Create the needed folder structure through a supported client first, or upload its files to the current Vault folder. ## Expected result Dosya displays **Uploaded**, refreshes the selected folder, and shows every successfully committed item. File contents were encrypted locally; storage receives ciphertext chunks, an encrypted file manifest, and encrypted folder-index data. A separately signed root manifest binds the folder-index Merkle root. A failed later file does not roll back files already completed. ## Related guides - [Understand Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Recover Vault](/files/vault-recovery)

title: Preview a vCard in the desktop app
summary: Review one or many contacts in a VCF preview, search parsed fields, copy exact values, and understand when external contact links share data.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/VCardView.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/vcard.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/file-type.ts and apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts. body: The vCard viewer fetches a `.vcf` or `.vcard` file and parses its contacts inside the desktop renderer. Reviewing or searching is read-only; it does not import contacts into an address book. ## Before you start Open a contact file you are permitted to view. Treat contact details as sensitive: copying places the exact value on the system clipboard, and opening a map or website can disclose that value to an external service. ## Steps 1. Open the file and wait while the surface shows **Loading contact…**. 2. Review the selected card's name, job title, organization, phone numbers, email addresses, postal addresses, websites, birthday, note and embedded photo when those fields exist. 3. If the file contains multiple contacts, use **Search contacts**. Matching checks full name, email, phone and organization; an empty result displays **No matches**. 4. Select an address to open its HTTP/HTTPS Google Maps destination, or select a website to open it in the system browser. The desktop navigation policy blocks `tel:` and `mailto:` destinations, so use the phone or email field's copy button instead of expecting a dialer or mail app to launch. 5. Use a field's copy button when you need the literal value. The success check remains for about **1.2 seconds**. Google Maps receives the address embedded in its URL, and websites receive an ordinary browser visit. Clear the clipboard afterward when copied contact data should not remain available to other local applications. ## Expected result The viewer separates each parsed contact and exposes only fields present in the file. No Dosya file, contact record or version is created by previewing. ## Troubleshooting **“This contact file couldn't be read.”** means the raw request or vCard parsing failed. Confirm that the stored file is valid vCard text and that your session can access it, then reopen the preview. If expected details are absent, inspect the source in another vCard tool; the viewer cannot display a field that was missing or malformed in the uploaded card. If selecting a phone number or email address does nothing, that is the desktop app's external-navigation restriction. Hover the row and select **Copy** to use the value in another application. ## Related guides - [Install the desktop app](/desktop/install-and-sign-in) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Verify desktop recovery after a restart
summary: After restarting Dosya, let its persisted queue resume, inspect Activity and Issues, then verify one cloud result or capture the repeated error.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-15 against apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/index-db.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/ops-queue.test.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/restart-policy.ts, apps/desktop/src/main/sync/remote-client.ts, and apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/SyncPage.tsx; production recovery was not forced.
body: Dosya stores unfinished sync operations in SQLite. After a restart, operations that were marked running return to pending and can resume; wait for that queue before manually retrying a file. ## Before you start Record the affected pair, path, status, timestamp, and nonsecret error. Avoid editing the same local file during restart, because a manual duplicate change can obscure whether the persisted operation recovered. ## Steps 1. In **Sync**, capture the current **Activity** entry and any row under **N files not synced** before closing Dosya. 2. Restart the application once, reopen Sync, and look for **Resuming N operations...** before taking another action. 3. Allow the desktop sync queue and multipart status checks to run; do not create a duplicate upload for the same path. 4. If rows remain, read every **will retry** or **won't retry** state, fix their causes, then use the pair's single **Retry** control to retry all listed errors. 5. Use **Sync now** when the pair needs a fresh scan rather than a retry of one recorded failure. 6. Verify the cloud path, version, and file size, or capture the identical repeated error with its new timestamp. Completed operation records are retained for seven days; failed and pending work is not removed by that completed-record sweep. Multipart uploads can query remote status and continue missing parts instead of blindly starting the entire file again. If the renderer cannot reach the engine, it shows **Couldn't read sync status** and **The app couldn't reach its sync engine - try restarting dosya.**, with **Try again**. The engine restarts immediately after its first crash, waits one second after a second crash within 60 seconds, and parks after a third; 60 healthy seconds reset that ladder. ## Expected result The persisted operation finishes and the cloud receipt matches the intended file, or the same specific error returns with enough evidence for diagnosis. A missing issue without a matching cloud result is not proof of success. If the engine has parked after repeated crashes, restart the application and preserve the captured evidence for a problem report rather than cycling Retry continuously. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot desktop sync](/desktop/sync-issues) - [Create a desktop problem report](/desktop/desktop-problem-report)
