summary: Stream a cloud video in the desktop viewer, use native playback controls, and recover when Chromium cannot decode the file’s video or audio codec.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/files/FileViewer.tsx and apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/file-type.ts. Verified routed extensions, raw-URL streaming, native controls, autoplay request, codec failure copy and download fallback. No dedicated video-playback test was found; production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The desktop viewer streams the selected cloud file into Chromium's native video player. Opening or seeking a video is read-only and does not create a new version, but downloading writes a separate local copy. ## Before you start Dosya routes MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WebM, WMV and FLV filenames to the video surface. The extension determines the viewer, while successful playback still depends on the codecs available in the installed desktop runtime. You need permission to view the file in the active workspace. ## Steps 1. Open the video from **Files**. The viewer requests autoplay, although operating-system or runtime policy may require you to press **Play**. 2. Use the native timeline to seek and the speaker control to change playback volume. 3. Select the native fullscreen control, then leave fullscreen with that control or **Esc**. 4. Confirm the current position remains correct after seeking and pausing. Playback comes from the file's authorized raw URL; Dosya does not first save the entire video as a user-visible local file. Position, volume and fullscreen state are transient viewer state. ## Expected result A supported stream responds to Chromium's play, pause, timeline, volume and fullscreen controls. Closing the viewer leaves the stored cloud object unchanged. ## Troubleshooting If the surface reports **“This app can't decode this video. Download it and open it in a player like VLC, which decodes everything.”**, select **Download** and open the saved copy in a suitable player. AVI and WMV content, or MKV files containing DTS audio or 10-bit video, may route correctly yet fail codec decoding. If playback stalls without the decode message, verify network access and reopen the file. A file extension alone cannot guarantee that every contained stream is supported. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Manage the audio queue](/files/audio-queue)

title: Start a streaming ZIP download
summary: Start a streamed ZIP from Files, allow the browser time to accept it, and confirm the download begins without starting duplicate archive requests.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts; apps/api/src/lib/archive-stream.ts.
body: Dosya does not build an archive job with a separate ready screen. **Download ZIP** navigates the browser to a streaming archive response, and the Files page immediately reports **Download started** with **Your ZIP is being prepared by the browser.** Keep the new archive tab or browser download active while the stream begins. A single request can include at most 10,000 files and 5 GiB of source data. The archive is named `dosya-download.zip`. You need access to Files and the `download_files` permission; a denied role receives **You don't have download permission**. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the workspace that contains the source items, and confirm your role shows download actions. 2. Select the required files or folders; the selection bar reports the selected count and exposes **Download ZIP**. 3. Choose **Download ZIP** once. For one archive, Dosya opens the streaming endpoint in a new tab and shows **Download started**. 4. Leave the new tab or browser transfer open while the server walks folders and begins the ZIP stream; there is no Dosya progress card to wait for. 5. Open the browser's downloads list and look for `dosya-download.zip`; a visible JSON error page means the archive was refused before downloading. 6. After the transfer finishes, open the ZIP and compare its top-level names with the selection before deleting or moving any originals. ## Expected result The browser starts one download named `dosya-download.zip`. Dosya records the archive transfer before streaming, while the original files and folders remain unchanged. If the new tab reports **Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)** or **Archive too large (max 5 GiB)**, reduce the folder or selection and start separate archives. **This folder is empty - there's nothing to download** means the chosen folder contains no downloadable files. A neutral **No items found** can also mean every candidate is hidden or blocked by a lock; return to Files, confirm the items are visible and unlocked, then select them again. ## Related guides - [Choose files and folders for an archive download](/uploading/download-files) - [Verify a downloaded Dosya ZIP archive](/uploading/verify-downloaded-archive)

title: Choose a direct download or ZIP archive
summary: Download one cloud file directly, or package folders and selected items as one or more streamed ZIP archives within Dosya's archive limits.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts, apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.test.ts, apps/web/src/pages/files.download.test.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.access.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.get.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.repo.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/archive-stream.ts and apps/api/src/lib/archive-stream.unit.test.ts. Verified direct-file and Download ZIP controls, streamed archive behavior, split-request ceilings, server archive limits, silent filtering of inaccessible entries, the ordinary all-inaccessible 404 response and object-read-only missing notes. The current single-file menu capture was inspected; the generic workflow map was removed rather than presented as product UI.
body: Use **Download** on a file when you want its current bytes and filename without an archive wrapper. Use a folder's download action or select several items and choose **Download ZIP** when you need one package that preserves folder structure. A large selection can arrive as several ZIP files. ## Steps ### Choose the right method | What you need | Action | What arrives | | --- | --- | --- | | One current file | Open the file menu and choose **Download** | The file itself, with its current name | | One folder | Open the folder menu and choose its download action | A ZIP containing the reachable folder contents | | Several selected files or folders | Select their checkboxes and choose **Download ZIP** | One or more streamed ZIP archives | | One older file version | Open version history and download that version | The chosen historical version, outside this Files-page workflow | Selecting one file with its checkbox and choosing **Download ZIP** still asks for an archive. Open that file's three-dot or right-click menu when you want the original file directly. ### Before downloading - Open **Files** in the workspace that owns the content. - Confirm your role includes download permission. Dosya hides ordinary download controls when `download_files` is absent. - Check the device's free storage and the browser's configured download location. - Review a multi-item selection before starting. A folder expands to its downloadable descendants on the server, so one selected row can represent thousands of files. - Keep cloud files in place until you verify the local result. Downloading creates a local copy; it does not remove the stored item. ### Download one file directly 1. Find the file in **Files** and verify the active workspace and breadcrumb. 2. Open the file row's three-dot or right-click menu and locate **Download**. 3. Choose **Download** for that named file. 4. Follow the browser's save behavior. It may ask for a location or save to its configured Downloads folder. 5. Open the result and compare its filename and byte size with the cloud item. A direct download avoids ZIP extraction and is the clearest choice for one file. The browser controls the final local location; Dosya does not save the result into another cloud folder. ### Download a folder or selection as ZIP 1. Under **Files**, tick each intended row and confirm the selection bar's top-level item count before choosing **Download ZIP**. 2. Choose **Download ZIP**. 3. For one archive request, Dosya reports **Your ZIP is being prepared by the browser.** 4. If the selection must be split, Dosya reports **Too many items for one file - arriving as _N_ ZIPs.** Allow multiple downloads only when that count matches your action. 5. Wait for every announced archive, then open each ZIP and compare its tree with the selection. ## Archive limits and split behavior - The web app places no more than 300 selected IDs in one archive request. - One click can start at most 20 separate downloads. If the proposed selection needs more, the page says how many parts it would require and asks you to select fewer items. - Each server-built ZIP can contain at most 10,000 entries and 5 GiB of source data. A folder can exceed either ceiling after its descendants are counted. - ZIPs are streamed to the browser. Preparation does not create a second stored copy in your Dosya workspace. - Archive entries use storage mode rather than recompressing media. Do not assume the ZIP will be much smaller than its source files. If one split part fails, retry a smaller group instead of starting the complete selection again. A single selected folder can still exceed the per-archive ceiling, so open that folder and download smaller subfolders or file groups. ## Expected result For a direct file, confirm the local name, size and opening application. For an archive, check every ZIP part, extract it into a temporary folder and compare its entry list and folder paths with every intended item you are permitted to download. A **MISSING -** text entry means an item passed access filtering but its object could not be read from storage while the ZIP streamed. Hidden, locked or otherwise inaccessible items are filtered before archive entries are built, so they can be absent from a successful ZIP without a **MISSING -** note. Preserve an archive containing that note and try the named file as a direct download; contact support if the direct download also fails. ## Troubleshooting **Download is absent from the menu.** Your role may lack download permission, or the item may be view-only, hidden, deleted or blocked by a lock. Ask an owner or admin to check the role and item state. **The ZIP request says `Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)`.** Divide the folder or selection into groups with fewer expanded entries. **The browser shows `Archive too large (max 5 GiB)`.** Select a smaller source-data total. The limit applies to each ZIP request, not to the size after compression. **The request returns `No items found`.** No downloadable item remained after current access checks, or the selected IDs are stale. Verify the workspace and selection, then ask an owner to inspect hidden and configured lock states. A selection containing only inaccessible items normally uses this 404 response without disclosing which state blocked it. **Only some of the announced ZIPs arrived.** Check the browser's automatic-download permission and download shelf. Then retry only the missing group with fewer selections. **A ZIP opens but an intended item is absent.** Compare the archive entry list with the selection. An inaccessible item can be filtered while permitted files still produce a successful ZIP and no **MISSING -** note. A visible **MISSING -** note instead identifies an object-read failure after access checks. ## Related guides - [Download one or several cloud files](/uploading/download-files) - [Verify a downloaded archive](/uploading/verify-downloaded-archive) - [Troubleshoot a folder download](/uploading/folder-download-troubleshoot) - [Remove a downloaded copy from a shared computer](/uploading/download-clean-up-local-copy) - [Confirm the upload workspace and folder](/uploading/upload-confirm-workspace)

title: Remove a downloaded file from a shared computer
summary: Delete downloaded files, extracted copies and browser traces from a shared computer while preserving the Dosya cloud original.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts, apps/web/src/pages/files.download.test.tsx, apps/web/src/components/layout/profile-menu.tsx and apps/web/src/lib/logout.ts for Dosya download and logout behavior. Local file removal, Trash and Recycle Bin steps are operating-system actions and are labelled as such. Verified that Dosya downloads create separate local data and that local deletion does not call a cloud delete route. The existing single-file screenshot was inspected; no visual asset changed.
keywords: delete local copy after cloud download
body: Downloading a cloud file creates a separate copy on the computer. Removing that local copy does not delete the original stored in Dosya. On a shared or public computer, check for the downloaded file, any extracted archive contents, and the signed-in browser session before you leave. ## Before you start - Prefer a trusted personal device for confidential files. A public computer may be managed or monitored in ways you cannot inspect. - Note the browser's download destination. Most browsers use **Downloads**, but a browser can ask for another folder or remember a different location. - Download only the item you need. Selecting several Dosya files can create a ZIP archive and may leave both the archive and extracted copies on the computer. - If the computer belongs to another person or organization, follow its retention and secure-deletion policy. ## Steps: download and identify the local copy 1. In Dosya, open **Files** in the correct workspace. 2. Open the file's three-dot menu or right-click the file, then select **Download**. 3. Wait for the browser to report that the download finished. A filename in the browser's download list is not proof that the complete file is available until the transfer finishes. 4. Open the containing folder from the browser's download list. Confirm the filename, extension, size and modified time so you know exactly which local item must be removed. 5. If the download is a ZIP, note both the ZIP filename and the folder where you extract it. ## Remove the downloaded data 1. Close the downloaded file in the browser, preview app, document editor or media player. An open application can keep the file locked. 2. Delete the downloaded file from its actual folder. If you extracted an archive, delete the original ZIP and the extracted folder unless you are authorized to keep either one. 3. Check every **download destination** you deliberately used, such as Desktop, Documents, a USB drive or a temporary working folder. 4. Empty **Trash** on macOS or **Recycle Bin** on Windows if the device policy permits it. Moving an item there is reversible and does not free the local copy immediately. 5. Remove the entry from the browser's download list if you do not want the filename visible to the next user. This clears a browser record only; it does not touch the disk copy. 6. Open the account menu and choose **Log out**. Close every Dosya tab so the next user cannot return to an authenticated page through browser history. 7. If you used a normal browser profile on a device you do not control, clear Dosya cookies and site data through that browser's privacy settings. This signs the profile out but does not erase downloaded files. ## Expected result Reopen the folder that contained the download and search the computer for the exact filename. Confirm the file, its ZIP archive and any extracted folder are absent. Check Trash or Recycle Bin as well. Then open Dosya from a trusted device and confirm the cloud original is still present in the intended workspace. A private window can discard its session when every private window closes, depending on the browser. It does not automatically remove files written to Downloads, another folder or an attached drive. ## Limits and important details - Clearing the browser's download history is different from deleting the downloaded file. - Signing out of Dosya ends access in that browser, but it does not remove files already saved to the computer. - Emptying Trash or Recycle Bin is irreversible through the normal restore action. Managed-device backups, snapshots or monitoring systems may retain other copies beyond your control. - If you downloaded a file into a synced local folder, another storage service may already have copied it. Remove it through that service's approved workflow too. - Do not use the Dosya **Delete** action for this task. That action changes the cloud item and may affect collaborators. ## Troubleshooting **The file will not delete.** Close every app or browser tab using it, wait for any extraction or virus scan to finish, and retry. If the device reports that another process owns the file, ask its administrator rather than installing cleanup software. **You cannot find the downloaded file.** Open the browser's downloads panel and use **Show in folder** or its equivalent. Also check the browser's configured download location and search for the exact filename. **You removed the browser entry but the file still opens.** The history entry and disk file are separate. Locate the file in Finder or File Explorer, delete it there, then empty Trash or Recycle Bin if required. **The filename still appears in recent items.** Close the application that opened the file and clear that application's recent-file entry if policy permits. A recent-item shortcut is separate from the downloaded bytes. **The file was saved in a synced folder.** Follow that service's removal and retention workflow on the account that received the copy. Deleting only the shared computer's local placeholder may leave its remote copy intact. **You accidentally deleted the Dosya original.** Stop changing the local copies and use the Dosya Trash recovery workflow as soon as possible. ## Related guides - [Download one file or several files](/uploading/download-files) - [Verify a downloaded archive](/uploading/verify-downloaded-archive) - [Review and revoke account sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Downloading one file or several files
summary: Download one cloud file directly, or select files and folders to receive one or more streamed ZIP archives with clear size and entry limits.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts, apps/web/src/pages/files.download.test.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts, apps/api/src/lib/archive-stream.ts and apps/api/src/lib/download-guard.ts. Verified exact Download and Download ZIP labels, download_files visibility, direct-file versus streamed-archive behavior, 300-ID request chunks, 20-download client ceiling, and the 10,000-entry and 5 GiB server archive limits. Existing screenshots were inspected against the current controls; no visual asset changed.
body: Open **Files** in the intended workspace. A single file downloads directly with its current filename. A folder or multi-item selection streams one or more ZIP archives, and a very large selection may be split across several ZIP files. ## Before you start - Select the workspace that contains the files. Files search, folders and selection apply to the active workspace. - Confirm your role includes the `download_files` capability. Dosya hides the download controls when that capability is absent. - Make sure the device has enough local disk space. Dosya storage capacity controls uploads; your browser and device control where a download can be saved. - Check the files and versions you intend to keep. Downloading an older version from version history is a separate action from downloading the current file in Files. - Use harmless samples when testing a browser's prompts, especially on a shared device. ## Steps: download one file 1. Open **Files** and browse or search for the file. 2. Check the active workspace and folder in the sidebar and breadcrumb. 3. Open the file's three-dot menu or right-click its row to find **Download**. 4. Choose **Download**. The browser opens Dosya's direct file response in a new tab and takes over when it receives the attachment. 5. Follow the browser's download prompt. Depending on browser settings, it may ask for a destination or save directly to the configured Downloads folder. 6. Open the local result and compare its filename and size with the cloud item. For an important **Download**, use a published checksum or your own integrity check. ## Steps: download several files or folders 1. In Files, select the checkbox beside each required file or folder. The selection bar shows the item count. 2. Review the names before continuing. A selected folder expands to its downloadable descendants when the archive is prepared. 3. Choose **Download ZIP**. 4. Read the confirmation. One archive shows **Your ZIP is being prepared by the browser.** A split selection says **Too many items for one file - arriving as _N_ ZIPs.** 5. Allow multiple downloads if the browser asks and you intended the large selection. Do not disable browser protections for an unfamiliar page. 6. Wait for every announced archive, then open each **Download ZIP** result and compare its contents with the selected items. ## Expected result One file downloads with its current filename, or the selected files and folders arrive in one or more ZIP archives. The local files open successfully and match the names and sizes you expected. The browser's save location is not a Dosya folder. Moving or deleting the downloaded local copy does not change the cloud file, and downloading does not remove the original from Dosya. When the device is shared, follow [the local-copy cleanup checklist](/uploading/download-clean-up-local-copy) after verifying the download. ## Limits and permission behavior - Each server-prepared archive is limited to 10,000 entries and 5 GiB of source data. A selected folder can exceed either limit even though it appears as one row. - The web app places at most 300 selected IDs in each archive request and starts at most 20 downloads from one click. A folder can expand after the request, so split parts still have to fit the server archive limits. - Dosya streams archive bytes to the browser instead of buffering the finished ZIP in the page. The browser chooses the final local filename and destination. - The browser can ask whether to allow multiple downloads. Blocking that prompt can leave only part of a multi-ZIP selection on your device. - A role without download permission does not receive the Download action. A file set to **view only** can be previewable while its download is refused. - Hidden, inaccessible or locked items are subject to their own access rules. Verify archive contents instead of assuming every item visible to another user was included. - Files in **Deleted** are handled through restore or permanent deletion controls rather than the ordinary live-file Download menu. ## Troubleshooting **Download is missing.** Confirm the file is in the live Files view and that your role has download permission. Ask an owner or admin to review the role and any folder-level restriction. View-only access deliberately removes downloading while preserving preview where supported. **Nothing appears after Download.** Check the browser's download indicator, popup or automatic-download permission, configured save location and device free space. Search the Downloads folder for the exact filename before starting another copy. **Fewer ZIPs arrived than announced.** A later part may have exceeded an archive limit or failed to start. Dosya reports how many parts started when it can detect the failure. Select fewer items and retry only the missing group. **The archive is too large or has too many entries.** Keep every archive below 5 GiB and 10,000 entries. Open a large folder and download smaller subfolders or file selections. **The local file will not open.** Compare its size with Dosya and download it once more on a stable connection. Preserve both copies until you know whether the problem is an incomplete download or the source format itself. **The browser saves without asking.** Change the browser's download-location setting if you want a prompt. Dosya sends the file; the browser chooses the local save behavior. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I download several files together? Yes. Select their checkboxes and choose **Download ZIP**. A very large selection can produce several ZIPs or ask you to select fewer items. ### Can I download a whole folder? Yes. Open the folder's menu and choose Download, or include it in a multi-selection. The result is a ZIP containing the downloadable folder contents. ### Why is my browser not saving the download? Check its download indicator, popup and multiple-download permissions, save location and available device storage. A missing Download action points to Dosya access rules; a clicked action with no saved file usually needs a browser-side check. ## Related guides - [Web app navigation](/account/navigate-web-app) - [Fixing a slow upload or download](/troubleshooting/slow-transfer) - [Understanding storage usage and failed quota checks](/uploading/storage-usage) - [Uploading large files with available storage](/uploading/large-files)

title: Download a cloud folder as a ZIP archive
summary: Download one Dosya folder with its nested paths intact, recognize protected or empty content, and resolve the exact archive size and file-count limits.
verification: Verified the folder context action, recursive entry rules and refusal text in apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/archive-entries.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: A folder download creates one streamed ZIP containing downloadable files from that folder and its descendants. Paths leading to included files are retained. Empty descendant folders are not represented because the ZIP contains file entries rather than standalone folder entries. You need a workspace role with **download_files**. The folder's **Download** action is absent when the role lacks that permission. Content protected by a hidden or locked boundary is not disclosed through the archive; unlock an item you are permitted to access before starting the download. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, confirm the workspace and browse to the folder's parent. 2. Open the target folder first if you need to review its contents. Return to its parent when the list is correct. 3. Open the folder row's action menu and choose **Download**. In a pointer context menu, the same action appears between **Open** and **Share**. 4. The browser opens the archive request and begins saving `dosya-download.zip`. A successful attachment normally closes the temporary tab into the browser download shelf. 5. Wait for the browser to mark the file complete before opening, moving or renaming it. ## Included names and protected items The ZIP begins with the chosen folder's name for every included file and preserves the folder segments leading to that file. Dosya makes each path segment safe for local extraction. Colliding paths are retained with numbered names instead of overwriting one another. Files marked **View only**, password-locked files, and hidden content outside your available view are excluded. This prevents the archive response from revealing that a protected name exists. If you expected such a file and are authorized to open it, unlock it in Files, verify that it appears, and request a new archive. ## Folder download limits Archive preparation refuses a tree containing more than **10,000 downloadable files** with **“Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)”**. The combined source size may not exceed **5 GiB**; over that boundary the response is **“Archive too large (max 5 GiB)”**. These are per-ZIP limits, independent of free disk space on your computer. A truly empty folder produces **“This folder is empty - there's nothing to download.”** If several empty folders were selected through the bulk action, the response uses **“These folders are empty - there's nothing to download.”** A protected or unavailable folder can instead return **“No items found”** without explaining what was concealed. ## Expected result Extract the ZIP into a new local directory. Match the top-level folder name, descendant paths and a sample of file sizes against Files. Do not delete the cloud folder until the archive opens, the expected branches exist, and representative files can be read. If an archived file vanished from object storage while the database still listed it, Dosya puts a `MISSING - .txt` notice at the corresponding path. For example, `report.pdf` becomes `MISSING - report.pdf.txt`. The notice means the original bytes are absent from this ZIP; try the file's individual **Download**, then give support the visible file name if that also fails. ## Related guides - [Handle a large folder download](/uploading/large-folder-download) - [Verify the downloaded ZIP](/uploading/verify-downloaded-archive)

title: Retry a failed archive download
summary: Rebuild the original Files selection and start a fresh streamed ZIP after an archive fails; Dosya does not keep an expiring prepared job to reopen.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts; apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/files.download.test.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts.
body: A Dosya ZIP is streamed directly to the browser. There is no stored preparation job, reusable completion page, or archive-expiry timer. If the tab shows an error or the browser transfer fails, return to the live Files view and submit a current selection. Selections containing more than 300 IDs are split into parts of at most 300 IDs. One action may start no more than 20 ZIP downloads. Folder IDs and file IDs are chunked separately, so the exact part count can be higher than a simple total divided by 300. ## Steps 1. Close the error tab or cancel the failed browser transfer, but keep a note of its exact response before retrying. 2. Return to **Files** and reopen the original folder so the selection reflects items that still exist and that your role can currently see. 3. Select the source rows again; if the prior response named the 10,000-entry or 5 GiB cap, divide the content into smaller folders or batches. 4. Choose **Download ZIP** once. If Dosya refuses more than 20 browser downloads, select fewer IDs and repeat after that smaller batch finishes. 5. For a split selection, let the browser run its automatic sequence: parts start 400 milliseconds apart, and the final hidden frame settles four seconds after it starts. This takes `(N - 1) × 400 ms + 4 s`, or about 11.6 seconds at the 20-part maximum. 6. Check the browser downloads list, open every completed ZIP, and compare their contents with the selection. If a part failed, Dosya reports only counts; retry a deliberately smaller, known subset so you can identify what is missing. ## Expected result Each accepted part appears as a new browser download. For one part, the toast says **Your ZIP is being prepared by the browser.** For several parts, it says **Too many items for one file - arriving as N ZIPs.** **That selection would need N separate downloads, and 20 is the most one action will start** is a client refusal: reduce the selected rows. **X of N downloads started** means one or more archive parts rendered an error instead of becoming a download, but the receipt does not identify the failed chunk or source IDs. Compare the completed ZIP contents with the original selection, or retry deliberately smaller known batches. Starting again can produce another complete ZIP, so remove duplicates locally only after opening and comparing them. ## Related guides - [Start a fresh download from Files](/uploading/download-files) - [Verify a downloaded Dosya ZIP archive](/uploading/verify-downloaded-archive)

title: Download selected files as ZIP archives
summary: Use Download ZIP for a mixed file selection, understand when Dosya creates multiple archives, and recover from size, count or permission errors.
verification: Verified selection controls, chunking, messages and streamed archive behavior in apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Use **Download ZIP** when you want one local download for several selected files or folders. Dosya streams each archive to the browser instead of building the entire ZIP in the page's memory. The control appears only when your workspace role has **download_files** permission. Locked and hidden content is protected during archive creation: a file or subtree you cannot download is omitted without revealing its name. Unlock permitted content before selecting it if it must be included. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** and enter the workspace and folder that contain the items. 2. Select each file or folder. The bulk-action bar shows the number selected. 3. Review the highlighted names, then choose **Download ZIP**. 4. Read the confirmation. One archive shows **Download started** with “Your ZIP is being prepared by the browser.” A larger selection can say “Too many items for one file - arriving as *N* ZIPs.” 5. Use the browser's download list to confirm that every planned ZIP reaches its completed state. ## Know when the selection becomes several ZIPs Up to **300 selected IDs** fit in one browser download request. A longer selection is divided into parts of at most 300 IDs, with folder parts and file parts kept separate. One action can start at most **20 downloads**. When more than 20 parts would be required, nothing starts. **Download problem** reports the required part count and says that 20 is the maximum. Clear part of the selection, download the remainder, and repeat for the items you removed. Each produced ZIP is still subject to the server limits: no more than **10,000 included files** and no more than **5 GiB** of source bytes per archive. A selected folder counts by all downloadable files in its tree, so one folder can exceed either ceiling even though it occupies only one selection row. ## What the ZIP contains Files selected directly appear at the archive root. A selected folder keeps its folder name in the paths of included files. Empty descendant folders have no ZIP entry. If two entries would have the same path, the later name gains a number such as `report (2).pdf` rather than replacing the first copy. Dosya supplies the attachment name `dosya-download.zip`. ## Fix a refused or incomplete selection - **“Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)”**: select fewer folders or download a large subtree separately. - **“Archive too large (max 5 GiB)”**: split the items into smaller groups whose total source size is below 5 GiB. - **“You don't have download permission”**: ask a workspace administrator for a role that includes file downloads. Retrying cannot bypass the role. - **“No items found”**: refresh Files. The IDs may no longer resolve, or all requested content may be hidden or locked from the current view. - **“This folder/file is outside the folder you're confined to”**: return to the folder assigned to your member access and select content inside that boundary. - **“Nothing to download - the selection contains no files”**: choose rows that contain downloadable files. - **Only some multi-part downloads started**: the **Download problem** toast gives counts, not the failed IDs. Use your source checklist to repeat known smaller groups and verify the resulting paths, avoiding duplicate local copies. ## Expected result Every planned ZIP reaches the browser's completed state. Open each one in a trusted archive tool, compare its paths with the downloadable files expected from the selection, and open at least one file from each included nested folder. If an object disappeared from storage during streaming, the ZIP contains `MISSING - .txt` in that file's place; download the original by itself and contact support if it also fails. ## Related guides - [Download individual files](/uploading/download-files) - [Check an archive before sharing it](/uploading/verify-downloaded-archive)

title: Verify a downloaded file by name and size
summary: Compare the downloaded file with Dosya File details by name and displayed size, then open the local copy to confirm the intended item arrived.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx; apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download.ts.
body: A single-file **Download** opens `/api/files/:id/download`, which checks membership, Files access, the `download_files` permission, confinement, hidden state, and locks. An accepted request redirects to a signed object URL that lasts 300 seconds. Downloading does not alter the Dosya item. Dosya's **File details** panel shows the stored name and a human-readable size. Use those values to identify the browser result; Dosya does not display or attach a checksum for this manual comparison. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, select the intended item and open **File details**; record its full name, extension, and displayed **Size**. 2. Confirm that you are viewing the current file rather than a historical version, because a version-row download can have a different byte size. 3. Choose **Download** and wait for the browser to mark the transfer complete; restart from Files if a stale 300-second signed redirect no longer works. 4. In the browser download list or operating-system file properties, compare the saved name with the Dosya name; browsers may add a local suffix when that name already exists. 5. Compare the local byte count or formatted size with **File details**, allowing only the display rounding introduced by human-readable units. 6. Open the local copy in an application you trust and inspect representative content before using, sharing, or deleting another copy. ## Expected result The local file represents the selected Dosya item: its original name is recognizable, its size agrees with File details after unit rounding, and a trusted application can read it. The source remains in its workspace. A locally appended name such as `report (1).pdf` normally means the browser avoided overwriting an existing local file; verify the size and content rather than assuming a Dosya rename. **This file is view-only and cannot be downloaded** requires a different item or a lock change by an authorized member. For **This file is locked. Enter the lock password to access it**, unlock the current file in Dosya and start a new download from that view. ## Related guides - [Download the source file you intend to verify](/uploading/download-files) - [Verify a downloaded Dosya ZIP archive](/uploading/verify-downloaded-archive)

title: Delete selected duplicate copies
summary: Select exact copies, keep the right cloud file, interpret Dosya's reclaimable total, and move only permitted duplicates into recoverable workspace trash.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/duplicates.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/duplicates.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/duplicates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/duplicates/group.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/batch-delete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/file-trash-many.ts and apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx. Verified exact labels, newest ordering, 100-group display cap, 500-file request chunks, permission and lock refusals, partial-batch behavior, soft-delete outcome, share revocation and retained storage usage. Local repository evidence only; no production files were deleted.
body: The Duplicates page groups files by exact content, but it does not decide which copy matters. Review names, folder locations, uploader context and creation times before moving anything. The **newest** badge describes the latest `created_at` value, not the best filename, preferred folder or most recently edited document. ## Steps 1. Open **Duplicates** in the correct workspace. Use the folder button on every candidate row to confirm where that copy lives; the button opens its containing folder, or **Files** for a root-level item. 2. Select copies manually when folder placement or naming determines the keeper. To keep the creation-time leader in one group, choose that group's **Select all but newest**. The page-level control applies the same choice to every displayed group. 3. Inspect the selection again. **Clear** removes the current selection. Selecting the row marked **newest** is allowed, so do not treat the automatic choice as protection against deleting the wrong copy. 4. Choose **Move _N_ to trash**. The confirmation title repeats the number of selected files and shows the selected groups' reclaimable byte total. 5. Stop if the red message says **In _N_ groups you selected EVERY copy - nothing of those files will remain outside the trash.** Clear at least one row in each affected group unless removing every live copy is intentional. 6. Select **Move to trash**. The browser sends up to 500 file IDs per request and splits a larger choice across sequential requests. Wait for the result before navigating away. 7. Reopen **Duplicates** and **Files → Deleted** to verify what moved. A successful web message reads **Moved to trash** and reports the selected count. This action is a soft delete. The chosen rows leave ordinary folders, their direct share links are revoked, and the files remain recoverable in **Deleted** until manual or scheduled permanent purge. They continue using storage while in trash. The confirmation sentence **This frees _X_** describes duplicate bytes that become reclaimable after permanent deletion; moving them to trash does not immediately reduce workspace usage. The server applies the role to each file. **Delete any file** covers every visible copy; **Delete own files** covers only uploads by the current member. The current Duplicates screen can still let an own-only member select a colleague's row, and its success toast uses the requested count rather than the API's moved count. Always verify the list after a mixed-owner cleanup. A batch is refused if any visible live file has its own lock: `This file is locked and cannot be deleted`. An unopened password-locked ancestor refuses the request with `This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to delete it.` A folder-confined member cannot submit IDs outside the assigned subtree. Hidden items are silently excluded for viewers who cannot see them. If a later 500-file chunk fails, earlier chunks may already be in trash. The page then shows **Delete failed** and refreshes its data; compare **Deleted** with the remaining groups instead of repeating the entire selection. Restoration returns file rows but does not recreate revoked share links. ## Expected result Only files accepted by the permission and protection gates move to **Deleted**. At least one reviewed keeper remains in each intended group, the Duplicates page recalculates its totals, and workspace storage falls only after permanent purge. ## Related guides - [Review exact duplicates](/files/review-duplicates) - [Restore deleted files](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Review a duplicate group before cleanup
summary: Inspect one exact-duplicate group by filename, folder, size, age, and uploader before choosing a safe keeper or moving any matching copy to trash.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/duplicates.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/duplicates.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/duplicates/group.ts on 2026-10-14. No production files were trashed.
body: A Dosya duplicate group contains files with the same content hash and byte size. Review the locations and business use before choosing a keeper; the `newest` badge describes creation order, not quality or importance. **What the page counts.** Each group contains at least two exact matches. Dosya orders copies newest first by `created_at`, using file ID to break a tie. Reclaimable size is one file size multiplied by all copies except one. The page sorts groups by greatest reclaimable space and displays at most 100 at once; totals still include every group. ## Steps 1. Open **Duplicates** in the correct workspace. Membership and `access_files` are required; a folder-confined member sees only the permitted subtree, and hidden files are excluded before grouping. 2. Read the group header, such as **3 identical copies**, and its reclaimable amount. Treat this as a storage estimate, not a deletion recommendation. 3. Compare every row’s filename, folder path, size, age, uploader tooltip, and `newest` badge. Use **Open containing folder** to inspect how each copy is referenced by current work. 4. Decide which file ID should remain outside trash. A renamed or older file may still be the team’s active copy. 5. Select only the entries you have confirmed can leave their folders. If you select every copy in a group, Dosya warns that nothing from that group will remain outside trash. **What review does not do.** Opening folders and selecting checkboxes does not move files. **Move N to trash** triggers a separate confirmation: **Move N files to trash?** and explains that the files can be restored. Clearing selection with **Clear** is safe. **Large result sets.** If more than 100 groups exist, Dosya says **Showing the {shown} largest groups of {total}. Clean these up and the rest move up.** Revisit the page after cleanup rather than assuming omitted groups vanished. ## Expected result You can identify one deliberate keeper and understand the folder impact of every selected copy before a trash request. No content changes until you confirm **Move N to trash**. ## Related guides - [Use the complete exact-duplicate cleanup page](/files/review-duplicates) - [Recover a duplicate moved to trash by mistake](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Run an exact duplicate scan
summary: Understand when Dosya's exact-file scan can run, its D1-only storage limitation, 256 MiB ceiling, progress, visibility, and empty-result meaning.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/duplicates.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/duplicates.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/duplicates.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/duplicate-hash-scan.ts, apps/api/src/lib/duplicates/plan.ts, apps/api/src/lib/duplicates/group.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/settings.ts, apps/cron/src/index.ts and apps/cron/wrangler.jsonc. Verified opt-in state, D1-only scanner limitation for data_home=do, automatic two-minute schedule, 15-second page polling, 100-candidate and 384 MiB run bounds, 256 MiB per-file ceiling, three attempts, access and visibility scope, group cap and exact empty/error labels. Local source and tests only; production scheduling and object reads were not exercised.
body: Dosya finds exact duplicates in a background job. Opening **Duplicates** does not start an on-demand scan, and the current web page has no **Run scan** button. The workspace setting must be enabled through the workspace-settings API by a session whose role has **Access settings** and **Change duplicate scanning**, or by an operator. Current shipped clients do not expose that switch. ## Steps 1. Confirm with the workspace administrator that duplicate scanning is enabled, then open **Duplicates** in the intended workspace. Your role needs **Access files**; otherwise the API returns `You don't have access to the files page`. The current page does not surface its `scan_enabled: false` response and can show **No duplicates found** when scanning is off, so an empty screen alone cannot verify opt-in. 2. Ask an operator or support to confirm the workspace's content placement. The scheduled scanner still reads file rows directly from D1. When `data_home` is `do`, enabling the setting re-arms the object-side queue but the D1-only scanner does not consume it, so automatic hashing is currently unavailable for those files. 3. Look for the progress chip, such as **24 files still being scanned**. While the reported pending count is above zero, the web page requests fresh results every 15 seconds. You may leave the page: the scanner runs independently on its schedule when the workspace uses D1 storage. 4. Allow a working scheduled queue to drain. The production cron is configured every two minutes and asks for at most 100 candidates per run. A run reads at most 384 MiB of eligible content, so a large backlog can need several cycles. 5. Review groups as they appear. Dosya first compares file sizes and reads the complete bytes only for files with a same-size peer. Matching content hashes form an exact group; filenames, extensions and folders can differ. 6. Use each row's folder control to inspect its containing location. Files in a group are ordered by creation time, newest first, and the first copy carries the **newest** label. 7. Read the page total before cleanup. The response can contain at most the 100 groups with the largest reclaimable total. If more exist, the page says **Showing the 100 largest groups of _N_. Clean these up and the rest move up.** The headline totals still cover all groups. Files larger than 268,435,456 bytes (256 MiB) are marked too large and are not hashed by this scanner version. A hash failure is tried no more than three times. Therefore **No duplicates found** means no exact groups are currently known among eligible, visible files; it is not proof that oversized or repeatedly failed files differ. For a `data_home = do` workspace, a pending counter that does not fall is consistent with the known scanner limitation. Existing hashes can still produce groups, but waiting through more cron cycles will not hash the object's queued rows; contact support while the product lacks a repository-aware scanner. The result also follows the viewer's boundaries. A folder-confined member sees only that subtree. Files hidden from the viewer are removed before grouping, so a hidden copy neither appears nor leaves a misleading one-file group. Members with **Hide files** can see hidden content according to the product's privileged visibility rule. If loading fails, the page shows **Duplicates could not be loaded** with **Retry**. **Scanning your files** means eligible work remains. Once the pending value reaches zero, the settled empty state reads **No duplicates found** and **Every file in this workspace is unique. New uploads are checked automatically.** ## Expected result In a D1-backed workspace with scanning enabled, eligible files are processed automatically, the pending counter falls over successive scheduled runs, and exact-content groups become available without changing file content. A `data_home = do` workspace will not reach that result through the current scanner. Hashing is read-only; deletion happens only if you separately choose copies and confirm moving them to trash. ## Related guides - [Review exact duplicates](/files/review-duplicates) - [Restore deleted files](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Select all but the newest duplicate
summary: Use Select all but newest as a starting point, review the creation-order choice in every matching group, and avoid trashing the only useful copy.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/duplicates.tsx and apps/api/src/lib/duplicates/group.ts plus apps/api/src/pages/api/files/batch-delete.ts on 2026-10-14. Production deletion was not performed.
body: **Select all but newest** checks older entries in duplicate groups and leaves the first creation-ordered entry unchecked. It is a convenience for selection, not proof that the unchecked file is the correct keeper. **How “newest” is decided.** Files in a group are ordered by `created_at` descending, then by file ID when times match. Dosya does not compare folder importance, comments, shares, filename clarity, or human preference when assigning the badge. ## Steps 1. Open **Duplicates** and review the workspace total and visible groups. The view shows no more than the 100 largest reclaimable groups at once. 2. Choose the page-level **Select all but newest**, or use the same control on one group when you want a smaller scope. 3. Inspect every checked row. The `newest` entry should remain unchecked; older copies should be selected. Uncheck any older file that is still the canonical working copy. 4. Open containing folders when names or dates do not establish business use. Selection itself does not alter a file. 5. Read the aggregate button **Move N to trash** and reclaimable amount. If Dosya warns **In N groups you selected EVERY copy - nothing of those files will remain outside the trash**, stop and restore at least one intended keeper to the unchecked set. 6. Continue only when you intend to use the separate trash confirmation. **Clear** discards the current checkbox selection. **If you confirm cleanup.** The dialog says **Move N files to trash?** and **This frees X. Files go to the trash and can be restored from there.** Requests are submitted in chunks of 500. Earlier chunks can remain trashed if a later chunk fails, so verify the result rather than assuming the whole operation was atomic. **Recovery.** Selected files are soft-deleted and can be restored while trash retention permits. Their former folder context matters when deciding whether a restored file belongs back in active work. ## Expected result The shortcut leaves the creation-ordered newest copy unchecked in each scoped group and selects the older matches. You retain final control over every checkbox before any file enters trash. ## Related guides - [Review each exact-match group before selection](/files/review-duplicates) - [Restore selected copies after an incorrect cleanup](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Troubleshoot duplicate scan results
summary: Diagnose missing or stalled duplicate results using scan status, exact-match rules, file-size limits, retry counts, and current workspace visibility scope.
verification: Reviewed against apps/api/src/pages/api/duplicates.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/duplicate-hash-scan.ts, apps/api/src/lib/duplicates/plan.ts, apps/web/src/pages/duplicates.tsx, apps/cron/src/index.ts, and apps/cron/wrangler.jsonc on 2026-10-14. Production queues were not inspected.
body: Duplicate results appear only after eligible files receive content hashes. The page can therefore be empty while a scan is still working, or remain empty because the suspected files are not byte-for-byte identical. **Recognize the page state.** While candidates remain, Dosya shows **Scanning your files** and says results appear as the scan progresses. The web page polls every 15 seconds. A request failure shows **Duplicates could not be loaded** with **Retry**. Do not treat **No duplicates found** as proof by itself: duplicate scanning is opt-in for each workspace, and the current page renders the same empty message when the API reports `scan_enabled: false`. ## Steps 1. Verify the active workspace and your scope. You need membership plus `access_files`; confinement limits results to your subtree and hidden files are filtered out. 2. Confirm that duplicate scanning is enabled for the workspace. It starts disabled until someone with `change_duplicate_scan` permission enables it. If the page offers no setting, ask a workspace owner or support to inspect the `/api/duplicates?workspace_id=...` response: `scan_enabled: false` means no duplicate verdict exists yet. 3. If **Scanning your files** appears, leave the page open for at least one 15-second poll, then refresh. The scheduled worker is configured to run every two minutes, so newly queued files may not start instantly. 4. Compare the suspected files outside visual preview. A group requires equal byte size and equal content hash; similar images, exports, or documents with metadata differences are not exact matches. 5. Check size. One scan run accepts up to 100 candidates and a total byte budget of 384 MiB. A single file above 256 MiB is marked too large for this scanner. Failed candidates stop retrying after three attempts. 6. If more than 100 groups exist, the page displays only the largest 100 while its totals cover all groups. Cleaning visible groups causes lower-ranked groups to move into view. 7. Use **Retry** only for a page-load failure. Repeated browser retries do not override file caps or reset exhausted hash attempts. **Current storage limitation.** The scheduled scanner reads its supported D1-backed file rows. Workspaces whose file records or object queues live only in the Durable Object storage path are not consumed by that worker, so an empty result there may reflect the current implementation rather than unique content. **Escalation details.** Record the workspace ID, affected file IDs, byte sizes, upload times, whether **Scanning your files** persists, and the exact load error. Do not repeatedly re-upload large files merely to trigger hashing; that consumes more storage without changing the scanner’s per-file ceiling. ## Expected result Eligible byte-identical files eventually appear together, or the investigation identifies disabled scanning, scope, visibility, size, retry exhaustion, unsupported storage routing, or genuine byte differences as the reason they do not. ## Related guides - [Interpret exact-duplicate results after scanning](/files/review-duplicates) - [Recover files after duplicate troubleshooting](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Edit a text file in the browser
summary: Edit supported text files up to 2 MiB in the Dosya browser, save the full content as a new version, and recover from save failures safely online.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/text-editor.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/text-detect.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: The browser viewer can edit recognized text files no larger than 2 MiB. Saving uploads the complete editor contents as a new version of the same Dosya file; it does not autosave individual keystrokes. ## Supported files and permissions Recognition includes common plain text, source code, configuration, markup, data, subtitle, shell, and diff extensions. Extensionless names such as `README`, `LICENSE`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, and familiar dotfiles are also eligible; recognized text MIME types provide another path. The editor supplies syntax modes for TypeScript and JavaScript, Python, JSON, Markdown, CSS, HTML, SQL, YAML, Rust, and Go, with plain text as the fallback. The **Edit** control is offered when text detection succeeds, the stored size is 2 MiB or less, and the file is not fully locked. Completing **Save version** must still pass the upload gates: workspace membership, **upload files** permission, folder confinement, active destination, lock policy, file-size and extension policy, storage quota, and transfer concurrency. A view-only or otherwise restricted file can therefore reach the editor but fail when saving. ## Steps 1. Open the file from **Files** in a web browser. Confirm the header name before choosing **Edit**. 2. Wait for the full-screen CodeMirror editor to load the raw content. It uses line wrapping and a dark editor theme. 3. Make the required change. Use the editor's normal undo command if you need to reverse an unsaved keystroke. 4. Select **Save version**. The button changes to **Saving…** while Dosya creates an upload session and sends the complete text blob. 5. Wait for **Saved — File saved as new version.** The editor closes, the file list refreshes, and version history reloads. 6. Reopen the file, verify the edited passage, then use **Versions** if you must compare the prior content. ## Save behavior and recovery Closing with the **Close** button does not upload the current buffer, and this editor does not show a dedicated unsaved-changes confirmation. Copy important unsaved text elsewhere before closing or refreshing. The save request does not include an expected-version guard, so coordinate with collaborators when two people might edit the same file at once; each successful upload can become another version. **Editor unavailable — Could not open the text editor.** means the raw content or editor modules did not load. Keep the source tab open, check access and connectivity, then reopen the file. A failed initialization reports **Save failed** with the API message or **Could not start upload**. A byte-transfer failure reports the returned message or **Failed to save**. In either case, the editor stays open, so preserve the buffer and retry only after resolving the named permission, policy, quota, lock, or network problem. If a failed request abandons its upload session, its held transfer slot is reclaimed after 15 minutes. The save is not in place at the storage-object level: it registers a new version of the same file. Previous versions remain according to workspace retention and version limits and may be restored while available. Restoring later is a separate mutation; closing without saving creates no version. ## Expected result The edited content reopens under the same file identity, and version history shows a newly saved version. If saving was refused, the prior stored version remains current and the unsent editor buffer exists only in that browser tab. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Use version history](/files/version-history)

title: Manage email notifications
summary: Set the Email channel and event groups, learn which notices remain mandatory, and diagnose delivery without exposing file details or secrets.
verification: Reviewed 2026-10-14 using apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/groups.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/logic.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/notify.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/email/notification-template.ts. No live email was generated, no account setting was edited, and production services were not contacted.
body: Dosya notification email uses the signed-in account address. Delivery is decided by the event’s supported channels, its event-group preference, and the **Email** master switch. Email is best effort, so the in-app inbox remains the authoritative place to inspect current account activity and access. ## What email can send For a new account with no stored overrides, email delivery defaults on for **Security and sign-in**, **Account**, **Team and permissions**, **Billing and storage**, **File requests**, **Sync and backup**, **Support and legal**, and **System**. It defaults off for **File activity**, **Share links**, **Comments**, **Imports and transfers**, **Integrations and API**, and **Product updates**. The event catalog is still a ceiling: enabling a group cannot add email to an event that has no email version. The settings page saves one switch at a time. There is no send-test button. Explicitly changing a group stores an account override, while the **Email** row remains a separate master gate. Some security, account, billing, legal, and service messages are mandatory. Mandatory mail ignores both the group preference and the Email master switch. Its footer says it was sent regardless of notification settings and omits the unsubscribe link. Ordinary notification messages include a settings link back to Dosya when an unsubscribe destination is available. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile** and verify the account email shown there. If it is wrong, correct the account identity before testing alerts. 2. Visit **Profile > Notifications** and turn on **Email** under **Delivery channels**. 3. Enable the group for the event you need. Read any always-on note beside that group. 4. Trigger a low-risk supported event once. Avoid putting confidential filenames or personal information in a test comment or request. 5. Check the primary inbox, spam or junk, rules, quarantines, and any forwarding destination for the account address. 6. Match the subject and action to the event in Dosya. Open the web app directly when the message concerns permissions, billing, or a shared file. 7. Reload notification settings to make sure the channel and group values persisted. ## When mail does not arrive If the Email switch immediately reverts, Dosya shows **Couldn’t save** and “Your channel preference could not be saved.” Retry after restoring connectivity. If the setting persists but mail is absent, verify that the specific event supports email, its group is enabled, and mailbox filtering did not divert it. A successful in-app entry does not prove the independent email transport succeeded. Do not forward a sensitive notification as a substitute for sharing through Dosya. The current file, role, link, or billing state can change after a message is sent. ## Expected result The selected Email and event-group controls survive a reload, and a supported controlled event arrives at the account mailbox with content and an action matching the corresponding Dosya activity. Mandatory notices remain deliverable even when optional email is muted. ## Related guides - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Open the Dosya notification inbox](/account/notifications-open-inbox) - [Update profile settings](/account/profile-settings)

title: Capture the visible page with the extension
summary: Capture the visible browser viewport, identify the resumable-upload refusal above 50 MiB, and safely verify the completed PNG from Recent saves.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/Actions.tsx, apps/extension/src/lib/background/handlers.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/screenshot.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/filename.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/config.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/background.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/file.ts. Production behavior for “Capture the visible page with the extension” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A visible-page capture records exactly the browser viewport at the moment you select **Save visible screenshot**. The extension queues the PNG immediately, so arrange the page before starting the save. ## Steps 1. Close menus, cookie notices, account details, or private overlays that must not appear in the image, then scroll the page to the exact viewport you want to preserve. 2. Open **Save to dosya** and read the account email plus the **Saving to** workspace and folder. Change **Choose a folder** before capture if either destination is wrong. 3. Select **Save visible screenshot**. The popup displays **Cmd Shift S** on macOS and **Ctrl Shift S** elsewhere, but that shortcut saves selected text first; use the button when a page selection is active. 4. Let the queued row finish instead of capturing the same viewport again. The one-shot upload route refuses a PNG above 50 MiB with **Files over 50 MB use /api/upload/init and the resumable upload**; a restricted browser page reports **This page cannot be captured**. 5. Find the generated PNG under **Recent saves**. Its name follows ` YYYY-MM-DD HH.MM.png`; unsafe filename characters become hyphens and an unusable title becomes `untitled`. 6. Open the completed row and compare the stored PNG with the viewport you prepared. Browser notifications may also say **Saved to dosya**, but Safari verification happens in the popup. ## Expected result A completed PNG opens from **Recent saves** in the destination selected before capture. It contains the visible viewport only, uses the generated timestamped filename, and has one queue receipt. If the row says **Waiting for network**, leave the capture queued. Use **Retry now** on that row after a terminal failure rather than creating another capture. ## Related guides - [Save from a browser](/extension/save-from-browser) - [Choose a save folder](/extension/extension-save-folder)

title: Installing and connecting Save to dosya
summary: Install the browser extension from its official listing, approve its connection to your account, and choose where browser saves will go.
verification: Reviewed browser installation links and current extension sign-in source on 2026-10-10. Captured the actual locally loaded Chrome extension popup, current consent page and folder picker. Real isolated API PKCE authorization/exchange issued the fixture session; tokens were seeded into the extension for capture. Store installation and native browser callback handoff were not verified in production or across all browsers.
body: Install **Save to dosya** using the browser links on the [official extension page](https://dosya.dev/browser-extension/), open its toolbar popup and select **Sign in with dosya**. Approve the connection on Dosya's consent page, then check **Saving to** before your first save. ## Before you start - Have a Dosya account and access to its normal sign-in method and any two-factor authentication. - Use the official browser-specific installation link. Check the current availability and requirements there; browser-store listings can change. - Choose a regular workspace and folder where you can add files. The extension's destination list excludes Vault workspaces. - Prepare a harmless ordinary web page for your first test. Browser settings, extension stores and other protected pages may refuse capture. ## Steps: install the extension 1. **Open the official extension page.** Go to [Save to dosya](https://dosya.dev/browser-extension/) and choose Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari for the browser you are using. 2. **Follow that browser's installation prompts.** Confirm the extension's name and source before adding it. Safari installation may also require enabling the extension in Safari's Extensions settings after installing its companion app. 3. **Find the toolbar popup.** Open the browser's extensions menu and select **Save to dosya**. Pin it to the toolbar if your browser supports pinning and you want a visible shortcut. 4. **Start from the popup.** Select **Sign in with dosya**. Keep the browser's sign-in or consent window open until the connection finishes. ## Steps: approve the account connection 1. **Sign in to Dosya when asked.** Use the account that should receive your saves and complete its required factors. The extension opens Dosya's account flow rather than collecting your account password in its popup. 2. **Read the permission page.** It is headed **Connect Save to dosya for** your browser. It explains that the extension can save files into your folders, create folders and create a share link for a file it saved. 3. **Approve deliberately.** Select **Allow** to connect, or **Cancel** to leave without approving this request. The connection page also states that the extension cannot delete, rename or move files, or manage your account, team or billing. 4. **Return to the extension.** Open its popup again after the browser completes the handoff. Check the email in the header and the destination under **Saving to**. ## Steps: choose the save destination 1. **Open the destination row.** Select the folder button under **Saving to**. Before choosing a specific folder, this may show the default workspace destination. 2. **Choose the workspace if available.** The picker shows a workspace selector when there is more than one available workspace. 3. **Choose a folder.** Use **Search folders** to find a name, then select it from **Folders**. A **Recent** section appears after you have chosen destinations. 4. **Create a folder if needed.** Enter its name in **New folder here**, then select the plus button. The new folder becomes your destination. It is created under the current destination folder when you remain in that workspace, or at the workspace root after switching workspaces. 5. **Confirm the row.** The popup should now show the intended workspace and folder. Changing it affects subsequent saves; it does not move files already saved elsewhere. ## Expected result The popup shows your account email, the intended **Saving to** destination and the **Save visible screenshot** and **Save selection** controls. Use the [browser saving guide](/extension/save-from-browser) for a small test, then open its completed row to check the saved file in Dosya. ## Disconnecting later Open the Settings gear at the bottom right of the popup and choose Sign out when you want to disconnect this browser. Signing out clears its saved destination, recent-save list and pending captures from the extension. Finish or resolve pending saves first. To revoke access from Dosya, open **Profile → Sessions**, find the session named for your browser extension and revoke it. Signing out of a web tab alone is not the same as revoking the extension's separate session. ## Limitations Browser permissions and account consent are separate. Allow on the account page connects Dosya; the browser may separately ask for permission to save an image from a particular site. Grant only the site access needed for your task. The extension saves into regular storage and does not select Vault workspaces. It is not a whole-browser backup, bookmark sync tool or full-page archive exporter. The captures here show Chrome; installation and permission prompts differ in other browsers. ## Troubleshooting **The account page says This link is incomplete.** Restart sign-in from the extension popup. Do not open a bookmarked or manually copied consent URL. **The connection was cancelled or did not match the request.** Start again from Sign in with dosya and complete the newly opened window. Avoid reusing a previous callback tab. **Choose a folder does nothing on an older build.** Update the extension. The current code initializes the destination after sign-in so the picker can open before the first capture; earlier builds could leave this row without a destination. **There are no workspaces or the folder is missing.** Check the account email and access to a regular workspace. Vault workspaces are excluded. The picker can cache a folder list for up to an hour. If a new folder is missing, wait for the cache to refresh or create the needed folder through the picker. **The popup shows the wrong account.** Use Settings → Sign out at the bottom right of the popup, then start a new connection with the intended account. ## Frequently asked questions ### Is an API key required? No. The extension uses its own account-consent sign-in. API keys are used by other tools such as Zapier. ### Can it delete my files? The extension connection does not grant delete, rename or move operations. Review the actual permission page before approving. ### Can I change the folder for each project? Yes. Open Saving to and choose another destination before making the next save. ## Related guides - [Saving images, text and screenshots from your browser](/extension/save-from-browser) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Recover a missing extension destination
summary: Find an eligible extension destination by checking workspace access, hidden-folder rules and the one-hour folder cache without losing queued saves.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/state.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/FolderPicker.tsx, apps/extension/src/lib/store/prefs.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/auth/sign-in.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/api/routes.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/tree.ts. Production behavior for “Recover a missing extension destination” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A missing destination can result from the selected workspace, folder visibility, role permissions, or the extension’s one-hour folder cache. The picker has no manual refresh control. ## Steps 1. Open the destination row beneath **Saving to**, then confirm the workspace shown in the **Choose a folder** dialog. 2. If more than one eligible workspace exists, switch to the intended one. Vault workspaces are deliberately absent because the extension excludes encrypted destinations. 3. Enter the exact folder name in **Search folders**. A folder-confined member sees only the assigned folder subtree, and hidden folders are omitted from the API result. 4. Check the same account in Dosya if the folder remains absent. The role must have `access_files`, and the folder must be visible within the member’s workspace boundary. 5. Account for the one-hour local folder cache. There is no **Refresh** button; close and reopen the picker after the cache expires, or use **New folder here** when creating an appropriate destination because that action invalidates the cached tree. 6. Select the recovered row and run one harmless save. Confirm its completed **Recent saves** entry names that folder before using it for private content. ## Expected result An eligible folder appears and becomes the **Saving to** destination, or its absence is explained by Vault exclusion, role access, confinement, hiding, or the one-hour cache. Do not sign out merely to refresh the picker. Sign-out clears tokens, the destination, cached and recent folders, blocked origins, and locally queued capture rows and blobs; files already uploaded remain in Dosya. ## Related guides - [Reconnect the browser extension](/extension/extension-reconnect) - [Review extension permissions](/extension/extension-permissions)

Choose the extension destination and save the screenshot, selection, or webpage image once; do not look for a pre-save title field because none exists. 2. Note the generated name in **Recent saves**. Screenshots include page title and local date-time, selections use the page title with `.txt`, and images prefer the source filename. 3. title: Resolve a denied page permission
summary: Distinguish an unsupported page from blocked image hosts, review every origin in the permission banner, and safely retry the matching failed rows.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/lib/permissions.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/capture.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/page.content.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/PermissionBanner.tsx, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/background.ts, apps/extension/wxt.config.ts. Production behavior for “Resolve a denied page permission” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Page capture failure and blocked image access are different conditions. Only the blocked HTTP or HTTPS image flow offers an origin permission request. ## Steps 1. Read the failed row or notification. **This page cannot be captured** means the current browser or internal page cannot supply content to the extension. 2. For that restricted-page message, move to an ordinary HTTP or HTTPS page if appropriate. Changing general site-access settings does not make browser-owned pages capturable. 3. When a right-click image save is blocked, reopen the popup and find **A site blocked saving an image. Allow dosya to read images from ``?** The banner can name several stored hosts separated by commas. 4.
