Confirm every host displayed belongs to an image you intended to save. **Allow** requests all origins currently named in the banner as one browser permission operation; **Not now** dismisses that complete stored list and leaves its rows failed. 5. After permission is granted, let the extension retry blocked rows whose image origins match that approved list. Do not reload the page or grant all-sites access manually unless the browser explicitly requires recovery. 6. Open the resulting completed row and verify the expected image. A `data:`, `blob:`, or extension URL cannot receive this HTTP-origin permission prompt. ## Expected result The displayed HTTP(S) origin list is requested only after the user selects **Allow**, and matching rows can retry. An unsupported browser page remains identified by **This page cannot be captured**. The installed extension already has `activeTab`, scripting, and Dosya API/app host access. Optional all-sites access is not requested during installation. ## Related guides - [Reconnect the browser extension](/extension/extension-reconnect) - [Review extension permissions](/extension/extension-permissions)

title: Understand Save to dosya browser permissions
summary: Review the extension's account access, built-in browser permissions, and per-site image prompt before deciding what access to allow.
verification: Verified against apps/extension/wxt.config.ts, src/lib/manifest-hooks.ts, permissions.ts, popup/components/PermissionBanner.tsx and apps/web/src/pages/connect/extension.tsx: install permissions, optional per-origin access and consent boundaries. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Save to dosya uses three distinct kinds of access: browser capabilities needed by the extension, account consent granted on Dosya, and optional access to an image host when that site blocks a save. Review them separately because one approval does not silently grant the other two. ## Browser capabilities in the released extension The manifest requests these capabilities for specific product functions: | Browser permission | Why Save to dosya uses it | | --- | --- | | **activeTab** and **scripting** | Read a selected passage or capture the visible area after you invoke the extension on the active tab. | | **contextMenus** | Add commands for saving an image, selected text or the visible screenshot. | | **storage** and **unlimitedStorage** | Keep authorization, destination preferences, captured bytes and the retry queue in the browser. | | **identity** | Complete the protected Dosya authorization handoff where the browser supports that API. | | **notifications** | Report completed saves and failures on platforms that expose extension notifications. | | **alarms** | Check queued uploads every minute and perform hourly cleanup work. | | **offscreen** | Let Chromium uploads continue away from the popup; Firefox uploads directly in the background, and Safari uses its supported fallback. | The required network origins are `https://api.dosya.dev/*` and `https://app.dosya.dev/*`. The store package removes blanket website access from install-time host permissions. Access to other `http` or `https` origins is optional and requested only for the affected host when an image cannot otherwise be fetched. Firefox builds require Firefox 140 or later. Firefox's store disclosure identifies authentication information and website content because the extension keeps its session token and uploads only the page content you choose to save. ## What account consent permits Selecting **Sign in with dosya** opens an account page titled **Connect Save to dosya for [browser]**. Its **Allow** button issues a browser-extension session that can: - save files into folders you can access; - create folders when your workspace role permits that action; - create a share link for a file the extension saved. That scoped connection cannot delete, rename or move files. It also cannot change account settings, manage team membership or control billing. Revoke the browser session later from **Profile → Sessions** if the installation should no longer connect. ## When a site-specific prompt appears Saving selected text and taking a visible screenshot rely on the active-tab grant created by your click or shortcut. They do not need standing access to every website. An image can be hosted on a different origin from the page displaying it. If both the background request and the current-page fallback are blocked, the failed row is retained and the popup shows: > A site blocked saving an image. Allow dosya to read images from [host]? Choose **Allow** to request that host pattern and automatically retry matching blocked rows. Choose **Not now** to dismiss the stored request; the failed capture remains available for a deliberate retry. Granting one host does not authorize unrelated domains. ## Steps: review current access 1. Open the browser's extension-management page and select **Save to dosya**. 2. Inspect its permissions or site-access section. Browser wording differs, but every manually granted website should correspond to an image host you recognize. 3. Compare the two required Dosya service origins with any optional website origins. 4. Open **Profile → Sessions** in Dosya and confirm that the extension session belongs to this browser installation. Remove an optional site's access when it is no longer needed. A later image from that host may fail again and present a fresh **Allow** choice. Removing the two Dosya service origins prevents sign-in and uploads; reconnecting cannot work until the browser grants them again. ## Expected result The browser retains access to Dosya's app and API origins, and any other granted origin has a known image-saving purpose. The account session remains limited to saving, folder creation and single-file sharing. ## Troubleshooting permission failures **The popup says dosya needs permission to reach api.dosya.dev to save files.** Accept the browser prompt for both official Dosya origins, then press **Sign in with dosya** again. **A capture reports This page cannot be captured.** Use an ordinary website tab. Browser settings, extension-store pages, internal URLs and some protected documents do not allow injected extension scripts or visible-tab capture. **The image banner returns after Allow.** Confirm that the named host is still serving the image and that the browser recorded its site permission. A page can load an image from another CDN host, so a changed source may require a separate decision. **A file reaches Dosya but folder creation fails.** Browser access is working; the workspace role lacks **Create folders**. Ask an administrator to create the folder or adjust the role. ## Related guides - [Installing and connecting Save to dosya](/extension/install-and-connect) - [Resolving a denied page permission](/extension/extension-page-permission-denied) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Fix an extension popup that will not open
summary: Restore the Save to dosya popup with browser-specific enablement checks while protecting local captures that have not finished uploading safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against src/lib/extension-stores.ts, apps/extension/README.md, apps/extension/wxt.config.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/App.tsx, apps/extension/src/lib/auth/sign-in.ts. Production behavior for “Fix an extension popup that will not open” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A popup that never renders cannot show a Dosya diagnostic. Check the installed browser target and profile first, and protect unfinished local captures before resetting the extension. ## Steps 1. Confirm that the active browser profile contains **Save to dosya** version 0.1.3 from its published Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari listing. 2. In Chrome, open the toolbar extensions menu, enable the extension, and pin it; in Edge, enable it under Extensions and pin the toolbar icon. 3. In Firefox, use version 140 or later, enable the add-on, and pin it. Chrome and Edge have no locally declared minimum version. 4. On Safari, use macOS 13 or later, open the installed containing app once, then enable **Save to dosya** under Safari Settings → Extensions. 5. Return to an ordinary tab and select the toolbar icon. A working target opens the configured 360 × 560 popup with **Save to dosya** at the top. 6. If it still does not render, record browser/version/profile details before disabling or reinstalling. Avoid a reset while the badge or prior popup indicated unfinished saves. ## Expected result The toolbar action opens the popup in the intended profile. Browser-level enablement or platform requirements explain failures without inventing an in-popup error that could not render. Signing out clears locally queued rows and captured blobs. Already completed Dosya files remain available in the web app. ## Related guides - [Reconnect the browser extension](/extension/extension-reconnect) - [Review extension permissions](/extension/extension-permissions)

title: Reconnect Save to dosya after the extension signs out
summary: Start a fresh browser authorization, approve the Dosya consent page, and confirm the account and save folder before capturing again.
verification: Verified against apps/extension/src/lib/auth/sign-in.ts, auth/refresh.ts, popup/components/SignedOut.tsx and apps/web/src/pages/connect/extension.tsx: fresh PKCE handoff, five-minute pending window, consent labels, scoped access and post-return identity checks. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: The extension keeps a separate Dosya session from the website. Reconnect when the popup returns to its signed-out screen or a supported browser notification says **Signed out of dosya** and **Sign in again from the popup**. ## Before reconnecting - Finish signing in to the Dosya account that should receive browser captures, including any passkey or two-factor step. - Open the extension in the browser profile where it was installed. A different profile has separate extension storage and sessions. - Leave any failed item alone until the account connection is restored; otherwise a retry will end as **Signed out**. ## Steps: reconnect the account 1. Open **Save to dosya** from the browser toolbar and select **Sign in with dosya**. 2. If the browser asks whether the extension may reach `api.dosya.dev` and `app.dosya.dev`, approve those two Dosya origins. Refusing this prompt leaves the popup signed out and shows **dosya needs permission to reach api.dosya.dev to save files**. 3. Complete the regular Dosya sign-in in the opened window or tab. The extension receives the approved result; it never receives the password entered on the account page. 4. On **Connect Save to dosya for [browser]**, review the access list and select **Allow**. The connection can save files, create folders and create a share link for a file it saved. It cannot delete, rename or move content, change the account, or administer the team or billing. 5. Return to the popup. Safari's tab handoff first displays **Save to dosya is connected** and **You can close this tab**; close that tab, then reopen the toolbar popup. ## Confirm the restored session Check the email in the popup header, then read the complete **Saving to** workspace and folder. An expired token normally leaves the previous destination preference in this browser, but that folder may have been renamed, removed or become inaccessible while the session was disconnected. Make one harmless visible screenshot and watch its row under **Recent saves**. A green check means the cloud upload completed; selecting that finished row opens the file in Dosya. Failed items retain **Retry now**, so retry them only after the new account and destination are correct. ## Expected result The toolbar popup shows the intended email, an accessible **Saving to** location and active capture controls. A small test reaches that folder once and opens from its completed Recent saves row. ## If reconnection does not finish **The popup still shows the sign-in page.** Start from its current **Sign in with dosya** button rather than an old consent bookmark or callback tab. A pending attempt is considered current for five minutes; after abandoning one, wait for that window to pass and begin again from the popup. **The consent page says This link is incomplete.** Close it. The required state and callback values come from the extension, so a copied address cannot be repaired manually. **The page reports Too many requests.** Authorization permits 10 attempts in 15 minutes for one web session. Stop repeating the button and try after that window has cleared. **The wrong account appears after returning.** Open the popup's **Settings** menu and choose **Sign out**, then authorize the intended account. Explicit sign-out clears the destination, recent folders, pending captures and cached folder data from that extension installation, so resolve useful pending work first. **A revoked session keeps returning to signed out.** In the web app, check **Profile → Sessions** for the browser-extension session. Start a new authorization after confirming the old session was revoked deliberately. ## Related guides - [Installing and connecting Save to dosya](/extension/install-and-connect) - [Choosing the browser extension destination](/extension/extension-save-folder) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Verify an extension save when confirmation is missing
summary: Use Recent saves when a notification is absent, read the exact queue state, and retry the existing save row without creating another capture.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/RecentSaves.tsx, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/state.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/upload/one-shot.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/queue/runner.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/background/handlers.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/background.ts. Production behavior for “Verify an extension save when confirmation is missing” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A missing system notification is not a failed save. Safari has no extension notification API, and other browsers can suppress notifications while the upload receipt remains in **Recent saves**. ## Steps 1. Open the popup and locate the generated filename under **Recent saves** rather than searching for a user-entered name; the extension does not provide pre-save naming. 2. Wait through an active **Waiting for network**, **Rate limited**, or **Finishing an earlier attempt** state. The popup refreshes queue state about every two seconds. 3. If the row shows **Signed out**, sign in again and return to that row. If it says **Capture is gone**, its stored bytes are no longer available and it cannot finish. 4. For a retryable upload failure, select **Retry now** once so that queue item keeps its idempotency identity. A blocked-image permission retry recaptures the source and replaces its failed row; repeating the page action yourself always creates a separate item. 5. When the row gains a completed check, open its body. It links directly to `app.dosya.dev/files?view=`. 6. Confirm the exact file and destination in Dosya. Treat the popup row as authoritative when no **Saved to dosya** operating-system notification appeared. ## Expected result The original queue row either opens one completed file or presents a specific terminal reason. A suppressed notification, especially on Safari, no longer causes an unnecessary second capture. The popup shows only the ten most recent local rows. Older receipts can still exist in Dosya even when they have left that shortened view. ## Related guides - [Reconnect the browser extension](/extension/extension-reconnect) - [Review extension permissions](/extension/extension-permissions)

title: Choose where the browser extension saves files
summary: Pick an accessible workspace and folder, understand when a new folder is nested, and test the destination before capturing private content.
verification: Verified against apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/FolderPicker.tsx, DestinationRow.tsx, state.ts, lib/store/prefs.ts and lib/background/handlers.ts: picker labels, five recents, one-hour cache, creation parent and per-capture destination binding. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: The **Saving to** row decides where each new browser capture is uploaded. Select the destination before capturing: changing it later does not move a queued or completed file. ## What appears in the picker The extension lists regular workspaces available to the connected account; Vault workspaces are excluded. When more than one regular workspace is available, the picker adds a workspace selector. A first-time connection defaults to the first available workspace at its root until you choose a folder. Under **Recent**, the picker keeps as many as five previously chosen destinations, most recent first. **Folders** contains the current workspace tree, while **Search folders** matches a folder name without regard to letter case. Folder results may be cached for one hour, so a folder created elsewhere can take time to appear. ## Steps: select an existing destination 1. Open the **Save to dosya** toolbar popup and verify the account email. 2. Select the folder button next to **Saving to**. 3. Choose the intended workspace when the workspace selector is present. 4. Enter part of the name in **Search folders**, or browse the list below **Folders**. 5. Select the exact folder. The picker closes and the destination row changes to `Workspace / Folder`. 6. Capture a harmless sample, wait for its green check under **Recent saves**, and select the finished row to open the stored file. ## Create a folder from the extension Enter a name in **New folder here**, then select the plus button. The account's workspace role must include folder creation. Placement depends on the workspace choice: - While staying in the same workspace as the current destination, the new folder is created inside that destination folder. - After switching to another workspace, the new folder is created at that workspace's root. The new folder becomes **Saving to** immediately, and its workspace cache is cleared so the refreshed list can include it. Creating the folder does not relocate earlier captures. ## Destination rules for queued work The extension records the workspace and folder at capture time. If you switch destinations while an upload is waiting, that existing row continues toward its original folder; only later captures use the replacement. Completed items show their folder name beneath the filename. Up to 10 recent rows appear in the popup, so use **Open dosya** when you need the full file list rather than relying on this short activity view. ## Expected result The destination breadcrumb names the chosen workspace and folder. A new sample capture finishes in that exact location, while any item captured before the change continues toward its earlier recorded folder. ## Fix a missing or unusable folder **A recently created folder is absent.** If it was made through the picker, close and reopen the picker after the create completes. For a folder made in another client, the extension's cached tree can remain current for up to one hour. **The plus button does not create the folder.** Confirm that your role permits folder creation. The server refusal for a role without that capability is **You don't have permission to create folders**; an owner or admin can grant it or create the destination for you. **The test row says You don't have upload permission in this workspace.** Folder visibility alone does not grant file uploads. Ask a workspace administrator for upload permission or select a workspace where your role already has it. **The upload reports Destination folder not found.** The selected folder was deleted, hidden from your role or otherwise became unavailable. Return to **Saving to**, pick a live folder, and make a new capture. Retrying the old row still targets its recorded destination. **The list is empty after connecting.** Check the account email and confirm that the account belongs to a regular workspace. A Vault-only account has no eligible extension destination. ## Related guides - [Saving images, text and screenshots from your browser](/extension/save-from-browser) - [Recovering a missing extension destination](/extension/extension-destination-missing) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders)

title: Save a specific webpage image to Dosya
summary: Choose the destination first, use Save image to dosya on the webpage, resolve an origin permission only if asked, and verify the completed image.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/lib/background/menus.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/capture.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/page.content.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/filename.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/config.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/PermissionBanner.tsx. Production behavior for “Save a specific webpage image to Dosya” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A webpage image is saved from its right-click menu, using the destination already stored in the popup. The extension does not show an image preview or destination chooser during that menu action. ## Steps 1. Open **Save to dosya** and set the intended value under **Saving to** before returning to the webpage. 2. Right-click the exact image and choose **Save image to dosya**. The browser immediately asks the background process to fetch and queue that source. 3. If direct fetching is blocked, reopen the popup and inspect every comma-separated host in **A site blocked saving an image**. **Allow** requests all HTTP(S) origins currently named in that banner together, so dismiss it with **Not now** if any listed host is unexpected. 4. Let the existing row upload. An image above the 50 MiB queue limit stops with **Larger than 50 MB**; **Not now** leaves a blocked row failed. 5. Read the generated filename. Dosya prefers a usable final segment from the image URL, otherwise it combines the page title with an extension inferred from content type. 6. Open the completed **Recent saves** row and compare dimensions and visible image content with the source you selected. ## Expected result One image file opens from the completed row in the destination selected beforehand. Any optional permission covered only the reviewed host list from the banner rather than all sites at installation. If the saved asset differs from the visual page element, the site may serve a responsive or protected source. Compare the actual completed file before deleting or recapturing anything. ## Related guides - [Save from a browser](/extension/save-from-browser) - [Choose a save folder](/extension/extension-save-folder)

title: Save a visible-page screenshot to Dosya
summary: Capture the active tab's visible area as a timestamped PNG, follow its upload in Recent saves, and verify the finished cloud file.
verification: Verified against apps/extension/src/lib/capture/capture.ts, capture/filename.ts, lib/background/handlers.ts, lib/queue/runner.ts and popup/components/RecentSaves.tsx: visible-tab PNG capture, filename, 50 MiB limit, two-upload queue and completion states. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: **Save visible screenshot** captures the currently displayed area of the active browser tab and uploads it as a PNG. The action starts immediately; there is no crop or preview step inside the extension, so arrange the page before selecting it. ## Prepare the page 1. Open the ordinary website tab whose visible area you need. Internal browser pages, add-on stores and some protected documents can refuse capture. 2. Scroll until the required section is on screen. A long page needs separate captures for sections outside the current viewport. 3. Close menus, cookie prompts, account popovers or notifications you do not want recorded. The PNG includes private information visible at that moment. 4. Open **Save to dosya** and inspect the workspace/folder beside **Saving to**. A destination change applies to this new capture after you select it. ## Steps: capture and upload the viewport 1. Select **Save visible screenshot**. On macOS you can instead use **Command + Shift + S**; other systems use **Ctrl + Shift + S**. 2. If text is selected on the page, the keyboard shortcut saves that selection as a text file. Clear the selection or use the screenshot button when the required output is an image. 3. Open the popup's **Recent saves** section. The captured bytes and queue record are stored in the browser before the cloud transfer begins, so closing the popup does not cancel the upload. 4. Wait for a green check. The extension can run two uploads at once, checks due queued work every minute, and automatically backs off temporary network failures from two seconds up to five minutes. 5. Select the completed row to open the file in Dosya, then inspect the image before sharing it. ## Identify the resulting file The filename uses the page title followed by the local capture date and time, for example `Studio 2026-10-07 09.05.png`. Characters that filesystems reject are replaced, and a title stem is limited to 200 characters. A title with no usable letters or numbers becomes `untitled`. The completed Recent saves row displays the filename, destination and a green check. Its filename link opens `app.dosya.dev` with that file selected; **Open dosya** above the list opens the general file area instead. Each extension capture is capped at 50 MiB (52,428,800 bytes), while the interface describes the ceiling as 50 MB. A workspace can also impose a lower per-file limit, file-type policy, storage allowance or member quota. The stored `.png` name must be allowed by that workspace. ## Expected result Recent saves contains one timestamped PNG with the selected folder name and a green completion check. Opening its row shows the same visible page area that was on screen when capture began. ## Correct a failed screenshot **This page cannot be captured.** Switch to a normal web page and trigger the action again. The browser does not expose protected tabs to extensions. **The image omits content below the fold.** The command records one visible viewport rather than scrolling the document. Move to the missing section and create another PNG. **The row says Waiting for network or Upload interrupted.** Keep the browser running so automatic retries can proceed, or select **Retry now** after connectivity returns. Restart recovery puts an interrupted upload back into the queue without intentionally creating a second capture. **The item reports Rate limited.** Leave the existing row in place. It uses the server's retry delay, defaulting to 30 seconds when no delay is supplied. **Recent saves shows Signed out.** Reconnect the extension, confirm its email and destination, then use **Retry now** on that retained capture. **The server refuses the file.** Read the row's exact message. Storage quota, workspace upload permission, destination availability, `.png` policy and workspace size limits are separate gates; correct the named rule before retrying. **The screenshot contains private data.** Delete the saved file in Dosya and retake it after removing the sensitive overlay. Screenshot capture cannot redact content after the PNG is produced. ## Related guides - [Saving images, text and screenshots from your browser](/extension/save-from-browser) - [Choosing the browser extension destination](/extension/extension-save-folder) - [Verifying a save when confirmation is missing](/extension/extension-save-confirmation-missing)

title: Save selected text from a webpage
summary: Save selected webpage text as a generated text file with title and source context, then verify the one-million-character-limited result in Dosya.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/Actions.tsx, apps/extension/src/lib/background/menus.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/selection.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/filename.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/config.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/background/handlers.ts. Production behavior for “Save selected text from a webpage” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Selection capture stores plain text plus its page title and source URL. It does not preserve HTML, images, colors, or the page’s visual formatting. ## Steps 1. Highlight the exact non-sensitive webpage text to preserve. A whitespace-only selection cannot be saved. 2. Open **Save to dosya**, confirm **Saving to**, and choose **Save selection**; its helper reads **Select text on the page first**. 3. Alternatively, right-click the highlighted text and choose **Save selection to dosya**. The global shortcut also saves the selection when it is nonempty. 4. If the extension responds **Select some text first**, select visible text again on a supported page and retry once. 5. Wait for the generated `.txt` row to complete. Selection content is truncated at 1,000,000 characters. 6. Open the file and verify the exact format: `Title: `, `Source: `, one blank line, then the captured text. ## Expected result Dosya contains one `.txt` file in the chosen destination with the page title, page URL, and selected text. Its content remains plain text and respects the one-million-character cap. If the global shortcut finds no selection, it captures a visible screenshot instead. Use the named **Save selection** action when the intended output must be unambiguous. ## Related guides - [Connect the extension](/extension/install-and-connect) - [Save from the browser](/extension/save-from-browser)

title: Saving images, text and screenshots from your browser
summary: Use Save to dosya to capture selected text, an image or the visible page area, then check progress and open the completed file.
verification: Verified a real text selection and visible screenshot through the current locally loaded Chrome extension and isolated API/R2 on 2026-10-10. The stored text contained the selected sample; screenshot PNG signature and byte length matched the completed queue item. A temporary capture build changed service origins and granted local test-page host access. Image context-menu capture, browser permission prompts and other browsers were source reviewed, not manually verified in production.
body: Open **Save to dosya**, check **Saving to**, then choose **Save selection** for highlighted text or **Save visible screenshot** for the current visible page area. To save an image, right-click it and select **Save image to dosya**. Check **Recent saves** before assuming the transfer finished. ## Before you start - [Install and connect the extension](/extension/install-and-connect). Check the account email and the workspace/folder under Saving to. - Open an ordinary web page you are allowed to save from. Browser settings, store pages and some embedded or protected content cannot be captured. - Keep a network connection available to complete the upload. A queued item is not yet a completed cloud copy. - Use a harmless page for the first test. The visible screenshot includes everything currently visible in the page area, including any private text displayed there. ## Steps: save selected text 1. **Highlight the text on the page.** Select the passage you want before opening the extension. 2. **Check the destination.** Open Save to dosya and check Saving to. Select that row if you need another workspace or folder. 3. **Save the selection.** Select **Save selection**. You can also right-click selected text and use **Save selection to dosya**. 4. **Follow the result.** Check Recent saves for a text-file row. The filename comes from the page title and ends in .txt. 5. **Open the completed file.** When its green check appears, select the row. The text file contains the page title, source URL and the selected plain text. Selected text is saved as text, without the page's layout, images or rich formatting. If you need the visual arrangement, use a screenshot of the relevant area instead. ## Steps: save a visible screenshot 1. **Show the area you need.** Scroll the page to the relevant section and close menus or overlays you do not want in the capture. 2. **Open the popup.** Check Saving to once more, then select **Save visible screenshot**. 3. **Check Recent saves.** Wait for the completed PNG row. Its filename includes the page title and a timestamp. 4. **Open and check the image.** Select the completed row to open it in Dosya. Confirm that the relevant section is visible and readable. This captures the visible viewport of the active tab. It does not scroll through the page, capture the whole page or save an offline HTML copy. For a long page, scroll to another section and make a separate capture. ## Steps: save an image 1. **Find the image on its page.** Right-click the image itself, rather than an empty area of the page. 2. **Choose the extension command.** Select **Save image to dosya** from the context menu. Some browsers group extension commands under the extension's name. 3. **Review any site-permission request.** A blocked image may require access to the image's source site. Open the extension and use its permission banner when offered, then retry. If the site continues to block saving, the extension cannot override that restriction. 4. **Check the completed row.** Open the popup, confirm the file in Recent saves, then open it in Dosya. The destination chosen in Saving to also applies to this image command. Images are saved as separate files, rather than as a bookmark to the page. ## Keyboard shortcut Use **Command + Shift + S** on macOS or **Ctrl + Shift + S** on other systems. The shortcut saves selected text when there is a selection; otherwise it captures the visible screenshot. Clear a selection if you intended to capture the page area instead. If another tool or the browser owns that shortcut, review the browser's extension shortcut settings or use the popup buttons. Changing your shortcut does not change the save destination. ## Expected result Recent saves shows the filename and destination with a green check for a completed item. Select its row to **Open in dosya**, or use **Open dosya** above the list and navigate to the same folder. Confirm the actual saved text or image before closing your source page. The list contains recent extension activity rather than a full inventory of your storage. An animation or notification can accompany a save, but the completed file is the useful confirmation. ## Sharing a completed save The link icon beside a completed row opens a sharing dialog. Review its expiry and generate the link deliberately; this creates a recipient-accessible share link rather than just copying the signed-in file-view address. Follow the [sharing guide](/sharing/create-link) for access and expiry decisions. ## Limitations The extension limits an individual capture to 50 MiB; its message labels this as 50 MB. Text selection is capped at one million characters. A larger selection is truncated, so choose a smaller passage when completeness matters. Ordinary web pages generally work, but protected browser pages and some cross-origin images may not. The extension is for images, selected text and visible screenshots; it does not export a full web page as HTML or PDF. Saves go to regular storage, separately from Vault. ## Troubleshooting **Select some text first.** Highlight a passage on the active page, then try Save selection again. Opening the popup without a selection does not create one. **This page cannot be captured.** Try an ordinary web page. Browser settings, extension stores and other protected pages can refuse access. **A save is waiting or failed.** Check the message in Recent saves, network access, account sign-in, destination permissions and storage. Use **Retry now** beside the affected row after correcting the cause. Some temporary failures retry automatically. **An image is blocked.** Review the permission banner for its source site and retry after granting the needed access. If the original image URL no longer works, return to its page and try a fresh capture. **The file is in the wrong folder.** Check Saving to. Changing it affects new captures; it does not move already captured or queued items to the new destination. Move the finished file in Dosya if needed. **The screenshot misses part of the page.** Scroll until that part is visible and capture again. Save visible screenshot covers one viewport. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does the shortcut always take a screenshot? No. It saves selected text if a selection exists; otherwise it takes a visible screenshot. ### Does text saving preserve formatting? It creates a plain-text file with the page title, source URL and selected text. ### Is a queued capture already stored in the cloud? Wait for the completed row and confirm its file. A queued capture still needs a successful upload. ## Related guides - [Installing and connecting Save to dosya](/extension/install-and-connect) - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders)

title: Fix an expired Save to Dosya browser session
summary: Sign in again when token refresh fails, restore the intended destination, and retry the existing Signed out row without discarding local captures.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/lib/api/client.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/auth/refresh.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/auth/sign-in.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/store/prefs.ts, apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/SignedOut.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/connect/extension.tsx. Production behavior for “Fix an expired Save to Dosya browser session” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The extension retries one request after refreshing an expired access token. When refresh itself is rejected, stored tokens are cleared and the popup returns to **Sign in with dosya**. ## Steps 1. Open the popup and distinguish the signed-out screen or a row marked **Signed out** from temporary states such as **Waiting for network**. 2. Select **Sign in with dosya**. The browser opens the normal Dosya authentication flow; passwords, passkeys, and two-factor checks stay on the Dosya page. 3. On **Connect Save to dosya for ``**, review the listed save, folder-creation, and single-file share abilities, then select **Allow**. 4. Return to the popup and confirm the account email plus **Saving to** destination. The extension cannot delete, rename, or move files or manage account, team, or billing settings. 5. Find the original failed row and select **Retry now**. A prior **Signed out** failure does not resume automatically merely because authentication succeeded. 6. Open the completed row and confirm it points to one file in the intended destination before clearing any other local state. ## Expected result The popup shows the intended account and destination, and the original failed row completes after **Retry now**. No invented session-expiry duration or nonexistent **Reconnect** control is required. Avoid explicit sign-out as a diagnostic reset: it clears tokens, destination settings, caches, pending sign-in data, queued rows, and captured blobs. Uploaded files remain in Dosya. ## Related guides - [Reconnect the browser extension](/extension/extension-reconnect) - [Review extension permissions](/extension/extension-permissions)

title: Verify an extension save in Dosya
summary: Open the completed Recent saves row by its exact file ID, then verify the generated name, destination, file type and captured content in Dosya.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/extension/src/entrypoints/popup/components/RecentSaves.tsx, apps/extension/src/lib/background/handlers.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/store/items.ts, apps/extension/src/lib/capture/selection.ts. Production behavior for “Verify an extension save in Dosya” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The completed **Recent saves** row is the strongest extension receipt because it opens the exact Dosya file ID returned by upload. ## Steps 1. Open the popup and find the target filename under **Recent saves**. A completed row carries a green check rather than a retry message. 2. Read its folder label and relative save time, then select the row body. Dosya opens `app.dosya.dev/files?view=` for that exact result. 3. Confirm the destination and generated filename. Screenshots end in `.png`, selections end in `.txt`, and webpage images use their source or inferred type. 4. For a screenshot, compare the saved pixels with the visible viewport captured at that time; the PNG does not contain a separate source-URL record. 5. For a selection, verify `Title:`, `Source:`, the blank separator, and the chosen text. For an image, compare the actual stored dimensions and content. 6. Keep the file if all checks agree. Use **Copy link** only after verification because creating or copying a share link does not validate the stored bytes. ## Expected result The completed row opens one file whose name, type, folder, and contents match the capture method. The exact file-ID link serves as the upload receipt. Only the ten newest rows appear in the popup. Local item records remain for 30 days, while blob data attached to failed rows is removed after seven days. ## Related guides - [Save from a browser](/extension/save-from-browser) - [Choose a save folder](/extension/extension-save-folder)

title: Troubleshooting a failed upload
summary: Read a failed upload’s message, retry while the original file is available, or use Resume after a reload and verify the completed copy.
verification: Verified the current Chrome web app against isolated API/D1/R2 on 2026-10-11. Deliberately interrupted a real upload PUT to produce Network error, restored the connection and retried; reloaded during another held PUT, rejected a mismatched file, then used Resume with the original. Both downloaded 49-byte samples matched their originals. Real local screenshots show the queue, dock Resume and completed transfers. Multipart recovery, every browser, workspace refusal and production behavior were source reviewed rather than manually exercised.
body: Read the failed item's message in **Uploads → Upload queue**. Fix the stated cause, then select **Retry** while the current tab still holds the original file. If an upload was interrupted by a reload, use **Resume** in the small upload list at the bottom right and reselect the original file. Confirm the completed destination copy before removing your original. ## Before you start - Keep the original file available on your device. A queued item or a progress bar does not establish that a cloud copy completed. - Note the exact error, approximate time, filename and intended workspace/folder. Read the complete message by hovering over a truncated queue error when needed. - Check the selected workspace and **Upload options → Folder**. An existing queue item keeps its original destination; changing the folder affects new uploads. - These steps cover ordinary signed-in uploads. Anonymous [file requests](/sharing/file-request) have their own expiry, file-type, size and count rules. - Keep the tab open and the computer awake for a retry test. Do not close the page merely to refresh a stalled progress display; that can require source-file selection again. ## Steps: diagnose a failed or stuck upload 1. **Open Uploads in the sidebar.** Find the affected row in **Upload queue**. An error row names its cause and shows **Retry**. The small upload list at the bottom right also contains progress and actions; expand it with its arrow if needed. 2. **Distinguish Queued, Error and Interrupted.** Queued can mean another upload is using the available transfer slots. An active transfer shows bytes or a percentage. Error needs its stated cause corrected. Interrupted in the bottom-right list means this tab needs the source file again. 3. **Check the connection and account.** Restore connectivity and complete sign-in if the app requires it. If all small test uploads fail, also check [service status](https://status.dosya.dev). One failed item alone does not establish a service outage. 4. **Check the refusal before retrying.** For a permission or folder error, ask the workspace owner to confirm your upload permission and the destination. For storage, size or file-type restrictions, correct the stated limit first. Retry cannot change a role or storage allowance. 5. **Avoid duplicate attempts.** Keep the original failed row until you understand its destination and result. Do not add the same large file repeatedly while another attempt might still be transferring. ## Steps: retry in the current tab 1. **Resolve the cause.** For a network interruption, reconnect first. For a workspace refusal, resolve the permission or policy issue before another attempt. 2. **Select the row’s Retry.** Use **Retry** beside the failed filename in Upload queue, or the circular-arrow Retry action in the bottom-right list. 3. **Use Retry all failed only when appropriate.** This retries the failed items whose source files remain available in this tab. For failed rows retained after a reload, the batch action changes them to **Interrupted** so you can use Resume and reselect their originals. 4. **Wait for Done.** Check the intended destination with **View file** or **Go to location** from the completed queue row. Open your own completed copy and confirm it is the expected version. If the individual Retry button is disabled, this tab no longer holds the source file. Its tooltip explains that you need to add the file again. You can also use **Retry all failed** to put retained error rows into the dock's Interrupted state, then follow Resume below. A right-click Retry label alone is not proof that the source is still available. ## Steps: resume after a reload 1. **Find Interrupted in the bottom-right upload list.** A reload preserves recent queue entries, but not the browser's in-memory File objects. The Upload queue page may show a neutral row; the bottom-right list offers the explicit **Resume** action. 2. **Select Resume.** In the operating system's file picker, choose the original file from your device. 3. **Check a mismatch before continuing.** The selected file must have the same filename and size as the queued entry. If it differs, the app says **That file does not match (name or size differs).** Reselect the correct original; do not rename an unrelated file to make it pass. 4. **Let the upload finish.** A small, single-request upload restarts its transfer. A multipart upload with a valid saved session can reuse server-recorded parts. Resume is not a guarantee that every interrupted session remains valid. 5. **Check the completed copy.** Find **Done**, then use View file or Go to location. For important work, compare your own destination copy with the original before removing the source. ## Expected result A retryable upload completes after its cause is corrected, or provides a more specific error to diagnose. An interrupted upload can continue after you reselect its original, subject to the session and destination still being valid. The completed file appears in the correct workspace and folder. Completion must include checking the actual destination. A 100% progress value, a queued entry or a dismissed error does not establish that the right file and version are available there. ## Limits and actions to use carefully - **Resume checks name and size, not identity.** A different file with the same name and size can pass that check. Choose the actual original, and avoid a file that was edited during recovery. - Recent queue entries are stored in this browser. Browser storage may be unavailable or cleared, and only the most recent entries are retained. Signing out clears upload state. A different browser cannot resume from this browser's list. - **Clear done** on the queue and **Clear** in the dock also dismiss failed or cancelled entries. They do not repair the cause or establish success. Keep the message until you have recorded what you need. - **Cancel** ends that transfer. It is different from a recoverable Interrupted entry; start a new upload if you deliberately cancelled and still need the file. - A saved multipart session can expire or be refused later. Do not promise recovery after the source changes, permissions are removed or the destination disappears. - An ordinary upload is separate from Vault's client-side encryption workflow. These queue-recovery controls do not convert a file into Vault content. ## Troubleshooting **Retry returns the same error.** The cause may still apply. Recheck the message, workspace, folder, role and applicable storage/file policy. Repeated clicks do not remove a refusal. **The progress seems stuck.** Check bytes, connection and the active transfer slots. A queued item can be waiting for another upload. Keep the tab open; use a small harmless test file in the same destination once you have resolved any restriction. **Resume is missing.** Expand the bottom-right list. If the old row is Error after a reload, use Retry all failed to make source selection available. If the item was cleared, cancelled or belongs to a previous signed-in account, add the original through Uploads after checking for a completed destination copy. **The file matches its name and size but its contents changed.** Do not treat the name/size check as proof. Use an unmodified original where available. If you cannot identify it, preserve the available versions and get private help before relying on partial recovery. **A file request refuses the same file.** Check the request's stated rules and contact its owner. Signed-in workspace uploads and recipient requests have different restrictions. **A small sample works but the original fails.** Report that distinction, the exact error, approximate size and type, browser/OS versions, time and destination. Start with [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support), or [contact support](https://dosya.dev/contact/) if you cannot sign in. Exclude passwords, keys, private share links and the original file from public questions. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does refreshing automatically continue the upload? No. A reload loses the browser's in-memory source file. An active item becomes Interrupted and needs Resume with the original. ### Must I reselect every failed file? No. Retry works while the current tab still holds its File object. After a reload, re-selection is needed before another transfer can use that source. ### Does Clear done remove completed cloud files? No. It dismisses queue entries. Removing cloud files is a separate action in Files. ### Can I delete my original after the bar reaches 100%? Keep it until the queue reports completion and you have checked the destination copy and expected version. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Receiving files from clients with a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Why large uploads fail](https://dosya.dev/blog/why-large-uploads-fail)

title: Add a file to Favourites
summary: Add a file shortcut to Favourites from Files, understand visibility and workspace rules, and recover when the star or favourite list does not update.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 using apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/FileActionsSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/mutationHooks.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/favourites.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/favourites.unit.test.ts. No favourite was added through the production service.
body: A favourite is a personal pointer to an existing cloud file. It consumes no extra storage, does not move the file, and is not shared with other workspace members. ## Before you start - Select the intended workspace and open **Files**. - The role must have **Files page** access. Favourites are unavailable to a member confined to one folder, and an API key pinned to another workspace is refused. - Locate a live, visible file. A file hidden from you returns “File not found”; one below an unopened full-lock folder returns “folder_locked.” ## Steps 1. In the browser, open the file's action menu and choose **Add to favourites**. You can also use the star button on a grid tile or in the full file viewer. 2. On mobile, open the file action sheet and tap **Add to favourites**. The audio player uses an **Add favourite** accessibility label for the same personal pointer. 3. Wait for the request to finish. The browser fills the star only after the server accepts the addition; mobile refreshes its Files and Favourites queries after success. 4. In the browser's left sidebar, expand **Favourites** and locate the filename. On mobile, open **Settings → Favourites**. 5. Open the entry and confirm it resolves to the same file ID, name, and workspace location. The API permits one favourite row per user and file. A duplicate request returns “Already in favourites” with status 409. The normal client changes the control to a removal state after success, which prevents an ordinary second add. ## Expected result The chosen file has a filled star and appears in your personal Favourites list. Its folder path, bytes, versions, sharing state, comments, and storage usage stay the same. If the file is later hidden from you or placed below a full-lock folder you have not unlocked, Dosya filters the shortcut from the list without deleting the saved favourite row. It can reappear when access returns. ## Troubleshooting **The star is missing.** Open a live file rather than a folder or Trash item. The reviewed browser workflow exposes favourites for files. **The toast says “Could not update favourites.”** The browser leaves its old state in place. Check connectivity, workspace membership, Files access, and any enclosing folder lock, then retry once. **The sidebar did not change.** Refresh Files or switch away and back to the workspace. The page and sidebar keep separate state and synchronize after a successful request. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Search files](/files/search-files)

title: Add a folder to Favourites
summary: Add a folder shortcut through Dosya's REST API, because current web and mobile clients expose file favourites but no folder-favourite control.
verification: Verified from local source on 2026-10-14: apps/api/src/pages/api/favourites.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/favourites.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts, apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/FolderActionsSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/api.ts, and apps/mobile/app/favourites.tsx. No production API mutation was sent.
body: The current data model supports personal folder favourites, but the reviewed web and mobile file menus do not provide an **Add to favourites** control for folders. Use a personal group for a fully graphical workflow. Advanced users can create the folder pointer through the REST API. A folder favourite references the existing folder. It does not copy its contents, change its parent, consume more storage, or grant access to anybody else. ## Before you start - Prefer **Add to group** when you need a client-only shortcut. Groups are available for folders in browser and mobile file menus. - For the POST route, obtain the workspace ID and live folder ID. Use a bearer API key with `full` scope, API access, and a pin to that same workspace; restricted `read`, `upload`, `clipper`, or `wp_site` scopes cannot perform this POST. - The key owner must be an unconfined workspace member. POST checks membership, target visibility, and the target's enclosing full-lock chain, but it does not require the role's Files page permission. - Reading the result is stricter: GET `/api/favourites` refuses a confined member and requires Files page access before it returns visible, unlocked rows. - Keep the credential out of terminal history, screenshots, and support messages. ## Steps 1. Put the secret in a protected environment variable and send this request with your real identifiers: curl --fail-with-body --request POST "https://api.dosya.dev/api/favourites" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{"workspace_id":"ws_...","folder_id":"fld_..."}' 2. A successful first addition returns HTTP 201 with an object containing ok: true and the new favourite-row ID. 3. Verify with GET /api/favourites?workspace_id=ws_.... If the role has Files page access, the matching object appears in the folders array with its real folder_id, folder_name, parent ID, and creation time. 4. On mobile, **Settings → Favourites** can render folder rows returned by this API. The browser sidebar currently reads only the response's files array, so it will not display the folder entry. 5. Open the folder from mobile or through its normal Files path and confirm the original breadcrumb and contents. A second POST for the same account and folder returns HTTP 409 with “Already in favourites.” An unknown or hidden target answers “Folder not found.” An enclosing full lock produces “folder_locked,” and a credential tied to another workspace receives “This API key is pinned to a different workspace.” ## Expected result The server stores one personal favourite row for the folder, and the source folder remains at its previous location with unchanged content and permissions. A caller that passes the GET membership and Files-access gates can read it, and mobile can display that returned row; the current browser sidebar cannot. Removal is reversible and affects only the pointer: call DELETE /api/favourites with the same workspace_id and folder_id, then POST again if you need to restore it. ## Troubleshooting **There is no folder star in Files.** That is the expected current client behavior. Choose **Add to group** or use the REST request above. **POST is refused before reaching the folder.** Confirm that the bearer key has `full` scope and API surface access. Non-GET REST operations default to full scope unless the route has an explicit narrower override, and favourites POST has none. **GET returns “Not a member” or a Files-access refusal.** Confirm the workspace ID, key pin, active membership, absence of folder confinement, and the role's Files page grant. These GET rules do not retroactively invalidate a successful POST pointer. **The request reports a duplicate.** Do not retry. Read the existing favourite row instead; the server enforces one pointer per user and folder. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Search files](/files/search-files)

title: Use breadcrumbs to confirm file location
summary: Navigate folder breadcrumbs from a deep file path, return to root safely, preserve the current filter, and troubleshoot missing or locked paths.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/files-params.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/files.test.tsx on 2026-10-14. Production navigation was not exercised.
body: Breadcrumbs show the ancestor folders of the current Files location. Each segment is a navigation control, while the home icon returns to the workspace root. **Where breadcrumbs appear.** The ordinary folder browser renders the home control and the `listing.breadcrumbs` ancestors. Library views such as Photos, Videos, and Documents use their library title and an all-folders scope instead of the same folder trail. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the intended workspace and enter the deepest folder you need. 2. Read the breadcrumb from left to right. Long labels can be visually truncated and the buttons have no tooltip, so open a segment and confirm the browser title and folder contents when two levels look similar. 3. Choose an ancestor segment to move directly to that folder. Dosya clears selected rows and updates the folder and page in the URL. 4. Choose the home icon to return to root. The current filter remains applied during folder navigation, so an apparently empty parent can still be filtered. 5. Use the browser title and visible folder contents to confirm the selected breadcrumb became the current location. **Access and locks.** The server returns breadcrumbs only for a path visible to the signed-in member. Confinement can make a higher ancestor unavailable, and a full-lock folder may require its normal unlock flow before listing succeeds. A hidden or deleted folder can also make a saved URL stop resolving. **If the path seems wrong.** Clear the active file filter, return home, and follow the known folder names again. Moving a file changes its folder reference, so an old written path can be stale even though the file still exists elsewhere. Breadcrumbs identify location; they do not record move history. **What navigation changes.** Opening a breadcrumb changes the current listing and resets row selection. It does not move, copy, rename, or delete any item, and it does not alter workspace storage. ## Expected result The Files page displays the chosen ancestor or root, the URL reflects that folder, and the breadcrumb trail matches the visible hierarchy. No file data changes during navigation. ## Related guides - [Open a file after following its folder path](/files/preview-files) - [Manage folders from the resolved location](/files/organize-files)

title: Choose whether to move or copy a file
summary: Choose Move when one file should change folders or Copy when a separate stored item is needed, with clear permission, quota, and identity checks.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/copy.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/repo/file-copy.ts on 2026-10-14. Production mutations were not run.
body: Choose **Move to...** when the same file should live in another folder. Choose **Copy** when you need a second independent item and have storage for another full object. **Move behavior.** A move retains the file ID, bytes, versions, and storage usage, then changes the folder reference. The old path stops listing it. The web action opens **Move to folder**, where you can search folders, expand the tree, choose **Root**, create a folder, **Cancel**, or **Move**. **Copy behavior.** Web **Copy** acts immediately in the current folder and names the result `Copy of {filename}`. It creates a new file ID and storage object, records the current user and client as the copy’s uploader and origin, and reserves the full byte size. The source remains unchanged. ## Steps 1. Decide whether links, comments, versions, and identity should continue to refer to one file. If yes, use **Move to...**. If the two items must be independently renamed, moved, or deleted, use **Copy**. 2. Confirm you have `upload_files`. Check the destination is in the same workspace, visible, unlocked, and inside any confinement boundary. 3. For Move, open the context menu, choose **Move to...**, select the folder in **Move to folder**, and choose **Move**. Success reports **Moved — The file has been moved.** 4. For Copy, remain in the desired source folder and choose **Copy**. Success reports **Copied — A copy has been added to this folder.** 5. Verify one item with the same ID at the new path for Move, or two separately identified items and increased storage for Copy. **Restrictions.** Locked files and locked ancestors block both operations. Moving into a locked target reports `Target folder is locked`. A copy can leave a protected WordPress backup but cannot be created inside one; a move is refused both into and out of a protected live backup. Neither operation overwrites a same-name destination. **Live Photos.** Web copy processes the still and paired video separately. If the still succeeds but the video fails, it reports **Copied — The photo was copied, but its video could not be.** Inspect both components before treating the pair as complete. ## Expected result Move leaves one file with its existing identity in a different folder and no extra storage charge. Copy leaves the source plus a new independent item that consumes another file-sized allocation. ## Related guides - [Move or rename an existing item](/files/move-and-rename) - [Create an independent file copy](/files/copy-file)

title: Verify a copied file independently
summary: Verify a copied file by destination, preview, size, identity, and Live Photo pair status; confirm the original source remains and storage increased.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/copy.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/repo/file-copy.ts on 2026-10-14. Production storage was not changed.
body: A successful copy should match the source’s content while remaining a separate file record. Verify both facts before deleting, renaming, sharing, or editing either item. **What copying creates.** The server writes a new storage object and file ID, reserves the source byte size, and sets new created and updated times. It preserves useful source timestamps, content hash, and hash status, but records the current actor and client as uploader and origin. Comments, share links, and the source file’s identity do not become the new item. ## Steps 1. After web **Copy**, remain in the current folder and locate `Copy of {filename}`. Other API clients can copy to a different folder under the original or an explicit name. 2. Open source and copy separately. Compare preview content, type, and exact displayed byte size. For a checksum-sensitive workflow, use the preserved content hash or download and hash both objects. 3. Compare file identifiers in the URL or API response. They must differ; seeing the same ID twice means you navigated back to the source rather than the copy. 4. Confirm the original still appears in its folder and that the workspace storage allocation increased by the copied object’s full size. 5. For a Live Photo, verify both the still and paired video. **Copied — The photo was copied, but its video could not be.** means the operation only partially reproduced the pair. **If the new item is absent.** Refresh before retrying. The web page reports **Copy failed — The file could not be copied** for detailed server failures such as a name conflict, locked source, insufficient `upload_files`, target invisibility, confinement, quota shortage, missing source object, or a storage-copy error. Check for an already-created result so a delayed response does not lead to an unnecessary second copy. **Independence after verification.** Renaming, moving, or trashing the copy does not rename, move, or trash the source. A separately shared source does not automatically grant access to the new file. Treat the copy’s new origin and uploader as the creation event, not as immutable provenance for the original bytes. ## Expected result Source and copy preview as matching content, report equal size, and have different IDs. The source remains intact, the copy can be managed independently, and quota reflects the extra object. ## Related guides - [Review the difference between moving and copying](/files/move-and-rename) - [Follow the full file-copy procedure](/files/copy-file)

title: View file details
summary: Open Dosya file details to verify size, MIME type, region, uploader, timestamps, origin, sharing state, versions, and permitted file actions.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions/restore.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/editor-config.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: File details identify the selected cloud object and place its primary actions, version controls, and format-specific editor entry in one panel. Use its identity fields before downloading, sharing, copying, restoring, editing, or deleting anything, and expect the server to enforce access again after a visible control is selected. ## Where details appear In the browser file list, selecting a file opens the **File details** panel at the side on larger screens and as a bottom sheet on smaller screens. Opening the file viewer provides a second inspector: select **Toggle inspector** or press its `i` shortcut, then choose **Details**, **Versions**, or **Comments**. The viewer inspector starts open at desktop widths and closed on small screens unless a linked tab requires it. The list panel and viewer inspector overlap, but they are not identical. The list panel also offers action buttons and active share-link cards. The viewer inspector adds **Modified**, active share and comment counts, Live Photo companion information when present, and an **Origin** badge. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the intended workspace and select one file. Check the full name at the top of **File details**. 2. Compare the summary line: file size, MIME type, and relative creation time. A badge shows `vN` when the current version is greater than one. 3. Review **Properties**. It reports **Uploaded by**, storage **Region**, **Created**, and **Extension**. Synced files add **Synced — Yes**; imported content can add **Source** and **Account**. 4. If the file has multiple versions, inspect **Versions**. Each row shows version number, size, uploader, relative time, and a download link. Every noncurrent row renders **Restore**; selecting it still requires `upload_files` at the API. 5. Under **Share links**, inspect each active URL, view count, expiry label, and **Password** badge. Use **Copy** only when you intend to distribute that exact link. 6. Confirm which primary actions are present. The Files page supplies **Download**, **Copy file**, **Share**, and **Delete file** callbacks only when the role has the corresponding capability; **View file** is always present. Historical-version download links, noncurrent **Restore**, and **Open in editor** for an Office filename render independently of those four callbacks, so the server can still refuse the request or limit editor write access. ## Locks, shares, and versions A full lock replaces the panel contents with **This file is locked**, an **Enter password** field, and **Unlock**. A rejected password displays the server message or **Incorrect password** and clears the field. After a successful unlock, the panel can load versions for that session. A view-only file remains visible and gains a **View only** badge. The four primary callbacks still follow the enclosing Files page, while version and Office controls remain visible and rely on their endpoints for the final decision. **Revoke link** is destructive for that share URL: after success it disappears from the active list and recipients can no longer use it. A failure shows **Revoke failed — The share link could not be revoked.** Copying the URL changes only your clipboard. Restoring a noncurrent version sends a separate request that requires `upload_files` and reports **Restored to vN.** when accepted. It changes which content is current, so preview the target version before selecting **Restore**. A refusal or other failed request reports **Restore failed** and leaves the current version unchanged. Version download links request the selected historical version without restoring it, but their presence does not guarantee that the download endpoint will release the bytes. Deleting from the details panel follows the normal confirmation flow and initially moves the file to trash, where it continues to use storage. Permanent deletion is a later explicit action and cannot be undone. Viewing metadata, closing the panel, or switching inspector tabs changes no file data. ## If information is missing **Unknown** for the uploader means the row has no resolved uploader name; it does not prove that the file has no creator. Share cards and version rows load separately. A transient request failure can leave those sections absent while the basic file properties remain visible, so refresh the Files page before concluding there is no history or active link. When one of the four primary actions is missing, the enclosing Files page usually withheld its callback for the current role; visible version and editor controls must still pass their server checks. ## Expected result The displayed name and at least two independent fields, such as size, MIME type, uploader, region, or timestamp, match the intended file. Simply inspecting them creates no version, share link, copy, download, or deletion. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Organize files](/files/organize-files)

title: Switch between grid and list views
summary: Switch Files between grid and list, understand Live Photo and column differences, and confirm that folder, filters, selection, and data stay intact.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/file-columns.tsx, and apps/web/src/pages/files.test.tsx on 2026-10-14. Production browser storage was not altered.
body: Grid and list change how the current Files result is presented. The choice is saved in this browser under `dosya_files_view`; it does not change the workspace or another device’s preference. **View differences.** Grid separates **Folders** and **Files** into cards and collapses a Live Photo still with its paired video. List uses a table and can show the twin video as a separate row. Its default columns are **Name**, **Size**, **Created**, and **Origin**; the column chooser can add other metadata, while **Name** remains required. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the intended workspace, folder, and filter state. Note a few filenames and the result count. 2. Use the two view-icon buttons in the toolbar to choose grid or list. In the ordinary folder view those icon buttons currently have no text label or tooltip, so identify them by the card-grid and row-list symbols. 3. In list view, open the column chooser when you need more metadata. Sorting and pagination continue to apply to the same current query. 4. Switch back and confirm the folder, filters, selected items, sorting, and underlying API result remain unchanged. A Live Photo can look like one grid item but more than one list row because of pair presentation. 5. Reload the page. The last chosen mode should return in the same browser profile. **What can reset the preference.** Clearing site data, using a private window, or changing browser/profile removes or isolates the local setting. The workspace does not sync this preference between people. **If the sets appear different.** Clear the search and filter controls, compare the current folder URL, and account for Live Photo pairing before reporting missing data. Switching views does not upload, copy, move, rename, or delete anything. A truly missing item should also be absent after refreshing the same folder in both modes. ## Expected result The selected layout persists locally, while the current folder query and stored files remain unchanged. Grid emphasizes visual cards; list exposes denser rows and configurable metadata. ## Related guides - [Search within the active Files view](/files/search-files) - [Organize items after choosing a layout](/files/organize-files)

title: Explore files on the map
summary: Use Dosya Map to find files and folders by EXIF or upload-origin location, apply date and folder filters, and understand privacy and access rules.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/pages/api/map/pins.ts, apps/api/src/lib/location/origin.ts, apps/web/src/pages/map.tsx, and apps/web/src/components/map-filter-panel.tsx; the production Map was not independently queried.
body: Map plots location-bearing file and folder pins returned for the current workspace and assigned folder scope. A file can use exact GPS extracted from image metadata or an approximate upload-origin coordinate. Folder coordinates are always upload origins. ## Before you use location data Dosya obtains an upload origin from the network location supplied with an upload request. It is approximate and may identify a VPN exit, office gateway, or mobile network rather than where the file was created. If later scanning finds EXIF GPS, that exact coordinate replaces the upload origin for the file. A folder has no EXIF and keeps its approximate origin. Turning off workspace upload-origin recording removes IP-derived file and folder pins from Map; EXIF pins can still appear. A missing, invalid, or zero coordinate from the request is not saved. Location data can reveal sensitive travel or work patterns, so verify the source label before sharing what the map shows. ## Steps 1. Open **Map** in the intended workspace. Your workspace role must allow file-page access; otherwise the API returns `You don't have access to the files page`. 2. Read the status values: `located` counts EXIF GPS pins, `approximate` counts upload-origin pins, and `scanning…` reports files still awaiting location extraction. 3. On web or desktop, choose **Show approximate locations** only when coarse upload origins are useful. Approximate pins are shown by default, and the toggle controls whether they remain visible. 4. Use **All folders** on web, or **Everywhere** on desktop, to select a folder. The selection includes that folder and all descendants. Folder-confined members cannot move the map filter outside their assigned subtree. 5. Enter **From** or **To** dates if needed. Web interprets each selected day as a UTC boundary; desktop uses the local day's boundary. File filtering uses capture time when available and otherwise upload time; folders use creation time. 6. Pan or zoom to the area you need, select a marker or cluster, and verify the file or folder name before continuing. ## Expected result Map limits coordinates to the current workspace and any assigned folder subtree. File pins exclude deleted, hidden, and locked files. Folder pins exclude deleted folders and obey the same subtree and date filters; the folder-pin query does not apply the file hidden or lock predicates. Raster images can use thumbnails, while other files and folders use icons. A file marker opens its viewer, and a folder marker opens that folder in Files. Map requests are returned with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Mobile still keeps its fetched pin query fresh for five minutes and provides plain markers without the web and desktop filter panel. ## Troubleshooting - **`No geotagged photos yet` or `No files or folders with a location yet` appears.** Check whether the files contain EXIF GPS, whether upload-origin recording is enabled, and whether scanning is still pending. - **`All located items are approximate - enable the toggle above to see them.` appears.** Turn on **Show approximate locations** or upload an image with EXIF GPS. - **`No pins to show` appears after filtering.** Select a broader folder, remove a date bound, or press **Clear**. Map **Clear** resets folder, **From**, and **To**; it does not change the approximate-location toggle. - **Mobile says `Couldn't load your map.`** Confirm an active workspace and network connection, then press **Retry**. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Recover from moving a file to the wrong folder
summary: Move a file back to its original folder when that destination still exists, passes access rules, and has no same-name conflict; then verify one item.
