verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/folder-picker-dialog.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts on 2026-10-14. No production move was made.
body: Dosya has no automatic undo or move-history control. You can move a file back only when you know the former folder and it remains a valid destination. **What a reverse move preserves.** The file keeps its ID, bytes, versions, and storage use. Its folder reference changes again. Comments and links that resolve by file ID continue to refer to that same item. ## Steps 1. Identify the original folder from a trusted record or colleague. **Get info**, breadcrumbs, and current details show the present location, not a historical path. 2. In **Files**, open the moved item’s context menu and choose **Move to...**. 3. In **Move to folder**, use **Search folders...**, the expandable tree, or **Root** to select the former folder. Folder search waits about 250 ms after typing. 4. Verify the folder name and its parent path, then choose **Move**. The success toast is **Moved — The file has been moved.** 5. Open the original folder and confirm exactly one file with the expected name and ID appears. Return to the intermediate folder and verify it is absent there. **When moving back is refused.** The target must still exist in the same workspace, be visible, and not be locked. You need `upload_files`; a confined member must have both source and destination inside the confinement anchor. A same-name file returns `A file with this name already exists in the target folder`, and selecting the current folder returns `File is already in this folder`. The web client summarizes these as **Move failed — The file could not be moved.** **Protected content.** A locked source or enclosing folder blocks the action. A live protected WordPress backup cannot be used as either side of a move until its backup protection no longer applies. Do not use Copy as a silent substitute unless a second file and additional storage are acceptable. ## Expected result The existing file ID is listed once in the original folder, disappears from the interim folder, and retains its bytes, versions, comments, and storage footprint. ## Related guides - [Use the general move and rename controls](/files/move-and-rename) - [Copy instead when two independent items are required](/files/copy-file)

title: Confirm a destination before moving a file
summary: Confirm a file-move destination by workspace, folder tree, search result, and final listing before committing a location change with no automatic undo.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/folder-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts on 2026-10-14. Production folders were unchanged.
body: The move picker displays folders from the active workspace. Confirm the full hierarchy before committing because identical folder names can exist under different parents and the web app has no automatic undo. **Picker controls.** The dialog title is **Move to folder**. It provides **Search folders...**, **Root**, a lazily expanded tree, **New folder in “…”** or **New folder at root**, **Cancel**, and **Move**. Search begins after a 250 ms typing pause. ## Steps 1. Confirm the active workspace and the source file’s name, folder, and ID before opening its context menu. 2. Choose **Move to...**. Expand the tree from a known ancestor instead of selecting the first search result with a matching leaf name. 3. Select the exact destination and reread its parent chain. If you create a folder from this dialog, verify whether the label says **New folder in “…”** or **New folder at root** before naming it. 4. Choose **Move** once. Success reports **Moved — The file has been moved.** 5. Open the destination folder and confirm the file appears with the same ID and expected metadata. Check the old folder to ensure it no longer lists the item. **Server-side validation.** The destination must be a live, visible folder in the same workspace. A locked target returns `Target folder is locked`; an absent or hidden target returns `Target folder not found`; selecting the current folder returns `File is already in this folder`. Confinement requires both the source and target inside the member’s allowed subtree. **Name collision.** Dosya never overwrites another file. If the target already contains the same name, the API returns `A file with this name already exists in the target folder`. Rename one item or choose another folder, then reopen the picker. The generic web failure toast is **Move failed — The file could not be moved.** **Reversal.** Moving back is possible only if the old folder still exists, remains accessible, and has no conflicting name. Record the source location when a later reversal matters. ## Expected result The same file record appears in the confirmed destination and no longer appears in its previous folder. Its bytes, versions, and storage allocation remain unchanged. ## Related guides - [Review all file move and rename rules](/files/move-and-rename) - [Choose Copy when the source must remain](/files/copy-file)

title: Check access before moving into a restricted folder
summary: Resolve a blocked file move by checking upload permission, confinement, destination visibility, locks, backup protection, and name conflicts.
verification: Reviewed against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/file-move.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx on 2026-10-14. Production permissions were not changed.
body: A destination can appear in the folder picker yet fail the server’s final authorization checks. Diagnose the exact rule before asking for broader workspace access. **Required capability.** File moves require `upload_files`. The web page normally hides **Move to...** when that capability is absent, while a direct request can return `You don't have permission to move files`. ## Steps 1. Confirm the source is visible and unlocked. A direct file lock returns `This file is locked and cannot be moved`; a locked ancestor returns `This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to move it.` 2. Open **Move to...** and select a destination in the same workspace. Do not treat its presence in the picker as final authorization. 3. For a folder-confined member, verify both source and destination are inside the confinement anchor. The API can return `This file is outside the folder you're confined to` or `You cannot move a file outside the folder you're confined to`. 4. Confirm the target still exists, is visible, and is unlocked. Exact API responses include `Target folder not found` and `Target folder is locked`. 5. Check for an existing same-name file. A collision returns `A file with this name already exists in the target folder`; Dosya will not overwrite it. 6. Retry with an allowed destination, then confirm the same file ID appears there and disappears from the source folder. **Protected backup folders.** A live WordPress backup cannot be used as the source or destination of a move while backup protection is active. Choose a normal workspace folder or follow the backup’s supported lifecycle instead of trying to bypass protection. **What failure changes.** A rejected move leaves the folder reference, bytes, versions, and storage allocation unchanged. The current web toast is **Move failed — The file could not be moved**, so inspect the role, confinement, lock, target, and collision conditions even when the detailed API message is not displayed. **Escalation.** Provide the file ID, source folder ID, intended destination ID, active workspace, and exact API response if available. Avoid sharing lock credentials or recovery secrets. ## Expected result An authorized destination accepts the existing file ID and the old folder no longer lists it. A refused request makes no partial copy and leaves the file at its original path. ## Related guides - [Check move permissions and file-location behavior](/files/move-and-rename) - [Use Copy only when a second object is intended](/files/copy-file)

title: Check where a file came from
summary: Read Origin, uploader, dates, region, import source, and account metadata correctly, including how copying changes the recorded creation event.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/helpers.ts, apps/web/src/lib/file-columns.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/copy.ts on 2026-10-14. Production metadata was not queried.
body: **Origin** identifies the client or protocol that created the current file record. It is useful operational metadata, but it is not a permanent chain of custody or the file’s previous folder. **Available labels.** The viewer’s **Details** tab always shows **Size**, **Type**, **Region**, **Uploaded by**, **Created**, and **Modified**. **Origin** appears only when the record has a stored value, and **Synced** appears only for a synced file. The Files details panel can additionally show import-specific **Source** and **Account**. **Get info** includes location and version details but does not present the general Origin field. ## Steps 1. Open the file preview and choose **Details**. Confirm the filename and file ID so you do not inspect a similarly named copy. 2. Read **Origin**, when present, with **Uploaded by**, **Created**, and **Modified**. Dosya maps stored values to **Web**, **Desktop**, **Mobile**, **CLI**, **WebDAV**, **S3**, **FTP**, or **Import**. Preview omits the row when no origin is stored; an unknown nonempty value displays `-`, as does a missing or unknown value in the Files table’s Origin column. 3. For an imported item, open the Files details panel and compare **Source** and **Account**. Those fields identify the import connection and are separate from the general origin label. 4. Compare **Region** and **Synced** only for the questions they answer. They do not reveal the former folder or the person who originally created the bytes outside Dosya. 5. If the item was copied, expect the copy to show the copying client as Origin and the current actor as uploader, even though source timestamps and content hash may have been preserved internally. **Do not infer unsupported provenance.** Origin does not name a share sender, prove ownership of the content, preserve every transfer hop, or record move history. Moving a file changes only its folder reference and keeps origin; copying creates a new record and therefore a new ingestion event. **If the field is absent or a dash.** An absent Preview row means the record has no stored origin. A dash in the Files table can mean the value is missing or unknown to the current label map. Use import **Source** and **Account**, uploader, timestamps, audit evidence, or the originating client’s logs for a deeper investigation. ## Expected result You can identify the supported client category that created this file record and distinguish it from uploader, import connection, storage region, sync state, and folder history. ## Related guides - [Open Preview to inspect complete file details](/files/preview-files) - [Organize a file without changing its origin record](/files/organize-files)

title: Create a client file upload request
summary: Create a client upload request, choose its destination and limits, test the public page, and verify each received file in your workspace.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/file-request-detail.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/create.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/title-folder.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/uploader-folder.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/guard.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/files.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/files.purge.unit.test.ts, multipart request routes, src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro and focused request tests. Verified current owner and guest labels, roles, link/email modes, 100-address invitation handling, default per-uploader folders, title-folder outcomes, destination gates, passwords, expiry, request/workspace limits, public error strings, completion receipts, irreversible public withdrawal purge and irreversible request revocation. Existing end-to-end captures were inspected and remain accurate.
body: A file request lets a client upload into a destination you control without joining your Dosya workspace. In **File requests**, select **New request**, choose **By link** or **By email**, set the acceptance rules, then test the recipient page before using it for important delivery. A sharing link sends files outward. Use [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) when the files already exist in your workspace and recipients need to open them. ## Before you start - Select the workspace that should own the received files. Creating a request requires **upload files** permission because its URL delegates that permission to someone outside the workspace. - Choose a live, visible destination inside your allowed folder subtree. A configured **Full lock** on that folder or an ancestor blocks public uploads even when you personally unlocked it for an hour. - Check the owning account’s remaining plan storage and any workspace total-storage cap. File requests have no separate storage pool: accepted bytes consume that workspace’s ordinary allocation. - Decide whether the request should use a public bearer URL or emailed invitations. **By link** needs no account. **By email** records and sends invitations to up to 100 valid addresses in one request. - Prepare a harmless sample. A successful test occupies one **Max files** slot and uses workspace storage until removed. ## Steps ### Build the request 1. Open **File requests** and select **New request**. On an empty page, **Create a request** opens the same **Request files** dialog. 2. Select the **Request files** tab that matches this client handoff: - **By link** creates one URL for you to copy and distribute. - **By email** requires at least one **Email addresses** entry and sends an invitation. Split a list larger than 100 across requests. 3. Enter **Title (optional)** and **Message (optional)** with the exact documents, naming rules and deadline. Do not include account credentials. 4. Add **Password (opt)** when the URL needs a shared secret. The trimmed password must contain at least eight characters. 5. Set **Expires** to **Never**, **1 day**, **7 days**, **30 days** or **90 days**. The form starts at **7 days**. Expiry closes new uploads; it does not delete received files. 6. Select **Upload destination**. **Root (workspace top level)** means the workspace root for an unrestricted member and the member’s assigned anchor for a folder-confined role. 7. Review **Put each uploader in their own folder**. It is on by default: - With a title, Dosya first creates a new title-named folder in the selected destination, using a suffix such as “(2)” if necessary. - Each browser then receives its own child folder, named from the entered name, the invited address associated with that recipient URL, typed email, dropped folder name or a six-character guest reference in that order. - Turning the option off places submitted paths directly in the selected destination. This setting is fixed at creation in the current web editor; create a new request if the organization model must change. 8. Expand **Advanced options** when the delivery needs narrower rules: - **Allowed extensions** accepts a comma-separated list such as `.pdf, .docx, .jpg`. A filename with a known extension outside the list is rejected. - **Max file size (MB)** caps each file, not the whole submission. - **Max files** counts accepted files across every uploader. Concurrent attempts reserve slots atomically so the cap cannot be exceeded by two clients racing for the final place. 9. For **By link**, select **Generate link**, save the URL under **Request link**, then select **Done**. For **By email**, choose **Send request** and wait for **Request sent**. ### Test the public upload page 1. Paste the generated client-upload address into a private browser window, then match its workspace identity, title, message, deadline and **Max files** terms to the owner form. 2. If it says **This request is locked**, enter the request password and select **Unlock**. This creates a request-specific access grant for 30 minutes; it is unrelated to a Dosya account password. 3. Choose a small sample with **Browse files**, **Choose a folder** or **Drop files here**. Touch devices can instead show **Photo library**, **Take a photo** and **Browse files**. 4. Inspect **This transfer** before sending. The page reports extension, size and remaining-count problems before eligible bytes move. 5. Optionally enter **Your name (optional)** and **Your email (optional)**. These labels help the owner recognize a delivery; typed values do not verify the sender’s identity. 6. Select the count-specific action, such as **Upload 1 file**. The browser transfers up to three files at once. Files above 50 MiB use 10 MiB multipart pieces with up to three part requests at a time. 7. Keep the page open until the row reads **Received**. If a password grant expires during a long transfer, enter it again under **Your access timed out** and choose **Unlock and continue**. ### Confirm what you received 1. Return to **File requests** and open the request detail. Reload an already-open tab. 2. Match the received row’s name, size, uploader label and timestamp to the client’s receipt. 3. Open **Files** and inspect the configured destination. When uploader folders are enabled, follow the title folder and uploader folder rather than expecting the file directly at the selected level. 4. Tell the client the delivery is accepted only after both sides agree on the received item. The public ledger is tied to that visitor’s request cookie and is not a universal proof of identity. ## Expected result The client’s completed row reads **Received**, the owner sees the same filename and byte size on the request detail, and the file exists under the chosen destination structure. The upload consumes ordinary workspace storage without making the client a workspace member. ## Limits and exact refusals Request-specific acceptance rules and the owner plan/workspace storage gates both apply; the stricter result wins. | Condition | Recipient response | | --- | --- | | Request was closed | **This request has been revoked** | | Deadline passed | **This request has expired** | | Count is exhausted | **This request has reached its file limit.** | | Request size rule fails | **File is too large. Maximum size is N.N MB** | | Extension is refused | **File type .ext is not allowed. Accepted: …** | | Destination later receives Full lock | **This upload request can no longer accept files.** | | Workspace storage is exhausted | A storage-quota refusal; the owner must free capacity or change the plan | Blank request fields mean no request-specific extension, per-file-size or file-count ceiling. The owning account’s storage entitlement and the workspace total-storage cap can still refuse incoming bytes. **Never** removes only the request deadline; it does not create extra storage. ## Manage or end collection The detail page provides **Copy link**, **Edit**, **Recipients**, the received-file table and **Revoke** while active. Editing future rules does not revalidate completed uploads. Moving the destination does not relocate earlier submissions. Revocation is irreversible and stops future single-part and multipart calls. It notifies recorded recipients, but it leaves their completed workspace files and the owner ledger intact. Use [Edit or close a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request) before deleting any retained material. ## Troubleshooting **The request cannot be created in a folder.** Confirm the folder exists, is inside your assigned subtree and is visible to your role. A hidden destination looks missing. A configured Full lock returns `folder_locked`; a personal unlock grant is intentionally ignored because the public URL outlives that grant. **An invitation did not arrive.** The request can exist even when delivery fails after creation. Copy its URL from **File requests**, verify the address, and use the recipient controls to resend without creating a duplicate inbox. **The sender only staged files.** Ask them to select the upload button and wait for **Received**. A filename under **This transfer** without that status is not an accepted delivery. **The client sees a storage refusal.** Only a workspace member can free capacity, raise the workspace cap or change the owning plan. The outside uploader cannot solve it by signing in or choosing a different browser. **A large upload stopped after revocation, expiry or a new destination lock.** Those gates are checked throughout multipart transfer. Reopen collection with an edited future expiry when appropriate, or create a new request after resolving the configured lock. A revoked token itself cannot return. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does a client need a Dosya account? No. The public request URL authorizes the upload subject to its password, deadline, destination and file rules. ### Is a file request private because it was emailed? An invitation can identify a recorded recipient, but anyone holding a plain request URL may still reach the public page unless its password protects it. Share sensitive request addresses carefully. ### Can uploaders remove a submitted file? The public page can show **Remove** to the same visitor while the request remains usable. Confirming it permanently purges the received file, its versions, its share records and the stored objects they reference. This withdrawal bypasses **Deleted**, so neither the uploader nor the owner can recover it from Dosya Trash. An ordinary owner-side **Delete** in **Files** is different: that soft-deleted item appears under **Deleted** and follows workspace retention until it is purged. ## Related guides - [Upload through a file request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Set file-request limits](/sharing/request-limits) - [Invite recipients and track submissions](/sharing/request-recipients) - [Edit or close the request](/sharing/manage-file-request) - [Troubleshoot a rejected submission](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request)

title: Complete your first upload and sharing task
summary: Upload a harmless sample file, confirm its completed cloud copy, create a suitable sharing link, and test the recipient experience before sending it.
verification: Reviewed this start-to-finish journey against the current locally verified upload and sharing flows on 2026-10-12. Screenshots come from isolated completed-upload and generated-link checks.
body: This quick journey takes one harmless sample file from your device to a tested recipient link. It helps confirm your workspace, upload permission and sharing setup before you send important material. ## Before you start - Use a small, non-confidential sample file you can recognize and open. - Select the intended workspace and check its name above the sidebar. - Make sure your role permits uploads and share-link creation. - Decide whether the recipient should download the file, whether the link needs a password and when it should expire. - Use a private browser window for the recipient test so your signed-in session does not hide access problems. ## Steps: upload and confirm the sample 1. Open **Uploads**. 2. Under **Upload options**, confirm the destination folder. **Root (top level)** means the workspace's top level. 3. Select **browse for files**, choose the sample and keep the browser tab open. 4. Wait until the upload row says **Done**. 5. Select **View file** or **Go to location**. 6. In **Files**, confirm the name, size and destination. Open the sample if its format supports a preview. ## Steps: create and test the sharing link 1. From the confirmed file, choose **Share**, then **By link**. 2. Review **Expires in** and open **Advanced options** if you need a password, view-only behavior or a download limit. 3. Select **Generate link**. 4. Copy the entire URL shown under **Share link created**. 5. Open a private browser window and paste the URL. 6. Confirm that the recipient page shows the intended file and enforces the password or other access choice. 7. If the test succeeds, send the link. Share a password separately when practical. ## Expected result The sample appears in **Files** in the intended workspace. The tested URL opens the correct recipient page without relying on your signed-in session, and the configured password, expiry, view-only choice or download limit applies. ## Limits and safety checks - **Done** confirms the upload; selecting a file or seeing partial progress does not. - A public link can be forwarded. Apply only the access settings suitable for that file. - Your own test download can consume a configured download allowance. - A share-link password protects that recipient route. It does not convert ordinary storage into Vault encryption. - Link availability still depends on expiry, revocation, download limits, the underlying file and workspace policies. ## Troubleshooting **The upload never reaches Done.** Read the queue error and check connectivity, available storage, destination access and workspace policies. Retry only the failed item when offered. **Share is unavailable.** Confirm the upload completed, the file is in the active workspace and your role permits share-link creation. A workspace policy can also disable links. **The private-window test asks for unexpected access.** Return to the link settings and verify whether you created a public link, named-recipient delivery or password-protected link. **The link opens the wrong file.** Revoke that URL in **Shared**, return to the intended file and generate a replacement. Do not send the mistaken URL. **The test works but the recipient cannot open it.** Copy the URL again, confirm it was not truncated and check its status and expiry in **Shared**. If password protected, verify that the recipient has the exact password through a separate channel. ## Related guides - [Upload files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Add a password to a sharing link](/sharing/password-link) - [Troubleshoot an unavailable sharing link](/sharing/unavailable-link)

title: Choose between a lock and a role restriction
summary: Choose a folder password, view-only lock, workspace role, or assigned root by matching the control to who needs access and what they may do.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/lock-modal.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/role-create.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-gate.unit.test.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A folder lock, a workspace role, and an assigned root solve different access problems. Decide which boundary you need before changing a live folder. **Choose the correct boundary** - **View only** is a folder lock mode. Authorized members may browse and preview the folder tree, but downloads are blocked. It does not ask for a password. - **Password** fully locks the folder tree. Members cannot browse its contents, add items inside it, or use existing share links until the folder is unlocked. A successful viewer unlock lasts one hour for that user. - A **workspace role** grants capabilities such as uploading, downloading, moving, hiding, or locking files across the workspace. A role does not itself unlock a password-protected folder. - An **assigned root folder** confines a member to one subtree. It controls which part of the workspace the member can reach, while locks inside that subtree still apply. These controls can be combined. For example, a contributor can be confined to Client A, denied download permission by role, and still encounter a password lock on Client A/Legal. ## Steps 1. Identify the people affected and the smallest folder subtree involved. Do not test with a workspace owner because elevated permissions can hide the member experience. 2. If everyone who can reach the folder should preview but not download it, open the folder menu, choose the lock action, select **View only**, and apply it. 3. If the subtree must be closed until a secret is entered, select **Password**, enter at least eight characters after leading and trailing spaces are removed, and save. Internal spaces count toward the minimum. 4. If the rule concerns capabilities or a permanent member boundary, change the member’s workspace role or assigned root in workspace settings instead. Only administrators who can manage members and roles should make that change. 5. Sign in as a representative member. Test listing the folder, previewing a file, downloading it, uploading into the folder, and opening any existing share link that matters. **Important interactions** A child marked **Unlocked** does not override a locked ancestor. The effective restriction comes from the nearest protected ancestor in the path. Removing a lock also does not remove hidden-item rules, role permissions, or an assigned-root boundary. Share access does not reuse the one-hour viewer unlock token, and full-lock or view-only subtrees are excluded from sync. Changing access can expose or block an entire subtree immediately. Record the original setting and test with non-sensitive files before applying the decision to a production folder. ## Expected result The selected control matches the intended scope: a lock protects one subtree, a role defines workspace actions, and an assigned root limits the member’s reachable subtree. The test member sees the same boundary on refresh and after signing in again. ## Related guides - [Lock a folder](/files/lock-folder) - [Understand inherited folder restrictions](/files/folder-restriction-inheritance)

title: Troubleshoot a folder archive download
summary: Use the archive tab and exact refusal text to separate empty, locked, oversized, permission, selection-size, and other browser transfer failures.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts; apps/api/src/lib/archive-entries.ts.
body: A folder download uses **Download** on the folder row or **Download ZIP** on a selection and streams `dosya-download.zip` directly to the browser. The server does not create a background archive job, so the new tab, browser download list, and exact API refusal are the evidence to diagnose. One folder remains one archive request regardless of how many descendants it contains. The server then applies the 10,000-entry and 5 GiB caps to the files it can include. Hidden files and content blocked by file or ancestor-folder locks are omitted; when everything is blocked, the neutral response can be **No items found**. ## Steps 1. Reopen **Files**, locate the folder, and verify that your role exposes its **Download** action; an absent action points to the download permission rather than archive size. 2. Start the folder download once and keep the new tab visible. Record the full response instead of repeatedly clicking while a stream may already be starting. 3. For **This folder is empty - there's nothing to download**, add a file or select a populated folder; for **No items found**, verify current visibility and unlock eligible content first. 4. For **Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)**, split the tree below the problem folder and download smaller child folders. 5. For **Archive too large (max 5 GiB)**, divide by total source bytes; deleting local browser copies does not reduce the server-side archive size. 6. Confirm the replacement `dosya-download.zip` finishes, then inspect its paths and names because partially blocked trees can legitimately omit files you cannot download. ## Expected result A permitted, nonempty test folder within both caps starts one browser download. The finished archive preserves internal directory paths for included content and leaves the workspace unchanged. **You don't have download permission** requires a workspace owner or admin to change the role. **Nothing to download - the selection contains no files** means the selected live rows produced no archive entries. A browser network failure after streaming begins can leave a partial local file without a Dosya retry control; discard that partial copy and repeat from Files after connectivity stabilizes. ## Related guides - [Download a smaller folder test from Files](/uploading/download-files) - [Fixing a slow upload or download](/troubleshooting/slow-transfer)

title: Share a cloud folder with one link
summary: Create and test one URL for a cloud folder, including dynamic subfolders, hidden or locked exclusions, view-only access and ZIP limits.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/share.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/visibility.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/lock-gate.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download-all.ts, apps/api/src/lib/archive-entries.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/egress.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/download-session.ts and focused folder-share tests. Verified role/subtree policy, dynamic membership, exclusion counts, root and descendant lock/hidden behavior, personal-unlock non-effect, view-only handling, 10,000-entry/5 GiB archive ceilings, 10 ZIP attempts per hour, one-slot archive and preview-session counting, Free-plan limits and separate link-result versus email-send completion paths. The current folder-share capture remains accurate.
body: A folder link gives recipients one address for the eligible files and subfolders beneath a selected cloud folder. It is a live view rather than a snapshot: later additions can appear, while hidden and fully locked descendants are withheld whenever the recipient opens or downloads it. ## Before you start - Select the intended workspace and finish uploading the delivery contents. - Use a dedicated delivery folder when possible. Reusing a working folder can expose eligible files added after the URL is sent. - Your role needs **create share links** permission and access to the folder. A folder-confined member can share only a target inside the assigned subtree. - One link targets one folder tree. The dialog cannot combine several folders or mix a folder with separately selected files. - Decide whether the URL is public, password protected, restricted to named email recipients or view-only. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** and locate the folder from its containing directory. Use the folder row/card menu or right-click it, then select **Share**. 2. Confirm the displayed folder name. The dialog opens on **By email**; choose **By link** when anyone holding the address may open it. 3. Review **Expires in**. Choose **1 hour**, **24 hours**, **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, **Custom date…** or **Never**. Workspace and Free-plan ceilings can shorten the saved result. 4. Expand **Advanced options** as needed: - **Password (optional)** requires at least eight characters. - **View only.** allows browsing and eligible previews without a folder ZIP or normal file download. - **Remove photo metadata.** strips location, camera and capture-time details from delivered photos while leaving originals intact. - **Download limit (optional)** accepts a whole number from 1 to 10,000. One successful **Download all** ZIP consumes one slot, not one per archived file. Opening an eligible file preview also claims one slot on its first byte session, including under View only; later Range reads for that file within the one-hour signed session reuse the claim. 5. Read the exclusion notice before proceeding. It reports how many hidden or fully locked items will not be shared, counting each excluded item once rather than expanding an excluded folder into every descendant. 6. Complete the selected delivery path: - With **By link**, select **Generate link**, wait for **Share link created**, save the address with its copy icon, and select **Done**. - With **By email**, add no more than 50 addresses, decide whether **Only these people can open it.** remains selected, and select **Send**. Read the success notice's sent count and failed-address list. The modal resets and closes without showing a generated URL. 7. Open **Shared → By me** and select the saved folder row. Use its recorded settings and URL for the owner-side check; email recipients have already been sent their invitations. 8. Open that folder address privately, traverse every intended subfolder, confirm protected branches are absent, and complete the password or invited-email code challenge when configured. 9. When downloads are enabled, download one representative file. Use **Download all** only when consuming one configured slot and the archive size is acceptable. If the delivery has a one-slot limit, do not open a file preview or archive during owner testing; either raise the limit for the test or leave its sole byte session for the recipient. 10. For **By link**, deliver the verified address manually and send its password separately when practical. For **By email**, correct any failed address and retry rather than expecting a copy-and-Done result. ## Expected result The tested URL opens the intended live folder tree, omits every protected descendant reported by the preflight notice, and presents only the preview or download actions allowed by the link and target settings. The recipient does not join the workspace. ## What recipients receive The public folder page lists eligible descendants without adding the visitor as a workspace member. New eligible content placed under the shared root can appear through the same active URL. Renames and moves inside the tree are reflected as the live folder is resolved again. The following items are not delivered normally: - Hidden folders and files, plus the branch beneath an excluded hidden folder. - Items configured **Full lock**, including descendants protected by a fully locked ancestor. - Items deleted from the live workspace tree. - Normal downloads for a descendant configured **View only**. It may remain previewable, but it is omitted from the ZIP archive. If the shared root itself becomes hidden from its link creator or receives **Full lock** after creation, the whole URL becomes unavailable. Removing that configured state can restore an unrevoked, unexpired link. A member’s temporary one-hour unlock does not restore public access because personal grants never travel with the URL. ## Folder ZIP limits **Download all** streams one ZIP containing the descendants the link may expose at that moment. - Maximum archive entries: 10,000. - Maximum total source size: 5 GiB. - Attempt limit: 10 folder ZIP requests per hour for the same link and client IP. - An empty eligible set returns **There is nothing in this folder to download**. - Too many entries returns **Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)**. - Excess size returns **Archive too large (max 5 GiB)**. - A view-only folder returns **This folder is view-only. Downloads are not allowed.** The archive’s full source size is checked against the Free owner’s daily public-share transfer allowance before streaming. Free accounts receive 10 GiB per UTC day across all their public links. A configured link download limit is claimed once for the complete ZIP; a refused archive that never starts does not become a successful delivery. Folder listing alone does not claim a byte slot, but opening an eligible descendant preview does. Split a folder that exceeds an archive ceiling, or let recipients retrieve eligible files individually when policy permits. Being able to browse a large tree does not guarantee it fits into one ZIP. ## Plan, policy and access rules - A Free creator can have five active links and every Free link is capped at seven days. Revoked and expired rows free a slot. - Workspace settings can disable sharing, require passwords, establish a default expiry or impose a shorter maximum. - **By link** is public to anyone holding the URL. **By email** with **Only these people can open it.** selected requires each invited address to pass a one-time email code. - Folder sharing refuses an out-of-scope target with **This folder is outside the folder you're confined to**. - A hidden root answers **Folder not found**. A configured locked ancestor reports **This folder is inside a locked folder and cannot be shared**; a locked root reports **This folder is fully locked and cannot be shared**. - Unlocking the folder for your own session does not satisfy either public-link lock gate. ## Revocation and later folder changes Open **Shared → By me** and revoke the exact folder-link row when the delivery must stop. Revocation is immediate and irreversible for that token. It does not delete the folder, remove another URL pointing to it or recall downloaded ZIPs. Moving the shared folder outside the link’s resolvable target or deleting it makes the delivery unavailable. Adding material can expose it automatically, so revoke the link before repurposing the folder for unrelated work. ## Troubleshooting **Generate link reports a locked folder.** A configured Full lock on the root or ancestor blocks persistent public access. A personal unlock cannot override it. Ask the authorized owner to change the configured lock or share an approved delivery copy elsewhere. **The recipient sees fewer descendants than the owner.** Compare the private recipient view with hidden and lock settings. The preflight count names how many protected items are excluded but deliberately does not reveal their names to the public visitor. **Download all is absent.** Check **View only** first. A target-level view-only rule can also block the affected file even when the folder link itself allows downloads. **The ZIP fails while individual files open.** Match the exact error to the 10,000-entry, 5 GiB, hourly attempt, link download-count or Free transfer allowance above. Do not repeatedly retry a size refusal; divide the delivery. **A new file unexpectedly appeared.** Folder links resolve contents dynamically. Move unrelated material outside the shared root or revoke the URL and create a dedicated delivery folder. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I share only selected files from a folder? Use a multi-file sharing link for up to 100 selected files, or place the intended set in a dedicated folder. A folder URL represents its eligible live tree. ### Can I restrict the folder to email addresses? Yes. Choose **By email**, add no more than 50 recipients, and keep **Only these people can open it.** selected. Each recipient proves access with an emailed code. ### Will revoking the link remove its folder? No. It ends only that public token. The source folder and its workspace access remain until separately changed. ## Related guides - [Create a secure sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Add a password to a link](/sharing/password-link) - [Disable folder downloads](/sharing/share-disable-downloads) - [Revoke a folder URL](/sharing/revoke-link) - [Collect files into a folder request](/sharing/file-request)

title: Move a protected file between folders
summary: Move a protected file only after checking its own lock, ancestor locks, destination state, assigned-root boundary, permissions, and name conflicts.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-write-gate.unit.test.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Moving a file changes its parent folder without copying its bytes or creating a new version. Protection is evaluated at both the source and destination, so test the result as the affected member. **Before moving the file** The member needs the workspace capability used for moving files. A confined member must be allowed to reach both the current and destination folders. The file cannot carry its own lock, its source ancestry cannot remain fully locked for that viewer, and the destination cannot be fully locked. If you also rename during the move, rename permission is required. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, note the file name, current folder, lock state, and the destination path. Confirm no file with the same name already exists at the destination. 2. If the source is password locked, unlock the relevant ancestor in the current browser session. The viewer unlock lasts one hour; it does not remove the folder’s protection for anyone else. 3. Open the file action menu, choose the move action, select an allowed destination, and confirm. If the web client reports **Move failed** and **The file could not be moved.**, inspect the API-specific cause listed below. 4. Refresh both folders. Verify that the file disappeared from the source and appears once at the destination with the same size and version. 5. Sign in as the intended member and retest listing, preview, download, and upload behavior under the destination’s inherited rules. **Exact refusal reasons** The server can return **This file is locked and cannot be moved**, **This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to move it.**, **Target folder is locked**, **File is already in this folder**, or **A file with this name already exists in the target folder**. Access boundaries can instead produce **This file is outside the folder you're confined to**, **You cannot move a file outside the folder you're confined to**, **You don't have permission to move files**, or **Target folder not found**. Do not remove a destination lock merely to make a move succeed unless expanding write access is intended. A successful move updates the parent relationship and activity record; it does not leave a recoverable copy in the old folder. Move the file back if the result is wrong. ## Expected result The file exists only in the chosen destination, keeps its bytes and version history, and immediately follows the destination’s inherited lock, hidden-item, role, and assigned-root rules. ## Related guides - [Lock a folder](/files/lock-folder) - [Understand inherited folder restrictions](/files/folder-restriction-inheritance)

title: Resolve a folder name conflict
summary: Resolve folder-name conflicts during create, rename, move, or restore by choosing a unique name and understanding Dosya’s automatic restore suffixes.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/rename.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/move.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/migrations/0068_folders_unique_root.sql, apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/folders.ts, apps/api/src/lib/workspace-do/schema/002_tree.ts, apps/api/src/lib/workspace-do/repo/folders.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.ts, and their conflict tests. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Dosya allows one live folder with a given name under the same parent. Creation, rename, move, and restore resolve collisions differently, so the right fix depends on which action produced the message. ## Before you start - Compare the entire breadcrumb. Identical names are allowed under different parents. - Folder names are trimmed, limited to 100 characters, and cannot be `.`, `..`, contain `/` or `\`, or include control characters. - A create field accepts a path up to 500 characters. Slashes and backslashes split that path into folder segments rather than becoming part of a folder name. - Server-side sibling matching uses SQLite’s case-sensitive `BINARY` comparison. `Foo` and `foo` are distinct folder names, so include capitalization when checking which sibling caused a conflict. ## Steps 1. Identify the action and use its rule: - **Create new folder:** entering an existing path succeeds and returns the existing leaf. `created_count` can be zero; no duplicate is made. - **Rename:** Dosya refuses the change with **A folder with this name already exists in this folder**. - **Move to folder:** Dosya leaves the source untouched and returns **A folder with this name already exists in the target folder**. - **Restore:** Dosya restores automatically as the original name, then `name (2)`, `name (3)`, through `name (99)`; a pathological larger collision set receives a timestamp suffix. 2. For a rename or move refusal, open the target parent and decide which folder should keep the desired name. 3. Rename one folder to a meaningful unique value. Avoid temporary slash-separated text because rename accepts only one segment. 4. Retry the original move or rename, then refresh the parent. 5. After restore, read the actual name in the **Restored** toast and use that name when locating the recovered tree. ## Expected result The parent contains one live row for each name. A refused rename or move changes nothing. Reusing a create path preserves the existing folder and contents. Restore keeps the recovered subtree intact while assigning only its root a free sibling name. ## Troubleshooting - **Creation says a folder exists after a concurrent request.** A rare race can return **A folder named “…” already exists here**. Refresh; if the intended path exists, open it instead of creating again. - **The name is rejected before conflict checking.** Follow **Name is required**, **Name too long (max 100)**, **Name contains invalid characters**, or the create-path equivalents naming the offending segment. - **A move still fails after renaming the target.** Confirm the source is not being moved into itself or a descendant, and that the picker has refreshed its folder tree. - **Restore used the workspace root.** The original parent is still deleted or no longer exists. Restore or recreate that parent, then move the recovered folder there. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Remove folder protection and retest access
summary: Remove only the intended folder lock, then retest inherited access, hidden rules, role permissions, assigned-root scope, shares, and sync behavior.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/lock-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/lock.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-gate.unit.test.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Selecting **Unlocked** removes the folder’s lock. It does not clear unrelated access controls, so verify each path that the affected person actually uses. **What changes** Removing **View only** restores downloads for members whose roles otherwise allow downloading. Removing **Password** restores normal browsing and writes for members with the required role capabilities. Descendants stop inheriting that lock unless another protected ancestor still applies. Existing hidden rules, assigned-root confinement, file-level locks, and workspace role permissions remain in force. ## Steps 1. Record the current folder path, lock mode, hidden state, and the role and assigned root of a representative member. 2. Open the folder’s lock dialog. Choose **Unlocked**, then apply the change. The success state says **Lock removed** and identifies the folder as open to everyone in the workspace, subject to their other access rules. 3. Refresh **Files** and reopen the folder. Test preview, download, upload, and move with the representative member rather than an owner account. 4. If the folder was password protected, open an existing share link separately. Share access never inherited the viewer’s one-hour unlock token; after removal, the link should follow its own expiry, revocation, recipient, and download settings. 5. If a sync client depends on this subtree, start a controlled sync and verify one harmless test file. Locked subtrees are omitted from sync, so removal can make previously absent content eligible. **If access is still blocked** Look upward in the path for another **Password** or **View only** ancestor. Then check whether the item itself is locked, hidden from the member, outside the member’s assigned root, or disallowed by the member’s workspace role. A hidden target may appear as **Folder not found**, which deliberately avoids revealing that it exists. Removing protection expands access immediately and is not a Trash operation. There is no restore entry for the old setting, but a permitted manager can apply a new lock again. Reapplying a password creates a new access decision; do not assume an earlier secret or browser unlock remains appropriate. ## Expected result The removed lock no longer blocks the tested action, while every unrelated role, hidden-item, assigned-root, share, and ancestor restriction continues to apply. ## Related guides - [Lock a folder](/files/lock-folder) - [Understand inherited folder restrictions](/files/folder-restriction-inheritance)

title: Understand inherited folder restrictions
summary: Trace password, view-only, hidden, and folder-scope rules from parent to child so you can explain the effective access without weakening it.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/lib/lock-mode.ts, apps/web/src/components/lock-modal.tsx, apps/web/src/components/hide-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/download-guard.ts, apps/api/src/lib/hidden/decide.ts, apps/api/src/lib/hidden/rest-gate.ts, apps/api/src/lib/sync/exclusions.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/scope.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-gate.unit.test.ts and apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-write-gate.unit.test.ts. Verified ancestor password and view-only effects, hidden-rule ancestry, per-viewer unlocks, sync/share behavior and membership folder confinement. Local source/tests only; production identities were not used.
body: A child's own badge is only part of its effective access. Dosya evaluates the item, every ancestor folder, the requesting member's role and any membership folder boundary. Diagnose access from the top of the path downward instead of changing the child first. ## Steps 1. Record the affected member, workspace and full folder path. Test with that member's account because unlock tokens and user-targeted hidden rules are identity-specific. 2. Check the membership's assigned root folder. A folder-confined member may use the anchor and its descendants only. A password cannot authorize a path above or beside that subtree. 3. Inspect every folder from the workspace root to the child. The lock dialog exposes **Unlocked**, **View only**, and **Password** for each selected folder. 4. For a **Password** ancestor, open that ancestor and submit its folder password. The correct value grants this member access for one hour. A token held by a colleague does not apply, and a public share never borrows the member token. 5. For **View only**, confirm the child can be browsed and previewed while attachment download is denied. Sync clients exclude view-only and password-locked subtrees, even though the web preview route intentionally allows view-only content. 6. Inspect hidden state with an account holding **Hide files**. An item's own **Visible** choice does not override a hidden parent. Hidden-from-everybody, selected-user and selected-role rules apply down the descendant chain. 7. Retest the actual action: list, preview, download, upload, move, delete, share or sync. Those surfaces intentionally use different gates, so a successful preview does not prove that download or mutation should succeed. A password-locked ancestor seals its subtree against new files and subfolders until that viewer unlocks it. It also blocks ordinary metadata actions, download, copy, move and delete for descendants. Share-link creation and access evaluate full locks without honoring personal unlock tokens; a member temporarily inside the vault cannot publish a path around it. View-only inheritance is narrower. It blocks downloadable bytes but leaves supported previews and browsing available. It does not use a password endpoint. Changing a child to **Unlocked** therefore cannot restore downloads while an ancestor remains **View only**. Hidden rules are visibility filters, not password challenges. Members without **Hide files** receive not-found behavior when their user, role or everyone-rule applies at the item or an ancestor. A holder of **Hide files** is privileged to see hidden content and configure it, so use a non-privileged test account to verify the audience experience. Each user/role hide configuration accepts up to 200 stored targets. When a lock is removed or changed, sync snapshot caches are invalidated so subsequent clients can reevaluate the subtree. A client may still need its normal refresh cycle. Removing a hidden rule invalidates workspace visibility state, but a remaining ancestor rule continues to hide the child. Do not solve an inherited denial by moving sensitive content to the workspace root unless that relocation is itself approved. Remove or change the controlling parent rule, or grant the correct role/scope, then test again with the affected identity. ## Expected result The child's observed behavior matches the strictest applicable parent and identity rule for the attempted surface. After a deliberate parent change, only that control disappears; unrelated workspace permissions, hidden rules and folder confinement continue to apply. ## Related guides - [Lock and hide files](/files/lock-and-hide) - [Workspace policies](/workspaces/policies)

title: Set a folder password safely
summary: Set a folder password with the exact eight-character rule, understand the one-hour viewer unlock, and test descendant, share, sync, and retry behavior.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/lock-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/lock.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/unlock.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-gate.unit.test.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A password lock closes a folder and its descendants until an authorized viewer enters the secret. Treat the password as a shared access credential and distribute it outside Dosya. **Rules to know** You need the **Lock files** workspace capability to set or replace a folder password. The password must contain at least eight characters after leading and trailing whitespace is removed; spaces inside the password count. The web form says **Use at least 8 characters.** and the API can return **Password must be at least 8 characters**. ## Steps 1. Open the intended folder and verify its full path. Check that no upload, move, share delivery, or sync job currently depends on the subtree. 2. Open the lock dialog, select **Password**, and enter a unique secret of eight or more trimmed characters. Store it in the approved password manager rather than a comment, filename, screenshot, or share message. 3. Apply the lock. A new lock reports **Locked with a password**; replacing an existing password reports **Password updated**. The new password controls future unlock attempts immediately. 4. Refresh and open the folder as a normal member. Enter the new password and confirm the folder opens. That successful viewer unlock is tied to the user and lasts 3,600 seconds. 5. Test one descendant file, one write action, and any important share or sync workflow. Full locking blocks browsing and writes inside the subtree; existing share links stop working, and locked subtrees are excluded from sync. **Failed-password limits** Five wrong passwords persistently lock further attempts for 15 minutes. The fifth wrong entry still returns **Incorrect password**; later attempts return **Too many attempts, try again later.** A separate per-isolate limit also allows five requests for the same folder and IP during 900 seconds, then responds **Too many requests** with a `Retry-After` header. Wait for the stated interval rather than repeatedly testing. Changing the password does not delete files, but it can interrupt every route into the subtree. Keep a recovery owner available. A permitted manager can select **Unlocked** without knowing the old password, so role assignment remains part of the security boundary. ## Expected result The folder and descendants require the new password, a correct entry grants that viewer one hour of browser access, and unauthorized shares, writes, downloads, and sync traversal remain blocked. ## Related guides - [Lock a folder](/files/lock-folder) - [Understand inherited folder restrictions](/files/folder-restriction-inheritance)

title: Test an inherited folder restriction
summary: Test a child item as the affected member to prove which ancestor lock, hidden rule, workspace role, or assigned-root boundary controls access.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-gate.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-write-gate.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/hidden/rest-gate.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/download-guard.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A child item may look unprotected in its own menu while an ancestor still controls it. Use a separate member account to test the effective rule, not merely the child’s stored setting. **Prepare a safe probe** Choose one non-sensitive child file and record every folder in its path. Note the member’s workspace role, assigned root, and whether any ancestor is hidden, **View only**, or **Password** protected. Owners and members with elevated hidden-item capabilities can see more than ordinary users, so they are poor test subjects. ## Steps 1. Sign in as the affected member in a private browser or separate profile. Navigate from the member’s visible root toward the child without using an owner’s cached state. 2. For a **Password** ancestor, confirm the child is unavailable before unlocking. Enter the correct password at the ancestor and retry; the viewer unlock lasts one hour for that member. 3. For a **View only** ancestor, confirm that browsing and preview work while download is refused. A child marked **Unlocked** must not bypass the ancestor. 4. Test one write operation such as upload or move. A full-password ancestor rejects writes inside the subtree even if the member’s role normally allows them. 5. Test the relevant share link and sync client independently. Share access does not consume the member’s viewer-unlock token, and both full-lock and view-only subtrees are excluded from sync. **Interpret a missing item** A missing child is not proof that the lock alone caused it. Hidden rules are inherited separately and may return **Folder not found** or omit rows. Assigned-root confinement can make a path unreachable. The member may also lack a required workspace capability such as file-page access or downloads. Change one control at a time, refresh, and repeat the same probe. If a correct password stops working, check whether the one-hour unlock expired or a manager changed the password. Do not repeatedly guess: five wrong entries can produce a 15-minute persistent lock, while a separate per-isolate request limit can return **Too many requests** with `Retry-After`. ## Expected result The test identifies the controlling ancestor or workspace boundary, and the child follows that rule consistently for browsing, preview, download, writes, shares, and sync. ## Related guides - [Lock a folder](/files/lock-folder) - [Understand inherited folder restrictions](/files/folder-restriction-inheritance)

title: Understanding Free-plan allowances
summary: Understand Free storage, protocol transfer, share-link, workspace, member and retention allowances, where to check usage and what happens when a limit is reached.
verification: Reviewed the production Fair use on the Free plan page and pricing page on 2026-10-12 and checked the current local web-app storage indicator. The published table confirmed 5 GB permanent base storage, referral storage, credential transfer and concurrency allowances, API-key and webhook counts, share-link download and active-link allowances, owned workspace and member counts, all 46 location choices, and Free retention windows. Paid-plan prices were deliberately not copied because the live pricing page is the current source.
body: The Free plan is permanent and starts with 5 GB of storage. It has no card requirement, expiry or countdown. Referrals can add 5 GB each for up to five referrals, giving up to 25 GB of additional storage under the current published policy. Every product feature remains available on Free, including the apps, API, WebDAV, S3, SFTP, share links and Vault. Fair-use allowances limit sustained transfer, object counts, team size and history retention. Check the live [Fair use page](https://dosya.dev/fair-use/) before designing an automated or high-volume workflow because allowances can change after this guide's review date. ## Before you start - Confirm that the active workspace shown in the web app is the one whose storage you want to inspect. - Separate **storage used** from **data transferred**. A 2 GB file stored once uses about 2 GB of storage; downloading or transferring it later can count against a daily transfer allowance without creating another stored copy. - Separate direct app use from a credential. API, WebDAV and S3 allowances apply per credential on Free, while public share-link downloads are counted per account. - Use the live [pricing page](https://dosya.dev/pricing/) for current paid-plan capacity and price. ## Steps: check which allowance applies 1. Open the web app and read the active workspace name at the top of the sidebar. 2. Check the storage indicator at the bottom of the sidebar for that workspace's used and available capacity. 3. Identify the action that stopped: an API or protocol transfer, a share-link download, creation of a key or link, a workspace invitation, or access to older history. 4. Match it to the table below and read whether the allowance resets, frees when an item expires or is removed, or requires a different plan. 5. Read the message shown by Dosya before retrying. A daily allowance resumes after its window resets; an object cap usually requires an old object to be removed or allowed to expire. ## Current Free allowances The following values were reviewed on 2026-10-12: | Area | Free allowance | What frees or resets it | | --- | --- | --- | | Base storage | 5 GB, permanent | Delete data you no longer need, empty trash when appropriate, add referral storage or change plan. | | Referral storage | 5 GB per referral, up to 5 referrals | Added capacity is governed by the referral program; see the account's referral screen for status. | | API, WebDAV and S3 per credential | 60 requests per minute, 5 GB transfer per day, 2 concurrent transfers | Minute and daily windows reset; a running transfer is allowed to finish. | | API keys | 3 | Delete a key that is no longer used, then create another. | | Webhook endpoints | 3 in total | Delete an unused endpoint, then create another. | | Share-link downloads | 10 GB per day per account | The daily window resets. Visitors see a temporary busy page after the allowance is used. | | Active share links | 5 at a time, each for up to 7 days | Revoke an unused link or wait for one to expire. | | Workspaces you own | 3 | Existing workspaces remain. Ownership of another person's workspace does not count unless you own it. | | Members in each workspace | 5 including you | Remove an unneeded member or change plan. Membership in someone else's workspace is not part of the three-workspace ownership cap. | | Storage locations | All 46 published locations | Choose at workspace creation; the plan does not reduce the catalog. | | Version history | 7 days and the newest 10 versions by default | Scheduled cleanup removes older versions; the current file version remains. Workspace policy can affect the version-count cap. | | Trash | 7 days | Deleted files are permanently removed after the retention window. | | Activity history | 7 days | Older activity leaves the visible retention window. | ## What happens when an allowance is reached Fair-use transfer allowances pause further work instead of slowing every transfer. Requests over a limit are refused until its time window resets, and a share link can show a temporary busy page. A transfer already in flight is allowed to finish. Reaching a transfer allowance does not delete files or revoke the credential. Count limits behave differently. At three API keys, for example, existing keys keep working but another cannot be created until one is deleted or the plan changes. At five active Free share links, existing links remain active; revoke one or wait for expiry before creating another. Retention is scheduled cleanup, not a usage counter. A Free file version older than the retention window can be removed automatically, trash is permanently emptied on its schedule, and old activity leaves the visible history. The current version of a live file is not removed by version-history cleanup. ## No egress fee does not mean unlimited Free transfer Dosya does not add a per-gigabyte egress charge to your bill. The Free plan still has documented daily fair-use allowances for API or protocol credentials and public share-link downloads. When one is reached, work pauses until the relevant window resets; it does not produce a surprise transfer charge. Paid plans currently show no default plan metering for API, WebDAV and S3, and unmetered share-link downloads. General abuse and safety rate limits can still apply to every plan. Check the developer reference for a protocol workload and contact support before treating a personal storage account as a public distribution backend. ## Expected result You can identify whether storage capacity, a time-based transfer allowance, an object count or a retention window explains the behavior. You know where the current workspace storage is shown and whether to wait for a reset, remove an unused item, restore something still inside retention or review the live paid plans. ## Limits and review date This guide records the public policy reviewed on 2026-10-12. The production [Fair use page](https://dosya.dev/fair-use/) and [pricing page](https://dosya.dev/pricing/) are authoritative for later changes. Exact reset timing and the relevant counter are communicated by the product or protocol response; do not assume that creating another credential changes an account-level share allowance. ## Troubleshooting **An upload says there is not enough storage.** Check the active workspace and its sidebar indicator. Remove unneeded data, review trash and stored versions, or add capacity. Switching workspace changes which capacity is displayed. **An API, WebDAV or S3 client receives a rate-limit response.** Stop automatic rapid retries. Each Free credential currently has request, daily transfer and concurrency allowances. Allow existing transfers to finish and retry after the indicated minute or daily window. **A public share link shows a temporary busy page.** The account may have served its 10 GB daily Free share-link allowance. The link and source file remain intact; visitors can return after the daily window resets. **Dosya will not create another share link.** Free allows five active links at a time. Revoke an unused link or wait for its expiry. Free links can last up to seven days. **Dosya will not create another workspace or invite another member.** Free currently allows ownership of three workspaces and five members per workspace including the owner. Reaching a cap does not remove existing workspaces or members. **An old version, deleted file or activity entry is missing.** Check the applicable seven-day Free retention window. Restore items before the deadline; expired history cannot be brought back by changing plan after cleanup. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does the Free plan expire? No. The published Free plan is permanent, starts with 5 GB and does not require a card. ### Are features disabled on Free? The current policy makes the product features available on every plan. Free differs through allowances, object counts, team size and shorter retention. ### Will Dosya charge me after I transfer too much data? No per-gigabyte egress charge is added. The relevant Free allowance pauses further requests or downloads until it resets. ### Does joining someone else's workspace use one of my three owned workspaces? No. The published cap is on workspaces you own. ## Related guides - [Creating an account and verifying your email](/account/create-and-verify-account) - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Creating a workspace and choosing its storage location](/workspaces/create-and-choose-region) - [Creating and protecting an API key](/developers/api-key)

title: Hide a folder from selected roles
summary: Hide a folder from everyone, selected users, or selected roles; understand inherited visibility, permission checks, target limits, and recovery.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/hide-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/hide.ts, apps/api/src/lib/hidden/decide.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/hidden/rest-gate.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Hiding changes who can discover a folder and its descendants. It is separate from locking: no password is created, and the folder remains usable by viewers who are not hidden from it. **Available modes** The **Hide folder** dialog offers **Visible**, **Hidden from everybody**, **Hidden from specific users**, and **Hidden from specific roles**. Targeted modes accept up to 200 users or roles. Your own user or role is disabled so you cannot deliberately hide the folder from your current identity. You need the **Hide files** capability; the API otherwise returns **You don't have permission to hide folders**. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, confirm the exact folder path and list the people or roles that must lose visibility. Remember that the rule is inherited by descendants. 2. Open the folder menu and choose the hide action. Select the narrowest mode that matches the requirement. 3. For a targeted mode, select at least one user or role. The web form shows **Select at least one user.** or **Select at least one role.** when empty; the API may answer **You must select at least one user** or **You must select at least one role**. 4. Choose **Apply**. The current success toast uses **File hidden** and **This file is now hidden.** even when the target is a folder. 5. Sign in as one affected member and one unaffected member. Refresh **Files**, search, map results, and direct folder navigation to verify both outcomes. **Visibility and recovery** Affected members may see **Folder not found** rather than an explanation, preventing the interface from disclosing a hidden name. People with the privileged hidden-item capability can still see protected content. Lock modes, assigned roots, and workspace roles continue to apply independently to anyone who remains able to see it. Hiding is reversible. To restore discovery, reopen the dialog as a permitted manager, choose **Visible**, apply, and have the member refresh. The action does not move content to Trash or erase bytes, but an overly broad rule can immediately remove an entire subtree from eligible members’ lists and navigation. ## Expected result The folder and descendants disappear only for the selected audience, remain visible to permitted viewers, and return after the mode is changed to Visible and clients refresh. ## Related guides - [Lock and hide files](/files/lock-and-hide) - [Workspace policies](/workspaces/policies)

title: Review account identity and sign-in methods
summary: Confirm the account email, determine whether a password exists, and add email-and-password sign-in safely to an OAuth-created account without lockout.
verification: Reviewed locally from apps/web/src/pages/profile/identity.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/profile/password.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/password.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/login.tsx. This source-only check made no live sign-in or provider request.
body: Dosya supports email and password plus **Continue with Google**, **Continue with GitHub**, and **Continue with Apple** on the sign-in page. The profile does not provide a connected-provider list or a disconnect button. It exposes the verified account email and whether the account currently has a usable password. An account created through Google, GitHub, or Apple can show **Password — Not set**. In that state, **Set a password** adds email-and-password sign-in to the same account; it does not remove the provider sign-in. The password must contain **8 to 256 characters**. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Identity** and read **Email address**. A **Verified** badge means the stored address has completed verification; **Unverified** means it has not. 2. Open **Profile → Password & 2FA**. 3. If the **Password** row offers **Change password**, the account already supports email-and-password sign-in. 4. If it shows **Not set**, select **Set a password**. Enter **New password** and **Confirm new password**, using at least 8 and no more than 256 characters. 5. Select **Set a password** in the dialog. The success message says **Password set — You can now sign in with your email and password too.** 6. Keep the current session open and use a private browser window to sign in with the email from **Identity** and the new password. ## Rules and effects OAuth-created accounts do not need a current password when setting their first one. Accounts that already have a password must use **Change password** and provide **Current password**. A successful password update keeps the requesting credential and revokes other browser and mobile sessions, so be prepared to sign in again on those devices. Two-factor authentication cannot be enabled from a no-password state in the web profile, because disabling it later requires password verification. Set the password first, then configure email or authenticator-app 2FA. The last-used badge on the sign-in page is stored in that browser and is only a convenience hint. It is not an authoritative inventory of identity providers attached to the account. ## Troubleshooting **Passwords do not match** means the two new values differ. **Password too short** is shown below 8 characters. If a private-window test fails, keep the original session open, confirm the email again, and use [Reset a password](/account/reset-password) rather than repeatedly guessing. ## Expected result You know the account's verified email and password status, and any new password signs into that same account without removing Google, GitHub, or Apple access. ## Related guides - [Update profile settings](/account/profile-settings) - [Reset a password](/account/reset-password) - [Use two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor)

title: Importing files and folders from Dropbox
summary: Connect a Dropbox account, choose files or folders, and check the imported copies in the selected Dosya workspace.
verification: Verified in production on 2026-10-11 with an existing connected Dropbox account: root browsing, one-file submission, a 9 KB SVG transfer into the selected workspace root, and the completed Files row with Import origin.
