Reviewed source for connection consent, unsupported types, source dates, cancellation and disconnect. The provider OAuth grant screen and team-space behavior were not repeated. Production screenshots replace account identifiers and source names for privacy. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Open **Integrations → Dropbox** in the web app, select **Connect Dropbox**, then use **Import from Dropbox** to choose files or folders. Imports from this setup page go to the selected workspace's top level. Check the completed copies in **Files** before treating your migration as finished. ## Before you start - Sign in to [the Dosya app](https://app.dosya.dev) and select the workspace that should receive the import. - Have the Dropbox account containing the files you intend to copy. - Your workspace role needs upload permission. Available storage and workspace file-type and size policies also apply to imports. - Start with a small folder or a few disposable files whose names are not already present at the destination. - This workflow adds ordinary workspace files. It does not place imports in the Vault, and it does not require a Dosya API key. ## Steps: connect Dropbox 1. **Open the setup page.** Select **Integrations** in the sidebar, then **Dropbox**, or open [Dropbox setup](https://app.dosya.dev/integrations/dropbox). 2. **Check the workspace.** Confirm the selected workspace before importing. The setup page does not include a destination-folder chooser. 3. **Select Connect Dropbox.** Continue through Dropbox's sign-in and connection screens using the intended account. Review the provider's request and complete the connection if it matches your intent. 4. **Check Connected accounts on return.** The account's email and Connected time label should appear on the setup page. A successful connection returns you here; it does not start an import by itself. 5. **Connect another account if needed.** Repeat **Connect Dropbox**. Each connected account appears separately. ## Steps: select and import 1. **Open the picker.** Select **Import from Dropbox**, or **Import** beside a connected account to start with that account selected. 2. **Choose the source account when offered.** If more than one Dropbox account is connected, the selector shows their email addresses. Switching accounts clears the current selection. 3. **Browse from Home.** Select a folder's name to open it. Use the breadcrumb buttons to return to a parent folder, and **Load more** when another page of items is available. 4. **Select files or folders with the checkboxes.** Checking a folder selects its whole subtree, including the selected folder itself. Selections remain while you browse other folders. Items marked **Cannot be imported** have disabled checkboxes. 5. **Check the destination footer.** It shows the number selected and **importing into workspace root**. This means the selected workspace's top level, not whichever Dosya folder you last viewed. 6. **Select Import.** The picker closes after the job starts, and **Import started** identifies the source account. Using **Cancel** in the picker before this step abandons the selection without creating a job. ## Steps: confirm the result 1. **Check progress.** The setup page shows active Dropbox imports; **Files** shows active cloud imports across providers. Preparation counts can grow while the folder tree is prepared. Transfer progress can show file counts, bytes and, once enough samples exist, speed and an estimated remaining time. 2. **Return when needed.** A started cloud import runs in the background and can continue after the browser tab closes. Reopen the Dropbox setup page or Files to check its current state. 3. **Check the completion message.** **Import complete** can include failed or skipped counts. Review them before assuming every selected item succeeded. 4. **Open Files in the destination workspace.** Check the top level, selected folders, nested structure and filenames. Open a few imported copies to check the result before continuing with a larger migration. ## Expected result Selected files appear at the workspace's top level. Selected folders appear there with their nested folder structure. Original items remain in Dropbox. The imported copies do not automatically follow later Dropbox changes. The import creates new files. It does not recreate Dropbox sharing settings, version history or the surrounding Dropbox collaboration workflow. Keep your original copies until you have checked the result. ## Limitations Only downloadable Dropbox files and folders are supported. Paper and other cloud-native items reported as non-downloadable are marked **Cannot be imported**. Such items found inside a selected folder can be skipped even though the parent folder was selectable. Export or download an appropriate file through Dropbox when available, then [upload it to Dosya](/uploading/files-and-folders). The picker browses the connected account's root and folders. It does not offer a separate team-space or namespace chooser. Confirm that any required team folder appears and can be selected; do not assume a team-account connection will include every area visible in Dropbox. Folders reuse an existing live destination folder with the same name. Two source folders with the same name at the same destination can therefore merge into that one folder. A file with the same destination name as an existing file can fail; the importer does not offer an overwrite or automatic rename choice. Check existing copies before submitting the same selection again. Files discovered inside selected folders carry Dropbox's reported original modification date when available, otherwise its server modification date. Files selected directly do not carry those source dates through the picker. Dropbox supplies no original creation date for this workflow or dates for folders, so those dates can show the import time. Do not use identical dates as the only check that a migration succeeded. You can select up to **500 files or folders** in one submission. A selected folder can contain more items; the limit counts the selected starting items, not every nested file. Storage, workspace file policies, Dropbox restrictions and temporary throttling can still prevent individual transfers. ## Cancel, retry or disconnect Use **Cancel** on an active import's progress card to stop that job. Completed files and created folders remain in Dosya. Cancellation does not undo those copies. Temporary throttling waits and retries automatically. The picker shows a retry notice for a throttled listing and **Retry** for an ordinary listing error. Transfer items retry ordinary temporary failures automatically, up to three attempts. A failed or cancelled job has no manual **Resume** or **Retry** button in this interface. Correct the cause, check completed files, then start a new selection for the missing items. Use **Disconnect** beside the account on this setup page or in **Profile → Integrations** to remove the saved connection. Cancel an active import first. Disconnect removes the connection and its import history; completed files remain. Dropbox's own app permissions are managed separately, so do not treat this button as confirmation that Dropbox's grant was revoked. ## Troubleshooting **The picker says No account connected yet.** Select **Connect an account**, finish the Dropbox connection, and check Connected accounts before trying again. **The connection returns an error.** Check that you used the intended Dropbox account. An expired sign-in attempt needs a fresh **Connect Dropbox** attempt. If you declined the connection, try again only when you intend to complete it. For a repeated provider or saving error, send the displayed message and time to [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support). **The account needs reconnecting.** Use **Reconnect** when the picker offers it. A job already failed because its connection expired does not resume automatically after reconnection. Check its completed files before starting another selection. **Import is unavailable or fails to start.** Select at least one supported item and a workspace. Check upload permission and whether the account is still connected. A start failure keeps the picker open and shows an error, preserving the current selection. **Paper or a team folder is missing.** Check the limits above. A non-downloadable item cannot be made importable by selecting its parent repeatedly. Confirm the Dropbox source account and the folders actually shown by the picker. **The result is incomplete.** Check failed and skipped counts, storage and workspace policies. A source item moved or removed during the job can fail, as can a filename already present at the destination. Check the files already imported before starting another job. ## Frequently asked questions ### Is this a continuous Dropbox sync? No. It creates copies of the selected items. Later changes in Dropbox do not automatically update those imported copies. ### Can I import Dropbox Paper? Paper and other items that Dropbox reports as non-downloadable are unsupported. If Dropbox offers an export for the item, export an appropriate file and upload it separately. ### Can I choose a destination folder or close the tab? This setup page imports into the selected workspace's root and has no destination-folder chooser. After **Import started**, the job can continue after the tab closes. Return to the setup page or Files to check the result. ### Does Disconnect delete my copies? No. Completed copies remain in Dosya. Cancel an active import first, then use Disconnect to remove its saved account connection and import history. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders), for files you downloaded or exported separately. - [API key management](/developers/api-key), for separate protocol or tool integrations; the built-in Dropbox importer does not need one.

title: Importing files and folders from Google Drive
summary: Import Google Drive copies into the selected workspace, understand document conversions and exact transfer limits, and recover incomplete jobs without resubmitting successful files.
verification: Verified in production on 2026-10-11 with an existing connected Google account: account selection, root browsing, unsupported-item labels, one-file submission, a 1.3 MB ODT transfer into the selected workspace root, and the completed Files row with Import origin. Preserve four production captures and original narrow verification scope; new details source-reviewed, no new production mutation. Official references: https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files/export; https://support.google.com/drive/answer/9700156?hl=en; https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/scopes#drive.
body:
In the web app, open **Integrations → Google Drive**, select **Connect Google Drive**, then use **Import from Google Drive** to choose files or folders. Imports from this setup page go to the selected workspace's top level. Check the completed copies in **Files** before treating your migration as finished. ## Before you start - Sign in to [the Dosya app](https://app.dosya.dev) and select the workspace that should receive the import. - Have the Google account containing the items you want to copy. Connecting Drive is a separate step from signing in to Dosya with Google. - Your workspace role needs upload permission. Available storage and workspace file-type and size policies also apply to imports. - Start with a small folder or a few disposable files with names that are not already present at the destination. - This workflow adds ordinary workspace files. It does not place imports in the Vault, and it does not require you to create a Dosya API key. ## Steps: connect Google Drive 1. **Open the setup page.** Select **Integrations** in the sidebar, then **Google Drive**, or open [Google Drive setup](https://app.dosya.dev/integrations/google). 2. **Check the workspace.** Confirm the selected workspace before importing. The setup page does not include a destination-folder chooser. 3. **Select Connect Google Drive.** The requested Drive permission is read-only, with email/profile identity and offline access so background imports can use a refreshed token. Continue through Google's sign-in and connection screens using the intended Google account. Review the provider's request and complete the connection if it matches your intent. 4. **Check Connected accounts on return.** The account's email and Connected time label should appear on the setup page. A successful connection returns you here; it does not start an import by itself. 5. **Connect another account if needed.** Repeat **Connect Google Drive** for another account. Each connected account is listed separately. Connections belong to your Dosya user, so selecting a different workspace does not create another Google connection; choose the destination workspace separately for each import. ## Steps: select and import 1. **Open the picker.** Select **Import from Google Drive**, or **Import** beside a connected account to start with that account selected. 2. **Choose the source account when offered.** If more than one Google account is connected, the selector shows their email addresses. Switching accounts clears the current selection. 3. **Browse from Home.** Select a folder's name to open it. Use the breadcrumb buttons to return to a parent folder, and **Load more** when another page of items is available. A listing requests up to 100 entries per page; an empty or short page is not a complete directory while another page is offered. 4. **Use the checkboxes to select items.** Checking a folder selects its whole subtree, including the selected folder itself. You can keep selections while browsing other folders. Items marked **Cannot be imported** have disabled checkboxes. 5. **Review Google document conversions.** Supported Google documents show a **will import as** extension. Check the format table below before selecting them. 6. **Check the footer.** It shows the number selected and **importing into workspace root**. This means the selected workspace's top level, not whichever Dosya folder you last viewed. 7. **Select Import.** The picker closes after the job starts, and **Import started** identifies the source account. Closing the picker with **Cancel** before this step abandons the selection without starting a job. ## Steps: confirm the result 1. **Check progress.** The setup page shows that provider's active imports; **Files** shows active cloud imports across providers. Preparation counts can grow while the folder tree is being prepared. Transfer progress can show file counts, bytes and, once enough progress samples exist, speed and an estimated remaining time. 2. **Return when needed.** A started cloud import runs in the background, so it can continue after the browser tab closes. Reopen the provider setup page or Files to check its current state. 3. **Check the completion message.** **Import complete** can include failed or skipped counts. It does not establish that every selected item succeeded when those counts are present. 4. **Open Files in the destination workspace.** Check the top level, folder structure, filenames and the converted document formats. Open a few imported copies and check that they match your intended result. ## Expected result Selected files appear at the workspace's top level. Selected folders appear there with their nested folder structure. Original items remain in Google Drive. The imported copies do not automatically follow later changes in Drive. The import creates new files; it does not recreate Google sharing settings, document revision history or the surrounding Google collaboration workflow. Keep your original copies until you have checked the result. ## Google documents, shortcuts and limits The current importer chooses these export formats automatically:
Google itemImported format
Google DocsPDF (.pdf)
Google SheetsExcel workbook (.xlsx)
Google SlidesPDF (.pdf)
Google DrawingsPDF (.pdf)
There is no export-format selector in the import dialog. Other Google-native types, including Google Forms, are unsupported. Ordinary uploaded files retain their existing file format. The Drive connection requests read-only access, so this import cannot delete or edit your Google originals. Google limits the exported result from the document-export endpoint to **10 MB**. This is a Google document-export limit, not a general 10 MB limit for ordinary Drive files. If a document export fails, try downloading an appropriate format through Google and then [uploading it to Dosya](/uploading/files-and-folders). See [Google's export endpoint documentation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files/export). The picker starts from your Drive root. It has no separate **Shared with me** or **Shared drives** selector. The importer supports a reachable shortcut's target, including a folder, but the original target must still be available to the connected Google account. A shortcut in My Drive can make a shared item reachable; it does not change the original item's Google permissions. Follow [Google's shortcut guidance](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/9700156?hl=en) and confirm the item appears in the picker before relying on it. A broken shortcut may be unavailable or fail during import. Folders reuse an existing live destination folder with the same name. Two source folders with the same name at the same destination can therefore merge into that one folder. A file with the same destination name as an existing file can fail; the importer does not offer an overwrite or automatic rename choice. Use a clear destination and check results before submitting the same selection again. You can select up to **500 files or folders** in one submission. A selected folder can contain more items; the limit counts the selected starting items, not every nested file. Storage, file policies, Google restrictions and temporary service throttling can still prevent individual transfers. The importer checks workspace file extensions and maximum size against the final exported filename, and checks actual transferred bytes against available storage. Ordinary known-size files use ranged transfer from 10 MiB upward; streamed exports or unreported-size content have a 32 MiB safety bound in the importer, in addition to Google’s export limit. These are transfer-path limits, not a 32 MiB cap on every Drive file. ## Cancel, retry or disconnect Use **Cancel** on an active import's progress card to stop that job. Completed files and created folders remain in Dosya; cancellation does not undo the imported copies. Check Files before starting another job. Temporary throttling waits and retries automatically. A Google 429 uses its Retry-After delay, or 30 seconds when none is supplied; recognized Google quota-related 403 responses also wait 30 seconds. These delays do not consume an item’s three ordinary failure attempts. The picker shows a retry notice for a throttled listing and **Retry** for an ordinary listing error. Transfer items also retry ordinary temporary failures automatically, up to three attempts. File-type/size policy refusals and backup-lock errors fail the affected item immediately. Lost workspace membership stops the job. Progress and completion have no fixed timing guarantee: folder discovery, provider delays, file bytes and destination checks determine duration. A failed or cancelled job has no manual **Resume** or **Retry** button in this interface. Correct the cause, check completed files, then start a new selection for the missing items. To remove the connection, use **Disconnect** beside the account on this setup page or in **Profile → Integrations**. Cancel an active import first. Disconnect removes the saved connection and its import history; completed files remain. Deleting completed copies afterward uses Dosya’s ordinary file/Trash controls and does not remove the originals from Drive. Permanent purge of a Dosya copy is irreversible. Provider-side app permissions are managed separately in Google, so do not treat this button as confirmation that Google's grant was revoked. ## Troubleshooting **The picker says No account connected yet.** Select **Connect an account**, finish the Google connection, and check Connected accounts before trying again. A Google sign-in to Dosya alone does not complete this connection. **The connection returns an error.** An expired sign-in attempt needs a fresh **Connect Google Drive** attempt. If you declined the connection, try again only when you intend to complete it. For a repeated provider or saving error, record the displayed message and time for [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support). **The account needs reconnecting.** A message such as **Google Drive access was revoked or is insufficient for download. Please reconnect.** means provider authentication needs attention. Use **Reconnect** when the picker offers it. An import already failed because its connection expired does not resume automatically after reconnection; check its completed files before starting another selection. **Import is unavailable or fails to start.** **Select at least one file or folder**, **Select at most 500 items at once**, **No upload permission** and **Not a member of this workspace** identify selection or access refusals. Select at least one supported item and a workspace. Check upload permission, whether the account is still connected and any error message. A start failure keeps the picker open so you can correct the issue without losing the current selection. **An item is missing or skipped.** Confirm the source account, folder and any Google shortcut target. Check the supported-type table and Google download/export restrictions. Items found inside a selected folder can be skipped even though the parent folder was selectable. **The result is incomplete.** Check failed and skipped counts, storage and workspace policies. Existing filenames and failed Google exports are possible causes. Do not resubmit a whole large folder without checking the copies already present. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I import directly into a chosen Dosya folder? The current Google setup page imports into the selected workspace's root. It does not offer a destination-folder chooser. Organize completed copies in Files afterward, subject to your role's permissions. ### Can I close the tab during an import? Yes, after **Import started**. The background job continues independently of that tab. Return to the setup page or Files to check completion and any failures. ### Will Google Docs stay editable as Google Docs? The current importer creates PDFs for Docs, Slides and Drawings, and XLSX workbooks for Sheets. It does not create a Google-native editing session in Dosya or offer other export formats in this picker. ### Does cancelling or disconnecting remove completed copies? No. Completed files remain. Cancel stops an active job; Disconnect removes the saved account connection and import history. Check the destination separately if you want to organize or remove its copies. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders), for files you downloaded or exported separately. - [API key management](/developers/api-key), for separate protocol or tool integrations; the built-in Drive importer does not need one.

The picker shows a retry notice for a throttled listing and **Retry** for an ordinary listing error. Transfer items retry ordinary temporary failures automatically, up to three attempts. A failed or cancelled job has no manual **Resume** or **Retry** button in this interface. Correct the cause, check completed files, then start a new selection for the missing items. Use **Disconnect** beside the account on this setup page or in **Profile → Integrations** to remove the saved connection. Cancel an active import first. Disconnect removes that connection and its import history; completed files remain. Microsoft's own app permissions are managed separately, so do not treat this button as confirmation that Microsoft's grant was revoked. ## Troubleshooting **The picker says No account connected yet.** Select **Connect an account**, finish the Microsoft connection, and check Connected accounts before trying again. **Microsoft sign-in or connection is refused.** Check that you selected the intended account. A work/school organization may have its own app policy; ask its administrator about the displayed Microsoft error. An expired sign-in attempt needs a fresh **Connect OneDrive** attempt. Persistent configuration errors should go to [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) with the time and displayed message. **The account needs reconnecting.** Use **Reconnect** when the picker offers it. A job already failed because its connection expired does not resume automatically after reconnection. Check its completed files before starting another selection. **Import is unavailable or fails to start.** Select at least one supported item and a workspace. Check upload permission and whether the account is still connected. A start failure keeps the picker open and shows an error, preserving the current selection. **A OneNote notebook or shared library is missing.** Check the limits above. Repeatedly selecting its parent folder does not make an unsupported item importable. For a missing ordinary file, confirm the account, source folder and any Microsoft download restriction. **The result is incomplete.** Check failed and skipped counts, storage and workspace policies. Existing filenames and unavailable source items can prevent a transfer. Check the files already present before starting another job. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I use a personal Microsoft account? The connection is designed for both personal and work/school accounts. Complete the connection with the account that contains the OneDrive files, and check its email under Connected accounts. ### Do Office files need conversion? Ordinary Word, Excel and PowerPoint files are imported in their existing file formats. OneNote notebooks are a separate unsupported package type. ### Can I close the tab or resume a cancelled job? A started import can continue after the tab closes. Cancellation is different: it stops that job, and there is no Resume control. Check completed copies and start a new selection for missing items when appropriate. ### Can I choose a destination folder or preserve Microsoft sharing? This setup page imports into the selected workspace's root and does not offer a destination-folder chooser. It creates file copies without recreating Microsoft sharing settings. Organize or share completed copies in Dosya separately. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders), for files you downloaded or exported separately. - [API key management](/developers/api-key), for separate protocol or tool integrations; the built-in OneDrive importer does not need one.

title: Inviting people to a workspace
summary: Open Team, choose an email invitation or an invite link, assign a role, and check whether the invitation has been accepted.
verification: Reviewed the current Team invitation dialog and a pending invitation against the isolated local current app and API on 2026-10-10. Real screenshots reviewed. The pending invitation was created through the local API with a test email adapter; inbox delivery, recipient acceptance, invite-link joins and production were not browser verified.
body: Select the workspace you want to share, open **Team**, then select **Invite to workspace**. Use **Email invite** for an invitation bound to a particular email address, or **Invite link** for a link people can use to join under the role and limits you choose. An invitation adds someone to a workspace after they accept it. It is different from sending a link to one file. ## Before you start - Sign in and select the correct workspace in the app's workspace switcher. Confirm the workspace name on the **Team** page before sending anything. - You need the workspace's permission to invite members. If **Invite to workspace** is unavailable, ask the workspace owner about your role. - Choose the access the recipient needs. The role selector only offers roles you may grant; you cannot grant permissions beyond your own or invite someone as **Owner**. - Workspace membership limits and allowed email-domain policies can restrict invitations or joins. Read any refusal message before retrying. ## Steps: invite specific email addresses 1. **Open the workspace's Team page.** Select **Team** in the workspace navigation, or open [Team](https://app.dosya.dev/teams) after selecting the workspace. Confirm its name in the workspace badge. 2. **Open the invitation dialog.** Select **Invite to workspace** near the page heading. A workspace with only you as a member also offers **Invite someone** in its empty state. Both open the same dialog. 3. **Choose Email invite.** In the **Invite to workspace** dialog, select **Email invite**. 4. **Add the recipients.** Enter an address in **Email addresses** and press Enter to add it. Repeat for each person. Check the address chips and remove a mistaken address with its small remove control. Each recipient gets a separate invitation tied to that email address. 5. **Choose Role.** Select the role each person in this batch should receive. If people need different roles, send separate batches. The page's **Role guide** explains the built-in roles; custom roles may also appear in the selector. 6. **Send the invitations.** Select **Send invite**. Successful requests show **Invites sent**. The email invitation expires after seven days. If only some addresses fail, the dialog keeps those failed addresses so you can correct or retry them. 7. **Check Pending invites.** Back on **Team**, find the recipients under **Pending invites** and check their roles and expiry. Sending an invitation does not immediately turn that recipient into a member. 8. **Have each recipient accept.** They open their invitation, check the workspace and role, sign in or create an account using the invited email address, and select **Accept invitation**. After acceptance, reload **Team** and confirm their entry under **Members**. ## Steps: create an invite link 1. **Open the same dialog.** On **Team**, select **Invite to workspace**, then select **Invite link**. 2. **Set the role.** Choose **Role for new members**. Everyone who joins through this link receives that role. 3. **Set the link's limits.** Choose **Max uses** and **Expires**. The expiry starts at **7 days**. You can select another offered duration; **Unlimited** uses and **Never** expiry are available, so review both fields deliberately. 4. **Create and copy it.** Select **Create invite link**. Under **Share this link**, use the copy button beside the generated URL. Send it privately to the intended recipients. 5. **Check joins and remaining use.** The **Invite links** section lists the link, its role and use count. Recipients still need to sign in and accept the invitation. Workspace email-domain and membership policies can prevent a join even while the link exists. An invite link is not bound to one recipient's email address. Someone who receives it can forward it. Choose a role, expiry and maximum use count appropriate to that possibility. ## Expected result For an email invitation, **Pending invites** shows the invitation until the recipient accepts or it becomes unavailable. After a successful acceptance, **Members** shows the person with the assigned role. For an invite link, the link appears under **Invite links** and its use count increases as eligible people join. The member's role governs their workspace permissions. ## Manage pending invitations In **Pending invites**, use **Copy link** to send the person's email-bound invitation yourself, **Resend** to request another invitation email, or **Revoke** to invalidate it. Email-invite revocation opens **Revoke invite**; check the recipient and select **Revoke** to confirm. In **Invite links**, use **Revoke** to stop future joins through that link. This link action starts directly without the email-invite confirmation dialog. Revoking an invitation does not remove someone who has already become a member. ## Limitations - A successful invitation request does not prove that an email has reached the recipient's inbox. Check the pending row and use its copy or resend controls when delivery needs attention. - Only the invited email address can accept an email invitation. An invite link uses a different joining workflow. - Invitation controls do not transfer workspace ownership. **Owner** is not an invitation role. - The invitation dialog selects a role, not a folder restriction. Members with the separate role-management permission can configure a member's folder access afterward; do not assume an invitation is folder-limited. - Plans and workspace policies can limit membership. An invite link does not bypass those restrictions. ## Troubleshooting If you see **An invite is already pending for this email**, find the existing row and use **Copy link** or **Resend**. If the person is already a member, review their member entry instead of repeatedly inviting them. For an expired or revoked email invitation, issue a fresh invitation after checking the recipient and role. If **Resend** reports a cooldown, wait as directed by the message. If sending is rate-limited, retry later rather than repeatedly submitting the same addresses. If a recipient cannot accept, check that they signed in with the invited address, that the link is still valid, and that the workspace's member and email-domain policies allow them to join. Use [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) for a persistent access problem. Include the workspace name and error message; do not post live invitation URLs in public comments. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I invite someone who does not have a Dosya account? Yes. They can create an account before accepting. For an email-bound invitation, that account's email address must match the invitation. ### Why is a role missing from the invitation selector? You can only grant roles whose permissions fit within your own. The workspace's owner can review the role or send the invitation. Ownership itself is transferred through a separate workflow. ### Does revoking a link remove people who used it? No. Revocation prevents subsequent acceptance or joins. A person who already joined is a workspace member; review that member's access separately. ## Related guides - [Creating a sharing link for a file](/sharing/create-link) - [Watch the existing team invitation tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/invite-your-team/) - [Watch the existing roles and permissions tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/set-roles-and-permissions/) - [Watch the existing workspace policies tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/set-workspace-limits-and-policies/)

title: Find invoices and update payment details
summary: Find recent and upcoming Stripe invoices, securely download available PDFs, inspect the charged card, and open the portal for payment changes.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/api/billing.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/portal.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts on 2026-10-14. Production Stripe records were not opened.
body: Billing combines the active subscription, default-card hint, recent invoice history, and links into Stripe’s protected portal. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing** and read the **Subscription** price, interval, renewal/end date, status badge, and masked card when present. 2. Review **Next invoice [amount] on [date]** for a noncancelling subscription. This is Stripe’s upcoming estimate and can change. 3. In **Invoices**, match a period, amount and status. Dosya requests 12 Stripe invoices, excludes draft and void entries, and provides **Download PDF** only when Stripe returns a PDF URL. 4. Select **Open Stripe portal** for Stripe-hosted billing records, or **Manage payment method** to replace the default card. 5. Return to Billing and reload before relying on a changed card or newly finalized invoice. Billing access is tied to the signed-in account rather than a workspace role and is refused for API-key authentication. The portal URL is a bearer credential; do not share or copy it into support messages. ## Expected result The intended invoice downloads from Stripe, the upcoming amount is treated as an estimate, and any payment-method change is visible through the card brand and last four digits. **Failed to load billing information.** means the status request failed. If invoice fetching alone fails, the rest of Billing can still load with an empty history; try the Stripe portal before concluding no invoices exist. ## Related guides - [Locate an invoice period](/account/billing-locate-invoice-period) - [Update a payment method](/account/billing-update-payment-method)

title: Split a large cloud folder download
summary: Measure a large Dosya folder against the 10,000-file and 5 GiB archive ceilings, split it safely, and recover when only some ZIP downloads start.
verification: Verified streaming, per-archive ceilings, multi-part timing and exact recovery messages in apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/download-archive.ts and apps/api/src/lib/archive-stream.ts. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Dosya streams folder ZIPs directly to the browser, so archive bytes do not accumulate in the Files page before saving begins. Large trees still have two hard per-archive ceilings: **10,000 included files** and **5 GiB** of source data. The five-gibibyte boundary is checked before streaming. Browser disk requirements can be higher because you need room for both the ZIP and any extracted copy. Check available local storage before attempting a large export. ## Steps 1. Open **Files**, find the parent folder and review **Get info** if you need its displayed size or item count. 2. From that folder's menu, choose **Download**. 3. Watch the browser download shelf. The response is streamed as `dosya-download.zip`; progress there is the reliable completion indicator. 4. If the ZIP completes, open it and verify the tree before making another copy. ## Split a folder that exceeds a ceiling If the temporary response tab shows **“Archive too large (max 5 GiB)”**, return to the parent and download its child folders separately. For **“Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)”**, split by subfolder until each requested tree contains at most 10,000 downloadable files. Where one directory has many loose files, select manageable groups and choose **Download ZIP**. The browser client places at most **300 selected IDs** in each request. It can begin up to **20 ZIPs** from one bulk action; a request needing more parts is refused before any download starts. Use a written checklist of child-folder names or selection ranges. Archives all receive the server name `dosya-download.zip`, so label completed local copies by their source batch only after the browser says each download finished. ## Understand multi-part progress For a bulk selection that needs several ZIPs, Dosya staggers their start and immediately reports the planned number: **“Too many items for one file - arriving as N ZIPs.”** The success toast means requests were started, not that the ZIP contents finished saving. If a part returns an error page instead of an attachment, **Download problem** eventually reports how many of the planned downloads began and how many could not be prepared. It does not name the failed IDs. Work through the recorded source checklist in smaller groups, then compare paths in the completed ZIPs so duplicate local copies remain identifiable. ## Handle other blocks - **No items found**: refresh the folder. Removed, inaccessible, hidden and locked content can share this neutral response. - **Empty-folder message**: no file bytes exist below the requested tree; download a different child rather than retrying the same one. ## Expected result Every checklist batch has a completed ZIP below both archive ceilings. Create one local parent directory and extract each batch beneath it. Compare the downloaded child-folder paths with Dosya and inspect numbered collision names or `MISSING - .txt` notices. Keep the cloud source until every batch opens and a sample from each extracted branch is readable. ## Related guides - [Download a folder as a ZIP](/uploading/download-folder-archive) - [Troubleshoot a slow transfer](/troubleshooting/slow-transfer)

title: Uploading large files with available storage
summary: Check storage and workspace limits, keep a large transfer running, and verify the completed file before removing the original.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx, apps/web/src/components/uploads/upload-dock.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-limits.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/body-pipeline.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/extension-policy.ts, and their focused tests. The controlled screenshots use fictional local data; no production file was transferred.
body: Dosya does not add a fixed per-file maximum to a plan. The effective ceiling is whichever applicable rule is smallest: the owner account's remaining storage, the workspace's remaining allocation, **Max upload file size**, **Storage per member**, or a credential-specific limit. File-type and role rules can reject a file even when its size fits. In the web app, a file larger than **50 MB** uses a resumable multipart session. It is divided into **10 MB** parts and the browser can send up to **four parts of that file concurrently**. Smaller files use one request and restart from zero after a reload. Keep the original file unchanged and available until verification finishes. ## Before you start - Sign in to [the Dosya app](https://app.dosya.dev), select the destination workspace and confirm that your role can upload there. - Check the storage indicator at the bottom of the sidebar. It belongs to the active workspace; switching workspaces changes the capacity you are viewing. - Ask a workspace owner or admin whether **Settings → Hard limits** applies a maximum file size, per-member storage cap, total workspace cap or file-type restriction. - Leave headroom beyond the source file's displayed size. The upload-limit hint is cached for up to **60 seconds**, and another tab or member can consume space before the server measures this upload. - Keep the browser tab running, the device awake and the source file in place until the result shows **Done**. ## Steps: check capacity and workspace limits 1. **Select the correct workspace.** Read the workspace name at the top of the app sidebar. 2. **Check available storage.** Read the storage indicator near the bottom of the sidebar. Compare the available amount with the size shown by your operating system for the source file. 3. **Check workspace rules.** If your role permits the relevant change, open **Settings → Hard limits**. Review **Max upload file size**, **Storage per member**, **Total workspace storage cap**, **Max simultaneous uploads**, **Allowed file types** and **Blocked file types**. Otherwise, ask a workspace administrator to read the values for you. 4. **Use the tightest applicable limit.** Remaining plan storage does not override a lower workspace file-size or member limit. A file can fit the plan and still be refused by workspace policy. 5. **Choose a safe sample when testing.** Use a non-confidential file that is large enough to exercise the workflow but small enough to leave comfortable storage headroom. ## Steps: upload and monitor the large file 1. Open **Uploads** and choose **Upload options → Folder**. Confirm the destination before adding the file. 2. Select **Select files**, choose the original file and confirm the selection. The page requires both **Access Upload** and **Upload files** role permissions; if the drop area is replaced by a permission notice, a role manager must grant the missing capability. 3. Find the file in **Upload queue** or the upload list at the bottom right. An active transfer shows its percentage and transferred bytes. A **Queued** item is waiting for a transfer slot; it has not failed merely because another file is running first. 4. Keep the tab open and the device awake. You can navigate to another page inside the Dosya web app while the global upload list continues, but closing or reloading the tab can interrupt access to the browser's source file. 5. If the connection is unstable, lower **Upload options → Simultaneous uploads**. The browser offers **1–5** and uses the lower of your choice and the workspace's **Max simultaneous uploads** setting. When a second tab fills every server slot, Dosya waits three seconds and retries the affected row, up to five times, before leaving an error. 6. Wait for **Done**. A progress value close to 100% is not completion; the service still needs to finish and record the file. ## Steps: verify the completed file 1. Confirm that the exact row shows **Done**. 2. Select **View file** or **Go to location** from the completed row. 3. In **Files**, check the workspace, folder, filename and displayed size. For important data, download or open the completed file and use your own checksum or application-level check when available. 4. Keep the original until that verification succeeds. Clearing a finished queue row only removes its transfer history from the display; it does not validate or delete the stored file. ## Expected result The upload reaches **Done**, and the destination contains the expected file with the correct name and size. You can open or download it, and any independent integrity check you use matches the original. If the file does not reach Done, retain the original and diagnose the displayed state. Do not infer completion from elapsed time, a full-looking progress bar or a queue row that disappeared. ## Limits and recovery expectations - The effective maximum is the smallest relevant constraint: available storage, workspace maximum file size, per-member storage, total workspace storage, file-type rules and your upload permission. - A multipart session preserves server-confirmed parts. Resume asks the server which part numbers arrived and sends the missing ones; a single-request upload cannot reuse partial bytes. - After a reload, the browser no longer holds the original file object. An **Interrupted** row can ask you to select the original again. Dosya checks its name and size, which is not a content-integrity guarantee. - Only the newest **50** transfer rows are retained in this browser. Treat the destination in **Files**, rather than queue history, as the lasting record of a completed upload. - Browser storage can be cleared, sessions can expire and workspace policy can change. Resumable transfer support does not guarantee indefinite recovery. - The Free plan's storage and transfer allowances are separate. See [Free plan allowances](/account/free-plan-allowances) and check the current public policy before planning sustained automation. ## Troubleshooting **The file is smaller than the available storage but is refused.** Compare the row with these exact policy messages: `File exceeds the N GB size limit for this workspace`, `You've reached your N GB per-member storage limit`, or `File type .ext is not allowed in this workspace`. The sidebar amount cannot override any of them. **The file is Queued for a long time.** Check the other active rows and **Simultaneous uploads**. If the row ends with `You have N uploads in progress. Wait for them to finish before starting more.`, let another session finish instead of repeatedly adding the source. **The transfer shows Error.** Read the exact message before retrying. Restore connectivity or resolve the named storage, permission, destination or file-type issue. Repeated Retry clicks cannot remove a workspace restriction. **The transfer shows Interrupted after a reload.** Expand the upload list at the bottom right, select **Resume** and choose the unchanged original file. See [Troubleshooting a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) for the complete recovery flow. **The transfer reached 100% but did not show Done.** Keep the tab running while Dosya finishes the request. If it changes to Error or Interrupted, follow that state. Check Files before starting another copy. **The workspace is almost full.** Remove unneeded data only after checking versions, trash and retention requirements, or add capacity. Confirm the active workspace before deleting anything. ## Frequently asked questions ### What is the maximum file size? Dosya does not publish a plan-level per-file cap. The practical maximum is the storage available to that file unless the workspace sets a lower maximum or another workspace rule applies. ### Can a workspace owner set a lower maximum? Yes. An owner or admin can configure **Max upload file size** under Hard limits, alongside member, total-storage, concurrency and file-type rules. ### Can I browse the app during a large upload? Yes. Navigation inside the web app can continue while the global upload list runs. Keep the tab open; closing or reloading it can interrupt the browser's access to the source file. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Understanding upload progress and transfer states](/uploading/progress-and-states) - [Troubleshooting a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Free plan allowances](/account/free-plan-allowances) - [Why large uploads fail](https://dosya.dev/blog/why-large-uploads-fail)

title: Archive Lightroom originals to Dosya
summary: Archive byte-for-byte Lightroom originals and XMP sidecars into mirrored Dosya folders, with duplicate validation and resumable large-file uploads.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14; no production originals were uploaded. Claims checked against apps/lightroom/README.md; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/Info.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaArchiveServiceProvider.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaArchive.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUploader.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaErrors.lua; apps/lightroom/tests/archive_test.lua; apps/lightroom/tests/upload_test.lua; and apps/lightroom/tests/final_fix_test.lua. Figures explain the verified flow without showing customer files.
body: The **dosya Archive (originals)** export service reads each source file directly from disk and stores the same bytes in Dosya. Lightroom rendering, catalog edits, naming presets, sharpening, watermarking, and metadata export settings do not rewrite that copy. ## Before you start - Lightroom Classic 10 or newer is required. The plug-in itself is free and consumes the storage included with the connected Dosya plan. - Connect under **File → Plug-in Manager → dosya.dev**. Approval requires an unconfined workspace member with `upload_files`, `create_folders`, and `create_share_links`; Lightroom receives a full-access key pinned to that workspace. - Keep an independent backup until you inspect the archived files. This operation never moves or deletes local originals, but it is an upload workflow rather than a restore test. Automated Lua and real-API end-to-end coverage verify the archive engine; the project notes that the plug-in has not yet been exercised inside Lightroom. Start with a small disposable selection and inspect its stored bytes. ## Steps 1. Select the photos to archive and open Lightroom's **Export** dialog. 2. For **Export To**, choose **dosya Archive (originals)**. This service accepts the original format and video; the rendering and file-transformation sections are hidden. 3. Under **dosya archive**, set **Folder in dosya**. Blank input falls back to `Lightroom Originals`. 4. Leave **Include XMP sidecar files** enabled when catalog edits are written to sidecars. The original is byte-for-byte and therefore does not contain edits that exist only in the catalog. 5. Keep **Skip files already in dosya (same name and size)** enabled for repeat exports. Originals skip on matching name and byte size; XMP sidecars skip only when size and SHA-256 content match. 6. Start **Export** and leave Lightroom running. The destination mirrors the source beneath the chosen root, beginning with the catalog's top-level folder; for example, `Lightroom Originals/Photos/2026/Wedding`. 7. Read the final **dosya archive** dialog: `Archived X files, skipped Y already in dosya, failed Z.` It separately reports skipped virtual copies, unattempted photos, grouped error messages, and **Your local files were not changed.** 8. Open the destination in Dosya and compare filenames and byte sizes with the local originals. A virtual copy is skipped because it shares its master's source file. The normal one-shot ceiling is 50 MiB. Files larger than 1 MiB stream that request from disk in 1 MiB chunks, while files at or below 1 MiB use a buffered body. If the server refuses a streamed body with HTTP `411`, Lightroom switches the current session to buffered one-shot uploads through 8 MiB and sends larger files by resumable multipart. Multipart files above the active ceiling keep their session for up to 23 idle hours; a retry asks which parts arrived, sends only the missing parts, and checks the completed byte count. ## Expected result Every successful source appears under the mirrored Dosya path with its original filename and exact byte size. Optional sidecars sit beside their originals, repeat exports skip confirmed duplicates, and Lightroom leaves the local files where they were. ## Recover from interruptions or errors - **Connect your dosya account in File > Plug-in Manager.** Reconnect, select the same workspace, and rerun the export. - **Could not read the local file (_name_). Check that it exists and that its drive is connected.** Remount the source drive or restore file access; the plug-in does not send an empty or partial replacement. - A full workspace stops the batch. Free space or increase the storage allocation, then export the selection again; finished files can be skipped by name and size. - After five retry attempts per network-failing upload, three consecutive affected photos produce **dosya could not be reached for 3 photos in a row, so the rest were not attempted. Check your connection, then export again.** The next export can resume an eligible large-file session. - A hidden same-name collision reports `_name_ was not archived: a file with this name that your account cannot see already exists in _folder_. Original filenames are kept, so no renamed copy was made.` Ask a workspace administrator to resolve that file; the archive does not invent a suffix. - Closing Lightroom stops in-process uploads. Reopen the catalog and repeat **Export**; local originals remain unchanged, completed duplicates can skip, and missing multipart pieces can resume. ## Related guides - [Configure Lightroom publishing](/integrations/lightroom-configure-publish-service) - [Resume an interrupted upload](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Archive Lightroom XMP sidecars with originals
summary: Archive original photo bytes with current XMP sidecars, understand exact skip checks, and verify the complete mirrored Lightroom folder tree in Dosya.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaArchive.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaArchiveServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUploader.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaErrors.lua. Production behavior for “Archive Lightroom XMP sidecars with originals” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **dosya Archive (originals)** export service skips rendering and reads each master’s source path. With **Include XMP sidecar files** enabled, it also uploads an adjacent `.xmp` file when that file actually exists; virtual copies are skipped because they share a master original. ## Steps 1. In Lightroom Classic’s Export dialog choose **dosya Archive (originals)** and confirm the connection points to the intended workspace. 2. Set **Folder in dosya**—default **Lightroom Originals**—and leave **Include XMP sidecar files** checked. 3. Choose the existing-file skip setting; originals use name plus size, while XMP sidecars require an identical content hash. 4. When refreshing an existing `.xmp`, compare it first and rename or remove the old Dosya sidecar; the archive keeps the original filename and cannot overwrite it. 5. Read the final **dosya archive** summary for archived, already-present, failed, virtual-copy, and not-attempted counts plus grouped errors. 6. Open the mirrored Dosya folder and verify each applicable original and current `.xmp`, including any refreshed sidecar whose old name you freed first. Local files are never moved or deleted. Missing sidecars simply add no second upload. Original filenames are preserved; a changed sidecar with an occupied name is not an identical skip, so it fails with a message explaining that no renamed copy was made. After three consecutive network failures, remaining photos are reported as not attempted and can be exported again. ## Expected result Every successful non-virtual master has its byte-for-byte original in the mirrored path, and each sidecar that was absent, identical, or given a free name is accounted for. The summary ends with **Your local files were not changed.** ## Related guides - [Configure Lightroom publishing](/integrations/lightroom-configure-publish-service) - [Resume an interrupted upload](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Retry Lightroom when the catalog is busy
summary: Recover from Lightroom catalog write contention without repeating successful uploads or losing the plug-in’s deferred local catalog updates.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaSelections.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenu.lua. Production behavior for “Retry Lightroom when the catalog is busy” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: “Catalog busy” refers to Lightroom Classic refusing a timed write-access block. It can affect syncing client selections or marking already-uploaded photos for republish; it does not necessarily mean the network upload itself failed. ## Steps 1. Read Lightroom’s full catalog-busy dialog; identify whether client selections were unwritten or uploaded photos were not marked for republishing. 2. Finish another Lightroom operation that may hold catalog write access, such as metadata save, import, publish, or a different plug-in task. 3. Wait a moment without closing the catalog, then select the same dosya collection or command context used by the failed operation. 4. For selection sync, run **Sync client selections from dosya** again; the plug-in re-fetches gallery selections before one new catalog write. 5. For a publish warning, inspect **Modified Photos to Re-Publish** and **New Photos to Publish**, then choose **Publish** once more as the message directs. 6. Verify Lightroom’s deferred catalog update: client flags appear, or uploaded photos register in the gallery and leave the republish queue. The exact selection-sync error is **Lightroom’s catalog is busy, so the client selections were not written. Try again in a moment.** Publish can instead warn that uploaded files were not marked for republishing; those bytes may already exist in Dosya, so deleting or manually re-uploading them can create confusion. Retry the named Lightroom command. ## Expected result The deferred catalog write completes after contention ends. Synced client selection fields and collections reflect the server, or the next publish registers the already-uploaded photos and clears the republish state. ## Related guides - [Connect Lightroom](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Choose a workspace for Lightroom publishing
summary: Bind a Lightroom Classic catalog to the correct Dosya workspace, verify the device code, and satisfy upload, folder, and sharing permissions.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/connect/lightroom.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connect/decide.ts, apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/connect.ts, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaAccount.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPluginInfoProvider.lua. Production behavior for “Choose a workspace for Lightroom publishing” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The workspace is chosen on Dosya’s browser approval page, not inside the publish settings after connection. The resulting Lightroom API key is pinned to that whole workspace and cannot be edited; reconnect to choose another workspace. ## Steps 1. In Lightroom Classic choose **Connect**, keep its `XXXX-XXXX` code visible, and let the plug-in open Dosya’s approval page. 2. Sign in as the account holder and compare the browser code with Lightroom; deny the request if somebody else supplied the link. 3. Under **Publish galleries to workspace**, choose the exact workspace; the active Dosya workspace is preselected when it is available, otherwise the first membership is used. 4. Confirm your unconfined role has **upload_files**, **create_folders**, and **create_share_links** permission, then choose **Allow**. 5. Read **Return to Lightroom Classic**. You may return to Lightroom or close the tab after **Allow**; the plug-in polls independently every 3 seconds and stores the approved key and workspace name. 6. In File → Plug-in Manager choose the connection check, then confirm the connected user and workspace names are correct. The request expires after 600 seconds and uses an 8-character human code; choose **Connect** again for a fresh one. An empty workspace list says **You have no workspace to publish to**. Free accounts can hold 3 API keys and all accounts 20; a cap refusal instructs you to revoke an unused key in **Settings → API keys**. Switching workspaces later requires disconnecting and reconnecting. ## Expected result The plug-in stores a key named `Lightroom Classic: ` and reports the selected workspace. Publishing can create folders, upload files, and create gallery links only within the permissions of that chosen workspace. ## Related guides - [Create and manage API keys](/developers/api-key) - [Choose a Dosya app](/account/choose-app)

title: Review per-client selection collections in Lightroom
summary: Inspect the exact per-client collection created by a Dosya sync, verify its membership and metadata, and understand how later syncs remove stale picks.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaSelections.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenu.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A selection sync builds a collection set named **dosya client selections**. Inside it, the plug-in keeps one ordinary Lightroom collection for each gallery/client pair, named from the gallery title and client name. Each collection is an exact snapshot: a later sync adds new favourites and removes photos the client has unselected. ## Steps 1. In the Publish Services panel, select the published Dosya collection whose clients you want to review. This limits the sync to that gallery; with no active Dosya collection, the command scans every Dosya published collection in the catalog. 2. Choose **Library > Plug-in Extras > Sync client selections from dosya**. If Lightroom says `Connect your dosya account in File > Plug-in Manager.`, reconnect before trying again. 3. Wait for **Client selections synced**. Read its counts for galleries, clients, photos marked, and photos cleared; it also lists any gallery read failure and client notes. 4. In Collections, expand **dosya client selections** and open ` - `. Duplicate names created in one run receive `(2)`, `(3)`, and later suffixes. 5. Compare the photos with that client’s live gallery choices. The plug-in maps published remote file IDs first and falls back to the original Lightroom photo UUID when available. 6. Check **Selected by (dosya)**, **Selection status (dosya)**, and **dosya gallery**. These fields are aggregated per photo: status is `submitted` when any client selecting that photo has submitted, and `in progress` only when none of its selecting clients has submitted. Use the per-client collection when mixed clients need separate interpretation. **Catalog behavior.** The plug-in performs the metadata and collection update in one catalog write with a 10-second timeout. If it reports `Lightroom's catalog is busy, so the client selections were not written. Try again in a moment.`, close another catalog-writing task and run the command again; no partial collection update should be trusted. **Optional marks.** **Set the Pick flag** and **Set color label** are publish-service options. They can add a Pick and one of Red, Yellow, Green, Blue, or Purple during sync; disabling them later does not undo marks already written. ## Expected result The selected client collection contains exactly the photos currently returned for that gallery/client pair, stale favourites are absent, and each selected photo lists its selecting clients and galleries with an aggregate submission state. ## Related guides - [Enable client favourites](/integrations/lightroom-enable-client-favourites) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Collect client favourites in a Lightroom gallery
summary: Run a client through gallery identification, favourites, notes, and submission, then confirm Lightroom can retrieve the recorded selection and status.
verification: Reviewed against apps/api/src/pages/api/galleries/[id]/selections.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/gallery/clients.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/gallery/selections.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/gallery/submit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/galleries/limits.ts, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaSelections.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenu.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A Dosya gallery records favourites per identified client when **Let clients pick favourites** is enabled. Use a test identity that you can recognize later; Lightroom imports client names, current picks, submission state, and notes, rather than changing the original photos in the catalog. ## Steps 1. Publish a gallery with **Let clients pick favourites** enabled, then open its client link in a signed-out or private browser so the test follows the recipient flow. 2. Enter a distinctive client name and any requested identity details. If the link also has a password or recipient gate, complete that access check before selecting photos. 3. Mark a small, known set of gallery photos as favourites. Add a short note if the gallery offers one; Lightroom displays retrieved notes, capped at 500 UTF-16 units plus an ellipsis when truncated. 4. Use the gallery’s submission control when the choices are final. Submitted selections become `submitted`; unsent choices remain `in progress` and can still be retrieved. 5. Return to Lightroom Classic, select the matching Dosya published collection, and choose **Library > Plug-in Extras > Sync client selections from dosya**. 6. Read the **Client selections synced** receipt, then open the client collection under **dosya client selections** and compare its members with the exact test favourites. **Visitor limits.** A gallery accepts at most 200 named selection clients. The next registration receives `This gallery has reached its limit of people picking favourites. Ask the photographer for help.` Dosya has no operation for deleting one gallery client, so publish a new gallery when additional identities must register after the current gallery reaches 200. **What the client receives.** The visitor keeps the gallery experience and its access rules; syncing does not notify the client or lock their choices. A later client change replaces the membership of that client collection on the next sync. **Failure boundary.** If one gallery cannot be read, the receipt names the number of failed galleries and the first server error. A batch-stopping authentication or connection error prevents the catalog write; resolve that error before treating Lightroom as current. ## Expected result The test identity appears in the sync receipt, its Lightroom collection contains the chosen photos, and the metadata distinguishes a submitted selection from work still in progress. ## Related guides - [Enable client favourites](/integrations/lightroom-enable-client-favourites) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Configure the Dosya Lightroom publish service
summary: Configure the Dosya publish service with its exact rendering, destination, removal, selection, and concurrency controls before publishing a gallery.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/README.md on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **dosya.dev** service in Lightroom Classic controls both the rendered JPEGs and how collections map into Dosya. Its defaults favor web galleries, but removal and client-selection choices have lasting effects, so review them before the first publish. ## Steps 1. Open Lightroom Classic’s Publishing Manager, add or edit the **dosya.dev** publish service, and confirm the account line names the intended user and workspace. 2. Under **dosya options**, set **Folder in dosya**. The default root is `Lightroom`; each published collection becomes a subfolder and collection sets add parent path segments. 3. Choose **When a photo is removed**: either **Hide it from the gallery (keep the file)** or **Hide it and move the file to dosya trash**. Neither option permanently deletes the file. 4. Decide whether sync should **Set the Pick flag** or **Set color label**. Available label values are Red, Yellow, Green, Blue, and Purple. 5. Set **Uploads at once** from 1 through 4. The default is 3; reduce it on a slow or unstable connection rather than changing image quality to diagnose transport failures. 6. Review Lightroom’s output settings and save. First-use defaults are JPEG quality 85, sRGB, long edge 2560 pixels, no enlargement, copyright-only metadata, and location removed. **Supported output.** This publish service accepts JPEG in sRGB and does not publish video. Lightroom Classic 10 or newer is required; the Lightroom cloud application cannot load this plug-in. **Credential scope.** Connecting creates a full API key pinned to the chosen workspace. The approving member must be unconfined and allowed to upload files, create folders, and create share links. ## Expected result The service stays under Publish Services with the chosen Dosya root, removal policy, selection marks, concurrency, and rendering settings ready for new or modified photos. ## Related guides - [Connect a Lightroom catalog](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link)

title: Connect a Lightroom catalog to Dosya
summary: Connect Lightroom Classic through a ten-minute browser approval, verify the eight-character code, choose a workspace, and confirm the stored account.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUI.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaAccount.lua, apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/connect.ts, apps/web/src/pages/connect/lightroom.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connect/decide.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The plug-in uses a device-code flow because Lightroom Classic cannot receive a browser redirect. A request lasts 600 seconds, the plug-in polls every 3 seconds, and the web approval creates a separate full API key for the workspace you select. ## Steps 1. In Lightroom Classic, open **File > Plug-in Manager**, select **dosya.dev**, and choose **Connect...** in the **dosya account** section. 2. Keep the **Connect to dosya** progress dialog open. It changes to `Waiting for approval in your browser, code XXXX-XXXX` after Dosya creates the request. 3. In the opened browser, sign in as the account holder. An impersonated session, API-key authentication, or a folder-confined membership cannot approve this connection. 4. Confirm the eight-character browser code matches Lightroom exactly, choose **Publish galleries to workspace**, and select **Allow**. Choose **Deny** if the request is not yours. 5. Wait while Lightroom polls. Temporary network or server errors keep retrying until the 10-minute deadline; a rate response increases the interval by 2 seconds, up to 30 seconds. 6. Confirm **Connected to dosya**, then read `Connected as , workspace `. Use **Check connection** once if you need a fresh server and storage-status check. **Required rights.** Approval needs an unrestricted workspace membership with `upload_files`, `create_folders`, and `create_share_links`. The page also refuses approval when the account has reached its API-key cap and directs you to **Settings > API keys**. **Security receipt.** The first poll after approval receives the plaintext key once, stores it in Lightroom’s password store, and consumes the request. Dosya records the API-key creation and sends the same mandatory integration notice used for other new keys. ## Expected result Lightroom reports the intended identity and workspace as connected, **Check connection** succeeds, and the browser says to return to Lightroom Classic and close the tab. ## Related guides - [Create and manage API keys](/developers/api-key) - [Choose a Dosya app](/account/choose-app)

title: Fix a Lightroom connection page that does not open
summary: Recover when Lightroom cannot launch the approval browser by constructing the official code URL, completing approval, and leaving the poll dialog open.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUI.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaAccount.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaHttp.lua, apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/connect.ts, apps/web/src/pages/connect/lightroom.tsx on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Lightroom asks the operating system to open the approval URL, but the plug-in does not show that URL or offer a copy button when the launch fails. The dialog does show the user code, so you can reconstruct the official route without canceling the live request. ## Steps 1. Leave **Connect to dosya** open and copy the displayed `XXXX-XXXX` code by hand. Canceling ends the local poll even though the server request may remain pending. 2. Open a current browser yourself and enter `https://app.dosya.dev/connect/lightroom?code=XXXX-XXXX`, replacing the placeholder with the exact code from Lightroom. 3. Sign in with a normal account-holder session. If the page says the request is incomplete, check the `code=` query value and preserve the dash or enter the same eight characters. 4. Compare the large browser code with Lightroom, choose the required workspace, and select **Allow** only when the device name is your Lightroom Classic computer. 5. Return to Lightroom without closing its progress dialog. It polls every 3 seconds and should show **Connected to dosya** after receiving the one-time key. 6. If the request reaches 10 minutes, start a fresh **Connect...** flow; an expired URL cannot be revived, and its code must not be reused. **Why the browser may stay closed.** The plug-in delegates directly to Lightroom’s `LrHttp.openUrlInBrowser`. There is no in-plug-in browser and no callback into Lightroom, so browser-default and OS URL-handler problems sit outside the approval service. **Do not share the URL.** The page warns that anyone sent the link should choose **Deny**. Matching the code on both surfaces binds your deliberate local action to the browser approval. ## Expected result The manually entered approval page accepts the still-live code, Lightroom receives approval before expiry, and its account section names the chosen workspace. ## Related guides - [Connect Lightroom](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Fix an expired Lightroom connection code
summary: Replace an expired Lightroom approval request with a fresh ten-minute code, approve it once, and verify the newly issued workspace connection.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaAccount.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUI.lua, apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/connect.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connect/poll.ts, apps/web/src/pages/connect/lightroom.tsx on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Each Lightroom connection request expires after 600 seconds. An expired, denied, or already-consumed request is terminal: the plug-in cannot extend it and the browser tells you to start again. ## Steps 1. Close the failed progress dialog after Lightroom reports `The connection request expired. Start again.` An old browser tab may instead say **This request has expired**. 2. Return to **File > Plug-in Manager > dosya.dev** and choose **Connect...** to create a different request token and eight-character code. 3. Wait for the fresh browser tab and confirm its code matches the new Lightroom dialog. Do not approve the earlier tab even if it is still open. 4. Select the intended **Publish galleries to workspace** value and choose **Allow** before the new 10-minute window ends. 5. Let Lightroom keep polling until **Connected to dosya** appears. `This connection request was already used. Start again.` means another poll already consumed that request. 6. Run **Check connection** and confirm the user and workspace. If approval fails because of an API-key cap, revoke an unused key in **Settings > API keys**, then create another request. **Other terminal messages.** `The connection was declined in the browser.` follows **Deny**. `Canceled.` means the Lightroom progress dialog was canceled. None of these outcomes stores a usable key. **Transient failures.** A network or server error during polling does not immediately discard the request; polling continues to its deadline. Repeatedly clicking **Connect...** creates more live requests and makes it easier to approve the wrong code. ## Expected result Only the new request is approved and consumed, Lightroom stores its issued key, and **Check connection** reports the chosen workspace without an expiry error. ## Related guides - [Connect Lightroom](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Copy and share a Lightroom gallery link
summary: Copy the remote URL for one published collection, handle Lightroom’s clipboard fallback, and validate the exact client gallery before sharing it.
