verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenu.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUI.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/Info.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **Copy gallery link** reads the remote URL already stored on the active Dosya published collection. It does not create a link. A collection must have completed its first publish, and the correct collection must be selected in the Publish Services panel. ## Steps 1. In Publish Services, click the exact Dosya published collection you intend to share. A regular collection or another plug-in’s publish collection is not accepted. 2. Choose **Library > Plug-in Extras > Copy gallery link**. If the collection has no remote URL, Lightroom says `Select a dosya.dev published collection in the Publish Services panel first, then publish it at least once.` 3. On macOS or Windows, wait for **Gallery link copied** and the URL. The command copies only plainly safe HTTPS URLs through the platform clipboard command. 4. If clipboard copying is unavailable or fails, Lightroom opens **Gallery link** with a selectable URL field; select and copy that field manually. 5. Paste the URL into a private browser before sending it. Confirm the title, cover, photos, password prompt, expiry, favourites, and download behavior belong to the intended client. 6. Send that validated URL through your chosen channel. If a later publish says the old link was revoked or expired and shows a new URL, replace the saved message or template. **Access remains enforced.** Copying does not bypass a password, recipient rule, view-only mode, or expiry. The recipient receives the same public gallery route that **Open dosya gallery** uses. **Clipboard detail.** The plug-in uses `pbcopy` on macOS and `clip` on Windows after validating the URL. Other environments receive the selectable-field fallback instead of a false success notice. ## Expected result The copied or manually selected HTTPS URL opens the chosen live gallery under its current access settings, and the shared message contains that same verified address. ## Related guides - [Enable client favourites](/integrations/lightroom-enable-client-favourites) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Create a published Lightroom collection
summary: Create a Dosya published collection with deliberate gallery settings, add eligible photos, and confirm Lightroom queues them for the first publish.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/README.md on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A Dosya published collection becomes one cloud folder, one client gallery, and one share link on its first publish. Creating the collection in Lightroom is local preparation; no online gallery exists until **Publish** runs successfully. ## Steps 1. Under the configured **dosya.dev** service in Publish Services, create a new **Gallery**. Lightroom’s default collection name is **Client gallery**. 2. Give the collection a clear internal name. Set **Gallery title** only when the client-facing title should differ; a blank title follows the collection name. 3. Choose **Let clients pick favourites**, a **Downloads** mode, **Link expires after** from 0 to 365 days, metadata stripping, and any password before the first publish. 4. Add the intended catalog photos. The service renders JPEG only, uses sRGB, and cannot publish video; incompatible items will not become valid gallery renditions. 5. Check **New Photos to Publish** and review order. Custom sort order is supported, and the first live item becomes the cover when no cover exists. 6. Stop before clicking **Publish** if the folder path or access settings are wrong. Collection creation is reversible locally; the next action creates remote files and a share link. **Folder mapping.** The destination begins with **Folder in dosya**, which defaults to `Lightroom`, followed by collection-set names and the collection name. Unsafe path characters are sanitized. If the intended folder already backs another gallery, the plug-in tries identifier-based suffixes. **Deletion distinction.** Deleting this new collection before the first publish is local. After publishing, deleting the Lightroom collection deliberately leaves its Dosya gallery, files, and link online. ## Expected result The new Gallery appears beneath the Dosya publish service, its chosen options are saved, and all added eligible photos wait under **New Photos to Publish** without an online link yet. ## Related guides - [Connect a Lightroom catalog](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link)

title: Understand deleting a Lightroom published collection
summary: Delete a Lightroom published collection with a clear record of what remains online, then separately revoke or remove Dosya resources when required.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/README.md, apps/web/src/pages/shared.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/revoke.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Deleting a published collection removes Lightroom’s local publish relationship only. The plug-in intentionally keeps the Dosya gallery, its folder and files, and its share link online so a catalog mistake does not destroy client delivery. ## Steps 1. Before deletion, select the collection and use **Library > Plug-in Extras > Copy gallery link**. Record the URL, collection name, and Dosya folder so you can identify the retained resources. 2. Confirm whether you only want to remove Lightroom’s collection. This action does not revoke recipient access and does not reclaim cloud storage. 3. Delete the published collection in Lightroom. Read **The dosya gallery stays online**, which states that the gallery, photos, and link are unchanged. 4. Open the saved URL in a private browser. Its continued availability is expected, subject to the existing password, expiry, or recipient gate. 5. If access must end, open Dosya **Shared > By me**, match the saved gallery URL or name, choose **Revoke**, and confirm the irreversible link revocation. The Lightroom integration page only reports gallery status; it does not provide this revoke control. 6. If storage must also be reclaimed, review and delete or trash the retained files in Dosya separately. Revoking a link alone leaves the folder bytes in cloud storage. **Irreversible boundary.** The Lightroom deletion severs the catalog’s stored remote collection relationship. Recreating a similarly named collection is a new local object and should not be assumed to adopt the old gallery. **Photo removal is different.** Removing a photo from a live published collection hides it from the gallery. The service setting decides whether the cloud file stays or moves to recoverable Dosya trash; the plug-in never permanently deletes it. ## Expected result The Lightroom collection is gone, while the recorded Dosya URL and files remain available until you explicitly revoke the link or remove the cloud content in Dosya. ## Related guides - [Publish a gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Edit gallery options](/integrations/lightroom-edit-gallery-options)

title: Edit options for a Lightroom client gallery
summary: Change an existing Lightroom gallery’s title, favourites, downloads, expiry, metadata, or password and verify the live link immediately after saving.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/api/src/lib/share/update.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **Edit Gallery** can update a published gallery without republishing its photos. Saving an existing collection calls the gallery update immediately; settings on an unpublished collection are applied during its first publish. ## Steps 1. In Publish Services, right-click the target Dosya collection and choose **Edit Gallery**. Confirm the collection already has the client link you intend to change. 2. Edit **Gallery title** or toggle **Let clients pick favourites**. A blank title follows the Lightroom collection name; enabling favourites exposes the client-selection flow. 3. Choose **Clients can download full size** or **View only, no downloads**, and decide whether **Remove photo metadata from downloads** should be enabled. 4. Enter **Link expires after** as a whole number from 0 through 365, where 0 requests no expiry. A workspace or plan expiry ceiling can shorten that request. 5. Use **Set password...** for a trimmed password of at least eight characters, or **Remove password**. Confirm both password fields before saving. 6. Save the dialog and open the client link privately. If Lightroom reports `Gallery settings were not updated: ...`, the photo publish may continue, but these option changes did not all reach Dosya. **Link continuity.** Ordinary option edits update the existing share record rather than minting a replacement URL. If that record was revoked or has expired, the next publish can relink the gallery and reports the newly created URL. **Workspace rules win.** A workspace can require passwords or cap expiry. Lightroom reports when Dosya substitutes an earlier expiry date; a refused setting change is a warning, not a reason to assume the old access policy changed. ## Expected result The live gallery retains its URL for an ordinary update and shows the saved title, selection, download, metadata, expiry, and password behavior allowed by workspace policy. ## Related guides - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Protect a share with a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Enable client favourites in a Lightroom gallery
summary: Enable client favourites on one Lightroom gallery, verify the visitor controls, and prepare the catalog settings needed to import selections later.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaSelections.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Favourites are a gallery-level option named **Let clients pick favourites**. Enabling it changes the client page; it does not automatically import choices into Lightroom, set Pick flags, or assign color labels. ## Steps 1. In Publish Services, right-click the required Dosya collection and choose **Edit Gallery**. Check its title so another client gallery is not changed by mistake. 2. Enable **Let clients pick favourites**. On an unpublished collection, the option waits for first publish; on an existing gallery, saving triggers an immediate update. 3. Save the dialog. If the server refuses the change, Lightroom reports `Gallery settings were not updated: ` and leaves the previous online behavior in place. 4. Open the gallery in a private browser and identify as a test client. Mark at least one photo and leave the choices in progress or submit them to test both states. 5. Back in Lightroom, optionally edit the publish service’s **Client selections** options: **Set the Pick flag** and **Set color label** control catalog marks during sync. 6. Select the collection and run **Library > Plug-in Extras > Sync client selections from dosya**. Confirm the receipt and the new per-client collection. **Existing clients.** Turning the option off removes the selection interface but should not be treated as a catalog cleanup. Run a successful sync while you can still verify the intended state, and remove any local Pick or color marks manually if they are no longer wanted. **Submission meaning.** Lightroom writes `in progress` for a client who has not sent the selection and `submitted` when `submitted_at` exists. Both states can contribute chosen photos to the per-client collection. ## Expected result The client page permits identified visitors to favourite photos, and a later Lightroom sync retrieves the test choices with the correct client and submission status. ## Related guides - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Protect a share with a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Create a client gallery during a Lightroom export
summary: Create a client gallery during Lightroom export, understand its dated folder and collision rules, and validate the link shown when upload finishes.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/README.md on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The regular **dosya.dev** export service can create a one-off client gallery without a published collection. With the default destination, it uploads into `Lightroom Exports//` and returns the public link at the end. <figure class="help-screenshot"><a class="workflow-map-link" href="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14.webp" data-light-href="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14.webp" data-dark-href="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14-dark.webp"><picture class="workflow-map"><source data-theme-source="dark" media="not all" srcset="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14-dark.webp" type="image/webp" /><img src="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14.webp" alt="Four-step workflow map for Create a client gallery during a Lightroom export: Choose the dosya.dev export service, verify the target workspace. Enable Create a client gallery, enter a distinctive title. Export the rendered photos, allow suffixes for folder conflicts. Open Your dosya link, verify title and complete photo count." width="1200" height="675" loading="lazy" decoding="async" /></picture></a><figcaption>The map starts with “Choose the dosya.dev export service, verify the target workspace.” and ends with “Open Your dosya link, verify title and complete photo count.” <a class="workflow-map-full" href="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14.webp" data-light-href="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14.webp" data-dark-href="/screenshots/lightroom-export-create-gallery-help-workflow-2026-10-14-dark.webp">Open full-size screenshot</a>.</figcaption></figure> ## Steps 1. Open Lightroom’s Export dialog and select the **dosya.dev** service, then confirm its account section names the intended workspace. 2. Leave **Upload to folder** at `Lightroom Exports/<date>` or enter another path. The `<date>` token is replaced with the current `YYYY-MM-DD` date. 3. Enable **Create a client gallery from this export, titled:** and enter the client-facing title. A blank title becomes `Gallery YYYY-MM-DD`. 4. Review JPEG rendering and choose **Uploads at once** from 1 through 4. Gallery creation enables client selections and full-size downloads by default. 5. Select **Export** and keep Lightroom running through rendering and upload. If the default title folder already backs another gallery, Dosya tries `(2)` through `(5)` suffixes. 6. Read **Your dosya link**, open it privately, and confirm title, photo count, order, and download behavior before giving it to the client. **Collision limit.** Gallery export attempts at most five candidate folders. A persistent `folder_in_use` conflict after those candidates stops gallery creation; choose a more distinctive title or destination and export again. **Result accounting.** A troubled run reports `Uploaded N, failed N, not attempted N.` Three consecutive network failures stop the remaining work, so the displayed link and cloud folder must be checked before assuming the full selection arrived. ## Expected result Dosya creates a gallery in the resolved export folder, Lightroom uploads the rendered photos, and the completion dialog provides a client link that opens that gallery. ## Related guides - [Configure Lightroom publishing](/integrations/lightroom-configure-publish-service) - [Resume an interrupted upload](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Export photos from Lightroom directly to Dosya
summary: Export rendered Lightroom photos into a chosen Dosya folder, control concurrency and sharing, and verify the final upload receipt and cloud files.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUploader.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **dosya.dev** export service uploads rendered JPEGs into a cloud folder without creating a persistent Lightroom published collection. You can optionally ask for a folder share link when client-gallery creation is off. ## Steps 1. Choose the photos in Lightroom and open Export with the **dosya.dev** service. Verify the connected account and workspace before rendering files. 2. Under **dosya options**, set **Upload to folder**. The default `Lightroom Exports/` expands the date token when the export starts. 3. Leave **Create a client gallery from this export** off for a plain folder upload. Enable **Otherwise, create a share link for the folder** only when recipients need a link. 4. Review JPEG, sRGB, sizing, and metadata output, then set **Uploads at once** between 1 and 4; 3 is the service default. 5. Select **Export** and watch `Uploading X of N (Y in flight)`. Existing destination names are checked so an unrelated same-named file is not silently versioned. 6. Read any `Uploaded N, failed N, not attempted N.` receipt, then open the target folder in Dosya and compare filenames, sizes, and item count with the export selection. **Name safety.** If the destination listing fails but the error is not batch-stopping, Lightroom warns that it could only check names against the current batch and known gallery photos; a same-named cloud file may have received a new version. **Retry behavior.** A plain export has no **New Photos to Publish** queue. For failed or unattempted items, correct the cause and export those originals again, checking the cloud folder first to avoid duplicate intent. ## Expected result Every successful rendition appears in the resolved Dosya folder, optional sharing produces a link, and the completion counts explain any item that needs a separate retry. ## Related guides - [Configure Lightroom publishing](/integrations/lightroom-configure-publish-service) - [Resume an interrupted upload](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Organize Lightroom galleries with collection sets
summary: Map Lightroom collection sets into a predictable Dosya folder hierarchy, stay within the four-level limit, and verify the published gallery path.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUtil.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Collection sets become parent folders beneath the publish service’s **Folder in dosya** root. The final published collection becomes the gallery folder. Lightroom permits this plug-in to nest sets to a maximum depth of four. ## Steps 1. Edit the Dosya publish service and confirm **Folder in dosya**, which defaults to `Lightroom`. This becomes the first part of every collection path. 2. Create a **Gallery folder** collection set and give it a durable project or client name. Add nested sets only when each level helps recipients or operators locate content. 3. Keep nesting at four collection-set levels or fewer. The provider declares `maxCollectionSetDepth = 4`, so deeper hierarchy is unsupported. 4. Create a child **Gallery** and set its collection name plus optional client-facing **Gallery title**. The title does not replace the folder path segments. 5. Add eligible photos and choose **Publish**. Dosya sanitizes path characters that are unsafe across clients before ensuring the folder hierarchy. 6. Open Dosya and verify `///` plus the gallery link. If another gallery already owns that folder, expect an identifier suffix rather than adoption. **Renaming behavior.** Renaming a published collection may update the gallery title when no custom title is set, but it does not move the existing Dosya folder. Plan the hierarchy before first publish when the cloud path matters. **Identity protection.** A per-catalog/service/collection source reference prevents a different catalog from silently adopting the gallery merely because its folder and names match. ## Expected result The child collection publishes to a sanitized folder path beneath the configured root, collection-set levels appear in order, and its client gallery opens independently. ## Related guides - [Connect a Lightroom catalog](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link)

title: Control full-resolution downloads from a Lightroom gallery
summary: Switch a Lightroom gallery between full-size downloads and view-only access, verify metadata handling, and test the complete recipient experience.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/api/src/lib/share/update.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/visibility.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **Downloads** menu controls the gallery share link’s lock mode. **Clients can download full size** uses `none`; **View only, no downloads** uses `view_only`, which still permits the public preview while blocking download actions. ## Steps 1. Right-click the intended published collection and choose **Edit Gallery**, then confirm the gallery title and existing client link. 2. Under **Downloads**, choose **Clients can download full size** when recipients may save originals, or **View only, no downloads** for preview-only delivery. 3. If downloads remain enabled, decide whether to select **Remove photo metadata from downloads**. That option changes downloadable output where the server can safely rewrite the format. 4. Save the gallery settings. Existing galleries update immediately; an unpublished collection carries the choice into its first publish. 5. Open the link in a private browser and try the visible recipient controls. View-only should preserve previews but withhold permitted file downloads. 6. If the behavior did not change, read Lightroom for `Gallery settings were not updated: `, resolve the workspace or connection refusal, and save again. **Meaning of full size.** The download is the complete file stored for the gallery. With the publish service defaults, that is a JPEG rendered at quality 85 and up to 2560 pixels on the long edge, not the camera original. **No full lock.** This two-choice Lightroom menu does not set `full_lock`; gallery password protection is configured separately with **Set password...**. Existing full-lock links are not downgraded by the ordinary download-mode comparison. **Metadata scope.** Metadata stripping applies to downloads, not Lightroom’s catalog or the already-rendered cloud record. Formats the service cannot safely rewrite may be refused rather than delivered with misleading privacy. ## Expected result The live gallery continues to preview its photos and either offers full-size downloads or enforces view-only access, with the chosen metadata rule applied to eligible downloads. ## Related guides - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Protect a share with a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Set an expiry date for a Lightroom gallery link
summary: Set a Lightroom gallery link to expire from zero through 365 days, account for workspace caps, and verify the effective server date after saving.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/api/src/lib/share/expiry.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/settings.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **Link expires after** accepts a whole number from 0 through 365. Zero requests a link that never expires, but a workspace or plan ceiling can replace that request with an earlier server date. ## Steps 1. Open **Edit Gallery** for the intended Dosya collection and note the current link before changing its lifetime. 2. Enter a whole number from 1 to 365 for that many days, or enter 0 to request **never**. Lightroom clamps its collection value to this range. 3. Save the dialog. For an existing gallery, the plug-in sends the new relative-day value only when it differs from the last applied setting. 4. Read any warning: `dosya set the link to expire on YYYY-MM-DD instead of never (your plan's limit).` means the server overrode a zero-day request. 5. For a shortened finite request, record the reported `YYYY-MM-DD` from `sooner than the N days asked for (your plan's limit)` as the effective deadline. 6. Open or inspect the link in Dosya and verify that effective date. After expiry, expect the old URL to stop working; a later publish may create and report a new link. **Timing.** The server calculates a relative expiry from the time the update is accepted. Saving the same already-applied number does not continually extend the link on every unrelated collection edit. **Relinking changes the address.** When a share is missing, revoked, or expired, publish can create a replacement and says `The gallery's old link was revoked or had expired, so it has a new link: `; update recipient messages accordingly. ## Expected result The gallery reports the effective expiry allowed by policy, the current link works until that deadline, and any server-shortened date is captured from Lightroom’s warning. ## Related guides - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Protect a share with a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Fix a Lightroom gallery that is missing online
summary: Diagnose a Lightroom gallery URL that no longer opens, distinguish missing gallery data from a dead share, and publish once to repair linkage.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenu.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaAccount.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Lightroom remembers both a remote gallery ID and a public URL. Publishing can recover a missing gallery record or replace a missing, revoked, or expired share, but those branches surface the current address differently. ## Steps 1. Select the Dosya published collection and choose **Library > Plug-in Extras > Open dosya gallery**. If Lightroom asks you to publish first, the collection has no stored remote URL. 2. Run **Check connection** in **File > Plug-in Manager > dosya.dev**. Reconnect if it reports `dosya connection expired or was revoked. Reconnect in File > Plug-in Manager.` 3. Inspect the gallery or its folder in Dosya. Determine whether the gallery record is missing, or only its share is revoked, expired, or absent. 4. Return to Lightroom and click **Publish** once. If the remote gallery ID returns not found, the plug-in creates or recovers a gallery using its stable source reference and collision-safe folder candidates, then records the returned gallery ID and URL in Lightroom. 5. Follow the branch that occurred. For an existing gallery with a missing, revoked, or expired share, read `The gallery's old link was revoked or had expired, so it has a new link: `. For a missing gallery record, do not wait for that relink sentence; after publishing, use **Library > Plug-in Extras > Copy gallery link** or **Open dosya gallery** to retrieve the recorded address. 6. Open the current link privately, verify the items and access settings, and update every client message or saved location that still contains a former URL. **What publish can repair.** A missing or moved cloud file is uploaded fresh into the gallery folder; photos that could not be registered are marked for republish. A gallery-settings refusal is reported separately and does not prove photo upload failed. **Do not infer from names.** The source reference ties a collection to its gallery. A same-named folder from another catalog is not automatically adopted, and a conflict may produce a suffixed folder. ## Expected result The collection resolves to a live gallery again. A dead share produces the relink notice, while a recreated or recovered gallery exposes its recorded address through **Copy gallery link** or **Open dosya gallery**; the private-browser check passes before clients receive it. ## Related guides - [Connect Lightroom](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Protect a Lightroom gallery with a password
summary: Set a trimmed password of at least eight characters on a Lightroom gallery, verify immediate application, and understand workspace enforcement.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUI.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/api/src/lib/share/update.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A gallery password protects the existing client link. Lightroom trims leading and trailing whitespace before comparing the two entries and checking the minimum length; the stored password must contain at least eight characters after trimming. ## Steps 1. Right-click the target Dosya published collection, choose **Edit Gallery**, and locate the **Password** row in **dosya gallery**. 2. Choose **Set password...**. Enter the same value in **Password:** and **Confirm:**; use at least eight characters excluding leading and trailing spaces. 3. Correct `The password needs at least 8 characters.` or `The two passwords do not match.` before returning to the collection dialog. 4. Confirm the status reads `Password set. Applied right away when you save (or on the first publish).`, then save **Edit Gallery**. 5. Open the gallery in a private browser and enter the trimmed password. Existing authenticated sessions can hide the prompt, so a clean session is the decisive test. 6. Share the password through a separate channel. To remove it later, choose **Remove password**, save, and verify the status and a new private session. **Secret handling.** The pending plaintext lives in Lightroom’s password store, while collection settings keep a non-secret reference and serial. After Dosya accepts the change, the plug-in marks that serial applied and clears the pending password value. **Workspace policy.** A workspace with forced share passwords refuses password removal with `This workspace requires a password on all share links`. A failed update appears as `Gallery settings were not updated: ...`; the previous protection remains authoritative. ## Expected result A new private session cannot open the gallery without the accepted password, the same link opens after successful entry, and Lightroom no longer holds a pending value after application. ## Related guides - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Protect a share with a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Open a Dosya gallery from Lightroom
summary: Select the correct published collection, run Lightroom's Open dosya gallery command, and diagnose a missing URL without changing the gallery.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14; the command was not run against a production gallery. Claims checked against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/Info.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenu.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenuOpenGallery.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaHttp.lua; and apps/lightroom/README.md. The workflow and overview images are explanatory assets.
body: Open the public gallery URL stored on a Dosya published collection without copying and pasting it. This command launches the system browser and makes no gallery, file, or catalog change. ## Before you start - Use Lightroom Classic 10 or newer with the `dosya.dev` plug-in installed. The current plug-in declares SDK 14 and version 0.1.0. - The collection must belong to the **dosya.dev** Publish Service and must have been published at least once. An ordinary collection, a collection from another service, or an unpublished Dosya collection has no usable gallery URL. - Opening the saved link does not require the Lightroom API key to be valid at that moment. Access in the browser still follows the gallery's current password, expiry, and revocation state. The repository verifies this command's selection and URL logic through Lua tests, but records no completed test inside Lightroom itself. Try it on a noncritical published collection before making it part of a delivery checklist. ## Steps 1. In Lightroom Classic's **Library** module, find **Publish Services → dosya.dev**. 2. Select the exact published collection whose gallery you want. Selecting a photo alone or a parent collection set does not satisfy the plug-in's collection check. 3. Choose **Library → Plug-in Extras → Open dosya gallery**. 4. Treat **Open dosya gallery** as successful only when the default browser loads the remote URL saved on that collection. 5. Compare the gallery title and visible photos with the selected Lightroom collection before sharing the browser URL. You can also right-click a Dosya published collection and use **Open gallery in browser**. For an individual published photo, Lightroom exposes **Show in dosya gallery**; both routes use the URL Lightroom supplies for the published item. ## Expected result Lightroom hands the selected collection's existing remote URL to the operating system, and the default browser navigates to that gallery. No API request is needed to obtain a new link, and the command does not publish pending photos. ## When the gallery does not open - The plug-in shows **Select a dosya.dev published collection in the Publish Services panel first, then publish it at least once.** Select the collection row and finish its first **Publish**. - If a browser window never appears, test another ordinary web link from Lightroom or the operating system; the command delegates opening to Lightroom's browser API. - If the page says the link is unavailable, return to the collection settings. A revoked or expired gallery link must be republished or relinked before this stored URL can work again. - If unpublished changes are pending, opening the link shows the currently live gallery. Click **Publish** separately to upload those edits. ## Related guides - [Publish a gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Edit gallery options](/integrations/lightroom-edit-gallery-options)

title: Install the Dosya Lightroom Classic plug-in
summary: Install dosya.lrplugin in Lightroom Classic, approve the browser connection and verify your workspace. Includes requirements, updates and disconnect recovery.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14; no production account or native client installation performed. Product claims checked against src/lib/lightroom-integration.ts; src/pages/integration/lightroom.astro; apps/lightroom/scripts/build.sh; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/Info.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUI.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaAccount.lua; apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaErrors.lua; apps/lightroom/tests/account_test.lua; apps/lightroom/tests/errors_test.lua; apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/connect.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connect/poll.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connect/decide.ts; apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/repo.ts; apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts; apps/lightroom/tests/static_test.lua; apps/lightroom/tests/final_fix_test.lua; apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connect/start.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connection.ts. External client procedure checked against https://helpx.adobe.com/lightroom-classic/desktop/export-photos/export-presets-settings-plug-ins.html. Light/dark process diagrams depict documented controls and outcomes, not captured UI.
body: Install the free **dosya.dev** plug-in in **Lightroom Classic 10 or newer** on macOS or Windows. The downloaded ZIP contains **dosya.lrplugin**; add that folder to Lightroom, then authorize the connection in your browser. Lightroom (the cloud app) is not supported. ## Before installing Download [dosya-lightroom.zip](https://dosya.dev/downloads/lightroom/dosya-lightroom.zip) from Dosya. The packaged release is **0.1.0**. Unzip it and move `dosya.lrplugin` to a permanent, readable local directory, such as a Lightroom plug-ins folder in your user directory. Lightroom runs the plug-in from that location: moving or deleting it later breaks the installed entry. Select the extracted folder, not the ZIP or a Lua file. The repository's development folder is named `.lrdevplugin`; the release installer uses `.lrplugin`. You need a Dosya account and a workspace where your membership permits **upload files**, **create folders** and **create share links**. A membership confined to a folder cannot authorize this workspace-wide connection. The plug-in uses your existing storage plan; it does not add Adobe storage. On Free, at most **5 active share links** are allowed and a gallery link can last at most **7 days**. Paid plans lift those share-link limits. Storage and workspace upload policies still govern photos and originals. ## Steps: add the plug-in and connect 1. In Lightroom Classic choose **File → Plug-in Manager**, click **Add**, browse to `dosya.lrplugin` and select it. 2. Select **dosya.dev** in the manager's installed plug-in list. Check its Status area and enable it if Lightroom has disabled it. The Dosya panel should show **dosya account**, initially **Not connected**, with **Connect...**, **Check connection** and **Disconnect** controls. 3. Click **Connect...**. Lightroom displays **Connect to dosya** and **Waiting for approval in your browser, code …**. A browser opens the Dosya approval page. Sign in there, check that the request is the one you just started, compare the code and choose the workspace for galleries. Approve only that request. Your Dosya password is entered in the browser, never into the plug-in. 4. Leave Lightroom open while it waits. The request expires after **10 minutes**; normal polling occurs every **3 seconds**. Cancellation or denial stops that attempt. On success the dialog reads **Connected to dosya**, with **Connected as …, workspace …**. 5. Click **Check connection**. A successful check says **dosya connection works** and refreshes the displayed account, workspace and storage use. Resolve a wrong workspace before publishing. Approval creates a dedicated, Full access, API-enabled key pinned to the approved workspace. It counts toward your account's API-key cap and has no configured expiry. Lightroom stores the secret through its password service; non-secret connection details remain in plug-in preferences. The key cannot enlarge your role's permissions. Do not manually paste another API key into this connection flow. ## Verify the result Close and reopen Plug-in Manager, select **dosya.dev**, and run **Check connection** again. The account and workspace should still be correct. Installation and authorization create no photo gallery by themselves. To verify publishing separately, configure a **dosya.dev** service in **Publish Services**, create a test published collection, add one non-confidential photo and click **Publish**. Confirm the resulting file/gallery in that workspace. The second service, **dosya Archive (originals)**, archives originals and XMP sidecars; it does not back up the Lightroom catalog or edit history. Keep your normal catalog backup. ## Fix installation or connection failures | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | Dosya is absent from Plug-in Manager | Confirm you are using Classic, unpack the ZIP and add the actual `dosya.lrplugin` directory. If it moved, add its new permanent location. | | **The connection request expired. Start again.** | Click Connect... for a fresh code and complete approval within ten minutes. Do not reuse the expired browser tab. | | **The connection was declined in the browser.** | Start again only if you intended to grant this workspace connection. | | **This connection request was already used. Start again.** | Return to Lightroom and initiate a new request. The authorization is single-use. | | API-key limit denial | Revoke an unused key from **Profile → API keys**, or review the plan's cap, then retry connecting. The browser and plug-in return the cap explanation. | | **dosya connection expired or was revoked. Reconnect in File > Plug-in Manager.** | Reconnect after checking that revocation was intentional. A failed authenticated check clears the obsolete local secret. | | **Could not reach dosya securely (…)** | Check the system clock, certificate trust, URL/network filtering and HTTPS connectivity. Do not bypass certificate checks. | | **Network problem talking to dosya (…)** | Restore connectivity and retry. Temporary poll errors are retried until the request expires; certificate failures need correction. | Under **dosya troubleshooting**, **Write a debug log (keys and passwords are never written)** enables diagnostic logging. Include the exact failure and plug-in/Classic versions when reporting it; do not share an API-key secret. ## Update, disable or remove There is no in-plug-in updater. Download a fresh official ZIP, finish any active publish/archive job, quit Classic and replace the installed folder at the same location with the new extracted package. Reopen Lightroom and verify the listed version and Check connection. The toolkit identifier remains the same, so reinstalling code is not a request to revoke a connection or remove online files. Keep a copy of the prior package until the new version works. Disabling or removing the entry stops Lightroom running the plug-in; it does not revoke the server key. For a complete disconnect, click **Disconnect** first. The confirmation says **The key Lightroom uses is deleted in dosya. Galleries and files stay online.** If offline, the plug-in forgets its local key even when server deletion fails; revoke the dedicated key in Dosya once connectivity returns. Existing galleries and their links must be managed separately if you want them taken offline. Removing the local plug-in folder cannot delete those files. ## Expected result Classic loads the released plug-in and its Check connection identifies the intended Dosya workspace. Publishing and originals archiving remain separate actions that you start after this installation check. ## Related guides - [Configure a Lightroom publish service](/integrations/lightroom-configure-publish-service) - [Choose a Dosya app](/account/choose-app)

title: Publish a Lightroom collection as a Dosya gallery
summary: Publish a Lightroom collection as a Dosya folder and client gallery, follow live progress, and reconcile the final receipt with retry queues.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUploader.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Publishing renders JPEGs, ensures a gallery folder and share link, uploads new bytes or versions existing files, and registers gallery items. A successful edit becomes a new Dosya file version instead of a duplicate when the stored remote file still exists in the gallery folder. ## Steps 1. Select the Dosya published collection and review **New Photos to Publish** plus **Modified Photos to Re-Publish**. Confirm the active service points to the intended workspace. 2. Open **Edit Gallery** and verify title, favourites, downloads, expiry, metadata stripping, and password; first publish applies these settings while creating the link. 3. Click **Publish**. Lightroom shows **Publishing N photos to dosya** and updates `Uploading X of N (Y in flight)` while up to the configured 1–4 uploads run. 4. Keep Lightroom and the catalog open until rendering, upload, and gallery registration finish. Canceling can leave already-uploaded files online while later renditions remain unattempted. 5. Read any `Published N, failed N, not attempted N.` summary and its grouped reasons. Failed or unattempted photos remain in Lightroom’s publish queues for a later **Publish**. 6. Open the gallery in a private browser and compare title, order, cover, photo count, access, and download behavior. The first live item becomes cover when no cover was set. **Partial registration.** If uploaded files could not yet be added as gallery items, Lightroom reports that they are uploaded and the next publish adds them. Such photos are marked **Modified Photos to Re-Publish** when the catalog write succeeds. **Deletion recovery.** If a remembered cloud file was deleted or moved out of the gallery folder, publish uploads a fresh file in the correct folder rather than versioning the missing or moved record. ## Expected result Successful photos show as published, the Dosya folder and gallery contain the intended live items, and every failure or unattempted photo remains visibly queued for retry. ## Related guides - [Connect a Lightroom catalog](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link)

title: Troubleshoot Lightroom publish network failures
summary: Recover from Lightroom publish network failures after the three-in-a-row stop, preserve completed uploads, and retry only queued photos safely.
verification: Reviewed against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaErrors.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUploader.lua on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The publisher counts consecutive failures classified as network errors. A successful upload resets the count; three network failures in a row stop the batch so every remaining photo does not repeat the same retries. ## Steps 1. Read the final dialog and record `Published N, failed N, not attempted N.` plus each grouped failure reason before dismissing it. 2. Look for `dosya could not be reached for 3 photos in a row, so the rest were not attempted. Check your connection, then publish again.` This identifies the deliberate batch stop. 3. Keep completed photos in the published collection. Do not remove and re-add them: successful renditions already have remote file IDs and remain published. 4. Restore internet access, DNS, TLS, or proxy reachability, then use **File > Plug-in Manager > dosya.dev > Check connection** to verify the stored key still works. 5. Reopen the collection and inspect **Modified Photos to Re-Publish** and **New Photos to Publish**. These queues hold failed and unattempted photos from the partial run. 6. Click **Publish** again and reconcile the new counts. If instability continues, reduce **Uploads at once** toward 1 in the publish-service settings before another attempt. **Different stop classes.** Authentication, connection, quota, and some rate or server conditions can stop a batch immediately instead of waiting for three network failures. Use the exact grouped message; reconnecting will not fix a quota refusal. **Idempotent intent.** The uploader uses stable remote IDs and idempotency keys. Retrying the queued Lightroom items is safer than manually uploading rendered files, because the publish relationship can version the correct file and restore gallery registration. ## Expected result Previously completed photos stay published, only queued work resumes after connectivity is healthy, and the final run leaves no unexplained failed or unattempted items. ## Related guides - [Connect Lightroom](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Remove a photo from a Lightroom gallery
summary: Remove a published photo, choose whether its file stays or enters recoverable Trash, and verify clients can no longer see that gallery item.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/tests/delete_sort_test.lua, and apps/api/src/pages/api/galleries/[id]/items/remove.ts. No Lightroom or production gallery was changed.
body: Removing a photo from a published collection first unregisters it from the client gallery. The publish-service setting **When a photo is removed:** decides whether the stored Dosya file stays in its gallery folder or moves to recoverable Trash; neither choice permanently deletes it. ## Steps 1. Open Lightroom Classic’s **Library** module and select the published collection under **Publish Services → dosya.dev**. 2. Open that publish service’s settings and read **When a photo is removed:** before changing the collection. **Hide it from the gallery (keep the file)** is the default; **Hide it and move the file to dosya trash** adds a Trash request. 3. Select the intended published photo and remove it from this collection. Lightroom places the removal in its pending publish state. 4. Choose **Publish** on the collection. If gallery-item removal fails with an error other than not found, the plug-in keeps the removal pending instead of claiming success. 5. Open the gallery link in a signed-out browser and confirm the photo is absent. Existing selections for that gallery item are also removed when the server unregisters it. 6. Check Dosya **Files** or **Trash** according to the saved setting. A Trash failure can still leave the photo hidden from clients and produces a warning that its file stayed in the gallery folder. The gallery-removal request accepts at most 1,000 file IDs at once. The plug-in confirms each successful Lightroom removal before trying optional Trash moves, which prevents a failed Trash request from re-registering the photo on the next publish. ## Expected result The chosen photo disappears from the public gallery. With the default option, its Dosya file remains live in the gallery folder; with the Trash option, it enters recoverable Trash unless the plug-in reports that move failed. No permanent deletion occurs in this workflow. If the plug-in reports **photos were removed from the gallery but their files could not be moved to the dosya trash**, do not publish repeatedly. Confirm the client-facing removal, then resolve the named permission, lock, storage or connection error before moving the file separately. ## Related guides - [Publish a gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Edit gallery options](/integrations/lightroom-edit-gallery-options)

title: Republish Lightroom edits without duplicate gallery items
summary: Republish a modified Lightroom photo as a new version of its existing Dosya file, preserve the gallery position, and confirm no duplicate item appears.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaGallery.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUploader.lua, and apps/lightroom/tests/publish_test.lua. Republish behavior was verified in repository tests; no production publish ran.
body: A Lightroom republish sends the rendered edit to the existing Dosya `file_id`. Dosya records another version of that file, keeps its server-side name and leaves the gallery item in place instead of inserting a duplicate. ## Steps 1. In Lightroom Classic, open the published collection and confirm the edited photo appears under **Modified Photos to Re-Publish**. 2. Check that the collection still has its remote gallery ID and the photo still points to its published remote file. A missing or moved remote file follows the fresh-upload recovery path instead. 3. Select the modified photo and choose **Publish**. Leave Lightroom open while **Publishing … photos to dosya** reports rendered and in-flight work. 4. Wait for the photo to leave **Modified Photos to Re-Publish**. Three consecutive photos that exhaust their network retries stop later photos and report that the rest were not attempted. 5. Open the gallery and confirm the photo occupies its previous position once. In Dosya, inspect **Versions** for the same file ID and verify the newest bytes contain the edit. 6. Read any **dosya** summary. Failed or unattempted photos remain under **Modified Photos to Re-Publish** or **New Photos to Publish** and can be retried with another Publish. Republishing is not an overwrite without history. The existing file receives a new version and keeps its stored name even when an export naming template now proposes another name. If the original Dosya file was deleted or moved outside the gallery folder, the plug-in uploads a fresh file into the gallery and replaces the stale item reference. ## Expected result One gallery item represents the Lightroom photo, its Dosya file keeps the same ID when still available, and its current version contains the new render. Earlier retained versions remain subject to the workspace history policy and continue consuming storage. For **A file with this name already exists in this folder**, inspect whether another visible or hidden file owns the name. The plug-in avoids turning a new photo into a version of an unrelated file and may use a suffixed name only for a genuinely new upload. ## Related guides - [Connect a Lightroom catalog](/integrations/lightroom-connect-catalog) - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link)

title: Resume an interrupted Lightroom archive upload
summary: Resume an interrupted Lightroom original archive within its 23-hour session window, skip completed parts safely, and verify stored size and summary counts.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaArchive.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaUploader.lua, apps/lightroom/tests/archive_test.lua, and apps/lightroom/tests/upload_test.lua. Production behavior for “Resume an interrupted Lightroom archive upload” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **dosya Archive** export reads original files directly instead of rendering them. Originals larger than the one-shot ceiling use a multipart session keyed by source path, byte size and modification time, so a later identical export can continue with missing parts. ## Steps 1. Keep the interrupted original at the same path with the same size and modification time. Changing any of those values intentionally starts a different upload identity. 2. Reopen Lightroom Classic **Export**, choose the **dosya Archive** service and retain the same **Archive root folder** and XMP-sidecar choice. 3. Start the export again before the stored session has been idle for 23 hours. The plug-in asks Dosya for session status and skips parts already accepted. 4. Leave Lightroom running until each original reports success or a named failure. Missing local bytes produce **Could not read the local file (…)** rather than an empty upload. 5. Read the **dosya archive** summary: **Archived _ files, skipped _ already in dosya, failed _.** It separately reports virtual copies and photos not attempted. 6. In Dosya, confirm the original’s exact filename and stored byte size. The completion path rejects a result with **Size check failed** when server and local sizes differ. Files at or below 50 MiB normally use one-shot upload; a buffered Lightroom session can lower that path to 8 MiB. Larger files use multipart. An original already present with the same name and size is skipped, while an XMP sidecar is skipped only when its stored SHA-256 also matches because edits can preserve sidecar size. ## Expected result A compatible interrupted multipart upload continues without resending accepted parts, then clears its saved session after completion. Unchanged finished originals are skipped, local source files remain untouched, and the summary accounts for every selected photo. An expired, failed, missing or mismatched session starts a new upload. Quota, authentication and stop-batch failures are not bypassed by rerunning; resolve the reported cause before another export. ## Related guides - [Configure Lightroom publishing](/integrations/lightroom-configure-publish-service) - [Resume an interrupted upload](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Review connected Lightroom catalogs
summary: Review every Lightroom catalog connection by computer, connected age, and last use; identify stale entries before revoking the matching catalog key.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/lightroom.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/connect.ts. The account-wide table was not opened in production.
body: The web page **Integrations → Lightroom Classic** lists catalog credentials created by the plug-in connect flow. This table is account-wide: changing the active workspace affects the gallery table below it, not which Lightroom connection rows appear. ## Steps 1. Sign in to the Dosya account used during Lightroom approval and open **Integrations → Lightroom Classic**. 2. Under **Your Lightroom connections**, match each **Computer** name to a Lightroom Classic installation you still control. The displayed name comes from the key label after `Lightroom Classic:`. 3. Read the relative connection age beneath the computer name, then distinguish key creation from catalog use. It is the API key creation time, not the catalog file’s date. 4. Compare **Last used** with recent publishing activity. **Never** means that stored connection has no recorded authenticated use yet. 5. If the table says **No catalog is connected yet. Follow the steps below to connect one.**, confirm you opened the correct Dosya account before starting another connection. 6. Record the exact stale computer row before using its actions menu; multiple catalog connections can have similar device names and revocation is immediate. A new Lightroom connection requires an unconfined workspace membership with `upload_files`, `create_share_links` and `create_folders`. The approval flow also creates an API key and therefore remains subject to the account’s API-key cap. ## Expected result Every active Lightroom installation has one recognizable computer row with plausible connected and last-used times. Unknown, duplicate or obsolete rows are identified for a deliberate revoke instead of being confused with galleries in the active workspace. **Could not load your connections. Please try again.** means the key list request failed; it does not prove that every catalog is disconnected. Reload while signed in and preserve the row names before changing anything. ## Related guides - [Create and manage API keys](/developers/api-key) - [Choose a Dosya app](/account/choose-app)

title: Review Lightroom gallery status in Dosya
summary: Read the active workspace gallery row, including photo, client, selection and link state, then open the link to verify the published collection.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/lightroom.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/galleries/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/galleries/store.ts, apps/api/src/lib/galleries/limits.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/galleries/access.ts. Production gallery data was not requested.
body: The **Galleries** table on **Integrations → Lightroom Classic** is scoped to the active Dosya workspace. It is a read-only status view; publishing and gallery edits remain in Lightroom Classic. ## Steps 1. Switch Dosya to the workspace that received the published collection, then open **Integrations → Lightroom Classic**. 2. Locate the gallery title and read the photo count beneath it. The server permits up to 10,000 registered gallery items. 3. Review the **Clients** column. With favourites enabled it shows named-client and selection totals; otherwise it reads **Selections off**. 4. Interpret **Link** exactly: **Live**, **Password protected**, **Link expired**, **Link revoked**, or **Link removed**. Revoked and expired links are not usable simply because a URL remains stored. 5. Use **Copy** only when a link exists, or choose the open icon. If clipboard access fails, Dosya reports **Could not copy the link** and tells you to copy from the address bar. 6. Open the link in a signed-out browser and compare its title and visible photos with the intended Lightroom collection before sending it to a client. The page loads gallery API pages newest-first, up to 20 pages in the current UI. Each server page defaults to 50 rows and is capped at 100. A gallery created by another member is visible only when your role can view all shares and the gallery folder is within your allowed reach. ## Expected result The active workspace row shows the expected title, registered-photo count, client/selection state and current link condition. The opened public gallery matches the published collection rather than a similarly named row elsewhere. If the card says **No galleries yet. Publish a collection from Lightroom Classic and it shows up here.**, verify both workspace and account. **Could not load your galleries. Please try again.** is a retrieval failure, not an empty-gallery result. ## Related guides - [Publish a gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Edit gallery options](/integrations/lightroom-edit-gallery-options)

title: Revoke a Lightroom catalog connection
summary: Revoke one Lightroom catalog key, confirm that computer is signed out immediately, and understand why its previously published galleries stay online.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/lightroom.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/lightroom/connection.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/lightroom/connect.ts. Production behavior for “Revoke a Lightroom catalog connection” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Revoking a Lightroom connection deletes the API key created for that computer. It signs the catalog out immediately after cache invalidation, but it does not revoke gallery links or remove files already published. ## Steps 1. Open **Integrations → Lightroom Classic** in the Dosya account that approved the catalog. 2. Under **Your Lightroom connections**, match the **Computer**, **Connected** and **Last used** values to the installation that must stop publishing. 3. Open that row’s actions menu and choose **Revoke**. 4. Read **Revoke _computer_?** and its warning: **Lightroom Classic on that computer is signed out and can no longer publish. Galleries already published stay online.** 5. Choose the destructive **Revoke** button once and wait for **Connection revoked — That catalog is signed out of dosya.** The row should disappear without a page reload. 6. On the affected computer, run a harmless status refresh. If that catalog should publish again, reconnect through browser approval. The revoked key cannot be restored. This action removes one API key, not the Lightroom catalog, collection, gallery, share URL or stored photo. A reconnect creates a new credential and still requires the workspace permissions for uploads, folders and share links. ## Expected result The selected connection row disappears and that Lightroom installation can no longer authenticate. Previously published galleries remain reachable according to their own link expiry, password and revocation settings. **Revoke failed** leaves the row in place and includes the server message. Do not assume access ended until the success toast appears or the key is absent from **Profile → API keys**. ## Related guides - [Create and manage API keys](/developers/api-key) - [Choose a Dosya app](/account/choose-app)

title: Find who selected a photo in Lightroom
summary: Sync gallery selections, filter on Selected by (dosya), read multiple client names and submission state, and confirm cleared picks disappear after resync.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMetadata.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaSelections.lua, and apps/lightroom/tests/selections_test.lua. Lightroom Library filtering was not exercised in a production catalog.
body: **Selected by (dosya)** is read-only plug-in metadata written by **Sync client selections from dosya**. It is searchable and browsable in Lightroom Library, and can contain several sorted client names separated by commas. ## Steps 1. Publish the collection with favourites enabled, let the client select photos, then choose **Library → Plug-in Extras → Sync client selections from dosya**. 2. Wait for **Client selections synced** and confirm the summary includes the intended gallery and client counts. 3. In Lightroom Classic’s **Library** module, expose plug-in metadata and choose **Selected by (dosya)** in the Metadata filter or searchable field list. 4. Select a client value. A photo chosen by Anna and Ben is stored as `Anna, Ben`; use the exact displayed client name when narrowing the result. 5. Inspect **Selection status (dosya)** as a photo-level aggregate: `submitted` means at least one selecting client submitted, while `in progress` means none did. Do not attribute `submitted` to every displayed name; use membership in each **dosya client selections → _gallery_ - _client_** collection to identify who selected the photo, then verify its **dosya gallery** value. 6. After a client deselects a photo, sync again and verify the names and status clear from that photo and it leaves the matching client collection. The plug-in maps remote file IDs back to published photos and falls back to the Lightroom photo UUID saved as `source_ref`. Client names identify what the visitor entered; they are not authenticated Dosya account identities. The per-client collections preserve individual selection membership even though **Selection status (dosya)** collapses every selecting client into one aggregate value. ## Expected result The Library filter returns photos currently selected by the named client, per-client collections identify each selector, the photo-level status follows the any-submitted rule, and a later sync removes metadata for selections that no longer exist. If the field is empty after a successful sync, confirm the chosen photo belongs to the synced published collection. A gallery read failure appears in the sync summary; **Lightroom’s catalog is busy, so the client selections were not written. Try again in a moment.** means nothing was changed. ## Related guides - [Enable client favourites](/integrations/lightroom-enable-client-favourites) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Set a Lightroom gallery cover
summary: Select one already-published photo, run Set as gallery cover, confirm the success dialog, and verify the public gallery opens with that cover.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMenu.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/Info.lua, apps/api/src/pages/api/galleries/[id].ts, and apps/api/src/lib/galleries/store.ts. Production behavior for “Set a Lightroom gallery cover” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The cover command accepts the current Lightroom target photo only when it is already a published item in the selected Dosya collection. It cannot use an unpublished photo or a photo published to another gallery. ## Steps 1. In the **Library** module, select the intended Dosya published collection in the **Publish Services** panel. 2. Publish the collection at least once. Without a remote gallery ID, the plug-in says **Select a dosya.dev published collection in the Publish Services panel first, then publish it at least once.** 3. Make one already-published photo the target photo. Merely highlighting an unpublished local image is insufficient. 4. Choose **Library → Plug-in Extras → Set as gallery cover**. 5. Wait for **Gallery cover updated**. **This photo is not published in this gallery yet. Publish first.** means its published-photo record was not found in that collection. 6. Open the gallery link in a signed-out browser and confirm the intended image is used as the cover without altering the gallery item order. The API accepts `cover_file_id` only when that file is registered in the same gallery. Changing the cover updates gallery metadata; it does not copy, re-render, version or delete the photo. ## Expected result The success dialog appears and the public gallery uses the selected published photo as its cover. The file stays in the same Dosya folder and no additional gallery item is created. A connection warning means the plug-in has no usable account credential. An API refusal can also indicate that the gallery is outside the key’s workspace, belongs to another member without `view_all_shares`, or no longer contains the photo. ## Related guides - [Publish a gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery) - [Edit gallery options](/integrations/lightroom-edit-gallery-options)

title: Sync Dosya client selections into Lightroom
summary: Import client favourites into read-only metadata and per-client collections, optionally add Pick or color labels, and verify the exact sync summary.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaSelections.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaPublishServiceProvider.lua, apps/lightroom/dosya.lrdevplugin/DosyaMetadata.lua, apps/lightroom/tests/selections_test.lua, and apps/api/src/lib/galleries/limits.ts. Production behavior for “Sync Dosya client selections into Lightroom” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The sync command reads favourites from Dosya and performs one Lightroom catalog write. It updates plug-in metadata, refreshes one collection per client and can optionally set Pick flags or a chosen color label. ## Steps 1. Open publish-service settings and choose whether **Set the Pick flag** or **Set color label** should alter metadata during the next selection sync. 2. To sync one gallery, select its Dosya published collection. With no selected Dosya collection, the command walks every published collection belonging to the plug-in. 3. Choose **Library → Plug-in Extras → Sync client selections from dosya**. 4. Wait while the plug-in reads each gallery’s clients and file IDs. A stop-batch authentication failure writes nothing; nonfatal gallery failures are reported in the final summary. 5. Read **Client selections synced** and its gallery, client, selected, and cleared counts. Client notes are appended once and capped at 500 UTF-16 units. 6. Inspect **dosya client selections** and its `_gallery_ - _client_` child collections, then verify **Selected by (dosya)** and **Selection status (dosya)** on representative photos. The server allows up to 200 named clients per gallery. The plug-in stores client-entered names, not verified account identities. A photo's **Selection status (dosya)** is aggregate: it reads `submitted` when any client selecting that photo has submitted, and `in progress` only when none has. Use the photo's membership in each per-client collection to identify who selected it; the aggregate field does not attribute submission to one client. Deselecting and syncing removes stale metadata and collection membership. ## Expected result Each client collection contains exactly that client’s current picks, affected photos show accurate read-only Dosya metadata, optional Pick/color changes follow the saved service settings, and the summary accounts for cleared selections and partial gallery-read failures. For **Lightroom’s catalog is busy, so the client selections were not written. Try again in a moment.**, close other catalog writes and retry. A reconnect message after 401 requires a new Lightroom approval; repeated sync cannot revive a revoked key. ## Related guides - [Enable client favourites](/integrations/lightroom-enable-client-favourites) - [Publish a Lightroom gallery](/integrations/lightroom-publish-gallery)

title: Reading link access and download activity
summary: Use a sharing link's analytics to review first opens, downloads, devices, countries and recipient verification without overstating identity.
verification: Verified the current English Shared analytics page, web/API source and focused analytics tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated local fixtures and fictional recipients and access events. The review confirmed 7/30/90-day timelines, first-open IP-hash deduplication, non-deduplicated downloads, eight-character visitor handles, country and user-agent fields, 5,000-row reach cap, 25-row access-log page, recipient verification timestamps, absent per-recipient event attribution, ownership and view-all permission gates, and revoke controls. No production traffic was generated.
body: Open **Shared**, select a link, and use its analytics page to review first opens, downloads and recent access events. Treat the data as delivery evidence rather than a complete identity record: public visitors are represented by an irreversible hashed-address handle, and even private-link events are not attached to a named recipient. ## Before you start - Select the workspace where the link was created. - Your role needs **View own shared links** for links you created or **View all shared links** for teammates' links. Folder confinement and hidden-item rules still apply. - Perform a controlled test in a fresh browser when you need to learn how a known action appears. - Do not compare these counters directly with Help Center page views or website analytics. They measure different events on different systems. ## Steps: open a link's analytics 1. Open **Shared**. 2. Stay on **By me** and find the link by file name, status or expiry. 3. Select the row or linked file name. 4. Check the header and URL bar to confirm the exact link. Different URLs for the same file have separate histories. 5. Review the exposure statement, link controls and access settings before interpreting the chart. ## Measurement limits and chart interpretation - **Exposure** reports distinct first-time visitors for a public link, or how many invited addresses completed verification for a restricted link. - **Access over time** separates **First opens** and **Downloads** by day. Choose **7d**, **30d** or **90d** to change the analysis window. - A returning visitor is deduplicated by its hashed IP address and does not create another first-open count. The system stores the hash rather than the raw address and cannot recover the address from it. - Downloads are counted separately and are not proof of unique people. One visitor can create more than one download event. - Device and browser summaries are derived from the request's user-agent string. They can be incomplete or misleading when software masks or changes that value. - The reach breakdown reads at most 5,000 rows and marks the result when that cap truncates it. For a restricted link, **Invited** shows each address and whether it has verified. A verification timestamp proves control of that inbox at that moment. It is not a record of every later open. ## Read the access log 1. Scroll to **Access log**. 2. Use **All**, **Opens** or **Downloads** to filter the currently loaded events. 3. Read **When**, **Event**, **Visitor**, **Country** and **Device** together. 4. Treat the eight-character visitor value as an opaque grouping handle. It is a shortened hash, not an account ID or recoverable IP address. 5. A dash in Country means the edge could not place that event or the row predates country collection. 6. The current response loads up to 25 newest log rows and reports how many events exist in total. ## Run a controlled test 1. Note the current first-open and download totals. 2. Open the exact URL in a fresh private browser or separate network you control. 3. Complete any email or password gate. 4. Open the file, then download it once if downloads are enabled. 5. Return to the analytics page and refresh. The first open can appear within about a minute; the download should be a separate event. 6. Compare the visitor handle, time, country and device with the test context, allowing for proxy, VPN and browser user-agent differences. Repeated opens from the same hashed address do not raise the first-open count again. This is why a manual sequence of three refreshes can produce one first open. ## Revoke when activity is unexpected If the link appears in a place you did not intend or the activity pattern is concerning, choose **Revoke** in the header, read the confirmation and revoke the link. The URL then stops working. The analytics record remains so you can review its earlier activity, but revocation cannot remove copies already downloaded. ## Expected result The analytics page shows the selected link's status, security controls, first-open timeline, download events, broad client context and, for restricted links, recipient verification state. It also explains the measurement gaps so the data is not mistaken for proof of a particular person's action. ## Troubleshooting **A known open does not increase the count.** The same hashed address may have opened the link before, the counter write may still be settling, or the workspace was temporarily migrating and skipped a statistical write rather than blocking the recipient. **The download total is larger than the visitor count.** Downloads are not deduplicated as unique people. One visitor can download more than once. **Country is missing or surprising.** Country comes from the network edge at event time. VPNs, corporate gateways and unavailable edge data can change or remove it. **A private link shows verified recipients but anonymous log rows.** This is expected. The recipient list records who completed the code check; access events have no recipient column and cannot be attributed to one invited address. **Link counts differ from Help Center views.** Share analytics records access to one delivery URL. Help Center views measure visits to documentation pages through a separate system, so the definitions and deduplication are unrelated. ## Frequently asked questions ### Do view and download counts identify a specific person? No. A public visitor is represented by a hashed-address handle, and restricted-link events are not joined to a named recipient. Recipient verification is shown separately. ### Why does refreshing the link not add another view? The view metric represents first opens by hashed address. Returning visits from the same address are deduplicated. ### Can I keep the history after revoking a link? Yes.
