The analytics record remains available for permitted workspace members while the public URL returns a revoked response. ## Related guides - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Sharing with named email recipients](/sharing/named-recipients) - [Setting link expiry and checking the actual expiration](/sharing/link-expiry) - [Revoking a sharing link](/sharing/revoke-link)

title: Setting link expiry and checking the actual expiration
summary: Choose a preset or custom expiry, understand workspace and plan caps, and confirm when the finished sharing link will stop working.
verification: Verified the current English Share dialog, public expired-link page, Shared and analytics views, web/API source and focused expiry tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated local current-API fixtures and a fictional file. The review confirmed preset, custom and Never input; one-minute minimum; ten-year validation ceiling; workspace default and maximum expiry behavior; Free-plan seven-day clamping; recipient 410 expired response; and retention of the original workspace file. No production link was allowed to expire during the review.
body: Choose **Expires in** while creating a sharing link, then verify the finished link in **Shared**. The selected value is a request: a workspace maximum or the Free-plan seven-day limit can shorten it, so the date shown after creation is the date to trust. Expiry stops new access through that URL. It does not delete the original file from its workspace and cannot remove a copy someone already downloaded. ## Before you start - Upload the file completely and confirm you have permission to create sharing links. - Decide when recipients should lose new access. Include enough time for their timezone and working hours. - Use a fresh recipient browser for testing. A browser already showing downloaded content is not evidence that a later request will still work. - Review workspace policy with an owner if links repeatedly end earlier than expected. ## Steps: choose an expiry 1. Open **Files**, find the item and choose **Share**. 2. Select **By link** for an ordinary URL, or stay on **By email** when sending to named recipients. Both flows use the same **Expires in** control. 3. Choose **1 hour**, **24 hours**, **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, **Custom date…** or **Never**. 4. For **Custom date…**, enter a local date and time at least one minute in the future. The app converts that local value to the exact timestamp stored for the link. 5. Review any password, view-only or download-limit settings separately, then generate or send the link. ## Check the actual expiry 1. Open **Shared** after the link is created. 2. Find the item and read **Expiry** and **Status**. An approaching deadline appears as **Expiring soon**. 3. Select the link to open its details. The **Link controls** rail shows the remaining time or **Never**. 4. If the date is earlier than your requested date, keep the displayed result. Do not promise the longer date to recipients. 5. Copy and test the final URL only after reviewing this value. The application currently validates custom expiries up to ten years from creation. A workspace can configure a shorter maximum. On Free, every newly created link is limited to seven days even when you selected **30 days**, **90 days** or **Never**. The tighter limit wins. ## Expiry limits and boundary behavior The API compares the stored expiry timestamp with the current time. Once it has passed, requests for that share URL return an expired response and the public page displays **Link expired**. A recipient who has not already saved the file cannot start a new view or download through that link. Because the value is an exact timestamp, two people in different timezones can see different clock representations of the same moment. Choose the deadline with the recipient's location in mind. ## Expected result The link remains usable until its stored expiry, subject to every other access setting. After that instant, the recipient sees **Link expired** and the owner sees the link as expired in **Shared**. The file, its versions, comments and other sharing links remain in the workspace. ## Troubleshooting **The expiry is earlier than the date I selected.** Check the finished link in Shared. A workspace maximum or the Free-plan seven-day cap can silently lower a longer request, including **Never**. **Custom date is rejected.** Choose a valid local date at least one minute ahead. Dates more than 3,650 days from creation are rejected by the current API. **The recipient says the link expired sooner than expected.** Compare the actual stored expiry, the recipient's timezone and the complete URL they used. Confirm they did not open an older link to the same file. **The page says revoked rather than expired.** Someone with permission ended the link manually. Revocation is a separate terminal state and can occur before the scheduled expiry. **The recipient still has a copy.** Expiry controls future service from Dosya. It cannot recall bytes already downloaded or a screen capture taken while the link was active. ## Frequently asked questions ### Why is the expiry earlier than the date I selected? A workspace maximum or the Free-plan seven-day maximum shortened the requested lifetime. Check the actual result in **Shared**. ### Does an expired link delete the original file? No. Only that URL stops working. The workspace file and other links remain until separately changed or deleted. ### What does Never mean? It requests no scheduled expiry. A workspace maximum or Free-plan policy can still replace it with a finite date, and the owner can revoke the link at any time. ## Related guides - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Sharing with named email recipients](/sharing/named-recipients) - [Reading link access and download activity](/sharing/link-activity) - [Revoking a sharing link](/sharing/revoke-link)

title: Work with Live Photos and paired media
summary: Identify Dosya Live Photo pairs, play their motion safely, move or copy both files, and avoid separating still and video during deletion or download.
verification: Verified locally against apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/live-pairs.ts, apps/web/src/components/live-photo-stage.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/live-photos.ts and apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx. Production media was not moved or deleted and no production action was performed.
body: Dosya derives a Live Photo pair when a HEIC, HEIF, JPG, or JPEG still and a MOV or MP4 share the same case-insensitive filename stem and folder. The motion file must be no larger than 40 MiB. Pairing is recalculated from the current listing rather than stored permanently. ## Before you start - Keep both files in the same folder with the same stem, such as IMG_0042.HEIC and IMG_0042.MOV. Renaming or moving only one file breaks the derived pair on the next listing. - When several eligible videos share a stem, the query chooses the lowest file ID. A video over 41,943,040 bytes remains a normal video and is not attached as motion. - A pair consumes storage as two independent files. Downloading the still does not automatically download its motion component. ## Steps 1. Find the still carrying the **Live Photo** badge. Grid and viewer filmstrip collapse its twin into one stop, while list view keeps the motion row directly beneath the still and labels it **Live Photo video**. 2. Open the still. On web, hover to play the muted motion once, or select **Play Live Photo**. Leaving the stage pauses and rewinds; with reduced motion enabled, only the explicit button starts playback. 3. On mobile, press and hold for 400 ms to play while held, or tap **LIVE** for a play-through. The video is muted and does not loop. 4. Open **Details** and find **Live Photo video**. Confirm its name and size, then use that row's **Download** plus the still's normal **Download** when you need a complete local pair. 5. Moving or copying the still asks Dosya to move or copy the video separately. Verify both rows in the destination because the second request can fail after the still has already succeeded. 6. For ordinary deletion, leave **Also delete _video name_** selected to send both items to trash. Clear it only when you deliberately want the motion file to remain. ## Failure and irreversible behavior If the motion cannot load, **Play Live Photo** becomes disabled with **Video unavailable** and the still remains usable. Copy can report **Copied** with **The photo was copied, but its video could not be.** Delete can report **Deleted** with **Photo deleted, but its video could not be deleted.** Inspect both folders after either partial result. Permanent deletion never carries a remembered twin automatically because the trash listing does not expose pairing fields. Permanently delete each intended component explicitly; that action cannot be undone. Ordinary deletion keeps each file in trash and continues using storage until purge. ## Expected result The still displays one Live Photo identity, motion plays from its paired file, and both components reach the intended folder or trash when requested. Separate downloads remain separate local files. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Download files](/uploading/download-files) - [Move files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Locking or hiding a file and understanding access
summary: Choose view-only, password locking or role-based hiding, and understand how each setting changes workspace and share-link access.
verification: Verified the current English Files page, lock and hide dialogs, web/API source and focused access-control tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use an isolated local owner workspace with controlled current-API fixtures and fictional members. The review confirmed unlocked, view-only and password modes; the eight-character password minimum and one-hour unlock; hide-everyone, user and role targeting; hide-files permission behavior; inherited folder restrictions; and exclusion of hidden or fully locked descendants from folder shares. Production files and real recipient accounts were not used.
body: Locking controls what someone can do after they find an item. Hiding controls whether selected workspace members can find or open it at all. Use **View only** or **Password** when the item should remain visible with tighter access, and use **Hide** when it should disappear for everybody, specific users or specific roles. These controls reduce ordinary access. Anything displayed on a screen can still be photographed or captured, so view-only access is not a screenshot-prevention feature. ## Before you start - Select the correct workspace and use a harmless sample item when comparing roles. - Your role needs the appropriate lock or hide permission. If an action is absent from the file menu, ask a workspace owner or admin to review your role. - Decide whether you need to prevent downloads, require a password or remove the item from selected members' views. These outcomes use different controls. - Check existing sharing links. A full password lock stops links to the item while the lock remains; view-only and hidden-item rules have different effects. ## Steps: choose a lock mode 1. Open **Files** and find the file or folder. 2. Open its menu and choose **Lock**. If it already has a lock, the menu can say **Unlock** while still opening the same access dialog. 3. Choose one of the three modes: - **Unlocked** allows people who already have access to open, download and work with the item. - **View only** allows previewing but blocks downloading and editing. On a folder, members can browse and preview its contents but cannot download them. - **Password** requires a password to open the item. A folder password also prevents new content from being added inside it while fully locked. 4. For **Password**, enter at least eight characters. Updating an existing password replaces the old one. 5. Apply the change and confirm the lock icon appears on the row. An accepted password unlock lasts one hour for that member. A full lock on a folder also applies through its descendant tree. Remove the lock when ordinary workspace access should resume. ## Hide an item from workspace members 1. Open the item's menu and choose **Hide**. 2. Select the visibility rule: - **Visible** removes the hidden state. - **Hidden from everybody** hides the item from ordinary members who cannot manage hidden items. - **Hidden from specific users** lets you choose individual workspace members. - **Hidden from specific roles** applies the rule to every member assigned one of the selected roles. 3. If you choose users or roles, select at least one target. You cannot select yourself or your own role in the dialog. 4. Choose **Apply**. 5. Open **Files → Hidden** to review items you can manage, then compare the result while signed in as an affected test member. ## Access limits and comparison | Setting | Appears in Files | Can preview | Can download or edit | Existing share links | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Unlocked | Yes, when normal access allows | Yes | Yes, when role permissions allow | Continue under their own settings | | View only | Yes | Yes | No download or edit through the protected item | Preview-only behavior applies; screen capture remains possible | | Password | Yes, with a lock indicator | Only after unlock | Only after unlock and other permissions | Stop working while the target is fully locked | | Hidden | No for the targeted viewer | No | No | Hidden or locked descendants are excluded from folder shares; direct access is also gated | Role permissions, folder confinement and parent-folder rules still apply in every row. A lock or hide setting cannot grant access someone did not already have. ## Folder shares and hidden descendants When you create a sharing link for a folder, the Share dialog reports how many hidden or locked items inside that tree will be excluded. The link can still be created for the remaining content. This means a hidden file should not appear merely because one of its parent folders was shared. The same principle applies if an item becomes hidden or fully locked after a link was created: public share access is checked again, rather than treating the original link as a permanent bypass. ## Expected result The selected lock mode changes the allowed action without widening workspace membership. A targeted hide rule removes the item and its protected descendants from affected members and sharing surfaces. Members with permission to manage hidden files can still see them so they can change or remove the rule. ## Troubleshooting **Lock or Hide is missing.** Your role may not include the matching permission, the item may be in Deleted, or the current view may not support that mutation. Return to the live Files view and ask an owner to check your role. **A member can still see a hidden item.** Confirm that you targeted the member's current role or exact user account. A member with permission to manage hidden files intentionally sees hidden content. Parent and child rules can also differ, so inspect the whole folder chain. **A folder link contains fewer files than expected.** Reopen Share and read the excluded-item count. Hidden and fully locked descendants are omitted. Remove only the protection you intend to remove, then create or test the link again. **A password no longer works.** Check whether another manager updated or removed the lock. Passwords are replaced rather than retained as a list. Enter the current password, and remember that an unlock expires after one hour. **View only still allows a screenshot.** That is expected. View only removes supported download and edit paths; it cannot control another device's operating-system capture tools or camera. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can a hidden file appear in a folder share? It should be excluded for a viewer who is not allowed to see it. The folder Share dialog reports hidden and locked descendants that will not be included. ### Does view-only stop someone from taking a screenshot? No. It blocks supported download and edit actions while preserving preview access. Anything visible on screen can still be captured. ### Is hiding the same as deleting? No. The item stays live in the workspace. Hidden controls who can see it; Deleted is a recoverable trash state. ## Related guides - [Commenting on a file and managing replies](/files/comments-and-replies) - [Sharing a folder with a link](/sharing/folder-link) - [Sharing with named email recipients](/sharing/named-recipients) - [Reviewing exact duplicate files before removing copies](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Lock a folder with a password
summary: Set an eight-character folder password, understand inherited access blocks, and test the one-hour personal unlock without sharing the secret.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/lock-modal.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/lock-mode.ts, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/folder-locked-panel.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/lock.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/lib/rate-limit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/unlock-throttle.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/folders.ts, apps/api/src/lib/download-guard.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-gate.unit.test.ts and apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-write-gate.unit.test.ts. Verified labels, trimmed eight-character minimum, lock_files permission, separate per-isolate and persistent throttles, inherited full-lock behavior, one-hour viewer token and share/sync effects. Local source and focused tests only; no production folder was locked.
body: A folder password protects the folder and its descendants from members who have not unlocked that ancestor. It works alongside workspace membership, role permissions, folder confinement and hidden rules; knowing the password does not create membership or add a missing role capability. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, right-click the target folder and choose **Lock**. The menu is available only when the listing reports that your role can lock items; the API requires **Lock files** and otherwise returns `You don't have permission to lock folders`. 2. Check the folder chip in **Lock folder**. It identifies the name, file count and known total size. If a lock already exists, the status can show **Currently password-locked** or the member and relative time that set it. 3. Select **Password**. The description states that the folder opens only with a password, nothing can be added while locked, share links to contents stop working, and an unlock lasts an hour. 4. Enter a password whose length is at least eight characters after leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Internal spaces count toward the minimum. The client says **Use at least 8 characters.** and the server rejects a shorter trimmed value with `Password must be at least 8 characters`. 5. Store the secret in an approved password manager, then choose **Lock with password**. Success appears as **Locked with a password** and says the folder now needs a password to open. 6. Leave the folder and open it again. The page displays **“_Folder_” is locked** or **This folder is locked**, a **Folder password** field, **Unlock**, and **Go back**. 7. Enter the correct password. That member receives a personal access token lasting 3,600 seconds. Test a second member separately: another person's token does not open the folder for them. A full folder lock propagates through every nested subfolder. Until the viewer unlocks the locked ancestor, ordinary file reads, metadata operations, moves, deletion and new content inside the subtree are gated. Current sync snapshots omit both password-locked and view-only subtrees. Public share creation and existing share access do not borrow a member's personal unlock token, so links to protected descendants stay blocked while the ancestor remains password-locked. The password is not required for a member who already has **Lock files** to change the folder's protection in the lock dialog. Re-selecting **Password** on an existing password lock requires **New password** and **Update password**; the new value replaces the old one. **Remove lock** changes the stored mode to **Unlocked**, which is different from entering the password for temporary access. The unlock endpoint first applies a per-isolate limit of five requests for the same folder and IP over 900 seconds. That inexpensive layer can answer `Too many requests` with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header; because its counters are not shared across Worker isolates, it is separate from the persistent lock below. Each wrong password also increments the folder's stored failure count, regardless of the time between guesses or the IP address. The fifth wrong password sets a 900-second lock, but that fifth response is still `Incorrect password`; later requests that reach the stored check return `Too many attempts, try again later.` A correct password, password replacement, or lock removal resets this persistent count. `Folder not found` can instead mean the folder is outside your assigned subtree or hidden from you. ## Expected result The folder retains **Password** mode, unverified members cannot enter its tree, and one correct credential opens that tree only for the requesting member for one hour. Removing or replacing the lock remains an explicit separate action. ## Related guides - [Lock and hide files](/files/lock-and-hide) - [Workspace policies](/workspaces/policies)

title: Edit or close a file request
summary: Change a file request’s instructions, password, deadline, destination or limits, then revoke it safely without losing files already received.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/file-request-detail.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-request-edit-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/manage-own.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/guard.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/requests.ts and focused request route tests. Verified owner labels, role gates, editable fields, deadline notification behavior, destination containment/hidden/full-lock refusals, live max-files accounting including reserved in-progress slots and the distinct counter effects of owner Trash deletion versus public permanent withdrawal, terminal revocation, the rendered closed-page heading versus its API error, one-hour account-scoped personal unlocks, retained uploads and existing multipart sessions preserving their recorded destination. Existing edit and revoked-state captures were inspected and remain accurate.
body: Open **File requests**, choose the request, and use **Edit** for future submissions or **Revoke** to close the public upload URL permanently. Received files are normal workspace files: neither action moves or deletes them. ## Before you start - Check the status shown beside the request: **Active**, **Expired** or **Revoked**. - Wait for any transfer you intend to keep. Every multipart step rechecks the request, so revoking or expiring it can stop an unfinished large upload. - Note the current destination and the request’s server-side upload counter. **Max files** includes completed submissions plus slots reserved by uploads still in progress, so the visible received-file rows can be lower than the enforced count. - Roles with permission to manage every share can edit colleagues’ requests. A role limited to its own shares can manage only requests it created. A Viewer normally sees neither action. - Changing the deadline, password, destination or upload rules also requires **upload files** permission because those settings delegate upload rights to outside visitors. A creator who later loses that permission may still change the title or message, or revoke their request. ## Steps ### Edit the request 1. Open **File requests**, select the request title, and verify the target workspace. 2. Select **Edit**. A revoked request has no Edit action. 3. Change the fields that should apply to later attempts: - **Title (optional)** and **Message (optional)** replace the public instructions. - **Password** accepts a new value of at least eight characters. Leave **Leave blank to keep** empty to preserve the current secret, or select **Remove password** to make the link unprotected. - **Expires** offers **Keep current**, **Never**, **1 day**, **7 days**, **30 days** and **90 days** as applicable. Changing the deadline sends a deadline-change notification to recorded recipients; other edits do not send that notification. - **Upload destination** sends newly started uploads to the selected folder. A multipart upload already initialized before the edit keeps its original session destination and can finish there; earlier completed submissions also stay where they landed. - **Advanced options** contains **Allowed extensions**, **Max file size (MB)** and **Max files**. Clearing a value removes that request-specific restriction, while the owner plan and workspace total-storage cap still apply. 4. Select **Save changes** and wait for **Request updated — Your changes have been saved.** 5. Reload the public URL in a private window. Confirm its visible instructions and, when appropriate, stage a harmless file that meets the new rules. ### Close the upload URL 1. Return to the active request’s detail header and select **Revoke** beside **Edit**. 2. Wait until its badge reads **Revoked**. Recorded recipients are notified that the request ended; email delivery can finish after the status change. 3. Paste the request URL into a private window. The page must render **This request was closed** instead of the upload controls. Its metadata request returns **This file request has been revoked**, which the public page translates into that visitor-facing heading. 4. Review the request’s upload table and destination folder. Keep, move, rename or delete received files separately according to your retention needs. An owner-side **Delete** moves a file to **Deleted** and does not return a slot to this request’s **Max files** counter. ## Expected result An edited request reloads with the saved instructions and acceptance rules. Newly started uploads use its current destination, while an already initialized multipart session can still complete in the folder recorded when that session began. A closed request shows **Revoked**, refuses every new upload attempt and leaves previously received workspace files available to the owner. ## What each change does | Change | Effect on later use | Existing material | | --- | --- | --- | | Title or message | New page loads show the revised instructions | Does not rename received files or folders | | Password | New unlocks require the replacement, or no password after removal | An already issued password grant can remain valid for up to 30 minutes | | Expiry | The public route opens or closes at the new time | Does not alter files already stored | | Destination | Newly started uploads land in the new folder | Completed files and already initialized multipart sessions retain their recorded destination | | Allowed extensions or size | Subsequent upload checks use the revised values | Completed files are not revalidated | | Max files | Remaining capacity uses the server counter, including completed uploads and in-progress reserved slots | Lowering it does not delete submissions; owner-side Trash deletion does not decrement the counter | | Revoke | Every future upload hop is refused immediately | Received files and owner-side records remain | An expired request is still editable. Set **Expires** to a future preset or **Never** to accept uploads again. The web interface shows **Revoke** only while the request is active; reopening an expired request first makes that control available again. ## Destination locks and visibility The destination must be live, inside a folder-confined member’s allowed subtree, and visible to the editor. A hidden or missing folder is reported as **Folder not found in workspace**. A configured **Full lock** on the destination or an ancestor returns `folder_locked` and blocks the change. Unlocking that folder for your own browser does not authorize a public upload channel. Personal folder unlock grants are scoped to the signed-in account and last one hour. They are deliberately ignored when a request is created, moved or used. An authorized owner must remove or change the configured lock, or choose another destination. ## Troubleshooting **Edit or Revoke is missing.** Confirm the request is yours or that your role can manage all shares. Revoked requests cannot be edited. Expired requests retain **Edit**, but the web app withholds **Revoke** until the deadline is moved forward. **Saving access rules says you lack upload permission.** Your role may still manage wording or revoke the request, but it cannot extend public upload rights. Ask an Owner or Admin with the appropriate custom-role permissions. **The public page shows old instructions.** Reload the URL. A page already open can display cached wording, while every upload call still enforces current server rules. **No file slots remain after lowering Max files.** The server counter includes completed submissions and slots reserved by active uploads. Raise the maximum, clear the field to remove that request-specific cap, or create a new request. Deleting a received file from **Files** only moves it to **Deleted** and does not restore a request slot. Only the original public visitor’s **Remove** action decrements the counter, and that withdrawal permanently purges the file without Dosya Trash recovery. **Files now appear in two destinations.** This is expected after moving the request. Use the upload ledger to identify submissions, then organize the old and new folders without assuming the edit migrated anything. **A client was uploading when the request closed.** Do not assume partial progress created a usable file. Check the owner ledger and destination. If no completed receipt exists, create a new request when the client should retry. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can a revoked request be reopened? No. Revocation is irreversible for that token. Create another request and send its new URL. ### Does closing a request free workspace storage? No. An owner’s ordinary **Delete** moves stored files to **Deleted**, where they continue to use workspace allocation until retention or a later purge removes them. A public uploader’s **Remove** action is different: it permanently purges that submission and decrements the request counter immediately. ### Does editing the password encrypt previous uploads? No. The password controls entry to the public request page. It does not retroactively encrypt workspace files. ## Related guides - [Create a client file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Set request file types, sizes and counts](/sharing/request-limits) - [Change a request destination](/sharing/request-change-destination) - [Invite uploaders and track submissions](/sharing/request-recipients) - [Troubleshoot a rejected request upload](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request)

title: Manage redeemed storage packages
summary: Read each redeemed package’s provider, contribution and end or renewal state, then verify its exact effect on the account’s total storage limit.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/license-timeline.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/billing/provider-entitlement.ts on 2026-10-14. Production provider memberships were not changed.
body: Billing lists storage activated through Gumroad licenses and Dosya coupons separately from the Stripe subscription. ## Steps 1. Open **Billing → Redeemed packages**. Each row shows package name, provider, interval when known, redeemed date, timeline status, and **Adds [size]**. 2. Count only rows whose status is active. Ended or revoked grants remain visible for history but contribute zero bytes. 3. Compare the active package contribution with its row in **Storage ledger** and the bold **Total limit**. 4. For Gumroad packages, select **Manage on Gumroad** to manage the external membership. Its displayed next renewal is estimated from purchase date; Gumroad controls the exact charge date. 5. For a time-limited coupon, note the shown end date. Its storage stops counting at that time without deleting existing files. Redeemed capacity stacks with the base plan, Stripe add-ons, and referral bonuses. If losing a grant leaves usage above the new total, uploads pause while stored files remain intact. ## Expected result Every package has a clear active/ending/ended state and only active contributions are included in the account’s effective storage ceiling. If a provider membership is active but the row is stale, verify it in Gumroad and reload Billing. Do not redeem the same code repeatedly; terminal claims report that the link/code is used, expired, or unavailable. ## Related guides - [Redeem a storage license](/account/redeem-license) - [Verify storage after an upgrade](/account/plan-verify-storage-upgrade)

title: Zoom and expand photo map clusters
summary: Expand crowded map clusters, understand zoom and identical-coordinate behavior across Dosya clients, and open the correct file or folder safely.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 with apps/web/src/lib/map-cluster.ts, apps/web/src/pages/map.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/MapPage.tsx, and apps/mobile/src/map/mapHtml.generated.ts; production cluster interaction was not repeated.
body: Map groups nearby coordinates so a dense area does not create hundreds of overlapping controls. The badge is the number of items in the cluster; values above 999 are shortened to a whole-thousand label such as `1k`. ## Steps 1. Open **Map** and find a marker with a count badge greater than one. 2. Select the cluster. Dosya calculates an expansion level and moves the map there; on mobile, this ease animation lasts 350 milliseconds. 3. Repeat the selection if the cluster remains expandable. Clustering uses a 60-pixel radius and stops calculating new expansion levels after zoom 16. 4. When individual pins appear, choose the intended thumbnail, file icon, or folder icon. 5. If the same cluster no longer zooms, its members either share a coordinate or remain within the 60-pixel cluster radius at zoom 16. On web and desktop, selecting it opens the first file among the cluster's sample items; a cluster containing only sampled folders does nothing. Mobile opens the first leaf, which can be a file or folder. ## Expected result Nearby positions split into smaller clusters and then individual markers as zoom increases. Web and desktop build a cluster cover from at most six sample items, preferring a raster-photo thumbnail when one is present. A cluster made entirely from approximate upload origins may remain together because those items can share the same network coordinate. Cluster selection never edits coordinates or file contents. The only follow-up action is map movement or opening one member according to the platform behavior above. ## Troubleshooting - **The count does not split after repeated zooming.** Its items share a coordinate or are still too close for the 60-pixel clustering radius at zoom 16. Use the platform fallback, or open Files and identify them by folder and filename. - **A web or desktop folder-only cluster does not open.** That fallback searches the sampled members for a file. Zoom, adjust the folder/date filter, or open the folder through Files. - **The marker you expected is outside the cluster.** Clear restrictive dates or choose a broader folder; hidden, deleted, and locked files are absent from the map data. - **Approximate uploads dominate one point.** Hide **Show approximate locations** on web or desktop to leave EXIF GPS pins visible. ## Related guides - [Explore files on the map](/files/file-map) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Filter files on the map
summary: Filter the web map by folder, inclusive UTC date range, or approximate-location toggle without changing file metadata or the main Files listing.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/map-filter-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/map.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/map/pins.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/location/origin.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The browser map can narrow pins by folder and date, then separately include or hide approximate locations. These filters affect the map response only; they do not edit files or the **Files** page. **Filter behavior** The user needs access to the file page; the API otherwise returns **You don't have access to the files page**. A member confined to an assigned folder can filter only within that reachable subtree. Choosing a folder includes its descendants. **From** and **To** are applied as inclusive UTC calendar-day boundaries, which can differ from local midnight. ## Steps 1. Open **Map** in the web app and note the current counters: **located**, **approximate**, and **scanning…** when present. 2. Choose **All folders** to open **Filter map by folder**. Pick an allowed folder, then select **Apply folder**. Folder filtering includes nested descendants. 3. Set **From** or **To** if needed. Use both for a bounded period and remember that the server evaluates the inclusive dates in UTC. 4. Turn **Show approximate locations** off when you want only embedded GPS coordinates. Upload-origin locations are approximate and may identify a VPN or gateway rather than the capture point. 5. Wait for the refreshed no-store map response, then compare the pin count with the intended folder and date window. **Clear and diagnose** **Clear** resets the folder, From, and To fields. It does not reset **Show approximate locations**, so check that toggle separately. If all located items are approximate and the toggle is off, the map says **No pins to show** and **All located items are approximate - enable the toggle above to see them.** Deleted, hidden, and locked file pins are omitted. Folder pins follow separate visibility rules and are not evidence that every descendant file is readable. A pending scan can temporarily show **No files or folders with a location yet** with **Scanning your files for location…**. Filters are reversible and do not modify coordinates, capture dates, folder membership, or stored bytes. ## Expected result The web map shows only pins inside the chosen reachable subtree and inclusive UTC date range, with approximate pins included or excluded by their separate toggle. ## Related guides - [Explore files on the map](/files/file-map) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Troubleshoot a photo missing from the map
summary: Diagnose a photo missing from Map by checking scan state, GPS metadata, approximate upload origin, map filters, locks, hiding, deletion, and refresh.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/pages/api/map/pins.ts, apps/api/src/lib/location/origin.ts, apps/web/src/pages/map.tsx, and apps/mobile/app/map.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A photo appears on Map only when Dosya has a usable location and the current viewer is allowed to receive its pin. Work through metadata, processing, visibility, and filters in that order. **Where a pin comes from** Dosya can use embedded EXIF GPS coordinates from the image or an approximate origin recorded at upload. Approximate origin can point to a network gateway or VPN rather than where the photo was taken. If upload-origin recording was disabled and the file contains no EXIF GPS, Dosya has no location from which to create a pin. ## Steps 1. Find the exact photo in **Files** and confirm it is not in Trash. Record its name, folder, upload time, lock state, and whether the current member can open it. 2. Open **Map** in the browser. If the header shows **scanning…**, allow the location scan to finish and refresh. A newly processed image may not appear in the response already on screen. 3. Clear the folder, **From**, and **To** filters. Then verify **Show approximate locations** separately because **Clear** does not change that toggle. 4. If the photo came from a camera, inspect the original for GPS metadata. A resized, exported, or privacy-scrubbed copy may have lost EXIF coordinates even when the source retained them. 5. Check access as the affected member. Deleted, hidden, and locked file pins are excluded, and an assigned-root boundary can exclude a folder before map filtering is applied. **Read the empty state** **No geotagged photos yet** means no visible pin and no pending scan remain. **No files or folders with a location yet** plus **Scanning your files for location…** means processing is still pending. **No pins to show** with the approximate-location message means the toggle is hiding all current results. The mobile map does not expose the browser’s folder and date panel and may reuse a response for up to five minutes. Reopen it after the server scan or verify first in the browser. Location display does not rewrite the photo, and turning approximate pins off only changes the current view. ## Expected result The photo appears after processing when it has EXIF GPS or an allowed upload-origin location, passes the active filters, and is visible and unlocked for the member. ## Related guides - [Explore files on the map](/files/file-map) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Open a file from its map marker
summary: Identify photo, file and folder markers on Dosya Map, open the intended item across each client, and handle clusters or approximate locations.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 with apps/web/src/pages/map.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/MapPage.tsx, apps/mobile/app/map.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/map/pins.ts; production marker routing remains untested in this revision.
body: A map marker can represent a raster image, another file type, or a folder. Confirm the marker shape and location source before opening it, especially where several uploads share one approximate coordinate. ## Steps 1. Open **Map** in the correct workspace and apply any needed folder or date filter. 2. On web or desktop, identify the marker: supported raster files can show a thumbnail, other files use a file icon, and folders use a folder icon. An approximate marker also carries the approximate visual treatment. 3. If the marker has a number, select it to expand the cluster before choosing a member. A web or desktop cluster that cannot expand opens the first sampled file; it may not be the visible cover item. 4. Select one individual marker. Web and desktop open a file in the file viewer or route a folder to **Files** with that folder selected. 5. On mobile, select the plain pin. The app routes a file to its file screen and a folder to its folder screen. 6. Verify the name, folder, and preview after navigation. Close the viewer or return to Map if the item is not the one you intended. ## Expected result An individual file marker opens the exact file represented by its pin, while a folder marker opens the corresponding folder. Opening a marker does not move, edit, download, or share the stored item. Only items returned for the current membership can become markers. Deleted, hidden, and fully locked files are omitted, and a folder-confined member sees coordinates only within the assigned subtree. ## Troubleshooting - **The thumbnail and opened file differ.** You probably selected an unexpandable cluster rather than an individual marker. Web and desktop use one of at most six sampled items for the cluster cover and open the first sampled file. - **Selecting a folder-only cluster does nothing on web or desktop.** Zoom or change the filters until folder pins separate, then choose the individual folder icon. - **A file has no marker.** Check its EXIF GPS or upload-origin availability, wait for pending scanning, and confirm it is not hidden, deleted, or locked. - **The location looks wrong.** An approximate pin describes the upload network. Treat it as coarse context and verify file details after opening. ## Related guides - [Explore files on the map](/files/file-map) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Open photos on the Dosya map
summary: Open Dosya Map on web, desktop or mobile, distinguish exact EXIF pins from approximate upload origins, and recover when locations are missing.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/api/src/pages/api/map/pins.ts, apps/api/src/lib/location/origin.ts, apps/web/src/pages/map.tsx, and apps/mobile/app/map.tsx on 2026-10-14; no production workspace was opened during this check.
body: Dosya Map can show a photo at GPS coordinates stored in its EXIF metadata. When the workspace records upload origins, it can also show an approximate location for an uploaded file that has no EXIF GPS. ## Steps 1. Select the correct workspace, then open **Map**. The account must be a workspace member whose role has file-page access. 2. On web or desktop, wait for the counters beside the map to settle. `located` means an EXIF GPS coordinate, `approximate` means an upload-origin coordinate, and `scanning…` is the number of files still pending location extraction. 3. Leave **Show approximate locations** enabled to include upload origins, or switch it off when you only want EXIF-derived positions. 4. Look for the photo thumbnail marker. If several items are close together, select the numbered cluster or zoom in until the photo becomes an individual marker. 5. Select the photo marker. Web and desktop open the file viewer; mobile opens the file route for that item. ## Expected result The selected file opens from its stored coordinate. A thumbnail identifies supported raster images on web and desktop; mobile sends only the pin ID, coordinate, and kind to its map view. Mobile considers the pin request fresh for five minutes, so a newly scanned position may require a refresh after that interval. The map position is navigation data, not proof of where an event occurred. An EXIF coordinate can be edited before upload, and an approximate pin can reflect a proxy or network gateway. ## Troubleshooting - **A new photo is missing.** If `scanning…` is nonzero, allow the location scan to finish and reload Map. Extraction runs after upload rather than during the map click. - **Only approximate pins exist.** On web or desktop, make sure **Show approximate locations** is on. Workspace settings can disable creation and display of upload-origin pins. - **The map is empty on mobile.** The exact empty message is `No geotagged photos yet`. Confirm the active workspace contains a readable located file; hidden, deleted, and locked files do not become pins. - **Mobile cannot fetch pins.** When `Couldn't load your map.` appears, restore connectivity and press **Retry**. ## Related guides - [Explore files on the map](/files/file-map) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Choose a Dosya MCP client configuration
summary: Choose a remote OAuth-capable MCP client, add Dosya’s connector URL, approve one workspace, and verify read-only file tools without API keys.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against src/lib/mcp-integration.ts, src/lib/mcp-integration.unit.test.ts, apps/web/src/pages/profile/ai-apps.tsx, apps/mcp/src/index.ts, apps/mcp/src/server.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/index.ts, apps/api/src/mcp-gateway.ts, apps/api/src/middleware.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/oauth/token-shape.ts. body: Dosya MCP is a hosted remote OAuth connector at `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp`. It is not a local stdio server and does not accept a Dosya REST API key, client secret, or shell command in client configuration. ## Before you start - Choose a client that supports remote HTTP MCP servers and OAuth. Claude exposes **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**. ChatGPT uses custom connectors or apps after developer mode is enabled, subject to plan availability. - Authorization pins one Dosya workspace to the connection. - The connector exposes nine read-only tools. Baseline file operations use `files.read`; account information needs the separate `account.read` step-up grant. ## Steps 1. Open the client’s connector settings. If it only accepts a local command, stdio executable, or static bearer token, select a remote OAuth-capable client instead. 2. Add one custom connector whose server URL is exactly `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp`. Leave API-key, client-secret, command, and environment fields empty. 3. Start the OAuth flow, sign in to Dosya, inspect the requested scopes, and select the intended workspace. Do not authorize a convenient workspace without checking its name. 4. Return to the client and confirm the connector reports connected. If the client displays available tools, verify the expected read-only set before sharing context with a model. 5. Run a low-impact file listing or search. Confirm results belong to the pinned workspace and that no create, rename, move, upload, share, or delete tool is offered. 6. Request account information only when needed and approve the `account.read` step-up deliberately. Remove and reconnect the connector to change its pinned workspace. ## Expected result The client completes remote OAuth, lists Dosya’s read-only tools, and returns data only from the workspace approved during connection. No REST API key appears in client configuration. ## Troubleshooting **The client asks for a command or stdio package.** It does not support Dosya’s remote connector format; use a client with remote HTTP MCP and OAuth. **REST API authentication fails at the MCP URL.** Remove the API key. MCP tokens are audience-bound to `mcp.dosya.dev` and REST API middleware rejects them in the opposite direction. **The wrong workspace appears.** Disconnect and authorize again, selecting the correct workspace during OAuth. A tool argument cannot escape the pinned grant. ## Related guides - [Connect an MCP client](/developers/mcp-connect) - [Troubleshoot MCP](/troubleshooting/mcp)

title: Connect MCP with a restricted credential
summary: Connect an AI client through Dosya OAuth, pin it to one readable workspace, limit optional account data, and verify the granted read boundary.

body: Dosya MCP uses OAuth rather than a pasted API key. The resulting grant is pinned to one readable workspace, requires file-reading access, and cannot change, share, or delete stored content. ## Steps 1. In the MCP client, add the server URL `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp`. Follow the browser sign-in opened by the client; do not create or paste a `dos_…` API key because Dosya rejects API keys and mobile tokens as MCP credentials. 2. On the consent screen, confirm the requesting app and its destination. A recognized callback shows **Verified**; a local client warns that access goes to an app on your computer, while any other self-registered app shows **Not verified** and names its redirect host. 3. Under **Workspace it can read**, choose the single workspace this connection needs. End-to-end encrypted Spaces are excluded because Dosya cannot decrypt their files; there is no folder-level MCP grant in the current release. 4. Keep the required **Find and read files in _workspace_** permission. Clear optional **See your plan and storage** unless the client needs `get_account_info`; selecting it adds `account.read` to the mandatory `files.read` scope. 5. Select **Allow _app_** before the ten-minute consent transaction expires. **Deny** returns control without creating a grant, and an expired request shows `This request expired. Go back to your AI app and connect again.` 6. Return to the client and run `list_workspaces`. The structured result should name only the workspace selected during consent, proving that the connection cannot enumerate another workspace or the Vault. The OAuth access token stays in the MCP client. Dosya’s consent page never reveals a reusable secret for manual storage, and unknown scopes submitted by a client are discarded rather than granted. ## Expected result The client connects to the Dosya MCP resource with `files.read`, sees one chosen non-encrypted workspace, and has no mutation capability. `get_account_info` works only when **See your plan and storage** was granted. **No workspace is available.** The consent page says `You have no workspace this app can read. End-to-end encrypted Spaces cannot be connected.` Join or create a standard workspace before restarting from the AI client. **The callback looks unfamiliar.** Choose **Deny**. Restart only from a client and redirect destination you recognize. ## Related guides - [Connect an MCP client](/developers/mcp-connect) - [Troubleshoot MCP](/troubleshooting/mcp)

keywords: connect MCP client to cloud storage
body: Connect your AI application's remote **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** client to **https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp**. Dosya uses **Streamable HTTP with OAuth authorization**, not an API key. The current connector is read-only: it can find/read permitted files and provide download links, but cannot upload, change, share or delete files. ## Check client support and access Your client needs remote HTTPS Streamable HTTP, OAuth discovery, authorization-code/PKCE support and dynamic client registration. A client offering only local command/stdio servers or only static API-key headers cannot complete this connection. Client plans and administrators may control whether remote connectors are available; check your application's current official instructions. Dosya's consent page recognizes Claude and ChatGPT callback domains, but that does not certify every client version or make a self-named client trusted. Use a Dosya account that is a member of the workspace you intend to expose. End-to-end encrypted **Spaces** and **Vault** are not connected. A grant is pinned to one selected workspace, and file access remains subject to your membership, folder confinement, hidden/locked content and role on every tool call. An AI connection cannot reveal a file your account cannot read. ## Steps: authorize the remote server 1. In your client's remote-server/connector setup, give the connection a recognizable name and enter the complete URL `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp`. Select HTTP/Streamable HTTP where a transport choice exists. Do not configure a shell command or replace `/mcp` with `/sse`. 2. Start the client's connect/authorize action. It discovers the protected resource at the MCP host and the authorization server at `https://api.dosya.dev`. Dynamic registration, token exchange and refresh are handled by the client. Do not paste `dos_…` API keys, mobile tokens or your account password into a bearer-header field. 3. In the Dosya browser consent screen, check the account and callback destination. A recognized hosted client shows **Verified: …**; a local or unknown callback shows **Not verified · sends to …**. Local-loopback clients are not inherently verified: approve only if you just started that application yourself. The registered name alone is self-asserted. 4. Under **Workspace it can read**, choose the intended workspace. **Read files and folders** (`files.read`) is required. **See your plan and storage** (`account.read`) is optional when requested; leave it off unless the client needs account usage. The consent also lists excluded capabilities: changing/sharing/deleting and opening your other workspaces or Vault. 5. Choose **Allow** (or **Allow Claude/ChatGPT** for recognized clients), return to the initiating client and let it finish. **Deny** abandons the grant. Consent transactions expire after **10 minutes**; restart a stale authorization from the client. These are connection values, not a universal client-specific JSON schema: ```text Server URL: https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp Transport: Streamable HTTP Authorization: OAuth through the browser Required scope: files.read Optional scope: account.read Workspace: selected on the Dosya consent page ``` ## Verify the result with a read-only call Ask the client to run **list_workspaces** with an empty argument object `{}` and to show the returned workspace ID/name. Its `structuredContent.workspaces` should identify only the authorized workspace. This checks the connection without reading a file's contents. If it reports the wrong workspace, disconnect that grant and authorize again; adding another workspace ID to tool arguments cannot widen it. Next, if desired, run **list_folder** with `{"page":1,"per_page":5}`. Omitting the folder uses the accessible root; a confined membership resolves to its permitted anchor. Compare the returned entry names with Dosya Files. Listings page at **25 entries** by default and accept **1–100** per page. Stop before asking the model to read confidential content merely to prove login. ## What the client can receive | Tool | Result/capability | | --- | --- | | `list_workspaces` | Authorized workspace identifiers and names. | | `list_folder`, `search_files` | Permitted folder/file entries and pagination; search is by name/query, not an unrestricted crawl of all accounts. | | `get_file_info` | Name, byte size, type, current version, folder/workspace and web URL without reading contents. | | `read_file` | Extracted text or an image description, with source/version metadata and a continuation cursor when truncated. | | `get_download_link` | URL valid for **300 seconds** and `expires_in_seconds` for original-file download. Anyone holding it can use it until expiry. | | `get_account_info` | Account plan and storage usage, requiring the optional account.read scope. | | `search`, `fetch` | Research-compatible name search and document text, with source links. | There are **9 tools** and no write/upload/delete tools. Download-link issuance and text conversion still create access/usage activity even though they do not alter stored files. The client receives readable content you choose to expose; that content may enter the AI application's chat/history under its own settings. Disconnecting later cannot recall bytes or transcripts already received. Keep signed download URLs out of public chats/logs. ## Limits, timing and reauthorization Free permits **100 file reads** and **25 image conversions per connection per UTC day**. Paid plans have no daily MCP read/image count cap; request rate, download egress and other API plan limits still apply. Listing/file metadata does not perform the text-read operation. Each requested text window can count as a read, including a cached extraction. Daily counts reset at **00:00 UTC**; wait for the reset shown in a cap response rather than repeatedly retrying. The shipped default text window is **100,000 characters**. Conversion normally accepts source files up to **26,214,400 bytes (25 MiB)** with a **45-second** conversion deadline; deployment settings can change these bounds. Oversized or unsupported types can still use get_download_link when permitted. `read_file` returns `truncated`, `cursor`, `offset`, `total_chars`, `file_version` and source information. Continue with the returned cursor, and restart without it if the file version changes; mixing windows from different versions is refused. OAuth access tokens last **1 hour**. The client refreshes them; the connection expires after **30 days unused** and at most **180 days** overall before renewed authorization is needed. There is no persistent MCP session to manage instead of the OAuth grant. Account ban/deletion/plan changes are checked on calls, and loss of workspace membership blocks subsequent access. ## Resolve authorization and tool failures | Response/state | Correct next step | | --- | --- | | Browser consent never opens | Check remote HTTP/OAuth/DCR support and network access to both MCP and API hosts. An API key is not a fallback. | | **You have no workspace this app can read. End-to-end encrypted Spaces cannot be connected.** | Use a permitted ordinary workspace/membership, not an encrypted Space. | | **This connection is not authenticated. Sign in to dosya again to reconnect.** | Restart client authorization after checking expiry/revocation. | | **dosya could not be reached just now. This is temporary: try again in a moment. Do not reconnect.** | Wait and retry; an infrastructure outage is different from revoked authorization. | | Missing account.read permission | Permit the optional scope through the client's renewed authorization if you want get_account_info; other file tools use files.read. | | **Not visible to this connection.** | Check workspace, member confinement, role and file state in Dosya. Do not try another account's ID. | | **dosya is rate limiting this connection right now. Wait a minute, then try again.** | Reduce parallel calls and wait at least the indicated minute. | | Conversion/type/size refusal | Use the original download link when needed, or supply a supported smaller document. | | Invalid/stale continuation cursor | Restart read_file without the old cursor and use the current file version. | ## Disconnect and change workspaces Open Dosya **Settings → Connected AI apps**, identify the exact client/workspace row and click **Disconnect**. Remove the connector from the AI client too if you no longer want it offered. Revocation stops new authorization checks, but an already validated token may continue working for up to **60 seconds** because successful token validation is cached. Previously downloaded bytes, exposed text and already issued download URLs are not erased by disconnecting. To change the selected workspace, revoke the old grant and connect again with the new selection. File storage is unchanged by granting, denying or disconnecting the AI application. ## Expected result The client discovers Dosya's read-only tools, list_workspaces identifies the intended grant and a permitted listing matches the web app. You can inspect and revoke that specific connection in Connected AI apps without managing an API key. ## Related guides - [Review AI app permissions](/integrations/ai-app-permissions) - [Test an MCP read-only operation](/developers/mcp-test-read-only-operation)

title: Disconnect MCP and rotate its credential
summary: Revoke an MCP OAuth grant from Connected AI apps, allow its brief validation-cache window to close, then reconnect with a fresh grant safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/ai-apps.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/ai-connections/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/oauth/token-cache.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/result.ts, apps/api/src/lib/oauth/connections.ts. Production behavior for “Disconnect MCP and rotate its credential” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: An MCP connection is an OAuth grant, not an API key. Removing a local client entry does not revoke Dosya access; use **Connected AI apps** to invalidate the server-side grant, then reconnect if the integration must continue. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings → Connected AI apps** in an interactive browser session. API keys and connected AI apps cannot list or manage these grants on your behalf. 2. Match the row by client name, workspace name, connection age, and scope chips such as **Read files** or **Plan and storage**. Each row represents one grant pinned to one workspace. 3. Stop current work in that AI client, then select **Disconnect** on the exact row. Dosya revokes the grant and reports **App disconnected** with `_client_ can no longer read _workspace_.` 4. Allow up to 60 seconds before testing the retired token. A worker that validated it recently may serve that cached validation until the one-minute entry expires; after that, a tool call returns `This connection is not authenticated. Sign in to dosya again to reconnect.` 5. If continued access is required, start a new connection from the MCP client using `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp`. Choose the intended workspace and optional account scope again; there is no in-place rotate operation. 6. Run `list_workspaces` through the new connection, then retry the old one after the cache window. The new grant should list its selected workspace while the revoked grant remains unauthenticated. Disconnect is reversible only by creating fresh consent. It does not delete files or change unrelated API keys, but the old OAuth grant itself cannot be restored. ## Expected result The selected grant disappears from **Connected AI apps** and stops authorizing MCP calls no later than the validation-cache window. A replacement connection has a distinct grant with newly chosen workspace and scopes. **Disconnect failed** means Dosya could not revoke the grant at that moment. Leave the client stopped, reload **Connected AI apps**, and retry only while the row is still present. **The old client works briefly.** Wait the full 60 seconds before treating that as a failed revocation; the implementation deliberately caches successful token validation for one minute. ## Related guides - [Connect an MCP client](/developers/mcp-connect) - [Troubleshoot MCP](/troubleshooting/mcp)

title: List Dosya MCP tools and resources
summary: Inspect Dosya’s nine read-only MCP tools, their schemas and scope needs, and understand why the server currently publishes no MCP resources.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mcp/src/server.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/index.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/simple-tools.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/list-folder.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/search-files.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/read-file.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/research.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/paging.ts, apps/mcp/src/index.ts, apps/api/src/mcp-gateway.ts. body: Dosya currently publishes MCP tools, not MCP resource objects. The protected resource URL `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp` identifies the OAuth audience; it does not imply that `resources/list` contains files. ## Steps 1. Open the connected Dosya server in the MCP client and refresh its capabilities. Confirm the server identifies itself as **dosya** and the connection is authenticated with required `files.read` access. 2. Check for the core navigation tools: `list_workspaces`, `list_folder`, `search_files`, and `get_file_info`. `list_folder` accepts an omitted `folder_id` for the top level and an optional `workspace_id` returned by `list_workspaces`. 3. Check the content tools: `read_file` and `get_download_link`. `read_file` returns bounded text with a continuation cursor; `get_download_link` creates a new five-minute bearer URL and is therefore read-only but not idempotent. 4. Check `get_account_info`. It is the only current tool requiring optional `account.read`; a client may open an OAuth scope prompt if that permission was not granted initially. 5. Check the research adapters `search` and `fetch`. They expose name search and document text in the shapes required by research clients; they do not add write capability beyond `search_files` and `read_file`. 6. Inspect the annotations and resource view. All nine tools declare `readOnlyHint: true` and `destructiveHint: false`; a blank or unsupported MCP resources view is expected because the server registers no resources. Listing defaults are bounded. `list_folder` returns 25 combined entries by default and accepts at most 100. `search_files` pages folders and files independently, so its default is up to 25 folders plus 25 files and its maximum is 100 folders plus 100 files. ## Expected result The client displays nine Dosya tools with input schemas and read-only annotations. No mutation tool appears, and the absence of MCP resource objects is recognized as the current server design rather than a connection failure. **A tool is missing.** Refresh the server definition or reconnect the client. If only `get_account_info` fails, grant **See your plan and storage** instead of replacing the whole connection blindly. **Files do not appear under Resources.** Use `list_folder` or `search_files`; Dosya files are returned through tools in this release. ## Related guides - [Connect an MCP client](/developers/mcp-connect) - [Troubleshoot MCP](/troubleshooting/mcp)

title: Test a read-only Dosya MCP operation
summary: Run list_workspaces and list_folder against the pinned workspace, inspect structured paging fields, and confirm that no stored content changes.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mcp/src/tools/list-folder.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/simple-tools.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/paging.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/result.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools/index.unit.test.ts, apps/mcp/src/index.ts, apps/api/src/mcp-gateway.ts, apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts. Production behavior for “Test a read-only Dosya MCP operation” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Use a listing call for the first MCP test. It proves authentication, workspace confinement, structured output, and read-only behavior without downloading file bytes or spending the daily content-read allowance. ## Steps 1. In the connected MCP client, call `list_workspaces` with no arguments. Record the returned `workspace_id`; a valid grant lists only the workspace chosen on the OAuth consent screen. 2. Call `list_folder` with that `workspace_id` and omit `folder_id` to request the workspace top level. Also omit paging values for the default page 1 and 25-entry window. 3. Inspect `structuredContent.entries`. Folder rows and file rows include `kind`, `id`, `name`, `folder_id`, and an app URL; files also report byte size, MIME type, and modification time when available. 4. Read `page` and `next_page`. If `next_page` is a number, call the same tool with that page; stop when it is `null`. A client may request 1 through 100 entries per page. 5. Open Dosya separately and compare the returned names with the selected workspace root. Hidden and deleted content is excluded, and the connection must not reveal another workspace or an end-to-end encrypted Space. 6. Refresh the web listing and confirm no file, folder, share, or version changed. The MCP server exposes no mutation tool, and every registered operation declares itself read-only and non-destructive. `list_folder` uses API request capacity but does not count as a content read. If you later test `read_file`, the current defaults are a 100,000-character window, a 25 MiB conversion ceiling, and a 45-second conversion deadline. The Free plan defaults to 100 file reads and 25 image conversions per UTC day; paid plan defaults are unlimited. ## Expected result `list_workspaces` returns the pinned workspace and `list_folder` returns a structured, paginated snapshot of its visible root. Rechecking Dosya shows that the operation created, changed, shared, and deleted nothing. **The result says `Not visible to this connection.`** Confirm the identifier belongs to the workspace selected during OAuth consent and that the signed-in member still has access. **The service says it is unavailable.** Retry shortly without reconnecting; temporary gateway failures deliberately produce `dosya could not be reached just now` rather than invalidating the credential. ## Related guides - [Connect an MCP client](/developers/mcp-connect) - [Troubleshoot MCP](/troubleshooting/mcp)

title: Troubleshoot a Dosya MCP connection
summary: Separate MCP transport, OAuth, scope, workspace visibility, rate-limit, and file-conversion failures, then verify with a read-only tool call.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/mcp/src/index.ts; apps/mcp/src/server.ts; apps/mcp/src/tools/result.ts; apps/mcp/src/tools/read-file.ts; apps/mcp/src/tools/list-folder.ts; apps/api/src/mcp-gateway.ts; apps/api/src/mcp-principal.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/consent.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/token-cache.ts; apps/api/src/lib/oauth/connections.ts; apps/web/src/pages/connect/ai.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/profile/ai-apps.tsx. No external MCP client was connected. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Start with the exact error and the first failing boundary. A client that cannot discover the server has a transport problem; a client that lists tools but cannot call one has an authorization, scope, workspace, visibility, usage, or conversion problem. Reconnecting for every error can discard useful state and will not fix a temporary service failure. ## Steps The server URL is `https://mcp.dosya.dev/mcp`, using remote HTTPS **Streamable HTTP** and browser-based OAuth. Do not configure `/sse`, a local stdio command, a `dos_…` API key, a mobile token or your Dosya password. Your client must support OAuth discovery, authorization code with PKCE, dynamic client registration and the remote transport. If its setup accepts only a command to run locally or a static bearer header, that client mode cannot complete Dosya authorization. Confirm that the client plan or organization administrator permits remote connectors. When consent opens, inspect the account, callback destination and **Workspace it can read**. **Read files and folders** (`files.read`) is required. **See your plan and storage** (`account.read`) is optional and needed only by `get_account_info`. The consent transaction expires after 10 minutes; restart it from the client if the browser page has been left open longer. ## Use the returned message to choose the repair | Message or symptom | Meaning and next action | | --- | --- | | The browser consent page never opens | Recheck the exact server URL, remote HTTP/OAuth support, and network access to both `mcp.dosya.dev` and `api.dosya.dev`. An API key is not a fallback transport. | | **You have no workspace this app can read. End-to-end encrypted Spaces cannot be connected.** | Join or select an ordinary readable workspace. Vault and encrypted Spaces are deliberately outside this connector. | | **This connection is not authenticated. Sign in to dosya again to reconnect.** | The access token or grant is invalid, expired, or revoked. Start a fresh authorization in the client. | | **dosya could not be reached just now. This is temporary: try again in a moment. Do not reconnect.** | Keep the grant and retry after the service recovers. Reauthorization does not repair the dependency failure. | | The client lists tools but `get_account_info` is refused | Renew authorization with `account.read` only if plan/storage information is needed. File tools continue to use `files.read`. | | **Not visible to this connection.** | Confirm the selected workspace, current membership, folder confinement, role, hidden/locked state, and current file ID in Dosya. Another workspace ID in a tool argument cannot widen the grant. | | **dosya is rate limiting this connection right now. Wait a minute, then try again.** | Stop parallel calls and wait at least the stated minute before retrying. Reconnecting creates no extra allowance. | | Today's read/image allowance is used | Free connections allow 100 file reads and 25 image conversions per UTC day. Wait for 00:00 UTC or use an applicable paid plan; metadata/listing calls are separate. | | A continuation cursor is invalid or stale | Restart `read_file` without the cursor and use the current file version. Windows from different file versions cannot be combined. | ## Expected result Ask the client to run `list_workspaces` with `{}`. A healthy response identifies exactly the workspace fixed during consent. If it shows the wrong workspace, open Dosya **Settings → Connected AI apps**, disconnect that exact client/workspace row, and authorize again with the intended selection. Next run `list_folder` with `{"page":1,"per_page":5}` and no folder ID. The default page size is 25 and the allowed range is 1–100. A confined membership begins at its permitted anchor. Compare the returned names with the Dosya Files view for the same account instead of asking the model to read a confidential file. Dosya currently exposes nine read-only tools. It has no MCP upload, edit, share or delete tool. If a client shows no tools after successful OAuth, remove and re-add its connector definition or refresh tool discovery; granting broader file permissions cannot make nonexistent write tools appear. ## Diagnose file reading and download-link failures `read_file` can return text windows up to 100,000 characters by default. Conversion normally accepts supported source files up to 26,214,400 bytes (25 MiB) and has a 45-second conversion deadline; deployment settings may narrow those values. For an unsupported or oversized type, use metadata or `get_download_link` when access is permitted. A generated original-file URL lasts 300 seconds. Anyone holding it can download until expiry, so do not paste it into public logs or support messages. Issuing a link or converting content can create access/usage activity even though the connector cannot alter stored files. OAuth access tokens last one hour and should be refreshed by the client. A connection must be authorized again after 30 days without use or 180 days overall. Membership loss, account state and plan changes are rechecked on calls. Disconnecting can take up to 60 seconds to reach a token already accepted by the validation cache, and it cannot recall content, transcripts or download URLs already received by the external application. ## Escalate with safe evidence If `list_workspaces` still fails, record the client name/version, server URL, approximate time and timezone, stage reached, exact nonsecret message, and whether consent appears under **Connected AI apps**. Keep bearer tokens, authorization codes, signed download URLs and file contents out of the ticket. ## Related guides - [Connect MCP](/developers/mcp-connect) - [Disconnect an AI app](/integrations/disconnect-ai-app) - [Contact support](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Check image dimensions in Dosya
summary: Read image dimensions from the mobile viewer, distinguish decoded size from server metadata, and avoid treating a HEIC derivative as original pixels.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/ImageStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts, and apps/mobile/src/viewer/imageSource.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The Dosya mobile viewer learns image dimensions from the native decoder after the image loads. The files API does not store or return a width and height for this display. **Choose a reliable test file** Use a JPEG or PNG when you must verify original pixel dimensions. The mobile viewer may display a generated thumbnail for HEIC content, so a reported HEIC width and height can describe the decoded derivative rather than the untouched original. Compare against the source file before using the value for print, design, or forensic work. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the Dosya mobile app and select the intended image. Confirm its filename and folder first so that a similarly named derivative is not mistaken for the original. 2. Wait until the image finishes loading. The viewer uses a contain layout, so the entire photo remains visible rather than being cropped to fill the screen. 3. Read the metadata line beneath the filename. When the decoder reports a natural size, Dosya adds a value such as **4032 x 3024** alongside size, kind, and created date. 4. Rotate the device or zoom the preview if useful, but do not interpret the onscreen rendered size as a new pixel count. Those view operations do not modify the file. 5. For a critical measurement, download the original through an allowed client and compare its dimensions with the viewer result. **If no dimensions appear** The dimension label is dynamic and is omitted until the native image loader supplies both non-zero values. A network, decode, access, or unsupported-format failure can therefore leave only the server-backed metadata. Retry after reconnecting, confirm the file is not hidden or locked for the member, and test a known JPEG or PNG.
