The pictured browser viewer shows the common file preview and **Details** layout, but that side panel contains identity and storage information rather than decoded image dimensions. Use the mobile viewer’s metadata line for this task. ## Expected result After a supported image decodes, the mobile viewer shows its width and height in pixels. Viewing, rotating, or zooming the image leaves the stored bytes and version unchanged. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [View file details](/files/file-details)

title: Compare preview metadata with File details
summary: Compare the preview with File details using filename, size, kind, and version while treating decoded dimensions or duration as viewer-only data.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/ImageStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/VideoStage.tsx, and apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Preview metadata and **File details** answer different questions. Compare their shared identity fields first, then treat dimensions and duration as values decoded by the active viewer. **What each surface knows** The file record supplies the filename, byte size, kind, timestamps, and version information. A mobile image stage can add natural dimensions after decoding. A mobile video stage can add duration after playback status loads. Those media-specific values are not general fields returned by the files API, and the browser Details panel does not promise them. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, select the exact item and record its name, folder, and current version before opening it. 2. Open the preview. Compare its filename, readable type, size, and created date with the list entry. Wait for the media stage to load before judging a missing dimension or duration. 3. Open **File details** in the available client. Compare file identity, storage size, timestamps, and version information with the previewed item. 4. Treat an image dimension or video duration as a decoder result. It may be absent when the format, network, or platform decoder cannot provide it; that absence does not by itself prove the file record is corrupt. 5. If shared fields disagree, refresh the file list and reopen the current version. A stale view after rename, replacement, or version change can display older metadata. **Resolve common mismatches** Size is the stored byte count, not the dimensions of an image or the playback length of a video. Created and modified dates also answer different questions. For HEIC images, the mobile viewer may decode a generated derivative, so its displayed dimensions should not be used as proof of the original pixel grid. Previewing does not rewrite the file. If the wrong version is open, return to the file record and deliberately choose the intended version rather than uploading a duplicate merely to force a refresh. ## Expected result The preview and details identify the same file and current version through their shared fields, while dimensions or duration appear only when the relevant viewer decodes them. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [View file details](/files/file-details)

title: Inspect audio title and artist metadata
summary: Inspect mobile audio title, artist, album, duration, bitrate, and sample rate while understanding parser formats, the 50 MiB ceiling, and fallbacks.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/extract.ts, apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/id3.ts, apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/mp4.ts, and apps/mobile/src/player/InfoSheet.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya extracts audio tags on the device from locally cached bytes. Start playback before inspecting the result because opening general file details alone does not run the audio parser. **Supported metadata path** The mobile parser recognizes ID3-tagged MP3 and MP4-family files such as M4A, M4B, MP4, AAC, and ALAC, with byte sniffing as a fallback for an incorrect extension. It reads the full file only when the stored size is at most 50 MiB. Larger tracks are marked parsed without embedded tags to avoid loading a large base64 copy into memory. ## Steps 1. Play the intended unlocked audio file in the Dosya mobile player and wait for playback to start. Metadata extraction uses the local cached copy and does not send tag contents to a separate server parser. 2. Open the button labelled **Track info**. The sheet always shows **Size**, **Type**, and **Modified**. 3. When present, compare **Artist**, **Album**, and **Duration** with the source. MP3 parsing can also add **Bitrate** in kbps and **Sample rate** in kHz. 4. Compare the player heading. If no embedded title exists, Dosya uses the filename without its extension; if no embedded artist exists, the queue uses the source folder name. 5. After replacing a track, play the current version again. Cached metadata is accepted only when its file ID, byte size, modified timestamp, and parser version still match. **Missing or partial tags** An unsupported container, malformed tags, or a file larger than 50 MiB can leave the sheet with only file properties. Playback may still supply a duration for a format the tag parser does not understand. ID3 MP3 provides the richer technical values; MP4-family parsing does not promise bitrate or sample rate. The browser screenshot illustrates the common preview and Details shell rather than the mobile **Track info** sheet. Do not expect embedded audio fields in that browser panel. ## Expected result The mobile Track info sheet shows each supported tag found in the cached audio bytes and uses filename or folder fallbacks without changing the stored track. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [View file details](/files/file-details)

title: Use image, audio and video preview controls
summary: Preview images, audio, and video in Dosya, use each format's real controls, understand browser limits, and recover without changing originals.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-preview-image.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/helpers.ts and apps/mobile/src/viewer/useFilePreview.ts. Production preview delivery was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: Dosya previews stored media without replacing its bytes. Opening a preview can read the original or a generated thumbnail, but playback, zooming, seeking, and switching viewer panels do not create a new file version. ## Before you start - Open **Files** in the workspace that contains the media. Folder scope, hidden-item rules, and a **full lock** password gate still control whether the bytes are available. - Confirm the filename, extension, displayed size, and version. The viewer can open an older version from **Versions**, so do not assume the stage always shows the latest bytes. - Browser playback depends on both container and codec. Dosya recognizes images including PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, SVG, ICO, HEIC, and HEIF; video and audio recognition does not guarantee that every browser can decode the file. ## Steps 1. Select a media file in **Files** to open the full-screen viewer. Use **Previous file** and **Next file**, or the left and right arrow keys, to move through the loaded file set. 2. For an image, use **Zoom out**, **Zoom in**, and **Fit to screen**. Desktop web zoom moves in 25-point steps from 25% through 300%; **Fit to screen** returns to 100%. These header controls are hidden on narrow screens. 3. For video, use the browser's native play, pause, timeline, volume, and full-screen controls. Playback starts automatically when browser policy allows it. 4. For audio, use **Play** or **Pause**, the seek control, 15-second back/forward controls, volume, and playback speed. Waveform analysis is skipped above 80 MiB, but a plain seek slider remains available. 5. Open **Details** to verify type, region, uploader, and size. Use the header **Download** control when local playback or exact metadata matters. ## Decode failures and privacy If video decoding fails, Dosya says **This browser can't decode this video. Download it and open it in a player like VLC, which decodes everything.** Audio uses **This browser can't decode this audio format. Download the file to play it in another app.** A failed HEIC thumbnail falls back to the file icon rather than changing the original. Preview requests use the signed-in session. Downloading creates a local copy outside Dosya's storage controls; later cloud deletion, revocation, or replacement does not recall that copy. Selecting **Edit** is a separate mutation and can upload a new version, so leave it closed when the goal is inspection only. ## Expected result The selected file remains unchanged while the supported viewer responds to zoom, seek, or playback controls. Unsupported decoding produces an explicit download path instead of an indefinite blank stage. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Download files](/uploading/download-files)

title: Troubleshoot missing album artwork
summary: Restore missing mobile album artwork by checking playback-triggered parsing, supported tag containers, the 50 MiB file limit, and the 2 MiB image cap.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/extract.ts, apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/id3.ts, apps/mobile/src/player/metadata/mp4.ts, and apps/mobile/src/player/InfoSheet.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Album artwork appears only when the mobile player extracts a supported embedded image and writes it to its local metadata cache. There is no server-side artwork refresh command. **Artwork requirements** Start playback so the app caches the audio and triggers parsing. Supported sources are ID3 artwork in MP3 and cover art in MP4-family containers. The full audio file must be 50 MiB or smaller for tag parsing, and embedded artwork larger than 2 MiB is ignored for both parser families. ## Steps 1. Play the intended track in the Dosya mobile app. Confirm that its filename, size, and modified time describe the version you expect. 2. Open **Track info**. If title, artist, or album appear but the artwork does not, the image may be absent, oversized, malformed, or unable to be written to the local cache. 3. Inspect the source audio in a trusted tag editor. Embed one JPEG or PNG cover within the supported container and keep that image at or below 2 MiB. 4. Upload the corrected audio as the intended new or replacement version. Playing the old version again cannot repair bytes that never contained usable artwork. 5. Play the current version and reopen **Track info**. The cache key includes file ID, byte size, modified timestamp, and parser version, so a changed file is parsed again. **When the music-note fallback remains** Files above 50 MiB deliberately skip the full tag read. Unsupported containers can still play but yield no embedded art. A local artwork-write failure preserves any text tags, which explains why title and artist can appear beside the fallback icon. Removing and reinstalling the app may clear local cache data, but it cannot create missing source artwork. The browser preview screenshot does not show an album-art processor. Use it only to identify the current file and version before returning to the mobile player. ## Expected result A supported track no larger than 50 MiB shows embedded JPEG or PNG artwork no larger than 2 MiB after playback triggers a successful local parse. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [View file details](/files/file-details)

title: Verify video duration and file details
summary: Verify video duration after the mobile player loads, compare it with the timeline, and distinguish decoder metadata from stored file details.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/VideoStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/VlcVideoStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts, and apps/mobile/src/files/download.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Video duration in the Dosya mobile viewer comes from the active player after media status loads. It is not a duration field stored in the general file record. **Before comparing values** Confirm the exact filename, size, and current version. Created or modified timestamps are dates, not playback lengths. The mobile viewer obtains a signed media URL and lets the native player, or its VLC fallback, report duration when the selected platform can decode the content. ## Steps 1. Open the video from **Files** in the Dosya mobile app. Wait for the first frame and playback controls rather than reading the initial loading state. 2. Read the duration added to the viewer metadata line when it becomes a positive value. Compare it with the end of the seek timeline. 3. Seek to a point near the end and play a short segment. This confirms that the reported duration and the playable timeline describe the same current version. 4. Return to file details and compare filename, stored byte size, type, and version. Do not expect the general details surface to reproduce a decoder-derived duration. 5. If the platform cannot decode the file, use the permitted save action and inspect the local copy with a compatible player. Saving creates a separate device copy and leaves the cloud file unchanged. **If duration never appears** A slow connection, expired media grant, unsupported codec, or decoder failure can prevent loaded status. The mobile viewer waits 15 seconds for a first frame before showing **Still loading**. Retry on a stable connection and verify access to the unlocked current version. A recognized filename extension does not guarantee that the device supports its codec. The browser preview shown here exposes common file metadata, while duration for this task must come from the mobile playback stage. ## Expected result The player reports a finite duration that agrees with its seek timeline for the current video, and the verification does not alter the cloud file or create a version. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [View file details](/files/file-details)

title: Filter workspace activity on mobile
summary: Filter mobile workspace activity by category, member, and action, understand its 50-member cap, and recover safely when filters return no events.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/activity.tsx, apps/mobile/src/activity/ActivityFilterSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/activity/api.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, and activity permission tests. Production activity data was not queried and no production action was performed.
body: The mobile **Activity** screen filters the active workspace’s audit trail. Filtering is read-only: it changes which rows are requested and never edits files, members, or recorded events. A member needs the workspace permission `view_activity`. Folder-confined memberships are refused because the feed covers the whole workspace. The **Member** list also requires `view_team_members`; without it, activity may load while that filter section says **No members to filter by.** ## Steps 1. In the mobile app, use the workspace name at the top to select the workspace you want to inspect. A switch displays **Switching workspace…** for two seconds while new workspace queries refresh. 2. Open **Settings**, then choose **Activity** under **Workspace**. 3. Select **Filter**. The sheet is titled **Filter activity** and contains **Category**, **Member**, and **Action** sections. 4. Pick one or more values. Actions offered in the last section follow the selected categories; removing a category also drops any action that is no longer visible. 5. Choose **Show activity**. Draft changes are not sent until this button is used. Tapping the backdrop closes the sheet and discards that draft. 6. Read the count above the list. A filtered result is labelled, for example, **12 activities (filtered)**. The filter button also shows the number of active selections. The client sends category and action lists to the API and caps the member selection at **50 user IDs**. Results restart at page 1 whenever a filter changes; the API returns **30 rows per page** by default. ## Expected result Only events matching every applied filter appear. If none match, the screen says **Nothing matches these filters.** Use **Clear filters** there, or reopen the sheet and choose **Clear all**, to restore the unfiltered feed. ## Troubleshooting **The Activity page returns a permission error.** The server message is **You don't have permission to view the activity log**. Ask a workspace owner to grant `view_activity`; changing a local filter cannot bypass it. **The Member section is empty.** Activity and roster access are separate. A role with `view_activity` but without `view_team_members` receives no member choices, although category and action filters still work. **Older rows fail to load.** Existing rows stay on screen with **Could not load more. Try again.** Choose **Retry** after connectivity returns. **Load older** appears while another page exists. ## Related guides - [Review phone permissions for activity access](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Diagnose alerts after filtering activity](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Open workspace activity on mobile
summary: Open a permitted mobile workspace audit trail, inspect exact event details, page through its 30-row results, and understand privacy filtering.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 with apps/mobile/app/activity.tsx, apps/mobile/src/activity/ActivityEntry.tsx, apps/mobile/src/activity/api.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts. No production workspace or audit record was accessed.
body: Use **Activity** to answer who performed a workspace action, what resource was involved, and when it happened. The feed is workspace-wide and requires `view_activity`; it is not a personal device log. ## Steps 1. Check the workspace name in the mobile header. If it is wrong, open the workspace picker and choose the intended entry before continuing. 2. Open **Settings → Activity**. The header initially reads **Loading…**, then shows the total as **1 activity** or **N activities**. 3. Read a row for its actor, action phrase, resource, relative time, and any badges such as a non-success outcome, mobile/CLI source, rename pair, email, file count, or “on behalf of” identity. 4. Tap the row to expand it in place. Available detail labels are **When**, **Where**, **Device**, **Source**, **Outcome**, **Resource**, **Account**, and **Session**. **When** includes both an absolute local timestamp and a relative time. 5. Choose **Load older** to fetch the next page. Mobile requests **30 audit rows per page**; the server accepts 10–100 but this screen uses the default. Owners and administrators can receive forensic details for other members. Other roles with activity access see their own full fields, but another member’s source IP, device/user agent, location, session, request ID, and unapproved metadata are removed by the API. Names of files or folders that the viewer cannot open are also stripped. These privacy gates run on the server, not just in the phone interface. ## Expected result The newest permitted event appears first, and expanding a row reveals only the details this account may receive. An unused workspace shows **Nothing has happened here yet.** ## Troubleshooting **You see “Not a member.”** The workspace may have been removed, your membership may have ended, or your account may be confined to one folder. Select another valid workspace or ask its owner to review membership. **A resource name or forensic field is absent.** That can be intentional. Hidden, locked, or unreachable resources lose their names, and non-owner/non-admin viewers do not receive another member’s sensitive request context. **Paging stopped with an error.** The list keeps the pages already loaded. Restore the connection and press **Retry** below **Could not load more. Try again.** ## Related guides - [Check mobile access before reading audits](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Investigate activity-related notification gaps](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Browse an archive on mobile
summary: Browse ZIP, ISO, and IMG folders on Dosya mobile, preview images, transfer other entries, and save eligible files into cloud storage safely.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/app/file/[id]/archive.tsx, apps/mobile/src/archive/ArchiveList.tsx, apps/mobile/app/pick-archive-destination.tsx, apps/mobile/src/archive/archiveSave.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/entry.ts. Production behavior was not re-tested.
body: Dosya mobile browses `.zip`, `.iso`, and ISO 9660 `.img` containers one folder level at a time. Opening the archive directory does not extract every member or download the full source file. ## Navigation and availability The header shows the current directory and **in archive-name**. A chip row begins with **Root**, followed by each directory in the current path, and reports the number of rows at that level. Tapping a folder drills down. The header Back button and Android hardware Back first move up one level; only Back at root leaves the archive. Swipe-back is disabled while you are inside a nested folder so it cannot discard the entire browsing context. STORE and DEFLATE members can open. Encrypted rows say **Password-protected** and unsupported methods say **Unsupported compression**; both are disabled. Folder rows display their item count, while an eligible file displays its uncompressed size. ## Steps 1. In the iOS or Android app, open a ZIP, ISO, or IMG file from the intended workspace. 2. Wait for the root list. The top strip identifies it as **Archive** or **Disk image**. 3. Tap a folder to enter it. Use a path chip to jump directly to any earlier level without repeatedly pressing Back. 4. Tap an image member to open the in-app dark preview. Its footer shows the member name and size; use **Close preview** to return. 5. Tap another eligible file type to download it to the app cache and open the operating system share sheet. The access token travels in the request header rather than in the URL. 6. To keep a member in cloud storage, use its **Save name to dosya** action, choose a folder in **Save to…**, and press **Save here**. ## Preview, transfer, and save rules Images use the preview permission path and can remain visible under view-only access. Every non-image tap invokes an export-capable request with `dl=1` because the operating-system sheet can offer Save to Files or AirDrop. If download access is blocked, the app says **You don't have permission to save or share this entry.** Other cache or network failures produce **This entry could not be transferred.** Saving into Dosya also requires upload permission and an allowed destination. Folder-confined members remain inside their assigned folder tree. For one item, success reports **Saved name to dosya**. A server refusal for a lock, quota, permission, or file limit is displayed in the picker. **Save all to dosya** is available at archive root and also requires **create folders** permission because it wraps the extracted hierarchy in a folder named after the archive. A folder plan can contain at most 500 eligible files. Above that, the app says **This folder has N files. Save smaller folders (up to 500), or transfer the archive.** Progress reads **Saving N of M** and offers **Cancel**. Cancellation and later failures do not remove directories or members already saved. If no safe rows exist, root says **There is nothing inside this archive.** Nested emptiness says **There is nothing in this folder.** A truncated index reports **Showing the first X of Y entries. Transfer the whole archive to get the rest.** A 413 list refusal becomes **This archive is too large to list. Download it to open its contents.** ## Expected result The path chips and header identify the current level. An image opens inside Dosya, another eligible format reaches the system share sheet when export is allowed, or a saved member appears as a separate file in the selected workspace folder. Merely browsing leaves the container unchanged. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Save one archive entry on mobile
summary: Save one supported archive entry into Dosya mobile, choose an allowed destination, understand the 4 GiB ceiling, collisions, permissions, and quota.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/file/[id]/archive.tsx, apps/mobile/app/pick-archive-destination.tsx, apps/mobile/src/archive/archiveSave.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/archive/save.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya mobile can save one entry from a stored ZIP, ISO, or IMG as a new cloud file. The archive remains unchanged, and the extracted file consumes storage in the destination workspace. **Eligibility and access** The entry must use STORE or DEFLATE compression and must not be encrypted. Its uncompressed size cannot exceed 4 GiB. You need upload permission for the destination, and the archive’s source bytes must be available through the preview gate; a blocked or view-only source can prevent extraction even though the endpoint does not separately require download permission. ## Steps 1. Open the archive in Dosya mobile and browse to the file entry. Password-protected rows say **This entry is password-protected and cannot be opened.** Unsupported compression says **This entry uses a compression method this app cannot open.** 2. Open the row action labelled **Save _filename_ to dosya**. The destination screen is titled **Save to…** and identifies **Saving _filename_ from archive**. 3. Choose a folder you may upload to. A fully locked destination, assigned-root boundary, missing upload capability, file-size policy, or insufficient storage can refuse the save. 4. Select **Save here** and wait for the success message **Saved _name_ to dosya**. A name collision receives a safe numeric suffix instead of overwriting the existing file. 5. Open the new file from the destination and verify its name and byte size against the archive entry. **Failures and recovery** The API can return **This entry is larger than 4 GiB. Download the archive to extract it.**, **No such entry in this archive.**, **This entry's data does not match its declared size; the archive is malformed.**, or **Could not write the extracted file to storage**. Correct the reported destination, access, quota, or archive problem and retry. Saving a folder is a different multi-entry operation, capped at 500 eligible files; cancellation or a later failure can leave earlier files saved. A single-entry failure should not create a usable destination record. Deleting the extracted file later does not remove its source entry from the archive. ## Expected result One eligible entry is streamed into the selected folder as a separate Dosya file, receives a collision-safe name when necessary, and leaves the source archive untouched. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Play audio in the mobile viewer
summary: Play unlocked audio in Dosya mobile, understand the 500-track queue, previous and next behavior, background controls, signed-link retry, and skips.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/player.tsx, apps/mobile/src/player/controller.ts, apps/mobile/src/player/queue.ts, and apps/mobile/src/player/service.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya mobile builds an audio queue from the current folder, filter, and sort order. It streams the current track through a resolved URL and prepares the next track just in time. **Queue rules** The member needs file access, and only audio rows whose lock mode is **none** enter the queue; view-only and password-locked tracks are omitted. Dosya fetches further list pages until it has at most 500 playable tracks. When more exist it reports **Queue capped at 500 tracks.** An empty source reports **No audio files here.** ## Steps 1. In the mobile **Files** view, enter the intended folder, apply any filter or sort order, and open an unlocked audio file. 2. Use the controls labelled **Play**, **Pause**, **Previous**, **Next**, **Shuffle**, and **Repeat**. The seek position updates while the player screen is mounted. 3. Press **Previous** after more than three seconds to restart the current track. At three seconds or earlier it opens the preceding track; on the first track it seeks to the beginning. 4. A deliberate **Next** press wraps from the last track to the first. Automatic playback with repeat off still stops at the end; repeat cycles through off, queue, and track modes. 5. Lock the phone or background the app and test the system play, pause, previous, next, and seek controls. Android removes the playback notification if the app is killed. **Playback recovery** On a playback error, Dosya re-resolves the signed URL once for that track, reloads it, restores the saved position, and resumes. If the retry fails, the toast says **Couldn't play "_title_" - skipping.** The error path advances without wrapping at the end, preventing an unplayable last track from looping forever. Opening a locked or non-audio file as a single playback request returns **This file can't be played.** Playback and local metadata caching do not create a cloud copy or a new file version. ## Expected result The unlocked track plays in its folder-derived queue, transport controls follow the documented boundaries, and one failed URL refresh either recovers the position or skips safely. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Fix paused mobile background backup
summary: Restore Dosya photo backup after permission, network, power, workspace, storage, manual-stop, or operating-system scheduling interruptions.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/backup/background.ts; apps/mobile/src/backup/policy.ts; apps/mobile/src/backup/settings.ts; apps/mobile/src/backup/runState.ts; apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/engineStatus.ts; apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/CoverageRing.tsx; apps/mobile/src/backup/orchestrator.ts; apps/mobile/src/backup/ledger.ts; apps/mobile/src/onboarding/permissions.ts; apps/mobile/src/upload/uploadBlock.ts. No physical-device background run was performed. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: First prove that one photo can upload while Dosya is open. A foreground failure points to permission, account, workspace, storage, or file policy; a foreground success followed by no closed-app progress points to operating-system scheduling or background restrictions. ## Steps Open **Backup** and confirm the workspace displayed at the top. The centre label identifies the next check: - **Paused — waiting for Wi-Fi**: connect to Wi-Fi or turn off the Wi-Fi-only setting. - **Paused — waiting for charger**: attach power or disable charging-only backup. - **Paused — offline**: restore network access before retrying. - **Cooling down…**: stop heavy device activity and let the phone cool; the run can continue automatically. - **Paused** with **Tap to retry**: a fatal upload condition was saved. Correct the visible reason, then tap once to clear the block and retry. - **Ready**: automatic backup is off. Enable it or start the backup manually. - **Protected**: the engine is enabled and idle; inspect coverage and the latest Activity rather than expecting a constant upload indicator. If you previously selected **Stop**, automatic triggers remain stopped until you start backup again. Relaunching alone does not override that choice. ## Repair photo access and selection Dosya must be allowed to read the photo or video before it can upload it. In the operating-system app settings, grant Photos/Media access. On iPhone, **Limited Access** backs up only the items selected for Dosya; add the missing item to the allowed selection or grant broader access if that matches your intent. Return to **Backup → What gets backed up** and check album, media-type, date and size filters. An excluded item is outside the coverage total and will not become pending. A library item that cannot be materialized, such as an unavailable iCloud original or a newly restricted photo, is retried on a later run and surfaced for attention. ## Check power and network policy The default configuration uses Wi-Fi only, does not require a charger, and starts only at 20% battery or higher when unplugged. The battery minimum is a start gate. An upload already in progress is held when connectivity, Wi-Fi, or charging-only requirements change; crossing below the battery floor mid-run does not by itself pause that active transfer. Operating systems decide when background work actually runs. Dosya requests periodic work with a 15-minute minimum interval, but Android and iOS can delay it for battery, thermal, network, or scheduling reasons. Treat 15 minutes as a requested floor, not a delivery promise. Allow background activity and data for Dosya in device settings. Disable any per-app battery optimization that prevents scheduled work if continuous backup is important. On iPhone, supported uploads can continue through the native background transfer after the phone locks; on Android the app uses its foreground backup service while transferring. A force-stop or operating-system restriction can prevent later wake-ups. ## Prove the upload path in the foreground 1. Keep Dosya open on **Backup** with an allowed network and sufficient power. 2. Choose one recent, non-confidential photo included by the current filters. 3. Start or retry backup once. Watch **Scanning…**, queued activity and the per-file upload state. 4. If the screen shows a storage, membership, upload-permission, blocked-extension or file-size refusal, fix that condition in the named workspace. Background scheduling cannot bypass a server policy. 5. Wait until the item leaves pending/queued activity. Open **Files** in the same workspace and open the cloud copy. Each repeatedly unreadable or failed asset has a five-attempt automatic cap. After that it remains in the failed count until you open the failed-items view and explicitly retry it. An item marked **too large** is not retried until the size filter or source is changed; tapping retry without changing that limit cannot make the same bytes acceptable. ## Expected result After the foreground sample succeeds, leave automatic backup enabled and create one new harmless photo that matches the filters. Lock or leave the app normally; do not force-stop it. Later, reopen Dosya. Returning to the foreground settles completed background work and runs a catch-up check, so inspect **Activity**, then open the new cloud copy in **Files**. A background run is skipped when the account is signed out, automatic backup is disabled, no destination workspace is selected, the user stopped the engine, policy blocks the run, or a fatal upload block awaits manual retry. If the foreground copy works but repeated background opportunities do not, include the phone model, operating-system and Dosya versions, displayed Backup state, selected workspace, power/network policy, approximate test time and whether the app was force-stopped in a private support ticket. Do not attach private photo contents unless support provides an approved transfer method. ## Related guides - [Manage mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Monitor backup progress](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Choose albums for mobile backup
summary: Select Android folders or iPhone albums, understand partial-library access, and verify exactly which device media enters future backup scans.
verification: Reviewed in local source at apps/mobile/app/backup-folders.tsx and apps/mobile/src/backup/albumDefaults.ts, scanner.ts, filters.ts, settings.ts, with the matching unit tests. Production has not yet received this article revision.
body: **Device folders** narrows the part of the photo library considered by later scans. Android exposes media buckets such as Camera, Screenshots, Downloads, and chat-app folders; iPhone exposes overlapping albums. ## Steps 1. Go to **Settings → Backup → Device folders**. The screen reads the library and shows **Reading your library...** while album data loads. 2. Review each folder or album name and its **N items** count. Empty sources are omitted, and the largest sources appear first. 3. In **Device folders**, turn on only the sources you want included. The footer reports how many items are selected out of the accessible total. 4. Leave every switch on to use **Every folder**. In this mode, newly created Android folders and later albums are automatically included. 5. If you turn every switch off, the app saves an empty include list and displays **No folders selected, so nothing will be backed up. Turn at least one on.** Enable at least one source before expecting another upload. 6. Return to the Backup tab. Filter changes remove pending scan rows and reset the scan watermark, so the next run re-evaluates the accessible library under the new selection. Work already queued or uploaded is left alone. On a fresh Android installation, Dosya looks for Camera or DCIM buckets and selects those by default. When no recognizable camera bucket exists, it deliberately falls back to every folder and raises a one-time review prompt instead of silently excluding media. Older installs that predate filters also keep their broad coverage until you choose. iPhone defaults to the full accessible library. Albums can overlap, and an asset may belong to several albums or none. During a selected-album scan, a per-run set prevents the same asset from being emitted twice. Selecting two albums that contain one photo therefore does not create two cloud copies. Operating-system access is an outer boundary. With iOS Limited Photos or Android 14 selected-photo access, Dosya can only list the items granted to the app even if **Every folder** is chosen. The Backup tab shows **Limited photo access** and can open device Settings to widen it. If the app cannot read any albums, this screen says **No folders found. Allow photo access to choose what gets backed up.** Folder selection does not choose the cloud path. Eligible items still land under `Mobile Backup//Camera Roll/YYYY/MM` inside each configured workspace. Removing a device folder from coverage does not delete its existing cloud copies or the phone originals. ## Expected result The Backup screen's coverage reflects the selected, OS-accessible sources. A new eligible item in an enabled source is queued on the next allowed run; a new item that exists only in a disabled source remains outside backup scope. When checking the result, use two newly created harmless items rather than relying on old cloud files: place one in an included source and one only in an excluded source. Existing uploads remain visible regardless of the current selection. ## Related guides - [Start copying a mobile library](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Configure media and destination rules](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Review mobile backup items needing attention
summary: Interpret each mobile backup warning, open the correct recovery control, and restart capped failures without overlooking size-limit skips or holds.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/attention.ts, coverageScope.ts, ledger.ts, orchestrator.ts and apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, backup-failed.tsx, including focused tests. This rewrite is not yet live in production.
body: The Backup tab separates setup and policy warnings from individual transfer failures. Use the wording on the row to choose the recovery path; not every row is an error or supports a tap. ## Steps 1. Open the **Backup** tab and confirm the workspace in the header. The heading becomes **N things before the first backup** during initial setup or **N things need attention** later when at least two rows exist. 2. Resolve **setup and access** rows first: - **Finish setting up backup** returns to onboarding. - **Allow photo access** requests library permission. - **Limited photo access** opens device Settings so you can widen the operating-system selection. - **No folders selected** opens **Device folders**; turn on at least one source. - **Choose what to back up** asks you to review broad, every-folder coverage. 3. Use an exclusion warning to open **Device folders** or **Backup settings**, depending on whether its cause is an album, media type, date floor, or size cap. 4. Read connection rows as state, not failed assets. **You're offline** says **Backup resumes when a connection returns.** **Waiting for Wi-Fi** links to settings because automatic work pauses on cellular. **Wi-Fi is off** warns that a manual backup now uses mobile data. 5. For **Auto-backup paused**, fix the displayed storage, membership, or permission cause, wait until the active run drains, then tap the row to retry. It is intentionally non-actionable while the engine still treats the main button as Stop. 6. Tap the **Failed** coverage figure to open **Failed items**. An item appears after its first recorded error. With fewer than 5 attempts it remains eligible for a later automatic scan; the fifth failure retires it until **Retry all N** resets its attempts. 7. Read each filename, byte size, and last error. The screen loads at most the 200 most recent rows but retains the true total and says **Showing the 200 most recent of N.** when more exist. 8. Choose **Retry 1 item** or **Retry all N**. The reset sets every error row in that workspace back to zero attempts and starts a run; **Retrying N items** confirms the action. **Retry failed: ** means the restart itself failed. 9. Treat **Skipped by your size limit** separately. Press **Change the size limit** to change future size decisions. The retry button does not reset size-capped rows. Unreadable originals can also appear in the Backup dashboard. On iPhone, the text identifies an iCloud download or access problem; Android identifies file access. These retry on a later run. An Android asset that still reports zero bytes after a 1.5-second restat consumes an attempt and eventually reaches Failed instead of uploading an empty cloud copy. Pressing Stop cancels queued work and clears originals waiting for delete-after-backup. A native upload already mid-transfer may still finish server-side; the next run rechecks server fingerprints before deciding whether bytes need to be sent again. ## Expected result A corrected policy or permission row disappears when its condition is re-evaluated. A reset transfer leaves **Failed items** after a successful upload; if it returns, its newest error remains visible for diagnosis or **Report these failures**. The empty failed-items message is **Nothing has failed. Every item in this workspace either finished or is still queued.** It does not count assets deliberately excluded by current filters; the size-limited section is tracked separately. In the current local implementation, raising the cap does not requeue rows already recorded as `skipped_large`; they remain visible as history. To copy one of those originals immediately, upload it through Files after confirming the workspace's upload limit and your role permission. ## Related guides - [Complete first-run photo protection](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Edit phone backup conditions](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Restore background mobile backup
summary: Restore automatic cloud backup when Dosya stops making progress in the background by checking backup settings, network rules, power conditions, and iPhone locked-screen uploads.
verification: Verified against current local product source for automatic-backup policy, background-task registration, iOS locked-screen transport, Backup status messages, and alert behavior on 2026-10-14.
body: Automatic mobile backup runs when Dosya is signed in, **Automatic backup** is enabled, and the device meets the network and power rules you selected. The operating system chooses when to give background work time, so background progress may arrive in batches rather than starting immediately after every photo. ## Before you start 1. Open Dosya and select **Backup**. 2. Read the status around the progress ring and any item under **Things need attention**. 3. If you see **Waiting for Wi-Fi**, connect to Wi-Fi or open **Settings → Backup settings** and turn off **Wi-Fi only**. 4. If the status is waiting for a charger, connect power or turn off **Only while charging**. 5. If **Auto-backup paused** appears, tap that row or the backup button. A manual run clears the saved pause and tries the queue again. 6. Confirm **What gets backed up** includes at least one device folder and the photo or video types you expect. ## Steps: restore background backup Open **Settings → Backup settings** and confirm: - **Automatic backup** is on. - **Wi-Fi only** matches the network you are currently using. - **Only while charging** matches the phone's power state. - On iPhone, **Upload while locked** is on if you want the native background transfer service to carry staged uploads while the phone is locked. On iPhone, keep Dosya in the app switcher and plug the phone in for a large first backup. When native background jobs are active, the Backup page shows **Uploading in the background**. Force-quitting the app can stop the app from receiving normal background opportunities. On either platform, check the operating-system settings for Dosya if background activity has been restricted. Allow background activity and data access, and remove battery restrictions that explicitly suspend Dosya. The names of these controls vary by phone manufacturer and OS version. ## Run a controlled test 1. Add one new, non-confidential photo to an included folder. 2. Open Dosya, return to **Backup**, and tap the backup button once. 3. Wait until the item enters scanning or uploading, then leave Dosya without force-closing it. 4. Reopen the app and check the coverage count and latest activity. The test succeeds when the new item is marked uploaded and remains available in the active Dosya workspace. If the test works only while the app is visible, recheck OS background permissions and the iPhone **Upload while locked** toggle. ## Troubleshooting Low battery can prevent an automatic run from starting. A loss of network, workspace storage limit, revoked workspace membership, or missing upload permission can also pause the engine. Dosya displays fatal pauses on the Backup page and can send a **Backup paused** notification. Open the notification, correct the named cause, and use one manual retry. ## Expected result A new test item uploads after the app leaves the foreground, and the Backup page no longer shows a policy or fatal pause. ## Limits and important details The operating system controls exact background timing. Dosya can prepare and register background work, but it cannot promise an immediate run after every new photo. ## Related guides - [Retry failed backup items](/files/mobile-backup-retry-failed) - [Troubleshoot background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Review battery restrictions that pause backup
summary: Diagnose mobile backup under battery restrictions by separating Dosya start gates from operating-system scheduling, active-run holds, and manual overrides.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/backup/policy.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/background.ts, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, and apps/mobile/app/backup-settings.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya checks its own power policy, while iOS and Android independently decide when background work may run. Diagnose those layers separately instead of expecting one battery switch to force an immediate backup. **Dosya power gates** An automatic run will not start while unplugged below the built-in 20% battery floor. That threshold is not exposed as an adjustable setting. **Only while charging** adds a separate charging requirement. Once a run has started, crossing below 20% does not pause it; active-run holds check connectivity, Wi-Fi-only, and charging-only settings. ## Steps 1. Open the **Backup** tab and read the current state before changing system settings. Confirm the active workspace and whether the app says it is waiting for a charger, Wi-Fi, or connectivity. 2. In mobile **Backup settings**, review **Automatic backup**, **Wi-Fi only**, **Only while charging**, and **Upload while locked**. Record their original values. 3. Check the operating system’s background and battery settings for Dosya. Control names vary by OS and device vendor, so use the installed system’s own labels rather than assuming one universal menu path. 4. For a controlled test, keep Dosya open, connect power, and back up one non-sensitive item. **Back up now** is a manual run: it bypasses the charging-only gate for that run, and a cellular confirmation can temporarily bypass Wi-Fi-only without changing saved preferences. 5. Verify the cloud copy in **Files** before deleting anything from the phone. Re-enable the desired restrictions after the test. **Background limits** Dosya requests a 15-minute minimum background cadence, but the operating system chooses actual timing. iOS gives the scheduled task an approximately 120-second staging budget. **Upload while locked** enables the native locked-device transport where supported; it is unavailable in Expo Go. Android uses a foreground service while active work is running. Do not promise an instant restart after changing battery settings. A permitted window, network, photo-library access, workspace access, and storage are all still required. ## Expected result The controlled item proceeds while the app is open and powered, and later automatic work resumes when both Dosya’s saved policy and the operating system’s scheduler allow it. ## Related guides - [Retry failed backup items](/files/mobile-backup-retry-failed) - [Troubleshoot background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Keep backup running while charging
summary: Use Only while charging for automatic backup, know what a manual run bypasses, and understand the five-minute hold after power is disconnected.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/backup-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/policy.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/orchestrator.ts, and apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **Only while charging** switch controls automatic starts and active-run holds. A manual **Back up now** test intentionally bypasses that charging requirement for the current run. **Set the automatic rule** Automatic backup also checks connectivity, **Wi-Fi only**, and a built-in 20% battery floor while unplugged. The battery percentage is a start gate; an active run is not paused merely because charge drops from 20% to 19%. ## Steps 1. Open the mobile app, choose the intended workspace, and go to **Backup settings**. 2. Under **When to back up**, turn on **Only while charging**. Leave **Automatic backup** enabled if you want scheduled work to start under that rule. 3. Disconnect power before an automatic run begins and confirm it does not start. The policy reason is **waiting-for-charge**, while the active Backup interface uses the wording **waiting for charger**. 4. Connect a recognized charger and leave network and photo-library permissions available. The operating system controls when the next background opportunity occurs, so charging does not guarantee immediate execution. 5. During a small active automatic run, disconnect power. Upload pacing enters **waiting for charger** and waits up to five minutes; if power does not return, the run ends cleanly and unfinished ledger rows remain eligible for a future run. **Manual-run exception** Tapping **Back up now** skips the charging-only gate for that run and does not change the saved switch. Use that manual path when you deliberately want to continue unplugged. It can also offer a one-time cellular override for Wi-Fi-only, so read that prompt before proceeding. Stopping or timing out does not erase unfinished source media. Confirm backed-up bytes in **Files** before using any delete-after-backup option or removing originals yourself. ## Expected result Automatic work starts only under the saved charging rule, an interrupted run shows the charger hold and exits after five minutes, and manual backup remains an explicit exception. ## Related guides - [Set up mobile backup](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Change backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Free device storage when mobile backup pauses
summary: Fix a Dosya mobile backup paused by low phone storage, safely remove originals already confirmed in cloud storage, and retry the pending upload queue.
verification: Verified against current local product source for the mobile backup staging, pause, Free up space, and retry implementation on 2026-10-14. The guide distinguishes device storage from workspace cloud-storage quota. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Dosya may pause mobile backup with **Not enough free space on this device to stage the next photos**. This message refers to storage on the phone, not the storage allowance in your Dosya workspace. On iPhone, locked-screen uploads use a temporary staging area before the app hands files to the operating system. Dosya removes each staged copy after the upload is acknowledged, but the next batch still needs enough local space to start. ## Before you start 1. Open Dosya and select the **Backup** tab. 2. Read the item under **Things need attention**. A device-space problem says there is not enough free space **on this device**. A workspace quota problem mentions the workspace storage limit instead. 3. Check the storage bar on the Backup page. If the workspace has available cloud storage, clear space on the phone before changing the workspace plan. 4. Leave the pending items in place. Dosya keeps them eligible for a later run; you do not need to select the photos again. ## Steps: safely free device storage 1. Open **Settings** in the mobile app, then choose **Backup settings**. 2. Under **Storage on this device**, tap **Free up space**. 3. Wait while Dosya checks the current workspace. The app rechecks every candidate against the server instead of relying only on its local backup history. 4. Review **Ready to remove**, the estimated number of photos and videos, and the amount of space that can be reclaimed. 5. Check **Kept on this device**. These items could not be confirmed in the workspace and will not be removed. 6. Tap **Remove originals**, then approve the operating-system confirmation. Removed originals stay in Dosya cloud storage. The current mobile app does not provide a one-tap way to put those originals back into the phone's photo library, so download any item you need locally before removing it. You can also free space through the phone's storage settings. Avoid clearing Dosya app data or uninstalling the app while uploads are pending because that can remove local transfer state. ## Retry the backup Return to **Backup** and tap the backup button. A manual retry clears the saved automatic-backup pause and scans the pending queue again. Keep Dosya open until you see scanning or upload progress. On iPhone, leave Dosya in the app switcher if **Upload while locked** is enabled. The recovery is complete when the low-storage attention item disappears, the pending count falls, and the latest activity shows uploaded items. If the warning returns immediately, free more device space and retry with the phone connected to power. ## Troubleshooting **The message is about workspace storage.** Device cleanup will not fix a full workspace. Switch to the intended workspace, review its storage bar, remove permanently deleted files if appropriate, or increase its storage allowance. Then return to Backup and tap the backup button to retry. ## Expected result The device-storage warning clears, the pending count starts falling, and the latest Backup activity records uploaded items in the intended workspace. ## Limits and important details Free up space only offers media the selected workspace currently confirms. It does not restore removed originals to the phone, and it cannot solve a full Dosya workspace. ## Related guides - [Retry failed backup items](/files/mobile-backup-retry-failed) - [Choose mobile backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Review mobile backup history
summary: Read the device-local Backup Activity feed, interpret backed-up, already-backed-up, failed, and nothing-new rows, and understand retention and sign-out.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/backup/history.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/ActivityFeed.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/orchestrator.ts, and apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The mobile **Activity** feed is a device-local summary of recent backup runs. Use it to find a run, then verify important files in cloud **Files** rather than treating the row as a byte-level receipt. **What a history row shows** Each row begins with the formatted run time and workspace name. Its second line starts with **_N_ backed up**, then adds **_N_ already backed up** and **_N_ failed** when those counts are non-zero. A run with zero in all three fields says **Nothing new**. The stored skipped-large count is not printed in this history row. ## Steps 1. Open the **Backup** tab and scroll to **Activity**. Live work can show **Scanning your library…**, individual upload percentages, a queued count, and up to five current error lines followed by **_N_ more failed**. 2. Find the newest row for the intended workspace. History is ordered newest first and paged six runs at a time. 3. Compare the counts with the live state and the **Failed items** screen. A run can identify failures, while oversized items remain a separate size-limit category. 4. Open **Files** and verify several expected cloud files, including their destination folder, size, and readable content. 5. If the feed says **No backups yet.**, confirm that a run actually performed work. A manual no-op can update the Last run state without adding an empty history record. **Retention and privacy** The local SQLite table keeps the 100 newest runs and removes older entries. The feed is stored on this device rather than synchronized as account history. Signing out clears the table entirely because its rows are not scoped for safe reuse by another account on the same installation. Deleting a history row through retention or sign-out does not delete uploaded cloud files. Conversely, a history count does not prove a later rename, move, lock, or deletion has not changed the file since that run. ## Expected result The Activity feed explains the recent run with device-local counts, pagination exposes retained older runs, and cloud Files confirms the important outputs independently. ## Related guides - [Monitor mobile backup](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Fix paused background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Expand limited photo access for mobile backup
summary: Allow Dosya to back up more iPhone photos by changing limited library access, then rescan the selected cloud-backup scope and verify one newly permitted item.
verification: Verified against current local product source for photo permission detection, the Limited photo access attention item, device-settings routing, library recounting, and backup scanning on 2026-10-14. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: When iPhone photo access is limited, Dosya can scan and back up only the photos and videos the operating system exposes to the app. The Backup page shows **Limited photo access** with the explanation **Only selected photos back up**. Expanding permission does not upload anything by itself; it lets the next scan see more eligible media. ## Before you start - Confirm the active Dosya workspace in the header of the **Backup** tab. - Choose one non-confidential photo that is currently outside the allowed selection. - Review **What gets backed up**. Device-folder, media-type, date, and file-size filters still apply after you expand permission. - Keep the phone online and use a workspace with enough cloud storage for the test item. ## Steps: expand photo access 1. Open Dosya and select **Backup**. 2. Tap the **Limited photo access** item under the attention list. Dosya opens the operating-system settings for the app. 3. Open the Photos permission. Choose full photo-library access if you want the selected Dosya backup filters to control the scope, or update the limited selection to add only the intended photos. 4. Return to Dosya and reopen **Backup**. The page checks photo access again whenever it receives focus. 5. Review the coverage total. It can increase because the app can now count newly available items. 6. Tap the backup button to scan again. 7. Watch the selected test photo enter the pending or uploading state, then wait for it to appear under **Backed up**. 8. Open **Files** in the active workspace and verify the cloud copy. ## Expected result The limited-access warning disappears after full access is granted, or the newly selected items become visible while limited access remains. The coverage total reflects the accessible, filtered library, and the test photo becomes available in the intended Dosya workspace. ## Limits and important details - Granting full access does not override **Device folders**, **Photos**, **Videos**, **Start from**, or **Skip large files** settings. - Previously uploaded cloud copies remain in Dosya when phone permission changes. - Removing photo access prevents new scans but does not delete files already stored in the workspace. - A larger permission scope can increase the pending count substantially on the next scan. ## Troubleshooting **The warning remains after changing the setting.** Leave the Backup tab, reopen it, and confirm the operating system saved the permission for Dosya. Restart the app if the OS settings screen did not return cleanly. **A newly allowed photo is still missing.** Check Dosya's device-folder, media-type, date, and size filters. The photo must pass both the phone permission and the backup filters. **The item appears but does not upload.** Read the Backup status for Wi-Fi, charging, storage, membership, or upload-permission pauses, then retry once. ## Related guides - [Retry failed backup items](/files/mobile-backup-retry-failed) - [Troubleshoot background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Back up Live Photos and motion photos
summary: Back up Live Photos and motion photos, distinguish pair detection from companion upload failure, and understand the current 25-item backfill limit.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/backup/livePhoto.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/motionPhoto.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/orchestrator.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/ledger.ts, and apps/mobile/src/backup/transport/backgroundTransport.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya detects supported paired media automatically during mobile backup. There is no Live Photo or motion-photo toggle: keep normal Photos backup enabled, then distinguish a pair that was never discovered from a discovered companion whose upload failed. **How pairing works** On iOS, the native media helper uses the Photos asset identifier to retrieve the paired video. On Android, Dosya reads the first 256 KiB of a motion photo for supported XMP offset or container-item metadata, then copies the motion-video tail. If no pair is detected, the format is unsupported, or extraction fails, the still image continues, the still is marked pair-checked, and no `#video` ledger row exists to retry. A temporary background-staging budget or no-space result is treated as inconclusive instead, so the still remains eligible for a later probe. ## Steps 1. In **Backup settings**, enable Photos and select the intended device folders and destination. Grant the operating system access to the original media and keep upload and destination-folder permissions available. 2. Start a backup with one supported Live Photo or motion photo. No separate paired-media option should appear. 3. In cloud **Files**, look for the still and, when discovery and staging succeeded, its sibling motion file in the same folder. They share a base name. The in-process iOS path creates a `.MOV` name, native iOS background staging keeps the exported companion filename, and Android creates `.MP4`. 4. Open both files when the sibling exists. A successfully discovered and staged motion part receives its own ledger row using the still asset ID plus `#video`; only that row can deduplicate, fail an upload, and retry independently. 5. If older stills were uploaded before pairing was checked, run backup again. Backfill probes at most 25 previously uploaded unpaired stills per run; remaining candidates wait for later runs. **Counts and recovery** The dashboard’s protected-library coverage counts the source media asset, not the companion as a second library item. Once staging succeeds, the companion owns a `#video` ledger row, but later failures do not all give that row the same status: - A native background job or registration failure normally returns the row to `pending` and increments its attempts. The background planner can retry it while its attempt count is below five; it does not appear in **Failed items** while pending. - An in-process upload failure records the row as `error` with another attempt. A later in-process scan can retry it while below five, and the row can also appear in **Failed items**. - A direct-upload initialization refusal records `error` immediately. Use the batch **Retry all** action after fixing the refusal’s cause; there is no per-row retry. A `#video` row that already exists is planned independently from its still. If its native restaging is unreadable, it remains pending while the attempt count increases. A budget or device-space stop leaves the probe inconclusive without charging that attempt. When detection or extraction returns no companion before a row exists, Dosya marks the still pair-checked and creates no failed item to reset; the destination contains only the still. Do not delete the device original until both expected files open correctly. The still and motion sibling are separate cloud files, so deleting or moving one does not automatically change the other. ## Expected result A discovered and successfully uploaded pair produces a readable still plus a MOV or MP4 sibling. A pair rejected before companion-row creation leaves only the still and no retry row. After a `#video` row exists, a native background failure can leave it retryable as `pending`, while in-process failure or direct initialization refusal can leave it as `error`. ## Related guides - [Set up mobile backup](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Change backup settings](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Choose Wi-Fi or cellular backup
summary: Control cellular, Wi-Fi, charging, and low-battery behavior, then use a one-run override without changing future automatic backup policy for later runs.
verification: Locally verified through apps/mobile/app/backup-settings.tsx, app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, src/backup/policy.ts, background.ts, orchestrator.ts, upload/pacing.ts, and focused tests. No production instance was consulted; publication is outstanding.
body: The mobile backup policy decides whether an automatic run may start and when an active transfer must wait. A manual run can use a temporary cellular or charging override without weakening future automation. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings → Backup** and find **When to back up**. 2. Keep **Wi-Fi only** on to prevent automatic starts over mobile data. Turn it off only when recurring cellular use is acceptable; the change saves immediately. 3. Enable **Only while charging** if automatic runs should wait for external power. Even with that switch off, an unplugged device below the built-in 20% battery floor will not start a new run. 4. Return to the Backup tab and inspect the attention text. **Waiting for Wi-Fi** means automatic backup is paused on cellular; **You're offline** means it resumes after connectivity returns. 5. To make a one-time cellular run while **Wi-Fi only** remains on, press **Backup now**, review **Back up over mobile data this time?**, and choose **Use mobile data**. The dialog explains that only this run is overridden. 6. A manual **Backup now** also ignores **Only while charging** for that run. Stop or queue completion withdraws the temporary override; later automatic activity uses the saved switches again. If connectivity disappears, Wi-Fi drops, or the charger is removed during an applicable run, uploads pause with **offline**, **waiting for Wi-Fi**, or **waiting for charger**. The scanner waits for up to 5 minutes. If the condition has not recovered, that run ends cleanly, keeps its unfinished ledger rows pending, and lets a later run resume. The 20% battery rule is checked only before starting while unplugged. It does not interrupt a transfer already underway when the battery crosses 19%. The operating system may still delay or stop background work according to its own battery and scheduling rules. When the app is active, Android uses a data-sync foreground service for backup work. iPhone can hand supported uploads to the native background transport when **Upload while locked** is enabled. Expo Go does not provide that native iOS transport. ## Expected result An automatic run begins only on an allowed connection and power state. A confirmed manual exception proceeds on cellular or without a charger, while **Wi-Fi only** and **Only while charging** keep their saved values for the next automatic run. If **Backup now** reports **Allow photo access first - see the list at the top of this screen.**, fix library permission before testing the network policy. **Backup failed: ** identifies a request-level problem; storage, membership, or upload-permission failures can also place automatic backup in a paused state until corrected and retried. ## Related guides - [Begin a Wi-Fi-first phone backup](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Review every backup control](/files/mobile-backup-settings)

title: Monitor mobile cloud backup progress
summary: Read Dosya's protected, pending, failed, queued, scanning, uploading, and paused states, then verify a recent cloud copy before removing the phone original.
verification: Verified against current local product source for the mobile coverage calculation, progress ring, engine states, live Activity rows, background jobs, failure counts, history, and workspace verification flow on 2026-10-14. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: A photo is protected only after its upload finishes and the cloud copy can be opened. The Dosya **Backup** tab separates library coverage from the current transfer: the ring shows how much of the selected scope is protected, the breakdown shows unresolved counts, and **Activity** shows what the current or previous run did. ## Before you start - Confirm the workspace shown at the top of the Backup tab. - Review **What gets backed up** so you know which device folders, media types, dates, and sizes belong to the coverage total. - Keep one recent, non-confidential photo available as a verification item. - Connect to a network and power state allowed by **Backup settings**. ## Steps: read backup progress 1. Open **Backup**. 2. Read the centre of the coverage ring: - **Scanning…** means Dosya is discovering eligible library items. - **Backing up** means one or more uploads are active. - **Paused — waiting for Wi-Fi**, **waiting for charger**, or **offline** names a temporary hold. - **Cooling down…** resumes automatically after the device cools. - **Paused** without a temporary hold indicates a saved failure that needs attention and a retry. - **Protected** means automatic backup is enabled and the engine is idle. 3. Read **X of Y protected**. The total is the accessible library after Dosya filters are applied, not necessarily every photo on the phone. 4. Compare **Backed up**, **Pending**, and **Failed**. Tap the Failed area when it has failed or skipped-too-large items. 5. Scroll to **Activity**. During a run, it shows scanning, queued count, per-file upload percentages, and up to five current errors. 6. Review backup history for the time, workspace, uploaded count, items already backed up, and failures from earlier runs. 7. When the run becomes idle, open **Files** in the same workspace and open the recent test photo. ## Expected result The protected count rises as uploads settle, the pending count falls, and the Activity history records the completed run in the intended workspace. The test photo opens from Dosya after a refresh. ## Limits and important details - Items excluded by date, folder, media type, or size filters are outside the protected total. - Failed items and items skipped by the size limit are settled separately, so **Pending** can reach zero while **Failed** or **too large** still needs review. - A queued iPhone background job can continue after the JavaScript upload list is empty; the screen shows an **Uploading in the background** hint. - Do not delete the phone original solely because a scan completed. Open the cloud copy first. ## Troubleshooting **The total is smaller than the phone library.** Check limited photo access and every backup filter. The ring describes the selected scope. **Progress is paused.** Read the exact hold or attention message. Restore Wi-Fi or power for a temporary hold; correct storage, membership, or upload permission for a fatal pause, then tap once to retry. **A file remains failed.** Open the failed-items view, read its error, and retry after correcting the cause. Items stop retrying automatically after the attempt limit. **The count changed after deleting phone media.** Coverage is recalculated from the current accessible library, while uploaded history can retain records for items already removed from the device. ## Related guides - [Set up mobile backup](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Fix background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Retry failed mobile backup items
summary: Reset every mobile backup error row in one batch, distinguish five-attempt foreground and background states, and handle size skips and fatal pauses.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/backup-failed.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/ledger.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/orchestrator.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/transport/backgroundTransport.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/ActivityFeed.tsx, and apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/CoverageRing.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya’s **Failed items** screen lists every ledger row whose current status is `error`; it does not wait for the row to reach five attempts. Retry behavior differs between foreground processing, background staging, and native background transfer. **What the screen contains** Open the Backup failure count to reach **Failed items**. It loads all `error` rows for the active workspace, whether the row failed once or has exhausted its five-attempt allowance. The list holds at most 200 recent error rows and says **Showing the 200 most recent of _N_.** when more exist; the button count and reset still use the true ledger total. ## Steps 1. Read the displayed filenames and exact errors, then fix the shared cause: restore photo access, make the original readable, unlock or permit the destination, reconnect, or resolve workspace storage and membership. 2. Select **Report these failures** when the visible errors cannot be explained. The report includes the total number of `error` rows, including rows beyond the 200 displayed. 3. Choose **Retry 1 item** or **Retry all _N_**. There is no item-details screen or per-row retry control. The batch action changes every `error` row in the active workspace to `pending`, sets its attempts to zero, clears its stored error, and starts a backup run. 4. Watch for **Retrying 1 item** or **Retrying _N_ items**. If the reset or run call throws, Dosya reports **Retry failed: _reason_**. 5. Check cloud **Files** and reopen **Failed items**. A successful row disappears from the error list; a current failure can return with a new error and attempt count. ### How the five-attempt limit differs by path In foreground processing, an `error` row below five attempts can be tried on a later run; the scanner excludes it after attempt five. Native background transfer failures instead return the row to `pending` and add one attempt, so the planner can retry it while `attempts < 5`. An unreadable native background staging result also stays `pending` while its attempt count increases. Once it reaches five, the planner excludes it, but it does not become an `error` row and therefore does not appear in **Failed items** or respond to **Retry all**. If the original is now readable but remains stuck in that state, report the case rather than expecting the failure screen to reset it. An empty background-staged file or a direct-upload initialization refusal becomes `error` immediately. That row appears in **Failed items** and waits for the batch retry action even if it has used fewer than five attempts. A native staging budget or device-space stop does not charge an item attempt. ### Skipped files and fatal pauses Rows under **Skipped by your size limit** are not part of retry. Use **Change the size limit**; retrying the same settings would skip them again. This list also loads at most 200 recent rows while retaining the true total. A workspace-fatal error can record the affected item and set a separate **Paused** state before later items begin. Resolve the workspace condition, return to the main **Backup** screen, and tap the **Paused** backup control whose caption says **Tap to retry**. **Retry all** resets error rows but does not clear that workspace pause by itself. When no error rows or size skips remain, the screen says **Nothing has failed.
