Every item in this workspace either finished or is still queued.** That message can include a pending background-staging row which has reached its attempt cap, because the screen checks only `error` and `skipped_large` rows. ## Expected result The batch button resets every visible or undisplayed `error` row for the active workspace and starts a run after its cause is fixed. Size skips, a separate workspace pause, and capped background-staging rows that remain `pending` require their own recovery paths. ## Related guides - [Monitor mobile backup](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Fix paused background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Retry a large video in mobile backup
summary: Understand why a large video was skipped, change the mobile backup size limit, and identify the current retry limitation before relying on it.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/backup-failed.tsx, apps/mobile/app/backup-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/orchestrator.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/ledger.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A video above the configured cap is recorded as `skipped_large`, not as an upload error. The mobile client exposes the skipped row and the size setting, but its current ledger logic does not return an existing skipped row to the queue after that setting changes. The available **Skip large files** choices are **No limit**, **Over 200 MB**, **Over 1 GB**, and **Over 5 GB**. Raising the cap can admit newly discovered videos, but **Retry all** affects only rows with status `error`. ## Steps 1. Open **Backup**, tap the **Failed** count, and find the video under **Skipped by your size limit**. 2. Check the displayed filename, byte size, and stored message before changing any backup rule. 3. Return to **Backup settings**, open **Skip large files**, and choose a cap above the video size or **No limit**. 4. Keep Videos and the containing device folder selected; confirm the intended destination workspace before starting another run. 5. Start backup again and watch **Pending**, the ring, and the activity feed for newly eligible videos. 6. If this exact video stays under the skipped count, use **Report these failures** or support; the released client has no control that resets a `skipped_large` ledger row. ### Why retry does not appear The failure screen deliberately offers **Change the size limit** for skipped rows instead of **Retry all**. The batch retry function resets only `error` rows. During later scans, the orchestrator also ignores an asset already marked `skipped_large`, so changing the cap alone does not requeue that historical row. Do not delete the device original while testing. A skipped video has not been copied to Dosya, and no success toast or completed row exists to protect it. ### Other conditions that can pause a large transfer The size cap is separate from network and power policy. With **Wi-Fi only** enabled, a run can show **Paused - waiting for Wi-Fi**; with **Only while charging**, it can wait for a charger. A manual run can begin despite the start policy, but a mid-run network or charger change can still hold uploads until the condition returns. ## Expected result New videos below the revised cap can enter the backup queue. The previously skipped video may remain listed as too large because the current client does not reset that row; treat it as not backed up until it appears in cloud **Files** and opens correctly. ## Related guides - [Retry failed backup items](/files/mobile-backup-retry-failed) - [Troubleshoot background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Change mobile backup settings
summary: Choose which phone media is backed up, when transfers may run, and which workspaces receive new copies without moving or replacing earlier uploads.
verification: Verified from local source in apps/mobile/app/backup-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/settings.ts, filters.ts, policy.ts, folders.ts, cleanup.ts, and their tests. Production behavior was not queried; this revision awaits publication.
body: Mobile **Backup settings** control future scans and transfers. They do not move files already in cloud storage or restore originals removed from the phone. ## Steps 1. In the mobile app, open **Settings** and choose **Backup** to reach **Backup settings**. 2. Under **What to back up**, leave **Photos**, **Videos**, or both enabled. The app prevents turning off the final enabled media type. 3. Open **Device folders** to use **Every folder** or a selected set. An include list with no selected folder backs up nothing. 4. Choose **Start from**: **Everything in my library**, **Only from today onward**, **The last 30 days**, or **The last year**. 5. Set **Skip large files** to **No limit**, **Skip files over 200 MB**, **Skip files over 1 GB**, or **Skip files over 5 GB**. This rule is applied after the original is available locally and its byte size is known. 6. Under **When to back up**, set **Automatic backup**, **Wi-Fi only**, and **Only while charging**. On iPhone, **Upload while locked** lets the native background transport continue after suspension. 7. If the account has several workspaces, use **Back up to** to select one or more. With no explicit selection, the active workspace is used. One run processes selected destinations sequentially. 8. Review **Delete originals after backup** carefully. After confirmed uploads, the operating system asks once to remove that run's originals. A declined or failed deletion is not repeated automatically, and Dosya has no in-app restore for the device copies. There is no Save button: each switch or choice is written immediately. Changing media, date, folder, or size filters clears only not-yet-started scan rows and scan watermarks. Queued transfers, completed records, failures, and prior size skips remain recorded. Cloud copies always go to `Mobile Backup//Camera Roll/YYYY/MM`, based on the capture month in the phone's local time. Backup settings offer workspace selection rather than an arbitrary destination-folder picker. Your role must be able to upload files and create the missing folders in that chain. ## Expected result The next eligible asset follows the saved media, date, size, network, power, and workspace rules. A destination change creates future copies in the new workspace; earlier cloud files stay where they were uploaded. If a new rule appears ignored, wait for any already-queued work to finish, then run **Back up now** with a newly eligible test photo. A storage-limit, membership, or upload-permission error pauses automatic runs until the cause is fixed and a manual retry clears the pause. Items already marked **Skipped by your size limit** remain historical `skipped_large` rows in the current mobile implementation, even after the limit is raised. The changed limit governs newly evaluated assets; use the regular Files upload flow for an already skipped original when it must be copied immediately. ## Related guides - [Prepare automatic phone copies](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Inspect ongoing phone transfers](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Choose cellular or Wi-Fi transfer](/files/mobile-backup-network)

title: Set up automatic mobile photo backup
summary: Grant photo access, choose an initial library range, start automatic backup, and confirm full-resolution copies reach the correct workspace safely.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/src/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx and steps/PhotoAccessStep.tsx, ChooseStep.tsx, FirstBackupStep.tsx, plus backup/orchestrator.ts and folders.ts. Live production was not used as evidence; deployment remains pending.
body: First-run setup enables automatic backup and immediately attempts a full-resolution transfer. You need photo-library access, workspace storage, and a role that can upload files and create folders. ## Steps 1. Sign in to the mobile app. If the account has no workspace, **Name your first workspace**, choose its storage **Location**, and press **Continue**. That workspace location is chosen once. 2. On **Turn on photo backup**, press **Continue**. The next system dialog is the actual iOS or Android permission request. Dosya copies originals at full resolution; it does not resize them for backup. 3. Grant **Full Access** for complete coverage. iOS Limited access and Android selected-photo access are supported, but only assets the operating system exposes can be scanned. 4. On **Choose what gets backed up**, enable **Photos**, **Videos**, or both. Pick **All time**, **12 months**, or **From today**. The screen estimates selected items and bytes and warns **That is more than your plan holds** when its estimate exceeds the workspace total. 5. Press **Start backup**. Setup saves Wi-Fi-only on, charging-only off, applies the platform's default folder choice, enables automatic backup, and starts the first run. 6. Keep this screen visible until **Backing up now** shows progress or the run finishes. Press **Done** when you are ready to use the rest of the app; the Backup tab remains available for progress and retries. 7. Open **Files** in the same workspace and follow `Mobile Backup//Camera Roll/YYYY/MM`. The year and month use the asset's capture time in the phone's local timezone. On a new Android setup, Dosya tries to select recognizable Camera or DCIM folders. If it cannot identify one safely, it covers every folder and later asks you to review the choice. iPhone starts with the whole accessible library because albums overlap and some assets have no album. If permission is denied, the app displays **Photo access is off**. Use **Open Settings**, or follow `Settings → dosya.dev → Photos → Full Access` on iPhone and `Settings → Apps → dosya.dev → Permissions → Photos and videos` on Android. **Continue without backup** leaves upload, browsing, sharing, and Vault available, but automatic photo backup cannot run. Automatic work is subject to the operating system scheduler. Dosya requests a 15-minute minimum interval, while Android WorkManager and iOS BGTaskScheduler decide the actual start time. New media events are debounced for about 2 seconds while the app is active. iOS background task windows budget roughly 120 seconds for staging, so large libraries continue over later opportunities. ## Expected result **Auto-backup is on** appears after settings are saved, and eligible originals begin copying to the selected workspace. Existing device files remain untouched unless **Delete originals after backup** is enabled later and the operating-system deletion prompt is accepted. If the first run says **Backup could not start**, finish onboarding with **Done**, correct access, storage, membership, or role permissions, and use **Back up now** on the Backup tab. The engine remembers per-workspace fingerprints, so a later run can link an already uploaded item instead of sending its bytes again. ## Related guides - [Grant phone library access](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Adjust future backup behavior](/files/mobile-backup-settings) - [Check workspace storage consumption](/uploading/storage-usage) - [Select eligible device albums](/files/mobile-backup-albums) - [Resolve dashboard attention states](/files/mobile-backup-attention)

title: Read the mobile backup status ring
summary: Read protected, pending, failed, skipped, paused, and filtered mobile-backup states correctly, including the ring’s three-second refresh timing.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/coverage.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/CoverageRing.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/CoverageFigures.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/coverageScope.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/ui/engineStatus.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The backup ring measures eligible photos and videos in the current filter scope. It is not a storage meter and it is not derived only from the rows already scanned into the ledger. When photo-library permission allows a count, the headline is **_uploaded_ of _total_ protected**. The arc uses that fraction. During a live run, ledger counts refresh every 3 seconds; the elapsed clock updates each second. ## Steps 1. Open **Backup** and read the headline inside the ring before interpreting its arc. 2. Read the scope line such as **Photos only**, **3 folders**, or **Since 17 Sep 2025**; tap it to change the limiting setting. 3. Compare **Backed up**, **Pending**, and **Failed** beneath the ring; a separate **_N_ too large** line can appear under Failed. 4. Tap the Failed column when it has errors or size skips to open **Failed items** and see filenames and messages. 5. Read the ring center and caption: **Start backup**, **Continue backup**, **Tap to stop**, **Tap to retry**, or **Select a workspace to back up**. 6. Confirm completion in cloud **Files** when the ring says **Protected**; the ring describes library coverage, not whether a specific cloud file opens. ### How the counts are calculated **Backed up** is the uploaded ledger count capped at the current eligible library size. **Pending** is calculated as eligible library items minus uploaded, skipped-large, and error rows, so queued transfers remain pending and a large library does not look nearly complete just because only a small scan window has been seeded. Without a readable library total, Dosya falls back to ledger counts: uploaded remains the completed count, and both `pending` and `queued` contribute to Pending. A restricted photo permission can therefore make the denominator unavailable or smaller than the whole phone library. ### Ring states - **Scanning…** means Dosya is discovering eligible media. - **Backing up** uses a green active core; the caption can add speed, estimated time left, and elapsed time. - **Paused - waiting for Wi-Fi**, **Paused - waiting for charger**, or **Paused - offline** resumes automatically when the condition clears. - **Cooling down…** means thermal pacing is active and also resumes automatically. - A destructive-color **Paused** with **Tap to retry** is a blocking failure, not a policy hold. - **Protected** appears when automatic backup is enabled and no blocking work is active; **Ready** appears when automatic backup is off. ## Expected result The protected fraction matches the selected media types, folders, and start date; Pending falls as eligible items settle; Failed and too-large items remain separately actionable; and the ring’s caption tells whether a tap starts, stops, continues, or retries. ## Related guides - [Monitor mobile backup](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Fix paused background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Add the Dosya backup widget on Android
summary: Add the Android home-screen backup widget and interpret its small and medium layouts, refresh timing, stale state, storage warning, and tap behavior.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/modules/dosya-backup-status/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, apps/mobile/modules/dosya-backup-status/android/src/main/res/xml/backup_widget_info.xml, apps/mobile/modules/dosya-backup-status/android/src/main/java/dev/dosya/backupstatus/BackupWidgetProvider.kt, apps/mobile/modules/dosya-backup-status/android/src/main/java/dev/dosya/backupstatus/WidgetRenderer.kt, apps/mobile/src/backup/statusBridge.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The Android home-screen widget is registered as **dosya backup** and supports horizontal or vertical resizing. The renderer chooses the medium layout at a reported minimum width of 180 dp or more; narrower placements use the small layout. This is a native Android widget. It is available only in a production/dev-client build that includes the `dosya-backup-status` module; Expo Go cannot load that native module. ## Steps 1. Long-press an empty area of the Android home screen and open the launcher’s **Widgets** picker. 2. Find **dosya backup** under Dosya, then drag it onto the home screen. 3. Resize it to a small card or at least 180 dp wide for the medium facts layout. 4. Open Dosya and sign in. The app can publish a snapshot immediately, but the workspace name stays blank until a backup scan starts. 5. Start a small backup; compare **Backing up**, progress, and current speed with the Backup screen. 6. Tap the widget to open Dosya and verify the active workspace and transfer there; do not use the widget name alone to confirm the destination. ### What each size shows The small card shows **dosya.dev**, a storage ring, **Backing up** or **Protected**, and the last-run time when one exists. The medium card adds the workspace name, **Free**, **Used**, and either live **Progress** plus **Speed now** or idle **Last backup** plus **Last speed**. The storage ring turns to the warning color at 90% used. Missing storage data renders as a dash rather than an invented percentage. If no snapshot exists, the widget says **Open dosya to see your backup**. ### Refresh and stale data Phase changes, active-workspace changes, theme changes, and a completed run push immediately. Ordinary progress snapshots are throttled to once every 15 seconds. A workspace switch changes the storage lookup, but it does not set `workspaceName`; that name is written only when a scan starts and is retained after the run returns to idle. Before the first run it can be blank, and after an idle workspace switch it can be stale or disagree with storage from the newly active workspace. Android also treats a non-idle snapshot older than 3,600 seconds as stale and renders it as **Protected** instead of claiming an hour-old transfer is still running. The widget follows the phone’s light or dark mode using both palettes supplied by the active Dosya theme. Tapping anywhere on the card launches the app; the widget has no pause or retry button. ## Expected result The placed widget shows the latest published backup snapshot, storage from the active workspace, and either live or last-run facts. Confirm the destination in Dosya whenever the displayed workspace name is blank or differs from the active workspace. It refreshes after meaningful app events, switches theme with the system, and opens Dosya when tapped. ## Related guides - [Monitor mobile backup](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Fix paused background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Add the Dosya backup widget on iPhone
summary: Add the iPhone backup widget, choose its supported size, read live and last-run facts, and understand refresh, theme, and Live Activity behavior.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/targets/backup-widget/index.swift, apps/mobile/modules/dosya-backup-status/ios/DosyaBackupStatusModule.swift, apps/mobile/src/backup/statusBridge.ts, apps/mobile/app.config.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya’s iOS extension provides **Backup status** in the system-small and system-medium families. The same target also provides a Live Activity for an active backup on supported iOS versions. The widget requires a signed production or development build containing the **BackupWidget** target and the shared App Group. It is not available in Expo Go. ## Steps 1. Long-press the iPhone Home Screen, choose **Edit** and **Add Widget**, then search for Dosya. 2. Select **Backup status** and choose the small or medium size; extra-large and Lock Screen widget families are not declared. 3. Open Dosya and sign in. The app can seed the shared snapshot immediately, but the workspace name stays blank until a backup scan starts. 4. Start a small backup and compare the widget’s **Backing up** state with progress shown inside Dosya. 5. Check the Lock Screen or Dynamic Island for the Live Activity when iOS 16.2 or later allows Live Activities. 6. Finish the run, reopen the widget, and check its last-backup facts; then open Dosya to verify the active workspace because the idle name is retained from the last scan. ### Small and medium facts The small widget shows **dosya.dev**, free storage inside its ring, **Backing up** or **Protected**, and the last-run time. The medium widget names the workspace and shows used percentage, **Free**, **Used**, and either **Progress** plus **Speed now** or **Last backup** plus **Last speed**. At 90% storage use, the ring and free-space fact switch to the warning color. Missing storage or last-run data appears as a dash. The widget uses the active Dosya theme’s light and dark palettes, then resolves the one matching the iPhone appearance. ### Update timing and Live Activity Dosya asks WidgetKit to reload immediately for phase, theme, active-workspace, and completed-run changes. Other progress pushes are limited to one every 15 seconds, while the timeline schedules a fallback refresh after 30 minutes. The storage values come from the active workspace query, but `workspaceName` is set only when a scan starts and remains after the run becomes idle. The name can be blank before any run, or stale and mismatched with storage after an idle workspace switch. The Live Activity starts only when a run has a positive item total, updates at most every 3 seconds unless the phase changes, and ends when the run drains. iOS can disable Live Activities, so absence there does not by itself mean backup stopped; confirm inside the app. ## Expected result The Home Screen widget reflects the latest shared snapshot in the chosen size and theme, while Dosya remains the authority for the active destination workspace. During a supported active run, the Live Activity shows progress separately; after completion, the widget switches to protected and last-run facts. ## Related guides - [Monitor mobile backup](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Fix paused background backup](/troubleshooting/mobile-background-backup)

title: Turn on biometric app lock
summary: Protect the signed-in mobile app with an enrolled device biometric, test the lock after backgrounding, and recover safely if biometrics become unavailable.
verification: Reviewed on 2026-10-14 against local sources apps/mobile/app/security.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/biometric.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/BiometricGate.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/purge.ts, and their focused Jest tests. The biometric prompt and OS fallback were not tried on a physical device or production service.
body: **Unlock with biometrics** protects the signed-in Dosya interface on one phone. It uses biometric hardware already enrolled with the operating system and does not replace the account password, enable two-factor authentication, encrypt cloud files differently or revoke any session. The control is available to every signed-in account regardless of plan or workspace role. Dosya hides the entire **App lock** section when the device reports no biometric hardware or no enrolled identity. ## Before you start - Add Face ID, Touch ID or a supported Android biometric in the phone's security settings. - Sign in to the Dosya account whose open app you want to protect. - Remember the Dosya account password and keep any 2FA recovery method available. App lock is not an account-recovery method. - Finish or pause sensitive file work before testing so a canceled biometric prompt does not interrupt an action you were reviewing. ## Steps 1. In Dosya, open **Settings**. 2. Select **Security**, whose description is **Password, 2FA & biometric unlock**. The destination screen is titled **Password & 2FA**. 3. Under **App lock**, turn on **Unlock with biometrics**. The switch stores the preference immediately; the current implementation does not show an enrollment confirmation prompt at this moment. 4. Send Dosya fully to the background by opening another app. Merely displaying the system biometric sheet creates an inactive state, not a real background event, so Dosya intentionally does not loop another prompt after a successful unlock. 5. Return to Dosya. The operating system shows the prompt with **Unlock dosya.dev**. 6. Complete the enrolled biometric. If authentication is canceled or fails, Dosya displays **Locked** with an **Unlock** button; tap it to try again. 7. Reopen **Settings → Security** and confirm **Unlock with biometrics** remains on after a normal app restart. ## Expected result Returning from a genuine background state invokes local authentication before Dosya renders the signed-in tabs. A successful check opens the app immediately. A canceled or unsuccessful attempt leaves the **Locked** screen visible and offers another **Unlock** action. ## Device and account consequences - The preference is stored in secure device storage under the installation. Explicit sign-out and account-switch cleanup deliberately keep it, so the next signed-in account on that phone is protected too. - If biometric hardware becomes unavailable or all enrolled biometrics are removed, Dosya fails open instead of trapping the user behind an impossible gate. Re-enroll at the OS level, then revisit the switch. - The app does not send a biometric template to Dosya. The Expo local-authentication bridge returns only whether the system check succeeded. - The lock applies after the app returns from the background and on startup. It is separate from the one-hour access token and the renewable 60-day mobile session. - Turning the switch off removes the local preference. That action is immediate and does not require a workspace permission. ## Troubleshooting **The App lock section is missing.** The source displays it only when the OS reports both compatible hardware and an enrolled biometric. Configure one in system security settings and reopen **Password & 2FA**. **No prompt appeared when the switch moved.** This is expected. Background Dosya, open it again, and test the gate on return. **The screen stays on Locked.** Tap **Unlock** and complete the OS dialog. If the enrolled identity no longer works, close Dosya, repair or remove that enrollment in system settings, and reopen the app. With no usable biometric, Dosya opens without the gate so you can revisit the switch. **Changing accounts did not turn the option off.** App lock is intentionally device-level. Disable **Unlock with biometrics** in the new session if that is not appropriate for the new user. ## Related guides - [Sign in to Dosya on mobile](/account/mobile-sign-in) - [Review and revoke sessions](/account/sessions) - [Switch accounts in the mobile app](/account/mobile-switch-account)

title: Browse backed-up files on mobile
summary: Switch to the right workspace, browse or search cloud folders, load more results, and open a backed-up item without confusing its phone original.
verification: Verified from local implementations in apps/mobile/src/files/FileBrowser.tsx, WorkspaceHeader.tsx, api.ts, hooks.ts and apps/mobile/app/search.tsx with their tests. Production content has not been checked because this revision is pending release.
body: Mobile Files lists the active workspace and applies your membership, folder confinement, visibility rules, current folder, and selected filter. A cloud file is independent from any original still stored in the phone's photo library. ## Steps 1. Open the **Files** tab. Use the workspace name at the top to switch if the expected backup belongs elsewhere. 2. At workspace root, browse into **Mobile Backup**, your device name, **Camera Roll**, then the capture year and two-digit month. The backup engine files media by the phone's local capture month. 3. Choose **All**, **Docs**, **Images**, **Videos**, or **Hidden**. Hidden results still depend on your viewer rules; a filter does not reveal items your account cannot see. 4. In **All**, choose **Newest**, **Oldest**, **Name A-Z**, **Name Z-A**, **Largest**, or **Smallest**. Switch between list and grid as needed. The media and document library filters keep their own presentation and do not expose every root-list sorting control. 5. In **Files**, pull down to refresh after an upload completes. Scrolling near the end loads the next API page automatically, so a visible first page is not necessarily the whole folder. 6. Tap a file to launch its supported viewer. The viewer's next/previous sequence contains the files currently loaded from this listing; load further pages before opening if you expect a later item in that sequence. 7. For an unknown location, press **Search** in the workspace header. Enter a name in **Search files and folders**, then choose **All**, **Files**, or **Folders** and sort by **Name (A–Z)**, **Name (Z–A)**, **Newest first**, or **Oldest first**. Search and folder browsing stay in the active workspace. A folder-confined member starts at the permitted anchor and cannot use mobile navigation to escape it. Role permissions also govern available actions such as **New folder**, rename, move, and upload; opening a file does not imply permission to change it. For Live Photos, grid presentation can collapse the still and motion component into one visual item. List view can show the paired file beneath it. That display difference does not create or remove stored objects. When a listing request fails, Files shows **Couldn't load files.** and **Retry**. **This folder is empty.** means the current folder and filter returned no visible children. Search uses **No results** for a non-empty query that finds no matching visible file or folder. Recheck workspace, folder, spelling, filter, and role scope before assuming backup lost the item. ## Expected result Refreshing the correct workspace and folder shows the backed-up cloud object under its capture-month path. Opening it uses the mobile viewer while leaving the phone-library original and the stored cloud bytes unchanged. To verify a recent backup, compare its filename and destination with the Backup tab's status. Deleting an original from the phone does not remove the cloud copy; deleting or changing a cloud file is a separate action governed by workspace permissions. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Switch workspaces](/account/switch-workspaces) - [Change a cloud filename from mobile](/files/mobile-rename-file) - [Relocate a stored file on mobile](/files/mobile-move-file)

title: Change phones without losing cloud copies
summary: Confirm the old phone finished uploading, revoke its session, sign in on the replacement, and restore device-only backup settings without duplicates.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, apps/mobile/app/backup-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/settings.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/ledger.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/orchestrator.ts, apps/mobile/app/sessions.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/purge.ts, and the sessions API. No real handset migration or production workspace was exercised.
body: Files that reached a Dosya workspace belong to the account, not the phone that uploaded them. A replacement handset can browse those cloud copies after sign-in. The old device's upload queue, backup ledger, permissions, selected folders and backup switches are local state and must not be treated as proof that the server has every item. Finish verification before erasing or trading in the old phone. Deleting a local original that never reached **Backed up** can be irreversible if no other copy exists. ## Before you start - Keep both phones powered and connected until the important cloud files have been checked from another signed-in client. - On the old phone, open **Backup** and resolve any storage, network, permission or membership pause shown in the engine status. - Leave **Delete originals after backup** off while checking the move unless you already understand and want its operating-system deletion confirmation. - Know which Dosya account and workspace receive the backups. A second account or similarly named workspace will show a different file set. ## Steps 1. On the old device, open **Backup** and wait until scanning and uploads are idle. Review the latest activity entry for **backed up**, **already backed up**, **failed** and **skipped large** counts. 2. Open several recent and important files from the web app or another trusted Dosya client. Confirm their filenames, previews and intended workspace rather than relying only on a completion percentage. 3. Install Dosya on the replacement phone from its supported platform channel and sign in with the same account. Complete 2FA if requested. 4. In **Files**, select the original workspace and open the same sample items. Cloud content should be available before photo permission is granted on the new phone. 5. Open **Backup** and choose the new device's photo access. The phone may expose a different library, album list or selected-photo scope than the old one. 6. Enter **Settings → Backup**. Recreate **Photos**, **Videos**, **Device folders**, **Start from**, **Skip large files**, **Automatic backup**, **Wi-Fi only**, **Only while charging** and the destination workspaces as needed. These settings do not roam with the account. 7. Run a small manual backup and inspect its activity. Dosya checks file fingerprints against each destination workspace; an existing match is counted as **already backed up** and linked instead of sending the bytes again. 8. When the new phone can browse and back up correctly, open **Settings**, tap the name-and-email account card, then choose **Sessions**. Locate the old mobile session by device label and last activity, then use its sign-out icon. The current row is marked **This device** and cannot be revoked from that row. 9. If you still hold the old phone, use **Settings → Sign out** there as well. Only after the cloud checks and session cleanup should you erase the handset. ## Expected result The replacement phone opens the verified cloud files, uses a newly reviewed permission and backup configuration, and records its own mobile session. The retired phone loses future account access after its session is revoked. Server-side files remain in their workspaces throughout this process. ## What does not transfer automatically - The per-workspace backup ledger and history live on the handset. The new device reconstructs coverage by scanning its library and checking fingerprints with the server. - Cached thumbnails, downloaded file bytes, staged uploads, contact-backup state, active workspace selection and pending queue entries are local. - Biometric-lock preference is device-wide. Configure it separately on the new phone; removing the old app or wiping the old handset removes that device's local preference. - Photo and notification grants belong to each operating-system installation. A grant on one phone gives the other no access. - Revoking a session blocks that credential; it does not delete the account or cloud storage. **Sign out all other devices** removes every other browser and mobile session while keeping the phone performing the action signed in. ## Troubleshooting **Recent photos are absent in the cloud.** Return to the old phone and inspect failed, skipped or pending work. Do not erase it until another client can open the missing items. **The new scan finds thousands of candidates.** Recheck **Start from**, media types and device folders before continuing. A fresh local ledger is expected, while server fingerprint matching prevents verified existing content from uploading again. **A duplicate appears anyway.** The source may have changed, lost readable bytes, or landed in another workspace. Compare file size and destination, then use the duplicate review instead of deleting blindly. **The old phone still opens cached content.** A remote session revocation stops authenticated server requests; erase the old device or uninstall the app to remove bytes already cached locally. ## Related guides - [Monitor mobile backup progress](/files/mobile-backup-progress) - [Review and revoke sessions](/account/sessions) - [Review duplicate files](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Choose the correct account on mobile
summary: Confirm the signed-in email and active workspace on mobile, then switch accounts safely without carrying cached files, backup state, or push routing.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx, apps/mobile/app/profile.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/authStore.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/purge.ts, and workspace-store tests. No live account switch was performed.
body: Dosya mobile has one signed-in account at a time. Confirm the account card and workspace context before uploading, opening a private notification, or configuring backup. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings**. The account card at the top shows the current name and email; select it to open **Profile** for the same identity. 2. Under **Workspace**, choose **My workspaces**. This screen is read-only and lists each workspace, its **Owner**, **Admin**, **Member**, or **Viewer** role, and when the account joined. 3. Return to a tab and inspect the workspace name in the header. Tap it to open **Your workspaces** and choose the intended one. The selected workspace is stored securely for later launches. 4. If the email is wrong, return to **Settings** and choose **Sign out**. There is no in-session account picker that swaps identities without signing out. 5. On **Welcome back**, select **Continue with Google**, **Sign in with Apple**, **Continue with GitHub**, or enter the correct **Email** and **Password**. A **Last used** marker identifies the previously successful method on this device; it does not prove which provider account will be chosen. 6. After authentication and any two-factor step, recheck the account card and workspace list before resuming backup or opening files. A workspace switch and an account switch have different effects. Changing workspaces keeps the session and shows a two-second **Switching workspace…** cover. Signing into a different account clears the previous account’s query cache immediately, then purges its active workspace, upload queue, backup history/settings, contacts state, audio history, Vault session, cached bytes, and iOS Files-provider link. ## Expected result The email in **Settings**, the entries under **My workspaces**, and the workspace shown in the header all belong to the intended identity. New uploads and account-wide notifications now use that session. ## Troubleshooting **The provider chose the wrong identity.** Sign out, reopen the same provider, and use its account chooser. Dosya cannot change the Google, Apple, or GitHub selection inside its own UI. **A workspace is missing.** Confirm the signed-in email first. Then refresh **My workspaces**; **Couldn't load workspaces.** with **Retry** indicates a load failure, while **No workspaces** means the API returned none. **Old content briefly appears after switching accounts.** Stop using the screen and restart the app. The implementation clears in-memory responses before exposing the new session; persistent account data is then removed best-effort. ## Related guides - [Install the verified mobile client](/account/mobile-install) - [Review permissions after changing accounts](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Back up only one mobile contact account
summary: Understand which contacts Dosya backs up on mobile, why there is no account selector, and how to verify the exported count before relying on the VCF.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/contactsSource.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/backupContacts.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya does not offer a Device, Google, iCloud, or other source-account selector. **Back up contacts now** reads every contact that the operating-system Contacts API returns to Dosya with the granted permission. If the phone’s Contacts app combines several accounts, the VCF can contain entries from all of them. Account labels and account identifiers are not included in Dosya’s normalized contact model. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings**, choose **Contacts**, and read the permission explanation before tapping **Allow contacts access**. 2. If access was declined, enable Contacts permission in the phone’s system Settings and return to Dosya. 3. Use the workspace switcher before backup; the screen writes one VCF into the active workspace. 4. Review the phone’s visible contact sources outside Dosya, because this screen has no source-account filter. 5. Tap **Back up contacts now** once and wait for **Backing up _N_ contacts**. 6. Open the active workspace’s Contacts backup folder and verify the new `contacts-YYYY-MM-DD.vcf` file before treating it as a scoped backup. ### Exactly what is exported Dosya requests contacts in pages of 100 until the operating system says there are no more. For each returned person it keeps the display name, first and last name when supplied, nonempty phone numbers, and nonempty email addresses. Missing phone or email labels become `other`; a contact with no usable name becomes **Unnamed**. The file is vCard 3.0. Fields outside that normalized set, including the original account membership, are not produced by this backup path. The success count is the number of contacts read, not proof that they came from only one account. ### If only one account must be backed up Use the phone’s contact-account visibility or export tools to create the desired source set before starting Dosya, then verify the generated VCF. Dosya itself cannot select or remember one address-book account. Avoid disabling or deleting contact accounts merely to alter a backup unless you understand the phone’s sync behavior. ## Expected result One dated VCF is queued to the active workspace and the toast reports how many operating-system contacts were included. The result is an all-visible-contacts backup; it is not restricted to one Google, iCloud, Exchange, or device account. ## Related guides - [Back up contacts](/files/contacts-backup) - [Restore contacts](/files/contacts-restore)

title: Export backed-up contacts as a vCard on mobile
summary: Create the mobile contact backup VCF, identify its exact filename and contents, and verify the queued cloud copy before using it for transfer or restore.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/backupContacts.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/contactsSource.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcard.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/folders.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The Contacts screen exports the phone address book as one vCard 3.0 file and queues that file for upload. There is no separate **Export vCard** button or local destination picker on this screen. The generated name is `contacts-YYYY-MM-DD.vcf` using the phone’s local calendar date. Repeating the action on the same day creates another upload item with the same filename; cloud versioning or collision behavior is handled by the upload service. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings** and select **Contacts** in the active workspace. 2. Tap **Allow contacts access** if the primer is shown; after a denial, grant permission in system Settings and return. 3. Check the workspace name before export, because the backup destination is the active workspace. 4. Tap **Back up contacts now** and note the **Backing up _N_ contacts** message. 5. Watch the upload dock until the VCF finishes instead of treating the enqueue toast as upload completion. 6. In cloud **Files**, open the Contacts backup folder and confirm the dated VCF exists and shows the expected contact cards. ### Data and timing Dosya reads the address book in 100-contact pages. It serializes names, phone numbers, email addresses, and their labels with CRLF line endings and vCard 3.0 escaping. The temporary VCF is written to the app cache, then queued as MIME type `text/vcard`. The **Last backup** timestamp is saved when the upload is queued, before the remote transfer necessarily completes. Use the upload dock and the cloud file as the decisive checks. If permission fails, the screen reports **Contacts permission was denied**; other failures use the source error or **Contacts backup failed**. This backup path produces a workspace file. To place a copy in Files, Drive, Mail, or another app, open the completed VCF in Dosya and use the viewer’s save/share controls, subject to its lock mode. ## Expected result A single dated VCF containing the contacts returned by the phone is queued into the active workspace’s Contacts folder. It is ready to transfer or restore only after its upload completes and the cloud copy opens successfully. ## Related guides - [Back up contacts](/files/contacts-backup) - [Restore contacts](/files/contacts-restore)

title: Restore contacts into the correct phone account
summary: Restore the newest workspace VCF on mobile, understand the missing account picker, and verify additions and failures in the phone’s Contacts app.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/restoreContacts.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/contactsSource.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcard.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **Restore from latest backup** adds contacts through the operating-system Contacts API. Dosya does not present a destination-account picker and does not pass a Google, iCloud, Exchange, or device account identifier when creating each person. The phone decides where newly created contacts go according to its Contacts settings and platform behavior. Set the preferred/default contact account in the operating system before restoring if account placement matters. ## Steps 1. In the phone’s Contacts settings, review the default account used for newly created contacts. 2. Open Dosya **Settings**, select **Contacts**, and grant Contacts permission. 3. Confirm the active workspace; **Restore from latest backup** searches that workspace’s Contacts folder. 4. Tap **Restore from latest backup** once and leave the app active while contacts are added sequentially. 5. Read **Added _N_ contacts** or **Added _N_ contacts, _M_ failed**; one failed card does not stop later cards. 6. Open the phone’s Contacts app, check the target account and several restored names, phones, and email addresses. ### Which backup is chosen Dosya lists up to 500 files in the Contacts folder, filters names ending in `.vcf`, and chooses the one with the newest `created_at` value. It does not show a preview or let you pick an older file from this button. To restore a specific VCF, open that file in Dosya and use **More** → **Restore to phone**. ### What restore creates The simple backup parser restores display name, first and last name, phone numbers, email addresses, and their labels. Each entry is added as a Person contact. The process is additive and has no rollback; removing an unwanted result must be done in the Contacts app. If permission is refused, Dosya reports **Contacts permission was denied**. When no Contacts folder or VCF exists, it reports **No contacts backup found**. A partial run counts failed additions rather than undoing contacts already added. ## Expected result The selected VCF’s parsable contacts are added to the phone, with exact added and failed counts. Their account placement follows the operating system’s contact-creation behavior because Dosya has no restore-account selector. ## Related guides - [Back up contacts](/files/contacts-backup) - [Restore contacts](/files/contacts-restore)

title: Avoid duplicate contacts during restore
summary: Avoid accidental duplicate contact restores by checking the VCF and phone first, because Dosya currently adds every card without preview, merge, or dedupe.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/restoreContacts.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/contactsSource.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcard.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya’s contact restore has no duplicate preview, matching rule, merge option, or skip-existing control. It parses every card in the VCF and calls the operating-system add-contact API for each one. Restoring the same file twice can create a second copy of every contact. A partial restore can also leave some contacts added and others failed, so immediately retrying the whole file may duplicate the successful subset. ## Steps 1. Open the VCF in Dosya and use **View _N_ contacts** to inspect its count, names, phone numbers, and email addresses. 2. Compare several distinctive entries with the phone’s Contacts app before starting. 3. Confirm the active workspace and the intended VCF; the Contacts screen otherwise chooses the newest backup automatically. 4. Tap **Restore from latest backup** or **More** → **Restore to phone** only once. 5. Record the exact **Added _N_ contacts, _M_ failed** result before deciding whether any follow-up is safe. 6. Use the phone’s Contacts duplicate-management tools to review and merge additions; Dosya cannot reverse or merge the batch. ### What happens during a partial failure Contacts are processed sequentially. Each successful add remains on the phone. A failed add increments the failed count, and the loop continues with the next card. There is no transaction or automatic rollback. Before retrying, identify which entries appeared in the Contacts app and which did not. If the cause was a permission denial, enable Contacts access first; repeating the restore without checking the successful subset can multiply entries. ### Limits of the comparison The backup path stores names, phones, emails, and labels. It does not carry a durable Dosya contact ID that could prove two cards represent the same person. Similar names with different phone numbers are therefore not safe to merge automatically. ## Expected result Every parsable card Dosya can add becomes a new phone contact, and the toast reports successes and failures. Existing contacts remain untouched, but duplicates are possible and must be reviewed or merged with the phone’s Contacts tools. ## Related guides - [Back up contacts](/files/contacts-backup) - [Restore contacts](/files/contacts-restore)

title: Review contacts before mobile backup
summary: Review exactly which contact fields Dosya exports, check the phone address book first, and verify the queued vCard before treating it as a backup.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/app/contacts.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/contactsSource.ts, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcard.ts, and apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/ContactsStage.tsx on 2026-10-14; production contact data was not accessed.
body: Dosya has no contact picker or preflight list. **Back up contacts now** scans every contact the operating system returns, so review the phone address book first. ## Included fields Dosya requests name, first name, last name, phones, and emails in pages of 100. A missing display name becomes first plus last name, then **Unnamed**. Empty numbers or addresses are skipped; blank labels become other. The vCard excludes source account, identifiers, addresses, organisations, birthdays, notes, relationships, photos, and custom properties. No account selector or per-contact checkbox exists. ## Steps 1. In the phone Contacts app, inspect representative names, required phone numbers and emails, and duplicates. 2. Correct unwanted or incomplete device records before exporting all readable contacts. 3. Select the target Dosya workspace, open **Settings** > **Contacts**, and grant access. 4. Select **Back up contacts now**. **Backing up N contacts** is the serialized and queued count, not upload proof. 5. After the queue finishes, open **Files** > **Mobile Backup** > device name > **Contacts**. 6. Open the dated vCard. Through 5 MiB, mobile shows up to four names, **and N more**, and a full count. ## Expected result The stored vCard contains every readable contact, limited to supported name, phone, and email fields. Preview count and sample identities match the intended address book. Review itself changes nothing. Removing source contacts can sync through their provider, so use that provider's recovery tools when needed. ## Troubleshooting - **No selection screen appears.** The current workflow exports the whole readable address book. - **The count is too high.** Review linked accounts and duplicates on the phone. - **A field is absent.** Confirm it is a supported name, telephone, or email value. - **No file arrives.** Inspect upload permission, quota, folder, and queue errors. ## Related guides - [Back up contacts](/files/contacts-backup) - [Restore contacts](/files/contacts-restore)

title: Delete and restore a cloud file on mobile
summary: Move a file to Trash in the Dosya mobile app, restore it safely, and understand when permanent deletion removes it from cloud storage.
verification: Verified against current local product source for the mobile file actions, Trash screen, restore mutation, permanent-delete confirmation, and active-workspace behavior on 2026-10-14.
body: Deleting a file in Dosya first moves it to the active workspace's **Trash**. You can restore it from the mobile app while it remains there. The separate permanent-delete action removes the file from cloud storage and cannot be undone. ## Before you start Confirm the active workspace, the exact filename, and that you have permission to delete and restore files. Use a disposable item for a first test. ## Steps: move a file to Trash 1. Open the **Files** tab and verify the workspace shown in the workspace header. 2. Browse to the file and check its name, size, and folder. 3. Open the file's actions menu and choose **Delete**. 4. Confirm the action if prompted. Dosya reports **Moved to Trash** after the request succeeds. 5. Return to the file list and confirm the file is no longer in its original folder. For a Live Photo, the app may ask whether to keep the paired video or delete both parts. Read that choice carefully because the still image and motion video can be separate stored files. ## Restore the file on mobile 1. Open **Settings**, then open **Trash**. 2. Confirm you are still in the workspace where the file was deleted. Trash is scoped to the active workspace. 3. Locate the item by filename, size, and date. 4. Tap the accent-colored **Restore** arrow beside the file. The destructive trash icon beside it is the permanent-delete control. 5. Wait for the **Restored** message, then return to **Files** and refresh the original folder. The restored file normally returns to its original location. If the original parent folder no longer exists, the server may restore content to the workspace root instead. Search for the exact filename if it does not reappear where expected. ## Permanently delete a file On the mobile **Trash** screen, tap the red trash icon beside one file to open **Delete permanently?**. The dialog states that the file will be removed from storage and the action cannot be undone. The **Empty** action at the top removes every item currently listed in that workspace's Trash after a separate confirmation. Permanent deletion can free workspace storage. Restoring does not consume a second copy of the file and does not add its bytes to the storage counter again; it changes the stored item's state back to active. ## Expected result The restored file reappears as an active item in the original folder or, when that folder no longer exists, in the workspace root. ## Troubleshooting **The file is not in Trash.** Check the active workspace and confirm that the delete request succeeded. If someone already deleted the item permanently, it cannot be restored from Dosya. **Restore is refused.** Your workspace role may not allow file deletion and restoration, or a workspace backup lock may currently block changes. Ask a workspace owner to confirm your permissions and retry after the lock is released. **The file restored but is hard to find.** Search the workspace by exact filename and check the workspace root as well as the original folder. ## Limits and important details Trash is workspace-specific. Permanent deletion cannot be reversed, and items in Trash continue to use workspace storage until they are permanently deleted. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Manage mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Download a Dosya file on mobile
summary: Download a cloud file from Dosya mobile, monitor or cancel large transfers, and understand permissions, cache limits, retries, and save locations.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerActions.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/byteStore.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/saveToDevice.ts, apps/api/src/lib/files/download-grant-core.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/roles-enforcement.int.test.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: The mobile **Download** action fetches the current cloud version to Dosya’s local cache, then hands that copy to the phone’s save flow. It does not remove or relocate the cloud file. ## Before you start - Open the intended file from **Files** and confirm its workspace and current version in the viewer. - The viewer decides whether **Download** is available from lock state: **View only** disables it and shows “The owner turned off downloads for this file. You can view it and share a link, but not save a copy.” A **Full lock** file keeps it unavailable until its password produces a current unlock token. - The action does not pre-check the workspace role. After a press, the download-grant API requires file access, membership and confinement, then `download_files`; a role refusal preserves the exact message **You don't have download permission**. - Ensure the phone has room for the file and a destination copy. Dosya’s ordinary-file cache is capped at 1 GiB and evicts least-recently-used items; the exported copy consumes storage separately. ## Steps 1. In the file viewer, tap **Download**. Its label advances through **Preparing**, **Downloading**, **Saving**, and **Saved**. 2. For a file of at least 25 MiB, read the progress line for transferred bytes, average speed, and estimated time remaining. Smaller files still display the circular progress indicator. 3. Tap the active download action to reveal the sheet again. Choose **Cancel** to stop a running native transfer. 4. When Dosya reaches the save phase, complete the platform prompt: - Images and videos request add-to-library access and save to Photos or Gallery. - On Android, other files up to and including 64 MiB open a folder picker and are written to the chosen folder. - On iOS, non-media files open the system share sheet; choose **Save to Files**. - Android non-media files over 64 MiB also use the streaming system share sheet instead of a buffered direct write. 5. Open the result from Photos, Gallery, Files, Downloads, an SD card, or the provider selected in the system sheet. Compare the filename and content with the Dosya item. ## Expected result The phone receives a plaintext copy in the selected external location. Dosya keeps the original cloud object, version history, sharing state, and workspace storage unchanged. The cache may retain an unrestricted current-version copy for faster reopening until eviction, cache clearing, or sign-out. ## Troubleshooting **Download is dimmed.** The file is **View only**, or a **Full lock** has no current unlock token. A missing `download_files` grant does not dim this client-side control; pressing it returns **You don't have download permission**. Ask a workspace owner or role manager to change that role grant. **The progress line says “Stopped at … · tap to resume.”** Tap **Retry**. The UI preserves the received byte count, although actual continuation depends on the native resumable task and server URL; verify the final file rather than assuming a partial copy is complete. **You see an API refusal before bytes move.** The URL request preserves server text such as **You don't have download permission**, **This file is locked. Enter the lock password to access it.**, or **Invalid or expired unlock token. Please re-enter the password.** Correct the named role or lock condition before retrying. **You see “Download failed (403).”** The native file transfer received HTTP 403 after Dosya had already obtained a URL, for example because that presigned URL was invalid or expired. It is not the missing-token or role-denial message. Refresh the file to obtain a new URL, then restart the download. **No destination appears.** On Android, selecting no folder produces “No folder chosen.” For photos or videos, denied library access produces “dosya needs permission to add photos to your gallery.” Grant the relevant permission in system settings or choose another supported route. **The transfer reports Saved but you cannot find it.** A gallery result says **Saved to your gallery**; an Android folder write says **Saved to your phone**; a share-sheet handoff says **Choose where to save it**. The last outcome is not complete until you select a destination in the system sheet. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Review exact duplicates on mobile
summary: Review content-identical files on mobile, keep the newest copy, understand the 100-group display cap, and move selected duplicates safely to trash.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/duplicates.tsx, apps/mobile/src/duplicates/api.ts, apps/mobile/src/duplicates/select.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/duplicates.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **Duplicates** screen groups files by content hash, so matching names alone do not create a group. It operates only in the active workspace and can show a partial list while file hashing is still in progress. Groups are sorted newest-first within each set. The first file receives the **newest** badge, and each row shows its folder path or **Workspace root**. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings** → **Duplicates** after confirming the workspace in the header. 2. If **Still scanning _N_ files - this list will fill in.** appears, wait for the 15-second polling cycle and let hashing continue. 3. Open each visible group and compare its filename, copy count, reclaimable bytes, folder paths, and **newest** marker. 4. Select individual copies, or use **All but newest** to select every visible group’s older copies. 5. Check the selected count and bytes; if every copy in any group is selected, read the warning that no copy will be left. 6. Choose **Trash**, then confirm **Move to trash** and verify the toast and refreshed file list. ### Display and deletion limits The server returns the 100 largest groups while also reporting the true group total. When more exist, the screen says **Showing the 100 largest groups of _N_. Clean these up and the rest move up.** Deletion is sent in chunks of 500 file IDs. Selected files go to Trash rather than being erased immediately. **Moved _N_ to trash** appears only after every chunk completes; the current request path cannot produce a partial-success count. If a later chunk fails, Dosya shows the request error, or **Could not move those to trash** when no specific message is available, and refreshes the duplicate query because earlier chunks may already have moved files. Do not repeat the full prior selection without checking what remains. **Couldn’t check for duplicates.** offers **Retry** and is distinct from **No duplicates / Nothing in this workspace is stored twice.** The API also returns `scan_enabled: false` when duplicate scanning is disabled, but the released mobile mapper drops that field. Mobile therefore shows the same **No duplicates** state for a clean enabled scan and a workspace that was never scanned. Confirm the workspace duplicate-scan setting outside this screen before treating the empty state as proof that no duplicates exist. ## Expected result Only the confirmed file IDs move to Trash, selected bytes become reclaimable, and the duplicate list refreshes. At least one copy remains when you use **All but newest**; a manual all-copy selection is allowed only after an explicit warning. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Enable mobile notifications deliberately
summary: Enable mobile push for the intended account and physical device, align Dosya and OS settings, and test delivery without changing unrelated channels.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 using apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/push.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/remote.ts, apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx, and push tests. No OS prompt or production push was triggered.
body: Mobile notifications require two independent choices: the Dosya **Push notifications** channel for the account and notification permission from iOS or Android for this installed app. ## Steps 1. In **Settings**, verify the account email, then choose **Notifications** under **Preferences**. 2. Wait for **Notification settings** to load. Under **Delivery**, note the current warning: **With In-app off, no notifications are delivered at all - email and push included.** The server actually evaluates Email and Push independently; this switch hides inbox rows and disables only the in-app leg. 3. Turn on **Push notifications**. Dosya saves the account channel first, then requests OS permission and registers this physical device’s Expo token to the current account. 4. On the system prompt, allow notifications. Configure banner, sound, lock-screen, or focus behavior in the OS settings; Dosya cannot override those choices. 5. Leave only the event groups you want under **What you hear about**. Use a harmless event from another test member when available, then watch the bell and the device alert. The setting is not plan- or workspace-role-gated. It is account-wide, while a notification’s linked file or team page still enforces workspace membership. Simulators cannot receive push and return **Push needs a physical device.** A build without its EAS project identity returns **Push isn't configured for this build (no EAS project id).** When Dosya is foregrounded, server push asks the OS to show a banner and notification-list entry with sound, without setting an app badge. Android uses the **Notifications** channel at high importance. System focus modes, per-app sound settings, battery controls, or a denied OS permission can still suppress presentation. ## Expected result The Push switch remains enabled after reloading settings, the physical device is registered to the current account, and an eligible event can appear as both an inbox row and an OS notification. ## Troubleshooting **The app says “Enable notifications for dosya.dev in Settings.”** The account preference may already have saved, but OS permission was denied. Open device Settings, allow Dosya notifications, return to the app, and toggle **Push notifications** off and on to register again. **No prompt appears.** The prompt is per installation. If the OS no longer permits asking, change permission in device Settings. Automatic sign-in registration uses a prompt-once rule and will not repeatedly interrupt you. **Another account receives this phone’s push.** Signing in re-points an existing token to the current account; explicit sign-out unregisters best-effort before clearing tokens. Sign out, reconnect, and verify the account card if routing seems stale. ## Related guides - [Choose the supported app distribution](/account/mobile-install) - [Control the phone notification permission](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Confirm the active workspace on mobile
summary: Confirm the active mobile workspace, role, folder scope, storage, and backup destination before opening, sharing, moving, or uploading files.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceHeader.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceGate.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/workspaceStore.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The workspace switcher is the name-and-role control at the top of **Files**, **Backup**, and **Settings**. It determines which workspace most mobile listings and actions use. The active selection is stored on the device and restored after a relaunch. If the saved workspace no longer exists, Dosya selects the first available workspace after the store finishes loading. ## Steps 1. Read the workspace name in the top header before opening a file or destructive action. 2. Read the second line for your role; a folder-confined member also sees the allowed folder name there. 3. Tap the workspace name to open **Your workspaces**. 4. Compare each workspace’s name, free storage, backup shield, and **Backing up…** marker where present. 5. Select the intended workspace and wait for the two-second switch screen while its queries refresh. 6. Return to **Files** and verify the expected root folders or empty state before uploading, moving, sharing, or deleting. ### What the indicators mean A checkmark marks the workspace currently shown. A shield marks a workspace configured as a backup destination; it does not mean every current file operation targets that workspace. **Backing up…** marks the workspace used by the live backup run. The role line can say Owner, Admin, or another configured role. When access is confined to one root folder, Dosya appends that folder name. Missing files outside that scope are expected and cannot be reached by changing folders inside the app. ### Actions that can carry their own context A file opened from search or a deep link can belong to a different workspace than the one currently visible. The download manager records the file’s own workspace ID when available so an in-progress transfer keeps the correct label after a switch. For new browsing, search, uploads, Contacts backup, map pins, and duplicate review, treat the header workspace as authoritative. Creating a workspace from this picker switches to it immediately. The quick-create path does not offer a storage-region picker; the server chooses the nearest region. ## Expected result The header shows the intended workspace and role, its file list matches that context after the switch screen clears, and subsequent workspace-scoped actions use that selection unless a file-specific route already carries its own workspace ID. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download a file on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Review mobile file details and actions
summary: Open the mobile file record, distinguish visible preview metadata from expanded details, and understand which rows appear only when data exists.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerDetails.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerMoreSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The mobile viewer separates a short metadata line from the expanded **Details** record. Unknown fields are omitted rather than displayed as **Unknown**, so two files can show different rows. The viewer’s summary starts with size and a readable type such as **JPEG image**, **PDF**, **Markdown**, or **Word document**, then adds type-specific facts when measured and the added date. ## Steps 1. Open the file from **Files** and confirm its filename at the bottom of the viewer. 2. Read the badge beside the name: **Locked** requires a password; **View only** permits viewing but disables saving. 3. Read the summary for size, kind, and added date; images may add dimensions, media duration, documents pages or lines, contacts a count, and books reading progress. 4. Drag the bottom sheet upward, or choose **More** → **File details** while the sheet is collapsed. 5. Inspect the rows that exist: **Kind**, **Size**, **Added**, and optional **Modified**, **Added by**, **Stored in**, **Version**, **Links**, and **Extension**. 6. Recheck the filename and preview before choosing Save, Link, Versions, More, or a destructive action. ### Detail rules **Modified** appears only when it differs from **Added**. **Stored in** names the storage region’s city, not a folder path. **Version** appears only above version 1, and **Links** appears only when at least one active share link exists. If the viewer was opened from a folder list, expanding Details can also show **In this folder** thumbnails. Selecting one changes the current file without adding another route to Back history. A deep link or search result may not have that neighbor context. ### Actions in More The menu can include **Rename**, **Move to folder**, **Make a copy**, **Share via…**, **Restore to phone** for VCF, **File details**, **Edit document** for Office formats, **Comments**, and **Move to trash**. Availability depends on the file type, lock mode, expanded state, and permissions. Moving a Live Photo still to trash asks whether its paired video should also be deleted. ## Expected result The expanded record identifies the selected file with every metadata value the API supplied, while absent values stay hidden. Any action you take is tied to the filename shown in the viewer and More sheet. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Open a Dosya file in another mobile app
summary: Hand a downloadable Dosya file to another mobile app through Share via, understand the local-cache step, and handle lock, network, and app support limits.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/download.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/byteStore.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/lock.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerMoreSheet.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya uses the operating-system share sheet for opening a cloud file in another app. The exact menu label in the viewer is **More** → **Share via…**; there is no separate **Open in** button. The file bytes are downloaded into Dosya’s cache first. If an unrestricted current-version copy is already cached, Dosya reuses it instead of downloading again. ## Steps 1. Open the file and confirm its filename, type, size, preview, and workspace context. 2. If the file is fully locked, enter its password before trying to hand off the bytes. 3. Tap **More**, then choose **Share via…**; this action is absent when downloads are not allowed. 4. Keep Dosya available while it retrieves the file; a large item can take time even before the system chooser appears. 5. Select a trusted app that supports the file type in the iOS or Android share sheet. 6. In the receiving app, verify the filename and content before editing, sending, or deleting any source copy. ### Access behavior A `view_only` file can be previewed in Dosya but cannot use **Share via…** because that would create a downloadable copy. A `full_lock` file hides byte-dependent actions until a successful unlock token exists. If the server refuses the download or the network fails, Dosya shows the returned error or **Couldn’t share this file.** The receiving app gets a local file copy, not ongoing access to the Dosya workspace. Changes made there do not update the cloud file unless that app later exports or uploads a replacement. ### Cache and privacy Unrestricted files may remain in Dosya’s bounded byte cache for reuse. View-only and locked bytes use transient storage and are swept between sessions. You can clear reconstructible cached content from **Settings** → **Storage** without deleting the cloud file. The system chooser controls which destinations appear. If a desired app is absent, confirm that it is installed and supports the file’s extension or MIME type; Dosya cannot force an incompatible target to register. ## Expected result The chosen compatible app receives the complete intended file through the system share flow. The original remains in Dosya, the handoff copy is independent, and restricted files do not expose **Share via…**. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download a file on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Remove an unwanted mobile download safely
summary: Clear mobile cached file bytes safely, understand that the control affects the whole cache, and distinguish app cache removal from Gallery or Files copies.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/cacheControl.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/fileCache.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/cachePolicy.ts, apps/mobile/src/upload/store.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The mobile app does not expose a per-file **Remove local copy** action. Its supported control is **Settings** → **Storage** → **Storage used by cache** → **Clear**, which clears reconstructible app caches together. This action does not remove copies you explicitly saved to Android Downloads, an SD card, iOS Files, Photos, or Gallery. Those live outside Dosya’s private cache and must be deleted in the corresponding system app. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings** and find **Storage used by cache** under **Storage**. 2. Read the measured cache size; it includes thumbnails, opened files, temporary copies, Live Photo extraction data, and decrypted Vault cache. 3. Finish or resolve every `queued`, `uploading`, staged, or retryable `error` upload row before clearing. Dosya refuses active transfers, but an error row alone does not block the action. 4. Tap **Clear** and wait for **Cache cleared** instead of leaving while the button says **Clearing…**. 5. Confirm that the measured value falls; clearing is best-effort, so a component that the operating system will not remove can leave some bytes. 6. Reopen an unrestricted cloud file and confirm it downloads again while the server copy remains unchanged. ### What is protected during clearing An unfinished upload row can point to the only staged copy of a file shared in from another app. If any item is currently `queued` or `uploading`, clearing stops with **An upload is in progress. Wait for it to finish, then clear the cache.** The general file-cache sweep receives the URIs of non-done rows, but the earlier Live Photo, transient-byte, and Vault sweeps do not use that keep set. A staged or retryable error source in one of those areas can be deleted even though its row remains. Finish the upload, remove the failed row after preserving its original elsewhere, or otherwise make sure no retryable staged/error row depends on Dosya’s cache before tapping **Clear**. Each sweep is best-effort, and one failure does not stop the later steps. ### What is irreversible Cached downloads can be fetched from the server again. The cloud file, comments, versions, share links, and workspace membership are not changed. Deleting an external Files/Downloads/Gallery copy is separate and may be irreversible outside that app’s trash policy. ## Expected result Dosya’s reusable and temporary cached bytes are removed wherever possible, and cloud files remain available.
