Because the preflight left no retryable staged or error row dependent on cache storage, no pending source is lost. Explicit device exports stay in their system destinations until removed there. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download a file on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Save a mobile file to a chosen device folder
summary: Save a Dosya file to the correct mobile destination by file type and platform, including Android’s 64 MiB direct-write cutoff and cancellation states.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/saveToDevice.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/downloadModel.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/downloadControl.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The viewer’s **Save** action first downloads the complete file into Dosya’s cache, then chooses a device destination according to the file type, platform, and size. Photos and videos go to the media library on both platforms. Other files use Android’s folder picker when they are at most 64 MiB; larger Android files and non-media files on iOS use the system share sheet. ## Steps 1. Open the file and confirm its name, size, type, and lock badge. 2. Tap **Save** in the viewer action row; a view-only file keeps this control disabled. 3. Watch the ring for preparing, downloading, and saving; tap an active ring to reopen progress rather than starting a duplicate transfer. 4. For an image or video, grant photo-library access and look in Photos or Gallery. 5. For another file, choose the Android folder when offered, or choose **Save to Files** or another destination in the iOS/system sheet. 6. Verify completed saves outside Dosya. For a **Choose where to save it** handoff, finish the system sheet before checking the destination. ### Android’s 64 MiB branch Android’s Storage Access Framework write requires Dosya to hold a base64 representation in JavaScript memory. To avoid an out-of-memory crash, files above 64 × 1024 × 1024 bytes bypass direct folder writing and open the streaming system share sheet with **Too large to save directly - choose where to put it**. For a direct Android save, cancelling the directory picker returns **No folder chosen.** and clears the transfer row. On media saves, denying permission returns **dosya needs permission to add photos to your gallery.** ### Transfer controls Cancelling while bytes are downloading stops the registered task. Pressing an error state restarts the transfer. A completed status remains visible briefly, then returns to the normal **Save** action. An already cached unrestricted file can skip a second network fetch. The exported copy is independent of the workspace item. Renaming, editing, or deleting it on the device does not update Dosya, and moving the cloud file to Trash does not remove the device export. ## Expected result The selected media reaches Gallery, or an Android file at most 64 MiB reaches the chosen folder. For iOS non-media and Android files above 64 MiB, Dosya confirms only that it handed the file to the system sheet; verify completion in the external destination. The cloud original remains unchanged and available subject to its workspace permissions. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download a file on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Share a mobile file with the correct access
summary: Create a mobile share with the correct expiry, recipient, password, view-only, metadata, and download-limit settings, then verify the live link.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/share/CreateShareSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/share/expiry.ts, apps/mobile/src/share/payload.ts, apps/mobile/src/share/api.ts, apps/mobile/src/lib/validationPolicy.generated.ts, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id]/share.tsx, apps/mobile/app/shares/index.tsx, apps/mobile/app/shares/[id].tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Mobile sharing has two delivery modes: **Get a link** creates a URL you copy or hand to another app, while **Send by email** can restrict access to named recipients who verify with a one-time code. The default expiry comes from the workspace when configured; otherwise the sheet starts at 7 days. Presets are **1 hour**, **24 hours**, **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, **Pick a date**, and **Never**. ## Steps 1. Open the file, choose **Link**, and select **Get a link** or **Send by email**. 2. Set **Expires**; a custom date must be picked before submission, and expiry cannot exceed 3,650 days. 3. For email delivery, add every recipient and enable **Only these people can open it** when forwarding must not grant access. 4. Configure **Password protect**, **View only - no downloads**, **Remove photo metadata**, and a whole-number **Download limit** as required. 5. Create or send the share; correct any exact validation message instead of weakening an unintended control. 6. Copy the URL from **Link is live**. Open **Settings** → **Shares**, choose the new link, verify its server settings, then test it signed out. ### What each control guarantees A password must contain at least 8 characters. **View only - no downloads** removes the download button and serves images as reduced previews, but anything visible can still be screenshotted. When view-only is enabled, the download-limit field is hidden because no downloads are allowed. **Remove photo metadata** strips EXIF, XMP, and IPTC information such as location, camera, and capture time from photos served through the share; the stored original remains unchanged. A download limit must be a whole number of at least 1 and makes the link stop after that many downloads. Recipient restriction exists only in the email flow. Without it, anyone who obtains the URL can open it. Folder shares also warn how many hidden or locked items stay out of the link. ### Exact validation messages The sheet can report **Pick a date for the link to expire, or choose one of the presets.**, **Download limit must be a whole number of at least 1.**, **Enter a password, or turn password protection off.**, **Add at least one email address.**, or name an invalid email. Workspace policy can still require a password or clamp expiry. The sentence below **Link is live** is built from the local picker labels; the create response supplies the URL but no authoritative `expires_at`. A custom date can therefore appear only as **Expires**, and a policy-clamped preset can still show the requested label. Treat the link detail under **Shares** as the record of the actual server result. ## Expected result The new link appears under **Shares** with the server-returned expiry and access rules, and a signed-out recipient test behaves accordingly. The original cloud file remains unchanged. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download a file on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Grant photo access for mobile backup
summary: Grant full or selected photo-library access for mobile backup, understand what each scope exposes, and refresh Dosya after an OS setting change.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/onboarding/steps/PhotoAccessStep.tsx, apps/mobile/src/onboarding/permissions.ts, apps/mobile/src/backup/scanner.ts, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, and permission/scanner tests. No device library or production backup was opened.
body: Photo permission controls which local photos and videos Dosya can discover for backup. Granting access alone uploads nothing; a backup run and its destination settings still decide what leaves the device. ## Steps 1. During first-run setup, read **Turn on photo backup** and select **Continue**. That action opens the real iOS or Android permission dialog; Dosya does not request photo access when the explanation screen merely appears. 2. Choose full access when every eligible photo and video should be considered. Choose selected/limited access when only hand-picked media should be visible to Dosya. 3. Complete backup setup, or open the **Backup** tab later. A denial produces **Allow photo access** with the explanation that permission is needed for full-resolution originals. 4. If the Backup page shows **Limited photo access**, select it to open device Settings. Expand or replace the allowed selection there. 5. Return to **Backup**. The screen rechecks both granted and limited state whenever it gains focus, then recalculates the library count for the current photo/video, folder, and date filters. Modern iOS calls partial scope **Limited**; Android 14 exposes **Select photos**. The library module normalizes both to limited access. A scan requests batches of **100 assets**, newest first. It reads IDs and metadata before materializing bytes, and an inaccessible iCloud/limited item is skipped as unreadable so a later run can retry it. Changing access does not delete anything from cloud storage. Removing permission stops future scanning and can make coverage totals unavailable. Already uploaded originals remain in the destination workspace unless you delete them there. ## Expected result The Backup screen no longer shows **Allow photo access**. Full access can count the permitted whole library; limited access stays usable but displays **Only selected photos back up. Tap to allow full access in Settings.** ## Troubleshooting **The system dialog does not return.** iOS and Android may show the prompt only once. Open the device’s app settings for dosya.dev and change Photos/Photos and videos there. **Some allowed media still fails.** An iCloud original may not download, a local URI may be unreadable, or a file can report zero bytes. Android waits **1.5 seconds** and checks a zero-size asset once more; unresolved items remain for a later run. **Nothing is selected after permission succeeds.** Review **Choose what to back up**. An include-mode folder filter with no folders is a valid empty selection and requires at least one folder before a run can find media. ## Related guides - [Install a build that supports photo backup](/account/mobile-install) - [Compare every mobile permission](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Zoom and pan an image on mobile
summary: View a full mobile image accurately, understand that pinch zoom and pan are not implemented, and use Save or Share via for detailed inspection.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/ImageStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerChrome.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/saveToDevice.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The current mobile image stage fits the complete image inside the viewer with `contain`. It does not implement pinch-to-zoom or drag-to-pan, so those gestures cannot reveal more detail inside Dosya. The viewer reports natural pixel dimensions after the native image loader succeeds. It can cache unrestricted images on disk, while view-only and fully locked images use memory-only caching. ## Steps 1. Open the image and confirm its filename, type, size, and lock badge. 2. Wait for the spinner to clear and read the measured dimensions in the metadata line. 3. Tap the stage once to hide the top and bottom viewer chrome and use the maximum available fit-to-screen area. 4. Do not rely on pinch or drag gestures; the released stage has no zoom or pan handler. 5. If downloads are allowed, use **Save** or **More** → **Share via…** and open the local copy in a photo app that supports detailed zoom. 6. Compare the inspected detail with the original filename and dimensions before taking any action on the cloud file. ### If the image does not decode The viewer separates a transfer failure from an unsupported decoder. A failed byte fetch offers **Try again**. A format the phone cannot decode should be saved and opened in a compatible app instead of repeatedly retried; Android, for example, may lack TIFF or older HEIC decoding even though Dosya recognizes the file as an image. **View only** intentionally disables Save and Share via. It can still show a reduced-size preview, and screenshots remain possible. A fully locked image must be unlocked before its bytes are available. ### Swiping is file navigation When opened from a folder list, a horizontal swipe moves to neighboring files; it does not pan the current image. Images on either side may be prefetched, but only the active page resolves its full stage. Use the bottom sheet or filename to confirm which file is current. ## Expected result Dosya shows the whole image uncropped and reports its dimensions when decoding succeeds. Fine-detail zoom requires an external viewer after an allowed Save or Share via handoff; restricted files remain viewable without an export control. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Install a verified Dosya mobile app
summary: Install Dosya from its maintained iOS, Google Play, AppGallery, or direct APK source, verify package identity, and avoid signature conflicts.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 using src/pages/mobile.astro, src/lib/store-links.ts, apps/mobile/app.config.ts, apps/mobile/eas.json, apps/mobile/src/update/sideloadUpdate.ts, and store-link/update tests. No store, APK, or production endpoint was opened.
body: Use the maintained Dosya mobile page to avoid similarly named or repackaged applications. Official identifiers are fixed even when store artwork or version numbers change. ## Steps 1. Open `https://dosya.dev/mobile/` from the device you will install on. 2. For iPhone or iPad, choose the App Store button and verify listing ID **6796702157**, iOS bundle ID `dev.dosya.app`, and the displayed product name **Dosya: Cloud Backup & Storage**. The supported minimum is **iOS 15.1**. 3. For Android from Google Play, verify package `dev.dosya`; Huawei users can follow the maintained AppGallery link for listing `C119259287`. Android support starts at **7.0**. 4. For the direct Android build, choose **Download .apk** on the Dosya page. Compare the displayed SHA-256 with `shasum -a 256 ` on macOS/Linux or `certutil -hashfile SHA256` on Windows. 5. Open the downloaded file, allow Chrome or Files to install from that source when Android asks, return, and choose **Install**. Play Protect may scan the file. 6. Launch Dosya and open **Settings** after sign-in. The footer’s **Version** value comes from the installed binary. Google Play and direct APK builds have different signing certificates. Android refuses to install one over the other and can show **App not installed** or `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`. Switching channels requires uninstalling first, which removes local tokens, cache, queued work, and backup configuration. Cloud files remain in the account. Direct APK builds check the Dosya API for a newer Android `versionCode` with an **8-second** request timeout. A definite result is cached for **six hours**. When newer, Settings shows **Version X is available** and opens the download page; the app does not download or silently install the APK. Store builds never perform this direct-channel check. ## Expected result The installed app identifies as dosya.dev, opens the signed-out welcome/authentication flow, and reports its runtime version in Settings. Installation itself does not sign in, request photo access, or alter cloud storage. ## Troubleshooting **The checksum differs.** Delete the APK and download it again from the maintained page. Do not install a file whose SHA-256 does not match. **A store says the device is unsupported.** Check the minimum OS: iOS 15.1+ or Android 7.0+. There is no supported direct iPhone package in this repository. **Android will not replace the current app.** Keep one distribution channel. Finish uploads, uninstall the differently signed copy, then install from Play or the direct page and configure the device again. ## Related guides - [Follow the complete mobile installation guide](/account/mobile-install) - [Set permissions after verified installation](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Install the Dosya mobile app
summary: Install Dosya on iOS 15.1+ or Android 7.0+ from its official store or supported Android APK, then verify the build before signing in on that device.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 using src/pages/mobile.astro, src/lib/store-links.ts, apps/mobile/app.config.ts, apps/mobile/eas.json, apps/mobile/src/lib/appVersion.ts, and store-link tests. Installation was not repeated on a physical handset and no live store or production-download request was made.
body: Dosya mobile supports **iOS 15.1 or later** and **Android 7.0 or later**. The iPhone app is distributed through the App Store. Android users can install from Google Play, Huawei AppGallery, or the current direct APK linked by Dosya. Use the buttons on `https://dosya.dev/mobile/` instead of searching by name. The maintained destinations identify the iPhone listing as App Store ID `6796702157`, the Android store package as `dev.dosya`, and the direct build as the latest file served by the Dosya API. ## Steps ### iPhone or iPad 1. Open `https://dosya.dev/mobile/` and find the **iPhone** card. 2. Confirm the device runs iOS 15.1 or newer, then tap **Download on the App Store**. 3. Check that the destination uses App Store ID `6796702157` and displays **Dosya: Cloud Backup & Storage**. 4. Install the app through Apple's normal confirmation flow. 5. Open Dosya. The first app screen should offer the signed-out welcome or authentication flow; installation alone does not request access to the photo library. ### Android from a store 1. On the same mobile page, use **Get it on Google Play** for package `dev.dosya`. Huawei phones without Play can use the AppGallery badge for listing `C119259287`. 2. Confirm Android 7.0 or later, then let the chosen store install the app. 3. Keep the Google Play or AppGallery installation in that same channel so its marketplace supplies future Dosya updates. ### Android from the direct APK 1. Select **Download .apk** on the Dosya mobile page. If a SHA-256 value is displayed, compare it before installation with `shasum -a 256 ` on macOS or Linux, or `certutil -hashfile SHA256` on Windows. 2. Open the APK from the browser notification or **Files → Downloads**. 3. When Android asks which app may install unknown applications, allow the source that opened the file, such as Chrome or Files, then go back. 4. Tap **Install** and allow Play Protect to scan the package if offered. 5. Open Dosya and later check **Settings** for the installed **Version** value. The app reads this from the installed binary. ## Expected result The installed application opens as **dosya.dev**, shows its build number under **Settings**, and presents the mobile sign-in experience. No cloud file, account membership or workspace content changes until you authenticate and perform an action. ## Android channel rules - Google Play signs its build with a different key from the direct APK. Android will not install one over the other and can show **App not installed** or `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`. - Switching between the Play and direct channels requires uninstalling the existing copy first. That deletion removes local tokens, cached files, queued work and backup configuration from the phone; files already in the Dosya account remain in cloud storage. - A direct APK installation is not updated by Google Play. The app checks for a newer direct build every few hours and shows an item in **Settings** when one is available. - Removing the direct build's install-source permission after setup does not uninstall Dosya. Android will ask again only when that source needs to install another APK. - iOS has no supported direct package route in this project. Use the App Store listing on Apple devices. ## Troubleshooting **The store says the device is unsupported.** Verify the operating-system version: the published requirements are iOS 15.1+ and Android 7.0+. **Android reports “App not installed.”** If a Play build and direct build are being mixed, finish any cloud uploads, uninstall the current app, and install from the chosen channel. You will need to sign in and configure backup again. **The downloaded APK does not match the checksum.** Delete it and download a fresh copy from the official mobile page. Do not install a file with a different SHA-256 result. **No version appears in Settings.** Reopen the installed release build. The app deliberately reads the runtime package version rather than a guessed configuration value. ## Related guides - [Choose the right Dosya app](/account/choose-app) - [Sign in to Dosya on mobile](/account/mobile-sign-in) - [Manage mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: View a Live Photo on mobile
summary: Play a paired Live Photo on mobile with the exact tap or 400 ms hold gesture, understand muted one-shot playback, and diagnose missing pair context.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/LivePhotoStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/livePhotos.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/FileRow.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya renders a Live Photo only when the file-list row identifies the still’s paired video. The still appears immediately; the motion layer mounts only while it is playing. Grid view hides the paired video beneath the still. List view shows the still with a **Live** pill and places an indented **Live Photo video** row directly below it. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the intended workspace and find a still marked **Live**. 2. Open the still from that list so the viewer receives its paired-video ID. 3. Wait for the still to load, then press and hold the image for 400 milliseconds. 4. Keep holding to watch the muted motion; releasing pauses it immediately. 5. Alternatively, tap the **LIVE** badge for one play-through from the beginning. 6. Return to list view and verify that the still and its **Live Photo video** row form the expected pair. ### Playback behavior Motion is muted, does not loop, and restarts at time zero for each play. The native player listens for the end and returns to the still automatically. The video uses `contain`, so neither the still nor motion is cropped to fill the stage. Opening a file through a deep link, notification, or search result may provide no folder-list pairing context. In that case the detail endpoint does not carry `live_video_id`, so Dosya honestly shows a normal image stage even if the server has a pair elsewhere. ### Missing or incorrect motion If there is no **Live** pill and no paired video row, confirm that both files exist in the workspace and open the still from the folder list. A separately uploaded short video is not enough; the API must have paired the file IDs. Moving the still to Trash from the viewer asks **Delete photo?** and **Also delete its Live Photo video?** Choose **Keep video** or **Delete both** deliberately. The delete choice is separate from playback. ## Expected result The still opens immediately, a 400 ms hold or **LIVE** tap plays its paired motion once without sound, and release or playback end returns to the still. Unpaired or context-free opens remain ordinary image previews. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Move a file on mobile
summary: Move one cloud file to a visible folder in its workspace, handle confinement, lock, and collision errors, and confirm the metadata-only result.
verification: Verified locally with apps/mobile/app/pick-destination.tsx, src/files/FileActionsSheet.tsx, mutations.ts, mutationHooks.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts plus gated tests. The revised guide is awaiting production publication.
body: Move relocates one stored file between folders in its current workspace. It changes cloud metadata rather than downloading or duplicating bytes, and the mobile picker cannot transfer an object to another workspace. ## Steps 1. Open **Files**, select the correct workspace, and locate the object to move. 2. Open its actions and press **Move**. The action is displayed for roles whose loaded permission set includes `upload_files`; the API verifies that permission again when you submit. 3. On **Move to…**, tap folders to descend. The picker shows subfolders only, sorted by name; **No sub-folders** means the directory currently displayed has no visible child folders, but that directory can still be selected. 4. Press **Move here** to use the currently displayed directory. At the top level, this means workspace root. 5. Wait for **Moved**. The picker then closes and file queries refresh. Open the destination and confirm the item is absent from its previous folder. The picker uses the active workspace and offers no cross-workspace destination. A folder-confined member may browse and move only within the assigned anchor. Choosing workspace root while confined produces **You cannot move a file outside the folder you're confined to**; selecting a source outside scope returns **This file is outside the folder you're confined to**. Other exact refusals identify the failed gate: - **You don't have permission to move files** means the role lacks `upload_files`. - **This file is locked and cannot be moved** protects a locked source. - **This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to move it.** applies to a locked ancestor. - **Target folder not found** covers a missing or hidden destination. - **Target folder is locked** prevents writing there. - **File is already in this folder** rejects a no-op. - **A file with this name already exists in the target folder** blocks a collision; mobile does not auto-rename the moved file. A live WordPress backup lock can also refuse a source or destination and includes the UTC time until which that backup is protected. The error toast comes from the server, the picker remains open, and no partial move is committed. On success, the API changes the file's folder reference, invalidates source and destination listings and sync snapshots, and records `file_moved` activity. The same file ID, stored bytes, and version history remain. This is immediately shared cloud state; there is no dedicated undo button. Move the file back manually if the destination was wrong. ## Expected result After refresh, the existing cloud object appears once in the chosen folder and no longer appears in the source listing. No device copy is created, and workspace storage usage should not increase merely because of the move. When an error persists, resolve the named role, confinement, lock, destination, or collision condition before retrying. Switching the workspace header changes what Files displays, but it does not turn Move into a transfer between workspaces. ## Related guides - [Locate stored files from mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Understand mobile access controls](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Navigate to a deeply nested folder on mobile
summary: Reach a deeply nested mobile folder using the workspace header, current-folder title, and Back stack, while accounting for global workspace search.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/index.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/folder/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/FileBrowser.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/FolderRow.tsx, apps/mobile/app/search.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Mobile folder navigation is a stack of screens. Each folder opens a new route whose native header title is that folder’s name. The released Files browser does not display a full breadcrumb trail. Folder rows show the name, item count, lock state, hidden state when applicable, and a chevron. The folder screen’s search button searches the whole active workspace, not only the current folder. ## Steps 1. Confirm the active workspace in the Files header before entering the path. 2. Open the first folder and check that its name becomes the screen title. 3. Continue one folder at a time, comparing each row’s name and item count with the intended path. 4. Use the native Back arrow immediately after a wrong turn; there is no breadcrumb segment picker. 5. At the final level, verify the title, expected files, filter chip, sort order, and list or grid mode. 6. Open the target file and confirm its filename and preview before saving, sharing, moving, or deleting it. ### Search behavior inside a folder The magnifying glass in a folder header opens **Search**, but the API query is scoped only to the active workspace. Results can come from other folders. Search rows do not display a folder path, so use size, added date, preview, and details to distinguish same-named files. ### Loading and access states **Couldn’t load files.** offers **Retry** and is not an empty folder. **This folder is empty.** means the listing succeeded with no visible rows. A lock icon means access restrictions apply, while a folder-confined role may be unable to navigate above or outside its assigned root. Pull to refresh reloads the current folder. Pagination fetches later pages as you approach the end; do not conclude a large folder is complete until loading at the footer has finished. ## Expected result The native header names the current folder at every level, Back returns one level through the navigation stack, and the final file list belongs to the selected workspace and folder route. Search remains workspace-wide. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Switch mobile accounts](/account/mobile-switch-account)

title: Open an item from a mobile notification
summary: Use a supported action on a mobile notification, understand which web destinations have mobile routes, and recover when an action is unavailable.
verification: Verified from local source on 2026-10-14 in apps/mobile/app/notifications.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/actionPath.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/inbox.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/remote.ts, and action-path tests. No production notification action was run.
body: A mobile notification may contain up to two catalog-defined actions. Dosya only displays an action when its handler and destination have a safe mobile implementation. ## Steps 1. Open the bell in the workspace header and locate the notification. The inbox belongs to the signed-in account, even though the header also shows an active workspace. 2. Read the title, body, actor, and relative time before using an action. Actions currently support navigation or dismissal; they do not directly mutate files, extend links, or revoke sessions. 3. Choose the visible action label. A navigation action marks the notification read and opens its mapped mobile destination. A dismiss action removes the row from this account’s inbox. 4. Confirm the destination and workspace membership before changing the linked resource. Mobile supports exact destinations for a single `/files/:id` item, Files, Shares, Teams, Workspaces, Profile, Notifications, and the Vault root. It does not open arbitrary web-only pages, HTTPS destinations, nested Vault spaces, or unmatched routes. Unsupported navigation actions are hidden rather than opening a blank screen. Tapping the notification row itself also marks it read. If its link has no mobile mapping, the row stays on the inbox instead of navigating. A tapped OS push with an unsupported or missing mobile target falls back to **Notifications**, so the message is still readable. ## Expected result A supported action opens the corresponding mobile screen once, and the unread dot clears. A dismissal removes only the notification record from view; it does not undo the event or delete its file, link, request, or membership. ## Troubleshooting **An action button is missing.** The server route may have no mobile equivalent. Open the web app for web-only billing, maintenance, or detailed settings destinations. **The resource cannot be opened.** Notifications can outlive access. The file may be trashed, the share revoked, or workspace membership changed. Recheck the account and resource permissions rather than repeatedly pressing the row. **A push opened only the inbox.** That is the designed fallback for unsupported `link_path` values. Read the notice, then use the relevant web or desktop surface if the mobile route is absent. ## Related guides - [Check access behind mobile notification actions](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Repair a notification action or alert](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Open the mobile notification inbox
summary: Read and manage the account-wide mobile notification inbox, including 30-item pages, unread state, dismissal, routing, and offline recovery.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/notifications.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/api.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/inbox.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/index.ts, and notification query tests. Production inbox data was not read.
body: The mobile inbox combines personal notifications and active account broadcasts, newest first. It is account-wide; changing the active workspace does not filter the rows. ## Steps 1. Tap the bell beside workspace search. Its unread badge shows an exact count through 99 and **99+** above that; the summary refreshes when the app regains focus and is considered fresh for **30 seconds**. 2. On **Notifications**, read rows under **Today** and **Earlier**, grouped using the device’s local midnight. Relative time appears as just now, minutes, hours, or days. 3. Tap a row to mark it read and open a supported destination. The colored dot is the unread indicator. 4. Use a row’s close button to dismiss it. Dismissal hides the notice for this account; it does not change the resource named in the message. 5. If any unread rows remain, choose **Mark all read** in the header. This changes read state but leaves rows in the inbox. 6. Scroll toward the end to load older pages automatically. Mobile asks for **30 items** at a time; the server caps a request at **50** and uses the prior page’s creation time as the cursor. The API merges personal rows and broadcasts before applying the page limit. Expired personal notices, dismissed rows, disabled broadcasts, and content suppressed by **In-app** do not appear. Pages are deduplicated by notification ID and sorted again on the phone. ## Expected result The list shows the current account’s permitted, non-dismissed messages in descending time order. With no returned rows, the mobile screen says **You're all caught up.** ## Troubleshooting **Mark all read comes back unread.** The phone applies the change optimistically. A failed server write restores/refetches state and shows **Could not mark all read**; reconnect and retry once. **A dismissed item returns.** Dismiss is also optimistic. If its request fails, the local overlay is cleared and the server list is fetched again. **The bell has no badge during an error.** Summary failures keep the bell usable and preserve no invented count. Open the inbox after connectivity returns. ## Related guides - [Review notification authorization on this phone](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Diagnose an incomplete mobile inbox](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Sign in on mobile with Google, Apple or GitHub
summary: Sign in on mobile with Google, GitHub, or Apple, complete provider and two-factor checks, and recover safely from cancelled or rejected callbacks.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 using apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx, apps/mobile/src/ui/AuthProviders.tsx, apps/mobile/src/ui/OAuthButton.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/oauth.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/authStore.ts, and mobile auth routes/tests. No identity provider or production session was contacted.
body: Dosya mobile offers **Continue with Google**, **Continue with GitHub**, and **Sign in with Apple** on both login and signup. iOS uses Apple’s native sheet; Android uses a protected browser flow. ## Steps 1. On **Welcome back**, check the optional **Last used** marker, then select the provider connected to the intended Dosya account. 2. For Google, GitHub, or Apple on Android, complete the provider page in the system authentication session. For Apple on iOS, approve the native Apple sheet. 3. Return through the `dosya://auth/callback` link. The app compares the callback nonce with the pending flow and exchanges the one-time code using PKCE. 4. If Dosya asks for two-factor authentication, enter the authenticator/email code or choose the recovery-code path. OAuth does not bypass an account’s 2FA requirement. 5. After the Files screen opens, check the email on the **Settings** account card and review **My workspaces**. Closing the browser or cancelling Apple’s native sheet returns without an error and creates no session. Apple may provide a name only on the first authorization. Provider credentials and the PKCE verifier are not shown in the app UI. A successful sign-in stores a mobile access/refresh token pair in secure storage. Refresh sessions can last up to the server policy’s lifetime; an explicit sign-out revokes this device best-effort. If another account replaces the saved identity, Dosya clears cached responses immediately and purges account-scoped local data. ## Expected result The provider returns to Dosya, any required 2FA completes, and the Settings card shows the intended account. No workspace file changes occur merely from authentication. ## Troubleshooting **The browser cannot open.** The app shows **Could not open the sign-in page.** Check the default browser, connectivity, and content restrictions, then try again. **The callback was interrupted.** Retry after **Sign-in was interrupted. Please try again.** A provider code is single-use and duplicate delivery from Android’s browser and deep link is ignored after one accepted exchange. **The app rejects the link.** **That sign-in link didn't come from this app. Please try signing in again.** means the saved nonce is absent or different. Start a new provider flow from Dosya instead of reopening an old callback URL. **Apple cannot complete.** A missing token produces **Apple sign in failed. Please try again.**; native availability failures say **Apple sign in is unavailable on this device.** ## Related guides - [Use the full mobile sign-in procedure](/account/mobile-sign-in) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Open a same-named mobile search result safely
summary: Distinguish same-named mobile search results using workspace, size, date, preview, and details while accounting for the missing folder-path field.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/search.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/search-view.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/FileRow.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Mobile search is scoped to the active workspace. Its file rows show the filename, size, added date, and lock/share indicators, but they do not show the containing folder path. The sort is applied on the returned search page inside the app. Available choices are **Name (A–Z)**, **Name (Z–A)**, **Newest first**, and **Oldest first**; folders remain before files on the **All** tab. ## Steps 1. Confirm the workspace in the header before opening **Search**. 2. Enter enough of the filename to narrow the result, then choose the **Files** tab. 3. Use **Newest first** or **Oldest first** when the added date is the clearest discriminator. 4. Compare each same-named row’s size, date, lock icon, and active-link icon. 5. Open one candidate, inspect its preview and expand **File details** for kind, timestamps, uploader, region, version, links, and extension when available. 6. Return to Search and repeat until the content matches; only then save, share, rename, move, or trash it. ### Information the mobile result does not provide Search rows and expanded file details do not expose the parent folder path. **Stored in** is the storage-region city, not a directory. If folder placement is the decisive fact, browse from the known folder hierarchy or use another Dosya client that surfaces that context. Opening a search result directly also lacks the folder viewer’s neighbor list, so swiping through nearby folder files is not a reliable comparison method here. ### Errors and stale clues An active share-link icon does not identify content; it only says the file has one or more links. A version number appears only above version 1, and Modified appears only when different from Added. A preview failure offers **Try again**; it should not be treated as evidence that a same-named file is wrong. ## Expected result The file you act on matches the intended content and available metadata within the confirmed workspace. When candidates remain indistinguishable because mobile omits folder paths, stop and verify from the folder hierarchy. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Switch mobile accounts](/account/mobile-switch-account)

title: Read a PDF on mobile
summary: Preview and read PDFs on mobile, resume a saved page, use contents and bookmarks, share a local copy, and recover when the document cannot open.
verification: Verified locally against apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/PdfStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/reader/PdfReader.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/useFilePreview.ts and apps/mobile/src/reader/PdfReader.test.tsx. Production mobile delivery was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: The mobile file viewer first shows a native PDF stage with a **Page _n_ of _total_** badge. Selecting **Read** opens the dedicated reader, which stores page progress and bookmarks on the device for that file ID. ## Before you start - Sign in to the account and workspace that owns the PDF. A fully locked file needs its password before mobile resolves preview bytes. - Mobile caches ordinary PDF files on device after the first network-backed open; a view-only file stays on the authenticated raw route and is not placed in the download cache. - The first open can use mobile data equal to the bytes the native PDF library needs. Use Wi-Fi for a large document and keep enough local space for the cache. ## Steps 1. Open the PDF in the mobile file viewer. Wait for the activity indicator, then verify **Page 1 of _total_** or the page where the preview settles. 2. Pinch to zoom and swipe or scroll to a known later page. A single tap toggles viewer chrome. 3. Select **Read** to open the full reader. After saved state resolves, Dosya returns to the last stored page location unless you already changed page during this open. 4. Turn a page and let the controls hide. Dosya waits 2 seconds after the latest page change before writing that position; tap once to restore the controls, then open the reader menu. 5. Use **Contents** for the PDF outline when the file provides one. Toggle the bookmark control for the current **Page _n_**, then open the separate **Bookmarks** tab to revisit or remove saved pages. The **Contents** tab lists only outline entries. 6. Use the reader's share action only when a local copy may leave Dosya. Search and theme controls are intentionally unavailable for PDFs in this mobile reader. 7. Close the reader normally. The queued position saver flushes the current page during unmount. ## Errors, storage, and recovery If the preview URL or body cannot be resolved, use **Try again** from the file viewer. The full reader reports **Couldn't open this book** and offers **Close** plus **Open file details** when that callback is available. Confirm the file version and retry on a stable connection before downloading another copy. PDF caching improves the next open and does not modify the cloud object. Sharing or saving creates a device copy governed by the phone and recipient app; deleting the Dosya file later does not retract it. Bookmarks and reading position are local reading state, not PDF annotations embedded into the document. ## Expected result The page badge matches the document, Read mode resumes the saved location, and bookmarks return to their stored pages. Previewing and reading leave the cloud PDF unchanged. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Manage mobile photo and notification permissions
summary: Set full, limited or denied photo access and control notification delivery on iPhone or Android without changing files already stored in Dosya.
verification: Reviewed on 2026-10-14 from apps/mobile/src/onboarding/permissions.ts, apps/mobile/src/onboarding/steps/PhotoAccessStep.tsx, apps/mobile/src/onboarding/steps/PermissionDeniedStep.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/scanner.ts, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, and apps/mobile/src/notifications/push.ts. No permission prompt was exercised on physical hardware or against the production push service.
body: The phone's operating system decides whether Dosya can read photos and display notifications. Dosya then applies its own backup filters and notification preferences inside that allowed scope. Neither permission is granted by a workspace role or paid plan. Photo access has three useful states: full access exposes the library, limited access exposes only selected items, and denied access prevents a scan. iOS calls partial access **Limited**; Android 14 presents **Select photos** and reports the same limited state to Dosya. ## Steps ### Set photo access 1. Open Dosya and select **Backup**. 2. If access has not been decided, tap the backup setup action and read **Turn on photo backup**. Tap **Continue** to open the one operating-system prompt used by onboarding. 3. Choose full library access for broad backup coverage, selected or limited access for a smaller OS-controlled scope, or deny the request if you do not want Dosya to read the library. 4. When access is denied, use **Open Settings** on the **Photo access is off** screen. On iPhone follow **Settings → dosya.dev → Photos → Full Access**. On Android follow **Settings → Apps → dosya.dev → Permissions → Photos and videos**. 5. Return to **Backup**. Dosya rechecks the permission whenever that tab receives focus. 6. If the attention list says **Limited photo access** and **Only selected photos back up. Tap to allow full access in Settings.**, tap it to change the OS scope. 7. Review **Backup settings → What to back up**. Photo permission exposes candidates; **Photos**, **Videos**, **Device folders**, **Start from** and **Skip large files** still determine what Dosya queues. ### Set notification access 1. Open **Settings → Notifications** in Dosya. 2. Under **Delivery**, turn on **Push notifications**. On a physical phone, Dosya asks the OS when it may still show the prompt, then registers that device's push token to the active account. 3. If the app reports **Enable notifications for dosya.dev in Settings.**, open the operating-system settings and allow notifications there. Once the OS says the app cannot ask again, toggling the Dosya switch cannot display another system prompt. 4. Set **In-app notifications** for the Dosya bell and notification inbox. Email and push use their own delivery switches and event-group rules, so either channel can continue while **In-app** is off. 5. Under **What you hear about**, enable the named Dosya event groups you expect to receive. Turning off a parent notification group also disables its child switches. ## Expected result The **Backup** tab counts only media visible under the OS scope and then narrows that count through Dosya's filters. With push allowed, **Push notifications** remains enabled and this physical device is registered to the signed-in account. Denying either permission leaves existing cloud files unchanged. ## What changes and what stays - Revoking photo access stops new scans from reading the library; it does not remove copies already uploaded to a workspace. - Limited access can make a photo appear missing even when **Photos** and its device folder are enabled in Backup settings. - The first signed-in session may ask for notification permission once. Later sessions silently reuse an existing decision rather than prompting on every launch. - Push registration is unsupported on a simulator and reports **Push needs a physical device.** A build without an EAS project ID reports **Push isn't configured for this build (no EAS project id).** - Turning **Push notifications** off unregisters that phone's token from server delivery. It does not turn off the notification groups themselves. - Contacts permission is requested separately from the Contacts screen; first-run photo onboarding does not ask for it. ## Troubleshooting **Backup still says photo access is off.** Reopen the Dosya app entry in system Settings and confirm the change was saved. Then leave and return to **Backup** so its focus check runs again. **Only some images are counted.** Check for **Limited photo access** or Android's selected-photo mode before changing Dosya filters. The app cannot enumerate items the OS withheld. **The push switch is on but no alert arrives.** Verify the relevant event group is enabled, the device is still registered, and system notifications are allowed. Push registration requires a physical device and an internet connection; the **In-app** switch affects the bell and inbox rather than push delivery. **The operating system no longer presents a prompt.** Use the manual settings path. Dosya deliberately does not loop a permission request that the platform has marked as unavailable. ## Related guides - [Set up mobile photo backup](/files/mobile-photo-backup) - [Expand limited photo access](/files/mobile-backup-limited-photo-access) - [Choose notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences)

title: Explore geotagged photos on the mobile map
summary: Use the mobile photo map’s workspace-scoped pins and clusters, understand its five-minute data cache, and open the correct file or folder from a location.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/map.tsx, apps/mobile/src/map/api.ts, apps/mobile/src/map/map-page/main.js, apps/mobile/src/map/mapHtml.generated.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The mobile **Map** plots workspace files and folders that have coordinates. It sends only ID, longitude, latitude, and kind into the local map page; markers do not contain filenames or photo thumbnails. The pin query treats cached data as fresh for 5 minutes; this is eligibility for reuse, not a scheduled refresh interval. The map automatically frames the pins once per workspace, then preserves your manual pan and zoom when data refetches. ## Steps 1. Confirm the active workspace, then open **Settings** → **Map**. 2. Wait for the map and pin query; read the **_N_ located** badge when points exist. 3. Pan and zoom to the expected area; tap a cluster to move closer even if the basemap is label-free or absent. 4. When a cluster cannot expand past the clustering ceiling, tap it to open its first returned leaf, which can be a file or a folder. 5. Tap one location marker to open it; Dosya uses the recorded pin kind to choose the file or folder route. 6. For a file, verify its filename, preview, and details; for a folder, verify its title and contents before acting. ### Cluster behavior MapLibre clusters nearby coordinates with a 60-pixel radius. At high zoom, items at exactly the same coordinates cannot separate into different dots. In that case, tapping opens the first cluster leaf and routes by that leaf’s recorded kind, so the destination can be either a file viewer or a folder. Return to the map or use the file list to inspect the others. The screen shows the count of plotted pins, not the server’s GPS/approximate/pending breakdown. **No geotagged photos yet** means the successful query returned no pins. **Couldn’t load your map.** means the workspace or network request failed and offers **Retry**. ### Missing basemap or recent uploads Dosya probes the basemap separately. If tiles are unavailable, it draws a flat light or dark background and still plots coordinates. Newly uploaded or newly scanned locations do not trigger a five-minute timer. Once the cached query becomes stale, a later mount of the Map screen can fetch it again. After a request error, **Retry** calls the pin query again immediately. ## Expected result The map displays the active workspace’s located items, expands ordinary clusters, and routes a marker tap to the matching file or folder. Missing labels, thumbnails, or tiles do not prevent pin navigation. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Review duplicates](/files/review-duplicates)

title: Preview source code or Markdown on mobile
summary: Preview code or Markdown on mobile within the 200 KiB text cap, use wrap, copy, and share tools, and understand the supported Markdown subset.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/useFilePreview.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/TextStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/codeHighlight.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/MarkdownStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/markdown.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya previews text-family files inline only when the declared size is at most 200 × 1024 bytes. Larger files show the too-large state and offer **Save to phone** when downloads are allowed. Source files use a monospaced line-numbered stage with lightweight syntax coloring. Markdown uses a formatted document stage rather than showing raw source. ## Steps 1. Open the file and confirm its extension, size, lock badge, and line count. 2. For code, inspect the language-colored lines and use **Wrap long lines** or horizontal scrolling. 3. Use the code toolbar’s **Copy** or **Share** only after confirming the entire body loaded. 4. For Markdown, compare headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, links, rules, inline code, and fenced code with the source’s intent. 5. Treat unsupported Markdown constructs as plain paragraph text rather than assuming a full CommonMark rendering. 6. If the file exceeds 200 KiB or the preview fails, save it when allowed and open it in a dedicated editor. ### Code classification Dosya recognizes common markup, JavaScript/TypeScript, CSS, Java/Kotlin/Swift/C-family, Go/Rust, JSON, SQL, YAML/TOML/INI, shell, Python/Ruby/Lua, and many plain-text extensions. Highlighting is line-at-a-time and does not retain parser state, so multiline strings or comments can color imperfectly. It is a reading aid, not a compiler. ### Markdown coverage The renderer supports level 1–3 visual headings, paragraphs, bold, italic, inline code, safe external links, fenced code, block quotes, ordered and unordered lists, and horizontal rules. Higher heading levels are displayed using the level-3 style. Tables, images, and nested structures are not parsed as rich blocks and degrade to readable text. Only safe external URLs open in the system browser. A view-only file can be read but not saved; restricted bytes are kept out of the persistent disk cache. ## Expected result A supported file at or below 200 KiB opens as readable highlighted code or formatted Markdown with the app theme. Long or unsupported content remains accessible through scrolling, plain-text fallback, or an allowed external save. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: View CSV data on mobile
summary: Read CSV or TSV data on mobile within the 200 KiB preview cap, understand delimiter detection and the 300-row render limit, and verify full data safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/useFilePreview.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/CsvStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/csvTable.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/TextStage.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: CSV and TSV files use the inline table only when their declared size is at most 200 × 1024 bytes and the body contains at least two rows and two columns. Dosya detects comma, semicolon, or tab from the first line outside quoted text. It supports quoted fields, doubled-quote escapes, delimiters inside quotes, and newlines inside quoted fields. ## Steps 1. Open the CSV or TSV and confirm the filename, size, lock badge, and table header. 2. Read the header summary **_N_ rows × _M_ cols**; the row count excludes the header. 3. Scroll horizontally for later columns and vertically through the rendered data rows. 4. Compare the header and several distinctive values with the source that produced the file. 5. If **+ _N_ more rows - save the file for all of it** appears, treat the inline view as a sample. 6. Save the file when allowed and open it in a spreadsheet app before making decisions that require every row or an unclipped long cell. ### Rendering limits The table renders at most 300 data rows after the header. It still reports the full parsed row count and tells you how many rows were omitted. Column widths are estimated from the header and first 20 rendered rows, clamped between 72 and 208 pixels; each cell displays one line. A file with no detectable delimiter, only one record, or only one column falls back to the line-numbered text stage. An Excel byte-order mark at the start is removed before parsing. Files above 200 KiB are not read into JavaScript. When download is permitted, the primary action becomes **Save to phone**. A view-only oversized CSV cannot be exported and must be obtained from the owner under different access. ## Expected result Eligible structured data appears as a two-direction table with an honest row and column count. Degenerate data falls back to text, and rows beyond 300 or long clipped cells are clearly treated as requiring the original file. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Read an ebook in the Dosya mobile app
summary: Read supported ebooks on mobile, resume saved progress, use contents, search, themes, bookmarks, and recover from download or renderer failures.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/files/format.ts, apps/mobile/app/file/[id]/read.tsx, apps/mobile/src/reader/BookReader.tsx, apps/mobile/src/reader/ReaderMenu.tsx, apps/mobile/src/reader/TocSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/reader/SearchSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/reader/ThemesSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/reader/readerPrefs.ts, apps/mobile/src/reader/reader-page/main.js, apps/mobile/src/reader/bookCache.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya’s mobile reader supports EPUB, MOBI, AZW, AZW3, CBZ, and FB2. CBR is not supported because its RAR container cannot be opened by the bundled reader. The file viewer shows a generated cover and **Read**. After saved progress exists, it shows the rounded percentage and changes the button to **Continue reading**. ## Steps 1. Open a supported ebook and confirm its filename, format, size, and lock badge. 2. Tap **Read** or **Continue reading** and wait while the file downloads and the reader prepares it. 3. With controls hidden, tap the left or right outer quarter of the middle page area to turn pages; tap the center to show controls. 4. Open the reader menu for **Contents**, **Search**, **Themes & Settings**, Share, and Bookmark. 5. Use Contents or a search result to jump, then read far enough for a new location and percentage to save. 6. Close and reopen the book to confirm it resumes at the stored position and shows the expected bookmark or progress. ### Reader capabilities Search is available for book formats and begins after at least two typed characters; PDF and plain-text reader modes do not expose it. Contents includes the book table of contents and saved bookmarks. Themes and font size persist across books. The smaller and larger **A** controls move in 10-point steps from 70% through 200%; the buttons stop at those limits. One whole-book search returns at most 100 matching locations, so refine the query when the wanted passage is not in the capped result list. External links are handed to the system browser only when their URL is considered safe. Share sends the cached local file through the system sheet. ### Download, cache, and errors Unrestricted books use the shared bounded byte cache and can reopen without downloading the same version again. A view-only book is still readable, but its temporary local path is released when the reader closes. A fully locked book without an unlock token returns to the file detail screen. A network download error shows its message and **Retry**. If the WebView renderer dies or the book parser rejects the file, the overlay says **This book didn’t open** and offers **Try again**, **Close book**, and **File details**. ## Expected result The supported book opens at its saved location, page navigation and reader tools respond, bookmarks and progress survive closing, and restricted files follow their lock and temporary-cache rules. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Preview an Office document on mobile
summary: Preview Office files on mobile through the server PDF conversion, understand the 50 MB source cap, and recover from preparation or access failures.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/OfficeStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/officePreview.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/useFilePreview.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/preview-pdf.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya mobile previews supported Office files by asking the server to convert the selected version to PDF. The viewer is read-only: editing remains in the web editor, and a full-lock, view-only, hidden, or otherwise inaccessible file is not converted. Supported Office formats include DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and the older DOC, XLS and PPT families accepted by the conversion service. The source must be 50 MB or smaller. A current-version conversion may be cached; an older selected version is converted for that view without being retained as the current preview. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** in the intended workspace and select the Office document by its full name. 2. If Dosya shows a lock badge, use an allowed download path instead; the PDF conversion route cannot accept full-lock or view-only source bytes, even after the mobile password gate is cleared. 3. Wait while the stage says **Preparing preview…**; mobile checks again every 3 seconds and allows 20 preparation attempts. 4. When the PDF appears, move through its pages and confirm a heading or value from the source document. 5. If the stage says **This file is too large to preview. Download it instead.**, use the download action; the source exceeded 50 MB or the converted PDF exceeded 50 MB. 6. For **This file type cannot be previewed** or **Could not prepare a preview for this file**, confirm access and format, then download the original or retry after the service recovers. A 503 response means conversion is still in flight, not that the document is broken. After 20 checks—about one minute plus request time—the mobile client stops polling and says the preview is taking too long. Unsupported formats return their own download guidance; missing, hidden, locked, and other failures use the generic preparation message. ## Expected result The supported document opens as a readable PDF for the selected version. If conversion cannot produce that PDF, the viewer ends in a specific size, type, timeout, or preparation state and leaves the original available for download. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Open a vCard on mobile
summary: Preview a vCard inline on mobile within the 200 KiB text ceiling, open its contact reader, and understand the reader’s separate 5 MiB parser cap.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/useFilePreview.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/viewerModel.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/ContactsStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcardFile.ts, and apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id]/contacts.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A `.vcf` file enters the inline contact preview only when it is no larger than 200 KiB. The first screen shows up to four cards instead of raw `BEGIN:VCARD` text; **View contact** or **View contacts** opens the searchable contact reader. The preview shows each contact’s display name and the first phone number, email address, organisation, or **No number**. If more than four cards exist, it adds **and _N_ more**. The dedicated contact route also refuses a body above 5 MiB, but that later parser guard does not raise the viewer’s 200 KiB fetch ceiling. ## Steps 1. Open the `.vcf` file in **Files** and check that its displayed size is no more than 200 KiB for an inline contact preview. 2. Inspect the vCard preview's four-card contact peek and remaining-contact count before opening the full list. 3. Tap **View 1 contact** or **View _N_ contacts** to open the contact reader. 4. In the vCard contact reader, use its search field to find a name, phone number, email address, or organisation without importing anything into the device address book. 5. From the vCard contact reader, tap a phone number or email only when you intend to hand it to the device dialler or mail app; merely opening the VCF performs no import. 6. If the file has no lock, choose **Save changes** only when a new cloud version is intended; unchanged hidden fields remain preserved. Full-lock files that still need a password and files above 200 KiB remain in the file viewer, where the large-text fallback offers download instead of parsing. The contact route itself has a separate 5 MiB ceiling for a direct or already-entered route. A view-only file opens read-only. A file with no lock can be edited in Dosya, but saving uploads a new VCF version; it does not silently add cards to the phone’s Contacts database. ## Expected result A VCF within the 200 KiB viewer ceiling shows parsed contact names and usable fields without device import. Larger files stay in the download fallback, and a deliberate edit creates a new Dosya version. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Fix mobile push notifications that do not arrive
summary: Diagnose mobile push using the Dosya channel, OS permission, physical-device registration, current account, and supported notification route.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/push.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/remote.ts, apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx, apps/mobile/app.config.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/push.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/notify.ts, and push tests. No physical device registration or production delivery occurred.
body: Push delivery crosses several independent gates: an eligible event, account preferences, server subscription lookup, a valid Expo token, Expo transport, and the operating system’s presentation rules. ## Steps 1. Confirm the account email in **Settings**, then open **Notifications**. Push registration belongs to that account and this installation. 2. Check **In-app** separately. Turning it off hides rows from the inbox, although the delivery planner can still send an enabled Email or Push leg; the current mobile warning overstates this relationship. 3. Turn **Push notifications** off, wait for the switch request, then turn it on. Enabling saves the channel and explicitly asks the OS for permission before registering the Expo token. 4. If prompted, allow notifications. If no prompt can be shown, open iOS/Android settings for dosya.dev and enable alerts there. 5. Test on a physical phone with a harmless event whose group is enabled. Simulators return **Push needs a physical device.** 6. Open the inbox even if no banner appears. A row proves the notification was created, but mobile push can still fail during subscription lookup, token validation, Expo delivery, or OS presentation. At sign-in, Dosya runs a prompt-once registration. After the device-wide prompt has been attempted, later launches register silently only when permission already exists. A release missing EAS configuration reports **Push isn't configured for this build (no EAS project id).** On Android, the app creates a high-importance channel named **Notifications**; users can still mute that channel in system settings. Foreground pushes request banner, notification-list entry, and sound, but do not set a badge. Cold-start taps are parked until the session is restored. A web-only route opens the inbox instead of a nonexistent mobile screen. ## Expected result The eligible event appears in the account inbox and, when OS policy permits, as a device notification. Selecting it routes to a supported mobile resource or to the inbox fallback. ## Troubleshooting **The Push switch is on but permission is denied.** Settings are saved before device registration. Change OS permission, then toggle Push off/on again so the token is registered. **Push stopped after an account change.** Sign-out unregisters best-effort while credentials still exist, and sign-in reassigns the token. Verify the new account and repeat registration if the device was offline during either step. **The inbox has the event but no device receives it.** The server reads live iOS and Android subscription rows, ignores tokens outside Expo’s accepted shape, and sends the remaining messages through Expo. Retry registration first; support can then distinguish a missing subscription lookup from an Expo transport failure. **Only some topics arrive.** Review **What you hear about**. A muted group blocks optional events; mandatory email has separate behavior and does not prove push should arrive. ## Related guides - [Audit push permission at the OS layer](/account/mobile-permissions) - [Run the wider notification checklist](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Recheck mobile permissions after an OS update
summary: Recheck photo and notification permissions after a mobile update, refresh the affected feature screens, and distinguish OS denial from Dosya settings.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 with apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/backup.tsx, apps/mobile/src/backup/scanner.ts, apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/push.ts, apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx, and permission tests. No device settings or production state changed.
body: An app or operating-system update does not grant new access automatically. Recheck the feature screen and device settings when backup or push changes after an update. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings** in Dosya and note the **Version** shown at the bottom. Direct Android builds may also show **Version X is available**; store builds rely on their store’s updater. 2. Open **Backup**. The screen rereads photo permission every time it gains focus. **Allow photo access** means no usable permission; **Limited photo access** means only selected media can be scanned. 3. If needed, tap the relevant attention row. Limited access opens system settings; a first permission request is started from Dosya’s explanatory flow. 4. Return to Backup and wait for coverage counts to refresh. Removing permission can make the library total unavailable without deleting cloud copies. 5. Open **Settings → Notifications** and review **In-app** and **Push notifications**. Compare them with the OS notification permission and, on Android, the **Notifications** channel. 6. Toggle Push off/on only when registration needs repair. This unregisters/registers the current device best-effort and may show the OS prompt if it can still be asked. Photo permission may be full, limited/selected, or denied. Push permission is device-wide, while Dosya’s delivery channel is stored for the signed-in account. Reinstalling resets app-local permission prompting and configuration, but can also remove tokens, cache, queued uploads, and backup settings from the phone. ## Expected result Backup accurately reports the current photo scope, and push reflects both the account switch and OS authorization. Existing cloud files and previously recorded notifications are not modified by this review. ## Troubleshooting **Returning from Settings shows old photo state.** Leave and reopen the Backup tab so its focus refresh runs. If the OS still says limited, add the missing photos or choose full access there. **Push remains silent.** Test the inbox first. If the row exists, check focus mode, alert/sound configuration, Android channel importance, physical-device status, and registration. If no row exists, review In-app and the event group. **The update came from another Android channel.** Play and direct builds have incompatible signatures. Do not try to install one over the other; switch channels only after completing uploads and accepting the local-data reset from uninstalling. ## Related guides - [Verify the current mobile release](/account/mobile-install) - [Revisit every post-update permission](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Rename a file on mobile
summary: Rename one cloud file within mobile filename rules, understand role and lock refusals, and verify the same object keeps its contents and folder.
verification: Source-verified locally in apps/mobile/src/files/FileActionsSheet.tsx, mutations.ts, mutationHooks.ts, packages/shared/src/validation/policy.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/rename.ts plus route tests. Production has not published revision 6.
body: Rename changes a cloud file's stored name in its current folder. It keeps the same file identity and contents, and it does not rename a separate original in the phone's photo library. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, choose the workspace and open the folder containing the target file. Folder-confined members can act only inside their assigned subtree. 2. Open the file's action sheet and choose **Rename**. The mobile list hides this action when a loaded role explicitly lacks `rename_files`; if permission data is missing or stale, the server still makes the final decision. 3. In **Rename file**, replace the prefilled name and press **Rename**. Keep the extension when the file should continue to be recognized as the same format. 4. Use a name from 1 through 255 characters after surrounding whitespace is trimmed. `/`, `\`, control characters, `.` by itself, and `..` by itself are rejected. Quotes, apostrophes, angle brackets, and spaces are permitted characters. 5. Wait for the **Renamed** toast, then refresh the folder or search for the new name. Open the result to confirm its content. Client validation uses these exact messages: - **Name is required** for an empty or whitespace-only value. - **Name too long (max 255)** beyond the file-name limit. - **Name contains invalid characters** for a path separator, control character, `.` or `..`. The API can refuse the change with **You don't have permission to rename files**, **This file is locked and cannot be renamed**, or **A file with this name already exists in this folder**. A hidden or unavailable object returns **File not found**. For a folder-confined member targeting an object outside the anchor, it says **This file is outside the folder you're confined to**. A file inside a retention-locked WordPress backup returns the backup-lock message with its unlock time. Mobile forwards request errors into a toast and leaves the old name in place. Permissions are cached for 60 seconds in the client UI, so a recently changed role can briefly show or hide the action incorrectly; the API does not rely on that cache. Successful rename updates metadata and the folder's modified state, invalidates path/listing caches, and records a `file_renamed` activity with old and new names. It does not create a second file or upload a new version. Because the operation changes shared cloud metadata, other clients see the new name after their listings refresh. ## Expected result The refreshed folder contains one object under the submitted name, in the same directory, with its prior bytes still readable. The former name no longer resolves in that folder. If a collision blocks the request, choose another name or first rename the existing sibling. If role, confinement, hidden, or lock rules cause the refusal, an authorized workspace administrator must change that condition; repeatedly submitting the same request cannot bypass it. ## Related guides - [Find the cloud object on a phone](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Review app and role permissions](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Return from a mobile preview to the same folder
summary: Return from a mobile preview with native Back, verify the current folder title or Search screen, and recover safely when no folder route is in history.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/ViewerChrome.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/FileBrowser.tsx, apps/mobile/app/search.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The mobile viewer’s top-left **Back** control calls navigation history. It returns to the folder only when that folder opened the file; a file opened from **Search** returns to Search instead. The viewer chrome can fade while media is immersive. Tap the preview once to reveal the controls, then use the chevron labelled **Back**. Swiping between files changes the active preview but does not create a new navigation entry for every file. ## Steps 1. Before opening the file, note the active workspace name and the current folder title, or confirm that **Search** is the visible screen. 2. Open the file from that list and, if needed, swipe to the neighbouring file you want to inspect. 3. Tap the preview once when the top controls are hidden, then press the top-left **Back** chevron. 4. Confirm that a folder-origin preview returns to that folder and a search-origin preview returns to the Search results. 5. After returning from the preview, check the workspace name before making a file change; Back does not deliberately switch workspaces. 6. If the destination is wrong, reopen **Files**, select the intended workspace, and enter the folder again by following its folders from the current Files root. Android’s system Back action follows the same router history. The viewer does not promise a particular scroll offset after the underlying list has refetched, and a deep link may have no folder page behind it.
