The mobile FileBrowser receives breadcrumb data internally for other features but does not display a breadcrumb trail, so use the visible folder title plus the native Back stack to orient yourself. ## Expected result Back closes the viewer and reveals the route that launched it. The visible folder title or Search heading confirms the destination; a deep link follows its actual native history rather than inventing a folder route. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Switch mobile accounts](/account/mobile-switch-account)

title: Save a Dosya file to the device
summary: Save a Dosya cloud file into Photos, Files, Downloads, an Android folder, or another provider while preserving the original cloud file and version.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/mobile/src/files/saveToDevice.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/download.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/cachePolicy.ts, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/(files)/file/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/lock.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/download-grant-core.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Saving creates a plaintext device copy of a Dosya cloud file. The mobile app chooses the destination flow from the file type, operating system, and size; there is no single cross-platform Downloads folder. ## Before you start - Confirm the file and workspace in the mobile viewer. The viewer enables saving from lock state, not from a cached role decision: **View only** disables it, while a full-lock file requires a current unlock token. - After a press, the server still requires file access, membership and confinement, then the role's `download_files` grant. A role refusal appears as **You don't have download permission** even though the control was available. - Check free storage for both the app’s temporary or retained cache and the exported copy. - Treat the destination as outside Dosya’s protection. Other apps, device backups, gallery sync, or a selected cloud provider may gain access according to that destination’s settings. ## Steps 1. Open the file, then tap **Download** in the action row. For file types whose main viewer action is saving, the filled action starts the same workflow. 2. Wait until the action changes from **Preparing** and **Downloading** to **Saving**. 3. Finish the operating-system step shown during **Saving**: - For an image or video, approve photo-library access. Dosya writes the item to the phone’s Photos or Gallery library. - For another file on Android at 64 MiB or less, select a folder in the system picker. Dosya creates a file with the original name and MIME type there. - For a non-media file on iOS, choose **Save to Files** or another target in the share sheet. - For an Android non-media file larger than 64 MiB, select a streaming destination in the share sheet. Direct Android folder writes use base64 in memory and are intentionally avoided above that threshold. 4. Read **Saved to your gallery**, **Saved to your phone**, or the destination prompt, then open the external copy from the chosen app or folder. 5. If the content is sensitive, remove the device copy from that destination when it is no longer needed; deleting the cloud item later does not recall exported copies. ## Expected result **Saved to your gallery** means a photo or video entered the media library. **Saved to your phone** confirms an Android folder write. **Choose where to save it** and **Too large to save directly - choose where to put it** mean the system sheet still needs your destination choice. The Dosya cloud original is unchanged in every case. ## Troubleshooting **The save control is unavailable.** The file is **View only**, or a **Full lock** has not been unlocked in the current viewer. Role permission does not control whether this button is drawn. If a press instead returns **You don't have download permission**, ask a workspace owner or role manager to grant `download_files`; device permissions cannot change that server decision. **The gallery permission prompt was denied.** Dosya reports “dosya needs permission to add photos to your gallery.” Allow add-to-library access in the phone’s settings, reopen the file, and retry. **Android says “No folder chosen.”** The directory picker was dismissed or access was not granted. Start the save again and select a writable folder such as Downloads, an SD card, or a supported provider. **You see “Sharing is not available on this device.”** The iOS non-media flow or large Android-file fallback cannot open a system share target. Update the OS/client or save from another supported device. **The exported file does not update later.** It is an independent snapshot. Saving a newer Dosya version creates another device copy; the existing external file is not synchronized. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Search from the correct mobile scope
summary: Search the active mobile workspace, separate files from folders, apply one of four client-side sort orders, and avoid assuming a folder-only scope.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/search.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/search-view.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/api.ts, apps/api/src/lib/listing/file-search-core.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Mobile **Search** queries the active workspace. It is not limited to the folder that was open before Search, so choosing the correct workspace is the scope-setting step. The screen offers **All**, **Files**, and **Folders**. Its sort sheet contains **Name (A–Z)**, **Name (Z–A)**, **Newest first**, and **Oldest first**; sorting is applied on the returned page, with folders kept above files. The API matches names by substring and enforces membership, file access, hidden-item, locked-ancestor, and confined-folder rules. ## Steps 1. Return to a main mobile tab and verify the workspace name in the header before opening **Search**. 2. Enter a distinctive part of the file or folder name in **Search files and folders**. 3. Choose **Files** or **Folders** when the mixed **All** list is ambiguous. 4. Open **Sort results** and apply one of the four displayed orders to the current result page. 5. Read the result name and its row metadata before opening it; mobile results do not display a full folder breadcrumb. 6. If the item is absent, switch to the workspace that owns it and search again; changing tabs or sort order cannot widen the workspace scope. A folder-confined member sees only the permitted subtree even though Search is workspace-wide. Hidden descendants and items behind a locked ancestor are withheld unless the current viewer is allowed to see them. Search does not provide a separate folder-scope chip on mobile. ## Expected result The result comes from the workspace named in the mobile header and respects the member’s accessible subtree. Tabs and sort order clarify the returned page without implying that the query searched another workspace or only the previously open folder. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Switch mobile accounts](/account/mobile-switch-account)

title: Share a Dosya file from your phone
summary: Create a protected Dosya link on iPhone or Android, confirm its live settings, then hand the URL to another app with the system share sheet.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/share/CreateShareSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/share/expiry.ts, apps/mobile/src/share/api.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts. Production status: no live link was created or sent.
body: The Dosya app for iPhone and Android creates the access-controlled URL first. Its final **Share** button then gives that URL to the phone's system share sheet. Messages, Mail, or another chosen app receives a link, not a second copy of the file. ## Requirements and choices Your workspace role needs **Create share links**, and the file must be inside the part of the workspace that role can access. An administrator can disable share links, require an eight-character-or-longer password, or impose a maximum lifetime. Free-plan creators may have five active links; their requested lifetime is reduced to seven days when it is longer. The mobile **Get a link** tab offers **1 hour**, **24 hours**, **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, **Pick a date**, and **Never**. A workspace default preselects its own duration; without one, the app starts at seven days. A workspace maximum or the free-plan ceiling can make the saved expiry earlier than the option requested. Optional controls include **Password protect**, **View only - no downloads**, **Remove photo metadata**, and **Download limit**. A limit must be a whole number of at least 1. View-only hides the download control and serves reduced-size image previews, but content visible on screen can still be captured. ## Steps 1. Open the intended file or folder in the Dosya mobile app and tap **Share**. 2. Leave **Get a link** selected. Use **Send by email** only when Dosya itself should mail recipients. 3. Under **Expires**, choose a preset, **Pick a date**, or **Never**. Review the displayed workspace default before changing it. 4. Enable the protection appropriate for this delivery. If **Password protect** is on, enter at least eight characters; if using **Download limit**, enter an integer of 1 or more. 5. Tap **Create link**. Wait for the **Link is live** confirmation, which summarizes expiry, password, view-only, and metadata behavior. 6. Use **Copy** when you want to paste the address yourself, scan the shown QR code for an in-person handoff, or tap **Share** to open the iOS or Android share sheet. 7. Pick the destination app and recipient there. Cancelling the system sheet leaves the Dosya link live even though no message was sent. 8. Tap **Done** after the destination app accepts the URL. ## If creation is refused - **Enter a password, or turn password protection off.** appears when protection is enabled with an empty value; a shorter value returns **Password must be at least 8 characters**. - **Download limit must be a whole number of at least 1.** rejects zero, decimals, and non-numeric text. - **Pick a date for the link to expire, or choose one of the presets.** means the calendar option has no saved date. - **Share links are disabled for this workspace** requires an administrator to change workspace sharing policy. - **The free plan allows 5 active share links at a time. Revoke one, let one expire, or upgrade for unlimited links.** means link creation stopped before the system share sheet opened. ## Expected result Dosya displays **Link is live**, and the destination app receives the same URL shown beside the QR code. The recipient gets only the access allowed by that link's saved expiry, password, download, and metadata settings. ## Related guides - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Add a password](/sharing/password-link) - [Troubleshoot unavailable links](/sharing/unavailable-link)

title: Sign in to Dosya on mobile
summary: Sign in on iPhone or Android with a password, Google, GitHub or Apple, complete any required challenge, and confirm the correct workspace first.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx, apps/mobile/src/ui/AuthProviders.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/authStore.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/tokenStore.ts, apps/mobile/src/api/client.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/auth/mobile/login.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/auth-login.ts. No physical iPhone, Android device, store build, or production account was used for this review.
body: The Dosya mobile app supports email and password, Google, GitHub and Apple sign-in. On iPhone, **Sign in with Apple** opens Apple's native sheet; on Android it uses a browser flow. Google and GitHub use the browser on both platforms. These account choices work on iOS 15.1 or later and Android 7.0 or later. A workspace role does not control whether you can authenticate. Your membership controls which workspaces and files appear after the account session opens. ## Before you start - Install Dosya from the platform source described in the installation guide. - Have the account email and password ready, or access to the Google, GitHub or Apple identity linked to the account. - If two-factor authentication is enabled, keep the authenticator, email inbox or an unused recovery code available. - Connect the phone to the internet. An offline launch can restore a previously saved session, but a new sign-in must reach the API. ## Steps 1. Open Dosya. A returning installation shows **Welcome back** with **Email**, **Password**, **Forgot password?** and **Log In**. 2. For password sign-in, enter the complete email address and password, then tap **Log In**. The app trims the email and normalizes its case before sending it. 3. Alternatively, choose **Continue with Google**, **Continue with GitHub** or **Sign in with Apple**. Finish the provider screen and return to Dosya. The provider used most recently carries a **Last used** badge on this phone. 4. If the account requires another factor, Dosya opens **Two-factor authentication**. Enter the emailed or authenticator code, or tap **Use a recovery code**, then press **Verify**. 5. After the session opens, select **Settings** and inspect the name and email on the account card. 6. Open **Files** and read the workspace name in its header. Change the workspace there if the intended files belong somewhere else. 7. Open one known, non-sensitive folder. Its contents should match the selected account and workspace before you enable backup or upload anything. ## Expected result Dosya opens the signed-in tabs, **Settings** displays the intended identity, and **Files** shows a workspace that belongs to that account. A new mobile session also appears under **Profile → Sessions**. The access token lasts one hour and is refreshed from a session credential that can remain valid for up to 60 days unless it is revoked. ## Security and session behavior - A successful login stores the token pair and last known profile in the operating system's secure store. On iPhone, the token is readable by background work after the device has been unlocked once following a restart. - The app retries an expired access token through the saved refresh session. A network outage or server error does not by itself erase the credential. - An explicit **Sign out** revokes the mobile session on the server when reachable, removes local tokens, clears cached account data and returns the app to its signed-out state. - The password door and OAuth doors all enforce the account's enrolled two-factor method. Completing a provider screen does not bypass 2FA. - Photo access, push permission and backup choices are device settings. Signing in does not silently grant them. ## Troubleshooting **The app says “Email and password are required.”** Fill both fields. A blank password or an email made only of spaces is rejected before authentication. **You see “Invalid email or password.”** Re-enter the credentials or use **Forgot password?**. Avoid repeated guesses: failures from one network trigger 15-minute and one-hour network locks, and 20 consecutive failures can lock the account for 24 hours. **The response is “Please verify your email before signing in.”** Complete the email-verification flow for that address, then return to **Welcome back**. **Dosya shows “Network request failed.”** Check connectivity and retry. That message means the app did not receive an API response; it is different from rejected credentials. **A provider callback is refused.** If the app says **That sign-in link didn't come from this app. Please try signing in again.**, start that provider flow again from Dosya instead of reopening an old link. **The wrong files appear after login.** Confirm the account card first, then inspect the workspace header. Changing workspaces is different from changing accounts. ## Related guides - [Install the Dosya mobile app](/account/mobile-install) - [Complete two-factor sign-in on mobile](/account/mobile-two-factor-signin) - [Review and revoke sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Sign out and clear mobile account data
summary: Sign out of Dosya mobile, understand the four-second server-revocation attempt and local data purge, then verify the next account starts clean.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/authStore.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/api.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/purge.ts, apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx, and sign-out/purge tests. No production session was revoked.
body: **Sign out** starts a bounded sign-out sequence before showing the signed-out screen, then schedules broad local cleanup so another account cannot inherit cached data. ## Steps 1. Finish or deliberately stop active uploads and note any backup configuration you will need later. Signing out clears queued and persisted transfer state from this device. 2. Open **Settings** and confirm the email on the account card. 3. Scroll to **Sign out** and tap it. The current mobile UI has no confirmation dialog. 4. Dosya first gives registered pre-sign-out hooks up to **3 seconds** to unregister push while the access token still works. 5. It then presents the latest stored refresh token to `/api/auth/mobile/logout`, waiting at most **4 seconds** for server revocation. Offline, timeout, or server failure does not keep the phone signed in. 6. Confirm that the app returns to **Welcome back** (or the once-per-device welcome deck on a new installation). Local tokens and cached API responses are cleared before the signed-out shell appears. Best-effort cleanup then stops audio and backup, cancels background uploads, clears upload queues, active workspace, backup ledger/history/settings, contacts state, CarPlay history, Vault session/decrypted cache, file bytes, image caches, account onboarding, and the linked iOS Files location. Device-level theme, biometric preference, reader presentation settings, and **Last used** sign-in hint remain. Server logout revokes this mobile session and its linked Files-provider child session when reachable. It does not delete the Dosya account, workspaces, cloud files, shares, or other devices’ independent sessions. ## Expected result The signed-out authentication screen replaces the account UI, this device no longer has usable local account tokens, and a later different account starts without the previous account’s cached workspace state. ## Troubleshooting **The phone was offline.** Local sign-out still completes. Because the server revocation attempt may have failed, use the web session-management page when online if you need to revoke sessions centrally. **Backup preferences disappeared after signing in again.** That is the documented local purge. Re-select destinations, folders, network policy, and photo permission as needed; cloud backups already uploaded remain stored. **The app appears signed out after a locked-keychain launch.** A background start can temporarily fail to read secure storage. That path records no explicit sign-out and avoids purging account data; unlock/restart before assuming the session was revoked. ## Related guides - [Sign back in after local cleanup](/account/mobile-sign-in) - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Switch accounts in the mobile app
summary: Sign out of the current Dosya account, clear its device-only data, sign in as the second account, and verify workspaces before restarting backup.
verification: Verified from local source on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/authStore.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/purge.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/sessionDrop.ts, apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx, and account-switch tests. No physical-device switch, production token revocation, or live cloud account was used.
body: The mobile app does not keep a visible list of multiple signed-in accounts. Switching means using **Sign out** for the current identity and then authenticating as the other one. This boundary prevents one account from inheriting another account's cached files, active workspace or photo-backup ledger. Wait for important uploads before starting. Explicit sign-out clears pending device work even if the phone cannot reach the logout endpoint, while completed cloud files stay with their original account and workspace. ## Before you start - Open **Backup** and the upload queue under the first account. Let required transfers finish, because queued and staged items are discarded during cleanup. - Verify the first account's important files from another Dosya client if this phone holds the only local originals. - Have the second account's password or provider access and any required two-factor method ready. - Record which workspaces and backup destinations belong to each identity. Similar names do not make them the same storage boundary. ## Steps 1. Select **Settings** and read the name and email on the account card. 2. Confirm **Backup** is idle and no manual file upload is still queued or uploading. 3. Return to **Settings** and tap **Sign out**. 4. Dosya first tries to unregister this phone from push delivery, then asks the server to revoke the current refresh session and its linked iOS Files session. The logout request waits at most four seconds; local sign-out continues when the phone is offline or the request fails. 5. At **Welcome back**, enter the second account under **Email** and **Password**, or choose its Google, GitHub or Apple provider. Complete **Two-factor authentication** when shown. 6. Open **Settings** and verify the second name and email. Do this before entering a folder or starting a backup. 7. Select **Files**, choose the intended workspace in the header, and open one known item that belongs to the second account. 8. Visit **Settings → Backup**. Recreate the second account's destinations and device-specific choices; sign-out resets photo-backup configuration to defaults. 9. Run one small test backup, then confirm its cloud copy under the selected second-account workspace. ## Expected result The account card, workspace list and file views all belong to the second identity. The first account's mobile credential is revoked when the server receives logout, and its local cached data no longer appears on the phone. Files already stored in either account are unchanged. ## Data removed from this phone Sign-out stops playback and backup work, cancels supported background jobs, clears the upload queue, backup ledger and history, backup settings, active workspace, contacts-backup state, notification registration, persisted API responses, cached thumbnails, downloaded file bytes, CarPlay recents, Vault unlock state and the first account's onboarding record. Cleanup is best effort so one failing step cannot keep the account signed in. Device-level preferences remain: **Unlock with biometrics**, the last sign-in-method hint, theme, and file-view presentation settings. Because biometric lock survives, it can protect the next account immediately. ## Important boundaries - There is no role or plan requirement for signing out. Membership and permissions are evaluated again after the second account opens a workspace. - Signing out is different from deleting an account; it does not erase server files, workspaces or billing records. - A failed network revocation can leave the old server credential live until another control revokes or expires it, even though local tokens are gone. Use **Sessions** from another signed-in client if the device was lost or the logout happened offline. - Switching only the active workspace does not change the account email. Use the workspace header for project boundaries and this sign-out flow for identity boundaries. ## Troubleshooting **The first account still appears after tapping Sign out.** Wait for the screen transition and reopen Dosya. If the process was interrupted, use **Settings → Sign out** again, then review **Sessions** elsewhere. **The second account sees empty Files.** Check its account email, then change the active workspace. An account can be valid while lacking membership in the workspace you expected. **Previous backup settings disappeared.** That reset is intentional account isolation. Configure destinations, media types, date, size, Wi-Fi and charging rules again for the new identity. **Biometric lock remained enabled.** The preference belongs to the installation rather than an account. Turn off **Settings → Security → Unlock with biometrics** if that is not appropriate for the new user. ## Related guides - [Sign in to Dosya on mobile](/account/mobile-sign-in) - [Review and revoke sessions](/account/sessions) - [Set up mobile photo backup](/files/mobile-photo-backup)

title: Switch mobile workspaces before browsing
summary: Switch mobile Files context before browsing, identify backup destinations and confined roles, and understand how keyed queries load the chosen workspace.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceSwitchSplash.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceHeader.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/workspaceStore.ts, and apps/mobile/src/files/hooks.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The workspace name at the top of Dosya controls Files, Search, Backup, and Settings context. Switch it before browsing so later file actions and searches target the intended workspace. The sheet is labelled **Your workspaces**. A checkmark marks the active workspace, a shield marks a configured backup destination, and a running destination can say **Backing up…**. Storage-enabled workspaces show free space. A confined member’s header also names the role and root folder. ## Steps 1. Tap the current workspace name in the header to open **Your workspaces**. 2. Compare workspace names, active checkmark, role or root-folder text, backup shield, and available storage. 3. Tap the workspace whose files you intend to browse; tapping the already active row is a no-op. 4. Wait for the **Switching workspace…** splash, which remains for a fixed two seconds while screens select and load queries keyed to the new workspace ID. 5. Confirm the chosen workspace name appears in the header and inspect the root Files listing. 6. Before uploading, deleting, sharing, or searching, recheck that header because those actions use the active workspace. The switch updates `activeId` immediately and persists it in secure storage. Screens then select query keys containing the new workspace ID and fetch that workspace as needed; cached entries for the previous workspace can remain stored but are no longer the active listing. A folder-confined role may land at its named root rather than the workspace’s global root. Switching does not move files, change membership, or alter which workspaces receive mobile backup. ## Expected result After the two-second transition, the header and file listing belong to the selected workspace. Existing files stay where they were, and later browsing or search uses the new active workspace subject to its role and root-folder limits. ## Related guides - [Browse files on mobile](/files/mobile-browse-files) - [Switch mobile accounts](/account/mobile-switch-account)

title: Complete two-factor sign-in on mobile
summary: Finish a Dosya mobile login with an email code, authenticator code or unused recovery code, and recover from expiry or attempt limits safely.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 using apps/mobile/app/(auth)/2fa.tsx, apps/mobile/src/auth/api.ts, apps/mobile/src/auth/authStore.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/auth/mobile/login.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/auth/mobile/2fa.ts, apps/api/src/lib/totp.ts, apps/api/src/lib/totp-consume.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/recovery.ts. No live email, authenticator device, physical phone, or production session was tested.
body: Dosya requests a second factor after a password or identity-provider login when the account has email or authenticator 2FA enabled. The first successful factor creates a **five-minute** challenge; it does not create a signed-in mobile session yet. The mobile screen accepts the method named by the account and also provides **Use a recovery code**. Workspace roles and subscription plans do not alter this account-security check. ## Before you start - Begin from **Welcome back** and complete the password, Google, GitHub or Apple step for the intended account. - For email 2FA, open the inbox attached to the Dosya account and use the most recent message whose subject begins with the six-digit code. - For authenticator 2FA, use the current six-digit value shown for `dosya.dev`. - If neither method is available, locate one unused recovery code saved when authenticator 2FA was enabled or regenerated. ## Steps 1. Wait for the screen titled **Two-factor authentication**. 2. Read its subtitle. Email accounts show **Enter the code we emailed you**; authenticator accounts show **Enter the code from your authenticator app**. 3. Enter the six digits in **Code** and tap **Verify**. Authenticator values advance every 30 seconds; Dosya accepts the matching current interval and one interval on either side to tolerate clock drift. 4. To use account recovery, tap **Use a recovery code**. The input changes to **Recovery code**, and the secondary action becomes **Use authenticator code**. 5. Enter one saved recovery value. Generated codes contain eight characters in `XXXX-XXXX` form, but spaces and the hyphen are ignored during verification. 6. Tap **Verify** once. A valid factor is consumed and the app opens the signed-in tabs. 7. Visit **Settings**, tap the identity card, open **Sessions**, and find the new row marked **This device**. That row proves the second factor completed and a mobile session was minted. ## Expected result The verification screen closes only after the server accepts the factor. Dosya stores a one-hour mobile access token plus a renewable refresh credential with a maximum 60-day lifetime, displays the intended account, and lists the phone in **Sessions**. ## Limits and irreversible effects - During a live challenge, every non-empty submitted value consumes one of five attempts. The error states how many attempts remain. - After the cap, Dosya returns **Too many attempts. Please log in again.** A fresh password or provider sign-in is required. - The challenge expires five minutes after the first factor. There is no resend button on the mobile 2FA screen; restart sign-in to create a new challenge and email code. - An authenticator value accepted for one protected action cannot be replayed during the same time window. - A recovery code is single-use. Two simultaneous requests using the same saved code cannot both succeed. - TOTP enrollment creates ten recovery codes. The current count is visible in **Settings → Security**; regenerating them invalidates the previous set. ## Troubleshooting **The message is “Invalid code. 4 attempts remaining.”** Confirm the requested method, use the newest email, or wait for a fresh authenticator interval. Do not keep guessing because each rejection spends an attempt. **Dosya says “This challenge has expired. Please log in again.”** Return to **Welcome back**, repeat the first factor, and finish the new challenge within five minutes. **You see “This challenge has already been used. Please log in again.”** The token was consumed by an earlier successful request. Start a clean login rather than resubmitting the screen. **An authenticator code is rejected immediately after another login.** The server makes an accepted TOTP interval single-use. Wait for the app to show the next six-digit value. **The email never arrives.** Check spam and the account address. If the first step reports **Could not send verification email. Try again.**, retry the full sign-in later; no redeemable challenge is stored when sending fails. ## Related guides - [Sign in to Dosya on mobile](/account/mobile-sign-in) - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Review and revoke sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Browse a Vault Space on mobile
summary: Find your own and shared Vault Spaces on mobile, open encrypted folders safely, and recover when a Space name, grant, or folder listing cannot load.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/vault/index.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/vault/space/[id]/[folderId].tsx, apps/mobile/src/vault/store.ts, apps/mobile/src/vault/engine.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/my-workspaces.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: A Vault Space is an end-to-end encrypted file tree. Discovery returns the caller's Space IDs plus plaintext `globalWorkspaceId` and `createdByMe` display metadata. Folder names, file names, sizes, manifests, and file contents remain encrypted records that mobile opens on the phone. ## Before you start - Sign in, select the intended Dosya workspace in the header, and unlock **Vault** on this phone. - You can browse a Space only while your account is a current member and has a valid sealed Space-key grant. Vault membership is separate from the role shown for ordinary workspace files. - **My Spaces** uses the discovery response's plaintext `createdByMe` and `globalWorkspaceId` fields to show your Spaces for the selected storage workspace, plus legacy or temporarily unscoped Spaces. **Shared with me** contains discovered entries whose scope creator is another account. - The storage workspace and its plan determine where Space bytes are charged. Browsing existing encrypted entries does not consume more storage. ## Steps 1. Open **Vault** and wait for Space discovery to finish. A newly discovered label may first appear as **Space** or **Shared Space** followed by six characters of its ID while the phone resolves its encrypted name. 2. Under **My Spaces** or **Shared with me**, tap the required Space. The app opens its key grant before navigating to the root folder. 3. At the root, confirm the header shows the Space name. Folders are sorted before files; names within each kind use case-insensitive alphabetical order. 4. Tap the named **folder row** to move into it. Returning to a parent clears the previous folder’s rows before loading the correct listing, so stale entries cannot be opened with the wrong folder ID. 5. Use the row’s more control when you need **Save to device** for a file or **Delete** for an entry. The **+** control offers **Upload photos or videos**, **Upload a file**, and **New folder**. ## Expected result The selected folder displays its decrypted entries without exposing names or file contents to the Dosya service. Opening folders is read-only. Saving creates an external plaintext copy, while **Delete** is a separate confirmed and irreversible Vault operation. ## Troubleshooting **You see “Couldn't check for Spaces.”** Space discovery failed. Keep Vault unlocked, restore the connection, and revisit the Vault tab to run discovery again. **You see “Couldn't open the Space.”** The grant may be missing, stale, revoked, or unreadable on this identity. Return to **Vault**, refresh the account session, and ask a current Space member to confirm your membership if the Space was shared. **You see “Couldn't load this folder.”** The Space opened but its encrypted folder index did not. Retry on a stable connection. Do not create a replacement folder with the same name as a recovery step; that would be a different encrypted folder. **The Space is absent from My Spaces.** Check the active storage workspace. Shared Spaces remain under **Shared with me**; an own Space scoped to another workspace is intentionally filtered from the current **My Spaces** list. **The lock card replaces the folder list.** The five-minute background timeout, an explicit **Lock**, sign-out, or an account switch ended the session. Unlock in place; the screen reopens the Space and reloads the current folder. ## Related guides - [Set up Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Manage Vault members](/files/vault-member-access)

title: Open a Vault file on mobile
summary: Open and decrypt a Vault file on mobile, learn which formats preview in place, and recover safely from Space, network, or integrity failures.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/vault/file.tsx, apps/mobile/src/vault/store.ts, apps/mobile/src/vault/cache.ts, apps/mobile/src/vault/client.ts, packages/e2ee-client/src/file.ts, packages/e2ee-core/src/file.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/saveToDevice.ts, and apps/mobile/src/files/download.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Opening a Vault file is a local decrypt operation. The phone obtains short-lived URLs for encrypted chunks, verifies each chunk against its SHA-256 identifier, authenticates it with XChaCha20-Poly1305, and writes plaintext into the app-private Vault cache. ## Before you start - Unlock **Vault**, open the correct Space, and navigate to the folder containing the file. - The account must still be a member of that Space and possess a valid Space-key grant. Ordinary workspace roles do not separately control Vault reads. - Keep enough free device storage for one decrypted copy. Vault downloads have no separate 1 GiB app-cache quota; available device storage and the file’s actual size are the practical limits. - Expect images and videos to preview in place. Other file types show their name and known size with **Save** and **Share** actions after decryption. ## Steps 1. Tap the file row in the Space folder. The file screen first ensures that the requested Space is open. 2. Leave the screen active while the transfer bar reports the file’s downloaded bytes. Encrypted data is fetched in content-defined chunks with a maximum plaintext chunk size of 4 MiB. 3. Wait for the **preview**. Images open in the image stage and videos in the video stage; an unsupported type opens a document card instead of pretending it can be rendered. 4. Use **Save to device** only for a durable plaintext copy outside Vault. It sends images and videos to Photos or Gallery, sends Android non-media files of 64 MiB or less to a folder picker, and opens the system share sheet only for iOS non-media files or larger Android documents. The adjacent **Share** action always hands the decrypted cache file to another app through the operating-system share sheet. 5. Return with the top-left back control when finished. Use **Lock** from the Vault overview if you want to erase the session’s decrypted Vault cache immediately. ## Expected result The selected file opens from a locally decrypted cache path. The cloud object remains encrypted, and merely viewing it does not export, share, rename, edit, or delete it. A second open during the same unlocked session may reuse the cached file. ## Troubleshooting **You see “Couldn't open the Space.”** The screen could not establish the requested Space before asking for bytes. Reopen the Space from **Vault** and confirm membership has not been revoked. **You see “Couldn't download filename.”** The encrypted transfer, manifest decrypt, chunk verification, device write, or available storage failed. Network and 5xx chunk requests retry after 500 ms, 1.5 seconds, and 4 seconds; 4xx responses do not retry. Return to the folder and open the file again after fixing connectivity or storage. **You see “Couldn't open this file.”** No usable local path was produced. Go back rather than waiting on the spinner, unlock again if necessary, and retry from the folder listing. **Vault locked while the file was open.** After five minutes in the background, explicit locking, sign-out, or account switching, the app redirects to **Vault**, aborts in-flight downloads, and wipes cached plaintext. Unlocking and reopening downloads the encrypted chunks again. **The file displays only a name and size.** That is the fallback for a format without an image or video stage. Choose **Save** to export it through the platform-specific destination above, or **Share** to hand it to a compatible app. Either action moves plaintext outside Vault. ## Related guides - [Set up Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Manage Vault members](/files/vault-member-access)

title: Save a Vault file to the mobile device
summary: Export a decrypted Vault file to a trusted mobile destination, understand platform and size rules, and remove plaintext copies when finished.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/vault/file.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/vault/space/[id]/[folderId].tsx, apps/mobile/src/vault/store.ts, apps/mobile/src/vault/cache.ts, and apps/mobile/src/files/saveToDevice.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: **Save to device** crosses the Vault privacy boundary: Dosya decrypts the selected file into its session cache, then exports plaintext to a location controlled by the phone or another app. Locking Vault cannot erase that exported copy. ## Before you start - Unlock Vault and open the file in its Space. Any current Space member who can decrypt the file can use the mobile export control; the ordinary workspace role table is not consulted for this action. - Verify that policy permits an unencrypted device copy. Photos, Files, Downloads, third-party providers, and device backups can retain it independently. - Reserve enough free space for the decrypted Vault cache file and the final exported file. - Know the size path: Android directly writes a non-media file only when its reported size is no more than 64 MiB. Larger documents use the streaming share sheet. ## Steps 1. In a Space folder, open the file and wait for its encrypted chunks to download and decrypt successfully. 2. Tap **Save to device** in the bottom action bar. For a non-previewable document, the stage also offers **Save** after the local file is ready. 3. Complete the native **destination flow**: - An image or video requests permission and saves to Photos or Gallery. - An Android document of 64 MiB or less asks you to select a writable folder. - An iOS document opens the system share sheet, where **Save to Files** is available. - An Android document over 64 MiB opens the streaming share sheet; choose its final location there. 4. Confirm the toast: **Saved to your gallery**, **Saved to your phone**, **Choose where to save it**, or **Too large to save directly - choose where to put it**. 5. Open and validate the exported file, then delete it from the external destination when its plaintext is no longer required. ## Expected result The chosen destination receives a standalone plaintext file. The encrypted Vault entry stays in its Space, consumes the same storage, and remains available to other members. No later lock, membership revocation, or Vault deletion can retract an already exported device copy. ## Troubleshooting **You see “Couldn't download filename.”** Export cannot begin until the local decrypt completes. Restore the connection and available storage, then reopen the file. The client retries chunk network and 5xx failures three times with 500 ms, 1.5-second, and 4-second delays. **The picker closes without a saved file.** Cancelling is treated as a choice and shows no error on this screen. Start **Save to device** again and finish the operating-system prompt. **Photo-library access is blocked.** The save helper creates the message **dosya needs permission to add photos to your gallery.** This Vault screen treats that `SaveCancelled` result like a dismissed picker and returns without a toast. If nothing is saved and no error appears, grant Dosya add-to-library access in system settings, then run **Save to device** again. **The share sheet appears instead of an Android folder picker.** The item is a non-media file reported above 64 MiB, so Dosya avoids loading a roughly one-third-larger base64 representation into JavaScript memory. **Locking did not remove the exported copy.** This is expected. Lock erases `/vault` under Dosya’s app cache and aborts current Vault transfers; it has no authority over Photos, Files, Downloads, SD cards, or another provider. ## Related guides - [Set up Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Manage Vault members](/files/vault-member-access)

title: Review Vault transfer progress on mobile
summary: Read Vault upload and download byte progress, retry failed uploads safely, handle download-only failures, and understand the five-minute lock boundary.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/vault/ui/TransferBar.tsx, apps/mobile/src/vault/store.ts, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/vault/space/[id]/[folderId].tsx, apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/vault/file.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Vault transfers exist only inside the unlocked session. Each row shows the file name and bytes written as `_done_ of _total_`; completed rows disappear automatically. A failed upload says **Couldn’t upload _name_.** and keeps a **Retry** action plus **Dismiss**. Retry reuses the same row and source so it cannot leave a second failed row that could upload a duplicate. A failed download says **Couldn’t download _name_.** but has no Retry payload; dismiss it, return to the folder, and open the file again. ## Steps 1. Keep Vault unlocked and remain in the relevant Space while the transfer is active. 2. Read the file name and byte counter in the transfer row; an unknown total shows only bytes completed. 3. For **Couldn’t upload _name_.**, fix connectivity or workspace attachment and tap **Retry** on that same row. 4. For **Couldn’t download _name_.**, tap **Dismiss**, return to the Space folder, and open the file again to start a fresh download. 5. After Vault removes a completed upload row, refresh or inspect the destination folder and open the new encrypted entry. 6. Finish or deliberately abandon transfers before leaving Vault in the background for five minutes, because the automatic lock aborts downloads and wipes decrypted cache. Uploads may retry workspace attachment once after a 412 response. **Dismiss** removes only the status row; pressing it during an active upload does not abort that upload. Dismissing a failed upload also deletes the picker’s plaintext cache copy, so its **Retry** option is gone. Locking clears all transfer rows, aborts cache downloads, and removes decrypted cached files from the session. ## Expected result A successful transfer row disappears and the uploaded entry is present or the downloaded file opens from session cache. A failed upload remains explicitly retryable; a failed download is restarted by reopening the file after dismissal. ## Related guides - [Set up Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Manage Vault members](/files/vault-member-access)

title: Unlock Vault on mobile
summary: Unlock Vault on your phone with its passphrase or recovery key, understand the five-minute background lock, and resolve exact unlock errors.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/mobile/src/vault/ui/UnlockCard.tsx, apps/mobile/src/vault/store.ts, apps/mobile/src/vault/engine.ts, apps/mobile/src/vault/backend.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/oprf-evaluate.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Vault unlocks locally on each phone. Your passphrase is hardened and used to unwrap your encrypted identity; Dosya does not receive the passphrase or hold a replacement for it. You must be signed in to the account that owns the Vault identity, but the mobile client applies no separate plan or workspace-role check to the unlock control. ## Before you start - Update to a released Dosya mobile build with the native Vault runtime; Expo Go does not provide the required native crypto module. - Confirm the signed-in Dosya account. Vault identities and Space memberships belong to the account, not merely to the selected storage workspace. - Have either the exact passphrase or the 64-character lowercase hexadecimal recovery key created during Vault setup. Spaces, line breaks, and hyphens in a pasted recovery key are ignored. - Stay online for unlock. Passphrase unlock needs the stored key bundle, public OPRF key, and an authenticated OPRF evaluation; recovery-key unlock fetches the stored key bundle but skips the OPRF round trip. ## Steps 1. Open the **Vault** tab. Wait while the app checks whether the current account has a Vault identity. 2. On **Unlock your Vault**, enter the value in **Passphrase**, then tap **Unlock**. The button remains unavailable while the field is empty or an attempt is running. 3. If the passphrase is unavailable, tap **Use recovery key**, paste the saved key into **Recovery key**, and choose **Unlock with recovery key**. Tap **Use your passphrase** to switch back. 4. After a successful unlock, confirm that **My Spaces** appears. Spaces shared by other people are listed separately under **Shared with me**. 5. For a deliberate lock, use the **Lock** row on the Vault screen. The app also locks Vault after five minutes in the background; returning then requires another local unlock. ## Expected result The phone holds the decrypted identity only for the active Vault session and can open Spaces assigned to that account. Unlocking does not export any plaintext file or change a workspace, member, plan, or cloud object. ## Troubleshooting **You see “Couldn't check encryption status.”** The identity lookup failed. Check the connection and tap **Retry**; do not start setup, because an unavailable identity check is not proof that the account has no Vault. **You see “Couldn't unlock. Check your passphrase and try again.”** Re-enter the original passphrase. The field was cleared immediately after the previous tap. Passphrase evaluation is limited to 10 attempts per user per hour in each current API isolate; this is not a globally shared counter. Mobile replaces every unlock failure, including HTTP 429, with the same generic sentence and does not expose `Retry-After` or reset time. Stop repeated attempts and try later rather than waiting for an in-app countdown. **You see “That recovery key didn't unlock your Vault.”** Verify that the key belongs to this account and that every hexadecimal character was copied. Formatting spaces and hyphens are harmless; missing or changed characters are not recoverable. **The app locks while you are reading or downloading.** Five minutes in the background ends the Vault session, aborts active Vault downloads, clears transfer rows, and wipes the decrypted Vault cache. Unlock again and reopen the file; the encrypted cloud copy remains intact. ## Related guides - [Set up Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Manage Vault members](/files/vault-member-access)

title: Play a video in the mobile viewer
summary: Play and seek mobile video with native controls, understand the one-hour stream URL and 15-second stall state, and recover from unsupported codecs.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/VideoStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/VlcVideoStage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/videoSupport.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/useFilePreview.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Mobile video uses the phone’s native controls when the container is supported and a built-in libVLC stage for known iOS-incompatible containers when that module is available. Stream URLs are requested for one hour so long playback can continue past the old five-minute boundary. The native stage supports fullscreen and Picture in Picture. On iOS, MKV, WebM, AVI, WMV, FLV, OGV, MPG, MPEG, RMVB, and TS are routed away from AVPlayer; Android gives its player the first attempt. A view-only source cannot be handed to libVLC because that player cannot attach the authentication header. ## Steps 1. Open the video from **Files** and wait for a frame rather than judging the initial black surface. 2. Use the native play, pause, seek, fullscreen, or Picture in Picture controls when they appear. 3. On the libVLC stage, use its play button and tap the seek bar after a duration has been detected. 4. If **Still loading** appears after 15 seconds without a first frame, choose **Retry** on a stable connection. 5. If the phone cannot decode the format, choose **Save to phone** and open it in a compatible player; view-only files may not offer Save. 6. Verify playback beyond the chosen seek point and listen for audio before treating the file as usable on this device. The 15-second message does not prove the file is corrupt; it covers both poor connectivity and a decoder that never produces a frame. libVLC failures say **Couldn’t play this video** and offer Retry or Save when allowed. Saving creates a device copy but does not change the cloud original. ## Expected result A supported file plays with video and audio, seeks to the chosen position, and can enter the native display modes. Unsupported or stalled playback ends with an actionable Retry or Save route rather than an indefinite black screen. ## Related guides - [Use media previews](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Download on mobile](/files/mobile-download-file)

title: Moving and renaming files or folders
summary: Rename an item in place or move files and folders to another location within the active workspace, with collision and permission checks.
verification: Verified the current English Files page and current web/API source on 2026-10-12. Local screenshots use an isolated owner workspace with controlled current-API fixtures and show the real rename and move dialogs. Source and tests confirmed file and folder permissions, same-folder and duplicate-name refusals, folder-cycle protection, single-segment name validation and multi-select moves. The fixture dialogs were reviewed before submission; cross-workspace transfer and the effect on every existing share-link configuration were not exercised.
body: Use **Rename** when the item should stay in the same folder with a new name. Use **Move to...** when its location should change inside the active workspace. The move picker contains folders from that workspace; it is not a cross-workspace transfer tool. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace and current folder. A similar name in another workspace is a different item. - Check that you have the required permission. File renaming, folder renaming and moving files can be controlled separately by the workspace role. - Close editors or sync tasks that are actively changing the item when possible. - Check the destination for an item with the same name. Dosya refuses a collision rather than silently overwriting it. - If the item has an active share link, protocol client or desktop sync relationship, test that workflow after reorganizing it. This review did not assume every external path behaves identically. ## Steps: rename a file or folder 1. Open **Files** and find the item. 2. Right-click its row or open the three-dot menu. 3. Choose **Rename**. 4. Enter the new name. For a file, keep the correct extension unless you deliberately intend to change the label; renaming does not convert the file's contents. 5. Choose **Rename**. 6. Confirm the updated name in the same folder and open the item once to verify you changed the intended row. ## Steps: move one item 1. Open the file or folder menu and choose **Move to...**. 2. In **Move to folder**, choose **Root** or select a destination folder. 3. Expand a folder to browse its children, or use **Search folders...** when the workspace has a large hierarchy. 4. Review the selected destination shown in the dialog. 5. Choose **Move**. 6. Open the destination and confirm the item appears there. Return to the source to confirm it no longer appears in its old location. ## Steps: move several items 1. Select the checkboxes beside the required files and folders. 2. Review the selection count in the bulk action bar. 3. Choose **Move**. 4. Select one destination folder and confirm. 5. Read the completion message. If a subset could not move, Dosya reports how many moved and how many were skipped. 6. Check both the destination and source before retrying any skipped item individually. ## Expected result A rename changes the displayed name while leaving the item in its current folder. A move removes the item from the source listing and places it in the chosen folder in the same workspace. Dosya keeps one item rather than creating an additional stored copy. Folder moves carry the folder's contained hierarchy with it, subject to access, lock and cycle checks. ## Limits and permission behavior - File names can contain up to 255 characters; folder names can contain up to 100. Names must be a single safe path segment, so `/`, `\`, control characters, `.` and `..` are refused. - A file cannot move to a destination that already contains a file with the same name. The equivalent duplicate-folder name is also refused. - Moving an item to the place it already occupies is refused because it would make no change. - A folder cannot move into itself or one of its own subfolders. - File moves require the role's file-upload capability for the destination. Folder moves use the folder-rename capability. The Rename actions follow the corresponding file or folder rename permission. - Locked, hidden, confined or backup-locked items and destinations can have additional restrictions. - The web picker moves within the active workspace. Moving data between workspaces requires a separate copy, download/upload or supported integration workflow. ## Troubleshooting **Rename or Move to is missing.** Your role may not have the required file or folder permission, or the item may be in a view where the action is unavailable. Ask a workspace owner to check the role rather than changing another permission at random. **A duplicate-name message appears.** Inspect the destination for the same file or folder name. Rename one item first, or choose another folder. Dosya does not silently replace the existing item. **The folder cannot move.** Make sure the destination is not the folder itself or any child below it. Choose a parent, sibling or unrelated folder instead. **The destination is missing from the picker.** Confirm the active workspace and your access to that folder. Use the picker's folder search. Hidden, inaccessible and out-of-scope destinations are not disclosed. **The file extension changed.** Rename the item again and restore the correct extension. Changing `.xlsx` to `.pdf`, for example, changes only the name and does not convert spreadsheet bytes into a PDF. **Only part of a bulk move completed.** Read the moved/skipped counts, inspect the destination, then retry each skipped item separately to expose its specific collision, permission or folder-cycle problem. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I move a file into another workspace? The current Files move picker works within the active workspace. Use an appropriate copy, download/upload or integration workflow for a different workspace, then verify both copies before deleting anything. ### What happens when the destination already has the same name? Dosya refuses the move with a duplicate-name message. It does not silently overwrite that file or folder. ### Does renaming convert the file format? No. Rename changes the label. Use an application that supports conversion when the file contents need a different format. ## Related guides - [Organizing files with folders, favourites and groups](/files/organize-files) - [Searching for files in the correct workspace](/files/search-files) - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Understanding and resolving desktop sync conflicts](/desktop/sync-conflicts)

title: Move a folder and its contents
summary: Move a complete Dosya folder tree without copying data, while resolving role, backup-lock, same-name, same-place, and cycle refusals safely.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/mobile/app/pick-destination.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/move.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/move.conflict.unit.test.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: A folder move reparents one folder and its entire live subtree inside the same workspace. It does not upload, duplicate, or re-encrypt the files below that folder. ## Before you start - Use a role with `rename_folders`; Dosya uses that permission for structural folder moves. - For a folder-confined member, the API requires the source folder to be inside the assigned subtree. It checks the destination only for a live, visible folder in the same workspace; a Dosya picker may narrow the choices it displays, but the move endpoint does not apply the source-confinement check to that destination. - A locked WordPress backup cannot be moved or renamed, and another folder cannot be moved into its protected tree. - Look for a sibling folder at the destination with the same name. Move never merges two folder trees. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, open the source folder’s menu and choose **Move to...** on web or desktop; mobile labels the action **Move to…**. 2. In **Move to folder** or **Move to…**, browse to the new parent. Leave the picker at the top level to move the folder to the workspace root. 3. Verify that the destination breadcrumb does not sit inside the source folder. 4. Choose **Move** or **Move here** and wait for **Moved** or **Moved successfully**. 5. Refresh the source parent and confirm the folder is gone from that level. 6. Open the destination, inspect the folder’s new breadcrumb, and check representative nested files and subfolders. ## Expected result The folder keeps its ID and stored name, and all descendant relationships remain intact. Workspace storage does not change. Path-based clients see the old path disappear and the new path appear after their next refreshed listing or sync snapshot. ## Troubleshooting - **“You don’t have permission to move folders.”** Ask an administrator for `rename_folders` or have an authorized member perform the move. - **“Destination folder not found.”** The target was deleted, hidden from your role, foreign to the workspace, or stale in the picker. Refresh and choose a visible destination. - **“Folder is already here.”** The selected parent is already the current parent; cancel without retrying. - **“Cannot move a folder into itself” or “Cannot move a folder into its own subfolder.”** Move upward or choose a separate branch. No part of the tree was changed. - **“A folder with this name already exists in the target folder.”** Rename either sibling first. Dosya leaves both trees separate and does not overwrite content. - **The old path remains in a mounted client.** Refresh that client’s directory listing. The API invalidates web, sync, WebDAV, and S3 path caches, but a client can still display its own cached view briefly. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Connect Dosya to n8n
summary: Install the current Dosya community node, attach a dedicated REST credential, and verify workspace access before activating file automation.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/package.json; apps/n8n/README.md; apps/n8n/credentials/DosyaApi.credentials.ts; apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/Dosya.node.ts; apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/methods.ts; apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/transport.ts; apps/n8n/test/package.test.mts; apps/n8n/test/actions.test.mts; apps/n8n/test/transport.test.mts; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts; apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts; apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/index.ts; and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts. Package contracts, mocked requests, and API-key cache invalidation were reviewed locally; public registry availability, a production n8n instance and the live Dosya API were not queried.
body: The `n8n-nodes-dosya` community package connects n8n to Dosya through the REST API. It can upload, download and list files, create or reuse folders, and create file or folder share links. ## Requirements and boundaries - The repository package is `n8n-nodes-dosya` version **0.1.1**. Its compatibility target is n8n **2.42** with Node.js **22**; community-node installation availability still depends on your n8n deployment policy. - The node uses a Dosya API key, never your Dosya password. For all five current operations, use **Full access**, include the **REST API** protocol, and leave **Folder access** unset. A workspace pin is supported. - The key owner's workspace membership and role still apply. Full-access scope cannot overcome an action the member is not permitted to perform. - Current operations are **File: Upload**, **File: Download**, **File: Get Many**, **Folder: Create**, and **Share Link: Create**. This release has no Dosya trigger, deletion, move, rename, sync or file-request operation. - Plan and workspace limits are enforced by Dosya. The Free-plan source defaults provide **5 GB** storage and **100 GB** daily egress, allow at most **5 active share links**, and cap share expiry at **7 days**. Workspace and per-file ceilings may be stricter. ## Steps 1. In a self-hosted n8n instance that permits community packages, open **Settings → Community Nodes → Install**. 2. Enter `n8n-nodes-dosya` and confirm installation. After installation, the node picker should contain **dosya.dev** and the credential picker should contain **dosya.dev API**. 3. In Dosya, open **Profile → API keys → New API key**. Name the key for this n8n instance, choose **Full access**, restrict **Protocols** to **REST API**, and optionally pin one workspace. 4. Generate the key and copy the one-time secret. Do not add a folder anchor: the API rejects folder-anchored keys outside WebDAV and S3. 5. In n8n, create a **dosya.dev API** credential and put the token in **API Key**. Saving tests it against `GET https://api.dosya.dev/api/me`. 6. Create a temporary workflow and add a **dosya.dev** node. Choose the saved credential, **File** as **Resource**, and **Get Many** as **Operation**. 7. Under **Workspace**, use **From List** and select the intended name. Choose **Workspace Root** under **Folder**, leave **Return All** off, and set a small **Limit** such as `1`. 8. Execute the node. Compare the returned `workspace_id`, `folder_id`, `id`, `name` and `type` with the harmless item you expected before adding any write operation. ## Expected result The credential test passes and the trial **Get Many** execution returns no more than the chosen limit from the selected root. The node receives only resources the key owner can reach within its workspace pin and role. Resource locators support **From List** and **By ID**. Workspace IDs begin `ws_`, folder IDs `fld_`, and file IDs `file_`. Folder choices show paths such as `Clients / Acme / Final`; a file search with no text lists the newest root files, while typed text searches the whole selected workspace in pages of **50**. ## Diagnose a failed connection - **dosya.dev did not accept the API key** means the token may be incomplete, expired or revoked. Replace the saved n8n credential with a valid one-time secret. - **This key is read-only. Uploads, folders and share links need a key with Full access scope.** is raised by the credential test for a read-only key even though `GET /api/me` authenticated. - A `403` mentioning the **api surface** means the key excludes REST. Generate a key that includes **REST API**. - A `403` stating the key is **anchored at a folder** requires a replacement without a folder anchor; selecting that folder in the node is the supported way to target it. - **No workspace selected** is an n8n validation error. Choose one from the list or enter its `ws_…` identifier. - A missing workspace can mean the key is pinned elsewhere or the owner lacks membership. Credential success alone does not promise access to every workspace. - The client retries a `429` at most **3 attempts** when `Retry-After` is **30 seconds or less**. A longer delay is reported to the execution instead of making the job wait silently. Removing the n8n package does not revoke its Dosya key. Revocation is permanent, but an already cached successful validation can remain accepted for up to **5 minutes**. Inventory affected workflows before rotation, then retest after that window. ## Related guides - [Choose API-key permission](/developers/api-key-scopes) - [Connect Zapier](/integrations/zapier)

title: Create a Dosya credential in n8n
summary: Create a dedicated Full-access REST key, save its one-time secret in n8n, and resolve exact credential-test failures without exposing your password.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/credentials/DosyaApi.credentials.ts; apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/transport.ts; apps/n8n/test/package.test.mts; apps/n8n/test/transport.test.mts; apps/n8n/README.md; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/index.refusal.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.ts; and apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts. Mocked package tests, credential contracts, and revocation-cache behavior were checked; no key was created and the production API was not called.
body: The Dosya community node has one required credential field: **API Key**. It stores a Dosya `dos_…` token as a password value, sends it as `Authorization: Bearer` only to `https://api.dosya.dev`, and tests it with `GET /api/me`. ## Before you create the credential - Install or select the `n8n-nodes-dosya` community node first. The repository package version is **0.1.1**, built and tested with n8n **2.42** (`n8n-workflow` 2.42.4) and Node.js **22**. - Use a separate key named for n8n so rotation does not interrupt another tool. The free plan permits **3** API keys per user; all accounts have a hard ceiling of **20**, and expired keys still count until revoked. - Prepare n8n's encrypted credential store before generating the token. Dosya displays the full API key only once. - The current node requires **Full access** for its full operation set. A read-only key can authenticate but fails the credential rule, while upload-only cannot pass the account test or perform read operations. ## Steps 1. In Dosya, open the account menu, select **Profile**, choose **API keys**, and select **New API key**. 2. Enter an identifying value in **What is it for?**, such as `n8n production uploads`. The maximum key-name length is **64 characters**. 3. Under **What can it do?**, choose **Full access**. Under **Restrictions and expiry**, set **Protocols** to **Only the ones I pick** and check **REST API**. 4. Optionally select one **Workspace** to pin the credential. Leave the folder anchor empty: folder-anchored keys are accepted only by WebDAV and S3, so the n8n REST node will refuse them. 5. Set an expiry and any IP, active-hours or usage controls the n8n host can satisfy. A workspace pin narrows the key; it does not give the owner permission beyond their role in that workspace. 6. Select **Generate key**, copy the complete token from the **is ready** dialog, and store it privately before selecting **Done**. 7. In n8n, create a credential of type **dosya.dev API**. Paste the token into **API Key**. Never enter your Dosya account password in this field. 8. Save the credential and run n8n's credential test. The test calls `https://api.dosya.dev/api/me` immediately and sends the node version in its `User-Agent`. ## Expected result n8n reports a successful credential check, and the saved credential is available to Dosya nodes. The test proves the key is accepted and has Full access; it does not prove that every selected workspace, folder, plan limit or member role permits a later action. In Dosya, the key row shows its name, **Full access**, **REST API**, reach, expiry and last-use information. n8n stores the secret; Dosya retains only a partial identifier and cannot display the full token again. ## Exact failures and recovery | Result | What to change | | --- | --- | | **This key is read-only. Uploads, folders and share links need a key with Full access scope.** | Create a Full-access replacement; changing n8n cannot widen the existing key. | | **dosya.dev did not accept the API key** | Check for a truncated, revoked or expired token. Generate a replacement if the one-time value was lost. | | **This API key is anchored at a folder and can only be used over WebDAV or the S3 gateway** | Recreate it without a folder anchor. A workspace pin is compatible with this node. | | **The free plan allows 3 API keys. Delete one or upgrade for more.** | Revoke an unused or expired key before generating another. | | **Maximum of 20 API keys reached** | Remove an obsolete credential from the account-level list. | | **Name must be 64 characters or less** | Shorten **What is it for?** and submit again. | Revoking the key is irreversible. A successful API-key lookup may remain cached for up to **5 minutes**, including a **30-second** in-isolate memory layer, so create and validate the replacement first, update affected workflows, revoke the old row, and retest after five minutes. If a token appears in logs, screenshots or workflow data, rotate it rather than relying on deletion of the exposed copy. ## Related guides - [Connect Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Connect n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect)

title: Create a Dosya sharing link in n8n
summary: Configure the Dosya Share Link Create operation for a file or folder, apply expiry and access options, then verify the returned public-link fields.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/Dosya.node.ts, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/actions.ts, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/transport.ts, apps/n8n/test/actions.test.mts, and apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts. No production link or n8n execution was created.
body: Use the **dosya.dev** community node with **Resource: Share Link** and **Operation: Create**. Every successful execution creates a new public link, so test with one controlled item and inspect the returned record before enabling retries. ## Steps 1. Add a **dosya.dev** node for **Share Link → Create**, then select a tested **dosya.dev API** credential. 2. Under **Share**, choose **File** or **Folder**. Map a `file_…` or `fld_…` ID from an earlier node; **Workspace** is optional when the ID is entered directly and only scopes list pickers. 3. Open **Options**. Set **Access Code** to at least 8 characters when needed; this recipient code is not the Dosya account password. 4. Set **Expires In Days**. `0` omits the value and uses the workspace default; the Free plan caps links at 7 days. Enable **View Only** to request preview without downloading. 5. Execute the node once and inspect `id`, `url`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `expires_at`, `view_only`, `access_code_required`, `access_mode`, and `created_at`. 6. Open `url` in a signed-out browser, enter the code when configured, and verify the expected file or folder before passing the URL to another node. A workspace role must permit share-link creation and the key needs Full access. Folder-anchored keys are refused by REST and work only over WebDAV or S3. Free accounts can hold five active share links; revoke or let one expire before another when the API returns `share_free_link_limit`. ## Expected result The node returns one server-created link record for the intended target, with effective expiry and access fields. The public test reaches only that file or folder and the workflow exposes no API key or access code in ordinary output. **The access code is shorter than 8 characters** is validated before any request. **No folder selected** means the Folder target resolved to root/empty. After **Could not reach dosya.dev**, inspect existing links first because an ambiguous response may have arrived after creation. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect) - [Build an n8n workflow](/integrations/n8n-workflow)

title: Build an n8n workflow that creates a Dosya share link
summary: Build an n8n sharing workflow from an earlier Dosya item ID, test one controlled input, and prevent duplicate links after an ambiguous network result.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/examples/02-store-and-share-pdf.json, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/actions.ts, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/transport.ts, apps/n8n/test/actions.test.mts, and apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts. Production behavior for “Build an n8n workflow that creates a Dosya share link” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A complete n8n sharing workflow should receive or create a Dosya item, pass its stable ID into **Share Link → Create**, and use the returned URL. The share step creates access; it does not upload bytes or notify a recipient by itself. ## Steps 1. Start with one non-confidential item. For an uploaded file, use the preceding Dosya node’s `id`; for a folder, retain its `fld_…` output. 2. Add **Create Share Link**, choose **Share Link → Create**, and map the target by ID rather than selecting a stale editor sample. 3. Configure **Access Code**, **Expires In Days**, and **View Only** for the real recipient. Use an access code of 8 or more characters and treat `0` days as the workspace default. 4. Connect downstream delivery only to the returned `url`. Keep `id` for later link management and retain `expires_at` when recipients need a deadline. 5. Execute one manual test. A successful test creates a real active link, so do not press test repeatedly and do not assume deactivating the workflow removes it. 6. Verify the signed-out link, then activate the workflow. Monitor its first live execution and confirm one input produced one expected link before increasing volume. The bundled **Store and share a PDF** example returns `file_id`, `name`, `share_url`, and `expires_at` from an Upload node followed by Create Share Link. Add an email or webhook response separately if somebody must receive the URL. ## Expected result Each accepted input maps to the intended Dosya resource and yields one verified public URL with the configured effective access. The workflow’s delivery step receives that URL only after creation succeeds. The node automatically retries a 429 at most within three total attempts when the wait is 30 seconds or less. It deliberately does not replay share creation after a timeout, 502, 503 or 504 because the first request may already have created a link; check Dosya before manual retry. ## Related guides - [Configure the n8n share-link node](/integrations/n8n-create-share-link-node) - [Connect n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect)

title: Handle a failed Dosya node in n8n
summary: Interpret Dosya node status text, bounded retries, Continue On Fail output and plan or permission refusals before replaying a workflow item.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/Dosya.node.ts, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/transport.ts, apps/n8n/test/transport.test.mts, and apps/n8n/test/actions.test.mts. Production behavior for “Handle a failed Dosya node in n8n” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Read both the node’s error message and description before replaying an item. The transport keeps Dosya’s human-readable refusal where possible, adds a recovery hint, and limits automatic retries to requests that are safe to repeat. ## Steps 1. Open the failed execution and record the node name, item index, HTTP code, message, description and run time. Redact the API key and public URLs before sharing diagnostics. 2.
