For **dosya.dev did not accept the API key** (`401`), replace a mistyped, expired or revoked key. Re-running with the same credential cannot restore it. 3. For `403`, act on the exact refusal: Full access is required for writes; a folder anchor cannot use REST; membership permissions and workspace pinning still apply. 4. For `404`, verify the mapped ID and whether the target was moved to Trash or hidden from the key. For `413`, compare the file with plan, workspace and key per-file limits. 5. For `429`, follow the displayed Retry-After. The node tries at most three attempts and sleeps only when the wait is 30 seconds or less; longer waits are reported for a Wait node or later run. 6. Decide whether to replay. Idempotent reads/folder creation and upload requests with an idempotency key can retry transient transport errors and 502/503/504; share creation cannot. With **Continue On Fail**, each failed input becomes an item shaped like `{ "error": "…" }` with its paired input index, and later input items continue. Without it, the node throws and stops. A successful earlier item is not rolled back when a later item fails. ## Expected result The corrected run either completes or emits an intentional error item for each failed input. Retries remain bounded, long server waits are respected, and potentially completed non-idempotent actions are inspected before another request. **Could not reach dosya.dev** on a non-idempotent step explicitly warns that work may already exist. Storage messages beginning **You’ve used …** require freeing plan storage or upgrading; a workspace storage-limit sentence requires its administrator to raise that separate cap. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect) - [Build an n8n workflow](/integrations/n8n-workflow)

title: List Dosya files in n8n
summary: List files from one Dosya workspace or folder with exact sort, limit and subfolder options, then verify IDs and pagination-derived output fields.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/Dosya.node.ts, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/actions.ts, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/methods.ts, and apps/n8n/test/actions.test.mts. No production file listing was fetched.
body: The Dosya node’s **File → Get Many** operation lists one workspace root or one folder. It returns a flat stream of file items; optional subfolders are returned as folder records without recursively listing their contents. ## Steps 1. Add **dosya.dev**, choose **Resource: File** and **Operation: Get Many**, then select the intended **Workspace**. 2. Choose **Folder** or leave **Workspace Root**. The folder picker displays full paths such as `Clients / Acme / Final` to distinguish duplicate leaf names. 3. Leave **Return All** off for a bounded test and set **Limit** to at least 1; the default is 50. The node fetches API pages up to 500 entries while stopping at your limit. 4. Under **Options**, choose **Sort By**: **Newest First**, **Oldest First**, **Name**, **Largest First**, or **Smallest First**. 5. Enable **Include Subfolders in Output** only when downstream logic expects records with `type: folder`. Child contents are not traversed by that option. 6. Execute once and compare representative `id`, `name`, `size`, `mime_type`, `extension`, `version`, `workspace_id`, `folder_id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` values with Dosya. When **Return All** is enabled, the node follows file pagination until the API reports the last page. Subfolders are taken from the first response only because the API repeats the complete subfolder list on every file page. ## Expected result The output contains files from exactly the chosen workspace root or folder in the selected order, stops at the requested limit unless Return All is enabled, and includes only immediate subfolder records when requested. An empty output is valid when the selected scope has no visible files. A missing workspace is rejected before the request; access failures require checking the credential’s workspace pin, Full/Read scope and the key owner’s file-view permission. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect) - [Build an n8n workflow](/integrations/n8n-workflow)

title: Test an n8n Dosya credential
summary: Create and test a full-access, unanchored Dosya API credential in n8n, distinguish scope failures, and confirm the key owner and workspace reach.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/credentials/DosyaApi.credentials.ts, apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/transport.ts, apps/n8n/test/package.test.mts, apps/n8n/test/transport.test.mts, and apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx. body: The n8n credential stores one secret field named **API Key** and sends it as a Bearer token to `https://api.dosya.dev`. Its test calls `GET /api/me`; a successful HTTP response can still fail the rule when the key is read-only. ## Steps 1. In Dosya, open **Profile → API keys** and choose **New API key**. Give the key a label that names this n8n instance. 2. Choose **Full access**, enable REST/API use, and leave the folder anchor empty. Pin one workspace when the workflow should not reach the key owner’s other memberships. 3. Generate the key and copy the complete secret once. Do not enter your Dosya password in n8n. 4. In n8n Credentials, create **dosya.dev API**, paste the secret into **API Key**, and run **Test connection**. 5. Treat **This key is read-only. Uploads, folders and share links need a key with Full access scope.** as a failed credential for this package even though `/api/me` was readable. 6. An Upload-only key cannot pass the authenticated `/api/me` test. A folder-anchored key is unsuitable for this REST node and returns a 403 explanation directing you to create an unanchored key. Revocation or expiry invalidates later requests even if n8n still stores the credential. ## Expected result n8n accepts the credential, the Dosya node can load the intended workspace, and write operations remain bounded by the key’s workspace pin plus the member’s permissions. The secret stays masked in the credential UI. **dosya.dev did not accept the API key** means the value is mistyped, expired or revoked. A scope sentence requires a newly generated Full access key; changing only the n8n credential name does not change authority. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect) - [Build an n8n workflow](/integrations/n8n-workflow)

title: Upload a file from an n8n workflow
summary: Configure File → Upload with binary input, a Full access key and your workspace. Verify returned file metadata, multipart transfers, retries and versions.

body: The **dosya.dev** n8n node uploads a binary file from an earlier workflow step into a selected Dosya workspace. Choose **Resource → File** and **Operation → Upload**. A URL in a JSON field is not the binary input this operation expects. ## Set up the node and credential On a self-hosted n8n instance, an Owner/Admin can open **Settings → Community Nodes → Install**, enter **n8n-nodes-dosya**, review the community-code acknowledgement and select **Install**. Your instance must permit community packages. The current package is **0.1.1**, with Node.js **20.15 or newer** required. If the node is missing, check package installation and your n8n administrator's policy rather than searching for a destination field in another node. Create a credential of type **dosya.dev API**. Its only secret field is **API Key**. In Dosya **Profile → API keys**, create a key with **Full access** scope, **REST API** enabled and no folder anchor; you can pin it to the one workspace used by the workflow. Supply the complete secret, not its displayed prefix. The credential test rejects a Read only key with **This key is read-only. Uploads, folders and share links need a key with Full access scope.** Upload only keys cannot pass the account/listing operations used by this node. The key owner's workspace role must permit uploads, and the chosen destination must fall inside any member folder restriction. Full access is a credential scope, not an administrator role. Key expiry, allowed addresses/hours, storage quota, file-type policy and explicit size/transfer limits still apply. The node cannot bypass them. ## Steps: build a small-file workflow 1. Add a manual trigger and an **HTTP Request** node. Use **GET** for a direct HTTPS URL to a small sample file you control. In **Options → Response**, set **Response Format → File** and **Put Output in Field → data**. Execute that node and open its output **Binary** tab. Verify that `data` holds the expected bytes, filename and type. Keep secrets out of the sample URL. 2. Connect a **dosya.dev** node and select the saved **dosya.dev API** credential. Set **Resource → File** and **Operation → Upload**. 3. Set **Workspace** using **From List** or **By ID** (`ws_…`). Set **Folder** to the destination; leave it empty or select **Workspace Root** for the top level. Folder IDs start with `fld_`. A confined member should select a folder they may write instead of assuming the workspace root is accessible. 4. Set **Input Data Field Name** to `data`. If your upstream node uses `attachment_0` or another name, enter that exact Binary-tab property instead. This is the field name, not the filename or a JSON expression returning a URL. 5. Set **File Name** to a unique test name with its extension, for example `n8n-proof-20261014.txt`. Leaving it empty keeps the incoming filename; without one it falls back to `file`. If your override lacks an extension, the binary's extension is appended when available. 6. Execute the Dosya node once. Compare the returned `id`, `name`, `size`, `workspace_id` and `folder_id` with the intended target before activating scheduled or event-based runs. For varying filenames, switch **File Name** to an expression such as `{{ $json.outputName }}` when the incoming JSON actually contains `outputName`. Workspace/folder locators support **By ID** values mapped from earlier steps. Node parameters are resolved per incoming item; an empty expression does not select a destination. Resource and Operation are fixed options rather than data expressions. ## Verify the result Open Dosya **Files** in the selected workspace and folder. Confirm the unique test filename, size and contents. The upload output is JSON metadata, not the uploaded bytes or a public share URL. It includes `id`, `name`, `size`, `mime_type`, `version`, `is_new_version`, `workspace_id`, `folder_id`, `created_at`, `hash_verified`, `deduplicated` and `upload_method`. A root upload has `folder_id: null`. A new name creates a file; an existing visible filename in the same folder creates another version of that file. `is_new_version` reflects whether the returned version exceeds 1. Choosing a different test name prevents the setup check from replacing an existing file's current contents. Uploading does not create a share link for recipients; use a deliberate **Share Link → Create** step only when you intend to share it. ## Size, timing and repeat runs Files up to **52,428,800 bytes (50 MiB)** use a single request. Larger binaries use a multipart session and sequential parts sized by Dosya's response. Stored n8n binaries are read as a stream for multipart; inline base64 data is already in memory. This removes the one-request ceiling, but plan, workspace/key limits and the n8n host's capacity still bound the upload. Upload/part/completion requests allow **10 minutes** per request; ordinary API requests use **60 seconds**. Safe transient requests are attempted at most **3 times**. Rate-limit waits longer than **30 seconds** are reported for the workflow to handle rather than blocking the node indefinitely. Use a Wait node or a deliberate retry policy for longer delays. The single-request upload derives an idempotency key from execution, node, item, target, filename and content. A retry of that same upload can return the saved result with `deduplicated: true`. A new workflow execution has a different key; the same filename can therefore create a new version. Multipart parts may retry safely, but an ambiguous init or completion is not automatically resent. On failure the node tries to abort the open multipart session. Inspect Dosya before rerunning a timed-out execution; do not assume a timeout means no file was saved. ## Fix the failing field or response | Failure | Action | | --- | --- | | **No workspace selected** | Choose Workspace or fix the mapped ID. **Workspace IDs start with ws_** identifies invalid manual IDs. | | Missing binary input | Run the upstream file-producing step and inspect Binary. Copy its property name into Input Data Field Name; JSON-only items cannot upload. | | **dosya.dev did not accept the API key** | Replace a mistyped, expired or revoked key in the credential. | | 403 mentioning **anchored at a folder** | Use an API-enabled key without a folder anchor; those anchors work over WebDAV/S3, not this REST node. | | Other 403 or invisible destination | Check the key's workspace pin, member role and folder access. An expired permission is not fixed by changing File Name. | | 413 | Check the actual plan, workspace or key file-size restriction. Multipart does not override that restriction. | | Storage-limit refusal | Free appropriate storage or ask the workspace admin to raise their limit; a workspace cap is not necessarily a plan upgrade issue. | | **dosya.dev did not open a multi-part upload** | Retry after checking service status. If persistent, retain execution details for support. | | 429 | Follow the displayed delay, reduce workflow concurrency or insert a Wait between batches. | ## Expected result Each successful input item produces file metadata for the correct destination and can be checked against its original binary. Disconnecting the n8n credential or revoking its key stops future API use; files already uploaded remain in Dosya, including versions created by earlier executions. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect) - [Build an n8n workflow](/integrations/n8n-workflow)

title: Build a safe n8n file workflow
summary: Map one Dosya operation with real node labels, test its returned file data, and account for upload versions, retry timing, and duplicate share links.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/Dosya.node.ts; apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/actions.ts; apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/methods.ts; apps/n8n/nodes/Dosya/transport.ts; apps/n8n/test/actions.test.mts; apps/n8n/test/transport.test.mts; apps/n8n/examples/01-archive-gmail-attachments.json; apps/n8n/examples/02-store-and-share-pdf.json; apps/n8n/examples/03-create-client-folder.json; and apps/n8n/README.md. Node behavior and mocked HTTP tests were checked locally; no workflow was activated and no production file or share link was created.
body: Build a Dosya workflow around one explicit operation and inspect a manual execution before activation. The community node has actions but no Dosya trigger, so the workflow begins with an n8n trigger or upstream application. ## Choose the operation deliberately | Resource and operation | Input and effect | | --- | --- | | **File → Upload** | Reads an incoming binary field, defaults to `data`, and stores it in the selected **Workspace** and **Folder**. A same-name file in that folder receives a new version. | | **File → Download** | Uses a selected or mapped file ID and writes the bytes to **Output Data Field Name** for later nodes. | | **File → Get Many** | Lists a folder or **Workspace Root**. **Return All** pages through results; otherwise **Limit** defaults to `50`. | | **Folder → Create** | Creates the named folder under **Parent Folder**, or returns the existing one. Optional slash replacement keeps names such as `A/B` in one folder. | | **Share Link → Create** | Creates a new public file or folder link, optionally with expiry, an access code of at least **8 characters**, and **View Only**. Each successful call makes another link. | Use **From List** while configuring a fixed destination. Use **By ID** or an expression when an earlier node supplies an ID; the identifier is more stable than a display name. ## Steps 1. Create an n8n workflow and add a manual or application-specific trigger. Fetch one disposable item so its JSON and binary fields are visible. 2. Add **dosya.dev**, choose the intended **Resource** and **Operation**, then select the dedicated **dosya.dev API** credential. 3. Choose **Workspace** and the destination **Folder**. An empty folder value or **Workspace Root** targets the top level. For download and share actions, a mapped target ID is sufficient; **Workspace** is used only to browse their pickers. 4. For **Upload**, inspect the previous node's **Binary** tab and enter its field name in **Input Data Field Name**. Common values are `data` and Gmail attachment names such as `attachment_0`. Leave **File Name** blank to keep the incoming name, or map an intentional replacement. 5. Execute only the Dosya node. Inspect its output before connecting downstream steps. Upload returns `id`, `name`, `size`, `mime_type`, `version`, `is_new_version`, `workspace_id`, `folder_id`, `created_at`, `hash_verified`, `deduplicated` and `upload_method`. 6. Add branching or an error workflow for refused operations. Keep credentials and file content out of error messages; retain the HTTP status, Dosya sentence and n8n execution ID. 7. Test the same input a second time only after reviewing the side effect rules below. Confirm the result in the intended Dosya folder, then activate the workflow. ## Expected result The manual execution changes only the selected destination and returns identifiers that downstream steps can map. For an upload, `hash_verified: true` confirms that Dosya matched the supplied SHA-256; `is_new_version: true` identifies a same-name version, and `deduplicated: true` identifies replay of an idempotent request within that execution. Folder creation returns `created: false` when an existing same-name folder was reused. Share creation returns its `url`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `expires_at`, `view_only`, `access_code_required`, `access_mode` and `created_at`. Send the returned link only after checking its target and restrictions. ## Timing, retries and repeat effects - Files up to **50 MiB** (**52,428,800 bytes**) use one upload request with a checksum and a **10-minute** upload timeout. Larger files use **10 MiB** (**10,485,760-byte**) parts and are finalized after every part succeeds. - Normal requests use a **60-second** timeout. For `429`, the node honors `Retry-After` up to **30 seconds** and stops after **3 total attempts**. - Credentialed reads, including the request for a short-lived signed download URL, folder creation, and upload parts may retry a dropped connection or `502`, `503` or `504`. The separate byte fetch from that signed URL has a **10-minute** timeout and no internal retry; rerun the node after checking the failure. Folder creation is repeat-safe because the server reuses an existing name. - A one-request upload carries an idempotency key derived from execution, node, destination, file name and content. n8n's **Retry On Fail** within that execution can receive the completed upload instead of writing it twice. - **Create Share Link** is not retried after an ambiguous network failure. Check Dosya before rerunning, because another attempt can produce a second active link. - Rerunning the entire workflow creates a new execution. A repeated same-name upload becomes another version, and a repeated share step creates another URL. Activation makes future trigger events external side effects. Uploading or creating a folder can alter shared workspace state; a share URL can be opened by its recipients until it expires or is revoked. Deactivating the workflow stops new n8n runs but does not remove stored files, versions, folders or links already created. ## Common failures - **No workspace selected**, **No file selected** or **No folder selected** means the required locator resolved to an empty value. Check the expression using the failed item. - **The folder name is empty** means the name or its expression contained no usable segment. - **The access code is shorter than 8 characters** is validated before the share request; lengthen the recipient code. - A `401` becomes **dosya.dev did not accept the API key**. Replace an expired, revoked or mistyped credential. - A `403` may name the key scope, member permission, workspace pin or unsupported folder anchor. Follow the specific server sentence instead of broadening every restriction. - A `404` can mean the ID is wrong, the item was deleted or trashed, or the key cannot see it. - A `413` means the file exceeds a plan, workspace or API-key per-file ceiling. Storage-cap errors direct either the owner to billing or the workspace admin to its configured limit. ## Related guides - [Connect n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect) - [Choose webhook events](/developers/webhook-events) - [Upload files](/uploading/files-and-folders)

title: Sharing with named email recipients
summary: Send a private link to specific addresses, test the one-time-code gate, and understand what happens when someone forwards the URL.
verification: Verified the current English By email dialog, public recipient-code gate, Shared and analytics views, web/API source and focused recipient tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated local fixtures and fictional addresses. The review confirmed one restricted link for up to 50 deduplicated lower-cased addresses, generic request-code responses, 15-minute code lifetime, five wrong attempts per issued code, ten request attempts per IP window, recipient grant cookies, optional independent password checks and forwarded-link behavior. Production email delivery was not sent.
body: Use **Share → By email** and keep **Only these people can open it** selected. Dosya creates one restricted link for the listed addresses. Each recipient must enter an invited address and verify a six-digit code before the file is served. Emailing an ordinary public URL does not create this restriction. The checkbox is the setting that changes the link from public to named-recipient access. ## Before you start - Complete the file upload and confirm you can create sharing links. - Collect the exact recipient addresses. A restricted link can contain up to 50 distinct addresses. - Use fictional or disposable addresses when testing. Do not publish the final URL or recipient list. - Decide whether to add a password as a second, independent gate. A recipient-restricted and password-protected link requires both checks. ## Steps: send a private link 1. Open the file's **Share** action. 2. Select **By email**. 3. Enter an address and press **Enter**, comma or Space to add it. You can paste several addresses separated by commas, semicolons, spaces or new lines. 4. Review every address chip. Duplicate addresses are ignored after they are normalized to lowercase. 5. Keep **Only these people can open it** selected. The explanation beneath it confirms that recipients use a one-time code and that forwarding the link alone gives no one else access. 6. Choose **Expires in** and any Advanced options. Add an optional message if the recipient needs context. 7. Choose **Send**. Read the completion message, especially when it reports that some email deliveries failed. If you clear the restriction, Dosya still emails the listed people, but the resulting link is public. Anyone who receives or is forwarded that URL can open it subject to its other settings. ## Recipient verification 1. The recipient opens the emailed URL. The page says **This file was shared privately** without exposing the file itself. 2. They enter the same address that was invited and choose **Send code**. 3. The page always gives a neutral response. This prevents someone holding the URL from testing which addresses were invited. 4. The recipient checks that inbox for the six-digit code, returns to the same page and enters it within 15 minutes. 5. They choose **Verify**. A valid code creates a recipient grant for that browser, and the page reloads the share. 6. If the link also has a password, the password gate appears after email verification. ## Recipient limits and forwarded links The forwarded URL opens the same private gate. An unlisted person can request a code, but the page does not reveal whether their address is on the list and no usable code is delivered to an uninvited inbox. Possessing the URL alone is insufficient. An invited recipient can still choose to share material after legitimate access, including by downloading it when downloads are allowed or capturing what appears on screen. Recipient restriction controls admission to the Dosya link; it is not digital-rights management. ## Expected result An invited address can complete verification and open the item. An unlisted address and a person who only received a forwarded URL cannot pass the recipient gate. **Shared** identifies the link as restricted and its analytics page shows invited and verified addresses without attaching individual access-log events to a named recipient. ## Troubleshooting **The recipient did not receive a code.** Confirm the exact invited address, check spam and mail filtering, and wait briefly before retrying. The neutral page response looks the same for invited and uninvited addresses, so recheck the sender's recipient list rather than using the message as proof of delivery. **The code expired.** Request a new one. Each code is valid for 15 minutes and replaces an earlier outstanding code for that recipient. **The code is repeatedly rejected.** Check all six digits and use the latest message. Five wrong guesses exhaust an issued code; request a new one rather than continuing. Request and verification endpoints also apply IP-based throttling. **A forwarded link opened for someone else.** Check whether **Only these people can open it** was cleared when the email was sent, or whether the browser already holds a grant for an invited address. Open a fresh private window to test the first-visit behavior. **The invited person passes email verification but then sees a password prompt.** The sender enabled both recipient restriction and password protection. The recipient needs the separately shared password as well. ## Frequently asked questions ### What happens if someone forwards a private link? The new person still has to verify an invited inbox. The URL alone does not grant access. ### Why does a recipient not receive their verification code? The address may not exactly match the recipient list, the message may be filtered, or delivery may have failed. Confirm the list in the sender's link details, then request a new code after checking the inbox. ### Does sending by email always make a link private? No. Keep **Only these people can open it** selected. Clearing it sends a public link to those addresses. ## Related guides - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Adding a password to a sharing link](/sharing/password-link) - [Setting link expiry and checking the actual expiration](/sharing/link-expiry) - [Reading link access and download activity](/sharing/link-activity)

title: Finding your way around the web app
summary: Use the workspace switcher, sidebar and search to find files, uploads, sharing, team controls, integrations and settings in the Dosya web app.
verification: Verified the current English web app locally on 2026-10-12 with an isolated owner account and two sample workspaces. The capture confirmed the loaded first-run dashboard, global search, Dashboard, Files, Uploads, Shared, Vault, Team, Integrations and Settings entries, storage indicator, active workspace label and switcher actions. The UI was checked at a 1160 by 900 desktop viewport. Role-limited and narrow mobile menus were confirmed from current source and existing permission tests but were not newly captured for this article. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: The Dosya web app keeps the active workspace in the upper-left corner, common destinations in the left sidebar and search across the top. Check the workspace name before uploading, sharing or changing settings: each workspace has its own files, members, integrations and policies. The exact menu can vary with your role. An owner normally sees every workspace destination. A custom role or folder-restricted membership can hide pages or show only the content that role can reach. ## Before you start - Sign in at [app.dosya.dev](https://app.dosya.dev/) in a current browser. - If you belong to more than one workspace, know which one contains the file or team you want to manage. - Finish or skip the welcome tour if it covers the dashboard. You can still use the sidebar while an empty workspace shows its first-run upload screen. - Use the menu labels you see in your account. Ask a workspace owner when a guide names a page that your role does not show. ## Steps: navigate the web app 1. Read the workspace name above the left sidebar and switch when it is not the intended destination. 2. Choose the sidebar page that matches your task: use **Uploads** to transfer, **Files** for completed copies and **Shared** for existing sharing activity. 3. Use the top search field when you know a file or folder name but not its location. 4. Check the page title and active workspace again before creating, moving, sharing or deleting anything. 5. Use the profile control for account security and the sidebar's **Settings** entry for workspace settings. ## Read the main screen Use these areas for the matching task: | Area | What it is for | | --- | --- | | **Dashboard** | A workspace overview. An empty workspace shows the first upload and import choices; an established workspace shows storage and recent activity. | | **Files** | Browse the workspace's completed cloud files and folders. Rename, move, preview, download and organize items here when your role permits it. | | **Uploads** | Start a file or folder upload and watch transfer progress. An item can appear here before it has finished and become available in Files only after completion. | | **Shared** | Review links and other sharing activity available to your account. Use a file or folder's sharing controls to create a new link. | | **Vault** | Open encrypted Vault content. Vault has its own unlock and recovery workflow and is separate from ordinary workspace files. | | **Team** | Review members, invitations and roles for the active workspace. This entry can be hidden when your role lacks team access. | | **Integrations** | Connect imports, automation and supported file clients for the active workspace or account. | | **Settings** | Manage the active workspace's details and policies that your role can change. Account-wide profile and security controls are available from the profile menu. | The storage indicator at the bottom of the sidebar applies to the active workspace. It helps explain why an upload can fail in one workspace while another still has room. ## Files and Uploads are different Use **Uploads** to begin and monitor a transfer. Use **Files** to work with the copy that successfully reached Dosya. For example, a large file can be listed in an upload queue as queued, uploading or failed without appearing as a completed file. After the transfer finishes, open **Files** and confirm its name, size and destination. Do not treat a progress bar alone as proof that the final cloud copy is ready. See [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) for the complete workflow. ## Switch workspaces safely 1. Select the workspace name at the top of the sidebar. 2. Review **Your workspaces**. A check marks the current one; each row shows its name and available storage when that information is available. 3. Select the intended workspace. Dosya returns to its dashboard while loading that workspace's data. 4. Confirm the new workspace name above the sidebar before uploading, sharing or opening Settings. Switching workspace context does not move or copy a file. If an expected file disappears after a switch, return to the previous workspace and check its Files page before assuming it was deleted. ## Search and profile controls Use the search field across the top to look for files and folders available to your account in the current context. Search cannot reveal content your workspace role or folder restriction does not permit. The profile control in the upper-right opens account-wide actions such as profile, security and sign out. Workspace Settings in the sidebar affects the selected workspace; profile and security settings affect your signed-in account. Check which surface you are on before changing a name, session or policy. ## Navigation limits on a narrow screen On a phone-sized browser, open the navigation control to reveal the same main destinations. The sidebar may collapse to icons on an intermediate width. Use the visible page title and active workspace name to confirm where you are after opening a link. Keyboard users can move through standard links and buttons with Tab and activate them with Enter or Space. The search shortcut is displayed inside the search field on supported desktop browsers. ## Expected result The intended workspace name remains visible, the selected sidebar entry opens the matching page and searches return only items available in that workspace and role. Completed uploads appear in Files; changing workspaces updates the visible file tree without moving data. ## Troubleshooting **A menu item from this guide is missing.** Your workspace role may not allow that page. Confirm the active workspace and ask its owner which role or folder restriction applies. Vault and Integrations can also depend on account or plan availability. **Files look missing after switching.** Read the workspace name at the top of the sidebar. Switching changes the active workspace; it does not combine their file lists. **The dashboard is empty.** A new or empty workspace intentionally shows the first-run upload screen. Upload a harmless sample, import from a connected service, paste a supported URL or connect a client. **An upload is visible but the file is not.** Open Uploads and wait for a completed state or inspect the error. Then check the correct destination in Files. **Search does not find an item.** Confirm the active workspace, try the exact filename and browse the expected folder. A folder-restricted membership sees only its permitted subtree. **The page keeps loading.** Check [Dosya status](https://status.dosya.dev/), reload once and test another page. If the issue persists, contact private support with the page, time, browser and visible error; do not include a password or private share link. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does changing workspaces move my files? No. It changes which workspace the web app is showing. The files remain in their existing workspace. ### Why can another member see more menu items? Page access follows the member's role and any folder restriction. Owners and admins can expose different controls from viewers or custom roles. ### Where do I manage my account instead of the workspace? Use the profile control in the upper-right for account-wide profile and security tasks. Use **Settings** in the sidebar for the active workspace. ### Where do I create a sharing link? Open the file or folder in **Files**, then use its sharing action. See [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) or [Sharing a folder with a link](/sharing/folder-link). ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [File requests](/sharing/file-request) - [Inviting people to a workspace](/workspaces/invite-team)

title: Set notification preferences
summary: Control account-wide notification groups and delivery channels, understand always-on notices, and confirm that each switch saves across your account.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/notifications.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/group-info.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/groups.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/logic.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/query.ts. Review used local repository evidence; no production preference was changed and no notification was sent.
body: Notification settings belong to your Dosya account and cover events from all of its workspaces. They do not require a paid plan or a workspace role. Three channel switches set the broad delivery boundary; fourteen event groups decide which supported events may pass through it. ## Before you change anything Open `/profile/notifications` while signed in to the account you intend to update. Wait for the group list to load before using a switch. The page has no **Save** button: every switch writes its own account preference immediately. The **Delivery channels** controls have these effects: - **In-app** controls whether eligible personal and broadcast entries appear in the bell and notification inbox. - **Email** is the account-wide email master switch. A mandatory email can still be sent because the delivery service treats those notices as always required. - **Browser push** gates delivery to registered web browsers. Turning it off does not delete the browser’s existing push subscription. An event must also be allowed by its catalog entry and event group. **Always on** means the whole group cannot be disabled. The note “Some messages in this group are always sent and cannot be switched off.” means ordinary events obey the switch while mandatory entries bypass the group choice. Channel rules still apply to mandatory in-app and push messages; mandatory email is the documented exception. ## Steps 1. Go to **Profile > Notifications** and check the account identity in the profile area. 2. Under **Delivery channels**, leave each method on only if you want eligible events delivered there. 3. Review the event groups. Switch off a group when you do not want its optional events. 4. If **File activity** is enabled, set its nested **Uploads to your workspace** and **Daily activity summary** options separately; they ship off until you opt in. 5. After each click, pause for the request to finish. A successful write leaves the switch where you placed it. 6. Reload the page and confirm the chosen states return from the server. 7. Create one harmless event covered by an enabled group, such as a test comment on a non-sensitive file, and check only the channels that event supports. ## If a switch moves back The interface updates optimistically. When the server refuses a group write, the switch returns to its previous value and shows **Couldn’t save** with either the server error or “Your notification preference could not be saved.” A failed channel change uses the same title with “Your channel preference could not be saved.” Restore connectivity, retry that single switch, and reload to confirm the server value. Changing these settings neither deletes inbox history nor revokes browser permission. Every choice is reversible from the same page. ## Expected result Reloading **Profile > Notifications** shows the saved channel and group states. A controlled eligible event reaches only its permitted, enabled methods, while the page continues to identify any mandatory messages that cannot be muted at group level. ## Related guides - [Manage email notifications](/account/email-notifications) - [Enable browser push notifications](/account/notifications-enable-browser-push) - [Contact support](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Troubleshoot missing Dosya notifications
summary: Trace a missing Dosya alert through event eligibility, group and channel settings, browser permission, email delivery, and the in-app inbox.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/web-push.ts; apps/web/src/pages/notifications.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/notifications.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/index.ts; apps/api/src/lib/notifications/groups.ts; apps/api/src/lib/notifications/group-info.ts; apps/api/src/lib/notifications/logic.ts; apps/api/src/lib/notifications/query.ts. No live email or push delivery was performed. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: A notification can disappear at four different points: Dosya may not create that event for your account, its group may be muted, its delivery channel may be off, or the browser/email provider may block the final message. Diagnose one expected event and one channel at a time so changing a second setting does not hide the original cause. ## Steps Write down the event, affected workspace, approximate time and intended channel. Check that you are signed in to the account that should receive it. Workspace notifications follow the event's recipient rules; observing an action does not necessarily make every member a recipient. Open **Notifications** from the app and look around the event time. The first page contains up to 30 items; **Load more** appends older pages, with a server maximum of 50 items per request. If the item is in this inbox, Dosya created it and the remaining problem is specific to email or push. If it is absent, continue with the group and in-app settings before changing browser permissions. ## Check the saved Dosya controls 1. Open **Profile → Notifications**. 2. Under **Delivery channels**, confirm the required master switch: **In-app**, **Email**, or **Browser push**. 3. Find the event's group, such as **Security and sign-in**, **File activity**, **Sync and backup**, or **Integrations and API**. Turn on only the group you are testing. 4. If the group contains a child switch, inspect it separately. **Uploads to your workspace** and **Daily activity summary** are off by default even when **File activity** is enabled. 5. Leave the page, reopen **Profile → Notifications**, and verify the switch retained its value. The page saves each switch immediately. A rejected write returns the control to its prior value and shows **Couldn't save** with either **Your notification preference could not be saved.** or **Your channel preference could not be saved.** Restore connectivity, change only that switch again, then reopen the page. Repeated clicking does not make an unsaved preference persistent. Some groups show **Always on** or the note **Some messages in this group are always sent and cannot be switched off.** Mandatory messages bypass the group preference. Mandatory email also bypasses the Email channel switch, while mandatory in-app and push messages still respect their channel switches. Do not use a security message as a harmless delivery test. ## When browser push is missing Browser push requires all of these conditions: the event permits push, its effective preference is on, **Browser push** is enabled, the browser granted notification permission, and the current browser has a registered push subscription. Select **Enable browser notifications**. The expected success is **Browser notifications enabled**. Use the displayed result to choose the next action: - **Permission denied — Allow notifications in your browser settings** means the site-level browser permission is blocked. Allow notifications for the Dosya app origin in browser settings, reload Dosya, and select the button again. - **Not supported — This browser can't receive web push** means this browser context lacks the service-worker or PushManager support Dosya needs. Test a supported, non-private browser profile. - A successful registration applies to that browser profile. Another browser or device needs its own permission and subscription. An operating-system focus mode or notification policy can still hide a push banner after the browser accepts it. Check the browser's notification permission first, then the operating-system notification list and focus settings. ## When email is missing Confirm the account email under **Profile → Identity** and make sure it is the address you are checking. Search all mail, spam, quarantine and organization filtering for the event time and Dosya sender. Mail forwarding and corporate gateways can delay or reject a message after Dosya hands it off. If the same event appears in the in-app inbox but no email arrives, do not repeatedly recreate the underlying action. Preserve the inbox time and title. For optional mail, recheck the group plus **Email** channel. For an always-on email, preference changes are not the explanation; investigate the destination address and mail filtering. ## Expected result Use a safe event of the same type when one is naturally available. Record its time, then confirm it appears only in the channels currently enabled for that event. Reopen the preferences page after the test so a temporary visual switch is not mistaken for a server-confirmed setting. If the alert remains absent, open a private support ticket with the event name, workspace, account email, local time and timezone, expected channel, browser/app version and whether the item appears in the in-app inbox. Exclude passwords, two-factor codes, API keys, private links and confidential file content. ## Related guides - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Manage email notifications](/account/email-notifications) - [Manage mobile permissions](/account/mobile-permissions)

title: Understand always-on Dosya notifications
summary: Identify mandatory notification types, understand which group and channel switches they bypass, and verify why required email can still arrive.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/notifications/logic.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/group-info.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/catalog.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/prefs.ts, apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, and notification logic tests. No production preference was changed.
body: Some notification catalog entries are mandatory because Dosya must preserve evidence that critical account, security, billing, or moderation information was sent. The settings API identifies groups containing these entries. ## Steps 1. Open **Settings → Notifications** on mobile or **Profile → Notifications** on web. 2. Read each group’s note. A group made entirely of mandatory entries shows **Always on** instead of a switch. A mixed group says **Some messages in this group are always sent and cannot be switched off.** 3. Adjust optional groups or channels separately. A mandatory entry bypasses its group switch. 4. Keep a valid email address on the account for required mail. Mandatory email ignores the Email channel switch; it covers cases such as password changes, payment failure, scheduled account deletion, or content removal. 5. For push and in-app delivery, channel switches still apply to mandatory entries. Turning those transports off can suppress their copy there, while required email remains deliverable. The “always on” rule attaches to notification types, not every message in a named group. Team, sharing, and integrations can contain mandatory items alongside optional ones, so a disabled group may still produce only its required entries. The server returns this profile dynamically; clients do not maintain their own hard-coded list. ## Expected result Settings accurately distinguishes fully mandatory, partly mandatory, and optional groups. Optional traffic follows your group/channel choices, while required email may arrive regardless of the Email master switch. ## Troubleshooting **A message arrived from a muted group.** Check its subject and the group note. It may be a mandatory type that intentionally skips the group gate. **Mandatory push did not arrive.** Mandatory does not override Push being off, OS denial, or an unregistered device. Read the inbox/email and repair device registration separately. **There is no switch beside a group.** **Always on** is the control state for an all-mandatory group; it is not a loading failure. ## Related guides - [Configure optional topics around required notices](/account/notification-preferences) - [Review security notifications](/account/security-notifications)

title: Choose notification delivery channels
summary: Configure in-app, email, and push delivery separately, understand their account and device scope, and avoid disabling every notification path.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 using apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/groups.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/push.ts, apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/notifications.ts, and delivery-gate tests. Production delivery was not exercised.
body: Dosya exposes three account delivery channels: **In-app**, **Email**, and **Push notifications** on mobile (**Browser push** on web). Each transport has a separate master switch. ## Steps 1. Open notification settings and wait for current server values to load. 2. Use **In-app** to control inbox visibility. The mobile screen currently warns **With In-app off, no notifications are delivered at all - email and push included.** Source behavior is narrower: Email and Push are planned independently and can still deliver when their own switches and group allow them. 3. Set **Email** for mail sent to the account address. Mandatory email can still bypass this switch. 4. Set **Push notifications** on mobile. The account value applies across delivery logic, while enabling it also registers this device after OS permission. On web, use **Browser push** and **Enable browser notifications** for that browser subscription. 5. Reload the page/screen and confirm the switches retain their server values before testing an event. Channel rows default to enabled when the user has never stored a choice. Event groups then supply per-channel defaults: every group defaults on in-app, while only selected groups default to email or push. A saved group choice overrides its defaults, except mandatory entries and the two explicit file opt-ins. Push settings do not replace OS/browser permission. Disabling mobile Push unregisters this device best-effort; another registered device may still receive account push while the channel remains enabled again. ## Expected result New optional notifications use only the enabled transport combination permitted by their event group. The inbox, mail, and device/browser alert can therefore differ without representing duplicate or lost cloud files. ## Troubleshooting **The inbox stopped but email or push continued.** That matches server behavior even though the mobile warning says otherwise. Re-enable In-app to make eligible rows visible again. **Browser permission was denied.** Web reports **Permission denied** and **Allow notifications in your browser settings**. Unsupported browsers show **Not supported** and **This browser can't receive web push**. **Mobile push is enabled but silent.** Review OS permission and registration on a physical device. The saved account channel alone does not create a platform token. ## Related guides - [Choose account delivery transports](/account/notification-preferences) - [Review security notifications](/account/security-notifications)

title: Troubleshoot an empty notification inbox
summary: Explain an empty notification inbox by checking account scope, in-app delivery, dismissal, expiry, pagination, and connectivity before retesting.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/notifications.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/query.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/inbox.ts, and inbox/query tests. No production notification record was inspected or dismissed.
body: An empty inbox can mean there are no visible messages, every row was dismissed, the **In-app** channel is off, or the current account has no eligible notification. It does not prove that all workspaces are quiet. ## Steps 1. Confirm the email on the mobile Settings card or web profile. Notification history is account-wide and never transfers between accounts. 2. On mobile, tap the bell; **You're all caught up.** appears when the merged list returns no rows. The web full page uses **Nothing here yet.** 3. Open notification settings and check **In-app**. When disabled, personal and broadcast inbox queries exclude rows. The stored record and separately enabled Email or Push delivery can still exist. 4. Review event groups. Muted broadcasts are omitted, and optional personal events may never have been written. 5. Restore connectivity and reopen the inbox. Mobile requests 30 newest rows and loads older pages near the list end; web can use **Load more**. 6. Trigger one harmless eligible event from a second account or member, then refresh/focus the client. The server excludes personal notices whose expiry time has passed and any row with a dismissal timestamp. Active broadcasts are also filtered by the account’s group opt-out and dismissal state. Marking a row read does not remove it; using the close/dismiss control does. ## Expected result The inbox either receives the controlled event or the checks isolate account, channel, group, expiry, dismissal, or connectivity as the reason it remains empty. ## Troubleshooting **The bell count is zero but rows exist.** Read rows remain visible without contributing to the unread summary. **Mark all read** changes count, not retention. **A workspace switch did nothing.** The inbox is scoped to the user, not the active workspace. Resource navigation may still require switching context after opening a notice. **A test event appears by email only.** Mandatory mail can bypass the Email preference, while In-app or Push remains disabled. Use an optional event when testing ordinary channel behavior. ## Related guides - [Restore inbox-producing preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Trace why the notification list is blank](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Enable browser push notifications
summary: Grant browser permission, register a secure web-push subscription, align Dosya channel settings, and diagnose denied or unsupported states safely.
verification: Reviewed 2026-10-14 using apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/web-push.ts, apps/web/public/sw.js, apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/push/subscribe.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/push.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/logic.ts. Browser permission was not requested and no production push subscription or delivery was created.
body: Browser push needs two independent approvals: the browser must grant notification permission and Dosya must register that browser to the signed-in account. Delivery then requires the **Browser push** master switch, an eligible event group, and a catalog entry that supports push. ## Requirements Use the signed-in web app in a browser that exposes both a service worker and **PushManager**. Service workers require a secure context in normal browser operation. The account plan and workspace role do not affect registration. If the browser has already blocked notifications for Dosya, its permission prompt may not reappear. Change the site permission in browser settings first, then return to the web app. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile > Notifications** in the browser and account that should receive alerts. 2. Under **Delivery channels**, turn on **Browser push**. This switch controls delivery but does not itself create a browser subscription. 3. Select **Enable browser notifications**. 4. In the browser prompt, choose **Allow**. 5. Wait for Dosya to obtain its application key, create a user-visible push subscription, and register the endpoint to your account. 6. Confirm the success toast **Browser notifications enabled**. 7. Keep the required event group enabled and trigger one harmless event whose catalog entry supports push. Registration stores the endpoint, encryption keys, and up to the first 80 characters of the browser user-agent as the device name. Re-registering the same endpoint for the same account refreshes its keys and clears a prior revocation. An endpoint already owned by a different account is rejected rather than reassigned. ## Permission and delivery failures - **Permission denied** with “Allow notifications in your browser settings” means the permission result was not `granted`. - **Not supported** with “This browser can’t receive web push” means service-worker or PushManager support is absent. - A server without a configured public push key returns **Push not configured**. Registration can also fail for missing fields, an unsupported endpoint host, or an endpoint tied to another account. Dosya submits web-push messages with a 60-second time-to-live. Delivery is best effort; closing the app is supported, but a push service or offline device can miss that short window. A 404 or 410 response from a push provider causes the stored subscription to be revoked automatically, after which enabling again creates or refreshes the live registration. Selecting an operating-system notification closes it, focuses the first existing Dosya window and navigates to the event path, or opens a new window. When no path is supplied, it goes to `/notifications`. Turning off **Browser push** stops eligible delivery without revoking browser permission or unsubscribing the endpoint. To remove site permission, use the browser’s settings; this action is reversible by granting it again. ## Expected result The browser grants notification access, Dosya confirms registration, and a push-eligible controlled event produces an operating-system notification for this account. Selecting it opens the stored destination or the notification inbox fallback. ## Related guides - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Choose which event groups notify you](/account/notifications-event-groups) - [Review security notifications](/account/security-notifications)

title: Choose which event groups notify you
summary: Configure all 14 notification groups, two high-volume opt-ins, per-channel defaults, and mandatory events from one account settings page clearly.
verification: Reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/notifications/groups.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/group-info.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/prefs.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/logic.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/notifications.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx. No production event was triggered and no user preference was written.
body: Dosya organizes roughly 100 granular notification types into 14 switches so related account events share one preference. The page renders the server’s current labels and effective values, and each click saves only the key you changed. ## The 14 groups - **Security and sign-in**: sign-ins, failed attempts, passwords, email, and two-factor changes. - **Account**: account or workspace deletion, ownership transfers, and workspace settings. - **Team and permissions**: invitations, membership, roles, and permission changes. - **Billing and storage**: payments, plans, renewals, and storage limits. - **File activity**: uploads, deletion, versions, and locks on files you own. - **Share links**: views, downloads, and link expiry. - **File requests**: received uploads and approaching deadlines. - **Comments**: new comments and replies on your files. - **Sync and backup**: failures, stopped devices, conflicts, and phone backup. - **Imports and transfers**: cloud imports, remote downloads, and connection problems. - **Integrations and API**: API keys, S3 credentials, and webhook health. - **Support and legal**: ticket replies, copyright, and moderation actions. - **Product updates**: features, improvements, and tips. - **System**: scheduled maintenance and service incidents. All groups default to in-app eligibility. Email initially applies to security, account, team, billing, requests, sync, support, and system. Push initially applies to security, billing, sync, support, and system. The event’s catalog may allow fewer channels, and the three **Delivery channels** master switches can suppress a method globally. ## High-volume options Two **File activity** types remain off until selected individually: - **Uploads to your workspace** sends at most one folder summary per hour when other people add files. - **Daily activity summary** sends one morning message counting the previous day’s renames and moves. Their sub-switches are disabled while **File activity** is off. Re-enabling the group does not silently enable either nested option. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile > Notifications** and wait until the server-provided groups appear. 2. Read the description and any italic always-on note for the category you intend to change. 3. Toggle that group. The interface updates immediately while a one-key request saves the value. 4. For **File activity**, enable the group before choosing either nested opt-in. 5. Reload the route and confirm the effective values returned by the account API. 6. Generate a harmless event in the selected category and verify only an allowed, enabled channel receives it. ## Mandatory and failed saves **Always on** replaces a switch when every catalog entry in that group is mandatory. When only some are mandatory, the optional entries follow your choice but the page warns that some messages cannot be switched off. Mandatory email is sent even if its group or Email channel is disabled; mandatory push and in-app delivery still respect their channel master switch. On a rejected write, Dosya restores the prior toggle and displays **Couldn’t save**. Retry only the affected row after connectivity returns. No category change deletes existing inbox records, and every stored preference can be reversed later. ## Expected result The selected group and nested-option values persist after refresh. New optional activity follows the group, per-type, catalog, and channel gates, while mandatory behavior remains accurately labelled beside the affected category. ## Related guides - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Manage email notifications](/account/email-notifications) - [Review security notifications](/account/security-notifications)

title: Fix notification preferences that revert
summary: Fix a notification switch that reverts by checking optimistic saves, session and network errors, device registration, and the server-confirmed value.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 with apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/api.ts, apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/notifications.ts, and preference endpoint tests. No production switch was toggled.
body: Notification switches move immediately, then Dosya saves one key to the server. If that request fails, the client restores the prior value rather than pretending the change persisted. ## Steps 1. Verify the account email and open notification settings with a stable connection. 2. Change only one group or channel. Mobile uses an optimistic overlay; web also moves the switch before the PUT response. 3. Watch for **Couldn't save. Try again.** on mobile, or web’s **Couldn't save** toast with the server error. 4. If no error appears, leave and reopen settings to force a fresh GET from `/api/me/notifications`. 5. For Push, also check device permission. The server channel is saved before mobile registration. An OS denial returns normally, shows the settings toast, and refreshes the query; it does not roll back the saved account value or explicitly remove the optimistic overlay. 6. Retry after restoring the authenticated session or network. Avoid rapidly toggling several values while diagnosing one failed write. The endpoint accepts partial maps and stores only recognized channels, 14 group keys, or supported `type:` opt-ins. An API key cannot change these account settings; the route requires session authentication. Clients intentionally send one changed key per request to avoid overwriting edits from another open session. ## Expected result Reopening the screen shows the intended server-confirmed value. For Push, the OS permission and device registration also agree with the account channel. ## Troubleshooting **The value returns immediately.** The save call failed and the optimistic UI rolled back. Reauthenticate if needed, reconnect, and repeat the single edit. **Push says enabled after permission denial.** Open device settings, allow notifications, then toggle Push off/on. The channel save and native registration are separate operations. **Another device changed the setting.** Refresh both sessions. Partial writes prevent a stale screen from intentionally sending its whole old map, but the latest successful write to the same key wins. ## Related guides - [Review the preference model after rollback](/account/notification-preferences) - [Test delivery after a saved setting](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Load older Dosya notifications
summary: Append the next 30-item cursor page, understand when Load more disappears, and recover when older account notifications do not appear in the inbox.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/notifications.tsx, apps/web/src/api/notifications.ts, apps/web/src/lib/notifications.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/query.ts. The pagination review made no production API call and did not mark or dismiss a user notification.
body: The full notification page fetches 30 items at a time. **Load more** requests entries created strictly before the final timestamp in the current page, merges personal and broadcast notices by newest first, and appends the returned page to what is already visible. ## Before you begin Open `/notifications` for the correct signed-in account. The list spans that account’s eligible notices across workspaces; changing the active workspace does not create a separate history. No plan or workspace permission controls this account page. The server omits dismissed items, expired personal notices, and entries hidden by the **In-app** channel preference. Broadcasts also respect the relevant muted event group. Those filters can make the available history shorter than expected. ## Steps 1. Select the bell labelled **Notifications**, then choose **See all**. 2. Wait for the initial page to finish. The newest eligible items appear first under **Today** and **Earlier**, based on the browser’s local midnight. 3. Scroll below the current list and select **Load more**. 4. While the request runs, confirm the button reads **Loading…** and is disabled. 5. Wait for older entries to append beneath the existing items. 6. Repeat until the control disappears. The page removes it after the server returns no next cursor. The web client does not expose a page-size selector. Although the API accepts a limit of up to 50, this screen always requests its default batch of 30. Loading another page is read-only: it does not mark those items read or dismiss them. ## If the next page is missing When **Load more** is absent, the current result has no next cursor. If you expected an older item, first check whether it was dismissed, expired, blocked by **In-app**, or muted by its group. If the button changes back after a connection failure but nothing appends, restore the network and select it again; the current page remains visible. Reloading starts again from the newest 30 entries. The cursor comparison is timestamp-based and asks for records strictly older than the last returned item. If pagination repeatedly skips or repeats an identifiable notice, record its displayed time and title before contacting support. ## Expected result Each successful selection adds an older chronological page below the current notifications without changing their read state. After the oldest eligible result, **Load more** is no longer shown. ## Related guides - [Open the Dosya notification inbox](/account/notifications-open-inbox) - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Troubleshoot notifications](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Narrow optional notification event groups
summary: Narrow all 14 notification groups and two opt-in file alerts while preserving mandatory messages and understanding their per-channel delivery defaults.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 using apps/api/src/lib/notifications/groups.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/group-info.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/prefs.ts, apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, and group preference tests. Production preferences remained unchanged.
body: Dosya describes **14** event groups from the server so mobile, web, and desktop present the same choices: Security and sign-in, Account, Team and permissions, Billing and storage, File activity, Share links, File requests, Comments, Sync and backup, Imports and transfers, Integrations and API, Support and legal, Product updates, and System. ## Steps 1. Open notification settings and scroll to **What you hear about**. 2. Turn off the broad group that produces unwanted optional traffic. A disabled group is the master mute for its nested optional switches. 3. In **File activity**, configure the narrower choices **Uploads to your workspace** and **Daily activity summary** if shown. Both are off by default and must be opted into separately. 4. Read any always-on note before assuming the group is silent. Mandatory entries bypass the group switch. 5. Reopen settings to confirm the server’s effective value, then test one event that belongs to the changed group. **Uploads to your workspace** batches one summary per folder per hour when other people add files. **Daily activity summary** counts yesterday’s renames and moves each morning. Turning File activity off suppresses these even if their sub-switch is on; turning the group back on does not automatically opt them in. Stored group choices override per-channel defaults for ordinary types. Channel master switches still decide whether an allowed event uses in-app, email, or push. Mandatory email remains the stated exception. ## Expected result Only optional events in the muted group stop. Other groups retain their values, nested file opt-ins keep honest states, and mandatory notices remain identified by their server-provided note. ## Troubleshooting **A sub-switch is disabled.** Its parent group is off. Enable the group before changing the narrower option. **Uploads still do not notify after enabling File activity.** Turn on **Uploads to your workspace** itself; the group’s on-state does not override that type’s off-by-default rule. **A required notice still arrived.** That is expected for a mandatory catalog entry. Use the group note and delivery-channel guide to understand which transport can be disabled. ## Related guides - [Tune individual notification topics](/account/notification-preferences) - [Check muted group delivery](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Open a notification in the correct workspace
summary: Open a notification safely when several workspaces exist, verify the active context, and recover when membership or resource visibility changed.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/src/files/WorkspaceSwitcher.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/workspaceStore.ts, apps/mobile/app/notifications.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/actionPath.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/query.ts, and workspace-switch tests. No production resource was opened.
body: Notification history belongs to the account, while files, teams, shares, and permissions belong to individual workspaces. Confirm context before acting when names repeat across workspaces. ## Steps 1. Check the signed-in email in Settings or Profile before opening the notice. 2. Read the notification title/body for a workspace or resource name. The inbox itself is not filtered by the workspace currently shown in the header. 3. Tap the workspace name and choose the expected entry under **Your workspaces**. The phone displays **Switching workspace…** for two seconds while queries refresh. 4. Return to the notification and open its supported action or row destination. 5. Compare the file/team/share name with the selected workspace before editing, downloading, or dismissing any resource-specific warning. Mobile route mapping converts `/files/:id` to its file screen and supports Files, Shares, Teams, Workspaces, Profile, Notifications, and the Vault root. The route itself does not grant access. Current membership, folder confinement, locks, hidden-item rules, and role permissions are checked by the destination APIs. Choosing the same workspace is a no-op and shows no splash. If no active workspace is stored, the app displays and persists the first returned membership; that fallback can be wrong for a notification from another workspace, so inspect the name. ## Expected result The resource opens under the intended account and workspace, or access is refused without exposing content from a workspace the user cannot reach. ## Troubleshooting **The notification opens a different-looking file list.** Check the workspace header; account-wide inbox rows can reference another membership than the active one. **The workspace is absent.** Membership may have ended or the current account is wrong. Review **My workspaces** before requesting a new invitation. **The route opens but the item is unavailable.** It may have been moved, trashed, hidden, locked, or purged after the notification was created. Ask a current workspace owner to verify its state. ## Related guides - [Review settings for cross-workspace notices](/account/notification-preferences) - [Resolve notification workspace mismatch](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Open the Dosya notification inbox
summary: Use the notification bell and full inbox, interpret unread and empty states, and avoid dismissing account activity you still need before it disappears.
verification: Reviewed and validated 2026-10-14 from apps/web/src/components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx, apps/web/src/components/notifications/notification-card.tsx, apps/web/src/stores/notifications.ts, apps/web/src/pages/notifications.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/query.ts. Inspection was read-only and did not open, read, or dismiss anything in a production inbox.
body: The bell’s popover provides a recent account-level view; **See all** opens the complete paginated inbox. Both surfaces combine eligible activity across the signed-in account rather than filtering to the currently selected workspace. ## What the bell shows The trigger is labelled **Notifications**. Its badge displays the unread total and caps the visible number at **99+**. Opening it loads recent entries grouped as **Today** and **Earlier** using the device’s local date boundary. The popover contains **Mark all read**, **See all**, and **Settings**. **Mark all read** immediately clears the local badge and records all current account notifications as read, including older pages that are not loaded on screen; there is no control to restore unread status. **Settings** opens `/profile/notifications`. Selecting a card with a destination marks that item read and navigates to its stored path. A card’s **Dismiss** button, or a dismiss action inside it, removes the entry from the inbox with no undo control. Review the title, body, actor, and destination before dismissing important security, billing, or sharing activity. ## Steps 1. Confirm the account from the avatar menu, then select the bell whose accessible label is **Notifications**. 2. Wait while the popover says **Loading…**. If no entries qualify, it changes to **You’re all caught up 🎉**. 3. Review unread dots, relative times such as **just now**, **5m**, **2h**, or **3d**, and the day grouping. 4. Choose **See all** to open `/notifications`. 5. Let the newest page load. A full-page empty result says **Nothing here yet.** 6. Select a notification only when you want to follow its destination and mark it read. 7. Use **Load more** below a non-empty page when older eligible entries remain. ## If activity is absent Check **Profile > Notifications** and make sure **In-app** is enabled. The inbox query hides dismissed records, expired personal entries, and broadcasts muted through their group preference. A transient summary or list failure keeps the previous client state, so reconnect and reopen the bell before changing settings. Opening either inbox surface alone does not mark every entry read. Only card navigation, **Mark all read**, or an explicit action changes state. ## Expected result The bell displays the current unread count and recent eligible activity; **See all** opens a newest-first account history with day labels and pagination. No read or dismissal state changes until you invoke the corresponding control. ## Related guides - [Load older Dosya notifications](/account/notifications-load-older) - [Choose which event groups notify you](/account/notifications-event-groups) - [Troubleshoot notifications](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Open the resource linked from a notification
summary: Follow supported notification destinations on mobile, understand mark-read behavior and hidden actions, and recover from removed or inaccessible resources.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 with apps/mobile/app/notifications.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/actionPath.ts, apps/mobile/src/notifications/remote.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/logic.ts, and notification action tests. No production link or resource was followed.
body: A notification link is a pointer, not an access grant. Mobile validates its route mapping and the destination checks current account/workspace authorization again. ## Steps 1. Open **Notifications** and read the actor, body, and timestamp for the relevant row. 2. Tap the row. Dosya immediately marks unread state locally and sends the read update in the background. 3. For supported routes, verify the destination: a file, Files root, Shares, Teams, Workspaces, Profile, Notifications, or Vault root. 4. If the row contains an explicit action, use it only after reading the label. Up to two catalog actions may be present; unsupported navigate targets are omitted on mobile. 5. Return to the inbox and confirm the unread dot is gone. Use the close icon only if you also want to dismiss the notice. Internal destinations must begin with one `/`; protocol-relative `//` links are rejected. The server catalog may permit HTTPS for web/system messages, but mobile has no external-route mapping and falls back to the inbox for a tapped push. A row whose route cannot be mapped is still marked read but stays in place. Read and dismiss requests are optimistic. If a request fails, the phone drops its local overlay and refetches server state. Neither operation changes the underlying file, share link, request, bill, or membership. ## Expected result A valid supported link opens the current authorized resource and clears unread state. Unsupported or stale destinations fail closed without navigating to an untrusted scheme. ## Troubleshooting **Nothing happens after tapping the row.** The link likely lacks a mobile equivalent. Use web/desktop for that notice, or open the related area manually. **The file screen denies access.** The event can remain after a file is deleted or permissions change. Confirm workspace membership and current resource status. **The unread dot returns.** The background read request failed.
