Restore connectivity and tap the row again; server state is authoritative. ## Related guides - [Control resource-notification topics](/account/notification-preferences) - [Recover a notification destination](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Fix a notification preference that will not save
summary: Recover from “Couldn’t save” by retrying one notification setting, verifying the signed-in session, and confirming the value after a fresh server read.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/notification-settings.tsx, apps/mobile/src/notifications/api.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/notifications.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/groups.ts, and preference failure tests. No production account setting was written.
body: A notification preference is saved only after the authenticated PUT succeeds. The exact mobile fallback error is **Couldn't save. Try again.**; the web toast title is **Couldn't save**. ## Steps 1. Confirm the signed-in account and reopen notification settings. If the page says **Couldn't load notification settings.**, select **Retry** before attempting edits. 2. Change one switch. Do not use an API key: `/api/me/notifications` requires a session because it changes account behavior rather than file access. 3. If the value rolls back, restore connectivity and verify the session has not expired. Then retry that same switch once. 4. Leave and reopen the screen. GET returns the effective server state for all 14 groups, nested opt-ins, and three channels. 5. For a Push failure, separately verify OS permission and physical-device support. A native registration error can occur after the account channel was already saved. The endpoint ignores unknown keys. It batches valid preference/channel rows and records a profile update audit event. Missing stored rows use documented defaults; therefore a reloaded value may be a default rather than a database row, but it is still the behavior delivery uses. ## Expected result The edited switch survives a fresh settings load and controls later eligible notifications. No file, share, workspace role, or existing inbox row changes during the preference write. ## Troubleshooting **The screen never leaves its load error.** Reauthenticate or check API connectivity, then press **Retry**. Editing is unavailable until the server list arrives. **The message contains a specific server error.** Resolve that condition first; mobile displays an `Error.message` instead of replacing it with the generic fallback. **Only Push still fails.** A saved account setting is insufficient without a platform token. Repair OS permission and toggle Push again on a physical, configured build. ## Related guides - [Edit notification preferences from scratch](/account/notification-preferences) - [Review security notifications](/account/security-notifications)

title: Recover browser push after denying permission
summary: Restore Dosya browser push after a denial by changing site permission, re-registering the browser, and checking both delivery switches safely.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/lib/web-push.ts, apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/push/subscribe.ts. Production delivery was not exercised.
body: Browser push needs three things at once: browser support for service workers and PushManager, permission for the Dosya site, and Dosya's **Browser push** delivery channel. A previous denial blocks the permission request before Dosya can create a subscription. ## Steps 1. In the browser's site settings for app.dosya.dev, change **Notifications** from **Block** to **Allow**. Browser wording differs; use the per-site permission, not a system-wide setting for every website. 2. Reload Dosya. Open **Profile → Notifications** and leave **Browser push** switched on under **Delivery channels**. 3. Select **Enable browser notifications**. A successful registration shows **Browser notifications enabled**. 4. If Dosya shows **Permission denied — Allow notifications in your browser settings**, recheck the site rule and reload. **Not supported — This browser can't receive web push** means this browser lacks the required APIs; use email or in-app delivery instead. 5. Trigger a harmless event that the notification catalog sends by push, then keep the tab and the operating system's notification settings available while testing. Changing the Dosya channel switch does not repair a browser denial. Conversely, allowing the site does not turn on a Dosya channel you switched off. Re-enabling creates or refreshes the browser subscription for the signed-in account; an endpoint already owned by another account is rejected. ## Expected result The site permission reads **Allow**, **Browser push** remains on, and **Enable browser notifications** completes without an error. A later push-eligible event can reach that browser. Push is best effort, so confirm the same event in the Dosya notification inbox if the operating system suppresses its banner. ## Related guides - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Troubleshoot notifications](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Read notification groups by day
summary: Use Today, Earlier, relative times, unread dots, and Load more to review Dosya notifications in the order the account received them, page by page.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/notifications.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/notifications.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/notifications/index.ts. Production inbox data was not inspected.
body: The notification inbox merges personal notices with active broadcasts and sorts the combined list newest first. The first request returns 30 items; the service accepts at most 50 per page, while the web client uses **Load more** to request the next 30. ## Steps 1. Open the bell and choose the full **Notifications** view. 2. Read **Today** first. Its boundary is midnight in your browser's local time zone, so a notification can change groups when the device clock or time zone changes. 3. Use **Earlier** for every older item currently loaded. The interface does not create separate Yesterday or calendar-date groups. 4. Interpret the small time as elapsed time: **just now**, minutes such as 8m, hours such as 3h, or whole days such as 2d. 5. An unread item has a green dot. Opening an item with a destination marks it read and navigates to that path. **Dismiss** removes it from the visible inbox; dismissal is different from reading. 6. Select **Load more** until the button disappears when you need older history. Items that expired, were dismissed, or are hidden by an off **In-app** channel are not returned. The two day headings describe when the notification row was created, not when an email arrived or a push banner appeared. Delivery transports are independent and can complete at different times. ## Expected result Loaded notices appear in descending creation order under **Today** or **Earlier**. The next page appends below the existing list without reshuffling the day rule, and **Load more** vanishes once the server returns no cursor. An empty eligible inbox displays **Nothing here yet.** ## Related guides - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Troubleshoot notifications](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Verify email notification delivery
summary: Check Dosya's Email channel, event rules, inbox placement, and mandatory notices to distinguish an opt-out from a delivery failure or provider delay.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/notifications.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/notify.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/email/notification-template.ts. No production email was sent.
body: Dosya has no **Send test email** control. It sends email only when the event's catalog entry includes email and the account permits that channel. Some security and account notices are mandatory: they are emailed even when the **Email** channel or their group is off, and their footer says the notice cannot be unsubscribed from. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Notifications → Delivery channels** and verify that **Email** is on for ordinary mail. 2. Find the event's group below the channel switches. Turn that group on; a nested option is effective only while its parent group is enabled. Groups marked **Always on** cannot be disabled, and a note identifies groups containing some mandatory events. 3. Generate one safe event whose documented channels include email. Do not use a browser-push-only or in-app-only event as an email test. 4. Check the inbox for the address shown in **Profile → Identity**, then inspect spam, junk, promotions, quarantine, and organization mail rules. Catalog mail uses the event-specific subject and a Dosya notification layout. 5. Compare the Dosya in-app notice with the email. Each transport is attempted independently: an inbox row can exist even if the email provider rejects or delays the message. 6. If a mandatory security notice is absent from email but present in Dosya, record the event time, account address, and notification title before contacting support. Switches save immediately. A failed save restores the previous position and shows **Couldn't save** with either the server error or **Your channel preference could not be saved.** ## Expected result A mail-enabled event reaches the current account email when its ordinary channel and group gates are on. Mandatory security/account mail can arrive regardless of those preferences and has no unsubscribe link. Dosya does not expose a delivery receipt to the recipient, so the inbox comparison and mail-provider search are the practical checks. ## Related guides - [Set notification preferences](/account/notification-preferences) - [Troubleshoot notifications](/troubleshooting/notifications)

title: Organizing files with folders, favourites and groups
summary: Use folders for file location, favourites for quick access and personal groups to collect related files and folders without moving them.
verification: Verified the current English Files page and current web/API source on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use an isolated local owner workspace with controlled current-API fixtures and fictional files. The review confirmed folder creation, file favourites, personal group creation, adding a file or folder to a group, group counts and expanded contents, and that deleting a group removes only the group. Creating, deleting and reorganizing the fixture through the production service was not performed. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Open **Files** in the intended workspace, then choose the organizer that matches the job. A folder determines where an item lives. A favourite gives you a quick link to a file. A group collects related files and folders from different locations without moving or copying them. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace in the upper-left workspace switcher. Folders, favourites and groups shown on the page belong to that workspace context. - Use non-confidential sample items while learning the controls. - Make sure your role can create folders if you need a new location. The available actions follow your workspace permissions. - Decide whether you need to change storage location or only create a shortcut. Use a folder for location; use a favourite or group for quick access. - Keep names short and distinct enough to recognize in the sidebar. ## Choose the right organizer | Organizer | What it changes | Best use | | --- | --- | --- | | Folder | The item's location in the workspace hierarchy | Project structure, ownership boundaries and predictable paths | | Favourite | Adds a file shortcut under **Favourites** for your account | A file you open often | | Group | Adds a file or folder to your personal collection without changing its location | A task or project that spans several folders | ## Steps: create a folder 1. Browse to the location that should contain the new folder. Use the home icon to return to the workspace root. 2. Choose **New folder**. 3. Enter a folder name. The creation field can also accept a path such as `Projects/Q4/Designs` when you need nested folders. 4. Choose **Create** and wait for the folder to appear. 5. Move existing items into it or upload new items while that folder is open. A folder changes the real path of items placed inside it. Moving an item later is a separate action. ## Steps: add or remove a favourite 1. Find the file in Files. 2. Right-click its row or open its three-dot menu. 3. Choose **Add to favourites**. 4. Confirm that the file appears under **Favourites** in the Files sidebar and has a star beside its name. 5. Select the favourite to open the file quickly. 6. To remove the shortcut, open the file menu and choose **Remove favourite**, or use the remove control beside the sidebar entry. Removing a favourite does not delete, move or rename the file. The current web Files menu offers favourites for files; use a group when you need a shortcut to a folder. ## Steps: create and fill a group 1. Under **Groups** in the Files sidebar, choose the **+** button. 2. Enter a name and choose a colour. The colour is a visual marker, not an access rule. 3. Choose **Create group**. 4. Find a file or folder you want to collect. 5. Right-click it or open its three-dot menu, then choose **Add to group**. 6. Select the target group. Repeat for other files or folders, even when they live in different workspace folders. 7. Choose the group name in the sidebar to open its flat Files view. Use the chevron beside the group to expand its contents in the sidebar. ## Expected result Folders show the workspace hierarchy in the main Files list. Favourite files appear under **Favourites**. Groups appear under **Groups**, show an item count and can expand to display their collected files and folders. Opening a group gives you one flat view of its members. Their original folder locations remain unchanged, and each group entry still refers to the original item rather than a second stored copy. ## Limits and permission behavior - Favourites and groups are personal organizers. They do not change another member's permissions or expose an item the member cannot otherwise access. - Adding an item to a group does not duplicate its bytes or consume storage again. - Deleting a group removes the group and its membership entries. The files and folders inside remain in their original locations. - A hidden item or an item inside a folder you can no longer open can disappear from favourites or groups until it becomes visible to you again. - A group is a flat collection, so it is not a destination folder. Uploading or creating a folder from a group view uses the workflow shown by the app and enrolls the completed item in that group. - A group name can contain up to 100 characters. Folder names and paths use their own validation rules. ## Troubleshooting **Add to favourites is missing.** Confirm you opened a file menu in the live Files view. The current web workflow uses favourites for files. For a folder shortcut, add the folder to a group. **The group list is empty.** Create a group with the **+** button first, then reopen **Add to group** on the file or folder. **The item did not move.** This is expected when you add a favourite or group entry. Use **Move to...** when the item's actual folder should change. **A favourite or group item disappeared.** Check the active workspace and your access to the original item. Hidden, deleted, locked or permission-restricted content is not exposed through an organizer shortcut. **Deleting a group did not delete its files.** This is intentional. A group contains references. Delete or move the original items from Files when that is the intended action. **The sidebar is too narrow or hidden.** On desktop, expand the Files sidebar with its chevron. On a smaller screen, use the available Files navigation and item menus; the layout can place sidebar tools behind compact navigation. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does adding a file to a group move it? No. The original stays in its folder. The group adds a personal reference to the same item. ### Do favourites create another copy? No. A favourite is a shortcut to the existing file and consumes no additional file storage. ### Can a group contain both files and folders? Yes. Add each file or folder from its menu. The group view collects them without replacing the normal folder hierarchy. ## Related guides - [Moving and renaming files or folders](/files/move-and-rename) - [Searching for files in the correct workspace](/files/search-files) - [Web app navigation](/account/navigate-web-app) - [Uploading files and folders in the web app](/uploading/files-and-folders)

title: Password protect a file sharing link
summary: Create and test a password-protected file, folder or bundle link, including private-recipient verification, unlock limits and workspace policy errors.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/recipients.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/request-code.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/verify-code.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/share.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/share.ts and focused creation, unlock, recipient-code and access tests. Confirmed create-share permission, eight-character trimmed minimum, force-password and full-lock rules, five password attempts per token and IP in 15 minutes, separate restricted-recipient verification with 15-minute five-attempt codes, separate 30-minute recipient/password grants, and format-specific View-only image delivery. Existing web and recipient captures remain accurate.
body: Add the password before generating or sending a sharing link. Every link keeps its own settings, so protecting a new URL does not change older URLs to the same file or folder. The secret controls access through that public token. It does not encrypt the stored item, identify the recipient, change workspace membership or recall a copy someone already downloaded. ## Steps: create a protected public link 1. Open **Files** and locate the file, folder or selected bundle. 2. Open **Share**, then select **By link**. 3. Review **Expires in**. Expiry and password are independent controls. 4. Expand **Advanced options**. 5. Enter the delivery secret in **Password (optional)**. The placeholder reads **Min 8 characters**. 6. Choose any separate controls you need, such as **View only.**, **Remove photo metadata.** or **Download limit (optional)**. 7. Select **Generate link**. 8. Under **Share link created**, copy the URL and select **Done**. Dosya trims whitespace around the password. A non-empty result shorter than eight characters returns **Password must be at least 8 characters**. The member's role needs the **create_share_links** capability. Workspace policy can refuse creation with **Share links are disabled for this workspace**. A workspace configured to require passwords returns **This workspace requires a password on all share links** when the field is empty. A **full_lock** link also requires a password. ## Test the first-time recipient experience 1. Open a new private browser window that has never visited this URL. 2. Paste the complete link. For a file, the locked page says **This file is password protected**. 3. Enter the delivery secret in **Password**. 4. Complete the human-verification control if it appears, then select **Unlock**. 5. Confirm the expected filename, folder or file collection appears. 6. Check that preview and download controls match the link settings. A test download can consume one use of a download-limited link. Successful password entry creates a signed 30-minute browser grant for this link token. Refreshing can continue without another prompt while that grant remains valid. Test with a fresh private window whenever you need to reproduce a new recipient's view. ## Understand password attempt limits The password endpoint allows five attempts per sharing token and client IP during 15 minutes. It also maintains a consecutive-failure lock on the link, which protects against guesses distributed across IP addresses. Errors include **Incorrect password** and **Too many attempts, try again later.** Stop guessing when the secret fails. Confirm the URL and password with the sender through a known private channel. Repeated attempts can block the correct recipient until the lockout ends or the owner rotates the password through the API. The password is case sensitive. Leading and trailing spaces are removed before verification. ## Combine a password with named-recipient access On **Share → By email**, the sender can select **Only these people can open it.** That creates a restricted link. Holding the URL and password is then insufficient: 1. The recipient enters the address that received the share. 2. **Send code** returns the same generic message whether or not the address is invited, preventing recipient-list discovery. 3. An invited address receives a six-digit code that expires after 15 minutes. 4. That code permits five incorrect guesses; after expiry or five failures, request a new one. 5. Successful verification creates a separate 30-minute recipient grant. 6. When the link also has a password, the page then asks for the password and creates its own 30-minute password grant. The two grants use different cookies and signed subjects. Email verification cannot substitute for the password, and a password grant cannot bypass the named-recipient gate. Public file requests use a different invitation model. Their recipient URL associates an address without an emailed verification code. ## Deliver and retain the access details safely Send the tested URL and exact password through separate trusted channels when practical. Anyone who obtains both can forward them unless the link is also restricted to named recipients. Open **Shared → By me** after delivery and verify the target, password indicator, expiry, access mode and download setting. Review older links to the same item. Revoke any URL that should no longer work; revocation ends that token immediately and cannot be undone. Password protection does not remove a recipient's saved download. **View only.** removes ordinary download controls and serves eligible content inline. JPEG, PNG and HEIC images are re-encoded as WebP derivatives with the longest edge capped at 1,600 px. WebP, AVIF, GIF, SVG, BMP and ICO can be served inline as their original bytes, so View only does not promise source-byte withholding for every previewable image. Visible content can still be captured. ## Change or remove the password later The current web app does not edit an existing link's password. Web users revoke the old URL and create a replacement with the new secret. This gives immediate cutoff because the replacement uses another token. The API can update a live link in place. New unlocks require the replacement password, while an already issued password grant can remain valid for the rest of its 30-minute life. An API update cannot remove the password when workspace policy requires one or the link uses full lock. Follow [Change a sharing-link password](/sharing/share-change-password) for both workflows. ## Troubleshooting **The password prompt is missing.** Use a new private window and confirm that you copied the protected URL rather than an older unprotected link. **A correct password receives a private-link error.** Complete the named-recipient email verification first. The server evaluates the recipient gate before it checks the password. **The link remains open after the password changed through the API.** The browser may hold a valid 30-minute grant. Revoke the link for immediate cutoff. **The protected link is expired or revoked.** A password cannot reopen it. The sender must extend an editable live link or create a replacement after revocation. **The page says the item is unavailable.** The shared target may have been deleted, moved behind a full lock or hidden from its creator. The owner must correct the target state or issue another link. ## Expected result A first-time public recipient must supply the link password before Dosya reveals the shared content. A restricted recipient must first prove control of an invited inbox and then pass the password when both controls are enabled. ## Related guides - [Create a secure file sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Change a sharing-link password](/sharing/share-change-password) - [Restrict a link to named recipients](/sharing/named-recipients) - [Revoke a file sharing link](/sharing/revoke-link) - [Test a link in a private browser](/sharing/share-preflight-private-window)

title: Signing in and resetting a forgotten password
summary: Request a password-reset link, choose a new password and complete two-factor authentication when the account requires it.
verification: Reviewed the current login, forgot-password, reset-password and post-reset 2FA flows against the local current web app, API and reset-password tests on 2026-10-12. Email delivery was not tested against production.
body: Use **Forgot password?** when an email-and-password account cannot sign in. The reset link changes the password; an account with two-factor authentication must still complete its second factor before a session is created. ## Before you start - Use the email address currently attached to the Dosya account. - Check whether you normally sign in through Google, GitHub or Apple. An account created only through a social provider may not have a password until one is set from Profile. - Keep access to the email inbox and, if enabled, the authenticator or recovery codes. - Use a private device and close any password-reset link after finishing. ## Steps: request and complete a reset 1. Open the Dosya sign-in page and select **Forgot password?**. 2. Enter the account email and complete the anti-abuse check. 3. Select **Send reset link**. 4. Check the inbox and spam folder. The confirmation intentionally does not reveal whether an account exists for that address. 5. Open the newest reset email and follow its link. 6. Enter and confirm a new password that meets the displayed requirements. 7. Submit the reset. Older reset links become unusable after a successful change. 8. If prompted, enter the authenticator, email or recovery code. A password reset does not bypass two-factor authentication. 9. After sign-in, review active sessions and revoke anything unfamiliar. ## Expected result The newest valid link opens the reset form. After the new password is accepted, accounts without 2FA sign in through the normal completion flow; accounts with 2FA continue to a second-factor challenge before receiving a session. ## Limits and security behavior - Reset links expire and are single-purpose. Request a fresh one when the page says it is invalid or expired. - Repeated requests can trigger a cooldown or rate limit. - The form does not confirm whether an email address belongs to an account. - Changing the password does not revoke API keys. Review them separately after suspected compromise. - Social-login-only accounts should use their provider or set a password from Profile while signed in. ## Troubleshooting **No email arrives.** Confirm spelling, check spam and wait for normal delivery. Use only the newest email after requesting more than once. **The link is expired or already used.** Return to **Forgot password?** and request a new link. **The new password works but 2FA blocks sign-in.** Use a saved recovery code for authenticator-based 2FA. See the recovery guide below. **The account uses social login.** Try the original provider. If you are signed in elsewhere, open **Profile → Password & 2FA** to set a password. **You did not request the reset.** Do not open the link. Review sessions, password, two-factor settings and API keys from a trusted signed-in device. ## Related guides - [Creating an account and verifying your email](/account/create-and-verify-account) - [Recovering access when a second factor is unavailable](/account/two-factor-recovery) - [Responding to suspicious account activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Preview a PDF in Dosya
summary: Open a PDF with ranged loading, navigate pages, zoom, search, print, and recover from corrupt or unsupported documents without editing the file.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/pdf-viewer/pdf-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/pdf-viewer/pdf-toolbar.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/use-pdf-find.ts and apps/web/src/components/pdf-viewer/pdf-viewer.test.tsx. Production PDF delivery was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: Dosya's web PDF viewer reads the stored PDF through authenticated range requests. It requests 1 MiB chunks and disables whole-file prefetch, so a large document can show its first page without downloading every byte first. ## Before you start - Open a PDF file from **Files** and confirm its name, size, and selected version. The PDF component resets page and zoom state when the file or version changes. - Unlock a fully locked file before requesting bytes. Workspace membership, folder scope, hidden-file rules, and read access still apply. - Interactive forms, scripts, signatures, and exact print color can behave differently from a dedicated PDF application. Download the original when those features are decisive. ## Steps 1. Wait for the spinner to disappear and confirm the toolbar reports page **1 / _total_**. 2. Enter a number in **Page number** and press Enter, or leave the field. Dosya reads the leading integer, so `2.9` goes to page 2, then clamps the result between page 1 and the document's last page. An entry with no leading integer returns to the current page. 3. Select **Toggle sidebar** to show page thumbnails. This preference is stored in the browser under **dosya:pdf-sidebar** for later PDF previews. 4. Use **Zoom out**, **Zoom options**, or **Zoom in**. The menu offers **Fit width**, **Fit page**, 50%, 75%, 100%, 125%, 150%, and 200%; the step ladder can continue to 300%. 5. Select **Search** to find text, then move through matches. Scrolling updates the current-page field; only the current page and two pages on either side keep live canvases to control memory use. 6. Select **Print** only after saving other work. Dosya renders every page at scale 2 into temporary images before opening the browser print dialog, which can take time and memory for long documents. 7. Use the viewer header's **Download** control to save the original PDF when preview fidelity is insufficient. ## Troubleshooting **Could not display this PDF** followed by **The file may be corrupted or use unsupported features.** means PDF.js could not open the document. Select **Download** and test the unchanged original in another reader. A slow first page can be network latency rather than corruption because later chunks are fetched on demand. Printing is a client-side rendering action and does not update the cloud file. Search, page jumps, sidebar state, and zoom also leave the stored PDF and its version history unchanged. ## Expected result The toolbar shows the correct page count, navigation reaches the requested page, and zoom or search updates only the viewer. Failures expose the original-file download without creating or replacing cloud data. ## Related guides - [Media preview controls](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Permanently deleting files and freeing storage
summary: Review items in Deleted, permanently remove only the intended files or folders, and understand when their stored bytes stop counting against workspace storage.
verification: Verified the current English Deleted view and current web/API source and focused tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use an isolated local owner workspace with controlled current-API fixtures and fictional deleted items. The review confirmed the trash storage notice, row and bulk permanent-delete actions, irreversible confirmation, delete-own/delete-any permission behavior, current-version and version-history purge, storage credit after purge, and bounded multi-pass folder purges. No production item was purged and a very large live folder purge was not executed end to end.
body: The first **Delete** moves a file or folder into **Deleted** so it can still be restored. It continues to count against workspace storage there. **Delete permanently** removes the selected trash item, its stored file versions and associated preview data; this action cannot be undone. ## Before you start - Use disposable items while learning this workflow. - Confirm the active workspace. Each workspace has its own Deleted view and storage total. - Restore anything you may need before you start. Version history is not a recovery path after the file itself has been permanently deleted. - Make sure your role can delete the item. **Delete own files** applies to items you uploaded or folders you created; **Delete any file** covers other members' items. - For a folder, review its name and file count carefully. Permanent deletion includes the selected trash-root folder and everything still inside it. - Consider downloading an independent copy when legal, retention or handoff requirements apply. ## Steps: inspect Deleted before removing anything 1. Open **Files** in the correct workspace. 2. Choose **Deleted** in the Files sidebar. 3. Read the storage notice above the list: items in the trash still count against storage. 4. Compare the item name, size, created date, deleted date and origin. 5. If an item is uncertain, open its menu and choose **Restore** instead of deleting it permanently. ## Steps: permanently delete one file or folder 1. Open the three-dot menu for the intended item, or right-click its row. 2. Choose **Delete permanently**. 3. Read the confirmation. A folder confirmation also names how many files are inside when that count is available. 4. Confirm that the name matches the item you intend to remove. 5. Choose **Delete permanently**. 6. Wait for the success message and let the Deleted list refresh. Do not send the request again while the first deletion is still working. ## Steps: permanently delete several selected items 1. In **Deleted**, select the checkboxes beside the required files and folders. 2. Review the selection count in the bulk bar. 3. Choose **Delete permanently**. 4. Read the confirmation counts for files and folders. Everything inside a selected folder is included. 5. Confirm the deletion and keep the page open while it works. 6. Read the final result. If Dosya reports failed, cancelled or still-emptying items, treat only the reported completed items as permanently removed. ## Expected result A successfully purged file or completed folder disappears from **Deleted**. Its current bytes and stored versions no longer count against the workspace's measured storage. Refresh the workspace storage summary if another open surface still shows a cached total. A very large folder can be emptied over several bounded passes. Dosya shows progress and keeps an unfinished folder in Deleted so the remaining work can be continued safely. ## Permanent-deletion limits and permission behavior - Permanent deletion has no undo. Support cannot promise recovery after the purge succeeds. - A routine Delete does not free quota; it only moves the item to Deleted. Storage is credited when the permanent purge removes the stored file rows and versions. - A file lock, folder lock, hidden-item rule, confined-folder role or ownership permission can prevent a purge. - Only a trash-root folder can be permanently deleted directly. A descendant that was deleted with its parent must be handled through that parent trash root. - A folder purge checks the contained files and folders before irreversible work. A locked descendant or an item the member cannot delete can stop the operation. - Large folder purges are deliberately processed in passes. Cancelling stops future passes; it does not restore files already removed by completed passes. - A bulk action can finish partially. Use the completion message and refreshed list as the record of what remains. ## Troubleshooting **Deleted is missing from the sidebar.** Your role may hold neither **Delete own files** nor **Delete any file**. Ask a workspace owner to review the role. **Delete permanently is missing for one item.** With only **Delete own files**, the item must be one you uploaded or a folder you created. Locks and trash-root rules can also restrict the action. **The folder says it is still emptying.** Keep it in Deleted and continue the purge later. Very large folders are bounded so one request does not run indefinitely. **The operation stopped after removing some files.** Read the progress count and error. Those completed removals are already permanent. Resolve the stated lock, permission or service problem before retrying the remaining folder. **Storage still looks unchanged.** Confirm the item disappeared from Deleted, then refresh the workspace switcher or storage page. A soft-deleted item still consumes storage, and an unfinished folder still contains bytes that have not been purged. **I deleted the wrong item permanently.** Stop any remaining bulk or folder operation if it is still running, preserve other copies, and contact support with the workspace, item name and approximate time. Do not expect recovery after a successful permanent purge. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does Delete free storage immediately? No. The normal Delete action moves the item to Deleted and keeps its bytes counted. A successful **Delete permanently** operation credits the bytes it purges. ### Can permanent deletion be undone? No. Restore the item before confirming when there is any uncertainty. ### What happens to previous versions? Permanent file deletion removes the file's stored versions along with the current file. Version history is available only while the file still exists. ## Related guides - [Restoring a deleted file or folder](/files/restore-deleted) - [Understanding storage usage and failed quota checks](/uploading/storage-usage) - [Reviewing exact duplicate files before removing copies](/files/review-duplicates) - [Restoring an earlier file version](/files/version-history)

title: Estimate storage needed before upgrading
summary: Calculate capacity accurately from owned-workspace usage, base plan, add-ons, licenses and referrals before selecting a plan or storage quantity.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/components/billing/plan-chooser.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts, apps/api/src/lib/addons.ts, and apps/api/migrations/0062_billing_v2_seed.sql on 2026-10-14. Production capacity was not changed.
body: Estimate against account-wide owned-workspace usage, because Billing’s usage numerator sums storage from every workspace you own. ## Steps 1. Record **[used] used** and **Total limit** from Billing. Subtract limit from used bytes to find an existing deficit. 2. Add expected uploads and a working margin to the current used value. Shared workspaces owned by someone else count against their owner, not your account total. 3. Inventory the ledger: base plan, each add-on quantity, active redeemed packages, and referral bonus. 4. Compare the forecast with the live catalog capacities. Static baselines are 5 GB Free, 100 GB Starter, 500 GB Plus, 1 TB Pro, and 2 TB Business. 5. If only capacity is missing, compare the live **Add storage** choices. The seed catalog defines `+100 GB` with a 50-unit maximum, `+1 TB` with a 20-unit maximum, and `+5 TB` with a 10-unit maximum. Use **Change plan** when plan-level capabilities or base storage must change. The chooser calculates against binary gigabytes (1 GB = 1,073,741,824 bytes). Active add-ons come from the database, with a five-minute cache, so the displayed catalog controls availability and pricing; there is no static add-on fallback. Leave headroom for active uploads and backup retention rather than selecting a total equal to today’s rounded display. ## Expected result The chosen plan plus extras exceeds current owned usage and the forecast, with a documented margin that prevents immediate quota failure. If the sum of visible ledger rows briefly differs from **Total limit**, use the total as the effective ceiling and reload after synchronization. Verify all workspace-specific caps separately. ## Related guides - [Choose a plan](/account/choose-plan) - [Review upgrade checkout](/account/plan-review-upgrade-checkout)

title: Prepare an over-quota account for a plan change
summary: Prepare an account above its future limit by measuring the deficit, choosing capacity or cleanup, and protecting every existing file from data loss.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/web/src/components/billing/cancel-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/subscription.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/cron.ts on 2026-10-14. Production quota was not changed.
body: An over-limit Billing banner means owned-workspace usage exceeds the account’s effective storage ceiling. Dosya pauses uploads across every workspace but does not delete stored files. ## Steps 1. Read the banner’s used amount, limit, and **[size] over** figure. 2. Decide between **Add storage** and **Free up space**. Add enough capacity to cover the deficit plus the next planned upload; cleanup must reduce counted owned-workspace bytes below the limit. 3. Before a downgrade or expiring package, calculate the future limit from the destination base plan plus extras that remain active. 4. Finish or stop active uploads before changing billing, and retain local originals until the new limit is confirmed. 5. After cleanup or purchase, reload Billing and wait until used storage is no greater than **Total limit** before retrying a small upload. Cancellation preserves paid storage through period end and then for a 14-day grace period. A confirmed plan downgrade can take effect through the subscription-update flow and create prorations; do not assume the cancellation grace applies to a deliberate tier swap. ## Expected result The red **Over the limit** state clears after capacity rises or counted data falls. Existing cloud files remain present throughout the restriction. If uploads stay paused, check workspace-specific limits and role upload permission in addition to the account total. Avoid duplicate checkout while Stripe synchronization is still running. ## Related guides - [Cancel or downgrade](/account/cancel-or-downgrade) - [Verify a storage upgrade](/account/plan-verify-storage-upgrade)

title: Review a pending plan downgrade
summary: Review a confirmed lower-tier plan change, its immediate storage result and proration, then correct it before quota blocks future uploads again.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/components/billing/plan-chooser.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/subscription.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/cancel.ts on 2026-10-14. Production subscriptions were not changed.
body: Dosya does not expose a deferred tier-downgrade queue. A lower plan submitted through **Change plan** is an existing-subscription update; period-end scheduling belongs to full cancellation. ## Steps 1. Open Billing and check whether the page shows the new plan or the amber cancellation state. 2. For a tier reduction, review the mandatory warning: **This replaces your [current] plan ([capacity]) with [new] ([capacity]).** Submit only after that explicit confirmation. 3. On success, inspect **Plan updated**, the new plan/interval, **Next invoice**, and **Total limit**. Stripe creates prorations for the item change. 4. For cancellation, look instead for **Cancelling**, **Ends [date]**, and **Resume subscription**. Storage remains paid through the end date plus 14 days of grace. 5. Compare current usage with the effective post-change limit and correct the plan immediately if the account is now over quota. Custom admin-granted subscription items are preserved during self-service plan changes. Add-on quantities come from the submitted cart and may change independently of the base tier. ## Expected result The interface clearly identifies either an already-applied plan replacement or a scheduled whole-subscription cancellation; there is no ambiguous “pending downgrade” state. If the wrong tier became active, reopen **Change plan** and restore the intended plan. That recovery may create a second proration, so retain both receipt states for reconciliation. ## Related guides - [Cancel or downgrade](/account/cancel-or-downgrade) - [Verify a plan change](/account/verify-plan-change)

title: Review a storage upgrade before checkout
summary: Review the selected plan, interval, add-on quantities, promotion and live Stripe total before authorizing and paying for a storage upgrade safely.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/components/billing/plan-chooser.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/catalog.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/preview.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/checkout.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/subscription.ts on 2026-10-14.
