body: Review the cart before leaving Dosya for Stripe, especially when plan storage and the 100 GB add-on appear beside one another. ## Steps 1. Open Billing and select **Change plan** for a base-tier replacement or **Add storage** to keep the current plan cards hidden. 2. Confirm the selected plan, monthly/yearly interval, and every add-on quantity. This walkthrough uses the seeded `+100 GB` choice, which permits up to 50 units; the live catalog can also offer larger storage choices. 3. Apply a promotion only after checking its amount/percentage, duration, interval restriction, and availability. The server validates it again. 4. Compare the live checkout amount and resulting capacity with current usage. For an existing subscription, review the proration preview rather than expecting a new checkout payment. 5. Continue once. Keep the Stripe tab open through authentication and the redirect to Dosya. The catalog loaded by the chooser is authoritative. Current fallback plan capacities range from 100 GB Starter to 2 TB Business, but active prices and availability can be edited server-side. ## Expected result The authorized purchase contains the intended plan, interval, and storage quantity, and the browser returns to a Dosya success state without a second checkout. A server refusal naming the old and new plan is the downgrade guard, not an upgrade failure. For invalid promotions, remove the code or choose an eligible billing interval before resubmitting. ## Related guides - [Estimate required storage](/account/plan-estimate-storage-upgrade) - [Verify the completed change](/account/verify-plan-change)

title: Verify storage after an upgrade
summary: Confirm an upgrade through the success state, storage ledger, total limit, subscription interval and Stripe receipt before retrying uploads.
verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/checkout-success.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/billing.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/sync.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts on 2026-10-14. Production checkout was not exercised.
body: Verify capacity in Billing after Stripe settles; the checkout confirmation alone does not prove that the account entitlement has synchronized. ## Steps 1. Wait for **Purchase complete** or **Plan updated** on the success page. 2. Confirm the capacity band’s added amount and total, then read the plan/interval and receipt rows. 3. The page runs an immediate billing sync and, while no subscription is visible, retries up to eight times at 2.5-second intervals. 4. Open Billing and check the new base-plan or add-on row in **Storage ledger** and the bold **Total limit**. 5. Compare the receipt amount, invoice number when available, masked card, and billing email. Retry a previously blocked upload only after the new limit is displayed. An active license or referral can make the total larger than the purchased item. Workspace-specific caps can still refuse an upload even when account capacity is sufficient. ## Expected result The success page and Billing agree on plan, interval and total storage, and the invoice/receipt identifies the transaction that caused the change. If status polling gives up, use its retry control or return to Billing and reload. If **Payment processing** remains, wait for Stripe rather than starting another checkout. ## Related guides - [Review upgrade checkout](/account/plan-review-upgrade-checkout) - [Reconcile an invoice with the plan](/account/billing-reconcile-invoice-plan)

title: Preview a CSV file as a table
summary: Preview comma-, semicolon-, or tab-delimited data as a table, understand the 2 MB fetch and 300-row limits, and download the complete original file.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/csv-table.ts, apps/web/src/lib/helpers.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The web viewer recognises `.csv` and `.tsv` files before the generic text path and renders a table when it can identify comma-, semicolon-, or tab-delimited rows. The first parsed row is used as the header. Text preview fetches stop at 2 MB. A parsed table displays at most 300 data rows; additional rows are reported as **+ _N_ more rows - download the file for all of it**. Cells stay on one line and may be visually shortened in narrow columns without changing the downloaded bytes. ## Steps 1. Open the `.csv` or `.tsv` file in the web Files viewer. 2. Wait for the table and compare its bold header row with the first row in the source format. 3. In the CSV preview, check a few early and late rows, especially quoted commas or semicolons, tabs, line breaks, and empty cells. 4. Read the row count above the table and the additional-row notice below it when more than 300 data rows exist. 5. Choose **Download** when the file exceeds 2 MB, parsing falls back to text, or the preview reports undisplayed rows. 6. Use **Download** to open the CSV in a spreadsheet tool and confirm the total rows and columns before using it for analysis. The parser supports quoted fields and comma-, semicolon-, or tab-separated input. It sniffs the first line, preferring tab on a tie and then semicolon before comma. A degenerate document that cannot form a useful table falls back to plain text. Preview truncation changes only what is rendered; it never rewrites or discards rows in cloud storage. ## Expected result A suitable CSV or TSV shows a header and up to 300 data rows in table form. When the preview cannot represent the whole file, the interface states that more rows exist and the downloaded original remains complete. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Inspect an archive](/files/archive-preview)

title: Download a file Dosya cannot preview
summary: Verify and download an unsupported file from Dosya cloud storage, then open the original safely in a trusted mobile or desktop application.
verification: Verified against current local product source for the web and mobile preview fallbacks, mobile Save to phone behavior, download permission checks, file locks, and Android/iOS save destinations on 2026-10-14.
body: Dosya can store file types that it cannot display inline. **No preview for this type** means the viewer has no compatible renderer; it does not mean the cloud-stored original is damaged. Check the file details, download the original, and open it only with an application you trust. ## Before you start ### Verify the file before downloading 1. Open the file in Dosya. 2. Check the filename, extension, MIME type, size, uploader, and workspace in the details panel. 3. Confirm you expected the file and recognize its source. Do not rename an unknown extension merely to make another application accept it. 4. If the viewer says **Could not load**, use **Try again** once. That message can indicate a network or preview-fetch failure. If it says **No preview for this type**, retrying will not add format support. ## Steps: download the original Select **Download** in the viewer. Your browser saves the original bytes using its normal download location. If the file is a text-like format, Dosya may also offer **Open as text**; this is useful for inspection but can show binary data for formats such as PSD, so it is not a replacement for the original file. ## Save from the mobile app In the mobile viewer, choose **Save to phone** when it appears: - Photos and videos are saved to the phone's media library after you approve access. - On Android, other files up to 64 MB use the system folder picker so you can choose Downloads, an SD card, or another available location. - On iPhone, other files open the system share sheet; choose **Save to Files** or another trusted destination. - On Android, files over 64 MB use the share sheet instead of direct folder writing because direct writing would require buffering the whole file in memory. Wait for **Saved to your gallery**, **Saved to your phone**, or **Choose where to save it** before closing the viewer. ## Troubleshooting ### When Download or Save is unavailable A role needs download permission to save the original. A file or parent folder in **view only** mode can allow preview while blocking download. A fully locked file requires its password before bytes are available. Ask the owner to change the access rule if you have a legitimate need for the original; repeated retries do not bypass these controls. ## Open the downloaded file safely Use an application that explicitly supports the extension. Keep the operating system and viewer updated, scan files from unfamiliar sources, and avoid enabling macros or embedded scripts unless you have verified the sender. After opening, compare the displayed filename and size with Dosya's details to confirm you selected the intended download. ## Expected result The original file is saved to the selected device location and opens in a trusted application that supports its format. The cloud copy remains unchanged. ## Limits and important details Preview support and download permission are separate. View-only and full-lock rules may prevent saving even when some file details or previews remain visible. ## Related guides - [Preview files without downloading](/files/preview-files) - [Handle a file type Dosya cannot preview](/files/preview-unsupported-download)

title: Preview an EPUB or ebook in Dosya
summary: Read supported ebooks in the web viewer, use contents, search, bookmarks, themes, and local progress, and recover when the book cannot open.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/book-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/reader/readingState.ts, apps/web/src/lib/helpers.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The web reader opens EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, and CBZ files with the vendored book engine. It provides page navigation, contents, search, bookmarks, reading themes, and text-size controls. The position line shows the current section and percentage. Position writes are debounced as pages change, and bookmarks and progress are stored in this browser for that file. They are not synced to another browser or to the mobile app. ## Steps 1. Open a supported ebook from the web Files viewer and wait for its first readable location. 2. Use **Contents**, **Previous page**, or **Next page** to move to a known section. 3. In the ebook preview, confirm the section title and percentage shown in the position line. 4. Use **Search in book**, a reading theme, or the smaller and larger text controls as needed. 5. Choose **Bookmark this page**, then verify its durable local marker in **Bookmarks**. 6. Close and reopen the same ebook in the same browser and confirm it resumes near the saved location. The reader keeps at most 200 accumulated search hits for a search session. If the raw file request fails, the message includes **Could not download the book (_status_)**; a reader error can instead say **This book could not be opened.** Download the original to test it in another reader. Removing browser storage also removes this device’s saved progress and bookmarks. ## Expected result The book renders with working navigation and a visible reading percentage, and the same browser resumes from its saved location. A download or parsing failure produces an error instead of presenting an empty reader. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Inspect an archive](/files/archive-preview)

title: Previewing files without downloading
summary: Open supported images, PDFs, media, documents, text, books and archives in the browser, and use the safe fallback when a format cannot preview.
verification: Verified the current English Files viewer and current web/API source on 2026-10-14. Screenshots use an isolated local owner workspace with controlled current-API fixtures and fictional files. The review confirmed the image viewer, details and versions rail, next/previous navigation, unsupported-format message, Open as text and Download fallbacks, browser-codec video failure, text-size cap, Office conversion cap, PDF reader and archive viewer branches. Production conversion services, every browser codec and every archive edge case were not exercised. Added a task-specific interface map derived from the verified controls.
body: Open **Files** in the intended workspace, then choose a filename or use its menu and choose **View**. Dosya opens the file in an overlay when it has a browser viewer. The file stays in the workspace; opening a preview does not create a download or change the stored file. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace and find a harmless sample file. - Make sure your role can access the file and its folder. A full lock can require its password before the viewer opens. - Allow the first preview a moment to prepare. PDF and Office viewers can load extra code or convert a document before displaying it. - Keep **Download** available as the fallback for formats or codecs your browser cannot render. - Treat a preview as a reading view. It does not prove that every feature of the file's original application is represented. ## Steps: open and navigate a preview 1. Open **Files** and locate the file. 2. Choose its filename, or open the file menu and choose **View**. 3. Inspect the file in the centre stage. Use the right-hand **Details** rail for size, type, region, uploader, dates, origin, share-link count and comment count. 4. Use the left and right arrows to move between files in the current listing. The filmstrip along the bottom shows the same sequence. 5. For an image, use the zoom controls in the header. For video or audio, use the media controls. PDF, archive, book, CSV, Markdown and text viewers provide controls suited to that format. 6. Choose the download icon when you need the original bytes in a local application. 7. Choose **×** or press Escape to close the viewer. ## What the current viewer handles | File family | Current browser behavior | | --- | --- | | Images | PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, SVG, ICO and HEIC/HEIF use image previews; HEIC/HEIF can fall back to browser-side decoding. | | PDF | Opens in Dosya's PDF reader with page navigation, thumbnails and find controls. | | Video and audio | Opens in an inline player when the browser supports the file's codec. A familiar extension does not guarantee that every browser can decode its contents. | | Office documents | DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and other listed Office/OpenDocument formats can prepare an inline PDF preview and offer **Open in editor**. | | Text and code | Supported text formats open as text, with syntax highlighting for smaller files. Markdown, CSV and TSV receive structured views. | | Books and contacts | EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, CBZ and vCard files have dedicated readers. | | Archives and disk images | ZIP, ISO and supported IMG images open an entry browser. Other archive formats can fall back to download. | Support here means the current Dosya viewer has a route for the format. The actual preview can still depend on valid file bytes, browser media support, conversion availability, size and permissions. ## Steps: use the fallback for an unsupported file 1. Open the file in the viewer. 2. Read the message in the centre card. For an unknown type, it states that a preview is unavailable. 3. Choose **Open as text** only when plain text is plausible. Binary data can appear as unreadable characters; opening it this way does not modify the file. 4. Choose **Download** to open the original in an application that understands the format. 5. If a normally supported file falls back unexpectedly, compare its extension with its actual content type and try another current browser before reporting the problem. ## Expected result A supported file appears in the browser viewer without a separate download. The viewer identifies the current file, provides relevant reading or playback controls, and lets you move through the current list. When inline preview is unavailable, Dosya shows a clear fallback with **Download** and, for unknown formats, an optional **Open as text** action. ## Preview limits and permission behavior - Text, Markdown, CSV and TSV previews are limited to 2 MB. Larger text-like files show a download fallback. Syntax highlighting is limited to smaller bodies even when plain-text preview still works. - An Office conversion larger than 20 MB falls back rather than loading the converted PDF inline. Conversion can also fall back when the document service cannot prepare the file. - Video and audio playback depends on the browser's codec support. An MP4, MOV, MKV or audio extension describes a container or family, not a guarantee that this browser can decode the streams inside. - The current archive browser handles ZIP and ISO content plus supported disk-image input. ZIP-like book formats use their book reader. Formats such as RAR, 7z, TAR and GZ are not claimed as browsable by this guide. - Preview follows file visibility, folder confinement and lock rules. It does not bypass access restrictions. - The preview is not a format conversion. Downloading or renaming a file does not change its underlying format. ## Troubleshooting **The viewer says preview is unavailable.** Use **Download** and open the file in its native application. If the file may contain text, **Open as text** is a read-only attempt and can display garbled binary data. **A text file says it is too large.** The browser text viewer stops at 2 MB. Download it and use an editor designed for larger files. **A video opens but will not play.** The browser could not decode its codec. Download it and use a player with broader codec support, such as VLC. **An Office file stays on Preparing preview and then falls back.** Retry once after a short wait. If it still fails, use **Open in editor** or **Download**. Include the file type, approximate size, time and redacted error when contacting support. **The preview looks incomplete or different from the source application.** Use the original application for layout-critical approval, editing, macros, embedded objects or other application-specific behavior. **The viewer asks for a lock password.** Enter the file or folder lock password supplied through your workspace process. Do not send the password in a support ticket. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does previewing a file download it to my Downloads folder? No. The browser fetches the data needed to render the preview, but it does not create a normal local download unless you choose **Download**. ### Can I preview PDFs, videos and ZIP archives? Yes. PDFs use Dosya's PDF reader, browser-supported video plays inline, and ZIP files use the archive browser. Media codecs and archive contents can still cause a fallback. ### Can I edit from the preview? The viewer is primarily for reading. Some supported images, videos, text and Office files expose edit actions, but editing is a separate workflow that saves a new version. ## Related guides - [Searching for files in the correct workspace](/files/search-files) - [Downloading one file or several files](/uploading/download-files) - [Restoring an earlier file version](/files/version-history) - [Contacting support with useful information](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Troubleshoot an image preview that will not load
summary: Diagnose a web image preview that falls through thumbnail, original, or HEIC decoding, then preserve and test the downloaded source without editing it.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/file-preview-image.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/file-url.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/thumb.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The web image viewer tries more than one path before giving up. Normal images request a server thumbnail and then the raw original; HEIC first requests a WebP thumbnail and can fall back to browser-side decoding. If every path fails, the viewer replaces the picture with the file-type icon; it does not show a dedicated Retry button or a detailed image error. Reopening a different file or version resets the preview failure state. ## Steps 1. In the image preview, confirm the filename, selected version, and displayed size in the viewer details. 2. Let the image fallback chain finish; a HEIC conversion or large original can take longer than a normal thumbnail. 3. Close and reopen the same image version once after confirming the network and session are active. 4. If the file icon replaces the image again, choose the header **Download** action to preserve the original bytes. 5. Open the download in a trusted image application and check whether it decodes at full resolution. 6. Report the image filename, version, format, size, and whether the downloaded original opens; do not resave over the source during diagnosis. A working download with a failed preview points to thumbnail or browser decoding. A download that also fails or will not decode points to access, incomplete bytes, misleading extension, or source corruption. The 128 MB Worker memory budget can make very large HEIC images use browser decoding, but that fallback is expected behavior rather than data loss. ## Expected result Either the preview renders through its thumbnail, raw, or HEIC path, or the original is downloaded unchanged and the failure is isolated with enough version and format detail to investigate. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Handle unsupported previews](/files/preview-unsupported-download)

title: Preview an Office document in Dosya
summary: Open supported Office documents as converted PDFs in the web viewer, use the editor when allowed, and understand source and rendered size limits.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/office-preview.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/preview-pdf.ts, apps/api/src/lib/onlyoffice/formats.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The web Files viewer converts supported Office documents to PDF on demand. DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX are editable in ONLYOFFICE; DOC, XLS, PPT, ODT, ODS, ODP, and RTF also use the read-only conversion preview. CSV files open in Dosya's table preview first. The source conversion cap is 50 MB and the web component will not embed a converted PDF larger than 20 MB. The preview is keyed to the selected file version. A current-version rendition is cached; an older version is converted transiently. ## Steps 1. Open the Office file from **Files** and verify the filename and version in the viewer. 2. Wait through **Loading preview...** and, when conversion is already in flight, **Preparing preview...**. 3. In the Office preview, read a heading, spreadsheet value, or slide title to confirm the intended version. 4. Use the PDF toolbar for page navigation; the preview does not edit the source document. 5. Choose **Open in editor** when the file type and your permissions allow editing, understanding that a save creates a new version. 6. If the viewer falls back to its file card, choose **Download** and open the original in a compatible Office application. The web preview retries a 503 response twice, using the server’s **Retry-After** value or 3 seconds by default. Any fetch failure, non-success response, source over 50 MB, or rendered PDF over 20 MB falls back to the file card. A view-only or locked source is not converted into a retained derivative. ## Expected result A supported, accessible document appears as a readable PDF for the chosen version. Editing is a separate explicit action, while size, access, and conversion failures preserve a Download route to the original. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Inspect an archive](/files/archive-preview)

title: Wait for an Office preview to finish processing
summary: Interpret Office preview processing, wait through two bounded web retries or twenty mobile polls, and choose Download when conversion cannot finish.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/office-preview.tsx, apps/mobile/src/viewer/officePreview.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/preview-pdf.ts, apps/api/src/lib/onlyoffice/convert.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **Preparing preview...** means another conversion currently holds the file-version lock. The server returns 503 with **Retry-After: 3** while that lock is present; it is a temporary state, not a request to re-upload the document. The web viewer makes the first request plus two retries. Mobile polls every 3 seconds for up to 20 attempts, matching the server’s 60-second conversion-lock lifetime. Repeatedly replacing the file during this window creates a new version and a different conversion key. ## Steps 1. Leave the viewer open on the intended version while **Preparing preview...** is visible. 2. Do not upload another same-named file merely to restart processing; that would create another version. 3. On web, allow the initial request and two timed retries to finish; on mobile, allow the 3-second polling cycle to settle. 4. When the Office PDF preview appears, confirm its version and a known piece of document content. 5. If web returns to the file card or mobile says the preview is taking too long, close and reopen once after the conversion lock has expired. 6. Use **Download** when another attempt gives the same fallback, then report the file version, size, format, and exact displayed message. A source over 50 MB returns `too_large` without conversion. Unsupported input returns 415. Conversion service failures return 502 and the UI falls back rather than polling forever. The current-version PDF is cached only after successful conversion, so a failed attempt does not replace the Office original. ## Expected result Processing either resolves to a PDF for the unchanged file version or stops at a bounded fallback with the original still downloadable. The workflow does not create a replacement version simply to clear a temporary conversion lock. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Handle unsupported previews](/files/preview-unsupported-download)

title: Troubleshoot a PDF preview
summary: Diagnose a PDF preview failure, use the exact viewer error and Download action, and separate access or network problems from corrupt PDF structure.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/pdf-viewer/pdf-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/file-url.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/raw.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The web PDF viewer reads the file in 1 MiB range chunks and renders only pages near the current page. This allows large PDFs to open without downloading the entire document before page one. When pdf.js cannot load the document, the viewer says **Could not display this PDF** and **The file may be corrupted or use unsupported features.** The same card offers **Download**. This message does not by itself identify whether the bytes, network, access, or PDF structure caused the failure. ## Steps 1. Check the filename and active version before troubleshooting so an older revision is not mistaken for the latest PDF. 2. After a PDF load failure, reload the viewer once with an active session and stable connection. 3. If the PDF preview renders page one, jump to the reported problem page and wait for its nearby render window. 4. When **Could not display this PDF** appears, choose its **Download** action. 5. Use **Download**, open the PDF bytes in a trusted desktop reader, and test the same page. 6. Report the file ID or name, version, size, failing page, and whether the downloaded file opens; keep the original unchanged. A download that opens normally isolates the problem to browser rendering, range delivery, or a PDF feature that pdf.js does not support. If another reader also rejects the same download, obtain a fresh source copy or repair it outside Dosya, then upload that as a new version only after preserving the original. ## Expected result The PDF either renders and navigates to the tested page, or the error card provides an intact download for comparison. The diagnosis distinguishes preview behavior from damage in the stored source. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Handle unsupported previews](/files/preview-unsupported-download)

title: Refresh a preview after replacing a file
summary: Refresh a preview after a same-name upload, select the row marked Latest, and avoid mistaking an intentionally selected older version for stale content.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/file-url.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Uploading another file with the same name creates a new version on the existing file record. The viewer loads the version list newest first and marks the newest row **Latest**. The raw and PDF preview URLs include the selected version. If you deliberately click an older version in the **Versions** tab, closing and reopening is the clearest way to return to the latest state after the listing refreshes. ## Steps 1. Finish replacing the file, wait for upload success, and refresh the preview only after that new version exists. 2. Close the open viewer so its current version selection cannot be confused with the refreshed listing. 3. Refresh the Files listing from the blank-area **Refresh** menu or reload the page, then reopen the same canonical file row. 4. Open **Versions** and select the first row carrying the **Latest** badge. 5. Confirm the version number, upload time, size, and a known content change in the preview. 6. If the old content remains, verify that the upload created a version on this file rather than a separate conflict-named file, then refresh once more. Choosing **Restore** on an older row is a write action: it makes that historical content current and cannot be used as a harmless refresh. Merely selecting an old version is read-only. Cached current previews are keyed by file and version, so a correctly incremented version receives a different source URL. ## Expected result The reopened viewer shows the row marked Latest and its new content. Historical versions remain selectable, and no restore or extra upload is needed merely to refresh the preview. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Handle unsupported previews](/files/preview-unsupported-download)

title: Handle a file type Dosya cannot preview
summary: Handle an unsupported preview with the exact Open as text and Download choices, protect binary readability, and preserve the untouched cloud original.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/helpers.ts, apps/web/src/lib/file-url.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: When no specialised viewer claims a file, Dosya shows its extension and says **Preview isn't available for this file type. You can open it as plain text - binary content will show up garbled.** **Open as text** is an opt-in diagnostic path; it does not convert the file. The text viewer refuses bodies over 2 MB and ordinarily warns when bytes look binary, while this explicit action accepts that binary output may be unreadable. **Download** keeps the stored bytes unchanged when your lock mode and permissions permit it. ## Steps 1. Check the filename, extension, MIME type, and selected version in the viewer details. 2. Choose **Open as text** only when the format may contain readable text or you intentionally need a raw diagnostic view. 3. In the unsupported preview's text view, do not treat garbled binary characters as source corruption. 4. Choose **Download** to obtain the untouched original for its native application. 5. Scan or validate the downloaded file as your organisation requires before opening an unfamiliar executable or archive. 6. Open the copy in a compatible app and verify its content; keep the cloud source unchanged until the format is confirmed. A full-lock file must be unlocked before its bytes can be read. A view-only file can be previewed only through allowed inline paths and may not permit attachment download. If neither action appears, confirm the file’s lock state and your access rather than renaming its extension. ## Expected result The unsupported file is either inspected knowingly as text or downloaded byte-for-byte for a compatible application. No preview attempt rewrites the original or promises that binary data will be human-readable. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Inspect an archive](/files/archive-preview)

title: Preview a vCard contact file
summary: Preview one or many vCard contacts, verify parsed fields, edit supported values safely, and preserve unshown contact data when saving a new version.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/vcard-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/vcard.ts, apps/web/src/lib/vcard.test.ts and apps/mobile/src/contacts/vcardFile.ts. Production contact files were not modified and no production action was performed.
body: Dosya recognizes files ending in VCF or vCard before the general text viewer. The web contact view parses one or many cards and can display names, organization, title, phones, emails, addresses, URLs, birthday, notes, and an embedded photo. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace, filename, and selected version. Previewing alone is read-only, while **Save** in the contact editor replaces the current content with a new file version. - Treat phone numbers, addresses, notes, birthdays, and embedded photos as personal data. Opening links can pass information to the phone, mail, map, or browser application. - Mobile parses a vCard into its contact interface only when the file is 5 MiB or smaller; larger files avoid synchronous contact parsing. The web viewer fetches the vCard body and does not apply that mobile limit. ## Steps 1. Open the VCF or vCard file from **Files** and wait for **Loading contact…** to clear. 2. For a multi-contact file, use **Search contacts**. Search matches the displayed name, email, phone, or organization and reports **No matches** when the filter returns none. 3. Select a contact and compare its visible name, organization or title, phones, emails, address, URL, birthday, note, and photo with the source you expect. 4. Use a phone, email, map, or URL link only after checking its destination. Hover a field and choose **Copy** when you need the literal value instead. 5. To change supported fields, select **Edit**. Web editing covers **Name**, **Phone**, and **Email** rows, with phone types mobile, home, work, main, fax, or other and email types home, work, or other. 6. Select **Save**. Success reports **Saved** and **Contact saved as new version.** Address, organization, notes, photo, and other untouched properties are preserved in the serialized vCard. ## Errors and recovery **This contact file couldn't be read.** appears when download fails or parsing returns no recognizable vCard entry. Download the original and look for `BEGIN:VCARD`. A matching `END:VCARD` is standard but not required by this viewer: an unterminated begun card is accepted when it contains at least one colon-delimited property, and an empty closed `BEGIN:VCARD`/`END:VCARD` block is recognized as an unnamed card. Save initialization can report **Save failed** with **Could not start upload**; the upload step can instead say **Failed to save**. The displayed contact stays unchanged when either request fails. After a successful save, use **Versions** if you need to inspect or restore the previous file version. ## Expected result Dosya presents the expected contacts and fields without importing them into the device address book. A successful edit creates a recoverable new cloud version while preserving fields the editor did not expose. ## Related guides - [Preview files](/files/preview-files) - [Inspect an archive](/files/archive-preview)

title: Changing profile details and account settings
summary: Navigate Dosya profile settings, update identity details, understand OAuth-only accounts, and know which security changes sign out devices safely.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/index.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/profile/identity.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/profile/password.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/name.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/avatar.ts, apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/auth-guards.ts. Production profile writes were not performed.
body: Dosya splits account settings into dedicated profile pages. On desktop, the left rail groups **Identity**, **Appearance**, **Password & 2FA**, **API keys**, **Sessions**, **Notifications**, **Integrations**, **Connected AI apps**, workspace membership, privacy, and account deletion. On a phone-width browser, /profile shows the same destinations as a list. The web settings screens use the signed-in session. At the API boundary, full-scope keys can currently update the display name with `PUT /api/me/name` and upload an avatar with `POST /api/me/avatar`; restricted keys cannot make those writes, and the email, password, 2FA, session, privacy, and deletion flows apply their own session-only guards. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Identity** to review the signed-in name, email, avatar, membership month, and workspace count. 2. Edit the name and select **Save**. A blank trimmed name is not submitted. A successful change shows **Saved — Your name has been updated.** 3. To replace the avatar, select the photo. Accepted browser pickers are PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF; the client refuses files over 2 MB with **File too large — Image must be under 2 MB**. 4. Treat an email change as a security operation. Enter the new address, confirm the current password, then use the six-digit code sent to the new inbox. It expires after 10 minutes and permits 5 attempts; code requests have a 30-second cooldown. The old address remains the sign-in identity until confirmation. OAuth-only accounts must set a password before changing email. 5. Use **Password & 2FA** for passwords and second factors. An account created only with Google, GitHub, or Apple shows **Not set** and **Set a password**; setting one adds email/password sign-in. 6. Review **Sessions** after changing a password. Password updates preserve the caller's credential and revoke other browser and mobile credentials immediately. The interface is currently English-only; there is no working preferred-language control. Account deletion lives on its own danger page and is outside an ordinary profile edit. ## Expected result Each saved change refreshes the profile and displays its success toast. Identity edits affect the account across workspaces. Security operations can email the account owner and revoke other devices, while changing the avatar or display name does not alter stored files or workspace roles. ## Related guides - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Create an API key](/developers/api-key)

title: Verify an rclone transfer with checksums
summary: Compare a completed rclone WebDAV transfer by downloaded bytes, record missing or differing paths, and treat a clean command exit as one check.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-download.md, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/xml.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.content-headers.unit.test.ts. Commands were not run against production storage.
body: A successful copy summary is not a byte comparison. For the released Dosya WebDAV workflow, use a separate local destination and `rclone check --download` so the generic `other` backend reads content instead of assuming a compatible remote hash. ## Steps 1. Save the exact source and destination used by the completed transfer, including whether an ordinary remote needs the `All/` prefix or an anchored remote exposes its folder directly. 2. List both trees recursively and preserve the output before checking: `rclone lsf ./sample-source --recursive` and `rclone lsf dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --recursive`. 3. Run a read-only comparison: `rclone check ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --download`. 4. Add `--one-way` only when destination-only files are expected and should not count as errors. Do not use it to hide source files missing at the destination. 5. Read every missing, differing and unreadable path, then capture the immediate process status with `echo $?` or PowerShell’s `$LASTEXITCODE`. 6. Verify one downloaded file before removing its local source. The `--download` check rereads remote bytes and consumes allowance. Dosya WebDAV can expose dates, ETags and a stored SHA-256 property, but the generic `other` backend does not guarantee a full compatible hash comparison. The explicit download comparison does not modify either tree. ## Expected result The check exits cleanly only when every required source path has matching destination bytes. Expected destination-only items are ignored only when `--one-way` was deliberately selected, and all mismatches remain recorded for repair. HTTP `401`, `403`, `404`, `423` and `429` failures are verification failures, not content matches. Resolve credential, permission, path, lock or Retry-After conditions before rerunning the check. ## Related guides - [Copy with rclone](/integrations/rclone) - [Download with rclone](/integrations/rclone-download)

title: Choose between rclone copy and sync
summary: Compare rclone copy and sync, preview destination deletions, understand Dosya versions and Trash retention, and check the completed operation.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14: src/pages/developer/rclone.astro; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts; apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.subtree-authz.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.ancestor-lock.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/trim-versions.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/purge-trash.ts; apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/plan-limits.ts; apps/cron/src/index.ts. Official references: https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/; https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/; https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/; https://rclone.org/webdav/; https://rclone.org/docs/. Current 2026-10-11 rclone-copy history verifies copy preservation only, not remote sync deletion. Retained accurate copy-vs-sync illustration, removed marketing overview figure. Examples safely checked on local files, no production sync executed. Local repository review; commands checked without production credentials.
body: Choose `rclone copy` when destination-only files must remain. Choose `rclone sync` only when the destination should mirror a complete, trusted source. Both can replace a changed file at the same relative path; only sync also removes destination files that are missing from its source. | Operation | Local-to-Dosya effect | Dosya-to-local effect | | --- | --- | --- | | `copy` | Adds or updates selected cloud files; retains cloud-only files | Adds or updates local files; retains local-only files | | `sync` | Makes the selected cloud destination match the source, including deletion | Makes the selected local destination match the cloud source, including deletion | The source is the **first** path and the destination is the **second** path. These are one-way operations, not a bidirectional sync pairing. See the official [copy](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/) and [sync](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/) references. ## Establish a working remote before choosing an operation Run `rclone version` after installing from [rclone downloads](https://rclone.org/downloads/). For Dosya WebDAV, create a key in [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api) and allow **WebDAV** in its protocol restrictions. Choose **Full access** for a remote destination you intend to mirror, because deleting requires that scope; your membership still needs the upload, folder-creation and appropriate delete permissions. A read-only key is sufficient for a cloud source being downloaded locally. Copy **Integrations → WebDAV → Endpoint & credentials** for the intended workspace. In `rclone config`, create `dosya-webdav` with Storage `webdav`, Vendor `other`, that complete HTTPS URL, the key owner's email as User, and the full API key through the hidden Password prompt. Leave bearer token empty and retain the remote. The [WebDAV reference](https://rclone.org/webdav/) documents these options; keep the private config out of shared diagnostics. ```sh rclone lsf dosya-webdav: rclone lsf dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --recursive ``` Ordinary mounts expose six collections; use **All** for the real writable tree. A folder-anchored key instead shows the permitted folder's children directly: remove the `All/` prefix and use its relative child path. Scope a mirror to a dedicated subfolder, not the connection root, a smart view, or a workspace with other people's files. Hidden or inaccessible source files can make a source listing incomplete, so establish that it contains everything your destination should retain. ## Steps: preview a harmless sample Use a curated local `sample-source` folder and a separate test destination `rclone-checks`. A source folder's contents go into the destination, without an extra source-folder nesting level. ```sh rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --dry-run --progress rclone sync ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --dry-run --progress ``` Review the reported paths and every planned deletion. A dry run can display planned totals, but no permanent copy or deletion has happened. If a remote-only file should be retained, the second plan is the wrong operation for that folder. Quote paths containing spaces and verify your terminal's current directory before using relative paths. An empty or wrong local source is especially dangerous for a mirror: it can make destination files appear unwanted. Filters change the selected set, and `--delete-excluded` allows sync to remove excluded destination items too. Do not add it to resolve an unexplained mismatch. Rclone normally avoids destination deletions after errors; `--ignore-errors` changes that safeguard. These effects are documented in [rclone sync](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/). ## Run copy, or deliberately approve the mirror yourself For the additive test: ```sh rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --progress ``` When you have reviewed the exact sync preview and every destination-only item may be removed, run: ```sh rclone sync ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --progress ``` The second command performs real deletions; this guide does not run it for you. Existing verified Dosya screenshots establish a successful sample **copy** and preservation of a remote-only file. They do not demonstrate a completed sync deletion. Sync examples here follow the official command contract and Dosya's source-verified delete behavior. Reversing the paths makes the local folder the destination. For example, `rclone sync dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ./sample-download` can delete local-only files in `sample-download`. Dosya Trash cannot restore a file removed solely from your computer; keep an independent local backup before that direction of sync. ## What replacement and deletion mean in Dosya When rclone sends different content to a matching live filename in the same real cloud folder, WebDAV writes a **new version of the existing file**, preserving its identity. `copy` therefore does not mean "never overwrite." With Vendor `other`, rclone's metadata/hash comparisons are limited; files it decides to retransmit can produce additional versions. The workspace history cap defaults to **10 versions**; a nonpositive configured cap disables the count limit. Free-plan owners' older versions are eligible for pruning after **7 days**, while retaining the newest version. Count limits also apply to paid workspaces, so replacement history is not an unlimited rollback promise. Original and retained version bytes use storage. A WebDAV DELETE moves the cloud file to Trash and revokes its share links; a folder deletion trashes its subtree. Delete permissions depend on whether you own each affected item. A locked file, locked ancestor or locked backup can refuse the operation even with a full-access key. Trashed files still consume storage until permanent purge. Restore eligible deleted cloud content through **Trash** before retention expires. The automatic purge window is **7 days** for effectively free workspace owners and **30 days** for other owners; it is based on the owner's effective plan, not the rclone operator's subscription. Permanent purge removes the data and retained versions irreversibly. A content restore should not be assumed to reactivate revoked share links. ## Check completion rather than trusting the progress bar ```sh rclone lsf dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --recursive rclone check ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --download --one-way ``` Capture the transfer command's exit status before the listing: `echo $?` in a POSIX shell or `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell. Exit **0** indicates no remaining errors, but not necessarily a transfer. Review nonzero exits and errors per [rclone's exit-code list](https://rclone.org/docs/#exit-code). `check --download --one-way` compares the source contents with downloaded destination bytes without modifying files, allowing destination-only extras after copy. After sync, omit `--one-way` if you also need differences on either side reported. See [rclone check](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/). Check the Dosya folder in **Files**, and if deletion was intended inspect **Trash** and the remaining live list as well. These checks read cloud bytes again and consume egress. Workspace storage, upload restrictions, key/role concurrency and daily egress allowances still constrain the run. If you get HTTP **429**, use the server's retry hint when supplied and investigate the applicable limit instead of looping immediately. ## Recover from a refused or partial mirror - **API key scope must be 'full' to delete** identifies insufficient key scope; **Delete not allowed** identifies a role/ownership refusal. A successful upload does not prove you can delete every destination item. - **Locked** (423) requires resolving the relevant file or ancestor lock; repeated commands cannot override it. - Some transfers can complete before a later failure. Review the live destination, Trash and version history before retrying; a nonzero exit does not roll back successful uploads. - If the wrong files were trashed, stop the job, restore eligible cloud items promptly and verify any replacement versions separately. If the local destination was damaged, recover from your local backup. Keep copy as the default when the destination holds independently created files. Use a dedicated mirror folder and a freshly reviewed dry run whenever the source selection or destination changes. ## Expected result Copy retains destination-only items; a deliberately approved sync removes them from the selected destination. Verify replacements and deletions separately, with no assumption that a successful transfer summary proves a complete recovery path. ## Related guides - [Configure and test rclone](/integrations/rclone) - [Download files with rclone](/integrations/rclone-download)

title: Copying files with rclone over WebDAV
summary: Set up rclone WebDAV with a workspace API key, preview a sample copy, verify the uploaded files, and understand root paths and replacement limits.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14: src/pages/developer/rclone.astro; apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts; apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/mkcol.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/xml.ts; apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/trim-versions.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/plan-limits.ts; apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts. Preserved 2026-10-11 verification: official rclone 1.75.2 macOS ARM64 checksum and native configuration, HTTPS isolated current-source fixture, six root collections, actual 56-byte upload plus remote-only-file preservation, separate download matching source bytes and dry-run zero exit/no mutation. Serial-download command flag parsing and content verified on a temporary local fixture, not a production remote.
body: Create an rclone remote with **WebDAV**, your workspace's copied HTTPS address, your account email and an API key. For an ordinary workspace connection, send your first sample to **All** or a folder beneath it. Preview with `--dry-run`, run `copy`, then check the destination and a separate downloaded copy. ## Before you start - Install rclone for your operating system from the [official downloads page](https://rclone.org/downloads/) and confirm that `rclone version` runs in your terminal. This walkthrough was checked with version 1.75.2 on macOS; prompts can vary between versions. - Sign in to Dosya and select the intended workspace. Your role must allow WebDAV and the operations you plan to use. - Prepare a local folder named `sample-source` containing one harmless, nonempty, uniquely named sample. Keep the original. Run the commands from the directory that contains this folder, or substitute your actual source path. - Choose a separate test destination. This guide uses an existing workspace folder named `rclone-checks`; create it in **Files** if needed. - This workflow reaches ordinary workspace files. Vault has its own workflow. ## Steps: prepare the key and address 1. **Create a dedicated key in Profile → API keys.** Give it a recognizable label, such as **rclone on this Mac**. Choose **Full access** for the upload walkthrough. That permission also allows moving and deleting within your account's allowed reach. **Read only** is sufficient for listing and downloading; **Upload only** cannot browse folders. 2. **Limit its reach.** Open **Restrictions and expiry**, choose **Only the ones I pick** under **Protocols**, check **WebDAV** and select the intended **Workspace**. Review any other limits before generating the key. 3. **Save the full key privately.** Select **Generate key** and copy it before closing the result dialog. You will enter it into rclone's password prompt. The label or saved prefix cannot authenticate the client. See [API key management](/developers/api-key). 4. **Copy the workspace's WebDAV address.** Open **Integrations → WebDAV** and copy the complete URL under **Endpoint & credentials**, including the mount path, encoded spaces and trailing slash. ## Steps: configure the remote 1. **Start the setup wizard.** Run `rclone config`, choose **New remote** and name it `dosya-webdav`. If that name already exists, choose a new name and use it consistently in the commands below. 2. **Choose the backend and credentials.** Type the textual option values rather than copying a provider number from a screenshot; numbers can change. Follow [rclone's WebDAV setup](https://rclone.org/webdav/) with these values: | Prompt | What to enter | | --- | --- | | Storage | `webdav` | | URL | Your complete copied Dosya HTTPS mount address | | Vendor | `other` | | User | The email of the account that owns the API key | | Password | Choose to enter your own password, then enter the full API key and confirm it | | Bearer token | Leave empty | | Edit advanced config? | No for this first connection | | Keep this remote? | Yes, then quit the wizard | Use the hidden password prompts. Keep the resulting configuration file private; rclone's password obscuring is reversible and does not protect the file as an encrypted secret store. See [rclone's explanation of obscuring](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/). Avoid putting the key in a command argument, a shared config snippet or a screenshot. 3. **Check the remote and folder listing.** Run: ```sh rclone listremotes rclone lsf dosya-webdav: ``` For an ordinary workspace connection, expect **All**, **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared** and **Deleted**. The colon separates the remote name from its path. A folder-restricted key has a different root; see the limits below. ## Steps: preview and copy the sample 1. **Check both paths.** The local `./sample-source` folder must exist in your current terminal directory. `dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks` means the `rclone-checks` folder beneath the writable **All** collection. Quote a path containing spaces. 2. **Preview the operation.** Run: ```sh rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --dry-run --progress ``` Review the filenames and direction. A dry run may show planned transfer totals or 100% progress. Look for the **Skipped copy as --dry-run is set** message: it is a preview, not evidence that a file arrived. 3. **Run the copy.** Once the paths and preview are correct, remove `--dry-run`: ```sh rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --progress rclone lsf dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ``` Wait for the command to finish and review any errors. `copy` can update matching destination filenames, but it does not delete other destination files. It places the files inside `sample-source` into the selected destination; it does not add another `sample-source` folder there. [rclone's copy reference](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/) explains this behavior. 4. **Verify in Dosya.** Open **Files → rclone-checks** in the same workspace and refresh if necessary. Confirm the sample's filename and size. The WebDAV **All** collection corresponds to the ordinary workspace tree in Files. 5. **Check a separate downloaded copy.** Choose a new, empty local folder and copy from the remote into it: ```sh rclone copy dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ./sample-download --progress ``` This direction downloads the files in the remote folder. Open your own downloaded sample and confirm it is the file you expected. Keep the original source while checking. ## Expected result The intended sample appears in rclone's destination listing and Dosya's **Files** page. Existing destination files that were absent from the source remain after `copy`, and your downloaded sample matches your original. ## Limits and choosing another operation - **Copy and sync have different effects.** `sync` updates the destination to match the source, including deletion when necessary. Do a dry run and review the direction and destination before choosing it. This guide's walkthrough uses `copy`; see the [sync reference](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/) before running a mirror operation. - **The normal root is a collection directory.** Upload into **All** or a folder beneath it. The connection root and **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared** and **Deleted** are read-only views. - **Folder-restricted roots differ.** With an anchored key, the permitted folder's children appear directly and there is no **All** collection. Do not add `All/` blindly. See [WebDAV folder restrictions](/integrations/webdav#folder-restricted-keys-and-other-limits). - **Metadata support varies.** With vendor `other`, rclone treats this as plain WebDAV and does not have its full hash/modification-time comparison features. Dosya serves file dates, ETags and a stored SHA-256 property when available, but that does not mean this backend uses them as a full content check. Compare a downloaded sample before trusting repeat-transfer decisions. - **Other backends have other settings.** Dosya's **Integrations → rclone** page describes its native backend setup. This guide chooses `webdav`; a `dosya`, S3 or SFTP remote uses different credentials/options and paths. - **A copy command does not schedule itself.** Automatic jobs, mounts and bidirectional sync need their own configuration. This walkthrough does not establish a desktop folder-sync pairing. ## Workspace rules, limits and replacements A key cannot grant permissions your membership lacks. Listing requires file access; downloading additionally requires download permission, while uploading and creating folders require their own role grants. Both the key and the role must allow the **WebDAV** protocol. A workspace pin cannot be used to reach another workspace, and a folder anchor confines the remote to that subtree. Locked files or ancestors can return HTTP **423 Locked** even when ordinary role permissions allow the operation. For a folder-restricted connection, use `rclone lsf dosya-webdav:` first. If `rclone-checks` is a child of that root, address it as `dosya-webdav:rclone-checks`, without `All/`. A key rooted directly at the test folder addresses its contents as `dosya-webdav:`. The smart collections are virtual views on an ordinary mount; do not try to synchronize their root as a writable filesystem. A transferred file whose name already exists in the selected real folder replaces its current content as a **new version of that file**. Prior versions consume storage and are subject to history limits: the workspace cap defaults to **10 versions**, and a nonpositive configured cap removes that count limit. Free-plan owners' old versions are also eligible for pruning after **7 days**, with the newest retained. A copy is therefore safer than a mirror for remote-only items, but it is not a guarantee that matching names stay untouched. Upload extension rules, workspace maximum file size, credential/role size limits and storage availability apply to WebDAV. A request must carry `Content-Length`; a client attempting unknown-length streaming can receive **Content-Length header is required** rather than a usable upload. Downloads also consume daily egress allowance. The built-in free-plan fallback is **100 GiB per day**, and the active plan catalog or explicit key/role limits can impose a different ceiling. Explicit request and transfer concurrency restrictions still apply even though plan-imposed call/concurrency ceilings are not applied to WebDAV protocol traffic. Rclone defaults to **4 files in parallel**; `--transfers 1` reduces the file count, but does not by itself serialize a large download. For remote-to-local files over the default **256 MiB** multi-thread cutoff, the client can open **4 range streams for one file**. Dosya takes a transfer slot for each streaming GET, so one file can exceed a one-slot key or role limit. For a controlled download retry, also disable per-file multi-threading: ```sh rclone copy dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ./sample-download --progress --transfers 1 --multi-thread-streams 0 ``` See [rclone's parallel-file setting](https://rclone.org/docs/#transfers-int) and [per-file stream setting](https://rclone.org/docs/#multi-thread-streams-int). These controls reduce concurrent downloads; they do not bypass request-rate or egress limits. HTTP **429** includes a retry hint when the usage policy supplies one. Reading a downloaded file again for verification consumes more egress, so keep the sample small. After the copy, check the command's exit status immediately: `echo $?` in a POSIX shell or `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell. Exit **0** means no remaining command errors; it can also mean nothing needed transferring. A nonzero status needs its error log reviewed before a scheduled job treats the run as complete. See [rclone exit codes](https://rclone.org/docs/#exit-code) and [transfer controls](https://rclone.org/docs/#transfers-int). ## Troubleshooting **Command not found.** Check the executable's installation and PATH using the official installation instructions. Open a new terminal if its PATH was changed. **Unknown remote or config file not found.** Run `rclone listremotes` and `rclone config file` in the same account/environment that runs the command. Check the chosen name, colon and any custom `--config` path. Another shell, scheduled job or container can use a different config. **Source directory not found.** Confirm your current terminal directory and the local folder path. A relative path such as `./sample-source` is resolved from the current directory. Quote paths with spaces. **Unauthorized or repeated authentication failures.** Use the key owner's email and the full API key in the wizard's password prompt. Check expiry/revocation and update this remote if the key was replaced. Pasting a raw key directly into a config's `pass` field is not the same as completing the password prompt. **Forbidden or an upload refusal.** **This API key is not permitted to use WebDAV**, **This role is not permitted to use WebDAV**, **Upload not allowed** and **API key scope 'read' cannot upload files** identify different gates. Check the corresponding setting instead of replacing a working password. For an ordinary connection, use **All** rather than a smart view. Address, schedule, usage and destination restrictions still apply. **A certificate error.** Check the copied HTTPS address and intended host. Do not disable certificate checks to make an unexplained production error disappear. Share the error privately with support. **The dry run says 100%, but no file appears.** The dry run planned the transfer. Run the reviewed copy without `--dry-run`, then verify the actual destination. For a persistent problem, send [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) the rclone version, backend, operation and error. Remove credentials and private paths from diagnostics; double-check even a redacted config before sharing it. ## Frequently asked questions ### Is WebDAV the same as the native Dosya backend? They are different rclone backends. This guide uses `type = webdav`, the workspace's WebDAV address and the **All** path for an ordinary root. ### Will copy remove files that are only in Dosya? `copy` leaves other destination files in place. It can still update a matching filename. `sync` has deletion behavior, so review that operation separately. ### Where should I upload if All is missing? Check whether the key or workspace membership is folder-restricted. Its allowed folder is the root, so its children appear directly. ## Related guides - [Connecting to Dosya with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [API key management](/developers/api-key) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Desktop sync setup](/desktop/sync-folder)

title: Create a dedicated rclone remote
summary: Create a task-specific rclone WebDAV remote with a protocol- and workspace-limited key, then verify its root without exposing the saved secret.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-copy.md, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts. Production behavior for “Create a dedicated rclone remote” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Create a separate WebDAV remote for each unattended job or trust boundary. A descriptive remote name plus a protocol- and workspace-limited API key makes the effective destination reviewable without sharing one broad credential. ## Steps 1. In Dosya **Profile → API keys**, create a key labelled for the machine and job. Choose **Read only** for retrieval or **Full access** when the job uploads, moves or deletes. 2. Under **Restrictions and expiry**, allow **WebDAV**, pin the intended workspace and add an expiry when rotation is planned. Save the complete key once. 3. Open that workspace’s **Integrations → WebDAV** and copy the entire HTTPS mount address, including mount path, encoded characters and trailing slash. 4. Run `rclone config`, choose **New remote**, and use a unique name such as `dosya-archive`. Select `webdav`, vendor `other`, the copied URL, the key owner’s email, and the API key through the hidden password prompt. 5. Keep **Bearer token** empty, decline advanced changes for the first test, save the remote, then run `rclone config redacted dosya-archive` before sharing any diagnostic. 6. Run `rclone lsf dosya-archive:`. An ordinary root lists **All**, **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared**, and **Deleted**; an anchored key exposes its permitted folder directly. Rclone’s obscured password in its config is reversible protection, not encryption. Restrict the config file to the job account and never paste a raw key into logs or command-line arguments. ## Expected result The named remote lists only the intended Dosya reach, uses the dedicated key owner’s email, and can perform no operation outside its key scope, protocol selection, workspace/folder pin or membership permissions. `401 Unauthorized` points to the email/key pair, expiry or revocation. **This API key is not permitted to use WebDAV** and **This role is not permitted to use WebDAV** identify separate gates. A missing **All** can be correct for an anchored remote. ## Related guides - [Use rclone with Dosya](/integrations/rclone) - [Run an rclone sync dry run](/integrations/rclone-sync-dry-run)

summary: Download cloud files with a read-only rclone WebDAV remote, preview the paths, handle local collisions and verify the resulting file contents.
