keywords: rclone download files from cloud storage
body: To download files from Dosya cloud storage with rclone, put the remote path first and the local directory second. This example retrieves the contents of `All/rclone-checks` into `./sample-download`, leaving the cloud originals in place: ```sh rclone copy dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ./sample-download --progress ``` Start with a new local destination. Review the setup and preview below before running it against your own files. ## Prepare a read-only WebDAV remote Install rclone from its [official downloads](https://rclone.org/downloads/) and run `rclone version`. Sign in to the key owner's account in Dosya and select the workspace containing the files. The account must have file-access and download permissions, and its role must permit WebDAV. In [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api), select **New API key**, choose **Read only** for this download task, and allow **WebDAV** under **Restrictions and expiry → Protocols**. Review the workspace and folder reach and save the full key after **Generate key**. An **Upload only** credential is refused for reads. In the chosen workspace's **Integrations → WebDAV**, copy the full HTTPS address under **Endpoint & credentials**, including its mount path and trailing slash. Run `rclone config`, create a remote named `dosya-webdav`, and enter: | Setting | Value | | --- | --- | | Storage | `webdav` | | URL | The copied workspace WebDAV mount address | | Vendor | `other` | | User | The email belonging to the API key owner | | Password | Enter the complete API key using the hidden password prompts | | Bearer token | Empty | | Advanced configuration | No for this setup | | Keep remote | Yes | The [official WebDAV backend reference](https://rclone.org/webdav/) documents these settings. Protect the configuration file and avoid exposing the credential in process arguments. Password obscuring is reversible; see [rclone obscure](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/). ## Steps: find the correct source and preview it ```sh rclone listremotes rclone lsf dosya-webdav: rclone lsf dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks --recursive rclone copy dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ./sample-download --dry-run --progress ``` Substitute an existing cloud folder you can read. An ordinary connection lists **All**, **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared** and **Deleted**; `All/` reaches the live workspace tree. An anchored key exposes its allowed folder's children directly, so `dosya-webdav:rclone-checks` may be the correct source instead. If the key is anchored at `rclone-checks` itself, use `dosya-webdav:`. Verify the root listing rather than adding `All/` to every address. The preview makes no permanent transfer. Check the names and the remote-to-local direction, then repeat the copy without `--dry-run`. A local path with spaces needs quotes; a relative local path is resolved from the terminal's current directory. The destination directory is created if absent, and receives the source directory's contents rather than an extra `rclone-checks` nesting level. Those path rules come from [rclone copy](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/). This real capture uses rclone **1.75.2 on macOS** against an isolated Dosya workspace fixture. The two downloaded files were checked against their source bytes. Your workspace address and selected filenames will differ; the capture does not establish a production transfer or verify every operating system. ## Existing local files and interrupted downloads `copy` preserves local files that exist only at the destination, but a differing file at the same relative path can be replaced. Choose an empty directory to avoid that collision. For an intentional additive download into an existing folder, `--ignore-existing` skips existing paths; it also skips stale or incomplete files with those names, so it is not an integrity check. Rclone documents this flag in its [copy options](https://rclone.org/docs/#ignore-existing). By default rclone downloads through a temporary file and renames it when complete; `--inplace` changes that behavior and can leave the destination file partially written. After interruption, keep successful local files and rerun the reviewed copy. Rclone can skip items it considers unchanged, but do not assume a partially downloaded file will resume at the same byte across runs. Check the result after retrying, especially if comparison metadata is limited. See [rclone's local backend](https://rclone.org/local/) and [in-place transfer option](https://rclone.org/docs/#inplace). Dosya WebDAV advertises byte-range support and serves **one byte range per request**. A valid range returns **206** with `Content-Range`; an unsatisfiable range returns **416**. Each streaming GET, including each range request, occupies its own usage slot. Range support does not promise that a client will resume a partial file. Rclone normally transfers **4 files at once**. Separately, a remote-to-local file above the default **256 MiB** cutoff can use **4 simultaneous range streams**. Setting only `--transfers 1` limits parallel files, but a single large file can still exceed a one-slot allowance. Retry the reviewed download with both concurrency controls: ```sh rclone copy dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ./sample-download --progress --transfers 1 --multi-thread-streams 0 ``` `--multi-thread-streams 0` disables multiple streams within each file. The [parallel-file control](https://rclone.org/docs/#transfers-int) and [multi-thread controls](https://rclone.org/docs/#multi-thread-streams-int) address different kinds of concurrency; neither removes daily egress or request-rate restrictions. Follow any HTTP **429** retry hint before starting another attempt. ## Verify the downloaded bytes Inspect the completion summary and exit status immediately after the copy: `echo $?` on macOS/Linux, or `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell. Rclone returns **0** when no errors remain, including when it did not need to transfer files. A nonzero return requires checking the preceding errors; [the exit-code reference](https://rclone.org/docs/#exit-code) lists the categories. List the downloaded directory, compare its names and sizes with the remote selection, and open representative files. A deeper check that does not rely on the backend exposing a compatible hash is: ```sh rclone check dosya-webdav:All/rclone-checks ./sample-download --download --one-way ``` This reads remote data again and compares it with the local data; it does not modify either side. `--one-way` ignores local-only extra files. Use the [rclone check reference](https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/) to interpret mismatch and missing-file reports. For a full-folder retrieval, verify the expected files rather than only a success count. With the `other` vendor, plain WebDAV does not provide rclone's full hash and modification-time comparison capabilities. Dosya returns file dates, ETags and stored SHA-256 properties when available, but this does not promise that the generic client uses them for a byte-for-byte comparison. Unix ownership, permissions, extended attributes and complete original metadata are not guaranteed by this setup. ## Egress, permission failures and what stays in cloud A download leaves Dosya's source file, its sharing configuration and version history intact. It creates an independent local copy that remains on your computer even if cloud access is later revoked; account revocation does not erase a downloaded file. Each WebDAV GET counts the requested body size against applicable egress allowances before streaming starts; a range is charged for its requested length. HEAD and unchanged conditional responses do not charge a body. Repeated downloads and `check --download` use additional allowance, and interruption should not be assumed to refund it. The built-in free-plan fallback is **100 GiB daily**, with the active plan catalog and stricter key/role restrictions determining the effective cap. Protocol traffic avoids plan-imposed request/concurrency ceilings, but explicit key/role limits still apply. | Server response | Resolve it before retrying | | --- | --- | | `Unauthorized` (401) | Check the key owner's email, full key, expiry and revocation. | | `API key scope 'upload' cannot download files` (403) | Replace the upload-only credential with one permitting reads. | | `Download not allowed` (403) | Ask the workspace administrator to review download permission. | | `Resource not found` (404) | Check the remote root, path, folder reach and whether the item is visible to this membership. | | `Locked` (423) | Resolve the file or ancestor-folder lock through the authorized Dosya workflow. | | Usage refusal (429) | Respect `Retry-After` when present and review egress, request or transfer restrictions. | Keep the downloaded directory and original cloud listing until verification is complete. Do not substitute `move` or `sync` simply to resolve a read failure: those commands have different deletion effects. ## Expected result The selected remote files are readable in sample-download and match the expected contents. The original workspace folder is still present, and the copy has not deleted cloud files or local-only extras. ## Related guides - [Set up rclone WebDAV](/integrations/rclone) - [Choose copy or sync](/integrations/rclone-copy-vs-sync)

title: Limit rclone transfer concurrency
summary: Reduce parallel rclone files and download streams, run a controlled WebDAV copy, and use Retry-After evidence to choose a stable concurrency.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-copy.md, apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-download.md, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].usage-placement.unit.test.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts. No load test reached production.
body: Rclone normally moves four files in parallel. Large remote-to-local files can additionally open four range streams above the 256 MiB cutoff, so `--transfers 1` alone does not guarantee one active Dosya download. ## Steps 1. Start with one non-confidential folder and record the current command, rclone version, direction and any API-key or role transfer limit. 2. Preview the same paths with `--dry-run`; concurrency changes do not repair a reversed source and destination. 3. For uploads or ordinary copies, begin with `--transfers 1 --checkers 2`. Increase one value at a time only after a clean measured run. 4. For Dosya-to-local downloads, add `--multi-thread-streams 0` when one file must use one range stream: `rclone copy dosya-webdav:All/sample ./sample-download --transfers 1 --multi-thread-streams 0 --progress`. 5. Watch for HTTP `429` and preserve its `Retry-After` value. Lowering concurrency does not bypass daily egress, storage, request-rate or per-file-size limits. 6. Capture elapsed time, final errors and exit status. Keep the smallest settings that meet the job’s deadline without repeated throttling. Each streaming WebDAV GET, including a range request, acquires its own usage slot. Protocol traffic avoids plan-imposed call/concurrency ceilings, while explicit key and role limits still apply. Uploads remain subject to storage and file-policy gates. ## Expected result The controlled transfer completes with no unexplained `429`, timeout or slot refusal, and the recorded flags bound both parallel files and, for downloads, streams inside a large file. If the server supplies a retry delay, wait for it rather than starting overlapping runs. A clean low-concurrency sample followed by failures at a higher value is evidence to return to the last stable setting, not to add unbounded retries. ## Related guides - [Use rclone with Dosya](/integrations/rclone) - [Run an rclone sync dry run](/integrations/rclone-sync-dry-run)

title: Troubleshoot rclone retries and timeouts
summary: Classify rclone WebDAV authentication, lock, rate and timeout failures, apply bounded retries, and verify before repeating a possibly partial run.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/backup-lock.unit.test.ts, and apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-copy.md. Only local failure contracts were reviewed; no production retry or transfer was exercised.
body: First separate permanent WebDAV refusals from transient failures. Authentication, scope, permissions, path and locks require correction; `429` and selected service failures can justify a delayed, bounded retry. ## Steps 1. Re-run the failing command once with `-vv --log-file /protected/path/rclone.log`, then record the first HTTP status and message without exposing credentials. 2. Stop retrying `401 Unauthorized`, `403`, `404 Resource not found`, or `423 Locked`. Repair the key/email, protocol or role permission, path, or Dosya lock first. 3. For `429`, honor `Retry-After` and ensure another scheduler instance is not running. Reduce `--transfers` and `--checkers` when parallel requests caused the limit. 4. For transport timeouts or transient server errors, choose finite controls such as `--retries 3 --low-level-retries 3 --timeout 1m`; retain the log and final exit status. 5. Before replaying a write, list the destination. WebDAV replacement can already have created a new file version even when the client lost the response. 6. Retry the smallest failed subset, then compare names, sizes and representative bytes. Do not mark the job complete from a later successful item alone. Dosya returns `503` with `Retry-After: 5` when a WebDAV mutation loses the repository busy-retry budget. A `429` can represent request, transfer or egress policy. Increasing the client timeout cannot fix an expired key, locked item or exhausted daily allowance. ## Expected result A corrected run uses a finite retry budget, respects server timing, avoids a tight parallel loop and ends with verified destination content. Permanent refusals remain stopped until their underlying gate changes. A nonzero run can leave earlier files or versions committed because a multi-file operation is not transactional. Preserve logs and inspect the destination before another attempt, especially after a timeout on a PUT. ## Related guides - [Copy with rclone](/integrations/rclone) - [Download with rclone](/integrations/rclone-download)

title: Schedule an rclone copy job
summary: Schedule a tested rclone copy with absolute paths, a protected config, durable logs and explicit exit capture, then verify the first unattended run.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-copy.md, apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-copy-vs-sync.md, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts. Production behavior for “Schedule an rclone copy job” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Schedule only an already verified `rclone copy` command. `copy` is additive for destination-only paths, but it can still replace a same-named Dosya file with a new version, so isolate the destination and retain logs. ## Steps 1. Run the exact command manually with `--dry-run`, then without it on one harmless file. Verify the destination before introducing a scheduler. 2. Find absolute paths for the rclone executable, source, config file and log directory. A scheduler can have a different PATH, home and working directory from your terminal. 3. Put the tested command in a protected script with absolute paths for rclone, source, remote, config and log file. 4. Prevent overlap with the previous run using the platform’s lock or single-instance facility. Keep the API key in the restricted config rather than the crontab or command history. 5. Add the POSIX cron entry or Windows Task Scheduler action under the intended service account, with the script’s absolute path and a deliberate working directory. 6. Trigger the schedule once now. Capture its exit status, read the fresh log, list the Dosya destination and compare one downloaded sample before waiting for the normal interval. A POSIX script can run `/usr/local/bin/rclone copy /srv/export dosya-webdav:All/nightly --config /etc/rclone/dosya.conf --log-file /var/log/rclone/nightly.log --log-level INFO`. A folder- or workspace-limited key reduces the scheduler’s reach but cannot exceed the member’s permissions. Revoking that key stops future runs; it does not delete files already copied. Replacing a same-name file appends version history and uses storage. ## Expected result The scheduler’s first unattended execution uses the intended config and paths, produces a durable log and verified destination, and records failure whenever the transfer or its verification command fails. `Unknown remote`, `config file not found` and local source errors usually reveal a different service-account environment. Fix that environment instead of copying the secret into a globally readable location. ## Related guides - [Use rclone with Dosya](/integrations/rclone) - [Run an rclone sync dry run](/integrations/rclone-sync-dry-run)

title: Run an rclone sync dry-run
summary: Preview a one-way rclone mirror with sync --dry-run, interpret planned transfers and deletions, then run the real command only after review.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/rclone.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts; src/pages/developer/rclone.astro; apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-copy-vs-sync.md; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.ts; and packages/prod-smoke/src/rclone-config.ts. Native and S3 fallback configuration plus dry-run examples were reviewed locally; no production sync was executed.
body: `rclone sync` makes its second path match its first path. Destination-only files can be removed, so confirm direction and preview the exact pair every time. `--dry-run` asks rclone to report intended work without applying copies, replacements, or deletions. ## Configure rclone without a fork The Dosya backend ships inside current rclone releases. Do not install a Dosya-specific fork. Run the standard configuration command: ```sh rclone config ``` Create an API key that has the permissions needed by the chosen direction. A cloud destination that may receive uploads and deletions needs **Full access** plus the corresponding workspace role permissions; a cloud source used only for local download can use **Read only**. Keep the key out of terminal history and shared logs. Choose a new remote, name it `dosya`, and select **dosya** from the storage-provider list. Enter the intended workspace ID and API key when prompted. Confirm the native remote before planning a mirror: ```sh rclone lsf dosya: ``` If **dosya** is absent from the provider list, update rclone or configure the stock S3 backend as the fallback described in the [Dosya rclone documentation](https://dosya.dev/developer/rclone/): ```sh rclone config create dosya s3 \ provider=Other \ access_key_id=dos_your_access_key \ secret_access_key=your_secret_access_key \ endpoint=https://api.dosya.dev/s3 \ region=us-east-1 rclone lsf dosya:WORKSPACE_ID ``` The remaining commands use the native path `dosya:/mirror-check`. With the S3 fallback, use `dosya:WORKSPACE_ID/mirror-check` because the workspace ID is the bucket. ## Steps 1. Run `rclone config`, choose the built-in **dosya** provider, and confirm `rclone lsf dosya:` works. If the provider is absent, configure the S3 fallback and list `dosya:WORKSPACE_ID` instead. 2. Create a small, known local source such as `./sample-source` and an isolated cloud destination such as `dosya:/mirror-check`. Back up anything already in that destination. 3. List the local source and `dosya:` destination recursively, then save the output: ```sh rclone lsf ./sample-source --recursive rclone lsf dosya:/mirror-check --recursive ``` 4. Run the preview with verbose operation lines: ```sh rclone sync ./sample-source dosya:/mirror-check --dry-run --progress -vv ``` 5. Review every path marked for copy, replacement, or deletion. **Skipped copy as --dry-run is set** confirms simulation. If a destination-only file must remain, stop and use `rclone copy` or move it outside the mirror. 6. Re-run the preview after changing filters, source contents, current directory, or destination. Only after that second review, run the live command by removing `--dry-run` yourself: ```sh rclone sync ./sample-source dosya:/mirror-check --progress -vv ``` ## Deletion and recovery rules An empty or mistaken source makes all destination entries candidates for removal. Filters also redefine the mirror set; `--delete-excluded` permits removal of excluded destination content. Rclone normally avoids destination deletion after transfer errors, while `--ignore-errors` relaxes that protection. Do not add either flag to bypass an unexplained plan. Reversing the paths changes the risk. This command makes a local directory match Dosya and can remove local-only files: ```sh rclone sync dosya:/mirror-check ./sample-download --dry-run --progress -vv ``` Dosya cannot restore data deleted only from your computer. Keep an independent local backup before approving that direction. A live sync to the native `dosya:` destination deletes each removed item twice: the first request moves it to Dosya Trash, and the second purges it permanently to free storage. Trash cannot recover a destination-only item removed by this backend, so preserve an independent copy before approving the live command. The dry-run itself is reversible because it writes nothing. The live command is not transactional: transfers can succeed before a later error, and a retry does not roll back earlier changes. ## Verify the live run Capture the command's exit status, list the destination again, and compare bytes without modifying either side: ```sh echo $? rclone lsf dosya:/mirror-check --recursive rclone check ./sample-source dosya:/mirror-check --download ``` An exit status of `0` means the command reported no remaining errors; it does not prove files were transferred. A nonzero result can leave partial successful work. Inspect the Dosya folder and compare it with the saved pre-run listing before retrying; native-backend deletions are already purged from Trash. ## Expected result The dry-run reports the exact one-way mirror plan while leaving both trees unchanged. If the approved live sync is later run, the destination matches the source, including intentional removal of destination-only entries, and `rclone check` finds no content differences. ## Related guides - [Copy with rclone](/integrations/rclone) - [Download with rclone](/integrations/rclone-download)

title: Filter files in an rclone transfer
summary: Exclude files with rclone rules, inspect selected paths, dry-run a Dosya WebDAV copy and verify bytes without accidental sync deletion.
verification: Reviewed 2026-10-14 against local repository implementation and tests. Local evidence: src/pages/developer/rclone.astro; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.ts; apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts. Official references: https://rclone.org/filtering/; https://rclone.org/webdav/; https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_copy/; https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_sync/; https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_check/; https://rclone.org/docs/; https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_obscure/. External commands are source-derived and checked on temporary local fixtures where reported; no production credentials or remote writes used. Existing captures retain their original verification scope. Review correction: replaced the earlier illustration with a source-derived process diagram following the current guide, inspected both 1200x675 themes with no text clipping and narrow-page/full-size behavior; diagrams show command stages, not an invented app UI.
body: Use rclone filters to leave backup files, temporary folders or unwanted extensions out of a transfer. First list the selected paths, then preview **copy** with the identical rules. A filter narrows a client command; it does not restrict what a stolen Dosya credential can access. ## Before you start The examples upload the **contents** of `./sample-source` into an existing `filter-checks` folder through a WebDAV remote named `dosya-webdav`. Create a harmless source tree with `report.pdf`, `draft.bak`, `tmp/cache.txt` and `photos/photo.jpg`; choose a destination that contains no important files. To configure a fresh remote, create a key in **Profile → API keys → New API key**. Choose **Full access**, select your **Workspace**, and under **Restrictions and expiry → Protocols → Only the ones I pick**, permit **WebDAV**. Save the full `dos_…` key when you generate it. In **Integrations → WebDAV**, copy the entire HTTPS mount URL. Run `rclone config`, choose a new `webdav` remote, Vendor `other`, that URL, your key owner's email as User and the API key in the hidden Password prompt. Keep the configuration private: rclone's obscured password is reversible. A normal mount lists six collections; write through `All`, not a smart view such as `Images`. For a folder-anchored key, the selected folder's children are already the root: replace `dosya-webdav:All/filter-checks` below with `dosya-webdav:filter-checks`. Create that destination first in Files or with `rclone mkdir`. Key permissions and your workspace role must both permit WebDAV and the transfer; selecting Full access cannot widen your role. ## Steps: exclude files and preview the transfer 1. **Confirm the two paths.** The first copy argument is the source; the second receives the files. For a download, reverse them and choose an empty local target. These examples never use `sync`. 2. **List the selected source files.** Repeated `--exclude` options omit `.bak` files anywhere and the top-level `tmp` subtree: ```sh rclone lsf ./sample-source --recursive --files-only --exclude '*.bak' --exclude '/tmp/**' ``` Expect `report.pdf` and `photos/photo.jpg` from the sample tree. No `draft.bak` or `tmp/cache.txt` should appear. A leading `/` anchors the rule at **the source argument's root**; `/tmp/**` does not exclude `photos/tmp/cache.txt`. `**` crosses directory separators, whereas `*` stays within a path segment. Use forward slashes in patterns on every platform. Matching is case-sensitive unless you deliberately add `--ignore-case`. 3. **Preview without writing.** Keep exactly those filters: ```sh rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/filter-checks --exclude '*.bak' --exclude '/tmp/**' --dry-run -vv ``` Read the planned paths and any errors. A dry run can contact/list the destination but does not upload the planned files; its simulated transferred counters are not proof that bytes arrived. If an unexpected filename is selected, fix the rule and repeat the listing and preview. 4. **Run the checked copy.** Remove only `--dry-run` and retain the paths/rules: ```sh rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/filter-checks --exclude '*.bak' --exclude '/tmp/**' --progress ``` Quote patterns so the shell passes the wildcard to rclone. Single quotes work for these examples in POSIX shells and PowerShell; use double quotes in Windows Command Prompt. Do not write `dosya-webdav:*.pdf` as a substitute for a filter. ## Include selected types or order mixed rules For PDFs only, use an include family on its own: ```sh rclone lsf ./sample-source --recursive --files-only --include '*.pdf' ``` `--include` adds a final exclude-all rule implicitly. When you need both allowed types and exceptions, use **only** the filter family, rather than mixing `--include`, `--exclude` and `--filter`. Create `transfer.rules` outside the source tree with this content: ```text # Drop private and temporary material before allowing document types. - /private/** - *.bak + *.pdf + *.jpg - ** ``` Rules run top to bottom; the first match wins. `+ *.pdf` alone does not reject everything else, so the explicit final `- **` is essential here. Whole-line `#` and `;` comments are supported; an inline comment becomes part of the pattern. Keep the same file throughout the workflow: ```sh rclone lsf ./sample-source --recursive --files-only --filter-from ./transfer.rules rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/filter-checks --filter-from ./transfer.rules --dry-run -vv --dump filters rclone copy ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/filter-checks --filter-from ./transfer.rules --progress rclone check ./sample-source dosya-webdav:All/filter-checks --filter-from ./transfer.rules --one-way --download ``` For the sample tree, that rule file selects `report.pdf` and `photos/photo.jpg`. `check --download` reads bytes to compare them and consumes download allowance. `--one-way` checks source-selected files without demanding that the destination have no extras. An exit status of zero plus the expected candidate list and successful byte check establish this filtered copy's result; a nonzero status needs investigation. ## Expected result and deletion risks Only the files your checked rules select are copied. Excluded local files remain on your computer, and ordinary **copy** does not delete destination-only objects. Matching destination names can still be replaced when rclone decides a transfer is needed; Dosya writes a new file version, with finite history retention, rather than guaranteeing permanent recovery. If you change the command to **sync**, destination files inside its selected scope can be deleted to match the source. Normally excluded destination paths are protected from sync deletion; `--delete-excluded` removes that protection and can delete the very files your filters hide. `rclone purge` ignores filters. Do not use either as a shortcut to clean this test. Remote deletion moves eligible files to Trash and revokes their share links; local destination deletion has no Dosya Trash recovery. ## Troubleshooting **Nothing is selected.** Check the root-relative slash, filename case and whether you accidentally matched only a directory (`/photos/`) instead of its files (`/photos/**`). `--dump filters -vv` shows the applied rules; do not change transfer direction while debugging patterns. **An exception is ignored.** Put the exclusion before the broader inclusion in a filter file. Mixing filter families does not preserve your visual command-line order; convert the command to one `--filter-from` file. **403, Locked, or a quota refusal.** Filters do not bypass role/key restrictions, locked destinations, blocked extensions or storage allowance. WebDAV upload requires Content-Length and an existing parent folder. For a 429, respect Retry-After and reduce client concurrency; multiple GET range streams may require `--multi-thread-streams 0` as well as `--transfers 1` when downloading. ## Related guides - [Configure a Dosya rclone remote](/integrations/rclone) - [Understand copy versus sync deletion](/integrations/rclone-copy-vs-sync) - [Official rclone filter rules](https://rclone.org/filtering/)

title: Verify an rclone automation exit status
summary: Capture rclone’s immediate process status, preserve its final errors and compare destination bytes before automation records a transfer as successful.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-copy.md, apps/help/src/content/articles/rclone-download.md, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts. Exit handling was documented without a production transfer.
body: Capture rclone’s status immediately after the command, before another shell command overwrites it. Exit `0` means that run reports no remaining errors; it can also mean nothing needed transferring and is not content proof. ## Steps 1. Run the scheduled or manual copy with a durable log and statistics, keeping source and destination explicit. 2. In POSIX shells assign `status=$?` on the next line; in PowerShell assign `$status = $LASTEXITCODE` before listing or checking anything else. 3. Preserve the final transfer summary and every preceding error. A multi-file failure can leave earlier files successfully stored. 4. If `status` is nonzero, mark the job failed and inspect the destination before retrying. Do not erase the log or replay the whole batch automatically. 5. When the copy status is zero, run a separate read-only comparison such as `rclone check SOURCE DESTINATION --download`; capture that command’s status independently. 6. Report success only when both statuses are zero and representative destination bytes match. Store the run time, paths, rclone version and counts with the receipt. For Dosya WebDAV, a successful same-name PUT creates a new file version. A later error does not roll that version back. Likewise, a `copy` leaves destination-only files in place; their presence is not evidence that this run processed the source. ## Expected result Automation records success only after the transfer process and independent comparison both exit cleanly, with logs that identify the exact run. Any nonzero status retains its evidence and blocks downstream success actions. A shell pipeline can hide rclone’s code behind another process unless its status is captured correctly. Test the wrapper with an intentional missing source before trusting alerts, then remove that test path. ## Related guides - [Use rclone with Dosya](/integrations/rclone) - [Run an rclone sync dry run](/integrations/rclone-sync-dry-run)

title: Write safe rclone job logs
summary: Capture useful rclone timing, counts, exit status, and errors while keeping API keys, configuration secrets, and sensitive file paths out of shared logs.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Write safe rclone job logs” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/rclone.tsx`, `apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts`, `packages/prod-smoke/src/lanes/rclone.ts`, `packages/prod-smoke/src/rclone-config.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya’s released rclone page configures a native `dosya:` remote with an API key, workspace ID, and `https://api.dosya.dev`. A useful job log records what happened without copying that credential or a complete configuration file into tickets, chat, or CI output. ## Before you start Use a dedicated API key whose permission, workspace, folder, protocol, IP range, active hours, and expiry match this one automation. The web key form shows the secret once, and the released rclone configuration stores it as `api_key`; treat both the key and the config file as secrets. The repository’s production smoke runner supplies a tested failure envelope: connection timeout `15s`, operation timeout `60s`, one high-level retry, two low-level retries, and a hard `120s` process ceiling. Those values keep an unattended failure finite and leave an exit status to record. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile > API keys**, create or identify the restricted key for this job, and confirm its workspace and folder reach before running rclone. 2. Keep the credential in the protected rclone config returned by `rclone config file`; do not place `dos_…`, an S3 secret, or the config contents in the command line or log header. 3. Run a harmless `rclone lsf dosya:` check with the job’s config and the fail-fast timeouts, then record the UTC start time, rclone version, command verb, and exit code. 4. Put `--` before file operands so a legal name such as `-x.bin` cannot be interpreted as a flag, and log redacted source and destination labels rather than sensitive full paths. 5. Capture stdout or stderr needed for diagnosis, but replace API keys, bearer strings, signed URLs, passwords, tokens, and confidential names before the log leaves its restricted storage. 6. Confirm the record contains elapsed time, transferred or checked counts, terminal exit status, and the first actionable error while a search for `dos_`, `secret_access_key`, and `Authorization` returns nothing. ## Expected result The log identifies when the rclone job ran, which safe command mode it used, what it attempted, and why it succeeded or failed. It contains enough timing and count evidence to reproduce the issue, while authentication material and protected names stay out of the artifact. If rclone never terminates, apply the finite retry and timeout values before collecting another run. If the log says the config is missing, use `rclone config file` and verify permissions; the strict-confined Snap build cannot necessarily read hidden or temporary paths. ## Related guides - [Use rclone with Dosya](/integrations/rclone) - [Run an rclone sync dry run](/integrations/rclone-sync-dry-run)

body: The redemption page accepts either a **Gumroad license** or **Coupon code**, exchanges the secret for an opaque one-time claim, and keeps only that claim through sign-in. ## Steps 1. Open `/redeem`, choose the correct source, and enter the code. Gumroad input is limited to 128 characters; coupon input is limited to 64. Both reject control characters, and coupons follow the `DOSYA-…` format. 2. Continue through **Securing your license code**. Redemption refuses unverified addresses with **Verify your dosya.dev email before redeeming a license.** 4. Review package name, storage contribution, provider, interval/end date, and current stacked total. Confirm activation once. 5. Check **Storage live**, then open Billing → **Redeemed packages** and match the contribution with **Total limit**. The opaque claim lasts 15 minutes. Five unknown coupon attempts trigger a 15-minute lock, and creating claims is capped at 10 attempts per IP per hour. Provider outages return **We could not verify this license right now. Please try again.** and preserve the claim for another attempt. The API marks a transient reservation race or **This redemption is already in progress. Please try again shortly.** as retryable; a claim reserved to another account, or a used, expired, invalid, or unavailable code, requires the owning account or a different valid claim. ## Expected result The package adds its stated bytes once, the raw code is absent from browser continuation state, and Billing records the grant’s lifecycle. For **This coupon code was already used** or **This redemption link has expired**, obtain a new valid code. Use **Redeem another** only for a different package. ## Related guides - [Manage redeemed packages](/account/manage-license-storage) - [Verify storage after an upgrade](/account/plan-verify-storage-upgrade)

body: The referral program adds 5 GB per qualifying friend for at most five credited friends, so the account can earn up to 25 GB. ## Steps 1. Open **Refer friends** and select **Copy** beside **Your invite link**. The label changes to **Copied** for two seconds. 2. Dosya checks qualification daily and displays a masked email plus a status such as pending, credited, held, blocked, expired, or revoked. 4. Confirm the progress text **[count] of 5 friends counted** and **+[size] earned**. 5. Open Billing and find **Referral bonus** in **Storage ledger**; it contributes to the bold total. Unqualified referrals expire after 30 days. Same-network referrals can be blocked, three sign-ups within one hour can be held for review, and a credited bonus can be revoked if the invitee is banned or requests deletion within 30 days after credit. ## Expected result Each eligible friend adds exactly 5 GB until the five-reward ceiling is reached, and the Billing total includes the credited bonus. **Failed to load your referrals. Please try again.** means the summary request failed. A pending row before day seven or 50 MB is expected; held and blocked results require review rather than repeated invitations. ## Related guides - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage) - [Choose a plan](/account/choose-plan)

body: Referral rewards depend on signup attribution, account age, verified email, owned storage, daily settlement, and anti-abuse review. The public row deliberately hides private rule details. ## Steps 1. Open **Refer friends** and locate the masked invited email under **Invited friends**. If no row exists, confirm privately whether the full invite URL was used during the account’s original signup. 2. Read the displayed label: **Waiting for activity**, **Under review**, **Counted**, or **Not eligible**. Internal pending or credited names are not shown to inviters. 3. For **Waiting for activity**, have the invited person verify their own email, let the account reach seven days old, and own at least 50 MiB of stored files. Do not request their password or private file links. 4. Allow the once-daily qualification sweep to run. The referral response can also remain privately cached for up to 30 seconds, so immediate repeated reloads do not force settlement. 5. When the row becomes **Counted**, compare progress with the **Referral bonus** Billing ledger line. Each qualifying friend grants 5 GB, up to five friends and 25 GB total. 6. If the result remains inconsistent, contact private support with masked email, approximate signup time, invite URL used, and visible label. Anti-abuse reasons remain private even when staff review is available. ## Expected result The missing reward is explained by absent signup attribution, **Waiting for activity**, **Under review**, **Not eligible**, daily timing, the reward cap, or a ledger discrepancy; a counted reward appears as **Referral bonus**. A referral that never qualifies expires after 30 days. A counted reward can be revoked during the 30-day clawback window if the invited account is banned or requests deletion. Unknown codes, self-referrals, and duplicate invited accounts are silent no-ops at signup. Visiting the link after an account already exists cannot retroactively attach that signup. ## Related guides - [Earn referral storage](/account/referral-storage) - [Understand Free allowances](/account/free-plan-allowances) - [Troubleshoot billing](/troubleshooting/billing) - [Contact support](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Understand an Address not allowed remote-download error
summary: Replace a blocked local, private, non-HTTPS, or redirected address with a public HTTPS file URL, then confirm Dosya accepts the new download job.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Understand an Address not allowed remote-download error” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/lib/ssrf-guard.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/probe.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/remote-downloads/index.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya accepts only public HTTPS sources for server-side downloads. The address guard rejects unsafe input before a job row is created, so this failure appears in the **Could not start download** toast as **This address isn’t allowed**, not as a failed item in the table. ## Before you start Open **Integrations > Remote download** in the intended workspace. You need membership plus the role permission to add files. Obtain a source URL that its owner authorizes Dosya’s server to fetch. The guard refuses non-HTTPS schemes, explicit ports other than `443`, and `localhost`, `.local`, or `.internal` hosts. For IPv4, it blocks loopback, private, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, Dosya’s own origin, and the `224.0.0.0/3` multicast and reserved range. For IPv6, it blocks `::`, `::1`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`, and IPv4-mapped or compatible forms whose embedded IPv4 address is blocked. DNS answers are checked too, and every redirect is checked again; five redirect hops are allowed. ## Steps 1. Copy the rejected address into a private note and identify its scheme, hostname, optional port, and redirect target without exposing embedded tokens. 2. Replace `http://` with a real provider-issued `https://` download URL; changing text alone does not help if that HTTPS endpoint still resolves to a blocked address. 3. Remove any non-443 port and avoid local machine names, router addresses, private cloud endpoints, or URLs that redirect into an internal network. 4. Test the replacement in a private browser window and require a public file response without VPN, local DNS, cookies, or an interactive sign-in. 5. Paste the replacement into the Remote download field, keep the intended destination selected, and choose **Fetch file** once. 6. Require the **Download started** toast and a new **Queued** row; if the same refusal returns, inspect every redirect rather than repeatedly submitting the original URL. ## Expected result Dosya accepts the public HTTPS source and creates a queued job. The browser may be closed after the success toast because the transfer runs on Dosya’s servers. A DNS lookup failure is reported as **Couldn’t reach that URL**, while a public URL that redirects to a private destination is still refused as an unsafe address. A blocked attempt consumes neither the three active-job slots nor the 20-job rolling daily allowance because no job was inserted. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot remote downloads](/integrations/remote-download-errors) - [Start a remote download](/integrations/remote-download-start)

title: Cancel an active remote download
summary: Cancel a queued or transferring remote download, understand the completion race, and remove its terminal row without deleting a file that already finished.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Cancel an active remote download” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/remote-downloads/[id].ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/durable-object.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: The X control has two meanings on the released Remote download table: an active row uses **Cancel download**, while a completed, failed, or cancelled row uses **Remove from list**. There is no confirmation dialog. ## Before you start Use the same Dosya account that started the job. Another workspace member receives **Only the person who started this download can remove it** even when they can see the workspace. Queued, downloading, and finalizing jobs are active. Cancellation is best effort at a defined commit boundary: a request that loses the race to completion leaves the row **Done** and preserves the registered file. ## Steps 1. Open **Integrations > Remote download** in the workspace shown when the job was submitted, then match the filename and start time. 2. Verify that the badge reads **Queued**, **Downloading**, or **Finalizing** and that the X tooltip says **Cancel download**. 3. Choose the X once; the page immediately sends the cancellation request without asking for another confirmation. 4. Wait for the next refresh, which occurs every three seconds while the page has an active job, and read the resulting badge instead of assuming cancellation won. 5. If the badge becomes **Cancelled**, verify that no file with this job’s result was registered in the selected folder; partial remote-download storage is cleaned up. 6. If the row is **Done**, keep or delete the completed file separately. Choose the terminal row’s X only when you want **Remove from list** to hide the job. ## Expected result A cancellation that wins stops the transfer, removes partial storage, and leaves a **Cancelled** row. A completion that wins stays **Done** with its file intact. Removing either terminal row only dismisses history; it does not delete a finished file and does not restore one of the 20 jobs allowed in the rolling 24-hour count. If the X reports **Could not remove download**, reload the workspace and check that you are signed in as the starter. Do not repeatedly click while the finalizing race is settling. ## Related guides - [Download a remote URL](/integrations/remote-download) - [Understand storage limits](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Choose a folder for a remote download
summary: Choose Home or a permitted folder in the active workspace, confirm the picker result before fetching, and find the completed file at that destination.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Choose a folder for a remote download” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/remote-downloads/index.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/ingest/register.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: A remote download is submitted to the active workspace and either **Home** or one live folder chosen through **Download into folder**. The destination is fixed in the job when **Fetch file** succeeds. ## Before you start Your workspace role must allow file uploads. A folder-confined member is automatically limited to that subtree: selecting Home with such a membership resolves to the member’s anchor rather than the literal workspace root. Changing workspaces after selecting a folder can leave a stale folder name in the form. The API refuses that combination with **Folder not found in this workspace**, so reselect the destination after every workspace switch. ## Steps 1. Switch to the workspace that should own the downloaded bytes before opening **Integrations > Remote download**. 2. Choose the folder button, initially labelled **Home**, and use the **Download into folder** dialog to browse only the permitted tree. 3. Highlight the intended folder and choose **Select**; confirm that its name replaces **Home** beside the URL field. 4. Paste the direct HTTPS file URL, recheck the active workspace and displayed folder together, then choose **Fetch file**. 5. Require **Download started** and note the queued row’s filename and byte total; the page can close while the server fetch continues. 6. After the badge reaches **Done**, open the chosen folder and verify the saved byte size. If that name already existed, look for the numeric suffix such as `report (2).pdf`. ## Expected result The completed file is registered in the folder captured at submission. A same-name file is preserved and the imported file receives a suffix rather than becoming a new version. Upload policy, storage quota, and backup locks still apply to this server-side ingest. If a folder was moved, trashed, or belongs to another workspace, select a current destination and create a new job. The existing job cannot be retargeted after submission. ## Related guides - [Download a remote URL](/integrations/remote-download) - [Understand storage limits](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Tell a direct file URL from a share page
summary: Test whether an HTTPS URL returns file bytes with a reliable size instead of an HTML share page, sign-in screen, or blocked redirect chain safely.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Tell a direct file URL from a share page” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/probe.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/ssrf-guard.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: The Remote download form expects a URL that returns file bytes directly. Dosya probes it with `GET` and `Range: bytes=0-0`; HTML and XHTML responses are treated as share pages even when a browser visually offers a download button. ## Before you start Use an authorized public HTTPS URL on port 443. The source must work without your browser session because Dosya does not forward cookies, interactive login state, or custom request headers. A usable response reports a positive total size through `Content-Range` on a `206` response or a numeric `Content-Length` otherwise. Dosya follows at most five redirects and applies the public-address check at every hop. ## Steps 1. Open the candidate link in a private browser window where you are signed out of the provider. 2. Reject any page that asks for login, renders sharing controls, or returns HTML instead of beginning the actual file response. 3. Inspect the final HTTPS address after redirects and confirm it uses no local hostname, private IP, or non-443 port. 4. Confirm the response identifies a positive byte length; a chunked stream with no total cannot be reserved as a remote download. 5. Paste the final direct URL into **Integrations > Remote download**, choose the destination, and select **Fetch file**. 6. Require **Download started**, then compare the queued filename and total bytes with the provider’s file before leaving the page. ## Expected result The probe accepts the response, derives the filename from `Content-Disposition` or the final URL, and creates a job with a known byte total. The stored name is sanitized and limited to 200 characters. **Not a direct file link** means the source returned HTML. **Source returned HTTP N** means the final response used an HTTP error status. Generate a provider download URL rather than reusing its sharing page. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot remote downloads](/integrations/remote-download-errors) - [Start a remote download](/integrations/remote-download-start)

title: Troubleshoot a failed remote download
summary: Use the exact startup toast or failed-row reason to separate URL, size, quota, lock, source, HTTP, and network failures before creating a new job.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Troubleshoot a failed remote download” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/remote-downloads/index.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/types.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/durable-object.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Remote-download failures happen either before submission or after a job exists. Startup refusals stay in the **Could not start download** toast; transfer failures remain as a **Failed** row with a specific reason. | Released message | What it means | | --- | --- | | **Address not allowed** | The URL or a redirect violates the public HTTPS address rules. | | **Not a direct file link** | The probe received HTML or XHTML. | | **Unknown file size** | No positive safe total came from `Content-Range` or `Content-Length`. | | **File too large** | The source exceeds 1 TB for resumable range mode or 10 GiB for stream mode. | | **Not enough storage** | Submission or completion could not reserve destination quota. | | **File changed on the source server** | Validator or byte count changed after the probe. | | **Connection to the source failed** | Network retries were exhausted. | | **Destination is a locked backup** | Final registration targeted a locked WordPress backup tree. | | **Source returned HTTP N** | The origin returned that terminal status. | ## Before you start Keep the failed row visible and record its filename, start time, byte progress, and exact reason. The table lists at most the newest 50 non-dismissed jobs. ## Steps 1. Decide whether the error appeared in the startup toast or in a created job row; this determines whether any transfer and daily-cap entry exists. 2. For URL errors, validate direct HTTPS access, public DNS, redirects, response content type, and a reliable positive size. 3. For **File too large**, use a range-capable source with a strong ETag for files up to 1 TB; otherwise the one-pass stream ceiling is 10 GiB. 4. For quota or lock failures, free capacity or select an unlocked folder before retrying, because the same failed job has no Retry action. 5. For network or HTTP failures, fix the origin first. Retryable `429` and `5xx` responses use 5, 10, 20, 40, and 80-second delays before the sixth failure becomes terminal. 6. Start one replacement job, watch its three-second page updates, and verify **Done** plus the destination file before dismissing the old row. ## Expected result The corrected request either creates a new queued job or exposes the remaining limit with its exact message. Failed rows do not resume; the new submission is the recovery unit. Dosya permits three active downloads per workspace and 20 created jobs in a rolling 24 hours. Dismissing a terminal row hides it but does not remove it from the daily count. ## Related guides - [Download a remote URL](/integrations/remote-download) - [Understand storage limits](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Monitor remote download progress
summary: Read remote-download states, byte progress, errors, and polling behavior; cancel active work or remove a finished row without deleting its file.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx, apps/web/src/stores/remote-downloads.ts, apps/web/src/components/layout/remote-download-indicator.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/remote-downloads/[id].ts, and apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/durable-object.ts. No production job was started or cancelled.
body: The Remote Downloads table shows server-side work for the active workspace. Active rows move through `queued`, `downloading`, and `finalizing`; terminal rows show **Done**, **Failed**, or **Cancelled**. A successful file is created only after finalization. ## Read each state - `queued` means the job row exists and is waiting for server execution. - `downloading` shows `bytes done / bytes total` and a floored percentage. Progress can pause while Dosya retries a transient network or source error. - `finalizing` means all source bytes may already be present while quota, destination locks, registration, and the final file row are completed. Do not treat 100% as **Done**. - **Done** displays the final size and stores a file ID. Only this state proves the file was registered in Dosya Files. - **Failed** retains an error label and does not register an incomplete object as a file. - **Cancelled** means remaining transfer work stopped and no incomplete file was registered or exposed in Dosya Files. Temporary-object teardown is best-effort, so the row does not prove that every storage cleanup call succeeded. The open Remote Downloads page polls every **3 seconds** while any row is active. The sidebar indicator uses a separate **5-second** refresh, aggregates sized jobs, lists at most four names, and adds `+N more` for additional active transfers. Neither interval is an estimate of source speed or completion time. ## Steps 1. Open **Integrations → Remote Downloads** in the workspace where the job was submitted. 2. Match the **File** column to the sanitized source filename. Hovering the truncated name exposes the submitted URL. 3. Track **Status**, **Progress**, and **Started**. Compare transferred bytes with the total rather than relying only on the progress ring. 4. When status becomes **Done**, open the selected Files folder and verify the final name and byte size. A collision may have added a suffix such as ` (2)` before the extension. 5. If the row becomes **Failed**, record its displayed reason before retrying with a corrected source or destination. ## Cancel or remove a row For an active job, the X control is titled **Cancel download**. Only the person who started the job can use it; another member receives **Only the person who started this download can remove it**. Cancellation can race with completion. If final registration wins, the response leaves the job done and the completed file remains. For **Done**, **Failed**, or **Cancelled**, the same X is titled **Remove from list**. It only hides the job row. It does not delete a completed file, does not erase the retained job record, and does not restore one of the workspace's 20 rolling daily starts. Delete an unwanted completed file separately in Files using the normal file controls. The list returns the newest **50** non-dismissed jobs for that workspace. Removing a row from this view is irreversible in the current UI because there is no restore control for dismissed transfer rows. ## Error labels and recovery - **Address not allowed** or **Not a direct file link** requires a different public HTTPS source. - **Unknown file size** means the origin did not provide a usable positive length. - **File too large** reflects the selected transfer strategy's ceiling. - **Not enough storage** can occur at start or again during finalization because capacity is rechecked. - **File changed on the source server** means the probed validator or size no longer matched; obtain a stable URL and create a new job. - **Connection to the source failed** follows exhausted network retries. **Source returned HTTP N** preserves the origin's terminal HTTP code. - **Destination is a locked backup** requires another live destination; retrying cannot bypass that lock. A failed or cancelled row has no registered or visible partial file to resume. Dosya attempts to abort multipart work and remove an unreferenced completed object, but those cleanup calls deliberately swallow teardown errors. Start a new job after fixing the named cause. A done row is independent of its source afterward, and removing it from the list does not affect cloud storage. ## Expected result The job either reaches **Done** and produces one complete file in the recorded folder, or ends with a specific failure/cancellation and no incomplete file. Any row removal has only a history-display effect, while file deletion remains a separate action. ## Related guides - [Download a remote URL](/integrations/remote-download) - [Understand storage limits](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Fix remote-download quota or locked-destination errors
summary: Resolve storage-cap and locked-backup destination failures, account for the completion-time quota check, and retry safely into a writable folder.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Fix remote-download quota or locked-destination errors” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/remote-downloads/index.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/durable-object.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/ingest/register.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: A remote download checks storage before it starts, checks again when it enters **Finalizing**, and performs an atomic reservation while registering the file. Capacity consumed by other work during the transfer can therefore produce **Not enough storage** at the end. A different terminal check protects WordPress backup trees. If the selected folder is under a live backup lock, the row reports **Destination is a locked backup** and no file is registered there. ## Before you start Record the destination workspace, folder, source size, and the failed row’s exact label. An owner-plan cap, workspace cap, file-size policy, extension policy, or upload role can block the request, but the Remote download table groups storage-cap failures under **Not enough storage**. ## Steps 1. Open the destination workspace’s storage view and compare available capacity with the failed job’s total bytes, allowing room for other active uploads. 2. Delete unneeded data or increase the applicable capacity, then refresh until the new free-space figure is visible. 3. If the row says **Destination is a locked backup**, choose a folder outside that backup tree or wait for its lock to end; repeated jobs to the same locked folder will fail again. 4. Return to **Integrations > Remote download**, reselect the active workspace and the verified writable folder. 5. Submit the direct URL as a new job; failed jobs cannot be resumed or retargeted, and their terminal X only removes them from the list. 6. Wait through **Finalizing**, require **Done**, and confirm the file’s full byte size inside the chosen folder before dismissing the failure. ## Expected result The replacement job passes the initial check, the completion-time check, and the final atomic reservation. The file is registered once in an unlocked destination, and the failed job remains only as removable history. If capacity still appears sufficient, check the workspace’s file-size and extension policies and confirm that your current membership can upload. The initial API toast preserves the detailed quota sentence even though a terminal row uses the shorter storage label. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot remote downloads](/integrations/remote-download-errors) - [Start a remote download](/integrations/remote-download-start)

title: Retry when a remote source file changed
summary: Replace a mutable source URL after Dosya detects changed length or validator data, then start a fresh job and verify the new file from zero.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Retry when a remote source file changed” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/chunks.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/durable-object.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya probes a source before transfer and expects the same object until completion. A range job sends the strong ETag through `If-Range`; a `200` response where `206` was expected proves the validator no longer matches. Stream mode also compares the received byte count with the probed size. ## Before you start Treat **File changed on the source server** as terminal. Dosya cleans up the partial object and does not continue by mixing bytes from two revisions. A signed URL can also become mutable when its provider regenerates content behind the same address. Prefer an immutable version URL or a fresh export whose contents will remain unchanged for the whole transfer. ## Steps 1. Record the failed row’s filename, expected total, and progress, then leave it visible while checking the origin. 2. Ask the source owner whether the object was replaced, regenerated, truncated, or still being uploaded after the Dosya job began. 3. Finish producing the source file and obtain a new public HTTPS URL tied to the final version rather than reusing a mutable endpoint. 4. Test that URL privately and confirm its reported total stays constant across two requests; a range-capable source should return `206` with a total and strong ETag. 5. Start a new Remote download job to the intended folder; the failed row has no restart-from-partial control. 6. Require **Done**, compare the stored byte size with the final source, and only then use the terminal X to remove the old row. ## Expected result The new transfer starts from byte zero and completes entirely from one source revision. No partial bytes from the changed job become a Dosya file. If the provider continuously rewrites the same URL, download the finished object locally and upload it through Dosya instead. A new remote job against an unstable address can reproduce the same terminal error. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot remote downloads](/integrations/remote-download-errors) - [Start a remote download](/integrations/remote-download-start)

title: Start a remote download from a direct URL
summary: Start a server-side remote download from a direct HTTPS file URL, choose its Dosya folder, and resolve permission, size, quota, or URL refusals.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/remote-downloads/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/probe.ts, apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/types.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/ingest/register.ts. No external URL or production workspace was fetched.
body: Remote download fetches a public HTTPS file on Dosya's servers and registers it in the chosen workspace folder. Your browser connection is not used for the file transfer, and you may close the page after the job starts. ## Requirements and limits Your role needs permission to add files to the destination. Folder-confined members can fetch only into their permitted subtree. The workspace's storage quota, per-file ceiling, allowed or blocked extensions, and locked-backup rules apply before or at completion. The source must be a publicly resolvable `https` URL that returns file bytes and a positive size. Google Drive or Dropbox share pages are HTML, so they are rejected; obtain a direct download address instead. Dosya follows at most **5 redirects** and rechecks every destination against its private-address guard. At most **3** remote jobs may run concurrently in one workspace, and the workspace can start **20** jobs in a rolling **24-hour** window. Dismissing an old row does not free its daily slot. Range-capable sources with a strong ETag can be as large as **1 TB**; sources that cannot resume are limited to **10 GiB**, and a smaller workspace policy may refuse either case. ## Steps 1. Switch to the destination workspace and open **Integrations → Remote Downloads**. 2. Paste the direct URL into the field showing `https://example.com/big-file.zip`. 3. Leave the folder button on **Home** for the workspace root, or select it to open **Download into folder**. Choose a live folder and press **Select**. 4. Select **Fetch file**. Dosya first probes the URL, reported size, content type, range support, quota, and workspace policy. 5. Wait for **Download started**. Its message says **dosya is fetching the file for you - you can close this page.** A new row appears with status **queued**. ## Resolve a refused start - **Could not start download – You don't have permission to add files** requires a role or destination change. - **That looks like a web page, not a file – paste a direct link to the file itself** means the source returned HTML. - **The server didn't report a file size, so this link can't be fetched** means Dosya could not establish the required positive size. - **This address isn't allowed** protects private, loopback, or otherwise disallowed network destinations. - **This file is too large to fetch** means the transfer strategy exceeded its 1 TB resumable or 10 GiB stream ceiling. - **Only 3 downloads can run at once - wait for one to finish** is the concurrency cap. **Daily limit of 20 remote downloads reached** clears only as earlier starts leave the rolling day. - **Folder not found in this workspace** means the selected destination is stale, trashed, or belongs elsewhere. The stored filename comes from `Content-Disposition` when available, otherwise from the final URL, and is sanitized to one path segment up to 200 characters. A live name collision is preserved by suffixing the new file, such as `report (2).pdf`; the existing file is not overwritten. ## Expected result The start toast appears and the newest job row names the sanitized file with `queued` status, zero transferred bytes, and the chosen workspace destination recorded. No file appears in Files until the server reaches **Done** and registers the completed object. ## Related guides - [Download a remote URL](/integrations/remote-download) - [Understand storage limits](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Fix an unknown-size remote download
summary: Choose a source that reports a positive Content-Length or total Content-Range, or download locally when Dosya cannot reserve an unknown byte count.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Fix an unknown-size remote download” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/pages/integrations/remote-download.tsx`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/probe.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/chunks.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/remote-download/types.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya must know the complete byte count before it can select a transfer strategy and check quota. Its probe requests `bytes=0-0`; a `206` response must include a numeric total in `Content-Range`, while a non-range response needs a numeric `Content-Length`. ## Before you start The startup toast says **The server didn’t report a file size, so this link can’t be fetched**. Because the probe fails before insertion, there is no failed job row and the attempt does not consume a daily job slot. Zero, negative, missing, malformed, or JavaScript-unsafe totals are refused. `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` by itself does not supply the reservation size Dosya requires. ## Steps 1. Test the direct HTTPS link outside your signed-in browser session and identify the final response after redirects. 2. Inspect the response to the range probe: accept `206` only when `Content-Range` ends with a positive total such as `/1048576`. 3. If the server answers `200`, require a positive decimal `Content-Length`; an estimated size in page text does not count. 4. Generate a different provider export or download endpoint that reports one of those exact headers and still returns file bytes rather than HTML. 5. Paste the replacement URL into Remote download, select the target folder, and choose **Fetch file** once. 6. Confirm **Download started** and verify the queued row shows a real total instead of `-` before relying on the transfer. ## Expected result The probe returns a positive known size, Dosya checks policy and quota, and a queued job is created. Range mode can accept up to 1 TB when a strong ETag is also present; the fallback stream path is limited to 10 GiB. When the origin cannot expose a stable length, download the file locally and use a normal Dosya upload. The released remote-download API has no unknown-length streaming mode. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot remote downloads](/integrations/remote-download-errors) - [Start a remote download](/integrations/remote-download-start)

title: Download a direct URL into your workspace
summary: Give Dosya a direct HTTPS file URL, choose the destination folder, monitor the server-side transfer, and resolve common source or quota failures.
verification: Reviewed the current Remote download form, destination picker, transfer states, progress, cancellation and source error labels against the local current web app and API on 2026-10-12. The screenshot uses isolated fictional URLs.
body: Remote download lets Dosya fetch a file from a direct HTTPS URL into an ordinary workspace folder. The source transfer runs on Dosya's servers, so the file does not pass through your local connection. ## Before you start - Use a direct HTTPS link that returns the file itself. A Google Drive, Dropbox or other share page is not a direct file link. - Select the destination workspace and confirm you have upload access there. - Check available storage and workspace file-size or file-type policies. - Use only a source you are authorized to copy. - These steps create an ordinary workspace file. They do not place the result in Vault. ## Steps: start and monitor a remote download 1. Open **Integrations → Remote download**. 2. Confirm the active workspace above the sidebar. 3. Paste the complete direct HTTPS file URL. 4. Select the folder button, choose the destination, and verify its name. **Home** is the workspace root. 5. Select **Fetch file**. 6. Watch the job move through **Queued**, **Downloading** and **Finalizing** until it shows **Done**. You may close this page after the job starts and return to review it. 7. Open **Files**, go to the destination and confirm the downloaded name and size. ## Expected result The job reaches **Done**, and the completed file appears in the chosen ordinary workspace folder. The local device did not need to relay the source bytes. ## Limits and source requirements - Only direct HTTPS file links are accepted. Web pages that require a click, cookie, interactive login or provider share flow may fail. - The source must report enough information for a safe download. A source with unknown size can be refused. - Workspace storage, file-size, file-type, permission and locked-destination rules still apply. - If the source changes during transfer, Dosya can stop rather than store an inconsistent result. - Removing a completed job from the list is separate from deleting its stored file in **Files**. ## Troubleshooting **Not a direct file link.** Open the provider's supported import integration, or obtain an authorized URL that returns the file body directly. Copying a browser share page is not enough. **Address not allowed.** Use a normal public HTTPS file source. Private, local or otherwise restricted network destinations are refused. **Unknown file size or File too large.** Use a source that reports its size and confirm the resulting file fits current account and workspace limits. **Not enough storage.** Check workspace usage, deleted items and applicable caps. Free space or choose a workspace with enough allowance before retrying. **File changed on the source server.** Wait for the source to stabilize, obtain a fresh direct link and start a new job. **Connection to the source failed or Source returned HTTP error.** Check that the source is online and the URL remains valid without your signed-in browser session. **The destination is a locked backup.** Choose a writable ordinary folder permitted by your role. ## Related guides - [Upload files and folders from your device](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Download files from Dosya](/uploading/download-files) - [Understand storage usage and quota checks](/uploading/storage-usage) - [Import from Google Drive](/integrations/google-drive)

title: Remove an item from Favourites
summary: Remove a personal file shortcut from Favourites without moving or deleting its source, then confirm both the sidebar and original file state.
verification: Locally source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 in apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/mobile/src/player/useFavourite.ts, apps/mobile/src/files/mutations.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/favourites.ts. Production removal was deliberately not exercised.
body: Removing a favourite deletes only your shortcut row. It does not send the source file to Trash, remove a version, revoke a share, or affect another member's list. ## Before you start - Note the file's original folder and name so you can distinguish shortcut removal from content deletion. - In the browser, keep the **Favourites** section expanded. Its X button appears when you hover the row and has the tooltip **Remove favourite**. - The file action menu may instead say **Remove favourite**, while grid and viewer star buttons use **Remove from favourites**. All three remove the same per-user row. ## Steps 1. Choose one removal control: - Hover the browser sidebar favourite and select its X button. - Open the file menu and choose **Remove favourite**. - Select the filled star labelled **Remove from favourites** in a grid or viewer. - In the mobile audio player, tap **Remove favourite**. 2. Wait until the request completes. Browser controls update only on success; the mobile player removes the cached favourite immediately and restores it if the request fails. Error copy differs by browser control, so note whether you used the sidebar X or a star/menu action. 3. Refresh or reopen Favourites and confirm the shortcut no longer appears. 4. Browse to the file's recorded folder and open it. Check that its name, size, current version, and comments still exist. The deletion endpoint is idempotent for your shortcut.
