Removing an already-absent favourite still returns success and does not emit a misleading removal event. It cannot remove a favourite owned by another account because the server always binds the deletion to the signed-in user. ## Expected result Your Favourites list no longer contains that file, and the file is still stored in its original folder. Storage usage and workspace permissions do not change. There is no destructive effect to undo. To restore the shortcut, open the source file and use **Add to favourites** again. ## Troubleshooting **The sidebar X is not visible.** Move the pointer over the favourite row, or use the filled star on the file. **The sidebar X reports “Remove failed.”** Its detail is **Could not remove from favourites.** The shortcut remains in the sidebar; restore network access and retry that X control. **A grid, menu, or viewer star reports “Something went wrong.”** Its detail is **Could not update favourites.** The old star remains selected. Retry after connectivity returns; **Delete** is a separate content action. **The shortcut vanished before you removed it.** A hidden rule or unopened full-lock ancestor can filter it from Favourites. Find the file through an allowed path or regain access before changing the saved pointer. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Search files](/files/search-files)

title: Remove a file from a group
summary: Remove one pinned file from a personal group in Dosya Desktop, then confirm the source file stays in its folder and only the shortcut disappears.
verification: Reviewed against local source on 2026-10-14 in apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/GroupsPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/groups-api.ts, apps/mobile/app/groups.tsx, apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/groups/[id]/files/[fileId].ts, and its unit test. Production group data was not changed.
body: A group stores personal pins to existing objects. Removing one file pin leaves the file, its folder, versions, comments, shares, and storage usage unchanged. The reviewed **Remove from group** control is available on Dosya Desktop's **Groups** page. Browser and mobile group views do not currently show an item-removal button. ## Before you start - Open Dosya Desktop and select the workspace containing the personal group. - Choose **Groups**, locate the group card, and note its item count. - Record the pinned file's normal folder and file size. The group can include same-named objects from different folders. - Only the group creator can change its pins. Another user's group is deliberately reported as “Group not found,” even to a workspace administrator. ## Steps 1. Expand the intended group card if needed and find the file row, identified by filename and displayed size. 2. Select the X button on that row. Its tooltip is **Remove from group**. 3. The desktop app sends the removal immediately; there is no confirmation dialog. 4. Wait for the Groups query to refresh. Confirm that the row disappears and the card count falls by one. 5. Open **Files**, browse to the recorded folder, and open the source file. The server returns success even if that file pin was already absent, making a retry safe. It emits a removal activity only when a stored pin actually matched. An unknown group or one owned by a different user produces “Group not found”; a network or API refusal appears in the desktop error toast. ## Expected result The file vanishes from that one personal group and remains openable in its original folder. Other groups can still point to it, and other users' organization views do not change. The removal has no automatic undo, but it is reversible: open the file's action menu, choose **Add to group**, and select the original group again. ## Troubleshooting **There is no X beside the item.** Confirm you are using Dosya Desktop's Groups page. The browser sidebar can expand a group, but its item rows only open their targets. **The wrong file was removed.** Nothing was deleted. Find the source in Files and add it back to the group. **The row remains after an error.** The mutation did not receive success, so the list was not refreshed. Verify the signed-in account owns that group, restore connectivity, and retry. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Search files](/files/search-files)

title: Rename a folder without losing contents
summary: Rename a Dosya folder without moving or re-uploading its contents, using exact name limits and resolving sibling-name or permission conflicts.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/mobile/src/files/mutations.ts, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/rename.ts, packages/shared/src/validation/policy.ts, and rename conflict tests. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Renaming changes one folder label under its existing parent. The folder ID, descendants, stored file bytes, and workspace usage remain the same. ## Before you start - The current role needs `rename_folders`. Web, mobile, and desktop hide **Rename** when that role grant is absent. - A folder name is one path segment from 1 through 100 trimmed characters. `/`, `\`, control characters, `.`, and `..` are invalid. - Check the current parent for a live sibling with the proposed name. The server refuses collisions instead of merging folders. - A folder inside a locked WordPress backup, or one containing a protected backup relationship, cannot be renamed until that backup lock permits it. ## Steps 1. Open the folder’s context or actions menu and choose **Rename**. 2. In the **Rename** dialog, replace the folder name. Do not enter a nested path; use **Move to...** for a parent change. 3. Press **Rename** or Enter. 4. Wait for **Renamed** or **The folder has been renamed**. 5. Refresh the current parent and open the renamed folder. 6. Inspect its breadcrumb and one nested file to confirm the child tree remains available. ## Expected result The same folder ID appears under the same parent with the new name. Child folders and files are not rewritten. ID-based sharing continues to reference the same folder, while WebDAV, S3, desktop sync, or local bookmarks that use the old path must refresh to the new path. ## Troubleshooting - **“Name is required.”** Enter at least one non-space character. - **“Name too long (max 100).”** Shorten the folder name; the limit counts characters after trimming. - **“Name contains invalid characters.”** Remove separators, control characters, or a whole-name `.` or `..` value. - **“A folder with this name already exists in this folder.”** Choose a unique sibling name. The rejected request leaves the original name and contents unchanged. - **“You don’t have permission to rename folders.”** Ask a workspace administrator for `rename_folders`. - **The old name remains on another device.** Refresh the directory or wait for that client’s next sync snapshot. Do not create a second folder while a stale listing is visible. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Rename an organization group
summary: Rename a personal group in Dosya Desktop, keep its pinned files and folders, and resolve empty, overlong, missing-access, or save failures safely.
verification: Source-verified on 2026-10-14 against apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/GroupsPage.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/groups-api.ts, apps/mobile/app/groups.tsx, apps/mobile/src/groups/api.ts, apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/groups/[id].ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/groups/[id].unit.test.ts. The rename was not performed against production.
body: Groups are personal shortcuts: only their creator sees them, even when several people belong to the same workspace. Renaming one changes its label and leaves every pinned file and folder in place. The current rename control is in **Dosya Desktop**. The browser sidebar and mobile **My groups** screen can create, open, or delete groups, but they do not currently expose Rename. ## Before you start - Open Dosya Desktop, select the correct workspace, and choose **Groups** in the sidebar. - Record the group's current item count. A group may contain files and folders from different locations in that workspace. - Your account must still belong to the workspace, have access to the Files page, and own the group. Workspace owner or admin status does not make another person's group editable. ## Steps 1. Find the group card and select its pencil button, whose tooltip is **Rename**. 2. Replace the text in the inline name field. Leading and trailing spaces are removed when the name is sent. 3. Keep the trimmed name between 1 and 100 characters. The checkmark is disabled for a blank value or more than 100 characters. 4. Select the checkmark to save. Pressing Enter also submits a nonblank value; Escape or the X button cancels the edit. 5. Wait for the Groups list to refresh, then reopen or inspect the renamed card. The server answers an empty value with “Group name is required” and a 101-character value with “Group name too long.” A missing, deleted, or someone else's group is reported as “Group not found”; a former member receives “Access denied.” The desktop error toast shows the server message and keeps the edit available for correction. ## Expected result The card displays the new trimmed name, while its colour, item count, file pins, folder pins, and the underlying stored content remain unchanged. Renaming neither moves data nor changes anybody's file access. There is no separate undo history for a group name. If the wrong label was saved, select **Rename** again and restore the previous text. ## Troubleshooting **Rename is absent.** Use Dosya Desktop. Browser and mobile group views do not offer that control in the reviewed release. **The group disappeared.** Confirm the active workspace and signed-in account. Because groups are per-user, switching accounts shows a different collection. **Saving failed but the old name remains.** Correct the length or retry after connectivity returns. The API updates the name only after a successful request, so a refused save does not partially rename the group. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Search files](/files/search-files)

title: Change a file-request destination folder
summary: Move future file-request uploads to another workspace folder without moving existing files, while checking scope, lock, permission, and visibility rules.
verification: Verified against apps/web/src/components/file-request-edit-dialog.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id].ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/manage-own.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts; and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: Changing **Upload destination** redirects files accepted after the save. Dosya does not relocate submissions that are already stored, so a request can have older files in its previous folder and newer files in the replacement folder. ## Availability and permissions The destination picker is available in the web app. Desktop and mobile can edit the request title and message, but their request screens do not expose a destination control. The editor must be allowed to manage the request and have **Upload files** permission. **View all shares** permits management of every request; **View own shares** permits management only when the signed-in member created it. Owners and Admins normally have all-share access, Members normally manage their own requests, and Viewers do not manage requests. No separate paid-tier check appears in the destination update endpoint. A folder-confined member can select only a live, visible folder inside their permitted subtree. Choosing the workspace root maps to that member's scope anchor instead of escaping the confinement boundary. ## Steps 1. In the web app, open **File requests** and locate the correct request by title, status, and creation date. 2. Choose **Edit**, then open **Upload destination**. 3. Select the new folder. Choose **Root (workspace top level)** only when future submissions truly belong at the root; a confined member's effective root is their assigned anchor. 4. Make sure the folder is active, visible to your role, and not fully locked. Do not delete or lock it while the request remains open. 5. Select **Save changes**. A successful web save shows **Request updated** followed by **Your changes have been saved.** 6. Send one small, non-sensitive test file through the existing request link. Find it in the new folder before asking recipients to continue. 7. Check the former folder separately for earlier submissions. Move those files manually only if your retention and access rules allow it. ## Folder behavior after saving The public request URL, recipient URLs, title, message, password, expiry, extension rule, size ceiling, and file-count limit do not change. Dosya does not mail recipients about a destination update. Uploaders normally see the workspace and request instructions rather than the owner's internal folder path. When **Put each uploader in their own folder** was enabled for the request, future uploader folders are created below the newly selected destination. The destination edit does not merge those folders with uploader folders at the prior location. Uploads already completed stay attached to their existing workspace files. The owner request view can therefore list files whose storage locations differ. Changing a destination is reversible for future files by selecting the former folder again, but it never rolls back an upload that has already completed. ## Expected result The request keeps its existing public address and accepts the next valid file into the newly selected folder. Older submissions remain in place, and recipients receive no automatic notice of the internal routing change. ## Troubleshooting **The picker is absent.** Open Dosya in a web browser. The desktop and mobile request editors currently offer **Edit title and message**, without folder selection. **Saving returns “You don't have upload permission in this workspace.”** Ask a workspace administrator to grant **Upload files**, or have an eligible manager perform the change. Share-management permission by itself is insufficient for destination edits. **Dosya reports “Folder not found in workspace.”** The chosen folder may have been removed, may belong to another workspace, may be hidden from your role, or may sit outside your allowed subtree. Select a visible folder within scope. **The API returns `folder_locked`.** A full folder lock blocks new content. Unlock that folder or point the request at an unlocked destination before another recipient uploads. **A new upload remains in the old location.** Reopen **Edit request** to confirm the saved destination, then verify the upload finished after the change. Anything accepted before the save remains in the earlier folder by design. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Close a file request after collecting uploads
summary: Review received and pending submissions, revoke the file-request upload link, and verify that new uploads stop while previously received files remain available.
verification: Reviewed the current web File requests list, request detail page, Revoke action, recipient notification path and public upload-request API against local product source and relevant tests on 2026-10-14. Revocation returns the public request as gone while preserving previously received files. The screenshot uses isolated request data.
body: Close a file request when you have received everything you expect or when its upload URL should no longer accept files. In the current Dosya web app, closing a request uses **Revoke**. Revocation stops new uploads immediately and keeps files that were already received. ## Before you start 1. Open **Shared**, then open **File requests**. 2. Confirm the active workspace and select the exact request. Requests with similar titles can point to different folders or recipient lists. 3. On the request detail page, review the status badge, file count and expiry. 4. Expand **Recipients** when the request was sent by email. Compare **uploaded** and **pending** counts and follow up with anyone who still needs to send a file. 5. Review the received file list. Check names, sizes, uploader details and received times. Download or preview a harmless sample when content verification is required. 6. Confirm the destination folder still contains the received files. Revoking the request does not move them to another folder. If the request should remain open but needs a different deadline, password, message or upload limit, use **Edit** instead. Use **Revoke** only when the public upload channel should close. ## Steps: close the request 1. On the active request's detail page, select **Revoke**. 2. Wait for the request to reload and show the **Revoked** status. 3. Confirm that **Edit** and **Revoke** are no longer available. The file list remains available to authorized workspace members. 4. If the request has named recipients, expect Dosya to notify them that the request was closed. Contact critical recipients directly when delivery confirmation matters. 5. Open the old request URL in a private browser window. It should report that the file request has been revoked and must not show upload controls. ## Expected result The request shows **Revoked** in Dosya. Opening its public URL returns a revoked message, and upload attempts through that URL are rejected. Files received before revocation remain in the request detail page and destination folder. ## Limits and important details - The request URL stops accepting single-part and resumable uploads. - Password unlock and recipient-specific invitation URLs do not reopen the request. - Existing received files remain ordinary workspace files and continue to follow workspace permissions, locks, retention and trash rules. - Revocation cannot be undone from the current web app. Create a new request when collection must resume, then send its new URL. - An expired request is already closed by its deadline. The current detail page does not offer **Revoke** after expiry. ## Troubleshooting **Revoke is missing.** Check the status badge. Revoked and expired requests are already closed. For an active request, confirm that you created it or have permission to manage file requests in the workspace. **A recipient says the old page is still open.** Ask them to refresh the page and try a harmless upload. A page left open before revocation cannot complete a new upload after the server rejects the request. **A file arrived near the time you revoked.** Check its received time, filename and size in the request detail page. An upload that completed before revocation can remain; an incomplete transfer cannot be resumed afterward. **You closed the wrong request.** Revocation is not reversible. Keep its received files, create a replacement request with the correct destination and settings, and send the new URL only to the intended recipients. **Received files appear missing.** Confirm the active workspace and request, clear any search filter, and inspect the destination folder. Contact private support with the request ID and nonsecret timestamps if the request count and folder listing disagree. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Change or close a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request) - [Review files submitted to a request](/sharing/request-review-uploads)

title: Choose a destination for requested files
summary: Choose where requested files land, understand root and per-uploader folders, and verify the destination safely before inviting external uploaders.
verification: Verified against apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/create.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts; and apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/guard.ts. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: The **Upload destination** controls where Dosya stores every accepted submission. Decide it before distributing the link, because selecting another folder later affects future uploads only. ## Before you choose The web creation dialog includes a folder picker. Desktop and mobile creation forms do not, so requests created there use the effective workspace root. Use the web app when a specific receiving folder is required. Creating a request requires **Upload files** in the current workspace. For a folder-confined member, the effective root is the member's assigned anchor and every chosen folder must remain within that subtree. A destination must be live, visible, and writable; a fully locked folder cannot accept a request. The creation endpoint does not apply a distinct paid-plan feature gate. The web form enables **Put each uploader in their own folder** by default. With that option on, Dosya separates submitters below the request destination. Turn it off only when all received files should share one folder. ## Steps 1. In the web app, open **File requests** and choose **New request**. 2. Select **By email** to send invitations, or **By link** to copy a public URL. 3. Enter **Title (optional)** and **Message (optional)**. A clear title makes the resulting storage folder easier to recognize. 4. Open **Upload destination** and select the intended live folder. Leaving the field blank displays **Root (workspace top level)**; scoped members are still confined to their anchor. 5. Decide whether to keep **Put each uploader in their own folder** enabled. When enabled, each submitter's files are grouped under the request location. 6. Configure **Expires**, **Password (opt)**, and any **Advanced options** such as **Allowed extensions**, **Max file size (MB)**, or **Max files**. 7. Complete the request. Email mode needs at least one valid address and accepts at most the first 100 submitted recipient addresses; link mode returns the shareable request URL. 8. Before distributing it widely, upload one harmless file through the public page and confirm its exact folder in workspace storage. ## How Dosya builds the folders If uploader folders are on and the request has a title, Dosya first creates a folder named from that title below the chosen destination, then records that folder as the request's receiving location. Individual uploader folders are created underneath it. Without a title, uploader folders sit directly below the selected destination. The public page may use a verified recipient identity, an entered name or email, a dropped folder name, or a generated guest label to build the uploader path. Folder names are normalized before storage. The uploader sees the workspace and request details, not a browser for the owner's internal folder tree. A recipient does not need a Dosya account. Their accepted files become workspace data that authorized members can see according to folder scope and hidden-item rules. The request's storage consumes workspace quota. ## Expected result A test upload is accepted once, appears beneath the chosen live destination, and follows the selected shared-folder or per-uploader layout. Invitations continue to use the same request policy that was confirmed during setup. ## Troubleshooting **Creation says “You don't have upload permission in this workspace.”** Use a role with **Upload files** or ask a workspace administrator to create the request. **You receive “Destination folder not found.”** Reopen the picker. The folder may be deleted, hidden, in another tenant, or outside the current member's scope. **The response contains “folder_locked.”** Full lock prevents any new file or folder below that destination. Choose another location or have an authorized member unlock it. **Dosya says it could not create the titled folder.** The API returns **Could not create the “Title” folder for this request** when per-uploader setup cannot create the request folder. Check naming, write access, folder state, and workspace quota before retrying. **The request opens but uploads fail later.** A destination can be locked or the workspace can fill after creation. The public uploader may show **This upload request can no longer accept files.** for a later lock; select an available destination or free storage before another attempt. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Edit file-request instructions
summary: Edit a file request's title and uploader message across supported clients, understand permission rules, and confirm what changes for existing invitees.
verification: Verified against apps/web/src/components/file-request-edit-dialog.tsx; apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileRequestsPage.tsx; apps/mobile/app/file-requests/[id].tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id].ts; and apps/api/src/lib/access/manage-own.ts. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: The request **Title** identifies the collection to uploaders, while **Message (optional)** carries directions such as a naming convention or deadline. Updating either field changes the public upload page after it is reloaded. It does not replace the request link, move files, or send a revised email to people who were invited earlier. ## Who can edit the wording An Owner or Admin can normally manage every request in the workspace. A Member can edit a request they created when the role includes **View own shares**. A Viewer has neither own-share nor all-share management by default. A custom role with **View all shares** can manage any request; **View own shares** limits the person to requests they created. Changing only the title or message does not require **Upload files** permission. Expiry, password, destination, extension, file-size, and file-count changes do require that additional permission. The request endpoints do not contain a paid-plan branch for these text fields; workspace permissions decide access. Use the web app, desktop app, or mobile app for this task. The web command is **Edit**. Desktop and mobile group these fields under **Edit title and message**. ## Steps 1. Open **File requests** in the workspace that owns the request. 2. On the web, find the request and choose **Edit**. On desktop or mobile, open its details and choose **Edit title and message**. 3. Change **Title** or **Message (optional)**. Leading and trailing spaces are removed when the value is saved; leaving either field empty clears it. 4. Select **Save changes** on the web, or the corresponding save action in the native client. The web confirms with **Request updated** and **Your changes have been saved.** 5. Open the existing request link in a private browser window and reload it. Check the displayed title and message as an uploader would see them. 6. If recipients need the new wording in their inbox, resend their invitations separately. Saving these fields alone does not send mail. ## What changes for uploaders The next load of the public page shows the current title and message. An invitation already delivered keeps the wording embedded in that email, although its link opens the updated page. The request token, personalized recipient token, password, expiry, accepted extensions, maximum size, maximum file count, and receiving folder remain unchanged. No file is renamed or moved by a wording edit. Existing upload records and recipient states also stay intact. Clearing the message simply removes that optional paragraph from the public page. ## Expected result The owner sees the saved text when reopening the edit form, and an uploader sees the same current wording after refreshing the public request. Existing invitations are not reissued, and previously received files remain where they were stored. ## Troubleshooting **You see “You don't have permission to change this file request.”** Confirm that you created the request and have **View own shares**, or ask a role with **View all shares** to edit it. Gaining **Upload files** alone does not grant request management. **The request cannot be opened.** The web detail screen reports **This file request does not exist or you do not have access to it.** Check the workspace and account, then ask an Admin to verify that the request still exists and falls inside your folder scope. **A recipient still sees the former wording.** Have them reload the public link. If they are reading the old invitation message itself, use **Recipients** and **Resend** after confirming the new copy. **You need to change the destination or limits.** Use the web **Edit request** dialog with **Upload files** permission. Those settings change upload behavior and should be verified independently. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Track a failed file-request submission
summary: Diagnose rejected or interrupted file-request uploads from exact messages, then retry safely without resending files that were already received.
verification: Verified against src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro; apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/guard.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts; and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/complete.ts. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: A failed item has not reached the request owner's live upload list. Diagnose the message beside that file, preserve every completed item, and retry only what remains failed or cancelled. Recipients do not need a Dosya account to use an active public request. ## Steps 1. Keep the upload page open and find the failed file. Record its name, byte size, and complete error text. 2. Leave completed items alone. The page retains prior successes, and retrying the whole selection can produce a second workspace file with a collision-adjusted name. 3. Correct the cause described below. If the request owner must change policy, ask them to update the active request before you retry. 4. Choose **Retry** on that failed row. Large multipart retries resume the same active session and send only missing parts. 5. If a stalled item is no longer needed, choose **Discard**. Dosya aborts an incomplete multipart session and releases its reserved file slot; it does not remove another file that already completed. 6. Wait for the finished receipt. It states that the requester has the files, shows total bytes and time, and includes a reference. Send that reference to the owner if reconciliation is needed. ## Read the exact rejection The browser checks several rules before transferring bytes: - **This file has no extension, so its type cannot be checked** means the request accepts only listed extensions and the selected item has none. - **.ext is not accepted here - send ...** identifies an extension outside **Allowed extensions**. - **This file is empty** rejects a zero-byte item. - **This file is over the X limit for this request** compares the local size with **Max file size (MB)**. - **There is no slot left on this request** means its configured maximum file count has been reached. The server checks the received data again. It can return **File type .ext is not allowed. Accepted: ...**, **File is too large. Maximum size is X.Y MB**, or **This request has reached its file limit.** The actual received byte length is authoritative. A direct single-part attempt above 50 MiB is refused with **File exceeds the 50 MB limit for a single upload; use the multipart flow**. Files larger than 50 MiB use multipart upload with 10 MiB parts. Dosya transfers up to three files in parallel, and a multipart file can send up to three parts concurrently. Completion waits for every expected part; **Only X of Y parts uploaded. Upload remaining parts before completing.** means the session can still be resumed. ## Access, storage, and connection failures **This request has expired** or **This file request has expired** means the deadline passed; only the owner can extend the request or create another one. **This request was closed** and **This file request has been revoked** mean the owner revoked access. Files already received remain with the workspace in both cases. **No request at this link** or **Request not found** indicates an invalid or deleted token. Ask the sender for a fresh link instead of editing the URL. **Could not reach dosya.dev** is a page-load network problem. If password access lapses during a transfer, the page pauses remaining work and shows **Your access timed out**. Enter the current password to continue; successfully received files are not lost. After repeated wrong guesses, **Too many attempts. Unlocking is paused for 15 minutes - ask the sender for the password rather than guessing.** Wait the full interval or obtain the correct password. **This upload request can no longer accept files.** means the destination became fully locked after the link was created. Workspace quota errors require the owner to free storage or adjust their workspace capacity. Neither condition is fixed by changing browser or by repeated retries. **The connection dropped. Nothing was saved.** applies to that failed attempt. Retry after connectivity stabilizes. A multipart session that reports **Upload session is no longer active - start the upload again** cannot resume; select the file again to create a new session. **Failed to finalize upload in storage** and **Failed to record file** require a new attempt after the service recovers. ## Platform and policy notes Uploaders use the public browser page on desktop or phone. Pointer devices offer **Browse files** and **Choose a folder**; touch devices show **Photo library**, **Take a photo**, and **Browse files**. The owner manages request limits and destination from the Dosya web app; desktop and mobile do not expose destination changes. Request upload access has no separate recipient role or paid-plan requirement. The workspace owner remains subject to storage quota, request expiry, password, extension, byte-size, file-count, and destination-lock rules. A rejected or aborted attempt deliberately releases its reserved request slot; a completed upload consumes one slot. ## Expected result Only the unsuccessful item is retried, its progress reaches completion, and the final receipt identifies the accepted bytes and time. The owner sees the new live file once, while earlier successful uploads remain unchanged. ## Troubleshooting **Retry repeats an extension or size error.** The file still violates current request policy. Select a permitted file or ask the owner to change **Allowed extensions** or **Max file size (MB)**; renaming an extension does not alter actual file content. **The page says all slots are full.** The owner must raise **Max files**, remove a suitable prior upload through an authorized flow, or create another request. Retrying cannot exceed the atomic slot limit. **The owner cannot find the file after a receipt.** Provide the receipt reference, filename, byte count, and time. The owner should inspect the request's current destination, visibility scope, and Trash rather than asking you to upload it again immediately. **A cancelled item appears ready again.** Cancellation stages the file for another attempt. Use **Discard** to abandon its incomplete session, or remove it from the list if the interface offers that control. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Setting file-request types, sizes, counts and expiry
summary: Choose what a request accepts, where submissions land, when uploading stops and how uploader folders are organized.
verification: Verified the current Request files and Edit request dialogs, public request terms and preflight errors, web/API source and focused file-request tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated local current-API fixtures and fictional request data. The review confirmed extension, per-file size, total-file count and expiry inputs; server-side enforcement; default uploader folders; title-folder creation; destination visibility and full-lock gates; and workspace storage enforcement. Production email delivery and large multipart transfer were not exercised. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Open **File requests → New request**, choose **By link** or **By email**, and expand **Advanced options**. Use **Allowed extensions** for file types, **Max file size (MB)** for each file and **Max files** for the request's total slots. The public page displays the active rules before an uploader selects anything. ## Before you start - Choose a live destination that you can access. Hidden, missing or fully locked folders cannot become a public upload destination. - Estimate the largest intended original file and the total number of submissions. Test uploads consume request slots too. - Check the receiving workspace's available storage. Leaving a field blank does not bypass storage or workspace policy. - Decide whether each uploader should receive a separate folder. This option is selected by default for new requests. ## Steps: set the request rules 1. Open **File requests** and select **New request**. 2. Choose **By link** for a URL you distribute yourself, or **By email** to create tracked invitations. 3. Enter a clear title and message. These tell uploaders what to submit. 4. Choose **Expires**: **Never**, **1 day**, **7 days**, **30 days** or **90 days**. The initial selection is **7 days**. 5. Choose **Upload destination**. If no folder is selected, the control shows **Root (workspace top level)**. 6. Keep **Put each uploader in their own folder** selected when submissions should stay separated. With a title, Dosya creates a title folder and then a folder for each uploader beneath it. 7. Expand **Advanced options**. 8. Enter comma-separated **Allowed extensions** with leading dots, such as `.pdf, .svg, .png`. 9. Enter **Max file size (MB)** for the largest permitted individual file. 10. Enter **Max files** for the total completed-file slots across the request. 11. Generate or send the request, then open its public page privately and verify the displayed **Accepts**, **Per file** and **Slots** rows. ## How each limit behaves **Allowed extensions** compares the final filename extension without regard to letter case. A file with no extension cannot pass the browser's type check when a list is present. Renaming an extension does not convert file contents. **Max file size (MB)** applies to one file. It is not a combined transfer-size limit. The browser rejects an oversized staged file before upload, and the API checks again before storing it. **Max files** counts completed uploads across the request. The public page subtracts the existing upload count and shows the remaining slots. Once every slot is taken, it closes the drop area and says the request is full. **Expires** stores a deadline from the time you create or edit the request. After the deadline, the public page stops accepting files. **Never** removes this request-level deadline; revocation, storage and other gates still apply. ## Uploader folders and destination When uploader folders are enabled, Dosya chooses a folder label from the typed name, verified invitation address, typed email, dropped folder name or a generated guest code. If two people choose the same name, the code keeps their folders distinct. Folder picks remain subject to workspace boundaries. A confined member can only target their allowed subtree. A request cannot point into a fully locked folder, even when its creator temporarily unlocked that folder in their own session. ## Expected result The public request page states the active rules. Accepted files can be staged and submitted; disallowed extensions, oversized files, empty files and files beyond the remaining slot count are marked before transfer. Completed files land in the selected destination, organized into uploader folders when enabled. ## Limits and editing behavior - Blank advanced fields add no request-specific restriction for that field. - Zero clears the size or count restriction when editing through the current controls; negative and non-finite values are rejected by the API. - Editing a rule affects later submissions. It does not rewrite or remove files already received. - Request limits do not reserve storage. Another upload or workspace policy can consume capacity before an uploader finishes. ## Troubleshooting **A valid file is marked not accepted.** Compare the final extension with the displayed chips. Export the file to an accepted format rather than only changing its name. **The request says every slot is full.** Open its detail page and review completed uploads. Raise **Max files** or create a new request when more submissions are intended. **A file fits the request but still fails.** Check workspace storage, folder locks and service status. The request's size limit is only one of the upload gates. **The destination cannot be selected.** Confirm the folder exists, is visible to your role and is not fully locked. Choose another accessible folder if needed. ## Frequently asked questions ### Is Max files per uploader? No. It is the request's total completed-file count across uploaders. ### Does Max file size apply to the whole batch? No. It applies to each file independently. ### Can I change the limits after sending the link? Yes, while you can still manage the request. Re-test the same public URL after saving because later uploads use the updated rules. ## Related guides - [File requests](/sharing/file-request) - [Adding a request password](/sharing/request-password) - [Inviting and tracking request uploaders](/sharing/request-recipients) - [Completing a request upload](/sharing/request-upload) - [Understanding storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Password protect a file request
summary: Add, replace or remove a file-request password and understand unlock attempts, browser grants, invited-recipient tracking and immediate shutdown.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-request-edit-dialog.tsx, src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/create.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/access.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts, apps/api/src/lib/rate-limit.ts and focused creation, permission, unlock and repository tests. Confirmed trimming and eight-character minimum, distinct By-email and By-link completion results, create/edit/remove behavior, upload permission requirement for access-rule changes, five attempts per token and IP in 15 minutes, 30-minute signed request grant, recipient-token independence and revoke semantics. Existing settings and unlock captures remain accurate.
body: A file-request password hides the message, acceptance rules and upload controls until the visitor unlocks that specific request. It is shared knowledge, separate from every Dosya account password, and it does not identify the person who entered it. Use an emailed recipient invitation when you need delivery and submission attribution. Use a password when possession of the request URL alone should not reveal the collection instructions or allow an upload. ## Steps: protect a new request 1. Open **File requests** and choose **New request**. 2. Select **By email** for tracked invitations or **By link** for a URL you will deliver yourself. 3. Complete the title, message, expiry and **Upload destination**. 4. Enter the secret under **Password (opt)**. The web app trims leading and trailing spaces; the remaining value must contain at least eight characters. 5. Set any **Advanced options**. 6. **Finish the selected delivery mode.** For **By email**, select **Send request**; the dialog closes and displays **Request sent**. Find the created row in **File requests** and select **Copy link** when you need the URL for testing. For **By link**, select **Generate link**, copy the inline **Request link**, then select **Done**. 7. **Open a private test.** Paste the copied request URL into a fresh private browser window. 8. **Inspect the locked request.** Confirm it names the requester when available, says where files will go and withholds the message and rules. 9. Enter the request password in **Password**, complete human verification when shown and select **Unlock**. The creator must be a workspace member whose role includes upload permission because a file request delegates that upload capability to visitors. A member confined to a folder subtree can target only that scope. A full-locked destination or ancestor cannot receive a public request, even when the creator personally unlocked it. ## Change the password on an active request 1. Return to **File requests** and choose **Edit** for the correct row. 2. Leave **Remove password** clear. 3. **Set the replacement.** Enter at least eight characters after surrounding spaces are removed. 4. Select **Save changes** and wait for **Request updated — Your changes have been saved.** 5. **Test the request URL.** In a new private window, try the old value and then the replacement. 6. **Deliver the new request password.** Use a trusted channel and avoid placing it in the same public message as the URL. Changing access rules requires upload permission in addition to authority to manage the request. A role with **view_all_shares** can manage another creator's request; **view_own_shares** applies to the member's own request. A creator who later loses upload permission can still change wording or revoke when their role allows managing the request, but cannot change its password, expiry, destination or upload limits. The stored password is hashed and the interface does not reveal it. If the original is lost, set a replacement. ## Remove password protection Open **Edit**, select **Remove password**, then save. Leaving the password input blank without selecting that checkbox keeps the current password. Removing protection makes the still-active URL usable by anyone who holds it, subject to expiry, file limits, destination state and workspace storage. Test the effect in a private window before distributing the link again. ## Unlock limits and browser timing The public unlock endpoint accepts five attempts per combination of request token and client IP during a 15-minute window. When the limit is reached, the page displays **Too many attempts. Unlocking is paused for 15 minutes - ask the sender for the password rather than guessing.** A correct password creates a signed browser grant for 30 minutes. The grant belongs to that request token and cannot be reused on a different request or sharing link. If the grant expires while files remain, the page shows **Your access timed out**. Enter the current password and choose **Unlock and continue**. Files already recorded remain in the receipt, and the remaining in-memory queue carries on. Changing or removing the password does not invalidate an already issued grant. A browser that unlocked before the edit can continue until its 30-minute grant ends. Revoke the request when access must stop immediately. ## Passwords and named invitations are separate **By email** invitations contain a recipient-specific URL parameter. Opening it associates the invited address with completed submissions; the request flow does not send a one-time inbox code or prove control of that email account. The password gate still applies when the request has one. Anyone who receives both a recipient URL and the password can upload under that invited address. Anyone with the base URL and password can upload without recipient attribution. For this reason: - send each recipient their own generated invitation; - treat **Uploaded** as token attribution, not verified identity; - avoid forwarding recipient-specific URLs; - use the request's receipt table to confirm actual filenames and counts. This differs from a restricted file-sharing link, whose recipients verify an emailed six-digit code. File-request invitations deliberately do not use that code ceremony. ## Immediate shutdown and irreversible effects Choose **Revoke** when the URL or password was exposed and waiting for a browser grant to expire is unacceptable. Revocation is permanent for that request token: the public page changes to **This request was closed**, and the owner must create a new request to collect more files. Revoking does not delete completed submissions. They remain in the destination and request ledger. An owner can soft-delete a received file into **Deleted**. The original public uploader's remove control has a different result: it permanently withdraws that submission, frees its storage, returns its request slot and provides no Trash recovery. ## Troubleshooting **Password must be at least 8 characters.** Count the trimmed value. Add characters rather than relying on spaces at either end. **Incorrect password.** Confirm the current secret and exact letter case with the requester. Verify that the URL belongs to the intended request. **The password was changed but an open browser still uploads.** That browser is using an earlier 30-minute grant. Revoke the request for immediate cutoff. **The locked page shows an unexpected requester or workspace.** Stop before entering the password. Confirm the URL with the sender through a known channel. **The request unlocks but rejects the file.** Password access does not bypass extension, size, count, destination or storage rules. Follow the message under the filename. ## Expected result A visitor without a current grant sees the locked page. Correct entry reveals the message, upload terms and picker for up to 30 minutes in that browser. Incorrect entry reveals none of those request details. ## Related guides - [Create a client file upload request](/sharing/file-request) - [Edit or close a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request) - [Invite and track file-request uploaders](/sharing/request-recipients) - [Complete a file-request upload](/sharing/request-upload) - [Recover a rejected or incomplete request upload](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request)

title: Invite file-request uploaders and track submissions
summary: Send recipient-specific upload invitations, interpret Pending and Uploaded, resend safely, and understand forwarding, removal and delivery limits.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/file-request-detail.tsx, src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/create.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/recipients.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/resend.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/uploads.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/requests.ts and focused repository/door tests. Confirmed the initial 100-address slice, one-at-a-time later additions with no separate total cap, lower-case duplicate handling, delivery timestamp limitations, recipient-token attribution without inbox verification, first-completion status, forwarding and removal effects. Existing recipient captures remain accurate.
body: Choose **By email** when Dosya should send each uploader a recipient-specific URL and track the first completed submission against that address. These invitations provide delivery and attribution signals. They do not make the file request invitation-only and they do not verify control of the recipient's inbox. Add a request password when the URL itself should not be sufficient to open the upload controls. ## Steps: send the initial recipient list 1. Open **File requests** and select **New request**. 2. Keep **By email** selected. 3. **Add each recipient.** Enter an address, then press Enter, comma or Space. The dialog trims and lowercases it and ignores a duplicate already entered. 4. Add the title and message recipients will recognize. 5. Choose the expiry, **Upload destination** and whether to **Put each uploader in their own folder**. 6. Add a password or **Advanced options** when required. 7. Select **Send request**. 8. Open **Recipients** for the new row and review the recorded addresses. Creation considers valid addresses in order and accepts at most the first 100. The API writes recipient records only when the mail transport is configured. Production delivery is asynchronous from the user's inbox, and a recorded invitation or sent time does not prove the provider placed it in the inbox. Each recipient receives the same base request token plus a unique recipient value in the URL. The email names the sender and request and can include the message and expiry. ## Add someone after creation 1. Open **Recipients** on the request row. 2. Enter one address under **Add email address...**. 3. Select **Add & send**. 4. Confirm that the address appears as **Pending**. Post-creation addition accepts one address per action. The endpoint does not apply the creation flow's 100-address slice or a separate total-recipient ceiling. Use this for genuine additions, not bulk mailing. Addresses are compared case-insensitively. An existing address returns **This email is already a recipient**; resend that row rather than changing capitalization. Invalid input shows **Enter a valid email address** in the dialog or **Valid email is required** from the API. Adding recipients requires authority to manage that request and the workspace's upload permission because the invitation delegates upload access. A role with **view_all_shares** can manage anyone's request; **view_own_shares** applies only to the creator's own request. Folder-confined members remain limited to requests whose destinations are inside their scope. ## Resend an invitation Select **Resend** beside one address, or **Resend all** to process every row that has no **Uploaded** time. The web app sends those reminders sequentially. The resend endpoint updates the recipient's sent time after its email helper resolves. That helper also resolves when an address is suppressed or when the provider or network returns a handled failure, so the timestamp does not prove provider acceptance or inbox delivery. An ordinary thrown exception returns **Failed to send email** and leaves the timestamp unchanged; a workspace-migration error is rethrown and surfaces as a retryable 503 response instead. **Resend all** reports how many pending rows it attempted, but its interface continues past individual failures; reopen the dialog and check the rows rather than treating the summary toast as delivery proof. Resending reuses the existing recipient token. It does not create a fresh request, reset the expiry, change the password or restore consumed file slots. ## Interpret Pending and Uploaded When a valid recipient URL opens, the public page displays **Sending as** with the recorded address and hides the optional email input. No six-digit code is sent or requested. The recipient token is the attribution credential. **Pending** means no completed file has marked that recipient row. It does not mean the message is unread, undelivered or ignored. **Uploaded** is stamped when the first small-file upload is recorded or a multipart upload completes through that recipient token. The timestamp remains the first completion time. Later files do not create another recipient status. Open the request detail to compare the recipient summary with the upload table. One address can submit several files, so uploaded-recipient count and received-file count answer different questions. ## Understand identity and forwarding A recipient invitation is a bearer URL, not an account login or inbox challenge. Anyone who receives a forwarded recipient URL can: - see **Sending as** with the invited address; - submit files attributed to that address; - see prior files associated with that recipient token; - withdraw those visible submissions while the request remains active. The optional **Your name** field is free text. It helps label a person or team but is not verified identity. Use a password and deliver it separately when accidental forwarding matters. The password adds a shared gate, while the recipient token preserves attribution. Neither proves which human held the device. Restricted file-sharing links use a different control: they email a six-digit code, allow five incorrect code attempts and create a 30-minute verified-recipient grant. File-request invitations do not use that workflow. ## Remove a recipient or close access Removing a row from **Recipients** deletes its tracking record. It does not: - revoke the base request token; - close the upload page; - remove files already received; - recall an email already delivered; - guarantee that a copied recipient URL cannot still open the public request. After removal, that old recipient value no longer resolves to the address. Because the base request remains public, the URL can still open as an anonymous request link and can upload without the removed attribution unless another gate blocks it. To end all future access immediately, revoke the request. Revocation is permanent and recorded recipients are notified, while completed files remain with the workspace owner. Change or add the request password when the goal is to replace the shared access secret without closing the token. ## Submission removal and retention Removing a recipient record leaves their completed files in the destination and request ledger. An owner may manage those files from **Files**; normal owner deletion is a soft delete into **Deleted** and does not decrement the request's upload count. The public uploader's own remove control is different. When the same recipient token or visitor cookie withdraws a received item from the still-active page, Dosya permanently purges that file, decrements the request count and frees storage. There is no Trash recovery for that withdrawal. ## Troubleshooting **No invitation arrived.** Confirm the address and check junk folders. If the recipient previously unsubscribed from Dosya invitations, they can open the unsubscribe page from an earlier message and select **Undo, and start receiving them again**, then you can resend. When the timestamp advances but repeated messages never arrive, stop resending and contact [Dosya support](https://dosya.dev/contact/) with the request title, recipient address, attempt time and time zone; do not include the request URL or password. Share the base link manually only when losing recipient attribution is acceptable. **The address is already a recipient.** Find the existing lower-cased row and resend it. Dosya will not add a case variant. **The row stays Pending after a claimed upload.** Confirm the uploader used that exact recipient URL and reached a received receipt. Upload through the base URL, an interrupted transfer or another recipient's URL will not stamp the expected address. **A removed recipient can still open the page.** This is expected for a bearer request. Add or change the password, or revoke the entire request for immediate closure. **The invitation shows the wrong sender or request.** Tell the uploader to stop and verify through an established channel before selecting files. ## Expected result The owner can see each recorded address, last send timestamp and first completed-upload state. The request detail lists the actual files and associated uploader labels, while the invited person can submit without creating a Dosya account. ## Related guides - [Create a client file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Protect a request with a password](/sharing/request-password) - [Verify a request invitation before upload](/sharing/request-uploader-confirm-invite) - [Upload through a file request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Edit or revoke a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Remove a recipient from a file request
summary: Remove a file-request recipient safely, understand why the public link may still work, and preserve files that the address already uploaded.
verification: Verified against apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx; apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileRequestsPage.tsx; apps/mobile/app/file-requests/[id].tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/recipients.ts; and apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/requests.ts. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: Removing an email deletes its recipient record and invalidates the personalized identity token. It does not close the file request, erase that person's completed uploads, or make the underlying public request URL private. ## Decide whether removal is enough Recipient removal is suitable when an address should disappear from invitation tracking or its personalized token should stop identifying uploads. The old invitation still contains the base public request URL and can open while the request remains active. With no recognized recipient token, the visitor may upload anonymously if they satisfy the current password and file rules. To stop every further submission, revoke the request. To keep the request available to others while adding a shared secret, set or change its password. Removing one row alone does not guarantee that the person cannot reach a public link copied elsewhere. Web, desktop, and mobile all support recipient removal. The mobile app shows **Remove recipient?** and explains that the address keeps files already uploaded. The web and desktop trash control removes the row without the same confirmation screen, so verify the exact email first. ## Steps 1. Open the relevant request, then choose **Recipients**. 2. Match the full email address and inspect whether its state is **Pending** or **Uploaded**. If it uploaded, identify the submitted files before removing the tracking row. 3. Decide whether the public request should remain active. If no one should add files, revoke it instead of relying on recipient removal. 4. On mobile, choose remove and approve **Remove recipient?**. On the web or desktop, select the trash control beside the address; the change is immediate. 5. Refresh the recipients panel and confirm that the email is absent. 6. Review **Uploads** to make sure prior files remain available. The removal endpoint does not delete them. 7. When appropriate, test the old personalized invitation in a private browser. It should no longer resolve to that recipient identity, although the active base request may still load. ## Permissions and permanent effects The actor needs **View all shares**, or **View own shares** on a request they created, and the request must be within folder scope. Owners and Admins ordinarily have all-request management, Members ordinarily have own-request management, and Viewers have neither. There is no distinct plan restriction in the recipient deletion handler. The recipient-row deletion itself cannot be undone. Adding the same address again creates a new row with a new personalized token; it does not restore the old token, sent timestamp, or uploaded state. Dosya does not notify the removed address. Files that were already accepted stay in workspace storage and retain their upload records. Deleting a recipient is therefore different from deleting or withdrawing a file. It also leaves the request's title, message, destination, expiry, password, extension rule, size maximum, and remaining slot count unchanged. ## Expected result The address vanishes from recipient tracking and its former token no longer supplies verified recipient identity. Earlier uploads remain with the workspace, and the public request continues accepting permitted submissions until it expires or is revoked. ## Troubleshooting **The removed person can still open the link.** This is expected for an active public request. Revoke the request to close it for everyone, or apply a password and share the new secret only with intended uploaders. **The row reappears or removal is unavailable.** Reload the request and confirm the active workspace. You need appropriate own-share or all-share management and access to the request's folder scope. **You removed the wrong address.** Add that email again. The replacement receives a new personalized URL and begins with a fresh recipient status; the deleted token cannot be recovered. **Files seem to be missing after removal.** Recipient deletion does not erase files. Check the request's **Uploads**, the original destination folder, hidden-item visibility, and Trash. A separately deleted file may be in Trash, while the recipient operation itself never puts files there. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Stop an uploader from using a file-request invitation
summary: Stop future invitation email, understand what recipient removal changes, and revoke the request when the existing upload URL must stop working.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/recipients.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts.
body: Removing an address from a file request stops it appearing in **Recipients**, but it does not invalidate a URL that person already has. Revoke the whole request when that bearer link must stop accepting uploads. ## Steps 1. Sign in to the web app, open **File requests**, and choose the request you need to control. You need `view_all_shares`, or `view_own_shares` and ownership of this request; folder-scoped members can manage only requests inside their allowed subtree. 2. Choose **Recipients**, find the exact email address, and note whether its row says **Pending** or **Uploaded**. Removing this row does not remove files already received. 3. Use the red trash button on that row. The recipient disappears immediately; this action has no confirmation dialog and the API returns success even if another session already removed the row. 4. Do not treat that removal as per-recipient revocation. The emailed `?r=` token no longer identifies the address, but the underlying request token is still a bearer upload URL and can accept anonymous uploads. 5. If the old invitation must stop working, return to the request row and choose **Revoke**. This closes the entire request for every recipient and future visitor; the public page then says **This request was closed**. 6. Open the old invitation in a private window. A removed recipient can still reach an active request, while a revoked request returns the closed state. Create a new request for everyone who should retain access. ## Expected result Recipient removal clears the tracked invitation only. Revoking closes the request for all uploaders, preserves files already delivered, and cannot be undone. **A recipient deletion emits `file_request_recipient_removed` only when a row existed.** **The public request explicitly says that files already sent remain with the requester after revocation.** ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Recover a file-request invitation that was not received
summary: Resend a pending file-request invitation, verify its Sent timestamp, and distinguish a delivered reminder from a mailbox or address problem.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/resend.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/recipients.ts.
body: Use **Resend** only for a recipient whose row is still **Pending**. A successful reminder keeps the same request and recipient URL; it does not create a duplicate request. ## Steps 1. Open **File requests** in the web app, identify the active request, and choose **Recipients**. The same share-management permission and folder-scope rules used for recipient removal apply. 2. Find the intended email row. **Resend** appears only while its state is **Pending**; a row marked **Uploaded** no longer offers that action. 3. Confirm the address is correct before resending. If it is wrong, remove the row and use **Add email address…** plus **Add & send**; duplicate addresses return **This email is already a recipient**. 4. Choose **Resend** for one address, or **Resend all** to attempt every pending address sequentially. The reminder carries the same recipient-specific request URL and current expiry. 5. Reopen **Recipients** and check that the row now shows **Sent** with a recent relative time. The server writes that timestamp only after the email provider accepts the reminder. 6. Ask the recipient to check spam and open the newest message. If **Resend all** reports success, still verify individual rows and inboxes: the current bulk control continues after failed sends and its toast reports the number attempted. ## Expected result The pending recipient receives another reminder for the existing request, and a successful send updates that row’s Sent time without creating another request. The API can return **Failed to send email** for a single resend. A revoked request returns **Request not found or revoked** and cannot be reminded. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Resend a file-request invitation
summary: Resend one or all pending file-request invitations, verify delivery timestamps, and understand what the reminder changes for each recipient.
verification: Verified against apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx; apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileRequestsPage.tsx; apps/mobile/app/file-requests/[id].tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/resend.ts; and apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/recipients.ts. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: A reminder is useful when a listed recipient has not uploaded, lost the first message, or needs the invitation again. Resending reuses that recipient's existing personalized request URL. It does not create another recipient, reset access, extend the deadline, or change any upload rule. ## Access and client support Web, desktop, and mobile expose recipient management. On the web, choose **Recipients** on the request row. Native clients show the same recipient list inside request details. A row is **Pending** until the first upload verified through that personalized recipient token; it becomes **Uploaded** after that first accepted file. A manager needs **View all shares**, or **View own shares** for a request they created. The request must also fall inside the manager's folder scope. Owner and Admin roles normally manage all requests, Member normally manages their own, and Viewer normally cannot. Resending has no separate paid-plan gate in the API. ## Steps 1. Open **File requests**, select the request, and enter **Recipients**. 2. Confirm that the request is active. Do not resend from an expired or revoked request. 3. Check the complete email address in the intended row. On the web, the row also shows **Sent ...** or **Not sent** and either **Pending** or **Uploaded**. 4. For one address that has not uploaded, choose **Resend**. To remind every pending address, choose **Resend all** or **Resend all (n)** in a native client. 5. Wait for the action to finish, then refresh the recipient list. Mobile reports **Resent to X of Y**, which exposes partial success. The web can show the broader **Invites resent** message, so inspect individual sent times if some deliveries matter. 6. Ask the recipient to search for the reminder and open its personalized link. Mail-provider acceptance and a recorded sent time do not guarantee that the message escaped spam or filtering. ## What the recipient receives The reminder contains the request title, requester identity, expiry information, workspace branding, and that recipient's existing personalized upload URL. It omits the optional request message, although the public upload page shows the current message when the recipient opens the link. Resending does not make a fresh token. A successful send updates **sent_at** only after the mail service accepts the message. The current password, destination, allowed extensions, per-file size limit, available file slots, and expiry still govern the link. If those settings were changed after the original invitation, the public page enforces their present values. A reminder cannot reopen an expired or revoked request. Resending never deletes uploaded files or clears the recipient's first-upload status. The one-recipient action is unavailable after the row has reached **Uploaded**; bulk resend targets rows whose **uploaded_at** remains empty. ## Expected result Each successful reminder uses the original recipient-specific address, records a newer sent time, and leaves request policy and stored files intact. The recipient remains **Pending** until Dosya accepts their first verified upload. ## Troubleshooting **You see “Request not found or revoked.”** Check that the selected request still exists and is not closed. Create a new request when access was deliberately revoked. **The API reports “Recipient not found.”** Refresh the list. Another manager may have removed the row; adding the email again creates a new recipient and a new personalized token. **Resend returns “Failed to send email.”** The mail provider did not accept that attempt. Verify the address, try later, or give the recipient the request link through an approved channel. Do not interpret an unchanged sent time as delivery. **The recipient never sees the message.** Have them inspect junk, quarantine, and organization filters. You can copy the request link, but remember that the base public URL can permit anonymous submission when the active request policy allows it. **The control is missing.** An uploaded recipient cannot be reminded from the per-row button. For a pending row, verify your all-share or own-share permission and the request's folder scope. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Review files submitted to a request
summary: Review file-request uploads by name, size, uploader, and time across web and native clients, then handle unexpected files without losing evidence.
verification: Verified against apps/web/src/pages/file-request-detail.tsx; apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileRequestsPage.tsx; apps/mobile/app/file-requests/[id].tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/[id]/uploads.ts; and apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/requests.ts. Production behavior was not exercised.
body: The request detail view reconciles what Dosya accepted with what you expected to receive. Review file name and size first, then use uploader identity and timestamp as context rather than proof that the file contents are safe. ## Choose the right client The web detail screen provides the fullest review. Its upload table has **Name**, **Size**, **Uploader**, and **Uploaded** columns, plus search and sorting by **Newest**, **Oldest**, **Name A–Z**, **Name Z–A**, **Largest**, or **Smallest**. It can preview, download, rename, delete, select multiple files, and build a ZIP download. Desktop request details show upload name and size. Mobile adds uploader identity but remains a read-only review surface. Use the web app when you must inspect timestamps or act on a file. A viewer needs **View all shares**, or **View own shares** when they created the request. Built-in Owners and Admins normally see every request, Members see their own, and Viewers see none. Folder confinement and hidden-file rules still apply. Read-only API keys may list permitted records but do not receive the public request token. ## Steps 1. Open **File requests** and select the request whose title, status, and creation time match the collection you expect. 2. Choose **Uploads (n)** on the web, or open **Uploads (n)** in desktop or mobile request details. 3. Compare the displayed count with the expected delivery. The owner endpoint lists only live file rows visible to your current scope, so trashed or hidden items can explain a difference. 4. On the web, search by file name and choose the sort order that exposes duplicates, unusually large files, or unexpected timing. 5. Read **Uploader** carefully. Dosya prefers an entered uploader name, then a verified recipient email, then **Anonymous**. An email is associated with the upload record only when the personalized recipient token resolved successfully. 6. Compare **Uploaded** with the sender's claimed time, allowing for their upload duration. Recipient status records the first verified upload time; it is not updated for every later file. 7. Preview a supported harmless file or download it according to your organization's scanning process. A familiar name or recipient label does not validate the content. 8. Rename or organize a confirmed file if necessary. For an unwanted item, delete it on the web after recording the details your team needs. ## Identity, retention, and deletion An upload made through a valid personalized link can carry the recipient's verified email. An anonymous visitor can enter a name or email for folder organization, but the owner record does not treat a typed email as verified recipient identity. Network address hashes are not shown as human identity. Deleting an upload from the owner web view uses the normal workspace deletion flow and moves the file to Trash. It can be restored until Trash is emptied; permanent removal occurs when Trash is purged. A recipient removing one of their own previous uploads from the public page uses a separate withdrawal flow that permanently purges the file and related versions, share links, and chunks. The request upload list joins live workspace files, so a trashed file disappears from that list. Renaming changes the workspace file itself. Bulk ZIP download reads the currently selected files and does not remove their originals. ## Expected result Every visible upload is matched to an expected file or isolated for follow-up, with its actual byte size, available uploader identity, and accepted time recorded. Any owner-side deletion is recoverable from Trash until permanent cleanup. ## Troubleshooting **The page says “No files uploaded yet.”** Check the request title and workspace, then confirm that the sender reached a completed receipt. A staged, rejected, cancelled, or interrupted item is not an upload. **Search reports “No uploads match your search.”** Clear the search term and reset sorting. This message means the current filter found nothing, rather than proving the request has no files. **The whole request is unavailable.** The web screen says **This file request does not exist or you do not have access to it.** Verify own-share or all-share access, folder scope, and the account currently selected. **The recipient is Uploaded but you see fewer files than expected.** **Uploaded** marks the first verified success, not a promised file count.
