Inspect Trash and hidden visibility, then ask the recipient for the success receipt or reference. **A sender appears as Anonymous.** The submission did not resolve to a retained verified recipient identity. Ask for the completion reference and compare the exact filename, size, and timestamp rather than assigning the file by guesswork. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Manage a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request)

title: Upload files through a file request
summary: Send files without a Dosya account, satisfy the request's extension, size and slot rules, recover interrupted transfers, and keep the delivery receipt.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/files.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/part/[partNumber].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/abort.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/guard.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/visitor.ts and focused upload-request unit tests. Verified source choices, exact closed and error states, three-file and three-part concurrency, 50 MiB multipart threshold, 10 MiB parts, same-page-only session reuse with every part request restarted at one, server acknowledgement of recorded part numbers without another object-store upload, ambiguous response-loss recovery through returning submissions and the receipt, best-effort multipart abort and slot release, completed-session and expired-grant cancellation outcomes, 30-minute password grants, 30-day visitor identity, server-side slot, extension, size, quota and folder-lock checks, receipt contents and withdrawal deletion. Existing staging and receipt captures were inspected and remain accurate.
body: A Dosya file request lets you upload into the sender's chosen cloud folder without creating an account. Choosing files only stages them. The sender receives a file after its row completes and the page shows a stamped receipt. ## Steps ### Verify the request before sending - Confirm the sender through a trusted channel when the link was unexpected. - Read the workspace name, requester, title, message and displayed terms. - Check the accepted extensions, maximum size for each file and remaining file slots. - Keep the page open until every intended row is received or has a clear failure. - Use the real source file. Renaming an extension does not convert its contents. An expired page says **This request has expired**. A revoked request says **This request was closed**. An unknown or broken URL says **No request at this link**. In all three cases, ask the sender for a current link instead of repeatedly submitting the old address. ### Unlock a protected request 1. Enter the request password under **Password** and choose **Unlock**. 2. If the value is wrong, the page displays the server's error without revealing the request rules. 3. **Too many attempts. Unlocking is paused for 15 minutes - ask the sender for the password rather than guessing.** Stop entering passwords until the pause ends. A successful password grant lasts 30 minutes. If it expires during a transfer, the page shows **Your access timed out** and **Unlock and continue**. Re-entering the current password continues remaining files; rows already received are not sent again. ### Stage files or a folder 1. On desktop, use **Drop files here**, **Browse files**, or **Choose a folder**. Supported touch devices offer **Photo library**, **Take a photo**, and **Browse files**. 2. Review **This transfer**. Accepted rows are numbered; rejected rows remain marked with their reason. 3. For a mistaken staged row, choose the control announced as **Remove _filename_**; an active row announces **Cancel _filename_** instead. 4. Enter **Your name (optional)**. On a public link, you may also enter **Your email (optional)**; these typed labels are not verified identity. 5. When the sender enabled uploader folders, review **Your folder** and **Your code**. Dosya uses them to keep submissions separated without revealing the workspace tree. A selected folder keeps safe relative subfolders beneath the sender's destination. A path that attempts to escape that destination is refused with **That folder path is not accepted - upload the files directly instead.** ### Upload and wait for the receipt 1. Choose **Upload 1 file**, **Upload 2 files**, or the count shown by the primary button. 2. Watch each row's transferred bytes and percentage. The page sends up to three files at a time. 3. Use a row's **Cancel** action to stop one transfer, or **Cancel all** to stop active work. A canceled file returns to a staged state and can be started again. 4. For a failed row, read its exact message and choose **Retry** only after correcting the cause. 5. Wait for the green stamp stating that the requester **has this file** or **has these _N_ files**. It includes total received size, local date and time, and a reference made from the first 12 characters of the request token. 6. Choose **Add more files** only if slots remain and another submission is intended. ## Large-file and retry behavior Files at or below 50 MiB use one request. A dropped connection can report **The connection dropped. Nothing was saved.**, but that client message does not prove the server failed before recording the file and losing its response. Check the receipt and the returning previous-submissions list, then ask the sender to verify the destination before replaying an ambiguous upload. If no received copy exists, **Retry** resends the complete file. Files larger than 50 MiB use resumable multipart upload with 10 MiB parts. The page can send three parts of one file concurrently. While the same loaded page still holds the source file and its session ID, **Retry** reuses that session but starts its part requests again at part 1. The browser reattempts every part request; for a part number already recorded, the server returns the stored result without uploading those bytes to object storage again. Completion checks the received total before registering the file. Refreshing the page loses the in-memory staged queue, source-file bytes and session retry context, so reselecting afterward starts a new upload instead of resuming that session. An error after the final completion request is ambiguous: before choosing **Retry**, open the same request in another tab to check returning previous submissions and ask the sender when no receipt confirms the outcome. Canceling or discarding a multipart row stops the browser requests and sends a best-effort server abort. An accepted abort attempts two separate writes: retiring the upload session and releasing its reserved file-request slot. Either write can remain pending, so a local cancel or successful abort response does not guarantee immediate slot recovery. An expired password grant can prevent the abort request from reaching those writes, and a session that already completed returns a conflict because its stored file legitimately keeps the counted slot. Check the request state instead of assuming a local cancel reversed server completion. ## Limits and server checks The sender chooses the extension list, per-file size ceiling and maximum file count. Dosya rechecks those rules at upload time because another visitor can take the last slot after your page loaded. Common exact responses include: - **This request has reached its file limit.** The owner can raise or clear the maximum, or create another request. If an unwanted submission should be removed, the original uploader can permanently withdraw it from the still-active public page; an owner's ordinary deletion does not return that request slot. - **File type ._ext_ is not allowed. Accepted: ...** Choose an allowed source or ask the sender to change the rule. - **File is too large. Maximum size is _N.N_ MB.** Use a smaller file or a request with a higher per-file maximum. - **This upload request can no longer accept files.** The destination was locked after the request was created. - A quota message means the receiving workspace lacks enough plan or workspace capacity. Only the owner can free or add storage. The server measures the received bytes rather than trusting a browser-supplied size. A request can therefore reject a file after an early browser check if the final transfer violates a live rule. ## Returning to your submissions For an ordinary public link, Dosya stores a high-entropy visitor secret in an HttpOnly browser cookie for 30 days and stores only its hash with the upload. Reopening the same request in that browser can list and withdraw only that visitor's previous submissions. An invited URL uses its recipient token for the same separation. Clearing cookies, changing browsers or losing the recipient-specific URL can remove that returning view without deleting files already delivered. The public page never lists another uploader's files or the rest of the destination workspace. Withdrawing a previous upload deletes that received file from the workspace. This is irreversible from the public page. Use it only when the sender agrees that the delivered copy should be removed. ## Expected result Every intended row reaches the received state, the stamp records the delivery, and the sender sees the files in the file-request detail and chosen Files destination. No account was required, and the public page exposed no unrelated workspace content. ## Troubleshooting **A row is red before upload.** Correct the displayed extension, empty-file, size or slot problem. Re-selecting the same invalid source will not change the rule. **Some files succeeded and others failed.** Preserve the receipt for completed rows. Retry only failed rows after fixing their specific messages. **Access timed out mid-batch.** Choose **Unlock and continue**. The remaining files carry on after a valid password; received rows stay received. **The receipt exists but the sender cannot find the file.** Send the private reference, filename, size and receipt time. The owner should inspect the request detail, active workspace and configured destination. ## Related guides - [Create a file request](/sharing/file-request) - [Set file-request limits](/sharing/request-limits) - [Protect a request with a password](/sharing/request-password) - [Invite and track uploaders](/sharing/request-recipients) - [Troubleshoot a rejected request upload](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request) - [Save a submission receipt](/sharing/request-uploader-save-receipt)

title: Check file-request limits before uploading
summary: Check accepted extensions, per-file size, and remaining slots before transfer, then recognize quota or concurrent-uploader refusals correctly.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/guard.ts.
body: The request page lists only the limits configured by its owner. Check **Accepts**, **Per file**, and **Slots** before choosing files; workspace storage can still refuse a compliant selection. ## Steps 1. Open the complete request URL. If the page says **This request has expired**, **This request was closed**, or **No request at this link**, ask the sender for a current link before selecting anything. 2. Read the terms block. **Accepts** lists allowed filename extensions, **Per file** is the maximum for each individual file, and **Slots** shows remaining count against the request maximum. 3. Compare extensions case-insensitively, including the leading dot. A file without an extension is rejected when type restrictions exist, and a zero-byte file is always rejected. 4. Compare each file’s actual size with **Per file**; do not total several smaller files against that value. Files over 50 MiB use resumable multipart transfer with 10 MiB parts, but still obey the same per-file ceiling. 5. Keep the selection within the displayed remaining slots. Staging counts accepted items immediately; a concurrent uploader can still take the final slot before your transfer reserves it. 6. Stage the files and read each ledger line. Rejected rows say why they cannot be sent; server-side storage quota, a newly locked destination, or **This request has reached its file limit.** can still stop an otherwise valid file. ## Expected result Only files matching the displayed extension, size, and slot rules enter the upload queue; later server refusals remain visible on their own failed rows. **The page cannot expose the owner’s remaining workspace storage, so there is no uploader-side quota number to precheck.** **A request can close between staging and upload; the server rechecks every gate.** ## Related guides - [Upload to a request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Troubleshoot a request](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request)

title: Verify a file-request invitation before uploading
summary: Confirm the sender, workspace, recipient address, request rules and final receipt before releasing files through a client upload invitation.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/lib/email/file-request-templates.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/files.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/visitor.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/uploader-folder.ts and focused public-request tests. Confirmed what locked and open pages disclose, recipient-token attribution without inbox verification, visible rules and reference, stage-versus-receipt behavior, prior-upload recognition and permanent original-uploader withdrawal. Existing staged-transfer capture remains accurate.
body: A file-request invitation lets you send files into another person's Dosya workspace without joining it. Confirm the sender and request context before choosing files. The recipient-specific URL is a bearer credential: it can label submissions with the invited address, but it does not prove who opened the email. ## Steps: check the invitation message Use an earlier conversation or another established channel to confirm that the person or organization expected these files. In the invitation, compare: - the sender name; - the request title and message; - the stated expiry, when present; - the destination domain in the upload link. The upload page should be on dosya.dev. A copied page, shortened URL or lookalike domain does not gain trust because it uses Dosya branding. Do not enter a Dosya account password, API key, recovery key or payment details into a file-request page. If the request was unexpected, contact the sender using a known address or phone number rather than replying only to the new message. ## Verify the public page before selecting files 1. Open the full invitation URL in a current browser. 2. Read the workspace name at the top and **Requested by** line when a requester name is available. 3. **Match the request purpose.** Compare the visible title and message with the work you agreed to provide. 4. Check **Sending as**. When the invitation is recipient-specific, it should show your intended email address and the page hides the free-text email field. 5. Review **Accepts**, **Per file** and **Slots** when those request rules are present. 6. Note **Your folder** and **Your code** when the requester enabled separate uploader folders. 7. Keep the displayed **Reference** available if you need to describe the request to the sender. 8. **Read the storage destination.** Files go to the named workspace's Dosya storage and only its members can open them through the workspace. The recipient value in the URL resolves directly to the recorded address. This flow does not email a six-digit verification code. A forwarded invitation can therefore show someone else's address and attribute the next completed upload to it. Ask for your own invitation when **Sending as** is wrong. ## Unlock a protected request safely A password-protected request initially shows limited context: the title, requester when available and the destination workspace. It withholds the message, file rules and upload picker. Obtain the request password from the sender through the agreed channel. It is not your Dosya account password. Enter it in **Password**, finish human verification if shown and choose **Unlock**. Five attempts are allowed for the request token and client IP within 15 minutes. Successful unlock creates 30 minutes of browser access. If **Your access timed out** appears during transfer, enter the current secret and select **Unlock and continue**. After unlocking, repeat the sender, recipient and file-rule checks because those details were hidden before entry. ## Inspect the files in This transfer Select **Browse files**, **Choose a folder**, or the available photo/camera action on a touch device. Selection only stages local files in the browser. Before choosing the final upload action: 1. Read every filename under **This transfer**. 2. **Check transfer sizes.** Compare the displayed byte total and each file size with what you selected. 3. **Inspect folder paths.** Expand the visual path for files selected from a folder. 4. **Remove unintended files.** Delete anything unrelated or confidential from the staged transfer. 5. **Resolve file rejections.** Read and correct every red message before upload. 6. Complete **Your name (optional)** only when the label will help the recipient; it is free text and is not verified. The owner has not received a staged item. Transfer begins only after you choose **Upload N files**. For an unfamiliar collection, a small non-confidential sample can confirm that the request accepts the expected format. Do not use identity documents, passwords or production secrets as a test. ## Confirm what Dosya received During transfer, each line shows bytes and percentage. Completion moves the file into the dated ledger and produces a stamp stating that the requester has the file or files. The stamp includes total received bytes, local date and time, and the request reference. That receipt means Dosya recorded the file for the request. It does not mean the requester opened, approved or retained the contents. When you return with the same recipient URL, Dosya can show earlier files associated with that invited address on another device. An anonymous base-link visitor is instead recognized through a browser cookie; changing browser can lose that anonymous history. Do not resend a file merely because an email acknowledgement did not arrive. Check the page receipt first or ask the owner to inspect the request detail. ## Withdraw a mistaken submission While the request remains active, the remove control beside a prior **Received** item lets the original uploader withdraw it. Dosya authorizes this through the recipient token and/or the browser visitor cookie that made the upload. This removal is permanent. It purges the file, versions and associated share links, frees measured workspace storage and returns the request slot. It does not move the item to **Deleted**, so the workspace owner cannot restore it from Trash. The control cannot withdraw another uploader's file. It also stops working once the request expires or is revoked. Contact the owner immediately when a closed request contains a mistaken submission. An owner's later deletion from **Files** behaves differently: it is a recoverable soft delete while retained, keeps using workspace storage and does not return a file-request slot. ## Stop and verify independently when - The request arrived without prior context. - The workspace, requester, title or purpose differs from the conversation. - **Sending as** names another address. - The URL is incomplete, shortened or outside the expected Dosya domain. - The visible rules require a broader file type or more data than agreed. - The page asks for account credentials rather than a request-only password. - The request displays **No request at this link**, **This request has expired** or **This request was closed**. For an expired request, the owner may set a future deadline. A revoked request cannot be reactivated; the owner must issue another token. ## Troubleshooting **The invitation URL opens but my address is absent.** You may have the base link or an invalid recipient value. Ask the owner to resend your recipient-specific invitation when attribution matters. **The page displays another person's email.** Close it without uploading. A forwarded recipient link would record your files under that address. **A selected file is rejected.** Follow its exact extension, size, empty-file or slot message. Do not disguise the content by renaming its suffix. **The connection stopped after progress began.** Keep the page open. Large-file **Retry** can reuse the same session on that page; a refresh loses the selected browser File objects. Check the dated receipt before starting over. **You cannot confirm the sender.** Leave the page and contact the organization through an official channel you already trust. ## Expected result The request context matches your agreement, **Sending as** shows your intended address when personalized, every selected item satisfies the visible terms, and the final dated ledger names exactly what Dosya received. ## Related guides - [Upload files through a file request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Unlock a password-protected request](/sharing/request-password) - [Fix a rejected or incomplete request upload](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request) - [Invite and track uploaders](/sharing/request-recipients) - [Verify a named file-sharing invitation](/sharing/named-recipients)

title: Replace a rejected file-request item
summary: Remove a preflight-rejected request item, stage a compliant replacement, and retry transfer failures without resending files already received.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/part/[partNumber].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/abort.ts.
body: A rejected row was never uploaded. Read its exact reason, remove it, and add a corrected file; use **Retry** only for a file that passed preflight but failed during transfer. ## Steps 1. Read the red text beneath the item. Preflight messages include **This file is empty**, **There is no slot left on this request**, missing or disallowed extension text, and the exact per-file size comparison. 2. If the row is rejected before upload, use its remove icon. Rejected items consume no request slot and send no bytes, so removing one does not delete anything from Dosya. 3. Prepare a replacement that fixes the named cause: add an accepted extension, export nonempty content, reduce the individual size, or ask the sender to raise a full request’s limit. 4. Add the replacement with the file picker, folder picker, drag and drop, paste, or the mobile photo/camera controls. Confirm its row no longer shows **cannot be sent**. 5. Choose **Upload 1 file** or the current queue count. Previously completed files live above the dated divider and are not put back into the active queue. 6. For a row marked failed after transfer began, choose **Retry** instead. Large-file retries reuse the resumable session and safely resend its 10 MiB parts; the server treats repeated part numbers idempotently. Discard aborts the session and releases its reserved slot. ## Expected result The invalid local item never leaves the browser, the corrected replacement uploads once, and earlier successful files remain in the received ledger. A 403 pauses remaining rows and opens **Your access timed out**; re-enter the request password to continue. A connection failure can show **The connection dropped. Nothing was saved.** on a small-file request. ## Related guides - [Upload to a request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Troubleshoot a request](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request)

title: Save a file-request submission receipt
summary: Save the on-page received stamp with file names, total bytes, local time, and request reference before changing browsers or losing visitor history.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/files.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/visitor.ts.
body: Dosya shows an on-page receipt after at least one file succeeds; it does not download a receipt file. Save that visible record before leaving if you need independent proof. ## Steps 1. Keep the request tab open until no row says **Uploading**. Leaving during a transfer can lose anything that has not landed, and the browser may warn before unloading. 2. Confirm every intended file appears under **Earlier today** or another dated divider with **Received**. Failed, paused, or rejected rows are not proof of delivery. 3. Read the receipt stamp beneath the ledger. It names who has the files, totals the successful count and bytes, shows the local received date and time, and includes the first 12 characters of the request token as **reference**. 4. Compare the receipt count and bytes with the received rows. A mixed run can announce both received and failed counts; save evidence only after handling every failed line. 5. Use a screenshot or the browser’s print-to-file command to preserve the visible stamp and filename list. Do not include the request password, email code, or full private URL in a ticket. 6. If you return later, use the same browser or the emailed recipient URL. Recipient identity works across devices; anonymous history depends on a per-request visitor cookie that lasts up to 30 days. ## Expected result The saved evidence contains the accepted filenames, aggregate bytes, receipt time, and short request reference, without claiming rejected or failed items arrived. **The receipt is page state plus the server’s prior-upload ledger, not an emailed or downloadable certificate.** **Removing a prior upload permanently deletes that file and gives one request slot back.** ## Related guides - [Upload to a request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Troubleshoot a request](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request)

title: Stage several files for a request
summary: Stage files from picker, folder, drop, paste, photo library, or camera; inspect paths and rejections before starting the three-file upload queue.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/relative-path.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/uploader-folder.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts.
body: Staging is reversible and sends no bytes. Add files through the controls available on your device, inspect every ledger row, and remove unintended items before choosing **Upload**. ## Steps 1. Open the active request and read its destination, sender, message, and terms. Enter **Your name (optional)** and **Your email (optional)** only if you want them used for the uploader folder label. 2. On desktop, click the drop area, choose **Files** or **Folder**, drag a tree onto the page, or paste copied files. Touch devices show **Photo library**, **Take a photo**, and **Browse files** instead of drag and drop. 3. Inspect the ledger after each addition. Folder picks and drops retain relative directories; byte-identical selections are skipped only when name, size, modified time, and path all match. 4. Remove any unintended waiting row with its × control. This changes only the local queue; nothing reaches Dosya until you press the upload button. 5. Correct all rows marked **cannot be sent**. Accepted staged rows consume provisional slots, while rejected and failed rows do not reduce the local remaining-slot calculation. 6. Choose **Upload N files**. Dosya runs at most three files concurrently; files over 50 MiB split into 10 MiB parts with up to three parts in flight for that file. ## Expected result Only reviewed, accepted rows enter the transfer queue; folder structure is retained, and rejected or removed items send no content. **Cancel all** aborts current requests and returns canceled rows to the staged state. **When uploader folders are enabled, Dosya chooses the folder from name, invited recipient email resolved from the bearer `?r=` token, typed email, dropped root folder, then guest code.** ## Related guides - [Upload to a request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Troubleshoot a request](/sharing/troubleshoot-file-request)

title: Cloud storage REST API quickstart
summary: Create a read-only REST key, list workspaces and files with curl, and diagnose authentication, access and retry responses without changing stored data.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Evidence: src/pages/developer/api.astro; apps/api/src/middleware.ts; apps/api/src/lib/api-key-auth.ts; apps/api/src/lib/api-key-auth.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/index.ts; apps/api/src/lib/auth-guards.ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/conditions.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts; apps/api/src/lib/paging.ts; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download-url.ts; apps/api/src/lib/listing/folder-listing-core.ts; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/index.refusal.unit.test.ts. Repository contracts and tests verified locally; no production requests or credentials used.
body: Use the cloud storage REST API at `https://api.dosya.dev/api` to list your workspaces, select a destination and read its files. This quickstart makes authenticated read requests without changing stored files. The API uses `/api`; do not add `/v1` or `/v2`. ## Create the test credential 1. Sign in at [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api) and select **New API key**. 2. Enter a recognizable label in **What is it for?** and choose **Read only** under **What can it do?** 3. Expand **Restrictions and expiry**. Under **Protocols**, choose **Only the ones I pick** and check **REST API**. Select the intended **Workspace** if this integration should reach only one workspace. Leave **Folder** unset: ordinary folder-anchored keys are refused over REST. 4. Choose **Expires in 30 days**, check the summary, then select **Generate key**. Copy the full `dos_` token from the **is ready** dialog before selecting **Done**; the key list cannot reveal it afterward. A free account can hold three API keys; the account-wide ceiling is 20 on other plans. Existing expired keys count toward those totals. Key permissions narrow your account's access; they do not grant workspace membership or a role permission you lack. ## Steps: send the first request You need a shell, curl and Python 3 for the examples. Set `DOSYA_API_KEY` through your secret manager or an interactive prompt; never replace the variable with a real token in a saved command. Here is an interactive option for Bash: ```bash read -r -s -p 'API key: ' DOSYA_API_KEY printf '\n' export DOSYA_API_KEY curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/workspaces' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ -o workspaces.json python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open("workspaces.json")); print([(w["id"],w["name"]) for w in d["workspaces"]])' ``` A successful request returns HTTP **200** with `ok: true` and a `workspaces` array. Use a returned workspace ID, not its display name. A workspace-pinned key sees only its pinned workspace. An empty array is not evidence that the whole account has no workspaces: check the key's reach and your current membership. Read files from one workspace's root folder: ```bash DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID='REPLACE_WITH_RETURNED_WORKSPACE_ID' curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --get \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/files' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ --data-urlencode "workspace_id=$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID" \ --data-urlencode 'page=1' --data-urlencode 'per_page=100' \ -o files.json python3 -m json.tool files.json ``` The file listing defaults to 100 items per page and accepts `per_page` from 10 to 500. Supply `folder_id` to list a known subfolder. File IDs returned here are the values used by metadata and download routes. Your workspace role must allow the files page; hidden content and folder confinement can narrow the listing. ## Check failures before adding writes | Response | What to change | | --- | --- | | **401**, `Invalid or expired API key` | Use the complete token, check expiry and revocation, and keep the exact `Authorization: Bearer …` header. | | **403**, `This API key is not permitted to use the api surface` | Include REST API in the credential's protocol selection. | | **403**, `This API key is anchored at a folder and can only be used over WebDAV or the S3 gateway` | Generate a workspace-pinned REST key without a folder anchor. | | **403**, `This API key is restricted to specific source addresses` | Send from an allowed address; do not spoof forwarding headers. | | **403**, `This API key is being used outside its allowed hours` | Check the selected timezone, weekdays and weekly window. | | **429** with `Retry-After` | Wait the indicated number of seconds; slow concurrent requests rather than continuously retrying. | | **503**, `Service temporarily unavailable` | Keep the credential and retry after the response's five-second delay. This authentication lookup failure is not a reason to replace a key. | Authentication is followed by protocol, address/time, folder-anchor, scope and workspace-pin checks before the key's request counter is charged. A **Read only** key can list and download, but an attempted write is refused with a message naming its scope, method and path. Do not test this boundary against valuable data using a full-access key. HTTP status and the JSON `error` identify a failure. Many JSON responses include `ok`, but the download-URL endpoint returns `url`, `size`, `name` and `region` without an `ok` field; validate the endpoint's actual response instead of assuming one universal shape. Retain status, error and any request identifier provided, with the authorization header redacted. ## Expected result and safe test cleanup Compare returned workspace IDs and filenames with the signed-in app. Listing does not upload, delete or create a share link, and no recipient receives a file from these requests. Save only metadata you are allowed to retain. Return to **Profile → API keys**, expand the test key, choose **Revoke** and confirm **Revoke** again when the test is finished. Revocation cannot be undone; integrations using that credential stop authenticating. Key creation, listing and deletion by ID require a signed-in session, so a bearer key cannot mint or administer sibling keys. For production, use separate credentials for read, upload and administrative work and recover uncertain write outcomes before replaying a request. ## Related guides - [Create and manage API keys](/developers/api-key) - [Upload file bytes and resume multipart transfers](/developers/api-upload-file) - [Download through a temporary signed URL](/developers/api-download-file) - [Register and verify a webhook receiver](/developers/webhook-create)

title: Restoring deleted files and folders
summary: Find an item in Deleted, restore it to your workspace, and understand folder recovery and retention limits.
verification: File recovery verified in the real web app against an isolated local API on 2026-10-10. Screenshots show the Deleted menu and the restored file. Folder recovery and retention details checked against current product behavior; production workflow not tested.
body: Open **Files**, select **Deleted** in the file sidebar, then open the deleted item's three-dot menu and choose **Restore**. Restore a deleted folder first when the file you need was inside it. ## Before you start - Sign in to [the Dosya app](https://app.dosya.dev) and select the workspace where the item was deleted. - Your role must allow restoring the item. Dosya uses the permission to delete your own files or other people's files for this action too. **Deleted** may be absent if your role has neither permission. - The item must still be in Deleted. Files already permanently removed are unavailable through this workflow. - Restore promptly. Trash retention follows the workspace owner's plan: 7 days on Free and 30 days on paid plans. ## Steps: restore one file 1. Open **Files** from the app navigation. 2. Choose **Deleted** in the file sidebar. If that sidebar is collapsed, use **Expand** to reveal its labels. The Deleted view is also available at [Files → Deleted](https://app.dosya.dev/files?filter=deleted). 3. Find the file by its name. If it was deleted with a folder, find that folder first. You can open a deleted folder to see its remaining deleted items. 4. Open the file's three-dot menu and select **Restore**. You can also right-click the file and choose **Restore** on devices that support a context menu. Clicking a deleted file alone selects it; it does not restore it. 5. Wait for the **Restored** message. The file disappears from Deleted when the list refreshes. 6. Return to **All**, open the file's original folder, and check that the file is available. Open or download it to confirm it is the item you intended to recover. ## Restore a folder or several items To recover a folder, find the folder that was deleted as a whole, open its three-dot menu, and choose **Restore**. The action brings back the folder and the remaining files and subfolders swept into Deleted with it. A nested folder deleted as part of that parent does not have its own **Restore** action; restore the parent instead. If the folder's original parent is unavailable, the folder returns to the workspace's top level. The **Restored** message tells you when this happens. If a live folder already uses the original name at the destination, Dosya chooses an available name, such as a name with a numbered suffix. Check the message for the restored name. To restore several items, select their checkboxes in Deleted, check the selection count, and use **Restore** in the selection toolbar. Read the result message: a bulk operation can restore some items while reporting failures for others. Restore a parent folder before retrying a file whose parent is still deleted. ## Expected result A restored file becomes available again in its original folder under its existing name. A restored folder returns with the remaining items associated with that folder's deletion, using the destination and name described above. Files you had deleted separately before deleting the folder remain in Deleted until you restore them separately. ## Limitations - **Delete permanently** is irreversible. Permanently removed files cannot be recovered through Deleted. - Deleted files still count toward storage until permanently removed. Restoring them does not add a second copy to the storage total. - A deleted folder can remain visible after some of its files have passed retention. Restoring it does not recover files already permanently removed. ## Troubleshooting **The app says to restore the folder first.** The file's containing folder is still in Deleted. Find and restore the parent folder, then check whether the file returned with it. If the file had been deleted separately, restore that file afterward. **Restore is missing from a nested folder's menu.** Return to the folder that was originally deleted as a whole. A folder deleted with its parent must be restored through that parent. If Restore is also missing there, ask the workspace owner to check your permissions. **The file is missing from Deleted.** Check the selected workspace, clear any search, and look inside its deleted parent folder. Retention or permanent deletion may have already removed it. Do not use **Delete permanently** while trying to recover an item. For a persistent **Restore failed** message, contact [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) with the workspace name, approximate deletion time and exact error. Keep private files and account details out of public questions. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I restore a file after its trash retention window? Restore is available only while the deleted file remains available. Automatic removal applies after the plan's retention window, so do not rely on recovery beyond it. See the [fair-use and retention policy](https://dosya.dev/fair-use/) for the published windows. ### Does restoring a folder restore everything it ever contained? It restores the remaining items deleted together with that folder. Previously deleted items and files already permanently removed do not return automatically. ### How do I recover an older copy of a file that is still in Files? Use [version history](/files/version-history). Deleted restores a deleted item; version history selects an earlier saved version of a live file. ## Related guides - [Using version history and restoring an earlier version](/files/version-history) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Watch the existing deleted-file tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/restore-a-deleted-file/)

title: Restore a deleted folder tree
summary: Restore a deleted folder tree to its original parent or workspace root, understand automatic conflict renaming, and verify every recovered child.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.unit.test.ts, and folder restore tests. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Restoring a folder trash root brings back the folder rows and files swept by that delete action. Dosya preserves the nested relationships, then resolves the root’s current parent and name. ## Before you start - Open **Deleted** in the workspace where the folder was removed. Trash is workspace-scoped. - Restore reuses deletion permissions: the creator needs `delete_own_files`; restoring someone else’s folder requires `delete_any_file`. - Select the trash root, not a descendant swept in with it. A descendant request returns **This folder was deleted as part of another folder - restore that one instead**. - Permanent deletion has no recovery path. If the root no longer appears in Deleted after a completed purge, this workflow cannot restore it. ## Steps 1. In **Deleted**, find the folder root and choose **Restore** from its menu or the selection bar. 2. Wait for **Restored**. Web includes the resolved folder name and warns when it was restored to the workspace root. 3. Open the original parent. If that parent is still live, locate the restored root there. 4. If the original parent is deleted or missing, return to the workspace root and find the restored folder. 5. If another live sibling already had the original name, look for `name (2)`, `name (3)`, and later available suffixes. 6. Open the restored root, traverse representative nested folders, and open sample files. Compare counts with what you expected from the deleted tree. 7. Recreate any sharing that is still needed. Links revoked at deletion remain revoked after restore. ## Expected result The folder and every row marked by that trash root return to live browsing in one restore operation. Storage usage does not increase because the trashed bytes never stopped counting. Hidden settings and nested parent relationships are retained; the root alone may receive a new parent or conflict-safe name. ## Troubleshooting - **“You don’t have permission to restore this folder.”** Use an account whose role has the applicable own-or-any delete permission. - **The restored folder is at root.** Its original parent is not live. The web toast states that it went to the workspace root; move it after restoring or recreating the parent. - **The restored name changed.** Another sibling held the original name. Dosya chooses the first available numbered suffix through `(99)`, then a timestamped suffix if necessary. - **A WordPress backup lock refuses the destination.** The original live parent is protected. Resolve that backup state before retrying the restore. - **Only some expected content returns.** Restore revives exactly the files and folders swept by this root. Items deleted earlier as separate actions have their own Deleted entries and must be restored separately. - **A second restore says the folder is not in the trash.** The first request already won and made the root live. Refresh Files rather than submitting again. ## Related guides - [Restore deleted items](/files/restore-deleted) - [Permanently delete files](/files/permanently-delete-files)

title: Review Deleted items before cleanup
summary: Inspect names, deletion times, folders, permissions, and storage impact in Deleted before choosing a reversible restore or permanent cleanup.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/file-columns.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/listing/folder-listing-core.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts and apps/web/src/lib/folder-purge.ts. Verified Deleted visibility, file-only 100-default/500-maximum paging, separately fetched trash folders, Deleted date column, trash-root browsing, context controls, restore/purge permissions and outcomes, quota notice, exact confirmations and bounded folder purge. Local source/UI review only; production trash was not altered.
body: Use **Deleted** as a decision screen before restore or permanent removal. Trashed bytes still count toward workspace storage, but the recovery choice disappears once a file or folder is purged. ## Steps 1. Select the workspace, open **Files**, then choose **Deleted** in the sidebar. The row appears only for a role with **Delete own files** or **Delete any file**, because those same permissions govern restore and purge. 2. Switch to list view when timing matters. In Deleted, the normal **Modified** column becomes the required **Deleted** column and displays `deleted_at`. Open **Columns** and enable **Exact dates** to show full local date and time instead of a relative label. 3. Use **Search files...** and the **Newest** or **Oldest** sort to narrow the current trash listing. The 100-entry default and 500-entry maximum apply only to file rows. Trashed folders are fetched separately and are not divided by that file-page limit, so inspect later pages for additional files before concluding an item is absent. 4. Open a trashed folder to inspect its descendants. Every folder row offers **Open** and **Get info**. Only a top-level trash-root folder that your role may act on also offers **Restore** and **Delete permanently**; a descendant removed with that folder must be handled through the root. 5. Right-click a trashed file and check its permission-dependent menu. A file you may restore or purge shows only **Restore** and **Delete permanently**. A file you cannot act on shows only **Get info**. Trashed file rows do not open the normal viewer or detail panel, and they never offer rename, move, share, download, lock or hide. 6. For recovery, choose **Restore**. A file whose containing folder is still in trash returns `This file's folder is in the trash - restore the folder first`. A restored folder returns to its prior live parent when available; if that parent is also gone, the web message explains that it was restored to the workspace root. 7. For cleanup, select only verified rows and choose **Delete permanently**. Read **This cannot be undone.** A selected folder includes every file and subfolder beneath it. A role with **Delete own files** may act only on files it uploaded and folders it created; **Delete any file** covers other members' items. Hidden content remains subject to hidden-item visibility. A folder-confined member cannot open Deleted at all and receives `Trash is not available to a folder-confined member`. `You don't have permission to restore this file` or the equivalent folder message identifies a role or ownership mismatch. Permanent file deletion removes stored objects and metadata and frees the charged bytes. A large folder is emptied through bounded repeated requests; the dialog reports files removed so far, and cancellation stops launching new requests after in-flight work settles. A partially emptied folder stays in trash and may require another pass. Do not interpret one completed progress step as proof that the entire tree is gone. The banner states: **Items in the trash still count against your storage. Delete them permanently to free up space.** Restoration does not need extra quota because the bytes were charged throughout trash. Restored files retain hidden and lock state, while share links revoked by the original soft deletion are not recreated. If nothing is present, the exact empty state is **Trash is empty**. If an expected row is missing, confirm workspace, ownership permission, folder scope, hidden visibility, search text, page number and whether scheduled retention has already purged it. ## Expected result You can account for each candidate by name, deletion time, trash folder and permitted action before cleanup. Restored records return to a live location; permanently deleted records and their bytes are removed without a recovery path. ## Related guides - [Restore deleted items](/files/restore-deleted) - [Permanently delete files](/files/permanently-delete-files)

title: Reviewing exact duplicate files before removing copies
summary: Compare byte-identical file groups, keep the intended copy, move selected copies to Deleted and permanently purge them only after review.
verification: Verified the current English Duplicates page and current web/API source and focused tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use an isolated local owner workspace with controlled current-API fixtures and fictional exact-copy groups. The review confirmed SHA-256 grouping after visibility filtering, newest-first ordering, all-but-newest selection, manual checkboxes, selected-byte calculation, all-copies warning, batch move to trash, scan progress, 100-group display cap and 256 MiB background-scan cap. A production workspace scan and destructive cleanup were not performed.
body: Dosya's Duplicates page groups files whose stored bytes have the same cryptographic fingerprint. Names and folders can differ. Similar-looking photos, resized exports and separately edited documents are not treated as duplicates unless their bytes are exactly identical. Moving selected copies to trash is recoverable, but those bytes still count against storage until you permanently delete them from **Deleted**. Review the keeper in each group before taking either action. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace. Duplicate results do not combine workspaces. - Use the application header search, enter `Duplicates`, and choose **Duplicates** to open the page. - Wait for any **still being scanned** count to finish before treating the results as complete. - Check whether any copy has a more useful name, folder, share link, comments or workflow history. Identical content does not make the surrounding records interchangeable. - Make sure your role can access Files and delete the copies you select. - Use **Move to trash** first. Permanently delete only after you verify the retained copy. ## Steps: compare duplicate groups 1. Open **Duplicates** in the correct workspace. 2. Read the number of duplicate groups and the total reclaimable bytes at the top. 3. Review each card. It shows the number of identical copies, the size of each copy and the bytes represented by all copies beyond one keeper. 4. Compare each filename, containing folder and creation time. 5. Use the folder path beside a copy to open its containing folder when you need more context. 6. Identify the copy you want to retain. The first row is labelled **newest**, based on when that copy was created in Dosya. ## Steps: select copies safely 1. For a single group, choose **Select all but newest** inside that card when the newest Dosya copy is the one you want to keep. 2. To apply that rule to every visible group, choose **Select all but newest** at the top of the page. 3. Adjust individual checkboxes when another copy has the preferred name or location. Leave at least one intended keeper unselected in every group. 4. Review the selected count and the highlighted rows before continuing. 5. If every copy in a group is selected, stop and clear at least one checkbox. The confirmation warns about this condition, but it does not choose a keeper for you. ## Steps: move selected copies to Deleted 1. Choose **Move _n_ to trash**. 2. Read the confirmation count and selected-byte estimate. 3. Choose **Move to trash**. 4. Wait for the completion message, then allow the Duplicates page to refresh. 5. Open the retained copy from its folder and confirm it still works. 6. Open **Files** → **Deleted** and verify that only the intended copies moved there. 7. Restore any mistaken selection. When the review is complete, permanently delete the unwanted copies to actually free workspace storage. ## Expected result The selected copies move to **Deleted**, while the unselected keeper remains in its original folder. The Duplicates page refreshes and removes any group that no longer has at least two visible live copies. Workspace storage is reclaimed only after the unwanted copies are deleted permanently from Deleted. Until then, the trash provides a recovery window. ## Duplicate-scan limits and permission behavior - Groups are based on the stored content fingerprint, not the filename, extension, image appearance or metadata similarity. - Duplicate scanning is opt-in per workspace and runs in the background. An unfinished scan can temporarily omit groups. - The current background scanner does not fingerprint a file larger than 256 MiB. Files without a completed fingerprint do not appear in duplicate groups, so an empty page is not proof that every possible copy was compared. - The page shows up to the 100 largest groups while keeping the total group and reclaimable-byte counts across all results. After cleanup, additional groups can move into view. - Hidden-item rules and folder confinement apply before groups are formed. You see only copies your role can access. - **Newest** refers to the most recently created copy record in Dosya. Because the bytes are identical, it is a convenient default keeper, not a judgment about the best filename, folder or surrounding activity. - The selected-byte estimate counts the full size of each selected copy. Moving it to Deleted does not reduce the storage meter yet. - Batch deletion is sent in bounded chunks. A failure can leave part of a large selection moved and part still live; use the refreshed page to decide what remains. ## Troubleshooting **Duplicates shows Scanning your files.** Leave the workspace scan running and return later. The page refreshes while pending candidates remain. **No duplicates appear even though filenames match.** Matching names are not enough. The bytes may differ, scanning may be disabled or unfinished, the files may exceed the current background-scan cap, or visibility rules may exclude a copy. **Similar photos are in different groups or no group.** Resizing, recompressing, cropping, editing metadata or exporting again changes the bytes. The current duplicate finder is for exact copies, not visual similarity. **I selected every copy.** Clear at least one checkbox before confirming. If you already moved them, restore the intended keeper from Deleted before any permanent deletion. **The reclaimable number did not change the storage meter.** Moving to trash preserves the files and their storage use. Permanently delete the reviewed unwanted copies from Deleted to free the bytes. **Some selected copies remain on the page.** Read the completion message and refresh. Resolve ownership, lock or permission failures, then retry only the remaining copies. ## Frequently asked questions ### Are similar-looking photos considered duplicates? Only when their stored bytes are identical. Visually similar images with different exports, metadata or edits are not grouped as exact copies. ### Which copy remains after Select all but newest? The first, newest Dosya copy in each group remains unselected. You can change the checkboxes when another name or folder should be kept. ### Does Move to trash free the displayed bytes immediately? No. It creates a recoverable trash state. Permanently delete the unwanted copies from Deleted after checking the keeper. ## Related guides - [Permanently deleting files and freeing storage](/files/permanently-delete-files) - [Restoring a deleted file or folder](/files/restore-deleted) - [Organizing files with folders, favourites and groups](/files/organize-files) - [Understanding storage usage and failed quota checks](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Revoke and replace an API key
summary: Identify an API key by name and prefix, replace it in the safe order for the incident, then revoke it and verify that the old secret is refused.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.ts, apps/api/src/lib/api-key-auth.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-defer.ts. Production behavior for “Revoke and replace an API key” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Revoking one API key invalidates that credential without changing the account password, browser sessions, or unrelated keys. Choose the replacement order according to whether continuity or immediate containment matters more. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → API keys**, search by the client’s descriptive name or visible `dos_····` prefix, and expand the row. Compare **Permission**, **Protocols**, **Reach**, **Created**, **Expires**, and **Last used** before acting. 2. Stop the client or scheduled job that uses the key. For a non-WordPress key, select **Duplicate settings**, create a narrowly scoped replacement, copy the one-time secret, update the client, and prove both an allowed and denied operation before revoking the old key. A `wp_site` row has no **Duplicate settings** action; reconnect that site through its WordPress plugin instead. 3. For a suspected leak, skip the overlap: revoke the exposed key first and accept temporary downtime. A replacement can use **Read only**, **Upload only**, or **Full access**, selected protocol surfaces, workspace or folder reach, IP ranges, active hours, and expiry. 4. Select **Revoke** on the exact row. In **Revoke _name_?**, review `Anything still using it stops working immediately. This can't be undone.` and choose **Revoke**. The control permanently deletes the row, while cached authorization can outlive the UI receipt briefly. 5. Confirm **Key revoked** and `Anything still using them will be refused from now on.` Dosya initiates invalidation for the API-key cache and any tied S3 access-key cache. Another worker isolate or edge cache can continue using a cached authorization until its entry expires. 6. Send harmless requests with the retired secret until authentication is refused, allowing up to five minutes for the longest API-key cache. Keep the old client stopped during that window, then resume only with the tested replacement. A Free account can hold three API keys; the absolute user cap is 20. Keys cannot be edited after creation. Revoking a `wp_site` key also disconnects that WordPress site because the key is its only credential. ## Expected result The old row disappears from **API keys**, cache invalidation begins, and the retired secret is rejected within five minutes. A routine replacement retains only the copied restrictions and passes its boundary test; an emergency rotation keeps the old client stopped until rejection is verified. **Revoke failed** leaves the outcome uncertain. Reload the list: if the row remains, stop the client and retry; if it is absent, test the old secret rather than creating duplicate replacements. **The replacement cannot be created.** Remove an unused key or upgrade when Dosya reports `The free plan allows 3 API keys. Delete one or upgrade for more.` The global refusal is `Maximum of 20 API keys reached`. ## Related guides - [Create and manage an API key](/developers/api-key) - [Choose key permission](/developers/api-key-scopes) - [Respond to suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Revoking a sharing link
summary: Find a link in Shared, revoke it, and check that the old URL is no longer available to recipients.
verification: Link revocation verified in the real web app against an isolated local API on 2026-10-10: the confirmation completed and Shared displayed the link as Revoked. Screenshots show the confirmation and resulting status. Access and permission rules checked against current product behavior; production workflow not tested.
body: Open **Shared**, find the link under **By me**, and select its **Revoke share link** control. Confirm with **Revoke**. The link becomes revoked, and recipients can no longer use that URL for new access. ## Before you start - Sign in to [the Dosya app](https://app.dosya.dev) and select the workspace that owns the link. - You need permission to manage that link. A role allowed to view only its own shares can revoke links it created; a role allowed to view all shares can manage other links in the workspace, subject to its folder access. - Identify the exact link you want to stop. A file or folder can have several links, and revoking one does not revoke the others. - Revocation cannot be undone. If you intend to share the item again afterward, you will need a new link and must send the new URL to recipients. ## Steps 1. Open **Shared** in the main app navigation, or go to [Shared](https://app.dosya.dev/shared). This is the link-management page. The **Shared** filter inside Files is a different view of your files. 2. Select **By me**. **With me** lists shares received from others and does not provide the sender's Revoke action. 3. Use **Active** or **Expiring soon** to narrow the list, or use **Filter by name or person...** to find the item. Choose **All** if you are uncertain about the link's status. 4. Check the file or folder name and the link's status and expiry. When several links target the same item, check which one corresponds to the URL you sent. The **Copy share link** control on a live row lets you compare that URL before revoking it. 5. Hover over the row or move keyboard focus to its action controls. At the right edge, choose the X-shaped button with the accessible label **Revoke share link**. Clicking the item name instead opens its sharing details. 6. In the **Revoke share link** dialog, check the displayed file or folder name. Select **Revoke** to confirm, or **Cancel** to leave the link working. 7. Wait for **Link revoked**. Use the **Revoked** filter to find the row and confirm its status. 8. Open the old URL in a fresh private browser window and confirm that it is unavailable. If your aim is to stop sharing the item completely, review and revoke its other active links as well. ## Expected result The selected link is marked **Revoked** and no longer grants new access through its old URL. The original file or folder remains in your workspace. You can still create another link if your role and workspace policy allow it. Revocation affects access through that particular link. It does not remove workspace membership or recall copies a recipient already downloaded, saved or captured. ## Limitations - There is no undo or reactivate action for a revoked link. Changing settings or sending the old URL again does not restore it. - The row's Revoke control is shown for active and expiring links. Expired and revoked rows already have an unavailable status and do not show that control here. - A recipient cannot revoke someone else's link from **With me**. Contact its owner when you need that sharing access changed. - Revocation does not promise to interrupt a download already in progress or remove a page or copy already on the recipient's device. Verify the result with a fresh request. ## Troubleshooting **I cannot find the link.** Check the workspace, select **By me**, clear the search and use **All**. Your role may show only your own links. If you only received the share, contact its sender. **The Revoke button is missing.** Hover over the row or focus its controls; the actions appear at the right. Check the status too: expired and revoked links do not offer Revoke in this list. Ask the workspace owner if your permissions or folder access changed. **The app shows Revoke failed.** Refresh Shared and check the status before trying again. Another authorized person may already have revoked it, or the underlying resource may no longer be available. If the link is still active and the action keeps failing, contact [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) with the workspace name, time and error. Share confidential URLs only through private support when needed. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does revoking a link delete the original file? No. Revocation changes that link's access. The file or folder remains in the workspace. ### Can I make the same URL work again? No. Create a [new sharing link](/sharing/create-link) with the intended settings and send its new URL. ### Why can someone still access the file after I revoked a link? They may have a downloaded copy, another active sharing link or direct workspace access. Verify the exact old URL in a fresh private window, then review the other access routes relevant to that person. ## Related guides - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Sharing a folder with a link](/sharing/folder-link) - [Adding a password to a sharing link](/sharing/password-link) - [Watch the existing folder-sharing tutorial, including revocation](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/share-a-folder-with-a-link/)

title: Revoke every other signed-in session
summary: Use Revoke all other sessions to end browser and mobile access on every other device while preserving the credential on your current device.
verification: Verified by tracing apps/web/src/pages/profile/sessions.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth/credential-revocation.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/me-sessions.int.test.ts. No production account, notification channel, or external provider was contacted.
body: **Revoke all other sessions** signs out every other active browser session and mobile app token for your account. The credential making the request stays active, so complete this from a device you trust. This is an account-security action and does not depend on the active workspace or workspace role. The **Active sessions** list combines browser and mobile access. Browser rows can show a device class, browser, stored location or IP address, and sign-in time. Mobile rows show **dosya.dev app** plus their latest activity. The current row has a **Current** badge in the web app. ## Steps 1. On the trusted device you want to keep, open **Profile → Sessions**. 2. Find the row marked **Current** and compare its device, browser, location or IP, and activity text with the device in your hand. 3. Review the other rows. If more than one session exists, the web page shows **Revoke all other sessions** beneath the list. 4. Select **Revoke all other sessions**. The web action runs immediately; it does not open a confirmation dialog. 5. Wait for **Sessions revoked — You are now signed out everywhere else.** 6. Let the page reload and confirm that the current device remains. A controlled browser or app on another device should require sign-in on its next authenticated request. ## What gets revoked The operation removes other browser sessions and marks other mobile tokens revoked, then clears their authentication caches so access stops immediately rather than waiting for cache expiry. Linked Files extension credentials created by a revoked device are revoked with that device. Linked credentials belonging to the current browser or mobile session are preserved because they represent the machine you chose to keep. The action succeeds even when no other session remains. The button is hidden in the web interface when the list contains only one entry. This action does not change the password, disable API keys, revoke public share links, or remove workspace memberships. If access is suspicious, change the password after reviewing the device list; a password change also ends other account sessions. ## Troubleshooting **Revoke failed** means the server did not complete the operation. If the underlying request no longer has a usable cookie or mobile token, the API can return **No active session**. Sign in again on the trusted device and repeat the review. If the current device disappears from the list or is signed out, sign back in and check whether you performed the action from a different browser profile or app installation than expected. ## Expected result Only the requesting device and its directly linked local credential remain usable; every other listed browser or mobile device must authenticate again. ## Related guides - [Update profile settings](/account/profile-settings) - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Rotate a protocol credential safely
summary: Duplicate a protocol key’s restrictions, test the replacement secret on its intended surface, migrate every client, and revoke the old key safely.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Rotate a protocol credential safely” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx`, `apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx`, `apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya API keys cannot be edited. Rotation uses **Duplicate settings** to create a separate key, a controlled protocol test, client migration, and the irreversible **Revoke** action on the retired row. ## Before you start Inventory every client using the old key and identify whether it authenticates with the `dos_…` secret over REST, WebDAV, or SFTP, or with a separate S3 access-key pair. The new-key dialog can preserve scope, protocols, workspace or folder reach, IP ranges, and active hours; usage limits return blank and expiry returns to **Never expires**, so review those manually. Each API-key secret is shown once. S3 additionally creates a 21-character `DOSYA…` access key ID and a 40-character secret that is also shown once. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile > API keys**, expand the old row, record its visible restrictions and **Last used** value, then choose **Duplicate settings**. 2. Give the replacement a distinct name, verify **What can it do?** and every item under **Restrictions and expiry**, and select **Generate key**. 3. Copy the one-time secret into the client’s protected credential store; for S3, choose **Enable** on the new row and save both values from **S3 credentials**. 4. Test a read or write permitted by the new key against the exact workspace, folder, protocol, address, and time window it is meant to use. 5. Update every scheduled job and interactive client, then repeat the test with only the replacement credential configured. 6. Open the old row, choose **Revoke**, read **Anything still using it stops working immediately. This can’t be undone.**, and confirm only after migration evidence is complete. ## Expected result The replacement authenticates within the same intended boundaries, every client has moved, and the old API key is deleted. Dosya invalidates both its API-key cache and any linked S3 credential cache immediately; a later request with the retired credential is refused. If **Generate key** is refused, the account may have reached its cap: 20 keys generally and three under free-plan fair use. Revoke an unrelated stale key only after verifying it is unused. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Restrict protocol access](/developers/api-key-protocols)

title: Connect the AWS CLI to Dosya S3
summary: Configure an isolated AWS CLI profile for Dosya’s path-style S3 endpoint, then list, upload, download, compare and clean up one sample safely.
