body: Use a dedicated named AWS CLI profile to test Dosya S3 without changing your normal AWS credentials. This walkthrough lists one workspace, uploads a uniquely named text file, downloads it and checks the bytes. It uses direct `s3api` calls so the small-file test is easy to inspect. ## Before you start Install AWS CLI v2 using [AWS's platform installation instructions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html), then run `aws --version`. The shell examples below use macOS/Linux POSIX syntax; the `aws` commands also run in PowerShell, but replace the local `printf`, `cmp` and `$?` checks with its equivalents. In the intended Dosya workspace, open **Integrations → S3** and copy the **Bucket** ID. The endpoint is `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`, region `us-east-1`, with **path** addressing. There is no WebDAV `All/` prefix. For a folder-anchored key, keys start below the anchor: use `aws-check.txt` to write inside the anchor, not `AnchorName/aws-check.txt`. Prepare credentials through **Profile → API keys → New API key**: choose **Full access** for all three tests, the intended **Workspace**, and **S3 gateway** under **Restrictions and expiry → Protocols → Only the ones I pick**. Generate it, then expand the key row and select **S3 credentials → Enable**. Copy the **Access key ID** and **Secret access key** from that dialog. The `dos_…` token is not the AWS CLI secret. The S3 secret is shown only when generated; **Active · show** cannot retrieve it afterward. If lost, replace the key/pair, migrate clients, then revoke the old key. Your role must allow S3 plus file listing, upload and download. A new nested prefix also needs folder creation. Free-plan use is permitted within allowances; a free account can have three API keys, with a global maximum of 20. Explicit access/usage restrictions remain effective on every command. ## Steps: configure one private profile 1. **Choose a profile that does not already exist.** These instructions use `dosya-help-check`. Check `aws configure list-profiles` first. Use a different name consistently if that profile belongs to an existing connection. 2. **Enter the pair interactively.** Run: ```sh aws configure --profile dosya-help-check ``` At the prompts, enter the generated S3 access ID, its S3 secret, `us-east-1` and `json`. Do not paste credentials as command arguments or commit the resulting files. The prompt avoids embedding the secret in shell command history, but do not run it in a recorded terminal session: AWS CLI configuration is not a promise of a masked prompt. AWS CLI stores the pair in `~/.aws/credentials` and settings in `~/.aws/config` by default (under your user home on Windows too). They are local files, not an encrypted password vault. On a private Unix account, restrict those files after configuring: ```sh chmod 600 ~/.aws/credentials ~/.aws/config ``` 3. **Set S3 path addressing for this profile.** This changes only its config: ```sh aws configure set s3.addressing_style path --profile dosya-help-check aws configure get region --profile dosya-help-check aws configure get s3.addressing_style --profile dosya-help-check ``` Expect `us-east-1` and `path`. Every remote command below supplies `--endpoint-url` explicitly; omitting it can send the request to AWS instead of Dosya. Do not run an STS identity command to validate these credentials: Dosya provides an S3 gateway, not AWS STS. 4. **Check the selected sources privately.** Run `aws configure list --profile dosya-help-check`: for this explicit named-profile walkthrough, the credentials should come from the shared credentials file and the region from its config. Commands that omit `--profile` use a different resolution path and can select environment credentials instead; keep the profile option on every test. Although the listing masks most credential characters, its output still belongs in private diagnostics. See [AWS credential precedence](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html). ## Steps: list, upload and download a sample Replace `ws_example` everywhere with the copied workspace ID, and replace `aws-check-20261014-unique.txt` with a new name you have confirmed is unused. Run from a disposable local working folder. Do not choose an existing important key: PUT can replace its current content with a new Dosya version. ```sh aws --profile dosya-help-check --region us-east-1 --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket ws_example --max-keys 10 --no-paginate printf 'Dosya AWS CLI connection check\n' > ./aws-check-20261014-unique.txt aws --profile dosya-help-check --region us-east-1 --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 s3api put-object --bucket ws_example --key aws-check-20261014-unique.txt --body ./aws-check-20261014-unique.txt aws --profile dosya-help-check --region us-east-1 --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 s3api head-object --bucket ws_example --key aws-check-20261014-unique.txt aws --profile dosya-help-check --region us-east-1 --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 s3api get-object --bucket ws_example --key aws-check-20261014-unique.txt ./aws-check-downloaded.txt cmp ./aws-check-20261014-unique.txt ./aws-check-downloaded.txt ``` `--max-keys 10 --no-paginate` requests one small listing page; an empty authorized root can legitimately have no Contents. It does not establish that no other pages exist. Normal larger walks must follow pagination; the gateway caps one page at 1,000 entries. PUT normally produces JSON containing **ETag**; HEAD includes **ContentLength**; GET writes the destination file and prints its response metadata. The sample line above is 31 bytes including the newline. Choose a new download filename too, since an existing local output file can be overwritten. `cmp` prints nothing and exits zero for identical files. On PowerShell, compare `(Get-FileHash ./source.txt).Hash` with `(Get-FileHash ./download.txt).Hash`, and inspect `$LASTEXITCODE` immediately after each native AWS command. On POSIX shells use `echo $?` immediately; a later command replaces that status. In Dosya **Files**, confirm the same filename and size in the selected workspace (or key anchor). A zero CLI exit code and matching downloaded bytes are the connection test; ETags for multipart files are not ordinary MD5 hashes. This procedure grants no recipient a public link. ## Expected result and deliberate cleanup You have a dedicated profile whose direct bucket listing succeeds and whose sample survives a byte-for-byte download check. Keep the profile only if you intend to use it, with the credential files private. To remove **only this known sample**, review the bucket/key again, then run: ```sh aws --profile dosya-help-check --region us-east-1 --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 s3api delete-object --bucket ws_example --key aws-check-20261014-unique.txt ``` DeleteObject returns 204 even for an absent key, so do not treat a quiet result as evidence the object previously existed. A real deletion sends the file to Dosya Trash and revokes its shares; it does not immediately free storage. Trash purge follows the owner's effective seven-day free or 30-day paid retention. Permanent purge destroys the recoverable bytes. To retire the connection, use **Revoke** on its dedicated API key. That is irreversible and also disables its S3 pair, without removing your cloud data. Remove just the `[dosya-help-check]` block from the local credentials file and `[profile dosya-help-check]` block from config after checking you are editing the intended profile; do not delete shared AWS configuration files. Erase local samples only after any inspection you still need. ## Troubleshooting **AccessDenied while listing or downloading.** Upload only is insufficient. Check key scope, S3 protocol, workspace pin, member role, address and active-hour restrictions. S3 root listing uses ordinary file paths rather than WebDAV collection names. **SignatureDoesNotMatch.** Verify that the access ID and secret came from the same S3 dialog, and that the client signs the exact endpoint, region and path actually sent. A proxy rewrite or a different profile selected by a wrapper can make a correctly saved profile fail. **Usage or front-door throttling.** A 429 XML **SlowDown** comes from key/role usage enforcement: read its Message and honor Retry-After if supplied. Reduce parallel transfers for a concurrency refusal; retries cannot replenish byte allowance. The separate front-door throttle returns 429 JSON **{"ok":false,"error":"Too many requests"}**, with Retry-After, after its 600 requests/minute per-user or 1,200/minute per-IP budget is exhausted. Wait for that interval and stagger request-heavy jobs. Workspace storage/file policies and daily egress remain separate limits. **A backup client requires bucket versioning or Object Lock.** Those AWS configuration features are unsupported here; configuring path style does not provide them. Matching-name uploads use Dosya history (default 10 versions, with pruning and free-owner seven-day aged-version retention), not AWS S3 version IDs. Keep independent originals. Never put full credentials, signed request URLs or unredacted `--debug` output into a public issue. For clock and presign-specific refusals, see the dedicated signature-time guide. ## Related guides - [S3 settings, operation support and permission errors](/integrations/s3-connect) - [S3 request signing and expiry recovery](/integrations/s3-fix-signature-time-error) - [AWS CLI configuration reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/topic/s3-config.html)

body: Connect your S3 client to `https://api.dosya.dev/s3` using **path-style addressing**, region `us-east-1` and the S3 credential pair attached to a Dosya API key. Your bucket is a workspace ID, not its display name. The gateway exposes ordinary workspace files; AWS bucket administration and immutability features are outside its supported boundary. ## Before you start Select the intended workspace and open **Integrations → S3**. Its **Connection settings** show Endpoint, Region and Bucket for the current workspace. If the page says **Your role can’t use the S3 gateway**, ask its owner/admin for S3 access before configuring the client. Role permissions for listing, uploading, downloading and deletion still apply separately. You can use S3 on the free plan, within its storage and download allowances. API-key creation has a three-key cap for effectively free users and a 20-key overall cap. An explicit key or role limit can narrow file size, daily download bytes, requests per minute or active transfers. The protocol is exempt from plan request-count and concurrency ceilings; that exemption does not remove explicit restrictions or egress limits. ## Steps: generate the right credential pair 1. Open **Profile → API keys → New API key**. Enter a label in **What is it for?**. For this list/upload/download test choose **Full access**; **Read only** permits browsing and downloading but rejects uploads, and **Upload only** cannot list or download objects. 2. Under **Restrictions and expiry**, choose **Only the ones I pick** for **Protocols**, select **S3 gateway**, and pin the intended **Workspace**. Choose a short expiry and review address, active-hour and usage controls appropriate to this client. **Choose folder…** can make a selected folder the client's root. 3. Select **Generate key**. Save the full `dos_…` API key if you also need that credential; it is shown at creation only. The S3 client needs a separate pair, not this value. 4. Expand the saved key's row. At **S3 credentials**, select **Enable**. In the **S3 credentials** dialog, copy **Access key ID**, **Secret access key**, **Endpoint** and **Region** before **Done**. The access ID starts with `DOSYA`; the generated secret has 40 characters. Store it in your client's protected credential facility. The screenshot shows the API-key restriction form, not the later S3-secret dialog. S3 **Active · show** can display the access ID again but replaces the secret with **(secret key is not retrievable - revoke and recreate the key to rotate)**. Enabling the same key twice is refused with **S3 credentials already exist for this API key. Delete and recreate to regenerate.** A lost secret requires a new key/pair; update dependent clients and then revoke the old key. Revocation cannot be undone and refuses both that key and its S3 pair; it does not delete stored files. ## Steps: enter the connection settings | Client field | Dosya value | | --- | --- | | S3-compatible endpoint / service URL | `https://api.dosya.dev/s3` | | Region | `us-east-1` | | Signature / authentication | AWS Signature Version 4 | | Access key | The generated `DOSYA…` access key ID | | Secret key | The accompanying S3 secret, never the `dos_…` API key | | Addressing | Path style (`forcePathStyle: true` in AWS SDK for JavaScript) | | Bucket | The exact workspace ID copied from Integrations → S3, such as `ws_example` | Do not put the bucket in the hostname. An object with key `checks/sample.txt` lives at `/s3/ws_example/checks/sample.txt` and appears as `sample.txt` inside `checks` in Files. S3 does not add WebDAV's `All` collection: `All/sample.txt` would instead name an ordinary folder. Copy IDs exactly even if a workspace was renamed. A folder-restricted key retains the workspace bucket ID but resolves every object key **relative to its anchor**. If its anchor is `Projects`, `checks/sample.txt` reaches `Projects/checks/sample.txt`; do not prepend `Projects` again. Workspace membership confinement intersects with key confinement. A key cannot reach a wider subtree than the member, another pinned workspace or a trashed anchor. Items hidden from the key owner or their role are excluded unless the role has **hide_files**, which permits viewing hidden items; the key does not independently bypass those visibility rules. ## Steps: prove a sample transfer 1. List the chosen bucket, preferably through its direct ID. Bucket discovery may be filtered to permitted workspaces; successful discovery alone proves no upload rights. 2. Choose a new sample name under an authorized disposable prefix, such as `checks/s3-first-sample.txt`. Upload harmless bytes and wait for the client's operation result. A nested new path can create missing folders if your role allows folder creation. 3. Refresh **Files** in Dosya, checking the actual workspace/anchor path, name and byte size. Download that exact key into a separate local file and compare the contents or a locally computed SHA-256. 4. Decide what happens to `checks/s3-first-sample.txt`: keep it for inspection or delete that exact object through the client. To retire this test connection, select **Revoke** on its dedicated row in **Profile → API keys**; deleting only the local profile leaves both the cloud sample and its key intact. PutObject returns HTTP 200 with an ETag after committing; GET returns object bytes (or a range response), and listing is XML with up to 1,000 entries per page. Clients must follow continuation tokens. An ETag alone is not a universal file hash: multipart objects use multipart ETags. These operations do not create a public sharing URL; use Dosya sharing when a recipient needs access without your credentials. ## Supported operations and consequences The router implements bucket/object listing, HEAD, upload/download, copy, delete, batch delete, directory markers and multipart initiate/upload-part/upload-part-copy/list/complete/abort. Batch delete accepts at most 1,000 keys and reports errors for individual keys. Multipart part numbers are 1–10,000 and each part has a 5 GiB maximum; your actual object/storage limits can be much smaller. A failed multipart transfer may leave an unfinished upload: use your client's abort operation rather than assuming a local cancel removed the parts. Buckets correspond to existing workspaces. A CreateBucket request for an accessible existing workspace can return 200 as a compatibility check; it cannot create a workspace. Bucket deletion, AWS IAM/ACLs, lifecycle rules, configurable CORS, replication, AWS S3 versioning and Object Lock/retention/legal hold are not available through this gateway. Configuration writes return 501 **NotImplemented**; some reads return empty configuration or a named absence error. Do not select this endpoint for software that requires S3 immutability or legal-hold guarantees. Uploading over a matching file path creates another **Dosya file version**, not an AWS version ID. The workspace's default history cap is 10 versions; a positive configured cap prunes excess history and free-owner aged versions have a seven-day retention pass. Keep originals for recovery. Deleting an eligible object returns 204 even if it was already absent; it moves the existing file to Trash and revokes its share links. Trash still occupies storage until purge and is subject to owner-effective retention (seven days on free, 30 otherwise). Purged bytes and revoked credentials cannot be recovered by reconnecting the client. ## Troubleshooting | Result | Check or corrective action | | --- | --- | | `InvalidAccessKeyId` / `The access key ID does not exist` | Confirm the S3 access ID; expired, revoked and invalid keys are refused. | | `SignatureDoesNotMatch` / `The request signature does not match` | Check the paired secret and exact signed endpoint/path; discard the old request and let the client sign again. | | `AccessDenied` / `This API key is not permitted to use the S3 gateway` | Create a key whose selected protocols include S3. | | `This API key is pinned to a different workspace` | Use the copied bucket ID matching the key pin. | | `This role is not permitted to use the S3 gateway` | The workspace owner/admin must review the role's S3 access. | | `Upload not allowed`, `Creating folders is not allowed`, or `Object is locked` | Match the requested operation to role permissions and destination state. | | `EntityTooLarge` or `QuotaExceeded` | Inspect file-size, workspace storage and explicit key/role limits before retrying. | | 429 XML `SlowDown` | Key/role usage enforcement refused the request or transfer. Read its specific Message, honor Retry-After when supplied, and reduce parallelism for a concurrency refusal; a byte allowance needs its reset or an authorized limit change. | | 429 JSON `{"ok":false,"error":"Too many requests"}` | The independent front-door throttle was reached: 600 requests/minute per user or 1,200/minute per IP. Pause until Retry-After, reduce request frequency and stagger jobs sharing that user/IP. | Authentication happens before protocol, key conditions, usage, workspace pin, member/anchor and role gates, so fixing one refusal may reveal another. Do not broaden a restricted key just to hide a different operation failure. ## Expected result The client reaches the copied workspace bucket with SigV4 path-style requests. Your sample's destination is visible in Files and its separately downloaded bytes match the original; a saved connection label or successful login without that check is incomplete setup. ## Related guides - [Run the AWS CLI sample with an isolated profile](/integrations/s3-aws-cli-connect) - [Recover signature and request-time errors](/integrations/s3-fix-signature-time-error) - [Set a key's protocol restrictions](/developers/api-key-protocols)

title: Correct an S3 endpoint or region mismatch
summary: Correct the Dosya S3 base path, path-style mode, workspace bucket, and signing inputs; use us-east-1 as the published, tested client default.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Correct an S3 endpoint or region mismatch” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/s3/auth.ts`, `packages/prod-smoke/src/lanes/s3.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya’s S3 gateway lives below the API host. The released client setup uses endpoint `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`, published region value `us-east-1`, path-style addressing, and a bucket name equal to the workspace ID such as `wks_…`. The region fills a required client field; the gateway does not enforce one fixed signing region. ## Before you start Use an S3 credential whose parent API key allows the **S3 gateway**. The user must still belong to the bucket workspace, and their role needs S3 access; listing objects additionally needs file access. The signer region is protocol configuration, not the physical storage location of uploaded bytes. Dosya stores new objects in the workspace’s configured region. Its client instructions and compatibility response publish `us-east-1`, while signature verification derives the signing key from the region and service written in each request’s credential scope. ## Steps 1. Open the client profile without exposing its secret, and compare the endpoint character for character with `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`. 2. Use `us-east-1` for the published and production-tested client setup. Another region is not a mismatch by itself when the client uses that same value consistently in its credential scope and signing key. 3. Enable path-style addressing so the request shape is `/s3/{workspace-id}/{key}` rather than a workspace subdomain. 4. Set the bucket to the exact workspace ID returned by Dosya, not its display name, slug, or a folder name. 5. Retest with a narrow root listing or `HEAD` request. For **SignatureDoesNotMatch**, inspect the secret, canonical path, query, signed headers, body hash, date, region, and service together; changing only the region does not repair a different signing fault. 6. If the request succeeds, list one permitted test prefix and verify the returned key names before restoring the client’s normal workload. ## Expected result The client signs the actual `/s3` request path and reaches the intended workspace bucket. A valid list returns only workspaces and objects permitted by the API key, membership role, and optional folder anchor. **InvalidAccessKeyId** points to an unknown or revoked S3 access ID. **SignatureDoesNotMatch** means the client and gateway calculated different canonical requests or signing keys; it does not prove that a non-`us-east-1` region caused the failure. **NoSuchBucket** means the workspace ID is wrong or unavailable to this user. ## Related guides - [Connect with S3-compatible tools](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Troubleshoot S3 access](/troubleshooting/s3)

title: Download an object with an S3 client
summary: Download one Dosya object through the S3 gateway with AWS CLI, using the documented endpoint, region, workspace bucket, and read permissions.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/s3.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts, apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/lib/s3/auth.ts, apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/get-object.ts, apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/head-object.ts, and S3 path/anchor tests. No production object was downloaded.
body: Dosya exposes each workspace through an S3-compatible bucket. The endpoint is `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`, the signing region is `us-east-1`, and the bucket name is the workspace ID shown on **Integrations → S3**. ## Prepare credentials and permissions Your workspace role must allow the **S3 gateway**, file access, and downloads. If S3 itself is denied, the setup page says **Your role can’t use the S3 gateway**. An owner or admin must change that role. In **Profile → API keys**, create a **Read only** key and restrict its protocols to **S3 gateway** when the credential is solely for downloads. Attach S3 credentials to that API key. Dosya displays the secret access key once, so copy it into a secure credential store at creation time. A workspace pin can limit the credential to the expected bucket. A folder anchor is also supported: that folder becomes `/` for the S3 view, so object keys are relative to the anchor and paths above or beside it are unreachable. Configure AWS CLI with the displayed S3 access key and secret: ```sh aws configure set aws_access_key_id DOSYA_your_access_key aws configure set aws_secret_access_key your_secret_key ``` Avoid saving these commands in shared transcripts. Use an isolated AWS profile if the machine already has unrelated credentials. ## Steps 1. Copy the workspace ID from **Integrations → S3** and identify the exact object key by listing a narrow prefix: ```sh aws --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 --region us-east-1 \ s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket WORKSPACE_ID --prefix 'path/to/' ``` 2. Inspect the S3 object's `ContentLength` without downloading content: ```sh aws --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 --region us-east-1 \ s3api head-object --bucket WORKSPACE_ID --key 'path/to/object.bin' ``` 3. Choose a new local filename or back up the current path. `aws s3 cp` can replace the local destination named in the command. 4. Download the object: ```sh aws --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 --region us-east-1 \ s3 cp 's3://WORKSPACE_ID/path/to/object.bin' './object.bin' ``` 5. Compare the local byte count with `ContentLength` from `head-object`. If the original source has a separately trusted checksum, calculate the same algorithm locally and compare it; do not assume every S3 ETag is a portable content hash. ## Troubleshooting - `AccessDenied: API key scope 'upload' cannot download files` means the key is upload-only; issue a read-only or full-access key instead. - `AccessDenied: Access denied` means the role lacks general file access. `AccessDenied: Download not allowed` identifies the separate download permission. - `NoSuchBucket` usually means the workspace ID is wrong, the key is pinned elsewhere, or the user no longer belongs to that workspace. - `NoSuchKey` means the relative path does not resolve to a visible live file. Hidden content also resolves as absent, and a folder-anchored key must omit every path segment above its anchor. - `AccessDenied: Object is locked` means the file or one of its ancestors has a full lock. Personal unlock state in the web app does not turn an S3 request into an allowed download. - `SignatureDoesNotMatch` requires checking the access-key pair, endpoint, and `us-east-1` signing region. Regenerating only the secret is not possible because it is shown once; attach a new S3 credential pair when lost. - An unsatisfiable byte range returns HTTP `416` with `Content-Range: bytes */SIZE`; retry without a stale range after checking the current object size. The download is read-only for Dosya: it does not remove, move, or alter the cloud object. Replacing an existing local output path is a local effect and cannot be recovered from Dosya unless another local copy exists. ## Expected result AWS CLI exits successfully, the local file size equals the S3 `ContentLength`, and an independently known checksum matches when available. The source object remains in the same Dosya workspace path with no cloud-side mutation. ## Related guides - [Connect an S3 client](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Restrict S3 permissions](/developers/s3-permissions)

title: Set the endpoint and region in an S3 client
summary: Configure an S3 client with Dosya’s exact endpoint, us-east-1 signer region, path-style addressing, workspace bucket, and one-time credentials.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Set the endpoint and region in an S3 client” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/s3-credentials.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts`, `packages/prod-smoke/src/lanes/s3.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Create S3 credentials from an existing Dosya API key, then configure the exact gateway values returned by the released dialog. The S3 secret cannot be retrieved after that dialog closes. ## Before you start In **Profile > API keys**, use a key whose protocols are unrestricted or explicitly include **S3 gateway**. A workspace-pinned key also requires current membership and a role permitted to use S3. Expired keys cannot be enabled. Choose **Read only**, **Upload only**, or **Full access** for the task and narrow the workspace or folder when possible. A folder anchor becomes the S3 root visible to that credential. ## Steps 1. Expand the intended API-key row and choose **Enable** in its S3 section; if no key exists, create one and include **S3 gateway** under protocol restrictions. 2. In **S3 credentials**, copy **Access key ID** and **Secret access key** into a protected client profile before closing the dialog. 3. Set **Endpoint** to `https://api.dosya.dev/s3` and **Region** to `us-east-1`, exactly as displayed. 4. Enable path-style addressing and use the exact workspace ID as the bucket name. 5. Run a non-destructive bucket or prefix listing that the key’s scope and role allow; an upload-only key cannot list existing files. 6. Confirm the expected workspace appears and one known permitted key is returned, then remove credentials from terminal history or temporary files. ## Expected result The client reaches Dosya through AWS Signature V4 at `/s3/{workspace-id}/…`. The access key remains visible in the API-key row, while reopening **S3 credentials** shows that the secret is not retrievable and rotation requires a new API key. If **Enable** is absent, inspect the key’s protocol restriction and expiry. The server refuses S3 credential creation for keys that exclude S3, expired keys, lost workspace memberships, and roles without S3 access. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Restrict protocol access](/developers/api-key-protocols)

title: Fix an S3 signature time error
summary: Diagnose S3 signature mismatch versus presigned expiry, inspect the signing machine’s clock and retry a newly signed read-only Dosya request.
verification: Reviewed 2026-10-14 against local repository implementation and tests. Local evidence: apps/api/src/lib/s3/auth.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/auth.presign-expiry.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/api-key-auth.ts; apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/xml.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/list-objects.ts; apps/web/src/pages/integrations/s3.tsx; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/s3-credentials.ts. Code review confirms no RequestTimeTooSkewed code or normal header/future-presign skew tolerance is implemented. Official references: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-troubleshooting.html; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/topic/s3-config.html; https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/set-the-date-and-time-mchlp2996/mac; https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/networking/windows-time-service/windows-time-service-tools-and-settings; https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/timedatectl.html. External commands are source-derived and checked on temporary local fixtures where reported; no production credentials or remote writes used. Existing captures retain their original verification scope. Supplemental official sources checked: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/man/timedatectl.xml; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-envvars.html. Review correction: replaced the earlier illustration with a source-derived process diagram following the current guide, inspected both 1200x675 themes with no text clipping and narrow-page/full-size behavior; diagrams show command stages, not an invented app UI.
body: Read the S3 response's exact **Code** and **Message** before changing your clock or credentials. `RequestTimeTooSkewed`, `SignatureDoesNotMatch` and an expired presigned URL describe different failures. The current Dosya gateway emits the latter two cases described below; it does **not** implement a `RequestTimeTooSkewed` response or a documented normal-request clock-skew tolerance. ## Before you start: identify the actual error Save the status and redacted XML Code/Message from one failed operation, plus the client version and actual endpoint host/path. Dosya authentication XML includes **RequestId** (currently `0`), not a guaranteed diagnostic server-time or maximum-skew field. Remove Authorization, S3 secrets and the entire presigned query string from anything you share. | Response | Meaning in the current Dosya implementation | | --- | --- | | 403 `SignatureDoesNotMatch` / `The request signature does not match` | The recomputed SigV4 signature differs; investigate secret pairing or changed signed data. This message alone does not prove a wrong clock. | | 403 `AccessDenied` / `Request has expired` | A presigned request is past its signed timestamp plus declared expiry. | | 400 `InvalidRequest` / `X-Amz-Expires is required for presigned requests` | The query-auth request omitted a required validity duration. | | 400 `InvalidRequest` / `X-Amz-Expires must be an integer between 1 and 604800 seconds` | Its declared duration is invalid; regenerate rather than editing it. | | 400 `InvalidRequest` / `Invalid X-Amz-Date` | The presigned date is not in the parser's `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` format. | | 403 `AccessDenied` / `Missing X-Amz-Date` | The signed header request has no timestamp. | | 403 `InvalidAccessKeyId` | Its access ID is invalid, revoked, expired or otherwise unavailable; synchronizing time will not restore the key. | The verified presign duration range is **1–604,800 seconds (seven days)**. The server accepts the exact expiry boundary and refuses any instant after it. The current header-auth code has no general “±5/15 minutes” check, and the presign code supplies no future-date skew window. Do not rely on an old header signature remaining usable or assume an AWS tolerance applies here; generate a fresh request for every retry. If your client reports **RequestTimeTooSkewed**, check whether the network request actually went to `api.dosya.dev/s3`, rather than AWS, a different service or a proxy. A client's displayed explanation may summarize a different underlying response. AWS's [troubleshooting guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-troubleshooting.html) explains clock-related AWS signing failures; it does not establish a Dosya timing policy. ## Steps: check time on the machine that signs 1. Pause the failing automated job so it stops resending the same signed payload. Note whether signing happens on your computer, a container, a build runner or an application server; correcting a browser clock cannot repair a signature created elsewhere. 2. Inspect that system's UTC time. The commands below only display time/status; they do not change the machine: ```sh # macOS or Linux date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' # Linux systems that use systemd (not every container has it) timedatectl status ``` ```powershell # Windows PowerShell (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ') w32tm /query /status ``` 3. Compare with a trusted time source used by your organization. UTC represents the same instant across time zones; changing the display zone alone does not synchronize a clock. A server's HTTP Date header can help spot gross differences but is not an authoritative time-synchronization service, and proxies/caches can make it misleading. 4. If time is wrong, use the operating system's supported automatic time setting or your administrator's time service. On macOS, Date & Time settings expose automatic date/time; Windows Date & time provides its time synchronization controls; on systemd Linux check the reported NTP state. Managed devices, VMs and containers may require the host administrator to repair synchronization. Confirm the UTC output again after a change. These commands may need a service or permission on your platform. A failed `timedatectl` or `w32tm` command is not evidence that Dosya credentials are invalid. Keep the signer synchronized without disabling HTTPS verification or broadening key permissions. ## Steps: issue a newly signed, read-only test Use a correctly configured AWS CLI v2 profile, here named `dosya-help-check`. It must hold the **S3** access ID/secret pair, with `us-east-1` and `s3.addressing_style` set to `path`. Obtain the pair via **Profile → API keys**, expand an S3-enabled key, and select **S3 credentials → Enable**; the secret is available only in that generation dialog. Use a **Read only** key for diagnosis, pinned to your workspace with S3 gateway allowed. Your workspace role must also permit S3 and listing. Configure the profile interactively with `aws configure --profile dosya-help-check` rather than passing the secret as a shell argument. Never overwrite an existing unrelated profile. Set path style with `aws configure set s3.addressing_style path --profile dosya-help-check`. Replace `ws_example` below with **Bucket** from **Integrations → S3**: ```sh aws --profile dosya-help-check --region us-east-1 --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket ws_example --max-keys 1 --no-paginate ``` Launching this command signs a new request; clicking retry on a stored presigned URL does not. Expect one listing page, possibly with no Contents for an empty location, and CLI exit zero. A read-only list neither overwrites nor deletes files. If the result changes to a protocol, role, IP, active-hours or usage refusal, the time/signature symptom is resolved but access setup still needs its own correction. The key cannot exceed your role; no plan upgrade is required just to fix signing, though key counts and normal allowance rules still apply. ## Presigned links, proxies and signature mismatch **Expired URL.** Ask the trusted application that generated the URL to create another after its signer has correct time. Do not extend `X-Amz-Expires`, rewrite `X-Amz-Date` or strip parameters by hand: those values participate in the signature. A presigned URL is a credential-bearing link; share it only with its intended recipient and never paste it into public diagnostics. Regeneration provides a new URL, not a permanent public Dosya share. Revoking its parent credential also removes access. **Clock is correct but SignatureDoesNotMatch persists.** Match the `DOSYA…` ID to the secret generated for that exact key. Confirm the endpoint includes `/s3`, path addressing is enabled, and the signed method, object path, encoded query, Host header and payload-hash header arrive unchanged. A proxy that rewrites any signed component can invalidate the signature. Check which profile the actual failing job selects; commands without the explicit `--profile` option can resolve environment credentials instead. Inspect the intended sources with `aws configure list --profile dosya-help-check` privately. **Cached or replayed request.** Disable the job's reuse of stored Authorization headers or presigned URLs and let its SDK sign each request at send time. Merely resending identical bytes keeps the old expiry. If testing direct access avoids a proxy, compare behavior using a fresh signature on each route rather than carrying one signature between different hosts. **Secret lost or exposed.** S3 **Active · show** cannot recover the secret. Create replacement credentials, update the affected signer and revoke the compromised key after validating the replacement. Revocation is irreversible and affects every client using that key/pair, while leaving cloud files intact. Do not rotate other clients' keys merely because one request was malformed. ## Expected result A freshly generated read-only request succeeds against the intended Dosya bucket, or returns an exact access refusal that can be diagnosed separately. No data mutation was needed to establish that signing works. Record the corrected signer, endpoint and timestamp privately so the scheduled job uses the same configuration next time. ## Related guides - [AWS CLI profile and transfer test](/integrations/s3-aws-cli-connect) - [S3 connection fields and permission boundary](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Troubleshoot other S3 access failures](/troubleshooting/s3)

title: List folders and prefixes over S3
summary: List a Dosya workspace by prefix and slash delimiter, follow every 1,000-key page, and distinguish file objects from folder common prefixes.
verification: Locally reviewed for “List folders and prefixes over S3” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/list-buckets.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/list-objects.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya maps each workspace to an S3 bucket named by workspace ID. File and folder names become keys; a slash delimiter returns immediate files as objects and immediate folders as `CommonPrefixes`. ## Before you start Use a read-capable or full-access API key with S3 allowed. An upload-only key can list buckets for client handshake but object listing returns **AccessDenied: API key scope 'upload' cannot list files**. The member role must allow both S3 and file access. A folder-anchored key starts at that folder as its logical root. Prefixes are relative to the anchor, so do not prepend the hidden parent path. ## Steps 1. List buckets and select the exact `wks_…` value for the workspace; never substitute its display name. 2. Request the root with `delimiter=/` and `max-keys` at or below `1000`. 3. Separate returned `Contents` entries from `CommonPrefixes`; a common prefix ends in `/` and represents a Dosya folder. 4. Choose one child prefix such as `photos/` and issue the next listing with that exact case and trailing slash. 5. When `IsTruncated` is true, pass `NextContinuationToken` to the following V2 request; V1 clients must continue with `NextMarker`. 6. Stop only after the final page reports no truncation, then compare the complete set with the permitted folder in Dosya. ## Expected result The client traverses the accessible Dosya tree without skipping entries after the first 1,000 results. Exact-file prefixes return that file alone, partial name prefixes filter siblings, and a nonexistent prefix returns an empty result rather than broadening to the bucket root. If the bucket appears but its contents do not, check API-key scope, the member role’s file permission, hidden-file rules, and any folder anchor. A pinned key lists only its pinned workspace. ## Related guides - [Connect an S3 client](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Restrict S3 permissions](/developers/s3-permissions)

title: Troubleshoot S3 endpoint and path-style errors
summary: Keep the workspace ID in the request path under the /s3 endpoint, correct virtual-host defaults, and retest with an allowed S3 credential safely.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Troubleshoot S3 endpoint and path-style errors” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts`, `packages/prod-smoke/src/rclone-config.ts`, `packages/prod-smoke/src/lanes/s3.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Dosya is mounted at `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`, so clients must keep the workspace bucket in the URL path. Virtual-host style changes the host and omits the bucket segment expected by the gateway route. ## Before you start Keep the S3 secret out of screenshots and logs. Confirm the parent API key includes the S3 surface and is not expired before changing network settings. For rclone’s S3 backend, the released working shape uses `provider = Other`, `endpoint = https://api.dosya.dev/s3`, `force_path_style = true`, and `region = us-east-1`. The tested large-upload cutoff is `64Mi`. ## Steps 1. Inspect the failed request URL and verify it should be `/s3/{workspace-id}/{object-key}` on host `api.dosya.dev`. 2. Replace any AWS default endpoint or bare `https://api.dosya.dev` value with `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`. 3. Turn on the client’s path-style option, named `forcePathStyle`, `s3ForcePathStyle`, or `force_path_style` depending on the tool. 4. Set the region to `us-east-1` and the bucket to the literal Dosya workspace ID. 5. Retry a `HEAD` bucket or shallow list; if rclone alone returns **SignatureDoesNotMatch**, set `sign_accept_encoding = false` so an upstream header rewrite is not signed. 6. Confirm the successful request reaches the intended bucket, then run one scoped object operation and inspect its exact key. ## Expected result The client sends and signs the gateway’s real path, Dosya parses the workspace as the bucket, and the request reaches S3 routing instead of an unrelated API route or virtual host. If authentication still fails, distinguish **InvalidAccessKeyId** from **SignatureDoesNotMatch**. The first requires a current access ID; the second requires checking secret, base path, signed headers, clock, and client canonicalization. ## Related guides - [Connect an S3 client](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Restrict S3 permissions](/developers/s3-permissions)

title: Restrict S3 credentials and verify access
summary: Limit an S3 credential by permission, protocol, workspace, folder, address, hours and usage, then prove allowed and denied object operations.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified API-key controls, S3 credential creation, role gates, anchors, scope errors, endpoint settings and request limits in apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts; apps/web/src/pages/integrations/s3.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/s3-credentials.ts; apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/auth.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/list-objects.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/get-object.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/put-object.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/delete-object.ts; and apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/scope.upload-cannot-read.unit.test.ts. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: An S3 request must pass every boundary attached to the credential and workspace. The API-key permission limits the operation, **Protocols** must permit the S3 gateway, the workspace and folder settings restrict location, and the caller's current workspace role can narrow access further. A successful credential creation does not override a later role or membership change. ## Steps Dosya offers three API-key permissions for S3: | Permission | Intended S3 use | Operations that are deliberately refused | | --- | --- | --- | | **Read only** | List buckets and objects, inspect metadata, and download objects. | Uploads return `API key scope 'read' cannot upload files`; delete and copy also require Full access. | | **Upload only** | Add new objects without exposing stored content. | Listing returns `API key scope 'upload' cannot list files`; reads return `API key scope 'upload' cannot download files`. | | **Full access** | Read, upload, copy, move through supported client operations, and delete when the role also permits it. | Role permissions, locks, anchors, usage limits, and workspace policy still apply. | Deleting an S3 object moves the Dosya file to Trash and returns 204; it does not immediately release storage. The key must have **Full access**, and the role needs `delete_own_files` or `delete_any_file` for the object. Treat `aws s3 rm` as a destructive action even though recovery may remain available in Trash. ## Create a narrowly scoped key 1. Sign in at [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api) and select **New API key**. 2. Enter a client-specific label under **What is it for?** and choose **Read only**, **Upload only**, or **Full access** under **What can it do?** 3. Expand **Restrictions and expiry**, then open **Where can it reach?** 4. Under **Protocols**, choose **Only the ones I pick** and check **S3 gateway**. Leaving S3 unchecked makes credential activation show **Not allowed** and the gateway return `This API key is not permitted to use the S3 gateway`. 5. Select the exact **Workspace**. Choose **Folder** when the client should see only that folder and its descendants; for an anchored key, the chosen folder becomes the S3 root. 6. Add **Allowed IP ranges**, **Only during a weekly window**, or limits under **How much can it use?** when the client has stable requirements. Blank usage fields mean no explicit key limit, while plan and role ceilings can still apply. 7. Choose an expiry, review the sentence describing the key, and select **Generate key**. Save the one-time `dos_` value. 8. Expand the new key. Beside **S3 credentials**, select **Enable** and save both `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key` from the reveal. The secret cannot be retrieved later. S3 credentials inherit the key's scope, reach, source conditions, expiry, and usage limits. If credentials already exist, activation returns `S3 credentials already exist for this API key. Delete and recreate to regenerate.` API keys cannot be edited after creation; use **Duplicate settings**, create the corrected replacement, test it, and then revoke the old key. ## Configure the client Use the endpoint `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`, region `us-east-1`, and the workspace ID as the bucket name. A display name is not a bucket identifier. ```bash export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID='REPLACE_WITH_DOSYA_ACCESS_KEY_ID' read -r -s -p 'S3 secret: ' AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY printf '\n' export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID='REPLACE_WITH_WORKSPACE_ID' aws --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 --region us-east-1 \ s3 ls "s3://$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID/" ``` For a folder-anchored key, paths begin at the selected folder. Do not prepend the folder's path from the web app, because that would look for a same-named child under the anchor. ## Test both sides of the boundary Use a non-confidential file and commands appropriate to the selected scope: ```bash printf 'S3 permission check\n' > s3-permission-check.txt # Upload test: suitable for Upload only or Full access. aws --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 --region us-east-1 \ s3 cp s3-permission-check.txt "s3://$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID/tests/s3-permission-check.txt" # Read test: suitable for Read only or Full access. aws --endpoint-url https://api.dosya.dev/s3 --region us-east-1 \ s3 cp "s3://$DOSYA_WORKSPACE_ID/tests/s3-permission-check.txt" ./received.txt ``` Then issue a harmless request that should fail: list with an upload-only key, upload with a read-only key, use another workspace ID with a pinned key, or request a sibling path outside the folder anchor. Expect an S3 XML error with HTTP 403 and `AccessDenied`. A different-workspace attempt returns `This API key is pinned to a different workspace`. The workspace role must include **Use the S3 gateway**. Object listing also needs file-page access, downloading needs `download_files`, uploading needs `upload_files`, and automatically creating missing path folders needs `create_folders`. Relevant refusals include `This role is not permitted to use the S3 gateway`, `This role cannot list files`, `Download not allowed`, `Upload not allowed`, and `Creating folders is not allowed`. Requests are additionally limited to 600 per minute per user and 1,200 per minute per IP before any narrower key or role request limit. A usage refusal returns `SlowDown` with HTTP 429 and `Retry-After`; reduce concurrency and wait instead of replacing a valid credential. ## Expiry, anchors, and revocation An expired API key cannot authenticate or mint S3 credentials. If the selected anchor folder is trashed or removed, requests fail with `This API key's anchor folder is no longer available`. A member later confined to another folder cannot use a credential anchor outside that permitted subtree. Revoking the API key stops its bearer token and attached S3 access key from authenticating. Revocation cannot be undone, so update the S3 client with a tested replacement before removing a credential used by a backup or automation. The files already uploaded remain in Dosya; revocation does not delete or recall them. ## Expected result The required operation succeeds inside the chosen bucket and folder, while the planned outside or wrong-scope request returns `AccessDenied`. The key row identifies its permission, S3 protocol, reach, expiry, and last use, allowing the credential to be audited and revoked independently. ## Related guides - [Connect an S3-compatible client](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Choose read, upload, or full permission](/developers/api-key-scopes) - [Anchor a key to one folder](/developers/api-key-folder-access)

title: Resolve denied access to an S3 prefix
summary: Match the bucket and relative prefix to the API key’s workspace or folder anchor, role permissions, and read scope before safely widening access.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Resolve denied access to an S3 prefix” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx`, `apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/list-objects.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/put-object.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: S3 reach is the intersection of the API key’s surface, scope, workspace and folder anchor; the user’s membership role; IP and active-hour conditions; and usage limits. Existing keys cannot be edited to widen that intersection. ## Before you start Expand the key under **Profile > API keys** and read its **Protocols**, **Workspace**, and optional **Folder** values. A folder anchor is presented as the S3 root, so object keys are relative to it. Common refusals include **This API key is pinned to a different workspace**, **This API key’s anchor folder is no longer available**, **This role cannot list files**, and **API key scope 'upload' cannot list files**. ## Steps 1. Compare the configured bucket with the key’s pinned workspace ID and correct the client if it names another workspace or a display name. 2. Remove the anchor’s parent path from the requested prefix; for a key anchored at `Projects`, request `2026/report.pdf`, not `Projects/2026/report.pdf`. 3. Verify that the anchor folder still exists and is not trashed, and that the current member confinement still contains the credential anchor. 4. Match the operation to the key scope: use read or full access for listing, and upload or full access for new objects. 5. Check the member role for S3 access, file access when listing, upload permission when writing, and folder-creation permission for missing prefix segments. 6. If broader reach is truly required, use **Duplicate settings**, choose the minimum new workspace or folder boundary, generate and enable S3 credentials, then retest before revoking the old key. ## Expected result The client operates inside the approved workspace subtree without gaining access above it. A replacement key is required for a different anchor because Dosya keys have create-and-revoke semantics rather than editable reach. When only writes are required, an upload-only key can be correct even though listing remains denied. Verify the created object from the Dosya web app or another read-authorized identity instead of broadening that upload credential solely for confirmation. ## Related guides - [Connect with S3-compatible tools](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Troubleshoot S3 access](/troubleshooting/s3)

title: Rotate an S3 access key without interruption
summary: Create and enable a separate S3-capable API key, save its one-time secret, migrate and test every client, then revoke the retired key safely.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Rotate an S3 access key without interruption” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/s3-credentials.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/api/me/api-keys/[id].ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/api-keys.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: An S3 credential belongs to one Dosya API key and cannot be regenerated in place. The safe rotation sequence creates another API key, enables a new S3 pair, proves it, migrates clients, and only then revokes the old row. ## Before you start Inventory every use of the old access key ID. Record the parent key’s scope, S3 surface, workspace or folder anchor, IP ranges, active hours, expiry, and any usage limits. **Duplicate settings** copies visible restrictions, but usage limits start blank and expiry resets to **Never expires**. The new 40-character S3 secret is shown only once. Store it in the client’s secret manager rather than a command line, screenshot, or ticket. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile > API keys**, expand the old key, and choose **Duplicate settings**. 2. Give the new key a rotation-specific name, restore any required usage limit and expiry, keep **S3 gateway** enabled, and choose **Generate key**. 3. Expand the new row, select **Enable**, and save the new **Access key ID**, **Secret access key**, endpoint, and region from **S3 credentials**. 4. Configure one test client with the new pair and verify an operation allowed by its scope against the intended workspace or prefix. 5. Replace the old pair in every production client, restart or reload each client as needed, and confirm successful requests use the new key. 6. On the retired API-key row choose **Revoke** and confirm the irreversible dialog, then prove the old S3 ID now returns **InvalidAccessKeyId**. ## Expected result New requests authenticate with the replacement pair, and deleting the old API key immediately invalidates both its normal API secret and linked S3 credential cache. There is no downtime when the overlap is kept until testing finishes. If a new S3 pair cannot be enabled, verify that the replacement includes S3, has not expired, and is pinned to a workspace where the user’s role allows S3. **S3 credentials already exist for this API key. Delete and recreate to regenerate.** confirms that in-place secret rotation is unsupported. ## Related guides - [Connect with S3-compatible tools](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Troubleshoot S3 access](/troubleshooting/s3)

title: Troubleshoot Dosya S3 authentication and access
summary: Use the S3 error code to repair credentials, SigV4 settings, workspace pinning, permissions, file limits, quota, or request throttling.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/s3.tsx; apps/api/src/lib/s3/auth.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/router.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/list-buckets.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/list-objects.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/put-object.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/complete-multipart.ts; apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/delete-object.ts; apps/api/src/lib/api-key-limits.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/enforce.ts. No production S3 request was made.
body: Keep the complete S3 error code, message, HTTP status and request time before changing the client profile. Authentication is evaluated before protocol permission, workspace pin, membership, folder anchor, role and upload policy, so correcting one layer can legitimately reveal the next refusal. ## Steps Copy the live values from **Integrations → S3** and the matching API-key row: | Client field | Required value | | --- | --- | | Endpoint | `https://api.dosya.dev/s3` | | Region | `us-east-1` | | Signing | AWS Signature Version 4 | | Addressing | Path style; `forcePathStyle: true` in the JavaScript AWS SDK | | Access key | The generated ID beginning `DOSYA`, not the `dos_…` API key | | Secret key | The 40-character S3 secret paired with that access ID | | Bucket | Exact workspace ID, such as `ws_example`, not the workspace name | Do not put the bucket into the hostname. A folder-restricted key keeps the workspace ID as its bucket and treats object keys as relative to the anchor. If the anchor is `Projects`, the object key `checks/a.txt` reaches `Projects/checks/a.txt`; adding `Projects/` again looks in the wrong nested path. The S3 secret cannot be retrieved later. A row displaying **(secret key is not retrievable - revoke and recreate the key to rotate)** requires a new key and credential pair if the stored client secret is lost. Update dependent clients, confirm the replacement, then revoke the old key. Revocation is permanent but does not delete files. ## Match the exact response | S3 result | Cause to check | Recovery | | --- | --- | --- | | `InvalidAccessKeyId` / **The access key ID does not exist** | Wrong access ID, revoked/expired key, or pasted `dos_…` key | Copy the `DOSYA…` access ID from the correct row. Create a replacement pair if that row is no longer active. | | `SignatureDoesNotMatch` / **The request signature does not match** | Secret does not match the access ID, or the client signed a different endpoint/path/query | Re-enter the paired secret, endpoint, region and path-style option; discard the failed request and let the SDK sign a new one. | | `AccessDenied` / **This API key is not permitted to use the S3 gateway** | The key's protocol restriction excludes S3 | Create or replace the key with **S3 gateway** selected under Protocols. | | **This API key is pinned to a different workspace** | Bucket and key workspace pin disagree | Use the bucket ID shown for the pinned workspace, or issue a different narrowly pinned key. | | **This role is not permitted to use the S3 gateway** | Member role lacks the S3 access gate | Ask a workspace owner or admin to grant the role's S3 permission. A broader key cannot override the role. | | `NoSuchBucket`, missing object, or an unexpectedly empty listing | Wrong workspace ID, folder-relative path, membership confinement, hidden/locked state, or Trash | List the permitted bucket/root and build the path from returned names. Compare with Dosya Files under the key owner's account. | | **Upload not allowed**, **Creating folders is not allowed**, or **Object is locked** | Scope/role denies the operation or destination is locked | Choose an allowed operation/destination; do not widen the key before confirming the user's role. | | `EntityTooLarge` | Object exceeds a file-size policy or active key/role limit | Read the returned message, use an accepted file, or have an authorized administrator change the actual limit. | | `QuotaExceeded` | Workspace does not have enough available storage | Free space or increase its storage allowance before starting another multipart upload. | | 429 XML `SlowDown` | Explicit request/transfer/byte rule refused the operation | Honor `Retry-After` when present. Reduce parallel transfers for concurrency limits; byte allowances require their reset or an authorized limit change. | | 429 JSON **Too many requests** | Front-door throttle reached 600 requests/minute per user or 1,200/minute per IP | Pause for `Retry-After`, lower polling/list frequency, and stagger clients sharing that identity or address. | For a presigned request, `X-Amz-Expires` must be an integer from 1 through 604,800 seconds. **Request has expired** means its signed lifetime ended; generate a new URL instead of modifying the query, because changing a signed parameter invalidates the signature. ## Expected result 1. List the exact workspace bucket or its allowed prefix. A successful bucket discovery proves visibility, not upload or delete permission. 2. Download one known harmless object into a new local path and compare its size or SHA-256 with the source. 3. If the key and role allow upload, send uniquely named test bytes to an authorized disposable prefix. Wait for HTTP 200, then refresh **Files** and download the object for comparison. 4. Abort any failed multipart upload through the client. A local cancellation can leave unfinished parts. Listing returns at most 1,000 entries per page, so a client must follow continuation tokens. Multipart part numbers range from 1 to 10,000 and a protocol part may be at most 5 GiB, but your effective object, storage, credential and role limits can be much smaller. ## Understand successful but unexpected changes Uploading to an existing Dosya path creates a new file version. It is not an AWS version ID, and version history/retention rules still apply. Deleting an eligible object moves it to Trash, revokes its share links and can return 204 even when the object was already absent. Trash continues to occupy storage until purge; permanent purge cannot be reversed. The gateway does not provide AWS IAM/ACL administration, lifecycle rules, replication, S3 versioning or Object Lock/legal hold. Configuration writes for unsupported features return `NotImplemented`. If a tool requires those guarantees, changing credentials will not make that workload compatible. ## Escalate without exposing credentials If a minimal listing still fails, provide the client/version, endpoint, region, addressing mode, bucket ID, method, object prefix, HTTP status, S3 code/message, approximate time and timezone, and whether the key is workspace/folder restricted. Redact the access ID if your policy requires it, and never send the secret key, `Authorization` header, presigned query or complete private object path. ## Related guides - [Connect S3](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Restrict S3 permissions](/developers/s3-permissions)

title: Upload an object with an S3 client
summary: Upload a small object through the Dosya S3 endpoint, interpret the returned ETag, and verify its key, byte size, and overwrite behavior safely.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Upload an object with an S3 client” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/put-object.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/s3/router.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/s3/[...path].ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: A Dosya S3 `PutObject` writes to bucket `{workspace-id}` at the configured key. Missing prefix segments can become folders when the member role permits folder creation; uploading to an existing file key creates a new Dosya version. ## Before you start Use endpoint `https://api.dosya.dev/s3`, region `us-east-1`, path-style addressing, and an S3 credential with upload or full scope. The member role must allow S3 and uploads. Start with a disposable object below 50 MB. Plain requests require a valid `Content-Length`; clients may instead use supported AWS chunked framing. Workspace extension policy, per-file limits, credential or role limits, quota, hidden paths, and folder locks all remain active. ## Steps 1. Create a small local test file and record its exact byte size and destination key, including case and every prefix segment. 2. Confirm the bucket is the workspace ID and the key sits inside any folder anchor assigned to the credential. 3. Upload once with the client’s `put`, `cp`, or `PutObject` command while keeping credentials outside command history. 4. Require an HTTP `200` response and save the returned `ETag`; a checksum header is echoed only after Dosya verifies it. 5. Issue `HEAD` or a permitted listing for the same key and compare the reported size and stored ETag with the upload result. 6. Open the destination in Dosya and confirm one file exists; if you intentionally upload the same key again, verify that its version number advances. ## Expected result The object is stored once at the requested key with the expected bytes. New nested prefixes create folders only when allowed, and an overwrite preserves history as a new file version rather than creating a second same-name row. Exact refusals identify the gate: **API key scope 'read' cannot upload files**, **Upload not allowed**, **Creating folders is not allowed**, **Destination folder is locked**, **Object is locked**, **QuotaExceeded**, or **EntityTooLarge**. Correct that gate before retrying. ## Related guides - [Connect an S3 client](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Restrict S3 permissions](/developers/s3-permissions)

title: Verify a large S3 transfer safely
summary: Use multipart upload for a large object, respect part and credential limits, complete or abort the upload, then verify stored size and ETag.
verification: Locally reviewed for “Verify a large S3 transfer safely” against the released implementation on 2026-10-14: `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/create-multipart.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/upload-part.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/complete-multipart.ts`, `packages/prod-smoke/src/rclone-config.ts`. The production surface remains routed by `apps/web/src/router.tsx` and the corresponding API handlers; no unreleased behavior is described.
body: Large S3 objects should use multipart upload. Dosya’s tested rclone configuration switches at `64Mi`; the gateway accepts part numbers 1 through 10,000 and limits each part to 5 GiB. ## Before you start Record source byte size, destination bucket and key, and the client’s multipart settings. Keep enough storage available until completion. Credential and role file-size limits are evaluated when the gateway can see the complete multipart total. Parts up to 50 MB are buffered and retried at the storage write; larger parts stream directly and cannot replay their consumed body inside the same request. The client must retry a failed part number. An unfinished multipart upload should be explicitly aborted so stored parts and its concurrency slot are released. ## Steps 1. Set the client’s multipart threshold below its single-request transport ceiling; for rclone use the released `upload_cutoff = 64Mi` value. 2. Start the upload to the exact workspace bucket and anchored-relative key, then record the returned upload ID without exposing credentials. 3. Monitor successful part responses and their ETags; keep part numbers within 1–10,000 and each declared size at or below 5 GiB. 4. On a failed part, retry that same number; if the transfer is abandoned, send AbortMultipartUpload rather than leaving it incomplete. 5. Complete the upload and require a successful CompleteMultipartUpload response; completion rechecks scope, role, quota, backup lock, and total-size limits. 6. Use `HEAD` to compare the stored `Content-Length` with the source bytes, record the multipart ETag, and download or sample-check content when stronger verification is required. ## Expected result One complete Dosya file appears at the requested key with the source byte count. The multipart ETag is an assembly receipt in the expected multi-part form, not a whole-file MD5 checksum. If completion returns **QuotaExceeded**, **EntityTooLarge**, a lock refusal, or **NoSuchUpload**, do not assume the file landed. Resolve the gate, abort any still-live upload, and begin a clean multipart session. The current multipart completion path enforces credential and role file-size limits and quota; it does not apply the workspace `max_file_size_gb` setting. ## Related guides - [Connect with S3-compatible tools](/integrations/s3-connect) - [Troubleshoot S3 access](/troubleshooting/s3)

title: Clear stale search filters
summary: Clear the real web search constraints: reset the results tab, remove any ext token, clear the query, and distinguish global Search from Files filters.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/search.tsx, apps/web/src/components/layout/global-search.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/listing/file-search-core.ts, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya has two different search surfaces. The header search and `/search` query the active workspace; the **Files** toolbar search can also sit inside a folder, sidebar filter, or group view. The results page has only **All**, **Files**, **Folders**, **Shared**, and **File requests** tabs. File type can be encoded in the query as `ext:pdf`; there are no date or folder filter chips on that page. In Files, the breadcrumb, sidebar selection, group, and search box are separate constraints. ## Steps 1. On the results page, choose **All** so a category tab is not hiding a valid result type. 2. Remove a leading or trailing `ext:_type_` token when you no longer want that extension restriction. 3. Clear the query field completely, then enter the new name without quotation marks or old suffix text. 4. If you are using **Files** instead, clear its **Search files…** box and inspect the breadcrumb, group, and active sidebar row. 5. Choose **All** in the Files sidebar, or use **Show all files** when another content or status view remains active. 6. Run the cleared search in the intended workspace and verify the result counts before opening an item. An `ext:` token is case-insensitive, accepts an optional dot, and must contain 1–16 letters or digits. Only leading and trailing tokens are parsed as filters. Switching a results tab changes what is shown locally; it does not issue a wider workspace query. ## Expected result The next search reflects only the new query and the active workspace. Any remaining folder or type restriction is visible in the Files breadcrumb or sidebar rather than silently carried as an imaginary results-page filter. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Filter search by file type](/files/search-file-type)

title: Search inside the correct folder
summary: Search file names in one Dosya folder, understand the non-recursive scope and 300 ms delay, and recover when expected matches do not appear.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 through apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/files-request.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/listing.ts; production search data was not accessed.
body: The regular **Search files...** field searches file names directly inside the folder in the breadcrumb. There is no separate scope selector, and matching files in descendant folders are not included. ## Steps 1. In web **Files**, use the breadcrumb or open folders until the target folder is current. A folder-confined member's apparent root is the assigned anchor, so searches cannot move above it. 2. Click **Search files...** and enter any part of the filename. Matching is case-insensitive for ASCII text, and % or _ is searched as an ordinary character rather than as a wildcard. 3. Wait 300 milliseconds after the final keystroke. Dosya writes the query to q in the URL and resets the result page to 1. 4. Review only the file rows in that folder. Subfolders stay visible because folder rows are loaded separately, but files inside them do not match until you open that subfolder. 5. Use **Previous** or **Next** if **Page X of Y** appears. The web request asks for 100 rows per page; the API itself accepts page sizes from 10 through 500. 6. To search another folder, navigate there while leaving the query in place. Folder navigation preserves q, reruns it against the new direct children, and resets pagination. ## Expected result The result contains listed, non-deleted file rows whose names contain the query and whose folder ID exactly matches the current location. An item can still appear as a restricted row when its own lock mode is `full_lock`; unlock it before opening file bytes. At workspace root, the same folder rule applies to root-level files. Search does not examine document text, audio tags, comments, or other metadata. The operation is read-only. It respects file-page permission, folder confinement, hidden-file rules, and full-lock visibility, so clearing the query cannot expose content beyond the member's access. ## Troubleshooting - **A match in a child folder is absent.** Open that child folder and let the preserved query run there; current-folder search is deliberately non-recursive. - **Folders still appear beside filtered files.** That is expected because the file query does not filter folder rows. - **No files match your search appears.** Remove punctuation or shorten the filename fragment, then wait for the debounce. - **Could not load this folder appears.** Read the specific error beneath it and press **Try again**. If access changed, return to a folder within your assigned scope. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Organize files](/files/organize-files)

title: Distinguish files with the same name
summary: Distinguish same-named search hits with workspace, folder destination, size, uploader, date, and version details before changing the intended file.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/search.tsx, apps/web/src/components/layout/global-search.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/listing/file-search-core.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya permits the same filename in different folders. Search results do not show a complete path, so identification is a two-stage check: compare result metadata, then open the destination folder or viewer details. The full results page shows file size, uploader, and created time. Selecting a file result navigates to its containing folder. The compact header search shows size and uploader and can return at most five file rows in its menu, so use the full results page when candidates exceed that preview. ## Steps 1. Before the same-name search, confirm the active workspace and enter the full filename, including its extension. 2. On the results page, compare size, uploader, and created time for every same-named file row. 3. Open one candidate to navigate to its containing folder, then read the folder **breadcrumb**. 4. Open the file viewer and inspect its current version, size, stored region, uploader, and timestamps where available. 5. Repeat with the remaining candidate until folder and version facts match the file you intend to use. 6. Use **Rename**, **Move**, **Share**, **Restore**, or **Delete** only after the viewer and breadcrumb identify the correct record. Search matches names by substring, so exact-looking rows can include near matches. A search row has no stable owner or full-path label in every surface, and file identifiers are not normally printed in the list. Treat the destination folder and viewer details as the decisive context. ## Expected result The chosen file is identified by its workspace, containing folder, metadata, and version rather than its duplicated name alone. Other same-named records remain unchanged. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Filter search by file type](/files/search-file-type)

title: Search for an exact file name
summary: Find a file by its full name and extension, understand substring rather than quoted exact matching, then verify metadata and folder before opening it.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/layout/global-search.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/search.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/listing/file-search-core.ts, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya search uses case-insensitive substring matching. Typing the complete filename and extension narrows the pattern, but quotation marks do not switch the service into an exact-match mode. The header search starts file requests after at least two trimmed characters and a 250 ms debounce, then shows up to five file hits and three folders.
