The full results page requests up to 50 rows per result type and separates them with tabs and counts. ## Steps 1. Open search in the workspace that owns the file and type its complete name, including extension. 2. Wait for the 250 ms header search delay or open the full results page for its complete category counts. 3. Choose **Files** and compare every returned name character-for-character; ignore near matches produced by substring search. 4. Use size, uploader, and created time to distinguish rows that share the exact same name. 5. Open the candidate’s folder and then its **Details** tab to verify folder context and current version. 6. If nothing matches, remove only uncertain characters or search a distinctive stem; do not add quotes expecting exact-search syntax. You can add a leading or trailing token such as `ext:pdf` to restrict file extension. `ext:pdf` alone lists that type. Access rules still remove hidden, locked-descendant, or out-of-scope items, so a missing result can reflect permissions rather than spelling. ## Expected result The intended record is identified by full-name comparison plus folder and metadata checks. Near matches and inaccessible files are not mistaken for an exact-name success. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Filter search by file type](/files/search-file-type)

title: Filter search results by file type
summary: Use Photos, Videos or Documents to search supported file extensions across accessible Dosya folders, then load and verify every match on web.
verification: Reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/library-request.ts, apps/web/src/components/library/library-view.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/library/kinds.ts; production library results were not requested.
body: The **Images**, **Videos**, and **Documents** sidebar choices open web library views across every accessible folder in the workspace. They do not narrow only the folder in the breadcrumb, inspect file contents, or infer a type from MIME data. ## Supported extensions - **Images** includes .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .svg, .webp, .bmp, .heic, .heif, .avif, .tif, and .tiff. - **Videos** includes .mp4, .mov, .avi, .mkv, .webm, .m4v, .3gp, .mpg, .mpeg, and .wmv. - **Documents** includes .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt, .pptx, .csv, .txt, .md, .rtf, .odt, .ods, .odp, and .epub. A file whose extension is outside these lists does not enter any of the three libraries. ## Steps 1. In web **Files**, choose **Images**, **Videos**, or **Documents** from the sidebar. Your role must allow file-page access; folder-confined members receive results only from their assigned subtree. 2. Use the matching field: **Search photos...**, **Search videos...**, or **Search documents...**. Search compares the filename as a case-insensitive substring after a 300-millisecond delay; % and _ are treated as literal characters. 3. Choose a date order. Photos offer **Date taken · newest**, **Date taken · oldest**, and **Date uploaded · newest**. Videos and documents use **Date created** for the first two labels. 4. Review the month groups and the total. The first request loads at most 60 items. 5. If more matches exist, select **Load N more**. The control loads no more than 60 additional items, and completion is shown as **That's all N photos.**, **That's all N videos.**, or **That's all N documents.** ## Expected result Every returned row has an extension from the selected kind and lies within the member's accessible scope. Deleted files are excluded. Members without the hide-files permission do not receive hidden files or descendants of hidden folders; members who can manage hidden items may see them. A file's own lock can remain visible as a restricted item. Descendants of a fully locked folder stay outside the library until that member has an unexpired folder-unlock token. The query is filename-only; matching text inside a document does not make that document appear. Choosing **All** leaves the library and returns to the folder that was in the URL. The selected type and query are read-only and never convert, move, or retag files. ## Troubleshooting - **The library reports no matches.** Try a shorter filename substring or clear the field. - **A familiar format is absent.** Compare its final extension with the lists above; unsupported extensions are intentionally outside these libraries. - **Only part of the total is visible.** Continue with **Load N more** until the final count message appears. - **The page says Could not load your photos, Could not load your videos, or Could not load your documents.** Read the displayed error and press **Try again**. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Organize files](/files/organize-files)

title: Searching for files in the correct workspace
summary: Use the Files-page search to match file and folder names in the active workspace and current view, then clear or adjust filters when an item is missing.
verification: Verified the current English Files page and current web/API source on 2026-10-14. The isolated local screenshot uses controlled current-API fixtures and confirms a page-level search for roadmap in the Acme Studio workspace. Source and tests confirmed the debounced name query, active workspace/folder/filter/group scope, first-page reset, case-normalized matching, literal percent and underscore handling, and hidden, lock and role visibility gates. File-content indexing and cross-workspace results were not observed and are not claimed. Added a task-specific interface map derived from the verified controls. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Open **Files** in the workspace that should contain the item, then use the smaller **Search files...** field in the Files toolbar. It matches file and folder names in the current Files view. It does not search file contents or combine every workspace into one result list. The larger field in the application header can search broader app destinations such as settings, integrations and help. Use the Files-toolbar field when you want to narrow the file list shown on the page. ## Before you start - Confirm the workspace name in the upper-left switcher. - Check the current folder breadcrumb and sidebar selection. A folder, type filter or group changes the view that the Files search narrows. - Start with a distinctive part of the filename, not a guessed full path. - Remember that another member can have access to an item you cannot see. Search results follow your role, hidden-item and folder-lock rules. - If the item may have been deleted, search the appropriate **Deleted** view only when your role can access it. ## Steps: search the current Files view 1. Open **Files**. 2. Select the correct workspace. 3. If you want to search the workspace root, choose the home icon and **All**. If you want only one folder, type or group, open that view first. 4. Enter part of the file or folder name in **Search files...**. Dosya waits briefly while you type, then starts from the first page of matching results. 5. Review the remaining rows and compare the name, type, size, date and origin columns when available. 6. Open the result to verify it is the intended item. 7. Clear the search field to restore the current folder or filtered view. ## Steps: widen a search that finds nothing 1. Clear the search field. 2. Choose the home icon to return to the current workspace root. 3. Choose **All** if **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared**, **Hidden**, **Deleted** or a group is selected. 4. Search a shorter, distinctive part of the name. Matching is case-normalized, so capitalization should not be the deciding factor. 5. Check likely folders by browsing into them and repeating the search when the item is not at the root. 6. Switch workspaces only when the item belongs to another workspace, then repeat the search there. 7. If another member can see the item but you cannot, ask a workspace owner to review your role, folder confinement, hidden-item rules and folder lock. ## Expected result The Files list updates to show files and folders whose names match the query inside the active view. Clearing the query restores that view without changing the selected workspace. A result opens the existing item. Search does not create a copy, move the item or change its permissions. ## Search limits and visibility - Search uses the active workspace. It does not return results from another workspace until you switch to it. - A current folder limits the listing to that folder. Return home or browse to another folder when the item lives elsewhere. - Type filters, groups, Deleted and Hidden views keep their own scope while a name query is present. - The query matches stored file and folder names. This guide does not claim full-text search inside PDFs, documents, archives, images or media metadata. - Hidden or inaccessible items remain subject to their visibility rules. Search is not a way around a role, folder confinement or lock. - Literal `%` and `_` characters are treated as filename characters rather than search wildcards. - Search resets the listing to page one when the query changes, preventing an old page number from hiding the first matches. ## Troubleshooting **No files match your search.** Clear the field, choose home and **All**, then search a shorter part of the name. Check whether you were inside a folder, group or type filter. **A file appears in one workspace but not another.** Workspace contents are separate. Switch to the workspace that owns the file; switching context does not move it. **A colleague finds the file but you cannot.** Compare the exact workspace and folder first. Then ask an owner to review access, hidden-item policy, folder lock and any confined-folder role. **The search finds the filename but not words inside the document.** The Files search documented here matches names. Open a supported preview and use its in-file controls, or download and search with an appropriate local application. **The result list looks too narrow.** Clear the active Documents, Videos, Images, Shared, Hidden, Deleted or group view before searching again. **A renamed file no longer matches the old query.** Search the new stored name. Rename changes what the name search indexes and displays. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I search files in another workspace? Yes, after switching to that workspace. The Files page searches one active workspace context at a time. ### Does Files search inside documents? The workflow documented here matches file and folder names. It does not claim full-text indexing of document contents. ### Why is a file missing even though I know its name? The usual causes are the wrong workspace, a different folder, an active filter or group, Deleted/Hidden state, or access restrictions. Widen the view in that order before escalating. ## Related guides - [Organizing files with folders, favourites and groups](/files/organize-files) - [Moving and renaming files or folders](/files/move-and-rename) - [Web app navigation](/account/navigate-web-app) - [Contacting support with useful information](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Combine a folder scope with a file-type filter
summary: Combine a live folder breadcrumb with the Files sidebar type view and local search, while understanding when Images, Videos, and Documents go global.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/files-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/files-params.ts, apps/web/src/lib/files-request.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Folder and type narrowing belongs to the web **Files** page, not the global Search results page. The Files URL carries folder, filter, query, and page as explicit view state. A normal server-side filter stays attached while navigating folders. **Images**, **Videos**, and **Documents** are library views that intentionally span all folders; their header says **all folders**, and the old folder parameter is retained only so leaving the library can return to it. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** and navigate by breadcrumb to the folder you want to search. 2. Choose the sidebar type row and read the main header before assuming the folder still limits it. 3. For **Images**, **Videos**, or **Documents**, accept the explicit **all folders** scope or return to **All** for a true folder listing. 4. Enter the filename stem in **Search files…** and wait for the 300 ms URL update. 5. Review the breadcrumb or the library’s **all folders** label together with the active sidebar row. 6. Open the result only when that visible scope and its file type match the intended task. Entering or leaving **Deleted** clears the live folder because trash folders use a different meaning. Opening a group clears both folder and filter because groups are flat collections. Page numbers reset whenever the query or navigation state changes. ## Expected result The result list reflects the scope visibly named by the Files page. A normal folder listing stays in its breadcrumb, while a library type correctly reports that it searches across all folders. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Filter search by file type](/files/search-file-type)

title: Find a file from a partial name
summary: Search by a stable filename fragment, understand case-insensitive substring matching and two-character header behavior, then verify candidates by metadata.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/layout/global-search.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/search.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/listing/file-search-core.ts, apps/web/src/lib/search/match.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Use the part of the filename least likely to change: a project code, uncommon noun, or date segment. Dosya matches that text anywhere in a name without requiring wildcard characters. Header file search waits until the trimmed query contains at least two characters, then waits 250 ms before requesting results. Matching is case-insensitive SQL substring search. A percent or underscore is escaped as text rather than acting as your wildcard. ## Steps 1. Before a partial-name search, confirm the active workspace and choose a distinctive fragment of at least two characters. 2. Enter the partial filename fragment without temporary conflict suffixes you are unsure about. 3. Choose the **Files** results group or open the full results page when the compact menu is too short. 4. Add a leading or trailing `ext:_type_` token only when the extension is known. 5. Compare name, size, uploader, and created time across the partial file search candidates. 6. Open the containing folder and viewer details before changing or sharing the selected file. A one-character header query does not call the file endpoint, although static navigation suggestions may still appear. The compact menu limits file rows to five and folder rows to three. Use the full results page when those caps hide possible candidates. ## Expected result The partial query produces a small, relevant candidate set, and the intended file is confirmed by its folder and metadata rather than by the filename fragment alone. ## Related guides - [Search files](/files/search-files) - [Filter search by file type](/files/search-file-type)

title: Review security notifications
summary: Interpret mandatory Dosya security alerts, compare device and location evidence, and respond to password, session, 2FA, or recovery-code changes.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/api/src/lib/auth-login.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/failed-attempts.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/catalog.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/security-login.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/notify.ts. Production security events were not triggered.
body: Security notices cover new-device sign-ins, failed-attempt thresholds, password and email changes, two-factor changes, recovery-code regeneration, and session revocation. Most of these entries are mandatory, so email is forced on even when notification preferences are disabled. A single-session revocation is the exception: it uses in-app and push, with no email. ## Steps 1. Open the notification and match its exact title and time to an action you performed. New-device mail includes city, country, IP address, browser, operating system, and an absolute timestamp. 2. Treat geography as context rather than proof. VPNs, mobile carriers, corporate gateways, and IP databases can make a legitimate sign-in appear in another place. 3. For **New sign-in from …**, use **Review sessions**. If you do not recognize it, use **Change password** and then verify the remaining session list. 4. A failed-attempt alert is emitted when a sign-in lockout threshold is crossed. The first password rung is 5 failures for the same account and IP while its one-hour counter record remains live; that rung locks the pair for 15 minutes. The notice reports the measured failure span from audit history, using **15 minutes** only when that lookup cannot supply a start time. Its copy says nobody gained access; enable 2FA if those attempts were not yours. 5. Password-change notices state that every other signed-in session ended. Email-change notices distinguish a requested change from a completed one; the completed alert says the old address no longer signs in. 6. For an unexpected 2FA enable/disable, recovery-code regeneration, or session revocation, contact support after securing the password and current session. A mandatory notice can still appear in-app and by push according to its catalog entry, but those transports are best effort. The security email is the channel the preference gate cannot turn off. ## Expected result A recognized action matches the alert's device, time, and account change. An unrecognized event results in a new password, revoked other credentials, reviewed 2FA state, and a support record where needed. Mandatory security emails have no unsubscribe control and explicitly state why they were sent; a routine single-session revocation remains visible through its enabled non-email channels. ## Related guides - [Changing profile details and account settings](/account/profile-settings) - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions)

title: Select multiple files safely
summary: Select files and folders for a batch action, understand page and lock boundaries, and verify the count before moving, sharing, downloading, or deleting.
verification: Verified against local implementation on 2026-10-14 in apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/hooks/use-files-listing.ts, apps/web/src/lib/files-request.ts, apps/web/src/lib/library-request.ts, apps/web/src/lib/bulk-run.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/index.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/batch-delete.ts. No production bulk action was run.
body: Multi-selection on the browser Files page can include files and folders. The badge counts both types, while each bulk action applies its own permission and combination rules. ## Before you start - Open the web Files page in the correct workspace, folder, filter, or personal group. - Use disposable items when learning Delete. Folder deletion includes everything below each selected folder; a selected Live Photo still can include its paired video. - A full-lock file cannot be selected until you unlock it. **Select all** skips locked files lacking an unlock token but still includes visible folders. ## Steps 1. Hover a list row or grid card and select its checkbox. Ctrl-click on Windows/Linux or Command-click on macOS also toggles that item instead of opening it. 2. Continue until the **N selected** badge matches the highlighted files and folders. 3. To replace the set with every item in the current result, select **Select all**: - A regular folder or group listing selects every visible folder plus the current file page, which contains up to 100 files by default. - Photos, Videos, or Documents selects the library items currently loaded in 60-item fetches, not unseen future results. 4. Remove an unintended item by selecting its checkbox again. Use **Clear** to discard the complete file-and-folder set. 5. Review the available action: - **Download ZIP** requires download permission. - **Share** requires share-link permission and accepts either one folder or one or more files; it is disabled for mixed selections and multiple folders. - **Move** appears when the role can upload files or rename folders. - **Delete** follows the role's own-file or any-file deletion permission and opens a confirmation. 6. Submit only after the badge, item types, and destination or destructive confirmation are correct. ## Expected result Every intended item is highlighted exactly once, and the badge equals the number of selected file plus folder IDs. No cloud data changes until a bulk action is submitted. Selection is per view. Navigating to a different page, folder, workspace, filter, group, search, or library ordering clears it, preventing hidden IDs from carrying into the new result. ## Troubleshooting **A locked file did not select.** Open and unlock it first, then return to selection. The toggle deliberately ignores an unopened full-lock file. **Select all did not include everything in the workspace.** It covers the current listing page or currently loaded library rows. Visit the next page or load more results and process a separate, verified batch. **A Delete toast claims more items than appear in Deleted.** Web treats an HTTP-successful 20-ID chunk as if every submitted ID was deleted and does not use the endpoint's actual `deleted` and `folders_deleted` counts. The API can silently omit hidden, missing, already-deleted, or own-only file rows. It can also skip a selected folder for ownership, a direct or ancestor lock, subtree authorization, hidden state, or an internal folder-trash error. Refresh both the source and **Deleted**, then reconcile the surviving IDs before retrying. **A mixed-owner selection completed only partly.** With `delete_own_files`, files uploaded by somebody else are omitted and a folder is skipped when any required descendant needs `delete_any_file`. A selected visible file with its own lock or a locked ancestor instead rejects its complete HTTP chunk. Split remaining rows by owner or lock state and submit only the corrected selection. **Another batch action reports failures.** Move and restore count their per-item successes and failures. Refresh the folder, compare the toast with the actual rows, and retry only objects that remain at the source. ## Related guides - [Organize files](/files/organize-files) - [Move and rename files](/files/move-and-rename)

title: Clear a selection after a batch action
summary: Clear web file and folder selections explicitly, know which completed batch actions clear them automatically, and prevent old IDs crossing view changes.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/select-checkbox.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/bulk-run.ts. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Selected files and folders are held separately on the web Files page, while the batch bar shows their combined count. Use **Clear** whenever you want to leave selection mode without starting another action. Move, soft delete, permanent delete, restore, and other successful batch flows clear selection after they settle. The page also clears selection when the folder or view, library type, search query, or active workspace changes. A dialog cancel can leave the original rows selected so you can revise the choice. ## Steps 1. Read the `_N_ selected` count and inspect every highlighted file and folder before acting. 2. Complete or cancel the confirmation dialog while selection mode remains visible; do not assume Cancel changed the selected IDs. 3. Press **Clear** at the right side of the batch bar to empty both file and folder selections. 4. Confirm the batch bar collapses and every row checkbox or card highlight returns to its unselected state. 5. Navigate or search only after clearing when you want an unmistakably fresh selection context. 6. Select one harmless row and verify the new count starts at 1 before beginning the next batch operation. A running batch operation can be non-cancelable even though its selection later clears; clearing the UI does not undo requests already sent. Deletion requires confirmation and may already have changed items by the time the final status appears. Use **Restore** from Deleted for reversible soft deletion; permanent deletion remains irreversible. ## Expected result No previous file or folder remains highlighted, the batch toolbar is collapsed, and the next selected row starts a new count independent of the completed or cancelled action. ## Related guides - [Select multiple files](/files/select-multiple-files) - [Clear a file selection](/files/clear-file-selection)

title: Select a contiguous group of files
summary: Select a contiguous visual run without a Shift-range shortcut by using row checkboxes or Select all plus deselection, then verify every included item.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/select-checkbox.tsx, apps/web/src/components/library/library-view.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya’s web Files list does not implement Shift-click range selection. A contiguous group must be built with the row checkboxes, or by using **Select all** and removing every row outside the intended run. Checkboxes appear on hover and remain visible once selection exists. Ctrl-click on Windows/Linux or Command-click on macOS toggles one row, but Shift-click has no range meaning. Full-lock files are excluded until unlocked. ## Steps 1. Sort files into a visible adjacent run, then note the first and last names. 2. Build the contiguous selection from the first row's checkbox through each following row at the last boundary. 3. For a mostly selected page, use **Select all** and deselect every file or folder outside the run instead. 4. Compare the `_N_ selected` count with the number of intended rows, including any selected folders. 5. Inspect both selection boundary rows and scan for a highlighted item beyond either boundary. 6. Choose the batch action only after the count and every highlight agree; use **Clear** to restart when they do not. **Select all** covers the items currently loaded in the view and excludes locked files that have not been unlocked. It can include folders as well as files. Batch sharing accepts either one folder or a set of files, not a mixed selection, even when the items look contiguous. ## Expected result Every intended row from the first boundary through the last is selected exactly once, no outside row is highlighted, and the batch count matches the reviewed set without relying on an unsupported Shift gesture. ## Related guides - [Select multiple files](/files/select-multiple-files) - [Clear a file selection](/files/clear-file-selection)

title: Select nonadjacent files
summary: Select separated web files with checkboxes or Command/Ctrl-click, understand locked-row and mixed-type limits, and verify the exact batch count.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/select-checkbox.tsx, apps/web/src/components/library/library-view.tsx. Production behavior was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Nonadjacent selection is additive on the web Files page. Use each row’s checkbox, or Command-click on macOS and Ctrl-click on Windows or Linux, to toggle separated items without opening them. In a normal folder list, clicking an ordinary row without the modifier opens its details instead of adding it. In an Images, Videos, or Documents library, an ordinary row click toggles the row after selection mode has started. A full-lock file cannot enter the set until it is unlocked. ## Steps 1. Begin the nonadjacent selection with the first file’s checkbox or the platform’s Command/Ctrl-click modifier. 2. Extend the nonadjacent selection by toggling each separated file while leaving intervening rows unselected. 3. Read the combined `_N_ selected` count and inspect every highlighted filename. 4. Correct the nonadjacent selection by clicking a selected checkbox or repeating Command/Ctrl-click on an accidental choice. 5. Confirm the offered action supports the selection: Share allows a set of files, but not files mixed with folders. 6. Run the action only after review, or press **Clear** to discard the entire set without changing any files. The selection belongs to the current view and clears when the folder, library view, search query, or workspace changes. Command/Ctrl+A invokes **Select all** for the loaded view; it is not an additive shortcut for one extra row. Deletion still requires its own confirmation. ## Expected result Only the individually chosen files are highlighted, the batch count matches them, and intervening rows stay untouched. Clearing the set changes no cloud content. ## Related guides - [Select multiple files](/files/select-multiple-files) - [Clear a file selection](/files/clear-file-selection)

title: Preflight a batch move
summary: Check a page-scoped selection, destination, permissions, locks, and name collisions before moving files or folders, then verify every outcome.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/folder-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/move.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/move.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A batch move acts on the rows selected in the current Files view. Preflight the exact page and destination because changing page, folder, filter, search, library kind, or workspace clears the selection. **Permissions and blockers.** Moving a file requires `upload_files`; moving a folder requires `rename_folders`. A confined member cannot move content outside the assigned subtree. Full file locks, locked ancestor folders, hidden destinations, locked targets, and locked WordPress backups can refuse the operation. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, open the source folder and page that contains the items. Remove any search or filter that hides a row you intend to move. 2. Select each file or folder with its checkbox, Ctrl-click, or Command-click. Read the **N selected** badge; **Select all** covers only the rows loaded on this page and skips a fully locked file unless it has been unlocked. 3. Check the destination before starting. A file or folder with the same name causes a `409` refusal, and moving an item to its current folder is rejected as already there. 4. Choose **Move**, then use **Search folders…**, the folder tree, or **Root (top level)**. Folder search waits 250 ms before requesting matches. The picker never changes workspaces. 5. Select the intended destination and choose **Move**. Dosya moves selected items concurrently; a Live Photo still also carries its paired video even when that video row was not selected. 6. Read the final toast. **Moved** reports the successful selected-item count. **Move finished** reports how many moved and how many were skipped; reopen both source and destination before retrying a skipped row. **Resolve a refusal before retrying.** The APIs can return `This file is locked and cannot be moved`, `Target folder is locked`, `A file with this name already exists in the target folder`, `Folder is already here`, or `Cannot move a folder into its own subfolder`. Rename or relocate the collision, unlock the relevant source or destination, or choose a location inside your permitted subtree. ## Expected result Every successful item appears once in the chosen folder and leaves the source. Any skipped item remains in place, so you can correct its specific lock, permission, cycle, or name-collision cause without moving the successful rows again. ## Related guides - [Select multiple files for one action](/files/select-multiple-files) - [Clear a selection without changing files](/files/clear-file-selection)

title: Verify a multi-file selection count
summary: Confirm the Files selection badge against visible highlighted rows, page boundaries, locked items, and Live Photo companions before a batch action.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/live-photos.ts, and apps/web/src/lib/files-request.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The **N selected** badge counts selected file rows plus selected folder rows in the current view. It does not mean every match across all result pages has been selected. **Selection scope.** Standard folder and search listings are paginated. Moving to **Previous** or **Next**, changing the folder, search, filter, workspace, or view identity clears the selection. In a Library view, **Select all** covers only the items already loaded, not items still available through **Load more**. ## Steps 1. Open the exact folder, filter, or library section where the batch action will run. Note **Page X of Y** when pagination is present. 2. Select rows using their checkboxes or Ctrl/Command-click. A normal click opens or navigates instead of extending the set. 3. Compare every highlighted row with the **N selected** badge. The total combines files and folders; it does not count the contents inside a selected folder. 4. If you use **Select all**, inspect the current page before proceeding. Fully locked files are omitted unless already unlocked, while folders on the page are included. 5. For a Live Photo, the badge counts the selected row. Delete or move may also include its paired video and disclose that companion separately in the confirmation copy. 6. Choose **Clear** and rebuild the set if the badge or highlights do not match your intended targets. Do this before **Move**, **Delete**, **Restore**, or **Delete permanently**. **Keyboard behavior.** Ctrl+A or Command+A selects the files and folders loaded in this view when focus is outside an input or editor. The text editor stops its keystrokes from reaching this page-wide shortcut, so selecting text there does not select file rows. ## Expected result The badge equals the number of intended selected rows on the active page. You understand any paired-media side effect before confirmation and can name each row the next batch command will address. ## Related guides - [Build a multi-file selection](/files/select-multiple-files) - [Remove all selected-row state](/files/clear-file-selection)

title: Compare session last-active times
summary: Compare browser creation time with mobile last-use time so Dosya session ages help identify devices without overstating live activity safely.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/sessions.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: The age shown on **Active sessions** is not one uniform last-activity measurement. A browser row uses its session creation time. A mobile row uses its recorded last-used time when available, otherwise its creation time. The current credential is always labeled **active now**. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Sessions** and find the **Current** badge before comparing ages. 2. Browser rows show browser, stored location, stored IP, then an age. Mobile rows show **dosya.dev app** and an age, without browser-location fields. 3. Treat **active now** only as confirmation that Dosya matched the credential used for this request. 4. Interpret browser ages as “session created this long ago.” They do not update on each click, so an old-looking browser can still be in use. 5. Interpret a non-current mobile age as the last recorded token use, falling back to sign-in time if no use was stored. 6. Compare the age with your sign-in history and device type. Web sessions expire after 30 days; mobile access tokens last 1 hour and can refresh within a 60-day window unless revoked. The display rounds down to minutes, hours, or days, then switches to a calendar date after seven days. Refresh before using a boundary value in a security decision. ## Expected result You can explain why each age appears and avoid treating a browser creation timestamp as continuous activity. A row that remains unfamiliar should be handled as an unknown credential by changing the password and revoking other sessions. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Revoke other sessions](/account/revoke-other-sessions)

title: Identify the current Dosya session
summary: Find the Current badge in Dosya, understand cookie and mobile-token matching, and avoid trying to revoke the credential you are using on this device.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/sessions.tsx and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: Dosya marks the credential that loaded **Active sessions** with a green **Current** badge. The server checks the browser session cookie and mobile bearer token separately, so the current row can be a browser or the Dosya app. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Sessions** from the device you want to keep signed in. 2. Locate **Current** beside a device label. Its metadata ends with **active now**. 3. For a browser, compare browser name and platform-derived label: **Mac**, **Windows PC**, **Linux**, **iPhone**, **iPad**, **Android Phone**, or **Android Tablet**. Unrecognized agents show **Unknown device**. 4. A native phone credential can appear as **Mobile app** and **dosya.dev app** when its user agent cannot name the phone model. 5. If no row is current after loading, do not assume the newest one is yours. Reload and sign in again; bulk revocation can return **No active session** when neither credential is valid. 6. Use normal sign-out to end the current credential. Direct revocation refuses it with **Cannot revoke your current session. Use logout instead.** A linked iOS Files or macOS File Provider credential belongs to its parent device. Bulk revocation preserves linked credentials minted by the caller while removing children of other devices. ## Expected result The credential making the request is identified as **Current** and reads **active now**. You can choose the device to preserve before using **Revoke all other sessions**, rather than guessing from recency. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Revoke other sessions](/account/revoke-other-sessions)

title: Review session location and IP context
summary: Interpret Dosya session location and IP fields with VPN, carrier, and geolocation caveats before deciding that a sign-in is unknown before acting.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/geo.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/request-context.ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: Browser session rows can include a stored location and IP address captured at sign-in. Mobile app rows in the current list do not expose those fields. Location is an IP-derived clue, not device GPS. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Sessions** and identify your **Current** row. 2. On browser rows, read metadata after the browser name. Dosya joins available values in this order: stored location, IP address, and session age. 3. A missing location or IP is omitted. Do not interpret a shorter row as evidence that the session is safe. 4. Compare the address with your home, office, VPN exit, mobile carrier gateway, or corporate proxy. Shared networks can make different devices use one public IP. 5. Compare location with device label and time. A correct city alone cannot authenticate a session, and a distant city can be a database error. 6. If the combined evidence is unfamiliar, change the password and select **Revoke all other sessions**. Save the security notification's absolute time, browser, OS, and IP for support. The list may show a raw IP beside a broad location string. Neither value reveals the device's precise physical position, and the browser row does not track travel after sign-in. ## Expected result You classify each browser location as consistent, explainable, or suspicious using several fields. Mobile rows are assessed with their app label and age. Suspicious credentials are removed without relying on geography alone. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Report suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Secure Dosya after losing a signed-in device
summary: Secure Dosya from a trusted device after a phone or computer is lost by changing the password, revoking credentials, and checking 2FA right away.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/api/src/pages/api/me/password.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/[id].ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: Use a device you still control. A password change keeps the credential making that change and revokes every other browser and mobile credential immediately, including linked file-provider children. ## Steps 1. Sign in on a trusted browser. If the lost device held your authenticator, use one unused recovery code. 2. Open **Profile → Password & 2FA → Change password**. Enter the current password and a new password of at least 8 characters; it must differ from the current one. 3. Confirm **Password changed — Your password has been updated.** Dosya deletes other web sessions, revokes other mobile token families, and clears their caches. 4. Open **Profile → Sessions**. If more than one credential remains, select **Revoke all other sessions** and wait for **Sessions revoked — You are now signed out everywhere else.** 5. For a lost authenticator phone, re-enroll on the replacement and regenerate recovery codes after confirming access. 6. Check security notifications for password, session, sign-in, or email changes. Contact support if an identity change was not yours. 7. Use the device vendor's remote-lock and erase tools for local files; Dosya cannot wipe the hardware. Revocation cannot retract files already downloaded to the lost device. It blocks future authenticated requests once the deleted cookie or revoked token is presented. ## Expected result The trusted caller stays signed in, every other Dosya credential is ended, and the lost device fails on its next authenticated request. Replacement 2FA works and old recovery codes no longer grant access after regeneration. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Revoke other sessions](/account/revoke-other-sessions)

title: Recognize devices in your Dosya session list
summary: Decode Dosya session device and browser labels, compare app rows with web rows, and decide which credentials belong to you before revocation.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts and apps/api/src/lib/share/user-agent.ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: Dosya derives browser device labels from the stored user-agent string. These labels describe software claims, not a verified hardware identity, and privacy tools can reduce their accuracy. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Sessions** and first mark the row carrying **Current**. 2. Browser parsing recognizes Firefox, Edge, Chrome, and Safari. If none matches, the browser field becomes **Unknown**. 3. Device classification recognizes iPhone, iPad, Android phone/tablet, Mac, Windows PC, and Linux. Everything else is listed as **Unknown device**. 4. A native-token row is normalized to **Mobile app** with **dosya.dev app**, even when its user agent cannot name the phone model. 5. Compare the label with location/IP context and time. Two browsers on one computer can be separate credentials, and signing in again can create another row. 6. Do not use order alone as identity. The list is sorted by creation time, while mobile metadata can use later token activity. 7. If a row is unknown, secure the account rather than waiting for its 30-day web expiry or 60-day mobile refresh window. Dosya does not display serial numbers, operating-system device names, or precise hardware models in this web list. ## Expected result Every familiar row has an explainable credential type, device class, browser/app label, and time context. Any unexplained entry is treated as a security incident and removed through password change or bulk revocation. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Report suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Revoke every other active session
summary: Keep the Current Dosya credential while revoking every other browser, mobile, and linked device session, then verify the final list and access.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/sessions.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/catalog.ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: **Revoke all other sessions** removes every active browser session and mobile token family except the credential making the request. The button appears only when the loaded list contains more than one row. ## Steps 1. From the device you intend to keep, open **Profile → Sessions** and confirm its green **Current** badge. 2. Review how many other rows are present. If only the caller remains, the bulk-revoke button is hidden. 3. Select **Revoke all other sessions**. The interface disables the control while the request runs. 4. On success, read **Sessions revoked — You are now signed out everywhere else.** The page reloads its list. 5. If it shows **Revoke failed**, retain the server message; the fallback is **The other sessions could not be revoked.** A caller without a live cookie or bearer receives **No active session**. 6. Confirm that only the intended current device and its linked extensions remain usable. Other session cookies are deleted, mobile tokens are revoked, and both cache types are invalidated immediately. This action does not delete cloud files, workspace content, or copies already downloaded. It is irreversible for those credentials: each removed device must sign in again. ## Expected result The current browser or mobile app continues working while all other devices lose authenticated access. Dosya emits a mandatory **All sessions were signed out** security notice whose count includes browser sessions and mobile tokens. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Revoke other sessions](/account/revoke-other-sessions)

title: Revoke one unfamiliar Dosya session
summary: Sign out one unfamiliar device from the Dosya mobile Sessions screen while keeping your current device and every unrelated session signed in.
verification: Reviewed and validated locally from apps/mobile/app/sessions.tsx, apps/mobile/src/profile/api.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/[id].ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/me-sessions.int.test.ts. Inspection made no production account or service request.
body: Use single-device revocation when one entry is unfamiliar and the rest of your signed-in devices are trusted. The current Dosya mobile app exposes this action on each non-current row. The web **Active sessions** page currently offers only **Revoke all other sessions**, so use the mobile Sessions screen for a targeted revocation. The list includes browser sessions and mobile app tokens. The mobile app labels its own row **This device** and hides the sign-out control on that row. This prevents a session revocation from being used as a disguised logout. ## Steps 1. In the Dosya mobile app, open **Profile → Sessions**. 2. Locate **This device** first. Keep that row as your trusted reference. 3. Compare every other row's device name and metadata. Browser metadata can include browser, stored location or IP, and last activity; app entries identify the **dosya.dev app**. 4. On the one row you do not recognize, select the sign-out icon. Its accessibility label is **Sign out [device]**. 5. Wait for the confirmation toast **Device signed out**. 6. Refresh the list. The selected row should be gone, while **This device** and unrelated trusted rows remain. ## What happens to the selected device Revoking a browser session deletes that session and clears its authentication cache. Revoking a phone token revokes that token family, including linked sessions it created, such as its Files extension access. The selected device must sign in again before it can reach protected files or account data. The server refuses the current browser or mobile credential with **Cannot revoke your current session. Use logout instead.** A missing or already-ended row returns **Session not found**. Session IDs are scoped to the current account, so another account's session is also reported as not found. Revocation does not erase local downloads already stored on that device. If the row represents a lost or stolen device, also change the account password and review public links, API keys, and connected applications. ## Troubleshooting If the app says **Couldn't load sessions.**, choose **Retry**. If a targeted sign-out is unavailable in the web app, do not assume the row is protected; use the mobile screen or choose the broader web action to end all other sessions. If the row reappears after a successful revocation, the person or device signed in again. Treat a repeated unfamiliar login as suspicious activity and secure the identity method immediately. ## Expected result The chosen device disappears from Sessions and must authenticate again, while the current device and every other session you did not select remain active. ## Related guides - [Review sessions](/account/sessions) - [Respond to suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Secure your account after an unknown session
summary: Respond to an unknown Dosya session by preserving evidence, changing the password, revoking other credentials, and reviewing identity security.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/api/src/pages/api/me/password.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/notifications/catalog.ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: An unknown session means someone may hold a live cookie or mobile refresh token. Work from a trusted device and preserve the notification or session details before removing access. ## Steps 1. Capture the unfamiliar row's device label, browser/app label, location or IP when present, and displayed age. Keep any **New sign-in from …** email because it includes an absolute time and fuller context. 2. Check whether a VPN, travel, another browser profile, or a recently reinstalled app explains it. Do not dismiss the event solely because the city is familiar. 3. Open **Profile → Password & 2FA → Change password** and choose a new password of at least 8 characters that differs from the current one. 4. The update preserves your current credential and revokes all other web and mobile credentials. Verify the **Password changed** toast. 5. Visit **Profile → Sessions** and use **Revoke all other sessions** if an unexpected row remains. 6. Review **Profile → Identity** for email-change notices and **Password & 2FA** for an unknown method change or recovery-code regeneration. 7. Contact support if the account email changed, you cannot verify your current device, or suspicious activity continues. Changing the password cannot erase data an intruder already downloaded. It also does not reverse file edits or shares; review workspace activity separately when the credential had time to act. ## Expected result Only the trusted credential remains active, password and 2FA settings match your choices, and mandatory security mail records the remediation. Escalate any data-control issue with the saved device, IP, and timestamp evidence. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Report suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Verify that a revoked session is closed
summary: Confirm a revoked Dosya browser or mobile credential disappears, fails its next authenticated request, and requires a fresh sign-in on every device.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/[id].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/sessions/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/mobile-auth.ts. Production session behavior was not exercised.
body: A successful revocation removes a browser session row or marks a mobile token family revoked, then invalidates the matching authentication cache. The target cannot be the credential currently making the request. ## Steps 1. On the trusted device, reload **Profile → Sessions** after revocation and check that the target row no longer appears. 2. If you used **Revoke all other sessions**, confirm the list retains **Current**. It may also preserve extensions linked to the caller because they represent the same device. 3. On the revoked device, refresh a private route or attempt another authenticated action. An already rendered screen can remain visible until it contacts the server; visibility alone is not proof of access. 4. Expect a sign-in requirement or authentication failure on that next request. A revoked phone loses its token family, including linked Files-extension credentials. 5. Review the **A session was signed out** in-app notice or push. It names the target using its stored browser/OS, age, and location or IP fallback; this routine event is not emailed. 6. If a row returns after a new login, compare its new time. Signing in legitimately creates a new credential. Revocation stops future server access but cannot recall content already cached or downloaded on that machine. Use device-level remote erase when local possession is the concern. ## Expected result The revoked entry is absent on a fresh list, its old credential cannot complete an authenticated request, and a new login is required. A single-device notice describes the credential ended rather than the trusted device that initiated revocation; bulk revocation instead reports the combined device count. ## Related guides - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Revoke other sessions](/account/revoke-other-sessions)

title: Reviewing active sessions
summary: Find signed-in devices in Profile, identify your current session, and revoke other sessions when you no longer need them.
verification: Verified with the isolated local current web app and API on 2026-10-10: another real login was revoked and returned 401 while the current session remained authenticated. Real before-and-after screenshots reviewed. Other session types were checked against source; production was not verified. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Open **Profile → Sessions** to review the devices signed in to your account. The **Current** badge marks the session you are using. Select **Revoke all other sessions** to sign out other sessions while keeping this one available. ## Before you start - Sign in on a device you intend to keep using. The revoke action preserves the caller's session. - Tell anyone using your account on another device that they may need to sign in again. Affected desktop or mobile clients may need a new sign-in before they can continue authenticated work. - Finish any work you need from another signed-in device before revoking it. - If your concern is a connected script or integration, also review **Profile → API keys**. API keys are managed separately from signed-in sessions. ## Steps: review your devices 1. **Open Profile.** Select the avatar's **Account menu** in the top bar, then select **Profile**. 2. **Find Sessions.** Select **Sessions** in the profile navigation, or open [the Sessions page](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/sessions). Look for the **Active sessions** heading. 3. **Identify this session.** Find the row with the **Current** badge. Use it as your reference before ending any other sessions. 4. **Review the other rows.** Check the device labels and the details beneath them. Browser-session details can include the browser, location, IP address and a relative time when that information is available. Mobile-app rows identify the Dosya app. 5. **Decide whether to keep the other sessions.** Separate browser sign-ins can create separate rows even when they belong to the same physical device. Treat unfamiliar labels as a reason to investigate, rather than proof of a particular person's identity. ## Steps: sign out other sessions 1. **Stay on the device you want to keep.** Confirm that you can see **Current** beside its row. 2. **Select Revoke all other sessions.** The button appears beneath the list when more than one session is listed. In the current web interface, selecting it starts revocation directly; there is no additional confirmation dialog. 3. **Wait for the result.** A successful request displays **Sessions revoked** and **You are now signed out everywhere else.** The list reloads. 4. **Check the remaining access.** Your current session remains available. Other revoked devices need to authenticate again to make authenticated requests. A linked system extension belonging to the current device can also be preserved. To sign out the current browser instead, open **Account menu** and select **Log out**. ## Expected result You have reviewed the active-session list and, if requested, ended the other sign-ins. Revocation affects other browser sessions and mobile-app credentials handled by this account action. It does not delete your account or your stored files. ## Limitations - The current web page provides **Revoke all other sessions**. It does not provide an individual **Revoke** control beside each device. - Device labels are inferred from client information. A row may say **Unknown device** or **Mobile app** when the available information does not identify it more precisely. - The list is not a complete historical login or activity log. For browser rows, the relative time for a non-current session is based on when that session was created; do not read it as proof of the device's most recent action. - The action preserves the current session and may preserve its linked extensions. It should not be interpreted as a requirement that exactly one row will remain. - Revoking a session does not erase files already downloaded onto that device. API keys and share links have their own access controls. ## Troubleshooting If the revoke button is missing, check whether only one session is listed. That is expected: there are no other listed sessions for the button to revoke. If you see **Revoke failed**, read the accompanying message and check your connection. If the current sign-in has expired, sign in again, return to **Sessions**, and review the list before retrying. If the page unexpectedly shows **No sessions**, reload it after checking connectivity. Do not assume that an empty display alone proves every other device has been signed out: confirm the result after the page has loaded successfully. Use [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) if a device remains unexplained or revocation repeatedly fails. Share the device label and error message privately. Redact IP addresses or other personal details from screenshots you post publicly. ## Frequently asked questions ### Will Revoke all other sessions sign me out here? The action is designed to keep the caller's session. Use **Log out** in **Account menu** if you want to end your current browser sign-in. ### Why do I see several rows for the same kind of device? Rows represent sessions or app credentials, rather than a unique inventory of physical hardware. Multiple sign-ins on a Mac, for example, can produce multiple **Mac** rows. ### Does this also stop a tool using an API key? API keys have a separate management page. Go to **Profile → API keys**, find the relevant key, and use its **Revoke** action if that credential should stop working. See [API key management](/developers/api-key). ## Related guides - [Turning on two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [API key management](/developers/api-key) - [Watch the existing sessions tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/review-your-sessions/)

title: Connect an SFTP client
summary: Configure SFTP host, port and password authentication, verify the SSH host key, and test workspace transfers within the gateway’s limits.
verification: Reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/sftp.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; src/pages/developer/sftp.astro; apps/ftp-server/src/sftp.ts; apps/ftp-server/src/api.ts; apps/ftp-server/src/vfs.ts; apps/ftp-server/src/config.ts; apps/ftp-server/src/access.ts; apps/ftp-server/src/memory-limit.ts; apps/ftp-server/src/streaming-writer.ts; apps/ftp-server/dosya-sftp.service; apps/api/src/middleware.ts; apps/api/src/middleware.sftp-metering.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/plan-limits.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/open.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/finalize-session.ts; apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts; apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/purge-trash.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/trim-versions.ts. Source-derived connection and process map, no production fingerprint or live-client certification. OPEN/CLOSE inspected: write handles start empty, zero-byte CLOSE skips upload, and the current gateway does not support durable upload resume. Official reference: https://man.openbsd.org/sftp.1; https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5.
body: Connect to **sftp.dosya.dev**, port **2222**, with **SFTP over SSH**. The username is your Dosya account email, and the password is a full API key. This service provides file operations only: it is not FTP, FTPS, or an interactive SSH shell. ## Create credentials this client can use In the web app, select the workspace and open **Integrations → SFTP**. If **Your role can’t use SFTP** appears, ask the workspace owner/admin for access before making a client profile. SFTP access and upload/download/delete permissions are separate role decisions. Open **Profile → API keys → New API key**. Name the key for this computer under **What is it for?**, and choose **Read only** for listing/downloads or **Full access** for upload and management. Select **Restrictions and expiry → Where can it reach? → Protocols → Only the ones I pick**, check **SFTP**, and choose the appropriate **Workspace** pin. Generate it and save the one-time secret privately. Do not select **Choose folder…** for an SFTP credential: folder-anchored keys are rejected at this protocol. Workspace-pinned keys are supported. A key with **Upload only** cannot perform the listing requests needed for this connection walkthrough. Also avoid allowed-IP restrictions: the gateway connects to the API on your behalf, so the API cannot verify your original address and refuses an IP-restricted key. Expiry, active-hour and applicable usage restrictions continue to matter. ## Configure the connection | Client setting | Dosya value | | --- | --- | | Protocol | SFTP / SSH File Transfer Protocol | | Host | `sftp.dosya.dev` | | Port | `2222` | | Username | Your key-owner account email, with the same letter case | | Authentication | Password | | Password | Complete `dos_…` API key | | Initial directory | `/` for the workspace list | The server supports password authentication, not login with an SSH public key. Your email is not a workspace name, and no account-password login is provided here. Save the key only in your client's private credential store. For OpenSSH, keep the email separate from the hostname with the SSH user option: ```sh sftp -P 2222 -o User=you@example.com -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o PubkeyAuthentication=no sftp.dosya.dev ``` Replace the sample email with yours. Enter the API key only at the password prompt; terminal commands, saved scripts and shell history should contain no secret. `-P` selects the SFTP port; lowercase `-p` has a different meaning. The client must be installed on your computer. ## Check the host before authenticating A first connection can show an SSH host-key fingerprint and ask whether to trust it. The host key identifies the server, while the API key identifies your account. Compare the displayed hostname, port, key type and fingerprint against a trusted value obtained from Dosya support or your administrator through a separate channel before accepting. This guide has no certified production fingerprint, and fetching a key with `ssh-keyscan` alone does not prove identity. If **REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!** appears, stop and confirm a legitimate change before altering known-host entries. Do not set `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` as a routine fix. A saved trust record is independent of the client password; rotating your API key will not resolve a host-key mismatch. ## Steps: navigate and verify a transfer 1. Connect, then use `pwd` and `ls`. At `/`, SFTP lists the workspaces available to this key and role. It does not expose WebDAV's All/smart-view collections. 2. Use `cd "My Workspace"`, replacing that example with a listed name. A workspace slug also resolves. Use `ls` again to see that workspace's actual folders and files. 3. Change into an existing destination folder, or create a disposable one with `mkdir "sftp-check"` when permitted. Workspaces cannot be created from the SFTP root. 4. Upload a uniquely named, non-empty local sample with `put sample.txt sftp-check-20261014.txt`. Wait for completion and any final close response. The gateway commits the upload at file close, so a progress bar reaching 100% can precede cloud completion. 5. Confirm that name and size in Dosya **Files**, at the same workspace/folder. Download with `get sftp-check-20261014.txt ./sftp-check-downloaded.txt`; compare its bytes or SHA-256 against the original. 6. Reconnect and list again to confirm the saved location. Changes from another client may briefly lag; directory caching defaults to 10 seconds, while misses are checked afresh. Read-only users can validate a known remote sample with `get` instead. Ordinary downloads can issue offset reads; large reads at 64 MiB or above use bounded range fetching, so first-byte timing and throughput can differ. No server-side hash command or shell session is available for comparison: calculate hashes on your local source and downloaded copy. ## Expected result The workspace path lists the intended files and a completed sample download matches the original. An uploaded sample becomes an ordinary file in Dosya Files only after a successful cloud commit; it is not a public share link. ## Supported operations and boundaries The gateway handles listing/stat, `get`, `put`, `mkdir`, rename/move, `rm` and `rmdir`. `chmod`/`chown` attribute requests are acknowledged without changing Dosya workspace permissions. Symbolic links and SSH shell/exec are unsupported. A client probing for a shell must continue using SFTP-only mode. The shipped server configuration sets an upload ceiling of **352 MiB (369,098,752 bytes)**. A deployment can configure a smaller cap; its error reports the active MB value. This ceiling is independent of your plan's total cloud storage. Workspace size/extension policy, remaining storage and explicit credential/role usage limits can refuse a smaller file. Free and paid accounts may use SFTP; plan request/concurrency ceilings are excluded for this protocol, but daily egress and explicit limits still apply. Start with one transfer and lower client concurrency if the service reports throttling. Uploads are buffered in the SFTP session until CLOSE; empty uploads currently create no file. An interrupted upload is not a durable resumable transfer. **Do not use upload Resume, Append, `reput` or `put -a`**: the current server does not reload the old prefix when opening a write. Restart the full upload from offset zero, preferably to a new filename. Uploading a complete file to an existing name passes the existing file ID to Dosya's versioned upload path. It can replace current bytes and add a version; version history defaults to 10 unless configured differently and is subject to retention/pruning. Preserve independent originals before replacement. `rm` and folder deletion affect cloud content, moving eligible items to Trash and revoking share links. Trash retention is seven days for free owners or 30 for other plans; permanent purge is irreversible. Restoring content does not reactivate an old revoked share URL. ## Diagnose refusals | Message or status | Action | | --- | --- | | Password authentication fails | Check exact email case/full API key, SFTP protocol selection, workspace pin, expiry and folder/IP restrictions. Repeated credential guesses can cause a temporary IP ban. | | **Your role can’t use SFTP** | Request workspace access; changing clients does not bypass the role gate. | | **access to that workspace is not permitted for this credential** (SFTP status 3) | Verify membership and the role's SFTP permission. | | **no such file or directory** (status 2) | Check the listed workspace name and path; resources you cannot see can appear absent. | | **the parent directory does not exist or is not writable by this credential** | Enter an existing workspace/folder and confirm create/upload permissions. | | **write past the 352 MB per-file limit** (or another active value) | Use the web uploader or another suitable protocol for a file beyond the gateway's ceiling; do not split offsets as a workaround. | | **close failed: API 403 …** or **close failed: API 429 (rate limited - back off and retry) …** | Inspect the permission/policy detail or back off. A successful WRITE did not prove CLOSE could commit. | | **access to this workspace was revoked while the upload was in flight** | The final commit was refused; contact the owner rather than resuming the partial write. | SFTP translates API 403 to permission denied, 404 to no-such-file and other failures to status 4; a client may show only these generic names. Server details are bounded to 180 characters and redact key-shaped secrets. Capture the displayed operation, error and time without exposing credentials. ## Disconnect and revoke Use `bye` or disconnect the client. Remove saved credentials separately and revoke the dedicated key in **Profile → API keys** when its access should end. A successful login cache and role-permission cache can each lag up to 60 seconds; an already-open connection is not proof a revoked key can still commit operations. Reconnect after a role change and verify the required action. Revoking credentials does not delete existing workspace files. ## Related guides - [Recover an interrupted SFTP transfer](/integrations/sftp-resume-transfer) - [API-key setup and restrictions](/developers/api-key)

title: Disconnect an SFTP client safely
summary: Finish every queued SFTP transfer, wait for the final close response, disconnect the session, and remove or revoke the saved API key safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/ftp-server/src/sftp.ts, apps/ftp-server/src/api.ts, apps/ftp-server/src/access.ts, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx, and apps/help/src/content/articles/sftp-connect.md. No production SFTP session was disconnected or credential revoked.
body: A transfer is not safely finished when its progress meter first reaches 100%. Dosya buffers SFTP uploads until the client closes the file handle; only a successful CLOSE response confirms that the cloud upload committed. Closing the connection earlier can leave no remote file, while an interrupted download can leave an incomplete local copy. Before disconnecting, identify whether the queue contains uploads, downloads, or only completed entries. An upload can still fail at CLOSE because workspace access changed, storage or policy rejected the file, or the service returned an API error. A download is complete only when the local client has written the expected byte count. ## Steps 1. Stop adding new work to the SFTP queue, then wait until every required transfer leaves its active or retrying state. Keep any failure message that names `close`, `read`, `write`, status 2, status 3, or status 4. 2. For an upload, refresh or relist the destination and compare the remote name and size with the local source. For a download, compare the local size or calculate a local checksum against a known-good copy. 3. Close open remote editors and file handles before ending the session. In an OpenSSH prompt use `bye`; in a graphical client choose its normal disconnect command instead of terminating the process. 4. Confirm the client shows no queued transfer and no live Dosya session. If it still reconnects automatically, disable that saved site's background synchronization or remove the site from the client's startup list. 5. Remove the saved `dos_…` password from that client's private credential store when this computer should no longer connect. Deleting a saved password does not invalidate copies of the same API key stored elsewhere. 6. For access that must end, open **Profile → API keys**, select the dedicated key, and choose **Revoke**. The receipt is **Key revoked**; fresh SFTP authentication can reflect a previously cached success for up to 60 seconds, so reconnect after that window to verify refusal. Revoking the key prevents later operations but does not delete files already transferred. Ending a session also does not cancel a cloud mutation that already returned a successful CLOSE; verify the destination before deciding whether cleanup is needed. If the queue is stuck, preserve the operation name and bounded server message. Dosya maps API 403 to **Permission denied**, API 404 to **No such file**, and other failures to status 4; key-shaped text is redacted and messages are capped at 180 characters. ## Expected result The client has no active file handle or queued transfer, required files have verified final bytes, and the session is closed. Any credential removed locally is absent from that device, while a revoked key is refused on a new connection after the short authentication-cache window. ## Related guides - [Connect an SFTP client](/integrations/sftp-connect) - [Troubleshoot SFTP](/troubleshooting/sftp)

title: Download a file over SFTP
summary: Download a Dosya file over SFTP, verify the local byte count or checksum, and understand offset reads, permissions, and stale-path failures.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/ftp-server/src/sftp.ts, apps/ftp-server/src/vfs.ts, apps/ftp-server/src/api.ts, apps/ftp-server/src/block-cache.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/sftp.int.test.ts. No production object was downloaded.
body: Dosya SFTP supports ordinary and offset reads. Files smaller than 64 MiB use an in-memory read path; files at or above 64 MiB use bounded range requests, so a large download can take longer to start or run at a different speed. There is no SFTP download-size ceiling, although role, key, egress, and concurrency limits can still refuse the request. Use a **Read only** or **Full access** API key that includes the SFTP protocol and the intended workspace. The login username must exactly match the key owner's email, including letter case. At `/`, choose a listed workspace name or slug before addressing its folders. ## Steps 1. Connect to `sftp.dosya.dev` on port `2222`, run `ls`, and enter the workspace that owns the file. Record the remote pathname and the size reported by `stat` or the client listing. 2. Choose a new local destination so an older partial copy cannot be mistaken for this run. In OpenSSH, use `get "remote-name.ext" "./remote-name.ext"`; a GUI client can use **Download**. 3. Wait for the transfer to finish without a `read failed`, **Permission denied**, or **No such file** response. A missing path is rechecked once when the directory cache had reported a miss. 4. Compare the local byte count with the remote listing. For an integrity check, calculate SHA-256 on the downloaded file and compare it with a trusted checksum or with a separately verified source copy. 5. If the transfer stopped but the remote file has not changed, resume through a client that performs offset reads. Restart from zero whenever the remote name, size, or current version changed during the interruption. 6. Open the completed local file, then relist the remote directory. Keep the client log and exact operation if a second download returns different bytes; SFTP has no shell or server-side hash command. **Permission denied** can mean the workspace role lacks SFTP or download access. **No such file** covers an absent or hidden path, and a replaced file may make one cached identifier stale; the gateway refreshes the path once when the old object returns 404. Rate-limited reads honor `Retry-After` for up to three retries, while transient GET network or 500/502/504 failures receive at most two retries. A successful download creates only a local copy. It does not remove, share, or change the remote Dosya file, and local deletion cannot affect cloud storage unless the client sends a separate remote delete. ## Expected result One complete local file exists at the chosen destination, its size matches the current remote listing, and any checksum comparison uses the bytes actually downloaded. The original remains in the same Dosya workspace and folder. ## Related guides - [Connect an SFTP client](/integrations/sftp-connect) - [Connect with SFTP using a restricted key](/integrations/sftp-restricted-key)

title: Connect FileZilla to Dosya with SFTP
summary: Configure FileZilla for Dosya SFTP on port 2222, use an API key as the password, verify the SSH host key, and safely open the allowed workspace.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/sftp.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx, apps/ftp-server/src/sftp.ts, and apps/ftp-server/src/access.ts. FileZilla and the production host fingerprint were not exercised.
body: FileZilla must use **SFTP - SSH File Transfer Protocol**, not FTP or FTPS. Dosya listens at `sftp.dosya.dev:2222`; the username is the API-key owner's exact account email, and the password field receives the complete `dos_…` API key. SSH public-key login and an interactive shell are not available. Create a dedicated credential in **Profile → API keys → New API key**. Pick **Read only** for browsing and downloads or **Full access** when FileZilla must upload, rename, move, or delete. Under protocol restrictions, include **SFTP**; a workspace pin is supported, while folder anchors and allowed-IP restrictions make the key unusable through this gateway. ## Steps 1. In FileZilla, open **File → Site Manager**, choose **New site**, and set **Protocol** to **SFTP - SSH File Transfer Protocol**. 2. Enter **Host** `sftp.dosya.dev` and **Port** `2222`. Use a password-based logon, put the exact key-owner email in **User**, and keep the API key out of the site name and comments. 3. Connect and inspect the SSH host-key prompt before sending the password.
