If activity is unexplained, preserve the displayed rows and revoke the link. ## Expected result A matching first-open or verification signal appears, with named-recipient proof kept separate from anonymous access events and download counts. The UI loads the newest 25 event rows; **Showing N of total events** discloses when older rows are outside the current table. Country is based only on loaded events and can be **Unknown**. ## Related guides - [Create a link](/sharing/create-link) - [Audit delivery](/sharing/audit-delivery)

title: Deliver several files as one share
summary: Create one link for 1–100 same-workspace files, apply recipient and download controls, then verify the complete public bundle before delivery.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: apps/api/src/lib/share/access.ts, apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/share-bundle.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/recipients.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/downloads.ts, src/components/share/ShareShell.astro.
body: A bundle puts several files behind one URL. The selected files must be live, visible, inside your scope, and in one workspace; the link can contain at most 100 files. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, select between 1 and 100 live files from the same workspace. You need `create_share_links`, and every selected item must be visible and inside your permitted folder scope. 2. Choose **Share** and confirm the dialog says the selection will use **one link for all of them**. Duplicate IDs, missing files, cross-workspace files, and hidden targets are refused. 3. Choose **By email** for delivery or **By link** for a bearer URL. Email sharing supports at most 50 deduplicated recipient addresses; leave **Only these people can open it** on when forwarding must not grant access. 4. Set **Expires in** and, if needed, a password of at least 8 characters. The bundle endpoint currently persists expiry, password, and recipient access; the web dialog’s view-only, metadata-removal, download-limit, title, and message fields are not applied to bundle creation. 5. Create or send the bundle. A partial result names addresses Dosya could not reach. If every email fails, **Could not send email** appears after the link was created, so check **Shared** before retrying to avoid another live link. Add view-only or a download cap afterward in mobile. 6. Open the resulting URL in a private window and check the file count and names. The page labels it **Bundle**. Open each tile to verify it; the current dock’s **Download all** URL resolves only the bundle’s first file, so do not promise recipients one combined archive. ## Expected result One active share URL opens the reviewed bundle with its expiry, password, and recipient restriction applied; any later mobile edit keeps that same URL. **Changing or deleting a source file changes what the share can serve; the bundle is not a detached archive.** **Creating a new bundle does not revoke any older link covering the same files.** ## Related guides - [Create a link](/sharing/create-link) - [Audit delivery](/sharing/audit-delivery)

title: Audit a sensitive file delivery
summary: Check one sensitive share's audience, password, expiry, download policy, recipient verification, event evidence, and final revocation state.
verification: Verified from the local share list, analytics, revoke route, public resolver, and authorization tests: apps/web/src/pages/shared.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/analytics.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/revoke.ts; apps/api/src/lib/repo/contract/shares.contract.unit.test.ts. No live production delivery was altered.
body: A delivery audit connects one link’s current controls with the evidence Dosya retained. It can show that an address verified a restricted share and that opens or downloads occurred, but it cannot establish who held the device or recover a downloaded copy. ## Steps 1. Open **Shared → By me** in the browser and locate the exact delivery. Match its file name, region, expiry and status, and record the lifetime view and download counts from the row’s **Views** cell. Where similar names exist, retain the `/shared/{link_id}` route or displayed share URL as the audit key. 2. Select the row and verify the header’s item, creator and creation age. Check whether the URL is **Open to anyone with the URL** or **Restricted to N invited addresses**. For confidential material, a public link does not identify its audience, even if a password was separately communicated. 3. Read **Link controls**. Record the end or expiry time, **Password** state, **Access** mode and **Downloads** value. **View only** means the recipient UI does not allow a download; **Allowed** permits it. Analytics does not show a configured maximum, downloads remaining or the lifetime count captured from **Shared**. 4. On a restricted share, compare the **Invited** list with the approved addresses. **Verified** means that address accepted its one-time code at least once before bytes were served. **Not opened** means no verification is stored. It does not guarantee that an invitation email was delivered or read. 5. Set **Access over time** to the relevant **7d**, **30d** or **90d** period. Treat the chart as daily first opens and downloads within that window. Do not substitute it for the lifetime counts recorded on **Shared**: first opens are deduplicated, and the selected range does not filter the remaining analytics panels. 6. Inspect **Access log**. It is newest first and returns a maximum of 25 rows, with **Showing X of Y events** disclosing whether older evidence is omitted from the screen. Capture the time, **Opened** or **Downloaded** event, opaque eight-character visitor handle, country availability and parsed device label needed for your private audit note. 7. Keep recipient verification separate from events. The database does not attach an invited email address to a view/download row, so no individual access event proves which named recipient acted. Public links provide even less identity: distinct reach is derived from a non-reversible IP hash. 8. Reconcile anomalies with expiration, download policy and expected recipient timing. A country may be absent for older or unplaceable traffic, a returning hash does not add another first open, and the country summary covers only loaded access rows. Document these limits beside any conclusion. 9. If the delivery should remain available, leave the link unchanged and record its current status. If it must end, select **Revoke**, open **Revoke this link**, and read the confirmation: link holders lose access the moment you confirm, the access log is kept, and **This cannot be undone.** 10. Confirm with **Revoke link**. Success reports **Link revoked — The share link no longer works.** The public URL then returns `410 Gone`; the analytics record stays available to authorized reviewers. Revocation cannot recall files already saved on recipient devices. ## Roles and failures The reviewer must be a member and remain inside any assigned folder subtree. **view_own_shares** covers a link the member created; **view_all_shares** covers another member’s delivery. A hidden or removed target returns **Share link not found** or **Associated resource not found** rather than disclosing inaccessible content. Revocation applies the same scope and ownership rules and also requires share permission. A denied request can report **You don't have permission to revoke this share link**. If it fails in the UI, Dosya shows **Revoke failed** and the API message or **The share link could not be revoked.** Reopen analytics before retrying so you do not mistake a stale button for a completed action. ## Expected result The audit identifies the exact delivery, records controls and qualified evidence, and leaves a clear live, expired or revoked disposition. If revoked, recipient access ends permanently while prior log rows remain for authorized review. ## Related guides - [Read sharing-link analytics](/sharing/analytics) - [Use named recipients](/sharing/named-recipients) - [Review download events](/sharing/share-review-download-events) - [Revoke a sharing link](/sharing/revoke-link)

title: Disable downloads on a sharing link
summary: Replace an active sharing URL with a view-only link, confirm file and folder download controls are blocked, and send recipients the new address.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/shared.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/share/access.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/lock-gate.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/view-only-image.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/view-only-image.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/download-session.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download-all.ts and focused share download tests. Verified creation-only web control, immediate terminal revocation, effective target view-only behavior, preview-family enforcement, format-specific derivative, passthrough and refusal behavior for View-only images, folder ZIP refusal, preview byte-session counting, persistent recipient grants, separate link-result and email-send completion paths and the distinction between configured locks and personal unlocks. The real Advanced options capture remains accurate.
body: The web app sets **View only** when a link is created. To remove downloads from an existing URL, revoke that link and create a replacement for the same target with **View only** selected. The replacement has a different address, so every recipient needs the new URL. ## Before you start - Identify the exact active row in **Shared → By me** and note its target, recipients, password, expiry and any download limit. These settings are not copied to the replacement automatically. - Warn recipients that the original URL will end immediately. Revocation cannot be undone. - Confirm the file type can open in Dosya’s browser preview. A view-only link refuses attachment bytes; an item without a supported preview may therefore be unusable to the recipient. - Understand the boundary: removing a download button reduces ordinary saving, but visible information can still be photographed, transcribed or captured from the screen. ## Steps 1. Open **Shared**, stay on **By me**, and locate the link whose downloads should stop. 2. Open its detail page and confirm **Downloads** currently reads **Allowed**. Copy the target name, not the URL, for reference. 3. Return to the list, select **Revoke**, and confirm the warning. The old token immediately returns **This share link has been revoked** and can never be restored. 4. Open **Files**, find that same file, bundle or folder, and choose **Share**. 5. Select **By link** for a public URL. Use **By email** and leave **Only these people can open it.** selected when named addresses must verify access. 6. Review **Expires in**, expand **Advanced options**, then select **View only.** It blocks ordinary attachment downloads. The dialog summarizes images as lower-resolution previews, but the exact byte behavior depends on format as described below. 7. Re-enter the old delivery’s required password, expiry, named-recipient mode and metadata choice from its **Shared** detail; none of those controls migrate automatically. 8. Replace the revoked delivery with **Generate link** or **Send** according to its recipient mode: - For **By link**, select **Generate link**, copy the address under **Share link created**, select **Done**, and open that copy privately. - For **By email**, select **Send**, note the sent count and any failed addresses, then let the modal reset and close. Open **Shared → By me**, find the new row, and retrieve its URL there for a private test with an invited inbox; email mode does not present a generated-link result. 9. Verify that a previewable file opens without a download control. An eligible View-only preview still claims one configured download slot when its first bytes are served; Range requests for that file reuse the claim only within the same one-hour signed session. Do not perform this byte test on a one-slot replacement intended for somebody else. For a folder, browse its visible tree and confirm **Download all** is unavailable. 10. Distribute a **By link** replacement manually. For **By email**, the invitations were sent by **Send**; correct reported failures. In either mode, update messages, bookmarks or documents that still point at the **Revoked** token. ## Expected result The original address is permanently revoked. Its replacement opens supported previews without file-download or folder-archive controls, appears as **Downloads: View only** in the owner detail, and is the only URL sent for future access. ## Expected recipient behavior - A normal download request is refused with **This file is view-only. Downloads are not allowed.** - A folder archive request is refused with **This folder is view-only. Downloads are not allowed.** - Previewable document, media and image families can still open inline. JPEG, PNG and HEIC images are re-encoded as WebP derivatives capped at 1,600 px on the longest edge. - WebP, AVIF, GIF, SVG, BMP and ICO have no server-side decoder in this path, so the browser receives their original bytes inline. View only therefore cannot promise original-byte withholding for every previewable image format. - Folder browsing can remain available while the ZIP action is blocked. Opening an eligible descendant preview still consumes one link slot when a download ceiling is configured; View only does not bypass that counter. - Unsupported preview formats do not become downloadable merely because the recipient holds the URL. - Files downloaded before revocation remain on recipients’ devices. View-only cannot recall those copies. The target’s configured lock can also determine the effective result. A file set to workspace **View only** remains view-only even when its share link was created without that option. A target or ancestor changed to **Full lock** makes the public link unavailable rather than asking the recipient for the workspace lock password. ## Locks and unlock grants A member’s personal folder or file unlock lasts for that signed-in member and does not weaken public sharing. It cannot make a full-locked target shareable, cannot enable downloads on a view-only link, and cannot revive a public link while the configured target lock remains. Changing the configured lock is a workspace action with wider consequences. Ask an authorized owner to decide whether the target itself should change, or leave the target protected and share a suitable copy instead. ## Troubleshooting **View only is absent.** Expand **Advanced options** in the current **Share** dialog. If link creation itself is unavailable, confirm your role has **create share links** permission and check workspace policy. **The old URL still shows content in an open tab.** An already-rendered page is not a valid revocation test. Reload or open the exact URL privately; new API access must be refused. **A recipient still has a download button.** Compare the complete address with the replacement shown in **Shared → By me**, then verify its detail page says **Downloads: View only**. Multiple links can point to the same target, and changing one does not change the others. **The recipient cannot preview the item.** The link may be correctly view-only while the format lacks an eligible inline renderer. For JPEG, PNG and HEIC, a source larger than 32 MiB or one the server cannot decode is refused instead of falling back to the original. Convert or provide a previewable delivery copy if downloading must remain disabled. **A folder ZIP is missing but individual previews work.** This is expected for a view-only folder. Remember that each first logical preview byte session can still spend a configured link slot. If the link is not view-only, also check its download count, Free-plan transfer allowance and the archive’s 10,000-entry and 5 GiB ceilings. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I turn downloads back on for the same URL? The current web workflow does not edit this field in place. Revoke and replace the link again with **View only** cleared. The authenticated share API has broader update capabilities, but that does not change what the web controls currently offer. ### Does view-only stop screenshots? No. It changes the bytes and controls Dosya serves; it cannot prevent someone from capturing content displayed on their device. ### Does a password also disable downloads? No. A password gates entry. Select **View only** separately when the unlocked recipient should preview without downloading. ## Related guides - [Create and test a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Share a folder through one URL](/sharing/folder-link) - [Revoke a sharing link permanently](/sharing/revoke-link) - [Preflight the recipient view privately](/sharing/share-preflight-private-window)

title: Choose download access for a sharing link
summary: Choose between normal download access, View only and a download-count limit when creating a Dosya sharing link, then test the recipient result.
verification: Reviewed the current web Share dialog, View only and download-limit controls, Shared list, analytics detail rail, recipient download enforcement and share-link creation API against local product source and relevant tests on 2026-10-14. Existing web links cannot be edited in place; changing their policy requires revocation and replacement. The screenshot uses an isolated sample file.
body: Dosya lets you choose how a recipient can receive a shared file or folder. Set the download policy before generating the link, then test the finished recipient page. The current web app does not edit an active link's download policy in place, so changing an existing link requires a new URL. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace and the exact file, folder or bundle you intend to share. - Decide whether the recipient needs the original file, preview access, or a limited number of downloads. - Use non-confidential test content when you are validating a new delivery policy. - Keep link passwords and unpublished sharing URLs out of screenshots and support messages. ## Choose the right control | Setting | Recipient behavior | Use it when | | --- | --- | --- | | Normal link | The recipient can use the available download controls. | The recipient needs an original local copy. | | **View only** | The recipient can open supported content without a download button. Images use a reduced-size preview instead of the original. | Review is enough and you do not want Dosya to offer the original as a download. | | **Download limit** | Downloads work until the link reaches the whole-number limit you set. | A small, known number of successful downloads should end delivery. | You can combine a download limit with other creation settings. Do not combine **View only** with an expectation that the recipient will download the original. ## Steps: set download access on a new link 1. In **Files**, confirm the active workspace and select the exact file, folder or bundle. 2. Choose **Share** and select **By link** or **By email**. 3. Set the expiry and any named recipients required for this delivery. 4. Open **Advanced options**. 5. For preview-only access, select **View only**. The explanation below the checkbox should state that there is no download button and that visible content can still be captured. 6. To allow downloads but stop after a fixed count, leave **View only** off and enter a whole number of at least 1 in **Download limit**. Leave the field empty for no configured count limit. 7. Review the password, metadata, title and message settings, then generate or send the link. ## Test the recipient experience 1. Open the finished link in a private browser window where you are not signed in as the owner. 2. Complete any password or named-recipient verification. 3. For **View only**, confirm the item opens and no download button appears. 4. For a limited-download link, use a harmless test only when you can afford to consume one count. Confirm the download completes and then review the link's analytics. 5. Return to **Shared**, open the exact link, and check the right-side **Link controls** panel. It should show **Downloads: View only** or **Downloads: Allowed** as appropriate. ## Expected result The finished sharing link opens for the intended recipient and follows the policy selected at creation. A view-only link omits the download control, while an allowed link serves the file until any configured download limit is reached. The link detail page reports the matching download status. ## Change an existing link The web app records the download policy when it creates the link. To change an active link: 1. Open **Shared -> By me** and identify the existing link by resource, creation time and URL. 2. Record the other controls you must preserve, including recipients, password, expiry, metadata removal, download limit and title. 3. Revoke the old link. 4. Create a replacement from the original item with the new download policy and the required controls. 5. Test both URLs. The old URL must report that it is unavailable or revoked; the replacement must show the intended recipient behavior. 6. Send the new URL to recipients and tell them the previous one was withdrawn. ## Limits and important details - **View only** removes supported Dosya download paths. It cannot prevent screenshots, photography, screen recording or manual copying of visible information. - A download limit controls successful delivery attempts through the link. Your own recipient-side test can consume part of the limit. - Browser previews and file-type support vary. If Dosya cannot preview a format, a view-only link may provide less utility than expected. - Revoking and replacing a link gives it a new URL. Bookmarks and messages containing the old URL do not update automatically. - Workspace policy, file locks, expiry, recipient restrictions and plan limits can impose additional controls. ## Troubleshooting **View only is missing.** Confirm that you are creating a new link in the current web app, then expand **Advanced options**. Check your role and workspace sharing policy if the control remains unavailable. **The recipient still sees Download.** Verify that they opened the replacement URL rather than an earlier link. Open the link from **Shared** and confirm its **Downloads** status. **The download stopped sooner than expected.** Check the configured limit and link analytics. Owner testing or repeated recipient activity may have used the available count. **The file cannot be previewed.** Create a harmless test link for the same format. If preview is unsupported, choose a delivery method that matches the recipient's need without claiming view-only review will work. ## Related guides - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Turn downloads off for an existing link](/sharing/share-disable-downloads) - [Test a sharing link in a private window](/sharing/share-preflight-private-window)

title: Email a share link with a message
summary: Email one Dosya share URL and a 500-character note to up to 50 people, then interpret web delivery details and mobile's simpler result message.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, apps/mobile/src/share/CreateShareSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/share/hooks.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/email.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/share-email.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/share-message-cap.unit.test.ts. Production status: no email was sent.
body: Dosya can create one share URL, mail it to a recipient list, and place an optional personal note in the same branded message. The note is context for the recipient; expiry, password, view-only, download limits, and named-recipient verification remain the actual access controls. ## Limits and delivery behavior One link accepts no more than 50 normalized, unique email addresses. The optional message can contain at most 500 characters after trimming. The API rejects a longer note with **Message is too long (max 500 characters)** before it creates the share. Do not place the link password, verification code, or confidential material in this note because every selected recipient receives it. Sending requires **Create share links** and access to the target. Workspace sharing rules and free-plan limits still apply. Registered recipients can receive an in-app inbox item and push notification in addition to the email; external recipients receive the mail containing the URL. ## Steps 1. Open the file or folder's **Share** control. On the web, you may select multiple files first to mail one bundle link. 2. Choose **By email** in the web dialog or **Send by email** in the mobile sheet. 3. Add the intended addresses under **Recipients** or **To**. Remove any chip that does not belong in the final audience. 4. Enter a concise note in **Message**, such as the requested action and due date. Keep it at 500 characters or fewer. 5. Decide whether to enable **Only these people can open it.** With it on, each recipient must verify that invited address; with it off, anyone who receives a forwarded URL can use the link. 6. Review **Expires in** or **Expires**, then configure any password and download restrictions. 7. Press **Send** on web or **Send to N people** on mobile. 8. Read the completion feedback before closing. On web, all successful sends report **Shared with N recipients.** and mixed results identify the addresses Dosya could not reach. Mobile instead shows **Email sent** after any successful HTTP response. ## Interpret the send result The web client displays **Private share sent** for a restricted delivery and **Share sent** for a public one. When only some messages fail, it reports **Sent to X of N. Could not reach: address...**. Those failures do not cancel successful mail or remove the already-created link. The mobile client discards the response's sent count and failed-address list. It shows **Email sent** for a successful HTTP response even when only some recipients were reached, so use the web flow when the sender must know which addresses failed. If every send fails, the server returns **Could not send email** to either client; inspect **Shared** before submitting again because link creation precedes outbound mail. The owner-side **Access log** records opens and downloads, not SMTP delivery. For a restricted link, the **Invited** panel changes from **Not opened** to **Verified** after a recipient completes the code gate. A public email share cannot prove which mailbox holder used a forwarded address. ## Expected result Each successfully reached address receives the same governed share URL and written note. Web reports full or partial delivery details; mobile confirms only that the request succeeded. Later analytics begins when recipients verify, open, or download. ## Related guides - [Create a link](/sharing/create-link) - [Read link activity](/sharing/link-activity)

title: Export sharing analytics for review
summary: Review the available 7-, 30-, or 90-day analytics and capture the visible 25-event table while recognizing that web CSV export is unavailable.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/analytics.ts.
body: The current web analytics page has no CSV or export control. You can review its range, counters, reach, recipients, and newest 25 events, then preserve that visible evidence. ## Steps 1. Open **Shared** → **By me**, select the link, and confirm its exact URL and status on the analytics page. 2. Choose **7d**, **30d**, or **90d**. The timeline shows first opens and downloads by day; a returning hashed IP is not counted as another first open. 3. Use **All**, **Opens**, or **Downloads** above the access log. This filter applies only to the rows already loaded; the web page requests 25 newest events and shows **Showing N of total events**. 4. Record the visible columns: **When**, **Event**, **Visitor**, **Country**, and **Device**. Visitor is an eight-character fragment of a one-way IP hash; **Unknown** country covers missing edge location and older rows written before country was recorded. 5. Capture the page with your browser’s print or screenshot tools if a review artifact is required. The current web client contains no **Export**, CSV, or download-analytics action. 6. Add the chosen range, capture time, loaded-row count, and total event count to your review note. Do not imply the visible country tally covers events beyond the loaded 25. ## Expected result You have a clearly scoped capture of the analytics that the web app actually displays, including its range and row limit, without a nonexistent export claim. **Reach tallies devices and browsers from at most 5,000 distinct visitor rows and marks truncation.** **Restricted-link events cannot be attributed to individual recipients.** ## Related guides - [Read sharing analytics](/sharing/analytics) - [Read link activity](/sharing/link-activity)

title: Share several files with one link
summary: Select up to 100 files in one workspace, create one bundle URL on the web, and verify that its recipient page shows exactly the intended file set.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/share-bundle.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/lock-gate.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/share/access.bundle-lock.unit.test.ts. Production status: no bundle was created.
body: A bundle places several selected files behind one URL and one access policy. Create it from the Dosya web Files page when separate links would be hard to manage. The mobile creation sheet currently handles one file or one folder, so multi-file bundle creation is a web task. ## Bundle rules A bundle contains between 1 and 100 unique, live files from the same workspace. It cannot mix files and folders, and it cannot include a file outside the member's assigned subtree. The Files toolbar prevents a mixed selection; the API separately rejects cross-workspace members with **All files must be in the same workspace** and missing, duplicate, deleted, or hidden choices with **Some files were not found**. The sender must hold **Create share links**. Workspace policies can disable link creation, force an eight-character password, or shorten the expiry. A free-plan creator can have five active links and receives a maximum seven-day lifetime even if the picker requests longer. ## Steps 1. In the web app, open **Files** inside the workspace that contains every item. 2. Select only the files for this delivery. Clear all selected folders; a folder must use its own folder link. 3. Use the bulk **Share** action. The dialog should identify the target as **N files · one link for all of them**. 4. Choose **By link** for a URL you will deliver yourself, or **By email** to enter up to 50 recipients. 5. Set **Expires in** and an optional password. For named-recipient access, enable **Only these people can open it.** on the email tab. 6. Recheck the selected count before submitting. Choose **Generate link** or **Send**. 7. For a link-only bundle, copy the address from **Share link created**. For email delivery, wait for **Shared with N recipients.** or the partial-delivery notice. 8. Open the bundle URL in a signed-out browser and compare every displayed file name with the selection from step 2. ## What changes after creation The bundle membership is stored when the URL is created; selecting another file later does not add it. The record also keeps its first member in the legacy `file_id` field. If that first file becomes fully locked, the target gate refuses the entire bundle with **This content has been locked by its owner**. A later member that becomes fully locked is omitted individually from the recipient listing, and a direct request for that member returns **File not found or has been deleted**. Neither case changes the link address. Recipient mail and notifications still describe the original delivery by its total file count. If no files reach the request, Dosya returns **file_ids array is required**. Selecting 101 or more produces **Maximum 100 files per share link**. These refusals happen without creating the bundle. If all outgoing emails fail after creation, the API reports **Could not send email**; the link record may already exist, so check **Shared** before retrying. ## Expected result One live URL opens a recipient page containing the reviewed file set under the selected expiry, password, and recipient policy. The Shared area records the delivery as one bundle link rather than one link per file. ## Related guides - [Create a link](/sharing/create-link) - [Read link activity](/sharing/link-activity)

title: Investigate unexpected sharing-link activity
summary: Preserve the newest event evidence, interpret anonymous visitor and country fields correctly, revoke the link, and verify access is contained.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/analytics.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/revoke.ts, src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, src/pages/report-abuse.astro.
body: Unexpected analytics can establish that a link was opened or downloaded, but not who did it. Preserve the visible evidence and revoke before investigating attribution elsewhere. ## Steps 1. Open the link from **Shared** → **By me** and confirm its URL, access rule, password state, expiry, and **Downloads** setting in **Link controls**. 2. Choose the relevant 7-, 30-, or 90-day range and filter the newest log rows by **Opens** or **Downloads**. Record timestamp, opaque visitor handle, device label, and country or **Unknown**. 3. For restricted links, compare **Verified** recipient rows separately. A verified address proves inbox control, but no individual access-log row can be assigned to that person. 4. Note the evidence boundary: the table loads 25 newest events, repeat visits do not add first-open rows, public visitors are anonymous, and reach may be truncated after 5,000 distinct visitors. 5. Choose **Revoke**, confirm **Revoke link**, and preserve the **Revoked** timestamp. Revocation is permanent, closes the URL immediately, and keeps the analytics record. 6. Test the URL in a private window for **Link revoked**. Contact intended recipients separately; if the content or URL is abusive, the public page’s **Report abuse** link opens a form prefilled with that share URL. ## Expected result The suspicious URL is permanently closed, the available event evidence remains in analytics, and any attribution conclusion stays within the data Dosya records. **Changing a password is available in the mobile editor, but revocation is the decisive response when continued access is unacceptable.** **Other active links to the same content require separate review.** ## Related guides - [Read sharing analytics](/sharing/analytics) - [Read link activity](/sharing/link-activity)

title: Match a recipient to sharing activity
summary: Use recipient verification and the anonymous access log correctly, without assigning individual opens or downloads to a named person without evidence.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/analytics.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/shares.unit.test.ts. Production status: no recipient activity was generated.
body: Dosya can show which invited addresses completed verification and can separately show anonymous link events. It cannot prove that a particular **Opened** or **Downloaded** row belongs to one named recipient. Use the two panels together without joining facts the product does not store. ## What the data means For a restricted link, **Invited** lists each email as **Verified** or **Not opened**. The verified timestamp is written when that address's one-time code succeeds. It proves control of the inbox and that the person reached the share gate; it is not a timestamp for every later open. The **Access log** stores event time, **Opened** or **Downloaded**, an eight-character prefix of a hashed network address, country when the edge supplied it, and parsed device information. It has no recipient-email column. The 30-minute recipient grant cookie also does not name the verified address in an event, so even restricted traffic remains unattributed row by row. For a public link there is no invited list at all. Anyone with the URL may use it, and the analytics headline correctly says that the owner does not know who those people are. ## Steps 1. Open **Shared**, select the relevant link, and enter its analytics page. 2. Confirm whether **Access** says **N invited people** or **Anyone with the link**. Only the first mode has named verification data. 3. On a restricted link, inspect **Invited**. Record only whether each address is **Verified** or **Not opened**. 4. Review the headline showing how many invited people verified. Do not treat that count as total visits. 5. Use **7 days**, **30 days**, or **90 days** to inspect first opens and downloads in the chosen chart window. 6. Under **Access log**, filter with **All**, **Opens**, or **Downloads**. Read the opaque visitor handle, country, and device as event context. 7. If an individual recipient asks whether their download succeeded, use their own confirmation or a separate controlled link. Do not assign an anonymous row to them based only on timing, location, or device. ## Counting and privacy limits An open is deduplicated by the stored address hash, so the chart reports first opens rather than repeat visits. Downloads are not deduplicated. Reach breakdowns read at most 5,000 visitors and display **Counted from the first 5,000 visitors.** when truncated. The access-log API returns 25 rows at a time; the screen states how many loaded events it is showing out of the total. Country can be `-` when the edge could not place an event or the row predates country capture. Browser and device labels are inferred from the recorded user agent. None of these fields is reliable enough to turn the anonymous visitor handle into an identity. Viewing this page requires **View own shared links** for the creator's record or **View all shared links** for another member's record, plus workspace and target scope. A hidden target returns the same not-found response as an unknown link. ## Expected result The review distinguishes verified invitees from anonymous access events. Reports may state who completed email verification and how the link was used, but they do not attribute a specific open or download to a named person. ## Related guides - [Read sharing analytics](/sharing/analytics) - [Read link activity](/sharing/link-activity)

title: Preflight a sharing link in a private window
summary: Test a share without account or grant cookies, complete gates in server order, and verify expiry, identity, preview, and download behavior before delivery.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/verify-code.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts.
body: A private window reproduces a new recipient session without your Dosya login or earlier share cookies. Test the exact final URL after setting every access control. ## Steps 1. Copy the exact link from its creation result or **Shared** page. Confirm its current status is active; a revoked token can never be reused. 2. Open a private or incognito window and paste the entire `/s/` URL. Do not sign in: public share access needs no Dosya account. 3. Complete gates in the server’s order. Restricted links request the invited email and six-digit code first; password-protected links then show **Unlock**. A full-lock password gate withholds file metadata. 4. Check the top bar after access: filename or bundle/folder title, size where available, kind, expiry chip, and view counter must match the intended share. 5. Open representative items and navigate folders or the bundle grid. View-only links show **View only** and provide no download action; downloadable items show **Download · size** or **Download all · size**. 6. Close the private window, reopen another clean session, and repeat the critical gate. Then send the same tested URL and communicate any password through a separate channel. ## Expected result The exact final URL works from a clean browser, exposes only the intended content, and enforces recipient, password, expiry, and download settings. **The recipient grant and password-unlock cookies last 30 minutes; a fresh private session avoids reusing them.** **Anything visible on screen can still be captured even when downloads are disabled.** ## Related guides - [Create a link](/sharing/create-link) - [Audit delivery](/sharing/audit-delivery)

title: Preview workspace sharing branding
summary: Compare desktop and phone share pages, a locked recipient view, and the real email template before saving workspace branding for recipients.
verification: Reviewed from local preview implementation and endpoint tests: apps/web/src/pages/settings/branding.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/settings/branding-share-preview.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/settings/branding.test.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/branding/preview-email.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/branding/preview-email.unit.test.ts. The released production preview was not exercised.
body: The Branding preview shows recipient presentation without creating a share, emailing anyone or changing access. Members with **access_settings** can open its local **Share page** view even when the page is read-only; eligible editors can also preview unsaved changes and request the server-rendered **Email** view. ## Steps 1. In the Dosya web app, go to **Workspace Settings → Branding**. Loading the page requires workspace membership and **access_settings**. The **View** button remains available when `can_edit` is false, including a lapsed plan, an administrative revocation or a role without **manage_branding**; those states show stored values in read-only controls. 2. If editing is allowed, enter a proposed **Brand name**, choose the six-digit **Brand colour**, upload the logo if needed, and set **Brand the share page**, **Brand email**, and **Hide the Save to dosya button**. A read-only viewer instead previews the stored form state. When the name is blank, the sample uses Dosya presentation because incomplete branding would not resolve for real recipients. 3. Select **View** in the **Preview** panel. The modal is titled **What recipients see** and explains: **Sample file and sender. Unsaved changes are shown; recipients see them only after you save.** 4. Choose **Share page**, then alternate **Desktop** and **Phone**. Phone sets the simulated page to 390 pixels. Check the sample file `Q4-report.pdf`, its 2.4 MB size and PDF type, the sender name, **Download**, **Copy link**, and—unless hidden—**Save to dosya**. The simulated share page deliberately uses Dosya’s dark recipient-page token scope in both application themes, so use the width controls rather than expecting separate light and dark share designs. 5. Turn on **Password protected**. The locked sample must show **This file is password protected**, a password field, **Unlock**, and **No account needed.** Before unlock, the filename, size and sender are concealed while allowed brand elements stay visible. Turn the switch off to return to the open sample. 6. Select **Email**. Unlike the local Share-page simulation, this tab posts the draft to the server and requires **access_settings**, **manage_branding**, a paid branding entitlement and a non-revoked workspace. An ineligible request reports **Branding is available on paid plans.**; a revoked workspace reports **Branding has been disabled for this workspace. Contact support.**; a missing edit permission reports **You do not have permission to change branding**. The request waits 400 ms after the latest draft change. During it, the pane says **Rendering the email...**; a failed render becomes **Could not render the email preview.** 7. Inspect the email masthead, logo and workspace name. Brand colour is not applied to email, and the sample remains black and white. The sender address stays `noreply@dosya.dev`; previewing does not transmit the sample message. 8. Close the modal, correct any clipped name, low-contrast accent or unsuitable logo, and reopen **View**. When the result is acceptable, choose **Save branding** on the settings page. Uploading or removing a logo has already taken effect; the name, colour and switches need this save. ## What the preview does not prove The Share-page sample is a browser-local mirror of the recipient screen, while the Email panel comes from the server template renderer and is limited to authorized editors. Neither panel creates access-log rows, sends an email, writes branding settings, validates a real link token or confirms delivery to a mailbox. A preview also cannot show how an unusually long real filename will fit because its sample values are fixed. ## Verify after saving Create or reuse a non-confidential live link, open it signed out, and compare its workspace name, logo, accent, buttons and locked state with the draft. If email branding matters, send that test share to an address you control and check the received masthead, sender name and `noreply@dosya.dev` address. This live comparison is the evidence that saved settings, entitlement and recipient delivery agree. ## Expected result The two preview tabs display the current draft without sending content or changing the workspace. After **Save branding**, permitted recipient surfaces use that draft while their access protections continue to operate independently. ## Related guides - [Customize sharing-page branding](/sharing/custom-branding) - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Read sharing-link analytics](/sharing/analytics)

title: Read sharing-link visitor counts
summary: Separate all-time hashed visitor reach from verified recipients and the 7-, 30-, or 90-day first-open chart when measuring a shared file's audience.
verification: Verified from local exposure, timeline, reach and recipient implementations plus analytics contracts: apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/analytics.ts; apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/shares.ts; apps/api/src/lib/repo/contract/shares.contract.unit.test.ts. No production visitor counts were inspected.
body: Dosya presents three different audience measures: all-time distinct public visitors, verified invited addresses, and first opens in a chosen chart window. They answer different questions and should not be added together. ## Steps 1. Open **Shared → By me** in the browser, then choose the link. Confirm its display name and URL so another link with the same file does not contaminate the comparison. 2. Read the URL strip. **Open to anyone with the URL** identifies a public share; **Restricted to N invited addresses** identifies a named-recipient share. A dead link instead says **This link no longer works**, although its earlier evidence remains available. 3. For a public link, use the exposure headline for all-time distinct reach. Dosya deduplicates a visitor by a non-reversible IP hash forever, so a return from the same hash does not add another person. Shared networks may collapse multiple people, while changing networks may separate one person; the count is reach evidence rather than identity. 4. For a restricted link, use the verified-recipient statement and **Invited** list. **Verified** means the email address accepted a one-time code before any bytes were served; **Not opened** means no verification time is stored. This is an all-time verification state and does not identify who produced a later event row. 5. Choose **7d**, **30d** or **90d** under **Access over time** to measure recent activity. The default is 30 days. **First opens** counts the first open for each distinct stored hash when that first open falls inside the chosen period. Changing the selector does not recalculate exposure, verified-recipient totals, access-log totals or reach. 6. Read **Downloads** separately from visitors. Each recorded download contributes to the selected-range chart without first-open deduplication. For the link’s lifetime download count, return to its **Shared → By me** row; the analytics detail does not render that counter. 7. Consult **Who reached it** for the device and browser mix among distinct visitors. Its backend reads at most 5,000 visitor rows. When truncated, the page discloses **Counted from the first 5,000 visitors.** 8. Treat the country breakdown as a snapshot of currently loaded access events, not of all visitors. At most 25 newest events feed that table, and absent country values are grouped as unknown. 9. Record the measure with its scope: for example, “12 all-time hashed visitors,” “4 of 7 invited addresses verified,” or “8 first opens in the last 30 days.” Include the link identifier and observation time. ## Empty and unavailable states With no traffic, the chart displays **Nothing recorded yet** and says the first open will appear within a minute. If all recorded opens are older than the current range, it reports **No opens in the last N days. Try a wider range.** Select a wider option before concluding that the link was never visited. Access follows workspace scope rather than a separate analytics plan. You need **view_own_shares** for a link you created or **view_all_shares** for someone else’s. Hidden, removed or out-of-scope targets may appear as **This share link is not available**. ## Expected result The audience statement names the correct all-time or range-limited measure and does not infer a person from a hash, device or event. Viewing these figures does not contact recipients or modify the link. ## Related guides - [Read sharing-link analytics](/sharing/analytics) - [Inspect a share access event](/sharing/share-access-event) - [Review file download events](/sharing/share-review-download-events)

title: Download an allowed file from a share
summary: Complete required gates, use the exact Download control, and recognize view-only, download-cap, archive-size, and interrupted-transfer outcomes.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: apps/api/src/lib/share/access.ts, src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download-all.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/downloads.ts.
body: After access is granted, a downloadable item shows **Download · size**. Folder pages offer a ZIP through **Download all · size**; a bundle must currently be downloaded one file at a time. ## Steps 1. Open the full share URL. If it is private, complete the invited-email code; if it is password protected, enter the sender’s password. No Dosya account is required. 2. Confirm the name, size, and file type in the top bar. In a folder or bundle, open the intended tile first if you need one file rather than the whole collection. 3. Choose **Download · size** for one item. For a folder, **Download all · size** creates an archive limited to 10,000 entries and 5 GiB. For a bundle, open and download each tile; its current dock-level **Download all** target resolves only the first member. 4. If the dock says **View only**, the page provides no download action and there is no recipient override. Ask the sender for a new downloadable link; a screen capture is still possible but is not the original file. 5. If Dosya says **This link has reached the number of downloads its sender allowed.**, do not keep retrying. The sender must raise or clear the cap in mobile, or issue a different link. 6. Wait for the browser download to finish, then compare the local filename and byte size with the page. Retry a network interruption from the same link while it remains active. ## Expected result The allowed file or folder archive arrives with the displayed name and size; bundle members are saved individually, and policy refusals remain explicit. A folder archive refusal names **Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)** or **Archive too large (max 5 GiB)**. **Deleting, revoking, expiring, or region-restricting the source can make a previously valid URL unavailable.** ## Related guides - [Open an unavailable link](/sharing/unavailable-link) - [Use recipient verification](/sharing/share-recipient-verification)

title: Complete named-recipient verification
summary: Use the invited address, request a six-digit code, enter it within 15 minutes and five attempts, and recover without exposing recipient membership.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/request-code.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/verify-code.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/recipients.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts.
body: Private shares require proof of an invited inbox. Dosya always gives the same send-code response, so the page never reveals whether an address is on the recipient list. ## Steps 1. At **This file was shared privately**, enter the exact email address that received the invitation and choose **Send code**. 2. Read the unconditional confirmation: **If address was invited, a 6-digit code is on its way. It expires in 15 minutes.** An uninvited address receives the same on-screen response but no email. 3. Open the newest **Your dosya.dev access code** message and confirm it describes the expected sender or shared item. Requesting another code replaces any still outstanding code. 4. Enter the six digits and choose **Verify** before 15 minutes pass. The code permits five wrong attempts; afterward the page requires a new code. 5. For **That code has expired. Request a new one.**, choose **Use a different email**, re-enter the address, and request again. For **That code is not correct**, clear the field and use only the newest message. 6. After success, let the page reload the share. The browser receives a 30-minute recipient grant; the sender can see that the address verified, but individual open and download rows remain anonymous. ## Expected result The invited address reaches the shared content with a 30-minute browser grant, and neither the request response nor the access log exposes recipient membership. **Code requests are limited to five per link and IP in 15 minutes; code verification is limited to ten requests per link and IP in that window.** **The code itself is single-purpose and should never be sent to the sharer or support.** ## Related guides - [Open an unavailable link](/sharing/unavailable-link) - [Use recipient verification](/sharing/share-recipient-verification)

title: Open a Dosya sharing link for the first time
summary: Open the complete dosya.dev share URL, distinguish recipient and password gates from terminal link errors, and confirm the revealed item before acting.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/pages/s/[token].astro, src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/meta.ts.
body: A Dosya public share uses `/s/` and needs no account. Treat the full URL as sensitive, then follow the gate or terminal status the page actually displays. ## Steps 1. Check that the address uses the expected `dosya.dev/s/` route and includes the complete long token. Links broken across email lines commonly produce **Invalid share link** or **Link unavailable**. 2. Open the URL in a current browser. You do not need a Dosya account; the page is intentionally excluded from search indexing. 3. If the page says **This file was shared privately**, enter the invited email and verify its code. For a link that is both restricted and password-protected, email verification appears first. 4. If the page asks for **Password**, obtain it from the sender through the agreed separate channel and choose **Unlock**. Full-lock mode hides filename, size, counts, and sender until this succeeds. 5. If you see **Link expired**, **Link revoked**, **File deleted**, or **Region restricted**, stop retrying and send that exact title to the owner; only they can provide another usable link or content. 6. After access, verify the top-bar name, size, type, expiry, and sender line before previewing or downloading. Use **Copy link** only when the sender permits forwarding. ## Expected result The browser either reveals the intended share with its current controls or gives a specific terminal state that tells the sender what must change. **A generic **Something went wrong** with **Could not load the shared file.** Try refreshing the page.** indicates a network or service failure. **Public bearer links can be opened by anyone holding the URL.** ## Related guides - [Open an unavailable link](/sharing/unavailable-link) - [Use recipient verification](/sharing/share-recipient-verification)

title: Enter a sharing-link password safely
summary: Enter the sender-provided password, recover from network and lockout errors, and understand the 30-minute browser grant and full-lock privacy behavior.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/lib/unlock-throttle.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/apply-update.ts.
body: Password access is separate from a Dosya account. The page trims surrounding spaces, rate-limits guesses, and grants the current browser 30 minutes after a correct unlock. ## Steps 1. At **This file is password protected** or **This file is fully locked**, confirm the brand matches the sender. Full-lock mode intentionally withholds file details until unlock. 2. Obtain the password through the separate channel agreed with the sender. Paste it into **Password**; the page trims leading and trailing whitespace. 3. Choose **Unlock** once. A wrong secret shows the API message or **Incorrect password.**; **Network error. Try again.** means the server was not reached and is safe to retry later. 4. Do not guess. Dosya allows five password attempts per share token and IP in 15 minutes, and five consecutive wrong attempts lock the link itself for 15 minutes. 5. For **Too many attempts, try again later.**, wait for the lockout or ask the sender to update the password in mobile. A password change clears the link’s stored unlock throttle. 6. After success, confirm the expected content. Dosya stores a signed 30-minute browser cookie, so refreshes skip the gate until it expires; a new private window must unlock again. ## Expected result The correct password reveals the intended share and grants only that browser temporary access; repeated failures stop with a named 15-minute lockout. **Restricted-and-password-protected links require email verification before this password gate.** **Never include the password in a problem report or send it in the same message as the share URL.** ## Related guides - [Open an unavailable link](/sharing/unavailable-link) - [Use recipient verification](/sharing/share-recipient-verification)

title: Report a sharing-link access problem
summary: Record the exact share-page state and safe context, contact the sender or Dosya, and use the prefilled abuse form without exposing passwords or codes.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, src/pages/report-abuse.astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts.
body: Report the visible title, time, browser, and share URL while omitting secrets. The public page provides **Contact** and a **Report abuse** form prefilled with the current link. ## Steps 1. Copy the exact error title and description, current time with time zone, device, browser version, and whether the failure happened before or after email or password verification. 2. Record the full share URL privately for the sender or Dosya support. Do not post it publicly; anyone holding a public bearer URL may be able to open the content. 3. Retry once only for **Network error. Try again.**, **Could not load that folder.**, or **Something went wrong**. Preserve terminal states such as **Link expired**, **Link revoked**, **File deleted**, and **Region restricted** without repeated attempts. 4. Contact the sender first for an expired or revoked link, wrong invited address, password, view-only policy, exhausted download cap, or deleted source. Only the owner can change those conditions. 5. Choose **Contact** in the share page footer for a Dosya service problem. Include the safe context from step 1, but never include the password or six-digit email code. 6. Choose **Report abuse** for harmful or unauthorized content. The form opens with the current share URL prefilled; review it, add the requested description, and submit through that page. ## Expected result The sender or Dosya receives the exact nonsecret state needed to investigate, while passwords and one-time codes remain outside the report. The public page’s **Copy link** can copy the URL for a private report, but forwarding it can expand access on a public link. **A screenshot may expose filenames, sender branding, or recipient email; redact those when they are unnecessary.** ## Related guides - [Open an unavailable link](/sharing/unavailable-link) - [Use recipient verification](/sharing/share-recipient-verification)

title: Use a recipient verification code
summary: Use a private share's six-digit email code, accounting for the email's 10-minute wording and the server's actual 15-minute acceptance window.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/mobile/app/s/[token].tsx, apps/api/src/lib/share/recipients.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/email.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/request-code.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/verify-code.ts. Production status: no code was requested.
body: A private Dosya share opens only after the visitor proves control of an address invited to that link. The server keeps the six-digit code usable for 15 minutes and a successful check grants this browser or app access for 30 minutes. A Dosya account is not required. ## Before entering a code This gate appears only for a link created with **Only these people can open it**. Enter the exact invited address; Dosya compares a normalized lowercase value. The request response always says **If that address was invited, a code is on its way.** whether the address is listed or not, so it cannot reveal the sender's recipient list. Requesting again replaces the earlier outstanding code. Each issued code allows five incorrect guesses. Code requests are limited to five per link and visitor IP in 15 minutes, while verification submissions are limited to ten over the same interval. These endpoint limits are separate from the five wrong-code ceiling. ## Steps 1. Open the private share URL. On mobile, the screen says **This link is for you only**. 2. Enter the address to which the sender delivered the share and choose **Send me a code**. 3. Find the email with subject **Your dosya.dev access code**. It names the sender or shared item when that information is available. The message currently says the code expires in 10 minutes, while the server stores and accepts it for 15 minutes. 4. Return to the same share page and type the current six-digit value in the code field. 5. Select **Verify**. Dosya refreshes the share after setting the recipient grant for that specific URL. 6. If the link also has a password, complete the separate **Password required** prompt. 7. Open or download the file as allowed. View-only shares omit downloads even after successful identity verification. ## Fix verification problems - **That code is not correct** spends one of the five attempts. Confirm the latest message and retype all six digits. - **That code has expired. Request a new one.** means more than 15 minutes passed; return to the address step and send a fresh value. - **Too many incorrect codes. Request a new one.** appears after the fifth wrong guess and requires reissuing the code. - **Request a new code to continue** means no active code is stored for that recipient. - **Could not send the code. Try again shortly.** indicates email delivery failed; wait before another request. - A throttling response requires the stated retry period. Repeated clicks do not extend the old code. Successful verification records the address as verified and sends the share creator an in-app event identifying which invited email passed. The access grant expires after 30 minutes, so a later visit can require another code even though the owner's invited list still shows **Verified**. The 10-minute email wording and 15-minute server lifetime do not currently match. During minutes 11–15, the newest code can still succeed when attempts remain and the link itself is available. Requesting another code replaces it immediately, and after the server's 15-minute lifetime the expired-code error applies. ## Expected result The shared item loads only after the current code for an invited inbox succeeds. Uninvited addresses receive no access, exhausted or expired codes fail, and a forwarded URL alone remains insufficient. ## Related guides - [Create a link](/sharing/create-link) - [Read link activity](/sharing/link-activity)

title: Require named recipients for a sensitive share
summary: Create a private file share for named email addresses, enforce one-time-code verification, and confirm that a forwarded URL alone cannot grant access.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/share-modal.tsx, apps/mobile/src/share/CreateShareSheet.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/share/recipients.ts. Production status: no private share was sent.
body: A restricted Dosya link requires both the URL and control of an invited inbox. Use it when forwarding the address must not extend access to another person. The recipient does not need a Dosya account, but must complete the emailed code challenge before any file bytes are served. ## Recipient rules The signed-in sender needs **Create share links** for the target's workspace scope. A link accepts at most 50 unique recipient addresses. Dosya trims and lowercases entries, removes duplicates, and rejects malformed addresses. External users cannot address Dosya-managed `dosya.dev` mailboxes; that attempt returns **You can't send to dosya.dev email addresses**. Staff whose own verified account uses that domain are exempt for internal delivery. The restricted choice exists on the email path: web uses **By email** and the checkbox **Only these people can open it.**; mobile uses **Send by email** and **Only these people can open it**. A link made through the plain link tab is public and has no invited list. ## Steps 1. From **Files**, open **Share** for one file or folder. On web, a multi-file selection can also create one restricted bundle. 2. Choose **By email** on web or **Send by email** on mobile. 3. Add every intended address under **Recipients** or **To**. Web accepts comma-separated paste and Enter; mobile accepts commas, semicolons, or spaces. 4. Enable **Only these people can open it.** Confirm the explanatory text says that recipients verify with a one-time code and a forwarded link does not work. 5. Choose expiry and any password or download policy needed. If a password is added, recipients must satisfy both the address gate and the password gate. 6. Select **Send** on web or **Send to N people** on mobile. 7. Ask one listed test recipient to open the email, submit the same address, and enter the current six-digit code. 8. In a separate private window, try an unlisted address. The request responds generically and never reveals whether an address is invited; it must not expose the file. ## Understand the outcome All listed people receive the same address, but each verifies independently. **A private link needs at least one recipient email** prevents a locked URL with nobody eligible to open it. More than 50 yields **A share link can have at most 50 recipients**. The web interface reports partial delivery as **Sent to X of N. Could not reach: ...**; successfully mailed recipients retain access while failed addresses still remain on the link's invite list. An invited person with a verified Dosya account can also see the record under **Shared → With me**. That list is available only after account email verification and does not replace the share-page code gate. ## Expected result Listed recipients can pass the email-code challenge and open the protected item. A person who only receives a forwarded URL cannot satisfy the gate with an address absent from the invite list. ## Related guides - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Add a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Review file download events for a share
summary: Filter the newest 25 access rows for downloads, compare the selected-range chart with Shared-list counts, and interpret anonymous evidence accurately.
verification: Verified against local analytics filters, endpoint limits, download counting, bundle naming, and repository tests: apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/analytics.ts; apps/api/src/lib/share/downloads.ts; apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/shares.ts; apps/api/src/lib/repo/contract/shares.contract.unit.test.ts. Production downloads were not reviewed.
body: The **Downloads** event filter shows downloads among the newest 25 access rows for one link. It cannot filter by file or recipient, and a row never names the person who downloaded. ## Steps 1. In the web app, choose **Shared → By me** and locate the exact link. Its **Views** cell shows lifetime views and a download count underneath; record the download count before opening analytics. For a bundle, the row uses the first file as its display name, so keep the link URL or ID in your review note. 2. Check **Link controls → Downloads**. **Allowed** means recipients can download under the link’s current policy, while **View only** means the recipient interface does not provide that action. An expired or revoked URL cannot serve a new download even if the historical policy says Allowed. 3. Note that the analytics detail does not render the lifetime download count, a maximum-download setting or `downloads_left`. Return to the selected **Shared** row whenever you need to recheck its lifetime count. 4. Under **Access over time**, choose **7d**, **30d** or **90d**. The **Downloads** bars report download events within that period; unlike first opens, downloads are not deduplicated by visitor. They can differ from the list-row lifetime count when older events exist. 5. Go to **Access log** and select **Downloads**. The browser filters only the newest 25 rows fetched for the page. It has no server request for “all downloads” and no next-page control, so **Showing X of Y events** can reveal that relevant older downloads are off-screen. 6. Read each visible row across **When**, **Event**, **Visitor**, **Country** and **Device**. Event should be **Downloaded**. Visitor is an eight-character prefix of a non-reversible IP hash or `unknown`; country is the edge code when available; device is parsed from user-agent data. 7. Do not assign the event to an invited email. On restricted shares, **Invited → Verified** confirms which addresses completed a one-time code, but access-log storage does not connect an event with that address. There is no supported recipient filter or per-recipient download report. 8. If no row remains after choosing **Downloads**, distinguish “none among the 25 loaded rows” from “none ever.” Compare the selected timeline and the download count back on **Shared**. Older download rows may have fallen beyond the current access-log page. 9. For an unexpected download, compare its time and approximate device/country context with the link’s expiry, password, audience mode and **Allowed** or **View only** policy. Revoke the link if future access must end, while remembering that revocation cannot delete a copy already downloaded. ## Access and errors Your workspace role needs **view_own_shares** for a link you made or **view_all_shares** for another creator’s link. Folder-confined members can inspect only targets inside their subtree, and hidden targets return the same missing result as unknown links. If analytics cannot load, the page says **This share link is not available** and may show **Share link not found**, **Associated resource not found**, **You don't have permission to view share links**, or **You don't have permission to view this share link**. Use **Back to Shared** to select a visible row again. ## Expected result You can identify the visible download rows for the chosen share and explain how they differ from the selected-range bars and the lifetime count on **Shared**. The review remains anonymous and may be incomplete once total events exceed 25. ## Related guides - [Read sharing-link analytics](/sharing/analytics) - [Inspect a share access event](/sharing/share-access-event) - [Read visitor counts](/sharing/share-read-visitors) - [Audit a sensitive delivery](/sharing/audit-delivery)

title: Revoke a sharing link after delivery
summary: Review a delivered link's access history, revoke it from Shared, and understand the permanent recipient cutoff plus the retained audit record afterward.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/shared.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx, apps/mobile/app/shares/[id].tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id]/revoke.ts. Production status: no URL was revoked.
body: Revoke a link when its delivery has finished, the wrong audience received it, or access must stop before expiry. Revocation is a terminal write: the same URL cannot be restored, although its access history remains available to authorized workspace members. ## Permission and scope rules The creator may revoke their own link when their role includes **View own shared links**. A role with **View all shared links** can stop a colleague's link. Workspace membership by itself is insufficient, and a member confined to a folder subtree cannot manage a target outside that subtree. Hidden targets can make a record appear as **Share link not found** rather than disclose its existence. Revocation is available on the web **Shared** list, on the web link analytics page, and in the mobile link detail screen. The two web confirmation dialogs use **Revoke** or **Revoke link**; mobile asks **Revoke this link?**. ## Steps 1. Open **Shared** and use **By me**, status filters, and the file name to locate the delivered URL. 2. Select the row to inspect analytics when deciding whether delivery is complete. Review **Access log**, **Opens**, and **Downloads**; the log lists events newest first. 3. Confirm the displayed file name and link status. Do not revoke a similarly named active delivery. 4. On the web list, press the row's **Revoke share link** action; from analytics use **Revoke link**. In the mobile detail screen, tap **Revoke**. 5. Read the warning that every holder loses access immediately and the operation cannot be undone. 6. Confirm **Revoke**, then wait for **Link revoked — The share link no longer works.** on web or **Revoked** on mobile. 7. Open the old URL in a signed-out window. The recipient endpoint now returns `410 Gone`; creating another link later produces a different address. ## After revocation The recipient loses previews and downloads at once, even if the link had time or downloads remaining. The analytics record stays visible, the chart can mark the revoke date, and the access log survives. This retained record is why revocation should be used instead of deleting evidence after delivery. **Already revoked** with status 409 means another session completed the action first. **You don't have permission to revoke this share link** means the role lacks the necessary own-link or all-link access. **Associated resource not found** indicates that the target needed for authorization has been removed. A failed request does not change the link. ## Expected result The Shared record shows **Revoked**, its previous URL answers `410 Gone`, and earlier opens and downloads remain readable to members who still have permission to view that link's analytics. ## Related guides - [Create a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Add a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Send an updated sharing link after changing settings
summary: Edit a live link in the Dosya mobile app, preserve its URL, retest changed access rules, and tell existing recipients exactly what now applies.
verification: Locally reviewed against current source behavior on 2026-10-14; production deployment was not verified. Sources: apps/mobile/src/share/EditShareSheet.tsx, apps/mobile/src/share/api.ts, apps/mobile/src/share/payload.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/shares/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/apply-update.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/update.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/access.ts, apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts, apps/web/src/pages/shared.tsx.
body: The current mobile app can edit a live share in place; the web Shared page cannot. Saving keeps the same URL while replacing the selected settings. ## Steps 1. In the Dosya mobile app, open **Shares** → **Shared by me**, select the active link, choose **Edit**, and open **Edit this link**. The sheet states **The address stays the same. Changes apply the moment you save.** 2. Change only the intended controls: **Expires**, **Password**, **View only - no downloads**, **Who can open it**, or **Download limit**. This editor cannot add or remove invited addresses. 3. For a new password, enter at least 8 characters; leave the field blank to keep an existing password. Turning password off is refused when workspace policy requires one or when full-lock mode still applies. 4. When restricting access, the existing invited list must contain at least one address. Switching a restricted link to public clears that list, so mobile cannot re-restrict it; create a new email-restricted link when that boundary is needed again. A download limit must be at least the number already taken and no more than 10,000. 5. Choose **Save changes**. The same share token remains live; changing password resets its failed-unlock throttle, while switching to public access clears the previous recipient list. 6. Open the existing URL in a fresh private window and test the new gates and download behavior, then tell recipients what changed. A browser holding an earlier recipient or password grant can retain access for up to 30 minutes because the token is unchanged; use a clean session to test current rules. ## Expected result The existing URL applies the saved settings to fresh sessions and keeps its analytics.
