Previously granted browsers can retain token-bound recipient or password access for up to 30 minutes. **The current web app exposes copy, analytics, and revoke controls but no share-settings editor.** **Revoked links are terminal and cannot be edited back to active.** ## Related guides - [Create a link](/sharing/create-link) - [Audit delivery](/sharing/audit-delivery)

title: Check your sessions after resetting your password
summary: Confirm the new password and second factor work, then verify that the password reset removed every earlier browser and mobile session.
verification: Reviewed the current web reset form, password-reset API, browser and mobile credential revocation, two-factor challenge path and Sessions page against local product source and relevant tests on 2026-10-14. Screenshots use an isolated account.
keywords: sign out devices after password change
body: A completed Dosya password reset invalidates the account's earlier browser sessions and mobile access tokens. The reset browser receives a fresh session when no second factor is enrolled. Accounts with two-factor authentication must finish the verification challenge first. ## Before you start - Use the newest password-reset email and finish the reset on a device you trust. - Never send the reset URL, new password or two-factor code to another person. - Keep access to the account email and enrolled authenticator or email factor. - If you did not request the reset, stop and secure the email account before continuing. ## Steps: complete the reset and check the current session 1. Open the reset link and enter the new password twice. Follow every rule shown by the strength meter. 2. Select **Reset password** once. A reset link is single-use, so retrying the same link after success reports that it was already used. 3. If Dosya opens the two-factor page, enter the expected code. The password has already changed at this point; the code controls the new sign-in session. 4. If Dosya reports that the password changed but it could not send the verification code, return to sign in and use the new password to start a fresh challenge. 5. After access is restored, open **Profile → Sessions**. 6. Confirm that the current post-reset session is present and earlier browsers or phones are absent. The reset revokes them automatically. 7. Test one other device you previously used. It should require a new sign-in rather than opening the account from its old credential. ## Expected result The new password works, any required two-factor check completes, and the Sessions page contains only sessions created after the reset. Every older browser and mobile device must authenticate again. ## Limits and important details - Password reset revokes both browser sessions and mobile refresh credentials, including devices that were offline during the reset. - A two-factor account does not receive a full session until its second factor succeeds. - Changing a password does not rotate API keys or third-party integration credentials. Review those separately if they may be exposed. - A session can appear with an approximate device or location label. Use timing and your own activity as context. ## Troubleshooting **The new password works but Dosya asks for a code.** This is expected when two-factor authentication is enrolled. Complete the challenge using the configured method. **An old device still displays cached content.** Refresh it and try an authenticated action. The revoked credential should be refused even if an old screen remains visible. **You still see an unfamiliar new session.** Revoke it immediately, secure the email account and two-factor method, then contact private support with nonsecret timestamps and device labels. ## Related guides - [Reset your password](/account/reset-password) - [Review active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Use two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor)

title: Verify an email before signing in
summary: Complete Dosya email verification with the newest six-digit code, understand expiry and attempt limits, and recover when delivery fails safely.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/verify.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/auth/verify.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/auth/resend-verification.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/verification-lockout.ts. Production authentication was not attempted.
body: Password sign-in refuses an unverified account with **Please verify your email before signing in.** The verification page accepts the six-digit code sent to the pending address; each code expires after 10 minutes. ## Steps 1. Open **Verify your email** from sign-up or the verification link and confirm the displayed address. 2. Enter exactly six digits and select **Verify email**. Other input is blocked locally with **Enter the 6-digit code from your email.** 3. Use only the newest message. **Resend code** invalidates every older unused code, creates a fresh 10-minute code, and shows **A new code has been sent to your email.** 4. Wait at least 30 seconds between resends. An early request returns **Please wait Ns before requesting another code.** Resends are capped at 5 per IP address per hour. 5. One code permits 5 submitted attempts. Expired or missing challenges say **This code has expired. Request a new one.** or **No active verification code. Request a new one.** 6. Across new codes, failed guesses trigger account-wide locks: 10 misses for 15 minutes, 20 for 1 hour, and 30 or more for 24 hours. 7. If mail never arrives, inspect spam/quarantine, then use **Contact support** or **Use a different email**. Verification requests also have a 20-per-IP, 15-minute rate limit. A successful code is consumed and cannot be reused. ## Expected result Dosya marks the email verified, clears failed-verification lock state, creates a 30-day browser session, and clears the pending-email cookie. The verification API returns `/welcome`, but the web page first checks its stored post-auth path: a pending redemption continues to `/redeem`; without one, the browser opens **Welcome**. Later password sign-in no longer returns the unverified-email error. ## Related guides - [Reset your password](/account/reset-password) - [Understand sign-in methods](/account/identity-and-sign-in)

title: Find a missing password reset email
summary: Verify the account address, check filtered mail, respect the reset cooldown and request one current Dosya recovery message without exposing whether an account exists.
verification: Reviewed the current forgot-password page, generic success response, verified-email requirement, 10-minute resend cooldown, 30-minute token lifetime and reset email generation against local product source and relevant tests on 2026-10-14. The screenshot uses an isolated account.
body: Dosya always shows the same success message after a reset request, even when the address is unknown or unverified. This protects account privacy, so the message confirms only that the request was accepted, not that an email was sent. ## Before you start - Write the exact address normally used to sign in, including spelling and domain. - Check whether the account was created only with Google, Apple or another sign-in method. - Keep access to the inbox and its spam, junk, quarantine and forwarding rules. - Do not share screenshots containing a reset URL or email security details. ## Steps: locate or replace the reset email 1. Open **Forgot password**, enter the exact account email and complete the verification challenge. 2. Select **Send reset link** once. The page says that a link is on its way only if an account exists for that address. 3. Wait several minutes, then search all mail for the subject **Reset your dosya.dev password** and the `dosya.dev` sender domain. 4. Check spam, junk, promotions, focused or other inbox tabs, organization quarantine and mailbox rules. 5. Confirm that the address is verified. Dosya does not send password resets for an unverified account address. 6. Avoid repeated clicks. Dosya allows one reset email per account every 10 minutes and silently ignores faster requests while keeping the same privacy-preserving success message. 7. After 10 minutes, request one new message if none arrived. Open only the newest message because a new issued token invalidates older unused reset tokens. ## Expected result One current reset message reaches the correct verified inbox and opens the Dosya **Set a new password** page. The link remains private and is used before its 30-minute expiry. ## Limits and important details - Reset links expire after 30 minutes and are single-use. - The success screen cannot confirm whether an account exists for the entered address. - A mailbox provider can delay or quarantine delivery after Dosya accepts the request. - Support should never ask for the reset URL, password or two-factor code. ## Troubleshooting **You may have used another sign-in address.** Check password-manager records, prior Dosya notifications and the identity provider used at registration. Do not test addresses that belong to other people. **The message exists but the link is expired.** Wait until the cooldown has passed, request one replacement and use the newest email. **No message arrives after a correct, verified address and one careful retry.** Contact private support with the address, approximate request time and mailbox provider. Do not include the inbox password or any reset link. ## Related guides - [Reset your password](/account/reset-password) - [Replace an expired reset link](/account/signin-replace-expired-reset-link) - [Understand sign-in methods](/account/identity-and-sign-in)

title: Replace an expired password reset link
summary: Request one replacement after the cooldown, discard older reset messages and use the newest single-use link within its 30-minute lifetime.
verification: Reviewed the current forgot-password and reset-password pages, 30-minute token expiry, single-use enforcement, old-token invalidation, 10-minute resend cooldown and two-factor continuation against local product source and relevant tests on 2026-10-14. The screenshot uses an isolated account.
body: A Dosya password-reset link expires 30 minutes after it is issued and works only once. A newly issued reset token also invalidates older unused tokens for the same account. Replace an expired link instead of repeatedly reopening old messages. ## Before you start - Confirm that the error came from a `dosya.dev` reset page. - Keep the correct verified account email available. - Close old reset tabs and avoid copying their URLs into chat, notes or support requests. - Wait 10 minutes after the most recent reset request before asking for another message. ## Steps: request and use a replacement 1. From the expired-link message, follow **request a new one**, or open **Forgot password** directly. 2. Enter the exact account email and complete the verification challenge. 3. Select **Send reset link** once. Requests inside the 10-minute account cooldown return the normal success message but do not send another email. 4. Find the newest message with subject **Reset your dosya.dev password**. Compare delivery times and ignore every earlier reset message. 5. Open the newest link on a trusted device. Dosya reads the token into memory and removes it from the address bar to reduce accidental exposure. 6. Enter and confirm a strong new password, then submit the form once. 7. Complete the two-factor challenge if prompted. The reset is already complete before that challenge; the second factor authorizes the new session. ## Expected result The newest link opens the password form, the new password is accepted, and the token cannot be reused. Dosya signs the account in with a fresh session or continues to two-factor verification. ## Limits and important details - Expired, already-used and invalidated links cannot be reactivated. - Requesting another reset too soon does not extend the existing token or send a second message. - Resetting the password revokes earlier browser and mobile credentials. - If two-factor delivery fails after the reset, sign in normally with the new password to start another challenge. ## Troubleshooting **The newest message still says expired.** Verify its delivery time and the device clock, then wait for the cooldown and request one final replacement. **The link says it was already used.** Try signing in with the password set during that attempt. If it does not work, request a new link. **The form says the reset link is missing or invalid.** Open the full link directly from the email. A security product or manual copy may have removed its token fragment. ## Related guides - [Reset your password](/account/reset-password) - [Find a missing reset email](/account/signin-find-missing-reset-email) - [Use two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor)

title: Resolve an OAuth and password identity mismatch
summary: Resolve Dosya sign-in confusion between Google, GitHub, Apple, and passwords by identifying the account's original method and adding a password.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/login.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/profile/password.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/oauth-accounts.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/password.ts. Production authentication was not attempted.
body: An account created with Google, GitHub, or Apple initially has no usable Dosya password. Entering a guessed provider password produces the same **Invalid email or password** response as any failed password login. ## Steps 1. On **Log In**, use the provider you originally chose: **Continue with Google**, **Continue with GitHub**, or **Continue with Apple**. A **Last used** badge reflects only this browser's stored choice, not server-confirmed account history. 2. For provider errors, follow the exact banner. A missing email asks for a verified/public provider email and email access; cancellation says sign-in was cancelled; other failures offer another method. 3. After provider sign-in, open **Profile → Password & 2FA**. An OAuth-only account shows **Password — Not set** and **Set a password**. 4. Set a password of at least 8 characters. No current password is requested because none exists. Success reads **Password set — You can now sign in with your email and password too.** 5. On later visits, either the linked provider identity or the newly set email/password can reach the same Dosya account. 6. If the provider's email changes, its stable provider subject remains linked to the existing account. On first linkage, a canonical email match can attach the provider to an existing Dosya user. 7. Contact support before creating a second account when the provider returns a different identity or inaccessible relay address. Setting a password is a security change: the caller remains signed in and other browser/mobile credentials are revoked. It does not change the provider password. ## Expected result The original provider signs in to the intended Dosya account, and **Set a password** adds a second working method when desired. Workspace membership and files stay with the resolved account rather than moving between identities. ## Related guides - [Reset your password](/account/reset-password) - [Understand sign-in methods](/account/identity-and-sign-in)

title: Fixing a slow upload or download
summary: Compare a small transfer, check status and queue state, reduce competing work, and separate network delay from policy or storage failures.
verification: Reviewed the current English web transfer states, upload controls, public status path, region documentation and current web/API source on 2026-10-12. Existing isolated screenshots show the real queue labels and progress fields. Source and public documentation confirmed fixed workspace storage location, nearest-edge routing, multipart uploads, concurrency controls and server-side remote downloads. No production bandwidth benchmark or guaranteed speed was used; network throttling, VPN paths and service incidents vary by user and time.
body: Start by identifying the state, then compare one small transfer on the same device and connection. A **Queued** upload is waiting, an **Error** is a refusal or failure, and an active upload with slowly changing bytes is a speed problem. Check [Dosya service status](https://status.dosya.dev/) when several actions or devices fail at once. If status is healthy and one connection is affected, test the local network, browser and competing traffic before changing the workflow. ## Before you start - Keep the original upload source and any incomplete local download. - Record the filename, approximate size, start time and timezone, workspace, client and visible state or error. - Avoid repeatedly starting the same large transfer. Duplicate attempts compete for bandwidth and make the evidence harder to read. - Check [storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage), role permission and file policy when the transfer is refused. A quota or permission error is not slow throughput. - Use a harmless small file for comparison. Do not upload confidential data merely to run a speed test. ## Steps: identify what is slow 1. Open **Uploads** for an upload, or the browser's download indicator for a download. 2. Read the individual state. **Queued** is waiting for a slot; **Uploading** shows progress; **Error** names a cause; **Interrupted** needs recovery; **Canceled** was stopped. 3. Watch transferred bytes for a short interval. Movement indicates an active but possibly slow transfer. A percentage alone can pause while a part finishes or the service finalizes the file. 4. Compare a small file in the same workspace and direction. If the small transfer works, the connection may be usable but the original exposes duration, size or many-file overhead. 5. Compare upload and download separately. Home connections commonly have less upstream capacity, so a fast download does not prove that a large upload should be equally fast. ## Steps: separate network, client and service causes 1. Open [status.dosya.dev](https://status.dosya.dev/) in a separate tab. A matching incident across users or components points to the service; a healthy page does not prove every local route is healthy. 2. Pause unrelated cloud sync, streaming, backups and other large transfers. For web uploads, lower **Upload options → Simultaneous uploads** so fewer files share the connection. 3. Keep the device awake and the tab open. Reconnect a stable wired network when practical. Wi-Fi roaming, sleep, VPN reconnects and mobile/Wi-Fi handoffs can interrupt long requests. 4. Test without a VPN or proxy only when your organisation permits it. A corporate path can be the cause, but bypassing a required control is not an appropriate test. 5. Try another current browser or the desktop/CLI workflow with the same harmless sample. A result that follows one client points to that client; a result that follows the connection points to the network. 6. If the source already has a direct public download URL, consider Dosya's **Remote download** integration. It fetches server to server and can continue without routing the file through your device. ## Steps: handle many small files 1. Check whether the slow task contains thousands of small files. Each item needs listing, policy and transfer work even when the total byte size is modest. 2. When your workflow permits, archive the folder locally and upload one archive. Keep the original folder until you verify the archive and destination. 3. For repeat sync or automation, use the desktop app, CLI, rclone, WebDAV or S3 workflow appropriate to the job. Tune concurrency conservatively and respect any credential allowance. 4. Verify the final contents. Faster transfer is not useful if archiving changed required metadata or made collaboration impractical. ## Expected result You can classify the issue as waiting for a slot, active but bandwidth-limited, interrupted, refused by policy or quota, specific to one client/network, or consistent with a service incident. The controlled small transfer and status evidence give support something concrete to investigate. No single test establishes a guaranteed speed. Throughput changes with the source device, local upstream or downstream capacity, route, competing traffic, file count, protocol and destination response. ## Limits and region behavior - A workspace's storage location is chosen at creation and fixed. Existing files are not moved by selecting or creating another workspace. - Uploads and downloads travel through the nearest Cloudflare edge before reaching the workspace's storage location. Storage residency and the network route are separate. - Creating a workspace in another region does not make an existing transfer move or become faster. It creates a separate storage destination for new files. - Multipart upload makes a dropped connection cheaper to recover; it cannot make a slow upstream connection exceed its available bandwidth. - Free API, WebDAV and S3 credentials and public share links have documented fair-use allowances. A rate-limit or allowance response needs its reset or policy action, not a speed tweak. Ordinary signed-in web behavior should be diagnosed from its own message. - Dosya does not promise a completion time for a particular file or connection. ## Troubleshooting **An upload remains Queued.** Check active rows and **Simultaneous uploads**. The workspace can impose a lower concurrent-upload limit. A waiting item is not consuming upload bandwidth yet. **A transfer is active but barely moves.** Stop competing traffic, keep the device awake, try a stable wired path and compare a small sample. Record bytes moved over a measured interval rather than describing it only as “slow.” **Every page and transfer fails.** Check service status and another network if available. Record the affected components and time. Do not keep retrying a destructive or paid action during an incident. **Only uploads are slow.** Measure the connection's upstream capacity and check other upload traffic. Consumer connections often provide much less upload bandwidth than download bandwidth. **Only one large file is affected.** Check remaining storage, workspace maximum file size, file-type policy and the row's message. See [Uploading large files](/uploading/large-files) and [failed-upload recovery](/troubleshooting/failed-upload). **A new region seems faster in a test.** Treat it as a different workspace and a different test, not a migration or guarantee. The original workspace and files remain in their fixed location, and normal route variation can affect one measurement. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does changing my workspace region make an existing upload faster? No. A workspace's location is fixed, so an existing transfer does not move. A new workspace is a different destination. Dosya already routes transfers through the nearest edge independently of storage residency. ### How do I tell a network issue from a service incident? Compare service status, another connection or device, and one small transfer. A matching multi-user incident points to the service; a problem that follows one network or client points locally. Preserve the time and exact state for support. ### Should I increase simultaneous uploads? Only when the connection has spare capacity and the workspace allows it. Lower concurrency is often more stable for one large file; higher concurrency can help many small files but can also make each one slower. ## Related guides - [Understanding upload progress and transfer states](/uploading/progress-and-states) - [Uploading large files with available storage](/uploading/large-files) - [Downloading one file or several files](/uploading/download-files) - [Troubleshooting a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Understanding storage usage and failed quota checks](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Sort files by name, size or date
summary: Sort Files with six toolbar presets or a visible table column, understand first-click direction, and verify ordering without changing stored files.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/list-sort.ts, apps/api/src/lib/list-sort.ts, and apps/web/src/lib/file-columns.tsx on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Sorting changes the order returned for the active standard Files view; it does not rename, move, or rewrite stored items. Standard folder, Deleted, and group views offer six toolbar presets, while list view can sort by any visible supported column. The photo Library uses its own sort state and choices. **Available preset labels.** Outside the photo Library, the toolbar supports **Newest**, **Oldest**, **Name A–Z**, **Name Z–A**, **Largest**, and **Smallest**. The default is newest-created first. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** and enter the standard folder, Deleted view, or group you want to order. Apply search first if the sort should cover only matching results. 2. Open the sort menu beside the search box and choose one of its six presets. The choice lives only in the current page state: refreshing the page or sharing its URL returns the standard view to **Newest**. 3. For another field, switch to list view, choose **Columns**, and enable the column. Supported headers include Type, Extension, Version, Uploader, Region, Origin, Shares, and Comments. 4. Select a column header once. Text fields begin ascending; sizes, dates, version numbers, shares, and comment counts begin descending. 5. Select the same header again to reverse it. The arrow beside the active header shows the current direction, and the toolbar displays a synthetic label such as **Uploader ↑**. 6. Check the first and last rows, comparing folders and files within their own sections because folders remain pinned above files. **Special date labels.** In Deleted items, the normal Modified column is presented as **Deleted** and uses deletion time. Photo libraries use Date taken based on captured time, then source-created time, then upload time. The Library layout has separate sort choices and loading state, so the six standard presets above do not describe it. ## Expected result The active arrow or sort label states the chosen field and direction, and rows within each folder/file section follow that order. No file metadata or bytes change merely because the list was sorted. ## Related guides - [Narrow the Files list with search](/files/search-files) - [Organize files into a durable structure](/files/organize-files)

title: Understanding storage usage and failed quota checks
summary: Read the active workspace’s storage total, account for retained versions and trash, and choose a safe cleanup or capacity action.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/dashboard.tsx, apps/web/src/components/layout/dashboard-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/upload-limits.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/purge-trash.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/trim-versions.ts, apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts, and their quota and retention tests. Screenshots use an isolated fictional 5 GB fixture; production billing data was not accessed.
body: The storage indicator describes the active workspace, while its owner's entitlement is one pool shared by every workspace that person owns. The server accepts new bytes only when both the account pool and the active workspace have enough room. A **Storage per member** limit can narrow that answer again. Every retained file version counts at its full stored size. Items in **Deleted** also consume quota so they can be restored. Automatic trash retention is **7 days** for an effectively Free owner and **30 days** for a paid owner; manual **Delete permanently** ends recovery earlier. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace name. Switching workspaces changes the sidebar and dashboard figures you are viewing. - Keep a copy of anything you may need. Permanent deletion and expired retention cannot be undone through the restore workflow. - Record the exact upload error before clearing its queue row. - Check **Billing** for the current plan, add-ons and grants. The source fallback for Free is **5 GB**, but the live catalog and account-specific entitlements determine the amount shown to you. - Ask an owner or admin about **Hard limits** when you cannot view workspace settings. ## Steps: inspect the active workspace 1. Read **Storage** at the bottom of the sidebar. It shows used and effective total capacity for the active workspace. 2. Open **Dashboard** and find **Storage used** and **Storage breakdown**. 3. Note any explicit amount **in trash**. Deleted items remain restorable because they still occupy storage. 4. Compare the category bars with the total. The bars group current and trashed bytes by type; retained historical versions can make the total exceed the sum you estimate from current filenames. 5. If the workspace belongs to a team, review **Team usage** and any per-member storage policy. Your own visible files may not be the only use of the pool. ## Steps: identify which limit refused the upload 1. Read the upload row's complete error in **Uploads → Upload queue**. 2. If it says you have used the plan capacity **across all your workspaces**, check every workspace you own. A nearly empty active workspace can still be blocked by account-wide usage elsewhere. 3. If it names **this workspace** and a storage limit, ask an owner or admin to review **Settings → Hard limits → Total workspace storage cap**. 4. If it names a member limit, review **Storage per member** and which member uploaded the retained data. 5. If it names a maximum file size or blocked type, storage cleanup will not resolve that different policy. Follow the stated rule. 6. After correcting the applicable limit, retry the failed row once while the original file is still available. ## Steps: free storage safely 1. **Review current files first.** Download or otherwise preserve anything required by your retention policy. 2. **Review version history.** Open a file's menu and choose **Version history**. The workspace keeps at most **10 versions per file** by default unless its setting uses another positive cap or unlimited mode. Free-plan versions older than **7 days** are also eligible for pruning, while the newest version is always retained. 3. **Review Deleted.** Open **Files → Deleted**. Ordinary Delete moved these items to trash and did not free their bytes. 4. **Restore mistakes before purging.** A restore does not need extra quota because the trashed bytes never left the storage count. 5. **Permanently delete only verified items.** Use **Delete permanently** for selected trash items when immediate removal is intended. The purge removes the stored versions and releases their measured bytes; it cannot be reversed through Dosya. 6. Refresh the workspace figures after cleanup settles. If policy requires keeping the data, add capacity or have an owner adjust a tighter workspace allocation instead of deleting it. ## Expected result You can reconcile the active workspace's current files, retained versions and trash with the storage total, then identify whether the upload was blocked by account capacity, a workspace cap, a member limit or a different file policy. After a successful permanent purge or capacity change, the relevant headroom increases and a permitted upload can start. A normal download can remain available while uploads are blocked because reading an existing file does not add stored bytes. ## Limits and accounting behavior - The owner's plan entitlement is account-wide across workspaces they own. An explicit workspace cap limits that workspace further; it does not create extra plan storage or reserve bytes from sibling workspaces. - Every retained version counts. Uploading a new version adds the full size of that version, rather than only the difference from the previous version. - Soft-deleted files and folders count until permanent purge. This guarantees that restoring them does not need capacity that may have been reused meanwhile. - Scheduled retention removes Free-plan versions older than 7 days while always preserving the newest. Trash becomes eligible after 7 days on Free or 30 days on paid plans; the daily job does not promise deletion at an exact minute. - Workspace storage hints and quota rows can be cached for up to **60 seconds**. Refresh after a purge completes, but do not create duplicate cleanup actions during that window. - Cached previews and transfer fragments are implementation details. Use the product's storage figure and exact refusal rather than estimating from local filenames alone. - Storage capacity is separate from daily transfer or request allowances. Free plan protocol and share-link limits can pause transfer without saying the storage is full. ## Troubleshooting **The dashboard total is larger than my current files.** Check retained versions, Deleted, other team members and other file categories. Historical versions and trash can explain bytes that are not visible in the main live-file list. **I deleted files but storage did not fall.** Ordinary **Delete** moves them to Deleted, where they still count. Use **Delete permanently** only after verification, then allow up to the quota cache window before assuming the counter is stale. **The active workspace looks empty but the error says all workspaces.** The owner's plan is shared across owned workspaces. Switch through those workspaces and inspect their storage, versions and trash. **I can download but cannot upload.** A download reads an existing object; an upload needs new capacity and passes workspace policy checks. Read the upload refusal for the limiting condition. **The file is smaller than the displayed free space but is refused.** Check the account-wide headroom, workspace total cap, per-member storage, maximum file size and file-type rules. The smallest applicable headroom wins. **Permanent deletion completed but the value still looks wrong.** Refresh once after the operation settles and confirm the active workspace. Record the time, workspace, deleted items and current figures, then [contact support](/troubleshooting/contact-support) without sending private file contents. **The refusal says the workspace has a limit.** The exact form is `This workspace has a N GB storage limit and this doesn't fit.` An owner or a role holding **Change total storage cap** can raise that value only within the owner's unallocated entitlement. **The message mentions all your workspaces.** That wording identifies the owner account pool. Deleting data from the active workspace helps, but bytes in another owned workspace, its versions, and its Deleted area also consume the same entitlement. ## Frequently asked questions ### Do old versions count toward storage? Yes. Every retained version counts by its full stored size until version pruning or permanent file purge removes it. ### Do deleted files count toward storage? Yes while they remain in Deleted. Their bytes are released when the items are permanently purged, either by an authorized action or the applicable retention process. ### Why can I download files but not upload more? Downloading reads data already stored. Uploading adds bytes and is refused when the account, workspace, member or file policy would be exceeded. ### Does restoring a deleted file need free space? No additional storage reservation is needed for the restore because the trashed file continued counting while it was deleted. ### When does deleted data stop counting? Immediately after an authorized permanent purge updates the measured usage, or when the scheduled retention job purges an eligible item. Moving a file to Deleted alone does not reduce the count. ## Related guides - [Understanding Free-plan allowances](/account/free-plan-allowances) - [Uploading large files with available storage](/uploading/large-files) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Using version history](/files/version-history) - [Restoring a deleted file or folder](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Share diagnostics with Dosya support safely
summary: Prepare reproducible steps, timestamps, client details, IDs, redacted logs, and screenshots without exposing credentials, private links, or file content.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/support.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/support-ticket.tsx; apps/web/src/components/support/attach-images.tsx; apps/web/src/components/support/report-problem-dialog.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/support/tickets/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/support/tickets/[id]/reply.ts; apps/api/src/lib/support.ts; apps/help/src/content/articles/contact-support.md; apps/help/src/content/articles/suspicious-activity.md. No ticket was submitted. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Support needs enough detail to reproduce and correlate a failure, but it does not need an authentication secret or an entire private file. Build the report around one action, one time window and the smallest evidence that shows the result. ## Steps Check [status.dosya.dev](https://status.dosya.dev/) first when several product areas fail together. Reproduce the action once only when doing so cannot duplicate a payment, invitation, deletion, upload, webhook job, public link or external message. Record: - the task, ordered steps, expected result and actual result; - date, local time and timezone, plus the last known successful time; - Dosya surface and version: browser, mobile, desktop, CLI, API, S3, SFTP, WebDAV or integration; - operating system and relevant client/runtime version; - active workspace name/ID and affected nonsecret resource ID when safe; - exact error text, HTTP/SFTP status, CLI exit code or request/delivery/job identifier; - whether the problem happens every time and what safe checks already ran. Use a disposable item where possible. For a confidential file failure, start with its type, approximate size, destination and policy result rather than attaching the source. ## Remove secrets and private capabilities Never include a Dosya password, email verification code, authenticator code, recovery code, session cookie, bearer token, API key, S3 secret, webhook signing secret, Vault passphrase/recovery key, payment-card number/security code, or private share/file-request URL. A signed download URL, OAuth authorization code and private link token grant access even though they do not look like a password. Redact query strings and fragments from URLs. In an HTTP request, remove `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `X-Dosya-Signature` and other credential headers before sharing. Replace secret values with labels such as `[API KEY REDACTED]`; do not leave the first or last characters visible. If a credential was already posted, rotate or revoke it immediately, then tell support what type was exposed and when. Editing a later ticket message does not guarantee that copies outside the visible conversation never existed. ## Crop logs and screenshots Include only lines around the failing request. Preserve the exact error, status, operation, timestamp and nonsecret ID, while removing environment dumps, authorization headers, local usernames, home-directory paths, unrelated filenames, email addresses and payload/file contents. The ticket attachment control accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF. Each image must be under 5 MB, and one message can contain at most three images. Crop to the relevant control and error before uploading. A screen recording, archive, document or arbitrary failing source file is not accepted by that image control; describe it and wait for an approved private transfer method. ## Create and review the private ticket 1. In the signed-in web app, open the profile menu and choose **Get help**. 2. Select **New ticket** and the closest category, such as **Technical issue**. 3. Use a subject naming the action and result. The subject limit is 200 characters. 4. Enter the reproduction and evidence. The description limit is 10,000 characters. 5. Attach at most three redacted supported images, each below 5 MB. 6. Read the complete draft again, including filenames and visible browser address bars, then select **Create ticket** once. The created conversation appears under **Open**. Add later evidence to the same ticket so timestamps and replies remain together; do not create duplicates merely to ask for an update. **Report a bug** is a separate structured-diagnostics flow. Review what it will send before submission, and use **New ticket** for an account-specific support conversation. ## Diagnostic examples by surface | Problem | Useful evidence | Exclude | | --- | --- | --- | | Upload/download | File type, approximate bytes, workspace/folder, transfer state, network change, exact error | Original confidential bytes, signed download URL, cookies | | Sharing/request | Creation/open/download stage, expiry, recipient/browser, request/share ID if safe | Public token, password/access code, recipient private data not needed for diagnosis | | MCP/OAuth | Client/version, server URL, consent stage, workspace, tool and exact nonsecret response | Access/refresh token, authorization code, exposed file text | | API/S3/SFTP/CLI | Method/operation, client version, endpoint/port, status/code, time, redacted request ID | Key, secret, Authorization header, complete private object path | | Mobile backup | Platform/app version, Backup label, permission scope, policy, workspace, item type/size | Photo contents, full library listing, device backup credentials | | Billing/account | Plan, invoice date, last four digits only when requested, sign-in method, displayed error | Full card number, security code, password, 2FA/recovery values | ## Expected result Search the draft and attachments for `dos_`, `DOSYA`, `whsec_`, `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `token=`, `code=`, long query strings, QR codes and private URLs. Confirm the time includes a timezone and the report identifies one concrete failing operation. Keep the resulting ticket reference. A legitimate support response does not need your password, two-factor code, Vault recovery key or complete API/S3 secret. If a reply requests one, do not provide it; use the existing signed-in support conversation to question the request and secure any credential already disclosed. ## Related guides - [Contact support](/troubleshooting/contact-support) - [Respond to suspicious activity](/account/suspicious-activity) - [Recover Vault access](/files/vault-recovery)

title: Responding to suspicious account activity
summary: Contain an unfamiliar sign-in or account change by securing email, changing the password, revoking sessions and keys, reviewing activity and contacting support.
verification: Reviewed current password, session, API-key, workspace activity and private-support controls against the local current app and related automated tests on 2026-10-12. This is a containment workflow, not a guarantee of forensic completeness. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: If a sign-in, password-reset message, API action or workspace change is unfamiliar, secure the account from a trusted device. Preserve useful details without delaying containment or exposing secrets. ## Before you start - Use a device you trust and secure the email account connected to Dosya. - Record the time, visible action and affected workspace or resource. Do not copy passwords, one-time codes, recovery codes, API-key secrets or private links. - If you cannot sign in, use the password and second-factor recovery guides first. ## Steps: contain the account 1. Change the Dosya password from **Profile → Password & 2FA**. If locked out, request a password reset. 2. Confirm two-factor authentication is enabled and replace recovery codes if they may have been exposed. 3. Open **Profile → Sessions**. Identify the current session and revoke every unfamiliar device. Use the revoke-others action when appropriate. 4. Open **Profile → API keys**. Revoke keys you do not recognize and rotate any key stored on a lost device or exposed system. 5. Review connected integrations and AI apps. Disconnect anything unfamiliar. 6. For each important workspace, open **Activity** and filter around the relevant time, member and action. 7. Check members, invitation links, share links and file requests for unexpected access. 8. Contact private support with redacted evidence when the source or impact is unclear. ## Expected result Unfamiliar sessions and credentials no longer provide access. New sign-ins require the changed password and current second factor. Workspace activity and current resource state give you a bounded view of recorded actions to include in a support case. ## Limits and investigation boundaries - Session revocation does not revoke API keys, and API-key revocation does not end browser sessions. - Password changes do not undo file, link, member or settings changes already completed. - The activity log records supported events and metadata; it is not a file-content inspection tool or complete forensic guarantee. - IP geolocation can reflect a VPN, proxy, carrier or corporate gateway. - Vault keys and unlock state have separate recovery and destruction boundaries. - Never post incident evidence containing private URLs, IP addresses or account identifiers publicly. ## Troubleshooting **I cannot access the account.** Secure the email inbox, reset the password and use a saved recovery code if authenticator 2FA is enabled. **I lost a device.** Revoke its session, rotate keys stored on it, disconnect integrations it authorized and review recent workspace activity. **An unfamiliar member joined.** Revoke active invitation links, remove the member, review role and folder changes, and preserve the activity timestamps. **Files or settings changed.** Use the appropriate restore or administration workflow. The activity log itself does not reverse changes. **Support needs evidence.** Provide the approximate time, account email, workspace name, action, outcome and any request or session ID through [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support). Keep all secrets out of the ticket. ## Related guides - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions) - [API key management](/developers/api-key) - [Reading workspace activity and audit details](/workspaces/activity) - [Contacting support with useful information](/troubleshooting/contact-support)

title: Switch between workspaces safely
summary: Change the active Dosya workspace, confirm its name and role, and avoid uploading, sharing or changing settings in the wrong workspace.
verification: Reviewed the workspace switcher, active-workspace state and dashboard transition against the local current web app on 2026-10-12. The screenshot uses two isolated representative workspaces.
body: The active workspace controls which files, uploads, members, integrations, policies and storage figure the web app shows. Switching changes that context; it does not move or combine files. ## Before you start - Finish any action whose destination is already fixed, especially an upload or settings form. - Know the name of the workspace you intend to use. - If you have similar workspace names, identify a known file, member or storage figure you can check after switching. - Remember that your role can differ between workspaces, so their menus may not match. ## Steps: switch to another workspace 1. Select the current workspace name at the top of the left sidebar. 2. Under **Your workspaces**, find the intended name. A check marks the workspace currently active. 3. Select the intended workspace. 4. Wait for the workspace transition to finish and the dashboard to load. 5. Confirm the new workspace name above the sidebar. 6. Before uploading or sharing, open **Files** and check a known folder or file. Before changing policies, open **Settings** and confirm the workspace name there too. ## Expected result The selected workspace name appears above the sidebar, its dashboard loads and workspace pages show only the data your membership can reach there. Returning to the previous workspace shows its files again. ## Limits and workspace boundaries - Switching does not copy, move or delete a file. - Search, storage usage, Files, Shared, Team, Integrations and workspace Settings follow the active workspace. - A role or folder restriction can hide menu entries and files in one workspace even when you can see them in another. - Account-wide profile and security settings continue to apply to your signed-in account. - A transfer already queued for a destination does not become a safe cross-workspace move merely because you switch the visible workspace. ## Troubleshooting **Files appear to be missing.** Read the workspace name above the sidebar. Switch back to the workspace where the files were uploaded and check **Files** there. **A menu entry disappeared.** Compare your role in the two workspaces. The new workspace may grant fewer page or folder permissions. **The switcher does not list a workspace.** Confirm that you are still a member and signed in to the expected account. An owner may have removed the membership or an invitation may still be pending. **The page keeps showing old data.** Wait for the workspace transition, then open the destination from the sidebar. If the name changes but the page remains stale, reload once and check service status. **You uploaded to the wrong workspace.** Keep the source file, verify the completed copy, and upload it to the correct workspace. Do not assume switching will relocate the existing copy; remove the mistaken copy only when you have permission and have confirmed the correct result. ## Related guides - [Find your way around the web app](/account/navigate-web-app) - [Upload files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Create and test a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Create a workspace and choose its storage location](/workspaces/create-and-choose-region)

title: Find text inside a Dosya text file
summary: Find a term inside the CodeMirror text editor, move among matches without invoking Files shortcuts, and leave the document unchanged until saved.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/text-editor.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/text-detect.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya’s browser text editor uses CodeMirror `basicSetup`, which includes its search panel. Searching changes the selection and viewport only; it does not create a version. **Before searching.** The editor’s **Edit** button appears only for a recognized text name or MIME type, a file no larger than 2 MiB, and a file that is not in `full_lock` mode. ## Steps 1. Open the text file in Files and choose **Edit** in the viewer header. Wait until the filename bar and editable document appear. 2. Click inside the document, then press Ctrl+F on Windows/Linux or Command+F on macOS. Keeping focus in the editor prevents the Files page from treating shortcuts as list actions. 3. Enter a distinctive word or phrase in the CodeMirror search panel. Use exact punctuation or case options only when the panel exposes and you need them. 4. Move to the next or previous match with the panel controls or its displayed shortcuts. Watch the active selection in the document rather than relying on the browser page-search counter. 5. If there are no matches, shorten the term and check whitespace, punctuation, or the version currently open. Selecting an older Versions row changes the previewed source before Edit is opened. 6. Close the search panel when finished. Choose the editor’s close button if you only inspected text; choose **Save version** only when you intentionally changed content. **Do not confuse the two searches.** **Search files…** filters filenames and metadata in the Files list. Ctrl/Command+F after the editor has focus searches the loaded document. The browser’s own page find may appear if focus is outside CodeMirror. ## Expected result The editor moves between occurrences of the search term while the file remains unchanged. No new version is created unless you alter the document and explicitly choose **Save version**. ## Related guides - [Edit supported text in the browser](/files/edit-text) - [Review versions before changing content](/files/version-history)

title: Open a text file in the Dosya editor
summary: Open a supported text file of 2 MiB or less in Dosya’s CodeMirror editor, choose the intended preview version, and recognize unavailable states.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/text-editor.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/text-detect.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Text preview and text editing use the same readable-type detector, but **Edit** adds two gates: the file must be 2 MiB or smaller and cannot have a full file lock. **Recognized text.** Dosya accepts common plain text, Markdown, JSON, YAML, CSV/TSV, XML, HTML/CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, SQL, shell, configuration, subtitle, and source-code extensions. It also recognizes text MIME types and extensionless names such as `README`, `LICENSE`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, and `.env`. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, select the filename to open its viewer. Choose **Latest** before editing current content, or deliberately select an older version when you intend to use its bytes as the editor starting point. 2. Check that the viewer renders text rather than an unsupported-file card. Text preview refuses content over 2 MiB and reports that the file is too large to preview. 3. Look for **Edit** in the viewer header. The control is absent for files over 2 MiB and for a file whose own lock mode is `full_lock`. 4. Choose **Edit**. Dosya fetches the raw bytes for the version currently selected in the preview, including a historical version, then initializes CodeMirror with line wrapping. 5. Confirm the full-screen editor header, including the same filename and **Save version**. Recognized languages load syntax support; other readable files use plain text. 6. If the editor closes, read the toast. **Editor unavailable** means loading failed; refresh the preview and retry once. **Encoding note.** Preview recognizes UTF-16 little-endian and big-endian byte-order marks. The editor itself loads the response as text through the browser, so preserve a separate local copy before editing an encoding-sensitive file. ## Expected result The CodeMirror editor opens with the bytes from the intended preview version and exposes **Save version**. If it cannot load, it closes without creating a version and reports the explicit Editor unavailable message. ## Related guides - [Use Dosya’s text editing workflow](/files/edit-text) - [Inspect the file’s version timeline](/files/version-history)

title: Save changes to a text file
summary: Save browser text edits as a new version, interpret Saving and failure messages, and confirm the latest content after the editor closes safely.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/text-editor.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/text-detect.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The text editor never mutates the existing version in place. **Save version** uploads the complete edited document against the same file ID and then closes the editor after success. **Required access.** You need workspace membership, Files access, `upload_files`, a writable destination, and enough plan/workspace storage. Upload extension policy, per-file size, member allowance, concurrency, hidden scope, and locked-backup rules still apply to this save. ## Steps 1. Open a supported file with **Edit** and make the smallest intended change. The editor wraps long lines but does not imply they were reformatted. 2. Re-read the surrounding lines. Dosya sends the whole editor document, not a patch, so unintended deletions elsewhere would be included. 3. Choose **Save version** once. The button becomes disabled and reads **Saving…** while the upload-init request and file PUT run. 4. Keep the tab open until the operation finishes. Closing or navigating away before success can discard the unsaved browser state. 5. On success, expect **Saved — File saved as new version.** The editor closes, the viewer refreshes, and the Versions count increases. 6. Reopen the file and check both the changed text and the newest Versions row. If the toast says **Save failed**, keep a local copy of the draft before retrying. **Failure wording.** Initialization may surface a server message or `Could not start upload`. The byte upload can report `Failed to save`. Other request failures appear under **Save failed** with the API error. A failed attempt does not display the success toast and keeps the editor open where the component can recover. ## Expected result The edited text appears in the latest file preview, a new version row preserves the prior bytes, and the file keeps its original ID and name. A failed save leaves no claimed success and provides a message to investigate. ## Related guides - [Learn which text files can be edited](/files/edit-text) - [Open and inspect version history](/files/version-history)

title: Troubleshoot a text file that will not open for editing
summary: Diagnose a missing Edit control or Editor unavailable toast using the 2 MiB limit, type detection, lock state, raw access, and upload rules.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/text-editor.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/text-detect.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Two failures look similar but have different causes: a missing **Edit** button means the file is ineligible, while **Editor unavailable** means an eligible editor failed while loading its raw content or modules. ## Steps 1. Confirm the file size in **Details**. Text preview and Edit use an exact ceiling of 2 × 1024 × 1024 bytes; a larger file must be downloaded and edited locally. 2. Check the filename extension or MIME type. Unsupported binary formats do not receive the text editor even if their name contains readable characters. 3. Check the file’s own lock mode. A `full_lock` file has no text **Edit** control even after a valid password unlock. 4. If **Edit** is present, select it once. A failed authenticated raw fetch or CodeMirror/language-module load produces **Editor unavailable — Could not open the text editor.** and closes the overlay. 5. Refresh the viewer and retry after restoring connectivity. If normal preview also fails, test **Download**; access, hidden-item, ancestor-lock, or file-not-found gates may be blocking the raw bytes. 6. If opening succeeds but saving fails, treat that separately. **Save failed** can reflect `upload_files`, storage, extension policy, concurrency, destination, or locked-backup rules. **Full-lock rule.** Unlocking grants byte access without changing the stored `full_lock` mode, and the editor always excludes that mode. If authorized, remove or change the full lock before reopening the viewer; otherwise download the file and edit it locally. **What the UI does not diagnose.** The Editor unavailable toast intentionally collapses fetch and initialization failures into one message. It does not claim the file is corrupt, and there is no cache-reset button in the editor. ## Expected result You either open the file in CodeMirror or identify the exact eligibility gate: unsupported text classification, more than 2 MiB, an unchanged full file lock, byte-access failure, or a transient editor-load problem. ## Related guides - [Edit readable text files](/files/edit-text) - [Use version history after a save problem](/files/version-history)

title: Recover from a text edit conflict
summary: Protect browser text edits when another version may have landed: preserve the draft, reopen the newest content, merge deliberately, and save once.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/components/text-editor.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/text-detect.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The current web text editor does not send `expected_version` when it starts a save. Therefore it has no dedicated “version conflict” dialog and cannot prove that nobody uploaded another version after you opened the editor. ## Steps 1. Stop editing as soon as you learn a colleague or another client saved the same file. Do not press **Save version** yet. 2. Copy the full draft to a local editor or secure temporary file. The Dosya overlay keeps its document only in browser memory. 3. Close the editor, reopen the file, and inspect **Versions**. The top row marked **Latest** is the current content; selecting older rows changes the preview but not the file. 4. Open **Edit** again from the refreshed latest preview. Compare the saved draft with this newest document and reapply only the intended changes. 5. Choose **Save version** once and wait for **Saved — File saved as new version.** If any save fails, preserve the merged draft before another reload. 6. Reopen **Versions** and inspect the new **Latest** row, confirming it contains the accepted changes and your merged edits. **Why this manual path matters.** The upload API supports an `expected_version` field and can reject stale clients with `409 version_conflict`, but `apps/web/src/components/text-editor.tsx` currently sends only workspace ID, file ID, filename, size, and MIME type. A browser save can therefore append over a newer current version without an automatic warning. **Recovery after an accidental save.** Previous bytes remain in append-only version history. Preview the preceding revision, compare it with the new latest row, and either merge forward or use Restore, which creates another new version rather than deleting history. ## Expected result The final latest version contains the consciously merged document, both prior revisions remain visible, and you did not depend on a conflict warning that the current web editor does not provide. ## Related guides - [Edit text with the current browser controls](/files/edit-text) - [Use append-only file version history](/files/version-history)

title: Permanently delete selected test items
summary: Permanently delete selected trash roots, understand folder progress and cancellation, verify partial outcomes, and confirm that recovery is impossible.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **Delete permanently** removes selected trash roots and their stored bytes. It is irreversible, and a large folder can be emptied over several bounded requests before its folder row disappears. ## Steps 1. Open **Files** and choose **Deleted**. Confirm each selected row is a top-level deleted item; descendants swept into a deleted folder are handled through that parent. 2. Select the disposable files and folders. Compare the separate file and folder counts in the confirmation, and note any Live Photo companion count. 3. Choose **Delete permanently**. Read `This cannot be undone.` A selected folder also permanently removes everything still inside it. 4. Confirm **Delete permanently** once. Individual file purges run with bounded concurrency. Folder purges may show `N files removed so far…` while repeated server passes continue. 5. To stop a long permanent batch, use the progress dialog’s cancel action. Requests already in flight may still finish, and a partially emptied folder remains in Deleted items. 6. Read the result toast before selecting anything else. It distinguishes completed items, failed items, unfinished folders, and files already removed before a failure or cancellation. **Common refusals.** Locked files, locked descendants, hidden scope, missing delete permission, a folder deleted as part of another folder, or a member confined inside the folder can block a purge. For the last case, change that member’s folder access before trying again. ## Expected result Completed file rows and fully emptied folder roots disappear from Deleted items and cannot be restored. Any cancelled, unfinished, or refused root stays visible with its remaining contents so its exact outcome can be reviewed. ## Related guides - [Review entries in Deleted items](/files/review-deleted-items) - [Restore a deleted item instead](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Move a file to Deleted items
summary: Move one file to Deleted items, include or exclude its Live Photo companion, understand storage impact, and verify the reversible soft-delete result.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Deleting a live file is a soft delete: its row leaves the normal folder and enters **Deleted**, while its bytes continue using workspace storage until a permanent deletion. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, locate the exact live file and inspect its name, folder, and details. A role needs `delete_any_file`, or `delete_own_files` when it uploaded the item. 2. Open the row menu or viewer menu and choose **Delete**. A locked file, a file inside an unlocked-required folder, or content in a locked WordPress backup is refused. 3. In **Delete file?**, verify the filename. Dosya states that the item moves to trash and keeps using storage until permanently deleted. 4. For a Live Photo still, decide whether to leave **Also delete [video name]** selected. The companion is a separate cloud file even when the library presents the pair together. 5. Choose **Delete** once and wait for **Deleted — [name] was deleted.** The confirm button is disabled while the request runs to prevent a second click from purging the just-trashed item. 6. Open **Deleted** and find the row. The original folder should no longer list it, while Restore and Delete permanently become the available destructive-state actions. **If deletion fails.** The API can report `This file is locked and cannot be deleted`, `This file is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to delete it.`, or `You don't have permission to delete this file`. Correct that gate instead of repeatedly confirming. ## Expected result The selected file disappears from its live folder, appears in Deleted items, and remains recoverable. Storage usage does not fall at this stage because soft-deleted bytes are still retained. ## Related guides - [Restore a file from Deleted items](/files/restore-deleted) - [Understand irreversible permanent deletion](/files/permanently-delete-files)

title: Move a folder to Deleted items
summary: Move a folder subtree to Deleted items, understand permission and lock checks, revoked links, retained storage, and permanent-delete boundaries.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/desktop/src/renderer/pages/FileBrowserPage.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/batch-delete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.ts, and folder trash tests. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Deleting a live folder normally moves its authorized subtree to **Deleted**. It is recoverable until someone explicitly purges that trash root; Dosya does not automatically expire folder trash. ## Before you start - A folder you created uses `delete_own_files`; a folder created by another member needs `delete_any_file`. Every live descendant must also pass the applicable ownership and lock rules. - Direct `view_only` or `full_lock`, an un-unlocked ancestor, a locked descendant file, or a protected WordPress backup can block deletion. - Folder-confined members can delete only within their assigned subtree. - Deletion revokes active share links for the root, child folders, and descendant files. Restoring the tree does not reactivate those links. ## Steps 1. Open the folder menu and choose **Delete**. 2. Read **Delete folder?** and verify the displayed root name. For a bulk selection, read **Delete selected items?** and the warning that everything inside selected folders is included. 3. Press **Delete** once. Avoid repeating the API action outside the UI: a second plain DELETE against an already-trashed root begins permanent purge. 4. Wait for **Deleted**, then open **Deleted** from the Files navigation. 5. Locate the folder root by its original display name. Descendants are attached to this root and may not appear as independent entries in the flat Deleted view. 6. Leave the root there for recovery, choose **Restore**, or use the separately labelled **Delete permanently** only after confirming the subtree is no longer needed. ## Expected result The root and its authorized descendants disappear from live browsing and sync snapshots. Their parent relationships, bytes, and storage charge remain recorded for restore. Existing share links return as revoked rather than continuing to expose deleted content. ## Troubleshooting - **“This folder is locked and cannot be deleted.”** Remove or change the folder’s direct lock before trying again. - **“This folder is inside a locked folder. Unlock the folder to delete it.”** Unlock the ancestor chain with the same account. - **“This folder contains a locked file and cannot be deleted.”** Find that descendant and resolve its lock; Dosya will not silently leave it behind. - **“This folder contains items you don’t have permission to delete.”** A descendant belongs to another member and your role lacks `delete_any_file`. Ask an authorized member to delete the tree. - **The root is absent from Deleted.** Refresh the current workspace and verify that the first request succeeded. A hidden or unauthorized root can be skipped during a batch. - **Storage did not decrease.** This is expected for recoverable trash. Only completed permanent purge releases the stored bytes. ## Related guides - [Restore deleted items](/files/restore-deleted) - [Permanently delete files](/files/permanently-delete-files)

title: Identify the correct deleted item
summary: Identify a deleted row using its type, size, deletion time, uploader, origin, and folder context before restoring or permanently deleting it.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Deleted items can contain repeated filenames. Use the row’s current metadata and its trash-root context before taking an action; the current web list does not expose a dedicated “original path” field for each deleted file. ## Steps 1. Choose **Deleted** under Files. The list orders trash results through the active sort, and its forced **Deleted** column shows `deleted_at` rather than normal modified time. 2. Search for the filename and switch to list view. Use **Columns** to expose Size, Type, Extension, Uploader, Region, Origin, Version, Shares, or Comments as needed. 3. Compare the **Deleted** timestamp and size first. For a folder, compare its file count; its descendants are represented through that deleted root. 4. Use uploader and Origin only as supporting evidence. Origin describes the ingest client, not the former folder or a complete custody trail. 5. If the row is a Live Photo still, check whether a companion video is also present. Restoring or permanently deleting one row can have different pairing consequences than acting on both. 6. Select only after the metadata matches your expected item. Re-read the **N selected** badge before **Restore** or **Delete permanently**. **When metadata is insufficient.** Restore the uncertain file when it is safe to do so, inspect it in its live folder, and delete it again if necessary. Do not permanently delete based only on a repeated filename; that operation has no undo. ## Expected result You have one verified trash row whose type, size, deletion time, and supporting metadata match the intended item, with no unsupported assumption that the Deleted table shows its original path. ## Related guides - [Review the Deleted items area](/files/review-deleted-items) - [Restore verified content safely](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Resolve a name conflict during restore
summary: Handle restore naming accurately: files can reappear beside the same name, folders receive an available numbered name, and results show the final name.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Restore behavior differs by item type. A file restore does not run a same-name conflict check, while a folder restore asks the repository for an available name and can return a numbered result such as `Photos (1)`. ## Steps 1. In **Deleted**, determine whether the target is a file or a folder. Compare timestamps and details before acting on a repeated name. 2. Check the original destination when you know it. If a folder with the desired name already exists there, expect the restored folder to receive the next available numbered name. 3. Choose **Restore** on the single row. You need the applicable delete-own or delete-any permission because the restore endpoint reuses those role gates. 4. For a folder, read the toast’s returned name. Dosya uses that server-selected final name instead of the stale trash-row name. 5. For a file, expect the same filename to be restored without an automatic rename. Open the destination and distinguish duplicate names by size, uploader, timestamps, file ID, or version history. 6. Rename or relocate one restored item only after confirming which record is which. File names allow up to 255 characters; folder names allow up to 100 and must remain one path segment. **Related restore blockers.** A file whose containing folder is still trashed fails with `This file's folder is in the trash - restore the folder first`. A folder deleted as part of another folder must be restored through that parent trash root. ## Expected result A conflicting folder returns under an available name such as `Name (1)`. A file may coexist with another same-named file, and you identify the records before making any follow-up rename or deletion. ## Related guides - [Inspect Deleted items before restoring](/files/review-deleted-items) - [Restore deleted files and folders](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Restore an item to its original location
summary: Restore files and folders to their recorded parent, understand workspace-root fallback, and fix the exact case where a file’s folder is still trashed.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Restore normally reactivates an item under its recorded parent. Folders can fall back to the workspace root when their former parent no longer exists live; individual files do not use that fallback. ## Steps 1. Open **Deleted** and identify the correct trash root. A child swept into a deleted folder is restored through that parent rather than as a separate root. 2. Choose **Restore** on one row, or select multiple roots and use the bulk **Restore** control. 3. For a file, wait for **Restored — “[name]” restored.** If its parent folder is still deleted, restore that folder first; the file endpoint returns a 409 rather than creating an invisible live row. 4. For a folder, read the result carefully. If its original parent is not live, Dosya restores the folder to **Root (top level)** and explicitly says the original folder is also in the trash. 5. Navigate to the reported destination. A folder-name collision may produce an available numbered name, so use the name shown in the toast. 6. Refresh once if the cached listing has not updated, then verify the item opens and no longer appears as a top-level Deleted entry. **Storage and timing.** Restore does not add charged bytes because soft deletion never released them. The UI disables a row’s restore while its request is in flight, preventing overlapping attempts that could corrupt accounting. ## Expected result The item returns live in its recorded parent when possible. A folder whose parent is unavailable appears at workspace root with an explicit notice; a file waits until its deleted parent has been restored. ## Related guides - [Review recoverable Deleted entries](/files/review-deleted-items) - [Use the standard restore workflow](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Understand automatic trash retention
summary: Know when Free and paid cloud trash becomes eligible for daily permanent purge, how plan changes affect timing, storage, and when recovery ends.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/purge-trash.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/purge-trash.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/plans.ts, apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts, apps/cron/src/index.ts, apps/cron/wrangler.jsonc, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts. Verified effective-owner-plan windows of 7/30 days, daily bounded sweep, restore-race check, leaf-first empty-folder removal, quota behavior, manual irreversible purge and restore limits. Local source/tests only; production cron execution was not observed.
body: Dosya automatically purges aged trash according to the workspace owner's effective plan: seven days for Free and 30 days for paid plans. The age starts from each item's `deleted_at` time. Purge permanently removes recoverability; it is not an archive tier. ## Steps 1. Open **Files → Deleted** in the correct workspace. The sidebar entry requires **Delete own files** or **Delete any file**. 2. Use list view and find the **Deleted** date. Under **Columns**, enable **Exact dates** if a relative value does not give enough precision. 3. Determine the workspace owner's effective plan, including subscription status and grace. A currently effective paid entitlement uses 30 days; an owner evaluated as Free uses seven days. 4. Count from the recorded deletion time. The server selects rows older than the applicable cutoff, so the item becomes eligible after the full seven- or 30-day interval rather than at the beginning of that calendar day. 5. Restore anything needed before eligibility. Select **Restore** on a file or a trash-root folder. Restore retains storage usage because trash never stopped counting those bytes. 6. If immediate space recovery is required and the data is disposable, choose **Delete permanently**, read the confirmation and proceed only with an independent copy.
