Manual purge can end recovery earlier than the automatic window. The production scheduler invokes trash cleanup daily. Eligibility does not promise deletion at an exact minute: the job processes bounded batches, retries failed work on later runs and can leave a backlog. Treat the plan duration as the latest safe restore window, not as a guaranteed grace period beyond it. Plan evaluation happens during the sweep. A cancellation that is still inside its recognized grace period remains effectively paid. Once the owner is effectively Free, trash already older than seven days can qualify on the next run even if it was originally deleted during a paid subscription. Upgrading can make the 30-day window apply to rows not yet purged, but it cannot recover objects already removed. Files are rechecked immediately before purge. If a restore wins that race and the row is no longer trashed, the cleanup skips it. Permanent purge removes file data, retained versions and associated metadata through the shared purge path, decrements workspace storage, and cannot recreate share links that soft deletion revoked. Folders are removed only after their contents are gone. The automatic job deletes eligible empty leaves first, so a deep trashed tree can disappear over consecutive daily runs. A folder used as a member's assigned root is deliberately retained instead of silently changing that member's scope. Folder-scoped API keys are removed when their eligible folder is finally purged. The current Deleted page's banner says trashed items continue using storage. If the workspace is full, waiting for retention leaves quota occupied until the purge actually succeeds; permanent deletion is the user-controlled way to reclaim it sooner. ## Expected result Free-owner trash becomes eligible after seven days and paid-owner trash after 30 days, then a daily bounded job removes due content permanently. Before that purge, permitted members can restore items without adding a second quota charge. ## Related guides - [Restore deleted items](/files/restore-deleted) - [Permanently delete files](/files/permanently-delete-files)

title: Verify storage after permanent deletion
summary: Confirm that trash still consumes quota, permanently purge a known item, allow the 60-second quota cache to invalidate, and verify released bytes.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Moving content to Deleted does not lower `storage_used_bytes`. Only a completed permanent purge removes the retained file bytes and credits the workspace counter. ## Steps 1. Record the workspace storage figure and the exact byte size of a disposable deleted file. A folder’s displayed size may aggregate many descendants, so a single file makes the clearest check. 2. Confirm the item is already in **Deleted**. The banner states: `Items in the trash still count against your storage. Delete them permanently to free up space.` 3. Choose **Delete permanently**, read the no-undo warning, and confirm. Do not use this test on the only copy of required content. 4. Wait for the success or partial-result toast. A large folder can return accepted-but-incomplete progress and must finish all passes before all of its bytes are gone. 5. Reload the storage display after the completed purge. The server invalidates the cached workspace quota; cached quota values otherwise have a 60-second lifetime. 6. Compare the new figure with other uploads, restores, version changes, or concurrent purges that occurred during the test. Use the item’s exact bytes when the rounded UI number does not visibly move. **Version storage matters.** Permanent file purge removes the file row and all stored version objects for that file. The released amount can therefore exceed the current-version size shown in the list. A failed or cancelled folder purge may have already released some bytes and leave the remainder in trash. ## Expected result After permanent deletion completes and reporting refreshes, charged storage no longer includes the purged file and its versions. Soft deletion alone produces no decrease, and partial folder outcomes release only what was actually removed. ## Related guides - [Review what remains in Deleted items](/files/review-deleted-items) - [Restore content instead of freeing its storage](/files/restore-deleted)

title: Fix a rejected or incomplete file-request upload
summary: Match the exact file-request error to its cause, recover an interrupted transfer and confirm whether Dosya received the file before retrying.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against src/pages/upload-request/[token].astro, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/upload.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/init.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/part/[partNumber].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/multipart/[sessionId]/abort.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload-request/[token]/files.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/access.ts, apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts and their focused unit tests. Confirmed exact visitor messages, 50 MiB multipart selection, 10 MiB parts, three file and three per-file part workers, same-page retry from part 1 with idempotent existing-part acknowledgement, access re-unlock, separate best-effort session-retirement and slot-release outcomes, cross-tab receipt checks and permanent visitor withdrawal. Existing captures were inspected and remain accurate.
body: Use the message beside the file before starting another transfer. Dosya checks the filename, byte size, remaining request slots, request status, destination lock and workspace storage at different points. A retry only helps after a connection failure; it cannot override a rule or reopen a closed request. ## Steps: identify where the upload stopped | Stage | Evidence on the page | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | Before upload | A red reason appears under the staged filename | No bytes were sent for that file | | During upload | The line shows a percentage, then **Retry** and an error | The browser did not complete the transfer | | After upload | The file moves into the dated receipt list and the page says the requester has it | Dosya recorded the file | | After reopening | The file appears under an earlier date with **Received** | This browser or recipient link can see the completed submission | If the connection drops, the page can display **The connection dropped. Nothing was saved.** That is the browser's network-error wording, not proof that the server did not finish before the response was lost. Keep the original page open so it retains the selected file and any multipart session. Open the same request in another tab, inspect the returning received history, then retry on the original page only when no receipt confirms completion. ## Fix a file rejected before transfer The public page performs the same basic checks before it enables **Upload N files**: - **This file has no extension, so its type cannot be checked** means the request has an extension allowlist and the filename has no suffix. Ask the owner which real format to provide. - A message such as **.exe is not accepted here - send .pdf, .docx** means the final filename extension is outside **Accepts**. Renaming unrelated content does not convert it. - A message such as **84 MB is over the 50 MB limit for this request** compares one file with the displayed **Per file** maximum. - **This file is empty** refuses a zero-byte item. - **There is no slot left on this request** means completed files and reserved in-progress sessions have consumed **Max files**. Remove the rejected line, correct the named problem and select the file again. The allowed-extension comparison is case-insensitive. A file can still be refused by the server if another uploader takes the last slot or the owner changes a rule after your page loaded. ## Match server errors to the owner action | Error or page state | What changed | Recovery | | --- | --- | --- | | **This request has expired** | Its deadline passed | The owner can edit the deadline to a future value or **Never** | | **This request was closed** | The owner revoked it | Revocation is irreversible; the owner must create another request | | **This request has reached its file limit.** | The atomic slot reservation found no capacity | The owner raises or clears **Max files**, or creates a replacement | | **This upload request can no longer accept files.** | The destination or an ancestor now has a full lock | The owner removes or changes the configured lock, or edits the destination | | **File is too large. Maximum size is N MB** | The measured or declared file exceeds the current request maximum | Supply a smaller permitted file or ask the owner to revise the limit | | **File type .ext is not allowed. Accepted: ...** | The server rejected the final extension | Send one of the listed formats | | A workspace storage-limit message | The receiving workspace lacks available allocation | The owner frees storage permanently, changes the workspace allowance or chooses another workspace | An owner can review **File requests**, open the request, then use **Edit** to check **Expires**, **Upload destination**, **Allowed extensions**, **Max file size (MB)** and **Max files**. Editing cannot restore a revoked token. ## Recover an interrupted transfer Files larger than 50 MiB use a resumable session. Dosya divides them into 10 MiB parts, sends as many as three parts for that file at once and can work on as many as three files concurrently. While the same loaded page still holds the source file and session ID, **Retry** reuses that session but starts its requests again at part 1. The browser reissues every part request; when the server already recorded a part number, it returns the stored result without writing those bytes to object storage again. 1. Leave the request tab open and keep the original file available on the device. 2. When the line changes to failed, read its exact error. 3. Restore a stable connection, then select **Retry** on that line. 4. If the request is password protected and the page shows **Your access timed out**, enter the current request password and choose **Unlock and continue**. Remaining files continue; completed receipt lines stay complete. 5. Wait for the dated receipt and the message that the requester has the file. Refreshing closes the browser's in-memory queue and discards access to the selected File objects. A new page cannot reconstruct that same resumable session from disk. After refresh, check the receipt; if the file is absent, select it again and begin a new upload. Small files use one request instead of a multipart session. Their progress cannot resume at an earlier byte. Retry sends the whole small file again after you confirm it is missing from the receipt. ## Cancel, discard or withdraw - **Cancel all** stops active browser requests. A staged item remains available to send again. - Removing a failed multipart row attempts a best-effort server abort. Retiring the session and releasing the request slot are separate best-effort writes; either can remain pending even if the abort endpoint answers success. A rejected password or inactive request can stop the call before both writes. Retirement failure leaves the pending or uploading session for the stale-session sweep. A failed slot release can leave one slot counted with no automatic age-down; the request owner or Dosya support may need to reconcile the occupied count. If the session already completed, abort returns a conflict and the recorded file legitimately keeps its counted slot. - Removing a staged item that never started changes only the browser list. - The remove control beside an earlier **Received** item is a withdrawal. It is available only to the same per-recipient token or browser visitor identity that uploaded the file. Withdrawal permanently purges the workspace file, its versions and associated shares, decrements the request count and frees its measured storage. It does not move the file to **Deleted**, so neither the uploader nor owner can restore it from Dosya Trash. A workspace owner deleting the received file from **Files** is different: that ordinary action is a soft delete, keeps using storage while retained and does not return a slot to the request. The public withdrawal action stops working after the request expires or is revoked. Ask the owner about retention if the request has already closed. ## Password and invitation checks A request password is separate from a Dosya account password. Five unlock attempts are allowed per request token and client IP in 15 minutes. After the limit, the page says unlocking is paused for 15 minutes. A successful unlock grants that browser 30 minutes of request access. An emailed invitation adds a recipient token to the URL. It associates uploads with the invited address without sending or checking an inbox code. Forwarding that URL can therefore attribute another person's submission to the invited address. Use the recipient's original link for correct tracking, but do not treat **Uploaded** as identity proof. ## Expected result The transfer is complete only when the received file appears in the dated ledger and the confirmation stamp includes the count, received size, time and request reference. The owner should also see it in the request's upload table and destination folder. If a permitted small test still fails, send the owner the request title, time and time zone, browser, approximate size, true filename extension and exact redacted message. Do not publish the request URL, password or file contents. The owner should verify request status, destination access and workspace storage before contacting [Dosya support](https://dosya.dev/contact/). ## Related guides - [Upload files through a file request](/sharing/request-upload) - [Set file-request types, sizes and counts](/sharing/request-limits) - [Protect a file request with a password](/sharing/request-password) - [Edit or close a file request](/sharing/manage-file-request) - [Understand workspace storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Confirm two-factor enrollment
summary: Confirm Dosya authenticator enrollment with a fresh six-digit code, understand the accepted time window, and save the recovery set safely offline.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/password.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/2fa/verify-totp.ts, apps/api/src/lib/totp.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/totp-consume.ts. Production 2FA changes were not performed.
body: Opening **Enable authenticator** creates a pending secret, but authenticator 2FA is not active until Dosya accepts a six-digit code. The live secret is promoted and recovery codes are created in one database batch. ## Steps 1. Open **Profile → Password & 2FA → Enable authenticator**. 2. Scan the QR or enter the displayed secret in your authenticator. The setup uses issuer **dosya.dev**, six digits, SHA-1, and a 30-second period. 3. Wait for a fresh code if the current one is about to roll over, type all six digits, and choose **Verify & enable**. 4. Dosya accepts the current 30-second step plus one step before or after, a 90-second tolerance for clock skew. An invalid value returns **Invalid code. Check your authenticator app and try again.** 5. If setup was not started or its pending secret is absent, the response is **No TOTP secret found. Start setup first.** 6. After success, save all 10 recovery codes with **Copy all** or **Download**, then choose **Done**. 7. Return to the settings row and verify the **Authenticator** badge and **10 of 10 codes remaining**. The setup code's time step is recorded as used, so that same authenticator value cannot immediately complete a sign-in. Closing the dialog before verification leaves 2FA unchanged. ## Expected result The pending encrypted secret becomes the live authenticator secret, the method becomes TOTP, and ten one-time recovery-code hashes replace any previous set. A mandatory security notice records that authenticator 2FA was enabled. ## Related guides - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Use two-factor recovery](/account/two-factor-recovery)

title: Move two-factor authentication to a new phone
summary: Move Dosya authenticator 2FA to a replacement phone without losing access by preserving recovery options, then disabling and re-enabling securely.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/password.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/2fa/disable.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/2fa/verify-totp.ts. Production 2FA changes were not performed.
body: The current web interface does not provide a direct “move phone” button. It requires disabling 2FA and enabling **Authenticator** again, which replaces the secret and recovery-code set. Keep the old phone, current session, and an unused recovery code until the new setup succeeds. ## Steps 1. Sign in on a trusted browser and verify that you know the account password. OAuth-only accounts must use **Set a password** first because disabling 2FA requires one. 2. Preserve an unused recovery code offline. Do not erase the old phone yet. 3. In **Profile → Password & 2FA**, select **Disable**, enter **Current password**, and choose **Disable 2FA**. Wrong credentials return **Incorrect password**. 4. Understand the transition: disabling clears the live and pending authenticator secrets and deletes every existing recovery code. The account temporarily has no second factor. 5. Select **Enable authenticator**, scan the new QR on the replacement phone, enter a fresh six-digit code, and choose **Verify & enable**. 6. Save the new set of 10 codes. Confirm the **Authenticator** badge before signing out or wiping the old device. 7. Test a separate login with the new phone. The 2FA challenge expires after 5 minutes and allows 5 attempts; repeated failure requires starting login again. Disabling and re-enabling generates mandatory security notices. If either action was not yours, change the password and review sessions immediately. ## Expected result Only the replacement phone's secret generates accepted authenticator codes. The previous secret and all earlier recovery codes are invalid, while the newly issued ten codes can recover future sign-ins one time each. ## Related guides - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Use two-factor recovery](/account/two-factor-recovery)

title: Recovering access when a second factor is unavailable
summary: Use a saved one-time recovery code when an authenticator device is unavailable, then replace codes and review account security.
verification: Reviewed the current login 2FA recovery-code path, one-time code behavior and regeneration controls against the local current web app, API and automated tests on 2026-10-12. No real recovery code was entered or captured.
body: Authenticator-based two-factor authentication provides one-time recovery codes during setup. Use one when you know the account password but cannot access the authenticator device. Email-based 2FA does not use authenticator recovery codes. Restore access to the email inbox or contact private support with non-secret account details. ## Before you start - Complete the normal email and password sign-in first. - Find the recovery codes saved during authenticator setup. Never send them to support or another person. - Use a trusted device and private connection. - Each recovery code works once. ## Steps: sign in with a recovery code 1. At **Two-factor authentication**, select **Use a recovery code instead**. 2. Enter one unused code in the displayed format. 3. Select **Use recovery code**. 4. After sign-in, open **Profile → Password & 2FA**. 5. Confirm the remaining recovery-code count. 6. If codes were exposed or are running low, choose the regenerate action and confirm with the current password. 7. Store the replacement codes offline. Regeneration invalidates the previous set. 8. Enroll a replacement authenticator if the original device is permanently unavailable. ## Expected result A valid unused recovery code completes the second-factor challenge and creates the signed-in session. That code is marked used and cannot authenticate another sign-in. ## Limits and security behavior - Recovery codes apply to authenticator-based 2FA and are single-use. - Regenerating codes invalidates every unused code from the old set. - Resetting the account password does not remove the second-factor requirement. - Support should never ask for a password, authenticator code or recovery code. - Losing both the authenticator and every recovery code can require private account-recovery review; recovery is not guaranteed from public information. ## Troubleshooting **The code is rejected.** Check for transcription errors and try another unused code from the same set. A code used before or invalidated by regeneration will fail. **The page expects six digits.** Select **Use a recovery code instead** before entering the alphanumeric recovery code. **The account uses email 2FA.** Recovery codes are not used. Restore inbox access and request a new email code through the sign-in flow. **No recovery material remains.** From a still-signed-in trusted session, open Password & 2FA and regenerate codes. Without a trusted session, contact [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) and do not share secrets. ## Related guides - [Turning on two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Signing in and resetting a forgotten password](/account/reset-password) - [Responding to suspicious account activity](/account/suspicious-activity)

title: Re-enroll two-factor authentication after recovery
summary: Re-enroll Dosya authenticator 2FA after recovery-code access, replace the old secret, and confirm new codes before ending the session securely.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/login-2fa.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/auth/2fa/verify.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/me/2fa/disable.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/2fa/verify-totp.ts. Production 2FA changes were not performed.
body: A recovery code signs in once; it does not disable authenticator 2FA or restore the lost secret. Use the resulting trusted session to replace the factor before it ends. ## Steps 1. Complete email/password login, select **Use a recovery code instead**, enter one XXXX-XXXX value, and choose **Use recovery code**. Spaces and hyphens are normalized, but a successful code is atomically marked used. 2. The login challenge lasts 5 minutes and permits 5 attempts. Errors count down **Invalid code. N attempts remaining.**; the cap returns **Too many attempts. Please log in again.** 3. Open **Profile → Password & 2FA**. Confirm that you know the current password; an OAuth-only account must set one before it can turn 2FA off. 4. Select **Disable**, provide the password, and complete **Disable 2FA**. This destroys the old authenticator secret and all remaining old recovery codes. 5. Immediately choose **Enable authenticator**, scan the new QR, enter the six-digit value, and select **Verify & enable**. 6. Store the newly displayed ten recovery codes and confirm the **Authenticator** badge. 7. Review sessions if the factor was lost through theft or account compromise. There is a short interval between disable and successful enrollment when the account has no second factor. Keep the authenticated browser private and finish the replacement without leaving it unattended. ## Expected result The recovery code used for entry cannot be reused, the lost authenticator secret no longer works, and the replacement app supplies valid TOTP codes. Only the new recovery-code set remains available. ## Related guides - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Use two-factor recovery](/account/two-factor-recovery)

title: Scan the authenticator QR code safely
summary: Scan Dosya's authenticator QR locally, protect the embedded shared secret, and confirm the six-digit setup code without exposing credentials.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/password.tsx and apps/api/src/lib/totp.ts. Production 2FA changes were not performed.
body: The authenticator QR contains the same raw shared secret shown beneath it. Anyone who copies either value can generate your future codes, so treat the setup screen like a password. ## Steps 1. Use a private device and open **Profile → Password & 2FA → Enable authenticator**. 2. Dosya renders the QR inside your browser from the otpauth URI; it is not sent to a third-party QR image service. 3. Scan it with an authenticator you control. If scanning fails, enter the displayed secret manually. 4. Confirm that the authenticator entry identifies **dosya.dev** and your account email. The URI specifies SHA-1, six digits, and a 30-second period. 5. Do not send the QR or secret through chat, email, tickets, or screenshots. A QR image is a reusable credential, not a one-time login code. 6. Type a fresh code in **6-digit code** and select **Verify & enable**. Dosya accepts one adjacent 30-second step on either side for clock skew. 7. After the recovery codes appear, store them separately and close the modal with **Done**. If you exposed the QR before confirmation, cancel and reopen setup to stage a different secret. If exposure occurred after activation, replace the factor through a controlled disable-and-enable cycle. ## Expected result The authenticator produces codes that Dosya verifies, the QR never leaves the controlled setup devices, and the settings page displays the **Authenticator** badge. Merely scanning without **Verify & enable** does not activate 2FA. ## Related guides - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Use two-factor recovery](/account/two-factor-recovery)

title: Store two-factor recovery codes
summary: Store all ten Dosya recovery codes offline, understand single-use behavior, and regenerate them safely when any copy may be exposed or lost.
verification: Source-verified locally against apps/web/src/pages/profile/password.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/recovery.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/me/2fa/recovery-codes.ts. Production 2FA changes were not performed.
body: Authenticator enrollment displays 10 recovery codes in XXXX-XXXX form. Dosya shows the plaintext set in that response and stores hashes; each matching code can complete only one login. ## Steps 1. On the **Recovery codes** screen, choose **Copy all** for a trusted password manager or **Download** for the file named dosya-recovery-codes.txt. 2. Keep the set outside the phone running your authenticator. A recovery copy on the same lost device does not help. 3. At login, select **Use a recovery code instead**, enter one value, and choose **Use recovery code**. Letter case, spaces, and hyphens are normalized. 4. After use, the server records that code as spent. The settings row reports how many of the original ten remain. 5. If any copy is exposed or the count is too low, choose **Regenerate codes**. Enter the current password and select **Regenerate**. 6. Regeneration deletes every old code before issuing ten replacements. The warning **This invalidates your existing codes** is literal and irreversible. 7. If the account has no password, set one first; the regeneration control is disabled because password confirmation is required. Missing password input shows **Password required — Enter your current password to continue.** A bad password returns **Incorrect password**. Recovery-code regeneration works only for authenticator-based 2FA. ## Expected result You hold a separate, protected copy of the current ten-code set and can identify how many remain. After regeneration, no old recovery code can authenticate, and a mandatory security notice records the replacement. ## Related guides - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor) - [Use two-factor recovery](/account/two-factor-recovery)

title: Turning on two-factor authentication
summary: Find Password & 2FA, connect an authenticator app, save your recovery codes, and manage your second sign-in step.
verification: Verified authenticator setup, TOTP confirmation and enabled status against the isolated local current web app and API on 2026-10-10. Real screenshots reviewed; setup secrets and recovery codes were not captured. Other controls were checked against current source. Production and email enrollment were not verified.
body: Open **Profile → Password & 2FA** to add an authenticator app to your account. Setup is complete only after you enter an app-generated code and select **Verify & enable**. Save the recovery codes before closing the setup dialog. ## Before you start - Sign in to the account you want to protect. These settings apply to your account, rather than only the selected workspace. - Have an authenticator app that supports time-based, six-digit codes available on your device. - Have somewhere private to save recovery codes, such as a password manager you can reach if you lose your authenticator device. - Your account needs a password for this web setup. If you first signed in with Google, GitHub or Apple and see **Not set** beside **Password**, select **Set a password**, enter **New password** and **Confirm new password**, and finish that dialog. The password must be at least eight characters. Reload the page if the setup controls do not appear after saving. ## Steps: connect an authenticator app 1. **Find the security settings.** Open the avatar's **Account menu** in the app's top bar, select **Profile**, then select **Password & 2FA** in the profile navigation. You can also open [Password & 2FA](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/password) directly. The page heading reads **Password & two-factor auth**. 2. **Start setup.** In the **Two-factor authentication** row, select **Enable authenticator**. The **Set up authenticator app** dialog displays a QR code and a setup secret. 3. **Add the account to your authenticator.** Use the app's account-add control to scan the displayed QR code. If you cannot scan it, use the app's manual setup option with the secret shown beneath the QR code. Keep the QR code and secret private. 4. **Confirm the connection.** Enter the authenticator's current code in **6-digit code**, then select **Verify & enable**. Opening the QR dialog alone does not enable two-factor authentication. 5. **Save your recovery codes.** When the dialog changes to **Recovery codes**, use **Copy all** or **Download** to save them privately. **Download** creates a text file named `dosya-recovery-codes.txt`. Each code can be used once if you lose access to the authenticator. 6. **Finish and check the status.** Select **Done**. The account settings should show **Authenticator**, **Enabled via authenticator app.**, and a **Recovery codes** row showing the remaining codes. ## Expected result Authenticator-based two-factor authentication is enabled. When a sign-in asks for a second verification step, enter the current six-digit authenticator code on the **Two-factor authentication** page and select **Verify**. If you cannot use the authenticator at that point, select **Use a recovery code instead**, enter an unused code in **Recovery code**, and select **Use recovery code**. Mark that code as used in your saved copy. ## Replace recovery codes or turn 2FA off To replace the recovery set, return to **Password & 2FA**, select **Regenerate codes**, enter **Current password**, and select **Regenerate**. This invalidates the previous codes. Save the new set with **Copy all** or **Download**, then select **Done**. To turn off the second step, select **Disable** in the **Two-factor authentication** row, enter **Current password**, and select **Disable 2FA**. Check for the **Disabled** message and the settings row's updated status. ## Limitations - Account two-factor authentication and Vault encryption are separate features. Enabling 2FA does not move files into the Vault or change their encryption workflow. - Recovery codes are for authenticator-based 2FA. They are not an account password or a Vault recovery credential. - The page also offers **Enable email 2FA**. If email enrollment fails, use the authenticator workflow or contact private support. - Enabling 2FA does not replace reviewing existing signed-in devices. See [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions). ## Troubleshooting If **Verify & enable** remains unavailable, enter all six digits. If verification fails, use a fresh code from the correct authenticator entry and check your device's time settings. If the app says to start setup first, close the dialog and begin again from **Enable authenticator**. If you cannot disable 2FA or regenerate codes, use your current Dosya account password. The password for a linked Google, GitHub or Apple account is a separate credential. If you are signed in, use [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support). If you cannot sign in, use the [public contact form](https://dosya.dev/contact/) instead. Describe the failing step and its error message. Never send your password, setup QR code, setup secret, current verification code or recovery codes. ## Frequently asked questions ### Is scanning the QR code enough to enable 2FA? No. Enter the authenticator's code and select **Verify & enable**. The recovery-code screen and updated **Authenticator** status confirm that setup progressed beyond scanning. ### Can I see my original recovery codes again later? The settings page shows how many remain; it does not reveal the original set. If you are signed in and have your account password, use **Regenerate codes** to replace them. Save the replacement set because the old codes stop working. ### What if I lose my authenticator device? Use an unused saved recovery code at the sign-in verification step. If you are still signed in on another device, keep that session available while reviewing your recovery options. Private support can help investigate an access problem; this guide does not promise a bypass of account verification. ## Related guides - [Reviewing active sessions](/account/sessions) - [Watch the existing two-factor authentication tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/turn-on-two-factor-login/) - [Learn about the separate Vault workflow](https://dosya.dev/vault/)

title: Troubleshoot an unavailable sharing link
summary: Match the public sharing message to expiry, revocation, deletion, locks, recipient checks, passwords, download controls, regional rules or transfer allowances.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against src/components/share/ShareShell.astro, src/lib/share-viewers/util.ts, apps/web/src/pages/shared.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/share-analytics.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/share/access.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/lock-gate.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/egress.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/downloads.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download-all.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/unlock.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/lock.ts. Verified public error copy, gate order, 30-minute password and recipient grants, wrong-password throttling, target revival only after configured full-lock removal or change, the non-effect of a member-only one-hour unlock grant on public sharing, revoked versus expired detail actions, terminal revocation, download-cap wording, view-only refusal, Free-plan 10 GB UTC-day allowance and folder archive ceilings. Existing expired and revoked captures were inspected and remain accurate.
body: Open the exact URL in a private browser window and use the page heading or download error to choose the recovery. The share page can be available while downloading is deliberately blocked, so separate “cannot open the link” from “cannot download the item.” ## Steps ### First checks for a recipient 1. Copy the complete URL again. Long sharing addresses can break across lines in email or chat. 2. Open it in a private window so an old password or recipient cookie does not hide the current gate. 3. Record the exact heading, message and time without posting the private URL publicly. 4. Confirm the sender and intended file through a trusted channel. ### Match the message to its cause | What you see | What it means | Next action | | --- | --- | --- | | **Link expired** | Its expiry time passed | The owner opens the target in **Files** and uses **Share** to create a replacement | | **Link revoked** | The owner permanently ended that token | Request a new sharing URL | | **File deleted** | The target no longer exists as a live file | The owner must restore or reshare the item | | **Region restricted** | The workspace country policy refused the request location | The owner must review the allowlist or blocklist | | **This file was shared privately** | The link accepts named recipient addresses only | Enter the exact invited address and verify its one-time email code | | **This file is password protected** | A separate sharing-link password is required | Enter the password supplied by the sender | | **This content has been locked by its owner** | The target or an ancestor received a full lock after sharing | An authorized owner must remove or change that configured **Full lock** | | **Link unavailable** | The token, hidden target or another protected state cannot be disclosed further | Ask the owner to inspect the link and item from **Shared → By me** | A link that is both restricted and password-protected asks for recipient email verification first, then the password. Each successful grant lasts 30 minutes in that browser. Opening the URL on another browser or after the grant expires repeats the relevant check. ### Owner checks in Shared 1. Open **Shared**, select **By me**, and set the filter to **All** so ended rows remain visible. 2. Find the item and open its link detail. Compare the displayed URL with the address the recipient used. 3. Read **Status**, **Expires**, **Access**, **Password** and **Downloads**. Several independent links can point to the same file or folder. 4. Open the target in **Files**. Confirm it is live, visible to the link creator and not beneath a full lock. 5. For a restricted link, review the invited list. The recipient must use an address on that list; forwarding the URL alone does not add them. 6. Use **Copy link** only for a live row. A revoked detail row offers **Create a new link**. An expired detail has no expiry editor or replacement button, so find the target in **Files**, use **Share**, and test the new URL privately before sending it. Removing or changing the configured **Full lock** on the target or an ancestor, or unhiding the target, can revive a still-live link because public access is rechecked on each request. A member password unlock creates a one-hour grant for that signed-in member; it does not change the configured lock or restore anonymous public sharing. Revocation cannot be undone. The revoked detail offers **Create a new link**, while an expired detail requires creating the replacement from the target in **Files**. ## When the page opens but download fails **`This file is view-only. Downloads are not allowed.`** The sender enabled view-only access. Supported content may still open in the browser, but the original attachment is withheld. Ask the sender for a download-enabled link when you need a local copy. **`This folder is view-only. Downloads are not allowed.`** The folder page can be browsed, but its archive action is disabled by the sender's link control. **`This link has reached the number of downloads its sender allowed.`** The link's download cap is exhausted. Counts are enforced atomically, and the owner must create or change access rather than asking the recipient to keep retrying. **`This link's owner has reached their free plan's daily share-transfer allowance.`** Free-plan owners share a 10 GB egress allowance per UTC day across all their public sharing links. Recipients can try after the reset, or the owner can upgrade for unmetered sharing. **`Too many files to archive at once (max 10000)` or `Archive too large (max 5 GiB)`.** The folder is accessible, but one ZIP cannot contain that expanded tree. Ask the owner to share or package smaller folders. A successful view does not guarantee a download: password, recipient and live-link checks authorize the page, while view-only mode, a link cap and daily transfer allowance decide whether bytes can be downloaded. ## Password and recipient recovery - A wrong link password returns **Incorrect password**. The unlock route permits five attempts per token and IP in 15 minutes, while the link also has a consecutive-failure lockout. Stop guessing and ask the sender for the current password. - Email verification and password access are independent. Completing one never substitutes for the other. - The address must match an invited recipient. A one-time code proves inbox control; it does not create a Dosya account requirement. - A recipient or password grant expires after 30 minutes. The page can ask again during a long session without meaning the link was revoked. ## Expected result The recipient either regains the intended level of access through a live, tested URL or receives the exact reason that only the owner can correct. The owner knows whether the original URL can revive or whether a replacement must be distributed. ## What recovery cannot undo Expiry or revocation does not delete the source item, and ending one link does not end another active link to the same target. These controls also cannot recall a copy someone already downloaded, exported or captured. Use link activity and private support details to investigate unexpected access, but rotate or revoke credentials promptly when the URL escaped its intended audience. ## Related guides - [Create a secure sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Set a link expiry](/sharing/link-expiry) - [Revoke a sharing URL](/sharing/revoke-link) - [Share with named recipients](/sharing/named-recipients) - [Disable downloads on a link](/sharing/share-disable-downloads) - [Review link activity](/sharing/link-activity) - [Change a sharing-link password](/sharing/share-change-password)

title: Make a hidden item visible again
summary: Choose Visible for a hidden file or folder, preserve other access controls, and test whether an ancestor rule still hides the item from members.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/hide-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/hide.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/hide.ts, apps/api/src/lib/hidden/decide.ts, apps/api/src/lib/hidden/rest-gate.ts and apps/api/src/lib/repo/types.ts. Verified Unhide/Visible/Apply labels, hide_files permission, exact errors and toasts, atomic rule clearing, 200-target cap, privileged visibility and ancestor-hidden behavior. Local source and focused tests only; no production visibility rule was changed.
body: Unhiding clears the selected item's own hidden mode and audience rules. It does not grant workspace membership, expand a folder-confined member's subtree, remove a lock, or override a hidden ancestor. ## Steps 1. Sign in with a role that includes **Hide files**. This permission is also the privileged visibility flag: its holder can see hidden items that ordinary members cannot. 2. In **Files**, right-click the hidden file or folder and choose **Unhide**. The dialog title remains **Hide file** or **Hide folder** because the same visibility editor handles both directions. 3. Review the active choice before changing it: **Hidden from everybody**, **Hidden from specific users**, or **Hidden from specific roles**. The user and role variants show their current targets. 4. Select **Visible**, whose description is **Everyone can see this**, then choose **Apply**. The server writes `hidden_mode: none`, clears the hidden flag, clears who and when set it, and removes that item's stored target rules in the same operation. 5. Wait for the success toast. The current web copy says **File unhidden** and **This file is now visible to everyone.** even when the target was a folder; treat that as confirmation of the visibility update, not a change of item type. 6. Refresh the containing folder as the previously affected member. Confirm the row appears only if that member also has ordinary workspace, role and folder access. If the row remains absent, inspect each parent folder. A hidden rule on any ancestor still filters the child, even after the child's own mode becomes **Visible**. Also confirm that the test membership is not confined to a different root folder and that its role includes **Access files**. The API returns `You don't have permission to hide files` for a file or `You don't have permission to hide folders` for a folder when **Hide files** is missing. A target hidden from the requester is deliberately reported as `File not found` or `Folder not found` before permission is disclosed. `Access denied` means the account is not a member of the workspace. When editing a targeted rule instead of clearing it, the interface requires at least one user or role and disables hiding from yourself or your own role. The API messages are `You must select at least one user` and `You must select at least one role`; the repository retains at most 200 targets. These limits matter when you decide to narrow a rule rather than make the item fully visible. Unhiding is reversible by applying a new hidden mode, but the visibility increase takes effect for every otherwise authorized member that the removed rule had excluded. Confirm the intended audience before selecting **Apply**, especially on a folder whose descendants inherit its visibility. ## Expected result The chosen item has no direct hidden rule, the old audience targets are gone, and eligible members can list it after refresh. Any parent hidden rule, lock, membership boundary or role restriction continues to control access. ## Related guides - [Lock and hide files](/files/lock-and-hide) - [Workspace policies](/workspaces/policies)

title: Unlock a protected file
summary: Open a password-locked cloud file with its current secret, handle the five-attempt lockout, and understand the personal one-hour access grant.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/unlock.ts, apps/api/src/lib/rate-limit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/unlock-throttle.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/files.ts, apps/api/src/lib/download-guard.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/lock.ts. Verified exact prompt and errors, the per-isolate five-request/900-second limiter, persistent fifth-failure 900-second lock, 3,600-second per-user token, replacement of prior tokens, hidden and folder-scope gates, and the distinction between temporary access and removing a lock. Local source review only; no production credential was entered.
body: Opening a password-protected file creates temporary access for your account; it does not remove or weaken the file's saved lock. The file must also be visible, inside your assigned folder scope and allowed by your workspace membership. ## Steps 1. Find the file in **Files** and click its row, name or viewer action. A file with **Password** protection opens the dialog titled **File is locked** instead of exposing the preview or details. 2. Confirm the filename in **Enter the password to access _filename_**. This prevents submitting a valid secret to a similarly named file in another folder. 3. Type the current credential into **Enter password**, then choose **Unlock**. A blank or whitespace-only API request is rejected as `Password is required`. 4. After success, continue to the view you originally requested. Dosya issues a per-user, per-file token valid for 3,600 seconds and replaces any older token for that same account and file. 5. Recheck sensitive operations before performing them. Temporary unlock satisfies the password gate, but download, edit, share, move and delete still apply their own role, lock-mode and ancestor-folder rules. The web client remembers the issued token in the current Files-page session. A reload or a new browser session can show the prompt again even before the server-side hour ends because the client no longer has the token string. Expiry also causes the next protected request to require the password again. Another member never receives your grant. An incorrect entry returns `Incorrect password` and clears the input. Before checking the stored file state, one Worker isolate admits at most five requests for the same file and IP over 900 seconds. That local limiter answers `Too many requests` with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header, but its counter is not shared with other isolates. Wrong passwords separately increment a persistent per-file counter across IP addresses and elapsed time. The fifth wrong password sets a 900-second lock while still returning `Incorrect password`; later requests that reach this check receive `Too many attempts, try again later.` A correct password, password replacement, or lock removal resets the stored counter. `This file is not locked with a password` means its current mode changed before submission. `File not found` can also protect a hidden file or an item outside a folder-confined membership. `Access denied` indicates workspace membership is missing. A connectivity failure is shown as **Can't reach the server. Check your connection and try again.** and keeps the typed value so you can retry after connectivity returns. Do not confuse the row-menu label **Unlock** with this access prompt. For someone holding **Lock files**, that menu opens lock settings and can choose **Remove lock** without asking for the existing password. Removing the mode affects every member and causes share and sync gates to reevaluate; entering the password affects only the requesting member's temporary session. ## Expected result The requested file view opens for your account, the underlying mode remains **Password**, and other members continue to see a lock. Access closes after one hour or when the client loses the token, whichever makes the protected request unauthenticated first. ## Related guides - [Lock and hide files](/files/lock-and-hide) - [Workspace policies](/workspaces/policies)

title: Upgrade a plan or add storage
summary: Choose a plan or 100 GB, 1 TB, or 5 TB storage add-ons, review live pricing, and verify the resulting account capacity after Stripe settles.

body: Use **Change plan** to replace the base tier and **Add storage** to retain it while adjusting separate capacity items. ## Steps 1. Record Billing’s used amount, base-plan row, extras, and **Total limit**. 2. Select **Change plan** for a new base capacity or feature ceiling. Select **Add storage** for the dedicated add-on-only chooser. 3. Choose the billing interval and quantity from the live catalog. Wait for **Purchase complete** or **Plan updated**, and verify the resulting ledger row and total before resuming large uploads. Add-on definitions and prices come from the database and a five-minute cache; no static add-on fallback is used. Plan changes preserve active custom packages, while add-ons are replaced by the quantities in the submitted cart. If a selected plan is smaller than the current plan, Dosya requires a separate downgrade confirmation. ## Expected result Billing shows the intended base plan or add-on quantity and the effective storage limit increases by the expected amount. If the success page still says **Adding your storage**, allow the eight 2.5-second status retries to finish and use Retry if offered. A completed card payment with stale Billing data should be reported with its invoice reference, not repurchased. ## Related guides - [Choose a plan](/account/choose-plan) - [Verify a plan change](/account/verify-plan-change)

title: Choose the correct workspace and folder before uploading
summary: Switch to the intended Dosya workspace, select a writable cloud folder, and verify a completed test upload before transferring important files.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/layout/dashboard-sidebar.tsx, apps/web/src/router.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx, apps/web/src/components/folder-picker-dialog.tsx, apps/web/src/hooks/use-permissions.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts and apps/api/src/lib/access/scope.ts. Verified the two-second workspace transition, active-workspace routing, Uploads and Upload files labels, Root destination behavior, folder search and creation controls, access_upload and upload_files gates, folder confinement, exact permission refusals, completion actions and group-upload placement. The existing destination capture was inspected and remains accurate.
body: Every upload is tied to the workspace that was active when its queue item was created. Choose the workspace before you select files, then set the **Folder** under **Upload options**. A matching folder name in another workspace is a different destination. ## Before you start - Sign in with the account that belongs to the receiving workspace. - Ask the workspace owner for the exact workspace and folder path when someone else assigned the destination. - Prepare one small, non-confidential file with a distinctive name, such as `destination-check-2026-10-14.txt`. - Confirm your role can open **Uploads** and add bytes. These are separate capabilities: `access_upload` exposes the page, while `upload_files` permits the transfer. ## Steps ### Switch to the intended workspace 1. Read the workspace name in the upper part of the left sidebar. 2. Open the workspace switcher and choose the intended workspace. 3. Dosya displays **Switching workspace…** for at least two seconds and then lands on that workspace's dashboard. 4. Read the sidebar name again. The data shown by **Files**, **Uploads**, **Shared**, **Team** and workspace settings now belongs to that active workspace. 5. If the workspace is missing, check the signed-in email and whether its invitation was accepted. Ask the owner to confirm membership instead of uploading to a similarly named workspace. The switch deliberately navigates away from the previous workspace page. Reopen **Uploads** after the transition rather than trusting an older destination control left in another tab. ### Select the destination folder 1. Choose **Uploads** in the sidebar. The page heading is **Upload files**. 2. In **Upload options**, find the **Folder** control before adding any files. 3. **Root (top level)** means the top level available to this member in the active workspace. A folder-confined member is resolved to the assigned anchor and cannot write to the unrestricted workspace root. 4. Open the folder control. The dialog title and confirmation action are **Select folder**. 5. Browse the folder tree or use **Search folders...**. Search results include their path, which helps distinguish repeated names. 6. Select the intended folder and choose **Select folder**. Dosya reports **Uploading here** and says that new files will go to the selected name. 7. If you are authorized to create folders, use **New folder at root** or **New folder in “_name_”**, enter the name and choose **Create**. A successful result says **Folder created**. ### Prove the destination with one file 1. With the workspace and folder visible, choose **Select files** and add the harmless test file. 2. Watch its row in **Upload queue**. **Queued** or a percentage is not proof of a stored copy. 3. Wait for **Done**. 4. Choose **View file** to open that result, or **Go to location** to open its containing folder. 5. Compare the file's exact name and size, then return to **Uploads** and reselect the same destination for the important transfer. Files chosen from a group view still land in a real folder. When the header says files will land at the top level and be added to a group, verify both the cloud location and group membership. ## Permission and folder rules - A role without `access_upload` does not receive the Uploads route or sidebar item. - A role that reaches the page but lacks `upload_files` sees **Your role can't upload files** and **Ask a workspace owner or admin if you need to add files here.** - The server can return **You don't have access to the upload page** or **You don't have upload permission in this workspace** if the role changed after the interface loaded. - A folder-confined member receives **This folder is outside the folder you're confined to** when a request names a destination beyond the assigned subtree. - A hidden, deleted or foreign folder is not a usable target. A full lock returns the folder's locked state rather than writing underneath it. - Workspace storage, file-size, extension, member-storage and simultaneous-upload policies remain active after the destination is chosen. ## If you selected the wrong place Do not start another copy until you know whether the first one completed. Use the queue row's **View file** or **Go to location**, or search **Files** in the workspace recorded on that row. Move the completed item when your role permits it; otherwise ask an owner or admin to move it. Deleting the first copy before verifying the correction can remove the only successful transfer. ## Expected result The test row reaches **Done** and appears once in the intended folder of the intended workspace. The important transfer is then started with the same confirmed destination, and each completed row can be opened from its recorded location. ## Troubleshooting **The active workspace is wrong after switching.** Wait for **Switching workspace…** to finish, then read the sidebar name. Close stale tabs if two workspaces are easy to confuse. **The folder search returns no match.** Confirm the active workspace and spelling. Your role may be confined to another subtree, or the folder may have been hidden, moved or deleted. **New folder fails.** Your role may lack folder-creation permission, the parent may be locked, or the name may conflict with an existing child. Choose an existing writable destination or ask an administrator to create it. **The completed file is not where expected.** Check **Root (top level)**, the queue row's workspace, and **Go to location** before uploading again. The first copy may be valid in a different folder. ## Related guides - [Upload files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Switch between workspaces safely](/account/switch-workspaces) - [Fix a destination-blocked upload](/uploading/upload-destination-locked) - [Verify a sample upload](/uploading/upload-test-one-file) - [Choose a direct download or ZIP archive](/uploading/download-choose-method)

title: Fix an upload blocked by the destination
summary: Check the destination's lock and role restrictions, then choose a writable folder and restart the affected upload deliberately.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/upload/open.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/download-guard.ts, apps/api/src/lib/folder-lock-write-gate.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/unlock.ts, apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/web/src/api/error-copy.ts, and focused local tests. The paired workflow map illustrates the source-backed lock recovery branches with fictional file details.
body: An upload cannot add content inside a **full lock** on its destination folder or any ancestor. The web app displays the server's `folder_locked` code as **This folder is locked. Enter its password to open it.** A **view only** lock controls downloading and does not by itself block a new upload. The failed row keeps the workspace and folder chosen when it was created. **Retry** sends it to that same destination; changing **Upload options → Folder** affects files you add afterward. Decide whether to unlock the original path or create a new row for another writable folder. ## Before you start - Keep the original source file available in this browser tab. After a reload, a failed row cannot retry until the source is selected again. - Confirm the active workspace and expand the upload list or open **Uploads → Upload queue**. - Read the entire row message before changing access. **Destination folder not found**, **This folder is outside the folder you're confined to**, and a role permission error require different fixes. ## Steps: fix an upload blocked by the destination 1. Locate the failed filename and note the destination shown in its row. Do not remove the row until you have recorded the error. 2. Open **Files** and navigate to that folder. If an ancestor is fully locked, the folder page shows a password field and **Unlock**; access granted this way lasts **one hour** for your account. 3. Enter the folder password. Unlocking another member's session does not unlock yours, and an expired grant must be renewed. 4. Return to the existing upload row and select **Retry** while the tab still holds the source bytes. A successful unlock lets that row keep its original target. 5. If you should not unlock that area, open **Uploads**, choose a permitted destination under **Upload options → Folder**, then select the source again. This creates a separate queue row. 6. Wait for **Done**, choose **Open in Files**, and verify the final folder, filename and size. **Safety note.** A new destination can already contain the same filename. Dosya may treat a same-name upload as another version, so inspect the target before starting the replacement row. ## Expected result The intended row reaches **Done** in a folder your account can write to. The other failed row can be removed from the list after you verify the stored result; removing queue history does not delete a cloud file. ## Limits and important details - A folder-level full lock seals its whole subtree, including otherwise unlocked child folders. Unlocking the relevant ancestor for your account opens uploads until that one-hour grant expires. - A missing or hidden folder deliberately returns **Destination folder not found**. Ask an administrator to confirm the path rather than guessing whether a concealed folder exists. - Folder-confined members can upload only inside their assigned root. The exact refusal is **This folder is outside the folder you're confined to**. - Opening the Upload page requires **Access Upload**; sending a file requires **Upload files**. The page shows **Your role can't upload files** when the latter permission is absent. - Changing a lock requires the role's lock permission. A member who only knows the password can unlock the folder temporarily without removing its configured lock. ## Troubleshooting **The folder opens but Retry still says it is locked.** Confirm you unlocked the locked ancestor with the same account that owns the upload row. If more than one ancestor is protected, open each required folder before retrying. **Retry returns the same destination error.** The row still points to the original folder. Remove it, select a writable destination under **Upload options**, and add the source file as a new upload. **The row survived a refresh and Retry is disabled.** The browser no longer has the local bytes. If the row is **Interrupted**, use **Resume** and reselect the matching filename and byte size; otherwise remove it and create a fresh row. **The error says Destination folder not found.** The folder was deleted, is hidden from your role, or is no longer accessible. Choose a visible folder, because retrying cannot repair that reference. **The page says your role cannot upload.** Ask a role manager for **Upload files**. Moving to an unlocked folder does not bypass a workspace permission. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Lock a folder with a password](/files/lock-folder) - [Restrict a workspace member to one folder](/workspaces/folder-access)

title: Estimate storage before a large upload
summary: Total the source bytes, compare them with workspace free space, and account for versions, trash, concurrent uploads, and workspace storage caps.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/components/layout/dashboard-sidebar.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/upload-limits.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/upload-limits.ts; apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/measured-quota.ts.
body: The workspace switcher shows **free of** total storage, while the sidebar shows **Storage** used and total. The upload preflight also reads a `storage_remaining_bytes` hint. That hint is based on a quota value cached for 60 seconds, so it warns rather than guarantees that a concurrent batch will fit. The authoritative server gate uses both the account owner's total entitlement across workspaces and any lower workspace storage cap. Trashed files still consume storage until permanently removed, and a same-name upload can add a retained version instead of replacing storage byte-for-byte. ## Steps 1. In the operating system, select the source files and record their combined byte size; count every file inside folders, not the folder entry alone. 2. Open the Dosya workspace switcher and read its **free of** value for the target workspace; confirm the workspace name before doing any subtraction. 3. Check the sidebar **Storage** used/total display, and investigate a mismatch caused by another active transfer, another workspace using the owner's entitlement, or a workspace cap. 4. Add margin for uploads running in other tabs or devices and for same-name items that will become new versions; trash is still charged until permanent deletion. 5. Open **Uploads**, set the final **Folder**, and add one small representative item. If a later batch exceeds the current hint, Dosya warns **This may not all fit** and reports approximately how far over it is. 6. Let the sample reach **Done**, refresh the workspace storage display, then add the remaining sources and watch each row while the server rechecks measured bytes. ## Expected result The planned source total sits below the workspace's current free-space display with enough margin for concurrent changes, and the test item completes in the intended folder before the large batch proceeds. A server refusal beginning **You've used ... across all your workspaces** means the owner's account-wide entitlement is binding; empty the trash or upgrade. **This workspace has a N GB storage limit and this doesn't fit** means the workspace cap is lower; empty trash there or ask an owner/admin to raise the cap. A per-member refusal says **You've reached your N GB per-member storage limit**. This is one workspace-wide **Storage per member** setting applied uniformly to members; ask an owner or admin to raise that workspace setting. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders to Dosya](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Watch storage-sensitive transfers through each state](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Uploading files and folders to Dosya
summary: Choose a cloud workspace and folder, upload individual files or a complete folder tree, then verify every completed item in Dosya.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/role-create.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/dropped-entries.ts, apps/web/src/lib/dropped-entries.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/folder-upload.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-drop.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-drop.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-tree.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-concurrency.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/batch.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/upload-limits.ts and apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts. Verified exact destination and picker labels, Access Upload, Upload files and Create folders role rules, failed-subtree skipping, retained source-folder names, dropped empty-directory reconstruction, the 2,000-file expansion ceiling and exact refusal copy, drag-and-drop fallback, concurrency controls, workspace policy checks, and completed-item actions. All three screenshots were inspected against current UI; no asset changed.
body: Open **Uploads**, choose the destination under **Upload options → Folder**, then use **browse for files** or **pick a folder**. Wait for **Done** in the upload queue before checking or sharing the uploaded files. ## Before you start - Sign in to [the Dosya app](https://app.dosya.dev) and select the workspace that should receive the files. - Your role needs **Access Upload** to open `/uploads` and **Upload files** to transfer bytes. Uploading a directory tree also needs **Create folders** whenever Dosya must recreate a missing directory. - The workspace must have room and must accept the file size and extension under its current policies. - Keep the original files available on your device and the browser running until the transfer finishes. Avoid changing the source files during the upload. - These steps cover ordinary workspace storage. The [Vault](https://dosya.dev/vault/) has a separate encryption workflow; selecting a file on this page does not automatically make it a Vault upload. ## Steps: choose the destination 1. **Open Uploads.** Select **Uploads** in the app navigation. The page heading is **Upload files**. You can also open [Uploads](https://app.dosya.dev/uploads) directly, or select **Upload** in the **Files** toolbar. 2. **Check the workspace.** Confirm the workspace selected in the app's workspace switcher. Files go into that workspace, so choose it before starting a new batch. 3. **Choose the folder.** Find **Upload options**, then **Folder**. The folder button initially shows **Root (top level)** unless a destination was supplied when you opened the page. Root means the workspace's top level. 4. **Confirm a different destination if needed.** Select the folder button, choose a folder in **Select folder**, and confirm with **Select folder**. Check the updated folder name before adding files. A destination change applies to new files you add, rather than relocating a batch already queued. ## Steps: add files or a folder 1. **Pick individual files.** Select **browse for files** in the drop area, choose the loose files, and confirm. Loose files land directly in the destination selected under **Folder**. 2. **Or pick a whole folder.** Select **pick a folder** and confirm the directory. The browser supplies relative paths including the selected folder name, so `Photos/a.jpg` is stored as `destination/Photos/a.jpg`. 3. **Or drag and drop.** Drop files or a directory into **Drop files or folders here to upload**. A supported directory drop retains its top-level name and nested structure. It also recreates nested empty directories and a wholly empty dropped directory. 4. **Check the queue.** The **Upload queue** appears after files are added. Review the file names, total size and individual progress. A selected file does not count as a completed upload until its row shows **Done**. 5. **Adjust simultaneous uploads only if useful.** The browser defaults to 3 concurrent files and offers 1 through 5. A lower workspace maximum removes choices above that cap. Reduce the setting if several transfers overwhelm the connection. ## Steps: confirm completion 1. **Wait for Done.** Keep the tab open until every required row finishes. Moving to another page inside the app can leave the upload dock available while the queue continues; closing or reloading the tab is a different action. 2. **Open the finished result.** Use **View file** beside a completed row to find the file, or **Go to location** to open its containing folder. 3. **Check the destination.** In **Files**, confirm the names and folder structure in the intended workspace. Open a small test file to check a new workflow. 4. **Clear the finished queue when ready.** **Clear done** tidies finished queue entries. Your completed files remain in storage. ## Expected result Completed loose files appear directly in the chosen workspace folder. A picked or dropped directory retains its own top-level name and nested paths instead of flattening its files. For example, adding `Photos/a.jpg` to `Client delivery` produces `Client delivery/Photos/a.jpg`. Dosya creates the missing directory tree before queuing its file rows. A supported directory drop also creates empty directories because the browser exposes directory entries. A folder picker exposes paths attached to files, so a wholly empty picked directory can provide no entry for Dosya to recreate. A batch started from a group still keeps these folder locations while adding the completed files to that flat collection. ## Troubleshooting and limits If the page says **Your role can't upload files**, ask the workspace owner or admin about upload permission. Repeatedly choosing the same files will not change your role. If a row shows **Error**, read the reason beside it. Check connectivity, available storage and access to the destination. Use its **Retry** control when available, or **Retry all failed** only after correcting the shared cause. Completed rows are not restarted. If the message says **This folder is locked. Enter its password to open it.**, unlock that exact destination before retrying. Picking another open folder does not move an existing queue row. If a file is rejected by a size or extension rule, the row keeps the reason and never begins transferring. An owner or admin must change the workspace rule, or you must choose a compliant source file. If a folder picker returns no files, the browser has not supplied any relative file paths. Drop the empty directory into a browser that exposes directory entries if it must exist in Dosya, or create that folder manually. If folder creation returns **You don't have permission to create folders**, ask an owner or admin for **Create folders**, or upload loose files into an existing destination. **Some folders could not be created** means other branches were usable; **Folders could not be created** means no file row could be queued. Files below every failed directory are skipped and reported as left out instead of being flattened into a parent folder. Picker and drop expansion stops after 2,000 files. For a folder tree, Dosya shows **Too many files in one go** and a detail in the form **Only the first 2,000 files were queued - _N_ files left out. Drop the rest separately.** Record that skipped count, let the queued set finish, then add the remaining files as another batch. A loose-file selection follows the direct queue path and may show only **Uploading 2,000 files**; compare the number you selected with the queue count and add any remainder separately. A file's transfer data may no longer be available after a browser reload. If **Retry** is disabled and its message asks you to add the file again, choose the original file from your device. Check the completed files first so you do not resubmit an entire folder unnecessarily. Use [the network-interruption recovery steps](/uploading/upload-resume-after-network) when the row changes to **Interrupted**, and consult [upload progress states](/uploading/progress-and-states) before restarting a mixed batch. Browser folder support, service limits, storage allowance and workspace policies all affect uploads. Do not infer that every format or size will be accepted from the drop area's examples. Recoverable connection errors can be retried, but unattended completion is not guaranteed. - A workspace can set file-size, per-member storage, extension, total-storage and simultaneous-upload rules. The failure row or available concurrency choices reflect the applicable rule. - File and folder names must pass server name checks. Renaming a rejected source locally changes the name submitted on the next new attempt. - One picker or drop expansion queues at most 2,000 files. Folder-tree expansion reports the skipped count; for loose files, compare the selection and queue counts yourself. - A picked or dropped directory preserves the source directory name. Loose files alone have no relative folder path and land directly in the chosen destination. - Directory drop retains explicit empty-directory entries. Folder picker reconstruction is limited to directory paths represented by selected files. - Changing **Folder** after items enter the queue affects later additions only. Existing rows retain their original destination IDs. - **Clear done** removes finished queue records and leaves the cloud files in place. For a persistent issue, use [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support). Include the browser, approximate file size, failing step and exact error. You do not need to post the private file itself in a public question. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I leave the Uploads page while a transfer runs? You can navigate inside the app while the global queue continues. Keep the browser tab running and check the upload dock or return to **Uploads** for completion. Closing or reloading the tab can interrupt the transfer. ### Why are files waiting instead of uploading together? **Simultaneous uploads** limits the number running at once, and a workspace can impose a lower cap. Waiting queue entries are not necessarily failures; check whether the running entries are progressing. ### Does Clear done delete my uploaded files? No. It removes finished entries from the queue display. Use **View file** or **Go to location** before clearing if you want to check where a completed file landed. ## Related guides - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Watch the existing upload tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/upload-files-and-folders/) - [Why large uploads fail](https://dosya.dev/blog/why-large-uploads-fail) explains broader transfer problems.

title: Prepare file names before uploading
summary: Prepare names for Dosya sanitization, the 255-character limit, extension rules, and same-name versioning before starting a large upload batch.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/lib/upload-limits.ts; apps/web/src/lib/validation-policy.generated.ts; apps/web/src/lib/dropped-entries.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts; apps/api/src/lib/workspace-do/durable-object.ts.
body: The web uploader sanitizes incoming names before validating them. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, `/` and `\\` become `_`, ASCII control characters are removed, and the complete names `.` or `..` become `_`. The result must be at most 255 characters. Workspace upload rules can allow or block extensions. Dosya derives the extension from the final suffix in lowercase. A same-name file in the same destination normally becomes a new version of the existing file; rename one source first when both should remain separate live items. ## Steps 1. Open the final Dosya folder and compare source names with existing live files; choose new names when a new version is not the intended outcome. 2. Keep each file name at 255 characters or fewer after trimming, including the extension; longer results are rejected as **Name too long (max 255)**. 3. Replace path separators and ASCII control characters yourself when the exact stored spelling matters, because ingest would otherwise sanitize them automatically. 4.
