Leave ordinary quotes, apostrophes, `<`, and `>` intact when the local platform permits them; Dosya's current single-segment policy does not reject those characters. 5. Confirm every final suffix satisfies the workspace's allowlist or blocklist; files without an extension are reported as **(no extension)** when an allowlist requires one. 6. Upload one sample, wait for **Done**, and choose **View file** to inspect the stored name; rename the local source before the larger batch if sanitization changed the intended label. ## Expected result Each accepted queue row has a recognizable, valid name and allowed extension. Distinct source names create distinct live items; an intentional exact match updates the existing item's version history. Folder uploads automatically skip `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini`, and AppleDouble names beginning `._`. A blocked suffix stays as an error row with **File type .ext is not allowed in this workspace**; an allowlist miss says it **is not in the allowed list**. Correct the local name, remove the refused row, and add the renamed source as a new upload rather than pressing Retry on unchanged input. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders to Dosya](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Read rejection and completion states for renamed files](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Preserve folder structure during an upload
summary: Use Select folder or a folder drop, let Dosya rebuild parent folders first, and verify skipped subtrees instead of accepting a flattened upload.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/upload-drop.ts; apps/web/src/lib/dropped-entries.ts; apps/web/src/lib/folder-upload.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/index.ts.
body: Use **Select folder** or drag a folder onto **Drop files or folders here to upload**. The browser supplies each file's relative path, then Dosya creates parents before children and sends each file to its resolved folder. Loose-file selection does not carry a tree. One folder action accepts the first 2,000 files. A directory drag or drop can preserve empty folders through the FileSystem Entry API. **Select folder** reconstructs directories only from file relative paths, so wholly empty directories are absent. `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini`, and `._` AppleDouble entries are skipped. You need `access_upload`, `upload_files`, and `create_folders`; without folder creation rights, Dosya leaves affected subtree files out instead of flattening them into the destination. ## Steps 1. Open **Uploads** and use **Folder** under **Upload options** to choose the parent that should contain the uploaded top-level folder. 2. Choose **Select folder** to rebuild directories represented by file paths, or drag and drop the directory when wholly empty folders must also be preserved. Do not use **Select files** when relative paths are required. 3. Approve the browser's folder access prompt and keep the tab open while Dosya reports **Recreating N folders, then uploading**. 4. Expand **Upload queue** to inspect nested folder rows, file counts, total bytes, and failed counts; trees over 50 visible rows open only their top level initially. 5. If Dosya reports **Some folders could not be created**, record the failed-folder and left-out-file counts, correct the named permission, lock, or name issue, and retry that subtree. 6. After every expected file shows **Done**, choose **Go to location** on representative rows and compare the resulting parent/child paths with the source tree. ## Expected result The chosen destination contains the supported hierarchy represented by the chosen input. Accepted files follow their relative paths; empty directories are retained only when the browser exposes them through a directory drag or drop. Source files on the device are not moved or deleted. **Too many files in one go** means only the first 2,000 were queued; the toast states how many were left out, and those files must be added separately. **You don't have permission to create folders** requires an owner or admin to change the role. A failed parent causes its descendants to fail and their files to remain unqueued, which protects the tree from silent flattening. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders to Dosya](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Track nested folder rows in the upload queue](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Understanding upload progress and transfer states
summary: Read Queued, Uploading, Done, Error, Interrupted and Canceled states, then choose the action that matches the current transfer.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/lib/upload-types.ts, apps/web/src/stores/uploads.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-scheduler.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-persistence.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-concurrency.ts, apps/web/src/components/uploads/upload-dock.tsx and apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx. Verified all six web states, exact labels and row actions, byte-weighted active progress, three-file default and five-file user ceiling, workspace-cap clamping, three-second concurrency backoff, Clear done behavior and reload hydration. Both existing visuals were inspected; no asset changed.
body: Use an upload's current state to decide what to do. **Queued** waits for a transfer slot, **Uploading** is moving data, **Done** is complete, **Error** needs its cause corrected, **Interrupted** needs the original source selected again, and **Canceled** was deliberately stopped. The current Dosya web queue uses **Interrupted**, not “Paused,” for a transfer that lost its browser source after a reload or similar interruption. Follow the label and action shown in your app; desktop or mobile surfaces can present their transfer controls differently. ## Before you start - Open **Uploads** in the active workspace and expand the small upload list at the bottom right if it is collapsed. - Identify the exact filename and destination. Similar filenames can represent separate attempts. - Keep the source file available and unchanged until you verify **Done** in Files. - Do not clear a failed, interrupted or canceled row until you have recorded its message and checked the destination. ## Steps: read the current state 1. Find the file under **Upload queue** or in the upload list at the bottom right. 2. Match **Queued**, **Uploading**, **Done**, **Error**, **Interrupted** or **Canceled** to the table below. 3. Read the filename, transferred bytes, percentage and message together. A dock heading such as **Uploading 1/6 · 43%** uses active-item bytes for its percentage, so it is not a simple average of every row. 4. Use only the action for that row: wait, Cancel, Retry, Resume, View file or Go to location. 5. After any recovery action, wait for **Done** and inspect the stored file. | Web state | Meaning | Appropriate action | | --- | --- | --- | | **Queued** | The item is waiting for the scheduler, a transfer slot or a temporary concurrency backoff. | Keep the tab open and let active rows finish. | | **Uploading** | Dosya is transferring the file. Percentage, bytes and speed can change as work continues. | Keep the tab and device running. Cancel only if you intend to stop this attempt. | | **Done** | The service completed this upload. | Use **View file** or **Go to location**, then verify the destination copy. | | **Error** | The attempt failed with a stated cause. | Read and correct the cause, then use **Retry** when the source is still available. | | **Interrupted** | The retained row no longer has direct access to its browser source, often after reload. | Select **Resume** and reselect the unchanged original file. | | **Canceled** | A user stopped this attempt and the browser discarded its source reference. | Check Files for a completed copy. Start a new row if the file is still needed. | ## Steps: monitor a running batch 1. Leave **Uploading** rows running while their bytes or percentage continue to move. 2. Let **Queued** rows wait behind active work. **Upload options → Simultaneous uploads** defaults to 3, offers 1 through 5, and is reduced automatically when the workspace cap is lower. 3. You may browse to another page inside Dosya; the bottom-right upload list remains available. Keep the tab open and avoid a reload during active work. 4. If the server says the workspace already has uploads in progress, the web queue waits 3 seconds and tries again, up to five times, before showing an error. Leave the row queued during this controlled backoff. 5. If one row changes to **Error**, read that row's message. Other files can continue and should not be restarted automatically. 6. If a reload leaves a row **Interrupted**, choose **Resume** and select the same filename and size from your device. The check helps locate the source but does not prove identical contents. 7. Wait until every required row is **Done** or has a clearly understood exception. ## Steps: confirm completion 1. Select **View file** beside a Done row, or **Go to location** for its folder. 2. Check the active workspace, folder, filename and size in **Files**. 3. Open or download the **Done** file and perform any integrity check your workflow requires. 4. Use **Clear done** only after verification. It tidies queue history and does not remove uploaded files. ## Expected result You can tell whether a file is waiting, transferring, finished, failed, recoverable or deliberately stopped. You use the action attached to the affected row and verify a Done item in its destination instead of restarting the full batch. ## Limits of the progress display - Progress reports the current transfer attempt. It does not replace checking the destination file. - Percentage, transferred bytes and speed can update at different intervals. A short pause in the number does not by itself establish failure. - The batch heading summarizes several files. It can show one active upload while another row is queued, done or failed. - Queue history keeps at most the latest 50 rows in the browser. **Clear done** removes complete, error and canceled rows while leaving queued, uploading and interrupted rows. - Web, desktop and mobile apps can use different layouts or labels. These instructions describe the current English web app. ## Troubleshooting **A file remains Queued after others finish.** Check every active row and the workspace's simultaneous limit. A temporary concurrency refusal can hold the item outside the runnable queue for 3 seconds. If five controlled retries fail, the row changes to Error. **The percentage has not moved.** Check whether bytes or speed are changing and whether the connection is available. Give an active request time to finish its current part. If the row changes to Error, diagnose that message rather than adding a duplicate. **The page says Error.** Resolve the named network, storage, permission, destination or file-type cause, then select Retry. See [Troubleshooting a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload). **The page says Interrupted.** Expand the bottom-right upload list and select Resume. Reselect the unchanged original file. [Network recovery details](/uploading/upload-resume-after-network) explain when Dosya can reuse prior parts and when it restarts. **The page says Canceled but I still need the file.** Check Files first. If no completed copy exists, add the source again as a new upload. A canceled attempt has no Resume action. **A row says Done but I cannot find the file.** Use **View file** or **Go to location** from that row and confirm the workspace. The upload keeps the destination selected when that attempt was added; changing the folder later affects new items. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I use another Dosya page while an upload runs? Yes. The global upload list can continue while you navigate inside the web app. Keep the browser tab open and the device awake. ### Why is an upload pending after another file appears complete? The previous request can still be releasing its slot, another item can be active, or the workspace can enforce a lower concurrency cap. Look at every row and allow a short transition before treating the queued item as stuck. ### Is Interrupted the same as Canceled? No. Interrupted can offer **Resume** after you reselect the original. Canceled records a deliberate stop; begin a new upload if no completed copy exists. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Uploading large files with available storage](/uploading/large-files) - [Troubleshooting a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Canceling an upload safely](/uploading/cancel-upload)

title: Record useful details for an upload failure
summary: Capture the failed row’s exact error, file name, size, destination, workspace, time, browser state, and retry outcome before clearing the queue.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx; apps/web/src/components/uploads/upload-dock.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts; apps/web/src/lib/upload-persistence.ts; apps/web/src/stores/uploads.ts.
body: A failed upload row displays the source file name, formatted size, **Error**, and the server or network message that caused the failure. The web UI does not expose a request ID for these rows, so do not invent one or copy session cookies, API keys, upload URLs, or file contents into a support note. Record the evidence before choosing **Clear done**, **Clear**, **Remove**, signing out, or reloading. The queue can persist up to 50 recent rows, but browser `File` objects do not. A persisted failure remains **Error** after reload with its retry control disabled until the batch recovery action parks byte-less failures as **Interrupted**. ## Steps 1. Expand **Upload queue** or the upload dock and keep the failed row visible; do not press **Clear done**, **Clear**, or **Remove** yet. 2. Copy the exact red message, including numeric values and punctuation, such as **Network error**, a workspace extension refusal, or a storage-limit sentence. 3. Record the file name, displayed size, active workspace, selected **Folder**, local date/time with time zone, and whether the row failed before or after progress began. 4. Note the surface as the Dosya web **Uploads** page, the browser and operating-system versions, and whether a reload or account switch occurred after selection. 5. Capture a screenshot limited to the failed row and destination context; redact email addresses or neighboring file names that support does not need. 6. If the row still holds its bytes, press its **Retry** once and record the result. If Retry is disabled after reload, record that state before using **Retry all failed**, which changes every byte-less **Error** row to **Interrupted** and may requeue other failed rows that still have bytes. ## Expected result The evidence identifies one failed operation without disclosing a secret: exact row text, source metadata, destination, workspace, time zone, client environment, and the controlled retry outcome are all present. If Retry is disabled with **Add the file again to upload it - this tab no longer has its contents**, record that state. Choose **Retry all failed** to park every byte-less Error row as **Interrupted**, then use that row’s **Resume** to reselect the same name and size; there is no per-row Error-to-Interrupted control. For **That file does not match (name or size differs)**, preserve the original row and locate the exact source used before. Removing a row deletes only the local queue record; it does not delete a successfully stored Dosya file. ## Related guides - [Troubleshooting a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Canceling an upload safely](/uploading/cancel-upload)

title: Recover an upload after refreshing the browser
summary: Resume an interrupted browser upload by reselecting the same source file, then verify the completed cloud copy without creating a duplicate.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/lib/upload-persistence.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/web/src/stores/uploads.ts, apps/web/src/components/uploads/upload-dock.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/upload-persistence.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/status.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/complete.ts, and focused local tests. Screenshots retain isolated sample files and match the current Interrupted and Done controls.
body: A browser refresh keeps recent queue metadata in local storage, but the refreshed page cannot regain permission to read your source automatically. Dosya changes rows that were **Uploading** or **Queued** to **Interrupted** and requires you to pick the source again. Completed, failed and canceled rows keep their terminal state. Recovery depends on how the file was sent. Files larger than **50 MB** use multipart upload, so Dosya can ask the server which **10 MB** parts arrived and send only missing parts. A smaller single-request upload restarts from byte zero after reselection. ## Before you start - Keep the original source file in its current location and do not rename or edit it. - Open Dosya with the same account and workspace that started the upload. - Check whether the file already appears as **Done** in the upload dock or **Upload queue**. Also inspect its intended folder in **Files**, because a server-completed session can be discovered during recovery even when the restored row lacks a direct file shortcut. - If the destination folder was deleted, locked or made read-only, resolve that access problem before resuming. ## Steps: resume the interrupted upload 1. Return to Dosya after the page reloads and expand the upload dock in the lower-right corner. 2. Find the row marked **Interrupted**. Confirm its filename, size and destination before selecting anything. 3. Select **Resume** on that row. Dosya opens the browser file picker because the refreshed tab cannot recover a local file automatically. 4. Choose the original file. Its name and byte size must match the interrupted row. If either value differs, Dosya refuses the selection so a different file cannot silently replace the original upload. 5. Keep the page open while the row returns to **Queued** and then displays byte progress. For multipart recovery, the server's status determines which part numbers are still missing; the saved percentage alone is not authoritative. 6. Wait for **Done**. If **Open in Files** is available, use it; otherwise navigate to **Files** and open the recorded destination yourself. Confirm the cloud item has the expected name and byte size. ## Expected result The interrupted row resumes after you reselect the matching source and eventually changes to **Done**. Exactly one intended cloud result appears in the original destination, and its displayed size matches the local source. ## Limits and important details - Browsers do not allow a website to retain unrestricted access to a local file after a reload. Reselecting the source file is required. - Dosya retains only the latest **50** transfer rows in that browser profile. Clearing site data, using a private session, changing browsers, or signing in as a different account can remove or hide the recovery row. - **Retry** works for a failed row only while the current tab still holds the source file. After a reload, a retained **Error** row keeps Retry disabled. Open **Uploads → Upload queue**, choose **Retry all failed** to move it to **Interrupted**, then select **Resume** and reselect the matching original. A row that was Queued or Uploading when the page reloaded is already Interrupted and can use Resume directly. - A mismatch produces **Could not resume** with `That file does not match (name or size differs).` Dosya does not hash two same-named, same-sized files before resuming, so choose the original deliberately. - Do not drag the file into the main upload area as a substitute for **Resume**. That starts a separate upload and can create a name conflict or another version. - Completed rows are preserved across a refresh. Verify **Done** before restarting a transfer that may already have finished. - Resume does not override current policy. Storage, role access, a deleted destination, an expired folder unlock or a newly blocked file type can still stop the remaining transfer or completion. ## Troubleshooting **Resume says the file does not match.** Select the original file with the same filename and exact byte size. If you renamed or edited it, remove the interrupted row and start a new upload so the changed source is handled explicitly. **The row stays Interrupted after selection.** Confirm that you chose a file instead of closing the picker. Reopen **Resume** and watch for the **Could not resume** message; it identifies a name or size mismatch. **The upload returns to Error.** Read the error beneath the filename. Check workspace storage, upload permission, the destination folder, and network stability before retrying. **The cloud file already exists.** Open the destination from Files and compare the name, size and current version. Remove the interrupted row if the intended upload is already complete; do not resume it merely to clear the warning. **You no longer have the source file.** The browser cannot finish the upload without those bytes. Remove the interrupted row and recover the source from its original device or another trusted copy. **Resume begins at zero percent.** That is expected for a file that used the single-request path or whose multipart session can no longer be recovered. Keep the original unchanged and let the new transfer finish. **The row is missing after you sign in.** Upload metadata is bound to the browser profile and account that stored it. Return to that browser and account; if the row was cleared or aged out of the latest 50 entries, check Files before creating a new attempt. ## Related guides - [Understand upload progress and transfer states](/uploading/progress-and-states) - [Troubleshoot a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Cancel an upload safely](/uploading/cancel-upload)

title: Resume an upload after a network interruption
summary: Recover a network-interrupted cloud upload by retrying in the same tab or reselecting its original source after a browser reload.
verification: Local source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-persistence.ts, apps/web/src/stores/uploads.ts, apps/web/src/components/uploads/upload-dock.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/upload-persistence.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/body-pipeline.ts and apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/status.ts. Verified Network error handling, terminal Error preservation after reload, queued/uploading-to-Interrupted hydration, Retry all failed parking without a retained File object, exact name-and-size Resume validation, the 50 MiB multipart threshold, 10 MiB part reuse, single-request restart behavior, completed-session rows without attached file shortcuts, and canceled-item handling. The existing failed-row screenshot was inspected; no visual asset changed.
body: A failed transfer can show **Network error** under an **Error** row. If the same tab still holds the source, **Retry** requeues that row. Reloading preserves a failed **Error** row but removes its file bytes. Choose **Retry all failed** to change that row to **Interrupted**, then use **Resume** to reselect the source. A row that was still **Queued** or **Uploading** at reload becomes **Interrupted** immediately. ## Before you start - Keep the original file at the same name and size. Resume rejects a different selection with **That file does not match (name or size differs).** - Confirm the row's workspace and destination before continuing. Retry does not move the upload to whichever folder is currently open. - Restore a stable connection before selecting an action. Repeated retries cannot repair an unavailable network. ## Steps: resume an upload after a network interruption 1. Open **Uploads** or expand the upload list at the bottom right. 2. Match the failed row by filename, size, workspace and destination. Record the error before changing anything. 3. Restore the connection and confirm the **Network error** condition has ended with an ordinary page request. 4. If the tab stayed open and **Retry** is enabled on the **Error** row, choose it. Dosya clears the old error and returns that same item to **Queued**. 5. After a reload, expect a failed row to remain **Error** with Retry disabled. Review every failed row, then choose **Retry all failed**. Rows without retained source files move to **Interrupted** and keep their previous error for reference. 6. Choose **Resume** on the affected **Interrupted** row, select the unchanged original file, and confirm the picker. A row that was Queued or Uploading during the reload can start at this step because hydration already marked it Interrupted. 7. Watch the row return to **Queued** or **Uploading**. Wait for **Done**, then use **View file** or **Go to location** to inspect the stored result. Retry one affected item first. **Retry all failed** requeues only rows whose files are still available to this tab; reloaded rows are parked as **Interrupted** so you can reselect them. ## Expected result The original queue row reaches **Done**, and one file appears in its original destination. A file larger than 50 MiB uses multipart transfer with 10 MiB parts and can reuse parts the server still reports as uploaded. A file at or below 50 MiB restarts its single request from zero after you reselect it. If the server reports that a resumed session is already complete, the row changes to **Done** without uploading again. The recovered row can lack a direct **View file** or **Go to location** shortcut; open **Files** and verify the recorded destination manually. ## Limits and important details - Retry continues the same queue item. Dropping the file into the main upload area creates another item and can produce a duplicate or name conflict. - Files larger than 50 MiB use 10 MiB multipart pieces and can resume from parts still reported by the server. Resume reads server status rather than trusting the percentage stored in the browser. - Files at or below 50 MiB use one request. They have no reusable part boundary, so resume begins that request again from zero. - Resume validates only name and size at selection time. Keep the source unchanged because another file can share both values. - A page reload preserves at most the latest 50 queue records in that browser. It preserves metadata, not the local file contents. - Dosya warns before closing or reloading while rows are **Queued** or **Uploading**. Browser or device shutdown can still interrupt them. - A deliberately **Canceled** row cannot resume. Check Files, then start a new upload if no completed copy exists. ## Troubleshooting **Retry is disabled after a reload.** The failed row correctly remains **Error**, but the browser no longer has its source bytes. Choose **Retry all failed** to move that row to **Interrupted**, then select **Resume** and reselect the original file with the same name and size. **The row is already Interrupted after reload.** It was Queued or Uploading when the page reloaded. Select **Resume** directly; **Retry all failed** is only needed to park retained Error rows. **Resume says the file does not match.** Select the original filename at its original byte size. If that source was edited or replaced, keep the interrupted row for reference and begin a deliberate new upload. **The row fails again immediately.** Copy the new message. Storage, extension, permission, destination-lock and workspace-limit failures need their stated cause corrected before another network retry. **You see two rows for the same file.** Do not keep retrying both. Verify whether either copy reached Files, cancel the unnecessary active attempt, and retain the row whose destination is correct. ## Related guides - [Troubleshoot a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Recover an upload after refreshing the browser](/uploading/upload-recover-after-refresh) - [Cancel an upload](/uploading/cancel-upload)

title: Retry one failed upload item
summary: Retry one failed row while its bytes remain in the tab, or reselect the same name and size after a reload so completed items stay untouched.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx; apps/web/src/components/uploads/upload-dock.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts; apps/web/src/stores/uploads.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts.
body: Use the row-level **Retry** for an **Error** item while the current tab still holds that file's bytes. It requeues only that row, keeps completed rows unchanged, and clears the prior error while the new attempt runs. **Retry all failed** is a separate batch action. After a reload, an existing **Error** row keeps that status but no longer has file bytes, so its row-level Retry is disabled. **Retry all failed** processes every Error row: byte-less rows become **Interrupted**, while any failed rows that still have bytes are requeued. Only then does **Resume** appear per interrupted row. A multipart session keeps server-tracked parts; a single-PUT upload restarts from zero. ## Steps 1. Expand **Upload queue** and read the failed row's complete message before deciding that another attempt can succeed. 2. Correct the stated cause: restore connectivity, free storage, change the file to an allowed extension, unlock the destination, or obtain the required permission. 3. If the row still offers **Retry**, press that row’s control once; this is the only path that isolates one Error row before a reload. 4. If Retry is disabled after reload, choose **Retry all failed** knowing it touches every Error row. Byte-less rows become **Interrupted**; then choose **Resume** on the intended row and select the same local name and byte size. 5. Reject a look-alike that triggers **That file does not match (name or size differs).** Watch the resumed row move through **Queued** and percentage progress while completed rows remain **Done**. 6. When the row reaches **Done**, choose **View file** or **Go to location** and compare the destination name and displayed size with the source. ## Expected result A row-level Retry requeues only the selected failure. After reload, the batch recovery action may requeue every failed row whose bytes remain and parks all byte-less failures as Interrupted; Resume then acts on one selected row. A successful attempt reaches **Done** without restarting earlier completed transfers. The client automatically waits three seconds and retries a workspace-concurrency refusal up to five times before showing it as an error. Do not repeatedly click Retry during that queued backoff. Canceling or removing the row is different: cancellation stops active requests and marks the row **Canceled**, while removal only clears the queue entry. A same-name retry can still become a new version if a live item with that name now exists in the destination. ## Related guides - [Troubleshooting a failed upload](/troubleshooting/failed-upload) - [Canceling an upload safely](/uploading/cancel-upload)

title: Run a one-file upload preflight
summary: Send one uniquely named sample to the final folder, wait for Done, then use View file and File details to verify destination, name, and size.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-15; production behavior was not exercised for this revision. Verified against: apps/web/src/router.tsx; apps/web/src/pages/uploads.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/body-pipeline.ts; apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx.
body: A one-file preflight checks the actual workspace, folder, role, storage gate, extension policy, transfer path, and completion receipt before a large upload. Use a small representative file with a unique name; an exact name collision in the destination can create a new version of the existing item. The **Uploads** route requires `access_upload`, and the upload area requires `upload_files`. Workspace settings can also restrict the extension, size, per-member storage, concurrent uploads, or destination folder. Files over 50 MiB use resumable 10 MiB parts, so a small test does not exercise that multipart path. ## Steps 1. Create or choose a small source file whose extension matches the larger batch and whose name does not already exist in the destination. 2. Open **Uploads**, confirm the active workspace, and set **Folder** under **Upload options** to the exact final location. 3. Choose **Select files**, add only the sample, and confirm the **Upload queue** shows one file with the expected name and size. 4. Keep the tab open as the row changes from **Queued** to percentage progress and finally **Done**; investigate an **Error** before adding more sources. 5. Choose **View file** on the completed row, open **File details**, and compare the stored name and displayed size with the local sample. 6. Choose **Go to location** and confirm the file sits in the final folder; download and open it when the preflight must also test byte retrieval. ## Expected result The sample reaches **Done**, opens from its completed row, and appears in the chosen workspace folder with the expected name and size. The local source remains unchanged. **Your role can't upload files** means the page is visible but `upload_files` is absent; ask an owner or admin. A workspace file-size or extension refusal names the exact setting. A successful small preflight proves the ordinary one-file path, destination, and permissions, but a production batch above 50 MiB per file should also include one large multipart sample before unattended transfer. ## Related guides - [Uploading files and folders to Dosya](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Interpret the sample file's queue states](/uploading/progress-and-states)

title: Clear a stale Vault device cache safely
summary: Clear only local Vault state safely: finish transfers, use Lock, understand persisted Space hints, and avoid the irreversible destroy-vault control.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/stores/e2ee.ts, apps/web/src/components/e2ee/unlock-gate.tsx, apps/web/src/components/e2ee/encrypted-browser.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/user-keys.ts, and packages/e2ee-client/src/file.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Vault secrets live only in memory. The persisted browser store keeps nonsecret Space hints—IDs, names, ownership anchors, workspace grouping, and shared status—but no passphrase, recovery key, private key, session, or file bytes. ## Steps 1. Wait until the Vault no longer shows its busy skeleton and any upload has produced **Uploaded** or **Upload failed**. There is no persistent transfer queue to resume after clearing browser state. 2. Choose **Lock** in the Vault header. This immediately drops the in-memory session, open Space, decrypted entries, member list, and current error. 3. Reload the Vault and unlock again. Use this supported reset first; it preserves the locally remembered nonsecret Space list while fetching encrypted state with a new session. 4. If stale Space labels remain, sign out and clear site data for Dosya in the browser settings. This removes the `dosya_e2ee` localStorage record and other site state, so expect to sign in again. 5. Return to **Vault** and unlock again, using the passphrase or **Use recovery key**. Allow Dosya to list the Spaces available to the server identity. 6. Open the expected Space and folder, then download a small known file. A successful decrypt proves the cloud data and current identity still agree. **Avoid the wrong control.** **Destroy vault and start over** is not cache cleanup. It permanently deletes the caller’s Vault identity, grants, and Space membership after account-password confirmation. Other members keep their identities and access to shared Space data. Authenticator-app 2FA also requires a current code; an account using email-code 2FA must switch to an authenticator app before destruction is available. ## Expected result A fresh in-memory session loads encrypted Space metadata and files without deleting server content. Only nonsecret browser hints are lost if site data is cleared; the Vault identity remains intact. ## Related guides - [Recover Vault access with saved credentials](/files/vault-recovery) - [Troubleshoot Vault unlock errors](/troubleshooting/vault-unlock)

title: Upload and download encrypted Vault files
summary: Create or select an encrypted Space, upload files after browser-side encryption, download and verify them, and work within current Vault limits.
verification: Reviewed Vault Space selection, encrypted upload, file listing and browser-side download behavior against the local current web app and API on 2026-10-12. The screenshot uses isolated representative files.
body: Files in Vault belong to an encrypted Space. Your browser encrypts an upload before sending it and decrypts a download after receiving it, so keep the Vault unlocked until the operation finishes. ## Before you start - Set up and unlock Vault. - Choose which Space should hold the file, and confirm you have access to it. - Keep enough local disk space for the original file and the completed download. - Upload individual files. Vault does not currently preserve folder structures. - For an important file, retain the source until you have downloaded and opened a verification copy. ## Steps: upload an encrypted file 1. Open **Vault** and unlock it. 2. Select an existing Space under **My Spaces** or **Shared with me**, or create the appropriate Space if the interface offers that action. 3. Select **Upload** and choose one or more files. 4. Keep the tab open while the browser encrypts and uploads each file. 5. Wait until the files appear in the selected Space without an active transfer state. 6. Confirm the displayed file names and sizes before removing your local originals. ## Steps: download and verify a file 1. Unlock Vault and open the Space containing the file. 2. Open the file's action menu and choose **Download**. 3. Keep Vault unlocked and the tab open while the browser receives and decrypts the file. 4. Open the downloaded copy locally. 5. For critical data, compare its size, format and contents with the expected original before treating the copy as verified. ## Expected result An uploaded file appears in its selected Space and remains available after you lock and unlock Vault. A completed download opens as the original readable file on your device; ciphertext is not presented as the final download. ## Limits and sharing boundaries - Folders are not supported yet. A dropped folder does not recreate its directory structure in Vault. - Ordinary Dosya share links do not grant decryption access to a Vault file. Use encrypted Space membership for the intended people. - Closing the tab, locking Vault or losing connectivity can interrupt an active operation. - Available actions depend on your access to that encrypted Space. - Vault encryption does not scan or repair a damaged source file. Verify the source before upload and the local copy after download. ## Troubleshooting **The upload stopped.** Unlock Vault if needed, confirm the network connection and retry while keeping the tab active. Check whether the file already appears before creating a duplicate. **Only loose files appeared after dropping a folder.** Vault does not support folders. Upload the needed files directly and use separate Spaces where a broader division is required. **The downloaded file will not open.** Wait for the browser download to finish, then retry while Vault remains unlocked. Compare the downloaded size with the listed file and verify that a suitable local application supports its format. **A collaborator cannot see the file.** Confirm that they have access to the same encrypted Space. Membership in an ordinary workspace or possession of a standard share link does not by itself grant Vault decryption access. ## Related guides - [Understand Dosya Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Set up and unlock Dosya Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Recover access to Dosya Vault](/files/vault-recovery) - [Download files from ordinary storage](/uploading/download-files)

title: Plan for a lost Vault passphrase
summary: Recover a Vault with the one-time recovery key, recognize exact unlock errors, and use identity destruction only when permanent unreadability is accepted.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/stores/e2ee.ts, apps/web/src/components/e2ee/unlock-gate.tsx, apps/web/src/components/e2ee/encrypted-browser.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/e2ee/user-keys.ts, and packages/e2ee-client/src/file.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya cannot reveal or reset a Vault passphrase. The recovery key shown once at setup is the supported alternative; spaces and dashes in a pasted key are ignored. ## Steps 1. On the **Unlock Vault** card, choose **Use recovery key**. Do not create a new identity while the existing encrypted files are still needed. 2. Paste the recovery key into **Recovery key**. It may contain spaces or dashes; normalization removes those characters without changing letter case. 3. Choose **Unlock** and wait for the Vault surface. A wrong key reports `That recovery key did not unlock your Vault.` A build without recovery support reports that recovery unlock is unavailable in this version. 4. Open each important Space and download one known file. Unlock success alone is weaker evidence than decrypting actual content. 5. Store the recovered access material offline. The setup dialog’s recovery key is shown once and is never persisted by the web store. 6. If recovery is impossible, use **Destroy vault and start over** only to remove your identity, grants, and Space memberships permanently. **Who loses access.** Destruction removes only the caller’s identity and access. Other members keep their identities and access to shared Space data; a Space with no remaining member has no one left who can open it. **Last-resort confirmation.** Identity destruction requires the Dosya account password and the checkbox `I understand my encrypted files cannot be recovered after this.` An account using authenticator-app 2FA must also provide a current code. Email-code 2FA cannot complete this operation; switch to an authenticator app in security settings before trying again. There is no undo, and support cannot reconstruct the destroyed identity keys. ## Expected result A valid recovery key restores decryption access and lets known files download. If no credential survives, you make an explicit irreversible decision rather than mistaking a new Vault setup for recovery. ## Related guides - [Follow the complete Vault recovery guide](/files/vault-recovery) - [Interpret Vault unlock failures](/troubleshooting/vault-unlock)

title: Give or remove access to a Vault Space
summary: Invite another Dosya user to an encrypted Space, verify the contact before trusting the key, and revoke future access with re-keying.
verification: Reviewed the Vault Members list, invite control, trust-on-first-use warning and revoke confirmation against the local current web app and encryption store on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated representative members.
body: Vault access is granted per encrypted Space. Invite the person's Dosya email from the Space's **Members** panel, verify the contact through another channel, and revoke access there when it should end. ## Before you start - Unlock Vault and open the exact Space you intend to share. - Confirm the recipient's Dosya account email through a trusted channel. - Ask the recipient to set up Vault encryption first. An account without an encrypted identity cannot be invited yet. - Remove files that do not belong in the shared Space before granting access. - Understand that revocation cannot erase copies already downloaded by the member. ## Steps: invite a member 1. Open **Vault**, unlock it and select the intended Space. 2. Select **Members** above the encrypted file list. 3. Review the existing member list and the Space name in the dialog title. 4. Enter the recipient's complete Dosya email address. 5. Verify the address with the recipient outside Dosya because current access uses trust on first use. 6. Select **Invite** and wait for the member list to refresh. 7. Ask the recipient to unlock Vault and check **Shared with me** for the Space. ## Steps: revoke a member 1. Open the Space and select **Members**. 2. Find the exact email whose access should end. 3. Select its revoke control. 4. Read the confirmation. Revocation re-keys the Space so the member cannot read future content, but copies they already downloaded stay with them. 5. Select **Revoke** and keep Vault open while re-keying completes. 6. Reopen **Members** and confirm the email is gone. ## Expected result An invited user sees the encrypted Space under **Shared with me** after unlocking Vault. After successful revocation and re-keying, the removed user cannot read future content in that Space, and their email no longer appears in its member list. ## Limits and trust boundaries - Vault Space membership is separate from ordinary workspace membership and ordinary share links. - Automatic key-transparency protection is not yet available in the current interface; verify a new contact out of band. - The recipient must already have a Vault encryption identity. - Revocation cannot remove local copies already downloaded or otherwise saved by the former member. - Re-keying a large Space can take time. Do not close the session or assume completion before the UI confirms it. ## Troubleshooting **The invite says the user has not set up encryption.** Ask the recipient to open Vault, create their encryption identity and save their recovery key. Retry after they finish. **The wrong email was invited.** Revoke that member promptly, wait for re-keying to complete, then invite the verified address. **The recipient cannot find the Space.** Confirm the exact account email, ask them to unlock Vault and check **Shared with me**, then refresh the current session. **Members will not load.** Keep Vault unlocked, verify the active Space and retry after checking the connection. Do not create a duplicate Space as a workaround. **Revocation appears stuck.** Leave Vault open while the Space re-keys. If it fails, preserve the visible error and Space name for private support; never include a passphrase or recovery key. ## Related guides - [Understand Dosya Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Set up and unlock Dosya Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Upload and download encrypted Vault files](/files/vault-files) - [Troubleshoot a Vault that will not unlock](/troubleshooting/vault-unlock)

title: Understand Dosya Vault
summary: Learn what Vault protects, how browser-side encryption and Spaces work, and when ordinary files or password-protected share links are more suitable.
verification: Reviewed the Vault setup, unlock, Space, upload, download and lock states against the local current web app and encryption store on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated representative data.
body: Dosya Vault is a separate area for end-to-end encrypted files. Your browser encrypts a file before it leaves the device, and Dosya stores ciphertext. You unlock the Vault locally with your Vault passphrase or recovery key. ## Before you start - Decide whether the file needs Vault protection or the collaboration features of ordinary storage. - Use a current browser on a device you trust. - Plan where to store the recovery key before setup. Dosya shows it once. - Remember that your Dosya account password and Vault passphrase protect different things. ## Steps: choose the right storage method 1. Use **ordinary files** when you need the normal file browser and standard sharing workflows. 2. Use a **password-protected share link** when a recipient needs a link protected by a password. This does not turn the stored file into a Vault file. 3. Use **Vault** when you need browser-side encryption and can manage a separate passphrase plus recovery key. 4. Inside Vault, choose or create a **Space**. **My Spaces** are yours; **Shared with me** contains encrypted Spaces to which another member granted access. 5. Lock Vault when you finish, especially on a shared device. Locking clears the active in-memory Vault session. ## Expected result When Vault is unlocked, you can see the Spaces available to you and work with their encrypted files. Upload encryption and download decryption happen in the browser. When you lock Vault or end the session, you must unlock it again to read those files. ## Limits and security boundaries - Dosya cannot reset a forgotten Vault passphrase or reconstruct a lost recovery key. - Folders are not supported in Vault yet. Dropping a folder uploads supported loose files at the Space root rather than recreating its folder tree. - Ordinary share links and their passwords are separate from Vault access and do not decrypt Vault files. - Anyone with your recovery key can use it to unlock your Vault identity. Store it like a high-value secret. - End-to-end encryption protects file contents in the Vault flow. It does not remove the need to secure the device, browser session and account. ## Troubleshooting **Vault asks for a different password.** Enter the Vault passphrase created during setup, rather than your normal account password. **A folder did not appear after dropping it.** Vault does not preserve folder structures yet. Upload individual files and organize them by Space. **A teammate cannot open an ordinary share link to a Vault file.** Vault uses encrypted Space membership. Add the intended member through the Vault access flow rather than sending a standard file link. **The files disappeared after locking.** Unlock Vault again. Locking removes the local session; it does not delete the encrypted Space or its files. ## Related guides - [Set up and unlock Dosya Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Upload and download encrypted Vault files](/files/vault-files) - [Recover access to Dosya Vault](/files/vault-recovery) - [Protect a sharing link with a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Recover access to Dosya Vault
summary: Unlock Vault with the recovery key when the passphrase is unavailable, and understand the permanent consequences of destroying a Vault identity.
verification: Reviewed recovery-key unlock and the destructive Vault reset path against the local current web app and encryption store on 2026-10-12. The illustrated key is fictional and isolated.
body: Use the recovery key when you cannot enter the Vault passphrase. It restores access to the encrypted identity; destroying the Vault is a separate last-resort action that makes every file encrypted under the old identity unreadable. ## Before you start - Look for the recovery key in the password manager or offline record chosen during setup. - Work privately. Do not paste the key into chat, email, support tickets or a screen recording. - Keep any still-unlocked Vault session open on another trusted device until recovery succeeds. - Treat **Destroy vault and start over** as permanent data loss, not a normal password reset. ## Steps: unlock with the recovery key 1. Sign in to Dosya and open **Vault**. 2. On the unlock screen, select **Use recovery key**. 3. Paste or type the complete recovery key. The field accepts the key with spaces or dashes removed or included. 4. Select **Unlock**. 5. Open the required Spaces and confirm that important files can be downloaded and opened. 6. Follow the available security controls to establish access you can retain. Keep the recovery key secured until you have verified the new access path. ## Expected result A valid recovery key unlocks the existing Vault identity and its encrypted Spaces in the browser. Confirm recovery by opening or downloading a known file, rather than relying only on the unlocked screen. ## Steps: start over only when the encrypted data can be lost 1. Exhaust searches for the Vault passphrase, recovery key and any trusted device with an active unlocked session. 2. Read the destructive warning in full. 3. If every old Vault file can be abandoned, select **Destroy vault and start over**. 4. Confirm with the requested account password and two-factor authentication when enabled. 5. Create a new encrypted identity and save its new recovery key. ## Limits and irreversible consequences - Dosya cannot reset the Vault passphrase or generate the old recovery key. - If both are lost, the old encrypted files cannot be recovered by Dosya support. - Destroying the Vault identity does not decrypt or migrate old files. It makes all files encrypted for that identity permanently unreadable. - Your account password and account password-reset email do not decrypt Vault data. - Removing spaces or dashes can help normalize a copied key, but missing or changed key characters cannot be reconstructed. ## Troubleshooting **The recovery key is rejected.** Copy it again from the original secure record. Remove surrounding whitespace, check the first and last characters, and avoid using a key from a different account or identity. **You still have an unlocked session elsewhere.** Keep it open. Download essential files from that trusted session before changing or destroying anything. **Two-factor authentication blocks the destructive reset.** Recover account-level two-factor access first. This does not recover the Vault passphrase, but it may be required to authorize identity destruction. **Both passphrase and recovery key are gone.** Search backups and password-manager history before using the destructive option. Support cannot bypass the encryption or restore the old files afterward. ## Related guides - [Set up and unlock Dosya Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Understand Dosya Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Upload and download encrypted Vault files](/files/vault-files) - [Reset your Dosya account password](/account/reset-password)

title: Set up and unlock Dosya Vault
summary: Create your encrypted Vault identity, save the one-time recovery key, enter the Vault, and lock or unlock it safely on later visits.
verification: Reviewed first-time Vault identity setup, the one-time recovery-key dialog, passphrase unlock and manual lock behavior against the local current web app on 2026-10-12. The shown recovery key is fictional and isolated.
body: Vault setup creates the encrypted identity used to open your Vault Spaces. It requires a dedicated passphrase and produces a recovery key that appears once during setup. ## Before you start - Use a trusted device and private browser session. - Prepare a password manager or secure offline location for the recovery key. - Choose a unique Vault passphrase you can retain. Your account password cannot replace it. - Finish setup without screen sharing or recording the recovery-key screen. ## Steps: create the Vault identity 1. Sign in to Dosya and open **Vault**. 2. Select **Set up encryption**. 3. Enter a strong Vault passphrase, then enter it again exactly. 4. Read the recovery warning and complete setup. 5. When **Save your recovery key** appears, copy the entire key to your password manager or secure offline record. 6. Check that the saved copy is complete before selecting **I've saved it**. The setup flow does not show the key again. ## Steps: unlock and lock Vault later 1. Open **Vault** while signed in. 2. Enter the Vault passphrase and select **Unlock**. 3. Work in the required Space. 4. When finished, select the lock control. This clears the active Vault session from memory. 5. Enter the passphrase again the next time you need access. ## Expected result After setup or unlock, Vault shows **My Spaces** and any **Shared with me** Spaces available to your account. Locking returns you to the unlock screen without deleting encrypted data. ## Limits and precautions - The recovery key is shown once. Dosya does not provide a later “show key” screen. - Losing both the Vault passphrase and recovery key makes the existing encrypted files unreadable. - Browser password autofill may not distinguish your account password from the Vault passphrase. Check the value before submitting. - The active keys are held for the unlocked browser session. Lock Vault before another person uses the device. ## Troubleshooting **The two passphrase fields do not match.** Re-enter both values carefully. Check keyboard layout, capitalization and password-manager suggestions. **The saved recovery key looks incomplete.** Do not close the one-time dialog. Copy it again and verify the beginning and end in the secure destination. **The passphrase does not unlock Vault.** Confirm you are using the Vault passphrase, not the Dosya sign-in password. If it is lost, switch to recovery-key unlock. **Vault locks after a reload or new session.** Unlock it again. Keys are not kept as a reusable secret in ordinary browser storage. ## Related guides - [Understand Dosya Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Upload and download encrypted Vault files](/files/vault-files) - [Recover access to Dosya Vault](/files/vault-recovery) - [Set up two-factor authentication](/account/two-factor)

title: Diagnose a stalled Vault transfer
summary: Diagnose Vault uploads and downloads that appear stalled, account for in-memory processing and sequential files, and retry without duplicating success.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/stores/e2ee.ts, apps/web/src/components/e2ee/unlock-gate.tsx, apps/web/src/components/e2ee/encrypted-browser.tsx, and packages/e2ee-client/src/file.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The current Vault UI exposes one shared busy state rather than per-file progress. It reads each selected upload into browser memory, encrypts and uploads files sequentially, refreshes the folder, then shows one success or failure toast. ## Steps 1. Keep the Vault tab open while the busy skeleton is visible. Locking, reloading, or clearing site data drops the in-memory operation and provides no resume queue. 2. For a multi-file upload, allow earlier files to finish before assuming the last one is stuck. `uploadFiles` processes the selected list one file at a time and reports success only after a folder refresh. 3. Check browser connectivity, active workspace storage, upload policy, and that the Space is associated with a live workspace. On a scope-required refusal, the web store attaches the Space to the active workspace and retries once. 4. Read the red Vault error and toast. Upload failures use **Upload failed** with a **Report** action; download failures use **Download failed**. The fallback messages are `Could not upload file.` and `Could not download file.` 5. Refresh the folder before retrying. A prior operation may have committed even if the final refresh or toast failed, so confirm whether the filename already exists. 6. Retry one small file or download at a time. Vault chunks plaintext with a 4 MiB maximum chunk size, but the web store still holds the selected file or reconstructed download in memory. **Concurrency recovery.** The encrypted client can re-seal and retry a file commit up to five times when the workspace key rotates. A hot workspace that continues changing can eventually return an error instead of waiting forever. **No background guarantee.** The browser Vault flow does not promise continued transfer after the tab closes or the device sleeps. For large files, keep the browser active and avoid memory pressure from many simultaneous tabs. ## Expected result The retried item either appears once in the refreshed encrypted folder or produces a specific visible error that can be reported. You do not rely on a progress percentage or resumable queue the current Vault UI does not provide. ## Related guides - [Recover and reopen a Vault identity](/files/vault-recovery) - [Fix passphrase and recovery-key unlock problems](/troubleshooting/vault-unlock)

title: Troubleshoot a Vault that will not unlock
summary: Diagnose encryption-status, passphrase and recovery-key failures without exposing secrets or destroying an encrypted Vault by mistake.
verification: Reviewed Vault identity-status retry, generic passphrase failure, recovery-key failure and destructive reset safeguards against the local current web app and store on 2026-10-12. The screenshot contains no real secret.
body: A Vault unlock failure usually belongs to one of three stages: Dosya cannot check whether the encrypted identity exists, the Vault passphrase is rejected, or the recovery key is rejected. Identify the stage before changing anything. ## Before you start - Keep any trusted device with an already-unlocked Vault session open. - Do not send a passphrase or recovery key to support or paste it into any page other than the Vault unlock form. - Check keyboard layout, Caps Lock and password-manager selection. - Treat **Destroy vault and start over** as permanent data loss. - If service status or connectivity is uncertain, resolve that before testing secrets repeatedly. ## Steps: identify and fix the failure 1. Open **Vault** and read the card title and error exactly. 2. If it says **Couldn't check encryption status**, select **Retry** after checking the connection. Do not create a new identity; the app has not established whether the existing one is present. 3. If it says **Unlock Vault**, enter the dedicated Vault passphrase. Your Dosya account password is a different credential. 4. If the passphrase is rejected, type it manually once after confirming keyboard layout and autofill. The app intentionally gives a generic failure instead of revealing details about the encrypted identity. 5. If the passphrase is unavailable, select **Use recovery key** and paste the complete key saved during setup. Spaces and dashes are ignored. 6. After recovery-key unlock, open or download a known file to confirm that the correct encrypted identity opened. ## Expected result A successful passphrase or recovery-key attempt opens the existing encrypted Spaces. A successful encryption-status retry shows the correct setup or unlock screen without overwriting an existing identity. ## Limits and irreversible actions - Dosya cannot reset the Vault passphrase or reconstruct a missing recovery key. - The account password-reset flow does not decrypt Vault data. - If the current build reports that recovery-key unlock is unavailable, update to the current version and retry; do not destroy the Vault to bypass a client-version problem. - Destroying the Vault identity makes every file encrypted under it permanently unreadable to you and everyone with whom a Space was shared. - Destructive reset requires the account password and, when enabled, a two-factor code. These checks authorize destruction; they do not decrypt old data. ## Troubleshooting specific messages **Couldn't check encryption status.** This is an identity-status or connection check, not evidence that no identity exists. Select **Retry** after connectivity recovers. **Incorrect passphrase or no identity found.** Confirm the dedicated Vault passphrase, keyboard layout and account. If it remains unavailable, use the recovery key. **That recovery key did not unlock your Vault.** Copy it again from the original secure record, remove surrounding whitespace and check its beginning and end. Make sure it belongs to this account's Vault identity. **Recovery key unlock is not available in this version yet.** Update or reload the current client and retry later. Preserve encrypted data; do not use destructive reset simply because this client path is unavailable. **You still have another unlocked device.** Keep it online and download essential files before taking any destructive action. **Both credentials are lost.** Search password-manager history, offline records and trusted devices. If none remains, support cannot bypass the encryption. Start over only when every old encrypted file can be abandoned. ## Related guides - [Recover access to Dosya Vault](/files/vault-recovery) - [Set up and unlock Dosya Vault](/files/vault-setup) - [Understand Dosya Vault](/files/vault-overview) - [Recover account-level two-factor access](/account/two-factor-recovery)

title: Verify a Vault recovery key
summary: Test a Vault recovery key through the real mobile unlock path, identify the exact failure message, and preserve the only offline recovery copy.
verification: Reviewed locally against apps/mobile/src/vault/ui/RecoveryKeyCard.tsx, apps/mobile/src/vault/ui/UnlockCard.tsx, apps/mobile/src/vault/store.ts, apps/mobile/src/vault/engine.ts, packages/e2ee-client/src/session.ts, and packages/e2ee-core/src/keys.ts. Production behavior was not tested during this documentation update.
body: Dosya has no separate recovery-key checker. The supported verification is a real unlock of the existing Vault identity with the saved key. Success proves that the key can unwrap the same encrypted identity used by your Spaces; it does not rotate the key or validate a printed copy you did not enter. ## Before you start - Keep the authoritative offline recovery key in place. Make a temporary working copy for entry; do not move or destroy the only copy during this check. - Confirm the signed-in account is the one that created the recovery key. A correct key for another Dosya account will fail authentication. - The generated recovery secret is 32 random bytes displayed as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The mobile parser accepts spaces, line breaks, and hyphens around that value. - Connect to the network so the app can fetch your account’s encrypted key bundle. Recovery unlock does not send the recovery key to Dosya and does not call the passphrase OPRF endpoint. ## Steps 1. If Vault is open, tap **Lock**. This clears the active session and decrypted Vault cache without changing cloud data or the stored recovery wrapper. 2. On **Unlock your Vault**, tap **Use recovery key**. 3. Paste the working copy into **Recovery key**. Visually compare its first and last groups with the offline original. 4. Tap **Unlock with recovery key**. The field clears as soon as it is submitted, whether the attempt succeeds or fails. 5. Confirm that the expected **My Spaces** and **Shared with me** entries appear. Open one known Space and folder to prove the recovered identity can use its existing grants. 6. Lock Vault again, remove the temporary clipboard or note copy, and retain the protected offline original. ## Expected result Vault unlocks and the known Space contents decrypt under the existing identity. Verification does not change the passphrase, recovery wrapper, public keys, membership, files, or plan. The recovery key remains the only fallback if the passphrase is later lost. ## Troubleshooting **You see “That recovery key didn't unlock your Vault.”** Check the account and all 64 hexadecimal characters. Spaces and hyphens are removed automatically, but a missing nibble, non-hex character, wrong account key, or altered stored wrapper cannot authenticate. **You see “Couldn't check encryption status.”** The account key-bundle lookup failed before verification. Restore connectivity and tap **Retry**; do not choose setup while identity status is unknown. **Unlock succeeds but a Space is missing.** The recovery key restores the account identity, not revoked membership. Refresh the Space list and ask a current member to inspect access if the Space was shared. **You dismissed “Save your recovery key” during setup without preserving it.** The setup card shows that generated value once and then the mobile store forgets it. Dosya cannot reveal or reconstruct it later. Keep the passphrase safe; if both secrets are lost, the encrypted identity and its data are unrecoverable. **You expected recovery to set a new passphrase.** The current mobile flow only unlocks a session with the recovery-derived key. It does not rewrap the identity or replace the old passphrase. ## Related guides - [Recover Vault](/files/vault-recovery) - [Troubleshoot Vault unlock](/troubleshooting/vault-unlock)

title: Show Vault Spaces for the correct workspace
summary: Switch the mobile Vault to the workspace attached to an expected encrypted Space, distinguish My Spaces from Shared with me, and refresh the account-scoped list safely.
verification: Verified against current local product source for the mobile workspace header, Vault Space discovery, active-workspace filtering, shared-Space listing, account-scoped persistence, and unlock behavior on 2026-10-14. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: The mobile Vault uses the workspace shown in its header to filter **My Spaces**. A Space attached to another workspace does not appear in that section until you switch workspace context. Spaces shared by someone else appear separately under **Shared with me**. ## Before you start - Confirm which Dosya account owns or receives the expected Space. - Identify the regular Dosya workspace associated with that Space. - Keep the Vault passphrase and offline recovery key private. A workspace switch does not require either value again while Vault remains unlocked. - Do not create a replacement Space merely because the expected one is missing from the current workspace view. ## Steps: switch Vault workspace scope 1. Open the **Vault** tab and unlock it normally. 2. Read the workspace name in the header above the Vault content. 3. Tap the workspace header to open **Your workspaces**. 4. Choose the workspace associated with the missing Space. Wait for the workspace-switch transition to finish. 5. Return to **My Spaces** and look for the expected name. 6. If it was created or renamed on another device, allow the discovered placeholder name a moment to update from the encrypted Space metadata. 7. Check **Shared with me** when another person shared the Space. Shared Spaces are listed separately from the active-workspace **My Spaces** filter. 8. Open the Space and verify one expected folder or harmless file. ## Expected result **My Spaces** shows the Spaces attached to the selected workspace, and opening the expected Space displays its own decrypted contents. A shared Space remains under **Shared with me** regardless of which workspace is active. ## Limits and important details - The known Space list is stored per signed-in account on the phone. Switching to another Dosya account changes the available Vault identity and list. - Legacy Spaces without a stored global-workspace association can appear across workspace contexts. - Creating **New Space** attaches it to the workspace active at creation time. Verify the header before creating one. - Workspace switching changes the list filter; it does not decrypt, copy, rename, or move encrypted files. ## Troubleshooting **The correct workspace shows no Spaces.** Confirm the Dosya account, unlock Vault, and allow the initial discovery request to finish. Use **Retry** if the identity check or Space check reports an error. **A Space has a placeholder name.** Leave the unlocked list open briefly. Dosya resolves names from encrypted Space metadata in the background. **The Space is shared, not owned.** Look under **Shared with me**. It is intentionally separated from **My Spaces**. **Vault asks for recovery information.** Complete the normal unlock or recovery flow first. Support cannot reconstruct a lost passphrase or recovery key. ## Related guides - [Recover Vault](/files/vault-recovery) - [Troubleshoot Vault unlock](/troubleshooting/vault-unlock)

title: How to check that a Dosya change worked
summary: Confirm a Dosya change by refreshing the relevant view, checking the exact saved state and testing one harmless item before repeating the action.
verification: Reviewed locally against persisted result patterns in the web Files view, upload workflow and desktop recovery guidance on 2026-10-14. The guide limits itself to observable state checks and links readers to task-specific instructions for exact result labels.
keywords: check if a Dosya change worked
body: After changing a Dosya setting, file or access rule, read the resulting status and refresh or reopen the same view. Confirm the exact saved value, location, count or access state before repeating the action. A success message shows that a request was accepted, but the task-specific result is the stronger check. For example, verify a copied file in its destination with [the file copy result steps](/files/file-copy-verify-result), or confirm a small upload with [the one-file upload test](/uploading/upload-test-one-file). ## Steps: check the task-specific result 1. Stay in the account and workspace where you made the change. 2. In the task view, read the **final status or error** before leaving the page. 3. Open the view that owns the result, such as the destination folder, member list, link details or setting panel. 4. Refresh that view once or close and reopen it. 5. Compare the saved value, path, item count, role, expiry or status with the result you intended. Use the result named in the task guide. A file action should produce the right item in the right folder. A member or sharing change should show the intended person and access level. A setting change should show the saved value after the view reloads. ## Test one harmless item when the result is unclear Use one nonconfidential file, temporary link or reversible setting when a larger action is uncertain. Record its starting state, make the change once and check the final state. This keeps duplicate uploads, invitations, charges or destructive actions from becoming part of the diagnosis. Do not repeat a payment, deletion, ownership transfer or other high-impact action only because the confirmation disappeared. Preserve the approximate time and exact nonsecret error, then [prepare a safe support request](/troubleshooting/contact-support-safely). ## When a restart is part of the check Restart only when the task guide or error asks for it. Save work and note the current status first. For desktop recovery, follow [the restart verification steps](/desktop/desktop-verify-recovery-restart) so you can compare the state before and after the restart. ## Expected result The intended value or item remains visible after the relevant view reloads. If it does not, stop before repeating the action and use the task guide's troubleshooting steps or send the recorded evidence to support. ## Related guides - [Verify a copied file in its destination](/files/file-copy-verify-result) - [Test an upload with one small file](/uploading/upload-test-one-file) - [Verify desktop recovery after a restart](/desktop/desktop-verify-recovery-restart)

title: Verify a downloaded Dosya ZIP archive
summary: Confirm a Dosya ZIP finished, compare its paths and file counts with the cloud selection, and identify collision names or missing-object notices before sharing.
verification: Verified archive naming, path collision handling and missing-object notices in apps/api/src/lib/archive-entries.ts, apps/api/src/lib/archive-stream.ts and apps/web/src/lib/archive-download.ts. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Verify an archive before sharing it, deleting its cloud source or treating it as a backup. A browser showing **Download started** confirms that archive preparation began; it does not prove that every byte reached local storage. Dosya supplies the filename `dosya-download.zip`. When several archives are requested, use the browser's completed-download list and your source checklist to identify which selection each local copy contains. ## Steps 1. Open the browser's downloads list and find the archive started at the expected time. 2. Wait until the browser marks that download complete. 3. Check that the item is not failed, canceled or blocked. If it did not complete, start a fresh Dosya archive download after correcting the reported cause. 4. Move the completed ZIP to a controlled folder before extracting it. Avoid opening an unfinished copy from a temporary download location. ## Compare structure and entries Open the ZIP with your operating system's archive viewer or another trusted tool without running executable content. For directly selected files, expect names at the ZIP root. A downloaded folder should begin with its folder name and retain descendant paths. Compare these details with the source: - every directly selected file appears once; - each chosen folder has the expected nested branches; - representative file sizes are plausible and sample documents open; - all ZIP parts reported by the bulk-download toast are present; - the archive tool reports no truncated central directory, CRC error or unexpected end of file. Two source entries that map to one archive path are both kept. The later entry is renamed with a suffix such as `name (2).ext`; treat that as collision handling, then match both files by contents or size. ## Read notices inside the ZIP A text entry named `MISSING - .txt` is not the original file. It means Dosya still listed that item but could not read its stored object while the archive streamed. Try the named file's individual **Download** action. If that fails, retain the notice and contact support with the workspace, visible path, approximate attempt time and archive batch; never send passwords, API keys or recovery keys. An archive created from a sharing link with photo-metadata removal can instead contain **`NOT INCLUDED - filename.txt`**. That note says the sender's privacy setting prevented the original format from being shipped. Ask the sender for a new link without metadata removal only if their policy permits the original file. Locked or hidden workspace items can be omitted without a notice when your current access does not allow them. Compare against the visible, unlocked selection available to your role rather than an administrator's private inventory. ## Expected result The browser marks every planned ZIP complete, each archive opens without a structure error, expected downloadable paths are present, and representative files are readable. Any collision suffix or missing-object notice has been reconciled with the cloud source. ## If validation fails - A ZIP that cannot open or reports an unexpected end is incomplete; delete that local copy and download again after the network stabilizes. - If one of several parts is absent, select only that source batch and use **Download ZIP** again. - If the browser saved a zero-byte file or an HTML/JSON error response, return to Dosya and address the displayed permission, size or entry-count message. - When the same individual file and a new archive both fail, keep the cloud entry unchanged while support investigates. Only rename the verified archive or pass it to another person after these checks. Extraction and verification do not change the original cloud files. ## Related guides - [Download a selected group](/uploading/download-selection-archive) - [Download one cloud folder](/uploading/download-folder-archive)

title: Verify a plan or storage change after checkout
summary: Verify a completed plan or storage purchase safely across the success page, receipt and Billing ledger without creating a duplicate checkout.
