verification: Locally verified against apps/web/src/pages/checkout-success.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/checkout-return.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/sync.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/status.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/billing/receipt.ts on 2026-10-14. Production checkout was not exercised.
body: The checkout-success screen reconciles Stripe immediately and separates the purchase receipt from the account entitlement that Billing ultimately enforces. ## Steps 1. Confirm the badge reads **Purchase complete** for checkout or **Plan updated** for an in-app subscription change. 2. Review the capacity figure, total-storage bar, plan name and monthly/yearly label. 3. Under **Order receipt · Stripe** or **Plan change · Stripe**, match invoice/next-invoice details, amount, card, email, and storage. 4. A checkout with an unpaid Stripe status shows **Payment processing**; wait until payment and storage settle. 5. Open Billing and confirm status, storage ledger, **Total limit**, and the corresponding invoice. Do not initiate another payment while reconciliation is pending. The screen makes one immediate sync, then checks status at 2.5-second intervals for up to eight retries when the subscription has not appeared. A typed or stale success URL without a valid checkout session/recent-change marker redirects to Billing. ## Expected result Receipt data, subscription state and effective capacity agree, and any formerly quota-blocked operation can be retried under the new ceiling. If receipt loading fails, Billing still provides invoice access. If polling gives up, retry synchronization from the page or reload Billing; preserve the Stripe invoice number for support. ## Related guides - [Verify storage after an upgrade](/account/plan-verify-storage-upgrade) - [Find invoices and payment details](/account/invoices-and-payment)

title: Compare entries in file version history
summary: Compare version number, Latest state, exact timestamp, size, uploader, and previewed bytes before restoring; understand fields history does not show.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions/restore.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The viewer’s **Versions** tab lists rows newest first. Each row shows a version number, byte size, local date and time, and uploader when available; only the current top row carries **Latest**. ## Steps 1. Open the file preview and make sure the inspector is visible. On a phone-width viewport, open the inspector bottom sheet. 2. Choose **Versions**. Its count includes the implicit first version even when an untouched file has no historical database row. 3. Compare `vN`, size, date, time, and uploader. The panel does not show a change summary, checksum, filename per revision, or side-by-side diff. 4. Select an older row to preview its bytes. Use ↑ and ↓ when multiple versions exist; the selected row gains the active styling. 5. Inspect the previewed content against **Latest**. Comments can carry a version association, but the version row itself does not summarize those comments. 6. Return to the top **Latest** row if you only needed comparison. Choose **Restore** only when you intend to create a new current version from older bytes. **Access rules.** Listing history requires workspace membership, Files-page access, folder scope, and visibility. A full-locked file refuses its version metadata until the file is appropriately accessible. ## Expected result You identify the intended revision by version number, timestamp, size, uploader, and actual previewed content, while leaving Latest unchanged until a deliberate restore action. ## Related guides - [Use the full version-history workflow](/files/version-history) - [Inspect current file metadata](/files/file-details)

title: Download a previous file version
summary: Download an older revision from the Files details panel, verify its metadata and local bytes, and avoid the viewer header link that targets Latest.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-detail-panel.tsx, apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/download.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Selecting a file row opens a details panel whose **Versions** section gives every revision its own download icon. This is the supported visible path for historical bytes. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, click the target row once to open its details panel. Confirm the filename, current version badge, folder context, and preview before downloading anything. 2. Find **Versions** in that panel. Each row shows `vN`, size, uploader or **Unknown**, relative time, and a download icon; the current row has green styling. 3. For a file without `full_lock`, choose the download icon on the required historical row. The link includes `?version=N`, so it requests that row rather than the current file. 4. Keep the tab open while Dosya checks membership, Files access, folder confinement, download permission, hidden or ancestor locks, and the file’s own lock mode. The per-row link omits the `ut` unlock token, so a `full_lock` historical download fails even after you unlocked the preview. 5. Save the response under a distinct local name. The server uses the cloud filename, so add a suffix such as `-v2` locally to avoid replacing another download. 6. Compare the local byte size with the chosen row and open it in a trusted application. If the API returns `Version not found`, refresh the panel and confirm that revision still exists. **Viewer-header warning.** The full preview viewer also lets you select an older row and inspect its raw bytes, but its header **Download** link is still built without a version parameter and retrieves Latest. Use the per-row icon in the Files details panel for a historical download. **Full-lock limitation.** If you are authorized to manage protection, remove or change the file’s full lock, download the required historical row, and restore the intended protection afterward. Without that permission, the current browser UI has no supported historical-download link that carries the unlock token. **What changes.** Downloading meters the selected revision’s bytes against applicable egress allowance. It does not restore the revision, create a version, or change the cloud file. ## Expected result For an eligible file, the saved local copy matches the selected historical row’s content and size, while the cloud record remains on its existing Latest version and its history stays unchanged. A full-locked file remains blocked until its protection is changed by an authorized user. ## Related guides - [Review version history before downloading](/files/version-history) - [Find the file metadata needed for verification](/files/file-details)

title: Using version history and restoring an earlier version
summary: Find saved versions in the file viewer, preview an older version, and make it current without discarding the previous latest version.
verification: Version controls and restore metadata verified in the real web app against an isolated local API on 2026-10-10: restoring v1 while v2 was latest created v3. The sample versions used identical file data, so distinct-content recovery was not tested. Screenshots show the Versions controls and resulting history. Restore semantics, retention and permissions checked against current source; production workflow not tested.
body: In **Files**, right-click the file and choose **Version history**. In the viewer, open the inspector if needed, select **Versions**, then choose **Restore** beside the earlier version you want to make current. ## Before you start - Sign in to [the Dosya app](https://app.dosya.dev) and select the file's workspace. - The file must be available in Files. If it is deleted, [restore the file or its parent folder](/files/restore-deleted) first. - Viewing history depends on your access to the file. Restoring an earlier version also requires permission to upload or modify files. - A locked file cannot have its versions restored. Ask the workspace owner about the lock and your access before changing it. - Only retained versions are available. Check the retention details below if the copy you need is missing. ## Steps: open and restore version history 1. Open **Files** and find the file you want to recover an earlier copy of. 2. Right-click the file and select **Version history**. This opens the full file viewer. 3. Find the inspector beside the preview. If it is closed, use the toolbar's **Inspector (i)** control, whose accessible label is **Toggle inspector**. On smaller screens, the inspector opens as a sheet rather than a side panel. 4. Select **Versions** next to **Details**. The tab includes a count of the available versions. 5. Compare the version numbers, dates, times and sizes. The current version carries the **Latest** label. An uploader name also appears when available. 6. Select an older version's row to preview it when that file type supports a preview. Selecting a row changes the preview; it does not make that version current. 7. Choose **Restore** on the older version's row when you are ready. This button performs the restore directly; there is no additional confirmation dialog in this workflow. 8. Wait for **Restored**, then check the refreshed version list. The restored contents appear as a new **Latest** version with a new version number. 9. Close and reopen the file, or download its current copy, to confirm that the restored version is now the one you want to use. ## Add a new version deliberately If you want to update an existing file while keeping available history, right-click it in Files and choose **Upload new version**. Select the replacement file in your device's picker, then follow its progress in the upload dock. Wait for completion before opening version history again. This action targets the existing file. Use it when you mean to revise that file, and check the selected file's name before choosing a replacement. See [uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) for destination selection and upload troubleshooting. ## Expected result Restore makes a new current version using the selected older version's saved data. In the example below, restoring v1 while v2 was current created a new history entry, v3. The existing versions, including v2, remain in history while allowed by retention and the version-count setting. The file keeps its place in the workspace; restoring a version does not create a separately named file in another folder. ## Limitations - On Free, older versions have a 7-day retention window; paid plans have no age limit. Both are also subject to the workspace's version-count cap, which defaults to the newest 10 versions and can be changed by a workspace administrator. The newest version is retained. See the [fair-use and retention policy](https://dosya.dev/fair-use/). - Stored versions count toward your storage quota. Uploading a replacement may fail if the workspace has insufficient space or its upload rules prevent the operation. - A preview depends on the file type. Having version history does not guarantee that every older file can be previewed in the browser. - Restoring cannot recover a version whose saved data is no longer available. ## Troubleshooting **I only see Details.** Open the inspector and select its **Versions** tab. Choosing **Version history** from the context menu opens the viewer; it does not automatically select the Versions tab. **There is only one version or an older version is missing.** Confirm you opened the intended file, then check whether the replacement upload finished. A separately uploaded file is not necessarily the history of this one. Older versions can also have been removed by retention or the workspace's version-count cap. **Restore failed.** Check that the file is still available, your role allows modifying it, and it is not locked. Reload the viewer before retrying. If a listed version repeatedly fails to restore, use [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) and include the version number, approximate time and error message; do not post private files publicly. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does selecting an older version change the file for everyone? Selecting its row changes your preview. **Restore** changes the current workspace file by creating a new latest version. ### Can I return to the version that was current before restoring? Yes, while that version remains in history. Find its row and choose **Restore** again. Each restore creates another version; retention and the workspace's cap still apply. ### Can I restore a file that was deleted instead? Use [Deleted](/files/restore-deleted) to restore the item first. Version history restores an earlier saved version of an available file. ## Related guides - [Restoring deleted files and folders](/files/restore-deleted) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Watch the existing version-history tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/use-version-history/)

title: Restore an earlier version with a safety check
summary: Restore older bytes as a new append-only version, check permissions and locks, verify the new Latest row, and keep the complete history recoverable.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions/restore.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Restore does not rewind or erase history. Dosya verifies the old object still exists, then creates a new version that points to those bytes and marks that new row as Latest. ## Steps 1. Open **Versions** and preview the candidate revision. Record its number, size, time, and content before making it current. 2. Preserve any work that exists only in the present Latest version. It remains in history, but active viewers will switch after restore. 3. Check eligibility: you need `upload_files`; the file cannot have any own lock mode, be hidden from you, sit outside your folder scope, or belong to a locked WordPress backup. 4. Choose **Restore** on the older row. The button is disabled while that request runs, and the UI reports **Restored — Restored to vN.** when successful. 5. Wait for the Versions list to reload. The restored bytes appear in a newly numbered top row marked **Latest**; the source row and former latest row remain below it. 6. Reopen or refresh the preview and test the file. Compare its size and content with the source revision, then keep or restore forward again if the validation fails. **Exact failures.** The API can return `Cannot restore versions on a locked file`, `You don't have permission to modify files`, `Version not found`, or `Version data no longer exists in storage`. A restore also changes current size and modification metadata and emits a version-restored activity/notification. ## Expected result A new highest version number becomes Latest and serves the chosen older bytes. Every prior row remains available, making the restore reversible through another append-only restore. ## Related guides - [Understand the Versions inspector](/files/version-history) - [Check file details after restoration](/files/file-details)

title: Upload a replacement as a new file version
summary: Upload a replacement through Upload new version, track the upload dock, verify one file ID with a higher version, and handle current race limits.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/upload-runner.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/init.ts, and apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **Upload new version** sends a selected local file through the shared upload runner with the existing cloud file’s ID. The local filename does not create a second cloud record in this flow. ## Steps 1. In **Files**, verify the target cloud file by name, location, details, and current version. You need `upload_files` for the context-menu action to appear. 2. Open the target’s menu and choose **Upload new version**. The hidden picker accepts one local file for that target. 3. Select the replacement. Dosya immediately reports **Uploading version — [local name] is uploading — track it in the upload dock.** 4. Keep the app open and use the upload dock for progress, cancel, or resume. The shared runner uses multipart transport above its configured threshold and applies plan, storage, extension, member, and concurrency limits. 5. After completion, reopen the target and choose **Versions**. A new highest row should be **Latest**, while the cloud file keeps its original ID and listing identity. 6. Preview the new row and compare size, MIME behavior, and content. If upload fails, inspect the dock before selecting the local file again to avoid an unnecessary duplicate attempt. **Race limitation.** The upload API supports `expected_version` and can reject stale clients, but this Files action currently enqueues only workspace ID, target file ID, and the selected file. It does not pin the current version seen before the picker opened; review Latest again after completion when collaborators may be uploading simultaneously. ## Expected result The existing cloud record gains one new Latest revision, retains its prior versions, and remains addressable by the same file ID. The operation does not add a separate same-named file row. ## Related guides - [Review all versions of the target](/files/version-history) - [Confirm the record identity in file details](/files/file-details)

title: Distinguish a file version from a copied file
summary: Distinguish a new version from a copied record by file ID, folder location, independent timeline, uploader, origin, and later edit histories.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/files.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/versions/restore.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/copy.ts on 2026-10-14. Production behavior was not queried; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A version belongs to one file ID and one Versions timeline. **Copy** creates another file record with its own ID and future history, even when both records initially have identical bytes and names. ## Steps 1. Locate both candidate records. Record each folder or group context and open them separately so a repeated filename does not collapse your investigation. 2. Compare file IDs through the file URL or information surface. Different IDs prove separate records; version rows never change their parent file ID. 3. Open **Versions** for each record. An uploaded replacement increments one timeline, while a copy begins and evolves independently. 4. Compare **Created**, **Modified**, **Uploaded by**, and **Origin** as supporting evidence. Copy preserves source timestamps and content hash internally but records the copying client and actor for the new record. 5. Make a harmless test only when necessary: upload a tiny replacement to the known disposable copy, then confirm only its Versions count changes. 6. Remove the test record or restore its previous bytes after identification. Do not permanently delete either candidate until its ID and timeline are unambiguous. **Moves are different again.** Moving changes only the folder reference for the same file record, so its ID and version timeline continue. Copy creates another record; Upload new version appends bytes to the existing one. ## Expected result You can name which record continues the original timeline and which is the independent copy using IDs and version histories, without relying on matching names or bytes. ## Related guides - [Inspect a file’s complete version timeline](/files/version-history) - [Read identity and location details](/files/file-details)

title: Use video preview controls
summary: Play and seek a Dosya video preview, understand browser and mobile decoder differences, and recover from a stalled or unsupported format safely.
verification: Verified locally against apps/web/src/components/file-viewer.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/helpers.ts, apps/mobile/src/viewer/stages/VideoStage.tsx and apps/mobile/src/viewer/videoSupport.ts. Production streaming was not tested and no production action was performed.
body: The web viewer passes the stored video to the browser's native player. Dosya recognizes MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WebM, WMV, and FLV by extension, but actual playback still depends on the browser, operating system, and codec inside the container. ## Before you start - Verify the selected filename and version in the viewer header. Previewing an older version streams that version rather than silently switching back to the current one. - Keep enough bandwidth for range requests. Mobile requests a streaming URL valid for 3,600 seconds so a large file does not lose authorization after the ordinary five-minute window. - A fully locked file must be unlocked first. A view-only file can be previewed through the authenticated raw route but cannot be saved when its lock policy forbids downloads. ## Steps 1. Open the video from **Files**. On web, the player attempts autoplay and exposes the controls supplied by the current browser. 2. Select play or pause, drag the timeline to a known scene, and adjust volume or full-screen mode. Wait for duration metadata before treating the timeline as ready. 3. If a comment marker appears below the web player, select it to seek to that timestamp and open the matching comment. 4. On mobile, wait for the first frame. Native playback reports **Still loading** after 15 seconds without a frame and offers retry or save actions. 5. If playback fails, use **Download** on web or **Save to phone** on mobile, then open the original in a compatible player. ## Platform behavior and errors Web displays **This browser can't decode this video. Download it and open it in a player like VLC, which decodes everything.** That result means the browser rejected the container or codec; it does not prove the stored bytes are corrupt. On iOS, the native route treats MKV, WebM, AVI, WMV, FLV, OGV, MPG, MPEG, RMVB, and TS as unsupported by AVPlayer. A build with the Dosya VLC module can route eligible presigned files to VLC; a view-only raw stream cannot use that fallback because VLC cannot attach the required authorization header. Android tries its native player first. Playback and seeking do not alter storage or upload a version. Saving the file creates a device copy that Dosya cannot remove later. ## Expected result A compatible file produces a visible frame, finite duration, responsive timeline, and working sound controls. A decoder or first-frame failure presents a named recovery path while the cloud object remains unchanged. ## Related guides - [Media preview controls](/files/media-preview-controls) - [Preview files](/files/preview-files)

title: Clear stale WebDAV credentials
summary: Remove a stale Dosya WebDAV login from the client or operating-system credential store, then reconnect with the correct email and API key safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, and apps/web/src/components/api-keys/api-keys-section.tsx. Operating-system credential dialogs and production authentication were not exercised.
body: A WebDAV client can keep submitting an old password after you update the visible mount. Dosya uses HTTP Basic authentication: the username must match the API-key owner's email without regard to case, and the password must be a valid full `dos_…` key. An account password, masked key prefix, revoked key, or key owned by another email receives **401 Unauthorized**. Before deleting credentials, copy the current endpoint from **Integrations → WebDAV** and record the intended workspace ID. Clearing a host-wide credential can affect other mounts that deliberately use the same `api.dosya.dev` login, so remove the narrowest matching entry and be ready to reconnect those mounts. ## Steps 1. Finish active transfers, close files opened from the mount, and disconnect or unmount the affected Dosya volume. A client may keep an authenticated connection alive until the mount closes. 2. Open the credential store used by that client. On macOS this may be Keychain Access; on Windows it may be Credential Manager; some WebDAV apps keep passwords in their own connection profile. 3. Search for `api.dosya.dev`, the WebDAV endpoint, or the saved account email. Delete only the stale Internet/network credential or clear the password in the specific client profile; do not remove unrelated browser or system sign-ins. 4. In Dosya **Profile → API keys**, confirm the replacement key is active, includes **WebDAV**, reaches the endpoint's workspace, and is owned by the email you will enter. Generate a new dedicated key if the full old secret is no longer available. 5. Reconnect with the labelled URL copied from the integration page, enter the key-owner email as username, and enter the full API key as password. Refuse any prompt that asks for your normal Dosya account password. 6. Open **All** and list a known folder. Download a harmless file, then perform a disposable write only when the key scope and role allow it; this distinguishes successful authentication from a later permission refusal. A 401 after clearing the store still points to Basic-auth input: malformed header, missing `dos_` password, invalid or revoked key, wrong owner email, or a WordPress site key. A 403 means authentication succeeded but a protocol, active-hours/IP condition, workspace pin, membership, or role gate refused the request. Server-side authentication lookup failure returns 500 rather than another password prompt. Revoking the stale API key in Dosya stops later use but does not remove copies saved on devices, and deleting a local credential does not revoke the key elsewhere. Use both actions when access must end completely. ## Expected result The client prompts for and saves the intended email/API-key pair, the correct workspace mount opens, and a known read succeeds. Any remaining refusal now identifies a WebDAV scope, workspace, role, condition, or content rule rather than a hidden stale password. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Troubleshoot WebDAV lock and permission errors](/integrations/webdav-lock-permission-errors)

title: Connecting to Dosya with WebDAV
summary: Set up Dosya WebDAV in Cyberduck with verified screens, an API key and workspace path; test bytes and resolve exact access, transfer and recovery limits.
verification: Reviewed 2026-10-14 against local repository implementation and tests. Verified current web UI key creation and native Cyberduck 9.5.4 on macOS on 2026-10-11 against isolated current-source API/D1/R2 through a local HTTPS transport. A workspace-pinned Full access key limited to WebDAV listed all six collections, created a sample folder, uploaded a 58-byte sample into All and downloaded it through the native client. Both the API/cloud download and native download matched the original bytes. Protocol checks verified read-only root/smart-view refusals, invalid-key rejection and REST exclusion. Four existing integration suites passed 37 tests without retries for methods, role access, folder anchors and labelled mounts. The known local fixture certificate was accepted for each connection without installing permanent trust; production certificate behavior was not certified. Finder, Windows Explorer, Linux mounts, other client versions, native anchored/read-only mounts and production remain unverified. All captures use sample accounts and actual controls. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed. Current-source supplemental review: src/pages/developer/webdav.astro; apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/path-resolver.ts; apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/plan-limits.ts; apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/trim-versions.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/purge-trash.ts; apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts; apps/cron/src/index.ts. Official reference: https://docs.cyberduck.io/protocols/webdav/. External commands are source-derived and checked on temporary local fixtures where reported; no production credentials or remote writes used. Existing captures retain their original verification scope. Restore/share-revocation evidence: apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts; apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/files.ts; apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts.
body: Open **Integrations → WebDAV** in the intended workspace and copy its address. Connect using **WebDAV over HTTPS**, your account email as the username and a full `dos_…` API key as the password. For a normal workspace connection, open **All** before uploading: the other collections at the connection root are read-only views. ## Before you start - Sign in to Dosya and select the workspace you want to reach. Your workspace role must allow WebDAV and the file operations you intend to use. - Use a WebDAV client that supports HTTPS and username/password authentication. The walkthrough below uses Cyberduck on macOS; another client's fields may have different names. - Decide whether the client only needs listing and downloading, or also uploads and file management. Keep a separate key for this client so you can replace or revoke it independently. - Prepare a harmless, uniquely named sample file for your first transfer. Keep your original local copy while checking the destination. - This connection is for ordinary workspace files. Vault uses its own workflow and is not exposed through WebDAV. ## Steps: create the client's key 1. **Open Profile → API keys.** Select **New API key**. Enter a recognizable label in **What is it for?**, such as the client and computer name. 2. **Choose What can it do?** Select **Read only** for listing and downloading. The upload walkthrough needs **Full access**, which also permits moving and deleting within your account's allowed reach. **Upload only** cannot list folders, so it is unsuitable for this browsing workflow. 3. **Limit its protocols and workspace.** Open **Restrictions and expiry**. Under **Where can it reach? → Protocols**, select **Only the ones I pick** and check **WebDAV**. Choose the intended **Workspace**. Review any expiry, address, schedule or usage limits you set; those restrictions continue to apply in the client. 4. **Generate and save it privately.** Check the form's summary, then select **Generate key**. Copy the full key from the result dialog before selecting **Done**; it is shown only once. The label and prefix in the saved list cannot authenticate a client. See [API key management](/developers/api-key) for the complete key workflow. ## Steps: connect to the workspace 1. **Copy the workspace address.** Return to **Integrations → WebDAV** and copy the URL under **Endpoint & credentials**. Copy the complete address, including its path and trailing slash. The workspace ID selects the workspace; the name segment supplies the connection's label. Keep encoded spaces such as `%20` when copying a URL. 2. **Open the client's connection dialog.** In Cyberduck, select **Open Connection** and choose **WebDAV (HTTPS)**. If your version calls it **WebDAV (HTTP/SSL)**, that is its secure WebDAV option. [Cyberduck's WebDAV documentation](https://docs.cyberduck.io/protocols/webdav/) explains HTTPS authentication. 3. **Enter the address and credentials.** If the client accepts a complete URL, paste the copied address. If it separates the settings, use the following fields. In Cyberduck, enter the path in **Path**; it is separate from **Server**. | Field | What to enter | | --- | --- | | Protocol | WebDAV over HTTPS | | Server | `api.dosya.dev` | | Port | `443` | | Path | Everything after the host in your copied URL, including `/webdav/mount/…/` | | Username | The email of the account that owns the API key | | Password | The full `dos_…` API key | Leave **Anonymous Login** off. Use your API key in the password field, rather than your account password or a share-link password. Save the credential in the client's private credential storage only if that is appropriate for this computer. 4. **Connect and inspect the result.** Select **Connect**, and enter the same email and API key if a login dialog follows. For a normal workspace connection, the root lists **All**, **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared** and **Deleted**. Open **All** to browse the real folder tree and choose an upload destination. ## Steps: verify a sample transfer 1. **Choose the destination in All.** Use **All** itself for the ordinary workspace root, or open the intended folder beneath it. You can create a sample folder if your key and workspace role allow it. The connection root and the five smart views are not upload destinations. 2. **Upload the sample.** In Cyberduck, use **File → Upload…** and select your uniquely named local sample. Wait for the transfer to finish. Avoid replacing an existing filename during this first check. 3. **Verify it in Dosya.** Open **Files** in the same workspace and folder, refresh the listing if needed, and confirm the sample's filename and size. WebDAV's **All** collection corresponds to the ordinary workspace folder tree; it is not an additional folder you need to find in the web app. 4. **Check a downloaded copy.** Download the sample through the client into a separate local location and open your own copy. Confirm that it is the file you expected before relying on the connection for other work. ## Expected result The client displays the intended workspace folders. With the required permissions, the sample appears in both the client's **All** tree and Dosya's **Files** listing, and your downloaded copy matches your source. Disconnecting the client ends that connection; it does not remove your cloud files or revoke the key. Reconnect using the saved address and credential when needed. A WebDAV connection by itself does not set up a desktop folder-sync pairing or guarantee offline copies. See [Desktop folder sync](/desktop/sync-folder) if that is your intended workflow. ## Folder-restricted keys and other limits If you select **Choose folder…** when creating a workspace-pinned key, that folder becomes the connection root. Its children appear directly, so the normal **All** and smart-view collections are absent. Use the workspace's copied mount address; do not append the anchor folder's name as if it were above this new root. Folder-anchored keys work over WebDAV and the S3 gateway, and are refused over REST API and SFTP. Moving the anchor to Trash makes that connection unavailable until the folder is restored. Key permissions do not grant additional workspace-role permissions. A successful login therefore does not guarantee permission to upload, create folders, move or delete. Key expiry, selected protocols, allowed addresses, active hours, usage limits and workspace storage limits also apply. The walkthrough above is for Cyberduck. A Finder or Explorer mount uses different controls and client-specific behavior; use the existing [WebDAV mounting tutorial](https://dosya.dev/tutorials/mount-your-storage-with-webdav/) and [protocol reference](https://dosya.dev/developer/webdav/) for those alternatives. ## Transfer behavior and recovery boundaries A successful new WebDAV PUT returns **201**; a same-path replacement returns **204** and creates a Dosya file version. Both carry an ETag. A filename collision is therefore not a harmless duplicate check: confirm the destination before approving a client's overwrite prompt. History defaults to 10 versions unless workspace settings change the cap, and older free-owner versions undergo a seven-day retention sweep. A backup kept only in version history is not a permanent independent copy. WebDAV uploads need **Content-Length**. Missing length produces **411** with **Content-Length header is required**; mismatched body length returns 400. The parent must exist, otherwise PUT reports **409 Parent folder does not exist**. Workspace extension policy, maximum file size and storage quota are enforced alongside explicit key/role byte limits; a size refusal can be 413, and insufficient storage 507. Those numbers come from your current policy, not a universal WebDAV upload-size promise. For downloads, GET supports one byte range with **206** and **Content-Range**; an invalid range produces **416**. GET checks access/download permissions and locks before returning bytes. Each download stream can consume a transfer slot and daily egress allowance; HEAD or a 304 without a body is not a file download. If your client opens several parallel range streams for one file, reducing the number of simultaneous files alone may not reduce stream concurrency. Lower the client's parallel transfers/range requests when an explicit limit refuses them. Free and paid plans can use this protocol. Plan request-count and concurrency ceilings are not imposed at the WebDAV door, but explicit key/role limits still apply, and plan daily egress remains relevant. Independent request throttles are **600 requests/minute per user** and **1,200 per IP**. A 429 can include **Retry-After**; respect it before retrying rather than reconnecting rapidly. Successful authentication does not bypass an active-hour or address condition. Deleting through a full-access client is a cloud action: eligible files and folder subtrees move to Trash and their share links are revoked. Your role may permit deleting only your own files; a mixed-ownership folder can be refused. Trashed bytes keep consuming storage until permanent purge. The owner's effective plan sets automatic Trash retention at seven days on free or 30 on other plans, with cron processing after the retention cutoff. Permanent purge is irreversible, and restoring a file does not recreate a revoked share URL. WebDAV's **Deleted** view is read-only; use Dosya's Trash controls to restore or permanently remove items. ## Exact connection refusals | Status and response | What to check | | --- | --- | | 401 **Unauthorized**, with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="dosya.dev"` | Missing/malformed Basic auth, wrong key-owner email, invalid/expired/revoked key or a WordPress site key. Email matching ignores letter case; the full password must start with `dos_`. | | 500 **Internal Server Error** during authentication | A credential-store outage is distinct from a bad password; wait before replacing a valid key. | | 403 **This API key is not permitted to use WebDAV** | The selected protocol list excludes this door. | | 403 **This API key is pinned to a different workspace** | The mount's workspace does not match its key pin. | | 403 **Not a member of this workspace** | Workspace membership is required in addition to possession of a key. | | 403 **This API key is anchored outside your permitted folder** | The key's root and the member's narrower confinement do not compose. | | 403 **This API key's anchor folder is no longer available** | Its selected folder was removed or trashed; restore the permitted anchor or make a correctly scoped replacement. | | 403 **This role is not permitted to use WebDAV** | Request WebDAV access from the workspace owner/admin. | | 403 **API key scope 'read' cannot upload files** | Keep this key read-only or make a separate appropriately scoped upload client. | | 423 **Locked** | The file or its ancestor/destination is locked; resolve the lock in Dosya rather than retrying an overwrite. | The door checks path/configuration and IP throttling, then authentication, key protocol, key conditions/usage, user throttling, workspace/membership/anchor and role gates before method-specific file permissions. One corrected error may therefore uncover a separate valid restriction. Hidden resources and their descendants resolve as absent for a viewer who cannot see them; guessing a path cannot widen the mount. ## Troubleshooting **The client repeatedly asks for a password or reports Unauthorized.** Use the key owner's account email and the full API key. Check whether the key expired or was revoked. A copied label or prefix is insufficient. Replace a lost key using Profile → API keys, update the client and revoke the old credential as appropriate. **The client reports Forbidden.** Check the key's **Permission**, **Protocols** and **Reach**, and confirm that your workspace role allows WebDAV. A workspace-pinned key cannot connect to a different workspace. Address and schedule restrictions can also refuse a valid credential. If a role needs changing, ask the workspace owner or administrator. **Listing works, but uploads fail.** Use **All** or a folder beneath it for an ordinary connection. **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared** and **Deleted** are read-only views. Check whether the key is Read only, whether your role permits uploads, and whether the destination is locked or has reached a limit. A missing parent folder must be created first. **Only one folder's children appear, without All.** Check whether the key or your workspace membership is folder-restricted. The folder is the connection root; its absence from its own listing is expected. **The server or workspace cannot be found.** Copy the current address from the intended workspace's integration page. Keep the workspace ID and full path, rather than using a bare host or guessing a workspace name. If the service reports temporary maintenance or a rate limit, wait for the stated retry period. **The client shows a certificate warning.** Stop and check that you used the copied HTTPS address and the intended host. Do not bypass an unexplained certificate warning to make a production connection succeed. Record the message for private support. **The client looks successful, but the destination is missing.** Check the active workspace and folder in both interfaces, refresh the lists, and inspect the client's transfer result. Confirm the actual destination and your downloaded copy instead of relying only on a connection or completion message. For a persistent problem, contact [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support) with the client/version, selected protocol, operation and error message. Omit your full API key, password field, authorization headers and private filenames from shared screenshots. ## Frequently asked questions ### Do I use my Dosya account password? No. Use your account email as the username and the full API key as the password. The key must allow WebDAV. ### Can I upload into Documents or Images? Those root collections are read-only views for an ordinary workspace connection. Upload into **All** or an intended folder beneath it. ### Can I restrict this client to one folder? Yes. Choose a workspace and folder when creating its key. That folder becomes the connection root; the workspace-wide collections are not shown. ### Does this connect my Vault? No. WebDAV exposes ordinary workspace files. Use Dosya's Vault workflow for Vault content. ## Related guides - [API key management](/developers/api-key) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Restoring an earlier file version](/files/version-history) - [WebDAV protocol reference](https://dosya.dev/developer/webdav/) - [What WebDAV is and when to use it](https://dosya.dev/blog/what-is-webdav/)

title: Correct a WebDAV workspace endpoint
summary: Replace an incorrect WebDAV URL with Dosya’s labelled workspace endpoint, verify its workspace ID, and avoid ambiguous mounts based on display names.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/mount-token.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/utils.ts, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, and apps/web/src/lib/integrations.test.ts. No production mount was changed.
body: The preferred Dosya WebDAV address is `https://api.dosya.dev/webdav/mount/{workspace_id}/{label}/`. The `ws_…` ID chooses the workspace; the final label is cosmetic text used by Finder and Explorer to name the volume. Renaming the workspace or editing that label does not redirect the mount to another workspace. Legacy URLs can use a workspace ID, exact name, or slug as the first token. Exact names become ambiguous when two accessible workspaces share a name; Dosya answers 409 and lists labelled ID-based alternatives. Copying the URL from the active workspace avoids that collision. ## Steps 1. In the web app, switch to the workspace you want and open **Integrations → WebDAV**. Copy the complete **Endpoint & credentials** URL, including `https://`, `/webdav/mount/`, the `ws_…` ID, label, and trailing slash. 2. Compare the `ws_…` segment with the workspace you intended. The label may be stale or customized; do not use it as the security boundary or replace the ID with a display name. 3. Finish pending writes, disconnect the old mount, and edit or recreate its connection profile with the copied URL. Keep the key-owner email and API key separate from the endpoint. 4. Confirm the API key includes WebDAV and is either unpinned or pinned to this same workspace. A mismatched pin returns **This API key is pinned to a different workspace**. 5. Reconnect and inspect the root. An unanchored mount shows **All**, **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared**, and **Deleted**; a folder-anchored key opens directly at that folder and has no smart-view namespace. 6. Open **All**, locate a known item, and compare it with Dosya **Files** in the same workspace. Remove the obsolete mount after the correct volume has passed this check. Error text narrows endpoint mistakes: **Workspace ID is required** means the URL stopped before a valid mount token; **A labelled mount needs a name segment** means the label is missing; **Unknown workspace** means the ID/name/slug did not resolve; and **Multiple of your workspaces are named…** provides usable ID-based URLs. A 403 after correct resolution points to membership, key pin, anchor, role, or condition rather than URL syntax. Changing the endpoint creates or alters a client mount only. It does not move files, rename the workspace, or modify stored data. ## Expected result The saved connection uses the labelled URL for the intended `ws_…` ID, opens the matching workspace or anchored folder, and shows a known item from that location. Any old wrong-root mount is disconnected without changing cloud content. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Troubleshoot WebDAV lock and permission errors](/integrations/webdav-lock-permission-errors)

title: Connect Cyberduck with WebDAV
summary: Save a Cyberduck HTTPS bookmark with the exact Dosya mount fields, choose All or an anchored root, and verify both transfer directions.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx; apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts; apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/path-resolver.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/propfind.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts; apps/api/src/lib/usage/plan-limits.ts; apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts; apps/api/src/lib/folder-trash.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/purge-trash.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/files/trim-versions.ts; apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/files.ts; src/pages/developer/cyberduck.astro. Native figures and the 58-byte Cyberduck check retain the 2026-10-11 isolated-source/macOS verification from hc-webdav-connect; no new production or Windows-client verification. Official references: https://docs.cyberduck.io/protocols/webdav/; https://docs.cyberduck.io/cyberduck/bookmarks/; https://docs.cyberduck.io/cyberduck/connection/.
body: To connect Cyberduck to Dosya cloud storage, save a **WebDAV HTTPS** bookmark using the address from **Integrations → WebDAV**. The login is your Dosya email plus an API key. A normal mount opens a collection list; its **All** collection is the writable folder tree. ## Prepare the key and address Select the destination workspace in the Dosya web app before opening **Integrations → WebDAV**. Copy the full address under **Endpoint & credentials**, including its `/webdav/mount/…/` path and trailing slash. The workspace ID identifies the storage; the final name segment labels the mount. A share URL is not a WebDAV endpoint. In **Profile → API keys → New API key**, give this computer's Cyberduck connection a recognizable label under **What is it for?**. Choose **Read only** for browsing/downloads or **Full access** for the upload check below. **Upload only** cannot list your folders. Under **Restrictions and expiry → Where can it reach? → Protocols**, choose **Only the ones I pick**, select **WebDAV**, and pin **Workspace** to the intended workspace. Select **Generate key** and copy the complete `dos_…` secret before **Done**: the saved prefix is insufficient and the secret cannot be shown again. Your role must permit WebDAV and each requested file action. A Full access key cannot expand a viewer's workspace permissions. Review expiry, allowed addresses, active hours and usage limits before saving the bookmark. ## Steps: create the Cyberduck bookmark 1. Open Cyberduck's **Bookmarks** view and use **Bookmark → New Bookmark**. Choose the secure **WebDAV (HTTPS)** protocol; versions using **WebDAV (HTTP/SSL)** mean HTTPS. Do not select plain HTTP, FTP or SFTP for this address. 2. Give **Nickname** a name that identifies the workspace and computer. Enter these connection values, with **Path** separate from **Server**. | Bookmark field | Value | | --- | --- | | Server | `api.dosya.dev` | | Port | `443` | | Username | The key owner's Dosya account email | | Password, when prompted | The full API-key secret | | Path | The entire path after the hostname in the copied endpoint | | Anonymous Login | Off | 3. Retain the copied path's encoded characters and workspace label. If a version accepts the complete URL, check the resulting Server and Path before connecting. Do not put the key into a URL or bookmark nickname. 4. Close the editor and open the bookmark. Enter the API key in the password prompt. Choose credential saving only for a computer whose user account you trust. Cyberduck stores saved passwords in macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager; deleting a bookmark should not be treated as revoking its secret. This connection capture is from Cyberduck 9.5.4 on macOS against an isolated current-source Dosya API. The same local check listed six collections and transferred a 58-byte sample; it did not certify a Windows client or production certificate behavior. A real connection must validate the certificate for `api.dosya.dev`; investigate certificate or hostname warnings before providing a key. ## Choose the correct root An ordinary workspace bookmark lists **All**, **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared** and **Deleted**. Open **All**, then the destination folder, before uploading. The mount root and the other five collections are read-only views, even with Full access. **All** represents the workspace's actual tree, so it is not an extra folder inside Dosya Files. If the key also uses **Choose folder…**, that selected folder becomes the root and its children appear immediately. There is no All collection in this case. Use the same copied workspace mount URL; do not append the anchor's name again. Trashing the anchor blocks the connection until it is restored. Workspace pinning alone does not imply a folder anchor. ## Check an upload and download 1. Make a small local text file with a unique name, such as `cyberduck-check-20261014.txt`. Keep the original outside your download destination. 2. Open an allowed folder in **All**, or inside the anchored root. Use **File → Upload…**, select the sample, and wait for Cyberduck's transfer completion. Stop at any overwrite prompt during this first test. 3. Refresh the browser listing. In Dosya **Files**, open the same workspace/folder and compare the name and byte size. A completed client transfer alone does not identify the intended destination. 4. Download the remote sample into another local directory. Compare its bytes with your original using a file comparison or SHA-256 tool. For read-only bookmarks, use a known existing file instead of uploading. 5. Close the connection and reopen the saved bookmark to confirm its path. This is an online file connection, not an offline folder-sync setup. ## Expected result The bookmark reopens the intended root, and the test file downloaded through Cyberduck matches your original. Your cloud copy is available in the same Dosya workspace; saving the bookmark does not create an offline backup. ## Limits and consequences WebDAV is available to free and paid accounts. Storage capacity, workspace extension/size policy and explicit role/key limits still apply. Protocol plan ceilings do not count WebDAV requests or concurrency at the door, but daily download egress still matters. Separate throttles allow 600 requests/minute per user and 1,200 per IP. On **429**, wait for **Retry-After** and reduce parallel transfers; repeated reconnects do not repair throttling. An upload to a new path returns 201; replacing an existing path returns 204 and writes a new Dosya version. History defaults to 10 versions unless the workspace changes it; free-owner versions are also subject to the seven-day retention sweep. Keep an independent copy before an intentional overwrite. A client delete moves eligible items to Trash and revokes their share links. Trash consumes storage until purge; retention is seven days for free owners and 30 days for other plans. Permanent purge cannot be undone, and restore does not recreate a revoked share link. ## Resolve the actual failure | Response | Recovery | | --- | --- | | **401 Unauthorized** or another password prompt | Check the full secret, owner email, expiry and revocation. A WordPress site key cannot authenticate WebDAV. | | **500 Internal Server Error** at login | Wait for the credential service; do not assume a valid secret changed. | | **403 This API key is not permitted to use WebDAV** | Select WebDAV in that key's protocol restrictions or create a replacement for this client. | | **403 This role is not permitted to use WebDAV** | Ask the workspace owner/admin to permit this door. | | **403 This API key is pinned to a different workspace** | Match the bookmark path to the key's pinned workspace. | | **411 Content-Length header is required** | The upload request needs its byte length; retry with a client mode that sends it. | | **409 Parent folder does not exist** | Refresh and open a real destination beneath All or the anchor. | | **423 Locked** | Resolve the file/folder lock in Dosya before retrying. | | **413** or **507** | Check the displayed size refusal or storage availability; changing the bookmark cannot raise workspace limits. | Cyberduck may wrap a server response in its own error dialog. Record the numeric response, filename and time, with the key redacted. Upload failures at the root require entering **All**; read-only smart views do not become writable by reconnecting. ## Remove this computer's access Disconnect the Cyberduck session and remove its bookmark when no longer needed. Delete its saved credential separately from Keychain Access or **Control Panel → User Accounts → Credential Manager → Windows Credentials** as applicable. In Dosya **Profile → API keys**, revoke the dedicated Cyberduck key to prevent its reuse. Removing the bookmark or key leaves existing cloud files in place; deleting files is a separate cloud action. ## Related guides - [WebDAV connection and protocol behavior](/integrations/webdav) - [API-key controls](/developers/api-key)

title: Diagnose a read-only WebDAV mount
summary: Find why a Dosya WebDAV mount is read-only by checking the API-key scope, workspace role, smart-view target, folder anchor, and content locks.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/mkcol.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/move.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts. No production write was attempted.
body: A mount can list files yet reject changes for several independent reasons. The API key may be **Read only**; the workspace role may lack upload, create, rename, move, or delete permission; the target can be a read-only smart view; or a file, ancestor folder, Vault, or WordPress backup can be locked. On an unanchored mount, **All** represents the real writable tree. **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared**, and **Deleted** are flat read-only views even when the same file can be changed through **All**. A folder-anchored mount has no reserved smart views, so a real folder named Documents remains ordinary. ## Steps 1. Reproduce one harmless operation with a uniquely named empty folder or small file, and capture the HTTP status or client text. Note whether listing, download, upload, folder creation, rename, move, or delete failed. 2. In **Profile → API keys**, inspect the credential's **Permission**. **Read only** cannot PUT, MKCOL, MOVE, DELETE, or LOCK; **Upload only** can upload but cannot download; MOVE/rename and DELETE require **Full access**. 3. Check that the key includes WebDAV, reaches this workspace or anchor, and satisfies its IP, active-hours, usage, size, and concurrency conditions. Then confirm the workspace role allows WebDAV plus the exact requested file action. 4. If the path begins with a smart-view label, repeat the test in **All** at the file's real folder. Do not treat a successful read from **Documents** or **Shared** as proof that the view accepts writes. 5. Inspect the target and its parent for lock state. Dosya returns 423 for a locked file, a sealed ancestor, a protected backup, or a destination that cannot receive new content; unlocking requires the owning product flow, not a WebDAV LOCK token. 6. Retry once after correcting the identified cause, then refresh both the client and Dosya Files. Remove the disposable item only after confirming the create or upload truly committed. Common server messages are exact: **API key scope 'read' cannot upload files**, **Upload not allowed**, **Folder creation not allowed**, **API key scope must be 'full' to move/rename**, **Delete not allowed**, **This is a read-only smart view**, and **This role is not permitted to use WebDAV**. A 412 is a changed-state precondition, not read-only access; a 429 is a usage or request limit and should honor `Retry-After`. Granting broader key scope cannot override a restrictive workspace role or content lock. Prefer a dedicated key with only the operations the client requires. ## Expected result The precise key, role, path, condition, or lock causing the refusal is identified. After an authorized correction, a disposable write succeeds in **All** or the anchored tree and appears in Dosya Files; otherwise the mount remains intentionally read-only. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Troubleshoot WebDAV lock and permission errors](/integrations/webdav-lock-permission-errors)

title: Troubleshoot WebDAV lock and permission errors
summary: Distinguish WebDAV 403 permission refusals, 412 precondition conflicts, and 423 content locks, then retry only after fixing the reported cause.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/lock.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/move.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/delete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/backup-lock.ts. Production errors were not reproduced.
body: WebDAV clients often collapse different server responses into “permission denied” or “file locked.” Preserve the HTTP status and body before changing credentials: Dosya uses 403 for authorization/policy refusals, 412 for a failed state precondition, 423 for protected content, and 429 for a rate or usage limit. Dosya advertises class-2 WebDAV locking for client compatibility. A normal LOCK receives an opaque token with a one-hour timeout, but that token is not a persistent Dosya content lock. Real 423 responses come from file/folder protection, an ancestor lock, a sealed Vault destination, or a locked WordPress backup. ## Steps 1. Stop automatic retries and record the verb, source path, destination path, HTTP status, response text, time, and client version. Remove authorization headers and `dos_…` secrets before saving a log. 2. For 403, read the body: key scope, WebDAV protocol selection, key/role IP or active-hour conditions, workspace pin, membership, role's WebDAV gate, action permission, smart-view target, extension policy, and folder anchor each have different remedies. 3. For 412 **Precondition Failed**, refresh the target and compare it with the local item. `If-Match` refuses an overwrite after the ETag changed; `If-None-Match: *` or `Overwrite: F` refuses replacing a name that now exists. 4. For 423 **Locked**, inspect the target and every destination ancestor in Dosya. Unlock through the relevant file, folder, Vault, or backup control; repeatedly issuing WebDAV UNLOCK cannot bypass a product lock. 5. For 429, pause concurrent work and honor `Retry-After`. Dosya applies a 1,200 requests/minute IP gate, a 600 requests/minute user gate, and any explicit key or role usage limits. 6. Retry one non-destructive operation after the cause changes, then refresh the containing folder. If the same status remains, keep the captured evidence and escalate without broadening unrelated permissions. A read-only key returns 403 before a write. MOVE requires full scope plus rename permission when the name changes, upload permission when the parent changes, and delete permission when overwriting an existing destination. A locked source or destination returns 423. A changed concurrent destination can return 409 with a retry message rather than 412. Avoid deleting and recreating the mount as the first response: that can clear useful status details and does not change a server-side role, lock, key scope, or content precondition. ## Expected result The client retry occurs only after the status-specific cause is corrected: 403 after permission or policy repair, 412 after reconciling changed state, 423 after an authorized unlock, or 429 after backoff. No access boundary is widened merely to silence the message. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Connect Dosya to Cyberduck](/integrations/webdav-cyberduck)

title: Map Dosya WebDAV in Windows
summary: Map the copied HTTPS WebDAV URL in Windows File Explorer, check WebClient limits, and verify the correct remote tree without assuming tested compatibility.
