Official references: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/iis/publish/using-webdav/using-the-webdav-redirector; https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/file-sharing-over-a-network-in-windows; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/deprecated-features; https://docs.cyberduck.io/cyberduck/bookmarks/.
body: Windows File Explorer can map an HTTPS WebDAV address when its **WebClient** service and redirector are available. Use the complete Dosya mount URL and an API key as the password. Microsoft has deprecated WebClient, so this built-in route depends on your Windows installation and policy; [Cyberduck](/integrations/webdav-cyberduck) is an alternative if the redirector is unavailable. This procedure combines Microsoft's documented WebDAV mapping with current Windows File Explorer controls. It has not been exercised against Dosya on a Windows computer. The diagram below is a process map, not a captured Windows dialog. ## Prepare the Windows connection Open Dosya **Integrations → WebDAV** in the correct workspace. Copy the whole URL under **Endpoint & credentials**, including the mount path and trailing slash. Use `https://api.dosya.dev/…`, not a marketing page, share link, or the hostname alone. Create a dedicated key in **Profile → API keys → New API key**. For browsing, choose **Read only**; for uploads and management, choose **Full access**. Select **Restrictions and expiry → Protocols → Only the ones I pick → WebDAV** and pin the intended **Workspace**. Copy the full secret after **Generate key**. Your workspace role must separately allow WebDAV and the requested file actions. On Windows, open **Services** and inspect **WebClient**. If it is present but stopped, an administrator can start it when organizational policy permits. If the service is absent or policy disables it, use another HTTPS WebDAV client rather than assuming every current Windows edition provides it. Microsoft lists WebClient as deprecated in its [Windows feature notice](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/deprecated-features). ## Steps: map a drive letter in File Explorer 1. Open **File Explorer → This PC**. Choose **More (…) → Map network drive**, or right-click **This PC** for that command. These current controls are described in [Microsoft's network-drive instructions](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/file-sharing-over-a-network-in-windows). 2. Select an unused **Drive** letter. In **Folder**, paste the copied HTTPS WebDAV URL with its full path. Microsoft's [WebDAV redirector procedure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/iis/publish/using-webdav/using-the-webdav-redirector) specifically documents a web URL in this wizard. 3. Use **Connect using different credentials** where offered. Decide whether to request **Reconnect at sign-in**; that setting asks Windows to reconnect later, but expired keys, unavailable network access or policy can still prevent it. 4. Select **Finish**. When credentials are requested, enter the exact key-owner email as username and the full `dos_…` API key as password. Do not use a Windows account password or Dosya sign-in password. Avoid remembering the credential on a shared computer. 5. Open the resulting drive. For a normal mount, enter **All** to reach the actual file tree. **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared** and **Deleted** are read-only views. An anchored key instead shows its allowed folder's children directly. **Add a network location** creates a named location rather than this drive-letter mapping. It is not necessary for the documented **Map network drive** procedure; do not switch between the two and then assume a drive letter was assigned. If your Windows wizard cannot accept the copied HTTPS URL, stop and use Cyberduck instead of guessing an SMB share address. ## Expected result: verify the remote location First open a known small file and download a copy to a separate local directory. Compare its byte size and contents. With Full access and upload permission, copy a uniquely named disposable text file into **All** or a permitted folder. Wait for the copy to finish, refresh **Files** in Dosya's matching workspace, and check the filename, size and downloaded contents there. Explorer is accessing cloud files. A mapped drive alone does not establish offline synchronization. Opening an editor and saving an existing remote filename may replace its content; test your application's saving behavior on a disposable file first. Versions have retention limits, so keep independent originals for recovery. Deleting cloud items can move them to Dosya Trash and revoke share links; permanently purged copies cannot be restored. ## Windows limits and errors Microsoft documents WebClient's default **FileSizeLimitInBytes** as **50,000,000 bytes** for transfers and **FileAttributesLimitInBytes** as **1,000,000 bytes** for a collection's properties. These are Windows client settings, not Dosya storage allowances. A small sample succeeding does not prove large files or a large listing will work. Use Cyberduck for those cases before considering administrator-managed registry changes. The documented **BasicAuthLevel** default of **1** permits Basic authentication over HTTPS only; **0** disables it. Keep HTTPS for Dosya's email/API-key authentication. Setting **2** would also permit unencrypted HTTP and is unnecessary for this endpoint. Local policy may differ from the documented defaults. | Symptom | What to check | | --- | --- | | **System error 67** / **The network name cannot be found** | Check WebClient availability and the full HTTPS URL; do not treat this message as proof that the key is wrong. | | **System error 5** / **Access is denied** or repeated login | Reenter owner email/full key, then check expiry, WebDAV protocol permission and role access. | | Works for small files only | Inspect Windows transfer/collection limits and retry the same task with a dedicated client. | | Can browse but cannot copy into the drive root | Enter All, or the anchored destination; read-only views refuse writes. | | **429**, **413**, **423** or **507** from Dosya | Respect retry delay, size policy, locks or storage refusal rather than altering Windows authentication settings. | Microsoft's redirector documentation targets older Windows releases. The current File Explorer control names and deprecation notice are separately sourced; neither establishes tested Dosya compatibility on your device. Capture the exact local error and time if further diagnosis is needed. ## Disconnect without deleting cloud files In This PC, disconnect the mapped drive when finished; `net use Z: /delete` is an alternative for a mapping you created as Z:. If Windows saved the login, remove the relevant saved entry through **Credential Manager → Windows Credentials**. Revoke the dedicated key in Dosya to prevent its future use. These connection-removal actions do not erase uploaded files; keep cloud deletion separate. ## Related guides - [Cyberduck WebDAV setup](/integrations/webdav-cyberduck) - [Complete WebDAV limits and recovery](/integrations/webdav)

title: Mount Dosya WebDAV in macOS Finder
summary: Mount the active workspace in macOS Finder with Dosya’s WebDAV URL, an email username, and a restricted API key, then diagnose mount failures.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts, apps/web/src/components/api-keys/create-key-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/auth.ts, apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts, and WebDAV method handlers. No Finder mount or production credential was exercised.
body: Finder can mount one Dosya workspace as a network volume. Use the endpoint shown for that workspace in **Integrations → WebDAV**; it contains the workspace ID, an encoded display label, and a trailing slash. The ID chooses the workspace. The final name only labels the mounted volume, so renaming the workspace does not invalidate an existing mount. ## Before you start Your workspace role must include **WebDAV access**. When it does not, the integration page says **Your role can’t use WebDAV** and explains that credentials will be refused. Ask an owner or admin to change the role before troubleshooting Finder. Create a separate key in **Profile → API keys**. Under **Restrictions and expiry → Where can it reach?**, choose **Only the ones I pick** and enable **WebDAV**. A **Read only** key can list and download; use **Full access** only when Finder must upload, move, rename, or delete. You may pin the key to this workspace. An optional folder anchor makes that folder the mount root and hides everything above or beside it, including the `Documents`, `Videos`, `Images`, `Shared`, and `Deleted` smart views. Copy the key when it is shown and store it securely. Finder uses the key owner's Dosya email as the username and the complete `dos_…` key as the password. ## Steps 1. In Dosya, switch to the workspace you intend to mount and open **Integrations → WebDAV**. 2. Copy the address under **Endpoint & credentials**. Its form is `https://api.dosya.dev/webdav/mount/WORKSPACE_ID/WORKSPACE_LABEL/`; keep the trailing slash. 3. In Finder, choose **Go → Connect to Server…** or press Command+K. 4. Paste the copied HTTPS address and select **Connect**. 5. Choose registered-user authentication when Finder asks. Enter the API key owner's account email in **Name** and paste the `dos_…` key into **Password**. 6. Complete the connection, then open the new Finder volume. Check a known folder and download a small test file. For a writable key, create a disposable folder and remove it after verification. ## Troubleshooting - Repeated credential prompts usually mean the Basic-auth pair was refused. Confirm the username is the key owner's email, the password starts with `dos_`, the key is active, and its protocol list includes WebDAV. A malformed or invalid pair returns `Unauthorized`. - **This API key is pinned to a different workspace** means the address and key name different workspaces. Copy the endpoint again after switching to the pinned workspace. - **This role is not permitted to use WebDAV** is a role permission issue; changing Finder settings cannot grant access. - **This API key's anchor folder is no longer available** means the credential's folder was trashed or removed. Restore that folder or issue a replacement key with a live anchor. - An anchored key deliberately fails on REST and SFTP, but remains valid for WebDAV and S3. If Finder shows the workspace root instead of the expected folder, stop and inspect the key's **Workspace** and **Folder** restrictions. - A `Read only` key refuses writes; Finder may display the volume normally while create, rename, or delete operations fail. Do not broaden scope just to clear a read test. Disconnecting the Finder volume changes no cloud data. Deleting through a full-access mount does change Dosya content and is subject to the member's delete permissions and lock rules. ## Expected result Finder shows a volume named from the endpoint's final label and lists only the workspace or anchored subtree allowed by the credential. The small read test succeeds; any attempted write matches both the key scope and the role's file permissions. ## Related guides - [Connect WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Use Cyberduck](/integrations/webdav-cyberduck)

title: Refresh a stale WebDAV directory listing
summary: Refresh a Dosya WebDAV folder after another client changes it, account for the 60-second cache backstop, and identify truncated large listings.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webdav/listing-cache.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/propfind.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/utils.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/path-resolver.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts. No production directory cache was measured.
body: Dosya invalidates WebDAV directory caches after supported mutations, while a 60-second server backstop limits stale direct-child listings when an invalidation is missed. A desktop client can keep its own cache longer, so refresh the exact folder and compare it with Dosya Files before remounting. A cached hit can retain an old child entry until expiry, whereas a missing item is not always a permission problem. Hidden content deliberately stays absent for viewers without access, and the flat smart views can change independently of a file's real location under **All**. ## Steps 1. In Dosya **Files**, confirm the item's current workspace, real folder, exact name, and whether it was created, renamed, moved, replaced, trashed, or restored. Keep that browser view as the source of truth for this check. 2. In the WebDAV client, navigate to the matching folder under **All** or inside the anchored root. Do not compare a real-tree folder with **Documents**, **Images**, **Shared**, or another flat view. 3. Use the client's refresh/reload command on that folder, then leave and reopen it. A successful WebDAV write normally invalidates the source and destination listings immediately. 4. If the old listing remains, wait at least 60 seconds and refresh again. Dosya's server read-through cache uses that fixed expiry for directories with at most 1,000 direct children; larger folders are served fresh. 5. Disconnect and remount only after the second refresh, with no active writes. Reopen the same path and compare the name and size against the browser. 6. If entries are still missing, test direct access to one known path and capture the PROPFIND response. A Depth:1 listing caps at 25,000 visible items and reports `X-Dosya-Truncated: returned/total`; refreshing cannot reveal entries beyond that cap. **Resource not found** can mean an absent or hidden path. A folder-anchored key shows only its subtree, and trashing the anchor makes the mount refuse access. Switching to a broader key to make an item appear is inappropriate unless the user's role and task genuinely require that reach. Client refresh and remount are read operations when no file is open. They do not roll back a rename, restore a deleted item, or recreate a missing upload. ## Expected result The mounted folder matches the verified Dosya Files location after refresh, the 60-second backstop, or a clean remount. If it cannot, the evidence identifies a hidden/anchored path, wrong workspace, missing resource, or 25,000-item truncation rather than an indefinite cache guess. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Troubleshoot WebDAV lock and permission errors](/integrations/webdav-lock-permission-errors)

title: Unmount and reconnect WebDAV safely
summary: Finish active WebDAV writes, unmount the Dosya volume through the client or operating system, and reconnect without duplicate mounts or data loss.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webdav.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/listing-cache.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts. No operating-system mount was unmounted in production.
body: Unmounting while a client still sends PUT bytes can leave the local application uncertain whether the write committed. Dosya validates the declared Content-Length, optional checksum, quota, policy, locks, and preconditions before recording the final file or version, so wait for the client's completed response and verify the destination first. A remount changes the client connection, not Dosya content. It is useful for clearing client-side listing state or replacing an endpoint, but it cannot repair a revoked key, role denial, wrong workspace pin, content lock, or failed upload. ## Steps 1. Pause sync jobs and stop adding work to the volume. Close documents opened directly from the mount so their applications cannot issue another background save during unmount. 2. Wait until uploads and downloads leave active, pending, retrying, or conflict states. Verify recent writes in Dosya **Files** by exact workspace, folder, name, and size before proceeding. 3. Record the mount's labelled endpoint and account email without copying its API-key password into notes. Confirm the `ws_…` ID is the workspace you intend to reconnect. 4. Use the WebDAV client or operating system's normal **Disconnect**, **Eject**, or **Unmount** action. Do not force-quit the client unless its own recovery flow says the connection is already closed. 5. Confirm the old volume disappears and no process still reports an active transfer. If the operating system says the volume is busy, locate the open file or process instead of forcing removal. 6. Reconnect once with the verified endpoint and current key, open **All** or the anchored root, and check one known file plus the recently written item. Remove any duplicate saved connection after the correct mount is stable. If the remount returns 401, clear or replace stale Basic credentials. A 403 identifies key, condition, workspace, membership, role, or smart-view restrictions. A 423 comes from protected content, while a stale directory can require one refresh and up to the 60-second server cache backstop. If an upload result was ambiguous before unmount, inspect versions and byte size before uploading again. Repeating a PUT to an existing filename can make a new current version, so preserve the local source until the server state is known. ## Expected result The original volume is cleanly disconnected with no active handles, one verified mount reconnects to the intended workspace, and known files plus any completed recent write appear at their expected paths. No duplicate replay was used to guess whether a write landed. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Troubleshoot WebDAV lock and permission errors](/integrations/webdav-lock-permission-errors)

title: Rename and move files over WebDAV
summary: Rename or move a Dosya file over WebDAV with a full-access key, confirm the required role permissions, and prevent accidental destination overwrites.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/move.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/utils.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/views.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/listing-cache.ts, apps/api/src/lib/backup-lock.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts. No production resource was renamed or moved.
body: WebDAV uses one MOVE request for a rename, a folder change, or both. Dosya requires a **Full access** API key. The workspace role must allow rename when the name changes, upload when the parent changes, and delete when an existing destination will be overwritten. Perform the operation in **All** or an anchored mount's real tree. The unanchored **Documents**, **Videos**, **Images**, **Shared**, and **Deleted** views are read-only projections and cannot be MOVE sources or destinations. ## Steps 1. Confirm the key has **Full access**, includes WebDAV, and reaches the current workspace. Verify the role's rename permission for a name change and upload permission for a move to another folder. 2. Inspect the source in Dosya Files and choose a destination whose final name is unused. Record the source folder, destination folder, name, size, and current version before the operation. 3. Check the target and both folder trees for file, ancestor, Vault, or WordPress-backup locks. A protected source or sealed destination returns 423 and must be unlocked through Dosya. 4. Rename or drag the item once in the WebDAV client, then wait for its MOVE result. The destination must remain on the same Dosya WebDAV origin and inside the mounted workspace/anchor. 5. Refresh the old and new folders. Confirm the source path no longer resolves and exactly one item with the intended name and size appears at the destination. 6. Open Dosya Files at the destination and verify the item. If the client reports 409 or 412, refresh and reconcile concurrent state before attempting another move. MOVE treats overwrite as allowed unless the client sends `Overwrite: F`. If a file already exists and overwrite proceeds, Dosya soft-deletes that destination, revokes its share links, and returns 204 after replacement; the role needs delete-own or delete-any permission according to the destination owner. A new destination returns 201. To avoid this irreversible current-location change and share revocation, choose an unused name. Different resource types cannot overwrite each other. Invalid or missing destinations return 400/409, a hidden source appears as 404, and a concurrent collision returns **Conflict: resource was modified concurrently, retry the move**. ## Expected result One MOVE places the file at the intended name and folder, the old path disappears, and both WebDAV and Dosya Files agree. No pre-existing destination was overwritten unless that action and its Trash/share-link effects were explicitly intended. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Connect Dosya to Cyberduck](/integrations/webdav-cyberduck)

title: Upload and download files over WebDAV
summary: Upload and download files through Dosya WebDAV, verify sizes or checksums, and understand scopes, multipart handling, versions, and transfer errors.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/put.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/methods/get.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webdav/utils.ts, apps/api/src/lib/usage/enforce.ts, apps/api/src/lib/versioned-write.ts, and apps/api/src/pages/webdav/[...path].ts. No production file transfer was run.
body: WebDAV PUT uploads to the real tree under **All** or an anchored root, while GET downloads from real paths and the flat smart views. **Read only** can download but cannot upload; **Upload only** can upload but cannot download; a client that must verify in both directions needs **Full access** plus the matching workspace permissions. Dosya requires `Content-Length` on uploads, streams files above 50 MiB as 10 MiB multipart parts, and checks the actual byte count before commit. Workspace extension/size policy, storage quota, key or role file-size limits, and concurrency limits can reject the transfer before or during byte movement. ## Steps 1. Mount the labelled workspace endpoint with the key-owner email and API key, then open **All** or the anchored root. Choose a writable destination and a uniquely named local sample. 2. Confirm the key and role can upload, and check remaining storage plus any maximum file size. Upload the sample and wait for the client to receive the final PUT response. 3. Refresh the destination and compare name and size in Dosya Files. If the client sends `OC-Checksum` with SHA-256/MD5 or `Content-MD5`, Dosya rejects a mismatch with **Checksum mismatch: the bytes received do not match the digest the client declared**. 4. Choose a known remote file that the role may download, save it under a new local name, and wait for completion. Dosya supports one byte range at a time and returns 206 for a valid ranged download. 5. Compare the downloaded size and calculate a local checksum against the trusted source or uploaded sample. Do not assume the displayed modification date alone proves identical content. 6. Reconnect or relist once to verify persistence. Remove disposable files only after the two-way check, because a permitted WebDAV delete moves cloud content to Trash and revokes its share links. A PUT without length returns 411; invalid length returns 400; policy or scope refusal returns 403; a too-large file returns 413; quota exhaustion returns 507; protected content returns 423; and usage/concurrency refusal returns 429 with `Retry-After`. An upload body shorter or longer than declared is rejected rather than recorded at the wrong size. Uploading to an existing name creates the next version and changes the current bytes after ETag preconditions pass. `If-Match` and `If-None-Match` can return 412 when another client changed or created the target. Verify state before replaying an ambiguous write. ## Expected result The uploaded file appears in the intended Dosya folder with the declared size, the downloaded copy contains the expected bytes, and any checksum comparison passes. Scope, policy, lock, quota, precondition, and usage failures remain distinguishable by their exact status and message. ## Related guides - [Connect with WebDAV](/integrations/webdav) - [Connect Dosya to Cyberduck](/integrations/webdav-cyberduck)

title: Acknowledge a webhook delivery promptly
summary: Verify a Dosya webhook signature over the raw body, store the event durably, and return a 2xx response before the ten-second delivery timeout.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/sign.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.ts, apps/cron/src/index.ts, apps/help/src/content/articles/webhook-signature.md, apps/help/src/content/articles/webhook-create.md, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx. Production behavior for “Acknowledge a webhook delivery promptly” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya considers any HTTP 2xx response successful. The receiver has ten seconds to verify and acknowledge the request, so durable intake belongs on the request path and slow business work belongs behind it. ## Steps 1. Read the untouched request bytes and the `X-Dosya-Signature` header before parsing JSON. Split its `t=,v1=` values and compute HMAC-SHA256 with the endpoint signing secret over `${t}.${rawBody}`. 2. Parse `t` as a safe integer and reject it when it is more than 300 seconds away from the receiver clock. Then compare the computed digest with `v1` using a constant-time operation. A stale, malformed, or mismatched signature must not enqueue the payload. 3. Capture `X-Dosya-Event-Id`, `X-Dosya-Delivery-Id`, and `X-Dosya-Event-Type`, then commit the verified raw event and its event-ID idempotency record to durable storage. 4. Return an empty or sanitized 2xx response as soon as that transaction commits. Finish downstream API calls, media work, notifications, and other slow effects in a worker after acknowledgement. 5. Keep the complete request under ten seconds. A timeout, network error, 3xx that remains after Dosya’s single allowed redirect, or any non-2xx status is recorded as a failed attempt. 6. In **Integrations → Webhooks**, open **Deliveries** and verify **Success**, the response status, and one attempt. Dosya stores up to 500 response characters, so never echo a secret or private payload in the acknowledgement body. A failed first attempt is due again after 30 seconds, followed by 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 6 hours. The retry sweep runs every ten minutes, so an attempt may occur after its earliest due time. ## Expected result A valid delivery is durably accepted once and receives a 2xx before the ten-second deadline. **Recent deliveries** shows **Success**, while slow processing continues independently without provoking retries. **Valid requests time out.** Move work after the durable queue commit and inspect proxy or platform timeouts; increasing receiver work does not change Dosya’s ten-second limit. **The signature differs.** Hash the exact bytes received, including whitespace, rather than re-serialized JSON, and verify with the current endpoint secret. ## Related guides - [Verify webhook signatures](/developers/webhook-signatures) - [Inspect deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Create a webhook endpoint
summary: Register a workspace webhook through the app or REST, verify signed events, test delivery and handle retries, endpoint caps, secret rotation and deletion.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Evidence: apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx; apps/web/src/router.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/index.cap.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/roll-secret.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/deliveries/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/deliveries/[did]/redeliver.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/events.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/events.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/guard.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/guard.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/emit.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/sign.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/sign.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/ssrf-guard.ts; apps/api/src/lib/upload/finalize-session.ts; src/pages/developer/api.astro; apps/api/src/lib/access/rest-scope.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/emit.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/authz.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/authz.unit.test.ts. Repository contracts and tests verified locally; no production requests or credentials used.
body: Set up a cloud storage webhook to receive signed JSON notifications at your own public HTTPS receiver. Dosya supports `file.uploaded`, `file.deleted` and `share.accessed`. Creating an endpoint activates it immediately, so deploy the receiver and its private secret storage before relying on production events. ## Access and receiver requirements Select the workspace whose activity should reach your server. Webhook administration requires workspace membership and **manage_settings**: built-in owner and administrator roles qualify, as does a custom role granted that permission. A REST credential additionally needs **Full access**, REST API protocol access and a workspace pin compatible with the endpoint. A read-only or upload-only key cannot administer webhooks. The receiver URL must use HTTPS and resolve to publicly reachable addresses. Localhost, private-network destinations and disallowed addresses are rejected, including when DNS changes after creation. A public HTTPS development tunnel may be used if its destination passes validation; `http://localhost` cannot be registered. The endpoint cap is **16 per workspace**, including inactive endpoints. Free-plan users can create **3 endpoints in total across their workspaces**, counted by creator. The workspace cap is checked before that free-plan cap. Delete an unused endpoint only after deciding whether you need its delivery history. ## Steps: create it in the app 1. Open [Integrations → Webhooks](https://app.dosya.dev/integrations/webhooks) with the intended workspace active. 2. Select **New endpoint**. In **New webhook endpoint**, enter **Endpoint URL**. 3. Under **Events**, choose at least one of **File uploaded**, **File deleted** or **Share accessed**. Add **Description** if it will help identify this receiver later. 4. Select **Create endpoint**. The form rejects a non-HTTPS address with `URL must be a valid https:// address.` and an empty event selection with `Select at least one event type.` 5. In **Signing secret**, select **Copy** and store the `whsec_` value in your receiver's secret configuration before closing the dialog. It will not be shown again. 6. The endpoint card should show **Active** and the subscribed event names. Select **Send test event**, then inspect **Deliveries** and the receiver's logs. The test button sends a synthetic `file.uploaded` event with `data.test: true`, `file_id: "test_file"`, `name: "test.txt"` and `size: 12`. It does not create a real file. This test is sent even if your endpoint subscribes only to a different event, so make the receiver handle it deliberately. The toast **Test event sent** confirms the trigger; a successful delivery and the receiver's verified record confirm receipt. ## Register and test through REST Set `DOSYA_API_KEY` privately to an authorized full-access key. Replace the workspace and receiver examples with your actual values: ```bash set -e umask 077 curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ 'https://api.dosya.dev/api/webhooks' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{ "workspace_id": "REPLACE_WITH_WORKSPACE_ID", "url": "https://receiver.example.com/dosya", "events": ["file.uploaded"], "description": "File processing receiver" }' -o webhook-created.json ``` `receiver.example.com` is a nonfunctional placeholder. The **201** response contains `ok: true` and `webhook` with `id`, `workspace_id`, `url`, `events`, `description`, `active: 1`, `source`, `secret` and `created_at`. Copy `webhook.secret` into private receiver configuration, never into the API-key field. A webhook signing secret verifies outbound events; it is not a REST authentication token. Read `webhook.id` and send the test after saving the secret: ```bash DOSYA_WEBHOOK_ID=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("webhook-created.json"))["webhook"]["id"])') curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --request POST \ "https://api.dosya.dev/api/webhooks/$DOSYA_WEBHOOK_ID/test" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ "https://api.dosya.dev/api/webhooks/$DOSYA_WEBHOOK_ID/deliveries?page=1&per_page=10" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" ``` The test response returns `delivery_id`; delivery may still be running when that response arrives. The list shows its status, attempts, response code and any recorded error. Remove `webhook-created.json` after saving the one-time secret. `GET /api/webhooks?workspace_id=…` lists endpoints without revealing their secrets. ## Verify each received request The receiver gets an HTTP **POST** with `Content-Type: application/json`, `User-Agent: dosya-webhooks/1` and these headers: - `X-Dosya-Signature: t=TIMESTAMP,v1=LOWERCASE_HEX_HMAC` - `X-Dosya-Event-Id`: the stable event ID - `X-Dosya-Event-Type`: the event name - `X-Dosya-Delivery-Id`: the delivery record ID The JSON envelope has `id`, `type`, `created` in Unix seconds, `workspace_id` and `data`. A file-upload event supplies `file_id`, `name`, `size` in bytes, `folder_id`, `version` and `is_new_version`. It notifies your receiver; it does not include the file bytes or grant file-download rights. Verify HMAC-SHA256 using the signing secret over `timestamp + "." + raw_body`. Preserve the original request bytes before JSON parsing; reserializing JSON can change the signature. Compare in constant time and reject timestamps more than **300 seconds** away from your clock. This Node.js verification function uses only built-in crypto: ```javascript import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto'; // rawBody must be a Buffer of the untouched HTTP request body. export function verified(rawBody, signature, secret, now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)) { const match = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(signature ?? ''); if (!match || Math.abs(now - Number(match[1])) > 300) return false; const expected = createHmac('sha256', secret) .update(match[1] + '.').update(rawBody).digest(); const received = Buffer.from(match[2], 'hex'); return received.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(expected, received); } ``` Only parse and enqueue the event after verification succeeds. Persist a deduplication record keyed by the envelope `id` before applying business effects; automated retries retain the event/delivery identity, and manual redelivery uses a new delivery ID for the same event and payload. Returning 2xx before durable acceptance risks acknowledging work you then lose. ## Delivery timing and recovery Any **2xx** response marks delivery success. The receiver has a **10-second** timeout; accept quickly and move long processing to a durable queue. Non-2xx responses, timeouts and URL-validation failures count as failed attempts. One allowed redirect hop may be followed; a second redirect is a failure. A direct stable receiver URL is easier to diagnose than redirect chains. There are **6 attempts total**, not six retries after the first. The first runs immediately; after successive failures, delays are **30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour and 6 hours**, measured from the preceding failed attempt. Scheduling and network work can add delay; these are not guaranteed delivery deadlines. An endpoint is auto-disabled after **15 consecutive failed attempts across events**. A successful attempt resets that failure run. Fix the receiver, inspect **Deliveries**, then use **Re-enable** on the disabled card; re-enabling clears its failure counter. Do not re-enable an unchanged broken receiver. For a retained delivery, use **Redeliver** in its expanded log or `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/redeliver`. It creates another delivery record, preserving the original event ID and payload. Keep deduplication in place so retrying a notification cannot duplicate a job, invoice or external action. Test and redelivery endpoints each allow **20 calls per user per 300 seconds**; obey a **429** response's `Retry-After`. ## Setup errors and irreversible changes | Failure | Resolution | | --- | --- | | **400**, `Endpoint URL not allowed: …` | Correct HTTPS, DNS or the named address-validation issue. The URL is checked at registration and delivery. | | **400**, `events must be a non-empty array` | Send at least one supported event string. | | **400**, `unknown event type: …` | Use `file.uploaded`, `file.deleted` or `share.accessed` exactly. | | **403**, `API key scope 'full' required` | Use an authorized full-access credential; a role change alone will not widen a restricted key. | | **403**, `You don't have permission to manage webhooks` | Request **manage_settings** from the workspace administrator. | | **400**, `Webhook endpoint limit reached (16 per workspace). Delete an unused endpoint first.` | Review the workspace's endpoints, including disabled ones. | | **403**, `The free plan allows 3 webhook endpoints in total. Delete one or upgrade for more.` | Review endpoints you created across all workspaces. | | **404**, `Webhook not found` or `Delivery not found` | Confirm the IDs and endpoint association before retrying. | **Roll secret** generates a new signing secret and makes the old one stop working immediately, without a grace period. Prepare the receiver to accept the replacement promptly, save the newly revealed value and remove the old secret. The REST equivalent is `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/roll-secret`, which returns `secret` once and allows **10 rotations per user per hour**. A missed reveal requires another rotation. **Edit** can change the URL, events, description and active state. **Delete** asks for confirmation and permanently removes the endpoint **and its delivery history**; it cannot be undone. Deletion stops future delivery to that endpoint but cannot recall events or data already received by another server. The receiver's response snippet can be retained in the log up to **500 characters**. Return a short neutral acknowledgement without credentials or confidential data. Log event IDs, delivery IDs and sanitized errors rather than secrets, signatures or complete sensitive payloads. Send a real harmless subscribed event after the synthetic test and verify it was accepted once before enabling downstream production actions. ## Expected result The endpoint is Active in the selected workspace, its receiver verifies the signature and persists one event record, and Deliveries shows success for the synthetic test and a harmless subscribed event. The endpoint’s saved secret is held privately by the receiver; endpoint listings do not reveal it. ## Related guides - [Set up REST authentication](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [Create or revoke an integration API key](/developers/api-key)

title: Deduplicate webhook deliveries
summary: Use the Dosya event ID as a transactional idempotency key so automatic retries and manual redelivery cannot repeat downstream side effects safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/deliveries/[did]/redeliver.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/emit.ts, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx. Production behavior for “Deduplicate webhook deliveries” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Use the event ID for business idempotency. Automatic retries reuse both IDs, but manual redelivery deliberately creates a new delivery ID while retaining the same event ID and exact payload. ## Steps 1. Verify `X-Dosya-Signature` over the raw body, then read `X-Dosya-Event-Id` and confirm it matches the body’s top-level `id`. Treat an absent or conflicting value as malformed input. 2. Begin a database transaction and insert the event ID into a table with a uniqueness constraint. Store the event type, first delivery ID, receipt time, and processing state without exposing the payload in ordinary logs. 3. If the insert conflicts, return a 2xx after confirming the existing record is committed. Do not reapply the downstream change merely because `X-Dosya-Delivery-Id` differs. 4. If the insert succeeds, apply the state change and commit the idempotency record in the same transaction or atomic workflow. A crash between the side effect and its marker is the duplicate window this design closes. 5. Retain each delivery ID in an attempt log for diagnostics. Automatic retry keeps the original delivery ID; **Redeliver** creates a fresh `whd_…` value but copies the original `evt_…` event ID. 6. Force one receiver failure, allow a retry, and then use **Redeliver** on that row. Verify that all requests are traceable while the business table changes exactly once for the shared event ID. Dosya event IDs are generated once per emitted event. One event can fan out to multiple subscribed endpoints, so event-based deduplication also protects a receiver accidentally registered more than once. ## Expected result The first verified event commits one downstream effect. Automatic attempts and manually queued redelivery receive 2xx acknowledgements without duplicating that effect, while delivery IDs remain available for operational tracing. **Duplicates still appear.** Check that the unique event-ID claim and the business mutation share one transaction; a separate “processed later” write can fail after the mutation. **A manual replay was ignored unexpectedly.** That is correct for an already completed event. Create a new business command if an operator truly intends a second effect. ## Related guides - [Verify webhook signatures](/developers/webhook-signatures) - [Inspect deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Delete an unused webhook endpoint
summary: Export any required delivery evidence, delete the selected webhook endpoint, and understand that its history and pending retries are removed permanently.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/webhooks/retry.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/guard.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/integrations.ts. Production behavior for “Delete an unused webhook endpoint” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Deleting a webhook endpoint removes its delivery history and pending retries as well as stopping new events. Export any evidence first because Dosya provides no restore operation. ## Steps 1. Sign in interactively, choose the workspace, and open **Integrations → Webhooks**. Your workspace role must include `manage_settings`; an API request made with a scoped key requires **Full access**. 2. Match the endpoint by its complete HTTPS URL, description, subscribed event badges, and **Active** or **Disabled** state. Do not rely on position because endpoints are listed newest first. 3. Open **Deliveries** and record any event ID, response status, attempt count, or failure evidence your audit process requires. Deletion removes all delivery rows for this endpoint. 4. Select **Delete** on the endpoint card. In **Delete webhook**, verify the URL and read `This can’t be undone and its delivery history will be lost.` 5. Choose the destructive **Delete** button. The API deletes the endpoint’s delivery rows and endpoint record together, preventing future event creation and retry selection. It cannot cancel an attempt a worker already selected or started, so the receiver may still observe one final in-flight request. 6. Confirm **Webhook deleted**, reload the page, and produce one controlled subscribed event only if safe. No new delivery row should appear for the deleted endpoint. Allow for the final in-flight request, and remember that the same receiver URL can still get requests when another active endpoint uses it. Deleting an unused endpoint can free one of the limits: 16 endpoints per workspace, and three endpoints in total for a Free user across all workspaces. Other workspace administrators receive an in-app notice of the removal. ## Expected result The endpoint card and its stored delivery history disappear. Dosya creates no future delivery rows for that endpoint and no longer selects its retries, although an attempt already in flight can still reach the receiver once. **Delete failed** means the endpoint may still exist. Reload before retrying so a delayed response does not lead to action on the wrong row. **The control is unavailable.** Confirm the selected workspace and ask for a role carrying `manage_settings`; owner/admin names are not the only valid roles because a custom role may hold that permission. ## Related guides - [Create a webhook](/developers/webhook-create) - [Inspect deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Inspect and redeliver webhook deliveries
summary: Read webhook delivery status, response details, retry timing and identifiers, then redeliver safely after correcting the receiving service.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified delivery fields, UI labels, pagination, retry intervals, timeout, response capture, redelivery behavior, rate limits and automatic disabling in apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/deliveries/index.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/deliveries/[did]/redeliver.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.unit.test.ts; and apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/webhooks/retry.ts. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: The delivery log shows what Dosya attempted, when the next retry is due, and what the receiver returned. Use it to separate an event-generation problem from a network, signature, or application failure. Correct the receiver before manually redelivering an event. ## Steps Open [Integrations → Webhooks](https://app.dosya.dev/integrations/webhooks), activate the intended workspace, find the endpoint, and select **Deliveries**. **Recent deliveries** displays ten rows per page with these columns: - **Event** is the subscribed `event_type`, such as `file.uploaded`. - **Created** is when the delivery record was added. - **Status** is **Pending**, **Success**, or **Failed**. - **Response** shows the HTTP status, `Error` for a recorded transport failure, or `-` when no result has been stored yet. - **Attempts** counts completed requests, including the first one. - **Next retry** is populated only while a failed delivery remains pending. Hover the **Response** cell to read the recorded error or response snippet. Dosya keeps at most the first 500 response characters, so return a small neutral body such as `ok`; do not echo tokens, personal data, stack traces, or request payloads in the acknowledgement. Each outbound request carries both `X-Dosya-Event-Id` and `X-Dosya-Delivery-Id`. Automated attempts for a retained delivery use the same identifiers. Manual **Redeliver** creates a new delivery ID while preserving the original event ID and JSON payload. Deduplicate business work by event ID so either path remains safe. ## Understand automatic retries Any HTTP status from 200 through 299 is a success. A non-2xx response, network error, rejected endpoint URL, or receiver that does not finish within **10 seconds** counts as a failed attempt. Dosya can follow one allowed HTTPS redirect; another redirect remains a non-2xx failure. There are **six attempts in total**. After the immediate first attempt fails, later attempts are scheduled after **30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 6 hours**. Queue and network time can make the observed delay longer. After attempt six fails, the delivery becomes **Failed** and has no next retry. An endpoint reaches **Disabled** after 15 consecutive failed delivery attempts across its events. One successful attempt resets that consecutive-failure incident. When the card says **Auto-disabled after repeated failures**, repair the receiver first and then choose **Re-enable**; this clears the counter but does not retroactively deliver missed product events. ## Diagnose a failed attempt 1. Copy the event ID, delivery ID, event type, HTTP response, and recorded time into the incident record. Exclude the signature and signing secret. 2. Match the delivery ID to the receiver's access log. No request normally points to DNS, TLS, public-address validation, firewall, or timeout trouble. 3. For a 4xx response, inspect signature parsing and the receiver's route or authentication middleware. For a 5xx response, correct the application failure before retrying. 4. Confirm the handler reads the untouched body and validates `X-Dosya-Signature` before parsing JSON. 5. Replay the captured payload only in a controlled test environment, using a deliberately invalid signature as a negative test. Never bypass verification in production to make the row turn green. 6. Make the receiver persist its deduplication record and queued job before returning 2xx. If **Deliveries** cannot be opened, webhook management requires membership in that workspace and the `manage_settings` permission. The REST API additionally requires a full-access credential; otherwise it returns `API key scope 'full' required`. ## Redeliver after the fix Select **Redeliver** on the affected row. The toast **Redelivery queued** means a new delivery record was created; it does not yet prove the receiver accepted it. Return to page 1, refresh **Recent deliveries**, and look for the new row. A success should show a 2xx response and one attempt. The REST sequence is: ```bash curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \ "https://api.dosya.dev/api/webhooks/$DOSYA_WEBHOOK_ID/deliveries?page=1&per_page=25" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --request POST \ "https://api.dosya.dev/api/webhooks/$DOSYA_WEBHOOK_ID/deliveries/$DOSYA_DELIVERY_ID/redeliver" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" ``` The list endpoint accepts `page` and clamps `per_page` to **10–100**, defaulting to 25. A missing endpoint returns `Webhook not found`; a delivery that does not belong to that endpoint returns `Delivery not found`. Manual redelivery permits **20 calls per user per 300 seconds** and can return 429 with `Retry-After` when exceeded. ## Expected result The replacement delivery reaches **Success**, the receiver log matches its delivery and event IDs, and downstream state changes once. Keep the original failed row as incident evidence; deleting the webhook permanently removes the endpoint and its entire delivery history. ## Related guides - [Choose subscribed event types](/developers/webhook-events) - [Verify signatures before processing](/developers/webhook-signatures) - [Troubleshoot webhook delivery failures](/troubleshooting/webhooks)

title: Choose webhook event subscriptions
summary: Choose file upload, file deletion, or share access events, understand each payload, and test the exact changes your receiver must process.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14. Verified the accepted names, selector labels, payload fields, update behavior and delivery headers in apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/events.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/emit.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/is-new-version-contract.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/share-accessed-timestamp-contract.unit.test.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download-all.ts; apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/index.ts; apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx; and src/pages/developer/api.astro. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Dosya can notify one endpoint about three event types: `file.uploaded`, `file.deleted`, and `share.accessed`. Subscribe only to the changes your receiver can authenticate and process. Event selection filters future notifications for that endpoint; it does not replay activity that occurred before the subscription was saved. ## What each event means | Event | When it fires | Fields inside `data` | | --- | --- | --- | | `file.uploaded` | A new file finishes uploading or a new version finishes replacing an existing file, including uploads through the web app, CLI, WebDAV, SFTP, or S3 gateway. | `file_id`, `name`, byte `size`, nullable `folder_id`, numeric `version`, and `is_new_version` | | `file.deleted` | A file moves to Trash or is permanently erased. Deleting a folder produces an event for each affected descendant file. | `file_id`, `name`, and boolean `permanent` | | `share.accessed` | A public share is viewed, a shared file is downloaded, or a shared folder archive is downloaded. | `share_id`, `token`, `access_type`, `accessed_at`, and the applicable `file_id` or `folder_id` | Treat `file.uploaded` as both “new file” and “new version.” Branch on `data.is_new_version`; do not infer that distinction from the event name. For deletion, `permanent: false` means the file was moved to Trash, while `permanent: true` means it was purged and cannot be restored. Share access uses `access_type` values such as `view`, `download`, and `download_all`; a view can identify a file, folder, or bundle. Every payload also has a top-level event `id`, `type`, Unix-second `created` time, `workspace_id`, and `data`. The request headers repeat the event identity as `X-Dosya-Event-Id` and the selected name as `X-Dosya-Event-Type`. Use the top-level `id` as the durable deduplication key. ## Steps 1. Open [Integrations → Webhooks](https://app.dosya.dev/integrations/webhooks) with the endpoint's workspace active. 2. Find the endpoint URL and select **Edit**. 3. Under **Events**, check **File uploaded**, **File deleted**, or **Share accessed**. At least one must remain selected; otherwise the form shows `Select at least one event type.` 4. Review **Endpoint URL**, **Description**, and **Active** while the dialog is open, then select **Save changes**. 5. Confirm the endpoint card shows the intended event names as badges. Webhook administration requires workspace membership plus the `manage_settings` permission. A scoped REST credential must have **Full access** to administer endpoints. If the API receives an unsupported string, it responds with `unknown event type: VALUE`; an empty list returns `events must be a non-empty array`. The REST equivalent is `PATCH /api/webhooks/{endpoint_id}`. Send the complete replacement list because `events` describes the endpoint's saved subscription, rather than an item to add to the existing list: ```bash curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --request PATCH \ "https://api.dosya.dev/api/webhooks/$DOSYA_WEBHOOK_ID" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOSYA_API_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{"events":["file.uploaded","file.deleted"]}' ``` Do not use `share.created`, `folder.created`, or `member.joined`; they are not accepted webhook event types in the current API. ## Prove the subscription with real actions **Send test event** always sends a synthetic `file.uploaded` payload with `data.test: true`, even when the endpoint is subscribed only to another event. Use it to prove URL reachability and signature handling, then perform one harmless real action for every selected type: - Upload a small disposable file and check `is_new_version: false`. - Upload a new version of that file and check `is_new_version: true` with an increased version number. - Move the test file to Trash and verify `permanent: false`; purge only if the test data is disposable. - Open a test share, then download it, and confirm the receiver distinguishes `view` from `download`. Open **Deliveries** on the endpoint card and match `event_type`, creation time, status, and event ID with the receiver log. A successful receiver should authenticate the raw body, persist the event ID, and return a 2xx response only after durable acceptance. Receiving an event twice must not repeat an external effect. ## Expected result The endpoint card lists only the required event names. Each controlled product action creates a matching signed delivery, and the receiver records its event once with the documented payload fields. Unselected event types do not create deliveries for that endpoint. ## Related guides - [Create a webhook endpoint](/developers/webhook-create) - [Inspect webhook delivery attempts](/developers/webhook-deliveries) - [Verify the webhook signature](/developers/webhook-signatures)

title: Handle webhook events received out of order
summary: Use event occurrence fields and file version numbers to reject stale webhook work, then reconcile current state when no ordering field exists.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/emit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/deliveries/[did]/redeliver.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/[sessionId]/complete.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts. Production behavior for “Handle webhook events received out of order” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Webhook arrival order is not a state-order guarantee. Retry delays and manual redelivery can make an older payload arrive after a newer event, and delivery-row creation time records the attempt rather than the original business change. ## Steps 1. Verify the signature, deduplicate by the top-level event `id`, and parse `type`, `created`, `workspace_id`, and `data`. Event IDs are opaque values and must not be sorted. 2. Store top-level `created` as the event’s Unix-second occurrence time, not a total-order sequence. Separate events may share the same second, and a redelivery retains the old payload while receiving a new delivery row. 3. For `file.uploaded`, key state by `data.file_id` and compare the integer `data.version`. Apply a higher version, treat the same event ID as duplicate, and ignore a lower version that arrives after a newer one. 4. For `share.accessed`, use `data.accessed_at` for the access occurrence and retain every distinct event ID. Two views of one link are separate events even when their timestamps are close. 5. For `file.deleted`, note that current payloads provide `file_id`, `name`, and `permanent` but no resource version. Reconcile current Dosya state through an independently authorized API read before triggering an irreversible downstream deletion. 6. Test by delaying an older upload event, processing a higher file version first, and then releasing the old request. Confirm the stored version does not move backward and both attempts receive deliberate acknowledgements. The sender offers no ordering contract across events or endpoints. Keep per-resource monotonic state where a reliable field exists and use current-state reconciliation where it does not. ## Expected result The consumer converges on the newest known file version, retains distinct share accesses, and refuses to infer deletion order from random IDs or delivery timestamps. Late retries cannot roll downstream state backward. **Two events have the same `created` value.** Use the resource-specific field or reconcile current state; the envelope timestamp has one-second precision. **A delete cannot be reconciled.** Quarantine that event for operator review and return according to the receiver’s retry policy instead of guessing at an irreversible transition. ## Related guides - [Verify webhook signatures](/developers/webhook-signatures) - [Inspect deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Log webhook diagnostics without secrets
summary: Record webhook event, delivery, type, timing, and status fields while excluding signing material, private payload data, and receiver secrets.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/sign.ts, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download-all.ts. Production behavior for “Log webhook diagnostics without secrets” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Webhook diagnostics should explain an attempt without copying its credentials or private data. This matters especially for `share.accessed`, whose current payload contains the live share token. ## Steps 1. After signature verification, create a structured log record containing `X-Dosya-Event-Id`, `X-Dosya-Delivery-Id`, `X-Dosya-Event-Type`, receiver time, verification outcome, and an internal correlation or queue ID. 2. Exclude the endpoint signing secret, raw `X-Dosya-Signature`, authorization material, and complete request body. Upload and deletion data contains file IDs and names; share-access data includes `share_id` and a bearer `token`. 3. When an operator needs payload context, allowlist non-secret fields by event type and redact values before logging. Do not depend on a broad JSON serializer whose future fields could enter logs automatically. 4. Return an empty or sanitized 2xx acknowledgement after durable intake. Dosya stores the first 500 characters of the receiver response, so response bodies can expose data in **Recent deliveries** even when application logs are clean. 5. On failure, log the local exception class and internal trace ID rather than the payload. Dosya separately records the HTTP status, a clipped response snippet, or the transport error when no response arrives. 6. Open **Integrations → Webhooks → Deliveries** and correlate a controlled test by event type, created time, status, attempts, and next retry. Confirm neither the receiver log nor Dosya’s response tooltip reveals a secret. Every outgoing request also carries `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: dosya-webhooks/1`. These are useful transport facts but do not authenticate a delivery. ## Expected result Operators can trace a webhook from Dosya to the receiver using event, delivery, and internal job identifiers. Logs and stored response snippets omit signing secrets, share tokens, file payloads, and other confidential content. **Private text appears under Response.** Remove it from the receiver response body, deploy the change, and avoid copying the existing snippet into tickets or chat. **A failure lacks an HTTP status.** Treat the stored error as a DNS, TLS, network, or timeout path and correlate it with the receiver platform trace ID. ## Related guides - [Verify webhook signatures](/developers/webhook-signatures) - [Inspect deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Handle webhook payload versions
summary: Validate the current unversioned webhook envelope by event type, distinguish file version from schema version, and tolerate additive fields safely.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/emit.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/events.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/is-new-version-contract.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/share-accessed-timestamp-contract.unit.test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/share/[token]/download-all.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/folders/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/lib/s3/operations/delete-object.ts. Production behavior for “Handle webhook payload versions” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: The current Dosya webhook envelope has no schema-version field. Its stable outer shape is `id`, `type`, `created`, `workspace_id`, and `data`; `data.version` on an upload is the file version, not a payload schema version. ## Steps 1. Verify the signature over the raw request body, parse JSON, and require top-level string `id`, supported `type`, numeric `created`, string `workspace_id`, and object `data`. 2. Accept only the current event types `file.uploaded`, `file.deleted`, and `share.accessed`. Route malformed or unsupported input to a durable quarantine rather than guessing at a schema. Attach the event ID only when the top-level `id` passed validation; otherwise record a receiver-generated trace ID. 3. For `file.uploaded`, validate `file_id`, `name`, byte `size`, nullable `folder_id`, integer `version`, and boolean `is_new_version`. Use that version only for ordering revisions of the named file. 4. For `file.deleted`, validate `file_id`, `name`, and boolean `permanent`. A move to trash sends `false`, while a permanent file or folder purge sends `true` for each erased file. 5. For `share.accessed`, require `share_id`, sensitive `token`, `accessed_at`, and an `access_type` of `view`, `download`, or `download_all`. A bundle `view` can have both `file_id` and `folder_id` set to `null`; validate the identifiers allowed by that access type instead of requiring one globally. Do not write the token to diagnostics. 6. Ignore additional fields your consumer does not need, then test with one extra property and one missing required property. The additive sample should process, while malformed input should be quarantined visibly without a partial side effect. Because there is no schema version to route today, code that requires `payload.version` will reject every valid Dosya event. Branch by `type` and keep event-specific validation isolated so a future contract can be added deliberately. ## Expected result Current payloads pass type-specific validation, additive properties do not break processing, and `data.version` remains a file revision number. Malformed events fail visibly without leaking the share token or applying partial work. **Every payload reports an unknown version.** Remove the top-level schema-version requirement; no such field is emitted in the current implementation. **A new field causes rejection.** Change strict object equality to required-field validation while retaining type checks for the fields your consumer uses. ## Related guides - [REST API quickstart](/developers/rest-api-quickstart) - [Inspect webhook deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Recover webhook delivery after receiver downtime
summary: Restore a webhook receiver, verify it with a controlled test, re-enable the endpoint, and manually replay required failed events without duplicates.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/health.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/internal/webhooks/retry.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/test.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/index.ts, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx. Production behavior for “Recover webhook delivery after receiver downtime” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Receiver recovery has two separate jobs: reopen future delivery and decide which failed historical events still need replay. Re-enabling an endpoint does not drain its terminal backlog. ## Steps 1. Restore the public HTTPS receiver and confirm it can verify the current signing secret, commit an event durably, and answer with 2xx inside Dosya’s ten-second timeout. 2. In **Integrations → Webhooks**, locate the endpoint. A sustained incident shows **Auto-disabled after repeated failures**, the failed-attempt count, disable time, and **Re-enable**. 3. While the endpoint is still disabled, choose **Send test event**. The test route sends a real signed request even when `active` is false; open **Deliveries** and wait for the new row to show **Success** rather than trusting the queued toast. 4. Select **Re-enable** only after that proof. The update clears `consecutive_failures` and `disabled_at`, but it does not change deliveries already marked **Failed**. 5. Review historical rows newest first and choose **Redeliver** only for business events the receiver still needs. Each replay has a new delivery ID but retains the original event ID and payload, so event-ID deduplication must be active. 6. Produce one controlled subscribed event and verify normal **Success**. Confirm the recovered business state once, then document any failed events intentionally left unreplayed. A delivery receives at most six attempts: initial, then due after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 6 hours. Fifteen consecutive failed attempts across an endpoint disable it. A later ten-minute health pass marks that endpoint’s remaining pending rows failed with `endpoint auto-disabled after sustained delivery failure`. Each pass examines at most 50 unhealthy endpoints, so a large incident may require subsequent sweeps before every disabled endpoint’s queue becomes terminal. ## Expected result The repaired receiver passes a controlled test before the endpoint resumes future traffic. Re-enabling clears the incident counters, and manually selected historical events recover without duplicate downstream changes. **A failed row stays failed after re-enable.** That is expected. Use **Redeliver** for the specific event after checking its business effect. **The test succeeds but new events do not arrive.** Confirm the card is **Active**, the intended event badges remain selected, and the producer action occurred in the same workspace. ## Related guides - [Verify webhook signatures](/developers/webhook-signatures) - [Inspect deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Redeliver a failed webhook event
summary: Queue a new delivery for one stored webhook event, distinguish its new delivery ID from the retained event ID, and verify the receiver result.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/deliveries/[did]/redeliver.ts, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.ts. body: Manual redelivery creates a new attempt record for the stored event. It copies the exact payload and event ID, assigns a new delivery ID, and starts another normal retry cycle. ## Steps 1. Repair the receiver and confirm event-ID idempotency before replaying anything. A manual replay can repeat a downstream effect if the consumer deduplicates only by delivery ID. 2. Open **Integrations → Webhooks**, choose the endpoint, and expand **Deliveries**. Identify the required **Failed** row by event type, created time, response or error, and attempt count. 3. Check whether the event already changed downstream state despite its failed acknowledgement. If it did, preserve that state and let the idempotency record absorb the replay. 4. Select **Redeliver** on the chosen row. Although the UI offers this action for every status, do not replay a **Success** row unless a deliberate second delivery is safe. 5. Treat **Redelivery queued — A new delivery attempt has been scheduled** as a scheduling receipt. The route creates a new `whd_…` delivery with zero attempts while retaining the original `evt_…` ID and body. 6. Refresh page 1 of **Recent deliveries** and inspect the new row until it shows **Success** or a scheduled retry. Correlate its new delivery ID at the receiver and confirm the event ID caused no duplicate effect. Each manual redelivery can receive six attempts under the standard backoff. Dosya limits this action to 20 requests per user in five minutes to prevent the endpoint from becoming an outbound flood source. ## Expected result A new delivery record carries the original event and reaches the repaired receiver. The delivery ID changes for tracing, the event ID remains stable for idempotency, and the downstream result exists once. **Redeliver failed** means no reliable replay receipt was returned. Reload the delivery list before clicking again so a delayed request does not queue an unnecessary duplicate. **The new row remains Pending.** Read **Next retry**; a non-2xx response or ten-second timeout follows the ordinary schedule rather than becoming immediate success. ## Related guides - [Create a webhook](/developers/webhook-create) - [Inspect deliveries](/developers/webhook-deliveries)

title: Re-enable a webhook after repeated failures
summary: Repair and test an auto-disabled webhook receiver before re-enabling it, then replay only the failed events the downstream system still needs.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/deliver.ts, apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/retry.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/index.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/test.ts, apps/web/src/pages/integrations/webhooks.tsx.
