Filters update the result count, and pagination exposes older rows. Expanding a row reveals the contextual fields recorded for that event. A denied or failed badge indicates the request did not complete successfully. Compare the event with the current resource state before deciding what changed. ## Limits and privacy behavior - Not every event contains every detail. Source IP, location, device, request ID or session ID may be absent. - Approximate location is derived context and may reflect a VPN, proxy, corporate gateway or mobile carrier. - Resource names are withheld when the viewer cannot open the corresponding file or folder. - Members without full activity permission may see only narrower activity summaries on other pages. - A folder-confined member cannot use the full workspace activity page. - The log records supported product actions; it is not a live network trace or file-content history. - Relative times change as the page ages. Use the expanded absolute timestamp in an investigation. ## Troubleshooting **Activity is unavailable.** Your role lacks **View activity log**, the page is blocked by page-access rules, or the member is folder-restricted. Ask an owner to review the role and scope. **No events match the filters.** Clear filters, broaden the time by moving through older pages, and check that the action belongs to the selected category. **A resource name is missing.** The resource may have been deleted, or your current access does not allow its name to be shown. Use the event type, timestamp and identifier without trying to bypass that boundary. **The location looks wrong.** Source locations are approximate and often identify the network exit point. Compare the IP, device and session with known access patterns. **An event needs investigation.** Preserve the timestamp, actor, action, outcome, resource, request ID and session ID. Send them through [private support](https://app.dosya.dev/support); do not publish sensitive IP or session information. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I filter by more than one member or category? Yes. The filter menus support multiple selections. The active combination controls the result set. ### Does a failed login mean the account was accessed? No. A failed or denied outcome means that recorded attempt did not succeed. Review nearby events and active sessions if the attempt is unfamiliar. ### Can activity restore a deleted file or member? No. It records context. Use the relevant recovery or administration workflow for the current resource. ## Related guides - [Checking who opened or downloaded a sharing link](/sharing/link-activity) - [Restricting a workspace member to one folder](/workspaces/folder-access) - [Removing a member, leaving or deleting a workspace](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Assign a custom role to a workspace member
summary: Assign an existing custom role to another workspace member, respect the permission ceiling, and verify the resulting access after caches refresh.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/role-grant.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/members/[id].ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/roles-enforcement.int.test.ts. No production member was changed.
body: Assigning a custom role replaces the member’s permission map but preserves an existing folder boundary. The actor must hold **Manage roles** and every permission granted by the target role. ## Before you start - Open **Team** in the intended workspace and identify the member by name and email. - Inspect the custom role under **Existing roles** first; its name alone does not describe its permissions. - Ensure another trusted person retains **Manage roles** if this assignment removes administrative access. ## Steps 1. Find the person under **Members** and confirm the row is neither the current owner nor the row marked **you**. 2. Review the role’s enabled permissions, access conditions, and usage limits in **View role permissions**. 3. Open **Role for _member name_** and choose the custom role; options granting more than you hold are unavailable. 4. Wait for **Role updated**, which states that the named member is now assigned to the selected role. 5. Ask the member to reload Dosya; distributed membership and permission caches can require roughly 60 seconds to converge. 6. In that member’s session, perform one permitted task and attempt one intentionally withheld task without using real customer data. ## Assignment effects The role change cannot assign **Owner**, alter your own row, or demote the sitting owner. Ownership moves through its separate transfer control. A role-only update leaves **Limit to a folder** unchanged, so role permissions and the folder subtree apply together. The affected member receives a role-change notice describing the old and new role and lost permissions. The operation is reversible by another manager who still satisfies the same grant ceiling. ## Expected result The Team row shows the custom role, the member remains inside any prior folder limit, allowed controls work, and the deliberately withheld operation is absent or refused. ## Troubleshooting **You don’t have permission to manage this member.** Your role lacks **Manage roles**. **You don’t have permission to assign this role.** At least one enabled permission exceeds your own map; use a narrower role or ask the owner. **The previous access still works.** Wait about one minute, reload the member session, and repeat the controlled check. ## Related guides - [Understand roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Change a member role](/workspaces/workspace-change-role)

title: Configure workspace branding
summary: Configure paid-plan workspace branding, preview public share pages and emails, validate asset limits, and understand permanent share-handle rules.
verification: Reviewed against apps/web/src/pages/settings/branding.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/branding.ts, branding/logo.ts, branding/handle.ts, branding/preview-email.ts, apps/api/src/lib/branding/entitlement.ts, and migration 0196. This was a local source review; it performed no production action.
body: Workspace branding changes what people outside a workspace see on public share pages and share-notification email. The feature is available on paid plans; the Free plan keeps dosya branding. The built-in Owner and Admin roles can edit branding because they hold both **Access Settings** and **Manage branding**. A custom role needs both permissions. Only the workspace owner can claim the permanent share handle. ## What each control changes | Control | Rule and recipient outcome | | --- | --- | | **Logo** | PNG, JPEG or WebP only, at most 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes). Empty files, GIF and SVG are refused. A successful upload replaces the public logo immediately. | | **Brand name** | Required before any custom branding appears. It is trimmed, limited to 48 characters and cannot contain line breaks or control characters. | | **Brand colour** | Optional six-digit hexadecimal value such as `#B4472E`. It accents the share page; email stays black and white. | | **Share page and share links** | Shows the name, logo and colour on the public page and uses a claimed handle in the URL. | | **Email** | Uses the brand name in the masthead and sender display name. The address remains `noreply@dosya.dev`, and subjects still identify dosya.dev. | | **Hide the Save to dosya button** | Removes that button only while share-page branding is enabled. | ## Steps 1. In the intended workspace, open **Settings → Workspace info** and find **Branding**. 2. Select **Configure**. If the row says **Branding is available on Starter and up**, the workspace owner's current plan does not include the feature. If **Configure** is disabled, inspect the role or contact support when the workspace says branding was disabled. 3. Upload a non-confidential logo. Use its preview to confirm that transparent padding, cropping and contrast work in both themes. 4. Enter **Brand name** and optionally **Brand colour**. A name must be present before the logo, colour or recipient switches take effect. 5. Choose **Share page and share links**, **Email**, and **Hide the Save to dosya button** for the surfaces the organization approved. 6. Open **Preview → View**. The share preview uses the unsaved form state; the email preview is rendered from the real template but is returned only to your browser and sends no message. 7. Select **Save branding**, then open a disposable share in a signed-out window to inspect the recipient view. ## Claim a share handle The owner can enter a handle that is 3–30 characters long. It must use lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens, start and end with a letter or number, and avoid reserved or already-held names. Availability checks are limited to 30 per minute per signed-in user. Review the confirmation dialog before choosing **Claim permanently**. A claimed handle produces URLs shaped like `dosya.dev/s/@yourname/…`; it cannot be changed in the workspace UI, is not released when branding is revoked, and requires support to change. ## Recovery and reset - **Use a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.** The declared MIME type or the file signature is unsupported; export a fresh raster image. - **Logos must be 2 MB or smaller.** Compress or resize the source below 2,097,152 bytes. - **A brand name can be at most 48 characters.** Shorten the visible name; whitespace is trimmed on save. - **Use a six-digit hex colour, for example #B4472E.** Enter all six digits after `#`. - **You do not have permission to change branding.** Ask an owner to grant **Access Settings** and **Manage branding**, or have an owner perform the change. - **Branding is available on paid plans.** The workspace owner's effective plan lacks the `white_label` feature; stored branding remains available for a later upgrade. - **Reset to dosya** clears the brand name and colour, then removes the logo. The three switches and permanent handle remain unchanged. If logo removal fails after the text reset, the UI reports **Partly reset** so you can retry removal. ## Expected result The saved share page shows the approved brand name, optional logo and colour, while recipient email keeps the dosya.dev address and subject conventions. Refreshing the branding page returns the saved values, and a claimed handle remains read-only. ## Related guides - [Customize sharing branding](/sharing/custom-branding) - [Preview sharing branding](/sharing/preview-branding)

title: Change a workspace member role
summary: Change another workspace member’s role, respect the permission ceiling, and verify when the new access and role-change notices take effect for them.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against the Team role selector, role-grant helper, member update API, notification catalog, and member role ceiling and notification tests. No production member or workspace was changed.
body: Changing a role replaces the member’s workspace permission map. A promotion can expose more files or administration controls; a downgrade can immediately remove upload, sharing, download, page, or protocol access. Review the actual permissions in a custom role rather than relying on its name. ## Who can change a role The acting account needs **Manage roles** in the target workspace. The **Team** page itself also requires **Access Team** and **View team members**. The role selector appears only on another member’s non-owner row; your own row and the current owner remain labels. Dosya applies a permission ceiling: every enabled permission in the target role must also be held by the person making the assignment. This rule covers built-in and custom roles. **Owner** never appears as an assignable choice because ownership moves through the separate transfer control. Before a downgrade, confirm that a second trusted person will retain **Manage roles**. A user cannot change their own role, so someone who loses administrative access cannot restore it from that same account. ## Steps 1. Switch to the correct workspace and open **Team**. 2. Under **Members**, find the person by name and email. Do not use the row marked **you**. 3. Open the **Role for _member name_** selector in the **Role** column. 4. Choose the intended built-in or custom role. Roles that exceed your permissions are omitted or disabled. 5. Wait for the **Role updated** message, which names the member and their new role. 6. Have the member reload any open Dosya tabs, then test one action they should retain and one they should no longer have. ## What changes for the member The new role is saved immediately. The affected member receives an important in-app notification, email, and push notification when enabled. The notice names the old and new roles, the actor, what access is now available, and permissions that were lost. Workspace administrators receive a separate in-app record of the change. Changing only `role_id` preserves the member’s **Limit to a folder** setting. Role permissions and folder confinement therefore apply together: selecting a broader role does not expand the person beyond their assigned folder. Open clients can retain an old permission result briefly. The member notification explicitly asks them to reload; distributed permission caches can take roughly 60 seconds to converge. If a correct role still behaves like the previous one, wait a minute, reload, and repeat a single representative action. ## Resolve a refused change - **You don't have permission to manage this member** means the actor lacks **Manage roles**. - **You don't have permission to assign this role** means the selected role contains at least one permission the actor does not hold. Ask the owner to make the change or select a narrower role. - **You cannot change your own role** protects against self-escalation and accidental self-lockout. Use another authorized account. - **Ownership is transferred, not assigned. Use the transfer control.** Use workspace ownership transfer rather than this role list. - **Cannot change the workspace owner's role. Transfer ownership first.** Complete the transfer, then change the former owner’s role if needed. - **Invalid role** can indicate a deleted role or a custom role from another workspace. Reload **Team** and choose from the current list. A role change is reversible by another member who still holds **Manage roles** and satisfies the permission ceiling. Access removed during the interval remains unavailable until a permitted role is assigned again. ## Expected result The member row displays the selected role, permitted controls match its current permission map, its folder boundary remains as configured, and the member receives a notice describing the access change. ## Related guides - [Workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Invite team members](/workspaces/invite-team)

title: Create a custom workspace role
summary: Create a custom workspace role with precise permissions, access conditions, and usage limits, then confirm the role is available for assignment.
verification: Source-verified locally on 2026-10-14 against the custom-role editor, permission registry, roles create/update APIs, grant ceiling logic, input validators, and roles integration tests. No production role was created.
body: A custom role combines workspace permissions with optional network, schedule, and usage restrictions. Create one when the built-in Owner, Admin, Member, and Viewer sets are broader or narrower than the job requires. ## Requirements and limits The creator must belong to the workspace and hold **Manage roles**. They can enable only permissions they already hold. Rows outside that ceiling are disabled with **You don't hold this permission, so you can't grant it.** The server names any disallowed keys if a stale or crafted request bypasses the interface. Choose a role name between 1 and 50 characters. A new role starts with every permission disabled and is created as a workspace-specific custom role. Saving it does not assign the role to any current or invited member. The editor groups 36 controls under **Files**, **Folders**, **Sharing**, **Team**, **Workspace identity**, **Workspace limits**, **Workspace general**, **File management**, **Page access**, and **Protocol access**. A capability and the page that exposes it can be separate; for example, **Create share links** and **Access Shared** solve different parts of the workflow. ## Steps 1. Open **Team** and select **Create custom role** in the **Role guide**, or open **Workspace settings** and the roles section. 2. In **Role identity**, enter a specific **Role name**, such as `External reviewer`. 3. Under **Permissions**, enable only the actions and pages required for the job. Pay particular attention to destructive controls such as **Delete any file**, **Manage roles**, **Lock files & folders**, and **Hide files & folders**. 4. If network boundaries are needed, add comma-separated CIDR values to **Allowed IP ranges**. REST and sync requests evaluate their request address, while WebDAV and S3 enforce the same condition at their gateways. SFTP refuses access for a role with an IP allowlist because its gateway cannot verify the member's original address. 5. Optionally enable **Restrict to active hours**, then choose a time zone, weekdays, and a from/to window. 6. Under **Usage limits**, leave a field blank for unlimited or set positive values for **Requests per minute**, **Egress per day (GB)**, **Max file size (MB)**, and **Max concurrent transfers**. 7. Select **Create role** and wait for **Role created — Your new role is ready to assign.** 8. In **Existing roles**, confirm the new row is marked **custom** and its enabled-permission count matches your review. ## How restrictions combine Role conditions apply to every member assigned that role. Individual API-key restrictions intersect with role restrictions; neither layer can widen the other. The four usage limits cover every protocol. An IP allowlist binds REST, sync, WebDAV, and S3 access, and makes SFTP unavailable for that role because SFTP cannot verify the original client address. Creating the definition does not notify anyone because nobody holds it yet. When an administrator later edits an assigned custom role’s permission switches, all holders receive an in-app notification describing what was gained and lost. Changes to conditions or usage limits do not currently produce that permission-change notice. ## Fix a creation error - **Role name is required** means the trimmed name is empty. - **Role name too long (max 50)** requires a shorter label. - **You don't have permission to manage roles** means your role lacks **Manage roles**. - **You can't grant permissions you don't hold yourself: ...** lists capabilities above your ceiling. Clear those switches or ask the owner to create the role. - **Can't reach the server. Check your connection and try again.** Nothing was confirmed; reconnect and submit once more. A custom role can later be deleted only after all assigned members move elsewhere and every pending invitation or active invite link using it is revoked. Deletion permanently removes the definition, so reassignment should precede cleanup. ## Expected result The custom role appears in **Existing roles**, reports the intended permission count, retains any access conditions and numeric limits, and is available in eligible member and invitation role selectors. ## Related guides - [Understand roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Change a member role](/workspaces/workspace-change-role)

title: Read the workspace dashboard
summary: Read total storage, entitlement sources, owned-workspace usage and shared memberships from the account-level Workspace dashboard accurately.
verification: Reviewed apps/web/src/pages/workspace-dashboard.tsx, components/layout/dashboard-sidebar.tsx, lib/workspace-dashboard.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspace-dashboard.ts and lib/workspace-dashboard.ts with their snapshot/unit tests. No deployment or production data access was used.
body: The account-level **Workspace dashboard** answers two different questions: how much storage you own across your workspaces, and which workspaces other owners have shared with you. It does not show recent activity or a member count. Only signed-in access is required for this page. Workspace-specific permissions still apply after you open a row; a shared workspace can show **Owner**, **Admin**, **Member**, **Viewer** or **Custom role**. ## Dashboard sections | Section | What it reports | | --- | --- | | **Your storage** | Bytes used by every workspace you own, free bytes and the effective account limit. Free space never displays below zero. | | Stacked usage bar | Each owned workspace's share of the used portion. The percentage printed on an owned row is that workspace's usage divided by the total entitlement, rounded to a whole percent. | | **Workspaces you own** | Workspace name, icon, used bytes and its percentage of your account limit. Choosing a row activates that workspace and opens its main Dashboard. | | **Where your space comes from** | Base plan and eligible add-on, custom package, active license and referral rows. Their byte values add up to **Your storage** total. | | **Shared with you** | Workspaces owned by somebody else, with owner name and your role. Their file bytes are charged to that owner and are intentionally absent from your total. | The response is private and may be cached for up to 60 seconds. A just-finished upload, deletion, plan reconciliation or license change can therefore need a refresh after that interval before the dashboard reflects it. ## Steps 1. Open the workspace switcher in the sidebar and select **Workspace dashboard**. 2. In **Your storage**, record the formatted `used`, `free of`, total, and the percentage below the bar. 3. Add the rows under **Where your space comes from**. The sum should equal the displayed total; a zero-byte optional source is omitted. 4. Inspect **Workspaces you own**. Hovering or reading the colored segments identifies how owned-workspace bytes contribute to the filled bar. 5. Review **Shared with you** separately. Its subtitle states **These use the owner's storage, not yours.** The owner name and role explain why a visible workspace contributes no bytes to your pool. 6. Select an owned or shared row only after checking its name and icon. The click changes the active workspace and navigates to its Dashboard. 7. Use **Get more storage** when the owner-level total is the binding limit; it opens Billing. Use that workspace's **Settings → Hard limits** when an explicit workspace cap is blocking writes instead. ## Resolve mismatched figures **A shared workspace is missing from usage.** This is expected: the owner's pool pays for it. Look under **Shared with you**, where the owner and your role are shown. **An owned row percentage seems smaller than its share of used bytes.** The printed row percentage uses the entire entitlement as its denominator, while each colored segment fills a share of the already-used portion of the bar. **A source row disappeared after a lapse.** A free or lapsed account drops paid add-on/custom rows from its effective source breakdown. Active redeemed license bytes and eligible referral storage are resolved separately. **The figures did not change immediately.** Wait for the private 60-second cache window to pass and reload once. If the number remains stale, open the workspace itself and compare its storage view before retrying any transfer. **Failed to load workspace dashboard.** Confirm the session is still valid, retry the page, and avoid using a partial or blank view for capacity decisions. ## Expected result The entitlement-source rows reconcile to the total limit, owned workspace bytes reconcile to the used value, and shared memberships remain outside the caller's storage calculation. Opening a row activates the workspace whose name and owner you checked. ## Related guides - [Workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Invite team members](/workspaces/invite-team)

title: Preview workspace deletion impact
summary: Review exact workspace deletion counts and blockers before requesting the 15-minute email code, while avoiding an irreversible removal by mistake.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/components/delete-workspace-dialog.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/delete-preview.ts, delete-request.ts, index.ts, workspace-operations/service.ts, and deletion tests. Nothing was deleted in production.
body: The deletion preview is the non-destructive first step of Dosya's three-step workspace deletion gate. It counts the data at risk and names blockers before any confirmation code is sent. Only the workspace owner can open this flow. An Admin or custom role cannot delete a workspace, even with settings permissions. Previewing and cancelling change nothing. ## What the preview counts - **Files permanently deleted** includes live files and files still in Trash. - **Storage freed** is the byte total for those files, formatted into a readable unit. - **Folders removed** includes the workspace folder tree that the deletion cascade removes. - **Team members losing access** counts other members, excluding the owner who opened the dialog. - Share links, file requests, comments and version history tied to the workspace are removed too. Deletion is blocked when another member remains or when this is the owner's last workspace. The preview reports **has_members** as a message to remove members or transfer ownership, and **last_workspace** as a requirement to create another workspace first. ## Steps 1. Switch to the exact workspace you intend to assess, then open **Settings → Danger zone**. 2. Select **Delete** beside **Delete workspace**. Do not use **Leave workspace** or **Transfer ownership** as substitutes; they have different effects. 3. Wait for **Counting what would be deleted…** to finish. If the preview fails, use the displayed error and reload it rather than proceeding from memory. 4. Compare the workspace name, file count, byte total, folder count and other-member count with your own inventory. Trash is included in these totals. 5. Read each red blocker. **Continue** stays disabled until the preview loads and the blocker list is empty. 6. Select **Cancel** when this is only an impact review. No email code is created and the workspace remains available. 7. If deletion is intended, first export or copy everything that must survive and verify the destination bytes. Remove other members, and create another owned workspace when this is the last one. ## If you continue past preview 1. **Continue** requests a six-digit code at the owner's account email. The message names the workspace and repeats file, size and member figures. 2. **Code lifetime and resend limits:** the code expires after 15 minutes. A new request has a 60-second cooldown, is limited to five deletion-code requests per hour, and invalidates any older unconsumed code. 3. Entering the six digits advances to the name check. The server still validates the code only when **Delete forever** is submitted. 4. Type the workspace name exactly. A name mismatch is refused with **The workspace name you typed does not match.** and does not spend a code attempt. 5. **Attempt limit:** each six-digit submission spends an attempt before comparison. The fifth attempt burns the token and is refused even if that fifth value is correct; request a new code afterward. 6. **Delete forever** begins logical removal. The workspace becomes unavailable immediately. Object cleanup can continue in the background, in which case the UI reports **Workspace deletion started**. The action is irreversible. Files, folders, Trash, versions, shares, file requests, comments and memberships have no restore path for the owner or dosya.dev support. Audit evidence is retained separately for forensic integrity. ## Recovery from blockers and errors **This workspace still has other members.** Remove each non-owner member, or transfer ownership and let the new owner decide. The server rechecks this condition immediately before deletion. **This is your only workspace. Create another one first.** Create a separate owned workspace; membership in somebody else's workspace does not satisfy the owner requirement. **A code was just sent. Check your inbox, or wait a minute to request another.** Use the newest message or wait 60 seconds. Repeatedly requesting codes invalidates previous values. **Your confirmation code has expired. Request a new one.** Return to the verification step and issue another code after the cooldown. **Workspace ownership or membership changed. Review the workspace and try again.** The atomic deletion gate caught a race. Close the dialog, reload the preview and reconcile its counts again. **Failed to delete workspace. Please try again.** The deletion batch did not complete. Reload the account: a retry returns the existing pending or complete receipt instead of starting a second deletion. ## Expected result For a preview-only review, closing the dialog leaves the workspace and every counted resource intact. If the owner completes all gates, the workspace disappears from access, its data cannot be restored, and background cleanup may finish after the accepted request. ## Related guides - [Workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Invite team members](/workspaces/invite-team)

title: Restricting a workspace member to one folder
summary: Limit a member to a selected folder and its contents across the web app, desktop sync, WebDAV and the S3 gateway.
verification: Reviewed the current Team folder-access dialog and server-side folder-anchor behavior against the local current web app, API and coverage tests on 2026-10-12. Screenshot data is isolated; no production member was confined.
body: A folder restriction confines a member to one selected folder and everything below it. Use it for a client, contractor or project team that should work in one branch of the workspace without seeing the rest of the file tree. This setting applies alongside the member's role. The role controls allowed actions; the folder restriction controls the visible scope. ## Before you start - Select the correct workspace and open **Team**. - You need **Manage roles**. - The target must be another non-owner member. You cannot restrict yourself or the workspace owner. - Create and organize the destination folder first. The folder must belong to the same workspace and must not be in Trash. - Review the member's role before limiting the folder. A folder restriction does not add upload, download, sharing or delete permissions. - Tell the member before applying the change because pages outside the restricted scope become unavailable. ## Steps: limit a member to a folder 1. Open **Team** and find the member under **Members**. 2. Move to the controls at the right side of their row and select the folder button whose tooltip is **Set folder access**. 3. In **Folder access**, select **Choose folder…**. 4. Browse the workspace tree, choose the top-level folder the member should see and confirm the selection. 5. Read **What this changes for them**. Confirm that the selected scope matches the intended project. 6. Select **Save**. 7. Check the member's role column. The selected folder name appears below the role instead of **Whole workspace**. 8. Ask the member to refresh or reconnect their client and confirm that they can reach the intended files. ## What changes for the member After the restriction is saved, the member sees the selected folder and its descendants across the web app, desktop sync, WebDAV and the S3 gateway. Their dashboard, search results and shared-link views are scoped to that tree. Workspace settings, the Team page and the full activity log remain unavailable to a folder-restricted member. This prevents control-plane or audit data outside the folder from becoming another view into the workspace. ## Steps: change or clear the restriction 1. Return to **Team** and open **Folder access** for the same member. 2. To move the boundary, clear the current folder, choose another folder and save. 3. To restore workspace-wide visibility, select **Clear**, leave the folder empty and select **Save**. 4. Confirm that the member row now shows the new folder name or **Whole workspace**. 5. Ask the member to refresh or reconnect before testing the new scope. ## Expected result The member can open the selected folder and its descendants, subject to their role. Items elsewhere in the workspace do not appear in their supported web, desktop and protocol views. The Team row records the boundary, and the workspace activity log records a folder-access change for later review. ## Limits and behavior - One member can have one root folder restriction. Selecting a folder includes its descendants. - The workspace owner cannot be restricted. - You cannot restrict yourself because doing so could remove the access needed to reverse the change. - The selected folder must be live and belong to the same workspace. - A folder restriction does not copy or move files. - It does not grant actions missing from the member's role. - Moving, deleting or reorganizing the selected folder can affect what the member can reach. Review the member after structural changes. - Existing API keys and integrations remain subject to their own credentials and conditions; verify the intended identity and scope rather than assuming a member setting changes every unrelated credential. ## Troubleshooting **The folder button is missing.** You lack **Manage roles**, the row is your own, or the target is the owner. **The folder cannot be selected.** Confirm it belongs to the active workspace and is not in Trash. Restore or recreate the folder before selecting it. **The member sees an empty area.** Confirm the Team row names the expected folder, the folder still contains live items and the member's role includes the required page and file permissions. **The member still sees old results.** Have them refresh the web app and reconnect desktop or protocol clients. Permission and membership caches can take a short time to settle across active connections. **The member cannot open Team, Settings or Activity.** That is expected for folder-confined members. A workspace-wide administrator should perform those tasks. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I select several unrelated folders? No. Choose one common parent folder, or restructure the workspace so the required folders sit beneath one controlled root. ### Can the restricted member create subfolders? Only if their role grants the relevant folder and upload permissions. Any created items remain within the restricted tree. ### Does clearing the restriction change the member's role? No. It restores workspace-wide scope while leaving the assigned role unchanged. ## Related guides - [Choosing built-in and custom workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Reading workspace activity and audit details](/workspaces/activity) - [Organizing files with folders and groups](/files/organize-files)

title: Correct a workspace invitation sent to the wrong email
summary: Revoke the incorrect pending invitation, verify its old link is unusable and create a new invitation with the intended address, role and folder access.
verification: Reviewed the current web Team page, pending-invite controls, invite revocation API, invitation creation flow and permission checks against local product source and relevant tests on 2026-10-14. The current UI does not edit a pending recipient address in place. Screenshots use isolated workspace data.
body: A pending Dosya invitation cannot have its recipient address edited in place. If it was sent to the wrong email, revoke that invitation first, then create a replacement for the verified address. This prevents both addresses from holding valid access links. ## Before you start - Confirm the active workspace at the top of the sidebar. - Obtain the intended address through a trusted conversation with the recipient. - Record the role and any folder boundary the person should receive. - Treat copied invitation URLs as access credentials until they expire, are accepted or are revoked. ## Steps: revoke the incorrect invitation 1. Open **Team** in the intended workspace. 2. Under **Pending invites**, locate the incorrect email. Compare the inviter, role and expiry so you do not revoke a similarly named invitation. 3. Select **Revoke** on that row. 4. In **Revoke invite**, read the displayed address and confirm the action. 5. Wait for **Invite revoked** and confirm the row disappears from Pending invites. 6. If the old link was copied or sent elsewhere, open it in a private window. It must no longer allow the invitation to be accepted. ## Create the corrected invitation 1. Select **Invite to workspace**. 2. Enter the verified email address exactly. 3. Choose the intended role and any folder boundary. 4. Send the invitation and confirm that one new row appears for the correct address. 5. Ask the recipient to confirm the workspace name and role before accepting. ## Expected result The incorrect invitation is revoked and its old URL cannot be accepted. Pending invites contains one replacement for the intended address with the correct role and access boundary. ## Limits and important details - Revoking an invitation does not remove an account that already accepted it. Review **Members** separately. - A custom role can invite or revoke only when it has the `invite_members` permission. - If the incorrect address belongs to an existing Dosya user, that user can receive an in-product revocation notice. - Invitation expiry does not correct the address; revoke promptly when the wrong person could access the mailbox. ## Troubleshooting **The incorrect address is already a member.** Review the member row, folder access and activity, then follow the member-removal workflow if access was unintended. **Revoke is unavailable or rejected.** Confirm the workspace and your invitation permission. Ask an owner or authorized admin to revoke it. **The corrected invite also looks wrong.** Revoke it before acceptance and verify the address outside Dosya. ## Related guides - [Review pending invitations](/workspaces/workspace-pending-invites) - [Create and control invitation links](/workspaces/invite-links) - [Set member folder access](/workspaces/folder-access)

title: Test a workspace invitation link policy
summary: Test an invite link in a private session, confirm its assigned role, expiry and use ceiling, then revoke the disposable link after validation.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/invite-link.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/join/[token].ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/team.int.test.ts. Production invitation links were not used.
body: An invite link is a bearer credential: an eligible nonmember other than its creator can join with the stored role until expiry, use, revocation, or workspace member limits stop acceptance. Current members receive `already_member`, and a former creator cannot redeem their own URL. ## Before you start - The tester needs **Invite members** and may create links only for roles within their own permission ceiling. - Choose a disposable account that is not already a workspace member and did not create the link. - The web choices are Unlimited, 1, 5, 10, 25, or 100 uses and Never, 1, 7, 30, or 90 days. ## Steps 1. Open **Team → Invite to workspace → Invite link** in the correct workspace. 2. Choose **Role for new members**, **Max uses**, and **Expires**, then select **Create link**. 3. Under **Invite links**, verify the displayed role, use count, and expiry before copying the URL. 4. Open the URL in a private browser session, sign in as the disposable account, and confirm the workspace and role shown before joining. 5. Accept once, return to **Team**, and verify the new member row plus the incremented use count. 6. Remove the disposable member if appropriate, then select **Revoke** on the tested invite link; the same URL must not be reused. ## Limits and security behavior The API accepts a whole-number `max_uses` from 1 through 10,000 or null for unlimited, and `expires_in_days` from 1 through 3,650 or null for no expiry. The interface intentionally offers a smaller preset list. The assigned role cannot be Owner and cannot grant permissions the creator lacks. Removing a joined tester does not automatically revoke the link. Revocation is irreversible for that URL, creates an activity event, and does not remove people who already joined. ## Expected result The private session shows the intended workspace and role, one successful acceptance increments usage, and the revoked disposable URL no longer admits another account. ## Troubleshooting **You don’t have invite permission.** The current role lacks **Invite members**. **You don’t have permission to invite this role.** Choose a role whose permission set is contained in your own. **The link refuses acceptance.** It may be expired, revoked, at its use ceiling, or blocked by the workspace member limit; inspect the active link row before creating another. **The signed-in account cannot be used for the test.** A current member receives `already_member`; a former creator receives **You created this invite link. Ask another member to invite you.** Use a separate nonmember account. ## Related guides - [Review pending invitations](/workspaces/workspace-pending-invites) - [Use invitation links](/workspaces/invite-links)

title: Using workspace invitation links safely
summary: Create a reusable workspace invite link with the right role, expiry and use limit, then monitor or revoke it from Team.
verification: Reviewed the current Team invite-link creation and management surfaces against the local current web app and API on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated representative workspace data. Link acceptance, email-domain enforcement and production delivery were verified from current source and automated tests, not a production invitation.
body: Use a workspace invitation link when several people should join with the same role and you do not need to bind each invitation to one email address. Anyone who has the URL can attempt to use it, so set a short expiry and a realistic use limit before sharing it. For one named person, an email invitation is usually easier to control. See [Inviting people to a workspace](/workspaces/invite-team) for the email-bound workflow. ## Before you start - Select the intended workspace and open **Team**. Confirm the workspace name below the page title. - You need **Invite members** permission. If **Invite to workspace** is missing, ask an owner or a member whose role carries that permission. - Decide which role every person using the link should receive. **Owner** is never available because ownership uses a separate transfer action. - Decide how many successful joins you expect and how long the link should remain useful. - Treat the URL like an access credential. Send it through a private channel and avoid placing it in tickets, public documents or screenshots. ## Steps: create an invitation link 1. In the web app, select **Team** in the workspace navigation. 2. Select **Invite to workspace** near the upper-right corner. 3. Select the **Invite link** tab. 4. Under **Role for new members**, choose the built-in or custom role that new members should receive. The selector only shows roles you are allowed to grant. 5. Under **Max uses**, choose the smallest number that covers the planned recipients. **Unlimited** removes this safeguard. 6. Under **Expires**, choose how long the URL should work. The initial selection is seven days. **Never** creates a link without a time limit. 7. Select **Create invite link**. 8. Copy the generated URL from **Share this link** and send it only to the intended people. ## Steps: monitor or revoke a link 1. Return to **Team** and scroll to **Invite links**. 2. Check the role, the number of uses and the expiry shown under the URL. 3. Use the copy control when you need to send the existing URL again. Creating another link gives you a separate URL with separate limits. 4. Select **Revoke** when the link was sent to the wrong place, enough people have joined, or the role is no longer appropriate. 5. Review **Members** after each expected recipient joins. The member row shows the role they received. ## Expected result The new URL appears under **Invite links** with its role, use count and expiry. An eligible person who opens it, signs in and accepts becomes a workspace member with the selected role. The use count increases after a successful join. Revoking the link stops future joins through that URL. It does not remove people who already joined. ## Limits and security behavior - The link is not tied to a recipient's email address and can be forwarded. - The current web form offers preset use counts and expiry periods. The API rejects non-positive, fractional or excessively large limits. - Workspace membership caps and allowed email-domain policies still apply when someone joins. - A creator cannot use their own link to create a second membership. - A person who is already a workspace member does not gain another seat through the same link. - You cannot create an invitation for a role that grants permissions you do not hold. - Revocation affects the link, not existing members. Change a member's role or remove the member separately. ## Troubleshooting **Invite to workspace is missing.** Your role does not currently carry **Invite members**, or Team access is unavailable. Ask the workspace owner to review your role. **The role I need is not listed.** You cannot grant **Owner** or a role with permissions beyond your own. An owner can create or review a suitable custom role. **A recipient sees that the link is expired, revoked or fully used.** Review the row under **Invite links**. Create a new link with deliberate limits if the person should still join; do not increase access by choosing a stronger role as a workaround. **A recipient is eligible but still cannot join.** Check the workspace member limit, the allowed email-domain policy and whether the person is already a member. Ask them to copy the exact error message without sharing the live invitation URL. **The link was posted publicly.** Revoke it immediately. Review **Members** and the workspace activity log for unexpected joins, then remove or adjust any account that should not have access. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I edit an invitation link after creating it? No edit control is shown. Revoke the old link and create a new one with the required role and limits. ### Does changing the role later change people who already joined? No. The link's role applies when a person joins. Change an existing member's role from their row on **Team**. ### Should I choose Never and Unlimited for a standing team link? Only when you have an intentional process for protecting and reviewing that URL. A short expiry and bounded use count reduce the impact of accidental forwarding. ## Related guides - [Inviting people to a workspace](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Choosing built-in and custom workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Removing a member, leaving or deleting a workspace](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Resend a pending workspace invitation
summary: Resend one active seven-day invitation without changing its token, role or expiry, observe the five-minute cooldown, and verify the pending row.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/invites/[id]/resend.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/team.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/team.int.test.ts. No production email was sent.
body: Resending uses the same email-bound invitation and remaining expiry. It sends another message but does not create a second pending row, extend seven-day validity, or alter the assigned role. ## Before you start - Your role needs **Invite members**, and outbound email must be configured. - Confirm the exact recipient, inviter, role, and remaining expiry under **Pending invites**. - Ask the recipient to check spam, quarantine, and filtering before another send. ## Steps 1. Open **Team** and locate the exact email address under **Pending invites**. 2. Read the role and **expires in** value; an accepted, revoked, or expired invitation cannot be resent. 3. Select **Resend** once on that row rather than creating another invitation. 4. Wait for **Invite resent — The invitation email was sent to _address_ again.** 5. Confirm the page still contains one pending row with the original role and expiry. 6. Ask the recipient to use the newest message and sign in with the same email address before accepting. ## Delivery and timing A five-minute cooldown begins with the original send and every successful resend. A premature retry returns **This invite was just re-sent. Try again in … minute(s).** The server updates `last_sent_at` only after email delivery succeeds. The resend keeps the same URL and expiry date. **Copy link** exposes that bearer URL and should be used only through a trusted direct channel. ## Expected result Dosya reports **Invite resent**, one pending record remains, and the recipient can open the unchanged email-bound invitation before its original expiry. ## Troubleshooting **This invite has expired. Send a new one.** Create a replacement after rechecking the address and role. **The email could not be sent. Try again later.** Delivery failed and the cooldown timestamp was not advanced; wait before one controlled retry. **The recipient sees an email mismatch.** They must sign in with the exact invited address; resending does not retarget the invitation. ## Related guides - [Review pending invitations](/workspaces/workspace-pending-invites) - [Correct an invitation sent to the wrong email](/workspaces/workspace-invite-correct-email) - [Create and control invitation links](/workspaces/invite-links)

title: Review every pending workspace invitation
summary: Audit every pending workspace invitation, identify unexpected access, and revoke or replace email-bound links before a recipient can accept them.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against the Team roster UI, invitation listing and acceptance routes, revoke notifications, permission gates, and invitation lifecycle tests. No production invite link was opened.
body: A periodic invitation audit finds access that has not become a membership yet. Treat each active link as a pending credential: it can add the addressed person with the preselected role until the seven-day deadline or an administrator revokes it. ## Prepare the audit Use an account with **Access Team** and **View team members** to open **Team**. To cancel or reissue access yourself, the same account must hold **Invite members**. Confirm the workspace badge before recording results, especially when your account belongs to several workspaces. Gather the approved recipient, intended role, request owner, and required access period from your staffing or vendor record. The product shows the sender and remaining lifetime, but it cannot decide whether the business request is still valid. An email invitation is identity-bound. During acceptance, Dosya compares the signed-in email with the invited address. A mismatch returns **This invite was sent to _invited address_. You're logged in as _current address_. Please log in with the correct account.** ## Steps 1. Record the **Pending invites · N** count so additions or removals during the review are visible. 2. Match every **Pending invites** recipient email to a currently approved person. 3. Compare **Invited by** with the expected requester. Investigate **Unknown** or an unfamiliar sender before leaving the link active. 4. Inspect the role badge at permission level. For a custom role, open its read-only permission view and check page, file, sharing, team, and protocol grants. 5. Read the **expires in** value. Leave a soon-to-expire row active only if the person still needs to join. 6. Revoke any wrong address, excessive role, departed contractor, duplicate business request, or unexplained invitation. 7. Refresh **Team** and reconcile the new pending count with your approved list. ## Correct a finding Select **Revoke** and confirm the dialog when any immutable field is wrong. Revocation is immediate and irreversible; the old URL cannot be reactivated. Create a new email invitation for the correct address or role after the unwanted record leaves the active list. Use **Resend** only for a valid request whose recipient missed the message. This operation cannot extend the deadline and is rate-limited to once per invite every five minutes. **Copy link** is useful for controlled manual delivery, but it exposes the same live bearer URL, so send it only to the approved recipient. An active duplicate cannot be created for the same email in the same workspace. Dosya reports **An invite is already pending for this email**. If the person already joined, the create endpoint instead answers **This person is already a member**; review their member role rather than issuing another invite. After revocation, an invited address that maps to an existing account gets an in-app cancellation notice. A non-user is not sent a separate withdrawal message. Record your organizational approval and evidence outside Dosya if your access-review policy requires it; the Team page supplies the current product state, not a compliance attestation. ## Expected result The refreshed pending count equals the approved invitation inventory, every live row has an authorized recipient and least-privilege role, and all rejected URLs fail immediately after revocation. ## Related guides - [Review pending invitations](/workspaces/workspace-pending-invites) - [Use invitation links](/workspaces/invite-links)

title: Revoke a stale workspace invitation
summary: Revoke a pending email invitation, confirm its bearer URL returns a revoked response, and understand which notifications and memberships remain unchanged.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/invites/[id]/revoke.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/invite/[token].ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/team.int.test.ts. No production invitation was revoked.
body: Revocation marks a pending email invitation unusable immediately. It does not remove an accepted member; use the member-removal workflow when the person already joined. ## Before you start - The acting role needs **Invite members** in the invitation’s workspace. - Save the old URL only when a controlled post-revocation test is necessary. Treat it as a credential until the action succeeds. - Confirm the intended person has not already accepted. ## Steps 1. Open **Team** in the workspace named on the invitation. 2. Under **Pending invites**, match the recipient email, role, inviter, and remaining expiry. 3. Select **Revoke** on that row and reread the address in the **Revoke invite** dialog. 4. Confirm **Revoke** and wait for **Invite revoked — The invitation is no longer valid.** 5. Verify the row disappears from **Pending invites** after the page reloads its team data. 6. Open the saved URL in a private session and confirm it returns **This invite has been revoked** rather than a join screen. ## Effects and reversibility The API stores a revocation timestamp and later invite lookups return HTTP 410. An existing Dosya account at the invited email receives an in-app revocation notice; an address without an account receives no additional email. Revoking cannot restore the same invitation. A later invitation to the address receives a fresh identifier, token, role, and seven-day expiry. Accepted membership is unaffected. ## Expected result The stale row is absent, its old URL is rejected as revoked, and no already accepted member loses workspace access as a side effect. ## Troubleshooting **Already revoked.** Reload Team; another administrator completed the action. **Invite not found.** The record was replaced, removed, or belongs to another workspace. **The person still appears under Members.** The invite was accepted earlier; use the member removal control after reviewing their live shares and file requests. ## Related guides - [Review pending invitations](/workspaces/workspace-pending-invites) - [Use invitation links](/workspaces/invite-links)

title: Add folder access for a workspace member
summary: Limit another workspace member to one live folder, understand the cross-surface scope, and verify the boundary after distributed caches refresh.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/members/[id].ts, packages/test-harness/tests/member-anchor.int.test.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/roles-enforcement.int.test.ts. No production membership was modified.
body: **Limit to a folder** confines a member to that folder and its descendants across the web app, desktop sync, WebDAV, and S3. Their role permissions still decide which actions work inside the subtree. ## Before you start - The administrator needs **Access Team**, **View team members**, and **Manage roles**. - The target cannot be the workspace owner or the acting account. - Choose an existing, untrashed folder in the same workspace; moving or deleting it later can change what the member can reach. ## Steps 1. Open **Team**, find the member by email, and confirm their current role and **Whole workspace** status. 2. Select the folder button whose tooltip is **Set folder access** on that member’s row. 3. In **Folder access**, select **Choose folder…**, navigate the current workspace, and choose the intended live folder. 4. Read **What this changes for them**, then select **Save** and wait for **Folder access updated**. 5. Ask the member to reload; distributed membership caches can take roughly 60 seconds to stop serving the old anchor. 6. From the member session, open one item inside the subtree and attempt one known item outside it across every surface they use. ## Scope and recovery The server rejects a missing or foreign folder with **Folder not found in this workspace**. It also refuses **The workspace owner cannot be confined to a folder** and **You cannot limit your own folder access**. A confined member sees scoped dashboard, search, share, file, WebDAV, S3, and desktop-sync results. Workspace settings, Team, and the full Activity log are unavailable. Selecting **Clear** and saving restores whole-workspace scope; the member cannot clear their own restriction from inside it. ## Expected result The Team row names the selected folder, content inside it follows the member’s role permissions, and known resources outside the subtree are absent or refused on each used surface. ## Troubleshooting **Update failed.** Reload Team and confirm the folder still exists and is not in Trash. **The member still sees an outside item.** Wait about one minute, reload or reconnect that client, and repeat the exact check. **The member lost more access than expected.** Verify both the folder anchor and role; confinement never grants missing file, page, or protocol permissions. ## Related guides - [Invite a team member](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Remove a member](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Choose a workspace role before inviting someone
summary: Choose a built-in or custom role before inviting someone, apply the inviter permission ceiling, and test the smallest access set the job requires.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/role-create.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/invite.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/invite/[token].ts, and apps/api/src/lib/role-rank.ts. No production invitation was created.
body: The role stored on an invitation becomes the new member’s permission map at acceptance. Select by concrete capabilities because a custom role name carries no security meaning by itself. ## Before you start - Your account needs **Invite members** and may offer only roles whose enabled permissions are contained in your own. - **Owner** cannot be assigned by invitation; ownership uses the transfer workflow. - A direct email invite is valid for seven days and is bound to its recipient address. ## Steps 1. List the pages, file actions, team duties, and protocol access the person actually needs. 2. Open **View role permissions** for each candidate and inspect all 36 switches plus any IP, active-hours, or usage restrictions. 3. Prefer the narrowest role that enables the required work; remember that page access and action permissions are separate. 4. Open **Team → Invite to workspace → Email invite** and add the exact recipient address. 5. Choose the reviewed value under **Role**, then select **Send invite**. 6. Confirm **Invites sent**, inspect the exact role on the new **Pending invites** row, and verify the accepted member’s role in **Team**. ## Role boundaries Built-in **Viewer** is read-oriented, **Member** handles ordinary file work, and **Admin** manages members and workspace content; verify actual permissions instead of relying on these summaries. Custom roles can combine any registry entries, subject to the creator’s grant ceiling. The recipient cannot change the offered role while accepting. The invite landing GET labels every custom role **Member**, even though acceptance POST applies the stored custom role ID. Treat **Pending invites** before acceptance and the **Team** member row afterward as the authoritative role checks. If the pending row is wrong, revoke it and issue a new invite; resending retains the original role. ## Expected result The pending and accepted Team rows display the intended role, its permissions fit the inviter’s ceiling, and the member can work without unrelated administrative access. ## Troubleshooting **You don’t have permission to invite this role.** Select a role fully contained in your permission map or ask a broader administrator. **Invalid role.** Reload Team; the custom role may have been deleted or belong to another workspace. **An invite is already pending for this email.** Review and either resend or revoke that row rather than creating a duplicate. **The acceptance page says Member for a custom role.** This is a display limitation in the public invite GET. Complete acceptance only after checking **Pending invites**, then confirm the stored role in **Team**. ## Related guides - [Invite a team member](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Remove a member](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Removing a member, leaving or deleting a workspace
summary: Choose the correct workspace departure action, remove another member, leave as a member, transfer ownership or complete the protected deletion flow.
verification: Reviewed the current Team member-removal dialog, Workspace settings danger zone and protected workspace-deletion component against the local current web app and API on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated data; destructive actions were not submitted against production.
body: Use the action that matches who should leave and whether the workspace itself should continue. Removing a member keeps the workspace. Leaving removes your own access. Deleting the workspace permanently removes its files and related data after a protected confirmation flow. If you own the workspace and only want to leave, transfer ownership to another member first. ## Before you start - Select the correct workspace and confirm its name. - Review active uploads, integrations, shared links and file requests owned or operated by the departing person. - Decide whether another member needs a different role, ownership or folder access before the departure. - Export or move anything that must remain available before workspace deletion. - Use the activity log to record the current context when the change is part of an access review. ## Steps: remove another member 1. Open **Team** and locate the person under **Members**. 2. Confirm their email address, role and folder scope. 3. Select the remove control at the right side of the row. 4. In **Remove member**, check the person's name and the immediate-loss warning. 5. Select **Remove**. 6. Confirm that the person no longer appears under **Members**. 7. Review related integrations, API keys, pending file requests or ownership responsibilities that may need separate cleanup. You need **Manage roles** to remove another non-owner member. The owner cannot be removed from Team. ## Steps: leave a workspace 1. Open **Settings** for the workspace. 2. In the settings navigation, select **Danger zone**. 3. Find **Leave workspace** and select **Leave**. 4. Read the confirmation that access to all workspace files will be lost immediately. 5. Select **Leave** again to confirm. An owner must transfer ownership before leaving. If the workspace should be retired instead, follow the deletion workflow only after reviewing its permanent effect. ## Steps: transfer ownership 1. Open **Settings → Danger zone** as the current owner. 2. Select **Transfer** beside **Transfer ownership**. 3. Choose an existing non-owner member. 4. Confirm the transfer. 5. Reload settings and verify that the selected person is the owner and your account is now a regular member. 6. Leave the workspace only after the ownership change is confirmed. ## Steps: delete a workspace 1. Open **Settings → Danger zone** as the owner. 2. Select **Delete** beside **Delete workspace**. 3. Review the deletion preview. It lists the workspace name and counts of files, storage, folders and members affected. 4. Resolve every blocker. A workspace with other members must have them removed or ownership handled, and an account must retain at least one workspace. 5. Continue to request the six-digit email code. 6. Enter the code sent to the owner's email. The code expires after 15 minutes. 7. Retype the workspace name exactly. 8. Submit the final deletion action and wait for completion or the pending-cleanup confirmation. ## Expected result After member removal or leaving, the departing account can no longer open the workspace. The workspace and remaining members continue to exist. After ownership transfer, the selected member becomes owner and the previous owner remains with a regular member role until they leave or are removed. After accepted deletion, the workspace becomes unavailable and its physical cleanup may continue in the background. Files, folders, members, share links, file requests, comments and version history belonging to it are permanently removed. ## Limits and irreversible effects - Removing a member does not delete the workspace. - A workspace owner cannot be removed or demoted through the Team member controls. - An owner must transfer ownership before leaving. - Workspace deletion is permanent and support cannot restore the deleted files. - A workspace with other members blocks deletion until they are removed or ownership is transferred as appropriate. - An account cannot delete its only workspace; create another workspace first. - The deletion code is sent to the owner and expires after 15 minutes. - The exact workspace name is case-sensitive in the final confirmation. - Revoking an invitation is different from removing an accepted member. ## Troubleshooting **The remove control is missing.** Your role lacks **Manage roles**, the row is your own, or the target is the owner. **I am the owner and cannot leave.** Transfer ownership to another current member first. If no suitable member exists and the data should be destroyed, review the deletion requirements. **Delete is blocked because members remain.** Return to Team and remove the other members, or transfer ownership if another person should retain the workspace. **Delete is blocked because this is my only workspace.** Create another workspace first. An account must always have at least one workspace. **The deletion email did not arrive.** Confirm the owner's account email, check filtered mail and request a fresh code after the current attempt. Never ask another person to share their code in a public channel. **The final name does not match.** Copy the workspace name from the deletion preview and enter it exactly, including capitalization and spacing. ## Frequently asked questions ### Does removing a member delete files they uploaded? Member removal is an access action, not a workspace deletion action. Review ownership and retention needs for their files and integrations before removing them. ### Can I undo leaving a workspace? There is no self-service undo. A member with invitation permission must invite you again, subject to the workspace's policies and limits. ### Can support restore a deleted workspace? No. The deletion flow states that the files are not recoverable by the user or Dosya support. ## Related guides - [Reading workspace activity and audit details](/workspaces/activity) - [Choosing built-in and custom workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Inviting people to a workspace](/workspaces/invite-team)

title: Verify a newly accepted workspace member
summary: Confirm an invitation became a live workspace membership, verify the assigned role and folder scope, and test access from the recipient’s own session.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/invite/[token].ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/team.ts, apps/api/src/lib/notifications/catalog.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/team.int.test.ts. No production account joined a workspace.
body: Acceptance succeeds only for the signed-in account whose email matches the invitation. The server creates the membership and marks the invite accepted together, then redirects to the dashboard. ## Before you start - Ask the recipient for the account email they used, without requesting credentials. - Keep the expected workspace, role, and any intended folder boundary written down. - The Team viewer needs **Access Team** and **View team members**. ## Steps 1. Open **Team** in the invited workspace and note the current **Members** and **Pending invites** counts. 2. Ask the recipient to open the invite while signed in with the exact invited email and select the acceptance control. 3. Reload Team and verify the email disappeared from **Pending invites**. 4. Find the person under **Members** and confirm their name, email, role, and **Whole workspace** or folder label. 5. Open the member profile and review **Joined** plus **Last active**; **No activity yet** is valid before their first recorded action. 6. In the recipient’s session, test one intended action and one excluded action after reloading the client. ## What acceptance changes A valid acceptance inserts one membership, marks the invitation accepted, records `member_joined`, and redirects to `/dashboard`. Owners and admins receive a join notice naming the person, workspace, role, and permission summary. A domain policy or workspace member ceiling can refuse the join without consuming the invitation. If the person was already a member, Dosya marks the invite accepted and redirects without creating a duplicate membership. ## Expected result Team shows one live member with the expected role and scope, the pending row is gone, and the recipient’s allowed and denied checks match that effective configuration. ## Troubleshooting **This invite was sent to … You’re logged in as ….** Sign out and use the addressed account; the invite cannot be reassigned. **This invite has expired, been revoked, or already been accepted.** Ask an inviter to review Team before issuing anything new. **The row appears but access is stale.** Wait roughly 60 seconds, reload, and retest before changing the role. ## Related guides - [Invite a team member](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Remove a member](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Verify access removal for a former member
summary: Verify a former member lost workspace access, review the live links that remain, and understand the irreversible membership and request cleanup effects.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/members/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload-request/departure.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/team.int.test.ts. No production member was removed.
body: Removing a member deletes the membership and invalidates its cache, but share links they created remain live. Favourites, groups, and open file requests enter separate best-effort cleanup passes. ## Before you start - The actor needs **Manage roles** to remove someone else. A member can remove themselves. - The current owner cannot be removed until ownership is transferred. - Record critical share links and file requests first; the membership deletion is not an undoable toggle. ## Steps 1. Open **Team**, match the target by name and email, and verify the row is not the workspace owner. 2. Review that member’s live share links and open file requests before choosing the removal control. 3. Select the destructive remove button and reread the name in the **Remove member** dialog. 4. Confirm **Remove** and wait for **Member removed — They no longer have access to this workspace.** 5. Reload Team and verify the person is absent from **Members** while relevant administrators receive the removal activity or notice. 6. From the former member’s session, confirm the workspace is unavailable; then verify the creator’s file requests are revoked and manually close any residual request or share URL. ## Permanent and surviving effects The membership row is deleted immediately and cannot be restored; returning requires a new invitation or link acceptance. Favourites, folder groups, and creator-owned file requests are swept after deletion. Those cleanup errors are swallowed because access removal is already final, so an administrator must verify that no request remains open. Existing files stay in the workspace. Share links created by the person remain live and the administrator notice includes their count, so removal alone is not a link-revocation strategy. ## Expected result The former person is absent from Team and cannot reopen the workspace. Every remaining file request is checked and revoked, while intentionally retained share links are documented. ## Troubleshooting **Cannot remove the workspace owner. Transfer ownership first.** Complete the ownership transfer before retrying. **You don’t have permission to remove members.** Ask someone holding **Manage roles**. **A public URL still opens.** Membership removal deliberately preserves share links; revoke the specific link from Shared if continued access is unwanted. **A former member’s file request still accepts uploads.** The post-removal request sweep is best-effort. Open **File requests**, identify records created by that account, and revoke each residual URL. ## Related guides - [Invite a team member](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Remove a member](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Review access after changing a member role
summary: Review a member’s effective access after a role change, account for the permission cache window, and confirm both retained and removed capabilities.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/team/members/[id].ts, apps/api/src/lib/team/role-copy.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/roles-enforcement.int.test.ts. Production roles were not changed.
body: A successful role change updates the membership immediately, preserves its folder anchor, and sends the affected person a notice describing the previous role, new role, and lost permissions. ## Before you start - Obtain the expected old role, new role, and list of gained or lost permissions. - Use a controlled member session; do not infer access solely from navigation visibility. - Allow roughly 60 seconds for distributed permission and membership caches. ## Steps 1. Open **Team** and confirm the member row displays the intended new role. 2. Check the line beneath the role for **Whole workspace** or the existing folder name; a role-only update must not clear it. 3. Ask the member to open the role-change notification and compare its old role, new role, and lost-access summary with the planned change. 4. Wait up to one minute, then reload all open Dosya tabs or reconnect the protocol client being tested. 5. Perform one action newly allowed or deliberately retained, using a disposable file or link where an operation has side effects. 6. Attempt one permission that should now be withheld and record the absent control or exact refusal rather than retrying destructively. ## Interpreting the outcome Role names do not prove a capability. The API reads the actual permission map, while IP ranges, active hours, usage limits, and folder confinement can apply additional restrictions. Page permissions also gate entry separately from action permissions. Another authorized manager can reverse the role later, but actions completed while a broader role was active are not automatically undone. ## Expected result The Team row, notification, and member-session checks agree: intended work succeeds, removed work is unavailable, and the previous folder boundary remains effective. ## Troubleshooting **A permitted action is still refused.** Check the page gate, folder anchor, role conditions, and usage limits before editing permissions again. **A removed action still succeeds.** Wait for cache convergence, reload or reconnect, and verify the request uses the intended workspace. **The member cannot restore access.** Self-role changes are prohibited; a different manager must assign another eligible role. ## Related guides - [Invite a team member](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Remove a member](/workspaces/member-removal)

title: Review pending workspace invitations
summary: Review active workspace invitations by recipient, inviter, role, and expiry, then resend, copy, or revoke each invitation without creating duplicates.
verification: Reviewed from local sources on 2026-10-14 using the Team UI and listing endpoint, invitation create/resend/revoke/accept handlers, workspace member-limit logic, and invite tests. Production invitations were not queried.
body: The **Pending invites** section is the current action queue for email invitations. It contains only records that remain unaccepted, unrevoked, and unexpired. Use it to deliver a missed link, withdraw incorrect access, or decide when a replacement invitation is necessary. ## What the list contains Open the correct workspace and select **Team**. The **Pending invites · N** heading reports the number of active email invitations. Each row contains: - the normalized recipient email address; - **Invited by** followed by the sender name, or **Unknown** when no name is available; - **expires in** followed by days, hours, or minutes; - the built-in or custom role assigned at creation; - **Copy link**, **Resend**, and **Revoke** actions. The page displays an expiry countdown, not a sent date. Email invitations start with a seven-day lifetime. Once a row expires, the Team API omits it; once accepted, the recipient moves into **Members** instead. Viewing this roster requires **Access Team** plus **View team members**. Sending, resending, and revoking are protected separately by **Invite members**. A visible button does not override the server permission check. ## Steps 1. Confirm the workspace badge near the **Team** heading. 2. Match each **Pending invites** email address to the person who should receive workspace access. 3. Check the role badge against the access that person needs. The role cannot be edited on a pending row. 4. Read **Invited by** and **expires in** to decide whether the access request is still expected. 5. For a correct invitation, leave it pending, use **Copy link**, or select **Resend** after the five-minute resend cooldown. 6.
