For an incorrect address or role, select **Revoke**, review the **Revoke invite** dialog, and confirm **Revoke**. 7. Use **Invite to workspace** only after the previous row has been revoked or has expired. ## Choose the correct action **Copy link** places the same bearer acceptance URL on the clipboard. Anyone can open the URL, but acceptance is bound to the invited email: a signed-in user with another address receives a message naming both accounts and must sign in correctly. **Resend** sends the existing invite again. It keeps the token, email, role, and original expiry. The same invitation cannot be mailed more than once within five minutes. **Revoke** sets a permanent withdrawal time. Its link stops working immediately and reports **This invite has been revoked** if opened later. If the email belongs to an existing Dosya account, that user also receives an in-app notice that the invitation was withdrawn; a person without an account receives no additional withdrawal email. Creating a second active record for the same workspace and email is blocked with **An invite is already pending for this email**. Inviting an address already present in **Members** returns **This person is already a member**. Expired, revoked, or previously accepted rows can be replaced with a newly issued token after the person is no longer a member. A pending row is not a reserved seat. Free-plan workspaces allow five added members, excluding the owner, and the acceptance write checks that cap atomically. Review unnecessary invitations, but upgrading or removing a member is required if an approved recipient reaches **Free plan workspaces can have at most 5 members. Upgrade to add more.** ## Expected result Every remaining pending row has a valid recipient and suitable role, its deadline is understood, and any unwanted link has been revoked before acceptance. Correct invitations remain singular rather than duplicated. ## Related guides - [Workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Invite team members](/workspaces/invite-team)

title: Setting workspace limits and sharing policies
summary: Configure upload, storage, sharing and access rules for a workspace, then understand how they combine with plan and role limits.
verification: Reviewed the current Hard limits and Security settings against the local current web app and API on 2026-10-12. Screenshots use isolated representative settings; cross-client enforcement claims were checked against current server gates and tests.
body: Workspace policies let an authorized administrator set a stricter operating boundary than the account plan. Use **Hard limits** for file size, storage and upload controls, and **Security** for sharing, sessions and access lists. ## Before you start - Select the intended workspace and open **Settings**. - You need the permission named by the setting. Most security controls require **Manage settings**; hard-limit controls have dedicated permissions. - Record the current values before changing them. - Test restrictive changes with a harmless file and a second test member before relying on them for a team. - A workspace policy can reduce an allowance. It cannot create storage or capabilities beyond the account plan. ## Steps: configure hard limits 1. Open **Settings → Hard limits**. 2. Set **Max upload file size** for the largest single file the workspace should accept. 3. Set **Storage per member** if one member should not consume the entire workspace allocation. Leave the field blank when no member-specific cap is needed. 4. Set **Total workspace storage cap** below or equal to the allocation available to the workspace. 5. Set **Max simultaneous uploads** to control per-member transfer concurrency. 6. Use **Allowed file types** as a comma-separated allowlist, or **Blocked file types** to reject selected extensions. Avoid contradictory lists. 7. Save each changed row and wait for its confirmation. ## Steps: configure sharing and access rules 1. Open **Settings → Security**. 2. Turn on **Disable public share links** when the workspace must prevent new share-link creation. 3. Turn on **Force password on share links** when every newly created link must have a password. 4. Choose **Share link max expiry** to cap link lifetime. **Default share link expiry** only preselects a value that an eligible sharer may change within the cap. 5. Set **Session timeout** and **Download rate limit** when required. 6. Manage IP, country and allowed email-domain lists carefully. A mistaken allowlist can block legitimate members. 7. Save, then perform one allowed and one deliberately denied test with a non-owner test member. ## Expected result Saved values remain visible after reload. New actions that exceed a cap or violate a rule are refused with an explanation. Existing members retain only the access allowed by their role, folder scope, workspace policies and account plan together. ## Limits and interactions - The effective upload limit is the smallest applicable plan, workspace, role, credential and request limit. - Disabling share links prevents creation; manage existing links separately. - Forcing passwords applies to share-link creation and does not turn ordinary storage into Vault encryption. - Allowed email domains affect joining. They do not rewrite existing member email addresses. - IP and country rules can be affected by VPNs, proxies and corporate gateways. - Settings shown by the API but absent from the current UI should not be assumed to be enforced. ## Troubleshooting **A member sees a smaller limit than the plan advertises.** Compare the plan allowance with workspace hard limits, their role conditions and the specific upload or file-request limit. The smallest boundary wins. **Share creation is unavailable.** Check **Disable public share links**, the member's role and folder scope. **A link cannot use the requested expiry.** The workspace maximum expiry clamps longer choices. Choose a shorter duration or have an authorized administrator review the cap. **A legitimate person cannot join.** Review the allowed email-domain list and member cap. Do not weaken unrelated role permissions as a workaround. **A policy locked out a test user.** Revert it from an owner or authorized administrator session. Preserve the exact error and setting name for private support. ## Related guides - [Choosing built-in and custom workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Understanding storage usage and failed quota checks](/uploading/storage-usage) - [Protecting a sharing link with a password](/sharing/password-link)

title: Review file-request controls under workspace policy
summary: Control file-request exposure through role permissions and per-request limits, then verify guest uploads obey the folder, count, size, type and expiry.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/file-requests.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/create.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/file-requests/index.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/file-requests.int.test.ts. No production request was created.
body: Dosya has no workspace-wide “disable file requests” switch. Control this public upload channel through role permissions, destination scope, and limits saved on each request. ## Before you start - Creating a request requires **Upload files** because its URL delegates upload rights to unauthenticated guests. - Listing requests uses **View own shared links** or **View all shared links**; folder confinement also filters visible destinations. - Use a disposable destination outside Vault and any full-lock folder. ## Steps 1. Open the custom role editor and decide which roles may hold **Upload files** and inspect their own or all shared records. 2. Save the least-privilege role, then reload a test member assigned to it. 3. Open **File requests** and create a disposable request aimed at a live folder inside that member’s scope. 4. Set a clear title plus needed expiry, maximum files, maximum file size, extension allowlist, password, and recipient addresses. 5. Open the returned guest URL in a private session and upload one allowed sample plus one sample designed to exceed a chosen limit. 6. Verify only the allowed upload appears in the destination, then revoke the request so its public URL stops accepting files. ## Enforced boundaries A password must contain at least eight characters. Negative expiry or size values and negative or non-integer file counts are refused. Up to 100 valid recipient addresses are processed, and reserved service addresses are rejected rather than silently skipped. A request cannot point at a missing, foreign, hidden, Vault, or full-lock destination. A folder-confined creator is anchored to their subtree. Guest uploads also face workspace extension, file-size, storage, concurrency, and lock gates. ## Expected result The authorized member can create and view only the intended request records, the guest’s valid file lands in the chosen subtree, the invalid sample is refused, and revocation closes the URL. ## Troubleshooting **You don’t have upload permission in this workspace.** Add **Upload files** only if the role should delegate guest uploads. **Destination folder not found** or **folder_locked.** Choose a visible, live destination outside Vault and full locks. **The member sees an empty request list.** They hold neither **View own shared links** nor **View all shared links**, or their folder scope excludes those destinations. ## Related guides - [Set workspace policies](/workspaces/policies) - [Choose roles](/workspaces/roles)

title: Verify a policy change as a regular member
summary: Validate a workspace policy from a regular member session, record the exact refusal or success, and separate role, page, scope and cached-setting effects.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/role-create.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/settings.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/roles-enforcement.int.test.ts. Production settings were not changed.
body: Policy validation should use a non-administrator account because owner access can hide permission failures. Test one controlled operation after the setting or role change has propagated. ## Before you start - Record the member’s role, folder anchor, active workspace, client surface, and the policy being changed. - Use disposable content whose upload, share, rename, or deletion cannot affect another person. - Expect settings and membership caches to remain stale briefly across distributed workers. ## Steps 1. As an authorized administrator, change one policy or permission and wait for its receipt: **Settings updated**, **Role updated**, or **Limit updated — Your hard limit has been saved.** 2. In **Team**, verify the test member’s role and **Whole workspace** or folder label. 3. Wait roughly 60 seconds, then reload the member’s web tab or reconnect the protocol client. 4. Confirm the member is operating in the intended workspace and can reach the page required for the test. 5. Perform exactly one representative action and capture the visible result or exact server error without repeated retries. 6. Compare the result with the configured policy, role permission, folder boundary, and any active-hours, IP, or usage condition. ## Reading a refusal **You don’t have access to …** identifies a page gate. **You don’t have permission …** identifies the capability needed for the operation. A missing resource can reflect folder confinement or hidden content. Quota, extension, password, link-expiry, active-hours, IP, and rate-limit messages come from separate gates. Changing several controls at once makes the result ambiguous. Restore the disposable configuration after the test and remember that completed actions are not undone by tightening policy later. ## Expected result The regular member receives the exact allowed or denied behavior predicted by the one changed rule, and the test record includes workspace, role, scope, client, time, and message. ## Troubleshooting **The result matches the old configuration.** Wait a minute, reload or reconnect, and run one new request. **The navigation item is absent.** Inspect the matching **Access …** permission before the action-level permission. **The web test passes but a protocol fails.** Verify **Use WebDAV**, **Use the S3 gateway**, or **SFTP access**, plus any IP condition the gateway can enforce. ## Related guides - [Set workspace policies](/workspaces/policies) - [Choose roles](/workspaces/roles)

title: Restrict public sharing links in a workspace
summary: Disable new public share links or require passwords, set default and maximum expiry, and verify existing URLs and silently clamped lifetimes correctly.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/share/create.ts, apps/api/src/lib/share/update.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/settings.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/share/create.unit.test.ts. No production share was changed.
body: Workspace security settings govern new and edited share links. Disabling creation does not revoke URLs that already exist, so active links require a separate review and revocation pass. ## Before you start - The administrator needs **Access Settings** and **Manage settings**. - A tester also needs **Create share links** plus access to the selected file or folder. - Prepare a disposable item; revoking its URL is irreversible for that token. ## Steps 1. Open **Workspace settings → Security** in the intended workspace. 2. Enable **Disable public share links** or **Force password on share links**, or select a **Share link max expiry** and **Default share link expiry**. 3. Select the row’s save control and wait for **Settings updated — Your security setting has been saved.** 4. After cache convergence, open the share dialog for the disposable item from a regular member session. 5. Attempt one new link, then inspect the returned URL in a private window for password and effective expiry behavior. 6. Open **Shared** to review older links separately and revoke any that no longer meet policy. ## Rule behavior With creation disabled, the server returns **Share links are disabled for this workspace**. Password enforcement returns **This workspace requires a password on all share links** when no password is supplied. Share passwords require at least eight characters. The expiry cap offers No limit, 1, 7, 30, 90, or 365 days in the UI; server validation accepts a whole number through 3,650 days. A longer requested lifetime is silently reduced to the workspace cap. The default controls the starting value and must not exceed that cap. ## Expected result New-link behavior matches the saved rule, the disposable URL demonstrates the effective password and lifetime, and every older link needing removal is revoked individually. ## Troubleshooting **You don’t have access to workspace settings.** The role lacks **Access Settings**. **You don’t have permission: manage settings.** A role with page access still needs the capability to save security fields. **The link expiry is shorter than selected.** The workspace maximum silently clamps requested lifetimes; inspect the created link rather than trusting the form input. ## Related guides - [Set workspace policies](/workspaces/policies) - [Choose roles](/workspaces/roles)

title: Require expiry for workspace sharing links
summary: Set a maximum lifetime for workspace share links, test how longer or Never choices are clamped, and distinguish the cap from the default expiry.
verification: Verified wording and behavior in apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx, components/share-modal.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/settings.ts, lib/share/expiry.ts, create.ts, update.ts and related tests. Inspection was repository-only and changed no production policy.
body: Dosya enforces required expiry through **Share link max expiry**. Once this field is set to a positive duration, a newly created link cannot be permanent: a longer date or **Never** is silently shortened to the workspace maximum. This cap differs from **Default share link expiry**. The default only preselects a value and the sharer can change it; the maximum is the final server-side ceiling. ## Available controls The Settings UI offers these maximums: **No limit**, **1 day**, **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, and **1 year**. **No limit** clears the workspace ceiling; it does not force links to be permanent, because the share dialog still starts at its default. **Default share link expiry** offers **7 days (standard)**, **1 day**, **7 days**, **30 days**, **90 days**, and **1 year**. With no workspace default, the web share dialog starts at 7 days. A saved default must be a whole number from 1 through 3,650 days and cannot exceed the workspace maximum. The built-in Owner and Admin roles can edit both fields. A custom role needs **Access Settings** and **Manage settings**. The cap applies to file, folder, bundle and email-created share links through the common share service. ## Steps 1. Activate the intended workspace and open **Settings → Security**. 2. Find **Share link max expiry**, whose description reads **Cap how long share links can live.** 3. Choose the longest lifetime the organization's policy permits, then select the adjacent Save control. 4. Set **Default share link expiry** to a value no longer than the cap. Use the default to guide ordinary sharing, not as the enforcement boundary. 5. Open a non-confidential file and create a disposable share. In **Expires in**, deliberately choose **Never** or a date beyond the maximum. 6. Complete the share and inspect its actual expiration in Shared or link analytics. The server should return a timestamp no later than `creation time + maximum days`. 7. Edit that disposable link and attempt another over-cap expiry. An expiry-changing edit is clamped by the same workspace rule while preserving the link token. 8. Select **Revoke** for the test link after recording the result. A revoked link cannot be edited again. ## Timing and existing links The maximum is calculated from the moment a link is created or its expiry is edited. A 7-day cap becomes the current Unix time plus 7 × 86,400 seconds. A dated expiry must also be at least 60 seconds in the future and no more than 3,650 days from now. Saving a new workspace maximum does not retroactively rewrite untouched links. An existing permanent or long-lived link keeps its stored timestamp until someone edits its expiry, revokes it, or it otherwise expires. Audit current links separately when tightening policy. Free-plan creators already have a seven-day fair-use ceiling, even when the workspace field is **No limit**. When both a free-plan rule and workspace maximum apply, the earlier expiration wins. Recipients can use the link only until its final stored expiration, not the overlong value the creator attempted. A silent clamp means a successful create response must be inspected; success alone does not prove the requested date was preserved. ## Troubleshooting **You don't have permission: manage settings.** Obtain both Settings page access and **Manage settings**, or ask an Owner/Admin to apply the cap. **default share expiry cannot be longer than this workspace's share link cap of … days.** Lower the default to the cap or below, or raise the maximum first. **default share expiry days must be a whole number between 1 and 3650, or empty for no default.** Use one of the UI presets or clear the default. The workspace maximum remains independent. **Expiry must be at least a minute in the future.** Pick a later custom date; client and server clock differences can make an almost-immediate timestamp invalid. **Expiry cannot be more than 3650 days from now.** Choose an earlier date. This absolute 10-year ceiling applies even when **Share link max expiry** says **No limit**. **A previously created link still says Never.** The maximum is not retroactive. Edit that link's expiration within policy or revoke and recreate it. ## Expected result Every newly created link in the workspace has an expiration no later than the configured maximum, including attempts to choose **Never**. The default remains a visible starting preference, and older links are handled deliberately rather than assumed to have changed. ## Related guides - [Set workspace policies](/workspaces/policies) - [Choose roles](/workspaces/roles)

title: Set a workspace upload-size policy
summary: Set the maximum size for one uploaded file, understand GiB enforcement across upload methods, and test the boundary without risking production data.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/settings.ts and upload-limits.ts, lib/upload/extension-policy.ts, init-gates.ts, measured-quota.ts, and their limit tests. No production setting or upload was attempted.
body: **Max upload file size** is the workspace-wide ceiling for one file. It applies independently of account storage, the total workspace cap, per-member storage, simultaneous-upload limits and limits attached to an API credential. The value is displayed as GB but enforced in binary bytes: one entered GB equals 1,073,741,824 bytes. A file exactly at the ceiling is accepted by this rule; one byte above is refused. ## Permission and value rules Built-in Owner and Admin roles can change this field. A custom role needs both **Access Settings** and **Change max file size**. Members who cannot edit the setting can still read the applicable upload constraint before sending files. Use a whole number of at least 1 GB for a practical policy. The API rounds storage-related settings to whole GB, allows an empty value to clear this cap, and refuses a number above the workspace owner's effective storage entitlement. Negative or non-numeric input is rejected. Entering `0` creates a zero-byte boundary and blocks every non-empty file, so clear the field instead when no per-file workspace cap is wanted. The server checks declared size before opening a resumable upload and checks the actual received bytes again at completion. Under-declaring a file cannot bypass the policy. The same shared size check covers regular upload sessions and measured-byte ingestion paths such as batch, sync and import flows; a specific client or protocol can impose an additional smaller limit. ## Steps 1. Switch to the workspace that should receive the rule, then open **Settings → Hard limits**. 2. Locate **Max upload file size**. Confirm that the suffix says **GB** and that you are not editing **Storage per member** or **Total workspace storage cap**. 3. Enter the approved whole-GB value. Keep it at or below the plan capacity shown for the workspace owner's effective entitlement. 4. Select the Save icon beside this row. The success toast reads **Limit updated** and **Your hard limit has been saved.** 5. Refresh **Settings → Hard limits** and verify that the same number returns. 6. Upload a disposable file comfortably below the boundary. Confirm that it completes and that its exact byte size is correct. 7. Try a second disposable file larger than `configured GB × 1,073,741,824`. The server should refuse it with the workspace size-limit message and must not publish a completed file. 8. Delete the accepted test file and empty Trash if you need its bytes released from storage accounting. ## What users and clients receive - Preflight responses expose `max_file_size_gb` to authenticated workspace members so clients can warn before sending. - A file over the workspace rule receives **File exceeds the … GB size limit for this workspace**. - A credential with a stricter byte limit can answer first with its own HTTP 413 refusal. Both the credential and workspace rule must pass. - The multipart body also has to match the size declared at initialization; an oversized body can receive **Upload body is larger than the file_size declared at init**. - The dedicated small batch endpoint has an independent 5 MiB per-file transport ceiling and can return **File too large for batch**, even when the workspace setting is higher. Existing files and completed versions are not resized or deleted when this value is lowered. The new limit governs subsequent byte-adding operations, including a new version uploaded under an existing filename. ## Troubleshooting **You don't have permission: change max file size.** Ask an owner to grant the granular permission together with Settings page access, or have an authorized administrator save the rule. **max_file_size_gb must be a positive number or empty.** Remove text and negative values. Use a whole-number GB value, or leave the input blank to store no workspace-specific file maximum. **max file size gb cannot exceed your plan's … GB storage limit. Upgrade your plan for more.** Reduce the field to the stated plan ceiling. A single file cannot be allowed to exceed the entire effective storage entitlement. **A supposedly below-limit file is refused.** Check its actual bytes rather than the rounded size shown by the operating system, then inspect credential, plan, total-workspace, per-member, extension and batch-route limits. **The save toast does not appear.** The UI reports **Couldn't save** and leaves the prior server value in force. Reload Settings before relying on the edited number. ## Expected result The saved whole-GB maximum survives refresh, a controlled file below or exactly at the byte ceiling can pass this policy, and an oversized file is refused before it becomes a completed workspace item. No existing file is removed by the settings change. ## Related guides - [Set workspace policies](/workspaces/policies) - [Choose roles](/workspaces/roles)

title: Understand workspace storage region and routing
summary: Confirm the workspace location chosen at creation, understand regional placement and routing, and migrate data safely when another location is needed.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/create-workspace.tsx and settings.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/regions.ts, workspaces/index.ts, workspaces/[id]/index.ts, lib/workspace/region.ts, lib/workspace-do/location.ts, and their tests. No production request was made.
body: A workspace's **Location** is selected when the workspace is created. Dosya uses that stored location to choose the workspace service placement and approved regional object bucket; uploads do not carry a per-file location override. Location is fixed for the workspace. A faster network path, a nearby edge, a protocol endpoint or the place from which somebody uploads does not rewrite it. ## How the location is chosen The creation form loads the current catalog and preselects a suggested location from the request's country or continent. If the catalog cannot load, the form stays usable and the server chooses a suggestion; when geography is unavailable, the fallback is Sydney (`ap-southeast-2`). An unrecognized submitted code is refused with **Unknown location**. The catalog currently contains 46 city choices across North America, South America, Europe, Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Africa. The city label is the choice shown to the creator. Several labels may map to the same regional bucket or service-location hint. Nine EU member-state choices use the EU jurisdiction; London and Istanbul are European catalog locations but do not use that EU jurisdiction mapping. ## Steps 1. Switch to the workspace whose location you need to confirm. 2. Open **Settings → Workspace info** and read the read-only **Location** row. It displays the city label and, when different, its stored region code in parentheses. 3. Compare that value with the region recorded in your organization's data-location decision. Do not infer storage location from latency, IP geolocation or an integration's endpoint string. 4. If the current location is acceptable, leave it unchanged; there is no location Save control. 5. When a different location is required, open **Create new workspace**, choose the destination **Location**, and optionally set a storage limit that fits the unallocated account capacity. 6. Copy or upload a controlled sample into the new workspace. Verify its file name, exact byte size, content and selected destination workspace before moving the full data set. 7. Under **Destination access**, re-create membership, API credentials, share links, file requests and automation targets as needed. Those workspace-bound records do not become destination resources merely because file bytes were copied. 8. Keep the source until file counts and bytes have been reconciled and recipients or integrations use the new links. Deleting the source workspace permanently removes its remaining files, versions, Trash, shares and members. ## Routing details that do not change Location - The uploader's approximate position can be recorded as upload-origin metadata when that workspace setting is enabled; it is unrelated to object placement. - Browser uploads and downloads use short-lived signed object URLs for the bucket assigned to the workspace. The request can traverse Cloudflare's network without altering the stored workspace choice. - S3-compatible clients use their documented signing region and gateway endpoint. That protocol configuration is not evidence that the workspace moved. - Existing file metadata keeps the workspace's region when copied within the same workspace. A destination workspace writes new destination records under its own placement. ## Errors and recovery **Location is fixed when a workspace is created.** The server returns HTTP 409 for any attempt to update `default_region`; no role or permission can override this. Create a workspace at the required location and perform a verified migration. **Couldn't load the list of locations. Try again.** Retry the catalog request. If it remains unavailable, creation can continue without a manual choice and the server will select its current geographic suggestion. **Pick a location for this workspace.** The picker loaded successfully but no option is selected. Choose the approved city before submitting. **Only … GB of your plan is unallocated.** The optional destination cap exceeds the remaining whole-GB allocation. Reduce the new cap, lower another owned workspace's cap, or add storage. **Free plan allows a maximum of 3 workspaces. Upgrade to create more.** Region choice itself is not tier-gated, but a Free owner at the three-workspace limit cannot create the destination needed for relocation until they upgrade or reduce their owned-workspace count. ## Expected result Workspace info displays the same immutable location after refresh. If relocation was necessary, the destination workspace shows its separately chosen location and validated copies remain accessible there before any irreversible source cleanup begins. ## Related guides - [Create a workspace and choose location](/workspaces/create-and-choose-region) - [Switch workspaces](/account/switch-workspaces)

title: Resend a workspace invitation
summary: Resend an active workspace invitation, understand the five-minute cooldown, and confirm what the recipient receives without extending its expiry.
verification: Source-reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/teams.tsx; the Team, resend, and invite acceptance APIs; apps/api/src/lib/workspace.ts; and resend cooldown tests. Confirmed locally without a production request or real recipient email.
body: Resend an invitation when the address and role are still correct but the recipient cannot find the first email. Dosya reuses the same email-bound invite and preserves its original expiration date, so resending is different from revoking and creating a replacement. ## Before resending Open the intended workspace and select **Team**. Loading this page requires both **Access Team** and **View team members**. Resending requires **Invite members**; a custom role can perform the action when that permission is enabled. The **Pending invites** row shows the recipient email, who invited them, an expiry countdown, and the assigned role. It does not show a last-sent timestamp. Only active invitations appear here: an accepted, revoked, or expired record is removed from this list. Check the email and role before sending. The recipient must sign in with the same email address to accept. If the address or role is wrong, choose **Revoke** and issue a new invitation instead, because **Resend** cannot edit either value. ## Steps 1. On **Team**, find the address under **Pending invites**. 2. Read the role badge and the **expires in** countdown on that row. 3. Select **Resend** once. While the request runs, the button is disabled and displays a spinner. 4. Look for the **Invite resent** toast stating that the invitation email was sent to the address again. 5. Have the recipient open the newest Dosya invitation email and select **Accept invitation** before the displayed deadline. ## What the recipient gets Dosya sends another invitation email containing the workspace name, assigned role, accept and decline links, and the existing expiry date. If the address already belongs to a Dosya account, that account also received the original invitation as an in-app notification with an **Accept invitation** action and a push notification when enabled. The resend does not reset the seven-day lifetime created with the first invitation. It also leaves the token and role intact. Consecutive sends of the same invite have a five-minute cooldown measured from the original send or latest successful resend. Resending does not reserve a member place. A free-plan workspace can admit at most five non-owner members, and Dosya enforces that ceiling again when the recipient accepts. If the workspace fills first, acceptance returns **Free plan workspaces can have at most 5 members. Upgrade to add more.** ## If Resend fails - **This invite was just re-sent. Try again in N minutes.** Wait for the five-minute window to end; repeated clicks do not shorten it. - **This invite has expired. Send a new one.** Open **Invite to workspace**, use **Email invite**, and create a replacement. The expired link cannot be revived. - **This invite was already accepted** or **This invite was revoked** means the stored invitation is no longer resendable. Refresh **Team** to load current membership and pending rows. - **You don't have permission to resend invites** means your role lacks **Invite members**. A role manager must add that capability or perform the resend. - **Email is not configured on this server** or **The email could not be sent. Try again later.** No successful resend was recorded. Retry later, or use **Copy link** to deliver the active URL through another channel. Revoking is immediate and cannot be undone. The revoked link stops accepting users, and an invitee with an existing Dosya account receives an in-app withdrawal notice. A new invitation is required after that action. ## Expected result The sender sees **Invite resent**, the recipient receives a fresh email for the same pending invitation, and the row keeps its original role and expiry countdown. The resend is also recorded as invitation activity. ## Related guides - [Workspace roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Invite team members](/workspaces/invite-team)

title: Grant activity-log access in a custom role
summary: Grant full workspace activity access to a custom role, verify the Activity page and forensic fields, and preserve hidden-resource privacy boundaries.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/role-create.tsx, apps/web/src/pages/activity.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/activity.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/team.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/activity.int.test.ts. No production role was edited.
body: **View activity log** grants workspace-wide audit visibility. Without it, the full Activity endpoint returns 403 and the Team sidebar narrows to the current member’s own events. ## Before you start - The editor needs **Manage roles** and must hold **View activity log** before granting it. - **View activity log** itself gates the Activity route; a folder-confined member still cannot open the workspace-wide page. - Activity may contain IP, device, session, and operational metadata that should remain private. ## Steps 1. Open **Workspace settings → Roles & permissions** and select **Edit** for the intended custom role. 2. Under **Workspace general**, enable **View activity log** and review the role for unrelated sensitive grants. 3. Select **Save changes** and wait for **Role updated — The role and its permissions have been saved.** 4. Assign the role to a controlled member if necessary, wait about 60 seconds, and reload their session. 5. Open **Activity log** and apply an **Action** filter; use **Member** only when the role also has **View team members**. 6. Expand a known event and confirm permitted context appears while hidden or locked resource names remain withheld. ## Access consequences Role-definition changes affect every member holding that custom role. Permission changes generate notices describing gained and lost capabilities. The Activity page requests 30 records at a time and provides Category, Member, and Action filters. The activity permission does not bypass file visibility, locks, or folder scope. It gives audit context, not authority to open or restore the target resource. **View team members** only populates the Member filter; the Action filter remains available without it. ## Expected result The test member can load and filter the full Activity page, inspect permitted details, and still cannot obtain names or content excluded by other access controls. ## Troubleshooting **You don’t have permission to view workspace activity.** The new role has not propagated, the switch was not saved, or the wrong workspace is active. **The Activity page remains unavailable.** Confirm **View activity log** is saved; remove folder confinement only if the member truly needs workspace-wide audit scope. **The Member filter has no choices.** Add **View team members** only when the investigator needs the workspace roster; use Category and Action without that permission. **A field is missing.** Not every event records every forensic value, and server-side privacy shaping may deliberately remove it. ## Related guides - [Understand roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Change a member role](/workspaces/workspace-change-role)

title: Grant file access in a custom role
summary: Configure file, folder and page permissions in a custom role, then test browsing, upload, download, rename and deletion without granting excess access.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/role-create.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/permissions.ts, apps/web/src/hooks/use-files-listing.ts, packages/test-harness/tests/files.int.test.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/folders-crud.int.test.ts. No production role was changed.
body: File access is a combination of page entry and action permissions. **Access Files** opens the browser; it does not automatically permit upload, download, rename, folder creation, or deletion. ## Before you start - The editor needs **Manage roles** and can enable only permissions they already hold. - Use a test member and disposable file tree. Folder anchors, hidden items, locks, and role conditions continue to apply. - Separate **Delete own files** from **Delete any file** deliberately. ## Steps 1. Open the custom role in **Edit custom role** and scroll to **Files**, **Folders**, and **Page access**. 2. Enable **Access Files** when the member must browse the file page. 3. Choose among **Upload files**, **Download files**, **Rename files**, **Create folders**, and **Rename folders** based on the job. 4. Enable **Delete own files** only for self-created content, or **Delete any file** only for trusted cleanup responsibility. 5. Select **Save changes**, wait for **Role updated**, then reload a test member’s session after cache convergence. 6. Test browsing plus each intended operation, and attempt one withheld action on disposable content to verify refusal. ## Independent controls **Access Upload** governs the upload page separately. **Lock files & folders** and **Hide files & folders** are administrative capabilities, not implied by file browsing. Protocol access also needs **Use WebDAV**, **Use the S3 gateway**, or **SFTP access**. Editing the shared role changes every current holder. Removing a permission does not reverse files already uploaded, renamed, shared, or moved to Trash. ## Expected result The member can enter only intended pages and perform exactly the selected file and folder operations, while destructive or administrative controls remain absent or refused. ## Troubleshooting **Files is unavailable.** Enable **Access Files** in addition to the needed action permissions. **Upload is refused despite Upload files.** Check **Access Upload** for the web page, workspace quota, file policy, role limits, and folder scope. **Delete works only on some items.** **Delete own files** is uploader-specific; use **Delete any file** only when broader deletion is required. ## Related guides - [Understand roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Change a member role](/workspaces/workspace-change-role)

title: Grant sharing permissions in a custom role
summary: Configure custom-role sharing access for creating, viewing, managing, and analyzing links, then test exactly which controls a member receives.
verification: Verified with local repository evidence on 2026-10-14: role-create sharing controls, Files and Shared page gates, share ownership authorization, analytics and revoke tests, and role-change notifications. No live link was altered.
body: Sharing access is split across four switches so a role can create links without seeing every colleague’s links, or audit workspace-wide links without receiving unrelated file-administration powers. Configure these controls as a set and test them from a member account. ## Choose the permission set In **Create custom role** or **Edit custom role**, the relevant switches are: - **Create share links** displays sharing actions and permits public or private link creation for accessible files and folders. - **View own shared links** lets a member see statistics for links they created and edit or revoke those links. - **View all shared links** exposes links created by any workspace member and authorizes management and analytics for another creator’s link. - **Access Shared** opens the Shared page. Without it, that page is denied even when another sharing capability is enabled. Page access and action access are independent. A member who has **Access Files** plus **Create share links** can use the **Share** control from Files even if **Access Shared** is off. Conversely, **Access Shared** alone does not reveal link rows; the role also needs **View own shared links** or **View all shared links**. Use **View own shared links** for ordinary creators. Add **View all shared links** only for people responsible for organization-wide link review. Hiding a target can remove its link from that member's view; a full lock can make the recipient URL unavailable. Broad share visibility does not bypass those controls. ## Steps 1. Open **Workspace settings**, find the custom role under **Existing roles**, and select **Edit**. 2. Scroll to the **Sharing** group and enable **Create share links**, **View own shared links**, or **View all shared links** according to the responsibilities above. 3. In **Page access**, enable **Access Shared** when the member should use the workspace link dashboard. 4. Review **Access Files** and **Download files** separately. Sharing switches do not automatically grant file browsing or downloading. 5. Select **Save changes** and confirm **Role updated — The role and its permissions have been saved.** 6. In a session belonging to a member with that role, reload Dosya and open **Files** and **Shared**. 7. Create a disposable link only if **Create share links** should be allowed. Then check whether the session can see its analytics, edit it, and revoke it. 8. When **View all shared links** is intended, verify one controlled link created by a different member; otherwise confirm that link is absent or refused. ## Administrative rules and effects Editing a custom role requires **Manage roles**. Newly enabled permissions cannot exceed those held by the editor. A refused save returns **You can't grant permissions you don't hold yourself: ...**, identifies the rejected rows, and leaves those grants unapplied. Changing the role definition affects every current holder rather than one member. When at least one permission moves, holders receive an in-app **Your permissions in _workspace_ changed** notice naming the editor, role, gained capabilities, and removed capabilities. Because a lost sharing permission can interrupt active work, ask members to reload before validating controls. The change is reversible by another authorized role manager, but access is enforced during the interval. Revoking a share link during testing is irreversible: the same public URL cannot be restored, so create a disposable link rather than using an active recipient-facing link. ## Troubleshoot the test - A missing **Share** action usually means **Create share links** is off or the Files page itself is unavailable. - An empty or refused **Shared** page can mean **Access Shared** is disabled, or neither view permission is present. - Analytics for the member’s own link requires **View own shared links** or the broader **View all shared links**. - Editing, analyzing, or revoking another member’s link requires **View all shared links**; ownership plus **View own shared links** covers only the creator’s records. - If the old controls remain after a successful save, reload the member session and retry after the permission cache refreshes. ## Expected result The test member can create links, open the Shared page, inspect analytics, and manage records only to the extent enabled by the four selected controls, with other members’ links withheld unless workspace-wide visibility was granted. ## Related guides - [Understand roles](/workspaces/roles) - [Change a member role](/workspaces/workspace-change-role)

title: Choosing built-in and custom workspace roles
summary: Compare Owner, Admin, Member and Viewer access, create a custom role, and assign a role without granting more access than intended.
verification: Reviewed the current Team role controls, role guide, custom-role editor and permission ceiling against the local current web app and API on 2026-10-12. Screenshot data is isolated and representative; no production role was changed.
body: A workspace role determines which pages and actions a member can use. Start with the least powerful built-in role that fits. Create a custom role when the built-in choices include permissions the person does not need or omit a permission they do need. Folder access is a separate boundary. A role answers what someone can do; a folder restriction answers which part of the workspace they can see. ## Before you start - Select the correct workspace and open **Team**. - You need **Manage roles** to create custom roles, change another member's role or set folder access. - You can grant only permissions you hold yourself. This rule also applies to custom roles and invitation links. - You cannot change your own role or assign **Owner** from the member role selector. Transfer ownership from Workspace settings when required. - Review what the person actually needs across files, folders, sharing, Team, settings and protocol access. ## Built-in roles The **Role guide** on Team summarizes the built-in roles: - **Owner** has full control, billing responsibility and the ability to delete the workspace. A workspace has one owner. - **Admin** can manage members and workspace files. It is a powerful operational role. - **Member** can upload, share and manage their own work under the workspace's policies. - **Viewer** is intended for viewing and downloading without write access. The permission matrix in **Settings → Roles & permissions** is the authoritative view for the current workspace. Review it when a decision depends on a specific action. ## Steps: change a member's role 1. Open **Team** and locate the person under **Members**. 2. Open the role selector in that member's row. 3. Choose the new built-in or custom role. 4. Wait for the **Role updated** confirmation. 5. Check that the member row displays the new role. 6. Ask the member to refresh or reopen the relevant page. Permission caches may take a short time to settle across active sessions. A role with permissions beyond your own remains unavailable. The owner's row is displayed as a badge because ownership uses the transfer workflow. ## Steps: create a custom role 1. On **Team**, select **Create custom role** in the Role guide. You can also open **Settings → Roles & permissions** and select **Add role**. 2. Enter a clear **Role name**, such as “External reviewer” or “Upload coordinator.” Name the responsibility rather than a person's name. 3. Review each permission group and enable only the required actions. 4. Include the necessary **Page access** permissions. For example, a file permission alone does not automatically make the Files page available. 5. Review protocol access for WebDAV, S3 and SFTP. Leave each protocol off unless the role needs it. 6. If needed, set role access conditions such as allowed IP addresses or active hours. 7. If needed, set usage limits such as requests per minute, daily egress, maximum file size or concurrent transfers. 8. Select **Create role**. 9. Return to **Team** and assign the new role to a member, email invitation or invitation link. ## Expected result A changed member row shows the newly assigned role. A newly created custom role appears in the workspace's role matrix and in eligible assignment and invitation selectors. The member receives the intersection of the role's permissions, workspace policies, any folder restriction and any access conditions. A role does not override those additional boundaries. ## Limits and permission rules - **Owner** is transferred, not assigned through a role selector or invitation. - You cannot change your own role from Team. - A custom role belongs to the workspace where it was created. - You cannot grant a permission you do not hold. - Built-in roles can be reviewed but are not edited like custom roles. - Deleting a custom role can be refused while members or invitations still reference it. Reassign those references first. - Removing a permission can immediately interrupt a member's work. Review active transfers and integrations before making a broad change. ## Troubleshooting **Manage-role controls are missing.** Your current role lacks **Manage roles**, or the page is restricted. Ask the owner to make the change. **A permission switch is disabled.** You do not hold that permission and therefore cannot grant it. An owner or sufficiently privileged administrator must create the role. **The role saves but a page is still unavailable.** Review **Page access** alongside the action permission. Also check folder access, workspace policies and role conditions. **The member still appears to have the old access.** Confirm the member row shows the new role, then have the person refresh the app or reconnect the client. If the behavior persists, capture the page, action and exact refusal message for private support. **The role cannot be deleted.** Reassign members, pending invitations and active invitation links that use it, then try again. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can a custom role be more powerful than the person creating it? No. The server checks the permissions of the person creating or assigning the role and refuses grants beyond that ceiling. ### Does a Viewer automatically see every file? A role alone does not define the visible tree. Hidden items, locks, workspace policies and an optional folder restriction can further limit access. ### Can I reuse a custom role in another workspace? No. Create and review the role separately in each workspace. ## Related guides - [Inviting people to a workspace](/workspaces/invite-team) - [Using workspace invitation links safely](/workspaces/invite-links) - [Restricting a workspace member to one folder](/workspaces/folder-access)

title: Review workspace storage allocation
summary: Compare account entitlement, owned-workspace usage and explicit workspace caps so you can identify the limit that will block the next upload.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts, plans.ts, pages/api/workspaces/[id]/index.ts and settings.ts, plus apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx and create-workspace.tsx. No production action was performed.
body: Dosya applies two storage ceilings to byte-adding operations: the workspace owner's account entitlement and the active workspace's optional **Total workspace storage cap**. An upload must fit under both. An explicit workspace cap is an upload boundary, not reserved capacity. An uncapped sibling workspace can still consume the owner's shared account pool, and the sum of all explicit workspace caps cannot exceed that owner's effective entitlement. ## Values to compare | Displayed value | Meaning | | --- | --- | | **Your storage** on the Workspace dashboard | Account-wide limit, used bytes across every workspace you own, and remaining entitlement. Shared workspaces do not consume your pool. | | **Where your space comes from** | Current base plan plus eligible packages, custom storage, active license grants and referral storage. These rows sum to the enforced account limit. | | Workspace **used** | Bytes currently charged to this workspace, including content that remains in Trash. | | **Total workspace storage cap** | Optional hard ceiling for this workspace. Blank means no workspace-specific cap; the account limit still applies. | | **GB left to allocate** | Whole-GB capacity that can still be assigned among explicit workspace caps. It is not the same as uploadable free space. | | **Storage per member** | An additional ceiling on bytes attributed to one uploader, independent of the total workspace cap. | The settings UI labels these values **GB**, while enforcement uses 1 GB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. Storage caps are stored as whole GB. New uploads are refused when their bytes would cross a ceiling; equality is allowed. ## Steps 1. Open the workspace switcher and choose **Workspace dashboard**. 2. Record **used**, **free of**, and the source rows under **Where your space comes from**. This view measures only workspaces you own; **Shared with you** uses each owner's storage. 3. Select the intended owned workspace, then open **Settings → Hard limits**. 4. Read **Total workspace storage cap**, **Storage per member**, and the **GB left to allocate** badge. Keep blank limits distinct from zero values. 5. Calculate workspace-cap headroom as `cap bytes − workspace used bytes`. Calculate account headroom as `account limit − usage across owned workspaces`. 6. Treat the smaller non-negative result as the capacity available to this workspace. A concurrent upload elsewhere can reduce account headroom before your next transfer begins. 7. If a cap must change, enter a whole number of GB and select its Save button. Built-in Owner and Admin roles have the required permission; a custom role needs **Access Settings** plus **Change total storage cap**. ## What happens after a cap change - Saving a tighter cap takes effect for new byte-adding operations after the settings cache is invalidated. Existing files are not deleted. - If current usage is already above the new cap, Settings warns: **This workspace uses …, above its … GB limit. New uploads are blocked until usage drops below the limit - emptying the trash frees space toward that.** - Lowering a cap can revoke an outstanding temporary storage allowance that no longer fits. That revocation is committed with the cap change. - Clearing **Total workspace storage cap** removes only this workspace-specific boundary. It does not increase the owner's plan or bypass a per-member limit. - Other workspace administrators receive a deduplicated settings-change notification; the action is also recorded in workspace activity. ## Resolve allocation errors **All … GB of your plan is already allocated to workspace limits. Lower another workspace's limit or upgrade your plan.** The explicit caps already consume the whole entitlement. Reduce a cap in another owned workspace or add storage. **You can allocate at most … GB more (… of … GB already allocated to workspace limits).** Enter that remaining amount or less. Editing an existing cap returns its current allocation to the available calculation before the replacement is checked. **This workspace has a … GB storage limit and this doesn't fit. Empty the trash here or raise the limit in workspace settings.** Permanently empty enough Trash content, reduce the incoming transfer, or raise the cap. **You've used … of … across all your workspaces.** The account entitlement binds first. Removing content from only the active workspace helps only after that content is permanently deleted; moving it to another owned workspace does not reduce account usage. ## Expected result You can name the exact binding limit before the next upload: owner entitlement, total workspace cap, or per-member cap. A saved cap reappears after refresh, and a small controlled upload increases usage in the intended workspace without crossing either storage ceiling. ## Related guides - [Set workspace policies](/workspaces/policies) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage) - [Add storage](/account/upgrade-storage)

title: Compare used and available workspace storage
summary: Calculate usable workspace headroom from the optional workspace cap and owner account pool, then compare the smaller result with the planned transfer.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/dashboard.tsx, apps/web/src/components/layout/profile-menu.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts, apps/api/src/lib/kv-cache.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/upload/measured-quota.ts. Production storage was not changed.
body: Usable headroom is constrained by both the active workspace and its owner’s account. An explicit workspace cap is a ceiling, not reserved capacity, so sibling workspaces can consume the shared account pool. ## Before you start - Confirm the workspace is owned by the account whose entitlement you are reading; shared workspaces consume their owner’s pool. - Record the planned transfer’s exact bytes, including every file that will be added. - Content in Trash still counts until permanent deletion completes. ## Steps 1. Open the account menu and record the owner-wide used and total storage; the Dashboard figures describe only the active workspace. 2. Switch to the destination workspace and open **Workspace settings → Hard limits**. 3. Record current workspace usage and **Total workspace storage cap**; a blank cap means no workspace-specific ceiling. 4. Compute displayed account headroom as `owner entitlement − usage across owned workspaces`. 5. When a workspace cap exists, compute displayed cap headroom as `cap bytes − workspace used bytes`; convert each GB using 1,073,741,824 bytes. 6. Use the smaller non-negative remainder and compare it with the planned transfer, leaving room for concurrent uploads. ## Other limits to check Equality with a ceiling is allowed, but a concurrent commit can consume space before yours completes. **Storage per member** can bind even when workspace headroom remains, and maximum file size, extension rules, role limits, and credential limits are separate. Displayed values are rounded and omit temporary storage allowances already reserved by in-progress writes. The upload gate subtracts both the workspace allowance and the sum of owner-wide allowances, so displayed headroom can exceed commit-time capacity. The server makes an atomic measured-byte decision at commit; this calculation is planning evidence rather than a reservation. ## Expected result You can identify the likely account or workspace ceiling and estimate whether planned bytes fit, while reserving margin for hidden allowances, concurrent writes, and other policies. ## Troubleshooting **Free space is lower than the cap calculation.** Another owned workspace is consuming the shared account entitlement. **The uploader is refused despite total headroom.** Review **Storage per member**, file-size policy, role limits, and the exact quota error. **The values changed during the calculation.** Refresh both views and recompute; capacity is not reserved by reading it. **The gate refuses fewer bytes than the interface showed free.** An in-progress operation may hold a workspace or owner allowance that the visible used totals do not include. Wait for it to settle, then retry the calculation. ## Related guides - [Review storage allocation](/workspaces/storage-allocation) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Change a workspace storage allocation safely
summary: Change the whole-GB workspace storage cap within the owner’s entitlement, understand over-cap behavior, and verify the saved limit without deleting files.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx, apps/api/src/pages/api/workspaces/[id]/settings.ts, apps/api/src/lib/workspace.ts, apps/api/src/lib/storage-allowance/revoke.ts, and packages/test-harness/tests/workspaces.int.test.ts. No production cap was changed.
body: **Total workspace storage cap** sets a hard ceiling for new byte-adding operations. Lowering it below current usage blocks further uploads but does not delete existing content. ## Before you start - The actor needs **Access Settings** plus **Change total workspace storage cap**. - Review workspace usage, owner entitlement, and every explicit cap across the owner’s workspaces. - Clearing the field removes only this workspace-specific cap; the account and per-member ceilings remain. ## Steps 1. Open **Workspace settings → Hard limits** and locate **Total workspace storage cap**. 2. Record current usage, the saved cap, and the **GB left to allocate** badge. 3. Choose a whole number of at least 1 GB, or leave the field empty to remove this boundary. 4. Select the row’s save control and wait for **Limit updated — Your hard limit has been saved.** 5. Reload Settings and confirm the stored value plus any warning that usage already exceeds it. 6. Use a small disposable upload to verify the new boundary without attempting to fill all remaining storage. ## Allocation rules and effects The sum of explicit caps across the owner’s workspaces cannot exceed effective account entitlement. Editing a cap returns that workspace’s old allocation before checking the replacement. Values are rounded to whole GB and cannot exceed the plan-backed storage pool. A tighter cap can revoke an outstanding temporary storage allowance that no longer fits. The change is reversible by an authorized administrator, but uploads refused while over cap do not resume automatically. ## Expected result The saved whole-GB value reappears after reload, existing files remain untouched, and new byte-adding work is allowed or refused according to the tighter of workspace and account capacity. ## Troubleshooting **All … GB of your plan is already allocated to workspace limits.** Lower another explicit cap or add entitlement. **You can allocate at most … GB more.** Enter no more than the remaining amount shown. **New uploads are blocked until usage drops below the limit.** Permanently empty enough Trash content or raise the cap; moving items to Trash is insufficient. ## Related guides - [Review storage allocation](/workspaces/storage-allocation) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Respond when a member upload reaches quota
summary: Diagnose a member’s per-uploader storage refusal, compare it with workspace and account capacity, then free or raise the correct limit before retrying.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/settings.tsx, apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/measured-quota.ts, apps/api/src/lib/upload/init-gates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/repo/repo-d1/gates.ts, apps/api/src/lib/workspace-do/repo/gates.ts, and apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts. No production upload was retried.
body: **Storage per member** measures bytes attributed to one uploader and can refuse that person while the workspace still shows free capacity. It is independent of the total workspace cap. ## Before you start - Capture the file size, active workspace, uploader account, and full error message. - The settings editor needs **Access Settings** and **Change storage per member**. - Moving a file to Trash removes it from the live per-member sum, but workspace and account storage stay charged until permanent purge; purging is irreversible. ## Steps 1. Confirm the upload reports **You’ve reached your _N_ GB per-member storage limit** rather than a workspace or account message. 2. Open **Workspace settings → Hard limits** and read **Storage per member** plus **Total workspace storage cap**. 3. Compare the member’s attributed bytes plus the incoming file with the per-member limit using 1 GB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. 4. Move disposable files attributed to that uploader to Trash to lower the member total, or save a higher allowed per-member value. 5. Retry after the live rows or saved limit update; permanently purge Trash only when the workspace or account storage ceiling also needs space. 6. Retry the single failed upload and verify it completes without crossing the workspace owner’s remaining entitlement. ## Limit interaction Raising the per-member value cannot exceed the owner’s plan storage ceiling and does not bypass the total workspace cap. An upload must satisfy the credential, role, file, member, workspace, and account gates. The final measured-byte reservation is atomic, so two concurrent writes cannot both claim the same remaining workspace capacity. A successful retry increases workspace usage by the committed bytes. ## Expected result The member’s controlled retry succeeds after live attributed usage plus the new file fits the per-member rule and both broader storage ceilings. Trash can resolve the member rule while the broader ceilings remain unchanged until purge. ## Troubleshooting **The same member message remains.** Confirm the trashed files were uploaded by that member and are no longer live; another uploader’s files do not reduce this member’s attributed total. **The error changes to a workspace or account limit.** The member ceiling is resolved, but Trash is still charged to those broader totals; permanently purge disposable content or raise the binding ceiling. **Only one client fails.** Inspect credential-specific maximum file size and role usage limits on that surface. ## Related guides - [Review storage allocation](/workspaces/storage-allocation) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Read workspace storage allocation
summary: Interpret used, total and free workspace storage, distinguish a hard cap from account headroom, and avoid treating allocation as reserved space.
verification: Verified locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/quota.ts, pages/api/workspaces/index.ts, workspaces/[id]/index.ts, workspaces/[id]/upload-limits.ts, apps/web/src/components/layout/dashboard-sidebar.tsx, and storage-view tests. No production request was made.
body: The workspace switcher summarizes the storage that can actually fit in each workspace. Read **used**, **total** and **free** together because a workspace cap and the owner's account pool are enforced at the same time. A cap does not reserve bytes. **Free** is the smaller of the workspace's remaining cap and the owner's account-wide remaining entitlement, so sibling workspaces can reduce it even when this workspace has not changed. ## How the values are calculated | Field | Calculation | | --- | --- | | **used** | Non-negative bytes charged to this workspace. Content in Trash continues to count until it is permanently emptied. | | **total** | The explicit workspace cap in bytes when set; otherwise the workspace owner's effective account entitlement. | | **free** | `max(0, min(total − workspace used, account limit − usage across all owned workspaces))`. | | **cap** | **Total workspace storage cap** × 1,073,741,824 bytes, or absent when the workspace is uncapped. | | **account used** | Sum of storage-used counters across every workspace owned by the same account. | The UI formats binary units: 1 MB is 1,048,576 bytes, 1 GB is 1,073,741,824 bytes and 1 TB is 1,099,511,627,776 bytes. Values at least 1 GB are rounded for display, so use exact byte sizes when testing a tight boundary. ## Steps 1. Open the workspace switcher and locate the intended workspace by name and icon. 2. Record its **… free of …** line. The first value is effective free space; the second is the workspace total described above. 3. Switch to that workspace and open **Settings → Hard limits** if your role has **Access Settings**. 4. Read **Total workspace storage cap**. A blank field means the workspace total follows the owner's entitlement; it does not mean zero bytes. 5. Compare **workspace cap headroom** with the owner's account-wide remaining limit. The smaller amount explains the switcher's effective free-space value. 6. Check **Storage per member** when one uploader is blocked despite workspace-level free space. That separate rule measures the member's existing bytes plus the incoming file. 7. For automation or a custom client, read the workspace upload-limits response. Treat `storage_remaining_bytes` as a hint because its quota cache can be up to 60 seconds old; the upload server makes the final measured-byte decision. ## Examples An account has 100 GB total and 80 GB used across owned workspaces. Workspace A has a 50 GB cap and 20 GB used. Its cap leaves 30 GB, but the account leaves 20 GB, so Workspace A shows 20 GB free. An account has 500 GB total and 100 GB used. Workspace B has a 25 GB cap and 24 GB used. Account headroom is 400 GB, but the workspace has only 1 GB left, so its displayed free value is 1 GB. Removing a 5 GB file to Trash does not immediately change the used counter. Permanently emptying that Trash content releases storage; moving it into another workspace owned by the same account can change the two workspace counters but does not reduce account-wide usage. ## Resolve unexpected readings **The workspace appears empty but has little free space.** Another workspace owned by the same account is consuming the shared entitlement. Open the account Workspace dashboard to find the owned usage. **The total equals a smaller round number than the plan.** An explicit **Total workspace storage cap** is active. Only someone with **Access Settings** and **Change total storage cap** can alter it. **The uploader reached a limit while free space remains.** Inspect **Storage per member**, **Max upload file size**, extension rules and credential-specific limits; the storage figure covers only account and workspace total capacity. **The value has not caught up with a recent transfer.** Refresh after the operation settles. Preflight remaining bytes may lag by as much as its 60-second cache, while the completion gate measures real bytes before committing them. ## Expected result The recorded free value matches the smaller applicable headroom and never becomes negative. You can explain whether an upload is constrained by the workspace cap, the owner's shared pool or a separate per-member/file rule before changing settings. ## Related guides - [Review storage allocation](/workspaces/storage-allocation) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Verify storage after cleanup
summary: Confirm permanent deletion released workspace storage, distinguish Trash from purge, and reconcile bytes after versions and concurrent activity settle.
verification: Locally reviewed on 2026-10-14 against apps/api/src/lib/files/purge.ts, apps/api/src/pages/api/files/batch-delete.ts, apps/api/src/lib/files/prune-versions.ts, apps/web/src/pages/dashboard.tsx, and apps/api/src/lib/upload/measured-quota.ts. No production file was deleted.
body: Moving a file to Trash does not reduce `storage_used_bytes`. Capacity returns only when the stored object and charged versions are permanently purged, an irreversible operation. ## Before you start - Select only disposable items and record their file plus version sizes before acting. - Pause or account for uploads, copies, imports, and version creation during the measurement. - Permanent deletion cannot restore the file, its versions, share context, comments, or related history. ## Steps 1. Open the destination workspace’s storage view and record its used bytes before cleanup. 2. Move the selected item to Trash and confirm the used value does not decrease at this stage. 3. Review the Trash selection again, including folders and every contained file or stored version. 4. Choose the permanent delete or empty-Trash action and confirm the irreversible prompt. 5. Wait for the purge and storage-counter update to complete, then refresh the workspace and account views. 6. Subtract the new value from the baseline and reconcile the result with purged bytes plus any concurrent storage changes. ## What frees capacity Trash preserves content for recovery and therefore remains charged. The purge path removes stored objects, file rows and relevant versions, then decrements the workspace counter without allowing it below zero. Version-retention pruning can also release bytes independently. A displayed total can be rounded, and cached preflight quota hints can lag by up to about 60 seconds. Use exact sizes and a quiet test window for a precise comparison. ## Expected result The used counter remains unchanged after trashing, falls only after permanent purge, and the measured difference is explainable from deleted versions and any concurrent writes. ## Troubleshooting **Usage did not change.** Confirm the item was permanently deleted rather than left in Trash, then refresh after the quota cache window. **The reduction is smaller than the visible file size.** Check whether some versions or folder contents remain and whether new uploads occurred. **The reduction is larger than expected.** Version pruning or another administrator’s cleanup may have happened concurrently; use activity timestamps and exact item records. ## Related guides - [Review storage allocation](/workspaces/storage-allocation) - [Understand storage usage](/uploading/storage-usage)

title: Connecting Zapier and building your first file automation
summary: Create a compatible API key, add Dosya to Zapier, and build a New File automation that creates a sharing link for the uploaded sample.
verification: Reviewed the current Dosya Zapier setup page, authentication requirements, New File trigger and Create Share Link source on 2026-10-10. Actual local setup and API-key form captures use a disposable account. Verified real SDK connection, New File sample lookup and Create Share Link against the isolated local API; new-version events were excluded. Zapier editor instructions checked against current official help. A live Zapier editor, provider callback delivery and published Zap run were not verified; this is a setup walkthrough with explicit user completion checks. Visual and repeated copy reviewed against this guide’s existing task instructions and screenshot subject; migration: apps/help/scripts/rewrite-task-copy.mjs. No product behavior or image assets changed.
body: Create a **Full access** API key that allows **REST API**, add Dosya through the Zapier invite on **Integrations → Zapier**, then connect the key in Zapier. For a first automation, use **New File** as the trigger and **Create Share Link** as the action. Test with a disposable file before publishing the Zap. ## Before you start - Have a Dosya account, a Zapier account and a regular workspace you are allowed to automate. - Choose a disposable sample file with a new filename. This example creates a public sharing link for it, so use material you intend to share and review the expiry. - Check your Zapier plan and account policies for the chosen workflow. Additional steps, other apps and organization controls can have their own requirements. - Prepare private credential storage for a dedicated Zapier API key. Do not put its full value in screenshots or support messages. ## Steps: create a compatible API key 1. **Open Profile → API keys.** Select **New API key** and name its purpose, such as Zapier file automation. 2. **Choose Full access.** The integration needs this permission to create the event subscription used by the trigger. A Read only or Upload only key is refused for this connection. 3. **Review Restrictions and expiry.** Under Protocols, allow **REST API**. You can choose **Only the ones I pick** and select REST API for a key dedicated to this integration. 4. **Limit the workspace when appropriate.** Select the workspace this automation should use. Leave the folder restriction unset: folder-restricted keys work over WebDAV or S3, not the REST API used here. 5. **Set expiry and access conditions deliberately.** An expired key or a key restricted to the wrong addresses or schedule will interrupt the automation. Arrange to replace an expiring key before its expiry. 6. **Generate and save the key.** Review the summary, select **Generate key**, copy the full key once and store it privately before closing the result. The list's partial identifier cannot authenticate Zapier. ## Steps: add Dosya and connect Zapier 1. **Open Dosya's setup page.** In the web app, select **Integrations → Zapier**, or open [Zapier setup](https://app.dosya.dev/integrations/zapier) after signing in. 2. **Use Open the Zapier invite.** Follow the invite to add the integration to your Zapier account. Use the link shown on this setup page rather than an old copied invitation. The current setup uses an invite; your Zapier organization may require an administrator to allow private apps. 3. **Create a Zap.** In Zapier, use its create-workflow action and choose Dosya for the trigger app. If Dosya is missing, confirm that you accepted the invite using the same Zapier account. 4. **Choose New File.** This trigger watches for a newly added file in a workspace. 5. **Connect the Dosya account.** When Zapier requests the **dosya API key**, paste the full key privately. Confirm the connection succeeds before configuring the trigger. ## Steps: test New File and create a sharing link 1. **Select Workspace in the trigger.** Choose the workspace where the new file will arrive. A key pinned to a workspace must use that same workspace. 2. **Upload a sample.** In Dosya, upload the disposable file into that workspace. Use a fresh filename, such as zapier-first-test.txt, rather than replacing an existing file. 3. **Test the trigger.** In Zapier's **Test** tab, select **Test trigger**, inspect a returned file record and continue with that selected record. Check its filename, File ID and folder. For Zapier's current editor controls, see its [trigger setup instructions](https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/8496288188429-Set-up-your-Zap-trigger). 4. **Add the action.** Choose Dosya and **Create Share Link**. Connect the same intended account/key and select the same workspace. 5. **Map the uploaded file.** Set **Share a** to **File**. In **File**, use the trigger's **File ID** rather than entering the filename or selecting a fixed sample file.
