Dynamic mapping makes later runs act on each new file. 6. **Set link controls.** Enter an appropriate **Expires in days**, such as 7 for this test. **Access code** is optional recipient protection; it is not your Dosya account password. Check the sharing implications before testing. 7. **Test the action.** Zapier's action test creates a real share link. Inspect the returned **Share URL**, open it as a recipient and check that it refers to the intended sample. Remove an unwanted test link in Dosya's Shared area. 8. **Publish when the tests match your intent.** Review the workspace, mapped File ID and expiry first. After publishing, upload a second file with a new filename and check its run in Zapier history, including the action output. Testing a trigger supplies sample data; testing an action can create the actual result. Zapier describes this distinction in [Test Zap steps](https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/18811411817741-Test-Zap-steps). A successful editor test is separate from verifying a run after publishing. ## Expected result The connection test accepts the dedicated key. Trigger testing returns the intended file's metadata. The action test returns a link for that file, and a new upload after publishing produces a successful run with the correct mapped file and Share URL. If you add another app later, map its fields from the correct preceding step. For example, a step that needs a share URL should use the Create Share Link output rather than a filename. Test any external destination with your own sample data and recipients. ## Limitations New File excludes uploads that replace an existing file with a new version. It does not turn old files into new events when you publish the Zap. Upload a new disposable file to check a live run. The trigger is scoped to a workspace, rather than a folder field. If you need one folder, add a condition using **Folder ID** where your Zapier workflow supports it. Check the plan requirements for additional steps. Full access is required for event subscriptions. Limit reach with a dedicated workspace and REST-only key where practical. Vault is a separate workflow; this example uses regular files and sharing. The screenshots show Dosya's setup controls, not a captured live Zapier editor, and a published provider run was not exercised for this guide. ## Troubleshooting **I cannot find Dosya in Zapier.** Reopen the current invite from Integrations → Zapier, accept it with the intended account and check any organization app-approval policy. **The key is refused.** Check its full copied value, Full access permission, REST API protocol, expiry and workspace reach. Do not use a folder-restricted key or the partial identifier from the key list. **Test trigger returns no useful sample.** Upload a new file into the selected workspace, wait for the upload to complete, then test again. Check workspace permissions and choose the returned record that matches your sample. **A re-upload did not trigger the Zap.** New File excludes new versions of an existing file. Use a different filename to create a new file for the test. **Every run shares the same sample file.** Replace a fixed File value with the trigger's File ID. Check the action input in run history, then test with another new file. **The action test worked but publishing did not.** Check that the Zap is on, the key still works and a genuinely new file was uploaded after publishing. Inspect run history to distinguish a missing trigger from a failed action. Share the relevant error with [support](https://dosya.dev/contact/), excluding keys and private share links. ## Frequently asked questions ### Can I use a read-only key for New File? No. The connection requires Full access to create its event subscription. ### Does publishing process everything already in the workspace? No. Trigger tests can return samples from existing files, but the live New File workflow starts with newly added files. ### How do I stop the automation? Turn off the Zap. Revoke its dedicated API key when you want to remove that integration's credential, and revoke any share links that should no longer work. ## Related guides - [API key management](/developers/api-key) - [Uploading files and folders](/uploading/files-and-folders) - [Creating a sharing link](/sharing/create-link) - [Revoking a sharing link](/sharing/revoke-link)

title: Inspect a failed Zapier run
summary: Inspect a failed Zapier task, classify Dosya authentication, scope, throttling, or input errors, and preserve enough evidence for a safe retry.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/zapier/src/middleware.js, apps/zapier/src/authentication.js, apps/zapier/src/lib/files.js, apps/zapier/test/middleware.test.js. Production behavior for “Inspect a failed Zapier run” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A Dosya step keeps the API’s error text and HTTP status for most failures. Authentication, anchored-key, and rate-limit responses are translated into distinct Zapier errors, so the response class determines the next action. ## Steps 1. Open the failed Zap execution in Zapier history and select the first failed Dosya step, not a later step that was skipped because of it. 2. Record the Zap name, run ID, step label, time, HTTP status, and redacted Dosya response. Never copy the `dos_…` API key, Authorization header, access code, or recipient secret. 3. Classify `401` as a connection failure. The integration raises Zapier’s reconnect-required error; replace the credential with a current full-scope, unanchored key. 4. For `403`, read the exact message. A folder-anchored key produces the corrective text **Create a key with no folder anchor and full scope, then reconnect.** A read or upload key is also insufficient for webhook triggers. 5. For `429`, retain the `Retry-After` value. Dosya raises a throttled error using that delay, or 60 seconds when the response has no usable header. 6. For other statuses, fix the preserved Dosya message or mapped input before replay. Check Dosya for an already-created result after a timeout, because some actions may have succeeded before Zapier lost the response. Credential middleware attaches the key only to the exact Dosya API origin and disables redirect following on authenticated requests. A third-party file-source failure therefore remains that provider’s error rather than being mislabeled as a Dosya reconnect problem. ## Expected result The failed run is tied to one step, request class, and nonsecret evidence set. Authentication failures lead to reconnection, throttling waits for the supplied delay, input or permission failures are corrected, and ambiguous writes are checked before replay. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Troubleshoot Zapier](/troubleshooting/zapier)

title: Map a Dosya file identifier in Zapier
summary: Map Dosya’s stable File ID in Zapier, distinguish root from an unknown folder, and keep actions pointed at the intended file across versions.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/zapier/src/lib/file-row.js, apps/zapier/src/triggers/new-file.js, apps/zapier/src/searches/find-file.js, apps/zapier/src/lib/files.js. Production behavior for “Map a Dosya file identifier in Zapier” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya file names can repeat and can change. Zapier outputs the stable identifier as both `id` and `file_id`; either value identifies the same file record, while `name` is display data. ## Steps 1. In the source Dosya trigger or **Find a File** step, test with a uniquely named non-confidential file and inspect the returned fields. 2. Map **File ID** (`file_id`) into downstream Dosya actions that ask for a file. The top-level `id` is identical and exists so Zapier can deduplicate trigger deliveries. 3. Do not map **File name** as the identity. Two folders can contain the same name, and a later rename leaves the stable file ID unchanged. 4. Use `folder_id` only for routing. A `null` folder ID explicitly means workspace root; it does not mean the integration failed to inspect the folder. 5. When version matters, use `version` from a **New File** webhook or trigger sample. **Find a File** deliberately promises no version because its two search paths do not return a consistent version field. 6. Run one downstream test and compare the returned file ID with the source output. If using a saved sample, refresh it before publishing so the test record still exists and belongs to the chosen workspace. A trigger’s `file` field is a lazy pointer. Zapier downloads the bytes only when a later step actually uses that field; mapping name or ID alone does not transfer the file or consume download egress. ## Expected result The action receives the exact stable Dosya file ID and targets the intended record even when names repeat or the file gains versions. Folder routing treats `null` as root, and workflows do not invent a version when the search response lacks one. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Troubleshoot Zapier](/troubleshooting/zapier)

title: Use the Dosya new-file trigger in Zapier
summary: Configure Zapier’s Dosya New File trigger with the required key and workspace, test one current sample, and exclude ordinary version uploads.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/zapier/src/authentication.js, apps/zapier/src/triggers/new-file.js, apps/zapier/src/lib/hooks.js, apps/zapier/src/lib/file-row.js, apps/zapier/test/acceptance.dedupe.test.js. Production behavior for “Use the Dosya new-file trigger in Zapier” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: **New File** subscribes one Zap webhook to the `file.uploaded` event for a required workspace. It returns only brand-new file records; an upload that creates a new version of an existing file is deliberately ignored. ## Steps 1. Create a Dosya API key at `https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api` with **full** scope. Do not folder-anchor it; REST rejects anchored keys. Pin the key to one workspace when narrower access is required. 2. In Zapier add the Dosya **New File** trigger and connect that key. The connection test calls the current user endpoint and rejects any scope other than `full` before the Zap is enabled. 3. Choose **Workspace**. Subscription creates one webhook endpoint for this Zap and event, labeled `Zapier (Zap )` when Zapier supplies the ID. 4. Upload one new, non-confidential file to the chosen workspace. Do not overwrite an existing file for this test, because deliveries with `is_new_version: true` return no trigger item. 5. Use Zapier’s trigger test to load a sample. Sampling lists the workspace root, then at most 12 folders until it finds about 25 recent rows; a very large workspace is intentionally not exhaustively scanned. 6. Confirm **File ID**, **File name**, **Size in bytes**, **Folder ID**, and **Version**, then publish the Zap. Switch it off cleanly so Zapier can delete the stored webhook endpoint. If unsubscription reports **Cannot unsubscribe: no dosya webhook endpoint id was stored for this Zap**, the app refuses to pretend cleanup succeeded. Resolve the stale connection so an endpoint is not leaked against webhook limits. ## Expected result One newly created file in the selected workspace produces one trigger item whose `id` and `file_id` are the stable file ID. New versions are ignored, and repeated delivery of the same event uses the same `id` so Zapier can deduplicate it. ## Related guides - [Connect Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Connect n8n](/integrations/n8n-connect)

title: Reconnect Dosya in Zapier
summary: Reconnect Zapier to Dosya with a current full-scope, unanchored API key, then verify workspace access before replaying failed automation runs.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/zapier/src/authentication.js, apps/zapier/src/middleware.js, apps/zapier/src/dropdowns/workspace.js, apps/zapier/test/authentication.test.js. Production behavior for “Reconnect Dosya in Zapier” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Dosya converts an API `401` into Zapier’s reconnect-required error. Recovery requires a replacement API key; reconnecting with a read, upload, or folder-anchored key will connect incompletely or fail when the Zap subscribes or calls REST. ## Steps 1. Open the affected Zapier connection and record which Zaps use it. In Dosya, open `https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api` under the intended account. 2. Create a new key with **full** scope. Do not choose a folder anchor; folder-anchored credentials work only with WebDAV or S3 and the Zapier integration uses the REST API. 3. If access must be limited, pin the key to the single workspace the Zaps need. Copy the secret at creation and store it in Zapier’s **dosya API key** field; do not place it in a Zap input. 4. Run the connection test. A non-full key reports **This key has “” scope… Create a full-scope key and reconnect.** An anchored key tells you to create an unanchored full-scope key. 5. Retest each trigger’s workspace dropdown and one read-only lookup before enabling writes. A pinned key should expose the intended workspace and refuse unrelated ones. 6. After all dependent Zaps use the new connection, revoke the old key in Dosya. Then monitor the first live event or controlled action and preserve any status other than success. The integration labels the connection with the Dosya user email returned by `/api/me`. Treat that label as an account check, then use the workspace dropdown or a pinned-key refusal to verify actual workspace scope. ## Expected result Zapier authenticates as the intended Dosya account with a full-scope key and can reach the chosen workspace. Existing Zaps have been retested before the old key is revoked, so the credential rotation does not silently strand a webhook or write step. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Troubleshoot Zapier](/troubleshooting/zapier)

title: Refresh a Dosya trigger sample in Zapier
summary: Create a current Dosya file sample for Zapier, understand the bounded workspace scan, and remap fields without changing the live trigger scope.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/zapier/src/triggers/new-file.js, apps/zapier/src/lib/file-row.js, apps/zapier/src/lib/samples.js, apps/zapier/test/triggers.new-file.test.js. Production behavior for “Refresh a Dosya trigger sample in Zapier” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: Testing **New File** loads recent file rows; it does not wait for a webhook delivery or scan an unlimited workspace. The loader checks root first, then a bounded set of folders, and returns the same field shape as live events. ## Steps 1. Confirm the Zap uses Dosya **New File** and the intended **Workspace**. Refreshing a sample does not change that saved workspace or recreate the live webhook by itself. 2. Create a small, uniquely named file in the workspace root when possible. Root is checked first and is the most reliable location for a sample in a workspace with many folders. 3. If the file must be in a folder, place it within a folder likely to appear early in the workspace tree. Sampling probes at most 12 folders and stops after collecting about 25 rows. 4. Run Zapier’s trigger test again. The loader requests up to 100 newest files per probed location, then maps the real `current_version` rather than defaulting every sample to version 1. 5. Choose the newly named sample and remap downstream fields if their schema was stale. Check `file_id`, `folder_id`, and `version`; a root file correctly has `folder_id: null`. 6. Publish only after one downstream test uses the refreshed File ID. Delete the test file later only if no published step still depends on it as fixed input. If the new file is absent, the bounded loader may simply not have reached its folder. Move a disposable sample to workspace root rather than repeatedly creating files throughout the workspace. ## Expected result The editor shows a current, identifiable Dosya sample with the same keys a live event supplies. The sample’s folder and version are accurate, and the live trigger remains scoped to the previously selected workspace. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Troubleshoot Zapier](/troubleshooting/zapier)

title: Retry a Zap without duplicate side effects
summary: Check Dosya after an ambiguous Zapier failure, identify idempotent upload retries, and avoid replaying actions that can create duplicate links.
verification: Source-reviewed locally on 2026-10-14 against apps/zapier/src/lib/files.js, apps/zapier/src/creates/upload-file.js, apps/zapier/src/creates/create-share-link.js, apps/api/src/pages/api/upload/file.ts, apps/zapier/test/acceptance.dedupe.test.js. Production behavior for “Retry a Zap without duplicate side effects” was not exercised; this revision is awaiting publication.
body: A failed Zapier task does not always mean Dosya rejected the write. If the network failed after acceptance, replay can duplicate a non-idempotent action. The safe decision depends on the specific Dosya operation. ## Steps 1. Open the failed run and capture its run ID, Dosya step, input file or target ID, time, status, and redacted error. Do not retry the whole Zap yet. 2. Check the destination workspace for the expected result. Match stable file ID, name, target folder, or returned share URL—not name alone—within the failed run’s time window. 3. For **Upload File**, a replay of the same Zap run is protected by a deterministic UUID `Idempotency-Key`; the one-shot upload route reclaims the same result instead of creating another version. 4. Do not apply that promise to a fresh Zap run or **Create Share Link**. Share creation has no equivalent Zap-run idempotency guard, so an ambiguous first request may already have made an active link. 5. If the result already exists, continue downstream with its recorded ID or URL rather than replaying creation. If it does not exist and the error proves rejection, retry only the failed step. 6. After recovery, verify one intended artifact and inspect for extras. Revoke any unintended share link; do not delete a duplicate file until confirming no later step references its ID. The direct **Upload File** action is limited to 50 MB; larger inputs fail with guidance to use **Upload File From URL**. A size refusal is definitive and safe to correct, while a timeout after a write remains ambiguous. ## Expected result The recovered workflow produces one intended side effect. Same-run Upload File retries reuse their idempotency key, while ambiguous share creation and fresh-run writes are checked in Dosya before any manual replay. ## Related guides - [Connect Dosya to Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Troubleshoot Zapier](/troubleshooting/zapier)

title: Troubleshoot a Dosya Zapier automation
summary: Trace a failed Zap through invitation, account connection, key restrictions, trigger subscription, sample data, field mapping, upload, and replay.
verification: Source-reviewed 2026-10-14 against apps/web/src/pages/integrations/zapier.tsx; apps/web/src/lib/integrations.ts; apps/zapier/src/authentication.js; apps/zapier/src/middleware.js; apps/zapier/src/lib/hooks.js; apps/zapier/src/lib/file-row.js; apps/zapier/src/triggers/new-file.js; apps/zapier/src/triggers/new-file-in-folder.js; apps/zapier/src/creates/upload-file.js; apps/zapier/src/creates/upload-file-from-url.js; apps/zapier/src/lib/files.js; apps/zapier/src/creates/create-share-link.js. No live Zap was published or replayed. Local repository evidence only; no production request was made.
body: Open the failed run in Zap history and identify the first Dosya step that did not produce the expected output. Record its time, connected-account label, input fields, status and redacted response. A missing trigger, failed action and completed-but-mis-mapped action require different repairs. ## Steps Dosya is currently a private Zapier app. Sign in to the Zapier account that owns the Zap, open Dosya **Integrations → Zapier**, select **Open the Zapier invite**, and accept it in that same account. Searching the public app directory will not find the private integration. An organization can require administrator approval for private apps. The connected account uses a complete `dos_…` API key from **Profile → API keys**. It must have **Full access**, permit **REST API**, and have no folder anchor. Pinning one workspace is supported. The account label in Zapier is the key owner's email, so compare that label before replacing anything. Use the returned message: - A 401 asks Zapier to refresh authentication. Replace an expired, revoked or incorrect key and retest the connection. - **This key has “…” scope. dosya needs a key with full scope to subscribe to file events. Create a full-scope key and reconnect.** means Read only/Upload only cannot create the trigger subscription. - **This dosya API key is anchored to a folder, which cannot be used over the REST API. Create a key with no folder anchor and full scope, then reconnect.** identifies an incompatible WebDAV/S3-style anchor. - A 403 with another message can come from protocol restriction, workspace pin, active hours, IP policy, membership or role. Correct the named boundary rather than repeatedly reconnecting. - A 429 is surfaced as a throttled Zapier error and uses the response's `Retry-After` or 60 seconds. Wait instead of replaying several runs. Create a dedicated replacement before revoking the old key when the Zap must remain available. Removing a Zapier connection or revoking its key stops future requests but does not delete files or share links already created. ## If New File does not trigger When a Zap is turned on, Dosya creates one webhook endpoint for that Zap and event. Full access plus workspace **manage_settings** is needed to subscribe. Endpoint caps or a role refusal can therefore appear when enabling a trigger even though the connection test succeeded. Confirm the trigger's **Workspace**. For **New File in Folder**, confirm **Folder** as well; leaving it empty watches only the workspace root. Then upload a genuinely new, uniquely named file and wait for its Dosya upload to complete. `New File` and `New File in Folder` intentionally ignore an overwrite/new version (`is_new_version: true`). Re-uploading under an existing path is not a valid trigger test. Trigger sample loading can return recent files that already existed; publishing does not replay those old samples. If **Test trigger** has no useful record, add a new harmless file in the selected scope and request samples again. Workspace-wide sampling collects at most 25 recent files while probing the root and up to 12 folders, so an older item can be absent even though future live events work. ## If an action targets the wrong item Inspect the failed step's **Data in**. Map **File ID** (`file_id`/`id`) or **Folder ID** from the trigger/search output, not the visible name. Names can repeat across folders. A root item has a null Folder ID, which is a real location rather than missing data. For **Create Share Link**, choose **Share a → File** or **Folder** and map the corresponding ID. **Choose a file to share.** or **Choose a folder to share.** means the required mapped identifier was empty. The action test creates a real public link; verify its target and expiry in Dosya, then revoke an unwanted test link. The optional **Access code** protects recipients and is not the Dosya account password. ## If Upload File fails or times out **File** must be a Zapier file object or directly downloadable URL. A preview/login page may answer HTTP 200 and be uploaded as HTML, so verify the saved bytes. Supply **File name** explicitly; the current fallback name is `upload` when that field is empty. The **Upload File** action accepts at most 52,428,800 bytes (50 MiB) and has Zapier's 30-second action deadline. Use the exact result: | Failure | Recovery | | --- | --- | | **Could not fetch the file: the source at … answered with status …** | Refresh or authorize the upstream file reference. Dosya credentials are not sent to that third-party host. | | **This file is larger than 50 MB…** | Use **Upload File From URL** with a public HTTPS source; Dosya performs that import asynchronously. | | **The app did not respond in-time. It may or may not have completed successfully.** | Check the target folder and Zap history before replaying. The first upload may already have committed. | | File saved as a web page | Replace the browser preview/login URL with a direct-download file output and use a new test name. | | Storage, extension or permission refusal | Resolve the actual workspace/key/role policy, then retest one small item. | The same Zap run derives a stable idempotency key for Upload File, so a retry of that run can reclaim its saved result. A new run is a different identity. Uploading the same visible name in one folder creates a Dosya version; use event-specific names when separate files are intended. **Upload File From URL** pauses until Dosya calls Zapier back. A failed callback appears as **dosya could not import that file: …**. Record its job ID and error code. Testing while Zapier loads sample fields returns sample output without starting a real long download, so verify one published/live run separately. ## Replay without duplicate side effects Before replaying a task, search Dosya by the returned File ID, Share ID, request ID or exact event-specific name. If the expected resource exists, continue from the failed downstream step when Zapier permits it. Re-running a create action can add a file version, link, folder or request. After the correction, test the single Dosya step with one non-confidential item. Confirm its output IDs, inspect the actual Dosya resource, then turn on the Zap and trigger one new live event. Keep it off while repairing mapping that could affect production files or recipients. For unresolved failures, send private support the Zap step name, operation, run time/timezone, account label, workspace ID, mapped field names, returned status/error, and nonsecret resource/job identifiers. Redact API keys, private share URLs, access codes, external signed file URLs and file content. ## Expected result The repaired Zap uses the intended Dosya account and workspace, processes one controlled test item, and leaves a single matching result in Task history and Dosya. ## Related guides - [Connect Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Choose key permission](/developers/api-key-scopes) - [Revoke a key](/developers/revoke-api-key)

keywords: Zapier upload file to cloud storage
body: Use the **dosya** app's **Upload File** action to copy a file from a Zap trigger or previous action into Dosya cloud storage. The **File** input is a Zapier file reference or downloadable URL, not n8n binary data or pasted base64 text. ## Accept the private-app invite and connect the account Dosya is currently a private Zapier app, so it does not appear in Zapier's public app search. Sign in to the Zapier account that will own the workflow. In the Dosya web app, open **Integrations → Zapier**, select **Open the Zapier invite**, and accept the invite with that same Zapier account. If your Zapier organization restricts private apps, ask its administrator to approve Dosya before building the Zap. When Dosya is missing from the step picker, revisit the setup page and confirm the invitation was accepted by the account currently open in Zapier. Return to the Zap editor, add **dosya → Upload File**, and connect it with **dosya API key**. Create the key at [Profile → API keys](https://app.dosya.dev/profile/api): choose **Full access**, enable **REST API** and leave the folder anchor empty. Pin it to a workspace if the Zap should access only that workspace. Do not use your Dosya password. The connection is labelled with the key owner's email. The authentication check requires full scope because the integration also subscribes to file events. Its scope error reads **This key has “…” scope. dosya needs a key with full scope to subscribe to file events. Create a full-scope key and reconnect.** A Full access key still needs the member's upload permission for the destination; workspace pinning, expiry and any explicit key limits are enforced. Folder-anchored WebDAV/S3 keys are unsuitable for this REST integration. ## Steps: configure and test Upload File 1. Test a trigger or file-producing action with a fresh, non-confidential file. Inspect the sample for an actual file reference or a direct-download URL. A preview page, login page or ordinary cloud-sharing page may return HTML rather than the desired file. 2. Add **dosya → Upload File** and select the connected account. Configure the fields below. | Action field | What to select | | --- | --- | | **Workspace** (required) | The intended workspace from the account's available list. | | **Folder** (optional) | A folder in that workspace; empty means workspace root. | | **File** (required) | The previous step's file reference, or a URL that Zapier can download without an interactive login. | | **File name** (optional) | An explicit name with extension, such as `zap-proof-20261014.pdf`. | 3. Use a unique File name for the first check. Although the field hint says the incoming name is retained, the current action actually defaults to **upload** if File name is empty. Map the upstream filename or enter one to preserve its extension and type. 4. Run the action's test once. Read **File ID**, **File name**, **Size in bytes** and **Folder ID** in the result, then inspect that file in Dosya before running the test again. 5. Check the entire Zap's trigger filters and downstream actions. Publish/turn on the Zap only after confirming its real destination and repeat-run behavior. A successful setup test already writes a real file; publishing does not undo it. Zapier resolves file objects into URLs for the action. Dosya's integration downloads the source without sending your Dosya API key to that external host, then uploads the received bytes. A public URL must return file content directly and remain valid when the Zap runs. For expiring references, refresh old test data. Avoid links requiring browser cookies; use your source app's file/download output. An HTTP 200 login/preview page can still be saved as a file, so verify the contents, not just success status. ## Verify the result and downstream mapping The result includes `id`, `file_id`, `name`, `size` and `folder_id`; `file_id` duplicates `id`. The selectable fields expose File ID, File name, Size in bytes and Folder ID. An upload to the top level has a null Folder ID. This action returns no `version` field and no dehydrated `file` pointer for another app to download. Do not map either from its sample. Use File ID in another Dosya action when you need an operation on the saved file. Open **Files** in the chosen Dosya workspace, locate the target folder and check the exact name/size. Download the sample to confirm its contents. Upload File does not create a public share link; recipients receive nothing unless another Zap step deliberately sends or shares it. ## Upload limits and retries The action accepts at most **52,428,800 bytes (50 MiB)**. The displayed message calls this **50 MB**. Declared source size is checked before buffering; actual downloaded size is checked too. Missing Content-Length and decompressed responses are measured from their real bytes. For a larger file choose **Upload File From URL**, which imports on Dosya's side instead of passing the file through this action; plan storage and upload policies still apply to that import. Zapier actions have a **30-second** execution deadline, so even a file under the ceiling can time out when download plus upload is slow. After **The app did not respond in-time. It may or may not have completed successfully.**, inspect Dosya and the run history before replaying. A run-based idempotency key allows retrying the same upload to reuse its saved result. A new run is distinct, and an intentional replay must not be assumed to reuse the original run identity. If the same visible filename already exists in that folder, Dosya writes a new version rather than another file with that name. Use stable naming when versioning is wanted and an event-specific name when separate files are wanted. A revoked key cannot authorize future runs; removing a connected account does not delete files already saved. Same-name updates change the current contents, so test in a dedicated folder before mapping production filenames. ## Recover from a failed test | Failure | Recovery | | --- | --- | | **Could not fetch the file: the source at … answered with status …** | Repair the source URL/access or refresh the source file reference. A 404/500 response is rejected before a Dosya upload. | | File contains a web page | Replace the preview/login URL with a direct file output and verify a new test name. A 200 response alone cannot establish correct contents. | | **This file is larger than 50 MB, which is the limit for the Upload File action.** | Switch to Upload File From URL; confirm the source is accessible to the import service and the plan has capacity. | | Authentication failure or full-scope message | Reconnect with a complete, valid Full access API key, without a folder anchor. | | Workspace/Folder missing or 403 | Check account email, pin and member permissions, then reload the field choices. Do not select a similarly named folder in another workspace. | | Storage or file-policy refusal | Resolve the actual account/workspace/key limit shown in the response before replaying. | | Timeout | Check whether a file/version was already saved; use a smaller/faster source or the asynchronous URL action. | ## Expected result The tested Zap action returns a real File ID whose bytes match the source in the chosen Dosya folder. After publishing, monitor the first live run and its filename/version behavior before relying on unattended uploads. ## Related guides - [Connect Zapier](/integrations/zapier) - [Manage API keys](/developers/api-key)
